Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Vinayapiṭake

In the Vinaya Piṭaka

Mahāvaggapāḷi

The Mahāvagga Pāḷi

1. Mahākhandhako

1. The Great Section

1. Bodhikathā

1. The Account of the Awakening

1. udā. 1 ādayo Tena [P 1.0001][M 0.0001][V 0.0001][T 1.0001] samayena buddho bhagavā uruvelāyaṃ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre bodhirukkhamūle paṭhamābhisambuddho. Atha kho bhagavā bodhirukkhamūle sattāhaṃ ekapallaṅkena nisīdi vimuttisukhapaṭisaṃvedī vimuttisukhaṃ paṭisaṃvedī (ka.). Atha kho bhagavā rattiyā paṭhamaṃ yāmaṃ paṭiccasamuppādaṃ anulomapaṭilomaṃ manasākāsi – “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ, nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ, saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti – evametassa [V 0.0002] kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti. “Avijjāyatveva asesavirāganirodhā saṅkhāranirodho, saṅkhāranirodhā viññāṇanirodho, viññāṇanirodhā nāmarūpanirodho, nāmarūpanirodhā saḷāyatananirodho, saḷāyatananirodhā phassanirodho, phassanirodhā vedanānirodho, vedanānirodhā taṇhānirodho, taṇhānirodhā upādānanirodho[T 1.0002], upādānanirodhā bhavanirodho, bhavanirodhā jātinirodho, jātinirodhā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā nirujjhanti – evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho [P 1.0002] hotī”ti.

1. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Uruvelā, on the bank of the river Nerañjarā, at the foot of the Bodhi tree, having first attained full enlightenment. Then the Blessed One sat at the foot of the Bodhi tree for seven days in one cross-legged posture, experiencing the bliss of liberation. Then, in the first watch of the night, the Blessed One attended to dependent origination in forward and reverse order: “From ignorance as condition, formations come to be; from formations as condition, consciousness comes to be; from consciousness as condition, name-and-form comes to be; from name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases come to be; from the six sense bases as condition, contact comes to be; from contact as condition, feeling comes to be; from feeling as condition, craving comes to be; from craving as condition, clinging comes to be; from clinging as condition, becoming comes to be; from becoming as condition, birth comes to be; from birth as condition, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair come to be. Thus is the origin of this whole mass of suffering. From the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very ignorance, there is the cessation of formations; from the cessation of formations, there is the cessation of consciousness; from the cessation of consciousness, there is the cessation of name-and-form; from the cessation of name-and-form, there is the cessation of the six sense bases; from the cessation of the six sense bases, there is the cessation of contact; from the cessation of contact, there is the cessation of feeling; from the cessation of feeling, there is the cessation of craving; from the cessation of craving, there is the cessation of clinging; from the cessation of clinging, there is the cessation of becoming; from the cessation of becoming, there is the cessation of birth; from the cessation of birth, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cease. Thus is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

Atha [M 0.0002] kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

“Yadā have pātubhavanti dhammā;

Ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa;

Athassa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā;

Yato pajānāti sahetudhamma”nti.

“When, indeed, phenomena become manifest to the ardent, meditating brahmin, then all his doubts are dispelled, for he understands the Dhamma together with its cause.”

2. udā. 2 Atha kho bhagavā rattiyā majjhimaṃ yāmaṃ paṭiccasamuppādaṃ anulomapaṭilomaṃ manasākāsi – “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ…pe… [T 1.0003] evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī…pe… nirodho hotī”ti.

2. Then, during the middle watch of the night, the Blessed One attended to dependent origination in forward and reverse order: “From ignorance as condition, formations come to be; from formations as condition, consciousness comes to be; from consciousness as condition, name-and-form comes to be… and so on… Thus is the origin of this whole mass of suffering… and so on… Thus is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

“Yadā have pātubhavanti dhammā;

Ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa;

Athassa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā;

Yato khayaṃ paccayānaṃ avedī”ti.

“When, indeed, phenomena become manifest to the ardent, meditating brahmin, then all his doubts are dispelled, because he has known the destruction of the conditions.”

3. udā. 3 Atha kho bhagavā rattiyā pacchimaṃ yāmaṃ paṭiccasamuppādaṃ anulomapaṭilomaṃ manasākāsi – “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ…pe… [T 1.0004] evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti…pe… nirodho hotī”ti.

3. Then, during the last watch of the night, the Blessed One attended to dependent origination in forward and reverse order: “From ignorance as condition, formations come to be; from formations as condition, consciousness comes to be; from consciousness as condition, name-and-form comes to be… and so on… Thus is the origin of this whole mass of suffering… and so on… Thus is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

Atha [V 0.0003] kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

“Yadā have pātubhavanti dhammā;

Ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa;

Vidhūpayaṃ tiṭṭhati mārasenaṃ;

Sūriyova suriyova (sī. syā. kaṃ.) obhāsayamantalikkha”nti.

“When, indeed, phenomena become manifest to the ardent, meditating brahmin, he stands dispelling the army of Māra, like the sun illuminating the sky.”

Bodhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Awakening is concluded.

2. Ajapālakathā

2. The Account at the Goatherd's Banyan

4. udā. 4 Atha [M 0.0003] kho bhagavā sattāhassa accayena tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhahitvā bodhirukkhamūlā yena ajapālanigrodho tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā ajapālanigrodhamūle sattāhaṃ ekapallaṅkena nisīdi vimuttisukhapaṭisaṃvedī. Atha kho aññataro huṃhuṅkajātiko brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ [T 1.0005] sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ [P 1.0003] etadavoca – “kittāvatā nu kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇo hoti, katame ca pana brāhmaṇakaraṇā brāhmaṇakārakā (ka.) brāhmaṇakarāṇā (?) dhammā”ti? Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

4. Then, after the passing of seven days, the Blessed One, having arisen from that concentration, went from the foot of the Bodhi tree to the Ajapāla banyan tree. Having approached, he sat at the foot of the Ajapāla banyan tree for seven days in one cross-legged posture, experiencing the bliss of liberation. Then a certain brahmin of a haughty nature approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded courteous and memorable talk, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, that brahmin said this to the Blessed One: “By what measure, Master Gotama, is one a brahmin? And what, indeed, are the qualities that make one a brahmin?” Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

netti. 103 Yo brāhmaṇo bāhitapāpadhammo;

Nihuṃhuṅko nikkasāvo yatatto;

Vedantagū vusitabrahmacariyo;

Dhammena so brahmavādaṃ vadeyya;

Yassussadā natthi kuhiñci loke”ti.

“The brahmin who has banished evil qualities, free from haughtiness, stainless, and self-controlled, a master of knowledge who has lived the holy life—rightly may he speak the word ‘brahmin,’ for whom there is no arrogance anywhere in the world.”

Ajapālakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account at the Goatherd's Banyan is concluded.

3. Mucalindakathā

3. The Account of Mucalinda

5. udā. 11 Atha kho bhagavā sattāhassa accayena tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhahitvā ajapālanigrodhamūlā [V 0.0004] yena mucalindo tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā mucalindamūle sattāhaṃ ekapallaṅkena nisīdi vimuttisukhapaṭisaṃvedī. Tena kho pana samayena mahā akālamegho udapādi, sattāhavaddalikā sītavātaduddinī. Atha kho mucalindo nāgarājā sakabhavanā nikkhamitvā bhagavato kāyaṃ sattakkhattuṃ bhogehi parikkhipitvā uparimuddhani [T 1.0006] mahantaṃ phaṇaṃ karitvā aṭṭhāsi – “mā bhagavantaṃ sītaṃ, mā bhagavantaṃ uṇhaṃ, mā bhagavantaṃ ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphasso”ti …siriṃ sapa… (sī. syā. kaṃ.). Atha [M 0.0004] kho mucalindo nāgarājā sattāhassa accayena viddhaṃ vigatavalāhakaṃ devaṃ viditvā bhagavato kāyā bhoge viniveṭhetvā sakavaṇṇaṃ paṭisaṃharitvā māṇavakavaṇṇaṃ abhinimminitvā bhagavato purato aṭṭhāsi pañjaliko bhagavantaṃ namassamāno. Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

5. Then, after the passing of seven days, the Blessed One arose from that concentration and went from the foot of the Ajapāla banyan tree to the Mucalinda tree. Having approached, he sat cross-legged at the foot of the Mucalinda tree for seven days, experiencing the bliss of liberation. At that time, a great unseasonal cloud arose, bringing a seven-day downpour with cold winds and gloomy weather. Then the Nāga king Mucalinda, coming out from his own abode, encircled the Blessed One's body seven times with his coils. He spread his great hood above the Blessed One’s head and stood there, thinking: "May the Blessed One not be afflicted by cold, may the Blessed One not be afflicted by heat, may the Blessed One not be afflicted by the touch of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, or creeping things." Then, after the passing of seven days, the Nāga king Mucalinda, knowing the sky to be clear and free from clouds, unwound his coils from the Blessed One's body. Withdrawing his own form, he created the appearance of a young man and stood before the Blessed One with hands joined in reverence, paying homage to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

kathā. 338 kathāvatthupāḷiyampi“Sukho viveko tuṭṭhassa, sutadhammassa passato;

Abyāpajjaṃ sukhaṃ loke, pāṇabhūtesu saṃyamo.

Blissful is seclusion for one who is content, who has heard the Dhamma and sees; blissful is non-affliction in the world, and restraint towards living beings.

kathā. 338 kathāvatthupāḷiyampi“Sukhā virāgatā loke, kāmānaṃ samatikkamo;

Asmimānassa yo vinayo, etaṃ ve paramaṃ sukha”nti.

Blissful is dispassion in the world, the overcoming of sensual pleasures; the subduing of the conceit ‘I am’—this is truly the supreme bliss.

Mucalindakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of Mucalinda is concluded.

4. Rājāyatanakathā

4. The Account of the Rājāyatana Tree

6. Atha kho bhagavā sattāhassa accayena tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhahitvā mucalindamūlā yena rājāyatanaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā rājāyatanamūle sattāhaṃ ekapallaṅkena nisīdi vimuttisukhapaṭisaṃvedī. Tena kho pana [P 1.0004] samayena tapussa tapassu (sī.) bhallikā vāṇijā ukkalā taṃ desaṃ addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Atha kho tapussabhallikānaṃ vāṇijānaṃ [T 1.0007] ñātisālohitā devatā tapussabhallike vāṇije etadavoca – “ayaṃ, mārisā, bhagavā rājāyatanamūle viharati paṭhamābhisambuddho; gacchatha taṃ bhagavantaṃ manthena ca madhupiṇḍikāya ca patimānetha; taṃ vo bhavissati dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā”ti. Atha kho tapussabhallikā vāṇijā manthañca madhupiṇḍikañca ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho tapussabhallikā vāṇijā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “paṭiggaṇhātu no, bhante, bhagavā manthañca madhupiṇḍikañca, yaṃ amhākaṃ assa dīgharattaṃ hitāya [V 0.0005] sukhāyā”ti. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “na kho tathāgatā hatthesu paṭiggaṇhanti. Kimhi nu kho ahaṃ paṭiggaṇheyyaṃ manthañca madhupiṇḍikañcā”ti? Atha [M 0.0005] kho cattāro mahārājāno bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya catuddisā cattāro selamaye patte bhagavato upanāmesuṃ – “idha, bhante, bhagavā paṭiggaṇhātu manthañca madhupiṇḍikañcā”ti. Paṭiggahesi bhagavā paccagghe selamaye patte manthañca madhupiṇḍikañca, paṭiggahetvā paribhuñji. Atha kho tapussabhallikā vāṇijā bhagavantaṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ viditvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ (onītapattapāṇiṃ viditvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ) ( ) sī. syā. potthakesu natthi etadavocuṃ – “ete mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma dhammañca, upāsake no bhagavā dhāretu [T 1.0008] ajjatagge pāṇupete saraṇaṃ gate”ti. Te ca loke paṭhamaṃ upāsakā ahesuṃ dvevācikā.

6. Then, after seven days, the Blessed One arose from that concentration and went from the foot of the Mucalinda tree to the Rājāyatana tree. Having approached, he sat at the foot of the Rājāyatana tree for seven days in a single cross-legged posture, experiencing the bliss of liberation. Now at that time, the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika from Ukkalā were journeying on a long road to that region. Then a deity who was a blood relative of the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika said this to them: ‘Sirs, this Blessed One, newly enlightened, is dwelling at the foot of the Rājāyatana tree. Go and honor that Blessed One with barley-meal and honey-balls. That will be for your long-term welfare and happiness.’ Then the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika, taking the barley-meal and the honey-balls, approached the Blessed One. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they stood to one side. Standing to one side, the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika said this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, may the Blessed One accept from us this barley-meal and these honey-balls, so that it may be for our long-term welfare and happiness.’ Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: ‘Tathāgatas do not accept with their hands. In what, then, should I accept the barley-meal and the honey-balls?’ Then the Four Great Kings, knowing with their own minds the thought in the Blessed One’s mind, from the four directions offered four bowls made of stone to the Blessed One, saying: ‘Venerable sir, in these may the Blessed One accept the barley-meal and the honey-balls.’ The Blessed One accepted the precious stone bowls with the barley-meal and the honey-balls; and having accepted them, he partook of them. Then the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika, knowing that the Blessed One had withdrawn his hand from the bowl, prostrated themselves with their heads at the Blessed One’s feet and said this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, we go to the Blessed One for refuge, and to the Dhamma. May the Blessed One remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts.’ They were the first lay followers in the world to take the twofold formula of refuge.

Rājāyatanakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Rājāyatana Week is concluded.

5. Brahmayācanakathā

5. The Account of Brahmā's Entreaty

7. ayaṃ brahmayācanakathā dī. ni. 2.64 ādayo; ma. ni. 1.281 ādayo; ma. ni. 2.336 ādayo; saṃ. ni. 1.172 ādayo Atha kho bhagavā sattāhassa accayena tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhahitvā rājāyatanamūlā yena ajapālanigrodho tenupasaṅkami. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā ajapālanigrodhamūle viharati. Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “adhigato kho myāyaṃ dhammo gambhīro duddaso duranubodho santo paṇīto atakkāvacaro nipuṇo paṇḍitavedanīyo. Ālayarāmā kho panāyaṃ pajā ālayaratā ālayasammuditā. Ālayarāmāya kho pana pajāya ālayaratāya ālayasammuditāya duddasaṃ idaṃ ṭhānaṃ [P 1.0005] yadidaṃ idappaccayatāpaaccasamuppādo; idampi kho ṭhānaṃ sududdasaṃ yadidaṃ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānaṃ. Ahañceva kho pana dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ, pare ca me na ājāneyyuṃ, so mamassa kilamatho, sā mamassa vihesā”ti. Apissu bhagavantaṃ imā anacchariyā gāthāyo paṭibhaṃsu pubbe assutapubbā –

7. Then, after the passing of seven days, the Blessed One, having arisen from that concentration, went from the foot of the Rājāyatana tree to where the Ajapāla banyan tree was. There the Blessed One dwelt at the foot of the Ajapāla banyan tree. Then, to the Blessed One, who had gone to a secluded place and was dwelling in solitude, this reflection of the mind arose: 'This Dhamma that has been attained by me is profound, difficult to see, difficult to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the sphere of reasoning, subtle, to be known by the wise. But this generation delights in attachment, is fond of attachment, and greatly rejoices in attachment. For a generation that delights in attachment, is fond of attachment, and greatly rejoices in attachment, this state is difficult to see, that is, this conditionality, Dependent Origination. This state, too, is very difficult to see, that is, the stilling of all formations, the relinquishing of all substrates, the destruction of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna. If I were to teach the Dhamma, and others were not to understand me, that would be a weariness for me, that would be a vexation for me.' Moreover, these amazing verses, never heard before, occurred to the Blessed One:

“Kicchena [T 1.0009] me adhigataṃ, halaṃ dāni pakāsituṃ;

Rāgadosaparetehi, nāyaṃ dhammo susambudho.

What was attained by me with difficulty, it is not fit to proclaim now. By those overcome by lust and hate, this Dhamma is not easily understood.

“Paṭisotagāmiṃ [M 0.0006] nipuṇaṃ, gambhīraṃ duddasaṃ aṇuṃ;

Rāgarattā na dakkhanti, tamokhandhena āvuṭā āvaṭā (sī.)”ti.

Going against the stream, subtle, profound, difficult to see, and minute; those dyed with lust will not see it, being covered by the mass of darkness.

Itiha [V 0.0006] bhagavato paṭisañcikkhato appossukkatāya cittaṃ namati, no dhammadesanāya.

Thus, as the Blessed One reflected, his mind inclined toward inaction, not toward teaching the Dhamma.

8. Atha kho brahmuno sahampatissa bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya etadahosi – “nassati vata bho loko, vinassati vata bho loko, yatra hi nāma tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa appossukkatāya cittaṃ namati namissati (?), no dhammadesanāyā”ti. Atha kho brahmā sahampati – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya evameva – brahmaloke antarahito bhagavato purato pāturahosi. Atha kho brahmā sahampati ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā dakkhiṇajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ pathaviyaṃ nihantvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “desetu, bhante, bhagavā dhammaṃ, desetu sugato dhammaṃ. Santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti[T 1.0010], bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro”ti. Idamavoca brahmā sahampati, idaṃ vatvāna athāparaṃ etadavoca –

8. Then Brahmā Sahampati, having known with his mind the thought in the Blessed One's mind, reflected: "The world is lost! The world is perishing! Since the mind of the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, inclines to little effort, not to teaching the Dhamma!" Then, just as a strong man might stretch out his drawn-in arm or draw in his outstretched arm, Brahmā Sahampati vanished from the Brahmā world and appeared before the Blessed One. Arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, he knelt with his right knee on the ground, raised his joined hands toward the Blessed One and said: "Venerable sir, let the Blessed One teach the Dhamma, let the Sugata teach the Dhamma! There are beings with little dust in their eyes who are declining from not hearing the Dhamma; there will be those who will understand the Dhamma." This is what Brahmā Sahampati said. Having said this, he then said further:

“Pāturahosi magadhesu pubbe;

Dhammo asuddho samalehi cintito;

Apāpuretaṃ avāpuretaṃ (sī.) amatassa dvāraṃ;

Suṇantu dhammaṃ vimalenānubuddhaṃ.

Formerly in Magadha there appeared an impure Dhamma, devised by the defiled. Open this door to the Deathless! Let them hear the Dhamma awakened to by the Stainless One.

“Sele yathā pabbatamuddhaniṭṭhito;

Yathāpi passe janataṃ samantato;

Tathūpamaṃ dhammamayaṃ sumedha;

Pāsādamāruyha samantacakkhu;

Sokāvatiṇṇaṃ [P 1.0006] janatamapetasoko;

Avekkhassu jātijarābhibhūtaṃ.

Just as a man with sight, standing on a rocky mountain peak, might see the people all around, so too, O One of good wisdom, O All-seeing One, having ascended the palace made of Dhamma, being yourself free from sorrow, please look upon the people plunged in sorrow, overcome by birth and old age.

“Uṭṭhehi [M 0.0007] vīra vijitasaṅgāma;

Satthavāha aṇaṇa anaṇa (ka.) vicara loke;

Desassu desetu (ka.) bhagavā dhammaṃ;

Aññātāro bhavissantī”ti.

Arise, O Hero, Victor in battle! O Caravan Leader, Debtless One, wander in the world! O Blessed One, teach the Dhamma! There will be those who understand.

[ ] sī. syā. potthakesu natthi, mūlapaṇṇāsakesu pāsarāsisutthe brahmayācanā sakiṃ yeva āgatā [ Evaṃ [V 0.0007] vutte bhagavā brahmānaṃ sahampatiṃ etadavoca – “mayhampi kho, brahme, etadahosi – ‘adhigato kho myāyaṃ dhammo gambhīro duddaso duranubodho santo paṇīto atakkāvacaro nipuṇo paṇḍitavedanīyo. Ālayarāmā kho panāyaṃ pajā ālayaratā ālayasammuditā. Ālayarāmāya kho pana pajāya ālayaratāya ālayasammuditāya duddasaṃ idaṃ ṭhānaṃ yadidaṃ idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppādo; idampi kho ṭhānaṃ sududdasaṃ yadidaṃ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānaṃ. Ahañceva kho pana dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ, pare ca me na ājāneyyuṃ, so mamassa kilamatho, sā mamassa vihesā’ti. Apissu maṃ, brahme, imā anacchariyā gāthāyo paṭibhaṃsu pubbe assutapubbā –

When this was said, the Blessed One said this to Brahmā Sahampati: “Indeed, Brahmā, this thought also occurred to me: ‘This Dhamma I have attained is deep, difficult to see, difficult to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the sphere of reasoning, subtle, to be known by the wise. This generation, however, delights in attachment, takes pleasure in attachment, rejoices in attachment. For a generation that delights in attachment, takes pleasure in attachment, and rejoices in attachment, this state is difficult to see: that is, specific conditionality, dependent origination. And this state is also exceedingly difficult to see: the stilling of all formations, the relinquishment of all acquisitions, the destruction of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna. If I were to teach the Dhamma, and others were not to understand me, that would be wearisome for me, that would be troublesome for me.’ Then, Brahmā, these amazing stanzas, unheard before, occurred to me:

‘Kicchena me adhigataṃ, halaṃ dāni pakāsituṃ;

Rāgadosaparetehi, nāyaṃ dhammo susambudho.

‘What was attained by me with difficulty, it is not fitting to proclaim it now. This Dhamma is not easily understood by those oppressed by lust and hate.’

‘Paṭisotagāmiṃ nipuṇaṃ, gambhīraṃ duddasaṃ aṇuṃ;

Rāgarattā na dakkhanti, tamokhandhena āvuṭā’ti.

‘Going against the stream, subtle, profound, difficult to see, minute, those impassioned with lust will not see it, enveloped as they are in a mass of darkness.’

Itiha me, brahme, paṭisañcikkhato appossukkatāya cittaṃ namati no dhammadesanāyā”ti.

Thus, O Brahmā, as I was reflecting, my mind inclined toward inaction, not toward teaching the Dhamma.”

Dutiyampi kho brahmā sahampati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “desetu, bhante, bhagavā dhammaṃ, desetu sugato dhammaṃ; santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti, bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro”ti. Idamavoca brahmā sahampati, idaṃ vatvāna athāparaṃ etadavoca –

A second time, Brahmā Sahampati said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One teach the Dhamma, let the Well-farer teach the Dhamma. There are beings with little dust in their eyes who are declining through not hearing the Dhamma. There will be those who will understand the Dhamma.” Brahmā Sahampati said this, and having said this, he further said this:

“Pāturahosi [M 0.0008] magadhesu pubbe;

Dhammo asuddho samalehi cintito;

Apāpuretaṃ amatassa dvāraṃ;

Suṇantu dhammaṃ vimalenānubuddhaṃ.

“Formerly in Magadha there appeared an impure Dhamma, conceived by the defiled. Open this door to the Deathless! Let them hear the Dhamma thoroughly realized by the Stainless One.

“Sele yathā pabbatamuddhaniṭṭhito;

Yathāpi passe janataṃ samantato;

Tathūpamaṃ [V 0.0008] dhammamayaṃ sumedha;

Pāsādamāruyha samantacakkhu;

Sokāvatiṇṇaṃ janatamapetasoko;

Avekkhassu jātijarābhibhūtaṃ.

Just as a man with sight, standing on a rocky mountain peak, might see the people all around, so too, O One of good wisdom, O All-seeing One, having ascended the palace made of Dhamma, being yourself free from sorrow, please look upon the people plunged in sorrow, overcome by birth and old age.

“Uṭṭhehi vīra vijitasaṅgāma;

Satthavāha aṇaṇa vicara loke;

Desassu bhagavā dhammaṃ;

Aññātāro bhavissantī”ti.

Arise, O Hero, Victor in battle! O Caravan Leader, Debtless One, wander in the world! O Blessed One, teach the Dhamma! There will be those who understand.

Dutiyampi kho bhagavā brahmānaṃ sahampatiṃ etadavoca – “mayhampi kho, brahme, etadahosi – ‘adhigato kho myāyaṃ dhammo gambhīro duddaso duranubodho santo paṇīto atakkāvacaro nipuṇo paṇḍitavedanīyo. Ālayarāmā kho panāyaṃ pajā ālayaratā ālayasammuditā. Ālayarāmāya kho pana pajāya ālayaratāya ālayasammuditāya duddasaṃ idaṃ ṭhānaṃ yadidaṃ idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppādo; idampi kho ṭhānaṃ sududdasaṃ yadidaṃ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānaṃ. Ahañceva kho pana dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ, pare ca me na ājāneyyuṃ, so mamassa kilamatho, sā mamassa vihesā’ti. Apissu maṃ, brahme, imā anacchariyā gāthāyo paṭibhaṃsu pubbe assutapubbā –

For a second time, the Blessed One said this to Brahmā Sahampati: 'To me also, O Brahmā, this thought occurred: “This Dhamma realized by me is deep, difficult to see, difficult to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the sphere of reasoning, subtle, to be known by the wise. But this generation delights in attachment, takes pleasure in attachment, and rejoices in attachment. For a generation that delights in attachment, takes pleasure in attachment, and rejoices in attachment, this state is difficult to see, that is, specific conditionality, dependent origination. This state is also exceedingly difficult to see, that is, the stilling of all formations, the relinquishment of all acquisitions, the destruction of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna. If I were to teach the Dhamma and others were not to understand me, that would be a weariness for me, that would be a vexation for me.” Furthermore, O Brahmā, these amazing verses, never heard before, occurred to me:'

‘Kicchena me adhigataṃ, halaṃ dāni pakāsituṃ;

Rāgadosaparetehi, nāyaṃ dhammo susambudho.

‘What was attained by me with difficulty, it is not fitting to proclaim it now. This Dhamma is not easily understood by those oppressed by lust and hate.’

‘Paṭisotagāmiṃ nipuṇaṃ, gambhīraṃ duddasaṃ aṇuṃ;

Rāgarattā na dakkhanti, tamokhandhena āvuṭā’ti.

‘Going against the stream, subtle, profound, difficult to see, minute, those impassioned with lust will not see it, enveloped as they are in a mass of darkness.’

Itiha [M 0.0009] me, brahme, paṭisañcikkhato appossukkatāya cittaṃ namati, no dhammadesanāyā”ti.

Thus, O Brahmā, as I was reflecting, my mind inclined toward inaction, not toward teaching the Dhamma.”

Tatiyampi kho brahmā sahampati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “desetu, bhante, bhagavā dhammaṃ, desetu sugato dhammaṃ. Santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti, bhavissanti [V 0.0009] dhammassa aññātāro”ti. Idamavoca brahmā sahampati, idaṃ vatvāna athāparaṃ etadavoca –

For the third time, Brahmā Sahampati said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One teach the Dhamma! Let the Well-farer teach the Dhamma! There are beings with little dust in their eyes; through not hearing the Dhamma, they are declining. There will be those who will understand the Dhamma.' Brahmā Sahampati said this, and having said this, he further said this:

“Pāturahosi magadhesu pubbe;

Dhammo asuddho samalehi cintito;

Apāpuretaṃ amatassa dvāraṃ;

Suṇantu dhammaṃ vimalenānubuddhaṃ.

“Formerly in Magadha there appeared an impure Dhamma, conceived by the defiled. Open this door to the Deathless! Let them hear the Dhamma thoroughly realized by the Stainless One.

“Sele yathā pabbatamuddhaniṭṭhito;

Yathāpi passe janataṃ samantato;

Tathūpamaṃ dhammamayaṃ sumedha;

Pāsādamāruyha samantacakkhu;

Sokāvatiṇṇaṃ janatamapetasoko;

Avekkhassu jātijarābhibhūtaṃ.

Just as a man with sight, standing on a rocky mountain peak, might see the people all around, so too, O One of good wisdom, O All-seeing One, having ascended the palace made of Dhamma, being yourself free from sorrow, please look upon the people plunged in sorrow, overcome by birth and old age.

“Uṭṭhehi vīra vijitasaṅgāma;

Satthavāha aṇaṇa vicara loke;

Desassu bhagavā dhammaṃ;

Aññātāro bhavissantī”ti.

Arise, O Hero, Victor in battle! O Caravan Leader, Debtless One, wander in the world! O Blessed One, teach the Dhamma! There will be those who understand.

9. Atha [T 1.0011] kho bhagavā brahmuno ca ajjhesanaṃ viditvā sattesu ca kāruññataṃ paṭicca buddhacakkhunā lokaṃ volokesi. Addasā kho bhagavā buddhacakkhunā lokaṃ volokento satte apparajakkhe mahārajakkhe tikkhindriye mudindriye svākāre dvākāre suviññāpaye duviññāpaye, appekacce paralokavajjabhayadassāvine dassāvino (sī. syā. kaṃ.) viharante, appekacce na paralokavajjabhayadassāvine viharante. Seyyathāpi nāma uppaliniyaṃ vā paduminiyaṃ vā puṇḍarīkiniyaṃ vā appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni udakānuggatāni anto nimuggaposīni[M 0.0010], appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni samodakaṃ ṭhitāni, appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni udakaṃ accuggamma ṭhitāni tiṭṭhanti (sī. syā.) anupalittāni udakena, evamevaṃ bhagavā buddhacakkhunā lokaṃ volokento addasa [V 0.0010] satte apparajakkhe mahārajakkhe tikkhindriye [P 1.0007] mudindriye svākāre dvākāre suviññāpaye duviññāpaye, appekacce paralokavajjabhayadassāvine viharante, appekacce na paralokavajjabhayadassāvine viharante; disvāna [T 1.0012] brahmānaṃ sahampatiṃ gāthāya paccabhāsi –

9. Then the Blessed One, having understood Brahmā's request and out of compassion for beings, surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye. As the Blessed One surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye, he saw beings with little dust and with much dust in their eyes, with sharp faculties and with dull faculties, with good dispositions and with bad dispositions, easy to teach and difficult to teach; he saw some who dwelt perceiving danger in faults concerning the next world, and some who dwelt not perceiving danger in faults concerning the next world. Just as in a pond of blue lotuses, or a pond of red lotuses, or a pond of white lotuses, some blue, red, or white lotuses are born in the water and grow in the water, not having risen from the water, thriving submerged within. Some blue, red, or white lotuses are born in the water and grow in the water, standing level with the water. And some blue, red, or white lotuses are born in the water and grow in the water, having risen above the water, they stand unsullied by the water. Even so, as the Blessed One surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye, he saw beings with little dust and with much dust in their eyes, with sharp faculties and with dull faculties, with good dispositions and with bad dispositions, easy to teach and difficult to teach; he saw some who dwelt perceiving danger in faults concerning the next world, and some who dwelt not perceiving danger in faults concerning the next world. Having seen this, he replied to Brahmā Sahampati in verse:

“Apārutā tesaṃ amatassa dvārā;

Ye sotavanto pamuñcantu saddhaṃ;

Vihiṃsasaññī paguṇaṃ na bhāsiṃ;

Dhammaṃ paṇītaṃ manujesu brahme”ti.

“Opened for them are the doors to the Deathless; let those with ears release their faith. Perceiving it as wearisome, O Brahmā, I did not speak the sublime and excellent Dhamma among humans.”

Atha kho brahmā sahampati “katāvakāso khomhi bhagavatā dhammadesanāyā”ti bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi.

Then Brahmā Sahampati, thinking, “The opportunity for the teaching of the Dhamma has been granted to me by the Blessed One,” paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him to the right, and vanished right there.

Brahmayācanakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of Brahmā's Request is concluded.

6. Pañcavaggiyakathā

6. The Account of the Group of Five

10. ma. ni. 1.284 ādayo; ma. ni. 2.339 ādayo Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “kassa nu kho ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ? Ko imaṃ dhammaṃ khippameva ājānissatī”ti? Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho āḷāro kālāmo paṇḍito byatto medhāvī dīgharattaṃ apparajakkhajātiko; yaṃnūnāhaṃ āḷārassa kālāmassa paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ, so imaṃ dhammaṃ khippameva ājānissatī”ti. Atha kho antarahitā devatā bhagavato ārocesi – “sattāhakālaṅkato, bhante, āḷāro kālāmo”ti. Bhagavatopi kho ñāṇaṃ udapādi – “sattāhakālaṅkato āḷāro [M 0.0011] kālāmo”ti. Atha kho bhagavato [T 1.0013] etadahosi – “mahājāniyo kho āḷāro kālāmo; sace hi so imaṃ dhammaṃ suṇeyya, khippameva ājāneyyā”ti. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “kassa nu kho ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ? Ko imaṃ dhammaṃ khippameva ājānissatī”ti? Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho udako uddako (sī. syā.) rāmaputto paṇḍito byatto medhāvī dīgharattaṃ apparajakkhajātiko; yaṃnūnāhaṃ udakassa rāmaputtassa paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ, so imaṃ dhammaṃ khippameva ājānissatī”ti. Atha kho antarahitā devatā bhagavato ārocesi – “abhidosakālaṅkato, bhante, udako rāmaputto”ti. Bhagavatopi kho ñāṇaṃ udapādi – “abhidosakālaṅkato [V 0.0011] udako rāmaputto”ti. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “mahājāniyo kho udako rāmaputto; sace hi so imaṃ dhammaṃ suṇeyya, khippameva ājāneyyā”ti

10. Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: “To whom should I first teach the Dhamma? Who will quickly understand this Dhamma?” Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: “This Āḷāra Kālāma is wise, astute, and intelligent; for a long time he has been of a nature with little dust in his eyes. What if I were to teach the Dhamma first to Āḷāra Kālāma? He would quickly understand this Dhamma.” Then an invisible deity informed the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, Āḷāra Kālāma passed away seven days ago.” And the knowledge arose in the Blessed One: “Āḷāra Kālāma passed away seven days ago.” Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: “Āḷāra Kālāma has suffered a great loss. For if he had heard this Dhamma, he would have quickly understood it.” Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: “To whom should I first teach the Dhamma? Who will quickly understand this Dhamma?” Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: “This Uddaka Rāmaputta is wise, astute, and intelligent; for a long time he has been of a nature with little dust in his eyes. What if I were to teach the Dhamma first to Uddaka Rāmaputta? He would quickly understand this Dhamma.” Then an invisible deity informed the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, Uddaka Rāmaputta passed away last night.” And the knowledge arose in the Blessed One: “Uddaka Rāmaputta passed away last night.” Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: “Uddaka Rāmaputta has suffered a great loss. For if he had heard this Dhamma, he would have quickly understood it.”

Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “kassa nu kho ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ? Ko imaṃ dhammaṃ [P 1.0008] khippameva ājānissatī”ti? Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “bahukārā kho me pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū, ye maṃ padhānapahitattaṃ upaṭṭhahiṃsu; yaṃnūnāhaṃ pañcavaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ deseyya”nti. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “kahaṃ nu kho etarahi pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū viharantī”ti? Addasā kho bhagavā dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena pañcavaggiye bhikkhū bārāṇasiyaṃ viharante [T 1.0014] isipatane migadāye. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelāyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena bārāṇasī tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi.

Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: “To whom should I first teach the Dhamma? Who will quickly understand this Dhamma?” Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: “The monks of the group of five were of great service to me; they attended on me when I was dedicated to striving. What if I were to teach the Dhamma first to the monks of the group of five?” Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: “Where, I wonder, are the monks of the group of five now dwelling?” With the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, the Blessed One saw the monks of the group of five dwelling in Bārāṇasī at Isipatana, in the Deer Park. Then the Blessed One, having dwelt at Uruvelā for as long as he pleased, set out on a journey towards Bārāṇasī.

11. Addasā kho upako ājīvako bhagavantaṃ antarā ca gayaṃ antarā ca bodhiṃ addhānamaggappaṭipannaṃ, disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “vippasannāni kho te, āvuso, indriyāni, parisuddho chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto. Kaṃsi tvaṃ, āvuso, uddissa pabbajito? Ko vā te satthā? Kassa vā tvaṃ dhammaṃ rocesī”ti? Evaṃ vutte bhagavā upakaṃ ājīvakaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

11. Upaka the Ājīvaka saw the Blessed One journeying on the high road between Gayā and the Bodhi tree. Having seen him, he said this to the Blessed One: “Friend, your faculties are serene, your skin complexion is pure and bright. In whose name, friend, have you gone forth? Who is your teacher? Whose Dhamma do you profess?” When this was said, the Blessed One addressed Upaka the Ājīvaka in verses:

dha. pa. 353; kathā. 405 “Sabbābhibhū [M 0.0012] sabbavidūhamasmi,

Sabbesu dhammesu anūpalitto;

Sabbañjaho taṇhākkhaye vimutto,

Sayaṃ abhiññāya kamuddiseyyaṃ.

“I am the all-conqueror, the all-knower, unstained in all things. I am one who has abandoned all, freed through the destruction of craving. Having realized this for myself through direct knowledge, whom should I point to as my teacher?

mi. pa. 4.5.11 milindapañhepi; kathā. 405 “Na me ācariyo atthi, sadiso me na vijjati;

Sadevakasmiṃ lokasmiṃ, natthi me paṭipuggalo.

I have no teacher; one like me is not to be found. In the world with its devas, there is no one who is my counterpart.

kathā. 405 kathāvatthupāḷiyampi “Ahañhi arahā loke, ahaṃ satthā anuttaro;

Ekomhi sammāsambuddho, sītibhūtosmi nibbuto.

For I am the Arahant in the world; I am the unsurpassed Teacher. I alone am the Perfectly Enlightened One; I have become cooled and extinguished.

kathā. 405 kathāvatthupāḷiyampi“Dhammacakkaṃ pavattetuṃ, gacchāmi kāsinaṃ puraṃ;

Andhībhūtasmiṃ lokasmiṃ, āhañchaṃ āhaññiṃ (ka.) amatadundubhi”nti.

To set the Wheel of Dhamma in motion, I go to the city of the Kāsīs. In a world that has become blind, I shall beat the drum of the Deathless.”

Yathā [V 0.0012] kho tvaṃ, āvuso, paṭijānāsi, arahasi anantajinoti.

“Friend, according to how you profess, are you worthy to be an Infinite Victor?”

kathā. 405 kathāvatthupāḷiyampi “Mādisā ve jinā honti, ye pattā āsavakkhayaṃ;

Jitā [T 1.0015] me pāpakā dhammā, tasmāhamupaka tasmāhamupakā (sī.) jino”ti.

“Indeed, those like me are Conquerors, who have attained the destruction of the taints. Evil states have been conquered by me; therefore, Upaka, I am a Conqueror.”

Evaṃ vutte upako ājīvako hupeyyapāvusoti huveyyapāvuso (sī.) huveyyāvuso (syā.) vatvā sīsaṃ okampetvā ummaggaṃ gahetvā pakkāmi.

When this was said, Upaka the Ājīvaka, saying, “It may be so, friend,” shook his head, took a side-road, and departed.

12. Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena bārāṇasī isipatanaṃ migadāyo, yena pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami. Addasaṃsu kho pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ; disvāna aññamaññaṃ katikaṃ idaṃ padaṃ kesuci natthi saṇṭhapesuṃ – “ayaṃ, āvuso, samaṇo gotamo āgacchati, bāhulliko padhānavibbhanto [P 1.0009] āvatto bāhullāya. So neva abhivādetabbo, na paccuṭṭhātabbo, nāssa pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ; api ca kho āsanaṃ ṭhapetabbaṃ, sace so ākaṅkhissati nisīdissatī”ti. Yathā yathā kho bhagavā pañcavaggiye bhikkhū upasaṅkamati, tathā tathā tathā tathā te (sī. syā.) pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū nāsakkhiṃsu sakāya katikāya saṇṭhātuṃ[M 0.0013]. Asaṇṭhahantā bhagavantaṃ paccuggantvā eko bhagavato pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahesi, eko āsanaṃ paññapesi, eko pādodakaṃ, eko pādapīṭhaṃ, eko pādakaṭhalikaṃ upanikkhipi. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane; nisajja kho bhagavā pāde pakkhālesi. Apissu api ca kho (pāsarāsisuttha) bhagavantaṃ nāmena ca āvusovādena ca samudācaranti. Evaṃ vutte bhagavā pañcavaggiye bhikkhū etadavoca – “mā, bhikkhave, tathāgataṃ nāmena ca āvusovādena ca [T 1.0016] samudācaratha samudācarittha (sī. syā.). Arahaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato sammāsambuddho, odahatha, bhikkhave, sotaṃ, amatamadhigataṃ, ahamanusāsāmi, ahaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamānā yathānusiṭṭhaṃ paṭipajjamānā (syā.) nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissathā”ti. Evaṃ vutte pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “tāyapi kho tvaṃ, āvuso gotama, iriyāya cariyāya (syā.), tāya paṭipadāya, tāya dukkarakārikāya nevajjhagā uttari manussadhammā uttarimanussadhammaṃ (syā. ka.) alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ, kiṃ pana tvaṃ etarahi, bāhulliko padhānavibbhanto āvatto bāhullāya, adhigamissasi uttari manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesa”nti? Evaṃ vutte bhagavā pañcavaggiye bhikkhū etadavoca – “na, bhikkhave, tathāgato bāhulliko, na padhānavibbhanto, na āvatto bāhullāya; arahaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato sammāsambuddho. Odahatha, bhikkhave, sotaṃ, amatamadhigataṃ, ahamanusāsāmi[V 0.0013], ahaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamānā nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃ [T 1.0017] – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭhevadhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissathā”ti. Dutiyampi kho pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ…pe…. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā pañcavaggiye bhikkhū etadavoca…pe…. Tatiyampi kho pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “tāyapi [P 1.0010] kho tvaṃ, āvuso gotama, iriyāya, tāya paṭipadāya, tāya dukkarakārikāya nevajjhagā uttari manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesaṃ, kiṃ pana tvaṃ etarahi, bāhulliko padhānavibbhanto [M 0.0014] āvatto bāhullāya, adhigamissasi uttari manussadhammā alamariyañāṇadassanavisesa”nti? Evaṃ vutte bhagavā pañcavaggiye bhikkhū etadavoca – “abhijānātha me no tumhe, bhikkhave, ito pubbe evarūpaṃ pabhāvitameta”nti bhāsitametanti (sī. syā. ka.) ṭīkāyo oloketabbā? “Nohetaṃ, bhante”. Arahaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato sammāsambuddho, odahatha, bhikkhave, sotaṃ, amatamadhigataṃ, ahamanusāsāmi, ahaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamānā nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti tadanuttaraṃbrahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭhevadhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissathāti. Asakkhi kho bhagavā pañcavaggiye bhikkhū saññāpetuṃ. Atha kho pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ sussūsiṃsu, sotaṃ odahiṃsu, aññā cittaṃ upaṭṭhāpesuṃ.

12. Then the Blessed One, traveling by stages, arrived at Isipatana, the Deer Park near Bārāṇasī, where the group of five bhikkhus were staying. The group of five bhikkhus saw the Blessed One coming from afar and made an agreement among themselves: “Friends, this ascetic Gotama is coming—indulgent, straying from exertion, reverting to luxury. We should not pay respects to him, nor rise to greet him, nor receive his bowl and robe. However, we may prepare a seat; if he wishes, he may sit down.” But as the Blessed One approached, the group of five bhikkhus were unable to adhere to their agreement. They went out to meet him: one received his bowl and robe, another prepared a seat, another set out water for his feet, another a footstool, and another a foot-rubbing potsherd. The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat and washed his feet. Still they addressed him by name and as “friend.” When they spoke thus, the Blessed One said to them: “Bhikkhus, do not address the Tathāgata by name or as ‘friend.’ The Tathāgata, bhikkhus, is an Arahant, a Fully Enlightened One. Listen, bhikkhus, the Deathless has been attained. I instruct, I teach the Dhamma. Practicing as instructed, you will soon realize for yourselves, in this very life, that supreme culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness—having directly known and realized it for yourselves, you will abide in it.” When this was said, the group of five bhikkhus replied: “Friend Gotama, by that conduct, that practice, those severe austerities, you did not attain any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones. How then, now that you are indulgent, straying from exertion, and reverting to luxury, will you attain any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones?” When this was said, the Blessed One replied to the group of five bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, the Tathāgata is not indulgent, nor has he strayed from exertion, nor has he reverted to luxury. The Tathāgata, bhikkhus, is an Arahant, a Fully Enlightened One. Listen, bhikkhus, the Deathless has been attained. I instruct, I teach the Dhamma. Practicing as instructed, you will soon realize for yourselves, in this very life, that supreme culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness—having directly known and realized it for yourselves, you will abide in it.” A second time, the group of five bhikkhus spoke to the Blessed One in the same way… A second time, the Blessed One replied to them in the same way… A third time, the group of five bhikkhus said to the Blessed One: “Friend Gotama, by that conduct, that practice, those severe austerities, you did not attain any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones. How then, now that you are indulgent, straying from exertion, and reverting to luxury, will you attain any superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones?” When this was said, the Blessed One asked them: “Bhikkhus, do you recall my having ever spoken to you like this before?” “No, Venerable Sir.” “The Tathāgata, bhikkhus, is an Arahant, a Fully Enlightened One. Listen, bhikkhus, the Deathless has been attained. I instruct, I teach the Dhamma. Practicing as instructed, you will soon realize for yourselves, in this very life, that supreme culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from home into homelessness—having directly known and realized it for yourselves, you will abide in it.” The Blessed One was able to convince the group of five bhikkhus. Then the group of five bhikkhus listened to the Blessed One, lent ear, and directed their minds toward final knowledge.

13. Atha kho bhagavā pañcavaggiye bhikkhū āmantesi –

13. Then the Blessed One addressed the group of five bhikkhus:

“saṃ. ni. 5.1081 ādayo Dveme, bhikkhave[T 1.0018], antā pabbajitena na sevitabbā. Katame dve idaṃ padadvayaṃ sī. syā. potthakesu natthi? Yo cāyaṃ kāmesu kāmasukhallikānuyogo hīno gammo pothujjaniko anariyo anatthasaṃhito, yo cāyaṃ attakilamathānuyogo dukkho anariyo anatthasaṃhito. Ete kho, bhikkhave, ubho ante anupagamma, majjhimā paṭipadā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā, cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Katamā ca sā, bhikkhave, majjhimā paṭipadā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā, cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho sā, bhikkhave, majjhimā paṭipadā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā, cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.

“Bhikkhus, these two extremes are not to be practiced by one who has gone forth. Which two? This devotion to indulgence in sensual pleasures, which is low, of the villagers, of the common folk, ignoble, and unbeneficial; and this devotion to self-mortification, which is painful, ignoble, and unbeneficial. Without approaching either of these two extremes, Bhikkhus, the Middle Path has been fully realized by the Tathāgata, which produces vision, produces knowledge, and leads to calm, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. And what, Bhikkhus, is that Middle Path fully realized by the Tathāgata, which produces vision, produces knowledge, and leads to calm, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path; that is: Right View, Right Intention, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, and Right Concentration. This, Bhikkhus, is that Middle Path fully realized by the Tathāgata, which produces vision, produces knowledge, and leads to calm, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.”

14. “Idaṃ [V 0.0014] kho pana, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ. Jātipi dukkhā, jarāpi dukkhā, byādhipi dukkho, maraṇampi dukkhaṃ, appiyehi sampayogo [T 1.0019] dukkho, piyehi vippayogo dukkho, yampicchaṃ na labhati tampi dukkhaṃ. Saṃkhittena, pañcupādānakkhandhā [M 0.0015] pañcupādānakhandhāpi (ka) dukkhā. “Idaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, dukkhasamudayaṃ ettha “idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccanti ādīsu dukkhasamudayo dukkhanirodhoti vattabbe dukkhasamudayaṃ dukkhanirodhanti liṅgavipallāso tato”ti paṭisambhidāmaggaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ. visuddhimaggaṭīkāyaṃ pana uppādo bhayantipāṭhavaṇṇanāyaṃ “satipi dvinnaṃ padānaṃ samānādhikaraṇabhāve liṅgabhedo gahito, yathā dukkhasamudayo ariyasacca”nti vuttaṃ. tesu dukkhasamudayo ariyasacca”nti sakaliṅgikapāṭho “dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasacca”nti pāḷiyā sameti. ariyasaccaṃ – yāyaṃ taṇhā ponobbhavikā ponobhavikā (ka.) nandīrāgasahagatā nandirāgasahagatā (sī. syā.) tatratatrābhinandinī, seyyathidaṃ – kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā.

14. “Now this, Bhikkhus, is the Noble Truth of Suffering. Birth is suffering, aging is suffering, sickness is suffering, death is suffering; association with the unloved is suffering, separation from the loved is suffering; not to get what one wants is also suffering. In brief, the five aggregates subject to clinging are suffering. Now this, Bhikkhus, is the Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering: it is this craving which produces re-becoming, is accompanied by delight and lust, and delights now here, now there; that is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for becoming, and craving for non-becoming.”

“Idaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ – yo tassā yeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodho, cāgo, paṭinissaggo, mutti, anālayo. “Idaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ – ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.

“Now this, O bhikkhus, is the Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering: the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very craving, the giving up of it, the relinquishing of it, release from it, and non-attachment to it. And this, O bhikkhus, is the Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering: it is this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: Right View, Right Intention, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, and Right Concentration.”

15. “Idaṃ [P 1.0011] dukkhaṃ ariyasaccanti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi[T 1.0020], āloko udapādi. Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ pariññeyyanti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi. Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ pariññātanti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.

15. “‘This is the Noble Truth of Suffering’—thus, O bhikkhus, in regard to dhammas unheard before, there arose in me vision, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose true knowledge, there arose light. ‘Indeed, this Noble Truth of Suffering is to be fully understood’—thus, O bhikkhus, in regard to dhammas unheard before, there arose in me vision, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose true knowledge, there arose light. ‘Indeed, this Noble Truth of Suffering has been fully understood’—thus, O bhikkhus, in regard to dhammas unheard before, there arose in me vision, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose true knowledge, there arose light.”

“Idaṃ dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccanti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi. Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ pahātabbanti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi. Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ pahīnanti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.

“‘This is the Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering’—thus, O bhikkhus, in regard to dhammas unheard before, there arose in me vision, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose true knowledge, there arose light. ‘Indeed, this Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering is to be abandoned’—thus, O bhikkhus, in regard to dhammas unheard before, there arose in me vision, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose true knowledge, there arose light. ‘Indeed, this Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering has been abandoned’—thus, O bhikkhus, in regard to dhammas unheard before, there arose in me vision, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose true knowledge, there arose light.”

“Idaṃ dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccanti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko [M 0.0016] udapādi. Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ sacchikātabbanti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi. Taṃ [V 0.0015] kho panidaṃ dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ sacchikatanti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.

“‘This is the Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering’—thus, O bhikkhus, in regard to dhammas unheard before, there arose in me vision, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose true knowledge, there arose light. ‘Indeed, this Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering is to be realized’—thus, O bhikkhus, in regard to dhammas unheard before, there arose in me vision, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose true knowledge, there arose light. ‘Indeed, this Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering has been realized’—thus, O bhikkhus, in regard to dhammas unheard before, there arose in me vision, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose true knowledge, there arose light.”

“Idaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccanti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi. Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ bhāvetabbanti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi. Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ bhāvitanti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ [T 1.0021] udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.

“‘This is the Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering’—thus, O bhikkhus, in regard to dhammas unheard before, there arose in me vision, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose true knowledge, there arose light. ‘Indeed, this Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering is to be developed’—thus, O bhikkhus, in regard to dhammas unheard before, there arose in me vision, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose true knowledge, there arose light. ‘Indeed, this Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering has been developed’—thus, O bhikkhus, in regard to dhammas unheard before, there arose in me vision, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose true knowledge, there arose light.”

16. “Yāvakīvañca me, bhikkhave, imesu catūsu ariyasaccesu evaṃ tiparivaṭṭaṃ dvādasākāraṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ na suvisuddhaṃ ahosi, neva tāvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddhoti paccaññāsiṃ. Yato ca kho me, bhikkhave, imesu catūsu ariyasaccesu evaṃ tiparivaṭṭaṃ dvādasākāraṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ suvisuddhaṃ ahosi, athāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddhoti abhisambuddho (sī. syā.) paccaññāsiṃ. Ñāṇañca pana me dassanaṃ udapādi – akuppā me vimutti, ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā attamanā pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti idamavoca…pe… abhinanduntivākyaṃ sī. syā. potthakesu natthi.

16. Monks, for as long as my knowledge and vision of these Four Noble Truths—with its three rounds and twelve aspects, just as it is—was not well purified, for that long, monks, I did not claim to have fully awakened to the unexcelled perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, its Māras, and its Brahmās, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. But when, monks, my knowledge and vision of these Four Noble Truths—with its three rounds and twelve aspects, just as it is—was well purified, then, monks, I claimed to have fully awakened to the unexcelled perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, its Māras, and its Brahmās, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. And the knowledge and vision arose in me: ‘Unshakeable is my liberation. This is the final birth. Now there is no future existence.’ This the Blessed One said. Pleased, the monks of the group of five rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words.

Imasmiñca [T 1.0022] pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne āyasmato koṇḍaññassa virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – “yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma”nti.

And while this exposition was being spoken, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose in the Venerable Koṇḍañña: “Whatever is of the nature to arise is all of the nature to cease.”

17. Pavattite [M 0.0017] ca pana bhagavatā dhammacakke, bhummā devā saddamanussāvesuṃ – “etaṃ bhagavatā bārāṇasiyaṃ isipatane migadāye [P 1.0012] anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ, appaṭivattiyaṃ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmi”nti. Bhummānaṃ devānaṃ saddaṃ sutvā cātumahārājikā devā saddamanussāvesuṃ…pe… cātumahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ saddaṃ sutvā tāvatiṃsā devā…pe… yāmā devā…pe… tusitā devā…pe… nimmānaratī [V 0.0016] devā…pe… paranimmitavasavattī devā…pe… brahmakāyikā devā saddamanussāvesuṃ – “etaṃ bhagavatā bārāṇasiyaṃ isipatane migadāye anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ appaṭivattiyaṃ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmi”nti. Itiha, tena khaṇena, tena layena tena layenāti padadvayaṃ sī. syā. potthakesu natthi tena muhuttena yāva brahmalokā saddo abbhuggacchi. Ayañca dasasahassilokadhātu saṃkampi sampakampi sampavedhi[T 1.0023]; appamāṇo ca uḷāro obhāso loke pāturahosi, atikkamma devānaṃ devānubhāvaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi – “aññāsi vata, bho koṇḍañño, aññāsi vata bho koṇḍañño”ti. Iti hidaṃ āyasmato koṇḍaññassa ‘aññāsikoṇḍañño’ tveva nāmaṃ ahosi.

17. And when the Wheel of Dhamma had been set in motion by the Blessed One, the earth-dwelling devas raised a cry: “At Bārāṇasī, in Isipatana, in the Deer Sanctuary, this unsurpassed Wheel of Dhamma has been set in motion by the Blessed One, which cannot be turned back by any ascetic or brahmin or deva or Māra or Brahmā or by anyone in the world.” Hearing the cry of the earth-dwelling devas, the devas of the Four Great Kings relayed the cry… Hearing the cry of the devas of the Four Great Kings, the Tāvatiṃsa devas… the Yāma devas… the Tusita devas… the Nimmānaratī devas… the Paranimmitavasavattī devas… the Brahmakāyika devas relayed the cry: “At Bārāṇasī, in Isipatana, in the Deer Sanctuary, this unsurpassed Wheel of Dhamma has been set in motion by the Blessed One, which cannot be turned back by any ascetic or brahmin or deva or Māra or Brahmā or by anyone in the world.” Thus, in that moment, in that instant, in that second, the sound rose up as far as the Brahmā world. And this ten-thousandfold world system quaked, shook, and trembled; and an immeasurable, magnificent radiance appeared in the world, surpassing the divine majesty of the devas. Then the Blessed One uttered this inspired utterance: “Indeed, friends, Koṇḍañña has understood! Indeed, friends, Koṇḍañña has understood!” For this very reason, the Venerable Koṇḍañña’s name became ‘Aññāsikoṇḍañño’.”

18. Atha kho āyasmā aññāsikoṇḍañño diṭṭhadhammo pattadhammo viditadhammo pariyogāḷhadhammo tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṃkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada”nti. “Ehi bhikkhū”ti bhagavā avoca – “svākkhāto dhammo, cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Sāva tassa āyasmato upasampadā ahosi.

18. Then the Venerable Aññāsikoṇḍañña, who had seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, known the Dhamma, and penetrated the Dhamma, who had crossed over doubt, was free from perplexity, had attained confidence, and was independent of others in the Teacher’s Dispensation, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, may I receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence; may I receive the higher ordination.” The Blessed One said: “Come, bhikkhu. The Dhamma is well-proclaimed; live the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.” That itself was the higher ordination for that venerable one.

19. Atha kho bhagavā tadavasese bhikkhū dhammiyā kathāya ovadi anusāsi. Atha kho āyasmato ca vappassa āyasmato ca bhaddiyassa bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya ovadiyamānānaṃ anusāsiyamānānaṃ virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti.

19. Then the Blessed One instructed and exhorted the remaining bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk. Then, as the Venerable Vappa and the Venerable Bhaddiya were being instructed and exhorted by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose in them: “Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing.”

Te [M 0.0018] diṭṭhadhammā pattadhammā viditadhammā pariyogāḷhadhammā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane [T 1.0024] bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyāma upasampada”nti. “Etha bhikkhavo”ti bhagavā avoca – “svākkhāto dhammo, caratha [P 1.0013] brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Sāva tesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ upasampadā ahosi.

They, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, known the Dhamma, penetrated the Dhamma, crossed over doubt, become free from perplexity, attained confidence, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s Dispensation, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, may we receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence, may we receive the higher ordination.” The Blessed One said: “Come, bhikkhus. The Dhamma is well-proclaimed. Practice the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.” That itself was the higher ordination for those venerable ones.

Atha kho bhagavā tadavasese bhikkhū nīhārabhatto dhammiyā kathāya ovadi anusāsi. Yaṃ tayo bhikkhū piṇḍāya caritvā āharanti, tena chabbaggo yāpeti. Atha kho āyasmato ca mahānāmassa āyasmato ca assajissa bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya ovadiyamānānaṃ anusāsiyamānānaṃ virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti[V 0.0017]. Te diṭṭhadhammā pattadhammā viditadhammā pariyogāḷhadhammā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyāma upasampada”nti. “Etha bhikkhavo”ti bhagavā avoca – “svākkhāto dhammo, caratha brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Sāva tesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ upasampadā ahosi.

Then the Blessed One, having eaten the food brought for him, instructed and exhorted the remaining bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk. The group of six sustained themselves on whatever food the three bhikkhus brought back from their alms round. Then, as the Venerable Mahānāma and the Venerable Assaji were being instructed and exhorted by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose in them: “Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing.” They, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, known the Dhamma, penetrated the Dhamma, crossed over doubt, become free from perplexity, attained confidence, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s Dispensation, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, may we receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence, may we receive the higher ordination.” The Blessed One said: “Come, bhikkhus. The Dhamma is well-proclaimed. Practice the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.” That itself was the higher ordination for those venerable ones.

20. Atha kho bhagavā pañcavaggiye bhikkhū āmantesi –

20. Then the Blessed One addressed the group-of-five bhikkhus:

saṃ. ni. 3.59 ādayo “Rūpaṃ, bhikkhave, anattā. Rūpañca hidaṃ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissa, nayidaṃ rūpaṃ ābādhāya saṃvatteyya, labbhetha ca rūpe – ‘evaṃ me rūpaṃ [T 1.0025] hotu, evaṃ me rūpaṃ mā ahosī’ti. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ anattā, tasmā rūpaṃ ābādhāya saṃvattati, na ca labbhati rūpe – ‘evaṃ me rūpaṃ hotu, evaṃ me rūpaṃ mā ahosī’ti. Vedanā, anattā. Vedanā ca hidaṃ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissa, nayidaṃ vedanā ābādhāya saṃvatteyya, labbhetha ca vedanāya – ‘evaṃ me vedanā hotu, evaṃ me vedanā mā ahosī’ti. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, vedanā anattā, tasmā vedanā ābādhāya saṃvattati, na ca labbhati vedanāya – ‘evaṃ me vedanā hotu, evaṃ me vedanā mā ahosī’ti. Saññā, anattā. Saññā ca hidaṃ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissa, nayidaṃ saññā ābādhāya saṃvatteyya, labbhetha [M 0.0019] ca saññāya – ‘evaṃ me saññā hotu, evaṃ me saññā mā ahosī’ti. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, saññā anattā, tasmā saññā ābādhāya saṃvattati, na ca labbhati saññāya – ‘evaṃ me saññā hotu, evaṃ me saññā mā ahosī’ti. Saṅkhārā, anattā. Saṅkhārā ca hidaṃ, bhikkhave, attā abhavissaṃsu, nayidaṃ nayime (ka.) saṅkhārā ābādhāya saṃvatteyyuṃ, labbhetha ca saṅkhāresu – ‘evaṃ me saṅkhārā hontu, evaṃ me saṅkhārā mā ahesu’nti. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā anattā, tasmā saṅkhārā ābādhāya saṃvattanti, na ca labbhati saṅkhāresu – ‘evaṃ me saṅkhārā hontu, evaṃ me saṅkhārā mā ahesu’nti. Viññāṇaṃ, anattā. Viññāṇañca hidaṃ[T 1.0026], bhikkhave, attā abhavissa, nayidaṃ viññāṇaṃ ābādhāya saṃvatteyya[P 1.0014], labbhetha ca viññāṇe – ‘evaṃ me viññāṇaṃ hotu, evaṃ me viññāṇaṃ mā ahosī’ti. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, viññāṇaṃ anattā, tasmā viññāṇaṃ ābādhāya saṃvattati, na ca labbhati viññāṇe – ‘evaṃ me viññāṇaṃ hotu, evaṃ me viññāṇaṃ mā ahosī’ti.

Bhikkhus, form is not-self. If, bhikkhus, this form were self, this form would not lead to affliction, and power could be exercised over form thus: ‘Let my form be thus; let my form not be thus.’ But because, bhikkhus, form is not-self, therefore form leads to affliction, and power cannot be exercised over form thus: ‘Let my form be thus; let my form not be thus.’ Feeling is not-self. If, bhikkhus, this feeling were self, this feeling would not lead to affliction, and power could be exercised over feeling thus: ‘Let my feeling be thus; let my feeling not be thus.’ But because, bhikkhus, feeling is not-self, therefore feeling leads to affliction, and power cannot be exercised over feeling thus: ‘Let my feeling be thus; let my feeling not be thus.’ Perception is not-self. If, bhikkhus, this perception were self, this perception would not lead to affliction, and power could be exercised over perception thus: ‘Let my perception be thus; let my perception not be thus.’ But because, bhikkhus, perception is not-self, therefore perception leads to affliction, and power cannot be exercised over perception thus: ‘Let my perception be thus; let my perception not be thus.’ Formations are not-self. If, bhikkhus, these formations were self, these formations would not lead to affliction, and power could be exercised over formations thus: ‘Let my formations be thus; let my formations not be thus.’ But because, bhikkhus, formations are not-self, therefore formations lead to affliction, and power cannot be exercised over formations thus: ‘Let my formations be thus; let my formations not be thus.’ Consciousness is not-self. If, bhikkhus, this consciousness were self, this consciousness would not lead to affliction, and power could be exercised over consciousness thus: ‘Let my consciousness be thus; let my consciousness not be thus.’ But because, bhikkhus, consciousness is not-self, therefore consciousness leads to affliction, and power cannot be exercised over consciousness thus: ‘Let my consciousness be thus; let my consciousness not be thus.’

21. “Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vāti? Aniccaṃ, bhante[V 0.0018]. Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vāti? Dukkhaṃ, bhante. Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attāti? No hetaṃ, bhante. Vedanā niccā vā aniccā vāti? Aniccā, bhante. Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vāti? Dukkhaṃ, bhante. Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attāti? No hetaṃ, bhante. Saññā niccā vā aniccā vāti? Aniccā, bhante. Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vāti? Dukkhaṃ, bhante. Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attāti? No hetaṃ, bhante. Saṅkhārā niccā vā aniccā vāti? Aniccā, bhante. Yaṃ panāniccaṃ, dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vāti? Dukkhaṃ, bhante. Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ [T 1.0027] vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attāti? No hetaṃ, bhante. Viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vāti? Aniccaṃ, bhante. Yaṃ panāniccaṃ, dukkhaṃ vā taṃ sukhaṃ vāti? Dukkhaṃ, bhante. Yaṃ panāniccaṃ dukkhaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, kallaṃ nu taṃ samanupassituṃ – etaṃ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attāti? No hetaṃ, bhante.

21. “What do you think, bhikkhus, is form permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, Venerable Sir.” “And that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, Venerable Sir.” “And that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fitting to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “Indeed not, Venerable Sir.” “Is feeling permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, Venerable Sir.” “And that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, Venerable Sir.” “And that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fitting to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “Indeed not, Venerable Sir.” “Is perception permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, Venerable Sir.” “And that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, Venerable Sir.” “And that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fitting to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “Indeed not, Venerable Sir.” “Are formations permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, Venerable Sir.” “And that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, Venerable Sir.” “And that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fitting to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “Indeed not, Venerable Sir.” “Is consciousness permanent or impermanent?” “Impermanent, Venerable Sir.” “And that which is impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?” “Suffering, Venerable Sir.” “And that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, is it fitting to regard it thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” “Indeed not, Venerable Sir.”

22. “Tasmātiha[M 0.0020], bhikkhave, yaṃ kiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre yaṃ dūre vā (syā.) santike vā, sabbaṃ rūpaṃ – netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attāti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yā kāci vedanā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā hīnā vā paṇītā vā yā dūre santike vā, sabbā vedanā – netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attāti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yā kāci saññā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā hīnā vā paṇītā vā yā dūre santike vā, sabbā saññā – netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attāti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ye keci saṅkhārā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā hīnā [T 1.0028] vā paṇītā vā ye dūre santike vā, sabbe saṅkhārā – netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attāti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ viññāṇaṃ – netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attāti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṃ.

22. “Therefore, bhikkhus, whatever form there is—past, future, or present, internal or external, coarse or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—all form should be seen as it actually is with proper wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Whatever feeling there is—past, future, or present, internal or external, coarse or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—all feeling should be seen as it actually is with proper wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Whatever perception there is—past, future, or present, internal or external, coarse or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—all perception should be seen as it actually is with proper wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Whatever mental formations there are—past, future, or present, internal or external, coarse or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—all mental formations should be seen as they actually are with proper wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Whatever consciousness there is—past, future, or present, internal or external, coarse or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—all consciousness should be seen as it actually is with proper wisdom thus: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’”

23. “Evaṃ [V 0.0019] passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpasmimpi nibbindati, vedanāyapi nibbindati, saññāyapi nibbindati, saṅkhāresupi nibbindati, viññāṇasmimpi nibbindati; nibbindaṃ virajjati; virāgā vimuccati; vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti, ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānātī”ti.

23. “Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form, disenchanted with feeling, disenchanted with perception, disenchanted with formations, and disenchanted with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. When liberated, there comes the knowledge: ‘I am liberated.’ He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’”

24. Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti abhinanduṃ (syā.). Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne pañcavaggiyānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṃsu. Tena kho pana samayena cha loke arahanto honti.

24. The Blessed One said this. The group-of-five bhikkhus, delighted, rejoiced at the Blessed One’s words. And while this exposition was being spoken, the minds of the group-of-five bhikkhus were liberated from the taints through non-clinging. At that time, there were six arahants in the world.

Pañcavaggiyakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse to the Group-of-Five is concluded.

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro.

The First Recitation Section.

7. Pabbajjākathā

7. The Discourse on the Going Forth

25. Tena [P 1.0015][M 0.0021] kho pana samayena bārāṇasiyaṃ yaso nāma kulaputto seṭṭhiputto sukhumālo hoti. Tassa tayo pāsādā honti – eko [T 1.0029] hemantiko, eko gimhiko, eko vassiko. So vassike pāsāde cattāro māse vassike pāsāde vassike cattāro māse (sī.) nippurisehi tūriyehi paricārayamāno na heṭṭhāpāsādaṃ orohati. Atha kho yasassa kulaputtassa pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitassa samaṅgībhūtassa paricārayamānassa paṭikacceva paṭigacceva (sī.) niddā okkami, parijanassapi niddā okkami, sabbarattiyo ca telapadīpo jhāyati. Atha kho yaso kulaputto paṭikacceva pabujjhitvā addasa sakaṃ parijanaṃ supantaṃ – aññissā kacche vīṇaṃ, aññissā kaṇṭhe mudiṅgaṃ, aññissā kacche āḷambaraṃ, aññaṃ vikesikaṃ, aññaṃ vikkheḷikaṃ, aññā vippalapantiyo, hatthappattaṃ susānaṃ maññe. Disvānassa ādīnavo pāturahosi, nibbidāya cittaṃ saṇṭhāsi. Atha kho yaso kulaputto udānaṃ udānesi – “upaddutaṃ vata bho, upassaṭṭhaṃ vata bho”ti.

25. Now at that time, in Benares, there was a clansman named Yasa, the son of a wealthy merchant, who was delicately brought up. He had three mansions—one for winter, one for summer, and one for the rainy season. In the rainy-season mansion, he spent four months being entertained by female musicians, with no men present, and did not descend to the lower part of the mansion. Then, while Yasa the clansman, endowed and provided with the five cords of sensual pleasure, was being entertained, sleep overcame him early. His attendants also fell asleep afterwards, and an oil lamp burned throughout the night. Then Yasa the clansman awoke early and saw his own attendants sleeping—one with a lute in her armpit, another with a small drum at her neck, another with a tabor in her armpit, one with disheveled hair, another drooling, and others muttering in their sleep—it seemed like a charnel ground that had come into his hands. Seeing this, the peril became manifest to him, and his mind was established in revulsion. Then Yasa the clansman uttered this heartfelt exclamation: “Oh, how afflicted! Oh, how oppressed!”

Atha kho yaso kulaputto suvaṇṇapādukāyo ārohitvā yena nivesanadvāraṃ tenupasaṅkami. Amanussā dvāraṃ vivariṃsu – mā yasassa kulaputtassa koci antarāyamakāsi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyāti[T 1.0030]. Atha kho yaso kulaputto yena nagaradvāraṃ tenupasaṅkami. Amanussā dvāraṃ [V 0.0020] vivariṃsu – mā yasassa kulaputtassa koci antarāyamakāsi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajjāyāti. Atha kho yaso kulaputto yena isipatanaṃ migadāyo tenupasaṅkami.

Then Yasa the clansman, having put on his golden sandals, approached the door of the residence. Non-human beings opened the door, thinking: “Let no one cause an obstacle to the going forth of Yasa the clansman from the household life into homelessness.” Then Yasa the clansman approached the city gate.
