Non-human beings opened the gate, thinking: “Let no one cause an obstacle to the going forth of Yasa the clansman from the household life into homelessness.” Then Yasa the clansman approached the Deer Park at Isipatana.

26. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya ajjhokāse caṅkamati. Addasā kho bhagavā yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ, disvāna caṅkamā orohitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho yaso kulaputto bhagavato avidūre udānaṃ udānesi – “upaddutaṃ vata bho, upassaṭṭhaṃ vata bho”ti. Atha kho bhagavā yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavoca – “idaṃ kho, yasa, anupaddutaṃ, idaṃ anupassaṭṭhaṃ. Ehi yasa, nisīda, dhammaṃ te desessāmī”ti. Atha kho yaso kulaputto – idaṃ kira anupaddutaṃ[M 0.0022], idaṃ anupassaṭṭhanti haṭṭho udaggo suvaṇṇapādukāhi orohitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnassa kho yasassa kulaputtassa bhagavā anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ, kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ, nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā bhagavā aññāsi [P 1.0016] yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ kallacittaṃ, muducittaṃ, vinīvaraṇacittaṃ, udaggacittaṃ, pasannacittaṃ, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā taṃ pakāsesi – dukkhaṃ, samudayaṃ, nirodhaṃ, maggaṃ. Seyyathāpi [T 1.0031] nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva yasassa kulaputtassa tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti.

26. At that time, the Blessed One, having risen at the time of dawn, was walking back and forth in the open. The Blessed One saw the clansman Yasa coming from afar. Having seen him, the Blessed One descended from the walkway and sat down on the prepared seat. Then the clansman Yasa, not far from the Blessed One, uttered this exclamation: “How distressed it is, sirs! How oppressed it is, sirs!” Then the Blessed One said this to the clansman Yasa: “This, Yasa, is not distressed; this is not oppressed. Come, Yasa, sit down; I will teach you the Dhamma.” Then the clansman Yasa, thinking, “This, it is said, is not distressed; this is not oppressed,” joyful and uplifted, took off his golden sandals and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. To the clansman Yasa who was sitting to one side, the Blessed One gave a progressive talk, that is to say: a talk on generosity, a talk on virtue, a talk on heaven; he explained the danger, degradation, and defilement of sensual pleasures, and the benefit of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that the clansman Yasa’s mind was ready, pliable, free from hindrances, uplifted, and clear, he then explained the teaching that is the special discovery of the Buddhas: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth free from stains would properly take up dye, even so, while in that very seat, there arose in the clansman Yasa the stainless, immaculate Eye of the Dhamma: “Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing.”

27. Atha kho yasassa kulaputtassa mātā pāsādaṃ abhiruhitvā yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ apassantī yena seṭṭhi gahapati tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā seṭṭhiṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “putto te, gahapati, yaso na dissatī”ti. Atha kho seṭṭhi gahapati catuddisā assadūte uyyojetvā sāmaṃyeva yena isipatanaṃ migadāyo tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho seṭṭhi gahapati suvaṇṇapādukānaṃ nikkhepaṃ, disvāna taṃyeva anugamāsi anugamā (sī. syā.). Addasā kho bhagavā seṭṭhiṃ gahapatiṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ, disvāna bhagavato etadahosi – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ tathārūpaṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkhareyyaṃ yathā seṭṭhi gahapati idha nisinno idha nisinnaṃ yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ na passeyyā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā tathārūpaṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharesi. Atha kho seṭṭhi gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “api, bhante, bhagavā yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ passeyyā”ti? Tena hi, gahapati, nisīda, appeva nāma idha nisinno idha nisinnaṃ yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ passeyyāsīti. Atha kho seṭṭhi gahapati – idheva kirāhaṃ nisinno idha nisinnaṃ [T 1.0032] yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ [V 0.0021] passissāmīti haṭṭho udaggo bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnassa kho seṭṭhissa gahapatissa bhagavā anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ, kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ, nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ [M 0.0023] pakāsesi. Yadā bhagavā aññāsi seṭṭhiṃ gahapatiṃ kallacittaṃ, muducittaṃ, vinīvaraṇacittaṃ, udaggacittaṃ, pasannacittaṃ, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā, taṃ pakāsesi – dukkhaṃ, samudayaṃ, nirodhaṃ, maggaṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya evameva seṭṭhissa gahapatissa tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti. Atha kho seṭṭhi gahapati diṭṭhadhammo pattadhammo viditadhammo pariyogāḷhadhammo tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṃkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante, seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ nikujjitaṃ (ka.) vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti – evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, dhammañca, bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti[T 1.0033]. Sova loke paṭhamaṃ upāsako ahosi tevāciko[P 1.0017].

27. Then Yasa's mother, having ascended the palace and not seeing the clansman Yasa, approached the wealthy householder and said, 'Householder, your son Yasa is not to be seen.' Then the wealthy householder dispatched horse-messengers to the four directions and himself went to the Isipatana Deer Park. The wealthy householder saw the place where the golden sandals were set down, and having seen it, he followed that very trail. The Blessed One saw the wealthy householder approaching from afar and thought: 'What if I were to perform such a psychic feat that the wealthy householder, sitting here, would not see the clansman Yasa sitting here?' Then the Blessed One performed such a psychic feat. Then the wealthy householder approached the Blessed One and said, 'Venerable sir, might the Blessed One have seen the clansman Yasa?' 'Well then, householder, sit down. It may be that by sitting here you will see the clansman Yasa sitting here.' Then the wealthy householder, joyful and uplifted, thinking, 'Indeed, by sitting right here I will see the clansman Yasa sitting here,' paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. To the wealthy householder sitting to one side, the Blessed One gave a progressive talk—that is, a talk on giving, a talk on virtue, and a talk on heaven; he explained the danger, degradation, and defilement of sensual pleasures and the benefit of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that the wealthy householder's mind was ready, pliable, free from hindrances, uplifted, and clear, he then proclaimed the Dhamma teaching that is the special discovery of the Buddhas: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth, free from stains, would properly take up dye, so too in the wealthy householder, right there on that seat, arose the stainless, immaculate Eye of the Dhamma: 'Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing.' Then the wealthy householder, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, and penetrated the Dhamma, having crossed over doubt, dispelled perplexity, gained confidence, and become independent of others in the Teacher's Dispensation, said to the Blessed One: 'Excellent, Venerable Sir! Excellent, Venerable Sir! Just as one might set upright what was overturned, reveal what was hidden, show the way to one who is lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms—even so has the Dhamma been explained by the Blessed One in many ways. Venerable Sir, I go for refuge to the Blessed One, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts.' He was the first lay follower in the world to declare the threefold refuge.

28. Atha kho yasassa kulaputtassa pituno dhamme desiyamāne yathādiṭṭhaṃ yathāviditaṃ bhūmiṃ paccavekkhantassa anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimucci. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “yasassa kho kulaputtassa pituno dhamme desiyamāne yathādiṭṭhaṃ yathāviditaṃ bhūmiṃ paccavekkhantassa anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuttaṃ. Abhabbo kho yaso kulaputto hīnāyāvattitvā kāme paribhuñjituṃ, seyyathāpi pubbe agārikabhūto; yaṃnūnāhaṃ taṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ paṭippassambheyya”nti. Atha kho bhagavā taṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ paṭippassambhesi. Addasā kho seṭṭhi gahapati yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ nisinnaṃ, disvāna yasaṃ kulaputtaṃ etadavoca – “mātā te tāta, yasa, parideva paridevī (ka.) sokasamāpannā, dehi mātuyā jīvita”nti. Atha kho yaso kulaputto bhagavantaṃ ullokesi. Atha kho bhagavā seṭṭhiṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “taṃ kiṃ maññasi, gahapati, yassa sekkhena ñāṇena sekkhena dassanena dhammo diṭṭho vidito seyyathāpi tayā? Tassa yathādiṭṭhaṃ yathāviditaṃ bhūmiṃ paccavekkhantassa anupādāya [M 0.0024] āsavehi cittaṃ vimuttaṃ. Bhabbo nu kho so, gahapati, hīnāyāvattitvā kāme paribhuñjituṃ seyyathāpi pubbe agārikabhūto”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Yasassa kho, gahapati, kulaputtassa sekkhena ñāṇena sekkhena dassanena [T 1.0034] dhammo diṭṭho vidito seyyathāpi tayā. Tassa yathādiṭṭhaṃ yathāviditaṃ bhūmiṃ paccavekkhantassa anupādāya āsavehi [V 0.0022] cittaṃ vimuttaṃ. Abhabbo kho, gahapati, yaso kulaputto hīnāyāvattitvā kāme paribhuñjituṃ seyyathāpi pubbe agārikabhūto”ti. “Lābhā, bhante, yasassa kulaputtassa, suladdhaṃ, bhante, yasassa kulaputtassa, yathā yasassa kulaputtassa anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuttaṃ. Adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā ajjatanāya bhattaṃ yasena kulaputtena pacchāsamaṇenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho seṭṭhi gahapati bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho yaso kulaputto acirapakkante seṭṭhimhi gahapatimhi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada”nti. “Ehi bhikkhū”ti bhagavā avoca – “svākkhāto dhammo, cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Sāva [P 1.0018] tassa āyasmato upasampadā ahosi. Tena kho pana samayena satta loke arahanto honti.

28. Then, while the Dhamma was being taught to the father of the clansman Yasa, the mind of Yasa the clansman, who was contemplating the truth-ground as he had seen it and as he had known it, was liberated from the taints without clinging. Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: 'While the Dhamma was being taught to his father, the mind of the clansman Yasa, who was contemplating the truth-ground as he had seen it and as he had known it, has been liberated from the taints without clinging. The clansman Yasa is now incapable of returning to the lower life to enjoy sensual pleasures as he did before when he was a householder. What if I were to withdraw that psychic manifestation?' Then the Blessed One withdrew that psychic manifestation. The wealthy householder saw the clansman Yasa seated there. Seeing him, he said to the clansman Yasa: 'My dear Yasa, your mother is overcome with lamentation and sorrow. Give your mother her life.' Then the clansman Yasa looked up at the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One said to the wealthy householder: 'What do you think, householder? For one who, with the knowledge and vision of a trainee, has seen and known the Dhamma just as you have, and for whom, while contemplating the truth-ground as seen and as known, the mind is liberated from the taints without clinging—is such a one, householder, capable of returning to the lower life to enjoy sensual pleasures as he did before when he was a householder?' 'Certainly not, venerable sir.' 'Householder, for the clansman Yasa, with the knowledge and vision of a trainee, the Dhamma has been seen and known, just as by you. For him, while contemplating the truth-ground as seen and as known, the mind has been liberated from the taints without clinging. The clansman Yasa, householder, is incapable of returning to the lower life to enjoy sensual pleasures as he did before when he was a householder.' 'It is a gain for the clansman Yasa, venerable sir, a great gain for the clansman Yasa, that his mind has been liberated from the taints without clinging. Venerable sir, may the Blessed One consent to today's meal from me, with the clansman Yasa as his attendant monk.' The Blessed One consented by silence. Then the wealthy householder, understanding the Blessed One’s consent, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him with his right side toward him, and departed. Then, not long after the wealthy householder had left, the clansman Yasa said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, may I receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence; may I receive the higher ordination.' 'Come, monk,' the Blessed One said, 'the Dhamma is well proclaimed. Live the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.' That itself was the venerable one’s higher ordination. At that time, there were seven arahants in the world.

Yasassa pabbajjā niṭṭhitā.

The account of the going forth of Yasa is concluded.

29. Atha [T 1.0035] kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya āyasmatā yasena pacchāsamaṇena yena seṭṭhissa gahapatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho āyasmato yasassa mātā ca purāṇadutiyikā ca yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Tāsaṃ bhagavā anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ, kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ, nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā tā bhagavā aññāsi kallacittā, muducittā, vinīvaraṇacittā, udaggacittā, pasannacittā, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā taṃ pakāsesi – dukkhaṃ, samudayaṃ, nirodhaṃ, maggaṃ[M 0.0025]. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva tāsaṃ tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti. Tā diṭṭhadhammā pattadhammā viditadhammā pariyogāḷhadhammā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante…pe… etā mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ [T 1.0036] saraṇaṃ gacchāma, dhammañca, bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsikāyo no bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetā saraṇaṃ gatā”ti. Tā ca loke paṭhamaṃ upāsikā ahesuṃ tevācikā.

29. Then, in the morning, the Blessed One, having dressed, took his bowl and robe, and with the Venerable Yasa as his attendant monk, went to the residence of the wealthy householder. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then the Venerable Yasa’s mother and his former wife approached where the Blessed One was; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. The Blessed One gave them a progressive discourse—that is to say, a discourse on giving, a discourse on virtue, a discourse on heaven; he explained the danger, inferiority, and defilement of sensual pleasures, and the benefit of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew them to have minds that were ready, pliable, free from hindrances, uplifted, and confident, he then explained that Dhamma teaching which is the special instruction of the Buddhas: suffering, the origin, the cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth, free from any dark specks, would rightly receive the dye, even so, for them, right on that very seat, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose: 'Whatever has the nature to arise, all that has the nature to cease.' Then they, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, and penetrated the Dhamma, having crossed over doubt, being without uncertainty, having attained to confidence, and being independent of others in the Teacher’s Dispensation, said this to the Blessed One: 'Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! … We, venerable sir, go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. May the Blessed One remember us as laywomen who have gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts.' And they were the first laywomen in the world to take the threefold refuge.

Atha kho āyasmato yasassa mātā ca pitā ca purāṇadutiyikā ca bhagavantañca āyasmantañca yasaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā, bhagavantaṃ [V 0.0023] bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ, ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmato yasassa mātarañca pitarañca purāṇadutiyikañca dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

Then the mother, father, and former wife of the Venerable Yasa, with their own hands, satisfied and served to their fill the Blessed One and the Venerable Yasa with choice hard and soft food. When the Blessed One had finished eating and removed his hand from the bowl, they sat down to one side. Then the Blessed One, having instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened the mother, father, and former wife of the Venerable Yasa with a Dhamma talk, rose from his seat and departed.

30. Assosuṃ kho āyasmato yasassa cattāro gihisahāyakā bārāṇasiyaṃ seṭṭhānuseṭṭhīnaṃ kulānaṃ puttā – vimalo, subāhu[P 1.0019], puṇṇaji, gavampati – yaso kira kulaputto kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitoti. Sutvāna nesaṃ etadahosi – “na hi nūna so orako dhammavinayo, na sā orakā pabbajjā, yattha yaso kulaputto kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito”ti. Te te cattāro janā (ka.) yenāyasmā yaso tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ yasaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Atha kho āyasmā yaso te cattāro gihisahāyake ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā [T 1.0037] bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā yaso bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ime me, bhante, cattāro gihisahāyakā bārāṇasiyaṃ seṭṭhānuseṭṭhīnaṃ kulānaṃ puttā – vimalo, subāhu, puṇṇaji, gavampati. Ime ime cattāro (ka.) bhagavā ovadatu anusāsatū”ti[M 0.0026]. Tesaṃ bhagavā anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi, yadā te bhagavā aññāsi kallacitte muducitte vinīvaraṇacitte udaggacitte pasannacitte, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā, taṃ pakāsesi dukkhaṃ samudayaṃ nirodhaṃ maggaṃ, seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva tesaṃ tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi “yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma”nti. Te diṭṭhadhammā pattadhammā viditadhammā pariyogāḷhadhammā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyāma upasampada”nti. “Etha bhikkhavo”ti bhagavā avoca – “svākkhāto dhammo, caratha brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Sāva tesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ upasampadā ahosi. Atha kho bhagavā te bhikkhū dhammiyā kathāya ovadi anusāsi. Tesaṃ bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya ovadiyamānānaṃ anusāsiyamānānaṃ anupādāya āsavehi [T 1.0038] cittāni vimucciṃsu. Tena kho pana samayena ekādasa loke arahanto honti.

30. The four lay friends of the Venerable Yasa in Bārāṇasī—Vimala, Subāhu, Puṇṇaji, and Gavampati, who were sons of successive merchant families—heard: 'It is said that Yasa the clansman, having shaved off his hair and beard and put on the ochre robes, has gone forth from the household life into homelessness.' Having heard this, it occurred to them: 'Surely, that Dhamma and Discipline in which Yasa the clansman has shaved off his hair and beard, put on the ochre robes, and gone forth from the household life into homelessness is not an inferior one; that going forth is not an inferior one.' They then approached the Venerable Yasa; having approached, they paid homage to the Venerable Yasa and stood to one side. Then the Venerable Yasa, taking those four lay friends, approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Yasa said this to the Blessed One: 'Bhante, these are my four lay friends in Bārāṇasī, sons of successive merchant families: Vimala, Subāhu, Puṇṇaji, and Gavampati. May the Blessed One advise and instruct them.' The Blessed One gave them a progressive talk, that is to say: a talk on giving, a talk on virtue, a talk on the heavens; he explained the danger, inferiority, and defilement of sensual pleasures, and the benefit of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that their minds were ready, pliable, free from hindrances, uplifted, and confident, he then explained the Dhamma teaching that is the Buddhas' own special discovery: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth free from stains would properly absorb dye, even so, as they sat in that very seat, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose in them: 'Whatever is subject to arising is all subject to cessation.' They, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, penetrated the Dhamma, having crossed over doubt, being without uncertainty, having attained confidence, and being independent of others in the Teacher’s Dispensation, said this to the Blessed One: 'Bhante, may we receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence, may we receive the higher ordination.' The Blessed One said: 'Come, bhikkhus. The Dhamma is well-expounded. Practice the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.' This itself was the higher ordination for those venerable ones. Then the Blessed One advised and instructed those bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk. For them, being advised and instructed by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, their minds were liberated from the taints through non-clinging. At that time, there were eleven arahants in the world.

Catugihisahāyakapabbajjā niṭṭhitā.

The going forth of the four lay friends is completed.

31. Assosuṃ [P 1.0020][V 0.0024] kho āyasmato yasassa paññāsamattā gihisahāyakā jānapadā pubbānupubbakānaṃ kulānaṃ puttā – yaso kira kulaputto kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitoti. Sutvāna nesaṃ etadahosi – “na hi nūna so orako dhammavinayo, na sā orakā pabbajjā, yattha yaso kulaputto kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito”ti. Te yenāyasmā yaso tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ yasaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Atha kho āyasmā yaso te paññāsamatte gihisahāyake ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā [M 0.0027] bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā yaso bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ime me, bhante, paññāsamattā gihisahāyakā jānapadā pubbānupubbakānaṃ kulānaṃ puttā. Ime bhagavā ovadatu anusāsatū”ti. Tesaṃ bhagavā anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā te bhagavā aññāsi kallacitte muducitte vinīvaraṇacitte udaggacitte pasannacitte, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā [T 1.0039] dhammadesanā, taṃ pakāsesi dukkhaṃ samudayaṃ nirodhaṃ maggaṃ, seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva tesaṃ tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti. Te diṭṭhadhammā pattadhammā viditadhammā pariyogāḷhadhammā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyāma upasampada”nti. “Etha bhikkhavo”ti bhagavā avoca – “svākkhāto dhammo, caratha brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Sāva tesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ upasampadā ahosi. Atha kho bhagavā te bhikkhū dhammiyā kathāya ovadi anusāsi. Tesaṃ bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya ovadiyamānānaṃ anusāsiyamānānaṃ anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṃsu. Tena kho pana samayena ekasaṭṭhi loke arahanto honti.

31. Then fifty lay friends of the Venerable Yasa, sons of successive, prominent families from the provinces, heard that Yasa, the clansman, had shaved off his hair and beard, put on the ochre-dyed robes, and gone forth from the household life into homelessness. Upon hearing this, they thought: 'Surely, this is no inferior Dhamma and Discipline, no inferior going forth, wherein Yasa the clansman has shaved off his hair and beard, put on the ochre-dyed robes, and gone forth from the household life into homelessness.' They approached the Venerable Yasa, paid homage to him, and stood to one side. Then the Venerable Yasa took those fifty lay friends and went to the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Yasa said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, these are my fifty lay friends, sons of successive, prominent families from the provinces. May the Blessed One advise and instruct them.' The Blessed One gave them a progressive discourse—that is, a discourse on giving, a discourse on virtue, a discourse on heaven; he explained the danger, inferiority, and defilement of sensual pleasures and the benefit in renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that their minds were ready, pliable, free from hindrances, uplifted, and confident, he revealed the teaching that is the special dispensation of the Buddhas: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth free from stains would properly take up dye, so too, while they sat there, the dust-free, stainless vision of the Dhamma arose in them: 'Whatever is subject to arising is all subject to cessation.' Having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, penetrated the Dhamma, having crossed over doubt, being rid of uncertainty, having gained confidence, and being independent of others in the Teacher’s Dispensation, they said to the Blessed One: 'May we receive the going forth, Venerable Sir, may we receive the higher ordination in the Blessed One’s presence.' 'Come, bhikkhus,' said the Blessed One, 'the Dhamma is well-expounded. Live the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.' That was the higher ordination of those venerable ones. Then the Blessed One advised and instructed those bhikkhus with a Dhamma discourse. As they were being advised and instructed by the Blessed One, their minds were liberated from the taints through non-clinging. At that time, there were sixty-one arahants in the world.

Paññāsagihisahāyakapabbajjā niṭṭhitā.

The Going Forth of the Fifty Lay Companions is concluded.

Niṭṭhitā ca pabbajjākathā.

And the Discourse on the Going Forth is concluded.

8. Mārakathā

8. The Discourse on Māra

32. Atha kho bhagavā te bhikkhū āmantesi saṃ. ni. 1.141 mārasaṃyuttepi – “muttāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sabbapāsehi, ye [V 0.0025] dibbā ye ca mānusā. Tumhepi, bhikkhave[P 1.0021], muttā sabbapāsehi, ye dibbā ye ca mānusā. Caratha, bhikkhave, cārikaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Mā ekena dve agamittha. Desetha, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ [T 1.0040] sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsetha. Santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā[M 0.0028], assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti, bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro. Ahampi, bhikkhave, yena uruvelā senānigamo tenupasaṅkamissāmi dhammadesanāyā”ti.

32. Then the Blessed One addressed those monks: 'I am freed, O monks, from all snares, both those that are divine and those that are human. You too, O monks, are freed from all snares, both those that are divine and those that are human. Go forth, O monks, on a journey for the welfare of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans. Let not two go by one way. Teach, O monks, the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, complete with meaning and phrasing. Proclaim the holy life that is utterly complete and perfectly pure. There are beings whose eyes have little dust; from not hearing the Dhamma, they decline. There will be those who will understand the Dhamma. I too, O monks, will go to Uruvelā, to Senānigama, in order to teach the Dhamma.'

33. Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

33. Then Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he addressed the Blessed One with a verse:

“Baddhosi sabbapāsehi, ye dibbā ye ca mānusā;

Mahābandhanabaddhosi, na me samaṇa mokkhasī”ti.

'You are bound by all snares, both those that are divine and those that are human. You are bound by a great bond; O ascetic, you shall not be freed from me.'

“Muttāhaṃ muttohaṃ (sī. syā.) sabbapāsehi, ye dibbā ye ca mānusā;

Mahābandhanamuttomhi, nihato tvamasi antakāti.

'I am freed from all snares, both those that are divine and those that are human. I am freed from the great bond. You are defeated, O Ender!'

saṃ. ni. 1.151 mārasaṃyuttepi “Antalikkhacaro pāso, yvāyaṃ carati mānaso;

Tena taṃ bādhayissāmi, na me samaṇa mokkhasīti.

'That snare which travels through the air, that which is mental and roams about—with that I shall harass you. O ascetic, you shall not be freed from me.'

saṃ. ni. 1.1151 mārasaṃyuttepi “Rūpā saddā rasā gandhā, phoṭṭhabbā ca manoramā;

Ettha me vigato chando, nihato tvamasi antakā”ti.

'As for delightful forms, sounds, tastes, scents, and tangible objects, my desire for them is gone. You are defeated, O Ender!'

Atha kho māro pāpimā – jānāti maṃ bhagavā, jānāti maṃ sugatoti dukkhī dummano

Then Māra the Evil One, thinking, 'The Blessed One knows me, the Well-Farer knows me,' became sorrowful and dejected,

Tatthevantaradhāyīti.

and vanished right on that very spot.

Mārakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Māra is concluded.

9. Pabbajjūpasampadākathā

9. The Discourse on the Going Forth and the Higher Ordination

34. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū nānādisā nānājanapadā pabbajjāpekkhe ca upasampadāpekkhe [V 0.0026] ca ānenti – bhagavā ne pabbājessati [T 1.0041] upasampādessatīti. Tattha bhikkhū ceva kilamanti pabbajjāpekkhā ca upasampadāpekkhā ca. Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “etarahi kho bhikkhū nānādisā nānājanapadā pabbajjāpekkhe ca upasampadāpekkhe ca ānenti – bhagavā ne pabbājessati [M 0.0029] upasampādessatīti. Tattha bhikkhū ceva kilamanti pabbajjāpekkhā ca upasampadāpekkhā ca. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anujāneyyaṃ – tumheva dāni, bhikkhave, tāsu tāsu disāsu tesu tesu janapadesu pabbājetha upasampādethā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū [P 1.0022] āmantesi – “idha mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘etarahi kho bhikkhū nānādisā nānājanapadā pabbajjāpekkhe ca upasampadāpekkhe ca ānenti bhagavā ne pabbājessati upasampādessatīti, tattha bhikkhū ceva kilamanti pabbajjāpekkhā ca upasampadāpekkhā ca, yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anujāneyyaṃ tumheva dāni, bhikkhave, tāsu tāsu disāsu tesu tesu janapadesu pabbājetha upasampādethā’”ti, anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tumheva dāni tāsu tāsu disāsu tesu tesu janapadesu pabbājetha upasampādetha. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, pabbājetabbo upasampādetabbo –

34. At that time, monks were bringing those seeking the going-forth and the full ordination from various regions and various countries, thinking, “The Blessed One will give them the going-forth and will give them the full ordination.” In that situation, both the monks and those seeking the going-forth and the full ordination became weary. Then, while the Blessed One was alone in seclusion, this thought arose in his mind: “Now, monks are bringing those seeking the going-forth and the full ordination from various regions and various countries, thinking, ‘The Blessed One will give them the going-forth and will give them the full ordination.’ In that situation, both the monks and those seeking the going-forth and the full ordination become weary. What if I were to permit the monks: ‘Now, O monks, you yourselves may give the going-forth and give the full ordination in those various regions and in those various countries.’” Then, in the evening, the Blessed One emerged from seclusion and, having given a Dhamma talk in connection with this reason and this matter, addressed the monks: “Here, O monks, while I was alone in seclusion, this thought arose in my mind: ‘Now, monks are bringing those seeking the going-forth and the full ordination from various regions and various countries, thinking, “The Blessed One will give them the going-forth and will give them the full ordination.” In that situation, both the monks and those seeking the going-forth and the full ordination become weary. What if I were to permit the monks: “Now, O monks, you yourselves may give the going-forth and give the full ordination in those various regions and in those various countries.”’ I permit, O monks, that you yourselves may now give the going-forth and the full ordination in those various regions and in those various countries. And, O monks, one should be given the going-forth and the full ordination in this way:

Paṭhamaṃ kesamassuṃ ohārāpetvā [T 1.0042] ohāretvā (ka.), kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādāpetvā, ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ kārāpetvā, bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vandāpetvā, ukkuṭikaṃ nisīdāpetvā, añjaliṃ paggaṇhāpetvā, evaṃ vadehīti vattabbo – buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi; dutiyampi buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, dutiyampi dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, dutiyampi saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi; tatiyampi buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, tatiyampi dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, tatiyampi saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmī”ti. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi tīhi saraṇagamanehi pabbajjaṃ upasampada”nti.

First, having had the hair and beard shaved off, having had saffron robes put on, having had the upper robe arranged over one shoulder, having had them bow at the monks’ feet, having had them sit in the squatting position, having had them raise their hands in añjali, one should be instructed to say thus: ‘I go for refuge to the Buddha, I go for refuge to the Dhamma, I go for refuge to the Saṅgha; for a second time, I go for refuge to the Buddha, for a second time, I go for refuge to the Dhamma, for a second time, I go for refuge to the Saṅgha; for a third time, I go for refuge to the Buddha, for a third time, I go for refuge to the Dhamma, for a third time, I go for refuge to the Saṅgha.’ O monks, I permit the going-forth and the full ordination by means of these three goings for refuge.

Tīhi saraṇagamanehi upasampadākathā niṭṭhitā.

The section on full ordination by means of the three goings for refuge is concluded.

10. Dutiyamārakathā

10. The Second Discourse on Māra

35. Atha kho bhagavā vassaṃvuṭṭho vassaṃvuttho (sī.) bhikkhū āmantesi saṃ. ni. 1.155 – “mayhaṃ kho, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā yoniso sammappadhānā anuttarā vimutti anuppattā, anuttarā vimutti sacchikatā[V 0.0027]. Tumhepi, bhikkhave, yoniso manasikārā [M 0.0030] yoniso sammappadhānā anuttaraṃ vimuttiṃ anupāpuṇātha, anuttaraṃ vimuttiṃ sacchikarothā”ti. Atha kho māro pāpimā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

35. Then the Blessed One, having completed the rains-residence, addressed the monks: ‘O monks, for me, through wise attention and wise right striving, the unsurpassed liberation has been attained, the unsurpassed liberation has been realized. You too, O monks, through wise attention and wise right striving, should attain the unsurpassed liberation, should realize the unsurpassed liberation.’ Then Māra the evil one approached the Blessed One and, having approached, addressed him with a verse:

“Baddhosi mārapāsehi, ye dibbā ye ca mānusā;

Mahābandhanabaddhosi mārabandhanabaddhosi (sī. syā.), na me samaṇa mokkhasī”ti.

‘You are bound by the snares of Māra, both the divine and the human. You are bound by a great bondage; O ascetic, you will not be freed from me.’

“Muttāhaṃ mārapāsehi, ye dibbā ye ca mānusā;

Mahābandhanamuttomhi [T 1.0043] mārabandhanamuttomhi (sī. syā.), nihato tvamasi antakā”ti.

‘I am freed from the snares of Māra, both the divine and the human. I am freed from the great bondage; you are defeated, O End-maker!’

Atha kho māro pāpimā – jānāti maṃ bhagavā, jānāti maṃ sugatoti dukkhī dummano

Then Māra the evil one, thinking, ‘The Blessed One knows me, the Well-gone One knows me,’ being afflicted and dejected,

Tatthevantaradhāyi.

vanished right there.

Dutiyamārakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Second Discourse on Māra is concluded.

11. Bhaddavaggiyavatthu

11. The Story of the Bhaddavaggiyas

36. Atha [P 1.0023] kho bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena uruvelā tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā maggā okkamma yena aññataro vanasaṇḍo tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā taṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ ajjhogāhetvā aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisīdi. Tena kho pana samayena tiṃsamattā bhaddavaggiyā sahāyakā sapajāpatikā tasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe paricārenti. Ekassa pajāpati nāhosi; tassa atthāya vesī ānītā ahosi. Atha kho sā vesī tesu pamattesu paricārentesu bhaṇḍaṃ ādāya palāyittha. Atha kho te sahāyakā sahāyakassa veyyāvaccaṃ karontā, taṃ itthiṃ gavesantā, taṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ āhiṇḍantā addasaṃsu bhagavantaṃ aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisinnaṃ. Disvāna yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “api, bhante, bhagavā ekaṃ itthiṃ passeyyā”ti? “Kiṃ pana vo, kumārā, itthiyā”ti? “Idha mayaṃ, bhante, tiṃsamattā bhaddavaggiyā sahāyakā sapajāpatikā imasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe paricārimhā. Ekassa pajāpati nāhosi; tassa atthāya vesī ānītā ahosi. Atha kho sā, bhante[M 0.0031], vesī amhesu pamattesu paricārentesu bhaṇḍaṃ ādāya [T 1.0044] palāyittha. Te mayaṃ, bhante, sahāyakā sahāyakassa veyyāvaccaṃ karontā, taṃ itthiṃ gavesantā, imaṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ āhiṇḍāmā”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññatha vo, kumārā, katamaṃ nu kho tumhākaṃ varaṃ [V 0.0028] – yaṃ vā tumhe itthiṃ gaveseyyātha, yaṃ vā attānaṃ gaveseyyāthā”ti? “Etadeva, bhante, amhākaṃ varaṃ yaṃ mayaṃ attānaṃ gaveseyyāmā”ti. “Tena hi vo, kumārā, nisīdatha, dhammaṃ vo desessāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhaddavaggiyā sahāyakā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Tesaṃ bhagavā anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi, yadā te bhagavā aññāsi kallacitte muducitte vinīvaraṇacitte udaggacitte pasannacitte, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā, taṃ pakāsesi dukkhaṃ samudayaṃ nirodhaṃ maggaṃ, seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva tesaṃ tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi “yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma”nti. Te diṭṭhadhammā pattadhammā viditadhammā pariyogāḷhadhammā tiṇṇavicikicchā [P 1.0024] vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyāma upasampada”nti. “Etha bhikkhavo”ti bhagavā avoca – “svākkhāto dhammo, caratha [T 1.0045] brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Sāva tesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ upasampadā ahosi.

36. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Bārāṇasī as long as he wished, journeyed towards Uruvelā. Leaving the road, the Blessed One approached a certain grove and, entering that grove, sat down at the foot of a tree. At that time, thirty Bhaddavaggiya companions were amusing themselves in that grove with their wives. One of them had no wife, so a courtesan had been brought for him. While they were heedlessly amusing themselves, that courtesan took their belongings and ran away. Then those companions, helping their friend, searching for that woman, wandering through the grove, saw the Blessed One seated at the foot of a tree. Seeing him, they approached and said, “Venerable sir, did the Blessed One see a woman?” “What is it to you, princes, about a woman?” “Here, venerable sir, we, thirty Bhaddavaggiya companions, were amusing ourselves in this grove with our wives. One of us had no wife, so a courtesan was brought for him. Then, venerable sir, while we were heedlessly amusing ourselves, that courtesan took our belongings and ran away. We, venerable sir, helping our friend, searching for that woman, are wandering through this grove.” “What do you think, princes, which is better for you—that you should search for a woman or that you should search for yourselves?” “Indeed, venerable sir, it would be better for us to search for ourselves.” “Well then, princes, sit down, I will teach you the Dhamma.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those Bhaddavaggiya companions replied, and having paid homage to the Blessed One, sat down to one side. The Blessed One gave them a progressive discourse: that is, a talk on generosity, on virtue, on heaven; he revealed the danger, degradation, and defilement of sensual pleasures and the benefits of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that their minds were ready, pliable, free from hindrances, uplifted, and confident, he revealed the supreme teaching of the Buddhas: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth free from stains would properly absorb dye, so too on that very seat the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose in them: “Whatever is subject to arising is all subject to cessation.” They, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, known the Dhamma, plunged into the Dhamma, were free from doubt, rid of perplexity, attained to confidence, and were independent of others in the Teacher's dispensation. They said to the Blessed One, “May we receive the going forth, venerable sir, may we receive the higher ordination in the Blessed One's presence.” “Come, bhikkhus!” the Blessed One said, “The Dhamma is well-proclaimed; lead the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.” That was the higher ordination of those venerable ones.

Bhaddavaggiyasahāyakānaṃ vatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story of the Bhaddavaggiya companions is finished.

Dutiyabhāṇavāro.

The Second Recitation Section is finished.

12. Uruvelapāṭihāriyakathā

12. The Discourse on the Miracle at Uruvelā

37. Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena uruvelā tadavasari. Tena kho pana samayena uruvelāyaṃ tayo jaṭilā paṭivasanti – uruvelakassapo, nadīkassapo, gayākassapoti. Tesu uruvelakassapo [M 0.0032] jaṭilo pañcannaṃ jaṭilasatānaṃ nāyako hoti, vināyako aggo pamukho pāmokkho. Nadīkassapo jaṭilo tiṇṇaṃ jaṭilasatānaṃ nāyako hoti, vināyako aggo pamukho pāmokkho. Gayākassapo jaṭilo dvinnaṃ jaṭilasatānaṃ nāyako hoti, vināyako aggo pamukho pāmokkho. Atha kho bhagavā yena uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa assamo tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – “sace te, kassapa[V 0.0029], agaru, vaseyyāma ekarattaṃ agyāgāre”ti? “Na kho me, mahāsamaṇa, garu, caṇḍettha nāgarājā iddhimā āsiviso [T 1.0046] ghoraviso, so taṃ mā viheṭhesī”ti. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – “sace te, kassapa, agaru, vaseyyāma ekarattaṃ agyāgāre”ti? “Na kho me, mahāsamaṇa, garu, caṇḍettha nāgarājā iddhimā āsiviso ghoraviso, so taṃ mā viheṭhesī”ti. Tatiyampi kho bhagavā uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – “sace te, kassapa, agaru, vaseyyāma ekarattaṃ agyāgāre”ti? “Na kho me, mahāsamaṇa, garu, caṇḍettha nāgarājā iddhimā āsiviso ghoraviso, so taṃ mā viheṭhesī”ti. “Appeva maṃ na viheṭheyya, iṅgha tvaṃ, kassapa, anujānāhi agyāgāra”nti. “Vihara, mahāsamaṇa, yathāsukha”nti. Atha kho bhagavā agyāgāraṃ pavisitvā tiṇasanthārakaṃ paññapetvā nisīdi pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā.

37. Then the Blessed One, wandering by stages, arrived at Uruvelā. At that time, three matted-hair ascetics were dwelling in Uruvelā: Uruvelakassapa, Nadīkassapa, and Gayākassapa. Among them, the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa was the leader, instructor, chief, foremost, and principal of five hundred matted-hair ascetics. The matted-hair ascetic Nadīkassapa was the leader, instructor, chief, foremost, and principal of three hundred matted-hair ascetics. The matted-hair ascetic Gayākassapa was the leader, instructor, chief, foremost, and principal of two hundred matted-hair ascetics. Then the Blessed One approached the hermitage of the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa and said to him: “If it is not burdensome for you, Kassapa, I would like to stay for one night in the fire-hall.” “It is not burdensome for me, great ascetic, but there is a fierce nāga-king here, possessed of psychic power, of swift and terrible venom. He might harm you.” For a second time, the Blessed One said to the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa: “If it is not burdensome for you, Kassapa, I would like to stay for one night in the fire-hall.” “It is not burdensome for me, great ascetic, but there is a fierce nāga-king here, possessed of psychic power, of swift and terrible venom. He might harm you.” For a third time, the Blessed One said to the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa: “If it is not burdensome for you, Kassapa, I would like to stay for one night in the fire-hall.” “It is not burdensome for me, great ascetic, but there is a fierce nāga-king here, possessed of psychic power, of swift and terrible venom. He might harm you.” “Indeed, he will not harm me. Please, Kassapa, permit me the fire-hall.” “Dwell, great ascetic, as you please.” Then the Blessed One entered the fire-hall, spread out a grass mat, and sat down cross-legged, holding his body erect and establishing mindfulness before him.

38. Addasā kho so nāgo bhagavantaṃ paviṭṭhaṃ, disvāna dummano dukkhī dummano (sī. syā.) padhūpāyi pakhūpāsi (ka.). Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ imassa nāgassa anupahacca chaviñca [P 1.0025] cammañca maṃsañca nhāruñca aṭṭhiñca aṭṭhimiñjañca tejasā tejaṃ pariyādiyeyya”nti. Atha kho bhagavā tathārūpaṃ iddhābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā padhūpāyi. Atha kho so nāgo makkhaṃ asahamāno pajjali. Bhagavāpi tejodhātuṃ samāpajjitvā pajjali. Ubhinnaṃ sajotibhūtānaṃ agyāgāraṃ ādittaṃ viya hoti sampajjalitaṃ sajotibhūtaṃ. Atha kho te jaṭilā agyāgāraṃ parivāretvā evamāhaṃsu – “abhirūpo vata bho mahāsamaṇo nāgena viheṭhiyatī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā tassā [M 0.0033] rattiyā accayena tassa nāgassa [T 1.0047] anupahacca chaviñca cammañca maṃsañca nhāruñca aṭṭhiñca aṭṭhimiñjañca tejasā tejaṃ pariyādiyitvā patte pakkhipitvā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa dassesi – “ayaṃ te, kassapa, nāgo pariyādinno pariyādiṇṇo (ka.) assa tejasā tejo”ti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma caṇḍassa nāgarājassa iddhimato āsivisassa ghoravisassa tejasā tejaṃ pariyādiyissati, natveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti.

38. That nāga saw the Blessed One entering, and upon seeing him, being displeased, it emitted smoke. Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: 'What if I, without harming this nāga’s outer skin, inner skin, flesh, sinews, bones, or bone marrow, were to exhaust its power with my power?' Then the Blessed One, having created such a psychic formation, emitted smoke. Then that nāga, unable to endure the anger, burst into flames. The Blessed One also, having entered the meditative absorption of the fire element, burst into flames. With both of them blazing, the fire-hall was as if ablaze, thoroughly burning and radiant with flames. Then those ascetics, surrounding the fire-hall, said this: 'Oh, the great ascetic is truly handsome, yet he is being harassed by the nāga!' Then the Blessed One, when that night had passed, without harming that nāga’s outer skin, inner skin, flesh, sinews, bones, or bone marrow, having exhausted its power with his power, placed it in his bowl and showed it to Uruvelakassapa the ascetic, saying: 'Kassapa, this is your nāga. Its power has been exhausted by my power.' Then this thought occurred to Uruvelakassapa the ascetic: 'The great ascetic is indeed of great psychic power and great might, in that he has exhausted with his own power the power of a fierce, powerful nāga king of swift and terrible venom. Yet, he is not an Arahant like I am.'

39.

39.

Nerañjarāyaṃ bhagavā, uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ avoca;

“Sace te kassapa agaru, viharemu ajjaṇho aggisālamhī”ti aggisaraṇamhīti (sī. syā.).

On the bank of the Nerañjarā, the Blessed One said to Uruvelakassapa the ascetic: 'Kassapa, if it is not a burden to you, let us stay for today in the fire-hall.'

“Na kho me mahāsamaṇa garu;

Phāsukāmova taṃ nivāremi;

Caṇḍettha nāgarājā;

Iddhimā āsiviso ghoraviso;

So [V 0.0030] taṃ mā viheṭhesī”ti.

'It is not a burden to me, Great Ascetic. It is only because I desire your well-being that I forbid you. Here there is a fierce nāga king, powerful, of swift venom and terrible venom. May he not harass you.'

“Appeva maṃ na viheṭheyya;

Iṅgha tvaṃ kassapa anujānāhi agyāgāra”nti;

Dinnanti naṃ viditvā;

Abhīto asambhīto (sī.) pāvisi bhayamatīto.

'Indeed, he would not be able to harass me. Come now, Kassapa, permit the fire-hall.' Knowing it was given, he who had overcome fear entered fearlessly.

Disvā isiṃ paviṭṭhaṃ, ahināgo dummano padhūpāyi;

Sumanamanaso adhimano avimano (katthaci), navimano (syā.), manussanāgopi tattha padhūpāyi.

Having seen the sage enter, the serpent-nāga, being of a displeased mind, emitted smoke. Being of a well-pleased and superior mind, the human-nāga also emitted smoke there.

Makkhañca [T 1.0048] asahamāno, ahināgo pāvakova pajjali;

Tejodhātusu kusalo, manussanāgopi tattha pajjali.

And the serpent-nāga, unable to endure the anger, blazed forth like fire. The human-nāga, skilled in the fire-element meditation, also blazed forth there.

Ubhinnaṃ sajotibhūtānaṃ;

Agyāgāraṃ ādittaṃ hoti sampajjalitaṃ sajotibhūtaṃ;

Udicchare jaṭilā;

“Abhirūpo vata bho mahāsamaṇo;

Nāgena viheṭhiyatī”ti bhaṇanti.

From the two who were emitting flames, the fire-hall was ablaze, burning all around with flames. The matted-hair ascetics looked on and said: 'Oh, the great ascetic is so very handsome! He is surely being harmed by the nāga!'

Atha [M 0.0034] tassā rattiyā atha rattiyā (sī. syā.) accayena;

Hatā nāgassa acciyo honti ahināgassa acciyo na honti (sī. syā.);

Iddhimato pana ṭhitā iddhimato panuṭṭhitā (sī.);

Anekavaṇṇā acciyo honti.

Then, with the passing of that night, the flames of the nāga were extinguished; but the flames of the one possessed of psychic power remained, being of many colors.

Nīlā atha lohitikā;

Mañjiṭṭhā pītakā phalikavaṇṇāyo;

Aṅgīrasassa kāye;

Anekavaṇṇā acciyo honti.

Blue, then red, madder, yellow, and crystal-hued; on the body of Aṅgīrasa, there were flames of many colors.

Pattamhi [V 0.0031] odahitvā;

Ahināgaṃ brāhmaṇassa dassesi;

“Ayaṃ te kassapa nāgo;

Pariyādinno assa tejasā tejo”ti.

Having placed the serpent-nāga in the bowl, he showed it to the brahmin, saying: 'Kassapa, this is your nāga. Its power has been overcome by my power.'

Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo bhagavato iminā iddhipāṭihāriyena abhippasanno bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idheva, mahāsamaṇa, vihara, ahaṃ te te upaṭṭhāmi (itipi) dhuvabhattenā”ti.

Then the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa, being exceedingly pleased by this miracle of psychic power, said this to the Blessed One: 'Dwell right here, Great Ascetic. I will attend to you with a constant supply of food.'

Paṭhamaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ.

The first miracle.

40. Atha [P 1.0026] kho bhagavā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa assamassa avidūre [T 1.0049] aññatarasmiṃ vanasaṇḍe vihāsi. Atha kho cattāro mahārājāno abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā catuddisā aṭṭhaṃsu seyyathāpi mahantā aggikkhandhā. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kālo, mahāsamaṇa, niṭṭhitaṃ bhattaṃ. Ke nu kho te, mahāsamaṇa, abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ obhāsetvā yena tvaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu[M 0.0035], upasaṅkamitvā taṃ abhivādetvā catuddisā aṭṭhaṃsu “seyyathāpi mahantā aggikkhandhā”ti. “Ete kho, kassapa, cattāro mahārājāno yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu dhammassavanāyā”ti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma cattāropi mahārājāno upasaṅkamissanti dhammassavanāya, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā tasmiṃyeva vanasaṇḍe vihāsi.

40. Then the Blessed One dwelt in a certain grove not far from the hermitage of Uruvelakassapa, the matted-hair ascetic. Then, when the night was far advanced, the Four Great Kings, with surpassing radiance, having illuminated the entire grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and stood in the four directions, like great masses of fire. Then, when the night had passed, Uruvelakassapa the matted-hair ascetic approached the Blessed One and said this: “It is time, Great Ascetic; the meal is ready. Who indeed were they, Great Ascetic, who, when the night was far advanced, with surpassing radiance, having illuminated the entire grove, approached you, paid homage to you, and stood in the four directions like great masses of fire?” “These, Kassapa, were the Four Great Kings; they approached me to hear the Dhamma.” Then this thought occurred to Uruvelakassapa the matted-hair ascetic: “The Great Ascetic is indeed of great psychic power and great might, in that even the Four Great Kings approach him to hear the Dhamma; yet he is certainly not an Arahant like me.” Then the Blessed One, having eaten the meal of Uruvelakassapa the matted-hair ascetic, dwelt in that very same grove.

Dutiyaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ.

The second miracle.

41. Atha kho sakko devānamindo abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami[T 1.0050], upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi seyyathāpi mahāaggikkhandho, purimāhi vaṇṇanibhāhi abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo tassā rattiyā accayena [V 0.0032] yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kālo, mahāsamaṇa, niṭṭhitaṃ bhattaṃ. Ko nu kho so, mahāsamaṇa, abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ obhāsetvā yena tvaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā taṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi seyyathāpi mahāaggikkhandho, purimāhi vaṇṇanibhāhi abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti? “Eso kho, kassapa, sakko devānamindo yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami dhammassavanāyā”ti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma sakkopi [P 1.0027] devānamindo upasaṅkamissati dhammassavanāya, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā tasmiṃyeva vanasaṇḍe vihāsi.

41. Then Sakka, lord of the devas, when the night was far advanced, with a most pleasing appearance, illuminating the entire grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side like a great mass of fire, more pleasing and more sublime than the radiances of those who came before. Then, when that night had passed, the ascetic Uruvelakassapa approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he said this to the Blessed One: 'It is time, Great Ascetic, the meal is ready. Who indeed was that, Great Ascetic, who, when the night was far advanced, with a most pleasing appearance, illuminating the entire grove, approached you, paid homage to you, and stood to one side like a great mass of fire, more pleasing and more sublime than the radiances of those who came before?' 'That, Kassapa, was Sakka, lord of the devas. He approached me to hear the Dhamma.' Then this thought occurred to the ascetic Uruvelakassapa: 'The Great Ascetic is of great psychic power and great might, since even Sakka, lord of the devas, approaches to hear the Dhamma. But he is certainly not an Arahant like me.' Then the Blessed One, having partaken of the meal of the ascetic Uruvelakassapa, dwelt in that very same grove.

Tatiyaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ.

The third miracle is finished.

42. Atha [M 0.0036] kho brahmā sahampati abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi seyyathāpi mahāaggikkhandho, purimāhi vaṇṇanibhāhi abhikkantataro ca [T 1.0051] paṇītataro ca. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kālo, mahāsamaṇa, niṭṭhitaṃ bhattaṃ. Ko nu kho so, mahāsamaṇa, abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ obhāsetvā yena tvaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā taṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi seyyathāpi mahāaggikkhandho, purimāhi vaṇṇanibhāhi abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti? “Eso kho, kassapa, brahmā sahampati yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami dhammassavanāyā”ti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma brahmāpi sahampati upasaṅkamissati dhammassavanāya, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā tasmiṃyeva vanasaṇḍe vihāsi.

42. Then Brahmā Sahampati, when the night was far advanced, with a most pleasing appearance, illuminating the entire grove, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side like a great mass of fire, more pleasing and more sublime than the previous radiances. Then, when that night had passed, the ascetic Uruvelakassapa approached the Blessed One and said: 'It is time, Great Ascetic, the meal is ready. Who was that, Great Ascetic, who, when the night was far advanced, with a most pleasing appearance, illuminating the entire grove, approached you, paid homage to you, and stood to one side like a great mass of fire, more pleasing and more sublime than the previous radiances?' 'That, Kassapa, was Brahmā Sahampati, who approached me to hear the Dhamma.' Then this thought occurred to the ascetic Uruvelakassapa: 'The Great Ascetic is indeed of great psychic power and great might, since even Brahmā Sahampati comes to hear the Dhamma. Yet he is not an Arahant like me.' Then the Blessed One, having eaten the meal of the ascetic Uruvelakassapa, dwelt in that same grove.

Catutthaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ.

The fourth miracle is finished.

43. Tena kho pana samayena uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa mahāyañño paccupaṭṭhito hoti, kevalakappā ca aṅgamagadhā pahūtaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ ādāya abhikkamitukāmā honti[V 0.0033]. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “etarahi kho me mahāyañño paccupaṭṭhito, kevalakappā ca aṅgamagadhā pahūtaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ ādāya abhikkamissanti. Sace mahāsamaṇo mahājanakāye iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissati[T 1.0052], mahāsamaṇassa lābhasakkāro abhivaḍḍhissati, mama lābhasakkāro parihāyissati. Aho nūna mahāsamaṇo svātanāya nāgaccheyyā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapassa [P 1.0028] jaṭilassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya uttarakuruṃ gantvā tato piṇḍapātaṃ āharitvā anotattadahe paribhuñjitvā tattheva divāvihāraṃ akāsi. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo tassā [M 0.0037] rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kālo, mahāsamaṇa, niṭṭhitaṃ bhattaṃ. Kiṃ nu kho, mahāsamaṇa, hiyyo nāgamāsi? Api ca mayaṃ taṃ sarāma – kiṃ nu kho mahāsamaṇo nāgacchatīti? Khādanīyassa ca bhojanīyassa ca te paṭivīso paṭiviṃso (sī.), paṭiviso (syā.) ṭhapito”ti. Nanu te, kassapa, etadahosi – “‘etarahi kho me mahāyañño paccupaṭṭhito, kevalakappā ca aṅgamagadhā pahūtaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ ādāya abhikkamissanti, sace mahāsamaṇo mahājanakāye iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissati, mahāsamaṇassa lābhasakkāro abhivaḍḍhissati, mama lābhasakkāro parihāyissati, aho nūna mahāsamaṇo svātanāya nāgaccheyyā’ti. So kho ahaṃ, kassapa, tava cetasā cetoparivitakkaṃ aññāya uttarakuruṃ gantvā tato piṇḍapātaṃ āharitvā anotattadahe paribhuñjitvā tattheva divāvihāraṃ akāsi”nti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma cetasāpi cittaṃ pajānissati[T 1.0053], na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā tasmiṃyeva vanasaṇḍe vihāsi.

43. Now at that time, a great sacrifice was prepared for the ascetic Uruvelakassapa, and the entire populace of Aṅga and Magadha intended to come, bringing abundant solid and soft food. Then this thought occurred to the ascetic Uruvelakassapa: 'Now a great sacrifice is prepared for me, and the entire populace of Aṅga and Magadha will come, bringing abundant solid and soft food. If the Great Ascetic performs a miracle of psychic power in the midst of the great assembly, the Great Ascetic’s gain and honor will increase, and my gain and honor will decline. Oh, if only the Great Ascetic would not come tomorrow!' Then the Blessed One, knowing with his mind the thought in the mind of the ascetic Uruvelakassapa, went to Uttarakuru, brought almsfood from there, ate it at Lake Anotatta, and spent the day there. Then, when that night had passed, the ascetic Uruvelakassapa approached the Blessed One and said to him: 'It is time, Great Ascetic, the meal is ready. Why, Great Ascetic, did you not come yesterday? We were indeed thinking of you: ‘Why does the Great Ascetic not come?’ A portion of solid and soft food was set aside for you.' 'Kassapa, did this thought not occur to you: ‘Now a great sacrifice is prepared for me, and the entire populace of Aṅga and Magadha will come, bringing abundant solid and soft food. If the Great Ascetic performs a miracle of psychic power in the midst of the great assembly, the Great Ascetic’s gain and honor will increase, and my gain and honor will decline. Oh, if only the Great Ascetic would not come tomorrow!’? So I, Kassapa, knowing your thought with my mind, went to Uttarakuru, brought almsfood from there, ate it at Lake Anotatta, and spent the day there.' Then this thought occurred to the ascetic Uruvelakassapa: 'The Great Ascetic is indeed of great psychic power and great might, since he can know the thoughts of others with his mind. Yet he is not an Arahant like me.' Then the Blessed One, having eaten the meal of the ascetic Uruvelakassapa, dwelt in that same grove.

Pañcamaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ.

The fifth miracle is finished.

44. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavato paṃsukūlaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “kattha nu kho ahaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ dhoveyya”nti? Atha kho sakko devānamindo bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya pāṇinā pokkharaṇiṃ khaṇitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idha, bhante, bhagavā paṃsukūlaṃ dhovatū”ti. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “kimhi nu kho ahaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ parimaddeyya”nti? Atha kho sakko devānamindo bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya mahatiṃ silaṃ upanikkhipi – idha, bhante, bhagavā paṃsukūlaṃ parimaddatūti. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “kimhi nu kho ahaṃ ahaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ (ka.) ālambitvā [V 0.0034] uttareyya”nti? Atha kho kakudhe adhivatthā devatā bhagavato [M 0.0038] cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya sākhaṃ onāmesi – idha, bhante, bhagavā ālambitvā [P 1.0029] uttaratūti. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “kimhi nu kho ahaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ vissajjeyya”nti? Atha kho sakko devānamindo bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya mahatiṃ silaṃ upanikkhipi – idha, bhante, bhagavā paṃsukūlaṃ vissajjetūti. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kālo[T 1.0054], mahāsamaṇa, niṭṭhitaṃ bhattaṃ. Kiṃ nu kho, mahāsamaṇa, nāyaṃ pubbe idha pokkharaṇī, sāyaṃ idha pokkharaṇī. Nayimā silā pubbe upanikkhittā. Kenimā silā upanikkhittā? Nayimassa kakudhassa pubbe sākhā onatā, sāyaṃ sākhā onatā”ti. Idha me, kassapa, paṃsukūlaṃ uppannaṃ ahosi. Tassa mayhaṃ, kassapa, etadahosi – “kattha nu kho ahaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ dhoveyya”nti? Atha kho, kassapa, sakko devānamindo mama cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya pāṇinā pokkharaṇiṃ khaṇitvā maṃ etadavoca – “idha, bhante, bhagavā paṃsukūlaṃ dhovatū”ti. Sāyaṃ kassapa amanussena pāṇinā khaṇitā pokkharaṇī. Tassa mayhaṃ, kassapa, etadahosi – “kimhi nu kho ahaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ parimaddeyya”nti? Atha kho, kassapa, sakko devānamindo mama cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya mahatiṃ silaṃ upanikkhipi – “idha, bhante, bhagavā paṃsukūlaṃ parimaddatū”ti. Sāyaṃ kassapa amanussena upanikkhittā silā. Tassa mayhaṃ, kassapa, etadahosi – “kimhi nu kho ahaṃ ālambitvā uttareyya”nti? Atha kho, kassapa, kakudhe adhivatthā devatā ja mama cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya sākhaṃ onāmesi – “idha, bhante, bhagavā ālambitvā uttaratū”ti. Svāyaṃ āharahattho kakudho. Tassa mayhaṃ, kassapa, etadahosi – “kimhi nu kho ahaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ vissajjeyya”nti? Atha kho, kassapa, sakko devānamindo mama cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya mahatiṃ silaṃ upanikkhipi – “idha, bhante, bhagavā paṃsukūlaṃ vissajjetū”ti[T 1.0055]. Sāyaṃ kassapa amanussena upanikkhittā silāti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma sakkopi devānamindo veyyāvaccaṃ karissati, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā tasmiṃyeva vanasaṇḍe vihāsi.

44. Now at that time, a rag-robe had arisen for the Blessed One. Then this thought arose in the Blessed One: 'Where, indeed, might I wash the rag-robe?' Then Sakka, lord of the devas, knowing with his mind the Blessed One’s thought, dug a pond with his hand and said this to the Blessed One: 'Here, Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One wash the rag-robe.' Then this thought arose in the Blessed One: 'On what, indeed, might I rub the rag-robe?' Then Sakka, lord of the devas, knowing with his mind the Blessed One’s thought, placed a great stone slab nearby, saying: 'Here, Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One rub the rag-robe.' Then this thought arose in the Blessed One: 'Holding on to what, indeed, might I wring it out?' Then the deity dwelling in the Kakudha tree, knowing with his mind the Blessed One’s thought, bent down a branch, saying: 'Here, Venerable Sir, holding on to this, let the Blessed One wring it out.' Then this thought arose in the Blessed One: 'Where, indeed, might I spread out the rag-robe?' Then Sakka, lord of the devas, knowing with his mind the Blessed One’s thought, placed a great stone slab nearby, saying: 'Here, Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One spread out the rag-robe.' Then, when that night had passed, the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa went to where the Blessed One was. Having approached, he said this to the Blessed One: 'It is time, Great Ascetic, the meal is ready. Great Ascetic, how is it that this pond was not here before, yet now this pond is here? These stone slabs were not placed here before; by whom were they placed? The branch of this Kakudha tree was not bent down before, yet now it is bent down.' 'Here, Kassapa, a rag-robe arose for me. To me, Kassapa, this thought arose: "Where, indeed, might I wash the rag-robe?" Then, Kassapa, Sakka, lord of the devas, knowing with his mind my thought, dug a pond with his hand and said this to me: "Here, Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One wash the rag-robe." That pond, Kassapa, was dug by the hand of a non-human. To me, Kassapa, this thought arose: "On what, indeed, might I rub the rag-robe?" Then, Kassapa, Sakka, lord of the devas, knowing with his mind my thought, placed a great stone slab nearby, saying: "Here, Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One rub the rag-robe." That stone slab, Kassapa, was placed by a non-human. To me, Kassapa, this thought arose: "Holding on to what, indeed, might I wring it out?" Then, Kassapa, the deity dwelling in the Kakudha tree, knowing with his mind my thought, bent down a branch, saying: "Here, Venerable Sir, holding on to this, let the Blessed One wring it out." That Kakudha tree is now within reach of the hand. To me, Kassapa, this thought arose: "Where, indeed, might I spread out the rag-robe?" Then, Kassapa, Sakka, lord of the devas, knowing with his mind my thought, placed a great stone slab nearby, saying: "Here, Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One spread out the rag-robe." That stone slab, Kassapa, was placed by a non-human.' Then this thought arose in the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa: 'The Great Ascetic is indeed of great psychic power and great might, in that even Sakka, lord of the devas, performs services for him. Yet, he is certainly not an Arahant like I am.' Then the Blessed One, having eaten the meal of the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa, dwelled in that very same forest grove.

Atha [M 0.0039] kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato [P 1.0030] kālaṃ ārocesi – “kālo, mahāsamaṇa, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. “Gaccha tvaṃ, kassapa, āyāmaha”nti uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ uyyojetvā yāya jambuyā [V 0.0035] ‘jambudīpo’ paññāyati, tato phalaṃ gahetvā paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā agyāgāre nisīdi. Addasā kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ agyāgāre nisinnaṃ, disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “katamena tvaṃ, mahāsamaṇa, maggena āgato? Ahaṃ tayā paṭhamataraṃ pakkanto, so tvaṃ paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā agyāgāre nisinno”ti. “Idhāhaṃ, kassapa, taṃ uyyojetvā yāya jambuyā ‘jambudīpo’ paññāyati, tato phalaṃ gahetvā paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā agyāgāre nisinno. Idaṃ kho, kassapa, jambuphalaṃ vaṇṇasampannaṃ gandhasampannaṃ rasasampannaṃ. Sace ākaṅkhasi paribhuñjā”ti. “Alaṃ, mahāsamaṇa, tvaṃyeva taṃ arahasi[T 1.0056], tvaṃyeva taṃ tvaṃyevetaṃ āharasi, tvaṃyevetaṃ (sī. syā.) paribhuñjāhī”ti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma maṃ paṭhamataraṃ uyyojetvā yāya jambuyā ‘jambudīpo’ paññāyati, tato phalaṃ gahetvā paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā agyāgāre nisīdissati, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā tasmiṃyeva vanasaṇḍe vihāsi.

Then, when that night had passed, the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa approached the Blessed One and, on arrival, announced the time to him: 'It is time, Great Ascetic, the meal is ready.' 'Go, Kassapa, I am coming.' Having dismissed the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa, he went to the Jambu tree by which Jambudīpa is known, took a fruit from it, arrived back before him, and sat down in the fire-chamber. The matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa saw the Blessed One sitting in the fire-chamber. Seeing him, he said this to the Blessed One: 'By which path did you come, Great Ascetic? I departed before you, yet you have arrived first and are seated in the fire-chamber.' 'Here, Kassapa, after dismissing you, I went to the Jambu tree by which Jambudīpa is known, took a fruit from it, arrived back before you, and sat down in the fire-chamber. This, Kassapa, is a rose-apple fruit endowed with color, fragrance, and taste. If you wish, partake of it.' 'Enough, Great Ascetic, you yourself are worthy of it; you yourself partake of it.' Then this thought arose in the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa: 'The Great Ascetic is indeed of great psychic power and great might, in that, after dismissing me first, he went to the Jambu tree by which Jambudīpa is known, took a fruit from it, arrived back before me, and sat down in the fire-chamber. Yet, he is certainly not an Arahant like I am.' Then the Blessed One, having eaten the meal of the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa, dwelled in that very same forest grove.

45. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocesi – “kālo, mahāsamaṇa, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Gaccha tvaṃ, kassapa, āyāmahanti uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ uyyojetvā yāya jambuyā ‘jambudīpo’ paññāyati, tassā avidūre ambo…pe… tassā avidūre āmalakī…pe… tassā avidūre harītakī…pe… tāvatiṃsaṃ gantvā pāricchattakapupphaṃ gahetvā paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā agyāgāre nisīdi. Addasā kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ agyāgāre nisinnaṃ, disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “katamena tvaṃ, mahāsamaṇa, maggena āgato? Ahaṃ tayā paṭhamataraṃ pakkanto, so tvaṃ paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā agyāgāre nisinno”ti. “Idhāhaṃ[M 0.0040], kassapa, taṃ uyyojetvā tāvatiṃsaṃ gantvā pāricchattakapupphaṃ gahetvā paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā agyāgāre nisinno. Idaṃ kho, kassapa, pāricchattakapupphaṃ [T 1.0057] vaṇṇasampannaṃ gandhasampannaṃ sugandhikaṃ (ka.). (Sace ākaṅkhasi gaṇhā”ti. “Alaṃ, mahāsamaṇa, tvaṃyeva taṃ arahasi, tvaṃyeva taṃ gaṇhā”ti) ( ) sī. syā. potthakesu natthi. [P 1.0031] Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma maṃ paṭhamataraṃ uyyojetvā tāvatiṃsaṃ gantvā pāricchattakapupphaṃ gahetvā paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā agyāgāre nisīdissati, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti.

45. Then, when the night had passed, the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa approached the Blessed One, and having approached, announced the time to the Blessed One: “It is time, great ascetic, the meal is ready.” “Go, Kassapa, I shall come.” Having dismissed the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa, then, by the Jambu tree by which ‘Jambudīpa’ is known, and not far from it a mango tree… and not far from it an emblic myrobalan tree… and not far from it a yellow myrobalan tree… he went to the Tāvatiṃsa realm, took a pāricchattaka flower, and arriving before him, sat down in the fire-hut. The matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa saw the Blessed One seated in the fire-hut, and upon seeing him, said this: “By which path did you come, great ascetic? I departed before you, yet you arrived before me and are seated in the fire-hut.” “Here, Kassapa, after dismissing you, I went to the Tāvatiṃsa realm, took a pāricchattaka flower, and arriving before you, am seated in the fire-hut. This, Kassapa, is a pāricchattaka flower, endowed with color and fragrance. If you wish, take it.” “Enough, great ascetic, you alone are worthy of it; you alone should take it.” Then this thought occurred to the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa: “The great ascetic is indeed of great psychic power and great might, in that after dismissing me first, he could go to the Tāvatiṃsa realm, take a pāricchattaka flower, arrive before me, and sit down in the fire-hut. Yet he is not an arahant like me.”

46. Tena kho pana samayena te jaṭilā aggiṃ paricaritukāmā na sakkonti kaṭṭhāni phāletuṃ[V 0.0036]. Atha kho tesaṃ jaṭilānaṃ etadahosi – “nissaṃsayaṃ kho mahāsamaṇassa iddhānubhāvo, yathā mayaṃ na sakkoma kaṭṭhāni phāletu”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – “phāliyantu, kassapa, kaṭṭhānī”ti. “Phāliyantu, mahāsamaṇā”ti. Sakideva pañca kaṭṭhasatāni phāliyiṃsu. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma kaṭṭhānipi phāliyissanti, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti.

46. At that time, those matted-hair ascetics, wishing to tend the fire, were unable to split the logs of firewood. Then this thought occurred to those matted-hair ascetics: “Without a doubt, it must be the psychic power and might of the great ascetic, by which we are unable to split the logs of firewood.” Then the Blessed One said to the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa: “Kassapa, let the logs of firewood be split.” “Great ascetic, let them be split.” At once, the five hundred logs of firewood split. Then this thought occurred to the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa: “Indeed, the great ascetic is of great psychic power and great might, in that he can even cause the logs of firewood to be split; however, he is not an Arahant like I am.”

47. Tena kho pana samayena te jaṭilā aggiṃ paricaritukāmā na sakkonti aggiṃ ujjaletuṃ jāletuṃ (sī.), ujjalituṃ (ka.). Atha kho tesaṃ jaṭilānaṃ etadahosi – “nissaṃsayaṃ kho mahāsamaṇassa iddhānubhāvo, yathā mayaṃ na sakkoma aggiṃ [T 1.0058] ujjaletu”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – “ujjaliyantu, kassapa, aggī”ti. “Ujjaliyantu, mahāsamaṇā”ti. Sakideva pañca aggisatāni ujjaliyiṃsu. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma aggīpi ujjaliyissanti, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti.

47. At that time, those matted-hair ascetics, wishing to tend the fire, were unable to kindle the fires. Then this thought occurred to those matted-hair ascetics: “Without a doubt, it must be the psychic power and might of the great ascetic, by which we are unable to kindle the fires.” Then the Blessed One said to the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa: “Kassapa, let the fires be kindled.” “Great ascetic, let them be kindled.” At once, the five hundred fires blazed up. Then this thought occurred to the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa: “Indeed, the great ascetic is of great psychic power and great might, in that he can even cause the fires to blaze up; however, he is not an Arahant like I am.”

48. Tena kho pana samayena te jaṭilā aggiṃ paricaritvā na sakkonti aggiṃ vijjhāpetuṃ. Atha kho tesaṃ jaṭilānaṃ etadahosi – “nissaṃsayaṃ kho mahāsamaṇassa iddhānubhāvo, yathā mayaṃ na sakkoma aggiṃ vijjhāpetu”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca [M 0.0041] – “vijjhāyantu, kassapa, aggī”ti. “Vijjhāyantu, mahāsamaṇā”ti. Sakideva pañca aggisatāni vijjhāyiṃsu. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma aggīpi vijjhāyissanti, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti.

48. At that time, those matted-hair ascetics, having tended the fire, were unable to extinguish the fires. Then this thought occurred to those matted-hair ascetics: “Surely, it is the great ascetic’s psychic power, by which we are unable to extinguish the fires.” Then the Blessed One said to the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa: “Let the fires be extinguished, Kassapa.” “Let them be extinguished, great ascetic.” At once, the five hundred fires were extinguished. Then this thought occurred to the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa: “The great ascetic is indeed of great psychic power and might, in that he could even cause the fires to be extinguished; yet he is not an arahant as I am.”

49. Tena kho pana samayena te jaṭilā sītāsu hemantikāsu rattīsu antaraṭṭhakāsu himapātasamaye najjā nerañjarāya ummujjantipi, nimujjantipi, ummujjananimujjanampi karonti. Atha kho bhagavā pañcamattāni mandāmukhisatāni abhinimmini, yattha te jaṭilā uttaritvā visibbesuṃ[P 1.0032]. Atha kho tesaṃ jaṭilānaṃ etadahosi – “nissaṃsayaṃ kho [T 1.0059] mahāsamaṇassa iddhānubhāvo, yathayimā mandāmukhiyo nimmitā”ti. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma tāva bahū mandāmukhiyopi abhinimminissati, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti.

49. At that time, on cold winter nights during the eight-day interval, at a time of snowfall, those matted-hair ascetics would emerge from and plunge into the Nerañjarā River, and they would perform immersions and submersions. Then the Blessed One manifested five hundred braziers, where those matted-hair ascetics, having come out of the water, warmed themselves. Then this thought occurred to those matted-hair ascetics: “Surely, it is the great ascetic’s psychic power, by which these braziers were created.” Then this thought occurred to the matted-hair ascetic Uruvelakassapa: “The great ascetic is indeed of great psychic power and might, in that he could manifest so many braziers; yet he is not an arahant as I am.”

50. Tena [V 0.0037] kho pana samayena mahā akālamegho pāvassi, mahā udakavāhako sañjāyi. Yasmiṃ padese bhagavā viharati, so padeso udakena na otthaṭo udakena otthaṭo (sī. syā.) hoti. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ samantā udakaṃ ussāretvā majjhe reṇuhatāya bhūmiyā caṅkameyya”nti. Atha kho bhagavā samantā udakaṃ ussāretvā majjhe reṇuhatāya bhūmiyā caṅkami. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo – māheva kho mahāsamaṇo udakena vūḷho ahosīti nāvāya sambahulehi jaṭilehi saddhiṃ yasmiṃ padese bhagavā viharati taṃ padesaṃ agamāsi.
