Addasā kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ samantā udakaṃ ussāretvā majjhe reṇuhatāya bhūmiyā caṅkamantaṃ, disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idaṃ nu tvaṃ, mahāsamaṇā”ti? “Ayamahamasmi āma ahamasmi (syā.), kassapā”ti bhagavā vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā nāvāya paccuṭṭhāsi. Atha kho uruvelakassapassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, yatra hi nāma udakampi na pavāhissati nappasahissati (sī.), na [T 1.0060] tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha”nti.

50. Now at that time, a great untimely rain poured down, and a great flood arose. The place where the Blessed One was staying was not submerged by the water. Then it occurred to the Blessed One: “What if I were to push back the water all around and walk back and forth in the middle on the dusty ground?” Then the Blessed One pushed back the water all around and walked back and forth in the middle on the dusty ground. Then Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic, thinking, “Lest the great ascetic has been swept away by the water!” went by boat with many matted-hair ascetics to the place where the Blessed One was staying. Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic saw the Blessed One, having pushed back the water all around, walking back and forth in the middle on the dusty ground. Having seen him, he said to the Blessed One: “Great Ascetic, is this you?” “It is I, Kassapa,” the Blessed One replied, and rising into the air, he stood upon the boat. Then it occurred to Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic: “The great ascetic is indeed of great psychic power and great might, in that even the water could not sweep him away. But he is not an Arahant like I am.”

51. Atha [M 0.0042] kho bhagavato etadahosi – “cirampi kho imassa moghapurisassa evaṃ bhavissati – ‘mahiddhiko kho mahāsamaṇo mahānubhāvo, na tveva ca kho arahā yathā aha’nti; yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ jaṭilaṃ saṃvejeyya”nti. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelakassapaṃ jaṭilaṃ etadavoca – “neva ca kho tvaṃ, kassapa, arahā, nāpi arahattamaggasamāpanno. Sāpi te paṭipadā natthi, yāya tvaṃ arahā vā assasi, arahattamaggaṃ vā samāpanno”ti. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada”nti. Tvaṃ khosi, kassapa, pañcannaṃ jaṭilasatānaṃ nāyako vināyako aggo pamukho pāmokkho. Tepi tāva apalokehi, yathā te maññissanti tathā te karissantīti. Atha kho uruvelakassapo jaṭilo yena te jaṭilā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā te jaṭile etadavoca – “icchāmahaṃ[P 1.0033], bho, mahāsamaṇe brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ, yathā bhavanto maññanti tathā karontū”ti. “Cirapaṭikā mayaṃ, bho, mahāsamaṇe abhippasannā, sace bhavaṃ, mahāsamaṇe brahmacariyaṃ carissati, sabbeva mayaṃ mahāsamaṇe brahmacariyaṃ carissāmā”ti. Atha kho te jaṭilā kesamissaṃ jaṭāmissaṃ khārikājamissaṃ aggihutamissaṃ udake pavāhetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “labheyyāma [T 1.0061] mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyāma upasampada”nti. “Etha bhikkhavo”ti bhagavā avoca – “svākkhāto dhammo, caratha brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Sāva tesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ upasampadā ahosi.

51. Then this reflection arose in the Blessed One: “For a long time this worthless man will think thus: ‘The great ascetic is of great psychic power and great might, but he is not an Arahant like I am.’ What if I were to stir this matted-hair ascetic?” Then the Blessed One said this to Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic: “You, Kassapa, are not an Arahant, nor have you entered upon the path to Arahantship. Nor do you have that practice by which you might be an Arahant or might enter upon the path to Arahantship.” Then Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic, having bowed with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, may I receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence, may I receive the higher ordination.” “You, Kassapa, are the leader, guide, chief, foremost, and principal of five hundred matted-hair ascetics. First, inform them; they will do as they think fit.” Then Uruvela Kassapa the matted-hair ascetic went to those matted-hair ascetics and, having approached, said this to them: “Sirs, I wish to lead the holy life under the great ascetic. Do as you think fit.” “Sir, for a long time we have had great faith in the great ascetic. If you, Sir, will lead the holy life under the great ascetic, we will all lead the holy life under the great ascetic.” Then those matted-hair ascetics, having cast their hair, matted locks, carrying poles, and fire-sacrifice implements into the water, went to the Blessed One. Having approached and bowed with their heads at the Blessed One’s feet, they said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, may we receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence, may we receive the higher ordination.” The Blessed One said: “Come, monks. The Dhamma is well-proclaimed. Practice the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.” That itself was the higher ordination of those venerable ones.

52. Addasā [V 0.0038] kho nadīkassapo jaṭilo kesamissaṃ jaṭāmissaṃ khārikājamissaṃ aggihutamissaṃ udake vuyhamāne, disvānassa etadahosi – “māheva me bhātuno upasaggo ahosī”ti. Jaṭile pāhesi – gacchatha me bhātaraṃ jānāthāti. Sāmañca tīhi jaṭilasatehi saddhiṃ yenāyasmā uruvelakassapo tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ uruvelakassapaṃ etadavoca – “idaṃ nu kho, kassapa, seyyo”ti? “Āmāvuso, idaṃ seyyo”ti. Atha kho te jaṭilā kesamissaṃ jaṭāmissaṃ khārikājamissaṃ aggihutamissaṃ udake pavāhetvā yena bhagavā [M 0.0043] tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyāma upasampada”nti. “Etha bhikkhavo”ti bhagavā avoca – “svākkhāto dhammo, caratha brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Sāva tesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ upasampadā ahosi.

52. The matted-hair ascetic Nadīkassapa saw the hair, matted locks, carrying poles, and fire-sacrifice implements being carried along in the water. Having seen this, it occurred to him: “May no danger have befallen my brother!” He sent the matted-hair ascetics, saying: “Go and find out about my brother.” He himself, together with three hundred matted-hair ascetics, went to where the Venerable Uruvelakassapa was. Having approached, he said this to the Venerable Uruvelakassapa: “Kassapa, is this way of life truly better?” “Yes, friend, this way of life is better.” Then those matted-hair ascetics, having cast their hair, matted locks, carrying poles, and fire-sacrifice implements into the water, went to where the Blessed One was. Having approached, they bowed with their heads at the Blessed One’s feet and said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, may we receive the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One; may we receive the higher ordination.” “Come, monks,” the Blessed One said, “the Dhamma is well-proclaimed. Practice the holy life rightly for the complete ending of suffering.” That itself was the higher ordination for those venerable ones.

53. Addasā kho gayākassapo jaṭilo kesamissaṃ jaṭāmissaṃ khārikājamissaṃ aggihutamissaṃ udake vuyhamāne, disvānassa etadahosi – “māheva me bhātūnaṃ upasaggo ahosī”ti. Jaṭile pāhesi [T 1.0062] – gacchatha me bhātaro jānāthāti. Sāmañca dvīhi jaṭilasatehi saddhiṃ yenāyasmā uruvelakassapo tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ uruvelakassapaṃ etadavoca – “idaṃ nu kho, kassapa, seyyo”ti? “Āmāvuso, idaṃ seyyo”ti. Atha kho te jaṭilā kesamissaṃ jaṭāmissaṃ khārikājamissaṃ aggihutamissaṃ udake pavāhetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato pādesu [P 1.0034] sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyāma upasampada”nti. “Etha bhikkhavo”ti bhagavā avoca – “svākkhāto dhammo, caratha brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Sāva tesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ upasampadā ahosi.

53. The matted-hair ascetic Gayākassapa saw the ascetics' paraphernalia—their hair, matted locks, carrying poles for requisites, and fire ladles—being carried away in the water. Having seen this, this thought occurred to him: 'May no danger have befallen my brothers!' He sent the matted-hair ascetics, saying: 'Go and find out about my brothers.' And he himself, together with two hundred matted-hair ascetics, approached the Venerable Uruvelakassapa. Having approached, he said this to the Venerable Uruvelakassapa: 'Kassapa, is this way of life indeed better?' 'Yes, friend, this way of life is better.' Then those matted-hair ascetics, having set adrift in the water their paraphernalia—their hair, matted locks, carrying poles for requisites, and fire ladles—approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they fell with their heads at the Blessed One's feet and said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, may we receive the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One; may we receive the higher ordination.' The Blessed One said: 'Come, monks. The Dhamma is well-proclaimed. Practice the holy life rightly for the complete ending of suffering.' That itself was the higher ordination for those venerable ones.

Bhagavato adhiṭṭhānena pañca kaṭṭhasatāni na phāliyiṃsu, phāliyiṃsu; aggī na ujjaliyiṃsu, ujjaliyiṃsu; na vijjhāyiṃsu, vijjhāyiṃsu; pañcamandāmukhisatāni abhinimmini. Etena nayena aḍḍhuḍḍhapāṭihāriyasahassāni honti.

By the Blessed One's determination, five hundred logs of wood could not be split, and then they were split; fires could not be lit, and then they were lit; they could not be extinguished, and then they were extinguished; he created five hundred fire-braziers. In this way, there were three thousand five hundred miracles.

54. Atha kho bhagavā uruvelāyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena gayāsīsaṃ tena pakkāmi mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ bhikkhusahassena sabbeheva purāṇajaṭilehi. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā gayāyaṃ viharati gayāsīse saddhiṃ bhikkhusahassena. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi –

54. Then the Blessed One, having dwelt in Uruvelā for as long as he was pleased, departed for Gayāsīsa together with a great Saṅgha of a thousand bhikkhus, all of whom were formerly matted-hair ascetics. There, near Gayā, the Blessed One dwelt at Gayāsīsa together with a thousand bhikkhus. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus:

saṃ. ni. 4.29 “Sabbaṃ[M 0.0044][V 0.0039], bhikkhave, ādittaṃ. Kiñca, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ ādittaṃ? Cakkhu [T 1.0063] ādittaṃ, rūpā ādittā, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ ādittaṃ, cakkhusamphasso āditto, yamidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi ādittaṃ. Kena ādittaṃ? Rāgagginā dosagginā mohagginā ādittaṃ, jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi ādittanti vadāmi. Sotaṃ ādittaṃ, saddā ādittā, sotaviññāṇaṃ ādittaṃ, sotasamphasso āditto, yamidaṃ sotasamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi ādittaṃ. Kena ādittaṃ? Rāgagginā dosagginā mohagginā ādittaṃ, jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi ādittanti vadāmi. Ghānaṃ ādittaṃ, gandhā ādittā, ghānaviññāṇaṃ ādittaṃ, ghānasamphasso āditto, yamidaṃ ghānasamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi ādittaṃ. Kena ādittaṃ? Rāgagginā dosagginā mohagginā ādittaṃ, jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi ādittanti vadāmi. Jivhā ādittā, rasā ādittā, jivhāviññāṇaṃ ādittaṃ jivhāsamphasso āditto, yamidaṃ jivhāsamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi ādittaṃ. Kena ādittaṃ? Rāgagginā dosagginā mohagginā ādittaṃ, jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi ādittanti vadāmi. Kāyo āditto, phoṭṭhabbā ādittā, kāyaviññāṇaṃ ādittaṃ kāyasamphasso āditto, yamidaṃ kāyasamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi ādittaṃ. Kena ādittaṃ? Rāgagginā dosagginā mohagginā ādittaṃ, jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi ādittanti vadāmi. Mano āditto, dhammā ādittā, manoviññāṇaṃ ādittaṃ manosamphasso āditto, yamidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tampi ādittaṃ. Kena ādittaṃ? Rāgagginā dosagginā mohagginā ādittaṃ, jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi ādittanti vadāmi.

“Monks, all is burning. And what, monks, is all that is burning? The eye is burning, forms are burning, eye-consciousness is burning, eye-contact is burning, and whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is burning. With what is it burning? It is burning with the fire of lust, with the fire of hatred, with the fire of delusion; it is burning with birth, aging, and death; with sorrows, lamentations, pains, griefs, and despairs, I say. The ear is burning, sounds are burning, ear-consciousness is burning, ear-contact is burning... and whatever feeling arises dependent on ear-contact... that too is burning... I say. The nose is burning, odors are burning... I say. The tongue is burning, flavors are burning... I say. The body is burning, tangibles are burning... I say. The mind is burning, mental objects are burning, mind-consciousness is burning, mind-contact is burning, and whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is burning. With what is it burning? It is burning with the fire of lust, with the fire of hatred, with the fire of delusion; it is burning with birth, aging, and death; with sorrows, lamentations, pains, griefs, and despairs, I say.”

“Evaṃ [M 0.0045] passaṃ, bhikkhave, sutavā ariyasāvako cakkhusmimpi nibbindati, rūpesupi nibbindati, cakkhuviññāṇepi nibbindati, cakkhusamphassepi nibbindati, yamidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, tasmimpi nibbindati. Sotasmimpi [T 1.0064] nibbindati, saddesupi nibbindati…pe… ghānasmimpi nibbindati[P 1.0035][V 0.0040], gandhesupi nibbindati…pe… jivhāyapi nibbindati, rasesupi nibbindati…pe… kāyasmimpi nibbindati, phoṭṭhabbesupi nibbindati…pe… manasmimpi nibbindati, dhammesupi nibbindati, manoviññāṇepi nibbindati, manosamphassepi nibbindati, yamidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā tasmimpi nibbindati, nibbindaṃ virajjati, virāgā vimuccati, vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānātī”ti.

“Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple becomes disenchanted with the eye, disenchanted with forms, disenchanted with eye-consciousness, disenchanted with eye-contact, and disenchanted with whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant. They become disenchanted with the ear, disenchanted with sounds… and so on… disenchanted with the nose, disenchanted with odors… and so on… disenchanted with the tongue, disenchanted with tastes… and so on… disenchanted with the body, disenchanted with tangibles… and so on… disenchanted with the mind, disenchanted with mental phenomena, disenchanted with mind-consciousness, disenchanted with mind-contact, and disenchanted with whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant. Being disenchanted, they become dispassionate. Through dispassion, they are liberated. When liberated, the knowledge arises, ‘Liberated.’ They understand: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.’”

Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne tassa bhikkhusahassassa anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṃsu.

And while this exposition was being delivered, the minds of those thousand bhikkhus were liberated from the taints through non-clinging.

Ādittapariyāyasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Fire Sermon is concluded.

Uruvelapāṭihāriyaṃ tatiyabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The Third Recitation Section, on the Miracle at Uruvelā, is concluded.

13. Bimbisārasamāgamakathā

13. The Account of the Meeting with Bimbisāra

55. Atha kho bhagavā gayāsīse yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena rājagahaṃ tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi, mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ bhikkhusahassena sabbeheva purāṇajaṭilehi. Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena rājagahaṃ tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati laṭṭhivane laṭṭhivanuyyāne (syā.) suppatiṭṭhe cetiye. Assosi kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro – samaṇo khalu [T 1.0065] bho gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito rājagahaṃ anuppatto rājagahe viharati laṭṭhivane suppatiṭṭhe cetiye. Taṃ kho pana bhagavantaṃ bhavantaṃ (ka.) gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā bhagavāti (ka.). So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ [M 0.0046] sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti. So dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti. Sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ hotīti.

55. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Gayāsīsa as long as he pleased, set out on a journey toward Rājagaha with a great assembly of bhikkhus, with the thousand bhikkhus who had all formerly been matted-hair ascetics. Then the Blessed One, journeying by stages, arrived at Rājagaha. There the Blessed One stayed in Rājagaha, in the Laṭṭhivana grove, at the Suppatiṭṭha shrine. King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha heard: “The ascetic Gotama, the Sakyan son who went forth from the Sakyan clan, has arrived at Rājagaha and is staying in the Laṭṭhivana grove, at the Suppatiṭṭha shrine. And of that Blessed One Gotama, this good report of his fame has spread: ‘That Blessed One is an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone, Knower of the World, an unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, Teacher of gods and humans, the Enlightened One, the Blessed One.’ He makes known this world—with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, this generation with its recluses and brahmins, its devas and humans—having realized it himself with direct knowledge. He teaches the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and its phrasing; he reveals a holy life that is entirely complete and perfectly pure. It is indeed good to see such Arahants.”

Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro dvādasanahutehi dvādasaniyutehi (yojanā) māgadhikehi brāhmaṇagahapatikehi [V 0.0041] parivuto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Tepi kho dvādasanahutā māgadhikā brāhmaṇagahapatikā [P 1.0036] appekacce bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu, appekacce bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu, appekacce yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu, appekacce bhagavato santike nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu, appekacce tuṇhībhūtā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Atha kho tesaṃ dvādasanahutānaṃ dvādasaniyutānaṃ (yojanā) māgadhikānaṃ [T 1.0066] brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ etadahosi – “kiṃ nu kho mahāsamaṇo uruvelakassape brahmacariyaṃ carati, udāhu uruvelakassapo mahāsamaṇe brahmacariyaṃ caratī”ti? Atha kho bhagavā tesaṃ dvādasanahutānaṃ māgadhikānaṃ brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya āyasmantaṃ uruvelakassapaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, surrounded by twelve myriads of Magadhan brahmins and householders, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Those twelve myriads of Magadhan brahmins and householders also—some paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side; some exchanged courteous pleasantries with the Blessed One and, after concluding their memorable and friendly conversation, sat down to one side; some, facing the Blessed One, raised their joined hands in salutation and sat down to one side; some announced their name and lineage in the presence of the Blessed One and sat down to one side; while some remained silent and sat down to one side. Then this thought occurred to those twelve myriads of Magadhan brahmins and householders: “Does the great ascetic practice the holy life under Uruvelakassapa, or does Uruvelakassapa practice the holy life under the great ascetic?” Then the Blessed One, having known with his own mind the thought in the minds of those twelve myriads of Magadhan brahmins and householders, addressed the Venerable Uruvelakassapa in verse:

“Kimeva disvā uruvelavāsi, pahāsi aggiṃ kisakovadāno;

Pucchāmi taṃ kassapa, etamatthaṃ kathaṃ pahīnaṃ tava aggihuttanti.

“Seeing what, O dweller of Uruvelā, you who instruct emaciated ascetics, did you abandon the fire? I ask you, Kassapa, about this matter: how was your fire-offering abandoned?”

“Rūpe ca sadde ca atho rase ca;

Kāmitthiyo cābhivadanti yaññā;

Etaṃ malanti upadhīsu ñatvā;

Tasmā na yiṭṭhe na hute arañjinti.

“Sacrifices proclaim sights, sounds, and also tastes, and desirable women. Having understood this to be a defilement in the substrata of existence, I therefore found no delight in great sacrifice or in small offering.”

“Ettheva te mano na ramittha (kassapāti bhagavā);

Rūpesu saddesu atho rasesu;

Atha ko carahi devamanussaloke;

Rato mano kassapa, brūhi metanti.

“If your mind, Kassapa, found no delight in these things—in sights, in sounds, and also in tastes—then in what, pray, in this world of devas and humans does your mind delight? Tell me this, Kassapa.”

“Disvā [T 1.0067][M 0.0047] padaṃ santamanūpadhīkaṃ;

Akiñcanaṃ kāmabhave asattaṃ;

Anaññathābhāvimanaññaneyyaṃ;

Tasmā na yiṭṭhe na hute arañji”nti.

“Having seen the peaceful state, free from substrata, without impediments, unattached in the realm of sensual existence, not subject to becoming otherwise, and not attainable by other means; therefore, I found no delight in great sacrifice or in small offering.”

56. Atha kho āyasmā uruvelakassapo uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhagavato [V 0.0042] pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “satthā me, bhante, bhagavā, sāvakohamasmi; satthā me, bhante, bhagavā, sāvakohamasmī”ti. Atha kho tesaṃ dvādasanahutānaṃ māgadhikānaṃ brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ etadahosi – “uruvelakassapo mahāsamaṇe brahmacariyaṃ caratī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā tesaṃ dvādasanahutānaṃ māgadhikānaṃ brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ cetasā [P 1.0037] cetoparivitakkamaññāya anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā te bhagavā aññāsi kallacitte muducitte vinīvaraṇacitte udaggacitte pasannacitte, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā, taṃ pakāsesi – dukkhaṃ, samudayaṃ, nirodhaṃ, maggaṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva ekādasanahutānaṃ māgadhikānaṃ brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ bimbisārappamukhānaṃ tasmiṃ yeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti. Ekanahutaṃ upāsakattaṃ [T 1.0068] paṭivedesi.

56. Then the Venerable Uruvelakassapa rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, bowed down with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, and said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the Blessed One is my teacher; I am a disciple. Venerable sir, the Blessed One is my teacher; I am a disciple.” Then this thought occurred to those twelve myriads of Magadhan brahmins and householders: “Uruvelakassapa is living the holy life under the great ascetic.” Then the Blessed One, having known with his own mind the thought in the minds of those twelve myriads of Magadhan brahmins and householders, gave a progressive talk, that is to say: he gave a talk on giving, a talk on virtue, and a talk on heaven; he explained the danger, degradation, and defilement of sensual pleasures, and the benefit in renunciation. When the Blessed One knew them to have ready minds, pliable minds, minds free from the hindrances, uplifted minds, and serene minds, he then revealed that Dhamma teaching which is the special discovery of the Buddhas: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth free from black marks would properly take up dye, even so, for the eleven myriads of Magadhan brahmins and householders headed by Bimbisāra, right on that very seat, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose: “Whatever is of the nature to arise, all that is of the nature to cease.” One myriad declared themselves to be lay followers.

57. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro diṭṭhadhammo pattadhammo viditadhammo pariyogāḷhadhammo tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṃkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “pubbe me, bhante, kumārassa sato pañca assāsakā ahesuṃ, te me etarahi samiddhā. Pubbe me, bhante, kumārassa sato etadahosi – ‘aho vata maṃ rajje abhisiñceyyu’nti, ayaṃ kho me, bhante, paṭhamo assāsako ahosi, so me etarahi samiddho. ‘Tassa ca me vijitaṃ arahaṃ sammāsambuddho okkameyyā’ti, ayaṃ kho me, bhante, dutiyo assāsako ahosi, so me etarahi samiddho. ‘Tañcāhaṃ bhagavantaṃ payirupāseyya’nti, ayaṃ kho me, bhante, tatiyo [M 0.0048] assāsako ahosi, so me etarahi samiddho. ‘So ca me bhagavā dhammaṃ deseyyā’ti, ayaṃ kho me, bhante, catuttho assāsako ahosi, so me etarahi samiddho. ‘Tassa cāhaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ ājāneyya’nti, ayaṃ kho me, bhante, pañcamo assāsako ahosi, so me etarahi samiddho. Pubbe me, bhante, kumārassa sato ime pañca assāsakā ahesuṃ, te me etarahi samiddhā. Abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante, seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya cakkhumanto [T 1.0069] rūpāni dakkhantīti – evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, dhammañca, bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ maṃ bhante (ka.), bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gataṃ, adhivāsetu ca me, bhante, bhagavā[P 1.0038], svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti[V 0.0043]. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro tassā rattiyā accayena paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – “kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti.

57. Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, who had seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, plunged into the Dhamma, crossed over doubt, got rid of perplexity, gained confidence, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s dispensation, addressed the Blessed One thus: “In the past, venerable sir, when I was a prince, I had five aspirations, which have now been fulfilled. In the past, venerable sir, when I was a prince, I thought: ‘Oh, may they anoint me as king!’ This was my first aspiration, which has now been fulfilled. ‘And may an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, come to my kingdom!’ This was my second aspiration, which has now been fulfilled. ‘And may I attend upon that Blessed One!’ This was my third aspiration, which has now been fulfilled. ‘And may that Blessed One teach me the Dhamma!’ This was my fourth aspiration, which has now been fulfilled. ‘And may I understand the Dhamma of the Blessed One!’ This was my fifth aspiration, which has now been fulfilled. In the past, venerable sir, when I was a prince, I had these five aspirations, which have now all been fulfilled. Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as one might set upright what had been overturned, reveal what was hidden, show the way to one who was lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms—so too has the Blessed One made the Dhamma clear in many ways. I go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward for life. And may the Blessed One accept my meal for tomorrow together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.” The Blessed One consented by silence. Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, understanding the Blessed One’s consent, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, and departed. Then, when the night had passed, King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha had fine hard and soft food prepared and had the time announced to the Blessed One: “It is time, venerable sir, the meal is ready.”

58. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṃ pāvisi mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ bhikkhusahassena sabbeheva purāṇajaṭilehi. Tena kho pana samayena sakko devānamindo māṇavakavaṇṇaṃ abhinimminitvā buddhappamukhassa bhikkhusaṅghassa purato purato gacchati imā gāthāyo gāyamāno –

58. Then the Blessed One, in the morning, having dressed, taking his bowl and robe, entered Rājagaha together with a great Saṅgha of bhikkhus, with a thousand bhikkhus, all of whom were formerly matted-hair ascetics. At that time Sakka, the lord of the devas, having created the appearance of a young man, was walking in front of the Saṅgha of bhikkhus with the Buddha at its head, singing these verses:

“Danto dantehi saha purāṇajaṭilehi, vippamutto vippamuttehi;

Siṅgīnikkhasavaṇṇo, rājagahaṃ pāvisi bhagavā.

“Tamed, with the tamed former matted-hair ascetics; freed, with the freed; the Blessed One, with a complexion like refined gold, entered Rājagaha.

“Mutto [T 1.0070] muttehi saha purāṇajaṭilehi, vippamutto vippamuttehi;

Siṅgīnikkhasavaṇṇo, rājagahaṃ pāvisi bhagavā.

“Released, with the released former matted-hair ascetics; freed, with the freed; the Blessed One, with a complexion like refined gold, entered Rājagaha.

“Tiṇṇo [M 0.0049] tiṇṇehi saha purāṇajaṭilehi;

Vippamutto vippamuttehi;

Siṅgīnikkhasuvaṇṇo;

Rājagahaṃ pāvisi bhagavā.

“Crossed over, with the crossed-over former matted-hair ascetics; freed, with the freed; the Blessed One, with a complexion like refined gold, entered Rājagaha.

“Santo santehi saha purāṇajaṭilehi;

Vippamutto vippamuttehi;

Siṅgīnikkhasavaṇṇo;

Rājagahaṃ pāvisi bhagavā.

“Tranquil, with the tranquil former matted-hair ascetics; freed, with the freed; the Blessed One, with a complexion like refined gold, entered Rājagaha.

“Dasavāso dasabalo, dasadhammavidū dasabhi cupeto;

So dasasataparivāro parivārako (ka.) rājagahaṃ, pāvisi bhagavā”ti.

“Possessing the ten abidings, the ten powers, knower of the ten dhammas, and endowed with the ten factors; that Blessed One, with a retinue of a thousand, entered Rājagaha.”

Manussā [V 0.0044] sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ passitvā evamāhaṃsu – “abhirūpo vatāyaṃ māṇavako, dassanīyo vatāyaṃ māṇavako, pāsādiko vatāyaṃ māṇavako. Kassa nu kho ayaṃ māṇavako”ti? Evaṃ vutte sakko devānamindo te manusse gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

Seeing Sakka, the lord of the devas, the people said thus: “Indeed, this young man is exceedingly handsome! Indeed, this young man is lovely to see! Indeed, this young man is graciously inspiring! Whose attendant, I wonder, is this young man?” When this was said, Sakka, the lord of the devas, addressed those people with a verse:

“Yo dhīro sabbadhi danto, suddho appaṭipuggalo;

Arahaṃ sugato loke, tassāhaṃ paricārako”ti.

“He who in the world is steadfast, tamed in all respects, pure, and without an equal; the Arahant, the Sugata—I am His attendant.”

59. Atha kho bhagavā yena rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane [T 1.0071] nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnassa [P 1.0039] kho rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa etadahosi cūḷava. 307 – “kattha nu kho bhagavā vihareyya? Yaṃ assa gāmato neva avidūre na accāsanne, gamanāgamanasampannaṃ, atthikānaṃ atthikānaṃ manussānaṃ abhikkamanīyaṃ, divā appākiṇṇaṃ appakiṇṇaṃ (sī. syā.), abbhokiṇṇaṃ (ka.), rattiṃ appasaddaṃ appanigghosaṃ vijanavātaṃ, manussarāhasseyyakaṃ, paṭisallānasāruppa”nti. Atha kho rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa etadahosi – “idaṃ kho amhākaṃ veḷuvanaṃ uyyānaṃ gāmato neva avidūre na accāsanne gamanāgamanasampannaṃ [M 0.0050] atthikānaṃ atthikānaṃ manussānaṃ abhikkamanīyaṃ divā appākiṇṇaṃ rattiṃ appasaddaṃ appanigghosaṃ vijanavātaṃ manussarāhasseyyakaṃ paṭisallānasāruppaṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ veḷuvanaṃ uyyānaṃ buddhappamukhassa bhikkhusaṅghassa dadeyya”nti. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro sovaṇṇamayaṃ bhiṅkāraṃ gahetvā bhagavato oṇojesi – “etāhaṃ, bhante, veḷuvanaṃ uyyānaṃ buddhappamukhassa bhikkhusaṅghassa dammī”ti. Paṭiggahesi bhagavā ārāmaṃ. Atha [T 1.0072] kho bhagavā rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ seniyaṃ bimbisāraṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ārāma”nti.

59. Then the Blessed One went to the residence of King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the community of monks. Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha personally served and satisfied the community of monks headed by the Buddha with choice hard and soft food. When the Blessed One had finished eating and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, the king sat down to one side. As he sat there, this thought arose to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha: “Where might the Blessed One dwell? A dwelling that is neither too far from a village nor too near, accessible for coming and going, easy to approach for people who have need of him, not crowded by day, with little sound and no clamor at night, secluded from people, suitable for private matters, and fitting for solitude.” Then this thought arose to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha: “This Bamboo Grove park of ours is neither too far from a village nor too near, is accessible for coming and going, easy to approach for people who have need of him, not crowded by day, with little sound and no clamor at night, secluded from people, suitable for private matters, and fitting for solitude. It would be good if I were to give the Bamboo Grove park to the community of monks headed by the Buddha.” Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha took a golden water vessel and dedicated it to the Blessed One, saying: “Venerable sir, I give this Bamboo Grove park to the community of monks headed by the Buddha.” The Blessed One accepted the park. Then the Blessed One, having instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha with a Dhamma talk, rose from his seat and departed. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this matter, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow a park.”

Bimbisārasamāgamakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Meeting with Bimbisāra is concluded.

14. Sāriputtamoggallānapabbajjākathā

14. The Account of the Going Forth of Sāriputta and Moggallāna

60. Tena [V 0.0045] kho pana samayena sañcayo sañjayo (sī. syā.) paribbājako rājagahe paṭivasati mahatiyā paribbājakaparisāya saddhiṃ aḍḍhateyyehi paribbājakasatehi. Tena kho pana samayena sāriputtamoggallānā sañcaye paribbājake brahmacariyaṃ caranti. Tehi katikā katā hoti – yo paṭhamaṃ amataṃ adhigacchati, so itarassa ārocetūti. Atha kho āyasmā assaji pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi pāsādikena abhikkantena paṭikkantena ālokitena vilokitena samiñjitena pasāritena, okkhittacakkhu iriyāpathasampanno. Addasā kho sāriputto paribbājako āyasmantaṃ assajiṃ rājagahe piṇḍāya carantaṃ pāsādikena abhikkantena paṭikkantena ālokitena vilokitena samiñjitena pasāritena okkhittacakkhuṃ iriyāpathasampannaṃ. Disvānassa etadahosi – “ye vata loke arahanto vā arahattamaggaṃ vā samāpannā, ayaṃ tesaṃ bhikkhu aññataro. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ [P 1.0040] imaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā [M 0.0051] puccheyyaṃ – ‘kaṃsi tvaṃ, āvuso, uddissa pabbajito, ko vā te satthā, kassa vā tvaṃ dhammaṃ rocesī’”ti? Atha [T 1.0073] kho sāriputtassa paribbājakassa etadahosi – “akālo kho imaṃ bhikkhuṃ pucchituṃ, antaragharaṃ paviṭṭho piṇḍāya carati. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ bhikkhuṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandheyyaṃ, atthikehi upaññātaṃ magga”nti. Atha kho āyasmā assaji rājagahe piṇḍāya caritvā piṇḍapātaṃ ādāya paṭikkami. Atha kho sāriputtopi paribbājako yenāyasmā assaji tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā assajinā saddhiṃ sammodi, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho sāriputto paribbājako āyasmantaṃ assajiṃ etadavoca – “vippasannāni kho te, āvuso, indriyāni, parisuddho chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto. Kaṃsi tvaṃ, āvuso, uddissa pabbajito, ko vā te satthā, kassa vā tvaṃ dhammaṃ rocesī”ti? “Atthāvuso, mahāsamaṇo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito, tāhaṃ bhagavantaṃ uddissa pabbajito, so ca me bhagavā satthā, tassa cāhaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ rocemī”ti. “Kiṃvādī panāyasmato satthā, kimakkhāyī”ti? “Ahaṃ kho, āvuso, navo acirapabbajito, adhunāgato imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ, na tāhaṃ sakkomi vitthārena dhammaṃ desetuṃ, api ca te saṃkhittena atthaṃ vakkhāmī”ti. Atha kho sāriputto paribbājako āyasmantaṃ assajiṃ etadavoca – “hotu, āvuso –

60. At that time, the wanderer Sañcaya was residing in Rājagaha with a large assembly of two hundred and fifty wanderers. At that time, Sāriputta and Moggallāna were practicing the holy life under the wanderer Sañcaya. They had made an agreement: whoever first attains the Deathless should inform the other. Then, in the morning, the Venerable Assaji dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Rājagaha for alms. His demeanor was graceful—moving forward and back, looking ahead and around, bending and stretching, with downcast eyes and composed in every action. The wanderer Sāriputta saw the Venerable Assaji going for alms in Rājagaha, his demeanor graceful in every way. On seeing him, this thought arose in him: “Surely, this monk is one of those in the world who are arahants or have entered the path to arahantship. What if I were to approach this monk and ask: ‘Under whom, friend, have you gone forth? Who is your teacher? Whose Dhamma do you profess?’” Then this thought arose to the wanderer Sāriputta: “This is not the right time to question this monk, as he has entered among the houses for alms. What if I were to follow this monk from behind? The path is known to those who seek it.” After the Venerable Assaji had walked for alms in Rājagaha and was returning with his almsfood, the wanderer Sāriputta approached him. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Venerable Assaji, and after courteous and memorable conversation, he stood to one side. Standing there, the wanderer Sāriputta said to the Venerable Assaji: “Your faculties, friend, are serene; your complexion is pure and bright. Under whom have you gone forth? Who is your teacher? Whose Dhamma do you profess?” “There is, friend, a great ascetic, a son of the Sakyans, who has gone forth from the Sakyan clan. I have gone forth on account of that Blessed One. That Blessed One is my teacher, and I profess His Dhamma.” “But what is your teacher's doctrine, what does he proclaim?” “I am new, friend, not long gone forth, and have just come to this Dhamma and Discipline. I cannot teach the Dhamma in detail, but I can tell you the meaning briefly.” Then the wanderer Sāriputta said to the Venerable Assaji: “So be it, friend—”

“Appaṃ [T 1.0074] vā bahuṃ vā bhāsassu, atthaṃyeva me brūhi;

Attheneva me attho, kiṃ kāhasi byañjanaṃ bahu”nti.

“Whether it be little or much, please speak. Tell me only the meaning. I have need only of the meaning. What is the use of many words?”

Atha [V 0.0046] kho āyasmā assaji sāriputtassa paribbājakassa imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ abhāsi –

Then the Venerable Assaji spoke this Dhamma exposition to the wanderer Sāriputta:

apa. 1.1.286 therāpadānepi “Ye dhammā hetuppabhavā, tesaṃ hetuṃ tathāgato āha;

Tesañca yo nirodho, evaṃvādī mahāsamaṇo”ti.

“Of phenomena that arise from a cause, the Tathāgata has declared the cause, and also their cessation. The Great Ascetic is one who speaks thus.”

Atha kho sāriputtassa paribbājakassa imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ sutvā virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – “yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma”nti.

Then, upon hearing this Dhamma exposition, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose in the wanderer Sāriputta: ‘Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing.’”

apa. 1.1.289 therāpadānepi Eseva [M 0.0052] dhammo yadi tāvadeva, paccabyattha padamasokaṃ;

Adiṭṭhaṃ abbhatītaṃ, bahukehi kappanahutehīti.

Even if it is only this much, this is the very Dhamma. You have penetrated the sorrowless state, which we have passed by, unseen, for many myriads of aeons.

61. Atha kho sāriputto paribbājako yena moggallāno paribbājako tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho moggallāno paribbājako sāriputtaṃ paribbājakaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ, disvāna sāriputtaṃ [P 1.0041] paribbājakaṃ etadavoca – “vippasannāni kho te, āvuso, indriyāni, parisuddho chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto. Kacci nu tvaṃ, āvuso, amataṃ adhigato”ti? “Āmāvuso, amataṃ adhigato”ti. “Yathākathaṃ pana tvaṃ, āvuso, amataṃ adhigato”ti? “Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, addasaṃ assajiṃ [T 1.0075] bhikkhuṃ rājagahe piṇḍāya carantaṃ pāsādikena abhikkantena paṭikkantena ālokitena vilokitena samiñjitena pasāritena okkhittacakkhuṃ iriyāpathasampannaṃ. Disvāna me etadahosi – ‘ye vata loke arahanto vā arahattamaggaṃ vā samāpannā, ayaṃ tesaṃ bhikkhu aññataro. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā puccheyyaṃ – kaṃsi tvaṃ, āvuso uddissa pabbajito, ko vā te satthā, kassa vā tvaṃ dhammaṃ rocesī’”ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, āvuso, etadahosi – “akālo kho imaṃ bhikkhuṃ pucchituṃ antaragharaṃ paviṭṭho piṇḍāya carati, yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ bhikkhuṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandheyyaṃ atthikehi upaññātaṃ magga”nti. Atha kho, āvuso, assaji bhikkhu rājagahe piṇḍāya caritvā piṇḍapātaṃ ādāya paṭikkami. Atha khvāhaṃ, āvuso, yena assaji bhikkhu tenupasaṅkamiṃ, upasaṅkamitvā assajinā bhikkhunā saddhiṃ sammodiṃ, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsiṃ. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho ahaṃ, āvuso, assajiṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavocaṃ – “vippasannāni kho te, āvuso, indriyāni, parisuddho chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto. ‘Kaṃsi tvaṃ, āvuso, uddissa pabbajito, ko vā te satthā, kassa vā tvaṃ dhammaṃ rocesī’”ti? ‘Atthāvuso, mahāsamaṇo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito, tāhaṃ bhagavantaṃ uddissa [V 0.0047] pabbajito, so ca me bhagavā satthā, tassa cāhaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ rocemī’ti. ‘Kiṃvādī panāyasmato satthā kimakkhāyī’ti[T 1.0076]. ‘Ahaṃ kho, āvuso, navo acirapabbajito adhunāgato imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ, na tāhaṃ sakkomi vitthārena dhammaṃ desetuṃ, api ca te saṃkhittena atthaṃ vakkhāmī’”ti[M 0.0053]. Atha khvāhaṃ, āvuso, assajiṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavocaṃ – “hotu, āvuso,

61. Then the wanderer Sāriputta approached the wanderer Moggallāna. The wanderer Moggallāna saw the wanderer Sāriputta coming from afar, and having seen him, said this to the wanderer Sāriputta: “Friend, your faculties are serene, your complexion is pure and bright. Friend, have you perhaps attained the deathless?” “Yes, friend, I have attained the deathless.” “But how, friend, did you attain the deathless?” “Here in Rājagaha, friend, I saw the monk Assaji wandering for alms, inspiring confidence with his advancing and returning, his looking ahead and looking aside, his bending and stretching, with downcast eyes, possessed of graceful deportment. Having seen him, this thought occurred to me: ‘Surely, of those in the world who are Arahants or have entered the path to Arahantship, this monk is one of them. What if I were to approach this monk and ask: “Friend, on whose account have you gone forth? Who is your teacher? Whose Dhamma do you profess?”’ Then, friend, this thought occurred to me: ‘It is not the right time to question this monk; he has entered among the houses and is wandering for alms. What if I were to follow this monk from behind, the path pointed out by those who have a need for it?’ Then, friend, the monk Assaji, having wandered for alms in Rājagaha and taken his alms-food, returned. Then, friend, I approached the monk Assaji. Having approached him, I exchanged greetings with the monk Assaji. Having concluded the courteous and memorable talk, I stood to one side. Standing to one side, friend, I said this to the monk Assaji: ‘Friend, your faculties are serene, your complexion is pure and bright. Friend, on whose account have you gone forth? Who is your teacher? Whose Dhamma do you profess?’ ‘Friend, there is the great ascetic, the son of the Sakyans, who went forth from the Sakyan clan. I have gone forth on account of that Blessed One. That Blessed One is my teacher, and I profess the Dhamma of that Blessed One.’ ‘But what does the venerable one’s teacher profess? What does he proclaim?’ ‘Friend, I am a novice, recently gone forth, newly come to this Dhamma and Vinaya. I am not able to teach the Dhamma in detail, but I will tell you the meaning in brief.’ Then, friend, I said this to the monk Assaji: ‘So be it, friend,

Appaṃ vā bahuṃ vā bhāsassu, atthaṃyeva me brūhi;

Attheneva me attho, kiṃ kāhasi byañjanaṃ bahu”nti.

Whether it be little or much, please speak. Tell me only the meaning; for me, there is need only of the meaning. What is to be done with many letters?

Atha kho, āvuso, assaji bhikkhu imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ abhāsi –

Then, friend, the monk Assaji spoke this Dhamma exposition:

“Ye dhammā hetuppabhavā, tesaṃ hetuṃ tathāgato āha;

Tesañca yo nirodho, evaṃvādī mahāsamaṇo”ti.

Of phenomena that arise from a cause, the Tathāgata has declared that cause, and also their cessation. The Great Ascetic is one who speaks thus.

Atha kho moggallānassa paribbājakassa imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ [P 1.0042] sutvā virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti.

Then, upon hearing this Dhamma exposition, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose in the wanderer Moggallāna: ‘Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing.’”

Eseva dhammo yadi tāvadeva, paccabyattha padamasokaṃ;

Adiṭṭhaṃ abbhatītaṃ, bahukehi kappanahutehīti.

Even if it is only this much, this is the very Dhamma. You have penetrated the sorrowless state, which we have passed by, unseen, for many myriads of aeons.

62. Atha kho moggallāno paribbājako sāriputtaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca “gacchāma mayaṃ, āvuso, bhagavato santike, so no bhagavā satthā”ti. “Imāni kho, āvuso, aḍḍhateyyāni paribbājakasatāni amhe nissāya amhe sampassantā idha viharanti, tepi tāva apalokema apalokāma (ka). Yathā te maññissanti, tathā te karissantī”ti. Atha kho sāriputtamoggallānā yena te paribbājakā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā te [T 1.0077] paribbājake etadavocuṃ – “gacchāma mayaṃ, āvuso, bhagavato santike, so no bhagavā satthā”ti. “Mayaṃ āyasmante nissāya āyasmante sampassantā idha viharāma, sace āyasmantā mahāsamaṇe brahmacariyaṃ carissanti, sabbeva mayaṃ mahāsamaṇe brahmacariyaṃ carissāmā”ti. Atha kho sāriputtamoggallānā yena sañcayo paribbājako tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā sañcayaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavocuṃ – “gacchāma mayaṃ, āvuso, bhagavato santike, so no bhagavā satthā”ti. “Alaṃ, āvuso, mā [V 0.0048] agamittha, sabbeva tayo imaṃ gaṇaṃ pariharissāmā”ti. Dutiyampi kho…pe… tatiyampi kho sāriputtamoggallānā [M 0.0054] sañcayaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavocuṃ – “gacchāma mayaṃ, āvuso, bhagavato santike, so no bhagavā satthā”ti. “Alaṃ, āvuso, mā agamittha, sabbeva tayo imaṃ gaṇaṃ pariharissāmā”ti. Atha kho sāriputtamoggallānā tāni aḍḍhateyyāni paribbājakasatāni ādāya yena veḷuvanaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Sañcayassa pana paribbājakassa tattheva uṇhaṃ lohitaṃ mukhato uggañchi.

62. Then the wanderer Moggallāna said to the wanderer Sāriputta: “Friend, let us go to the Blessed One; the Blessed One is our teacher.” “But friend, these two hundred and fifty wanderers dwell here relying on us, looking up to us. Let us first inform them. They will act as they think fit.” Then Sāriputta and Moggallāna approached those wanderers and said: “Friends, let us go to the Blessed One; the Blessed One is our teacher.” “Venerable sirs, we dwell here relying on you, looking up to you. If the venerable ones will lead the holy life under the great ascetic, we will all lead the holy life under the great ascetic.” Then Sāriputta and Moggallāna approached the wanderer Sañjaya and said: “Friend, let us go to the Blessed One; the Blessed One is our teacher.” “Enough, friends, do not go. The three of us shall lead this group together.” A second time… and a third time Sāriputta and Moggallāna said to the wanderer Sañjaya: “Friend, let us go to the Blessed One; the Blessed One is our teacher.” “Enough, friends, do not go. The three of us shall lead this group together.” Then Sāriputta and Moggallāna, taking those two hundred and fifty wanderers, went to the Bamboo Grove. But as for the wanderer Sañjaya, hot blood gushed from his mouth right there.

Addasā kho bhagavā bhagavāte (ka) sāriputtamoggallāne dūratova āgacchante, disvāna bhikkhū āmantesi – “ete, bhikkhave, dve sahāyakā āgacchanti, kolito upatisso ca. Etaṃ me sāvakayugaṃ bhavissati aggaṃ bhaddayuga”nti.

The Blessed One indeed saw Sāriputta and Moggallāna coming from afar. Having seen them, he addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, these two companions, Kolita and Upatissa, are coming. This will be my pair of disciples, the foremost, the excellent pair.”

Gambhīre [T 1.0078] ñāṇavisaye, anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye;

Vimutte appatte veḷuvanaṃ, atha ne satthā byākāsi.

The Teacher then declared concerning them—liberated in the profound realm of wisdom, in the unexcelled exhaustion of attachments—while they had not yet reached the Bamboo Grove:

Ete dve sahāyakā, āgacchanti kolito upatisso ca;

Etaṃ me sāvakayugaṃ, bhavissati aggaṃ bhaddayuganti.

“These two companions, Kolita and Upatissa, are coming; this will be my pair of disciples, the foremost, the excellent pair.”

Atha kho sāriputtamoggallānā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu[P 1.0043], upasaṅkamitvā

Then Sāriputta and Moggallāna approached the Blessed One; having approached,

Bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyāma upasampada”nti. “Etha bhikkhavo”ti bhagavā avoca – “svākkhāto dhammo, caratha brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Sāva tesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ upasampadā ahosi.

having fallen with their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, they said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may we receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence, may we receive the higher ordination?” “Come, bhikkhus,” the Blessed One said, “the Dhamma is well-proclaimed. Practice the holy life for the complete ending of suffering.” That itself was the higher ordination for those venerable ones.

Abhiññātānaṃ pabbajjā

The Going Forth of the Well-Known

63. Tena kho pana samayena abhiññātā abhiññātā māgadhikā kulaputtā bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ caranti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – aputtakatāya paṭipanno samaṇo gotamo, vedhabyāya paṭipanno samaṇo gotamo, kulupacchedāya paṭipanno samaṇo gotamo, idāni anena jaṭilasahassaṃ pabbājitaṃ, imāni ca aḍḍhateyyāni paribbājakasatāni sañcayāni sañjeyyāni (sī.), sañjayāni (syā.) pabbājitāni. Ime ca abhiññātā abhiññātā māgadhikā [M 0.0055] kulaputtā samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ carantīti. Apissu bhikkhū disvā imāya gāthāya codenti –

63. Now at that time, very well-known young men of good family from Magadha were practicing the holy life under the Blessed One. People complained, criticized, and spread rumors: “The ascetic Gotama is practicing to bring about childlessness, the ascetic Gotama is practicing to bring about widowhood, the ascetic Gotama is practicing to bring about the cutting off of family lines. Now a thousand matted-hair ascetics have been ordained by him, and these two hundred and fifty wanderers, followers of Sañjaya, have been ordained. And these very well-known young men of good family from Magadha are practicing the holy life under the ascetic Gotama.” And when they saw the bhikkhus, they reproached them with this verse:

“Āgato [T 1.0079][V 0.0049] kho mahāsamaṇo, māgadhānaṃ giribbajaṃ;

Sabbe sañcaye netvāna sañjeyyake netvā (sī.), kaṃsu dāni nayissatī”ti.

“The great ascetic has indeed come to Giribbaja of the Magadhans; having led away all of Sañjaya’s followers, whom will he now lead away?”

Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… na, bhikkhave, so saddo ciraṃ bhavissati, sattāhameva bhavissati, sattāhassa accayena antaradhāyissati. Tena hi, bhikkhave, ye tumhe imāya gāthāya codenti –

The bhikkhus indeed heard those people complaining, grumbling, and speaking disparagingly. Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, that sound will not last long. It will last for only seven days; after the passing of seven days, it will disappear. Therefore, bhikkhus, those who rebuke you with this verse—”

“Āgato kho mahāsamaṇo, māgadhānaṃ giribbajaṃ;

Sabbe sañcaye netvāna, kaṃsu dāni nayissatī”ti.

“The great ascetic has indeed come to Giribbaja of the Magadhans; having led away all of Sañcaya’s disciples, whom will he now lead away?”

Te tumhe imāya gāthāya paṭicodetha –

You should rebuke them in return with this verse—

“Nayanti ve mahāvīrā, saddhammena tathāgatā;

Dhammena nayamānānaṃ nīyamānānaṃ (ka.), kā usūyā ussuyā (ka.) vijānata”nti.

“Indeed, the great heroes, the Tathāgatas, lead by the good Dhamma. What envy can there be towards the wise who lead by the Dhamma?”

Tena kho pana samayena manussā bhikkhū disvā imāya gāthāya codenti –

Now at that time, people, upon seeing the bhikkhus, would rebuke them with this verse—

“Āgato kho mahāsamaṇo, māgadhānaṃ giribbajaṃ;

Sabbe sañcaye netvāna, kaṃsu dāni nayissatī”ti.

“The great ascetic has indeed come to Giribbaja of the Magadhans; having led away all of Sañcaya’s disciples, whom will he now lead away?”

Bhikkhū te manusse imāya gāthāya paṭicodenti –

The bhikkhus would rebuke those people in return with this verse—

“Nayanti ve mahāvīrā, saddhammena tathāgatā;

Dhammena nayamānānaṃ, kā usūyā vijānata”nti.

“Indeed, the great heroes, the Tathāgatas, lead by the good Dhamma. What envy can there be towards the wise who lead by the Dhamma?”

Manussā [P 1.0044] dhammena kira samaṇā sakyaputtiyā nenti [T 1.0080] no adhammenāti sattāhameva so saddo ahosi, sattāhassa accayena antaradhāyi.

The people said: “It is said that the ascetics who are sons of the Sakyan lead by the Dhamma, not by what is not the Dhamma.” That sound lasted for only seven days; after the passing of seven days, it disappeared.

Sāriputtamoggallānapabbajjākathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on the going forth of Sāriputta and Moggallāna is concluded.

Catutthabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The Fourth Recitation Section is concluded.

15. Upajjhāyavattakathā

15. The Discourse on the Duties towards a Preceptor

64. Tena [M 0.0056][V 0.0050] kho pana samayena bhikkhū anupajjhāyakā anācariyakā idaṃ padaṃ sī. syā. potthakesu natthi anovadiyamānā ananusāsiyamānā dunnivatthā duppārutā anākappasampannā piṇḍāya caranti; manussānaṃ te manussānaṃ (ka.) bhuñjamānānaṃ uparibhojanepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmenti, uparikhādanīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmenti, uparisāyanīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmenti, uparipānīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmenti; sāmaṃ sūpampi odanampi viññāpetvā bhuñjanti; bhattaggepi uccāsaddā mahāsaddā viharanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā dunnivatthā duppārutā anākappasampannā piṇḍāya carissanti; manussānaṃ bhuñjamānānaṃ, uparibhojanepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmessanti, uparikhādanīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmessanti, uparisāyanīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmessanti, uparipānīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmessanti; sāmaṃ sūpampi odanampi viññāpetvā bhuñjissanti; bhattaggepi uccāsaddā mahāsaddā viharissanti seyyathāpi brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇabhojane”ti.

64. Now at that time, monks—being without preceptors, without teachers, not being admonished, and not being instructed—wandered for alms poorly dressed, improperly clad, and lacking in proper conduct. While people were eating, they would hold out the alms-bowl over the food, hold out the alms-bowl over the edibles, hold out the alms-bowl over the delicacies, and hold out the alms-bowl over the drinks. They themselves, having requested curry and rice, would eat. In the dining hall, they lived making loud and great noises. People complained, criticized, and spread disparaging talk: ‘How indeed can these ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, wander for alms poorly dressed, improperly clad, and lacking in proper conduct? While people are eating, how can they hold out the alms-bowl over the food, hold out the alms-bowl over the edibles, hold out the alms-bowl over the delicacies, and hold out the alms-bowl over the drinks? How can they themselves, having requested curry and rice, eat? In the dining hall, how can they live making loud and great noises, just like brahmins at a meal for brahmins!’

Assosuṃ [T 1.0081] kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā santuṭṭhā lajjino kukkuccakā sikkhākāmā, te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhū dunnivatthā duppārutā anākappasampannā piṇḍāya carissanti; manussānaṃ bhuñjamānānaṃ, uparibhojanepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmessanti, uparikhādanīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmessanti, uparisāyanīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmessanti, uparipānīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmessanti; sāmaṃ sūpampi odanampi viññāpetvā bhuñjissanti; bhattaggepi uccāsaddā mahāsaddā viharissantī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū…pe… bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

The monks indeed heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading disparaging talk. Those monks who were of few wishes, content, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of the training complained, criticized, and spread disparaging talk: ‘How indeed can monks wander for alms poorly dressed, improperly clad, and lacking in proper conduct? While people are eating, how can they hold out the alms-bowl over the food, hold out the alms-bowl over the edibles, hold out the alms-bowl over the delicacies, and hold out the alms-bowl over the drinks? How can they themselves, having requested curry and rice, eat? In the dining hall, how can they live making loud and great noises?’ Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū dunnivatthā duppārutā anākappasampannā piṇḍāya caranti, manussānaṃ bhuñjamānānaṃ upari [P 1.0045] bhojanepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmenti, uparikhādanīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmenti, uparisāyanīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmenti, uparipānīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ [M 0.0057] upanāmenti, sāmaṃ sūpampi odanampi viññāpetvā bhuñjanti, bhattaggepi uccāsaddā mahāsaddā viharantī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho [T 1.0082] bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ, bhikkhave, tesaṃ moghapurisānaṃ ananulomikaṃ appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma [V 0.0051] te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā dunnivatthā duppārutā anākappasampannā piṇḍāya carissanti, manussānaṃ bhuñjamānānaṃ uparibhojanepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmessanti, uparikhādanīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmessanti, uparisāyanīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmessanti, uparipānīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmessanti, sāmaṃ sūpampi odanampi viññāpetvā bhuñjissanti, bhattaggepi uccāsaddā mahāsaddā viharissanti. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya, pasannānaṃ vā bhiyyobhāvāya. Atha khvetaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānañceva appasādāya, pasannānañca ekaccānaṃ aññathattāyā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā te bhikkhū anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā dubbharatāya dupposatāya mahicchatāya asantuṭṭhitāya asantuṭṭhiyā (sī.), asantuṭṭhatāya (syā) saṅgaṇikāya kosajjassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsitvā anekapariyāyena subharatāya suposatāya appicchassa santuṭṭhassa sallekhassa dhutassa pāsādikassa apacayassa vīriyārambhassa viriyārambhassa (sī. syā.) vaṇṇaṃ bhāsitvā bhikkhūnaṃ tadanucchavikaṃ tadanulomikaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having convened the community of monks, questioned the monks: “Is it true, monks, as it is said, that monks—being poorly dressed, improperly clad, and lacking in proper conduct—wander for alms; that while people are eating, they hold out the alms-bowl over the food, over the edibles, over the delicacies, and over the drinks; that they themselves, having requested curry and rice, eat; and that in the dining hall they live making loud and great noises?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them: “This is unsuitable for those foolish men, O monks, it is inappropriate, improper, not befitting a recluse, not allowable, and not to be done. How indeed, monks, could those foolish men—being poorly dressed, improperly clad, and lacking in proper conduct—wander for alms; while people are eating, hold out the alms-bowl over the food, over the edibles, over the delicacies, and over the drinks; themselves, having requested curry and rice, eat; and live in the dining hall making loud and great noises? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconvinced, nor for the increase of the convinced. Rather, monks, it is for the lack of confidence of the unconvinced and for the change of mind in some of the convinced.” Then the Blessed One, having rebuked those monks in many ways, spoke in dispraise of being difficult to support, difficult to maintain, having great desires, being discontented, delighting in company, and being indolent; and having spoken in many ways in praise of being easy to support, easy to maintain, having few wishes, being content, of effacement, of shaking off defilements, of inspiring confidence, of non-accumulation, and of energetic endeavor, gave a Dhamma talk to the monks that was suitable and appropriate for the occasion, and addressed the monks:

65. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, upajjhāyaṃ. Upajjhāyo, bhikkhave, saddhivihārikamhi puttacittaṃ upaṭṭhapessati[T 1.0083], saddhivihāriko upajjhāyamhi pitucittaṃ upaṭṭhapessati. Evaṃ te aññamaññaṃ sagāravā sappatissā sabhāgavuttino viharantā imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuḍḍhiṃ viruḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissanti. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, upajjhāyo gahetabbo – ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘upajjhāyo me, bhante, hohi; upajjhāyo me, bhante, hohi; upajjhāyo me, bhante, hohī’ti. Sāhūti vā lahūti vā opāyikanti vā patirūpanti vā pāsādikena sampādehīti vā kāyena viññāpeti, vācāya viññāpeti, kāyena vācāya na vācāya (ka.) viññāpeti, gahito hoti upajjhāyo; na kāyena viññāpeti, na vācāya viññāpeti[P 1.0046][M 0.0058], na kāyena vācāya viññāpeti, na gahito hoti upajjhāyo.

65. “I allow, monks, a preceptor. The preceptor, monks, shall establish the mind of a son toward the co-resident disciple, and the co-resident disciple shall establish the mind of a father toward the preceptor. Thus, dwelling with mutual respect, deference, and sharing a common way of life, they will attain growth, prosperity, and abundance in this Dhamma and Discipline. And, monks, a preceptor should be taken in this way: having arranged the upper robe over one shoulder, having venerated his feet, having sat down in a squatting position, and having raised the joined palms, he should be addressed thus: ‘Venerable sir, be my preceptor; venerable sir, be my preceptor; venerable sir, be my preceptor.’ If the preceptor makes it known by body, by speech, or by body and speech—by saying ‘Good,’ or ‘It is light,’ or ‘It is suitable,’ or ‘It is proper,’ or ‘Accomplish it with an inspiring demeanor’—the preceptor is taken. If he does not make it known by body, by speech, or by body and speech, the preceptor is not taken.

66. cūḷava. 376 ādayo“Saddhivihārikena, bhikkhave, upajjhāyamhi sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā –

66. “A co-resident disciple, monks, should conduct himself properly towards his preceptor. Herein, this is the proper conduct:

“Kālasseva vuṭṭhāya upāhanā omuñcitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā dantakaṭṭhaṃ dātabbaṃ, mukhodakaṃ dātabbaṃ, āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Sace yāgu hoti, bhājanaṃ dhovitvā yāgu upanāmetabbā. Yāguṃ pītassa udakaṃ datvā bhājanaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena [V 0.0052] dhovitvā paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Upajjhāyamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti, so deso sammajjitabbo.

Having risen early, having removed one's footwear and arranged the upper robe over one shoulder, a tooth-stick should be given, water for the face should be given, and a seat should be prepared. If there is gruel, having washed the bowl, the gruel should be offered. To the preceptor who has drunk the gruel, water should be given, the bowl should be received, and holding it low, it should be washed carefully without scraping it, and then put away. When the preceptor has risen, the seat should be removed. If that place is littered, that place should be swept.

“Sace upajjhāyo gāmaṃ pavisitukāmo [T 1.0084] hoti, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, kāyabandhanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo dātabbā, dhovitvā patto sodako saudako (ka.) dātabbo. Sace upajjhāyo pacchāsamaṇaṃ ākaṅkhati, timaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādentena parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsetvā kāyabandhanaṃ bandhitvā saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo pārupitvā gaṇṭhikaṃ paṭimuñcitvā dhovitvā pattaṃ gahetvā upajjhāyassa pacchāsamaṇena hotabbaṃ. Nātidūre gantabbaṃ, nāccāsanne gantabbaṃ, pattapariyāpannaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Na upajjhāyassa bhaṇamānassa antarantarā kathā opātetabbā. Upajjhāyo āpattisāmantā bhaṇamāno nivāretabbo.

If the preceptor wishes to enter the village, the lower robe for wearing in the village should be given, and the lower robe worn in the monastery should be received. The belt should be given. The outer robes, having been folded, should be given. The bowl, having been washed, should be given with water. If the preceptor desires an accompanying monk, one should become his accompanying monk by covering the three circles, wearing the lower robe evenly all around, tying the belt, putting on the folded outer robes, fastening the toggle, and taking the washed bowl. One should not go too far away, nor too close. The alms received in the bowl should be accepted. One should not interrupt while the preceptor is speaking. A preceptor who is speaking on the verge of an offense should be stopped.

“Nivattantena paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ, paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Sace cīvaraṃ sinnaṃ hoti, muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbaṃ, na ca uṇhe cīvaraṃ nidahitabbaṃ; cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ, cīvaraṃ saṅgharantena caturaṅgulaṃ kaṇṇaṃ ussāretvā cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ – mā majjhe bhaṅgo ahosīti. Obhoge kāyabandhanaṃ kātabbaṃ.

When returning, one should arrive first and prepare a seat. Water for the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet should be placed nearby. Going out to meet him, the bowl and robes should be received. The lower robe for the monastery should be given, and the lower robe for the village should be received. If a robe is damp, it should be aired for a moment in the sun's heat, but a robe should not be left in the sun's heat for long. The robe should be folded. When folding the robe, one should leave a margin of four finger-breadths at the corner when folding it, so that there will be no crease in the middle. The belt should be placed in the fold.

“Sace piṇḍapāto hoti, upajjhāyo ca bhuñjitukāmo hoti, udakaṃ datvā piṇḍapāto upanāmetabbo. Upajjhāyo pānīyena pucchitabbo[T 1.0085]. Bhuttāvissa udakaṃ datvā pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ [M 0.0059] appaṭighaṃsantena dhovitvā vodakaṃ katvā muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbo, na ca uṇhe patto nidahitabbo. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ [P 1.0047] vā parāmasitvā patto nikkhipitabbo. Na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ vā pamajjitvā pārato antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Upajjhāyamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti, so deso sammajjitabbo.

If there is almsfood and the preceptor wishes to eat, water should be given and the almsfood presented. The preceptor should be asked about drinking water. After he has eaten, water should be given, the bowl received, held low, washed well without scraping, made waterless, and dried for a moment in the sun—but the bowl should not be left for a long time in the sun. The bowl and robe should be put away. When putting away the bowl, one should take the bowl with one hand, feel under the cot or under the seat with the other hand, and then put the bowl away. The bowl should not be put away on the bare ground. When putting away the robe, one should take the robe with one hand, wipe the robe-pole or robe-rope with the other hand, and place the robe with its end on the far side and the fold on the near side. When the preceptor has risen, the seat should be removed; the foot-water, footstool, and foot-scraper should be put away. If that place has rubbish, it should be swept.

“Sace upajjhāyo nahāyitukāmo hoti, nahānaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace sītena attho hoti, sītaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace uṇhena attho hoti, uṇhaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ.

If the preceptor wishes to bathe, bathing water should be prepared. If he needs cold water, cold water should be prepared. If he needs warm water, warm water should be prepared.

“Sace [V 0.0053] upajjhāyo jantāgharaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, cuṇṇaṃ sannetabbaṃ, mattikā temetabbā, jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya upajjhāyassa piṭṭhito piṭṭhito gantvā jantāgharapīṭhaṃ datvā cīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, cuṇṇaṃ dātabbaṃ, mattikā dātabbā. Sace ussahati, jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Jantāgharaṃ pavisantena mattikāya mukhaṃ makkhetvā purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Na there bhikkhū anupakhajja nisīditabbaṃ. Na [T 1.0086] navā bhikkhū āsanena paṭibāhitabbā. Jantāghare upajjhāyassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Jantāgharā nikkhamantena jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharā nikkhamitabbaṃ.

If the preceptor wishes to enter the steam-room, the powder should be mixed with water, and the clay should be moistened. Taking the steam-room stool, one should go behind the preceptor, give the steam-room stool, receive the robe, and place it aside. The powder should be given; the clay should be given. If one is able, one should enter the steam-room. When entering the steam-room, having smeared the face with clay and having covered oneself in front and behind, one should enter the steam-room. One should not sit down by crowding the senior monks. Junior monks should not be obstructed from their seats. In the steam-room, attendance should be given to the preceptor. When leaving the steam-room, taking the steam-room stool and having covered oneself in front and behind, one should exit from the steam-room.

“Udakepi upajjhāyassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Nahātena paṭhamataraṃ uttaritvā attano gattaṃ vodakaṃ katvā nivāsetvā upajjhāyassa gattato udakaṃ pamajjitabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saṅghāṭi dātabbā, jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ, upajjhāyo pānīyena pucchitabbo. Sace uddisāpetukāmo hoti, uddisitabbo. Sace paripucchitukāmo hoti, paripucchitabbo.

Attendance should also be given to the preceptor in the water. Having bathed, one should emerge first, dry one's own body, put on the lower robe, and then wipe the water from the preceptor’s body. The lower robe should be given; the outer robe should be given. Taking the steam-room stool, one should return first, prepare the seat, and place nearby the foot-washing water, the footstool, and the potsherd for rubbing the feet. The preceptor should be asked about drinking water. If he wishes to have the text recited, it should be recited. If he wishes to be questioned, he should be questioned.

“Yasmiṃ vihāre upajjhāyo viharati, sace so vihāro uklāpo hoti, sace ussahati, sodhetabbo. Vihāraṃ sodhentena paṭhamaṃ pattacīvaraṃ [M 0.0060] nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Bhisibibbohanaṃ bhisibimbohanaṃ (sī. syā.) nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Mañco nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo. Pīṭhaṃ nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena[P 1.0048], asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Mañcapaṭipādakā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbā. Kheḷamallako nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo. Apassenaphalakaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Bhūmattharaṇaṃ yathāpaññattaṃ sallakkhetvā [T 1.0087] nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Sace vihāre santānakaṃ hoti, ullokā paṭhamaṃ ohāretabbaṃ, ālokasandhikaṇṇabhāgā pamajjitabbā. Sace gerukaparikammakatā bhitti kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace kāḷavaṇṇakatā bhūmi kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace akatā hoti bhūmi, udakena paripphositvā sammajjitabbā – mā vihāro rajena uhaññīti. Saṅkāraṃ vicinitvā ekamantaṃ chaḍḍetabbaṃ.

In whichever dwelling the preceptor resides, if that dwelling is untidy, and if one is capable, it should be cleaned. When cleaning the dwelling, one should first remove the bowl and robe and set them aside in a suitable place. One should remove the sitting-cloth and ground-sheet and set them aside in a suitable place. One should remove the mattress and pillow and set them aside in a suitable place. Lowering the bed carefully, without scraping it on the ground or knocking it against the door-panel and door-post, one should remove it and set it aside in a suitable place. Lowering the stool carefully, without scraping it on the ground or knocking it against the door-panel and door-post, one should remove it and set it aside in a suitable place. One should remove the bed-legs and set them aside in a suitable place. One should remove the spittoon and set it aside in a suitable place. One should remove the leaning-board and set it aside in a suitable place. Noting how the floor covering was laid out, one should remove it and set it aside in a suitable place. If the dwelling has cobwebs, one should first remove them from the ceiling; the window openings and corners should be wiped. If the walls, finished with red ochre, have become mildewed, one should moisten a cloth, wring it out, and wipe them. If the floor, finished with a black colour, has become mildewed, one should moisten a cloth, wring it out, and wipe it. If the floor is unfinished, one should sprinkle it with water and sweep it—lest the dwelling be soiled with dust. One should gather the rubbish and discard it in a suitable place.

“Bhūmattharaṇaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Mañcapaṭipādakā [V 0.0054] otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbā. Mañco otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbo. Pīṭhaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Bhisibibbohanaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Kheḷamallako otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbo. Apassenaphalakaṃ otāpetvā pamajjitvā [T 1.0088] atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbaṃ. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā patto nikkhipitabbo. Na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā [M 0.0061] ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ vā pamajjitvā pārato antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ.

The floor covering should be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, brought back, and laid out as it was before. The bed legs should be aired in the sun, wiped, brought back, and placed in their proper place. The bed should be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, lowered carefully, without scraping it on the ground and without bumping it against the door leaf or door frame, brought back, and laid out as it was before. The stool should be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, lowered carefully, without scraping it on the ground and without bumping it against the door leaf or door frame, brought back, and laid out as it was before. The mattress and pillow should be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, brought back, and laid out as they were before. The sitting-cloth and ground-sheet should be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, brought back, and laid out as they were before. The spittoon should be aired in the sun, wiped, brought back, and placed in its proper place. The leaning-board should be aired in the sun, wiped, brought back, and placed in its proper place. The bowl and robe should be put away. When putting away the bowl, one should hold it with one hand and feel underneath the bed or stool with the other before setting the bowl down. The bowl should not be set on the bare ground. When putting away the robe, one should hold the robe with one hand, wipe the robe-pole or robe-rope with the other hand, and then put the robe away, making a fold on the near side from the far end.

“Sace puratthimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, puratthimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace pacchimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, pacchimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace uttarā sarajā vātā vāyanti, uttarā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace dakkhiṇā sarajā vātā vāyanti, dakkhiṇā vātapānā [P 1.0049] thaketabbā. Sace sītakālo hoti, divā vātapānā vivaritabbā, rattiṃ thaketabbā. Sace uṇhakālo hoti, divā vātapānā thaketabbā, rattiṃ vivaritabbā.

If dusty winds blow from the east, the eastern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the west, the western windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the north, the northern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the south, the southern windows should be closed. If it is the cold season, the windows should be opened during the day and closed at night. If it is the hot season, the windows should be closed during the day and opened at night.

“Sace pariveṇaṃ uklāpaṃ hoti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ. Sace koṭṭhako uklāpo hoti, koṭṭhako sammajjitabbo. Sace upaṭṭhānasālā uklāpā hoti, upaṭṭhānasālā sammajjitabbā. Sace aggisālā uklāpā hoti, aggisālā sammajjitabbā. Sace vaccakuṭi uklāpā hoti, vaccakuṭi sammajjitabbā. Sace pānīyaṃ na hoti, pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace paribhojanīyaṃ na hoti, paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ na hoti, ācamanakumbhiyā [T 1.0089] udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ.

If the precinct is untidy, it should be swept. If the gatehouse is untidy, it should be swept. If the assembly hall is untidy, it should be swept. If the fire-hall is untidy, it should be swept. If the latrine is untidy, it should be swept. If there is no drinking water, drinking water should be provided. If there is no water for use, water for use should be provided. If there is no water in the rinsing pot, water should be poured into the rinsing pot.

“Sace upajjhāyassa anabhirati uppannā hoti, saddhivihārikena vūpakāsetabbo, vūpakāsāpetabbo, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace upajjhāyassa kukkuccaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, saddhivihārikena vinodetabbaṃ, vinodāpetabbaṃ, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā.
