Sace upajjhāyassa diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti, saddhivihārikena vivecetabbaṃ, vivecāpetabbaṃ, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā[V 0.0055]. Sace upajjhāyo garudhammaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti parivāsāraho, saddhivihārikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho upajjhāyassa parivāsaṃ dadeyyāti. Sace upajjhāyo mūlāya paṭikassanāraho hoti, saddhivihārikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho upajjhāyaṃ mūlāya paṭikasseyyāti. Sace upajjhāyo mānattāraho hoti, saddhivihārikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho upajjhāyassa mānattaṃ dadeyyāti. Sace upajjhāyo abbhānāraho hoti, saddhivihārikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho upajjhāyaṃ abbheyyāti. Sace saṅgho upajjhāyassa [M 0.0062] kammaṃ kattukāmo hoti tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ niyasaṃ (ka.) vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ vā, saddhivihārikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho upajjhāyassa kammaṃ na kareyya lahukāya vā pariṇāmeyyāti. Kataṃ vā panassa hoti saṅghena kammaṃ tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ [T 1.0090] vā, saddhivihārikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho upajjhāyo sammā vatteyya, lomaṃ pāteyya, netthāraṃ vatteyya, saṅgho taṃ kammaṃ paṭippassambheyyāti.

If dissatisfaction arises in the preceptor, the co-resident pupil should lead him away, or cause him to be led away, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If remorse arises in the preceptor, the co-resident pupil should dispel it, or cause it to be dispelled, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If a wrong view arises in the preceptor, the co-resident pupil should make him abandon it, or cause him to be made to abandon it, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If the preceptor has committed a grave offense and is deserving of probation, the co-resident pupil should make an effort: ‘How might the Saṅgha grant probation to the preceptor?’ If the preceptor is deserving of being sent back to the beginning, the co-resident pupil should make an effort: ‘How might the Saṅgha send the preceptor back to the beginning?’ If the preceptor is deserving of mānatta, the co-resident pupil should make an effort: ‘How might the Saṅgha grant mānatta to the preceptor?’ If the preceptor is deserving of rehabilitation, the co-resident pupil should make an effort: ‘How might the Saṅgha rehabilitate the preceptor?’ If the Saṅgha desires to perform a formal act against the preceptor—whether an act of censure, an act of subordination, an act of banishment, an act of reconciliation, or an act of suspension—the co-resident pupil should make an effort: ‘How might the Saṅgha not perform the formal act against the preceptor, or how might it be changed to a lighter one?’ Or if a formal act has been performed against him by the Saṅgha—whether an act of censure, an act of subordination, an act of banishment, an act of reconciliation, or an act of suspension—the co-resident pupil should make an effort: ‘How might the preceptor behave properly, humble himself, and conduct himself for his rehabilitation, so that the Saṅgha may revoke that formal act?’

“Sace upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ dhovitabbaṃ hoti, saddhivihārikena dhovitabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ [P 1.0050] – kinti nu kho upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ dhoviyethāti. Sace upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ kātabbaṃ hoti, saddhivihārikena kātabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ kariyethāti. Sace upajjhāyassa rajanaṃ pacitabbaṃ hoti, saddhivihārikena pacitabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho upajjhāyassa rajanaṃ paciyethāti. Sace upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ rajitabbaṃ rajetabbaṃ (sī. syā.) hoti, saddhivihārikena rajitabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ rajiyethāti. Cīvaraṃ rajantena rajentena (sī. syā.) sādhukaṃ samparivattakaṃ samparivattakaṃ rajitabbaṃ, na ca acchinne theve pakkamitabbaṃ.

If the preceptor’s robe is to be washed, it should be washed by the co-resident pupil, or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How indeed might the preceptor’s robe be washed?’ If the preceptor’s robe is to be made, it should be made by the co-resident pupil, or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How indeed might the preceptor’s robe be made?’ If dye for the preceptor is to be boiled, it should be boiled by the co-resident pupil, or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How indeed might dye for the preceptor be boiled?’ If the preceptor’s robe is to be dyed, it should be dyed by the co-resident pupil, or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How indeed might the preceptor’s robe be dyed?’ When dyeing the robe, it should be dyed well, turning it over and over, and one should not depart before the dripping has ceased.

“Na upajjhāyaṃ anāpucchā ekaccassa patto dātabbo, na ekaccassa patto paṭiggahetabbo; na ekaccassa cīvaraṃ dātabbaṃ, na ekaccassa cīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ; na ekaccassa parikkhāro dātabbo, na ekaccassa parikkhāro paṭiggahetabbo; na ekaccassa kesā chedetabbā chettabbā (sī.), cheditabbā (ka.), na ekaccena kesā chedāpetabbā; na ekaccassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ, na ekaccena parikammaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ; na ekaccassa veyyāvacco veyyāvaccaṃ (katthaci) kātabbo[T 1.0091], na ekaccena veyyāvacco kārāpetabbo; na ekaccassa pacchāsamaṇena hotabbaṃ, na ekacco pacchāsamaṇo ādātabbo; na ekaccassa piṇḍapāto nīharitabbo, na ekaccena piṇḍapāto nīharāpetabbo; na [V 0.0056] upajjhāyaṃ anāpucchā [M 0.0063] gāmo pavisitabbo; na susānaṃ gantabbaṃ; na disā pakkamitabbā. Sace upajjhāyo gilāno hoti, yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhātabbo; vuṭṭhānamassa āgametabba”nti.

Without asking the preceptor, a bowl should not be given to a certain monk, nor should a bowl be received from a certain monk; a robe should not be given to a certain monk, nor should a robe be received from a certain monk; a requisite should not be given to a certain monk, nor should a requisite be received from a certain monk; the hair of a certain monk should not be cut, nor should one have one's hair cut by a certain monk; a personal service should not be performed for a certain monk, nor should one have a personal service performed by a certain monk; a service should not be rendered to a certain monk, nor should one have a service rendered by a certain monk; one should not be an attendant for a certain monk, nor should a certain monk be taken as an attendant; alms-food should not be carried for a certain monk, nor should one have one's alms-food carried by a certain monk. Without asking the preceptor, a village should not be entered; a charnel ground should not be gone to; one should not depart to another direction. If the preceptor is sick, he should be attended to for as long as he lives; his recovery should be awaited.

Upajjhāyavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The duties toward the preceptor are concluded.

16. Saddhivihārikavattakathā

16. The Discourse on the Duties towards a Co-resident Pupil

67. cūḷava. 378 ādayo “Upajjhāyena, bhikkhave, saddhivihārikamhi sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā –

67. Monks, a preceptor should conduct himself properly towards his co-resident pupil. Herein, this is the proper conduct:

“Upajjhāyena, bhikkhave, saddhivihāriko saṅgahetabbo anuggahetabbo uddesena paripucchāya ovādena anusāsaniyā. Sace upajjhāyassa patto hoti, saddhivihārikassa patto na hoti, upajjhāyena saddhivihārikassa patto dātabbo, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saddhivihārikassa patto uppajjiyethāti. Sace upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ hoti, saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ na hoti, upajjhāyena saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ dātabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ uppajjiyethāti. Sace upajjhāyassa parikkhāro hoti, saddhivihārikassa parikkhāro na hoti, upajjhāyena saddhivihārikassa parikkhāro [P 1.0051] dātabbo, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saddhivihārikassa parikkhāro uppajjiyethāti.

Monks, a preceptor should support and assist his co-resident pupil by teaching the Pali text, by teaching the commentary, by exhortation, and by instruction. If the preceptor has a bowl and the co-resident pupil does not have a bowl, a bowl should be given to the co-resident pupil by the preceptor, or an effort should be made, thinking: 'How indeed might a bowl arise for the co-resident pupil?' If the preceptor has a robe and the co-resident pupil does not have a robe, a robe should be given to the co-resident pupil by the preceptor, or an effort should be made, thinking: 'How indeed might a robe arise for the co-resident pupil?' If the preceptor has requisites and the co-resident pupil does not have requisites, requisites should be given to the co-resident pupil by the preceptor, or an effort should be made, thinking: 'How indeed might requisites arise for the co-resident pupil?'

“Sace [T 1.0092] saddhivihāriko gilāno hoti, kālasseva uṭṭhāya dantakaṭṭhaṃ dātabbaṃ, mukhodakaṃ dātabbaṃ, āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Sace yāgu hoti, bhājanaṃ dhovitvā yāgu upanāmetabbā. Yāguṃ pītassa udakaṃ datvā bhājanaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena dhovitvā paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Saddhivihārikamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti, so deso sammajjitabbo.

If the co-resident pupil is sick, having risen early, a tooth-stick should be given, water for the face should be given, and a seat should be prepared. If there is gruel, the vessel should be washed and the gruel offered. After he has drunk the gruel, water should be given, the vessel should be received, held low, and carefully washed without scraping it on the ground, then put away. When the co-resident pupil has risen, the seat should be removed. If that place is littered, that place should be swept.

“Sace saddhivihāriko gāmaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, kāyabandhanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo dātabbā, dhovitvā patto sodako dātabbo. Ettāvatā nivattissatīti āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ [M 0.0064] upanikkhipitabbaṃ, paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ[V 0.0057]. Sace cīvaraṃ sinnaṃ hoti, muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbaṃ, na ca uṇhe cīvaraṃ nidahitabbaṃ; cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ, cīvaraṃ saṅgharantena caturaṅgulaṃ kaṇṇaṃ ussāretvā cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ – mā majjhe bhaṅgo ahosīti. Obhoge kāyabandhanaṃ kātabbaṃ.

If a co-resident pupil wishes to enter a village, the lower robe should be given, and the other lower robe should be received. The waistband should be given. The double-layered robes should be given, having been doubled. The bowl, having been washed, should be given with water. Thinking, 'He will return by this time,' a seat should be prepared; water for the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet should be placed nearby. Having gone out to meet him, the bowl and robes should be received. The other lower robe should be given, and the lower robe should be received. If a robe is damp with sweat, it should be aired in the sun for a moment, but the robe should not be left in the sun for a long time. The robe should be folded. When folding a robe, one should fold it leaving a margin of four finger-breadths at the corner, so that there will be no crease in the middle. The waistband should be placed in the fold.

“Sace piṇḍapāto hoti, saddhivihāriko ca bhuñjitukāmo hoti, udakaṃ datvā piṇḍapāto upanāmetabbo. Saddhivihāriko pānīyena pucchitabbo. Bhuttāvissa udakaṃ datvā pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena dhovitvā vodakaṃ katvā muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbo, na ca uṇhe patto nidahitabbo. Pattacīvaraṃ [T 1.0093] nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā patto nikkhipitabbo. Na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ vā pamajjitvā pārato antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Saddhivihārikamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti, so deso sammajjitabbo.

If there is almsfood and the co-resident pupil wishes to eat, water should be given and the almsfood should be offered. The co-resident pupil should be asked about drinking water. After he has eaten, water should be given, the bowl should be received, and holding it low, it should be washed carefully without scraping it on the ground. Having been made free of water, it should be aired in the sun for a moment, but the bowl should not be left in the sun for a long time. The bowl and robes should be put away. When putting away the bowl, holding the bowl with one hand and feeling under the bed or under the stool with the other hand, the bowl should be put down. The bowl should not be put down on the bare ground. When putting away a robe, holding the robe with one hand and wiping the robe-rail or robe-line with the other hand, the robe should be put away by placing the end on the far side and making the fold on the near side. When the co-resident pupil has risen, the seat should be cleared away; the water for the feet, the footstool, and the potsherd for rubbing the feet should be put away. If that place is littered, that place should be swept.

“Sace saddhivihāriko nahāyitukāmo hoti, nahānaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace sītena attho hoti, sītaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace uṇhena attho hoti, uṇhaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ[P 1.0052].

If the co-resident pupil wishes to bathe, bathing water should be prepared. If there is a need for cold water, cold water should be prepared. If there is a need for hot water, hot water should be prepared.

“Sace saddhivihāriko jantāgharaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, cuṇṇaṃ sannetabbaṃ, mattikā temetabbā, jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya gantvā jantāgharapīṭhaṃ datvā cīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, cuṇṇaṃ dātabbaṃ, mattikā dātabbā. Sace ussahati, jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Jantāgharaṃ pavisantena mattikāya mukhaṃ makkhetvā purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Na there bhikkhū anupakhajja nisīditabbaṃ. Na navā bhikkhū āsanena paṭibāhitabbā. Jantāghare saddhivihārikassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Jantāgharā nikkhamantena jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharā nikkhamitabbaṃ.

If the co-resident pupil wishes to enter the steam bath, bathing powder should be kneaded with water, and clay should be moistened. Having taken the steam bath stool and gone, the steam bath stool should be given; having received the robe, it should be placed in a suitable place. Bathing powder should be given; clay should be given. If one is able, the steam bath should be entered. When entering the steam bath, having smeared the face with clay and having covered oneself in front and in back, the steam bath should be entered. One should not sit down encroaching upon senior bhikkhus. Junior bhikkhus should not be obstructed from a seat. In the steam bath, service should be performed for the co-resident pupil. When leaving the steam bath, having taken the steam bath stool and having covered oneself in front and in back, one should leave the steam bath.

“Udakepi [M 0.0065] saddhivihārikassa [T 1.0094] parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Nahātena paṭhamataraṃ uttaritvā attano gattaṃ vodakaṃ katvā nivāsetvā saddhivihārikassa gattato udakaṃ pamajjitabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saṅghāṭi dātabbā. Jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ. Saddhivihāriko pānīyena pucchitabbo.

At the bathing place also, service should be performed for the co-resident pupil. Having bathed, one should come out from the water first, and having dried one's own body and put on the lower robe, the water should be wiped from the co-resident pupil's body. The lower robe should be given, and the outer robe should be given. Having taken the steam bath stool and having arrived first, a seat should be prepared; water for the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet should be placed nearby. The co-resident pupil should be asked about drinking water.

“Yasmiṃ [V 0.0058] vihāre saddhivihāriko viharati, sace so vihāro uklāpo hoti, sace ussahati, sodhetabbo. Vihāraṃ sodhentena paṭhamaṃ pattacīvaraṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; bhisibibbohanaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; mañco nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo; pīṭhaṃ nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; mañcapaṭipādakā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbā; kheḷamallako nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo; apassenaphalakaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; bhūmattharaṇaṃ yathāpaññattaṃ sallakkhetvā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Sace vihāre santānakaṃ hoti, ullokā paṭhamaṃ ohāretabbaṃ, ālokasandhikaṇṇabhāgā pamajjitabbā. Sace gerukaparikammakatā bhitti kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace kāḷavaṇṇakatā bhūmi kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā [T 1.0095] pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace akatā hoti bhūmi, udakena paripphositvā sammajjitabbā – mā vihāro rajena uhaññīti. Saṅkāraṃ vicinitvā ekamantaṃ chaḍḍetabbaṃ.

In whatever dwelling the co-resident pupil dwells, if that dwelling is untidy, and one is able, it should be cleaned. When cleaning the dwelling, first the bowl and robes should be taken out and set aside; the sitting mat and cover should be taken out and set aside; the bolster and pillow should be taken out and set aside; the bed should be lowered carefully, without scraping it or bumping it against the door-leaf and door-post, taken out, and set aside; the stool should be lowered carefully, without scraping it or bumping it against the door-leaf and door-post, taken out, and set aside; the legs of the bed should be taken out and set aside; the spittoon should be taken out and set aside; the leaning board should be taken out and set aside; after noting how the floor covering was laid out, it should be taken out and set aside. If there are cobwebs in the dwelling, they should first be removed from the ceiling, and the window openings and corners should be wiped. If the walls finished with red ochre are mouldy, a cloth should be dampened, wrung out, and used to wipe them. If the floor finished with a black color is mouldy, a cloth should be dampened, wrung out, and used to wipe it. If the floor is unfinished, it should be sprinkled with water and swept—lest the dwelling be covered with dust. The rubbish should be collected and thrown away to one side.

“Bhūmattharaṇaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Mañcapaṭipādakā otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbā. Mañco otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbo. Pīṭhaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Bhisibibbohanaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ [M 0.0066] paññapetabbaṃ. Nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Kheḷamallako otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbo. Apassenaphalakaṃ otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbaṃ. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā patto nikkhipitabbo. Na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ vā pamajjitvā pārato [T 1.0096] antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ.

The floor covering, having been aired in the sun, cleaned, and shaken out, should be brought back and laid out as it was previously laid out. The legs of the bed, having been aired in the sun and wiped, should be brought back and placed in their usual place. The bed, having been aired in the sun, cleaned, and shaken out, should be lowered and, carefully, without scraping it on the ground and without striking the door-leaf or door-post, brought back and laid out as it was previously laid out. The stool, having been aired in the sun, cleaned, and shaken out, should be lowered and, carefully, without scraping it on the ground and without striking the door-leaf or door-post, brought back and laid out as it was previously laid out. The bolster and pillow, having been aired in the sun, cleaned, and shaken out, should be brought back and laid out as they were previously laid out. The sitting mat and cover, having been aired in the sun, cleaned, and shaken out, should be brought back and laid out as they were previously laid out. The spittoon, having been aired in the sun and wiped, should be brought back and placed in its usual place. The leaning board, having been aired in the sun and wiped, should be brought back and placed in its usual place. The bowl and robes should be put away. When putting away the bowl, having taken the bowl with one hand and having felt with the other hand either under the bed or under the stool, the bowl should be put down. And the bowl should not be put down on the bare ground. When putting away the robe, having taken the robe with one hand and having wiped either the robe-pole or the robe-rope with the other hand, making a fold on the near side with the end on the far side, the robe should be put away.

“Sace puratthimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, puratthimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace pacchimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, pacchimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace uttarā sarajā vātā vāyanti, uttarā [V 0.0059] vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace dakkhiṇā sarajā vātā vāyanti, dakkhiṇā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace sītakālo hoti, divā vātapānā vivaritabbā, rattiṃ thaketabbā. Sace uṇhakālo hoti, divā vātapānā thaketabbā, rattiṃ vivaritabbā.

If dusty winds blow from the east, the eastern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the west, the western windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the north, the northern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the south, the southern windows should be closed. If it is the cold season, the windows should be opened during the day and closed at night. If it is the hot season, the windows should be closed during the day and opened at night.

“Sace pariveṇaṃ uklāpaṃ hoti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ. Sace koṭṭhako uklāpo hoti, koṭṭhako sammajjitabbo. Sace upaṭṭhānasālā uklāpā hoti, upaṭṭhānasālā sammajjitabbā. Sace aggisālā uklāpā hoti, aggisālā sammajjitabbā. Sace vaccakuṭi uklāpā hoti, vaccakuṭi sammajjitabbā. Sace pānīyaṃ na hoti, pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace paribhojanīyaṃ na hoti, paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ na hoti, ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ.

If the precincts are dirty, the precincts should be swept. If the gateway is dirty, the gateway should be swept. If the assembly hall is dirty, the assembly hall should be swept. If the fire-hall is dirty, the fire-hall should be swept. If the toilet is dirty, the toilet should be swept. If there is no drinking water, drinking water should be provided. If there is no water for use, water for use should be provided. If there is no water in the rinsing pot, water should be poured into it.

“Sace saddhivihārikassa anabhirati uppannā hoti, upajjhāyena vūpakāsetabbo, vūpakāsāpetabbo, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace saddhivihārikassa kukkuccaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, upajjhāyena vinodetabbaṃ, vinodāpetabbaṃ, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā[T 1.0097]. Sace saddhivihārikassa diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti, upajjhāyena vivecetabbaṃ, vivecāpetabbaṃ, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace saddhivihāriko garudhammaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti parivāsāraho, upajjhāyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho [M 0.0067] saddhivihārikassa parivāsaṃ dadeyyāti. Sace saddhivihāriko mūlāya paṭikassanāraho hoti, upajjhāyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho saddhivihārikaṃ mūlāya paṭikasseyyāti. Sace saddhivihāriko mānattāraho hoti, upajjhāyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho saddhivihārikassa mānattaṃ dadeyyāti. Sace saddhivihāriko [P 1.0053] abbhānāraho hoti, upajjhāyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho saddhivihārikaṃ abbheyyāti. Sace saṅgho saddhivihārikassa kammaṃ kattukāmo hoti, tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ vā, upajjhāyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho saddhivihārikassa kammaṃ na kareyya, lahukāya vā pariṇāmeyyāti. Kataṃ vā panassa hoti saṅghena kammaṃ, tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ vā, upajjhāyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saddhivihāriko sammā vatteyya, lomaṃ pāteyya, netthāraṃ vatteyya, saṅgho taṃ kammaṃ paṭippassambheyyāti.

If discontent arises in the co-resident pupil, the preceptor should remove him to another place, or have him removed, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If remorse arises in the co-resident pupil, the preceptor should dispel it, or have it dispelled, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If a wrong view arises in the co-resident pupil, the preceptor should make him relinquish it, or have it relinquished, or a Dhamma talk should be given to him. If the co-resident pupil has committed a serious offense and is deserving of probation, the preceptor should make an effort: ‘How, indeed, might the Saṅgha grant probation to the co-resident pupil?’ If the co-resident pupil is deserving of being sent back to the beginning, the preceptor should make an effort: ‘How, indeed, might the Saṅgha send the co-resident pupil back to the beginning?’ If the co-resident pupil is deserving of penance, the preceptor should make an effort: ‘How, indeed, might the Saṅgha grant penance to the co-resident pupil?’ If the co-resident pupil is deserving of rehabilitation, the preceptor should make an effort: ‘How, indeed, might the Saṅgha rehabilitate the co-resident pupil?’ If the Saṅgha wishes to carry out a formal act against the co-resident pupil—be it an act of censure, subordination, banishment, reconciliation, or suspension—the preceptor should make an effort: ‘How, indeed, might the Saṅgha not carry out the formal act against the co-resident pupil, or how might it be modified to a lighter one?’ Or if a formal act has been carried out against him by the Saṅgha—be it an act of censure, subordination, banishment, reconciliation, or suspension—the preceptor should make an effort: ‘How, indeed, might the co-resident pupil conduct himself properly, humble himself, and undertake the conduct for rehabilitation, so that the Saṅgha might revoke that formal act?’

“Sace saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ dhovitabbaṃ hoti, upajjhāyena ācikkhitabbaṃ evaṃ dhoveyyāsīti[V 0.0060], ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ dhoviyethāti. Sace saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ kātabbaṃ [T 1.0098] hoti, upajjhāyena ācikkhitabbaṃ evaṃ kareyyāsīti, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ kariyethāti. Sace saddhivihārikassa rajanaṃ pacitabbaṃ hoti, upajjhāyena ācikkhitabbaṃ evaṃ paceyyāsīti, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saddhivihārikassa rajanaṃ paciyethāti. Sace saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ rajitabbaṃ hoti, upajjhāyena ācikkhitabbaṃ, evaṃ rajeyyāsīti, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saddhivihārikassa cīvaraṃ rajiyethāti. Cīvaraṃ rajantena sādhukaṃ samparivattakaṃ samparivattakaṃ rajitabbaṃ. Na ca acchinne theve pakkamitabbaṃ. Sace saddhivihāriko gilāno hoti, yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhātabbo, vuṭṭhānamassa āgametabba”nti.

If the co-resident pupil’s robe is to be washed, the preceptor should instruct him, saying, ‘Wash it in this way,’ or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How might the co-resident pupil’s robe be washed?’ If the co-resident pupil’s robe is to be made, the preceptor should instruct him, saying, ‘Make it in this way,’ or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How might the co-resident pupil’s robe be made?’ If dye is to be prepared for the co-resident pupil, the preceptor should instruct him, saying, ‘Prepare it in this way,’ or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How might dye be prepared for the co-resident pupil?’ If the co-resident pupil’s robe is to be dyed, the preceptor should instruct him, saying, ‘Dye it in this way,’ or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How might the co-resident pupil’s robe be dyed?’ When dyeing the robe, it should be dyed well, turning it over and over. One should not depart before the dripping has ceased. If the co-resident pupil is sick, he is to be attended to for as long as life lasts; his recovery is to be awaited.

Saddhivihārikavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The duties concerning the co-resident pupil are concluded.

17. Paṇāmitakathā

17. The Discourse on Dismissal

68. Tena [M 0.0068] kho pana samayena saddhivihārikā upajjhāyesu na sammā vattanti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma saddhivihārikā upajjhāyesu na sammā vattissantī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, saddhivihārikā upajjhāyesu na sammā vattantīti? Saccaṃ bhagavāti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma, bhikkhave, saddhivihārikā upajjhāyesu na sammā vattissantīti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, saddhivihārikena [P 1.0054] upajjhāyamhi na sammā vattitabbaṃ. Yo na sammā vatteyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti[T 1.0099]. Neva sammā vattanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, asammāvattantaṃ paṇāmetuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, paṇāmetabbo – “paṇāmemi ta”nti vā, “māyidha paṭikkamī”ti vā, “nīhara te pattacīvara”nti vā, “nāhaṃ tayā upaṭṭhātabbo”ti vā, kāyena viññāpeti, vācāya viññāpeti, kāyena vācāya viññāpeti, paṇāmito hoti saddhivihāriko; na kāyena viññāpeti, na vācāya viññāpeti, na kāyena vācāya viññāpeti, na paṇāmito hoti saddhivihārikoti.

68. Now at that time, co-resident pupils did not conduct themselves properly towards their preceptors. Those monks who were of few wishes… they complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly, saying: “How indeed can co-resident pupils not conduct themselves properly towards their preceptors?” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, monks, that co-resident pupils do not conduct themselves properly towards their preceptors?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, monks, can co-resident pupils not conduct themselves properly towards their preceptors?”… Having rebuked them… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, a co-resident pupil is to conduct himself properly towards his preceptor. For any who would not conduct himself properly, there is an offense of wrong conduct.” They still did not conduct themselves properly. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, the dismissal of one who does not conduct himself properly. And this, monks, is how he is to be dismissed: by saying, ‘I dismiss you,’ or ‘Do not return here,’ or ‘Take away your bowl and robes,’ or ‘I am not to be attended by you.’ When he makes it known by body, by speech, or by body and speech, the co-resident pupil is dismissed; when he does not make it known by body, by speech, or by body and speech, the co-resident pupil is not dismissed.”

Tena kho pana samayena saddhivihārikā paṇāmitā na khamāpenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, khamāpetunti. Neva khamāpenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[V 0.0061]. Na, bhikkhave, paṇāmitena na khamāpetabbo. Yo na khamāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, the dismissed co-resident pupils did not ask for forgiveness. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, that they ask for forgiveness.” Still, they did not ask for forgiveness. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, one who has been dismissed is to ask for forgiveness. For any who would not ask for forgiveness, there is an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena upajjhāyā khamāpiyamānā na khamanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, khamitunti. Neva khamanti. Saddhivihārikā pakkamantipi vibbhamantipi titthiyesupi saṅkamanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, khamāpiyamānena na khamitabbaṃ. Yo na khameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, preceptors, when being asked for forgiveness, would not forgive. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “O monks, I allow forgiveness.” Yet they would not forgive. The co-resident pupils departed, disrobed, or even went over to the adherents of other teachings. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “O monks, one who is being asked for forgiveness should not refuse to forgive. Whoever does not forgive incurs an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena upajjhāyā sammāvattantaṃ paṇāmenti, asammāvattantaṃ na paṇāmenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, sammāvattanto paṇāmetabbo. Yo paṇāmeyya[T 1.0100], āpatti dukkaṭassa[M 0.0069]. Na ca, bhikkhave, asammāvattanto na paṇāmetabbo. Yo na paṇāmeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, preceptors would dismiss one who behaves properly, but would not dismiss one who behaves improperly. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “O monks, one who behaves properly should not be dismissed. Whoever should dismiss such a one incurs an offense of wrong conduct. And, O monks, one who behaves improperly should indeed be dismissed. Whoever should not dismiss such a one incurs an offense of wrong conduct.”

“Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato saddhivihāriko paṇāmetabbo. Upajjhāyamhi nādhimattaṃ pemaṃ hoti, nādhimatto pasādo hoti, nādhimattā hirī hoti, nādhimatto gāravo hoti, nādhimattā bhāvanā hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saddhivihāriko paṇāmetabbo.

“O monks, a co-resident pupil endowed with five qualities is to be dismissed. He has no excessive affection for his preceptor, no excessive confidence, no excessive moral shame, no excessive respect, and no excessive development of loving-kindness. O monks, a co-resident pupil endowed with these five qualities is to be dismissed.”

“Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato saddhivihāriko na paṇāmetabbo. Upajjhāyamhi adhimattaṃ pemaṃ hoti, adhimatto pasādo hoti, adhimattā hirī hoti, adhimatto gāravo hoti, adhimattā bhāvanā hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saddhivihāriko na paṇāmetabbo.

“O monks, a co-resident pupil endowed with five qualities is not to be dismissed. He has excessive affection for his preceptor, excessive confidence, excessive moral shame, excessive respect, and excessive development of loving-kindness. O monks, a co-resident pupil endowed with these five qualities is not to be dismissed.”

“Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato saddhivihāriko alaṃ paṇāmetuṃ. Upajjhāyamhi [P 1.0055] nādhimattaṃ pemaṃ hoti, nādhimatto pasādo hoti, nādhimattā hirī hoti, nādhimattā gāravo hoti, nādhimattā bhāvanā hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saddhivihāriko alaṃ paṇāmetuṃ.

“O monks, a co-resident pupil endowed with five qualities is fit to be dismissed. He has no excessive affection for his preceptor, no excessive confidence, no excessive moral shame, no excessive respect, and no excessive development of loving-kindness. O monks, a co-resident pupil endowed with these five qualities is fit to be dismissed.”

“Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato saddhivihāriko nālaṃ paṇāmetuṃ. Upajjhāyamhi adhimattaṃ [V 0.0062] pemaṃ hoti, adhimatto pasādo hoti, adhimattā hirī hoti, adhimatto gāravo hoti, adhimattā bhāvanā hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato saddhivihāriko nālaṃ paṇāmetuṃ.

“O monks, a co-resident pupil endowed with five qualities is not fit to be dismissed. He has excessive affection for his preceptor, excessive confidence, excessive moral shame, excessive respect, and excessive development of loving-kindness. O monks, a co-resident pupil endowed with these five qualities is not fit to be dismissed.”

“Pañcahi[T 1.0101], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ saddhivihārikaṃ appaṇāmento upajjhāyo sātisāro hoti, paṇāmento anatisāro hoti. Upajjhāyamhi nādhimattaṃ pemaṃ hoti, nādhimatto pasādo hoti, nādhimattā hirī hoti, nādhimatto gāravo hoti, nādhimattā bhāvanā hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ [M 0.0070] saddhivihārikaṃ appaṇāmento upajjhāyo sātisāro hoti, paṇāmento anatisāro hoti.

“O monks, a preceptor who does not dismiss a co-resident pupil endowed with five qualities is blameworthy, but one who dismisses him is not blameworthy. He has no excessive affection for his preceptor, no excessive confidence, no excessive moral shame, no excessive respect, and no excessive development of loving-kindness. O monks, a preceptor who does not dismiss a co-resident pupil endowed with these five qualities is blameworthy, but one who dismisses him is not blameworthy.”

“Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ saddhivihārikaṃ paṇāmento upajjhāyo sātisāro hoti, appaṇāmento anatisāro hoti. Upajjhāyamhi adhimattaṃ pemaṃ hoti, adhimatto pasādo hoti, adhimattā hirī hoti, adhimatto gāravo hoti, adhimattā bhāvanā hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ saddhivihārikaṃ paṇāmento upajjhāyo sātisāro hoti, appaṇāmento anatisāro hotī”ti.

“O monks, a preceptor who dismisses a co-resident pupil endowed with five qualities is blameworthy, but one who does not dismiss him is not blameworthy. He has excessive affection for his preceptor, excessive confidence, excessive moral shame, excessive respect, and excessive development of loving-kindness. O monks, a preceptor who dismisses a co-resident pupil endowed with these five qualities is blameworthy, but one who does not dismiss him is not blameworthy.”

69. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro brāhmaṇo bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā pabbajjaṃ yāci. Taṃ bhikkhū na icchiṃsu pabbājetuṃ. So bhikkhūsu pabbajjaṃ alabhamāno kiso ahosi lūkho dubbaṇṇo uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajāto [T 1.0102] dhamanisanthatagatto. Addasā kho bhagavā taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ kisaṃ lūkhaṃ dubbaṇṇaṃ uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajātaṃ dhamanisanthatagattaṃ, disvāna bhikkhū āmantesi – “kiṃ nu kho so, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇo kiso lūkho dubbaṇṇo uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajāto dhamanisanthatagatto”ti? Eso, bhante, brāhmaṇo bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā pabbajjaṃ yāci. Taṃ bhikkhū na icchiṃsu pabbājetuṃ. So bhikkhūsu pabbajjaṃ alabhamāno kiso lūkho dubbaṇṇo uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajāto dhamanisanthatagattoti. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “ko nu kho, bhikkhave, tassa brāhmaṇassa adhikāraṃ sarasī”ti? Evaṃ vutte āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ahaṃ kho, bhante, tassa brāhmaṇassa adhikāraṃ sarāmī”ti. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, sāriputta, tassa brāhmaṇassa adhikāraṃ sarasī”ti? “Idha me, bhante, so brāhmaṇo rājagahe piṇḍāya carantassa kaṭacchubhikkhaṃ dāpesi. Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, tassa brāhmaṇassa adhikāraṃ [P 1.0056] sarāmī”ti. “Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta, kataññuno hi, sāriputta, sappurisā katavedino. Tena hi tvaṃ, sāriputta, taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ pabbājehi upasampādehī”ti[V 0.0063]. “Kathāhaṃ, bhante[T 1.0103], taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ pabbājemi upasampādemī”ti? Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – yā sā, bhikkhave, mayā tīhi saraṇagamanehi upasampadā anuññātā, taṃ ajjatagge paṭikkhipāmi. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ñatticatutthena kammena upasampādetuṃ [M 0.0071] upasampadaṃ (sī. syā.). Evañca pana, bhikkhave, upasampādetabbo. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

69. At that time, a certain brahmin approached the monks and requested the going forth. The monks were unwilling to give him the going forth. Unable to obtain the going forth from the monks, he became thin, haggard, of poor complexion, pale, with veins standing out all over his body. The Blessed One saw that brahmin—thin, haggard, of poor complexion, pale, with veins standing out all over his body—and having seen him, he addressed the monks: “Why, monks, is that brahmin so thin, haggard, of poor complexion, pale, with veins standing out all over his body?” “Venerable sir, this brahmin approached the monks and requested the going forth. The monks were unwilling to give him the going forth. Unable to obtain the going forth from the monks, he has become thin, haggard, of poor complexion, pale, with veins standing out all over his body.” Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks, who among you remembers a kindness done by that brahmin?” When this was said, Venerable Sāriputta said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I remember a kindness done by that brahmin.” “But what kindness do you remember, Sāriputta?” “Venerable sir, while I was wandering for alms in Rājagaha, this brahmin offered me a ladleful of alms-food. This, venerable sir, is the kindness I remember from that brahmin.” “Good, good, Sāriputta. For good people, Sāriputta, are grateful and acknowledge what has been done for them. Well then, Sāriputta, you should give the going forth to that brahmin and confer the higher ordination on him.” “But how, venerable sir, should I give him the going forth and confer the higher ordination on him?” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this connection, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: “Monks, the higher ordination that I allowed through the three refuges—from today onwards, I revoke that. I allow, monks, to confer the higher ordination by means of a formal act with a motion and three announcements. And monks, this is how one should be conferred the higher ordination. A competent and capable monk should inform the Sangha:

70. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeyya itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Esā ñatti.

70. “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination of the venerable so-and-so. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should confer higher ordination on so-and-so with so-and-so as preceptor. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeti itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa upasampadā itthannāmena upajjhāyena, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination under the venerable so-and-so. The Saṅgha confers higher ordination on so-and-so with so-and-so as preceptor. Whichever venerable one approves of the higher ordination of so-and-so with so-and-so as preceptor, he should be silent; whoever does not approve, he should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeti itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa upasampadā itthannāmena upajjhāyena, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya[T 1.0104].

For a second time I speak on this matter: Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination under the venerable so-and-so. The Saṅgha confers higher ordination on so-and-so with so-and-so as preceptor. Whichever venerable one approves of the higher ordination of so-and-so with so-and-so as preceptor, he should be silent; whoever does not approve, he should speak.

“Tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeti itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa upasampadā itthannāmena upajjhāyena, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

For a third time I speak on this matter: Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination under the venerable so-and-so. The Saṅgha confers higher ordination on so-and-so with so-and-so as preceptor. Whichever venerable one approves of the higher ordination of so-and-so with so-and-so as preceptor, he should be silent; whoever does not approve, he should speak.

“Upasampanno saṅghena itthannāmo itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

So-and-so has been conferred higher ordination by the Saṅgha with so-and-so as preceptor. It is approved by the Saṅgha; therefore, it is silent. Thus do I hold this.

71. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu upasampannasamanantarā anācāraṃ ācarati. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “māvuso, evarūpaṃ akāsi, netaṃ kappatī”ti. So evamāha – “nevāhaṃ āyasmante yāciṃ upasampādetha manti. Kissa maṃ tumhe ayācitā upasampāditthā”ti? [V 0.0064] Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[P 1.0057]. Na, bhikkhave, ayācitena upasampādetabbo[M 0.0072]. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yācitena upasampādetuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, yācitabbo. Tena upasampadāpekkhena saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “saṅghaṃ, bhante, upasampadaṃ yācāmi, ullumpatu maṃ, bhante, saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāyā”ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

71. Now at that time a certain monk, immediately after his higher ordination, behaved improperly. The monks said to him, 'Friend, do not act like this; this is not allowable.' He replied, 'I did not ask you venerable sirs to confer higher ordination on me. Why did you confer higher ordination on me without my asking?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, one who has not requested should not be given higher ordination. Whoever confers higher ordination on such a one commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, that higher ordination be given to one who has requested. And, monks, the request should be made in this way. That candidate for higher ordination should approach the Saṅgha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the monks, sit down squatting, raise his joined palms, and should speak thus: “Venerable sirs, I ask the Saṅgha for higher ordination. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha, out of compassion, raise me up.” The request should be made a second time. The request should be made a third time. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:'

72. “Suṇātu me, bhante[T 1.0105], saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho. Itthannāmo saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeyya itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Esā ñatti.

72. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination under the venerable so-and-so. So-and-so asks the Saṅgha for higher ordination with so-and-so as preceptor. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should confer higher ordination on so-and-so with so-and-so as preceptor. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho. Itthannāmo saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeti itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa upasampadā itthannāmena upajjhāyena, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This so-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination under the venerable so-and-so. So-and-so asks the Saṅgha for higher ordination with so-and-so as preceptor. The Saṅgha confers higher ordination on so-and-so with so-and-so as preceptor. To whichever venerable one the higher ordination of so-and-so with so-and-so as preceptor is agreeable, he should remain silent; he to whom it is not agreeable should speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe… tatiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi…pe….

For a second time I speak on this matter… For a third time I speak on this matter….

“Upasampanno saṅghena itthannāmo itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

So-and-so has been conferred higher ordination by the Saṅgha with so-and-so as preceptor. The Saṅgha approves; therefore, it is silent. Thus do I hold this.

73. Tena kho pana samayena rājagahe paṇītānaṃ bhattānaṃ bhattapaṭipāṭi aṭṭhitā adhiṭṭhitā (ka.) hoti. Atha kho aññatarassa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – “ime kho samaṇā sakyaputtiyā sukhasīlā sukhasamācārā, subhojanāni bhuñjitvā nivātesu sayanesu sayanti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ samaṇesu sakyaputtiyesu pabbajeyya”nti. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā pabbajjaṃ yāci. Taṃ bhikkhū pabbājesuṃ upasampādesuṃ. Tasmiṃ [T 1.0106] pabbajite bhattapaṭipāṭi khīyittha. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “ehi dāni, āvuso, piṇḍāya carissāmā”ti. So evamāha – “nāhaṃ, āvuso, etaṃkāraṇā pabbajito piṇḍāya carissāmīti. Sace me dassatha bhuñjissāmi[M 0.0073], no ce me dassatha vibbhamissāmī”ti. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, āvuso, udarassa kāraṇā pabbajito”ti[P 1.0058][V 0.0065]? “Evamāvuso”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – kathañhi nāma bhikkhu evaṃ svākkhāte dhammavinaye udarassa kāraṇā pabbajissatīti. Te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, udarassa kāraṇā pabbajitoti? Saccaṃ bhagavāti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… “kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, evaṃ svākkhāte dhammavinaye udarassa kāraṇā pabbajissasi. Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya pasannānaṃ vā bhiyyobhāvāya”…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, upasampādentena cattāro nissaye ācikkhituṃ – piṇḍiyālopabhojanaṃ nissāya pabbajjā, tattha te yāvajīvaṃ ussāho karaṇīyo; atirekalābho – saṅghabhattaṃ, uddesabhattaṃ, nimantanaṃ, salākabhattaṃ, pakkhikaṃ, uposathikaṃ, pāṭipadikaṃ. Paṃsukūlacīvaraṃ nissāya pabbajjā, tattha te yāvajīvaṃ ussāho karaṇīyo; atirekalābho – khomaṃ, kappāsikaṃ, koseyyaṃ, kambalaṃ, sāṇaṃ, bhaṅgaṃ. Rukkhamūlasenāsanaṃ nissāya pabbajjā, tattha te yāvajīvaṃ ussāho karaṇīyo; atirekalābho – vihāro[T 1.0107], aḍḍhayogo, pāsādo, hammiyaṃ, guhā. Pūtimuttabhesajjaṃ nissāya pabbajjā, tattha te yāvajīvaṃ ussāho karaṇīyo; atirekalābho – sappi, navanītaṃ, telaṃ, madhu, phāṇita”nti.

73. Now at that time in Rājagaha, a succession of offerings of choice foods was established. Then this thought occurred to a certain brahmin: ‘These recluses, the Sakyan sons, are of comfortable disposition and comfortable conduct. Having eaten good food, they sleep in beds sheltered from the wind. It would be good if I were to go forth among the recluses, the Sakyan sons.’ Then that brahmin approached the monks and requested the going forth. The monks gave him the going forth and conferred the higher ordination. When he had gone forth, the succession of meal offerings came to an end. The monks said: ‘Come now, friend, we shall go for alms-food.’ He said: ‘Friends, I did not go forth for this reason, to go for alms-food. If you give to me, I will eat; if you do not give to me, I will disrobe.’ ‘But friend, did you go forth for the sake of your belly?’ ‘Yes, friends.’ Those monks who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: ‘How indeed could a monk go forth in this well-proclaimed Dhamma and Discipline for the sake of the belly?’ Those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… ‘Is it true, monk, as is said, that you went forth for the sake of the belly?’ ‘It is true, Blessed One.’ The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… ‘How indeed could you, worthless man, go forth in this well-proclaimed Dhamma and Discipline for the sake of the belly? This, worthless man, is not for the confidence of the unconverted, nor for the increase of the converted…’ Having rebuked him… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: ‘Monks, I allow one who is conferring the higher ordination to declare the four requisites: The going forth depends on alms-food gathered in morsels; therein, you must make an effort for as long as life lasts. An extra allowance is: a meal for the Sangha, a designated meal, an invitation meal, a meal distributed by ticket, a fortnightly meal, an observance day meal, and a meal on the first day of the fortnight. The going forth depends on robes made from discarded rags; therein, you must make an effort for as long as life lasts. An extra allowance is: linen, cotton, silk, wool, hemp, and mixed-fabric cloth. The going forth depends on lodging at the foot of a tree; therein, you must make an effort for as long as life lasts. An extra allowance is: a monastery, a lean-to, a storied building, an upper-storey, and a cave. The going forth depends on medicine of fermented urine; therein, you must make an effort for as long as life lasts. An extra allowance is: ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, and molasses.’

Paṇāmitakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Expulsion is concluded.

Upajjhāyavattabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito pañcamo.

The fifth recitation section on the duties to a preceptor is concluded.

Pañcamabhāṇavāro

The fifth recitation section.

18. Ācariyavattakathā

18. The Discourse on the Duties to a Teacher

74. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro māṇavako bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā pabbajjaṃ yāci. Tassa bhikkhū paṭikacceva nissaye ācikkhiṃsu. So evamāha – “sace me, bhante, pabbajite nissaye ācikkheyyātha, abhirameyyāmahaṃ abhirameyyañcāhaṃ (sī.), abhirameyyaṃ svāhaṃ (ka.). Na dānāhaṃ, bhante, pabbajissāmi; jegucchā me nissayā [M 0.0074] paṭikūlā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, paṭikacceva nissayā ācikkhitabbā. Yo ācikkheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, upasampannasamanantarā nissaye ācikkhitunti.

74. Now at that time, a certain young man approached the monks and requested the going forth. The monks told him about the requisites beforehand. He said thus: 'Venerable sirs, if you were to tell me about the requisites after I have gone forth, I would be very pleased. But now, venerable sirs, I will not go forth; to me, the requisites are disgusting and repulsive.' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, the requisites are not to be told beforehand. Whoever should tell them, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, the requisites to be told immediately after the higher ordination.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū duvaggenapi tivaggenapi gaṇena upasampādenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ [V 0.0066] ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, ūnadasavaggena gaṇena upasampādetabbo. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dasavaggena vā atirekadasavaggena vā gaṇena upasampādetunti[P 1.0059].

Now at that time, monks were conferring the higher ordination with a group of two and with a group of three. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, the higher ordination is not to be conferred by a group of less than ten. Whoever should confer it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, the higher ordination to be conferred by a group of ten or by a group of more than ten.'

75. Tena [T 1.0108] kho pana samayena bhikkhū ekavassāpi duvassāpi saddhivihārikaṃ upasampādenti. Āyasmāpi upaseno vaṅgantaputto ekavasso saddhivihārikaṃ upasampādesi. So vassaṃvuṭṭho duvasso ekavassaṃ saddhivihārikaṃ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Āciṇṇaṃ kho panetaṃ buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ āgantukehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ paṭisammodituṃ. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ upasenaṃ vaṅgantaputtaṃ etadavoca – “kacci, bhikkhu, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kacci tvaṃ appakilamathena addhānaṃ āgato”ti? “Khamanīyaṃ, bhagavā, yāpanīyaṃ, bhagavā. Appakilamathena mayaṃ, bhante, addhānaṃ āgatā”ti. Jānantāpi tathāgatā pucchanti, jānantāpi na pucchanti, kālaṃ viditvā pucchanti, kālaṃ viditvā na pucchanti; atthasaṃhitaṃ tathāgatā pucchanti; no anatthasaṃhitaṃ. Anatthasaṃhite setughāto tathāgatānaṃ. Dvīhi ākārehi buddhā bhagavanto bhikkhū paṭipucchanti – dhammaṃ vā desessāma, sāvakānaṃ vā sikkhāpadaṃ paññapessāmāti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ upasenaṃ vaṅgantaputtaṃ etadavoca – “kativassosi tvaṃ, bhikkhū”ti? “Duvassohaṃ, bhagavā”ti. “Ayaṃ pana bhikkhu kativasso”ti? “Ekavasso, bhagavā”ti. “Kiṃ tāyaṃ bhikkhu hotī”ti? “Saddhivihāriko me, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ, moghapurisa, ananulomikaṃ appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi [T 1.0109] nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, aññehi ovadiyo anusāsiyo aññaṃ ovadituṃ anusāsituṃ maññissasi. Atilahuṃ kho tvaṃ, moghapurisa, bāhullāya āvatto, yadidaṃ gaṇabandhikaṃ. Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya pasannānaṃ [M 0.0075] vā bhiyyobhāvāya”…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, ūnadasavassena upasampādetabbo. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dasavassena vā atirekadasavassena vā upasampādetu”nti.

75. At that time, monks of one rains-residence and of two rains-residences were giving the higher ordination to a co-resident. The Venerable Upasena Vaṅgantaputta, being of one rains-residence, also gave the higher ordination to a co-resident. Having completed the rains-residence, being of two rains-residences, he took his co-resident of one rains-residence and approached the Blessed One. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. Now, it is the custom of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, to exchange friendly greetings with incoming monks. Then the Blessed One said this to the Venerable Upasena Vaṅgantaputta: ‘Is it tolerable for you, monk? Is it manageable for you? Have you come on a long journey with little fatigue?’ ‘It is tolerable, Blessed One. It is manageable, Blessed One. We, venerable sir, have come on a long journey with little fatigue.’ The Tathāgatas ask even when knowing; they do not ask even when knowing. Knowing the time, they ask; knowing the time, they do not ask. The Tathāgatas ask what is connected with the goal, not what is unconnected with the goal. For the Tathāgatas, the causeway to what is unconnected with the goal has been destroyed. The Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, question monks for two reasons: ‘We will teach the Dhamma,’ or ‘We will lay down a training rule for the disciples.’ Then the Blessed One said this to the Venerable Upasena Vaṅgantaputta: ‘How many rains-residences are you, monk?’ ‘I am of two rains-residences, Blessed One.’ ‘And this monk, how many rains-residences is he?’ ‘He is of one rains-residence, Blessed One.’ ‘What is this monk to you?’ ‘He is my co-resident, Blessed One.’ The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him: ‘It is unsuitable, worthless man, improper, unseemly, not befitting a recluse, not allowable, not to be done. How indeed, worthless man, could you, who should be advised and instructed by others, think to advise and instruct another? Too quickly, worthless man, you have turned to abundance, that is, to forming a faction. This, worthless man, is not for inspiring confidence in the uninspired, nor for increasing the confidence of the inspired...’ Having rebuked him... having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: ‘Monks, one who has less than ten rains-residences should not give the higher ordination. Whoever should give the higher ordination, commits an offence of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, one who has ten rains-residences or more than ten rains-residences to give the higher ordination.’”

76. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū – dasavassamhā dasavassamhāti – bālā abyattā upasampādenti. Dissanti upajjhāyā bālā, saddhivihārikā paṇḍitā. Dissanti upajjhāyā abyattā, saddhivihārikā byattā. Dissanti upajjhāyā appassutā, saddhivihārikā bahussutā. Dissanti upajjhāyā duppaññā, saddhivihārikā [P 1.0060] paññavanto. Aññataropi aññatitthiyapubbo [V 0.0067] upajjhāyena sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno upajjhāyassa vādaṃ āropetvā taṃyeva titthāyatanaṃ saṅkami. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – kathañhi nāma bhikkhū – dasavassamhā dasavassamhāti – bālā abyattā upasampādessanti. Dissanti upajjhāyā bālā saddhivihārikā paṇḍitā, dissanti upajjhāyā abyattā [T 1.0110] saddhivihārikā byattā, dissanti upajjhāyā appassutā saddhivihārikā bahussutā, dissanti upajjhāyā duppaññā, saddhivihārikā paññavantoti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū – dasavassamhā dasavassamhāti – bālā abyattā upasampādenti. Dissanti upajjhāyā bālā, saddhivihārikā paṇḍitā, dissanti upajjhāyā abyattā saddhivihārikā byattā, dissanti upajjhāyā appassutā, saddhivihārikā bahussutā, dissanti upajjhāyā duppaññā, saddhivihārikā paññavanto”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā – dasavassamhā dasavassamhāti – bālā abyattā upasampādessanti. Dissanti upajjhāyā bālā, saddhivihārikā paṇḍitā, dissanti upajjhāyā abyattā saddhivihārikā byattā, dissanti upajjhāyā appassutā, saddhivihārikā bahussutā, dissanti upajjhāyā duppaññā, saddhivihārikā paññavanto. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, bālena abyattena upasampādetabbo. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena dasavassena vā atirekadasavassena vā upasampādetu”nti.

76. Now at that time, monks—thinking, ‘We are of ten rains-residences, we are of ten rains-residences’—were giving the higher ordination while being ignorant and incompetent. There were seen preceptors who were ignorant, while their co-residents were wise. There were seen preceptors who were incompetent, while their co-residents were competent. There were seen preceptors who were of little learning, while their co-residents were of great learning. There were seen preceptors who were of poor wisdom, while their co-residents were wise. A certain one who had formerly belonged to another sect, when being instructed in accordance with the Dhamma by his preceptor, criticized his preceptor's teaching and returned to that very sectarian fold. Those monks who were of few wishes… they criticized, condemned, and disparaged them, saying: ‘How can monks—thinking, “We are of ten rains-residences, we are of ten rains-residences”—give the higher ordination while being ignorant and incompetent? There are seen preceptors who are ignorant, while their co-residents are wise; preceptors who are incompetent, while their co-residents are competent; preceptors who are of little learning, while their co-residents are of great learning; preceptors who are of poor wisdom, while their co-residents are wise.’ Then those monks informed the Blessed One of this matter. ‘Is it true, monks, as is said, that monks—thinking, “We are of ten rains-residences, we are of ten rains-residences”—are giving the higher ordination while being ignorant and incompetent? That there are seen preceptors who are ignorant, while their co-residents are wise; preceptors who are incompetent, while their co-residents are competent; preceptors who are of little learning, while their co-residents are of great learning; preceptors who are of poor wisdom, while their co-residents are wise?’ ‘It is true, Blessed One.’ The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… ‘How can those worthless men, monks—thinking, “We are of ten rains-residences, we are of ten rains-residences”—give the higher ordination while being ignorant and incompetent? How can there be seen preceptors who are ignorant, while their co-residents are wise; preceptors who are incompetent, while their co-residents are competent; preceptors who are of little learning, while their co-residents are of great learning; preceptors who are of poor wisdom, while their co-residents are wise? This, monks, is not for inspiring confidence in the uninspired…’ After rebuking them… having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: ‘Monks, the higher ordination should not be given by one who is ignorant and incompetent. Whoever should give it, commits an offence of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, the higher ordination to be given by a monk who is competent, capable, and of ten rains-residences or more than ten rains-residences.’”

77. Tena [M 0.0076] kho pana samayena bhikkhū upajjhāyesu pakkantesupi vibbhantesupi [T 1.0111] kālaṅkatesupi pakkhasaṅkantesupi anācariyakā anovadiyamānā ananusāsiyamānā dunnivatthā duppārutā anākappasampannā piṇḍāya caranti, manussānaṃ bhuñjamānānaṃ uparibhojanepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmenti, uparikhādanīyepi – uparisāyanīyepi – uparipānīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmenti; sāmaṃ sūpampi odanampi viññāpetvā bhuñjanti; bhattaggepi uccāsaddā mahāsaddā viharanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā dunnivatthā duppārutā anākappasampannā piṇḍāya carissanti; manussānaṃ bhuñjamānānaṃ uparibhojanepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmessanti, uparikhādanīyepi – uparisāyanīyepi – uparipānīyepi uttiṭṭhapattaṃ upanāmessanti; sāmaṃ sūpampi odanampi viññāpetvā bhuñjissanti; bhattaggepi uccāsaddā mahāsaddā viharissanti, seyyathāpi brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇabhojane”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ [V 0.0068] …pe… atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave…pe… saccaṃ, bhagavāti…pe… vigarahitvā [T 1.0112] dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

77. Now at that time, when their preceptors had gone to another place, had disrobed, had passed away, or had gone over to another faction, the monks, being without a teacher, unadmonished, and uninstructed, went for alms poorly dressed, improperly robed, and lacking in proper deportment. While people were eating, they held out their alms bowl over the food; they held out their alms bowl over the hard food, over the soft food, and over the drinks. They themselves asked for curry and rice and ate them. In the refectory, they dwelt making loud and great noises. People complained, despised, and spread ill-repute, saying: “How can these ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, go for alms poorly dressed, improperly robed, and lacking in proper deportment? While people are eating, they hold out their alms bowl over the food; they hold out their alms bowl over the hard food, over the soft food, and over the drinks. They themselves ask for curry and rice and eat them. In the refectory, they dwell making loud and great noises, just like brahmins at a brahmin feast!” The monks heard those people complaining, despising, and spreading ill-repute… Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, is it true, as is said…?” “It is true, Blessed One.” … Having rebuked them and given a talk on the Dhamma, the Blessed One addressed the monks:

“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ācariyaṃ. Ācariyo, bhikkhave, antevāsikamhi puttacittaṃ upaṭṭhāpessati, antevāsiko ācariyamhi pitucittaṃ upaṭṭhāpessati. Evaṃ te aññamaññaṃ sagāravā sappatissā sabhāgavuttino viharantā imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ viruḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissanti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dasavassaṃ nissāya vatthuṃ, dasavassena nissayaṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, ācariyo gahetabbo. Ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘ācariyo me, bhante, hohi, āyasmato nissāya vacchāmi; ācariyo me, bhante, hohi, āyasmato nissāya vacchāmi; ācariyo me, bhante, hohi, āyasmato [P 1.0061] nissāya vacchāmī’ti. ‘Sāhūti’ vā ‘lahūti’ vā ‘opāyika’nti vā ‘patirūpa’nti vā ‘pāsādikena sampādehī’ti vā kāyena viññāpeti, vācāya viññāpeti, kāyena vācāya viññāpeti, gahito hoti ācariyo; na kāyena viññāpeti, na vācāya viññāpeti, na kāyena vācāya viññāpeti, na gahito hoti ācariyo.

“Monks, I allow a teacher. The teacher, monks, shall establish the thought of a son towards the resident pupil, and the resident pupil shall establish the thought of a father towards the teacher. Thus, living with mutual respect, deference, and with a shared way of life, they will attain growth, increase, and abundance in this Dhamma and Discipline. Monks, I allow living in dependence on a bhikkhu of ten years’ standing, and for a bhikkhu of ten years’ standing to give dependence. And, monks, a teacher should be accepted in this way: having arranged the upper robe over one shoulder, bowed at the feet, sat in a squatting position, and raised the joined palms, one should say thus: ‘Venerable sir, be my teacher; I will live in dependence on the venerable one. Venerable sir, be my teacher; I will live in dependence on the venerable one. Venerable sir, be my teacher; I will live in dependence on the venerable one.’ If he indicates by body, or by speech, or by both body and speech, saying, ‘Good,’ or ‘It is not a burden,’ or ‘It is suitable,’ or ‘It is proper,’ or ‘Accomplish it with inspiring conduct,’ then the teacher is accepted. If he does not indicate by body, nor by speech, nor by both body and speech, then the teacher is not accepted.”

78. cūḷava. 380 ādayo “Antevāsikena[M 0.0077], bhikkhave, ācariyamhi sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā –

78. “Monks, a resident pupil should conduct himself properly towards the teacher. Herein, this is the proper conduct:”

“Kālasseva uṭṭhāya upāhanaṃ omuñcitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā dantakaṭṭhaṃ dātabbaṃ, mukhodakaṃ dātabbaṃ, āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Sace yāgu hoti, bhājanaṃ dhovitvā yāgu upanāmetabbā[T 1.0113]. Yāguṃ pītassa udakaṃ datvā bhājanaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena dhovitvā paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Ācariyamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti, so deso sammajjitabbo.

“Having risen early, one should take off one's sandals, arrange the upper robe over one shoulder, and offer a tooth-stick. Water for the face should be given, and a seat should be prepared. If there is gruel, the bowl should be washed and the gruel offered. After the gruel has been drunk, water should be given, and the bowl should be received back. Holding it low, one should wash it well without scraping it on the ground and put it away. When the teacher has risen, the seat should be removed. If that place has rubbish, it should be swept.”

“Sace ācariyo gāmaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, kāyabandhanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo dātabbā, dhovitvā patto sodako dātabbo. Sace ācariyo pacchāsamaṇaṃ ākaṅkhati, timaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādentena parimaṇḍalaṃ nivāsetvā kāyabandhanaṃ bandhitvā saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo pārupitvā gaṇṭhikaṃ paṭimuñcitvā dhovitvā [V 0.0069] pattaṃ gahetvā ācariyassa pacchāsamaṇena hotabbaṃ. Nātidūre gantabbaṃ, nāccāsanne gantabbaṃ, pattapariyāpannaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Na ācariyassa bhaṇamānassa antarantarā kathā opātetabbā. Ācariyo āpattisāmantā bhaṇamāno nivāretabbo.

“If the teacher wishes to enter the village, the lower robe for the village should be given, the lower robe for the monastery should be received, the waistband should be given, the double-layered robes should be given folded, and the bowl should be given, washed and with water. If the teacher desires an attendant monk, one should become the teacher's attendant monk by covering the three circles, wearing the lower robe evenly all around, fastening the waistband, folding the double-layered robes and putting them on, fastening the clasp, and taking the washed bowl. One should not go too far away, nor too near. One should receive the alms-bowl and its contents. One should not interrupt with speech while the teacher is speaking. The teacher, when speaking of what is close to an offense, should be prevented.”

“Nivattantena paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ, paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Sace cīvaraṃ sinnaṃ hoti, muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbaṃ, na ca uṇhe cīvaraṃ nidahitabbaṃ. Cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ. Cīvaraṃ saṅgharantena caturaṅgulaṃ kaṇṇaṃ ussāretvā cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ – mā majjhe bhaṅgo ahosīti. Obhoge kāyabandhanaṃ kātabbaṃ.

“Upon returning, having come back first, a seat should be prepared; water for the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet should be set down nearby. Having gone out to meet him, the bowl and robes should be received. The lower robe for the monastery should be given; the lower robe for the village should be received. If the robe is damp with sweat, it should be aired in the heat for a moment, but the robe should not be left in the heat. The robe should be folded. When folding the robe, leaving a border of four finger-widths, the robe should be folded, thinking, 'Let there not be a crease in the middle.' The waistband should be placed within the fold.”

“Sace piṇḍapāto hoti[T 1.0114], ācariyo ca bhuñjitukāmo hoti, udakaṃ datvā piṇḍapāto upanāmetabbo. Ācariyo pānīyena pucchitabbo. Bhuttāvissa udakaṃ datvā pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena dhovitvā vodakaṃ katvā muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbo, na ca uṇhe patto nidahitabbo. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā patto nikkhipitabbo. Na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto [M 0.0078] nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ vā pamajjitvā pārato antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Ācariyamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti, so deso sammajjitabbo.

If there is almsfood and the teacher wishes to eat, having given water, the almsfood should be presented. The teacher should be asked about drinking water. When he has eaten, having given water and received the bowl, having lowered it and washed it carefully without scraping it on the ground, having made it free of water, it should be dried in the sun for a moment. And the bowl should not be left in the sun for a long time. The bowl and robe should be put away. When putting away the bowl, taking the bowl with one hand and feeling under the bed or under the chair with the other hand, the bowl should be put away. And the bowl should not be put away on uncovered ground. When putting away the robe, taking the robe with one hand and wiping the robe-pole or the robe-rope with the other hand, making a fold on the near side with the end from the far side, the robe should be put away. When the teacher has risen, the seat should be put away; the foot-washing water, the footstool, and the potsherd for rubbing the feet should be put away. If that place has rubbish, that place should be swept.

“Sace ācariyo nahāyitukāmo hoti, nahānaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace sītena attho hoti, sītaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace uṇhena attho hoti, uṇhaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ.

If the teacher wishes to bathe, bathing water should be prepared. If cool water is needed, cool water should be prepared. If hot water is needed, hot water should be prepared.

“Sace ācariyo jantāgharaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, cuṇṇaṃ sannetabbaṃ, mattikā temetabbā, jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya ācariyassa piṭṭhito piṭṭhito gantvā jantāgharapīṭhaṃ datvā cīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, cuṇṇaṃ dātabbaṃ, mattikā dātabbā. Sace ussahati, jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Jantāgharaṃ pavisantena [T 1.0115] mattikāya mukhaṃ makkhetvā purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Na there bhikkhū anupakhajja nisīditabbaṃ. Na navā bhikkhū āsanena paṭibāhitabbā. Jantāghare ācariyassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Jantāgharā nikkhamantena [V 0.0070] jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharā nikkhamitabbaṃ.

If the teacher wishes to enter the steam room, bathing powder should be kneaded, and clay should be moistened. Taking the steam room stool, one should go right behind the teacher, give him the stool, and after receiving his robe, it should be placed in a suitable place. Bathing powder should be given, and clay should be given. If one is able, one should enter the steam room. When entering the steam room, one should smear one's face with clay, cover oneself in front and in back, and then enter the steam room. One should not sit down encroaching upon the elder bhikkhus. Junior bhikkhus should not be debarred from a seat. In the steam room, service should be done for the teacher. When leaving the steam room, one should take the steam room stool, cover oneself in front and in back, and then leave the steam room.

“Udakepi ācariyassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Nahātena paṭhamataraṃ uttaritvā attano gattaṃ vodakaṃ katvā nivāsetvā ācariyassa gattato udakaṃ pamajjitabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saṅghāṭi dātabbā, jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ. Ācariyo pānīyena pucchitabbo. Sace uddisāpetukāmo hoti, uddisāpetabbo. Sace paripucchitukāmo hoti, paripucchitabbo.

In the bathing place also, service should be done for the teacher. Having bathed, one should emerge from the water first, make one's own body dry, put on one's lower robe, and then wipe the water from the teacher’s body. The lower robe should be given, and the outer robe should be given. Taking the steam room stool, one should arrive first, prepare the seat, and place nearby water for the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet. The teacher should be asked about drinking water. If he wishes to teach the recitation, he should be prompted for the recitation. If he wishes to be questioned, he should be questioned.

“Yasmiṃ vihāre ācariyo viharati, sace so vihāro uklāpo hoti, sace ussahati, sodhetabbo. Vihāraṃ sodhentena paṭhamaṃ pattacīvaraṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; bhisibibbohanaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; mañco nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo; pīṭhaṃ nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena [M 0.0079] kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; mañcapaṭipādakā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbā; kheḷamallako nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo[T 1.0116]; apassenaphalakaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; bhūmattharaṇaṃ yathāpaññattaṃ sallakkhetvā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Sace vihāre santānakaṃ hoti, ullokā paṭhamaṃ ohāretabbaṃ, ālokasandhikaṇṇabhāgā pamajjitabbā. Sace gerukaparikammakatā bhitti kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace kāḷavaṇṇakatā bhūmi kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace akatā hoti bhūmi, udakena paripphositvā sammajjitabbā – mā vihāro rajena uhaññīti. Saṅkāraṃ vicinitvā ekamantaṃ chaḍḍetabbaṃ.

In the dwelling where the teacher resides, if the dwelling is untidy, and one is capable, it should be cleaned. When cleaning the dwelling, first the bowl and robe should be taken out and set aside. The sitting mat and spread should be taken out and set aside. The mattress and bolster should be taken out and set aside. The bed should be lowered carefully, without scraping or knocking against the doorposts, taken out, and set aside. The stool should be lowered carefully, without scraping or knocking against the doorposts, taken out, and set aside. The bed legs should be taken out and set aside. The spittoon should be taken out and set aside. The backrest should be taken out and set aside. The floor covering should be inspected according to the arrangement, taken up, and set aside. If the dwelling has cobwebs, they should first be removed from above. The corners of the window openings should be wiped. If the walls, treated with red ochre, are mildewed, a cloth should be moistened and wrung out to wipe them. If the floor, treated with black color, is mildewed, a cloth should be moistened and wrung out to wipe it. If the floor is untreated, it should be sprinkled with water and swept—lest the dwelling be soiled with dust. Rubbish should be collected and discarded to one side.

“Bhūmattharaṇaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Mañcapaṭipādakā otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbā. Mañco otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbo. Pīṭhaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Bhisibibbohanaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ.
