Kheḷamallako [V 0.0071] otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbo[T 1.0117]. Apassenaphalakaṃ otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbaṃ. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā patto nikkhipitabbo. Na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ vā pamajjitvā pārato antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ.

The ground covering, having been aired in the sun, cleaned, and shaken out, should be brought back and laid out as it was before. The legs of the couch, having been aired in the sun and wiped, should be brought back and placed in their usual place. The couch, having been aired in the sun, cleaned, and shaken out, should be lowered carefully, brought back without scraping on the ground and without striking the door-leaf or door-post, and laid out as it was before. The chair, having been aired in the sun, cleaned, and shaken out, should be lowered carefully, brought back without scraping on the ground and without striking the door-leaf or door-post, and laid out as it was before. The mattress and pillow, having been aired in the sun, cleaned, and shaken out, should be brought back and laid out as they were before. The sitting-cloth cover, having been aired in the sun, cleaned, and shaken out, should be brought back and laid out as it was before. The spittoon, having been aired in the sun and wiped, should be brought back and placed in its usual place. The leaning-board, having been aired in the sun and wiped, should be brought back and placed in its usual place. The bowl and robes should be put down. When putting down the bowl, one should take the bowl with one hand, feel under the couch or chair with the other hand, and then put the bowl down. The bowl should not be put down on the bare ground. When putting down the robe, one should take the robe with one hand, wipe the robe-bamboo or robe-rope with the other hand, and then, making a fold on the near side with the end on the far side, place the robe upon it.

“Sace puratthimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, puratthimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace pacchimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, pacchimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace uttarā sarajā vātā vāyanti, uttarā vātapānā thaketabbā[M 0.0080]. Sace dakkhiṇā sarajā vātā vāyanti, dakkhiṇā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace sītakālo hoti, divā vātapānā vivaritabbā, rattiṃ thaketabbā. Sace uṇhakālo hoti, divā vātapānā thaketabbā, rattiṃ vivaritabbā.

If dusty winds blow from the east, the eastern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the west, the western windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the north, the northern windows should be closed. If dusty winds blow from the south, the southern windows should be closed. If it is the cold season, the windows should be opened during the day and closed at night. If it is the hot season, the windows should be closed during the day and opened at night.

“Sace pariveṇaṃ uklāpaṃ hoti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ. Sace koṭṭhako uklāpo hoti, koṭṭhako sammajjitabbo. Sace upaṭṭhānasālā uklāpā hoti, upaṭṭhānasālā sammajjitabbā. Sace aggisālā uklāpā hoti, aggisālā sammajjitabbā. Sace vaccakuṭi uklāpā hoti, vaccakuṭi sammajjitabbā. Sace pānīyaṃ na hoti, pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace paribhojanīyaṃ na hoti, paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ[T 1.0118]. Sace ācamanakumbhiyaṃ udakaṃ na hoti, ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ.

If the enclosure is dirty, the enclosure should be swept. If the gatehouse is dirty, the gatehouse should be swept. If the service hall is dirty, the service hall should be swept. If the fire-hall is dirty, the fire-hall should be swept. If the toilet is dirty, the toilet should be swept. If there is no drinking water, drinking water should be provided. If there is no water for use, water for use should be provided. If there is no water in the rinsing pot, water should be poured into the rinsing pot.

“Sace ācariyassa anabhirati uppannā hoti, antevāsikena vūpakāsetabbo, vūpakāsāpetabbo, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace ācariyassa kukkuccaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, antevāsikena vinodetabbaṃ, vinodāpetabbaṃ, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace ācariyassa diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti, antevāsikena vivecetabbaṃ, vivecāpetabbaṃ, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace ācariyo garudhammaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti parivāsāraho, antevāsikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho ācariyassa parivāsaṃ dadeyyāti. Sace ācariyo mūlāya paṭikassanāraho hoti, antevāsikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho ācariyaṃ mūlāya paṭikasseyyāti. Sace ācariyo mānattāraho hoti, antevāsikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho ācariyassa mānattaṃ dadeyyāti. Sace ācariyo abbhānāraho hoti, antevāsikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho ācariyaṃ abbheyyāti[V 0.0072]. Sace saṅgho ācariyassa kammaṃ kattukāmo hoti, tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ vā, antevāsikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho ācariyassa kammaṃ na kareyya, lahukāya vā pariṇāmeyyāti. Kataṃ vā panassa hoti saṅghena kammaṃ, tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ [M 0.0081][T 1.0119] vā ukkhepanīyaṃ vā, antevāsikena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho ācariyo sammā vatteyya, lomaṃ pāteyya, netthāraṃ vatteyya, saṅgho taṃ kammaṃ paṭippassambheyyāti.

If dissatisfaction arises in the teacher, the student should pacify him, have him pacified by another, or give him a Dhamma talk. If remorse arises in the teacher, the student should dispel it, have it dispelled by another, or give him a Dhamma talk. If a wrong view arises in the teacher, the student should resolve it, have it resolved by another, or give him a Dhamma talk. If the teacher has committed a serious offense deserving probation, the student should make an effort, thinking: ‘How might the Saṅgha grant the teacher probation?’ If the teacher deserves to be sent back to the beginning of his probation period, the student should make an effort, thinking: ‘How might the Saṅgha send the teacher back to the beginning?’ If the teacher deserves penance, the student should make an effort, thinking: ‘How might the Saṅgha grant the teacher penance?’ If the teacher deserves rehabilitation, the student should make an effort, thinking: ‘How might the Saṅgha rehabilitate the teacher?’ If the Saṅgha wishes to carry out a formal act against the teacher—whether of censure, subordination, banishment, reconciliation, or suspension—the student should make an effort, thinking: ‘How might the Saṅgha not carry out a formal act against the teacher, or how might it be changed to a lighter one?’ If a formal act has been carried out against the teacher by the Saṅgha—whether of censure, subordination, banishment, reconciliation, or suspension—the student should make an effort, thinking: ‘How might the teacher behave properly, humble himself, and conduct himself for his deliverance from that penalty, so that the Saṅgha might rescind that formal act?’

“Sace ācariyassa cīvaraṃ dhovitabbaṃ hoti, antevāsikena dhovitabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho ācariyassa cīvaraṃ dhoviyethāti. Sace ācariyassa cīvaraṃ kātabbaṃ hoti, antevāsikena kātabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho ācariyassa cīvaraṃ kariyethāti. Sace ācariyassa rajanaṃ pacitabbaṃ hoti, antevāsikena pacitabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho ācariyassa rajanaṃ paciyethāti. Sace ācariyassa cīvaraṃ rajitabbaṃ hoti, antevāsikena rajitabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho ācariyassa cīvaraṃ rajiyethāti. Cīvaraṃ rajantena sādhukaṃ samparivattakaṃ samparivattakaṃ rajitabbaṃ, na ca acchinne theve pakkamitabbaṃ.

If the teacher’s robe is to be washed, it should be washed by the resident pupil, or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How indeed might the teacher’s robe be washed?’ If the teacher’s robe is to be made, it should be made by the resident pupil, or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How indeed might the teacher’s robe be made?’ If dye for the teacher is to be boiled, it should be boiled by the resident pupil, or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How indeed might the dye for the teacher be boiled?’ If the teacher’s robe is to be dyed, it should be dyed by the resident pupil, or an effort should be made, thinking: ‘How indeed might the teacher’s robe be dyed?’ When dyeing the robe, it should be dyed well, turning it over and over again, and one should not depart before the dripping of the dye has ceased.

“Na ācariyaṃ anāpucchā ekaccassa patto dātabbo, na ekaccassa patto paṭiggahetabbo; na ekaccassa cīvaraṃ dātabbaṃ; na ekaccassa cīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ; na ekaccassa parikkhāro dātabbo; na ekaccassa parikkhāro paṭiggahetabbo; na ekaccassa kesā chedetabbā; na ekaccena kesā chedāpetabbā; na ekaccassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ; na ekaccena parikammaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ; na ekaccassa veyyāvacco kātabbo; na ekaccena veyyāvacco kārāpetabbo; na ekaccassa pacchāsamaṇena [T 1.0120] hotabbaṃ; na ekacco pacchāsamaṇo ādātabbo; na ekaccassa piṇḍapāto nīharitabbo; na ekaccena piṇḍapāto nīharāpetabbo. Na ācariyaṃ anāpucchā gāmo pavisitabbo, na susānaṃ gantabbaṃ, na disā pakkamitabbā. Sace ācariyo gilāno hoti, yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhātabbo, vuṭṭhānamassa āgametabba”nti.

Without asking the teacher, a bowl should not be given to a certain person, nor should a bowl be received from a certain person; a robe should not be given to a certain person, nor should a robe be received from a certain person; a requisite should not be given to a certain person, nor should a requisite be received from a certain person; the hair of a certain person should not be cut, nor should one’s own hair be caused to be cut by a certain person; a personal service should not be performed for a certain person, nor should a personal service be caused to be performed by a certain person; a duty should not be performed for a certain person, nor should a duty be caused to be performed by a certain person; one should not become an attendant for a certain person, nor should a certain person be taken as an attendant; almsfood should not be brought for a certain person, nor should one’s own almsfood be caused to be brought by a certain person. Without asking the teacher, a village should not be entered, a charnel ground should not be gone to, nor should one depart for another region. If the teacher is sick, he should be attended to for as long as life lasts, and his recovery should be awaited.

Ācariyavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The duties towards a teacher are concluded.

19. Antevāsikavattakathā

19. The Discourse on the Duties towards a Resident Pupil

79. cūḷava. 381-382 “Ācariyena[V 0.0073], bhikkhave, antevāsikamhi sammā vattitabbaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanā –

79. Monks, a teacher should conduct himself properly towards his pupil. Herein is the proper conduct:

“Ācariyena[M 0.0082], bhikkhave, antevāsiko saṅgahetabbo anuggahetabbo uddesena paripucchāya ovādena anusāsaniyā. Sace ācariyassa patto hoti, antevāsikassa patto na hoti, ācariyena antevāsikassa patto dātabbo, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho antevāsikassa patto uppajjiyethāti. Sace ācariyassa cīvaraṃ hoti, antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ na hoti, ācariyena antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ dātabbaṃ, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ uppajjiyethāti. Sace ācariyassa parikkhāro hoti, antevāsikassa parikkhāro na hoti, ācariyena antevāsikassa parikkhāro dātabbo, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho antevāsikassa parikkhāro uppajjiyethāti.

A teacher, monks, should support and assist his pupil with instruction, questioning, advice, and admonition. If the teacher has a bowl but the pupil does not, the teacher should give a bowl to the pupil, or an effort should be made, thinking, ‘How indeed might a bowl arise for the pupil?’ If the teacher has a robe but the pupil does not, the teacher should give a robe to the pupil, or an effort should be made, thinking, ‘How indeed might a robe arise for the pupil?’ If the teacher has requisites but the pupil does not, the teacher should give requisites to the pupil, or an effort should be made, thinking, ‘How indeed might requisites arise for the pupil?’

“Sace antevāsiko gilāno hoti, kālasseva uṭṭhāya dantakaṭṭhaṃ dātabbaṃ, mukhodakaṃ dātabbaṃ, āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Sace yāgu hoti, bhājanaṃ [T 1.0121] dhovitvā yāgu upanāmetabbā. Yāguṃ pītassa udakaṃ datvā bhājanaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena dhovitvā paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Antevāsikamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti, so deso sammajjitabbo.

If the pupil is sick, one should rise early, give him a tooth-stick and water for the face, and prepare a seat. If there is rice-gruel, one should wash the bowl and offer the rice-gruel. After he has drunk the rice-gruel, one should give him water, receive the bowl, lower it, wash it carefully without scraping, and put it away. When the pupil has risen, the seat should be removed. If that place has rubbish, that place should be swept.

“Sace antevāsiko gāmaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, kāyabandhanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saguṇaṃ katvā saṅghāṭiyo dātabbā, dhovitvā patto sodako dātabbo.

If the pupil wishes to enter the village, the lower robe for going out should be given, and the lower robe for the monastery should be received. The belt should be given. The outer robes should be given, having been folded. The bowl, having been washed, should be given with water.

“Ettāvatā nivattissatīti āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ, paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, paṭinivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ. Sace cīvaraṃ sinnaṃ hoti, muhuttaṃ uṇhe otāpetabbaṃ, na ca uṇhe cīvaraṃ nidahitabbaṃ. Cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ. Cīvaraṃ saṅgharantena caturaṅgulaṃ kaṇṇaṃ ussāretvā cīvaraṃ saṅgharitabbaṃ – mā majjhe bhaṅgo ahosīti. Obhoge kāyabandhanaṃ kātabbaṃ.

Thinking, 'He will return by this time,' a seat should be prepared. Foot-washing water, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet should be placed nearby. One should go to meet him and receive his bowl and robe. A lower robe for wearing in the monastery should be given, and the lower robe for wearing in the village should be received. If the robe is damp with perspiration, it should be aired in the sun for a moment, but the robe should not be left in the sun for a long time. The robe should be folded. When folding the robe, one should leave a margin of four finger-breadths at the edge and fold the robe, thinking, 'Let there not be a crease in the middle.' The waistband should be placed inside the fold.

“Sace [V 0.0074] piṇḍapāto hoti, antevāsiko ca bhuñjitukāmo hoti, udakaṃ datvā piṇḍapāto upanāmetabbo. Antevāsiko pānīyena pucchitabbo. Bhuttāvissa udakaṃ datvā pattaṃ paṭiggahetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena dhovitvā vodakaṃ katvā muhuttaṃ uṇhe [M 0.0083] otāpetabbo, na ca uṇhe patto nidahitabbo. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā [T 1.0122] patto nikkhipitabbo. Na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ vā pamajjitvā pārato antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Antevāsikamhi vuṭṭhite āsanaṃ uddharitabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ paṭisāmetabbaṃ. Sace so deso uklāpo hoti, so deso sammajjitabbo.

If there is almsfood and the resident pupil wishes to eat, water should be given and the almsfood should be offered. The resident pupil should be asked if he needs drinking water. When he has finished eating, water should be given and the bowl received. Holding it low, it should be washed well without scraping it on the ground. Having made it free of water, it should be aired in the sun for a moment, but the bowl should not be left in the sun for a long time. The bowl and robe should be put away. When putting away the bowl, holding the bowl with one hand and feeling under the bed or under the stool with the other hand, the bowl should be put away. The bowl should not be placed on the bare ground. When putting away the robe, holding the robe with one hand and wiping the robe-pole or robe-rope with the other hand, the robe should be put away with the end on the far side and the fold on this side. When the resident pupil has risen, the seat should be removed. The foot-washing water, the footstool, and the potsherd for rubbing the feet should be put away. If that place has rubbish, that place should be swept.

“Sace antevāsiko nahāyitukāmo hoti, nahānaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace sītena attho hoti, sītaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ. Sace uṇhena attho hoti, uṇhaṃ paṭiyādetabbaṃ.

If the resident pupil wishes to bathe, bathing water should be prepared. If there is a need for cool water, cool water should be prepared. If there is a need for hot water, hot water should be prepared.

“Sace antevāsiko jantāgharaṃ pavisitukāmo hoti, cuṇṇaṃ sannetabbaṃ, mattikā temetabbā, jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya gantvā jantāgharapīṭhaṃ datvā cīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ, cuṇṇaṃ dātabbaṃ, mattikā dātabbā. Sace ussahati, jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Jantāgharaṃ pavisantena mattikāya mukhaṃ makkhetvā purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharaṃ pavisitabbaṃ. Na ca there bhikkhū anupakhajja nisīditabbaṃ, na navā bhikkhū āsanena paṭibāhitabbā. Jantāghare antevāsikassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Jantāgharā nikkhamantena jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya purato ca pacchato ca paṭicchādetvā jantāgharā nikkhamitabbaṃ.

If the resident pupil wishes to enter the steam-room, bath powder is to be mixed with water, and clay is to be moistened. Taking the steam-room stool, one should go, give the steam-room stool, receive the pupil's robe, and place it in a suitable place. Bath powder is to be given; clay is to be given. If one is able, one should enter the steam-room. When entering the steam-room, one should smear one's face with clay, cover oneself in front and behind, and then enter. One should not sit down crowding the elder monks, nor should newly ordained monks be obstructed from their seats. In the steam-room, service is to be rendered to the resident pupil. When leaving the steam-room, one should take the steam-room stool, cover oneself in front and behind, and then leave.

“Udakepi antevāsikassa parikammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Nahātena paṭhamataraṃ uttaritvā attano gattaṃ vodakaṃ katvā nivāsetvā antevāsikassa [T 1.0123] gattato udakaṃ pamajjitabbaṃ, nivāsanaṃ dātabbaṃ, saṅghāṭi dātabbā, jantāgharapīṭhaṃ ādāya paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ. Antevāsiko pānīyena pucchitabbo.

At the bathing place also, service is to be rendered to the resident pupil. After bathing, one should emerge from the water first, make one's own body dry, and put on the lower robe; then the water is to be wiped from the resident pupil's body. The lower robe is to be given, and the outer robe is to be given. Having taken the steam-room stool and returned first, a seat is to be prepared. Water for the feet, a footstool, and a foot-scraper are to be placed nearby. The resident pupil is to be asked if he requires drinking water.

“Yasmiṃ vihāre antevāsiko viharati, sace so vihāro uklāpo hoti, sace ussahati, sodhetabbo. Vihāraṃ sodhentena paṭhamaṃ pattacīvaraṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; bhisibibbohanaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ[V 0.0075]; [M 0.0084] mañco nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo; pīṭhaṃ nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; mañcapaṭipādakā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbā; kheḷamallako nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbo; apassenaphalakaṃ nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ; bhūmattharaṇaṃ yathāpaññattaṃ sallakkhetvā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Sace vihāre santānakaṃ hoti, ullokā paṭhamaṃ otāretabbaṃ, ālokasandhikaṇṇabhāgā pamajjitabbā. Sace gerukaparikammakatā bhitti kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace kāḷavaṇṇakatā bhūmi kaṇṇakitā hoti, coḷakaṃ temetvā pīḷetvā pamajjitabbā. Sace akatā hoti bhūmi, udakena paripphositvā sammajjitabbā – mā vihāro rajena [T 1.0124] uhaññīti. Saṅkāraṃ vicinitvā ekamantaṃ chaḍḍetabbaṃ.

If the dwelling where the resident pupil resides is dirty, and if one is able, it is to be cleaned. When cleaning the dwelling, first the bowl and robes are to be taken out and placed to one side. The sitting mat and floor covering are to be taken out and placed to one side. The mattress and pillow are to be taken out and placed to one side. The bed is to be lowered and taken out carefully, without scraping it on the ground or knocking it against the door-leaf and door-frame, and placed to one side. The stool is to be lowered and taken out carefully, without scraping it on the ground or knocking it against the door-leaf and door-frame, and placed to one side. The bed legs are to be taken out and placed to one side. The spittoon is to be taken out and placed to one side. The leaning board is to be taken out and placed to one side. The floor covering is to be taken out, after noting how it was laid, and placed to one side. If there are cobwebs in the dwelling, they are first to be removed from the ceiling. The window joints and corners are to be wiped. If a wall finished with red ochre has become moldy, a cloth is to be moistened, wrung out, and used to wipe it. If a floor finished with black coloring has become moldy, a cloth is to be moistened, wrung out, and used to wipe it. If the floor is unfinished, it is to be sprinkled with water and swept, so that the dwelling is not stirred up with dust. The rubbish is to be collected and discarded to one side.

“Bhūmattharaṇaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Mañcapaṭipādakā otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbā. Mañco otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbo. Pīṭhaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā nīcaṃ katvā sādhukaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena, asaṅghaṭṭentena kavāṭapiṭṭhaṃ, atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Bhisibibbohanaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Nisīdanapaccattharaṇaṃ otāpetvā sodhetvā papphoṭetvā atiharitvā yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Kheḷamallako otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbo. Apassenaphalakaṃ otāpetvā pamajjitvā atiharitvā yathāṭhāne ṭhapetabbaṃ. Pattacīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Pattaṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena pattaṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena heṭṭhāmañcaṃ vā heṭṭhāpīṭhaṃ vā parāmasitvā patto nikkhipitabbo. Na ca anantarahitāya bhūmiyā patto nikkhipitabbo. Cīvaraṃ nikkhipantena ekena hatthena cīvaraṃ gahetvā ekena hatthena cīvaravaṃsaṃ vā cīvararajjuṃ vā pamajjitvā pārato antaṃ orato bhogaṃ katvā cīvaraṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ.

The floor covering is to be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, brought back, and spread as it was before. The bed legs are to be aired in the sun, wiped, brought back, and placed in their usual place. The bed is to be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, lowered, and carefully brought back without scraping it on the ground or knocking it against the door-leaf and door-frame, and spread as it was before. The stool is to be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, lowered, and carefully brought back without scraping it on the ground or knocking it against the door-leaf and door-frame, and spread as it was before. The mattress and pillow are to be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, brought back, and spread as they were before. The sitting mat and floor covering are to be aired in the sun, cleaned, shaken out, brought back, and spread as they were before. The spittoon is to be aired in the sun, wiped, brought back, and placed in its usual place. The leaning board is to be aired in the sun, wiped, brought back, and placed in its usual place. The bowl and robes are to be put away. When putting away the bowl, one should take the bowl with one hand, and with the other hand feel under the bed or under the stool, and then put the bowl down. The bowl is not to be placed on the bare ground. When putting away the robe, one should take the robe with one hand, and with the other hand wipe the robe-pole or the robe-rope, and place the robe over it, making a fold on this side with the end from the other side.

“Sace [M 0.0085] puratthimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, puratthimā vātapānā [T 1.0125] thaketabbā. Sace pacchimā sarajā vātā vāyanti, pacchimā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace uttarā sarajā vātā vāyanti, uttarā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace dakkhiṇā sarajā vātā vāyanti, dakkhiṇā vātapānā thaketabbā. Sace sītakālo hoti, divā vātapānā vivaritabbā, rattiṃ thaketabbā. Sace uṇhakālo hoti, divā vātapānā thaketabbā, rattiṃ vivaritabbā.

If dusty winds blow from the east, the eastern windows are to be closed. If dusty winds blow from the west, the western windows are to be closed. If dusty winds blow from the north, the northern windows are to be closed. If dusty winds blow from the south, the southern windows are to be closed. If it is the cold season, the windows are to be opened during the day and closed at night. If it is the hot season, the windows are to be closed during the day and opened at night.

“Sace [V 0.0076] pariveṇaṃ uklāpaṃ hoti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ. Sace koṭṭhako uklāpo hoti, koṭṭhako sammajjitabbo. Sace upaṭṭhānasālā uklāpā hoti, upaṭṭhānasālā sammajjitabbā. Sace aggisālā uklāpā hoti, aggisālā sammajjitabbā. Sace vaccakuṭi uklāpā hoti, vaccakuṭi sammajjitabbā. Sace pānīyaṃ na hoti, pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace paribhojanīyaṃ na hoti, paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Sace ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ na hoti, ācamanakumbhiyā udakaṃ āsiñcitabbaṃ.

If the monastery enclosure is dirty, the monastery enclosure should be swept. If the gatehouse is dirty, the gatehouse should be swept. If the service hall is dirty, the service hall should be swept. If the fire hall is dirty, the fire hall should be swept. If the toilet is dirty, the toilet should be swept. If there is no drinking water, drinking water should be provided. If there is no water for use, water for use should be provided. If there is no water in the rinsing water pot, water should be poured into the rinsing water pot.

“Sace antevāsikassa anabhirati uppannā hoti, ācariyena vūpakāsetabbo, vūpakāsāpetabbo, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace antevāsikassa kukkuccaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, ācariyena vinodetabbaṃ, vinodāpetabbaṃ, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace antevāsikassa diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti, ācariyena vivecetabbaṃ, vivecāpetabbaṃ, dhammakathā vāssa kātabbā. Sace antevāsiko garudhammaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti parivāsāraho, ācariyena ussukkaṃ [T 1.0126] kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho, antevāsikassa parivāsaṃ dadeyyāti. Sace antevāsiko mūlāya paṭikassanāraho hoti, ācariyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho antevāsikaṃ mūlāya paṭikasseyyāti. Sace antevāsiko mānattāraho hoti, ācariyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho antevāsikassa mānattaṃ dadeyyāti. Sace antevāsiko abbhānāraho hoti, ācariyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho antevāsikaṃ abbheyyāti. Sace saṅgho antevāsikassa kammaṃ kattukāmo hoti, tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ [M 0.0086] vā, ācariyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho saṅgho antevāsikassa kammaṃ na kareyya, lahukāya vā pariṇāmeyyāti. Kataṃ vā panassa hoti saṅghena kammaṃ, tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ vā, ācariyena ussukkaṃ kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho antevāsiko sammā vatteyya, lomaṃ pāteyya, netthāraṃ vatteyya, saṅgho taṃ kammaṃ paṭippassambheyyāti.

If dissatisfaction arises in a pupil, the teacher should lead him away to another place, have him led away, or give him a Dhamma talk. If remorse arises in a pupil, the teacher should dispel it, have it dispelled, or give him a Dhamma talk. If a wrong view arises in a pupil, the teacher should make him relinquish it, have it relinquished, or give him a Dhamma talk. If a pupil has committed a grave offense warranting probation, the teacher should make an effort: ‘How might the Saṅgha grant the pupil probation?’ If a pupil deserves to be sent back to the beginning, the teacher should make an effort: ‘How might the Saṅgha send the pupil back to the beginning?’ If a pupil deserves penance, the teacher should make an effort: ‘How might the Saṅgha grant the pupil penance?’ If a pupil deserves reinstatement, the teacher should make an effort: ‘How might the Saṅgha reinstate the pupil?’ If the Saṅgha intends to carry out an act against a pupil—whether of censure, subordination, banishment, reconciliation, or suspension—the teacher should make an effort: ‘How might the Saṅgha not carry out the act against the pupil, or change it to a lighter one?’ But if an act has been carried out against him by the Saṅgha—whether of censure, subordination, banishment, reconciliation, or suspension—the teacher should make an effort: ‘How might the pupil behave rightly, lower his pride, and undertake his rehabilitation, so that the Saṅgha might rescind that act?’”

“Sace antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ dhovitabbaṃ hoti, ācariyena ācikkhitabbaṃ – ‘evaṃ dhoveyyāsī’ti, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ dhoviyethāti. Sace antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ kātabbaṃ hoti, ācariyena ācikkhitabbaṃ – ‘evaṃ kareyyāsī’ti, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ kariyethāti. Sace [T 1.0127] antevāsikassa rajanaṃ pacitabbaṃ hoti, ācariyena ācikkhitabbaṃ – ‘evaṃ paceyyāsī’ti, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho antevāsikassa rajanaṃ paciyethāti. Sace [V 0.0077] antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ rajitabbaṃ hoti, ācariyena ācikkhitabbaṃ – ‘evaṃ rajeyyāsī’ti, ussukkaṃ vā kātabbaṃ – kinti nu kho antevāsikassa cīvaraṃ rajiyethāti. Cīvaraṃ rajantena sādhukaṃ samparivattakaṃ samparivattakaṃ rajitabbaṃ, na ca acchinne theve pakkamitabbaṃ. Sace antevāsiko gilāno hoti, yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhātabbo, vuṭṭhānamassa āgametabba”nti.

If a resident pupil's robe is to be washed, the teacher should instruct, 'You should wash it thus,' or an effort should be made, 'How indeed might the resident pupil's robe be washed?' If a resident pupil's robe is to be made, the teacher should instruct, 'You should make it thus,' or an effort should be made, 'How indeed might the resident pupil's robe be made?' If dye for the resident pupil is to be cooked, the teacher should instruct, 'You should cook it thus,' or an effort should be made, 'How indeed might the dye for the resident pupil be cooked?' If a resident pupil's robe is to be dyed, the teacher should instruct, 'You should dye it thus,' or an effort should be made, 'How indeed might the resident pupil's robe be dyed?' When dyeing a robe, it should be dyed well, turning it over and over, and one should not depart before the dripping has ceased. If the resident pupil is ill, he should be attended to for as long as he lives; his recovery should be awaited.

Antevāsikavattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The duties concerning the resident pupil are concluded.

Chaṭṭhabhāṇavāro.

The Sixth Recitation Section.

20. Paṇāmanā khamāpanā

20. Dismissal and Asking for Forgiveness

80. Tena kho pana samayena antevāsikā ācariyesu na sammā vattanti…pe… bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… na, bhikkhave, antevāsikena ācariyamhi na sammā vattitabbaṃ. Yo na sammā vatteyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti. Neva sammā vattanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, asammāvattantaṃ paṇāmetuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, paṇāmetabbo – paṇāmemi tanti vā, māyidha paṭikkamīti [M 0.0087] vā, nīhara te pattacīvaranti vā, nāhaṃ tayā upaṭṭhātabboti vā. Kāyena viññāpeti, vācāya viññāpeti, kāyena vācāya viññāpeti, paṇāmito hoti antevāsiko; na kāyena viññāpeti, na vācāya viññāpeti, na kāyena vācāya viññāpeti, na paṇāmito hoti antevāsikoti.

80. Now at that time, the resident pupils did not conduct themselves properly towards their teachers... They reported this matter to the Blessed One... 'Monks, it is not that a resident pupil should not conduct himself properly towards his teacher; he should indeed conduct himself properly. Whichever monk should not conduct himself properly, there is an offense of wrong-doing.' They still did not conduct themselves properly. They reported this matter to the Blessed One... 'I allow, monks, to dismiss one who does not conduct himself properly. And, monks, he should be dismissed in this way: "I dismiss you," or "Do not enter my presence here," or "Take out your bowl and robe," or "I am not to be attended upon by you." If he makes it known by body, or makes it known by speech, or makes it known by body and speech, the resident pupil is dismissed. If he does not make it known by body, does not make it known by speech, and does not make it known by body and speech, the resident pupil is not dismissed.'

Tena kho pana samayena [T 1.0128] antevāsikā paṇāmitā na khamāpenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, khamāpetunti. Neva khamāpenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, paṇāmitena na khamāpetabbo. Yo na khamāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, dismissed resident pupils did not ask for forgiveness. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, the asking for forgiveness.' Still, they did not ask for forgiveness. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, it is not that one who has been dismissed should not ask for forgiveness; he should indeed ask for forgiveness. Whichever monk should not ask for forgiveness, there is an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena ācariyā khamāpiyamānā na khamanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, khamitunti. Neva khamanti. Antevāsikā pakkamantipi vibbhamantipi titthiyesupi saṅkamanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, khamāpiyamānena na khamitabbaṃ. Yo na khameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, when being asked for forgiveness, teachers did not forgive. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, to forgive.' Still, they did not forgive. The resident pupils also departed, also disrobed, and also went over to the adherents of other teachings. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, it is not that one who is being asked for forgiveness should not forgive; he should indeed forgive. Whichever monk should not forgive, there is an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena [V 0.0078] kho pana samayena ācariyā sammāvattantaṃ paṇāmenti, asammāvattantaṃ na paṇāmenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, sammāvattanto paṇāmetabbo. Yo paṇāmeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na ca, bhikkhave, asammāvattanto na paṇāmetabbo. Yo na paṇāmeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

At that time, teachers dismissed the pupil who conducts himself properly and did not dismiss the pupil who does not conduct himself properly. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, one who conducts himself properly is not to be dismissed. Whoever should dismiss him commits an offense of wrong-doing. And, monks, it is not that one who does not conduct himself properly is not to be dismissed; he is indeed to be dismissed. Whoever should not dismiss him commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

81. “Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato antevāsiko paṇāmetabbo. Ācariyamhi nādhimattaṃ pemaṃ hoti, nādhimatto pasādo hoti, nādhimattā hirī hoti, nādhimatto gāravo hoti, nādhimattā bhāvanā hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato antevāsiko paṇāmetabbo.

81. “Monks, a resident pupil endowed with five factors is to be dismissed. He has no excessive affection for the teacher, no excessive confidence in the teacher, no excessive shame toward the teacher, no excessive reverence for the teacher, and no excessive development of loving-kindness toward the teacher. Monks, a resident pupil endowed with these five factors is to be dismissed.”

“Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato antevāsiko na paṇāmetabbo. Ācariyamhi adhimattaṃ pemaṃ hoti, adhimatto pasādo hoti, adhimattā [T 1.0129] hirī hoti, adhimatto gāravo hoti, adhimattā bhāvanā hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato antevāsiko na paṇāmetabbo.

“Monks, a resident pupil endowed with five factors is not to be dismissed. He has excessive affection for the teacher, excessive confidence in the teacher, excessive shame toward the teacher, excessive reverence for the teacher, and excessive development of loving-kindness toward the teacher. Monks, a resident pupil endowed with these five factors is not to be dismissed.”

“Pañcahi[M 0.0088], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato antevāsiko alaṃ paṇāmetuṃ. Ācariyamhi nādhimattaṃ pemaṃ hoti, nādhimatto pasādo hoti, nādhimattā hirī hoti, nādhimatto gāravo hoti, nādhimattā bhāvanā hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato antevāsiko alaṃ paṇāmetuṃ.

“Monks, a resident pupil endowed with five factors is fit to be dismissed. He has no excessive affection for the teacher, no excessive confidence in the teacher, no excessive shame toward the teacher, no excessive reverence for the teacher, and no excessive development of loving-kindness toward the teacher. Monks, a resident pupil endowed with these five factors is fit to be dismissed.”

“Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato antevāsiko nālaṃ paṇāmetuṃ. Ācariyamhi adhimattaṃ pemaṃ hoti, adhimatto pasādo hoti, adhimattā hirī hoti, adhimatto gāravo hoti, adhimattā bhāvanā hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato antevāsiko nālaṃ paṇāmetuṃ.

“Monks, a resident pupil endowed with five factors is not fit to be dismissed. He has excessive affection for the teacher, excessive confidence in the teacher, excessive shame toward the teacher, excessive reverence for the teacher, and excessive development of loving-kindness toward the teacher. Monks, a resident pupil endowed with these five factors is not fit to be dismissed.”

“Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ antevāsikaṃ appaṇāmento ācariyo sātisāro hoti, paṇāmento anatisāro hoti. Ācariyamhi nādhimattaṃ pemaṃ hoti, nādhimatto pasādo hoti, nādhimattā hirī hoti, nādhimatto gāravo hoti, nādhimattā bhāvanā hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ antevāsikaṃ appaṇāmento ācariyo sātisāro hoti, paṇāmento anatisāro hoti.

“Monks, a teacher who does not dismiss a resident pupil endowed with five factors is blameworthy; one who dismisses him is not blameworthy. The pupil has no excessive affection for the teacher, no excessive confidence in the teacher, no excessive shame toward the teacher, no excessive reverence for the teacher, and no excessive development of loving-kindness toward the teacher. Monks, a teacher who does not dismiss a resident pupil endowed with these five factors is blameworthy; one who dismisses him is not blameworthy.”

“Pañcahi[V 0.0079], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ antevāsikaṃ paṇāmento ācariyo sātisāro hoti, appaṇāmento anatisāro hoti. Ācariyamhi adhimattaṃ pemaṃ hoti, adhimatto pasādo hoti, adhimattā [T 1.0130] hirī hoti, adhimatto gāravo hoti, adhimattā bhāvanā hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ antevāsikaṃ paṇāmento ācariyo sātisāro hoti, appaṇāmento anatisāro hotī”ti.

“Monks, a teacher who dismisses a resident pupil endowed with five factors is at fault; one who does not dismiss him is not at fault. He has excessive affection for the teacher, excessive confidence in the teacher, excessive shame toward the teacher, excessive reverence for the teacher, and excessive development of loving-kindness toward the teacher. Monks, a teacher who dismisses a resident pupil endowed with these five factors is at fault; one who does not dismiss him is not at fault.”

Paṇāmanā khamāpanā niṭṭhitā.

The Salutation and Asking for Forgiveness are concluded.

21. Bālaabyattavatthu

The Story of the Foolish and Inexpert

82. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū, dasavassamhā dasavassamhāti, bālā abyattā nissayaṃ denti. Dissanti ācariyā bālā, antevāsikā paṇḍitā[M 0.0089]. Dissanti ācariyā abyattā, antevāsikā byattā. Dissanti ācariyā appassutā, antevāsikā bahussutā. Dissanti ācariyā duppaññā, antevāsikā paññavanto. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… [P 1.0062] te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhū, dasavassamhā dasavassamhāti, bālā abyattā nissayaṃ dassanti. Dissanti ācariyā bālā antevāsikā paṇḍitā, dissanti ācariyā abyattā antevāsikā byattā, dissanti ācariyā appassutā antevāsikā bahussutā, dissanti ācariyā duppaññā antevāsikā paññavanto”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū, dasavassamhā dasavassamhāti, bālā abyattā nissayaṃ denti…pe… saccaṃ, bhagavāti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, bālena abyattena nissayo dātabbo. Yo dadeyya, āpatti [T 1.0131] dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena dasavassena vā atirekadasavassena vā nissayaṃ dātu”nti.

21. Now at that time, some monks, saying, 'We have ten vassas, we have ten vassas,' gave dependence while being foolish and inexpert. Foolish teachers were seen with wise resident pupils. Inexpert teachers were seen with expert resident pupils. Teachers of little learning were seen with resident pupils of great learning. Unwise teachers were seen with wise resident pupils. Those monks who were of few wishes… murmured, criticized, and spread it about, saying: 'How can monks, saying, “We have ten vassas, we have ten vassas,” give dependence while being foolish and inexpert? Foolish teachers are seen with wise resident pupils, inexpert teachers are seen with expert resident pupils, teachers of little learning are seen with resident pupils of great learning, and unwise teachers are seen with wise resident pupils.' Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… 'Is it true, monks, that some monks, saying, “We have ten vassas, we have ten vassas,” give dependence while being foolish and inexpert?'… 'It is true, Blessed One.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… Having rebuked them… after giving a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: 'Monks, dependence is not to be given by one who is foolish and inexpert. Whoever should give it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, dependence to be given by a monk who is expert, competent, and of ten vassas or more than ten vassas.'

Bālaabyattavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Story of the Foolish and Inexpert is concluded.

22. Nissayapaṭippassaddhikathā

82. The Discourse on the Cessation of Dependence

83. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ācariyupajjhāyesu pakkantesupi vibbhantesupi kālaṅkatesupi [V 0.0080] pakkhasaṅkantesupi nissayapaṭippassaddhiyo na jānanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

Now at that time, the monks did not know the cessations of dependence when their teachers and preceptors had departed, or had disrobed, or had passed away, or had gone over to another sect. They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

“Pañcimā, bhikkhave, nissayapaṭippassaddhiyo upajjhāyamhā – upajjhāyo pakkanto vā hoti, vibbhanto vā, kālaṅkato vā, pakkhasaṅkanto vā, āṇattiyeva pañcamī. Imā kho, bhikkhave, pañca nissayapaṭippassaddhiyo upajjhāyamhā.

22. “Monks, there are these five cessations of dependence from a preceptor: the preceptor has departed, or has disrobed, or has passed away, or has gone over to another sect, and expulsion is the fifth. These, monks, are the five cessations of dependence from a preceptor.”

“Chayimā, bhikkhave, nissayapaṭippassaddhiyo ācariyamhā – ācariyo pakkanto vā hoti, vibbhanto vā, kālaṅkato vā, pakkhasaṅkanto vā, āṇattiyeva pañcamī, upajjhāyena vā samodhānagato hoti. Imā kho, bhikkhave, cha nissayapaṭippassaddhiyo ācariyamhā”.

83. “Monks, there are these six cessations of dependence from a teacher: the teacher has departed, or has disrobed, or has passed away, or has gone over to another sect, expulsion is the fifth, or the pupil has come together with the preceptor. These, monks, are the six cessations of dependence from a teacher.”

Nissapaṭippassaddhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Revocation of Dependence is concluded.

23. Upasampādetabbapañcakaṃ

The Pentad on Who is to be Ordained

84. “Pañcahi[M 0.0090], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Na asekkhena na asekhena (ka.) sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena paññākkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi [T 1.0132] samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

84. “Monks, a monk endowed with five factors should not confer higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him. He is not endowed with the aggregate of moral discipline of one beyond training, he is not endowed with the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training, he is not endowed with the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training, he is not endowed with the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training, and he is not endowed with the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training. Monks, a monk endowed with these five factors should not confer higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him.”

“Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena paññākkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā [P 1.0063] upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Monks, a monk endowed with five factors should confer higher ordination, should give dependence, and should have a novice attend on him. He is endowed with the aggregate of moral discipline of one beyond training, he is endowed with the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training, he is endowed with the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training, he is endowed with the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training, and he is endowed with the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training. Monks, a monk endowed with these five factors should confer higher ordination, should give dependence, and should have a novice attend on him.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo [V 0.0081] dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Attanā na asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na paraṃ asekkhe sīlakkhandhe samādapetā; attanā na asekkhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na paraṃ asekkhe samādhikkhandhe samādapetā; attanā na asekkhena paññākkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na paraṃ asekkhe paññākkhandhe samādapetā; attanā na asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na paraṃ asekkhe vimuttikkhandhe samādapetā; attanā na asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na paraṃ asekkhe vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhe samādapetā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na [T 1.0133] nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Monks, a monk endowed with another five factors should not confer higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him. He himself is not endowed with the aggregate of moral discipline of one beyond training, nor does he establish others in the aggregate of moral discipline of one beyond training; he himself is not endowed with the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training, nor does he establish others in the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training; he himself is not endowed with the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training, nor does he establish others in the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training; he himself is not endowed with the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training, nor does he establish others in the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training; he himself is not endowed with the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training, nor does he establish others in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training. Monks, a monk endowed with these five factors should not confer higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him.”

“Pañcahi[M 0.0091], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Attanā asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, paraṃ asekkhe sīlakkhandhe samādapetā; attanā asekkhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, paraṃ asekkhe samādhikkhandhe samādapetā; attanā asekkhena paññākkhandhena samannāgato hoti, paraṃ asekkhe paññākkhandhe samādapetā; attanā asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, paraṃ asekkhe vimuttikkhandhe samādapetā; attanā asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, paraṃ asekkhe vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhe samādapetā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Monks, a monk endowed with five factors should confer higher ordination, should give dependence, and should have a novice attend on him. He himself is endowed with the aggregate of moral discipline of one beyond training and establishes others in the aggregate of moral discipline of one beyond training; he himself is endowed with the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training and establishes others in the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training; he himself is endowed with the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training and establishes others in the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training; he himself is endowed with the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training and establishes others in the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training; he himself is endowed with the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training and establishes others in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training. Monks, a monk endowed with these five factors should confer higher ordination, should give dependence, and should have a novice attend on him.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Assaddho hoti, ahiriko hoti, anottappī hoti, kusīto hoti, muṭṭhassati hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Monks, a monk endowed with another five factors should not confer higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him. He is faithless, shameless, without moral dread, indolent, and lacking mindfulness. Monks, a monk endowed with these five factors should not confer higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him.”

“Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo[T 1.0134], sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Saddho hoti, hirimā hoti, ottappī hoti, āraddhavīriyo hoti, upaṭṭhitassati hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Monks, a monk endowed with five factors should confer higher ordination, should give dependence, and should have a novice attend on him. He is faithful, has a sense of shame, has moral dread, is energetic, and is mindful. Monks, a monk endowed with these five factors should confer higher ordination, should give dependence, and should have a novice attend on him.”

“Aparehipi[V 0.0082], bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti, appassuto hoti, duppañño hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Monks, a monk endowed with another five factors should not confer higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him. He is corrupt in higher virtue, corrupt in higher conduct, corrupt in higher view, has little learning, and is unwise. Monks, a monk endowed with these five factors should not confer higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him.”

“Pañcahi[M 0.0092], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ[P 1.0064], nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Na adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, na ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, na atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti, bahussuto hoti, paññavā hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Monks, a monk endowed with five factors should confer higher ordination, should give dependence, and should have a novice attend on him. He is not corrupt in higher virtue, not corrupt in higher conduct, not corrupt in higher view, is very learned, and is wise. Monks, a monk endowed with these five factors should confer higher ordination, should give dependence, and should have a novice attend on him.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Na paṭibalo hoti antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā [T 1.0135] gilānaṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ vā upaṭṭhāpetuṃ vā, anabhirataṃ anabhiratiṃ (syā.), uppannaṃ anabhiratiṃ (ka.) vūpakāsetuṃ vā vūpakāsāpetuṃ vā, uppannaṃ kukkuccaṃ dhammato vinodetuṃ vinodetuṃ vā vinodāpetuṃ vā (sabbattha, vimativinodanī ṭīkā oloketabbā) āpattiṃ na jānāti, āpattiyā vuṭṭhānaṃ na jānāti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors should not confer higher ordination, should not grant dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him. He is not capable of attending to or having another attend to a resident pupil or co-resident who is sick; he is not capable of leading away or having another lead away one who is discontented; he is not capable of dispelling, according to the Dhamma, remorse that has arisen; he does not know an offense; he does not know the rehabilitation from an offense. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not confer higher ordination, should not grant dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him.

“Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Paṭibalo hoti antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā gilānaṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ vā upaṭṭhāpetuṃ vā, anabhirataṃ vūpakāsetuṃ vā vūpakāsāpetuṃ vā, uppannaṃ kukkuccaṃ dhammato vinodetuṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, āpattiyā vuṭṭhānaṃ jānāti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should confer higher ordination, should grant dependence, and should have a novice attend on him. He is capable of attending to or having another attend to a resident pupil or co-resident who is sick; he is capable of leading away or having another lead away one who is discontented; he is capable of dispelling, according to the Dhamma, remorse that has arisen; he knows an offense; he knows the rehabilitation from an offense. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should confer higher ordination, should grant dependence, and should have a novice attend on him.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Na paṭibalo hoti antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā abhisamācārikāya sikkhāya sikkhāpetuṃ, ādibrahmacariyakāya sikkhāya vinetuṃ, abhidhamme vinetuṃ, abhivinaye vinetuṃ, uppannaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ dhammato vivecetuṃ – imehi kho[V 0.0083], bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na [T 1.0136] nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors should not confer higher ordination, should not grant dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him. He is not capable of training a resident pupil or co-resident in the training in proper conduct, of disciplining them in the training fundamental to the holy life, of disciplining them in the Abhidhamma, of disciplining them in the entire Vinaya, or of dispelling an arisen wrong view according to the Dhamma. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not confer higher ordination, should not grant dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him.

“Pañcahi[M 0.0093], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Paṭibalo hoti antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā abhisamācārikāya sikkhāya sikkhāpetuṃ, ādibrahmacariyakāya sikkhāya vinetuṃ, abhidhamme vinetuṃ, abhivinaye vinetuṃ, uppannaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ dhammato [P 1.0065] vivecetuṃ – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should confer higher ordination, should grant dependence, and should have a novice attend on him. He is capable of training a resident pupil or co-resident in the training in proper conduct, of disciplining them in the training fundamental to the holy life, of disciplining them in the Abhidhamma, of disciplining them in the entire Vinaya, and of dispelling an arisen wrong view according to the Dhamma. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should confer higher ordination, should grant dependence, and should have a novice attend on him.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Āpattiṃ na jānāti, anāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena na svāgatāni honti na suvibhattāni na suppavattīni na suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors should not confer higher ordination, should not grant dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him. He does not know an offense, he does not know what is not an offense, he does not know a light offense, and he does not know a serious offense; and for him, the two Pātimokkhas are not well-mastered in detail, not well-analyzed, not well-recited, and not well-adjudicated according to the rules and their detailed analysis. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not confer higher ordination, should not grant dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him.

“Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Āpattiṃ jānāti, anāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso [T 1.0137] – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should confer higher ordination, should grant dependence, and should have a novice attend on him. He knows an offense, he knows what is not an offense, he knows a light offense, and he knows a serious offense; and for him, the two Pātimokkhas are well-mastered in detail, well-analyzed, well-recited, and well-adjudicated according to the rules and their detailed analysis. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should confer higher ordination, should grant dependence, and should have a novice attend on him.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Āpattiṃ na jānāti, anāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, ūnadasavasso hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with another five factors should not confer higher ordination, should not grant dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him. He does not know an offense, he does not know what is not an offense, he does not know a light offense, he does not know a serious offense, and he is of less than ten years’ standing. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should not confer higher ordination, should not grant dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him.

“Pañcahi[V 0.0084], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Āpattiṃ jānāti, anāpattiṃ [M 0.0094] jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, dasavasso vā hoti atirekadasavasso vā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo”ti.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with five factors should confer higher ordination, should grant dependence, and should have a novice attend on him. He knows an offense, he knows what is not an offense, he knows a light offense, he knows a serious offense, and he is of ten years’ standing or more. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these five factors should confer higher ordination, should grant dependence, and should have a novice attend on him.”

Upasampādetabbapañcakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Pentad on Conferring Higher Ordination is concluded.

24. Upasampādetabbachakkaṃ

24. The Hexad on Conferring Higher Ordination

85. “Chahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo[P 1.0066]. Na asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena paññākkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena [T 1.0138] samannāgato hoti, ūnadasavasso hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

85. “Monks, a monk endowed with six qualities should not give ordination, should not give dependence, and should not take a novice into his charge. He is not endowed with the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training, not endowed with the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training, not endowed with the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training, not endowed with the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training, not endowed with the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training, and he is of less than ten rains' standing. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities should not give ordination, should not give dependence, and should not take a novice into his charge.”

“Chahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena paññākkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, dasavasso vā hoti atirekadasavasso vā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Monks, a monk endowed with six qualities is fit to give ordination, to give dependence, and to take a novice into his charge. He is endowed with the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training, endowed with the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training, endowed with the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training, endowed with the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training, endowed with the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training, and is of ten rains' standing or more than ten rains' standing. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities is fit to give ordination, to give dependence, and to take a novice into his charge.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Attanā na asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na paraṃ asekkhe sīlakkhandhe samādapetā; attanā na asekkhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato [M 0.0095] hoti, na paraṃ asekkhe samādhikkhandhe samādapetā; attanā [V 0.0085] na asekkhena paññākkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na paraṃ asekkhe paññākkhandhe samādapetā; attanā na asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na paraṃ asekkhe vimuttikkhandhe samādapetā; attanā na asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na paraṃ asekkhe vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhe [T 1.0139] samādapetā; ūnadasavasso hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Furthermore, monks, a monk endowed with another six qualities should not give ordination, should not give dependence, and should not take a novice into his charge. He himself is not endowed with the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training, nor does he establish another in the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training; he himself is not endowed with the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training, nor does he establish another in the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training; he himself is not endowed with the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training, nor does he establish another in the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training; he himself is not endowed with the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training, nor does he establish another in the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training; he himself is not endowed with the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training, nor does he establish another in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training; and he is of less than ten rains' standing. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities should not give ordination, should not give dependence, and should not take a novice into his charge.”

“Chahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Attanā asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, paraṃ asekkhe sīlakkhandhe samādapetā attanā asekkhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, paraṃ asekkhe samādhikkhandhe samādapetā. Attanā asekkhena paññākkhandhena samannāgato hoti, paraṃ asekkhe paññākkhandhe samādapetā. Attanā asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, paraṃ asekkhe vimuttikkhandhe samādapetā. Attanā asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, paraṃ asekkhe vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhe samādapetā; dasavasso vā hoti atirekadasavasso vā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Monks, a monk endowed with six qualities is fit to give ordination, to give dependence, and to take a novice into his charge. He himself is endowed with the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training, and he establishes another in the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training. He himself is endowed with the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training, and he establishes another in the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training. He himself is endowed with the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training, and he establishes another in the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training. He himself is endowed with the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training, and he establishes another in the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training. He himself is endowed with the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training, and he establishes another in the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training. He is of ten rains' standing or more than ten rains' standing. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities is fit to give ordination, to give dependence, and to take a novice into his charge.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Assaddho hoti, ahiriko hoti, anottappī hoti, kusīto hoti, muṭṭhassati hoti, ūnadasavasso hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero [T 1.0140] upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Furthermore, monks, a monk endowed with another six qualities should not give ordination, should not give dependence, and should not take a novice into his charge. He is without faith, he is shameless, he is without moral dread, he is lazy, he is of lapsed mindfulness, and he is of less than ten rains' standing. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities should not give ordination, should not give dependence, and should not take a novice into his charge.”

“Chahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ[P 1.0067], nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Saddho hoti, hirimā hoti, ottappī hoti, āraddhavīriyo hoti, upaṭṭhitassati hoti, dasavasso vā hoti atirekadasavasso vā – imehi [M 0.0096] kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Monks, a monk endowed with six qualities is fit to give ordination, to give dependence, and to take a novice into his charge. He has faith, he has a sense of shame, he has moral dread, he has aroused energy, he has established mindfulness, and he is of ten rains' standing or more than ten rains' standing. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities is fit to give ordination, to give dependence, and to take a novice into his charge.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti, appassuto hoti, duppañño hoti, ūnadasavasso [V 0.0086] hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

“Furthermore, monks, a monk endowed with another six qualities should not give ordination, should not give dependence, and should not take a novice into his charge. He is corrupt in higher virtue, corrupt in higher conduct, corrupt in higher view, is of little learning, is unwise, and is of less than ten rains' standing. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities should not give ordination, should not give dependence, and should not take a novice into his charge.”

“Chahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Na adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, na ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, na atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti, bahussuto hoti, paññavā hoti, dasavasso vā hoti atirekadasavasso vā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

Monks, a monk endowed with six qualities may give higher ordination, may give dependence, and may have a novice attend on him. He is not corrupt in higher virtue, not corrupt in higher conduct, not corrupt in higher view, is of great learning, is wise, and is of ten rains or more. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities may give higher ordination, may give dependence, and may have a novice attend on him.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena [T 1.0141] bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Na paṭibalo hoti antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā gilānaṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ vā upaṭṭhāpetuṃ vā, anabhirataṃ vūpakāsetuṃ vā vūpakāsāpetuṃ vā, uppannaṃ kukkuccaṃ dhammato vinodetuṃ, āpattiṃ na jānāti, āpattiyā vuṭṭhānaṃ na jānāti, ūnadasavasso hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

Furthermore, monks, a monk endowed with another six qualities should not give higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him. He is not capable of attending to a sick resident pupil or co-resident, or of having one attended to; he is not capable of leading away a discontented one, or of having one led away; he is not capable of dispelling arisen remorse in accordance with the Dhamma; he does not know an offense; he does not know the rehabilitation from an offense; and he is of less than ten rains. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities should not give higher ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him.

“Chahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Paṭibalo hoti antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā gilānaṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ vā upaṭṭhāpetuṃ vā, anabhirataṃ vūpakāsetuṃ vā vūpakāsāpetuṃ vā, uppannaṃ kukkuccaṃ dhammato vinodetuṃ, āpattiṃ jānāti, āpattiyā vuṭṭhānaṃ jānāti, dasavasso [M 0.0097] vā hoti atirekadasavasso vā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

Monks, a monk endowed with six qualities may confer ordination, may give dependence, and may have a novice attend on him. He is capable of attending to a sick resident pupil or co-resident, or of having one attended to; he is capable of leading away a discontented one, or of having one led away; he is capable of dispelling arisen remorse in accordance with the Dhamma; he knows an offense; he knows the rehabilitation from an offense; and he is of ten rains or more than ten rains. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities may confer ordination, may give dependence, and may have a novice attend on him.

“Aparehipi[P 1.0068], bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Na paṭibalo hoti antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā abhisamācārikāya sikkhāya sikkhāpetuṃ, ādibrahmacariyakāya sikkhāya vinetuṃ, abhidhamme vinetuṃ[T 1.0142], abhivinaye vinetuṃ, uppannaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ dhammato vivecetuṃ, ūnadasavasso hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

Furthermore, monks, a monk endowed with another six qualities should not confer ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him. He is not capable of training a resident pupil or co-resident in the training concerning proper conduct, of instructing them in the training concerning the fundamentals of the holy life, of instructing them in the Abhidhamma, of instructing them in the Abhivinaya, or of dispelling an arisen wrong view in accordance with the Dhamma; and he is of less than ten rains. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities should not confer ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him.

“Chahi[V 0.0087], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Paṭibalo hoti antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā abhisamācārikāya sikkhāya sikkhāpetuṃ ādibrahmacariyakāya sikkhāya vinetuṃ, abhidhamme vinetuṃ, abhivinaye vinetuṃ, uppannaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ dhammato vivecetuṃ, dasavasso vā hoti atirekadasavasso vā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

Monks, a monk endowed with six qualities may confer ordination, may give dependence, and may have a novice attend on him. He is capable of training a resident pupil or co-resident in the training concerning proper conduct, of instructing them in the training concerning the fundamentals of the holy life, of instructing them in the Abhidhamma, of instructing them in the Abhivinaya, and of dispelling an arisen wrong view in accordance with the Dhamma; and he is of ten rains or more than ten rains. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities may confer ordination, may give dependence, and may have a novice attend on him.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Āpattiṃ na jānāti, anāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena na svāgatāni honti na suvibhattāni na suppavattīni na suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso, ūnadasavasso hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na upasampādetabbaṃ, na nissayo dātabbo, na sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo.

Furthermore, monks, a monk endowed with another six qualities should not give ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him. He does not know an offense, he does not know a non-offense, he does not know a light offense, he does not know a grave offense; and furthermore, the two Pātimokkhas have not been well-learned by him in detail, are not well-analyzed, are not well-recited, and are not well-determined in terms of the rules and their detailed analysis; he is of less than ten rains. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities should not give ordination, should not give dependence, and should not have a novice attend on him.

“Chahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo[T 1.0143], sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Āpattiṃ jānāti[M 0.0098], anāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso, dasavasso vā hoti atirekadasavasso vā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo”ti.

Monks, a monk endowed with six qualities may give ordination, may give dependence, and may have a novice attend on him. He knows an offense, he knows a non-offense, he knows a light offense, he knows a grave offense; and furthermore, the two Pātimokkhas have been well-learned by him in detail, are well-analyzed, are well-recited, and are well-determined in terms of the rules and their detailed analysis; he is of ten rains or more than ten rains. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities may give ordination, may give dependence, and may have a novice attend on him.

Upasampādetabbachakkaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section of Six on Giving Ordination is concluded.

25. Aññatitthiyapubbakathā

25. Discourse on a Former Adherent of Another Sect

86. Tena [P 1.0069] kho pana samayena yo so aññatitthiyapubbo yo so pasuraparibbājako aññatitthiyapubbo (ka.) pajjhāyena sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno upajjhāyassa vādaṃ āropetvā taṃyeva titthāyatanaṃ saṅkami. So puna paccāgantvā bhikkhū upasampadaṃ yāci. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Yo so, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo upajjhāyena sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno upajjhāyassa vādaṃ āropetvā taṃyeva titthāyatanaṃ [V 0.0088] saṅkanto, so āgato na upasampādetabbo. Yo so, bhikkhave, aññopi aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhati pabbajjaṃ, ākaṅkhati upasampadaṃ, tassa cattāro māse parivāso dātabbo.
