Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbo – paṭhamaṃ kesamassuṃ ohārāpetvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādāpetvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ kārāpetvā bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vandāpetvā [T 1.0144] ukkuṭikaṃ nisīdāpetvā añjaliṃ paggaṇhāpetvā evaṃ vadehīti vattabbo – “buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi; dutiyampi buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, dutiyampi dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, dutiyampi saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi; tatiyampi buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, tatiyampi dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, tatiyampi saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmī”ti.

86. At that time, a certain former adherent of another sect, when being addressed in accordance with the Dhamma by his preceptor, having found fault with his preceptor's doctrine, returned to that same sectarian establishment. Later, he came back and asked the monks for the higher ordination. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, that former adherent of another sect who, when being addressed in accordance with the Dhamma by his preceptor, found fault with his preceptor's doctrine and returned to that same sectarian establishment—he, having come back, should not be given the higher ordination. Monks, any other former adherent of another sect who desires the going forth and desires the higher ordination in this Dhamma and Discipline, should be given probation for four months. And, monks, it should be given in this way: First, having had his hair and beard shaved off, having had him dressed in ochre robes, having had him arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, having had him venerate the feet of the monks, having had him sit in a squatting position, and having had him raise his joined palms, he should be told to say thus: “I go for refuge to the Buddha, I go for refuge to the Dhamma, I go for refuge to the Sangha; for a second time I go for refuge to the Buddha, for a second time I go for refuge to the Dhamma, for a second time I go for refuge to the Sangha; for a third time I go for refuge to the Buddha, for a third time I go for refuge to the Dhamma, for a third time I go for refuge to the Sangha.”'

Tena, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbena saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “ahaṃ, bhante, aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṃ [M 0.0099] dhammavinaye ākaṅkhāmi upasampadaṃ. Sohaṃ, bhante, saṅghaṃ cattāro māse parivāsaṃ yācāmī”ti. Dutiyampi yācitabbo. Tatiyampi yācitabbo. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Monks, that former adherent of another sect should approach the Sangha, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, venerate the feet of the monks, sit in a squatting position, raise his joined palms, and speak thus: ‘Venerable sirs, I, a former adherent of another sect, desire the higher ordination in this Dhamma and Discipline. So I, venerable sirs, ask the Sangha for probation for four months.’ He should request a second time. He should request a third time. The Sangha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhati upasampadaṃ. So saṅghaṃ cattāro māse parivāsaṃ yācati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ saṅgho itthannāmassa aññatitthiyapubbassa cattāro māse parivāsaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This person of such-and-such a name, a former adherent of another sect, desires the higher ordination in this Dhamma and Discipline. He asks the Sangha for probation for four months. If the time is right for the Sangha, may the Sangha grant probation for four months to this person of such-and-such a name, a former adherent of another sect. This is the motion.’

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhati upasampadaṃ. So saṅghaṃ cattāro māse parivāsaṃ yācati. Saṅgho itthannāmassa aññatitthiyapubbassa cattāro māse parivāsaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa aññatitthiyapubbassa [T 1.0145] cattāro māse parivāsassa dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. This person of such-and-such a name, a former adherent of another sect, desires the higher ordination in this Dhamma and Discipline. He asks the Sangha for probation for four months. The Sangha grants probation for four months to this person of such-and-such a name, a former adherent of another sect. To whichever venerable one the granting of probation for four months to this person of such-and-such a name, a former adherent of another sect, is agreeable, let him be silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, let him speak.’

“Dinno saṅghena itthannāmassa aññatitthiyapubbassa cattāro māse parivāso. Khamati [P 1.0070] saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

‘Probation for four months has been granted by the Sangha to this person of such-and-such a name, a former adherent of another sect. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold it.’

87. “Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo ārādhako hoti, evaṃ anārādhako. Kathañca, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo anārādhako hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo atikālena [V 0.0089] gāmaṃ pavisati, atidivā paṭikkamati. Evampi, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo anārādhako hoti.

87. In this way, monks, a former adherent of another sect is satisfactory, and in this way, unsatisfactory. And how, monks, is a former adherent of another sect unsatisfactory? Here, monks, a former adherent of another sect enters a village too early and returns too late in the day. In this way also, monks, a former adherent of another sect is unsatisfactory.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo vesiyāgocaro vā hoti, vidhavāgocaro vā hoti, thullakumārikāgocaro vā hoti, paṇḍakagocaro vā hoti, bhikkhunigocaro vā hoti. Evampi, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo anārādhako hoti.

Furthermore, monks, a former adherent of another sect is one whose alms-round resort is prostitutes, or is one whose alms-round resort is widows, or is one whose alms-round resort is mature unmarried women, or is one whose alms-round resort is paṇḍakas, or is one whose alms-round resort is bhikkhunīs. In this way also, monks, a former adherent of another sect is unsatisfactory.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo yāni tāni sabrahmacārīnaṃ uccāvacāni karaṇīyāni, tattha na dakkho hoti, na analaso, na tatrupāyāya vīmaṃsāya samannāgato, na alaṃ kātuṃ, na alaṃ saṃvidhātuṃ. Evampi, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo anārādhako hoti.

Furthermore, monks, regarding the various duties, great and small, for his companions in the holy life, a former adherent of another sect is not skilled, not diligent, not endowed with the discerning inquiry for accomplishing the task, not able to do it, and not able to arrange it. In this way also, monks, a former adherent of another sect is unsatisfactory.

“Puna [M 0.0100] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo na tibbacchando hoti uddese, paripucchāya, adhisīle, adhicitte, adhipaññāya. Evampi, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo anārādhako hoti.

Furthermore, monks, a former adherent of another sect does not have keen desire for recitation, for inquiry, for the higher virtue, for the higher mind, or for the higher wisdom. In this way also, monks, a former adherent of another sect is unsatisfactory.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo yassa titthāyatanā saṅkanto hoti, tassa satthuno tassa diṭṭhiyā tassa khantiyā tassa ruciyā tassa ādāyassa [T 1.0146] avaṇṇe bhaññamāne kupito hoti anattamano anabhiraddho, buddhassa vā dhammassa vā saṅghassa vā avaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamano hoti udaggo abhiraddho. Yassa vā pana titthāyatanā saṅkanto hoti, tassa satthuno tassa diṭṭhiyā tassa khantiyā tassa ruciyā tassa ādāyassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamano hoti udaggo abhiraddho, buddhassa vā dhammassa vā saṅghassa vā vaṇṇe bhaññamāne kupito hoti anattamano anabhiraddho. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, saṅghātanikaṃ aññatitthiyapubbassa anārādhanīyasmiṃ. Evampi kho, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo anārādhako hoti. Evaṃ anārādhako kho, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo āgato na upasampādetabbo.

Furthermore, monks, regarding a former adherent of another sect, when dispraise is spoken of the teacher from whose sectarian establishment he has come—of his view, his preference, his inclination, or his adherence—he becomes angry, displeased at heart, and dissatisfied. But when dispraise is spoken of the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Sangha, he becomes pleased at heart, elated, and satisfied. And when praise is spoken of the teacher from whose sectarian establishment he has come—of his view, his preference, his inclination, or his adherence—he becomes pleased at heart, elated, and satisfied. But when praise is spoken of the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Sangha, he becomes angry, displeased at heart, and dissatisfied. This, monks, is the defining characteristic of what is unsatisfactory in a former adherent of another sect. In this way also, monks, a former adherent of another sect is unsatisfactory. Indeed, monks, such an unsatisfactory former adherent of another sect, having come, should not be given the higher ordination.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo ārādhako hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo nātikālena gāmaṃ pavisati nātidivā paṭikkamati. Evampi, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo ārādhako hoti.

“And how, monks, is one who was formerly of another sect one who pleases? Here, monks, one who was formerly of another sect does not enter a village too early, nor does he return too late in the day. In this way, monks, one who was formerly of another sect is one who pleases.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo na vesiyāgocaro hoti, na vidhavāgocaro hoti, na thullakumārikāgocaro hoti, na paṇḍakagocaro hoti, na bhikkhunigocaro hoti. Evampi, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo [P 1.0071] ārādhako hoti.

“Furthermore, monks, one who was formerly of another sect does not have a prostitute as his alms-round resort, does not have a widow as his alms-round resort, does not have a mature spinster as his alms-round resort, does not have a paṇḍaka as his alms-round resort, and does not have a bhikkhunī as his alms-round resort. In this way, monks, one who was formerly of another sect is one who pleases.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo yāni tāni sabrahmacārīnaṃ uccāvacāni karaṇīyāni, tattha dakkho hoti, analaso, tatrupāyāya vīmaṃsāya samannāgato, alaṃ kātuṃ, alaṃ saṃvidhātuṃ. Evampi, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo ārādhako hoti.

“Furthermore, monks, regarding the various duties, high and low, for his companions in the holy life, one who was formerly of another sect is skilled and not lazy; he is endowed with the investigative wisdom that is a means thereto, is capable of doing them, and is capable of arranging them. In this way, monks, one who was formerly of another sect is one who pleases.

“Puna [V 0.0090] caparaṃ, bhikkhave[T 1.0147], aññatitthiyapubbo tibbacchando hoti uddese, paripucchāya, adhisīle, adhicitte, adhipaññāya. Evampi, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo ārādhako hoti.

“Furthermore, monks, one who was formerly of another sect has a keen desire for learning, for questioning, for the higher virtue, for the higher mind, and for the higher wisdom. In this way, monks, one who was formerly of another sect is one who pleases.

“Puna [M 0.0101] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo yassa titthāyatanā saṅkanto hoti, tassa satthuno tassa diṭṭhiyā tassa khantiyā tassa ruciyā tassa ādāyassa avaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamano hoti udaggo abhiraddho, buddhassa vā dhammassa vā saṅghassa vā avaṇṇe bhaññamāne kupito hoti anattamano anabhiraddho. Yassa vā pana titthāyatanā saṅkanto hoti, tassa satthuno tassa diṭṭhiyā tassa khantiyā tassa ruciyā tassa ādāyassa vaṇṇe bhaññamāne kupito hoti anattamano anabhiraddho, buddhassa vā dhammassa vā saṅghassa vā vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamano hoti udaggo abhiraddho. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, saṅghātanikaṃ aññatitthiyapubbassa ārādhanīyasmiṃ. Evampi kho, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo ārādhako hoti. Evaṃ ārādhako kho, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo āgato upasampādetabbo.

“Furthermore, monks, from whichever teacher’s heretical abode one who was formerly of another sect has come, when dispraise is spoken of that teacher, of his view, of his preference, of his inclination, or of his adherence, he is pleased, uplifted, and gratified; but when dispraise is spoken of the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Saṅgha, he is angered, displeased, and ungratified. And from whichever teacher’s heretical abode he has come, when praise is spoken of that teacher, of his view, of his preference, of his inclination, or of his adherence, he is angered, displeased, and ungratified; but when praise is spoken of the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Saṅgha, he is pleased, uplifted, and gratified. This, monks, is the measure of what is pleasing in one who was formerly of another sect. In this way, monks, one who was formerly of another sect is one who pleases. Indeed, monks, one who was formerly of another sect who is pleasing in this way, having come, should be given the higher ordination.

“Sace, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyapubbo naggo āgacchati, upajjhāyamūlakaṃ cīvaraṃ pariyesitabbaṃ. Sace acchinnakeso āgacchati, saṅgho apaloketabbo bhaṇḍukammāya. Ye te, bhikkhave, aggikā jaṭilakā, te āgatā upasampādetabbā, na tesaṃ parivāso dātabbo. Taṃ kissa hetu? Kammavādino ete, bhikkhave, kiriyavādino. Sace, bhikkhave, jātiyā sākiyo aññatitthiyapubbo āgacchati[T 1.0148], so āgato upasampādetabbo, na tassa parivāso dātabbo. Imāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ñātīnaṃ āveṇikaṃ parihāraṃ dammī”ti.

“If, monks, one who was formerly of another sect comes naked, a robe should be sought with the preceptor as the basis. If he comes with uncut hair, the Saṅgha should be informed for the purpose of tonsure. Those fire-worshipping ascetics with matted hair, monks, upon their arrival, should be given the higher ordination; no period of probation is to be given to them. For what reason? These, monks, are proponents of kamma, proponents of action. If, monks, one who was formerly of another sect who is a Sakyan by birth comes, upon his arrival he is to be given the higher ordination; no period of probation is to be given to him. I, monks, grant this special dispensation to my kinsmen.”

Aññatitthiyapubbakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on those formerly of other sects is concluded.

Sattamabhāṇavāro.

The Seventh Recitation Section is finished.

26. Pañcābādhavatthu

26. The Story of the Five Diseases

88. Tena [V 0.0091] kho pana samayena magadhesu pañca ābādhā ussannā honti – kuṭṭhaṃ, gaṇḍo, kilāso, soso, apamāro. Manussā pañcahi ābādhehi phuṭṭhā jīvakaṃ komārabhaccaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadanti – “sādhu no, ācariya, tikicchāhī”ti. “Ahaṃ khvayyo, bahukicco bahukaraṇīyo; rājā ca me māgadho seniyo [P 1.0072] bimbisāro upaṭṭhātabbo [M 0.0102] itthāgārañca buddhappamukho ca bhikkhusaṅgho; nāhaṃ sakkomi tikicchitu”nti. “Sabbaṃ sāpateyyañca te, ācariya, hotu; mayañca te dāsā; sādhu, no, ācariya, tikicchāhī”ti. “Ahaṃ khvayyo, bahukicco bahukaraṇīyo rājā ca me māgadho seniyo bimbisāro upaṭṭhātabbo itthāgārañca buddhappamukho ca bhikkhusaṅgho; nāhaṃ sakkomi tikicchitu”nti. Atha kho tesaṃ manussānaṃ etadahosi – “ime kho samaṇā sakyaputtiyā sukhasīlā sukhasamācārā, subhojanāni bhuñjitvā nivātesu sayanesu sayanti. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ samaṇesu sakyaputtiyesu pabbajeyyāma. Tattha bhikkhū ceva upaṭṭhahissanti, jīvako ca komārabhacco tikicchissatī”ti[T 1.0149]. Atha kho te manussā bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā pabbajjaṃ yāciṃsu. Te bhikkhū pabbājesuṃ, upasampādesuṃ. Te bhikkhū ceva upaṭṭhahiṃsu jīvako ca komārabhacco tikicchi. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū bahū gilāne bhikkhū upaṭṭhahantā yācanabahulā viññattibahulā viharanti – gilānabhattaṃ detha, gilānupaṭṭhākabhattaṃ detha, gilānabhesajjaṃ dethāti. Jīvakopi komārabhacco bahū gilāne bhikkhū tikicchanto aññataraṃ rājakiccaṃ parihāpesi.

88. At that time, five diseases were prevalent in Magadha—leprosy, boils, skin disease, consumption, and epilepsy. People afflicted by these five diseases approached Jīvaka Komārabhacca and said, “Please, teacher, treat us.” “Sirs, I am busy, with much to do. I must attend to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, the women’s quarters, and the community of monks with the Buddha at its head. I cannot treat you.” “All our property shall be yours, teacher, and we will be your slaves. Please, teacher, treat us.” “Sirs, I am busy, with much to do. I must attend to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, the women’s quarters, and the community of monks with the Buddha at its head. I cannot treat you.” Then those people thought, “These Sakyan ascetics are of comfortable habits and pleasant conduct; they eat good food and sleep in sheltered beds. Why don’t we go forth among the Sakyan ascetics? There, the monks will care for us, and Jīvaka Komārabhacca will treat us.” So they approached the monks and requested the going forth. The monks gave them the going forth and the higher ordination. The monks cared for them, and Jīvaka Komārabhacca treated them. At that time, monks who were caring for many sick monks were much given to asking and making requests: “Give food for the sick, give food for those attending the sick, give medicine for the sick.” Jīvaka Komārabhacca, while treating many sick monks, neglected a certain royal duty.

89. Aññataropi puriso pañcahi ābādhehi phuṭṭho jīvakaṃ komārabhaccaṃ upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – “sādhu maṃ, ācariya, tikicchāhī”ti. “Ahaṃ khvayyo, bahukicco, bahukaraṇīyo, rājā ca me māgadho seniyo bimbisāro upaṭṭhātabbo itthāgārañca buddhappamukho ca bhikkhusaṅgho; nāhaṃ sakkomi tikicchitu”nti. “Sabbaṃ sāpateyyañca te, ācariya, hotu, ahañca te dāso; sādhu maṃ, ācariya, tikicchāhī”ti. “Ahaṃ khvayyo, bahukicco bahukaraṇīyo, rājā ca me māgadho seniyo bimbisāro upaṭṭhātabbo itthāgārañca buddhappamukho ca bhikkhusaṅgho, nāhaṃ sakkomi tikicchitu”nti. Atha kho tassa purisassa etadahosi – “ime kho samaṇā sakyaputtiyā sukhasīlā sukhasamācārā, subhojanāni bhuñjitvā nivātesu sayanesu sayanti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ samaṇesu sakyaputtiyesu pabbajeyyaṃ. Tattha bhikkhū ceva upaṭṭhahissanti, jīvako ca komārabhacco tikicchissati. Somhi sohaṃ (bahūsu, vimativinodanīṭīkā oloketabbā) arogo vibbhamissāmī”ti[V 0.0092]. Atha kho so [T 1.0150] puriso bhikkhu upasaṅkamitvā [M 0.0103] pabbajjaṃ yāci. Taṃ bhikkhū pabbājesuṃ, upasampādesuṃ. Taṃ bhikkhū ceva upaṭṭhahiṃsu, jīvako ca komārabhacco tikicchi. So arogo vibbhami. Addasā kho jīvako [P 1.0073] komārabhacco taṃ purisaṃ vibbhantaṃ, disvāna taṃ purisaṃ etadavoca – “nanu tvaṃ, ayyo, bhikkhūsu pabbajito ahosī”ti? “Evaṃ, ācariyā”ti. “Kissa pana tvaṃ, ayyo, evarūpamakāsī”ti? Atha kho so puriso jīvakassa komārabhaccassa etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Jīvako komārabhacco ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma bhadantā bhaddantā (ka.) pañcahi ābādhehi phuṭṭhaṃ pabbājessantī”ti. Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho jīvako komārabhacco bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu, bhante, ayyā pañcahi ābādhehi phuṭṭhaṃ na pabbājeyyu”nti. Atha kho bhagavā jīvakaṃ komārabhaccaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, pañcahi ābādhehi phuṭṭho pabbājetabbo. Yo pabbājeyya, āpatti [T 1.0151] dukkaṭassā”ti.

89. A certain man afflicted with five diseases approached Jīvaka Komārabhacca and said, “I implore you, Master, treat me.” “Sir, I am very busy with many duties. I must attend to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, the women’s quarters, and the community of monks with the Buddha at its head. I cannot treat you.” “Master, let all my possessions be yours, and I will be your slave. I implore you, Master, treat me.” “Sir, I am very busy with many duties. I must attend to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, the women’s quarters, and the community of monks with the Buddha at its head. I cannot treat you.” Then that man thought, “These Sakyan ascetics have comfortable habits and comfortable conduct, eat good food, and sleep in beds sheltered from the wind. What if I were to go forth among the Sakyan ascetics? There, the monks will attend to me, and Jīvaka Komārabhacca will treat me. Then I will recover and leave the Order.” So that man approached the monks and requested the going forth. The monks gave him the going forth and the higher ordination. The monks attended to him, and Jīvaka Komārabhacca treated him. He recovered and left the Order. Jīvaka Komārabhacca saw that man after he had left the Order and said to him, “Sir, were you not one who had gone forth among the monks?” “Yes, Master.” “Then why, sir, did you act in such a way?” Then that man explained the matter to Jīvaka Komārabhacca. Jīvaka Komārabhacca complained, criticized, and protested, “How could the venerable ones give the going forth to someone afflicted with five diseases?” Then Jīvaka Komārabhacca approached the Blessed One, paid homage, and sat down to one side. Seated there, he said, “Venerable sir, it would be good if the venerable ones did not give the going forth to someone afflicted with five diseases.” Then the Blessed One instructed, roused, encouraged, and gladdened Jīvaka Komārabhacca with a talk on the Dhamma. Having been instructed, roused, encouraged, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a talk on the Dhamma, Jīvaka Komārabhacca rose from his seat, paid homage, circumambulated the Blessed One, and departed. Then, on this occasion, the Blessed One gave a talk on the Dhamma and addressed the monks: “Monks, one afflicted with five diseases is not to be given the going forth. Whoever gives the going forth commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Pañcābādhavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Story of the Five Diseases is concluded.

27. Rājabhaṭavatthu

27. The Story of the Royal Servant

90. Tena kho pana samayena rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa paccanto kupito hoti. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro senānāyake mahāmatte āṇāpesi – “gacchatha, bhaṇe, paccantaṃ uccinathā”ti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho senānāyakā mahāmattā rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa paccassosuṃ. Atha kho abhiññātānaṃ abhiññātānaṃ yodhānaṃ etadahosi – “mayaṃ kho yuddhābhinandino gacchantā pāpañca karoma, bahuñca apuññaṃ pasavāma. Kena nu kho mayaṃ upāyena pāpā ca virameyyāma kalyāṇañca kareyyāmā”ti? Atha kho tesaṃ yodhānaṃ etadahosi – “ime kho [M 0.0104] samaṇā sakyaputtiyā dhammacārino samacārino brahmacārino saccavādino sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā. Sace kho mayaṃ samaṇesu sakyaputtiyesu pabbajeyyāma, evaṃ mayaṃ pāpā ca virameyyāma kalyāṇañca kareyyāmā”ti. Atha kho te yodhā bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā pabbajjaṃ yāciṃsu. Te bhikkhū pabbājesuṃ, upasampādesuṃ. Senānāyakā mahāmattā rājabhaṭe [V 0.0093] pucchiṃsu – “kiṃ nu [P 1.0074] kho, bhaṇe, itthannāmo ca itthannāmo ca yodhā na dissantī”ti? “Itthannāmo ca itthannāmo ca, sāmi, yodhā bhikkhūsu pabbajitā”ti. Senānāyakā mahāmattā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā rājabhaṭaṃ pabbājessantī”ti. Senānāyakā mahāmattā rañño [T 1.0152] māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro vohārike mahāmatte pucchi – “yo, bhaṇe, rājabhaṭaṃ pabbājeti, kiṃ so pasavatī”ti? “Upajjhāyassa, deva, sīsaṃ chetabbaṃ, anussāvakassa anusāvakassa (ka.) jivhā uddharitabbā, gaṇassa upaḍḍhaphāsukā bhañjitabbā”ti. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “santi, bhante, rājāno assaddhā appasannā. Te appamattakenapi bhikkhū viheṭheyyuṃ. Sādhu, bhante, ayyā rājabhaṭaṃ na pabbājeyyu”nti. Atha kho bhagavā rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ seniyaṃ bimbisāraṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, rājabhaṭo pabbājetabbo. Yo pabbājeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

90. Now at that time, the border region of King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha was in revolt. Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha ordered his generals and great ministers: ‘Go, sirs, and quell the border region.’ ‘Yes, Your Majesty,’ replied the generals and great ministers to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha. Then this thought occurred to the most renowned warriors: ‘We, delighting in battle, will do evil and generate much demerit by going. By what means could we refrain from evil and do good?’ Then this thought occurred to those warriors: ‘These recluses, the sons of the Sakyan, practice the Dhamma, are of peaceful conduct, live the holy life, are truthful, virtuous, and of good character. If we were to go forth among the recluses, the sons of the Sakyan, we would thus refrain from evil and do good.’ Then those warriors approached the monks and asked for the going forth. The monks gave them the going forth and the full admission. The generals and great ministers asked the king’s men: ‘Why is it, sirs, that the warriors so-and-so and so-and-so are not seen?’ ‘Sirs, the warriors so-and-so and so-and-so have gone forth among the monks.’ The generals and great ministers complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: ‘How indeed can the recluses, the sons of the Sakyan, give the going forth to a king’s man?’ The generals and great ministers informed King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha of this matter. Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha asked the judicial ministers: ‘Sirs, one who gives the going forth to a king’s man, what penalty does he incur?’ ‘Your Majesty, the preceptor’s head should be cut off, the announcer’s tongue should be pulled out, and half the ribs of the chapter should be broken.’ Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha went to the Blessed One, and having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha said this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, there are kings who are faithless and displeased. They might harass the monks for even a trivial reason. It would be good, venerable sir, if the noble ones did not give the going forth to a king’s man.’ Then the Blessed One instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha with a talk on the Dhamma. Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, having been instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a talk on the Dhamma, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping him to the right, and departed. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this matter, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: ‘Monks, a king’s man is not to be given the going forth. Whoever should give one the going forth commits an offense of wrong-doing.’

Rājabhaṭavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story of the king’s man is concluded.

28. Aṅgulimālacoravatthu

28. The Story of the Robber Aṅgulimāla

91. Tena kho pana samayena coro aṅgulimālo bhikkhūsu pabbajito hoti. Manussā passitvā ubbijjantipi, uttasantipi, palāyantipi[T 1.0153], aññenapi gacchanti, aññenapi mukhaṃ karonti, dvārampi thakenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti [M 0.0105] khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā dhajabandhaṃ coraṃ pabbājessantī”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… na, bhikkhave, dhajabandho coro pabbājetabbo. Yo pabbājeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

91. At that time, the robber Aṅgulimāla had gone forth among the monks. People, upon seeing him, were alarmed, terrified, and fled; they went by another way, turned their faces in another direction, and also closed their doors. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed could the recluses, sons of the Sakyan, give the going forth to a notorious robber?” The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and speaking disparagingly. Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Monks, a notorious robber is not to be given the going forth. Whoever should give one the going forth commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Aṅgulimālacoravatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story of the robber Aṅgulimāla is concluded.

29. Kārabhedakacoravatthu

29. The Story of the Prison-Breaking Robber

92. Tena [V 0.0094] kho pana samayena raññā māgadhena seniyena bimbisārena [P 1.0075] anuññātaṃ hoti – “ye samaṇesu sakyaputtiyesu pabbajanti, na te labbhā kiñci kātuṃ; svākkhāto dhammo, carantu brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro puriso corikaṃ katvā kārāya baddho hoti. So kāraṃ bhinditvā palāyitvā bhikkhūsu pabbajito hoti. Manussā passitvā evamāhaṃsu – “ayaṃ so kārabhedako coro. Handa, naṃ nemā”ti. Ekacce evamāhaṃsu – “māyyo, evaṃ avacuttha. Anuññātaṃ raññā māgadhena seniyena bimbisārena – “ye samaṇesu sakyaputtiyesu pabbajanti, na te labbhā kiñci kātuṃ; svākkhāto dhammo, carantu brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “abhayūvarā ime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā, nayime [T 1.0154] labbhā kiñci kātuṃ. Kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā kārabhedakaṃ coraṃ pabbājessantī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, kārabhedako coro pabbājetabbo. Yo pabbājeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

92. Now at that time, King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha had granted permission: “Nothing may be done to those who go forth among the recluses, the sons of the Sakyan; the Dhamma is well-proclaimed, let them practice the holy life rightly for the complete ending of suffering.” At that time, a certain man, having committed theft, was bound in prison. He broke out of prison, escaped, and went forth among the monks. People, upon seeing him, said: “This is that prison-breaking thief. Come, let us seize him.” Some said: “Sirs, do not speak thus. King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha has granted permission: ‘Nothing may be done to those who go forth among the recluses, the sons of the Sakyan; the Dhamma is well-proclaimed, let them practice the holy life rightly for the complete ending of suffering.’” People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “These recluses, the sons of the Sakyan, are a safe refuge; nothing can be done to them. How indeed can the recluses, the sons of the Sakyan, give the going forth to a prison-breaking thief?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a prison-breaking thief is not to be given the going forth. Whoever should give one the going forth commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Kārabhedakacoravatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story of the prison-breaking robber is concluded.

30. Likhitakacoravatthu

30. The Story of the Proscribed Robber

93. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro puriso corikaṃ katvā palāyitvā bhikkhūsu pabbajito hoti. So ca rañño antepure likhito hoti – yattha passati, tattha hantabboti. Manussā passitvā evamāhaṃsu – “ayaṃ so likhitako coro. Handa, naṃ hanāmā”ti. Ekacce evamāhaṃsu – “māyyo, evaṃ avacuttha. Anuññātaṃ raññā māgadhena seniyena bimbisārena “ye samaṇesu sakyaputtiyesu pabbajanti, na te labbhā kiñci kātuṃ, svākkhāto dhammo, carantu brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “abhayūvarā [M 0.0106] ime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā, nayime labbhā kiñci kātuṃ. Kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā likhitakaṃ coraṃ pabbājessantī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, likhitako coro pabbājetabbo. Yo pabbājeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

93. Now at that time, a certain man, having committed theft, fled and went forth among the monks. He had been proscribed by the king’s inner court: “Wherever he is seen, he should be killed.” People, upon seeing him, said: “This is that proscribed thief. Come, let us kill him.” Some said: “Sirs, do not speak thus. King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha has granted permission: ‘Nothing may be done to those who go forth among the Sakyan ascetics; the Dhamma is well-proclaimed, let them practice the holy life rightly for making an end of suffering.’” People complained, criticized, and spread disparaging talk: “These Sakyan ascetics are immune; nothing can be done to them. How can the Sakyan ascetics ordain a proscribed thief?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a proscribed thief should not be ordained. Whoever ordains him commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Likhitakacoravatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Story of the Proscribed Thief is concluded.

31. Kasāhatavatthu

The Story of the Flogged Man

94. Tena [V 0.0095] kho pana samayena aññataro puriso kasāhato katadaṇḍakammo bhikkhūsu pabbajito hoti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā kasāhataṃ katadaṇḍakammaṃ pabbājessantī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na[T 1.0155], bhikkhave, kasāhato katadaṇḍakammo pabbājetabbo. Yo pabbājeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

31. Now at that time a certain man who had been flogged and had undergone punishment had gone forth among the monks. People complained, criticized, and spread disparaging talk, saying: “How can these Sakyan ascetics ordain one who has been flogged and has undergone punishment?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, one who has been flogged and has undergone punishment should not be ordained. Whoever ordains such a person incurs an offense of wrong-doing.”

Kasāhatavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Story of the Flogged Man is concluded.

32. Lakkhaṇāhatavatthu

94. The Story of the Branded Man

95. Tena [P 1.0076] kho pana samayena aññataro puriso lakkhaṇāhato katadaṇḍakammo bhikkhūsu pabbajito hoti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā lakkhaṇāhataṃ katadaṇḍakammaṃ pabbājessantī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, lakkhaṇāhato katadaṇḍakammo pabbājetabbo. Yo pabbājeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Now at that time, a certain man who was branded and had undergone punishment went forth among the monks. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the Sakyan ascetics ordain a man who is branded and has undergone punishment?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, one who is branded and has undergone punishment should not be ordained. Whoever ordains such a one commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Lakkhaṇāhatavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Story of the Branded Man is concluded.

33. Iṇāyikavatthu

32. The Story of the Debtor

96. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro puriso iṇāyiko palāyitvā bhikkhūsu pabbajito hoti. Dhaniyā passitvā evamāhaṃsu – “ayaṃ so amhākaṃ iṇāyiko. Handa, naṃ nemā”ti. Ekacce evamāhaṃsu – “māyyo, evaṃ avacuttha. Anuññātaṃ raññā māgadhena seniyena bimbisārena – “ye samaṇesu sakyaputtiyesu pabbajanti, na te labbhā kiñci kātuṃ; svākkhāto dhammo, carantu brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “abhayūvarā ime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā. Nayime labbhā kiñci kātuṃ. Kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā iṇāyikaṃ pabbājessantī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ [V 0.0096] ārocesuṃ[M 0.0107]. Na, bhikkhave, iṇāyiko pabbājetabbo. Yo pabbājeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

95. Now at that time, a certain man, being in debt, fled and went forth among the monks. His creditors saw him and said, “This is our debtor. Come, let us take him.” Some said, “Sirs, do not speak thus. King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha has granted permission: ‘Nothing may be done to those who go forth among the Sakyan ascetics; the Dhamma is well-proclaimed, let them practice the holy life rightly for making an end of suffering.’” People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “These Sakyan ascetics are immune. Nothing can be done to them. How indeed can the Sakyan ascetics ordain a debtor?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a debtor should not be ordained. Whoever ordains such a one commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Iṇāyikavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Story of the Debtor is concluded.

34. Dāsavatthu

The Story of a Slave

97. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro dāso palāyitvā bhikkhūsu [T 1.0156] pabbajito hoti. Ayyakā ayyikā (ka.), ayirakā (sī.) passitvā evamāhaṃsu – “ayaṃ so amhākaṃ dāso. Handa, naṃ nemā”ti. Ekacce evamāhaṃsu – “māyyo, evaṃ avacuttha, anuññātaṃ raññā māgadhena seniyena bimbisārena “ye samaṇesu sakyaputtiyesu pabbajanti, na te labbhā kiñci kātuṃ, svākkhāto dhammo, carantu brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā”ti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “abhayūvarā ime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā, nayime labbhā kiñci kātuṃ. Kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā dāsaṃ pabbājessantī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, dāso pabbājetabbo. Yo pabbājeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

33. Now at that time, a certain slave, having run away, had gone forth among the monks. His masters saw him and said, “This is our slave. Come, let us take him.” Some said, “Sirs, do not speak thus. King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha has granted permission: ‘Nothing may be done to those who go forth among the Sakyan ascetics; the Dhamma is well-proclaimed, let them practice the holy life rightly for making an end of suffering.’” People complained, scorned, and spoke disparagingly: “These Sakyan ascetics are immune; nothing can be done to them. How indeed could the Sakyan ascetics ordain a slave?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a slave is not to be ordained. Whoever should ordain one, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Dāsavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Story of the Slave is concluded.

35. Kammārabhaṇḍuvatthu

96. The Story of Kammārabhaṇḍu

98. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro kammārabhaṇḍu mātāpitūhi saddhiṃ bhaṇḍitvā ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhūsu pabbajito hoti. Atha kho tassa kammārabhaṇḍussa mātāpitaro taṃ kammārabhaṇḍuṃ vicinantā ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhū pucchiṃsu – “api, bhante, evarūpaṃ dārakaṃ passeyyāthā”ti? Bhikkhū ajānaṃyeva āhaṃsu – “na jānāmā”ti, apassaṃyeva āhaṃsu – “na passāmā”ti. Atha kho tassa kammārabhaṇḍussa mātāpitaro taṃ kammārabhaṇḍuṃ vicinantā [P 1.0077] bhikkhūsu pabbajitaṃ disvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “alajjino ime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā, dussīlā musāvādino. Jānaṃyeva āhaṃsu – ‘na jānāmā’ti, passaṃyeva āhaṃsu – ‘na passāmā’ti. Ayaṃ dārako bhikkhūsu [T 1.0157] pabbajito”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tassa kammārabhaṇḍussa mātāpitūnaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū [V 0.0097] bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghaṃ apaloketuṃ bhaṇḍukammāyāti.

Now at that time a certain bald-headed son of a goldsmith, having quarreled with his parents, went to the monastery and was ordained among the monks. Then that bald-headed son of a goldsmith's parents, searching for him, went to the monastery and asked the monks: “Venerable sirs, have you seen a boy like this?” The monks, not knowing, said: “We do not know.” Not seeing, they said: “We do not see.” Then that bald-headed son of a goldsmith's parents, searching for him, saw him ordained among the monks and complained, grumbled, and protested: “These shameless Sakyan ascetics are immoral and liars. Though they knew, they said, ‘We do not know’; though they saw, they said, ‘We do not see.’ This boy has been ordained among the monks!” The monks heard the complaining, grumbling, and protesting of that bald-headed son of a goldsmith's parents. Then those monks informed the Blessed One of this matter. “I allow, monks, to consult the Sangha for the act of tonsure.”

Kammārabhaṇḍuvatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Story of the Bald-headed Son of a Goldsmith is concluded.

36. Upālidārakavatthu

34. The Story of Upāli the Boy

99. idaṃ vatthu pāci. 402 ādayo Tena [M 0.0108] kho pana samayena rājagahe sattarasavaggiyā dārakā sahāyakā honti. Upālidārako tesaṃ pāmokkho hoti. Atha kho upālissa mātāpitūnaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho upāyena upāli amhākaṃ accayena sukhañca jīveyya, na ca kilameyyā”ti? Atha kho upālissa mātāpitūnaṃ etadahosi – “sace kho upāli lekhaṃ sikkheyya, evaṃ kho upāli amhākaṃ accayena sukhañca jīveyya, na ca kilameyyā”ti. Atha kho upālissa mātāpitūnaṃ etadahosi – “sace kho upāli lekhaṃ sikkhissati, aṅguliyo dukkhā bhavissanti. Sace kho upāli gaṇanaṃ sikkheyya, evaṃ kho upāli amhākaṃ accayena sukhañca jīveyya, na ca kilameyyā”ti. Atha kho upālissa mātāpitūnaṃ etadahosi – “sace kho upāli gaṇanaṃ sikkhissati, urassa dukkho bhavissati. Sace kho upāli rūpaṃ sikkheyya, evaṃ kho upāli amhākaṃ accayena sukhañca jīveyya, na ca kilameyyā”ti. Atha kho upālissa mātāpitūnaṃ etadahosi – “sace kho upāli rūpaṃ sikkhissati, akkhīni dukkhā bhavissanti. Ime kho samaṇā sakyaputtiyā sukhasīlā sukhasamācārā, subhojanāni bhuñjitvā nivātesu sayanesu sayanti[T 1.0158]. Sace kho upāli samaṇesu sakyaputtiyesu pabbajeyya, evaṃ kho upāli amhākaṃ accayena sukhañca jīveyya, na ca kilameyyā”ti.

99. Now at that time in Rājagaha, there was a group of seventeen boys who were friends. Among them, the boy Upāli was the foremost. Then Upāli’s parents thought: “By what means could Upāli live happily after our passing, without toiling?” Then Upāli’s parents thought: “If Upāli were to learn writing, then after our passing, he could live happily and without toiling.” Then Upāli’s parents thought: “But if Upāli learns writing, his fingers will ache. If Upāli were to learn arithmetic, then after our passing, he could live happily and without toiling.” Then Upāli’s parents thought: “But if Upāli learns arithmetic, his chest will ache. If Upāli were to learn assaying, then after our passing, he could live happily and without toiling.” Then Upāli’s parents thought: “But if Upāli learns assaying, his eyes will ache. These ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, are of pleasant habits and conduct; they eat good food and sleep in beds sheltered from the wind. If Upāli were to go forth among the ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, then after our passing, he could live happily and without toiling.”

Assosi kho upālidārako mātāpitūnaṃ imaṃ kathāsallāpaṃ. Atha kho upālidārako yena te dārakā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā te dārake etadavoca – “etha mayaṃ, ayyā, samaṇesu sakyaputtiyesu pabbajissāmā”ti. “Sace kho tvaṃ, ayya, pabbajissasi, evaṃ mayampi pabbajissāmā”ti. Atha kho te dārakā ekamekassa mātāpitaro upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – “anujānātha maṃ agārasmā anāgāriyaṃ pabbajjāyā”ti. Atha kho tesaṃ dārakānaṃ [P 1.0078] mātāpitaro – “sabbepime dārakā samānacchandā kalyāṇādhippāyā”ti – anujāniṃsu. Te bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā pabbajjaṃ yāciṃsu. Te bhikkhū pabbājesuṃ upasampādesuṃ[V 0.0098]. Te rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya rodanti – “yāguṃ detha, bhattaṃ detha, khādanīyaṃ dethā”ti. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “āgametha, āvuso, yāva ratti vibhāyati. Sace yāgu bhavissati [M 0.0109] pivissatha, sace bhattaṃ bhavissati bhuñjissatha, sace khādanīyaṃ bhavissati khādissatha; no ce bhavissati yāgu vā bhattaṃ vā khādanīyaṃ vā, piṇḍāya caritvā bhuñjissathā”ti. Evampi kho te bhikkhū bhikkhūhi vuccamānā rodantiyeva “yāguṃ detha, bhattaṃ detha, khādanīyaṃ dethā”ti; senāsanaṃ uhadantipi ummihantipi.

The boy Upāli heard this conversation of his parents. Then the boy Upāli went to where those boys were, and having approached them, he said this: “Come, sirs, let us go forth among the ascetics, sons of the Sakyan.” They replied, “If you, sir, will go forth, then we too will go forth.” Then those boys, having approached the parents of each one, said this: “Permit me to go forth from the household life into the homeless life.” Then the parents of those boys, thinking, “All these boys have the same desire and a noble intention,” gave their permission. They approached the monks and requested the going forth. The monks gave them the going forth and the higher ordination. Having risen early at dawn, they would cry: “Give us gruel! Give us rice! Give us snacks!” The monks said this: “Wait, friends, until daybreak. If there is gruel, you may drink it; if there is rice, you may eat it; if there are snacks, you may eat them. If there is no gruel, or rice, or snacks, you may eat after going on alms round.” Even when spoken to thus by the monks, they just kept crying, “Give us gruel! Give us rice! Give us snacks!” and they would soil the lodging with excrement and urine.

Assosi kho bhagavā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ [T 1.0159] paccuṭṭhāya dārakasaddaṃ. Sutvāna āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “kiṃ nu kho so, ānanda, dārakasaddo”ti? Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū jānaṃ ūnavīsativassaṃ puggalaṃ upasampādentī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… “kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā jānaṃ ūnavīsativassaṃ puggalaṃ upasampādessanti. Ūnavīsativasso, bhikkhave, puggalo akkhamo hoti sītassa uṇhassa jighacchāya pipāsāya ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṃ duruttānaṃ durāgatānaṃ vacanapathānaṃ uppannānaṃ sārīrikānaṃ vedanānaṃ dukkhānaṃ tibbānaṃ kharānaṃ kaṭukānaṃ asātānaṃ amanāpānaṃ pāṇaharānaṃ anadhivāsakajātiko hoti. Vīsativassova kho, bhikkhave, puggalo khamo hoti sītassa uṇhassa jighacchāya pipāsāya ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṃ duruttānaṃ durāgatānaṃ vacanapathānaṃ, uppannānaṃ sārīrikānaṃ vedanānaṃ dukkhānaṃ tibbānaṃ kharānaṃ kaṭukānaṃ asātānaṃ amanāpānaṃ pāṇaharānaṃ adhivāsakajātiko hoti. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya, pasannānaṃ vā bhiyyobhāvāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, jānaṃ ūnavīsativasso puggalo upasampādetabbo. Yo upasampādeyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.

The Blessed One, having arisen in the early morning, heard the sound of the boys. Having heard it, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda, “Ānanda, what is that sound of boys?” Then the Venerable Ānanda informed the Blessed One of this matter… “Is it true, monks, as is said, that monks knowingly give the higher ordination to a person under twenty years of age?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How indeed, monks, can those foolish men knowingly give the higher ordination to a person under twenty years of age? A person under twenty years of age, monks, is incapable of enduring cold, heat, hunger, and thirst; the touch of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things; ill-spoken and ill-come courses of speech; and is of a nature unable to endure arisen bodily feelings that are painful, sharp, harsh, piercing, disagreeable, unpleasant, and life-taking. A person of twenty years of age, monks, is capable of enduring cold, heat, hunger, and thirst; the touch of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things; ill-spoken and ill-come courses of speech; and is of a nature able to endure arisen bodily feelings that are painful, sharp, harsh, piercing, disagreeable, unpleasant, and life-taking. This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident, nor for the increase of the confident…” Having rebuked them… having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, a person known to be under twenty years of age is not to be given the higher ordination. Whoever should give the higher ordination is to be dealt with according to the Dhamma.”

Upālidārakavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Story of the Boy Upāli is concluded.

37. Ahivātakarogavatthu

37. The Story of the Snake-Wind Disease

100. Tena kho pana samayena aññataraṃ kulaṃ ahivātakarogena kālaṅkataṃ hoti. Tassa pitāputtakā sesā honti. Te bhikkhūsu pabbajitvā [T 1.0160] ekatova piṇḍāya caranti. Atha kho so dārako pituno bhikkhāya dinnāya upadhāvitvā etadavoca – “mayhampi, tāta, dehi; mayhampi[V 0.0099], tāta, dehī”ti. Manussā ujjhāyanti [P 1.0079] khiyyanti vipācenti – “abrahmacārino ime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā. Ayampi dārako bhikkhuniyā jāto”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ [M 0.0110] khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, ūnapannarasavasso dārako pabbājetabbo. Yo pabbājeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

100. At that time, a certain family had died from a wind-disease like snake venom. Only the father and son of that family remained. Those two, having gone forth among the bhikkhus, went for alms together. Then, when alms were given to his father, that boy ran up and said, 'Father, give some to me too! Father, give some to me too!' People complained, grumbled, and criticized, saying, 'These ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, are unchaste. This boy was born of a bhikkhunī.' The bhikkhus heard those people complaining, grumbling, and criticizing. Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, 'Bhikkhus, a boy under fifteen years of age should not be given the going forth. Whoever should give the going forth commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato ānandassa upaṭṭhākakulaṃ saddhaṃ pasannaṃ ahivātakarogena kālaṅkataṃ hoti, dve ca dārakā sesā honti. Te porāṇakena āciṇṇakappena bhikkhū passitvā upadhāvanti. Bhikkhū apasādenti. Te bhikkhūhi apasādiyamānā rodanti. Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘na ūnapannarasavasso dārako pabbājetabbo’ti. Ime ca dārakā ūnapannarasavassā. Kena nu kho upāyena ime dārakā na vinasseyyu”nti? Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Ussahanti pana te, ānanda, dārakā kāke uḍḍāpetunti? Ussahanti, bhagavāti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ūnapannarasavassaṃ dārakaṃ kākuḍḍepakaṃ pabbājetu”nti.

At that time, the faithful and devoted supporter family of the Venerable Ānanda had died from a wind-disease like snake venom, and two boys remained. Following a former custom, upon seeing the bhikkhus, they ran up to them. The bhikkhus drove them away. Being driven away by the bhikkhus, those boys cried. Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Ānanda: 'It has been laid down by the Blessed One: "A boy under fifteen years of age should not be given the going forth." And these boys are under fifteen years of age. By what means, indeed, might these boys not be ruined?' Then the Venerable Ānanda reported this matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One asked, 'Ānanda, are those boys able to scare away crows?' 'They are able, Blessed One,' he replied. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: 'Bhikkhus, I allow the going forth for a boy under fifteen years of age who is able to scare away crows.'

Ahivātakarogavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Story of the Snake-Wind Disease is concluded.

38. Kaṇṭakavatthu

The Story concerning Kaṇṭaka

101. Tena [T 1.0161] kho pana samayena āyasmato upanandassa sakyaputtassa dve sāmaṇerā honti – kaṇṭako ca mahako ca. Te aññamaññaṃ dūsesuṃ. Bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma sāmaṇerā evarūpaṃ anācāraṃ ācarissantī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, ekena dve sāmaṇerā upaṭṭhāpetabbā. Yo upaṭṭhāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

38. At that time, the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan had two novices, Kaṇṭaka and Mahaka. They corrupted one another. The bhikkhus complained, grumbled, and criticized: 'How indeed could novices engage in such improper conduct?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, 'Bhikkhus, two novices are not to be taken into service by a single bhikkhu. Whoever should take them into service commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

Kaṇṭakavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Story of Kaṇṭaka is concluded.

39. Āhundarikavatthu

101. The Story concerning Confinement

102. Tena [V 0.0100] kho pana samayena bhagavā tattheva rājagahe vassaṃ vasi, tattha hemantaṃ, tattha gimhaṃ. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “āhundarikā samaṇānaṃ sakyaputtiyānaṃ disā andhakārā, na imesaṃ disā pakkhāyantī”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi [M 0.0111] – “gacchānanda, avāpuraṇaṃ apāpuraṇaṃ (ka.) ādāya [P 1.0080] anupariveṇiyaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ārocehi – “icchatāvuso bhagavā dakkhiṇāgiriṃ cārikaṃ pakkamituṃ. Yassāyasmato attho, so āgacchatū”ti. Evaṃ, bhante, ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā avāpuraṇaṃ ādāya anupariveṇiyaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ārocesi – ‘icchatāvuso bhagavā dakkhiṇāgiriṃ cārikaṃ pakkamituṃ. Yassāyasmato attho, so āgacchatū’”ti. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “bhagavatā, āvuso ānanda, paññattaṃ dasavassāni nissāya vatthuṃ, dasavassena [T 1.0162] nissayaṃ dātuṃ. Tattha ca no gantabbaṃ bhavissati, nissayo ca gahetabbo bhavissati, ittaro ca vāso bhavissati, puna ca paccāgantabbaṃ bhavissati, puna ca nissayo gahetabbo bhavissati. Sace amhākaṃ ācariyupajjhāyā gamissanti, mayampi gamissāma; no ce amhākaṃ ācariyupajjhāyā gamissanti, mayampi na gamissāma. Lahucittakatā no, āvuso ānanda, paññāyissatī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā ogaṇena bhikkhusaṅghena dakkhiṇāgiriṃ cārikaṃ pakkāmi.

At that time, the Blessed One dwelt right there in Rājagaha for the rainy season, there for the winter, and there for the summer. People complained, grumbled, and criticized: 'Are the horizons for the Sakyan ascetics confined? Are they obscured? Do their horizons not appear clearly?' The bhikkhus heard those people complaining, grumbling, and criticizing. Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: 'Go, Ānanda, take the sounding-bar and announce to the bhikkhus in every residence: “Friends, the Blessed One wishes to set out on a journey to Dakkhiṇāgiri. Let any venerable one who wishes to, come.”' 'Very well, venerable sir,' replied the Venerable Ānanda to the Blessed One. Taking the sounding-bar, he announced to the bhikkhus in every residence: 'Friends, the Blessed One wishes to set out on a journey to Dakkhiṇāgiri. Let any venerable one who wishes to, come.' The bhikkhus said: 'Friend Ānanda, it has been laid down by the Blessed One that one must live in dependence for ten years, and that one of ten years' standing may grant dependence. We would have to go there and take dependence, our stay would be brief, and we would have to return and take dependence again. If our teachers and preceptors go, we too will go; but if our teachers and preceptors do not go, we too will not go. Friend Ānanda, our light-mindedness will become apparent.' Then the Blessed One set out on a journey to Dakkhiṇāgiri with a small company of bhikkhus.

Āhundarikavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Story of Āhundarika is concluded.

40. Nissayamuccanakakathā

39. The Discourse on Release from Dependence

103. Atha kho bhagavā dakkhiṇāgirismiṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā punadeva rājagahaṃ paccāgacchi. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “kiṃ nu kho, ānanda, tathāgato ogaṇena bhikkhusaṅghena dakkhiṇāgiriṃ cārikaṃ pakkanto”ti? Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena pañcavassāni nissāya vatthuṃ, abyattena yāvajīvaṃ.

102. Then the Blessed One, having stayed in Dakkhiṇāgiri for as long as he was pleased, returned once again to Rājagaha. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “For what reason, Ānanda, did the Tathāgata set out on tour to Dakkhiṇāgiri with a small company of bhikkhus?” Then the Venerable Ānanda informed the Blessed One of this matter. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow a bhikkhu who is skilled and competent to live in dependence for five years; one who is unskilled, for life.”

“Pañcahi[V 0.0101], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Na asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti na asekkhena samādhikkhandhena, na asekkhena paññākkhandhena na asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena na asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato [T 1.0163] hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu possessed of five qualities should not live without dependence. He is not possessed of the adept's aggregate of virtue, nor the adept's aggregate of concentration, nor the adept's aggregate of wisdom, nor the adept's aggregate of liberation, nor the adept's aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu possessed of these five qualities should not live without dependence.”

“Pañcahi[M 0.0112], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti asekkhena samādhikkhandhena. Asekkhena paññākkhandhena… asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena… asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

“Monks, a monk endowed with five qualities may live without dependence. He is endowed with the consummate aggregate of virtue, the consummate aggregate of concentration, the consummate aggregate of wisdom, the consummate aggregate of liberation, and the consummate aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation. Monks, a monk endowed with these five qualities may live without dependence.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Assaddho hoti, ahiriko hoti, anottappī hoti, kusīto hoti, muṭṭhassati hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

“Monks, a monk endowed with another five qualities should not live without dependence. He is faithless, shameless, without moral dread, lazy, and of lapsed mindfulness. Monks, a monk endowed with these five qualities should not live without dependence.”

“Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Saddho hoti[P 1.0081], hirimā hoti, ottappī hoti, āraddhavīriyo hoti, upaṭṭhitassati hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

“Monks, a monk endowed with five qualities may live without dependence. He is faithful, conscientious, scrupulous, energetic, and established in mindfulness. Monks, a monk endowed with these five qualities may live without dependence.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti, appassuto hoti, duppañño hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

“Monks, a monk endowed with another five qualities should not live without dependence. He is corrupt in higher virtue, corrupt in conduct, corrupt in view, has little learning, and is unwise. Monks, a monk endowed with these five qualities should not live without dependence.”

“Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā [T 1.0164] anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Na adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, na ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, na atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti, bahussuto hoti, paññavā hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

“Monks, a monk endowed with five qualities may live without dependence. He is not corrupt in higher virtue, not corrupt in conduct, not corrupt in view, is well-learned, and is wise. Monks, a monk endowed with these five qualities may live without dependence.”

“Aparehipi[V 0.0102], bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Āpattiṃ na jānāti, anāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena na svāgatāni honti na suvibhattāni na suppavattīni na suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

“Monks, a monk endowed with another five qualities should not live without dependence. He does not know an offense, does not know what is not an offense, does not know a light offense, does not know a heavy offense; and the two Pātimokkhas have not been well-mastered by him in detail, are not well-analyzed, not well-recited, and not well-determined, both by rule and by detailed analysis. Monks, a monk endowed with these five qualities should not live without dependence.”

“Pañcahi[M 0.0113], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Āpattiṃ jānāti, anāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

“Monks, a monk endowed with five qualities may live without dependence. He knows an offense, he knows what is not an offense, he knows a light offense, he knows a grave offense; and indeed, for him, the two Pātimokkhas are well-mastered in detail, well-analyzed, well-recited, and well-adjudicated, both by rule and by detailed analysis. Monks, a monk endowed with these five qualities may live without dependence.”

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Āpattiṃ na jānāti, anāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, ūnapañcavasso hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

“Monks, a monk endowed with another five qualities should not live without dependence. He does not know an offense, does not know what is not an offense, does not know a light offense, does not know a grave offense, and he is of less than five years’ standing. Monks, a monk endowed with these five qualities should not live without dependence.”

“Pañcahi[T 1.0165], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Āpattiṃ jānāti, anāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, pañcavasso vā hoti atireka pañcavasso vā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

“Monks, a monk endowed with five qualities may live without dependence. He knows an offense, he knows what is not an offense, he knows a light offense, he knows a grave offense, and he is of five years’ standing or of more than five years’ standing. Monks, a monk endowed with these five qualities may live without dependence.”

Nissayamuccanakakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Release from Dependence is concluded.

Pañcakadasavāro niṭṭhito.

The fifteenth recitation is concluded.

104. “Chahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Na asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, na asekkhena samādhikkhandhena, na asekkhena paññākkhandhena, na asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena, na asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato [V 0.0103] hoti, ūnapañcavasso hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

“Monks, a monk endowed with six qualities should not live without dependence. He is not endowed with the consummate aggregate of virtue, nor with the consummate aggregate of concentration, nor with the consummate aggregate of wisdom, nor with the consummate aggregate of liberation, nor with the consummate aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation, and he is of less than five years’ standing. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities should not live without dependence.”

“Chahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena samādhikkhandhena, asekkhena paññākkhandhena, asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena, asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, pañcavasso vā hoti atirekapañcavasso vā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

104. “Monks, a monk endowed with six qualities may live without dependence. He is endowed with the consummate aggregate of virtue, the consummate aggregate of concentration, the consummate aggregate of wisdom, the consummate aggregate of liberation, and the consummate aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation; and he is of five years’ standing or of more than five years’ standing. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities may live without dependence.”

“Aparehipi[M 0.0114], bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Assaddho hoti, ahiriko hoti, anottappī hoti, kusīto [T 1.0166] hoti, muṭṭhassati hoti, ūnapañcavasso hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

“Monks, a monk endowed with another six qualities should not live without dependence. He is faithless, shameless, without moral dread, lazy, of lapsed mindfulness, and of less than five years’ standing. Monks, a monk endowed with these six qualities should not live without dependence.”

“Chahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Saddho hoti, hirimā hoti, ottappī hoti, āraddhavīriyo hoti, upaṭṭhitassati hoti, pañcavasso vā hoti atirekapañcavasso vā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with six factors may live without dependence. He is faithful, has a sense of moral shame, has moral dread, is energetic, is established in mindfulness, and is of five rains or more than five rains. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these six factors may live without dependence.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti, appassuto hoti, duppañño hoti, ūnapañcavasso hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with another six factors should not live without dependence. He is corrupt in higher virtue, corrupt in fundamental conduct, corrupt in view, is of little learning, is unwise, and is of less than five rains. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these six factors should not live without dependence.

“Chahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Na adhisīle sīlavipanno hoti, na ajjhācāre ācāravipanno hoti, na atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno hoti, bahussuto hoti, paññavā hoti, pañcavasso vā hoti atirekapañcavasso vā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with six factors may live without dependence. He is not corrupt in higher virtue, not corrupt in conduct, and not corrupt in view; he is of great learning, is wise, and is of five rains or more than five rains. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these six factors may live without dependence.

“Aparehipi, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Āpattiṃ [V 0.0104] na jānāti, anāpattiṃ na jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ na jānāti, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena na svāgatāni [T 1.0167] honti na suvibhattāni na suppavattīni na suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso, ūnapañcavasso hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā na anissitena vatthabbaṃ.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with another six factors should not live without dependence. He does not know what is an offense, he does not know what is not an offense, he does not know what is a light offense, he does not know what is a grave offense; furthermore, for that bhikkhu, the two Pātimokkhas are not well-mastered in detail, not well-analyzed, not well-recited, not well-adjudicated according to the rule and according to the detailed analysis, and he is of less than five rains. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these six factors should not live without dependence.

“Chahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabbaṃ. Āpattiṃ jānāti, anāpattiṃ jānāti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ jānāti, ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso [M 0.0115] anubyañjanaso, pañcavasso vā hoti atirekapañcavasso vā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahaṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā anissitena vatthabba”nti.

Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with six factors may live without dependence. He knows what is an offense, he knows what is not an offense, he knows what is a light offense, he knows what is a grave offense; furthermore, for that bhikkhu, the two Pātimokkhas are well-mastered in detail, well-analyzed, well-recited, and well-adjudicated according to the rule and according to the detailed analysis; and he is of five rains or more than five rains. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these six factors may live without dependence.

Abhayūvarabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito aṭṭhamo.

The Eighth Recitation Section, the Abhayūvara, is concluded.

Aṭṭhamabhāṇavāro.

The Eighth Recitation Section.

41. Rāhulavatthu

The Account of Rāhula

105. Atha [P 1.0082] kho bhagavā rājagahe yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena kapilavatthu tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena kapilavatthu tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena suddhodanassa sakkassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho rāhulamātā devī rāhulaṃ kumāraṃ etadavoca – “eso te, rāhula, pitā. Gacchassu gacchassa (syā.), dāyajjaṃ yācāhī”ti. Atha kho rāhulo kumāro yena [T 1.0168] bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato purato, aṭṭhāsi – “sukhā te, samaṇa, chāyā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho rāhulo kumāro bhagavantaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhi – “dāyajjaṃ me, samaṇa, dehi; dāyajjaṃ me, samaṇa, dehī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ āmantesi – “tena hi tvaṃ, sāriputta, rāhulaṃ kumāraṃ pabbājehī”ti. “Kathāhaṃ, bhante, rāhulaṃ kumāraṃ pabbājemī”ti? Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tīhi saraṇagamanehi sāmaṇerapabbajjaṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, pabbājetabbo – paṭhamaṃ kesamassuṃ ohārāpetvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādāpetvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ kārāpetvā bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vandāpetvā [V 0.0105] ukkuṭikaṃ nisīdāpetvā añjaliṃ paggaṇhāpetvā evaṃ vadehīti vattabbo – buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi; dutiyampi buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, dutiyampi dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, dutiyampi saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi; tatiyampi buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, tatiyampi [M 0.0116] dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, tatiyampi saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmīti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi tīhi saraṇagamanehi sāmaṇerapabbajja”nti. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto rāhulaṃ kumāraṃ pabbājesi.

41. Then the Blessed One, having dwelt in Rājagaha for as long as he was pleased, set out on a journey toward Kapilavatthu. Traveling stage by stage, he arrived at Kapilavatthu. There the Blessed One dwelt among the Sakyans in Kapilavatthu, at the Nigrodha's Banyan Grove. Then, in the forenoon, the Blessed One, having put on his lower robe, took his bowl and outer robe and went to the residence of Suddhodana the Sakyan. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then the queen, Rāhula’s mother, said this to Prince Rāhula: “That, Rāhula, is your father. Go and ask for your inheritance.” Then Prince Rāhula approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he stood before the Blessed One and said: “Pleasant is your shade, ascetic.” Then the Blessed One rose from his seat and departed. Then Prince Rāhula followed closely behind the Blessed One, saying: “Give me my inheritance, ascetic; give me my inheritance, ascetic.” Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Sāriputta: “Well then, Sāriputta, you should give the going forth to Prince Rāhula.” “How, Venerable Sir, am I to give the going forth to Prince Rāhula?” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this connection, having given a discourse on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: “I allow, bhikkhus, the going forth as a novice by means of the three goings for refuge. And this is how, bhikkhus, one is to be given the going forth: First, having had the hair and beard shaved off, having had him put on the ochre robes, having had him arrange the upper robe over one shoulder, having had him pay homage at the feet of the bhikkhus, having had him sit down in the squatting position, having had him raise his hands with palms together, he should be told to speak thus: ‘I go to the Buddha for refuge. I go to the Dhamma for refuge. I go to the Saṅgha for refuge. For the second time, I go to the Buddha for refuge. For the second time, I go to the Dhamma for refuge. For the second time, I go to the Saṅgha for refuge. For the third time, I go to the Buddha for refuge. For the third time, I go to the Dhamma for refuge. For the third time, I go to the Saṅgha for refuge.’ I allow, bhikkhus, the going forth as a novice by means of these three goings for refuge.” Then the Venerable Sāriputta gave the going forth to Prince Rāhula.

Atha kho suddhodano sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ [T 1.0169] abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho suddhodano sakko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ekāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ varaṃ yācāmī”ti. “Atikkantavarā kho, gotama, tathāgatā”ti. “Yañca, bhante, kappati, yañca anavajja”nti. “Vadehi, gotamā”ti. “Bhagavati me, bhante, pabbajite anappakaṃ dukkhaṃ ahosi, tathā nande, adhimattaṃ rāhule. Puttapemaṃ[P 1.0083], bhante, chaviṃ chindati, chaviṃ chetvā cammaṃ chindati, cammaṃ chetvā maṃsaṃ chindati, maṃsaṃ chetvā nhāruṃ chindati, nhāruṃ chetvā aṭṭhiṃ chindati, aṭṭhiṃ chetvā aṭṭhimiñjaṃ āhacca tiṭṭhati. Sādhu, bhante, ayyā ananuññātaṃ mātāpitūhi puttaṃ na pabbājeyyu”nti. Atha kho bhagavā suddhodanaṃ sakkaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho suddhodano sakko bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, ananuññāto mātāpitūhi putto pabbājetabbo. Yo pabbājeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

Then the Sakyan king Suddhodana approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Sakyan king Suddhodana said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, I ask for one boon from the Blessed One.' 'The Tathāgatas, Gotama, have gone beyond boons.' 'Venerable sir, a boon that is permissible and blameless.' 'Speak, Gotama.' 'Venerable sir, when the Blessed One went forth, immeasurable suffering arose for me; likewise for Nanda; and exceedingly so for Rāhula. The love for a son, venerable sir, cuts through the skin; having cut through the skin, it cuts through the hide; having cut through the hide, it cuts through the flesh; having cut through the flesh, it cuts through the sinews; having cut through the sinews, it cuts through the bone; having cut through the bone, it strikes the bone marrow and remains. It would be good, venerable sir, if the noble ones would not ordain a son without the permission of his parents.' Then the Blessed One instructed, caused to undertake, roused, and gladdened the Sakyan king Suddhodana with a Dhamma talk. Then the Sakyan king Suddhodana, having been instructed, caused to undertake, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and departed. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: 'Monks, a son should not be ordained without the permission of his parents. Whoever should ordain one, commits an offense of wrongdoing.'

Atha kho bhagavā kapilavatthusmiṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena sāvatthi tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena sāvatthi tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena [T 1.0170] kho pana samayena āyasmato sāriputtassa upaṭṭhākakulaṃ āyasmato sāriputtassa santike dārakaṃ pāhesi – “imaṃ dārakaṃ thero pabbājetū”ti. Atha kho āyasmato sāriputtassa etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘na ekena dve sāmaṇerā upaṭṭhāpetabbā’ti. Ayañca me rāhulo sāmaṇero. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, byattena bhikkhunā [V 0.0106] paṭibalena ekena dve sāmaṇere upaṭṭhāpetuṃ, yāvatake [M 0.0117] vā pana ussahati ovadituṃ anusāsituṃ tāvatake upaṭṭhāpetunti.

Then the Blessed One, having dwelt in Kapilavatthu for as long as he was pleased, departed on a journey towards Sāvatthī. Wandering on tour in due course, he arrived at Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One dwelt in Sāvatthī, in the Jeta Grove, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika. Now at that time, the attendant family of the Venerable Sāriputta sent a boy to the Venerable Sāriputta, saying, 'May the Elder give the going forth to this boy.' Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Sāriputta: 'It has been laid down by the Blessed One thus: “Two novices are not to be attended to by one monk.” And I have this novice, Rāhula. How then should I act?' He reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I permit two novices to be attended to by one competent, capable monk; or however many he is able to admonish and instruct, I permit that many to be attended to.'

Rāhulavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story concerning Rāhula is concluded.

42. Sikkhāpadakathā

42. The Exposition on the Training Rules

106. Atha kho sāmaṇerānaṃ etadahosi – “kati nu kho amhākaṃ sikkhāpadāni, kattha ca amhehi sikkhitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sāmaṇerānaṃ dasa sikkhāpadāni, tesu ca sāmaṇerehi sikkhituṃ – pāṇātipātā veramaṇī veramaṇi, veramaṇiṃ (ka.), adinnādānā veramaṇī, abrahmacariyā veramaṇī, musāvādā veramaṇī, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī, vikālabhojanā veramaṇī, naccagītavāditavisūkadassanā veramaṇī, mālāgandhavilepanadhāraṇamaṇḍanavibhūsanaṭṭhānā veramaṇī[P 1.0084], uccāsayanamahāsayanā veramaṇī, jātarūparajatapaṭiggahaṇā veramaṇī. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sāmaṇerānaṃ imāni dasa sikkhāpadāni, imesu ca sāmaṇerehi sikkhitunti.

106. Then this thought occurred to the novices: 'How many, indeed, are our training rules, and in what should we train?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One... 'Monks, I permit ten training rules for novices, and in these the novices are to train: abstaining from destroying life; abstaining from taking what is not given; abstaining from unchaste conduct; abstaining from false speech; abstaining from drinking liquor and intoxicants which are a cause for heedlessness; abstaining from eating at the wrong time; abstaining from dancing, singing, music, and watching unseemly shows; abstaining from wearing garlands, using scents, and beautifying the body with cosmetics; abstaining from high and luxurious beds and seats; and abstaining from accepting gold and silver. Monks, I permit these ten training rules for novices, and in these the novices are to train.'

Sikkhāpadakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition on the Training Rules is concluded.

43. Daṇḍakammavatthu

43. The Case of Disciplinary Action

107. Tena kho pana samayena sāmaṇerā bhikkhūsu agāravā appatissā [T 1.0171] asabhāgavuttikā viharanti. Bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma sāmaṇerā bhikkhūsu agāravā appatissā asabhāgavuttikā viharissantī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa sāmaṇerassa daṇḍakammaṃ kātuṃ. Bhikkhūnaṃ alābhāya parisakkati, bhikkhūnaṃ anatthāya parisakkati, bhikkhūnaṃ avāsāya parisakkati, bhikkhū akkosati paribhāsati, bhikkhū bhikkhūhi bhedeti – anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa sāmaṇerassa daṇḍakammaṃ kātunti.

107. Now at that time, novices were dwelling without respect for, without deference to, and not in communion with the bhikkhus. The bhikkhus criticized, condemned, and spoke disparagingly, saying: “How indeed can novices dwell without respect for, without deference to, and not in communion with the bhikkhus?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Bhikkhus, I allow a disciplinary action to be performed on a novice who is endowed with five factors.
