He strives for the non-gain of the bhikkhus; he strives for the non-benefit of the bhikkhus; he strives for the non-residence of the bhikkhus; he insults and abuses the bhikkhus; he causes division among the bhikkhus. Bhikkhus, I allow a disciplinary action to be performed on a novice who is endowed with these five factors.”

Atha [V 0.0107] kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kiṃ nu kho daṇḍakammaṃ kātabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āvaraṇaṃ kātunti.

Then this thought occurred to the bhikkhus: “What disciplinary action, I wonder, should be performed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow a restriction to be made.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū sāmaṇerānaṃ sabbaṃ saṅghārāmaṃ āvaraṇaṃ karonti. Sāmaṇerā ārāmaṃ pavisituṃ alabhamānā pakkamantipi[M 0.0118], vibbhamantipi, titthiyesupi saṅkamanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, sabbo saṅghārāmo āvaraṇaṃ kātabbo. Yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yattha vā vasati, yattha vā paṭikkamati, tattha āvaraṇaṃ kātunti.

Now at that time, the bhikkhus were making the entire monastery a restricted area for the novices. The novices, being unable to enter the monastery, also departed, also disrobed, and also went over to the adherents of other teachings. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, the entire monastery is not to be made a restricted area. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong-doing. Bhikkhus, I allow a restriction to be made in the place where he dwells or where he retreats.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū sāmaṇerānaṃ mukhadvārikaṃ āhāraṃ āvaraṇaṃ karonti. Manussā yāgupānampi saṅghabhattampi karontā sāmaṇere evaṃ vadenti – “etha, bhante, yāguṃ pivatha; etha, bhante, bhattaṃ bhuñjathā”ti. Sāmaṇerā evaṃ [T 1.0172] vadenti – “nāvuso, labbhā. Bhikkhūhi āvaraṇaṃ kata”nti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhadantā sāmaṇerānaṃ mukhadvārikaṃ āhāraṃ āvaraṇaṃ karissantī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, mukhadvāriko āhāro āvaraṇaṃ kātabbo. Yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Now at that time, the bhikkhus were imposing a restriction on the novices regarding food taken by mouth. People, when preparing rice-gruel or a meal for the Sangha, would say to the novices: “Come, venerable sirs, drink rice-gruel; come, venerable sirs, eat the meal.” The novices would say: “Friends, it is not allowed. A restriction has been imposed by the bhikkhus.” People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed could the venerable sirs impose a restriction on the novices regarding food taken by mouth?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a restriction on food taken by mouth should not be made. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Daṇḍakammavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Account of the Disciplinary Action is concluded.

44. Anāpucchāvaraṇavatthu

44. The Account of Restriction Without Asking

108. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū upajjhāye [P 1.0085] anāpucchā sāmaṇerānaṃ āvaraṇaṃ karonti. Upajjhāyā gavesanti – kathaṃ kahaṃ (ka.) nu kho amhākaṃ sāmaṇerā na dissantīti. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “chabbaggiyehi, āvuso, bhikkhūhi āvaraṇaṃ kata”nti. Upajjhāyā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū amhe anāpucchā amhākaṃ sāmaṇerānaṃ āvaraṇaṃ karissantī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, upajjhāye anāpucchā āvaraṇaṃ kātabbaṃ. Yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

108. Now at that time, the bhikkhus of the group of six, without asking their preceptors, were imposing a restriction on the novices. The preceptors searched, wondering: “Why indeed are our novices not seen?” The bhikkhus said thus: “Friends, a restriction has been imposed by the bhikkhus of the group of six.” The preceptors complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly: “How indeed could the bhikkhus of the group of six, without asking us, impose a restriction on our novices?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a restriction should not be imposed without asking the preceptors. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Anāpucchāvaraṇavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Account of Restriction Without Asking is concluded.

45. Apalāḷanavatthu

45. The Account of Enticing

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū therānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sāmaṇere apalāḷenti. Therā sāmaṃ dantakaṭṭhampi mukhodakampi gaṇhantā kilamanti[M 0.0119]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, aññassa parisā apalāḷetabbā. Yo apalāḷeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā [V 0.0108] ti.

Now at that time, the bhikkhus of the group of six were enticing away the novices of the elder bhikkhus. The elders, fetching tooth-sticks and water for washing the face themselves, became weary. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, another’s following should not be enticed away. Whoever should do so, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Apalāḷanavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Account of Enticing is concluded.

46. Kaṇṭakasāmaṇeravatthu

46. The Account of the Novice Kaṇṭaka

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato upanandassa sakyaputtassa kaṇṭako [T 1.0173] nāma sāmaṇero kaṇṭakiṃ nāma bhikkhuniṃ dūsesi. Bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma sāmaṇero evarūpaṃ anācāraṃ ācarissatī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dasahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ sāmaṇeraṃ nāsetuṃ. Pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, abrahmacārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, majjapāyī hoti, buddhassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, dhammassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, saṅghassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, micchādiṭṭhiko hoti, bhikkhunidūsako hoti – anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi dasahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ sāmaṇeraṃ nāsetunti.

Now at that time, a novice named Kaṇṭaka, belonging to the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan, corrupted a bhikkhunī named Kaṇṭakī. The bhikkhus complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly, saying: “How indeed could a novice commit such improper conduct?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow the expulsion of a novice who is endowed with ten factors. He is one who destroys living beings, he is one who takes what is not given, he is one who is unchaste, he is one who speaks falsehood, he is one who drinks intoxicants, he speaks in dispraise of the Buddha, he speaks in dispraise of the Dhamma, he speaks in dispraise of the Saṅgha, he is one who holds wrong view, and he is one who corrupts bhikkhunīs. Bhikkhus, I allow the expulsion of a novice who is endowed with these ten factors.”

47. Paṇḍakavatthu

47. The Account of the Paṇḍaka

109. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro paṇḍako bhikkhūsu pabbajito hoti. So dahare dahare bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadeti – “etha, maṃ āyasmanto dūsethā”ti. Bhikkhū apasādenti – “nassa, paṇḍaka, vinassa, paṇḍaka, ko tayā attho”ti. So bhikkhūhi apasādito mahante mahante moḷigalle sāmaṇere upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadeti – “etha, maṃ āvuso dūsethā”ti. Sāmaṇerā apasādenti – “nassa, paṇḍaka, vinassa, paṇḍaka, ko tayā attho”ti. So sāmaṇerehi apasādito hatthibhaṇḍe assabhaṇḍe upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadeti – “etha, maṃ, āvuso[P 1.0086], dūsethā”ti. Hatthibhaṇḍā assabhaṇḍā dūsesuṃ. Te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “paṇḍakā [T 1.0174] ime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā. Yepi imesaṃ na paṇḍakā, tepi ime paṇḍake dūsenti. Evaṃ ime sabbeva abrahmacārino”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ hatthibhaṇḍānaṃ [V 0.0109] assabhaṇḍānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Paṇḍako, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabboti.

109. Now at that time, a certain paṇḍaka had gone forth among the bhikkhus. He approached very young bhikkhus and said, “Come, venerables, defile me.” The bhikkhus rejected him, saying, “Get lost, paṇḍaka, perish, paṇḍaka, what use are you?” Rejected by the bhikkhus, he then approached large, stout novices and said, “Come, friends, defile me.” The novices rejected him, saying, “Get lost, paṇḍaka, perish, paṇḍaka, what use are you?” Rejected by the novices, he then approached elephant keepers and horse keepers and said, “Come, friends, defile me.” The elephant keepers and horse keepers defiled him. They complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly, saying, “These Sakyan ascetics are paṇḍakas. Even those among them who are not paṇḍakas defile these paṇḍakas. Thus, they are all unchaste.” The bhikkhus heard the elephant keepers and horse keepers complaining, criticizing, and speaking disparagingly. Then those bhikkhus reported the matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a paṇḍaka who has not been ordained should not be ordained; one who has been ordained should be expelled.”

48. Theyyasaṃvāsakavatthu

48. The Account of Living in Communion by Theft

110. Tena [M 0.0120] kho pana samayena aññataro purāṇakulaputto khīṇakolañño sukhumālo hoti. Atha kho tassa purāṇakulaputtassa khīṇakolaññassa etadahosi – “ahaṃ kho sukhumālo, na paṭibalo anadhigataṃ vā bhogaṃ adhigantuṃ, adhigataṃ vā bhogaṃ phātiṃ kātuṃ. Kena nu kho ahaṃ upāyena sukhañca jīveyyaṃ, na ca kilameyya”nti? Atha kho tassa purāṇakulaputtassa khīṇakolaññassa etadahosi – “ime kho samaṇā sakyaputtiyā sukhasīlā sukhasamācārā, subhojanāni bhuñjitvā nivātesu sayanesu sayanti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ sāmaṃ pattacīvaraṃ paṭiyādetvā kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ saṃvaseyya”nti. Atha kho so purāṇakulaputto khīṇakolañño sāmaṃ pattacīvaraṃ paṭiyādetvā kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhū abhivādeti. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “kativassosi tvaṃ, āvuso”ti? Kiṃ etaṃ, āvuso, kativasso nāmāti? Ko pana te, āvuso, upajjhāyoti? Kiṃ etaṃ[T 1.0175], āvuso, upajjhāyo nāmāti? Bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ upāliṃ etadavocuṃ – “iṅghāvuso upāli, imaṃ pabbajitaṃ anuyuñjāhī”ti. Atha kho so purāṇakulaputto khīṇakolañño āyasmatā upālinā anuyuñjiyamāno etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Āyasmā upāli bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Theyyasaṃvāsako, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabboti. Titthiyapakkantako, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabboti.

110. Now at that time a certain clansman of an old family, whose family had declined, was delicate. Then it occurred to that clansman of an old family, whose family had declined: “I am delicate, not capable of acquiring unacquired wealth or increasing acquired wealth. By what means could I live happily and without exertion?” Then it occurred to that clansman of an old family, whose family had declined: “These ascetics, the Sakyan sons, are easy in their habits and conduct; having eaten excellent meals, they sleep in sheltered resting places. What if I were to prepare a bowl and robes myself, shave off my hair and beard, put on ochre robes, go to the monastery, and live together with the monks?” Then that clansman of an old family, whose family had declined, prepared a bowl and robes himself, shaved off his hair and beard, put on ochre robes, went to the monastery, and paid homage to the monks. The monks said to him: “How many years [ordained] are you, friend?” “What is this, friends, called ‘how many years [ordained]’?” “Then who is your preceptor, friend?” “What is this, friends, called ‘preceptor’?” The monks said to Venerable Upāli: “Come, friend Upāli, investigate this one who has gone forth.” Then that clansman of an old family, whose family had declined, being investigated by Venerable Upāli, explained this matter. Venerable Upāli informed the monks of this matter. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, one in communion by theft who has not been ordained should not be ordained; one who has been ordained should be expelled. Monks, one who has gone over to another sect who has not been ordained should not be ordained; one who has been ordained should be expelled.”

49. Tiracchānagatavatthu

49. The Case of the Animal

111. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro nāgo nāgayoniyā aṭṭīyati [P 1.0087] harāyati jigucchati. Atha kho tassa nāgassa etadahosi – “kena nu kho ahaṃ upāyena nāgayoniyā ca parimucceyyaṃ khippañca manussattaṃ paṭilabheyya”nti. Atha kho tassa nāgassa etadahosi – “ime kho samaṇā sakyaputtiyā dhammacārino samacārino brahmacārino saccavādino [M 0.0121] sīlavanto [V 0.0110] kalyāṇadhammā. Sace kho ahaṃ samaṇesu sakyaputtiyesu pabbajeyyaṃ, evāhaṃ nāgayoniyā ca parimucceyyaṃ, khippañca manussattaṃ paṭilabheyya”nti. Atha kho so nāgo māṇavakavaṇṇena bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā pabbajjaṃ yāci. Taṃ bhikkhū pabbājesuṃ, upasampādesuṃ. Tena kho pana samayena so nāgo aññatarena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ paccantime vihāre paṭivasati. Atha kho so bhikkhu rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya ajjhokāse caṅkamati. Atha kho so [T 1.0176] nāgo tassa bhikkhuno nikkhante vissaṭṭho niddaṃ okkami. Sabbo vihāro ahinā puṇṇo, vātapānehi bhogā nikkhantā honti. Atha kho so bhikkhu vihāraṃ pavisissāmīti kavāṭaṃ paṇāmento addasa sabbaṃ vihāraṃ ahinā puṇṇaṃ, vātapānehi bhoge nikkhante, disvāna bhīto vissaramakāsi. Bhikkhū upadhāvitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavocuṃ – “kissa tvaṃ, āvuso, vissaramakāsī”ti? “Ayaṃ, āvuso, sabbo vihāro ahinā puṇṇo, vātapānehi bhogā nikkhantā”ti. Atha kho so nāgo tena saddena paṭibujjhitvā sake āsane nisīdi. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “kosi tvaṃ, āvuso”ti? “Ahaṃ, bhante, nāgo”ti. “Kissa pana tvaṃ, āvuso, evarūpaṃ akāsī”ti? Atha kho so nāgo bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā taṃ nāgaṃ etadavoca – “tumhe khottha nāgā aviruḷhidhammā imasmiṃ dhammavinaye. Gaccha tvaṃ, nāga, tattheva cātuddase pannarase aṭṭhamiyā ca pakkhassa uposathaṃ upavasa, evaṃ tvaṃ nāgayoniyā ca parimuccissasi, khippañca manussattaṃ paṭilabhissasī”ti. Atha kho so nāgo aviruḷhidhammo kirāhaṃ imasmiṃ dhammavinayeti dukkhī dummano assūni pavattayamāno vissaraṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “dveme, bhikkhave, paccayā nāgassa sabhāvapātukammāya. Yadā ca sajātiyā methunaṃ dhammaṃ [T 1.0177] paṭisevati, yadā ca vissaṭṭho niddaṃ okkamati – ime kho, bhikkhave, dve paccayā nāgassa sabhāvapātukammāya[P 1.0088]. Tiracchānagato, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabbo”ti.

111. Now at that time, a certain nāga was weary, ashamed, and disgusted with his nāga birth. Then it occurred to that nāga: “By what means could I be freed from this nāga birth and quickly attain the human state?” Then it occurred to that nāga: “These recluses, the Sons of the Sakyans, are practitioners of the Dhamma, practitioners of good conduct, practitioners of the holy life, speakers of truth, virtuous, and of good character. If I were to go forth among the recluses, the Sons of the Sakyans, I would be freed from this nāga birth and quickly attain the human state.” Then that nāga, in the guise of a young man, approached the monks and requested the going forth. The monks gave him the going forth and the higher ordination. Now at that time, that nāga was dwelling in a border monastery together with a certain monk. Then that monk, having risen at dawn, was walking back and forth in the open. Then, when that monk had gone out, the nāga, being unguarded, fell asleep. The entire monastery was filled with the serpent, its coils protruding from the windows. Then that monk, thinking, “I will enter the monastery,” while pushing the door, saw the entire monastery filled with the serpent, its coils protruding from the windows. Seeing this, terrified, he made a cry of alarm. The monks came running and said to that monk, “Why did you make a cry of alarm, friend?” “Friends, this entire monastery is filled with a serpent, its coils protruding from the windows!” Then that nāga, awakened by the sound, sat down on his own seat. The monks asked, “Who are you, friend?” “I am a nāga, venerable sirs.” “But why, friend, did you do such a thing?” Then that nāga informed the monks of the matter. The monks informed the Blessed One of the matter. Then the Blessed One, having assembled the Sangha of monks on this occasion, addressed that nāga: “You nāgas are of a nature incapable of growth in this Dhamma and Discipline. Go, nāga, and right there observe the Uposatha on the fourteenth, fifteenth, and eighth day of the fortnight. Thus you will be freed from this nāga birth and quickly attain the human state.” Then that nāga, thinking, “It seems I am of a nature incapable of growth in this Dhamma and Discipline,” sorrowful and dejected, shedding tears, made a cry of alarm and departed. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks, there are two conditions for a nāga’s true nature to be revealed: when he engages in sexual intercourse with one of his own kind, and when, being unguarded, he falls asleep. These, monks, are the two conditions for a nāga’s true nature to be revealed. Monks, an animal who has not been ordained should not be ordained; one who has been ordained should be expelled.”

50. Mātughātakavatthu

50. The Case of the Matricide

112. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro māṇavako mātaraṃ jīvitā voropesi. So tena pāpakena kammena aṭṭīyati harāyati jigucchati[M 0.0122]. Atha kho tassa māṇavakassa etadahosi – “kena nu kho ahaṃ upāyena imassa pāpakassa kammassa nikkhantiṃ kareyya”nti? Atha kho tassa māṇavakassa etadahosi – “ime kho samaṇā sakyaputtiyā dhammacārino [V 0.0111] samacārino brahmacārino saccavādino sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā. Sace kho ahaṃ samaṇesu sakyaputtiyesu pabbajeyyaṃ, evāhaṃ imassa pāpakassa kammassa nikkhantiṃ kareyya”nti. Atha kho so māṇavako bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā pabbajjaṃ yāci. Bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ upāliṃ etadavocuṃ – “pubbepi kho, āvuso upāli, nāgo māṇavakavaṇṇena bhikkhūsu pabbajito. Iṅghāvuso upāli, imaṃ māṇavakaṃ anuyuñjāhī”ti. Atha kho so māṇavako āyasmatā upālinā anuyuñjīyamāno etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Āyasmā upāli bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… mātughātako, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabboti.

112. Now at that time, a certain young man deprived his mother of life. He was troubled, ashamed, and disgusted by that evil deed. Then this reflection occurred to him: “By what means, indeed, might I find release from this evil deed?” Then this reflection occurred to him: “Indeed, these recluses, the sons of the Sakyan, are practitioners of the Dhamma, practitioners of good conduct, practitioners of the noble life, speakers of truth, virtuous, and of excellent character. If I were to go forth among the recluses who are sons of the Sakyan, in this way I might find release from this evil deed.” Then that young man approached the monks and requested the going forth. The monks said to the Venerable Upāli: “Friend Upāli, indeed, in the past a nāga in the guise of a young man went forth among the monks. Come, friend Upāli, question this young man.” Then, being questioned by the Venerable Upāli, that young man disclosed this matter. The Venerable Upāli reported this matter to the monks. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a matricide who has not received the higher ordination should not be given the higher ordination; if he has received the higher ordination, he should be expelled.”

51. Pitughātakavatthu

51. The Story of the Patricide

113. Tena [T 1.0178] kho pana samayena aññataro māṇavako pitaraṃ jīvitā voropesi. So tena pāpakena kammena aṭṭīyati harāyati jigucchati. Atha kho tassa māṇavakassa etadahosi “kena nu kho ahaṃ upāyena imassa pāpakassa kammassa nikkhantiṃ kareyya”nti. Atha kho tassa māṇavakassa etadahosi “ime kho samaṇā sakyaputtiyā dhammacārino samacārino brahmacārino saccavādino sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā, sace kho ahaṃ samaṇesu sakyaputtiyesu pabbajeyyaṃ, evāhaṃ imassa pāpakassa kammassa nikkhantiṃ kareyya”nti. Atha kho so māṇavako bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā pabbajjaṃ yāci. Bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ upāliṃ etadavocuṃ – “pubbepi kho, āvuso upāli, nāgo māṇavakavaṇṇena bhikkhūsu pabbajito, iṅghāvuso, upāli, imaṃ māṇavakaṃ anuyuñjāhī”ti. Atha kho so māṇavako āyasmatā upālinā anuyuñjīyamāno etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Āyasmā upāli bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Pitughātako, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabboti.

113. At that time, a certain young man deprived his father of life. He was troubled, ashamed, and disgusted by that evil deed. Then this reflection occurred to the young man: ‘By what means could I find release from this evil deed?’ Then this reflection occurred to the young man: ‘These recluses, the sons of the Sakyan, are practitioners of the Dhamma, practitioners of good conduct, practitioners of the noble life, speakers of truth, virtuous, and of excellent character. If I were to go forth among the recluses, the sons of the Sakyan, in this way I could find release from this evil deed.’ Then that young man, having approached the monks, requested the going forth. The monks said this to the Venerable Upāli: ‘Friend Upāli, previously a nāga also went forth among the monks in the guise of a young man. Come now, friend Upāli, question this young man.’ Then, being questioned by the Venerable Upāli, that young man disclosed this matter. The Venerable Upāli reported this matter to the monks. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Monks, a patricide who has not received the higher ordination should not be given the higher ordination. If he has received the higher ordination, he should be expelled.’

52. Arahantaghātakavatthu

52. The Story of the Slayer of an Arahant

114. Tena [M 0.0123] kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū sāketā sāvatthiṃ addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Antarāmagge corā nikkhamitvā ekacce bhikkhū acchindiṃsu, ekacce bhikkhū haniṃsu. Sāvatthiyā rājabhaṭā nikkhamitvā ekacce core aggahesuṃ, ekacce [T 1.0179] corā palāyiṃsu. Ye te palāyiṃsu te bhikkhūsu pabbajiṃsu, ye te gahitā te vadhāya oniyyanti[V 0.0112]. Addasaṃsu kho te palāyitvā pabbajitā te core vadhāya oniyyamāne, disvāna evamāhaṃsu – “sādhu kho mayaṃ palāyimhā, sacā ca sace ca, sacajja (aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pāṭhantarā) mayaṃ gayheyyāma gaṇheyyāma (ka.), mayampi evameva haññeyyāmā”ti[P 1.0089]. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “kiṃ pana tumhe, āvuso, akatthā”ti? Atha kho te pabbajitā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Arahanto ete, bhikkhave, bhikkhū. Arahantaghātako, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabboti.

114. At that time, many monks were traveling on the long road from Sāketa to Sāvatthī. On the way, thieves emerged and robbed some monks, and killed others. Royal officers from Sāvatthī went out and captured some of the thieves, while others fled. Those who fled went forth among the monks, while those who were captured were being led away for execution. Those who had fled and gone forth saw those thieves being led away for execution, and having seen them, said: ‘It is indeed good that we fled, for if we had been captured, we too would be killed in just this way.’ The monks said, ‘Friends, what deed have you done?’ Then those who had gone forth reported this matter to the monks. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Monks, those monks were arahants. Monks, one who has killed an arahant, who has not received the higher ordination, should not be given the higher ordination; if he has received the higher ordination, he should be expelled.’

53. Bhikkhunīdūsakavatthu

53. The Story of One Who Violated a Bhikkhunī

115. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhuniyo sāketā sāvatthiṃ addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Antarāmagge corā nikkhamitvā ekaccā bhikkhuniyo acchindiṃsu, ekaccā bhikkhuniyo dūsesuṃ. Sāvatthiyā rājabhaṭā nikkhamitvā ekacce core aggahesuṃ, ekacce corā palāyiṃsu. Ye te palāyiṃsu, te bhikkhūsu pabbajiṃsu. Ye te gahitā, te vadhāya oniyyanti. Addasaṃsu kho te palāyitvā pabbajitā te core vadhāya oniyyamāne, disvāna evamāhaṃsu “sādhu kho mayaṃ palāyimhā, sacā ca mayaṃ gayheyyāma, mayampi evameva haññeyyāmā”ti. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu “kiṃ pana tumhe, āvuso, akatthā”ti. Atha kho te pabbajitā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhunidūsako, bhikkhave[T 1.0180], anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabboti. Saṅghabhedako, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabboti. Lohituppādako, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabboti.

115. At that time, many bhikkhunīs were traveling on a long journey from Sāketa to Sāvatthī. On the way, thieves emerged and robbed some bhikkhunīs, and violated others. Royal officers from Sāvatthī went out and captured some of the thieves, while others fled. Those who fled then went forth among the monks. Those who were captured were being led away for execution. Those who had fled and gone forth saw those thieves being led away for execution, and having seen them, said: ‘It is indeed good that we fled, for if we had been captured, we too would have been killed in just this way.’ The monks said, ‘Friends, what deed did you do?’ Then those who had gone forth reported this matter to the monks. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Monks, one who has violated a bhikkhunī, who has not received the higher ordination, should not be given the higher ordination; if he has received the higher ordination, he should be expelled. Monks, one who has created a schism in the Sangha, who has not received the higher ordination, should not be given the higher ordination; if he has received the higher ordination, he should be expelled. Monks, one who has, with malicious intent, drawn the blood of a Tathāgata, who has not received the higher ordination, should not be given the higher ordination; if he has received the higher ordination, he should be expelled.’

54. Ubhatobyañjanakavatthu

54. The Case of the Ubhatobyañjanaka

116. Tena [M 0.0124] kho pana samayena aññataro ubhatobyañjanako bhikkhūsu pabbajito hoti. So karotipi kārāpetipi. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Ubhatobyañjanako, bhikkhave, anupasampanno na upasampādetabbo, upasampanno nāsetabboti.

116. At that time, a certain ubhatobyañjanaka had gone forth among the monks. He both performed sexual acts and had them performed on him. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, an ubhatobyañjanaka who has not received the higher ordination should not be given the higher ordination. If he has received the higher ordination, he should be expelled.”

55. Anupajjhāyakādivatthūni

55. Cases of One Without a Preceptor, and So Forth

117. Tena [V 0.0113] kho pana samayena bhikkhū anupajjhāyakaṃ upasampādenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, anupajjhāyako upasampādetabbo. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

117. At that time, bhikkhus were conferring the higher ordination upon one without a preceptor. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, one without a preceptor is not to be given the higher ordination. Whosoever should confer it incurs an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū saṅghena upajjhāyena upasampādenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, saṅghena upajjhāyena upasampādetabbo. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, bhikkhus were conferring the higher ordination with the Saṅgha as preceptor. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, one is not to be given the higher ordination with the Saṅgha as preceptor. Whosoever should confer it incurs an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū gaṇena upajjhāyena upasampādenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, gaṇena upajjhāyena upasampādetabbo. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, bhikkhus were conferring the higher ordination with a group as preceptor. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, one is not to be given the higher ordination with a group as preceptor. Whosoever should confer it incurs an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū paṇḍakupajjhāyena upasampādenti…pe… theyyasaṃvāsakupajjhāyena upasampādenti…pe… titthiyapakkantakupajjhāyena upasampādenti …pe… tiracchānagatupajjhāyena [T 1.0181][P 1.0090] upasampādenti…pe… mātughātakupajjhāyena upasampādenti…pe… pitughātakupajjhāyena upasampādenti…pe… arahantaghātakupajjhāyena upasampādenti…pe… bhikkhunidūsakupajjhāyena upasampādenti…pe… saṅghabhedakupajjhāyena upasampādenti…pe… lohituppādakupajjhāyena upasampādenti…pe… ubhatobyañjanakupajjhāyena upasampādenti bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, paṇḍakupajjhāyena upasampādetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, theyyasaṃvāsakupajjhāyena upasampādetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, titthiyapakkantakupajjhāyena upasampādetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, tiracchānagatupajjhāyena upasampādetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, mātughātakupajjhāyena upasampādetabbo …pe… na, bhikkhave, pitughātakupajjhāyena upasampādetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, arahantaghātakupajjhāyena upasampādetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, bhikkhunidūsakupajjhāyena upasampādetabbo [M 0.0125]…pe… na, bhikkhave, saṅghabhedakupajjhāyena upasampādetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, lohituppādakupajjhāyena upasampādetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, ubhatobyañjanakupajjhāyena upasampādetabbo. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, bhikkhus were conferring the higher ordination with a eunuch as the preceptor… with a thief in the guise of a bhikkhu as the preceptor… with one who had gone over to another sect as the preceptor… with an animal as the preceptor… with a matricide as the preceptor… with a patricide as the preceptor… with a murderer of an Arahant as the preceptor… with a defiler of a bhikkhunī as the preceptor… with a schismatic as the preceptor… with one who has shed a Buddha's blood as the preceptor… with a hermaphrodite as the preceptor. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, one is not to be given the higher ordination with a eunuch as the preceptor… with a thief in the guise of a bhikkhu as the preceptor… with one who had gone over to another sect as the preceptor… with an animal as the preceptor… with a matricide as the preceptor… with a patricide as the preceptor… with a murderer of an Arahant as the preceptor… with a defiler of a bhikkhunī as the preceptor… with a schismatic as the preceptor… with one who has shed a Buddha's blood as the preceptor… with a hermaphrodite as the preceptor. Whosoever should confer it incurs an offense of wrong-doing.'

56. Apattakādivatthu

56. The Story of One Without a Bowl, and So Forth

118. Tena [V 0.0114] kho pana samayena bhikkhū apattakaṃ upasampādenti. Hatthesu piṇḍāya caranti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi titthiyāti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, apattako upasampādetabbo. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

118. At that time, bhikkhus were conferring the higher ordination upon one without a bowl. They went for alms using their hands. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, 'Just like the sectarians!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, one without a bowl is not to be given the higher ordination. Whosoever should confer it incurs an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū acīvarakaṃ upasampādenti[T 1.0182]. Naggā piṇḍāya caranti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi titthiyāti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, acīvarako upasampādetabbo. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, bhikkhus were conferring the higher ordination upon one without robes. They went for alms naked. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, 'Just like the sectarians!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, one without robes is not to be given the higher ordination. Whosoever should confer it incurs an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū apattacīvarakaṃ upasampādenti. Naggā hatthesu piṇḍāya caranti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi titthiyāti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, apattacīvarako upasampādetabbo. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, bhikkhus were conferring the higher ordination upon one without a bowl and robes. Naked, they went for alms using their hands. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, 'Just like the sectarians!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, one without a bowl and robes is not to be given the higher ordination. Whosoever should confer it incurs an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū yācitakena pattena upasampādenti. Upasampanne pattaṃ paṭiharanti. Hatthesu piṇḍāya caranti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi titthiyāti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, yācitakena pattena upasampādetabbo. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, bhikkhus were conferring the higher ordination with a borrowed bowl. After the higher ordination, the bowl was taken back. The newly ordained bhikkhu then went for alms using his hands. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, 'Just like the sectarians!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, one is not to be given the higher ordination with a borrowed bowl. Whosoever should confer it incurs an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū yācitakena cīvarena upasampādenti. Upasampanne cīvaraṃ paṭiharanti. Naggā piṇḍāya caranti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi titthiyāti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, yācitakena cīvarena upasampādetabbo. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, bhikkhus were conferring the higher ordination with borrowed robes. After the higher ordination, the robes were taken back. The newly ordained bhikkhu then went for alms naked. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, 'Just like the sectarians!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, one is not to be given the higher ordination with borrowed robes. Whosoever should confer it incurs an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena [M 0.0126] kho pana samayena bhikkhū yācitakena pattacīvarena upasampādenti. Upasampanne pattacīvaraṃ [P 1.0091] paṭiharanti. Naggā hatthesu [T 1.0183] piṇḍāya caranti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti [V 0.0115] – seyyathāpi titthiyāti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, yācitakena pattacīvarena upasampādetabbo. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, bhikkhus were conferring the higher ordination with a borrowed bowl and robes. After the higher ordination, the bowl and robes were taken back. Naked, the newly ordained bhikkhu then went for alms using his hands. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, 'Just like the sectarians!' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, one is not to be given the higher ordination with a borrowed bowl and robes. Whosoever should confer it incurs an offense of wrong-doing.'

Naupasampādetabbekavīsativāro niṭṭhito.

The section on the twenty-one who are not to be given the higher ordination is concluded.

57. Napabbājetabbadvattiṃsavāro

57. The Section on the Thirty-Two Who Are Not to Be Given the Going Forth

119. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū hatthacchinnaṃ pabbājenti…pe… pādacchinnaṃ pabbājenti…pe… hatthapādacchinnaṃ pabbājenti…pe… kaṇṇacchinnaṃ pabbājenti…pe… nāsacchinnaṃ pabbājenti…pe… kaṇṇanāsacchinnaṃ pabbājenti…pe… aṅgulicchinnaṃ pabbājenti…pe… aḷacchinnaṃ pabbājenti…pe… kaṇḍaracchinnaṃ pabbājenti…pe… phaṇahatthakaṃ pabbājenti…pe… khujjaṃ pabbājenti…pe… vāmanaṃ pabbājenti…pe… galagaṇḍiṃ pabbājenti…pe… lakkhaṇāhataṃ pabbājenti…pe… kasāhataṃ pabbājenti…pe… likhitakaṃ pabbājenti…pe… sīpadiṃ pabbājenti…pe… pāparogiṃ pabbājenti…pe… parisadūsakaṃ pabbājenti…pe… kāṇaṃ pabbājenti…pe… kuṇiṃ pabbājenti…pe… khañjaṃ pabbājenti…pe… pakkhahataṃ pabbājenti…pe… chinniriyāpathaṃ pabbājenti…pe… jarādubbalaṃ pabbājenti…pe… andhaṃ pabbājenti…pe… mūgaṃ pabbājenti…pe… badhiraṃ pabbājenti…pe… andhamūgaṃ pabbājenti…pe… andhabadhiraṃ pabbājenti…pe… mūgabadhiraṃ pabbājenti…pe… andhamūgabadhiraṃ pabbājenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… na, bhikkhave, hatthacchinno [T 1.0184] pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, pādacchinno pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, hatthapādacchinno pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, kaṇṇacchinno pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, nāsacchinno pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, kaṇṇanāsacchinno pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, aṅgulicchinno pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, aḷacchinno pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, kaṇḍaracchinno pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, phaṇahatthako pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, khujjo pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, vāmano pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, galagaṇḍī pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, lakkhaṇāhato [M 0.0127] pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, kasāhato pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, likhitako pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, sīpadī pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, pāparogī pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, parisadūsako pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, kāṇo pabbājetabbo…pe… na[V 0.0116], bhikkhave, kuṇī pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, khañjo pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, pakkhahato pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, chinniriyāpatho pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, jarādubbalo pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, andho pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, mūgo pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, badhiro pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, andhamūgo pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, andhabadhiro pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, mūgabadhiro pabbājetabbo…pe… na, bhikkhave, andhamūgabadhiro pabbājetabbo. Yo pabbājeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

119. At that time, monks were ordaining those with hands cut off… those with feet cut off… those with hands and feet cut off… those with ears cut off… those with noses cut off… those with ears and noses cut off… those with fingers cut off… those with a thumb or big toe cut off… those with a main tendon cut off… those with webbed hands… the hunchbacked… the dwarfed… those with goiters… the branded… the whipped… the proscribed… those with elephantiasis… those with serious diseases… those who corrupt the assembly… the one-eyed… those with a crooked hand or foot… the lame… the paralyzed… the crippled… the aged and feeble… the blind… the mute… the deaf… the blind and mute… the blind and deaf… the mute and deaf… the blind, mute, and deaf. They reported this matter to the Blessed One… Monks, one whose hand is cut off should not be ordained… one whose foot is cut off should not be ordained… one whose hands and feet are cut off should not be ordained… one whose ear is cut off should not be ordained… one whose nose is cut off should not be ordained… one whose ears and nose are cut off should not be ordained… one whose fingers are cut off should not be ordained… one whose thumb or big toe is cut off should not be ordained… one whose main tendon is cut off should not be ordained… one with webbed hands should not be ordained… the hunchbacked should not be ordained… the dwarfed should not be ordained… one with a goiter should not be ordained… one who is branded should not be ordained… one who is whipped should not be ordained… one who is proscribed should not be ordained… one with elephantiasis should not be ordained… one with a serious disease should not be ordained… one who corrupts the assembly should not be ordained… the one-eyed should not be ordained… one with a crooked hand or foot should not be ordained… the lame should not be ordained… the paralyzed should not be ordained… the crippled should not be ordained… the aged and feeble should not be ordained… the blind should not be ordained… the mute should not be ordained… the deaf should not be ordained… the blind and mute should not be ordained… the blind and deaf should not be ordained… the mute and deaf should not be ordained… the blind, mute, and deaf should not be ordained. Whoever should ordain such a person, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Napabbājetabbadvattiṃsavāro niṭṭhito.

The Section on the Thirty-two Not to Be Ordained is completed.

Dāyajjabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito navamo.

The ninth Recitation Section on Inheritance is completed.

58. Alajjīnissayavatthūni

58. The Stories Concerning Dependence on the Shameless

120. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū alajjīnaṃ nissayaṃ [T 1.0185] denti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, alajjīnaṃ nissayo dātabbo. Yo dadeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

120. At that time, the group-of-six monks gave dependence to the shameless. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, dependence is not to be given to the shameless. Whoever should give it, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū alajjīnaṃ nissāya vasanti. Tepi nacirasseva alajjino honti pāpakābhikkhū. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, alajjīnaṃ nissāya vatthabbaṃ. Yo vaseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, monks were living in dependence on the shameless. Before long, they too became evil, shameless persons. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, one should not live in dependence on the shameless. Whoever should so live, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘na alajjīnaṃ nissayo dātabbo, na alajjīnaṃ nissāya vatthabba’nti. Kathaṃ nu kho mayaṃ jāneyyāma lajjiṃ vā alajjiṃ vā”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, catūhapañcāhaṃ āgametuṃ yāva bhikkhusabhāgataṃ jānāmīti.

Then this reflection occurred to the monks: “It has been laid down by the Blessed One, ‘Dependence is not to be given to the shameless; one should not live in dependence on the shameless.’ How then are we to know who is scrupulous or who is shameless?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow you to wait for four or five days, until one knows the nature of the monk.”

59. Gamikādinissayavatthūni

59. The Stories Concerning Dependence, Beginning with a Traveler

121. Tena [P 1.0092][M 0.0128] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu kosalesu janapade addhānamaggappaṭipanno hoti. Atha kho tassa bhikkhuno etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘na anissitena [V 0.0117] vatthabba’nti. Ahañcamhi nissayakaraṇīyo addhānamaggappaṭipanno, kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, addhānamaggappaṭipannena bhikkhunā nissayaṃ alabhamānena anissitena vatthunti.

121. At that time, a certain monk was traveling on a long road in the country of Kosala. Then this reflection occurred to that monk: “It has been laid down by the Blessed One, ‘One should not live without dependence.’ I am one who has the duty of taking dependence, and I am traveling on a long road. How then should I proceed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow a monk traveling on a long road, who is unable to obtain dependence, to live without dependence.”

Tena kho pana samayena dve bhikkhū kosalesu janapade addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Te aññataraṃ āvāsaṃ upagacchiṃsu. Tattha eko bhikkhu gilāno hoti. Atha kho tassa gilānassa bhikkhuno etadahosi [T 1.0186] – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘na anissitena vatthabba’nti. Ahañcamhi nissayakaraṇīyo gilāno, kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānena bhikkhunā nissayaṃ alabhamānena anissitena vatthunti.

At that time, two monks were traveling along a long road in the Kosala country. They approached a certain monastery. There, one monk was ill. Then this thought occurred to that sick monk: “The Blessed One has laid down, ‘One should not dwell without dependence.’ I am one who needs to take dependence, and I am ill. How then should I proceed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a sick monk who is unable to obtain dependence to dwell without dependence.”

Atha kho tassa gilānupaṭṭhākassa bhikkhuno etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘na anissitena vatthabba’nti. Ahañcamhi nissayakaraṇīyo, ayañca bhikkhu gilāno, kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānupaṭṭhākena bhikkhunā nissayaṃ alabhamānena yāciyamānena anissitena vatthunti.

Then this thought occurred to the bhikkhu attending to the sick one: ‘The Blessed One has laid down, “One should not dwell without dependence.” I am required to take dependence, and this bhikkhu is ill. How then should I proceed?’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Bhikkhus, I allow a bhikkhu attending to a sick one, if he is unable to obtain dependence and is requested to stay, to dwell without dependence.’

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu araññe viharati. Tassa ca tasmiṃ senāsane phāsu hoti. Atha kho tassa bhikkhuno etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘na anissitena vatthabba’nti. Ahañcamhi nissayakaraṇīyo araññe viharāmi, mayhañca imasmiṃ senāsane phāsu hoti, kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āraññikena bhikkhunā phāsuvihāraṃ sallakkhentena nissayaṃ alabhamānena anissitena vatthuṃ – yadā patirūpo nissayadāyako āgacchissati, tadā tassa nissāya vasissāmīti.

At that time, a certain bhikkhu was dwelling in the forest. And he was comfortable in that lodging. Then this thought occurred to that bhikkhu: ‘The Blessed One has laid down, “One should not dwell without dependence.” I am required to take dependence, I dwell in the forest, and I am comfortable in this lodging. How then should I proceed?’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Bhikkhus, I allow a forest-dwelling bhikkhu, having noted his comfortable dwelling and being unable to obtain dependence, to dwell without dependence with the thought, “When a suitable preceptor who can give dependence comes, then I will dwell in dependence on him.”’

60. Gottena anussāvanānujānanā

60. Permission for the Formal Announcement by Clan Name

122. Tena [M 0.0129] kho pana samayena āyasmato mahākassapassa upasampadāpekkho hoti. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmato ānandassa santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – āgacchatu ānando imaṃ anussāvessatūti [T 1.0187] anussāvessatīti (syā.). Āyasmā ānando evamāha – “nāhaṃ ussahāmi therassa nāmaṃ [V 0.0118] gahetuṃ, garu me thero”ti[P 1.0093]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gottenapi anussāvetunti.

122. At that time, the Venerable Mahākassapa had a candidate for higher ordination. Then the Venerable Mahākassapa sent a messenger to the Venerable Ānanda, saying, ‘Let Ānanda come and recite the formal announcement for this one.’ The Venerable Ānanda replied, ‘I do not dare to take the elder’s name, for the elder is revered by me.’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Bhikkhus, I allow the formal announcement to be made even by clan name.’

61. Dveupasampadāpekkhādivatthu

61. The Story of the Two Candidates for Higher Ordination and Others

123. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato mahākassapassa dve upasampadāpekkhā honti. Te vivadanti – ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ upasampajjissāmi, ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ upasampajjissāmīti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dve ekānussāvane kātunti.

123. At that time, the Venerable Mahākassapa had two candidates for higher ordination. They argued, ‘I will receive the higher ordination first!’ ‘I will receive the higher ordination first!’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Bhikkhus, I allow two to be ordained with a single formal announcement.’

Tena kho pana samayena sambahulānaṃ therānaṃ upasampadāpekkhā honti. Te vivadanti – ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ upasampajjissāmi, ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ upasampajjissāmīti. Therā evamāhaṃsu – “handa, mayaṃ, āvuso, sabbeva ekānussāvane karomā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dve tayo ekānussāvane kātuṃ, tañca kho ekena upajjhāyena, na tveva nānupajjhāyenāti.

At that time, many elders had candidates for higher ordination. They argued, ‘I will receive the higher ordination first!’ ‘I will receive the higher ordination first!’ The elders said, ‘Come, friends, let us perform a single formal announcement for all of you.’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Bhikkhus, I allow a single formal announcement to be made for two or three candidates, and that with one preceptor, but certainly not with different preceptors.’

62. Gabbhavīsūpasampadānujānanā

62. Permission for the Higher Ordination of One Who is Twenty Years of Age Including Gestation

124. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā kumārakassapo gabbhavīso upasampanno ahosi. Atha kho āyasmato kumārakassapassa etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘na ūnavīsativasso puggalo upasampādetabbo’ti. Ahañcamhi gabbhavīso upasampanno. Upasampanno nu khomhi, nanu kho upasampanno”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Yaṃ, bhikkhave, mātukucchismiṃ paṭhamaṃ cittaṃ uppannaṃ, paṭhamaṃ viññāṇaṃ pātubhūtaṃ[T 1.0188], tadupādāya sāvassa jāti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gabbhavīsaṃ upasampādetunti.

124. At that time, the Venerable Kumārakassapa had been ordained being twenty years of age including gestation. Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Kumārakassapa: ‘It has been laid down by the Blessed One: “A person less than twenty years of age is not to be ordained.” And I was ordained being twenty years of age including gestation. Am I ordained, or am I not ordained?’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Bhikkhus, when the first mind arose in the mother’s womb, when the first consciousness appeared, taking that as the starting point, that is his birth. Bhikkhus, I allow one who is twenty years of age including gestation to be ordained.’

63. Upasampadāvidhi

63. The Procedure for Higher Ordination

125. Tena [M 0.0130] kho pana samayena upasampannā dissanti kuṭṭhikāpi gaṇḍikāpi kilāsikāpi sosikāpi apamārikāpi. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, upasampādentena terasa tassa (ka.) antarāyike dhamme pucchituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, pucchitabbo – “santi te evarūpā ābādhā – kuṭṭhaṃ, gaṇḍo, kilāso, soso, apamāro? Manussosi[V 0.0119]? Purisosi? Bhujissosi? Aṇaṇosi? Nasi rājabhaṭo? Anuññātosi mātāpitūhi? Paripuṇṇavīsativassosi? Paripuṇṇaṃ te pattacīvaraṃ? Kiṃnāmosi? Konāmo te upajjhāyo”ti?

125. Now at that time, those who had been ordained were seen to have leprosy, boils, skin disease, consumption, and epilepsy. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Bhikkhus, I allow the one giving the higher ordination to ask about the thirteen impediments. And, Bhikkhus, he should be asked in this way: “Do you have such diseases as leprosy, boils, skin disease, consumption, or epilepsy? Are you a human being? Are you a male? Are you a free man? Are you free from debt? Are you not in the king’s service? Are you permitted by your mother and father? Are you fully twenty years of age? Are your bowl and robes complete? What is your name? What is the name of your preceptor?”’

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ananusiṭṭhe upasampadāpekkhe antarāyike dhamme pucchanti. Upasampadāpekkhā vitthāyanti, maṅkū honti, na sakkonti vissajjetuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṃ anusāsitvā pacchā antarāyike [P 1.0094] dhamme pucchitunti.

At that time, bhikkhus were questioning candidates for higher ordination about the impediments without having first instructed them. The candidates for higher ordination became hesitant, were troubled, and were unable to answer. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Bhikkhus, I allow that having first instructed them, you may then ask about the impediments.’

Tattheva saṅghamajjhe anusāsanti. Upasampadāpekkhā tatheva vitthāyanti, maṅkū honti, na sakkonti vissajjetuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekamantaṃ anusāsitvā saṅghamajjhe antarāyike dhamme pucchituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, anusāsitabbo –

They instructed them right there in the midst of the Saṅgha. The candidates for higher ordination became hesitant just as before, were troubled, and were unable to answer. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Bhikkhus, I allow that having instructed him in a secluded place, you may ask him about the impediments in the midst of the Saṅgha. And, Bhikkhus, he should be instructed in this way:

126. Paṭhamaṃ upajjhaṃ gāhāpetabbo. Upajjhaṃ gāhāpetvā [T 1.0189] pattacīvaraṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ – ayaṃ te patto, ayaṃ saṅghāṭi, ayaṃ uttarāsaṅgo, ayaṃ antaravāsako. Gaccha, amumhi okāse tiṭṭhāhīti.

126. First, he should be made to take a preceptor. Having made him take a preceptor, the bowl and robes should be pointed out to him: ‘This is your bowl, this is your outer robe, this is your upper robe, and this is your lower robe. Go, stand in that place.’

Bālā abyattā anusāsanti. Duranusiṭṭhā upasampadāpekkhā vitthāyanti, maṅkū honti, na sakkonti vissajjetuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, bālena abyattena anusāsitabbo. Yo anusāseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena anusāsitunti.

Foolish and incompetent bhikkhus instructed them. The badly instructed candidates for higher ordination became hesitant, were troubled, and were unable to answer. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Bhikkhus, one should not be instructed by a foolish, incompetent bhikkhu. Whichever bhikkhu should so instruct, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, Bhikkhus, that a competent and capable bhikkhu should instruct.’

Asammatā anusāsanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, asammatena anusāsitabbo. Yo anusāseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi[M 0.0131], bhikkhave, sammatena anusāsituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbo sammanitabbo (ka.) – attanā vā attanāva (syā.) attānaṃ sammannitabbaṃ, parena vā paro sammannitabbo.

Unappointed monks were instructing. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, one who is unappointed should not instruct. Whichever monk should instruct, for that monk there is an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, one who has been appointed to instruct. And in this way, monks, one should be appointed: either one should appoint oneself, or another should appoint another.'

Kathañca [V 0.0120] attanāva attānaṃ sammannitabbaṃ? Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo – “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ itthannāmaṃ anusāseyya”nti. Evaṃ attanāva attānaṃ sammannitabbaṃ.

And how should one appoint oneself? A competent and capable monk should inform the Saṅgha: 'Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. So-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination of the venerable so-and-so. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, I would instruct so-and-so.' In this way, one should appoint oneself.

Kathañca pana parena paro sammannitabbo? Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo – “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, itthannāmo itthannāmaṃ anusāseyyā”ti[T 1.0190]. Evaṃ parena paro sammannitabbo.

And how then should another be appointed by another? A competent and capable monk should inform the Saṅgha: 'Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. So-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination of the venerable so-and-so. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the venerable so-and-so should instruct the candidate so-and-so.' In this way, another is appointed by another.

Tena sammatena bhikkhunā upasampadāpekkho upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – “suṇasi, itthannāma, ayaṃ te saccakālo bhūtakālo. Yaṃ jātaṃ taṃ saṅghamajjhe pucchante santaṃ atthīti vattabbaṃ, asantaṃ natthī”ti vattabbaṃ. Mā kho vitthāyi, mā kho maṅku ahosi. Evaṃ taṃ pucchissanti – “santi te evarūpā ābādhā – kuṭṭhaṃ, gaṇḍo, kilāso, soso, apamāro? Manussosi? Purisosi? Bhujissosi? Aṇaṇosi? Nasi rājabhaṭo? Anuññātosi mātāpitūhi? Paripuṇṇavīsativassosi? Paripuṇṇaṃ te pattacīvaraṃ? Kiṃnāmosi? Konāmo te upajjhāyo”ti?

That appointed monk, having approached the candidate for higher ordination, should speak to him thus: 'Listen, so-and-so, this is your time for truth, your time for fact. When asked in the midst of the Saṅgha about what has occurred, what is present should be stated as, “It is,” and what is not present should be stated as, “It is not.” Do not be hesitant, do not be troubled. They will ask you thus: “Do you have such diseases as these—leprosy, boils, skin disease, consumption, or epilepsy? Are you a human being? Are you a man? Are you a free man? Are you free from debt? Are you not in the king’s service? Are you permitted by your mother and father? Are you of twenty full years of age? Are your bowl and robes complete? What is your name? What is the name of your preceptor?”'

Ekato āgacchanti. Na, bhikkhave, ekato āgantabbaṃ. Anusāsakena paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā saṅgho ñāpetabbo – “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho[P 1.0095]. Anusiṭṭho so mayā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, itthannāmo āgaccheyyā”ti. Āgacchāhīti vattabbo.

They come together. Monks, they should not come together. The instructor should come first and inform the Saṅgha: ‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. So-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination under the Venerable So-and-so. He has been instructed by me. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, So-and-so may come.’ He should be told: ‘Come!’”

Ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ kārāpetvā bhikkhūnaṃ pāde vandāpetvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīdāpetvā añjaliṃ paggaṇhāpetvā upasampadaṃ yācāpetabbo – “saṅghaṃ, bhante, upasampadaṃ yācāmi. Ullumpatu maṃ, bhante, saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāya. Dutiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācāmi. Ullumpatu maṃ, bhante, saṅgho anukampaṃ [M 0.0132] upādāya. Tatiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācāmi. Ullumpatu maṃ[T 1.0191], bhante, saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāyā”ti. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Having had him arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, had him pay homage to the monks’ feet, had him sit in a squatting position, and had him raise his hands in añjali, he should be made to request the higher ordination: ‘Venerable sirs, I request the higher ordination from the Saṅgha. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha lift me up out of compassion. For the second time, venerable sirs, I request the higher ordination from the Saṅgha. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha lift me up out of compassion. For the third time, venerable sirs, I request the higher ordination from the Saṅgha. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha lift me up out of compassion.’ A competent and capable monk should inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho. Yadi [V 0.0121] saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ itthannāmaṃ antarāyike dhamme puccheyya”nti? Suṇasi, itthannāma, ayaṃ te saccakālo bhūtakālo. Yaṃ jātaṃ taṃ pucchāmi. Santaṃ atthīti vattabbaṃ, asantaṃ natthīti vattabbaṃ. Santi te evarūpā ābādhā – kuṭṭhaṃ gaṇḍo kileso soso apamāro, manussosi, purisosi, bhujissosi, aṇaṇosi, nasi rājabhaṭo, anuññātosi mātāpitūhi, paripuṇṇavīsativassosi, paripuṇṇaṃ te pattacīvaraṃ, kiṃnāmosi, konāmo te upajjhāyoti? Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This So-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination under the Venerable So-and-so. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, I would ask So-and-so about the obstructing conditions.” “So-and-so, do you hear? This is your time for truth, your time for fact. I ask you about what has occurred. If it exists, you should say, ‘It exists’; if it does not exist, you should say, ‘It does not exist.’ Do you have such diseases as these: leprosy, boils, skin disease, consumption, or epilepsy? Are you a human being? Are you a man? Are you a free man? Are you free from debt? Are you not a royal servant? Are you permitted by your parents? Are you fully twenty years of age? Are your bowl and robes complete? What is your name? What is the name of your preceptor?” A competent and capable monk should inform the Saṅgha:

127. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho, parisuddho antarāyikehi dhammehi, paripuṇṇassa pattacīvaraṃ. Itthannāmo saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeyya itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Esā ñatti.

127. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This So-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination of the Venerable So-and-so; he is pure from the obstructing conditions, and his bowl and robes are complete. So-and-so requests higher ordination from the Saṅgha with So-and-so as preceptor. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should confer higher ordination on So-and-so with So-and-so as preceptor. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho, parisuddho antarāyikehi dhammehi, paripuṇṇassa pattacīvaraṃ. Itthannāmo saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeti itthannāmena upajjhāyena[T 1.0192]. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa upasampadā itthannāmena upajjhāyena, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This So-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination of the Venerable So-and-so; he is pure from the obstructing conditions, and his bowl and robes are complete. So-and-so requests higher ordination from the Saṅgha with So-and-so as preceptor. The Saṅgha confers higher ordination on So-and-so with So-and-so as preceptor. Whichever venerable one approves of the higher ordination of So-and-so with So-and-so as preceptor, let him be silent; whoever does not approve, let him speak.

“Dutiyampi etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho, parisuddho antarāyikehi dhammehi, paripuṇṇassa pattacīvaraṃ. Itthannāmo saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeti itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa upasampadā itthannāmena upajjhāyena, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

For a second time, I state this matter: Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This So-and-so is a candidate for higher ordination of the Venerable So-and-so; he is pure from the obstructing conditions, and his bowl and robes are complete. So-and-so requests higher ordination from the Saṅgha with So-and-so as preceptor. The Saṅgha confers higher ordination on So-and-so with So-and-so as preceptor. Whichever venerable one approves of the higher ordination of So-and-so with So-and-so as preceptor, let him be silent; whoever does not approve, let him speak.

“Tatiyampi [M 0.0133] etamatthaṃ vadāmi – suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato upasampadāpekkho, parisuddho antarāyikehi dhammehi, paripuṇṇassa pattacīvaraṃ. Itthannāmo saṅghaṃ upasampadaṃ yācati itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ upasampādeti itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa upasampadā itthannāmena upajjhāyena, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

For the third time, I speak on this matter. Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. This person, named so-and-so, is an aspirant for higher ordination under the venerable so-and-so. He is purified of obstructive qualities; his bowl and robes are complete. So-and-so requests higher ordination from the Saṅgha with so-and-so as preceptor. The Saṅgha ordains so-and-so with so-and-so as preceptor. If the higher ordination of so-and-so with so-and-so as preceptor is agreeable to any venerable one, they should remain silent. If it is not agreeable to anyone, they should speak.

“Upasampanno [V 0.0122] saṅghena itthannāmo itthannāmena upajjhāyena. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

So-and-so has been ordained by the Saṅgha with so-and-so as preceptor. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I record this.

Upasampadākammaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The act of higher ordination is concluded.

64. Cattāro nissayā

64. The Four Supports

128. Tāvadeva chāyā metabbā, utuppamāṇaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ, divasabhāgo [T 1.0193] ācikkhitabbo, saṅgīti ācikkhitabbā[P 1.0096], cattāro nissayā ācikkhitabbā ācikkhitabbā, cattāri akaraṇīyāni ācikkhitabbāni. (ka.) –

128. At that very moment, the shadow should be measured, the measure of the season should be told, the part of the day should be told, the summary should be told, and the four supports should be told:

“Piṇḍiyālopabhojanaṃ nissāya pabbajjā. Tattha te yāvajīvaṃ ussāho karaṇīyo. Atirekalābho – saṅghabhattaṃ, uddesabhattaṃ, nimantanaṃ, salākabhattaṃ, pakkhikaṃ, uposathikaṃ, pāṭipadikaṃ.

The going forth is dependent on food from collected morsels. In this, you must make an effort for as long as you live. Extra allowances are: a meal for the Saṅgha, a designated meal, an invitation, a meal distributed by ticket, a fortnightly meal, an observance-day meal, and a first-day-of-the-fortnight meal.

“Paṃsukūlacīvaraṃ nissāya pabbajjā. Tattha te yāvajīvaṃ ussāho karaṇīyo. Atirekalābho – khomaṃ, kappāsikaṃ, koseyyaṃ, kambalaṃ, sāṇaṃ, bhaṅgaṃ.

The going forth is dependent on refuse-rag robes. In this, you must make an effort for as long as you live. Extra allowances are: linen cloth, cotton cloth, silk cloth, woolen cloth, hempen cloth, and cloth of mixed fibres.

“Rukkhamūlasenāsanaṃ nissāya pabbajjā. Tattha te yāvajīvaṃ ussāho karaṇīyo. Atirekalābho – vihāro, aḍḍhayogo, pāsādo, hammiyaṃ, guhā.

The going forth is dependent on lodging at the root of a tree. In this, you must make an effort for as long as you live. Extra allowances are: a monastery, a gabled lodging, a long-house, a storied building, and a cave.

“Pūtimuttabhesajjaṃ nissāya pabbajjā. Tattha te yāvajīvaṃ ussāho karaṇīyo. Atirekalābho – sappi, navanītaṃ, telaṃ, madhu, phāṇita”nti.

The going forth is dependent on medicine of fermented urine. In this, you must make an effort for as long as you live. Extra allowances are: ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, and molasses.

Cattāro nissayā niṭṭhitā.

The four supports are concluded.

65. Cattāri akaraṇīyāni

65. The Four Things Not to Be Done

129. Tena [M 0.0134] kho pana samayena bhikkhū aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ upasampādetvā ekakaṃ ohāya pakkamiṃsu. So pacchā ekakova āgacchanto antarāmagge purāṇadutiyikāya samāgañchi. Sā evamāha – “kiṃdāni pabbajitosī”ti? “Āma, pabbajitomhī”ti. “Dullabho kho pabbajitānaṃ methuno dhammo; ehi, methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevā”ti. So tassā methunaṃ dhammaṃ [V 0.0123] paṭisevitvā cirena agamāsi. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “kissa tvaṃ, āvuso, evaṃ ciraṃ akāsī”ti? Atha kho so bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[T 1.0194]. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, upasampādetvā dutiyaṃ dātuṃ, cattāri ca akaraṇīyāni ācikkhituṃ –

129. Now at that time, some bhikkhus, having given higher ordination to a certain bhikkhu, left him alone and departed. Later, as he was returning alone, he met his former wife on the way. She said to him: 'Have you now gone forth?' 'Yes, I have gone forth.' 'Sexual intercourse is indeed difficult to obtain for those who have gone forth. Come, let us engage in sexual intercourse.' He engaged in sexual intercourse with her and arrived after a long time. The bhikkhus asked him: 'Friend, why have you been so long?' Then that bhikkhu told the bhikkhus about this matter. The bhikkhus told the Blessed One about this matter. 'Bhikkhus, I allow that after higher ordination, a companion be given, and the four things not to be done be explained—'

“Upasampannena bhikkhunā methuno dhammo na paṭisevitabbo, antamaso tiracchānagatāyapi. Yo bhikkhu methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevati, assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo. Seyyathāpi nāma puriso sīsacchinno abhabbo tena sarīrabandhanena jīvituṃ, evameva bhikkhu methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevitvā assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo. Taṃ te yāvajīvaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ.

A bhikkhu who has received higher ordination should not engage in sexual intercourse, not even with a female animal. Any bhikkhu who engages in sexual intercourse is no longer a recluse, no longer a son of the Sakyan. Just as a person whose head has been cut off is unable to live with that body, so too a bhikkhu who engages in sexual intercourse is no longer a recluse, no longer a son of the Sakyan. That is not to be done by you for as long as you live.

“Upasampannena bhikkhunā adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ na ādātabbaṃ, antamaso tiṇasalākaṃ upādāya. Yo bhikkhu pādaṃ vā pādārahaṃ vā atirekapādaṃ vā adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyati, assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo. Seyyathāpi nāma paṇḍupalāso bandhanā pamutto abhabbo haritatthāya, evameva bhikkhu pādaṃ vā pādārahaṃ vā atirekapādaṃ vā adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyitvā assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo. Taṃ te yāvajīvaṃ [P 1.0097] akaraṇīyaṃ.

A bhikkhu who has received higher ordination should not take what is not given, with the intention of theft, not even so much as a blade of grass. Any bhikkhu who takes what is not given with the intention of theft—whether a pāda, what is worth a pāda, or more than a pāda—is no longer a recluse, no longer a son of the Sakyan. Just as a yellow leaf fallen from its stalk is incapable of becoming green again, so too a bhikkhu who takes what is not given with the intention of theft—whether a pāda, what is worth a pāda, or more than a pāda—is no longer a recluse, no longer a son of the Sakyan. That is not to be done by you for as long as you live.

“Upasampannena bhikkhunā sañcicca pāṇo jīvitā na voropetabbo, antamaso kunthakipillikaṃ upādāya. Yo bhikkhu sañcicca manussaviggahaṃ jīvitā voropeti, antamaso gabbhapātanaṃ upādāya, assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo. Seyyathāpi nāma puthusilā dvedhā bhinnā appaṭisandhikā hoti, evameva bhikkhu sañcicca manussaviggahaṃ jīvitā voropetvā assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo[T 1.0195]. Taṃ te yāvajīvaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ.

A bhikkhu who has received higher ordination should not intentionally deprive a living being of life, not even an ant or a termite. Any bhikkhu who intentionally deprives a human being of life, even down to causing an abortion, is not a recluse, not a son of the Sakyan. Just as a large stone slab, split in two, cannot be rejoined, even so, a bhikkhu who intentionally deprives a human being of life is not a recluse, not a son of the Sakyan. This is not to be done by you for as long as you live.

“Upasampannena [M 0.0135] bhikkhunā uttarimanussadhammo na ullapitabbo, antamaso ‘suññāgāre abhiramāmī’ti. Yo bhikkhu pāpiccho icchāpakato asantaṃ abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapati jhānaṃ vā vimokkhaṃ vā samādhiṃ vā samāpattiṃ vā maggaṃ vā phalaṃ vā, assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo. Seyyathāpi nāma tālo matthakacchinno abhabbo puna viruḷhiyā, evameva bhikkhu pāpiccho icchāpakato asantaṃ abhūtaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ ullapitvā assamaṇo hoti asakyaputtiyo. Taṃ te yāvajīvaṃ akaraṇīya”nti.

A bhikkhu who has received higher ordination should not speak of a superhuman state, not even to say, ‘I delight in a secluded dwelling.’ Any bhikkhu who, having evil wishes and being overcome by desire, speaks of a non-existent, untrue superhuman state—be it jhāna, liberation, concentration, attainment, path, or fruition—is not a recluse, not a son of the Sakyan. Just as a palm tree with its top cut off is incapable of new growth, even so, a bhikkhu who, having evil wishes and being overcome by desire, speaks of a non-existent, untrue superhuman state is not a recluse, not a son of the Sakyan. This is not to be done by you for as long as you live.

Cattāri akaraṇīyāni niṭṭhitāni.

The four things not to be done are concluded.

66. Āpattiyā adassane ukkhittakavatthūni

66. The Cases of Suspension for Not Seeing an Offense

130. Tena [V 0.0124] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu āpattiyā adassane ukkhittako vibbhami. So puna paccāgantvā bhikkhū upasampadaṃ yāci. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

130. At that time, a certain bhikkhu who had been suspended for not seeing an offense disrobed. He later returned and asked the bhikkhus for higher ordination. They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āpattiyā adassane ukkhittako vibbhamati. So puna paccāgantvā bhikkhū upasampadaṃ yācati. So evamassa vacanīyo – “passissasi taṃ āpatti”nti? Sacāhaṃ passissāmīti, pabbājetabbo. Sacāhaṃ na passissāmīti, na pabbājetabbo. Pabbājetvā vattabbo – “passissasi taṃ āpatti”nti? Sacāhaṃ passissāmīti, upasampādetabbo. Sacāhaṃ na passissāmīti, na upasampādetabbo. Upasampādetvā vattabbo – “passissasi taṃ āpatti”nti? Sacāhaṃ passissāmīti[T 1.0196], osāretabbo. Sacāhaṃ na passissāmīti, na osāretabbo. Osāretvā vattabbo – “passasi passāhi (sī.) taṃ āpatti”nti? Sace passati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce passati, labbhamānāya sāmaggiyā puna ukkhipitabbo. Alabbhamānāya sāmaggiyā anāpatti sambhoge saṃvāse.

Furthermore, monks, a monk who has been suspended for not seeing an offense disrobes. Having returned again, he asks the monks for higher ordination. He should be told thus: ‘Will you see that offense?’ If he says, ‘I will see it,’ he should be given the going-forth. If he says, ‘I will not see it,’ he should not be given the going-forth. Having given him the going-forth, he should be told: ‘Will you see that offense?’ If he says, ‘I will see it,’ he should be given higher ordination. If he says, ‘I will not see it,’ he should not be given higher ordination. Having given him higher ordination, he should be told: ‘Will you see that offense?’ If he says, ‘I will see it,’ he should be reinstated. If he says, ‘I will not see it,’ he should not be reinstated. Having reinstated him, he should be told: ‘See that offense.’ If he sees it, this is good. If he does not see it, and if harmony of the Saṅgha is obtained, he should be suspended again. If harmony of the Saṅgha is not obtained, there is no offense in communion or in co-residence.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittako vibbhamati. So puna paccāgantvā bhikkhū upasampadaṃ yācati. So evamassa vacanīyo – “paṭikarissasi taṃ āpatti”nti? Sacāhaṃ paṭikarissāmīti, pabbājetabbo[P 1.0098]. Sacāhaṃ na paṭikarissāmīti, na pabbājetabbo. Pabbājetvā vattabbo – “paṭikarissasi [M 0.0136] taṃ āpatti”nti? Sacāhaṃ paṭikarissāmīti, upasampādetabbo. Sacāhaṃ na paṭikarissāmīti, na upasampādetabbo. Upasampādetvā vattabbo – “paṭikarissasi taṃ āpatti”nti? Sacāhaṃ paṭikarissāmīti, osāretabbo. Sacāhaṃ na paṭikarissāmīti, na osāretabbo. Osāretvā vattabbo – “paṭikarohi taṃ āpatti”nti. Sace paṭikaroti, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce paṭikaroti labbhamānāya sāmaggiyā puna ukkhipitabbo. Alabbhamānāya sāmaggiyā anāpatti sambhoge saṃvāse.

Furthermore, monks, a monk who has been suspended for not making amends for an offense disrobes. Having returned again, he asks the monks for higher ordination. He should be told thus: ‘Will you make amends for that offense?’ If he says, ‘I will make amends,’ he should be given the going-forth. If he says, ‘I will not make amends,’ he should not be given the going-forth. Having given him the going-forth, he should be told: ‘Will you make amends for that offense?’ If he says, ‘I will make amends,’ he should be given higher ordination. If he says, ‘I will not make amends,’ he should not be given higher ordination. Having given him higher ordination, he should be told: ‘Will you make amends for that offense?’ If he says, ‘I will make amends,’ he should be reinstated. If he says, ‘I will not make amends,’ he should not be reinstated. Having reinstated him, he should be told: ‘Make amends for that offense.’ If he makes amends, this is good. If he does not make amends, and if harmony of the Saṅgha is obtained, he should be suspended again. If harmony of the Saṅgha is not obtained, there is no offense in communion or in co-residence.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittako vibbhamati. So puna paccāgantvā bhikkhū upasampadaṃ yācati. So evamassa vacanīyo – “paṭinissajjissasi taṃ pāpikaṃ diṭṭhi”nti? Sacāhaṃ paṭinissajjissāmīti, pabbājetabbo. Sacāhaṃ na paṭinissajjissāmīti, na pabbājetabbo. Pabbājetvā vattabbo – “paṭinissajjissasi [V 0.0125] taṃ [T 1.0197] pāpikaṃ diṭṭhi”nti? Sacāhaṃ paṭinissajjissāmīti, upasampādetabbo. Sacāhaṃ na paṭinissajjissāmīti, na upasampādetabbo. Upasampādetvā vattabbo – “paṭinissajjissasi taṃ pāpikaṃ diṭṭhi”nti? Sacāhaṃ paṭinissajjissāmīti, osāretabbo. Sacāhaṃ na paṭinissajjissāmīti, na osāretabbo. Osāretvā vattabbo – “paṭinissajjehi taṃ pāpikaṃ diṭṭhi”nti. Sace paṭinissajjati, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce paṭinissajjati, labbhamānāya sāmaggiyā puna ukkhipitabbo. Alabbhamānāya sāmaggiyā anāpatti sambhoge saṃvāseti.

Furthermore, monks, a monk who has been suspended for not relinquishing a wicked view disrobes. Having returned again, he asks the monks for higher ordination. He should be told thus: ‘Will you relinquish that wicked view?’ If he says, ‘I will relinquish it,’ he should be given the going-forth. If he says, ‘I will not relinquish it,’ he should not be given the going-forth. Having given him the going-forth, he should be told: ‘Will you relinquish that wicked view?’ If he says, ‘I will relinquish it,’ he should be given higher ordination. If he says, ‘I will not relinquish it,’ he should not be given higher ordination. Having given him higher ordination, he should be told: ‘Will you relinquish that wicked view?’ If he says, ‘I will relinquish it,’ he should be reinstated. If he says, ‘I will not relinquish it,’ he should not be reinstated. Having reinstated him, he should be told: ‘Relinquish that wicked view.’ If he relinquishes it, this is good. If he does not relinquish it, and if harmony of the Saṅgha is obtained, he should be suspended again. If harmony of the Saṅgha is not obtained, there is no offense in communion or in co-residence.

Mahākhandhako paṭhamo.

The First Great Section is finished.

67. Tassuddānaṃ

67. The summary thereof:

131.

131.

Vinayamhi mahatthesu, pesalānaṃ sukhāvahe;

Niggahānañca pāpicche, lajjīnaṃ paggahesu ca.

In the Vinaya, which brings happiness to the virtuous, in matters of great benefit, in the restraining of those with evil wishes, and in the supporting of the conscientious.

Sāsanādhāraṇe ceva, sabbaññujinagocare;

Anaññavisaye kheme, supaññatte asaṃsaye.

And in upholding the Dispensation, which is the domain of the All-knowing Conquerors, not the domain of others, secure, well-proclaimed, and free from doubt.

Khandhake vinaye ceva, parivāre ca mātike;

Yathātthakārī kusalo, paṭipajjati yoniso.

In the Khandhakas, in the Vinaya, in the Parivāra, and in the Mātikā, a skilled monk, acting in accordance with the meaning, practices appropriately.

Yo [M 0.0137] gavaṃ na vijānāti, na so rakkhati gogaṇaṃ;

Evaṃ [T 1.0198] sīlaṃ ajānanto, kiṃ so rakkheyya saṃvaraṃ.

Just as one who does not know the cow does not protect the herd of cows, so too, one who does not know virtue, how could they guard restraint?

Pamuṭṭhamhi ca suttante, abhidhamme ca tāvade;

Vinaye [P 1.0099] avinaṭṭhamhi, puna tiṭṭhati sāsanaṃ.

Even if the Suttanta Piṭaka and the Abhidhamma Piṭaka are forgotten, if the Vinaya Piṭaka is not lost, the Dispensation stands again.

Tasmā saṅgāhaṇāhetuṃ saṅgāhanāhetuṃ (ka.), uddānaṃ anupubbaso;

Pavakkhāmi yathāñāyaṃ, suṇātha mama bhāsato.

Therefore, for the purpose of compilation, I will recite the summary in due order, according to what is known. Listen to me as I speak.

Vatthu [V 0.0126] nidānaṃ āpatti, nayā peyyālameva ca;

Dukkaraṃ taṃ asesetuṃ, nayato taṃ vijānathāti.

The story, the origin, the offense, the detailed method, and the abbreviated sections—it is difficult to explain all of that without remainder. You should understand all of that by the concise method.

Bodhi rājāyatanañca, ajapālo sahampati;

Brahmā āḷāro udako, bhikkhu ca upako isi.

The Bodhi tree, the Rājāyatana tree, and the Ajapāla tree; Sahampati Brahmā's request; Āḷāra and Udaka; the five monks; the ascetic Upaka; and the journey to Isipatana.

Koṇḍañño vappo bhaddiyo, mahānāmo ca assaji;

Yaso cattāro paññāsa, sabbe pesesi so disā.

Thera Koṇḍañña, Thera Vappa, Thera Bhaddiya, Thera Mahānāma, and Thera Assaji; Thera Yasa, the four Theras, and the fifty Theras. That Sage sent them all forth to the various regions.

Vatthu mārehi tiṃsā ca, uruvelaṃ tayo jaṭī;

Agyāgāraṃ mahārājā, sakko brahmā ca kevalā.
