The chapter on permitting ordination with the three refuges; the chapter concerning Māra; the chapter on the thirty Bhaddavaggīya princes; the journey to Uruvelā; the three matted-hair ascetic brothers; entering the fire-hut; illuminating the entire forest; the coming of the four Great Kings; the coming of Sakka; and the coming of Brahmā.

Paṃsukūlaṃ pokkharaṇī, silā ca kakudho silā;

Jambu [T 1.0199] ambo ca āmalo, pāripupphañca āhari.

The chapter on picking up the rag-robe; digging the pond; placing the stone slab nearby; the bending of the Kakudha tree; placing the stone slab nearby; bringing the Jambu fruit; bringing the mango fruit; bringing the myrobalan fruit; and bringing the Pārichattaka flower.

Phāliyantu ujjalantu, vijjhāyantu ca kassapa;

Nimujjanti mukhī megho, gayā laṭṭhi ca māgadho.

The chapter on saying, 'Let them split,' 'Let them blaze,' and 'Let them be extinguished,' concerning Kassapa; the five hundred ascetics diving; creating five hundred braziers; the great rain; dwelling at Gayā; dwelling in the palm-grove; and the request of the King of Magadha.

Upatisso kolito ca, abhiññātā ca pabbajuṃ;

Dunnivatthā paṇāmanā, kiso lūkho ca brāhmaṇo.

Upatissa and Kolita; well-known men going forth; the badly dressed; bending the bowl; and the emaciated, austere brahmin (Rādha).

Anācāraṃ ācarati, udaraṃ māṇavo gaṇo;

Vassaṃ bālehi pakkanto, dasa vassāni nissayo.

The chapter on the monk who practices improperly; the brahmin who ordained for his belly's sake; the young man who inquired about requisites; ordination by a group; Upasena giving ordination after one rains-residence; ordination given by foolish monks; the departure of the preceptor; and giving dependence after ten rains-residences.

Na vattanti paṇāmetuṃ, bālā passaddhi pañca cha;

Yo so añño ca naggo ca, acchinnajaṭilasākiyo.

Pupils who do not practice well; permission to banish; foolish monks giving dependence; cessation of dependence; the five and six factors; the one who reverts to another sect; the naked ascetic; the one with uncut hair; the matted-hair ascetic; and the Sākiyan.

Magadhesu pañcābādhā, eko rājā bhaṭo coro (syā.) ca aṅguli;

Māgadho ca anuññāsi, kārā likhi kasāhato.

The five diseases in Magadha; a certain young man; the king's order; Aṅgulimāla; the King of Magadha's permission; a prison-breaker; a proclaimed offender; and one who has been flogged.

Lakkhaṇā [M 0.0138][V 0.0127] iṇā dāso ca, bhaṇḍuko upāli ahi;

Saddhaṃ kulaṃ kaṇṭako ca, āhundarikameva ca.

One who has been branded; a debtor; a slave; the bald-headed Bhaṇḍuka; the boy Upāli; the skin disease; a faithful family; the novice Kaṇḍaka; and the narrow region.

Vatthumhi dārako sikkhā, viharanti ca kiṃ nu kho;

Sabbaṃ mukhaṃ upajjhāye, apalāḷana kaṇṭako.

Dwelling in Kapilavatthu; the boy Rāhula; the training rules; 'How should they be punished?'; prohibiting the preceptor's entire allowance; prohibiting food; prohibiting novices without the preceptor's leave; enticing pupils; and the novice Kaṇḍaka.

Paṇḍako theyyapakkanto, ahi ca mātarī pitā;

Arahantabhikkhunībhedā, ruhirena ca byañjanaṃ.

A paṇḍaka, one in clandestine communion, one who has gone over to the heretics, a nāga, a matricide, a patricide, a killer of an Arahant, a violator of a nun, a creator of schism, one who has shed the Buddha's blood, and a hermaphrodite.

Anupajjhāyasaṅghena, gaṇapaṇḍakapattako;

Acīvaraṃ [T 1.0200] tadubhayaṃ, yācitenapi ye tayo.

Without a preceptor, with the Sangha as preceptor, with a group as preceptor, with a paṇḍaka as preceptor, one without a bowl, one without robes, one without both, with borrowed requisites, and the three persons.

Hatthā pādā hatthapādā, kaṇṇā nāsā tadūbhayaṃ;

Aṅguliaḷakaṇḍaraṃ, phaṇaṃ khujjañca vāmanaṃ.

One with hands cut off, with feet cut off, with hands and feet cut off, with ears cut off, with the nose cut off, with both cut off, with fingers cut off, with thumbs or big toes cut off, with sinews cut off, with webbed fingers, a hunchback, and a dwarf.

Galagaṇḍī lakkhaṇā ceva, kasā likhitasīpadī;

Pāpaparisadūsī ca, kāṇaṃ kuṇi tatheva ca.

One with a goiter, one who has been branded, one who has been flogged, a proclaimed offender, one with elephantiasis, one with a bad disease, a corrupter of the assembly, one-eyed, one with a crooked limb, and likewise.

Khañjaṃ [P 1.0100] pakkhahatañceva, sacchinnairiyāpathaṃ;

Jarāndhamūgabadhiraṃ, andhamūgañca yaṃ tahiṃ.

The lame, one afflicted with paralysis, one with impaired movement, the aged, the blind, the mute, the deaf, and the blind and mute among them.

Andhabadhiraṃ yaṃ vuttaṃ, mūgabadhirameva ca;

Andhamūgabadhirañca, alajjīnañca nissayaṃ.

The blind and deaf, it was said, and the mute and deaf, and the blind, mute, and deaf, and the giving of dependence to the shameless.

Vatthabbañca tathāddhānaṃ, yācamānena lakkhaṇā pekkhanā (sabbattha);

Āgacchatu vivadanti, ekupajjhāyena kassapo.

Living in dependence, likewise a long journey, being requested, looking out for one who is coming, they dispute, by one preceptor, Kassapa.

Dissanti upasampannā, ābādhehi ca pīḷitā;

Ananusiṭṭhā vitthenti, tattheva anusāsanā.

Those ordained who are afflicted by diseases are seen. Those who are uninstructed are hesitant; the instruction is given right there.

Saṅghepi [V 0.0128] ca atho bālā, asammatā ca ekato;

Ullumpatupasampadā, nissayo ekako tayoti.

And in the Sangha; furthermore, the foolish and the unauthorized; together. 'May he be raised up'; ordination; the four dependences; at once, three.

Imamhi khandhake vatthūni ekasatañca dvāsattati.

In this Khandhaka, there are one hundred and seventy-two topics.

Mahākhandhako niṭṭhito.

The Mahākhandhaka is concluded.

2. Uposathakkhandhako

2. The Chapter on the Uposatha

68. Sannipātānujānanā

68. The Allowance for Assembly

132. Tena [P 1.0101][M 0.0139][V 0.0129][T 1.0201] samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Tena kho pana samayena aññatitthiyā paribbājakā cātuddase pannarase aṭṭhamiyā ca pakkhassa sannipatitvā dhammaṃ bhāsanti. Te manussā upasaṅkamanti dhammassavanāya. Te labhanti aññatitthiyesu paribbājakesu pemaṃ, labhanti pasādaṃ, labhanti aññatitthiyā paribbājakā pakkhaṃ. Atha kho rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “etarahi kho aññatitthiyā paribbājakā cātuddase pannarase aṭṭhamiyā ca pakkhassa sannipatitvā dhammaṃ bhāsanti. Te manussā upasaṅkamanti dhammassavanāya. Te labhanti aññatitthiyesu paribbājakesu pemaṃ, labhanti pasādaṃ, labhanti aññatitthiyā paribbājakā pakkhaṃ. Yaṃnūna ayyāpi cātuddase pannarase aṭṭhamiyā ca pakkhassa sannipateyyu”nti. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idha mayhaṃ, bhante, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi ‘etarahi kho aññatitthiyā paribbājakā cātuddase pannarase aṭṭhamiyā ca pakkhassa sannipatitvā dhammaṃ bhāsanti. Te manussā [T 1.0202] upasaṅkamanti dhammassavanāya. Te labhanti aññatitthiyesu paribbājakesu pemaṃ, labhanti pasādaṃ, labhanti aññatitthiyā paribbājakā pakkhaṃ. Yaṃnūna ayyāpi cātuddase pannarase aṭṭhamiyā ca pakkhassa sannipateyyu’nti. Sādhu, bhante, ayyāpi cātuddase pannarase aṭṭhamiyā ca pakkhassa sannipateyyu”nti. Atha kho bhagavā rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ seniyaṃ bimbisāraṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ [V 0.0130] abhivādetvā [P 1.0102] padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi [M 0.0140] – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cātuddase pannarase aṭṭhamiyā ca pakkhassa sannipatitu”nti.

132. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha on Vulture Peak Mountain. Now at that time, wandering ascetics of other sects gathered on the fourteenth, fifteenth, and eighth days of the fortnight to teach the Dhamma. People approached them to listen to the Dhamma. They gained affection for the wandering ascetics of other sects, they gained confidence in them, and the wandering ascetics of other sects gained a following. Then, while King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha was alone in seclusion, this thought arose in his mind: 'Nowadays, wandering ascetics of other sects gather on the fourteenth, fifteenth, and eighth days of the fortnight to teach the Dhamma. People approach them to listen to the Dhamma. They gain affection for the wandering ascetics of other sects, they gain confidence in them, and the wandering ascetics of other sects gain a following. It would be good if the venerable ones were also to gather on the fourteenth, fifteenth, and eighth days of the fortnight.' Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha said to the Blessed One: 'Just now, Venerable Sir, while I was alone in seclusion, this thought arose in my mind: "Nowadays, wandering ascetics of other sects gather on the fourteenth, fifteenth, and eighth days of the fortnight to teach the Dhamma. People approach them to listen to the Dhamma. They gain affection for the wandering ascetics of other sects, they gain confidence in them, and the wandering ascetics of other sects gain a following. It would be good if the venerable ones were also to gather on the fourteenth, fifteenth, and eighth days of the fortnight." It would be good, Venerable Sir, if the venerable ones also gathered on the fourteenth, fifteenth, and eighth days of the fortnight.' Then the Blessed One instructed, inspired, aroused, and gladdened King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha with a Dhamma talk. Having been instructed, inspired, aroused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, and departed. Then, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a Dhamma talk, the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'Monks, I allow you to gather on the fourteenth, fifteenth, and eighth days of the fortnight.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū – bhagavatā anuññātā cātuddase pannarase aṭṭhamiyā ca pakkhassa sannipatitunti – cātuddase pannarase aṭṭhamiyā ca pakkhassa sannipatitvā tuṇhī nisīdanti. Te manussā upasaṅkamanti dhammassavanāya. Te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā cātuddase pannarase aṭṭhamiyā ca pakkhassa sannipatitvā tuṇhī nisīdissanti, seyyathāpi mūgasūkarā. Nanu nāma sannipatitehi dhammo bhāsitabbo”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ [T 1.0203] vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cātuddase pannarase aṭṭhamiyā ca pakkhassa sannipatitvā dhammaṃ bhāsitu”nti.

At that time, the monks, thinking, 'The Blessed One has permitted us to assemble on the fourteenth, fifteenth, and eighth days of the fortnight,' assembled on those days and sat in silence. People approached to hear the Dhamma. They complained, were displeased, and criticized: 'How indeed can these Sakyan ascetics assemble on the fourteenth, fifteenth, and eighth days of the fortnight and sit in silence, like mute pigs? Surely, when assembled, the Dhamma should be spoken!' The monks heard these people complaining, being displeased, and criticizing. Then those monks reported the matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on that occasion, in this connection, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: 'Monks, I allow you to assemble on the fourteenth, fifteenth, and eighth days of the fortnight and speak the Dhamma.'

69. Pātimokkhuddesānujānanā

69. The Authorization to Recite the Pātimokkha

133. Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ yāni mayā bhikkhūnaṃ paññattāni sikkhāpadāni, tāni nesaṃ pātimokkhuddesaṃ anujāneyyaṃ. So nesaṃ bhavissati uposathakamma”nti. Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – idha mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ yāni mayā bhikkhūnaṃ paññattāni sikkhāpadāni, tāni nesaṃ pātimokkhuddesaṃ anujāneyyaṃ. So nesaṃ bhavissati uposathakamma’nti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pātimokkhaṃ uddisituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, uddisitabbaṃ. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

133. Then, while the Blessed One was alone in seclusion, this thought arose in his mind: 'What if I were to authorize for the bhikkhus the recitation of the Pātimokkha, which consists of those training rules that were laid down by me? That would be their Uposatha observance.' Then, in the evening, the Blessed One emerged from seclusion and, on that occasion, in this connection, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the bhikkhus: 'Bhikkhus, while I was alone in seclusion, this thought arose in my mind: “What if I were to authorize for the bhikkhus the recitation of the Pātimokkha, which consists of those training rules that were laid down by me? That would be their Uposatha observance.” Bhikkhus, I authorize you to recite the Pātimokkha. And, bhikkhus, it should be recited thus. A competent and capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:'

134. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa [T 1.0204] pattakallaṃ, saṅgho uposathaṃ kareyya, pātimokkhaṃ uddiseyya. Kiṃ saṅghassa pubbakiccaṃ? Pārisuddhiṃ āyasmanto ārocetha[P 1.0103]. Pātimokkhaṃ uddisissāmi. Taṃ sabbeva santā sādhukaṃ suṇoma manasi karoma. Yassa siyā āpatti[M 0.0141], so āvikareyya. Asantiyā āpattiyā tuṇhī bhavitabbaṃ. Tuṇhībhāvena kho panāyasmante [V 0.0131] parisuddhāti vedissāmi. Yathā kho pana paccekapuṭṭhassa veyyākaraṇaṃ hoti, evamevaṃ evameva (ka) evarūpāya parisāya yāvatatiyaṃ anussāvitaṃ hoti. Yo pana bhikkhu yāvatatiyaṃ anussāviyamāne saramāno santiṃ āpattiṃ nāvikareyya, sampajānamusāvādassa hoti. Sampajānamusāvādo kho panāyasmanto antarāyiko dhammo vutto bhagavatā. Tasmā, saramānena bhikkhunā āpannena visuddhāpekkhena santī āpatti āvikātabbā; āvikatā hissa phāsu hotī”ti.

134. Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. What is the Saṅgha’s preliminary duty? Venerable sirs, announce your purity. I will recite the Pātimokkha. Let all of us, being good people, listen to it carefully and bear it in mind. Whoever should have an offense, he should reveal it. If there is no offense, one should be silent. By your silence, indeed, I will know the venerable ones to be pure. Just as there is an answer for one who is asked individually, even so in an assembly of this kind is it announced up to the third time. Whatever bhikkhu, while it is being announced up to the third time, remembering an existing offense, does not reveal it, it is for him an act of intentional false speech. Venerable sirs, intentional false speech has indeed been called an obstructive factor by the Blessed One. Therefore, an existing offense should be revealed by a bhikkhu who remembers, has transgressed, and is desirous of purity; for, having been revealed, it is a comfort for him.

135. Pātimokkhanti ādimetaṃ mukhametaṃ pamukhametaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ. Tena vuccati pātimokkhanti. Āyasmantoti piyavacanametaṃ garuvacanametaṃ sagāravasappatissādhivacanametaṃ āyasmantoti. Uddisissāmīti ācikkhissāmi desessāmi paññapessāmi paṭṭhapessāmi vivarissāmi vibhajissāmi [T 1.0205] uttāniṃ karissāmi uttānī karissāmi (sī. syā.) pakāsessāmi. Tanti pātimokkhaṃ vuccati. Sabbeva santāti yāvatikā tassā parisāya therā ca navā ca majjhimā ca, ete vuccanti sabbeva santāti. Sādhukaṃ suṇomāti aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā sabbaṃ cetasā (syā. ka.) samannāharāma. Manasi karomāti ekaggacittā avikkhittacittā avisāhaṭacittā nisāmema. Yassa siyā āpattīti therassa vā navassa vā majjhimassa vā, pañcannaṃ vā āpattikkhandhānaṃ aññatarā āpatti, sattannaṃ vā āpattikkhandhānaṃ aññatarā āpatti. So āvikareyyāti so deseyya, so vivareyya, so uttāniṃ kareyya, so pakāseyya saṅghamajjhe vā gaṇamajjhe vā ekapuggale vā. Asantī nāma āpatti anajjhāpannā vā hoti, āpajjitvā vā vuṭṭhitā. Tuṇhī bhavitabbanti adhivāsetabbaṃ na byāharitabbaṃ. Parisuddhāti vedissāmīti jānissāmi dhāressāmi. Yathā kho pana paccekapuṭṭhassa veyyākaraṇaṃ hotīti yathā ekena eko puṭṭho byākareyya, evameva tassā parisāya jānitabbaṃ maṃ pucchatīti. Evarūpā nāma parisā [T 1.0206] bhikkhuparisā vuccati. Yāvatatiyaṃ anussāvitaṃ hotīti sakimpi anussāvitaṃ hoti, dutiyampi anussāvitaṃ hoti, tatiyampi anussāvitaṃ [M 0.0142] hoti. Saramānoti jānamāno sañjānamāno. Santī nāma āpatti ajjhāpannā vā hoti, āpajjitvā vā avuṭṭhitā. Nāvikareyyāti na deseyya, na vivareyya, na uttāniṃ kareyya, na pakāseyya saṅghamajjhe [P 1.0104] vā gaṇamajjhe vā ekapuggale vā. Sampajānamusāvādassa hotīti. Sampajānamusāvāde kiṃ hoti? Dukkaṭaṃ hoti. Antarāyiko dhammo vutto bhagavatāti. Kissa antarāyiko? Paṭhamassa jhānassa adhigamāya antarāyiko, dutiyassa jhānassa adhigamāya antarāyiko, tatiyassa jhānassa adhigamāya antarāyiko, catutthassa jhānassa adhigamāya antarāyiko, jhānānaṃ vimokkhānaṃ samādhīnaṃ samāpattīnaṃ nekkhammānaṃ nissaraṇānaṃ pavivekānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhigamāya [V 0.0132] antarāyiko. Tasmāti taṅkāraṇā. Saramānenāti jānamānena sañjānamānena. Visuddhāpekkhenāti vuṭṭhātukāmena visujjhitukāmena. Santī nāma āpatti ajjhāpannā vā hoti, āpajjitvā vā avuṭṭhitā. Āvikātabbāti āvikātabbā saṅghamajjhe vā gaṇamajjhe vā ekapuggale vā. Āvikatā hissa phāsu hotīti. Kissa phāsu hoti? Paṭhamassa jhānassa adhigamāya phāsu hoti, dutiyassa jhānassa adhigamāya phāsu hoti, tatiyassa jhānassa [T 1.0207] adhigamāya phāsu hoti, catutthassa jhānassa adhigamāya phāsu hoti, jhānānaṃ vimokkhānaṃ samādhīnaṃ samāpattīnaṃ nekkhammānaṃ nissaraṇānaṃ pavivekānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhigamāya phāsu hotīti.

135. The Pātimokkha is the beginning, the cause, the forefront of wholesome states. Therefore, it is called the Pātimokkha. ‘Venerable ones’ is a term of endearment, a term of respect, a term with reverence and deference—thus, ‘venerable ones.’ ‘I will recite’ means: I will declare, I will teach, I will prescribe, I will establish, I will clarify, I will analyze, I will make plain, I will make known. By ‘that,’ the Pātimokkha is meant. ‘All of us being good people’ means: however many are in that assembly—elders, newly ordained monks, and monks of middle standing—these are called ‘all of us being good people’. ‘Let us listen well’ means: let us give it importance, take it to heart, and attend with our whole mind. ‘Let us take it to heart’ means: with a concentrated mind, with an undistracted mind, with an unwearied mind, let us listen. ‘If there is an offense for anyone’ means: if there is for an elder, or for a newly ordained monk, or for a monk of middle standing, some offense among the five groups of offenses, or some offense among the seven groups of offenses. ‘He should disclose it’ means he should confess, reveal, make it plain, and make it known, whether in the midst of the Saṅgha, a group, or to an individual. An offense called ‘non-existent’ is one that has not been incurred, or one that has been incurred and then risen from. ‘One should be silent’ means: it should be endured, one should not speak. ‘I will know as pure’ means: I will know, I will remember. ‘Just as there is an explanation for one who is asked individually’ means: just as one, asked by another, would answer, so too in that assembly it should be known, “He is asking me.” An assembly of such a kind is called an assembly of monks. ‘It is announced up to the third time’ means: it is announced once, it is announced a second time, it is announced a third time. ‘Remembering’ means: knowing, recognizing. An offense called ‘existent’ is one that has been incurred, or one that has been incurred and not risen from. ‘He would not disclose it’ means: he would not confess, he would not reveal, he would not make it plain, he would not make it known, whether in the midst of the Saṅgha, or in the midst of a group, or to a single individual. ‘It is an act of intentional false speech’ means: In the case of intentional false speech, what is incurred? A dukkaṭa offense is incurred. ‘An obstructive state has been spoken of by the Blessed One.’ Obstructive to what? It is obstructive to the attainment of the first jhāna, obstructive to the attainment of the second jhāna, obstructive to the attainment of the third jhāna, obstructive to the attainment of the fourth jhāna; it is obstructive to the attainment of jhānas, liberations, concentrations, attainments, renunciations, escapes, seclusions, and wholesome states. ‘Therefore’ means: for that reason. ‘By one who is remembering’ means: by one who is knowing, by one who is recognizing. ‘By one who is aiming for purity’ means: by one who desires to rise from the offense, by one who desires to be purified. An offense called ‘existent’ is one that has been incurred, or one that has been incurred and not risen from. ‘It should be disclosed’ means: it should be disclosed, whether in the midst of the Saṅgha, a group, or to an individual. ‘For one who has made it manifest, there is ease.’ Ease for what? There is ease for the attainment of the first jhāna, there is ease for the attainment of the second jhāna, there is ease for the attainment of the third jhāna, there is ease for the attainment of the fourth jhāna; there is ease for the attainment of jhānas, liberations, concentrations, attainments, renunciations, escapes, seclusions, and wholesome states.

136. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū – bhagavatā pātimokkhuddeso anuññātoti – devasikaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, devasikaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Yo uddiseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uposathe pātimokkhaṃ uddisitunti.

136. At that time, the bhikkhus—thinking, “The recitation of the Pātimokkha has been allowed by the Blessed One”—recited the Pātimokkha daily. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha should not be recited daily. Whoever recites it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. Bhikkhus, I allow the Pātimokkha to be recited on the Uposatha day.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū – bhagavatā uposathe pātimokkhuddeso anuññātoti – pakkhassa tikkhattuṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti, cātuddase pannarase aṭṭhamiyā ca pakkhassa. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, pakkhassa tikkhattuṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Yo uddiseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sakiṃ pakkhassa cātuddase vā pannarase vā pātimokkhaṃ uddisitunti.

At that time, bhikkhus—thinking, “The Blessed One has allowed the recitation of the Pātimokkha on the Uposatha day”—recited the Pātimokkha three times a fortnight: on the fourteenth, the fifteenth, and the eighth day of the fortnight. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha should not be recited three times a fortnight. Whoever recites it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. Bhikkhus, I allow the Pātimokkha to be recited once a fortnight, either on the fourteenth or the fifteenth.”

Tena [M 0.0143] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū yathāparisāya pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti sakāya sakāya parisāya. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, yathāparisāya [P 1.0105] pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ sakāya sakāya parisāya. Yo uddiseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, samaggānaṃ uposathakammanti.

At that time the bhikkhus of the group of six recited the Pātimokkha in their own respective assemblies, according to the assembly. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha should not be recited in one’s own respective assembly, according to the assembly. Whoever recites it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. Bhikkhus, I allow the Uposatha ceremony for those who are united.”

Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘samaggānaṃ uposathakamma’nti. Kittāvatā [T 1.0208] nu kho sāmaggī hoti, yāvatā ekāvāso, udāhu sabbā pathavī”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ettāvatā sāmaggī yāvatā ekāvāsoti.

Then this thought occurred to the bhikkhus: “The Blessed One has laid down, ‘The Uposatha ceremony is for those who are united.’ To what extent, indeed, is there unity? Is it as far as a single residence, or is it the entire earth?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow that unity is to this extent: as far as a single residence.”

70. Mahākappinavatthu

70. The Story of Mahākappina

137. Tena [V 0.0133] kho pana samayena āyasmā mahākappino rājagahe viharati maddakucchimhi migadāye. Atha kho āyasmato mahākappinassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “gaccheyyaṃ vāhaṃ uposathaṃ na vā gaccheyyaṃ, gaccheyyaṃ vāhaṃ saṅghakammaṃ na vā gaccheyyaṃ, atha khvāhaṃ visuddho paramāya visuddhiyā”ti? Atha kho bhagavā āyasmato mahākappinassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva – gijjhakūṭe pabbate antarahito maddakucchimhi migadāye āyasmato mahākappinassa sammukhe pāturahosi. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Āyasmāpi kho mahākappino bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ mahākappinaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “nanu te, kappina, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – gaccheyyaṃ vāhaṃ uposathaṃ na vā gaccheyyaṃ, gaccheyyaṃ vāhaṃ saṅghakammaṃ na vā gaccheyyaṃ, atha khvāhaṃ visuddho paramāya visuddhiyā”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Tumhe ce brāhmaṇā uposathaṃ na sakkarissatha na [T 1.0209] garukarissatha na garuṃ karissatha (ka.) na mānessatha na pūjessatha, atha ko carahi uposathaṃ sakkarissati garukarissati mānessati pūjessati? Gaccha tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, uposathaṃ, mā no agamāsi. Gaccha tvaṃ saṅghakammaṃ, mā no agamāsī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā mahākappino [M 0.0144] bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ mahākappinaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva – maddakucchimhi migadāye āyasmato mahākappinassa sammukhe antarahito gijjhakūṭe pabbate pāturahosi.

137. Now at that time, Venerable Mahākappina was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Maddakucchi Deer Park. Then, while Venerable Mahākappina was in seclusion and solitude, the following thought arose in his mind: 'Should I go to the Uposatha, or should I not go? Should I go to the Saṅgha act, or should I not go? For I am purified by the supreme purity.' Then the Blessed One, knowing with his mind the thought in Venerable Mahākappina’s mind—just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm—vanished from the Vulture’s Peak and appeared before Venerable Mahākappina in the Maddakucchi Deer Park. The Blessed One sat down on a prepared seat. Venerable Mahākappina also paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Blessed One said to Venerable Mahākappina: 'Kappina, while you were in seclusion and solitude, did this thought not arise in your mind: "Should I go to the Uposatha, or should I not go? Should I go to the Saṅgha act, or should I not go? For I am purified by the supreme purity"?' 'Yes, venerable sir.' 'If you, brahmins, do not honor, respect, esteem, or venerate the Uposatha, then who else will honor, respect, esteem, or venerate the Uposatha? Go, brahmin, to the Uposatha; do not fail to go. Go to the Saṅgha act; do not fail to go.' 'Yes, venerable sir,' Venerable Mahākappina assented to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, having instructed, urged, inspired, and gladdened Venerable Mahākappina with a Dhamma talk—just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm—vanished from the presence of Venerable Mahākappina in the Maddakucchi Deer Park and reappeared on the Vulture’s Peak.

71. Sīmānujānanā

71. Permission for a Boundary

138. Atha [P 1.0106] kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘ettāvatā sāmaggī yāvatā ekāvāso’ti, kittāvatā nu kho ekāvāso hotī”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sīmaṃ sammannituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbā – paṭhamaṃ nimittā kittetabbā – pabbatanimittaṃ, pāsāṇanimittaṃ, vananimittaṃ, rukkhanimittaṃ, magganimittaṃ, vammikanimittaṃ, nadīnimittaṃ, udakanimittaṃ. Nimitte kittetvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

138. Then the bhikkhus had this thought: "The Blessed One has laid down that 'unity extends as far as a single residence.' But how far does a single residence extend?" They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "I allow, bhikkhus, the establishment of a boundary. And thus, bhikkhus, should it be established: First, the markers should be announced—a mountain marker, a rock marker, a forest marker, a tree marker, a road marker, an anthill marker, a river marker, or a water marker. Having announced the markers, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and able bhikkhu—

139. “Suṇātu [V 0.0134] me, bhante, saṅgho[T 1.0210]. Yāvatā samantā nimittā kittitā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho etehi nimittehi sīmaṃ sammanneyya samānasaṃvāsaṃ ekuposathaṃ ekūposathaṃ (ka.). Esā ñatti.

139. “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The surrounding markers have been announced. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should establish a boundary with these markers, one of common co-residence and a single Uposatha. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yāvatā samantā nimittā kittitā. Saṅgho etehi nimittehi sīmaṃ sammannati samānasaṃvāsaṃ ekuposathaṃ. Yassāyasmato khamati etehi nimittehi sīmāya sammuti sammati (syā.) samānasaṃvāsāya ekuposathāya, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya. Sammatā sīmā saṅghena etehi nimittehi samānasaṃvāsā ekuposathā. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The surrounding markers have been announced. The Saṅgha establishes a boundary with these markers, one of common co-residence and a single Uposatha. Whichever venerable one approves of the establishment of the boundary with these markers for common co-residence and a single Uposatha, let him be silent; whoever does not approve, let him speak. The boundary has been established by the Saṅgha with these markers for common co-residence and a single Uposatha. It is approved by the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.”

140. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū – bhagavatā sīmāsammuti anuññātāti – atimahatiyo sīmāyo sammannanti, catuyojanikāpi pañcayojanikāpi chayojanikāpi. Bhikkhū uposathaṃ āgacchantā uddissamānepi pātimokkhe āgacchanti, uddiṭṭhamattepi āgacchanti, antarāpi [M 0.0145] parivasanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, atimahatī sīmā sammannitabbā, catuyojanikā vā pañcayojanikā vā chayojanikā vā. Yo sammanneyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tiyojanaparamaṃ sīmaṃ sammannitunti.

140. At that time, the monks of the group of six—thinking, 'The Blessed One has permitted the establishment of a boundary'—established exceedingly large boundaries of four, five, and even six yojanas. Monks coming for the Uposatha would arrive even while the Pātimokkha was being recited, they would arrive just after it had been recited, or they would stay on the way. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, an exceedingly large boundary of four, five, or six yojanas is not to be established. Whoever should establish one incurs an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, a boundary of at most three yojanas to be established.'

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū nadīpārasīmaṃ nadīpāraṃ sīmaṃ (sī. syā.) sammannanti. Uposathaṃ āgacchantā bhikkhūpi vuyhanti, pattāpi vuyhanti[T 1.0211], cīvarānipi vuyhanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, nadīpārasīmā sammannitabbā. Yo sammanneyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yatthassa dhuvanāvā vā dhuvasetu vā, evarūpaṃ nadīpārasīmaṃ sammannitunti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six established a boundary across a river. Monks coming for the Uposatha were swept away, their bowls were swept away, and their robes were swept away. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, a boundary across a river is not to be established. Whoever should establish one incurs an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, such a boundary across a river to be established where there is a permanent boat or a permanent bridge.'

72. Uposathāgārakathā

72. The Discourse on the Uposatha Hall

141. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū anupariveṇiyaṃ pātimokkhaṃ [P 1.0107] uddisanti asaṅketena. Āgantukā bhikkhū na jānanti – “kattha vā ajjuposatho karīyissatī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, anupariveṇiyaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ asaṅketena. Yo uddiseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uposathāgāraṃ sammannitvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ, yaṃ saṅgho ākaṅkhati vihāraṃ vā aḍḍhayogaṃ vā pāsādaṃ vā hammiyaṃ vā [V 0.0135] guhaṃ vā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbaṃ. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

141. At that time, monks recited the Pātimokkha in each and every residence without an agreement. Visiting monks did not know, 'Where will the Uposatha be performed today?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, the Pātimokkha is not to be recited in each and every residence without an agreement. Whoever should recite it incurs an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, having established an Uposatha hall, to perform the Uposatha in whatever monastery, building with a single-sloped roof, storied building, terraced building, or cave the Saṅgha desires. And, monks, it is to be established in this way: the Saṅgha is to be informed by a competent and capable monk:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ vihāraṃ uposathāgāraṃ sammanneyya. Esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should establish the monastery named so-and-so as the Uposatha hall. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ vihāraṃ uposathāgāraṃ sammannati. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa vihārassa uposathāgārassa sammuti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya. Sammato saṅghena itthannāmo vihāro uposathāgāraṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha designates the monastery named so-and-so as an Uposatha hall. To whichever venerable one the designation of the monastery named so-and-so as an Uposatha hall is agreeable, he should be silent. To whom it is not agreeable, he should speak. The monastery named so-and-so has been designated by the Saṅgha as an Uposatha hall. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this.

Tena [T 1.0212] kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse dve uposathāgārāni sammatāni honti. Bhikkhū ubhayattha sannipatanti – “idha uposatho karīyissati, idha uposatho karīyissatī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[M 0.0146]. Na, bhikkhave, ekasmiṃ āvāse dve uposathāgārāni sammannitabbāni. Yo sammanneyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekaṃ samūhanitvā samuhanitvā (ka.) ekattha uposathaṃ kātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, samūhantabbaṃ. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Now at that time, in a certain residence, two Uposatha halls had been designated. The monks gathered in both places, thinking, “The Uposatha will be performed here; the Uposatha will be performed here.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, in a single residence, two Uposatha halls are not to be designated. Whoever should designate them incurs an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, having rescinded one, to perform the Uposatha in one place. And thus, monks, it should be rescinded. The Saṅgha is to be informed by a competent and capable monk:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ uposathāgāraṃ samūhaneyya samuhaneyya (ka.). Esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should rescind the Uposatha hall named so-and-so. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ uposathāgāraṃ samūhanati. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa uposathāgārassa samugghāto, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya. Samūhataṃ saṅghena itthannāmaṃ uposathāgāraṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha rescinds the Uposatha hall named so-and-so. To whichever venerable one the rescission of the Uposatha hall named so-and-so is agreeable, he should be silent. To whom it is not agreeable, he should speak. The Uposatha hall named so-and-so has been rescinded by the Saṅgha. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this.

73. Uposathappamukhānujānanā

73. Authorization of the Uposatha Precinct

142. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse atikhuddakaṃ uposathāgāraṃ sammataṃ hoti, tadahuposathe mahābhikkhusaṅgho sannipatito hoti. Bhikkhū asammatāya bhūmiyā nisinnā pātimokkhaṃ [V 0.0136] assosuṃ. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘uposathāgāraṃ sammannitvā [P 1.0108] uposatho kātabbo’ti, mayañcamhā asammatāya bhūmiyā nisinno pātimokkhaṃ assumhā, kato nu kho amhākaṃ uposatho, akato [T 1.0213] nu kho”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Sammatāya vā, bhikkhave, bhūmiyā nisinnā asammatāya vā yato pātimokkhaṃ suṇāti, katovassa uposatho. Tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho yāva mahantaṃ uposathappamukhaṃ uposathamukhaṃ (syā.) ākaṅkhati, tāva mahantaṃ uposathappamukhaṃ sammannatu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbaṃ. Paṭhamaṃ nimittā kittetabbā. Nimitte kittetvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

142. Now at that time, in a certain monastery, a very small Uposatha hall had been designated. On that Uposatha day, a great Saṅgha of monks had assembled. The monks, sitting on undesignated ground, listened to the Pātimokkha. Then this thought occurred to those monks: 'It has been laid down by the Blessed One: "The Uposatha is to be performed after having designated an Uposatha hall." We, however, have listened to the Pātimokkha while sitting on undesignated ground. Has our Uposatha been performed, or has it not been performed?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, whether sitting on designated ground or on undesignated ground, since one hears the Pātimokkha, the Uposatha is indeed performed. Therefore, monks, let the Saṅgha designate a Uposatha precinct as large as it desires. And it should be designated in this way, monks. First, the boundary markers should be announced. Having announced the boundary markers, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:'

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yāvatā samantā nimittā kittitā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho etehi nimittehi uposathappamukhaṃ sammanneyya. Esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The boundary markers have been announced all around. If the time is right for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should designate the Uposatha precinct by these boundary markers. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yāvatā samantā nimittā kittitā. Saṅgho etehi nimittehi uposathappamukhaṃ sammannati. Yassāyasmato [M 0.0147] khamati etehi nimittehi uposathappamukhassa sammuti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya. Sammataṃ saṅghena etehi nimittehi uposathappamukhaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The boundary markers have been announced all around. The Saṅgha designates the Uposatha precinct by these boundary markers. To whichever venerable one the designation of the Uposatha precinct by these boundary markers is agreeable, he should be silent. To whom it is not agreeable, he should speak. The Uposatha precinct has been designated by the Saṅgha with these boundary markers. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this.

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe navakā bhikkhū paṭhamataraṃ sannipatitvā – “na tāva therā āgacchantī”ti – pakkamiṃsu. Uposatho vikāle ahosi. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe therehi bhikkhūhi paṭhamataraṃ sannipatitunti.

At that time, in a certain monastery, on that Uposatha day, the junior monks assembled first and, thinking, “The elders have not yet come,” they departed. The Uposatha was held at the wrong time. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, I allow the elder monks to assemble first on the Uposatha day.”

Tena [T 1.0214] kho pana samayena rājagahe sambahulā āvāsā samānasīmā honti. Tattha bhikkhū vivadanti – “amhākaṃ āvāse uposatho karīyatu, amhākaṃ āvāse uposatho karīyatū”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Idha pana, bhikkhave, sambahulā āvāsā samānasīmā honti. Tattha bhikkhū vivadanti – “amhākaṃ āvāse uposatho karīyatu, amhākaṃ āvāse uposatho karīyatū”ti. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi sabbeheva ekajjhaṃ sannipatitvā uposatho kātabbo. Yattha vā pana thero bhikkhu viharati, tattha sannipatitvā uposatho kātabbo, na tveva vaggena saṅghena uposatho kātabbo. Yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, in Rājagaha, there were many monasteries with a common boundary. There, the monks disputed, saying, “Let the Uposatha be performed in our monastery; let the Uposatha be performed in our monastery!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Here, monks, where there are many monasteries with a common boundary, and the monks dispute, saying, ‘Let the Uposatha be performed in our monastery; let the Uposatha be performed in our monastery!’—in that case, monks, all those monks should assemble together and perform the Uposatha. Or else, wherever the elder monk resides, they should assemble there and perform the Uposatha. The Uposatha should certainly not be performed by a factional Sangha. Whoever should do so commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

74. Avippavāsasīmānujānanā

74. Permission for the Boundary of Non-Separation

143. Tena [P 1.0109][V 0.0137] kho pana samayena āyasmā mahākassapo andhakavindā rājagahaṃ uposathaṃ āgacchanto antarāmagge nadiṃ taranto manaṃ vūḷho ahosi, cīvarānissa tena cīvarānissa (ka.) allāni. Bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ etadavocuṃ – “kissa te, āvuso, cīvarāni allānī”ti? “Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, andhakavindā rājagahaṃ uposathaṃ āgacchanto antarāmagge nadiṃ taranto manamhi vūḷho. Tena me cīvarāni allānī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Yā sā, bhikkhave, saṅghena sīmā sammatā samānasaṃvāsā ekuposathā, saṅgho taṃ sīmaṃ ticīvarena avippavāsaṃ sammannatu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbā. Byattena [T 1.0215] bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

143. At that time, the Venerable Mahākassapa, while coming from Andhakavinda to Rājagaha for the Uposatha, was slightly carried away while crossing a river on the way, and his robes were wet. The monks said this to the Venerable Mahākassapa: “Friend, why are your robes wet?” He replied, “Friends, while coming from Andhakavinda to Rājagaha for the Uposatha, I was slightly carried away while crossing a river on the way. That is why my robes are wet.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, “Monks, that boundary which has been agreed upon by the Sangha, being of common residence and one Uposatha—the Sangha should designate that boundary as one of non-separation from the three robes. And, monks, it should be designated in this way. The Sangha should be informed by an expert and capable monk:

“Suṇātu [M 0.0148] me, bhante, saṅgho. Yā sā saṅghena sīmā sammatā samānasaṃvāsā ekuposathā, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ saṅgho taṃ sīmaṃ ticīvarena avippavāsaṃ sammanneyya. Esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha listen to me. That boundary which has been agreed upon by the Sangha for common residence and a single Uposatha—if it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should designate that boundary for non-separation from the three robes. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yā sā saṅghena sīmā sammatā samānasaṃvāsā ekuposathā, saṅgho taṃ sīmaṃ ticīvarena avippavāsaṃ sammannati. Yassāyasmato khamati etissā sīmāya ticīvarena avippavāsāya avippavāsassa (syā.) sammuti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya. Sammatā sā sīmā saṅghena ticīvarena avippavāsā avippavāso (syā.). Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha listen to me. That boundary which has been agreed upon by the Sangha for common residence and a single Uposatha—the Sangha designates that boundary for non-separation from the three robes. To whichever venerable one the designation of this boundary for non-separation from the three robes is agreeable, he should be silent. To whom it is not agreeable, he should speak. This boundary has been designated by the Sangha for non-separation from the three robes. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold it.

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū bhagavatā ticīvarena avippavāsasammuti anuññātāti antaraghare cīvarāni nikkhipanti. Tāni cīvarāni nassantipi ḍayhantipi undūrehipi khajjanti. Bhikkhū duccoḷā honti lūkhacīvarā. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “kissa tumhe, āvuso, duccoḷā lūkhacīvarā”ti? “Idha mayaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā ticīvarena avippavāsasammuti anuññātāti antaraghare cīvarāni nikkhipimhā[T 1.0216]. Tāni cīvarāni naṭṭhānipi daḍḍhānipi, undūrehipi khāyitāni, tena mayaṃ duccoḷā lūkhacīvarā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Yā sā, bhikkhave, saṅghena sīmā sammatā samānasaṃvāsā ekuposathā, saṅgho taṃ sīmaṃ ticīvarena avippavāsaṃ sammannatu, ṭhapetvā gāmañca gāmūpacārañca. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbā. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

At that time, the monks, thinking, 'The Blessed One has permitted the designation of non-separation from the three robes,' placed their robes inside the village. Those robes were lost, were burned, and were eaten by rats. The monks came to have poor cloths and shabby robes. The monks said thus: 'Friends, why do you have poor cloths and shabby robes?' 'Friends, thinking, "The Blessed One has permitted the designation of non-separation from the three robes," we placed our robes inside the village. Those robes were lost, were burned, and were eaten by rats. Therefore, we have poor cloths and shabby robes.' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, that boundary which has been agreed upon by the Sangha for common residence and a single Uposatha—let the Sangha designate that boundary for non-separation from the three robes, excluding the village and the village precincts. And, monks, it should be designated in this way: The Sangha should be informed by an expert and capable monk:'

144. “Suṇātu [V 0.0138] me, bhante, saṅgho. Yā sā saṅghena sīmā sammatā samānasaṃvāsā ekuposathā yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho taṃ sīmaṃ ticīvarena avippavāsaṃ sammanneyya, ṭhapetvā gāmañca [P 1.0110] gāmūpacārañca. Esā ñatti.

144. Venerable sirs, may the Sangha listen to me. That boundary which has been agreed upon by the Sangha for common residence and a single Uposatha—if it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should designate that boundary for non-separation from the three robes, excluding the village and the village precincts. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yā sā saṅghena sīmā sammatā samānasaṃvāsā ekuposathā, saṅgho taṃ sīmaṃ ticīvarena avippavāsaṃ sammannati, ṭhapetvā gāmañca gāmūpacārañca. Yassāyasmato khamati etissā sīmāya ticīvarena avippavāsāya avippavāsassa (syā.) sammuti, ṭhapetvā gāmañca gāmūpacārañca, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya. Sammatā sā [M 0.0149] sīmā saṅghena ticīvarena avippavāsā avippavāso (syā.), ṭhapetvā gāmañca gāmūpacārañca. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha listen to me. That boundary which has been agreed upon by the Sangha for common residence and a single Uposatha—the Sangha designates that boundary for non-separation from the three robes, excluding the village and its precincts. To whichever venerable one the designation of this boundary for non-separation from the three robes, excluding the village and its precincts, is agreeable, he should be silent. To whom it is not agreeable, he should speak. This boundary has been designated by the Sangha for non-separation from the three robes, excluding the village and its precincts. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold it.

75. Sīmāsamūhanana

75. The Rescinding of a Boundary

“Sīmaṃ, bhikkhave, sammannantena paṭhamaṃ samānasaṃvāsasīmā samānasaṃvāsā sīmā (syā.) sammannitabbā[T 1.0217], pacchā ticīvarena avippavāso sammannitabbo. Sīmaṃ, bhikkhave, samūhanantena paṭhamaṃ ticīvarena avippavāso samūhantabbo, pacchā samānasaṃvāsasīmā samūhantabbā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, ticīvarena avippavāso samūhantabbo. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Monks, when designating a boundary, first the boundary for common residence should be designated, and afterward, the non-separation from the three robes should be designated. Monks, when rescinding a boundary, first the non-separation from the three robes should be rescinded, and afterward, the boundary for common residence should be rescinded. And in this way, monks, should the non-separation from the three robes be rescinded. An expert and capable monk should inform the Sangha:

145. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yo so saṅghena ticīvarena avippavāso sammato, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho taṃ ticīvarena avippavāsaṃ samūhaneyya. Esā ñatti.

145. Venerable sirs, may the Sangha listen to me. That non-separation from the three robes which was designated by the Sangha—if it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should rescind that non-separation from the three robes. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yo so saṅghena ticīvarena avippavāso sammato, saṅgho taṃ ticīvarena avippavāsaṃ samūhanati. Yassāyasmato khamati etassa ticīvarena avippavāsassa samugghāto, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya. Samūhato so saṅghena ticīvarena avippavāso. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. Regarding that place of non-separation from the three robes which has been designated by the Sangha, the Sangha now rescinds that place of non-separation from the three robes. If the rescinding of this place of non-separation from the three robes is agreeable to the venerable ones, let them be silent. If it is not agreeable, let them speak. That place of non-separation from the three robes has been rescinded by the Sangha. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.

Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sīmā samānasaṃvāsā sīmā (syā.). Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

And in this way, monks, should a boundary be rescinded. A competent and capable monk should inform the Sangha:

146. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yā sā saṅghena sīmā sammatā samānasaṃvāsā ekuposathā[V 0.0139], yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho taṃ sīmaṃ samūhaneyya samānasaṃvāsaṃ ekuposathaṃ. Esā ñatti.

146. Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. Regarding that boundary which has been established by the Sangha for common communion and a single Uposatha—if it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should revoke that boundary for common communion and a single Uposatha. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yā sā saṅghena sīmā sammatā samānasaṃvāsā ekuposathā, saṅgho taṃ [T 1.0218] sīmaṃ samūhanati samānasaṃvāsaṃ ekuposathaṃ. Yassāyasmato khamati etissā sīmāya samānasaṃvāsāya ekuposathāya samugghāto, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya. Samūhatā sā sīmā saṅghena samānasaṃvāsā ekuposathā. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. Regarding the boundary that has been established by the Sangha for common communion and a single Uposatha—the Sangha revokes that boundary for common communion and a single Uposatha. If the revocation of this boundary for common communion and a single Uposatha is agreeable to any venerable one, let him be silent; if it is not agreeable, let him speak. That boundary for common communion and a single Uposatha has been revoked by the Sangha. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.

76. Gāmasīmādi

76. Village Boundary, etc.

147. Asammatāya[M 0.0150], bhikkhave, sīmāya aṭṭhapitāya, yaṃ gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā upanissāya viharati, yā tassa vā gāmassa gāmasīmā, nigamassa [T 1.0219] vā nigamasīmā, ayaṃ tattha samānasaṃvāsā [P 1.0111] ekuposathā. Agāmake ce, bhikkhave, araññe samantā sattabbhantarā, ayaṃ tattha samānasaṃvāsā ekuposathā. Sabbā, bhikkhave, nadī asīmā; sabbo samuddo asīmo; sabbo jātassaro asīmo. Nadiyā vā, bhikkhave, samudde vā jātassare vā yaṃ majjhimassa purisassa samantā udakukkhepā, ayaṃ tattha samānasaṃvāsā ekuposathāti.

147. Monks, when a boundary has not been designated or established, if one dwells depending on a village or a town, then whatever is the village boundary of that village, or the town boundary of that town, that is the boundary there for common communion and a single Uposatha. And if, monks, in a forest without a nearby village, there is an area of seven abbhantaras all around, that is the boundary there for common communion and a single Uposatha. Every river, monks, is without a boundary; every ocean is without a boundary; every natural lake is without a boundary. In a river, monks, or in an ocean, or in a natural lake, the area all around that is encompassed by one throw of water from a man of medium strength, that is the boundary there for common communion and a single Uposatha.

148. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sīmāya sīmaṃ sambhindanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Yesaṃ, bhikkhave, sīmā paṭhamaṃ sammatā tesaṃ taṃ kammaṃ dhammikaṃ akuppaṃ ṭhānārahaṃ. Yesaṃ, bhikkhave, sīmā pacchā sammatā tesaṃ taṃ kammaṃ adhammikaṃ kuppaṃ aṭṭhānārahaṃ. Na, bhikkhave, sīmāya sīmā sambhinditabbā. Yo sambhindeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

148. At that time, the monks of the group of six were joining one boundary to another. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. Monks, for those whose boundary was established first, that formal act is lawful, unshakeable, and fit to stand. Monks, for those whose boundary was established later, that formal act is unlawful, shakeable, and unfit to stand. Monks, a boundary should not be joined to another boundary. Whoever should join them, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sīmāya sīmaṃ ajjhottharanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Yesaṃ, bhikkhave, sīmā paṭhamaṃ sammatā tesaṃ taṃ kammaṃ dhammikaṃ akuppaṃ ṭhānārahaṃ. Yesaṃ, bhikkhave, sīmā pacchā sammatā tesaṃ taṃ kammaṃ adhammikaṃ kuppaṃ aṭṭhānārahaṃ. Na, bhikkhave, sīmāya sīmā ajjhottharitabbā. Yo ajjhotthareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sīmaṃ sammannantena sīmantarikaṃ ṭhapetvā sīmaṃ sammannitunti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six were overlapping another's boundary with their own. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. Monks, for those whose boundary was established first, that formal act of theirs is lawful, unshakeable, and fit to stand. For those whose boundary was established later, that formal act of theirs is unlawful, shakeable, and unfit to stand. Monks, a boundary should not be overlapped by another boundary. Whoever should overlap it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, for one establishing a boundary to establish it after having set aside an interval between boundaries.

77. Uposathabhedādi

77. Divisions of the Uposatha, etc.

149. Atha [V 0.0140] kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kati nu kho uposathā”ti? Bhagavato [T 1.0220] etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Dveme, bhikkhave, uposathā – cātuddasiko ca pannarasiko ca. Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve uposathāti.

149. Then this thought occurred to the monks: “How many Uposathas are there?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, there are these two Uposathas: the fourteenth-day and the fifteenth-day. These, monks, are the two Uposathas.”

Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kati nu kho uposathakammānī”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, uposathakammāni [M 0.0151] – adhammena vaggaṃ uposathakammaṃ, adhammena samaggaṃ uposathakammaṃ, dhammena vaggaṃ uposathakammaṃ, dhammena samaggaṃ uposathakammanti. Tatra, bhikkhave, yadidaṃ adhammena vaggaṃ uposathakammaṃ, na, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ uposathakammaṃ, kātabbaṃ. Na ca mayā evarūpaṃ uposathakammaṃ anuññātaṃ. Tatra, bhikkhave, yadidaṃ adhammena samaggaṃ uposathakammaṃ, na, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ [P 1.0112] uposathakammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Na ca mayā evarūpaṃ uposathakammaṃ anuññātaṃ. Tatra, bhikkhave, yadidaṃ dhammena vaggaṃ uposathakammaṃ, na, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ uposathakammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Na ca mayā evarūpaṃ uposathakammaṃ anuññātaṃ. Tatra, bhikkhave, yadidaṃ dhammena samaggaṃ uposathakammaṃ, evarūpaṃ, bhikkhave, uposathakammaṃ kātabbaṃ, evarūpañca mayā uposathakammaṃ anuññātaṃ. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ uposathakammaṃ karissāma yadidaṃ dhammena samagganti – evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbanti.

Then this thought occurred to the monks: 'How many Uposatha acts are there?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, there are these four Uposatha acts: an unlawful, divisive Uposatha act; an unlawful, harmonious Uposatha act; a lawful, divisive Uposatha act; and a lawful, harmonious Uposatha act. Among these, monks, as to this unlawful, divisive Uposatha act—monks, such an Uposatha act should not be performed. And such an Uposatha act has not been allowed by me. Among these, monks, as to this unlawful, harmonious Uposatha act—monks, such an Uposatha act should not be performed. And such an Uposatha act has not been allowed by me. Among these, monks, as to this lawful, divisive Uposatha act—monks, such an Uposatha act should not be performed. And such an Uposatha act has not been allowed by me. Among these, monks, as to this lawful, harmonious Uposatha act—monks, such an Uposatha act should be performed, and such an Uposatha act has been allowed by me. Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: "We shall perform such an Uposatha act that is lawful and harmonious."

78. Saṃkhittena pātimokkhuddesādi

78. The Brief Recitation of the Pātimokkha, etc.

150. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kati nu kho pātimokkhuddesā”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Pañcime, bhikkhave, pātimokkhuddesā – nidānaṃ uddisitvā avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbaṃ. Ayaṃ [T 1.0221] paṭhamo pātimokkhuddeso. Nidānaṃ uddisitvā cattāri pārājikāni uddisitvā avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbaṃ. Ayaṃ dutiyo pātimokkhuddeso. Nidānaṃ uddisitvā cattāri pārājikāni uddisitvā terasa saṅghādisese uddisitvā avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbaṃ. Ayaṃ tatiyo pātimokkhuddeso. Nidānaṃ uddisitvā cattāri pārājikāni uddisitvā terasa saṅghādisese uddisitvā dve aniyate uddisitvā avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbaṃ. Ayaṃ catuttho pātimokkhuddeso. Vitthāreneva pañcamo. Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca pātimokkhuddesāti.

150. Then this thought arose in the monks: 'How many recitations of the Pātimokkha are there?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, there are these five recitations of the Pātimokkha: having recited the introduction, the remainder should be announced with the word 'heard'. This is the first recitation of the Pātimokkha. Having recited the introduction and having recited the four Pārājikas, the remainder should be announced with the word 'heard'. This is the second recitation of the Pātimokkha. Having recited the introduction, having recited the four Pārājikas, and having recited the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, the remainder should be announced with the word 'heard'. This is the third recitation of the Pātimokkha. Having recited the introduction, having recited the four Pārājikas, having recited the thirteen Saṅghādisesas, and having recited the two Aniyatas, the remainder should be announced with the word 'heard'. This is the fourth recitation of the Pātimokkha. The fifth is in full. These, monks, are the five recitations of the Pātimokkha.'

Tena [V 0.0141] kho pana samayena bhikkhū – bhagavatā saṃkhittena pātimokkhuddeso anuññātoti – sabbakālaṃ saṃkhittena pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, saṃkhittena pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Yo uddiseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Now at that time, the monks, thinking, 'The recitation of the Pātimokkha in brief has been allowed by the Blessed One,' recited the Pātimokkha in brief at all times. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, the Pātimokkha is not to be recited in brief. Whoever should recite it, commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena [M 0.0152] kho pana samayena kosalesu janapade aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe savarabhayaṃ saṃcarabhayaṃ (syā.) ahosi. Bhikkhū nāsakkhiṃsu vitthārena pātimokkhaṃ uddisituṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sati antarāye saṃkhittena pātimokkhaṃ uddisitunti.

Now at that time, in a certain monastery in the Kosala country, on that Uposatha day, there arose a danger from savages. The monks were not able to recite the Pātimokkha in full. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, monks, when there is a danger, to recite the Pātimokkha in brief.'

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū [T 1.0222] asatipi antarāye saṃkhittena pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, asati antarāye saṃkhittena pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Yo uddiseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sati antarāye saṃkhittena pātimokkhaṃ uddisituṃ. Tatrime antarāyā – rājantarāyo, corantarāyo, agyantarāyo, udakantarāyo, manussantarāyo, amanussantarāyo[P 1.0113], vāḷantarāyo, sarīsapantarāyo, jīvitantarāyo, brahmacariyantarāyoti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, evarūpesu antarāyesu saṃkhittena pātimokkhaṃ uddisituṃ, asati antarāye vitthārenāti.

At that time the group-of-six monks were reciting the Pātimokkha in brief even when there was no danger. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "Monks, the Pātimokkha should not be recited in brief when there is no danger. Whoever should recite it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, that when there is danger, the Pātimokkha may be recited in brief. These are the dangers: danger from a king, danger from thieves, danger from fire, danger from water, danger from humans, danger from non-humans, danger from wild animals, danger from reptiles, danger to life, danger to the holy life. I allow, monks, that in such dangers, the Pātimokkha may be recited in brief; when there is no danger, it should be recited in full."

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū saṅghamajjhe anajjhiṭṭhā dhammaṃ bhāsanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, saṅghamajjhe anajjhiṭṭhena dhammo bhāsitabbo. Yo bhāseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, therena bhikkhunā sāmaṃ vā dhammaṃ bhāsituṃ paraṃ vā ajjhesitunti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma in the midst of the Sangha without being requested. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "Monks, the Dhamma should not be taught in the midst of the Sangha by one who has not been requested. Whoever should teach it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, that a senior monk may either teach the Dhamma himself or request another to do so."

79. Vinayapucchanakathā

79. The Section on Questioning the Vinaya

151. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū saṅghamajjhe asammatā vinayaṃ pucchanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, saṅghamajjhe asammatena vinayo pucchitabbo. Yo puccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghamajjhe sammatena vinayaṃ pucchituṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbo – attanā vā attanāva (syā.) attānaṃ sammannitabbaṃ, parena vā paro sammannitabbo. Kathañca [T 1.0223] attanāva attānaṃ sammannitabbaṃ? Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

151. At that time, the group-of-six monks, being unauthorized, questioned the Vinaya in the midst of the Sangha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "Monks, the Vinaya should not be questioned in the midst of the Sangha by one who is unauthorized. Whoever should question it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, that one who is authorized may question the Vinaya in the midst of the Sangha. And thus, monks, should one be authorized: either one should authorize oneself, or another should authorize another. And how should one authorize oneself? A competent and capable monk should inform the Sangha:

“Suṇātu [M 0.0153][V 0.0142] me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ itthannāmaṃ vinayaṃ puccheyya”nti. Evaṃ attanāva attānaṃ sammannitabbaṃ.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, I would question the venerable so-and-so about the Vinaya.” Thus should one authorize oneself.

Kathañca parena paro sammannitabbo? Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

And how should another authorize another? A competent and capable monk should inform the Sangha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, itthannāmo itthannāmaṃ vinayaṃ puccheyyā”ti. Evaṃ parena paro sammannitabboti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, let so-and-so question so-and-so about the Vinaya.” Thus should another authorize another.

Tena kho pana samayena pesalā bhikkhū saṅghamajjhe sammatā vinayaṃ pucchanti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū labhanti āghātaṃ, labhanti appaccayaṃ, vadhena tajjenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghamajjhe sammatenapi parisaṃ oloketvā puggalaṃ tulayitvā vinayaṃ pucchitunti.

At that time, conscientious monks, authorized in the midst of the Sangha, questioned the Vinaya. The group-of-six monks conceived resentment, conceived displeasure, and threatened them with violence. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, that even one authorized in the midst of the Sangha, after surveying the assembly and weighing the individual, may question the Vinaya.”

80. Vinayavissajjanakathā

80. The Section on Answering the Vinaya

152. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū saṅghamajjhe asammatā vinayaṃ vissajjenti vissajjanti (ka.). Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, saṅghamajjhe asammatena vinayo vissajjetabbo. Yo vissajjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghamajjhe sammatena vinayaṃ vissajjetuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbaṃ. Attanā vā attanāva (syā.) attānaṃ sammannitabbaṃ, parena vā paro sammannitabbo. Kathañca [P 1.0114] attanāva attānaṃ sammannitabbaṃ? Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

152. At that time, the group-of-six monks, unauthorized in the midst of the Sangha, answered questions on the Vinaya. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, the Vinaya should not be answered in the midst of the Sangha by one who is unauthorized. Whoever answers commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, that the Vinaya may be answered in the midst of the Sangha by one who is authorized. And thus, monks, should one be authorized: either one should authorize oneself, or another should authorize another. And how should one authorize oneself? A competent and capable monk should inform the Sangha:”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, ahaṃ [T 1.0224] itthannāmena vinayaṃ puṭṭho vissajjeyya”nti. Evaṃ attanāva attānaṃ sammannitabbaṃ.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, I, having been questioned about the Vinaya by so-and-so, would answer.” Thus should one authorize oneself.

Kathañca parena paro sammannitabbo? Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

And how should another authorize another? A competent and capable monk should inform the Sangha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, itthannāmo itthannāmena vinayaṃ puṭṭho vissajjeyyā”ti. Evaṃ parena paro sammannitabboti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, so-and-so, having been questioned on the Discipline by so-and-so, should answer.” Thus should one person authorize another.

Tena [M 0.0154][V 0.0143] kho pana samayena pesalā bhikkhū saṅghamajjhe sammatā vinayaṃ vissajjenti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū labhanti āghātaṃ, labhanti appaccayaṃ, vadhena tajjenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghamajjhe sammatenapi parisaṃ oloketvā puggalaṃ tulayitvā vinayaṃ vissajjetunti.

At that time, virtuous monks, authorized in the midst of the Saṅgha, answered questions on the Discipline. The group-of-six monks conceived resentment, conceived displeasure, and threatened them with violence. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "I allow, monks, that even one authorized in the midst of the Saṅgha, after surveying the assembly and assessing the individual, may answer questions on the Discipline."

81. Codanākathā

81. The Discourse on Accusation

153. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū anokāsakataṃ bhikkhuṃ āpattiyā codenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, anokāsakato bhikkhu āpattiyā codetabbo. Yo codeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, okāsaṃ kārāpetvā āpattiyā codetuṃ – karotu āyasmā okāsaṃ, ahaṃ taṃ vattukāmoti.

153. At that time, the group-of-six monks accused a monk of an offense without asking for permission. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "Monks, a monk should not be accused of an offense without first being asked for permission. Whoever does so commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, that after obtaining permission, one may accuse another of an offense, saying: ‘Venerable, grant me permission, I wish to speak to you.’”

Tena kho pana samayena pesalā bhikkhū chabbaggiye bhikkhū okāsaṃ kārāpetvā āpattiyā codenti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū labhanti āghātaṃ, labhanti appaccayaṃ, vadhena tajjenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, katepi okāse puggalaṃ tulayitvā āpattiyā codetunti.

At that time, virtuous monks, after obtaining permission, accused the group-of-six monks of an offense. The group-of-six monks became resentful, became displeased, and threatened them with violence. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "I allow, monks, even after permission has been granted, to accuse a person of an offense after assessing the individual."

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā [T 1.0225] bhikkhū – puramhākaṃ pesalā bhikkhū okāsaṃ kārāpentīti – paṭikacceva suddhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anāpattikānaṃ avatthusmiṃ akāraṇe okāsaṃ kārāpenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, suddhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anāpattikānaṃ avatthusmiṃ akāraṇe okāso kārāpetabbo. Yo kārāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, puggalaṃ tulayitvā okāsaṃ kātu kārāpetuṃ (syā.) nti.

At that time the group-of-six monks, thinking, "The virtuous monks ask permission from us beforehand," would preemptively ask for permission from monks who were pure and without offense, without basis and without reason. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "Monks, permission should not be sought from monks who are pure and without offense, without basis and without reason. Whoever should seek it, commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, to grant permission after assessing the person."

82. Adhammakammapaṭikkosanādi

82. Protesting Unlawful Acts, etc.

154. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū saṅghamajjhe adhammakammaṃ karonti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, adhammakammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti. Karontiyeva adhammakammaṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[P 1.0115]. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, adhammakamme kayiramāne paṭikkositunti.

154. At that time, the group-of-six monks performed an unlawful act in the midst of the Saṅgha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "Monks, an unlawful act is not to be performed. Whoever should perform one, commits an offense of wrong conduct." They continued to perform the unlawful act. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "I allow, monks, that when an unlawful act is being performed, it is to be protested against."

Tena [M 0.0155][V 0.0144] kho pana samayena pesalā bhikkhū chabbaggiyehi bhikkhūhi adhammakamme kayiramāne paṭikkosanti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū labhanti āghātaṃ, labhanti appaccayaṃ, vadhena tajjenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, diṭṭhimpi āvikātunti. Tesaṃyeva santike diṭṭhiṃ āvikaronti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū labhanti āghātaṃ, labhanti appaccayaṃ, vadhena tajjenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, catūhi pañcahi paṭikkosituṃ, dvīhi tīhi diṭṭhiṃ āvikātuṃ, ekena adhiṭṭhātuṃ – ‘na metaṃ khamatī’ti.

At that time, virtuous monks protested when an unlawful act was being performed by the group-of-six monks. The group-of-six monks conceived animosity, conceived displeasure, and threatened them with violence. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "I allow, monks, to make one's view known." They made their view known in the presence of those very monks. The group-of-six monks conceived animosity, conceived displeasure, and threatened them with violence. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "I allow, monks, for four or five to protest, for two or three to make their view known, and for one to make a formal resolution, saying: ‘This act is not agreeable to me.’”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū saṅghamajjhe pātimokkhaṃ [T 1.0226] uddisamānā sañcicca na sāventi. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, pātimokkhuddesakena sañcicca na sāvetabbaṃ. Yo na sāveyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks, while reciting the Pātimokkha in the midst of the Saṅgha, deliberately did not make it audible. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "Monks, a Pātimokkha reciter should not deliberately recite it inaudibly. Whoever does not make it audible, commits an offense of wrong conduct."

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā udāyī saṅghassa pātimokkhuddesako hoti kākassarako. Atha kho āyasmato udāyissa etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘pātimokkhuddesakena sāvetabba’nti, ahañcamhi kākassarako, kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pātimokkhuddesakena vāyamituṃ – ‘kathaṃ sāveyya’nti. Vāyamantassa anāpattīti.

At that time, the Venerable Udāyī was the Saṅgha's Pātimokkha reciter, and he had a voice like a crow. Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Udāyī: 'It has been laid down by the Blessed One, "The Pātimokkha reciter must make it audible." But I have a voice like a crow. How then should I proceed?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "I allow, monks, the Pātimokkha reciter to strive, thinking: 'How might I make it audible?' For one who is striving, there is no offense."

Tena kho pana samayena devadatto sagahaṭṭhāya parisāya pātimokkhaṃ uddisati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, sagahaṭṭhāya parisāya pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Yo uddiseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, Devadatta was reciting the Pātimokkha to an assembly that included laypeople. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "Monks, the Pātimokkha should not be recited to an assembly that includes laypeople. Whoever does recite it, commits an offense of wrong conduct."

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū saṅghamajjhe anajjhiṭṭhā pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, saṅghamajjhe anajjhiṭṭhena pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Yo uddiseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, therādhikaṃ therādheyyaṃ (aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pāṭhantaraṃ) pātimokkhanti.

At that time the group-of-six monks recited the Pātimokkha in the midst of the Saṅgha without being requested. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "Monks, the Pātimokkha should not be recited in the midst of the Saṅgha by one who has not been requested. Whoever recites it commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, that the Pātimokkha pertains to the senior monk."

Aññatitthiyabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito paṭhamo ekādasamo (ka.).

The First Chapter on Other Sects is finished.

83. Pātimokkhuddesakaajjhesanādi

83. Requesting the Pātimokkha Reciter, etc.

155. Atha [M 0.0156][V 0.0145][T 1.0227] kho bhagavā rājagahe yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena codanāvatthu tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena codanāvatthu tadavasari. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse sambahulā bhikkhū viharanti[P 1.0116]. Tattha thero bhikkhu bālo hoti abyatto. So na jānāti uposathaṃ vā uposathakammaṃ vā, pātimokkhaṃ vā pātimokkhuddesaṃ vā. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘therādhikaṃ pātimokkha’nti, ayañca amhākaṃ thero bālo abyatto, na jānāti uposathaṃ vā uposathakammaṃ vā, pātimokkhaṃ vā pātimokkhuddesaṃ vā. Kathaṃ nu kho amhehi paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yo tattha bhikkhu byatto paṭibalo tassādheyyaṃ pātimokkhanti.

155. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Rājagaha for as long as he pleased, set out on a journey toward Codanāvatthu. Traveling in stages, he arrived at Codanāvatthu. At that time, in a certain monastery, many monks were residing. There, the senior monk was ignorant and unskilled. He did not know the Uposatha or the Uposatha procedure, the Pātimokkha or the recitation of the Pātimokkha. Then this thought occurred to those monks: “The Blessed One has laid down the rule, ‘The Pātimokkha pertains to the senior monk,’ but this senior monk of ours is ignorant and unskilled; he does not know the Uposatha or the Uposatha procedure, the Pātimokkha or the recitation of the Pātimokkha. How, indeed, should we proceed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, that the Pātimokkha pertains to whichever monk there is who is skilled and capable.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā bhikkhū viharanti bālā abyattā. Te na jānanti uposathaṃ vā uposathakammaṃ vā, pātimokkhaṃ vā pātimokkhuddesaṃ vā. Te theraṃ ajjhesiṃsu – “uddisatu, bhante, thero pātimokkha”nti. So evamāha – “na me, āvuso, vattatī”ti. Dutiyaṃ theraṃ ajjhesiṃsu – “uddisatu, bhante, thero pātimokkha”nti. Sopi evamāha – “na me, āvuso, vattatī”ti. Tatiyaṃ theraṃ ajjhesiṃsu – “uddisatu[T 1.0228], bhante, thero pātimokkha”nti. Sopi evamāha – “na me, āvuso, vattatī”ti. Eteneva upāyena yāva saṅghanavakaṃ ajjhesiṃsu – “uddisatu āyasmā pātimokkha”nti. Sopi evamāha – “na me, bhante, vattatī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

At that time, in a certain monastery, on that Uposatha day, many monks who were ignorant and unskilled were staying. They did not know the Uposatha or the Uposatha procedure, the Pātimokkha or the recitation of the Pātimokkha. They requested the senior monk, saying, “Venerable sir, may the senior monk recite the Pātimokkha.” He said thus, “Friends, I am not fluent in it.” They requested the second senior monk, saying, “Venerable sir, may the senior monk recite the Pātimokkha.” He also said thus, “Friends, I am not fluent in it.” They requested the third senior monk, saying, “Venerable sir, may the senior monk recite the Pātimokkha.” He also said thus, “Friends, I am not fluent in it.” In this very way, they requested down to the most junior monk of the Saṅgha, saying, “Venerable one, may you recite the Pātimokkha.” He also said thus, “Venerable sirs, I am not fluent in it.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā bhikkhū viharanti bālā abyattā. Te na jānanti uposathaṃ vā uposathakammaṃ vā, pātimokkhaṃ vā pātimokkhuddesaṃ vā. Te theraṃ ajjhesanti – “uddisatu, bhante, thero pātimokkha”nti. So evaṃ vadeti – “na me, āvuso, vattatī”ti. Dutiyaṃ theraṃ ajjhesanti – “uddisatu, bhante, thero pātimokkha”nti.
