Sopi evaṃ vadeti – “na me, āvuso, vattatī”ti. Tatiyaṃ [M 0.0157] theraṃ ajjhesanti – “uddisatu, bhante, thero pātimokkha”nti. Sopi evaṃ vadeti – “na me, āvuso, vattatī”ti. Eteneva upāyena yāva saṅghanavakaṃ ajjhesanti – “uddisatu āyasmā pātimokkha”nti. Sopi evaṃ vadeti – “na me, bhante, vattatī”ti. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi [V 0.0146] eko bhikkhu sāmantā āvāsā sajjukaṃ pāhetabbo – gacchāvuso, saṃkhittena vā vitthārena vā pātimokkhaṃ pariyāpuṇitvāna āgacchāhīti.

Here in this Dispensation, monks, in a certain monastery, on that Uposatha day, many monks who are ignorant and unskilled are staying. They do not know the Uposatha or the Uposatha procedure, the Pātimokkha or the recitation of the Pātimokkha. They request the senior monk, saying, ‘Venerable sir, may the senior monk recite the Pātimokkha.’ He says thus, ‘Friends, I am not fluent in it.’ They request the second senior monk, saying, ‘Venerable sir, may the senior monk recite the Pātimokkha.’ He also says thus, ‘Friends, I am not fluent in it.’ They request the third senior monk, saying, ‘Venerable sir, may the senior monk recite the Pātimokkha.’ He also says thus, ‘Friends, I am not fluent in it.’ In this very way, they request down to the most junior monk of the Saṅgha, saying, ‘Venerable one, may you recite the Pātimokkha.’ He also says thus, ‘Venerable sirs, I am not fluent in it.’ Monks, those monks should send one monk to a nearby monastery on the same day, with the instruction: ‘Go, friend, learn the Pātimokkha either in brief or in detail, and then come back.’”

Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho pāhetabbo”ti? Bhagavato [T 1.0229] etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, therena bhikkhunā navaṃ bhikkhuṃ āṇāpetunti. Therena āṇattā navā bhikkhū na gacchanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, therena [P 1.0117] āṇattena agilānena na gantabbaṃ. Yo na gaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Then the monks had this thought: “Now, by whom should one be sent?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, monks, that a senior monk should instruct a junior monk.” Instructed by the senior monk, the junior monks did not go. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, one who is not ill should not fail to go when instructed by a senior monk. Whoever should fail to go incurs an offense of wrong-doing.”

84. Pakkhagaṇanādiuggahaṇānujānanā

84. The Allowance for Learning the Counting of the Fortnight, etc.

156. Atha kho bhagavā codanāvatthusmiṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā punadeva rājagahaṃ paccāgañchi.

156. Then the Blessed One, having stayed in Codanāvatthu for as long as he wished, returned once again to Rājagaha.

Tena kho pana samayena manussā bhikkhū piṇḍāya carante pucchanti – “katimī, bhante, pakkhassā”ti? Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “na kho mayaṃ, āvuso, jānāmā”ti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “pakkhagaṇanamattamampime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā na jānanti, kiṃ panime aññaṃ kiñci kalyāṇaṃ jānissantī”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pakkhagaṇanaṃ uggahetunti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho pakkhagaṇanā uggahetabbā”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sabbeheva pakkhagaṇanaṃ uggahetunti.

At that time, people asked the monks who were going for alms, “Venerable sirs, what day of the fortnight is it?” The monks replied, “Friends, we do not know.” The people complained, criticized, and disparaged, saying, “These Sakyan ascetics do not even know the mere counting of the fortnight; what other good thing will they know?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow you to learn the counting of the fortnight.” Then the monks had this thought: “By whom, now, should the counting of the fortnight be learned?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow that the counting of the fortnight be learned by all.”

157. Tena kho pana samayena manussā bhikkhū piṇḍāya carante pucchanti – “kīvatikā, bhante, bhikkhū”ti? Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “na kho mayaṃ, āvuso, jānāmā”ti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “aññamaññampime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā na jānanti, kiṃ panime aññaṃ kiñci [T 1.0230] kalyāṇaṃ jānissantī”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhū gaṇetunti.

157. At that time, people asked the monks who were going for alms, “Venerable sirs, how many monks are there?” The monks replied, “Friends, we do not know.” The people complained, criticized, and disparaged, saying, “These Sakyan ascetics do not even know one another; what other good thing will they know?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow you to count the monks.”

Atha [M 0.0158] kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kadā nu kho bhikkhū gaṇetabbā”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe nāmaggena nāmamattena (syā.), gaṇamaggena (ka.) gaṇetuṃ, salākaṃ vā gāhetunti.

Then this thought occurred to the monks: 'When, indeed, should the monks be counted?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, on that Uposatha day, I allow you to count by name or to take a ticket.'

158. Tena [V 0.0147] kho pana samayena bhikkhū ajānantā ajjuposathoti dūraṃ gāmaṃ piṇḍāya caranti. Te uddissamānepi pātimokkhe āgacchanti, uddiṭṭhamattepi āgacchanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ārocetuṃ ‘ajjuposatho’ti.

158. Now at that time, monks, not knowing that it was the Uposatha day, would go to a distant village for alms. They would arrive while the Pātimokkha was being recited, or even just after it had been recited. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow you to announce: “Today is the Uposatha.”'

Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho ārocetabbo”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, therena bhikkhunā kālavato ārocetunti.

Then this thought occurred to the monks: 'By whom, indeed, should it be announced?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I permit it to be announced early by the senior monk.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro thero kālavato nassarati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhattakālepi ārocetunti.

Now at that time, a certain elder would forget to announce it early. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I permit it to be announced even at mealtime.'

Bhattakālepi nassarati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yaṃ kālaṃ sarati, taṃ kālaṃ ārocetunti.

He would forget even at mealtime. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I permit it to be announced at whatever time one remembers.'

85. Pubbakaraṇānujānanā

85. Permission for Preliminary Duties

159. Tena [P 1.0118] kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse uposathāgāraṃ uklāpaṃ hoti. Āgantukā bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi [T 1.0231] nāma āvāsikā bhikkhū uposathāgāraṃ na sammajjissantī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uposathāgāraṃ sammajjitunti.

159. Now at that time in a certain monastery, the Uposatha hall was full of rubbish. The visiting monks complained, criticized, and grumbled, 'How is it that the resident monks do not sweep the Uposatha hall?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I permit the Uposatha hall to be swept.'

Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho uposathāgāraṃ sammajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, therena bhikkhunā navaṃ bhikkhuṃ āṇāpetunti.

Then this thought occurred to the monks: 'By whom, indeed, should the Uposatha hall be swept?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I permit a senior monk to instruct a junior monk.'

Therena āṇattā navā bhikkhū na sammajjanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, therena āṇattena agilānena na sammajjitabbaṃ. Yo na sammajjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

When instructed by a senior monk, the junior monks did not sweep. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, a junior monk who is not ill, when instructed by a senior, should not fail to sweep. Whoever does not sweep commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

160. Tena [M 0.0159] kho pana samayena uposathāgāre āsanaṃ apaññattaṃ hoti. Bhikkhū chamāyaṃ [V 0.0148] nisīdanti, gattānipi cīvarānipi paṃsukitāni honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uposathāgāre āsanaṃ paññapetunti.

160. At that time, seating was not prepared in the Uposatha hall. The monks sat on the ground, and their bodies and robes became dusty. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I permit seating to be prepared in the Uposatha hall.'

Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho uposathāgāre āsanaṃ paññapetabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, therena bhikkhunā navaṃ bhikkhuṃ āṇāpetunti.

Then this thought occurred to the monks: 'By whom, indeed, should the seating in the Uposatha hall be prepared?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I permit a senior monk to instruct a junior monk.'

Therena āṇattā navā bhikkhū na paññapenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, therena āṇattena agilānena na paññapetabbaṃ. Yo na paññapeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

When instructed by a senior monk, the junior monks did not prepare the seating. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, a junior monk who is not ill, when instructed by a senior, should not fail to prepare it. Whoever does not prepare it commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

161. Tena kho pana samayena uposathāgāre padīpo na hoti. Bhikkhū andhakāre kāyampi cīvarampi akkamanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uposathāgāre padīpaṃ [T 1.0232] kātunti.

161. At that time, there was no lamp in the Uposatha hall. In the darkness, the monks stepped on bodies and robes. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I permit a lamp to be prepared in the Uposatha hall.'

Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho uposathāgāre padīpo kātabbo”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, therena bhikkhunā navaṃ bhikkhuṃ āṇāpetunti.

Then this thought occurred to the monks: 'By whom, indeed, should the lamp in the Uposatha hall be prepared?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I permit a senior monk to instruct a junior monk.'

Therena āṇattā navā bhikkhū na padīpenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, therena āṇattena agilānena na padīpetabbo. Yo na padīpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

When instructed by a senior monk, the junior monks did not light the lamp. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, a junior monk who is not ill, when instructed by a senior, should not fail to light it. Whoever does not light it commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

162. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse āvāsikā bhikkhū neva pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpenti, na paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpenti. Āgantukā bhikkhū ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āvāsikā bhikkhū neva pānīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpessanti, na paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpessantī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave[P 1.0119], pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetunti.

162. At that time, in a certain monastery, the resident monks provided neither drinking water nor water for use. The visiting monks complained, criticized, and grumbled, 'How is it that the resident monks provide neither drinking water nor water for use?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I permit drinking water and water for use to be provided.'

Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabba”nti[V 0.0149]? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, therena bhikkhunā navaṃ bhikkhuṃ āṇāpetunti.

Then this thought occurred to the monks: 'By whom, indeed, should drinking water and water for use be provided?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I permit a senior monk to instruct a junior monk.'

Therena [M 0.0160] āṇattā navā bhikkhū na upaṭṭhāpenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, therena āṇattena agilānena na upaṭṭhāpetabbaṃ. Yo na upaṭṭhāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

When instructed by a senior monk, the junior monks did not provide it. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, a junior monk who is not ill, when instructed by a senior, should not fail to provide it. Whoever does not provide it commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

86. Disaṃgamikādivatthu

86. The Story concerning Those Going to Another Region, etc.

163. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū bālā abyattā disaṃgamikā [T 1.0233] ācariyupajjhāye na āpucchiṃsu na āpucchiṃsu (ka.). Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

163. Now at that time, many foolish and unskilled monks, intending to go to another region, did not take leave of their teachers and preceptors. They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, sambahulā bhikkhū bālā abyattā disaṃgamikā ācariyupajjhāye na āpucchanti na āpucchanti (ka.). Te tehi (ka.), bhikkhave, ācariyupajjhāyehi pucchitabbā – “kahaṃ gamissatha, kena saddhiṃ gamissathā”ti? Te ce, bhikkhave, bālā abyattā aññe bāle abyatte apadiseyyuṃ, na, bhikkhave, ācariyupajjhāyehi anujānitabbā. Anujāneyyuṃ ce, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te ca, bhikkhave, bālā abyattā ananuññātā ācariyupajjhāyehi gaccheyyuṃ ce, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Here, monks, many foolish and unskilled monks, intending to go to another region, do not take leave of their teachers and preceptors. They, monks, should be asked by their teachers and preceptors: 'Where will you go? With whom will you go?' If, monks, those foolish and unskilled monks should point out other foolish and unskilled ones, they should not be given permission by their teachers and preceptors. If they should give permission, it is an offense of wrong-doing. And if, monks, those foolish and unskilled monks should go without being given permission by their teachers and preceptors, it is an offense of wrong-doing.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse sambahulā bhikkhū viharanti bālā abyattā. Te na jānanti uposathaṃ vā uposathakammaṃ vā, pātimokkhaṃ vā pātimokkhuddesaṃ vā. Tattha añño bhikkhu āgacchati bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito byatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi so bhikkhu saṅgahetabbo anuggahetabbo upalāpetabbo upaṭṭhāpetabbo cuṇṇena mattikāya dantakaṭṭhena mukhodakena. No ce saṅgaṇheyyuṃ anuggaṇheyyuṃ upalāpeyyuṃ upaṭṭhāpeyyuṃ cuṇṇena mattikāya dantakaṭṭhena mukhodakena, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Here in this Dispensation, monks, in a certain monastery, many monks who are ignorant and unskilled reside. They do not know the Uposatha or the Uposatha ceremony, the Pātimokkha or the recitation of the Pātimokkha. To that place another monk arrives—learned, with the tradition come down to him, a Dhamma-holder, a Vinaya-holder, a matrix-holder, wise, competent, intelligent, modest, conscientious, desirous of training. Monks, that monk should be supported, assisted, conciliated with endearing speech, and attended upon by those monks with powder, clay, a tooth-stick, and water for washing the face. If they should not support, assist, conciliate, or attend upon him with powder, clay, a tooth-stick, and water for washing the face, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā bhikkhū [T 1.0234] viharanti bālā abyattā. Te na jānanti uposathaṃ vā uposathakammaṃ vā, pātimokkhaṃ vā pātimokkhuddesaṃ vā. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi eko bhikkhu sāmantā āvāsā sajjukaṃ pāhetabbo [V 0.0150] – “gacchāvuso, saṃkhittena vā vitthārena vā pātimokkhaṃ pariyāpuṇitvā āgacchā”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi [M 0.0161] sabbeheva yattha jānanti uposathaṃ vā uposathakammaṃ vā pātimokkhaṃ vā pātimokkhuddesaṃ vā, so āvāso gantabbo[P 1.0120]. No ce gaccheyyuṃ, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Here in this Dispensation, monks, in a certain monastery on the Uposatha day, many monks who are ignorant and unskilled reside. They do not know the Uposatha or the Uposatha ceremony, the Pātimokkha or the recitation of the Pātimokkha. Monks, those monks should send one monk to a nearby monastery to return the same day, with the instruction: ‘Go, friend, learn the Pātimokkha either in brief or in detail and return.’ If they should succeed in this, it is good. If they should not succeed, monks, all those monks should go to a monastery where they know the Uposatha, or the Uposatha ceremony, or the Pātimokkha, or the recitation of the Pātimokkha. If they should not go, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse sambahulā bhikkhū vassaṃ vasanti bālā abyattā. Te na jānanti uposathaṃ vā uposathakammaṃ vā pātimokkhaṃ vā pātimokkhuddesaṃ vā. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi eko bhikkhu sāmantā āvāsā sajjukaṃ pāhetabbo – “gacchāvuso, saṃkhittena vā vitthārena vā pātimokkhaṃ pariyāpuṇitvā āgacchā”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, eko bhikkhu sattāhakālikaṃ pāhetabbo – “gacchāvuso, saṃkhittena vā vitthārena vā pātimokkhaṃ pariyāpuṇitvā āgacchā”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, na, bhikkhave, tehi bhikkhūhi tasmiṃ āvāse vassaṃ vasitabbaṃ. Vaseyyuṃ ce, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Furthermore, monks, in a certain monastery, many monks who are ignorant and unskilled spend the rains-residence. They do not know the Uposatha, or the Uposatha ceremony, or the Pātimokkha, or the recitation of the Pātimokkha. Monks, those monks should send one monk to a nearby monastery to return the same day, with the instruction: ‘Go, friend, learn the Pātimokkha either in brief or in detail, and return.’ If they should find such a one, this is good. If they should not find such a one, they should send one monk for a week with the instruction: ‘Go, friend, learn the Pātimokkha either in brief or in detail, and return.’ If they should find such a one, this is good. If they should not find such a one, monks, those monks should not spend the rains-residence in that monastery. If they should spend it, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.

87. Pārisuddhidānakathā

87. The Chapter on Giving the Declaration of Purity

164. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “sannipatatha, bhikkhave, saṅgho uposathaṃ karissatī”ti. Evaṃ vutte aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca [T 1.0235] – “atthi, bhante, bhikkhu gilāno, so anāgato”ti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānena bhikkhunā pārisuddhiṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbā – tena gilānena bhikkhunā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “pārisuddhiṃ dammi, pārisuddhiṃ me hara, pārisuddhiṃ me ārocehī”ti. Kāyena viññāpeti, vācāya viññāpeti, kāyena vācāya viññāpeti, dinnā hoti pārisuddhi. Na kāyena viññāpeti, na vācāya viññāpeti, na kāyena vācāya viññāpeti, na dinnā hoti pārisuddhi. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, so, bhikkhave, gilāno bhikkhu mañcena vā pīṭhena vā saṅghamajjhe ānetvā uposatho kātabbo. Sace, bhikkhave, gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “sace kho mayaṃ gilānaṃ ṭhānā cāvessāma, ābādho vā abhivaḍḍhissati kālaṃkiriyā vā bhavissatī”ti, na, bhikkhave, gilāno bhikkhu ṭhānā cāvetabbo. Saṅghena tattha gantvā uposatho [M 0.0162] kātabbo. Na tveva vaggena saṅghena uposatho kātabbo. Kareyya ce, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

164. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: ‘Gather, monks, the Saṅgha will perform the Uposatha.’ When this was said, a certain monk said to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, there is a sick monk; he has not come.’ ‘I allow, monks, a sick monk to give his declaration of purity. And in this way, monks, it should be given: that sick monk should approach one monk, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, sit on his heels, raise his joined palms, and say this: “I give my declaration of purity, convey my declaration of purity, announce my declaration of purity.” If he makes it known by body, by speech, or by body and speech, the declaration of purity is given. If he does not make it known by body, by speech, or by body and speech, the declaration of purity is not given. If he can find such a one, that is good. If he cannot find one, monks, that sick monk should be brought into the midst of the Saṅgha on a bed or a chair, and the Uposatha should be performed. If, monks, the monks attending the sick think: “If we move the sick one from his place, his illness will worsen or he will die,” then, monks, the sick monk should not be moved from his place. The Saṅgha should go there and perform the Uposatha. But the Uposatha should not be performed by an incomplete Saṅgha. If one does so, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

Pārisuddhihārako [V 0.0151] ce, bhikkhave, dinnāya pārisuddhiyā tattheva pakkamati, aññassa dātabbā pārisuddhi. Pārisuddhihārako ce, bhikkhave, dinnāya pārisuddhiyā tattheva vibbhamati,…pe… kālaṃ karoti – sāmaṇero paṭijānāti [P 1.0121] – sikkhaṃ paccakkhātako paṭijānāti – antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannako [T 1.0236] paṭijānāti – ummattako paṭijānāti – khittacitto paṭijānāti – vedanāṭṭo paṭijānāti – āpattiyā adassane ukkhittako paṭijānāti – āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittako paṭijānāti – pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittako paṭijānāti – paṇḍako paṭijānāti – theyyasaṃvāsako paṭijānāti – titthiyapakkantako paṭijānāti – tiracchānagato paṭijānāti – mātughātako paṭijānāti – pitughātako paṭijānāti – arahantaghātako paṭijānāti – bhikkhunidūsako paṭijānāti – saṅghabhedako paṭijānāti – lohituppādako paṭijānāti – ubhatobyañjanako paṭijānāti, aññassa dātabbā pārisuddhi.

Monks, if the purity-bearer, after the declaration of purity has been given, departs from that very place, the declaration of purity should be given to another. Monks, if the purity-bearer, after the declaration of purity has been given, disrobes at that very place, … or dies; or declares himself to be a novice; or declares himself to be one who has renounced the training; or declares himself to have committed a terminal offense; or declares himself to be insane; or declares himself to be one whose mind is unhinged; or declares himself to be afflicted by pain; or declares himself to be one suspended for not seeing an offense; or declares himself to be one suspended for not making amends for an offense; or declares himself to be one suspended for not renouncing a wrong view; or declares himself to be a paṇḍaka; or declares himself to be one who has entered the community by stealth; or declares himself to be one who has gone over to the sectarians; or declares himself to be an animal; or declares himself to be a matricide; or declares himself to be a patricide; or declares himself to be a killer of an arahant; or declares himself to be a corrupter of a bhikkhunī; or declares himself to be a creator of schism in the Saṅgha; or declares himself to be one who has drawn the blood of a Buddha; or declares himself to be one with the characteristics of both sexes, the declaration of purity should be given to another.

Pārisuddhihārako ce, bhikkhave, dinnāya pārisuddhiyā antarāmagge pakkamati, anāhaṭā hoti pārisuddhi. Pārisuddhihārako ce, bhikkhave, dinnāya pārisuddhiyā antarāmagge vibbhamati,…pe… ubhatobyañjanako paṭijānāti, anāhaṭā hoti pārisuddhi.

Bhikkhus, if the purity-bearer, having been given the purity, departs on the way, the purity is not conveyed. Bhikkhus, if the purity-bearer, having been given the purity, disrobes on the way, … or declares himself to be one with the characteristics of both sexes, the purity is not conveyed.

Pārisuddhihārako ce, bhikkhave, dinnāya pārisuddhiyā saṅghappatto pakkamati, āhaṭā hoti pārisuddhi. Pārisuddhihārako ce, bhikkhave, dinnāya pārisuddhiyā saṅghappatto vibbhamati,…pe… ubhatobyañjanako paṭijānāti, āhaṭā hoti pārisuddhi.

Bhikkhus, if the purity-bearer, having been given the purity, departs after reaching the Saṅgha, the purity is conveyed. Bhikkhus, if the purity-bearer, having been given the purity, disrobes after reaching the Saṅgha, … or declares himself to be one with the characteristics of both sexes, the purity is conveyed.

Pārisuddhihārako ce, bhikkhave, dinnāya pārisuddhiyā saṅghappatto sutto na āroceti, pamatto na āroceti, samāpanno na āroceti, āhaṭā hoti pārisuddhi. Pārisuddhihārakassa anāpatti.

Bhikkhus, if the purity-bearer, having been given the purity, reaches the Saṅgha but does not announce it because he is asleep, heedless, or in attainment, the purity is conveyed. There is no offense for the purity-bearer.

Pārisuddhihārako ce, bhikkhave[T 1.0237], dinnāya pārisuddhiyā saṅghappatto sañcicca na āroceti, āhaṭā hoti pārisuddhi. Pārisuddhihārakassa āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Bhikkhus, if the purity-bearer, having been given the purity, reaches the Saṅgha and intentionally does not announce it, the purity is conveyed. The purity-bearer incurs an offense of wrong conduct.

88. Chandadānakathā

88. The Discourse on Giving Consent

165. Atha [M 0.0163] kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “sannipatatha, bhikkhave, saṅgho kammaṃ karissatī”ti[V 0.0152]. Evaṃ vutte aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “atthi, bhante, bhikkhu gilāno, so anāgato”ti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānena bhikkhunā chandaṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbo. Tena gilānena bhikkhunā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “chandaṃ dammi, chandaṃ me hara, chandaṃ me ārocehī”ti. Kāyena viññāpeti, vācāya viññāpeti, kāyena vācāya viññāpeti, dinno hoti chando. Na kāyena viññāpeti, na vācāya viññāpeti, na kāyena vācāya viññāpeti, na dinno hoti chando. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, so, bhikkhave[P 1.0122], gilāno bhikkhu mañcena vā pīṭhena vā saṅghamajjhe ānetvā kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Sace, bhikkhave, gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “sace kho mayaṃ gilānaṃ ṭhānā cāvessāma, ābādho vā abhivaḍḍhissati kālaṃkiriyā vā bhavissatī”ti, na, bhikkhave, gilāno bhikkhu ṭhānā cāvetabbo. Saṅghena tattha gantvā kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Na tveva vaggena saṅghena kammaṃ kātabbaṃ. Kareyya ce, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

165. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Assemble, monks, the Sangha will perform a formal act.” When this was said, a certain monk said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, there is a sick monk; he has not come.” “I allow, monks, a sick monk to give his consent. And it should be given in this way, monks: That sick monk, having approached a certain monk, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having sat down on his heels, and having raised his joined hands, should speak thus: ‘I give my consent; convey my consent; announce my consent.’ If he makes it known by body, by speech, or by body and speech, the consent is given. If he does not make it known by body, does not make it known by speech, or does not make it known by body and speech, the consent is not given. If one should find such a bearer, that is good. If one should not find one, that sick monk, monks, should be brought into the midst of the Sangha on a bed or a seat, and the formal act should be performed. If, monks, it occurs to the monks attending the sick: ‘If we move the sick monk from his place, his illness will worsen or he will die,’ then, monks, the sick monk should not be moved from his place. The Sangha should go there and perform the formal act. But a formal act should not be performed by an incomplete Sangha. If one should do so, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

Chandahārako [T 1.0238] ce, bhikkhave, dinne chande tattheva pakkamati, aññassa dātabbo chando. Chandahārako ce, bhikkhave, dinne chande tattheva vibbhamati…pe… kālaṃkaroti – sāmaṇero paṭijānāti – sikkhaṃ paccakkhātako paṭijānāti – antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannako paṭijānāti – ummattako paṭijānāti – khittacitto paṭijānāti – vedanāṭṭo paṭijānāti – āpattiyā adassane ukkhittako paṭijānāti – āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittako paṭijānāti – pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittako paṭijānāti – paṇḍako paṭijānāti – theyyasaṃvāsako paṭijānāti – titthiyapakkantako paṭijānāti – tiracchānagato paṭijānāti – mātughātako paṭijānāti – pitughātako paṭijānāti – arahantaghātako paṭijānāti – bhikkhunidūsako paṭijānāti – saṅghabhedako paṭijānāti – lohituppādako paṭijānāti – ubhatobyañjanako paṭijānāti, aññassa dātabbo chando.

Bhikkhus, if the bearer of consent, having been given the consent, departs from that very place, the consent should be given to another. Bhikkhus, if the bearer of consent, having been given the consent, disrobes at that very place... or dies; or acknowledges that he is a novice; or acknowledges that he is one who has given up the training; or acknowledges that he is one who has committed a terminal offense; or acknowledges that he is insane; or acknowledges that he is one of distracted mind; or acknowledges that he is one afflicted by pain; or acknowledges that he is one suspended for not seeing an offense; or acknowledges that he is one suspended for not making amends for an offense; or acknowledges that he is one suspended for not renouncing a wrong view; or acknowledges that he is a paṇḍaka; or acknowledges that he is one in clandestine communion; or acknowledges that he is one who has gone over to another sect; or acknowledges that he is an animal; or acknowledges that he is a matricide; or acknowledges that he is a patricide; or acknowledges that he is a murderer of an Arahant; or acknowledges that he is a corrupter of a bhikkhunī; or acknowledges that he is a schismatic of the Saṅgha; or acknowledges that he is one who has caused the Buddha's blood to flow; or acknowledges that he is one with the characteristics of both sexes, the consent should be given to another.

Chandahārako [M 0.0164] ce, bhikkhave, dinne chande antarāmagge pakkamati, anāhaṭo hoti chando. Chandahārako ce, bhikkhave, dinne chande antarāmagge vibbhamati…pe… ubhatobyañjanako paṭijānāti, anāhaṭo hoti chando.

Bhikkhus, if the bearer of consent, having been given the consent, departs on the way, the consent is not conveyed. Bhikkhus, if the bearer of consent, having been given the consent, disrobes on the way, … or declares himself to be one with the characteristics of both sexes, the consent is not conveyed.

Chandahārako ce, bhikkhave, dinne chande saṅghappatto pakkamati, āhaṭo hoti chando. Chandahārako [V 0.0153] ce, bhikkhave, dinne chande saṅghappatto vibbhamati…pe… ubhatobyañjanako paṭijānāti, āhaṭo hoti chando.

Bhikkhus, if the bearer of consent, having been given the consent and having reached the Saṅgha, departs, the consent is conveyed. Bhikkhus, if the bearer of consent, having been given the consent and having reached the Saṅgha, disrobes, … or declares himself to be one with the characteristics of both sexes, the consent is conveyed.

Chandahārako ce, bhikkhave, dinne [T 1.0239] chande saṅghappatto sutto na āroceti, pamatto na āroceti, samāpanno na āroceti, āhaṭo hoti chando. Chandahārakassa anāpatti.

Bhikkhus, if the bearer of consent, having been given the consent and having reached the Saṅgha, being asleep, does not announce it; or being heedless, does not announce it; or having entered an attainment, does not announce it, the consent is conveyed. There is no offense for the bearer of consent.

Chandahārako ce, bhikkhave, dinne chande saṅghappatto sañcicca na āroceti, āhaṭo hoti chando. Chandahārakassa āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe pārisuddhiṃ dentena chandampi dātuṃ, santi saṅghassa karaṇīyanti.

Bhikkhus, if the bearer of consent, when consent has been given, having reached the Saṅgha, intentionally does not announce it, the consent is conveyed. The bearer of consent commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, Bhikkhus, that on that Uposatha day, one who is giving his declaration of purity may also give consent, for there are duties to be done by the Saṅgha.

89. Ñātakādiggahaṇakathā

89. The Account of Seizing by Relatives and Others

166. Tena kho pana samayena aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ tadahuposathe ñātakā gaṇhiṃsuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

166. Now at that time, on that Uposatha day, a certain monk was seized by his relatives. They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ tadahuposathe ñātakā gaṇhanti. Te ñātakā bhikkhūhi evamassu vacanīyā – “iṅgha, tumhe āyasmanto imaṃ bhikkhuṃ muhuttaṃ muñcatha, yāvāyaṃ bhikkhu uposathaṃ karotī”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, te ñātakā bhikkhūhi evamassu vacanīyā – “iṅgha, tumhe āyasmanto muhuttaṃ ekamantaṃ hotha, yāvāyaṃ bhikkhu pārisuddhiṃ detī”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, te ñātakā bhikkhūhi evamassu vacanīyā – “iṅgha, tumhe āyasmanto imaṃ bhikkhuṃ muhuttaṃ nissīmaṃ netha, yāva saṅgho uposathaṃ karotī”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, na tveva vaggena saṅghena uposatho kātabbo. Kareyya ce, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Here, Bhikkhus, on that Uposatha day a bhikkhu is seized by his relatives. Those relatives should be addressed by the bhikkhus thus: ‘Come now, good sirs, please release this bhikkhu for a moment, until this bhikkhu performs the Uposatha.’ If they obtain this, it is good. If they do not obtain it, those relatives should be addressed by the bhikkhus thus: ‘Come now, good sirs, please stand aside for a moment, until this bhikkhu gives his declaration of purity.’ If they obtain this, it is good. If they do not obtain it, those relatives should be addressed by the bhikkhus thus: ‘Come now, good sirs, please take this bhikkhu outside the boundary for a moment, until the Saṅgha performs the Uposatha.’ If they obtain this, it is good. If they do not obtain it, the Uposatha must certainly not be performed by an incomplete Saṅgha. If it is performed, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Idha [M 0.0165] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ tadahuposathe rājāno gaṇhanti,…pe… corā gaṇhanti – dhuttā [T 1.0240] gaṇhanti – bhikkhupaccatthikā gaṇhanti, te bhikkhupaccatthikā bhikkhūhi evamassu vacanīyā – “iṅgha, tumhe āyasmanto imaṃ bhikkhuṃ muhuttaṃ muñcatha, yāvāyaṃ bhikkhu uposathaṃ karotī”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, te bhikkhupaccatthikā bhikkhūhi evamassu vacanīyā – “iṅgha, tumhe āyasmanto muhuttaṃ ekamantaṃ hotha, yāvāyaṃ bhikkhu pārisuddhiṃ detī”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, te bhikkhupaccatthikā [V 0.0154] bhikkhūhi evamassu vacanīyā – “iṅgha, tumhe āyasmanto imaṃ bhikkhuṃ muhuttaṃ nissīmaṃ netha, yāva saṅgho uposathaṃ karotī”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, na tveva vaggena saṅghena uposatho kātabbo. Kareyya ce, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Here, Bhikkhus, on that Uposatha day, a bhikkhu is seized by kings… seized by thieves… seized by drunkards… seized by hostile bhikkhus. Those hostile bhikkhus should be addressed by the bhikkhus thus: “Venerables, please release this bhikkhu for a moment, until this bhikkhu performs the Uposatha.” If they obtain this, it is good. If they do not obtain this, those hostile bhikkhus should be addressed by the bhikkhus thus: “Venerables, please stand aside for a moment, until this bhikkhu gives his declaration of purity.” If they obtain this, it is good. If they do not obtain this, those hostile bhikkhus should be addressed by the bhikkhus thus: “Venerables, please take this bhikkhu outside the boundary for a moment, until the Saṅgha performs the Uposatha.” If they obtain this, it is good. If they do not obtain this, the Uposatha should certainly not be performed by an incomplete Saṅgha. If it is performed, it is an offense of wrong-doing.

90. Ummattakasammuti

90. Designation of Insanity

167. Atha [P 1.0123] kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “sannipatatha, bhikkhave, atthi saṅghassa karaṇīya”nti. Evaṃ vutte aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “atthi, bhante, gaggo nāma bhikkhu ummattako, so anāgato”ti.

167. Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Assemble, Bhikkhus; there is business for the Saṅgha to do.” When this was said, a certain bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, there is a bhikkhu named Gagga who is insane; he has not come.”

“Dveme, bhikkhave, ummattakā – atthi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ummattako saratipi uposathaṃ napi sarati, saratipi saṅghakammaṃ napi sarati, atthi neva sarati; āgacchatipi uposathaṃ napi āgacchati, āgacchatipi saṅghakammaṃ napi āgacchati, atthi neva āgacchati. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ ummattako saratipi uposathaṃ napi sarati, saratipi saṅghakammaṃ napi sarati, āgacchatipi uposathaṃ napi āgacchati, āgacchatipi saṅghakammaṃ [T 1.0241] napi āgacchati, anujānāmi, bhikkhave, evarūpassa ummattakassa ummattakasammuttiṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbā. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

“Bhikkhus, there are these two kinds of insane persons. There is, Bhikkhus, an insane bhikkhu who sometimes remembers the Uposatha and sometimes does not remember, sometimes remembers a formal act of the Saṅgha and sometimes does not remember; and there is one who never remembers. Sometimes he comes for the Uposatha and sometimes does not come, sometimes he comes for a formal act of the Saṅgha and sometimes does not come; and there is one who never comes. Among them, Bhikkhus, regarding that insane bhikkhu who sometimes remembers the Uposatha and sometimes does not remember, sometimes remembers a formal act of the Saṅgha and sometimes does not remember, sometimes comes for the Uposatha and sometimes does not come, and sometimes comes for a formal act of the Saṅgha and sometimes does not come—I allow, Bhikkhus, that a designation of insanity be given to such an insane bhikkhu. And, Bhikkhus, it should be given in this way: A competent and able bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Gaggo bhikkhu ummattako – saratipi uposathaṃ napi sarati, saratipi saṅghakammaṃ napi sarati, āgacchatipi uposathaṃ napi āgacchati, āgacchatipi saṅghakammaṃ napi āgacchati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho gaggassa bhikkhuno ummattakassa ummattakasammutiṃ [M 0.0166] dadeyya. Sareyya vā gaggo bhikkhu uposathaṃ na vā sareyya, sareyya vā saṅghakammaṃ na vā sareyya, āgaccheyya vā uposathaṃ na vā āgaccheyya, āgaccheyya vā saṅghakammaṃ na vā āgaccheyya, saṅgho saha vā gaggena vinā vā gaggena uposathaṃ kareyya, saṅghakammaṃ kareyya. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The bhikkhu Gagga is insane—he sometimes remembers the Uposatha and sometimes does not remember, sometimes remembers a formal act of the Saṅgha and sometimes does not remember, sometimes comes for the Uposatha and sometimes does not come, and sometimes comes for a formal act of the Saṅgha and sometimes does not come. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should grant the designation of insanity to the insane bhikkhu Gagga. Whether the bhikkhu Gagga might remember the Uposatha or not, whether he might remember a formal act of the Saṅgha or not, whether he might come for the Uposatha or not, whether he might come for a formal act of the Saṅgha or not, the Saṅgha may perform the Uposatha and formal acts of the Saṅgha either with Gagga or without Gagga. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Gaggo bhikkhu ummattako – saratipi uposathaṃ napi sarati, saratipi saṅghakammaṃ napi sarati, āgacchatipi uposathaṃ napi āgacchati, āgacchatipi saṅghakammaṃ napi āgacchati. Saṅgho gaggassa bhikkhuno ummattakassa ummattakasammutiṃ [V 0.0155] deti. Sareyya vā gaggo bhikkhu uposathaṃ na vā sareyya, sareyya vā saṅghakammaṃ na vā sareyyaṃ, āgaccheyya vā uposathaṃ na vā āgaccheyya, āgaccheyya vā saṅghakammaṃ na vā āgaccheyya, saṅgho saha vā gaggena, vinā vā gaggena uposathaṃ karissati, saṅghakammaṃ karissati. Yassāyasmato khamati gaggassa bhikkhuno [T 1.0242] ummattakassa ummattakasammutiyā dānaṃ – sareyya vā gaggo bhikkhu uposathaṃ na vā sareyya, sareyya vā saṅghakammaṃ na vā sareyya, āgaccheyya vā uposathaṃ na vā āgaccheyya, āgaccheyya vā saṅghakammaṃ na vā āgaccheyya, saṅgho saha vā gaggena, vinā vā gaggena uposathaṃ karissati, saṅghakammaṃ karissati, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable Sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. The bhikkhu Gagga is insane: he sometimes remembers the Uposatha and sometimes does not remember; he sometimes remembers a formal act of the Saṅgha and sometimes does not remember; he sometimes comes for the Uposatha and sometimes does not come; he sometimes comes for a formal act of the Saṅgha and sometimes does not come. The Saṅgha grants the designation of insanity to the insane bhikkhu Gagga. Whether the bhikkhu Gagga might remember the Uposatha or not, whether he might remember a formal act of the Saṅgha or not, whether he might come for the Uposatha or not, whether he might come for a formal act of the Saṅgha or not, the Saṅgha will perform the Uposatha and formal acts of the Saṅgha with or without Gagga. To whichever venerable one the granting of the designation of insanity to the insane bhikkhu Gagga is agreeable—whether the bhikkhu Gagga might remember the Uposatha or not, whether he might remember a formal act of the Saṅgha or not, whether he might come for the Uposatha or not, whether he might come for a formal act of the Saṅgha or not, the Saṅgha will perform the Uposatha and formal acts of the Saṅgha with or without Gagga—he should remain silent. To whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.”

“Dinnā saṅghena gaggassa bhikkhuno ummattakassa ummattakasammuti. Sareyya vā gaggo bhikkhu uposathaṃ na vā sareyya, sareyya vā saṅghakammaṃ na vā sareyya, āgaccheyya vā uposathaṃ na vā āgaccheyya, āgaccheyya vā saṅghakammaṃ na vā āgaccheyya, saṅgho saha vā gaggena vinā vā gaggena uposathaṃ karissati, saṅghakammaṃ karissati. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The designation of insanity has been granted by the Saṅgha to the insane bhikkhu Gagga. Whether the bhikkhu Gagga remembers the Uposatha or does not remember, whether he remembers a formal act of the Saṅgha or does not remember, whether he comes for the Uposatha or does not come, whether he comes for a formal act of the Saṅgha or does not come, the Saṅgha will perform the Uposatha and will perform formal acts with or without Gagga. This is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold this.”

91. Saṅghuposathādippabhedaṃ

91. The Classification of the Saṅgha Uposatha and so forth

168. Tena [P 1.0124] kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe cattāro bhikkhū viharanti. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘uposatho kātabbo’ti, mayañcamhā cattāro janā, kathaṃ nu kho amhehi uposatho kātabbo”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ [M 0.0167] ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisitunti.

168. Now at that time, in a certain residence, four bhikkhus were dwelling on that Uposatha day. Then this thought occurred to those bhikkhus: “The Blessed One has prescribed, ‘The Uposatha is to be performed.’ And we are four persons. How then is the Uposatha to be performed by us?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow four to recite the Pātimokkha,” he said.

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe tayo bhikkhū viharanti. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “bhagavatā anuññātaṃ catunnaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisituṃ, mayañcamhā tayo [T 1.0243] janā, kathaṃ nu kho amhehi uposatho kātabbo”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ pārisuddhiuposathaṃ kātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbo. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena te bhikkhū ñāpetabbā –

Now at that time, in a certain residence, three bhikkhus were dwelling on that Uposatha day. Then this thought occurred to those bhikkhus: “The Blessed One has allowed four to recite the Pātimokkha. And we are three persons. How then is the Uposatha to be performed by us?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow three to perform the Uposatha of purity. And, bhikkhus, it is to be performed in this way. Those bhikkhus are to be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhu:

“Suṇantu me āyasmantā. Ajjuposatho pannaraso. Yadāyasmantānaṃ pattakallaṃ, mayaṃ aññamaññaṃ pārisuddhiuposathaṃ kareyyāmā”ti.

“May the venerable sirs hear me. Today is the Uposatha of the fifteenth. If it is the proper time for the venerable sirs, let us perform the Uposatha of purity with one another.”

Therena [V 0.0156] bhikkhunā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā te bhikkhū evamassu vacanīyā – “parisuddho ahaṃ, āvuso; parisuddhoti maṃ dhāretha. Parisuddho ahaṃ, āvuso; parisuddhoti maṃ dhāretha. Parisuddho ahaṃ, āvuso; parisuddhoti maṃ dhārethā”ti.

The senior bhikkhu, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having sat down squatting, and having raised his hands in añjali, should address those bhikkhus thus: “Friends, I am pure; you should regard me as pure. Friends, I am pure; you should regard me as pure. Friends, I am pure; you should regard me as pure.”

Navakena bhikkhunā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā te bhikkhū evamassu vacanīyā – “parisuddho ahaṃ, bhante; parisuddhoti maṃ dhāretha. Parisuddho ahaṃ, bhante; parisuddhoti maṃ dhāretha. Parisuddho ahaṃ, bhante; parisuddhoti maṃ dhārethā”ti.

The junior bhikkhu, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having sat down squatting, and having raised his hands in añjali, should address those bhikkhus thus: “Venerable sirs, I am pure; you should regard me as pure. Venerable sirs, I am pure; you should regard me as pure. Venerable sirs, I am pure; you should regard me as pure.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe dve bhikkhū viharanti. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “bhagavatā anuññātaṃ catunnaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisituṃ, tiṇṇannaṃ pārisuddhiuposathaṃ kātuṃ. Mayañcamhā dve janā. Kathaṃ nu kho amhehi uposatho kātabbo”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dvinnaṃ pārisuddhiuposathaṃ kātuṃ[T 1.0244]. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbo. Therena bhikkhunā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā navo bhikkhu evamassa vacanīyo – “parisuddho ahaṃ, āvuso; parisuddhoti maṃ dhārehi. Parisuddho ahaṃ, āvuso; parisuddhoti [P 1.0125] maṃ dhārehi. Parisuddho ahaṃ, āvuso; parisuddhoti maṃ dhārehī”ti.

Now at that time, in a certain residence, two bhikkhus were dwelling on that Uposatha day. Then this thought occurred to those bhikkhus: “It has been allowed by the Blessed One for four to recite the Pātimokkha, and for three to perform the Uposatha of purity. And we are two. How then should the Uposatha be performed by us?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow the Uposatha of purity to be performed by two. And, bhikkhus, it should be performed in this way: The senior bhikkhu, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having sat down squatting, and having raised his hands in añjali, should address the junior bhikkhu thus: ‘Friend, I am pure; regard me as pure. Friend, I am pure; regard me as pure. Friend, I am pure; regard me as pure.’”

Navakena [M 0.0168] bhikkhunā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā thero bhikkhu evamassa vacanīyo – “parisuddho ahaṃ, bhante; parisuddhoti maṃ dhāretha. Parisuddho ahaṃ, bhante; parisuddhoti maṃ dhāretha. Parisuddho ahaṃ, bhante; parisuddhoti maṃ dhārethā”ti.

The junior bhikkhu, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having sat down squatting, and having raised his hands in añjali, should address the senior bhikkhu thus: ‘Venerable sir, I am pure; you should regard me as pure. Venerable sir, I am pure; you should regard me as pure. Venerable sir, I am pure; you should regard me as pure.’”

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe eko bhikkhu viharati. Atha kho tassa bhikkhuno etadahosi – “bhagavatā anuññātaṃ catunnaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisituṃ, tiṇṇannaṃ pārisuddhiuposathaṃ kātuṃ, dvinnaṃ pārisuddhiuposathaṃ kātuṃ. Ahañcamhi ekako. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā uposatho kātabbo”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe eko bhikkhu viharati. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā yattha bhikkhū paṭikkamanti upaṭṭhānasālāya vā, maṇḍape vā, rukkhamūle vā, so deso sammajjitvā [V 0.0157] pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā āsanaṃ [T 1.0245] paññapetvā padīpaṃ katvā nisīditabbaṃ. Sace aññe bhikkhū āgacchanti, tehi saddhiṃ uposatho kātabbo. No ce āgacchanti, ajja me uposathoti adhiṭṭhātabbo. No ce adhiṭṭhaheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Now at that time, in a certain residence, a single bhikkhu was dwelling on the Uposatha day. Then this thought occurred to that bhikkhu: “The Blessed One has allowed the recitation of the Pātimokkha for four bhikkhus, the performance of the Uposatha of purity for three, and the performance of the Uposatha of purity for two. But I am alone. How then should the Uposatha be performed by me?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Here, bhikkhus, in a certain residence, a single bhikkhu is dwelling on the Uposatha day. That bhikkhu, bhikkhus, should sweep the place where bhikkhus are expected to come—whether an assembly hall, a pavilion, or the foot of a tree—set out drinking water and water for use, prepare a seat, light a lamp, and then sit down. If other bhikkhus arrive, the Uposatha should be performed with them. If they do not arrive, he should make the determination: ‘Today is my Uposatha.’ If he does not make this determination, he commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Tatra, bhikkhave, yattha cattāro bhikkhū viharanti, na ekassa pārisuddhiṃ āharitvā tīhi pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Uddiseyyuṃ ce, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tatra, bhikkhave, yattha tayo bhikkhū viharanti, na ekassa pārisuddhiṃ āharitvā dvīhi pārisuddhiuposatho kātabbo. Kareyyuṃ ce, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tatra, bhikkhave, yattha dve bhikkhū viharanti, na ekassa pārisuddhiṃ āharitvā ekena adhiṭṭhātabbo. Adhiṭṭhaheyya ce, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

“Bhikkhus, where four bhikkhus are dwelling, the Pātimokkha should not be recited by three after bringing the purification of one. If they should recite it, they commit an offense of wrong-doing. Bhikkhus, where three bhikkhus are dwelling, the Uposatha of purity should not be performed by two after bringing the purification of one. If they should perform it, they commit an offense of wrong-doing. Bhikkhus, where two bhikkhus are dwelling, the determination should not be made by one after bringing the purification of the other. If he should make the determination, he commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

92. Āpattipaṭikammavidhi

92. The Procedure for Remedying Offenses

169. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu tadahuposathe āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. Atha kho tassa bhikkhuno etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘na sāpattikena uposatho kātabbo’ti. Ahañcamhi āpattiṃ āpanno. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tadahuposathe āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā [P 1.0126] añjaliṃ paggahetvā [M 0.0169] evamassa vacanīyo – “ahaṃ, āvuso, itthannāmaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno, taṃ paṭidesemī”ti. Tena vattabbo – “passasī”ti. “Āma [T 1.0246] passāmī”ti. “Āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsī”ti.

169. Now on that occasion, a certain monk had committed an offense on that Uposatha day. Then this thought occurred to that monk: 'It has been laid down by the Blessed One that, “The Uposatha is not to be performed by one with an offense.” And I have committed an offense. How should I act?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'In this case, monks, a monk has committed an offense on that Uposatha day. That monk, monks, should approach another monk, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, sit down squatting, raise his joined hands, and speak thus: “Friend, I have committed an offense of such-and-such a name; I confess it.” He should be told by that monk: “Do you see it?” “Yes, I see it.” “You should restrain yourself in the future.”'

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tadahuposathe āpattiyā vematiko hoti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “ahaṃ, āvuso, itthannāmāya āpattiyā vematiko; yadā nibbematiko bhavissāmi, tadā taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmī”ti vatvā uposatho kātabbo, pātimokkhaṃ sotabbaṃ, na tveva tappaccayā uposathassa antarāyo kātabboti.

In this case, monks, a monk is doubtful about an offense on that Uposatha day. That monk, monks, should approach another monk, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, sit down squatting, raise his joined hands, and speak thus: 'Friend, I am doubtful about an offense of such-and-such a name. When I am free from doubt, I will then make amends for that offense.' Having said this, the Uposatha is to be performed, and the Pātimokkha is to be heard. But on that account, an obstacle to the Uposatha should certainly not be made.

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ desenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, sabhāgā āpatti desetabbā. Yo deseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Now on that occasion, the monks of the group of six confessed a similar offense. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, a similar offense is not to be confessed. Whoever should confess it, commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena [V 0.0158] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ paṭiggaṇhanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, sabhāgā āpatti paṭiggahetabbā. Yo paṭiggaṇheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Now on that occasion, the monks of the group of six were receiving the confession of a similar offense. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, a similar offense is not to be received. Whoever should receive it, commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

93. Āpattiāvikaraṇavidhi

93. The Method for Disclosing an Offense

170. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu pātimokkhe uddissamāne āpattiṃ sarati. Atha kho tassa bhikkhuno etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘na sāpattikena uposatho kātabbo’ti. Ahañcamhi āpattiṃ āpanno. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

170. Now on that occasion, a certain monk, while the Pātimokkha was being recited, remembered an offense. Then this thought occurred to that monk: “It has been laid down by the Blessed One, ‘The Uposatha should not be performed by one who has an offense.’ And I have committed an offense. How now should I act?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pātimokkhe uddissamāne [T 1.0247] āpattiṃ sarati. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sāmanto bhikkhu evamassa vacanīyo – “ahaṃ, āvuso, itthannāmaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno. Ito vuṭṭhahitvā taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmī”ti vatvā uposatho kātabbo, pātimokkhaṃ sotabbaṃ, na tveva tappaccayā uposathassa antarāyo kātabbo.

In this case, monks, if a monk, while the Pātimokkha is being recited, remembers an offense, that monk, monks, should address a nearby monk thus: ‘Friend, I have committed an offense of such-and-such a name. Having risen from here, I will make amends for that offense.’ Having said this, the Uposatha should be performed and the Pātimokkha should be heard. An obstacle to the Uposatha should certainly not be made on that account.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pātimokkhe uddissamāne āpattiyā vematiko hoti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sāmanto bhikkhu evamassa vacanīyo [M 0.0170] – “ahaṃ, āvuso, itthannāmāya āpattiyā vematiko. Yadā nibbematiko bhavissāmi, tadā taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmī”ti vatvā uposatho kātabbo, pātimokkhaṃ sotabbaṃ; na tveva tappaccayā uposathassa antarāyo kātabboti.

In this case, monks, if a monk, while the Pātimokkha is being recited, is doubtful about an offense, that monk, monks, should address a nearby monk thus: ‘Friend, I am doubtful about an offense of such-and-such a name. When I am free from doubt, I will then make amends for that offense.’ Having said this, the Uposatha should be performed and the Pātimokkha should be heard; an obstacle to the Uposatha should certainly not be made on that account.

94. Sabhāgāpattipaṭikammavidhi

94. The Procedure for Making Amends for a Shared Offense

171. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sabbo saṅgho sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘na sabhāgā āpatti desetabbā, na sabhāgā āpatti paṭiggahetabbā’ti[P 1.0127]. Ayañca sabbo saṅgho sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno. Kathaṃ nu kho amhehi paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

171. Now on that occasion, in a certain monastery on the Uposatha day, the entire Saṅgha had committed a shared offense. Then this thought occurred to those monks: “It has been laid down by the Blessed One, ‘A shared offense should not be confessed, nor should a shared offense be received.’ And this entire Saṅgha has committed a shared offense. How now should we act?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha [V 0.0159] pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sabbo saṅgho sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi eko bhikkhu sāmantā āvāsā sajjukaṃ pāhetabbo – gacchāvuso, taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikaritvā [T 1.0248] āgaccha; mayaṃ te santike āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmāti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

In this case, monks, if in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day the entire Saṅgha has committed a common offense, those monks should send one monk to a nearby monastery for a same-day return, saying: 'Go, friend, and having made amends for that offense, come back. We will make amends for that offense in your presence.' If they should obtain this, it is good. If they should not obtain it, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ sabbo saṅgho sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno. Yadā aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ suddhaṃ anāpattikaṃ passissati, tadā tassa santike taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissatī”ti vatvā uposatho kātabbo, pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ, na tveva tappaccayā uposathassa antarāyo kātabbo.

'Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my words. This entire Saṅgha has committed a common offense. When it sees another monk who is pure and without offense, it will then make amends for that offense in his presence.' Having said this, the Uposatha should be performed and the Pātimokkha should be recited. An obstacle to the Uposatha should certainly not be made on account of that.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sabbo saṅgho sabhāgāya āpattiyā vematiko hoti. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

In this case, monks, if in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day the entire Saṅgha is doubtful regarding a common offense, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ sabbo saṅgho sabhāgāya āpattiyā vematiko. Yadā nibbematiko bhavissati, tadā taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissatī”ti vatvā uposatho kātabbo, pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ; na tveva tappaccayā uposathassa antarāyo kātabbo.

'Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my words. This entire Saṅgha is doubtful regarding a common offense. When it becomes free from doubt, it will then make amends for that offense.' Having said this, the Uposatha should be performed and the Pātimokkha should be recited. An obstacle to the Uposatha should certainly not be made on account of that.

Idha [M 0.0171] pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse vassūpagato saṅgho sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi eko bhikkhu sāmantā āvāsā sajjukaṃ pāhetabbo – gacchāvuso, taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikaritvā āgaccha; mayaṃ te santike taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmāti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, eko bhikkhu sattāhakālikaṃ pāhetabbo – gacchāvuso, taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikaritvā āgaccha; mayaṃ te santike taṃ [T 1.0249] āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmāti.

Moreover, bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, if in a certain monastery a Saṅgha that has entered the rains-residence has fallen into a common offense, those bhikkhus should send one bhikkhu to a nearby monastery for a same-day return, saying: 'Go, friend, and having made amends for that offense, come back. We will make amends for that offense in your presence.' If they should obtain this, it is good. If they should not obtain it, one bhikkhu should be sent with a seven-day leave, saying: 'Go, friend, and having made amends for that offense, come back. We will make amends for that offense in your presence.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse sabbo saṅgho sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. So na jānāti tassā āpattiyā nāmagottaṃ. Tattha añño bhikkhu āgacchati bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito byatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. Tamenaṃ aññataro bhikkhu yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “yo nu kho, āvuso, evañcevañca karoti, kiṃ nāma [V 0.0160] so āpattiṃ āpajjatī”ti? So evamāha – “yo kho, āvuso, evañcevañca karoti, imaṃ nāma so āpattiṃ āpajjati. Imaṃ nāma tvaṃ, āvuso, āpattiṃ āpanno; paṭikarohi taṃ āpatti”nti. So evamāha – “na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, ekova imaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno; ayaṃ sabbo [P 1.0128] saṅgho imaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno”ti. So evamāha – “kiṃ te, āvuso, karissati paro āpanno vā anāpanno vā. Iṅgha, tvaṃ, āvuso, sakāya āpattiyā vuṭṭhāhī”ti. Atha kho so bhikkhu tassa bhikkhuno vacanena taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikaritvā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “yo kira, āvuso, evañcevañca karoti, imaṃ nāma so āpattiṃ āpajjati. Imaṃ nāma tumhe, āvuso, āpattiṃ āpannā; paṭikarotha taṃ āpatti”nti. Atha kho te bhikkhū na icchiṃsu tassa bhikkhuno vacanena [T 1.0250] taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikātuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

Now on that occasion, in a certain monastery, the entire Saṅgha had committed a common offense. They did not know the name and class of that offense. Then another bhikkhu arrived—learned, versed in the tradition, a bearer of the Dhamma, a bearer of the Vinaya, a bearer of the mātikās, wise, skilled, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training. A certain bhikkhu approached that bhikkhu and said: 'Friend, when someone does such and such, what offense does he commit?' He replied: 'Friend, when someone does such and such, he commits such and such an offense. You, friend, have committed such and such an offense. Make amends for that offense.' The other bhikkhu said: 'Friend, I am not the only one who has committed this offense; this entire Saṅgha has committed this offense.' The first bhikkhu said: 'What is it to you, friend, whether another has committed it or not? Come, friend, emerge from your own offense.' Then that bhikkhu, following that bhikkhu’s advice, made amends for the offense and approached those bhikkhus, saying: 'Friends, it is said that when someone does such and such, he commits such and such an offense. You, friends, have committed such and such an offense. Make amends for that offense.' But those bhikkhus were unwilling to make amends for the offense on the advice of that bhikkhu. They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse sabbo saṅgho sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. So na jānāti tassā āpattiyā nāmagottaṃ. Tattha añño bhikkhu āgacchati bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo [M 0.0172] vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito byatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. Tamenaṃ aññataro bhikkhu yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ evaṃ vadeti – “yo nu kho, āvuso, evañcevañca karoti, kiṃ nāma so āpattiṃ āpajjatī”ti? So evaṃ vadeti – “yo kho, āvuso, evañcevañca karoti, imaṃ nāma so āpattiṃ āpajjati. Imaṃ nāma tvaṃ, āvuso, āpattiṃ āpanno; paṭikarohi taṃ āpatti”nti. So evaṃ vadeti – “na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, ekova imaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno. Ayaṃ sabbo saṅgho imaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno”ti. So evaṃ vadeti – “kiṃ te, āvuso, karissati paro āpanno vā anāpanno vā. Iṅgha, tvaṃ, āvuso, sakāya āpattiyā vuṭṭhāhī”ti. So ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tassa bhikkhuno vacanena taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikaritvā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū evaṃ vadeti – “yo kira, āvuso, evañcevañca karoti imaṃ nāma so āpattiṃ āpajjati, imaṃ nāma tumhe āvuso āpattiṃ āpannā, paṭikarotha taṃ āpatti”nti. Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū tassa bhikkhuno vacanena taṃ āpattiṃ [T 1.0251] paṭikareyyuṃ, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce paṭikareyyuṃ, na te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū tena bhikkhunā akāmā vacanīyāti.

Here, bhikkhus, in a certain monastery the entire Saṅgha has incurred a common offense. The Saṅgha does not know the name or class of that offense. Then another bhikkhu arrives—learned, versed in tradition, a bearer of the Dhamma, a bearer of the Vinaya, a bearer of the mātikās, wise, competent, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training. Then a certain bhikkhu approaches that bhikkhu and says to him: “Friend, if someone does such and such, what offense does he incur?” He replies: “Friend, if someone does such and such, he incurs such and such an offense. You, friend, have incurred such and such an offense; make amends for that offense.” He says: “Friend, I have not incurred this offense alone; this entire Saṅgha has incurred this offense.” He says: “Friend, what does it matter to you whether others have incurred it or not? Come, friend, you should emerge from your own offense.” If, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu, following the advice of that bhikkhu, makes amends for that offense, and then approaches those bhikkhus and says to them: “Friends, it seems that if someone does such and such, he incurs such and such an offense. You, friends, have incurred such and such an offense; make amends for that offense.” If, bhikkhus, those bhikkhus, following the advice of that bhikkhu, make amends for that offense, that is good. If they do not make amends, bhikkhus, those bhikkhus should not be admonished by that bhikkhu against their will.

Codanāvatthubhāṇavāro niṭṭhito dutiyo.

The Second Recitation Section on the Grounds for Accusation is finished.

95. Anāpattipannarasakaṃ

95. The Fifteen Cases of No Offense

172. Tena [V 0.0161] kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatiṃsu cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te na jāniṃsu “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti[P 1.0129]. Te dhammasaññino vinayasaññino vaggā samaggasaññino uposathaṃ akaṃsu, pātimokkhaṃ uddisiṃsu. Tehi uddissamāne pātimokkhe, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchiṃsu bahutarā. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

172. Now at that time, in a certain monastery, on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assembled—four or more. They did not know: 'There are other resident bhikkhus who have not come.' Perceiving it as a lawful act, perceiving it as in accordance with the Vinaya, and perceiving themselves as a complete assembly, though they were an incomplete group, they performed the Uposatha and recited the Pātimokkha. While the Pātimokkha was being recited by them, other resident bhikkhus, who were more numerous, arrived. They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te na jānanti “atthaññe [M 0.0173] āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te dhammasaññino vinayasaññino vaggā samaggasaññino uposathaṃ karonti, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddissamāne pātimokkhe, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti bahutarā. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi puna pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ anāpatti.

Here, bhikkhus, in a certain monastery, on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble—four or more. They do not know: 'There are other resident bhikkhus who have not come.' Perceiving it as a lawful act, perceiving it as in accordance with the Vinaya, and perceiving themselves as a complete assembly, though they are an incomplete group, they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. While the Pātimokkha is being recited by them, other resident bhikkhus, who are more numerous, arrive. Bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha should be recited again by those bhikkhus. There is no offense for the reciters.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te na jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te dhammasaññino vinayasaññino [T 1.0252] vaggā samaggasaññino uposathaṃ karonti, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddissamāne pātimokkhe, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti samasamā. Uddiṭṭhaṃ suuddiṭṭhaṃ, avasesaṃ sotabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ anāpatti.

While the Pātimokkha is being recited by them, other resident bhikkhus, equal in number, arrive. What has been recited is well-recited; the remainder should be heard. There is no offense for the reciters.

Tehi uddissamāne pātimokkhe, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti thokatarā. Uddiṭṭhaṃ suuddiṭṭhaṃ, avasesaṃ sotabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ anāpatti.

Just as the Pātimokkha has been recited by them, after a portion of the assembly has risen, other resident bhikkhus, who are fewer in number, arrive. The recitation is a good recitation.
