Idha [V 0.0164] pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te na jānanti atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatāti, te dhammasaññino vinayasaññino vaggā samaggasaññino uposathaṃ karonti pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddiṭṭhamatte pātimokkhe, sabbāya vuṭṭhitāya parisāya, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti bahutarā. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi puna pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ anāpatti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble—four or more. They do not know that there are other resident bhikkhus who have not yet arrived. Perceiving the act as being in accordance with the Dhamma, perceiving it as being in accordance with the Vinaya, and, though being an incomplete group, perceiving the assembly as complete, they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. Just as the Pātimokkha has been recited by them, after the entire assembly has risen, other resident bhikkhus, who are more numerous, arrive. Bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha should be recited again by those bhikkhus. There is no offense for the reciters.

Idha [M 0.0176] pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te na jānanti atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatāti, te dhammasaññino vinayasaññino vaggā samaggasaññino uposathaṃ karonti pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddiṭṭhamatte pātimokkhe, sabbāya vuṭṭhitāya parisāya, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti samasamā. Uddiṭṭhaṃ suuddiṭṭhaṃ, tesaṃ santike pārisuddhi ārocetabbā. Uddesakānaṃ anāpatti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble—four or more. They do not know that there are other resident bhikkhus who have not yet arrived. Perceiving the act as being in accordance with the Dhamma, perceiving it as being in accordance with the Vinaya, and, though being an incomplete group, perceiving the assembly as complete, they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. Just as the Pātimokkha has been recited by them, after the entire assembly has risen, other resident bhikkhus, who are equal in number, arrive. The recitation is a good recitation. Purity should be declared in their presence. There is no offense for the reciters.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te na jānanti atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatāti, te dhammasaññino vinayasaññino vaggā samaggasaññino uposathaṃ karonti pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddiṭṭhamatte pātimokkhe, sabbāya vuṭṭhitāya parisāya, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti thokatarā. Uddiṭṭhaṃ suuddiṭṭhaṃ, tesaṃ santike pārisuddhi ārocetabbā. Uddesakānaṃ anāpatti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble—four or more. They do not know that there are other resident bhikkhus who have not yet arrived. Perceiving the act as being in accordance with the Dhamma, perceiving it as being in accordance with the Vinaya, and, though being an incomplete group, perceiving the assembly as complete, they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. Just as the Pātimokkha has been recited by them, after the entire assembly has risen, other resident bhikkhus, who are fewer in number, arrive. The recitation is a good recitation. Purity should be declared in their presence. There is no offense for the reciters.

Anāpattipannarasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section on the fifteen cases of no offense is concluded.

96. Vaggāvaggasaññīpannarasakaṃ

96. The Fifteen Cases of Being an Incomplete Group and Perceiving it as an Incomplete Group

173. Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te dhammasaññino vinayasaññino vaggā vaggasaññino uposathaṃ karonti[T 1.0256], pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddissamāne pātimokkhe, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti [V 0.0165] bahutarā. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi puna pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ āpatti dukkaṭassa.

173. Furthermore, bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble—four or more. They know that there are other resident bhikkhus who have not yet arrived. Perceiving the act as being in accordance with the Dhamma, perceiving it as being in accordance with the Vinaya, and, being an incomplete group and perceiving it as an incomplete group, they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. While the Pātimokkha is being recited by them, other resident bhikkhus, who are more numerous, arrive. Bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha should be recited again by those bhikkhus. The reciters incur an offense of wrong-doing.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatāti, te dhammasaññino vinayasaññino vaggā samaggasaññino uposathaṃ karonti pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddissamāne pātimokkhe, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti samasamā[M 0.0177]. Uddiṭṭhaṃ suuddiṭṭhaṃ, avasesaṃ sotabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble—four or more. They know that there are other resident bhikkhus who have not yet arrived. Perceiving the act as being in accordance with the Dhamma, perceiving it as being in accordance with the Vinaya, and, though being an incomplete group, perceiving the assembly as complete, they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. While the Pātimokkha is being recited by them, other resident bhikkhus, who are equal in number, arrive. The recitation is a good recitation; the remainder should be heard. The reciters incur an offense of wrong-doing.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatāti te dhammasaññino vinayasaññino vaggā vaggasaññino uposathaṃ karonti pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddissamāne pātimokkhe, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti thokatarā. Uddiṭṭhaṃ suuddiṭṭhaṃ, avasesaṃ sotabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble—four or more. They know that there are other resident bhikkhus who have not yet arrived. Perceiving the act as being in accordance with the Dhamma, perceiving it as being in accordance with the Vinaya, and, being an incomplete group and perceiving it as an incomplete group, they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. While the Pātimokkha is being recited by them, other resident bhikkhus, who are fewer in number, arrive. The recitation is a good recitation; the remainder should be heard. The reciters incur an offense of wrong-doing.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te dhammasaññino vinayasaññino vaggā vaggasaññino uposathaṃ karonti, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddiṭṭhamatte pātimokkhe…pe… avuṭṭhitāya [T 1.0257] parisāya…pe… ekaccāya vuṭṭhitāya parisāya…pe… sabbāya vuṭṭhitāya [P 1.0131] parisāya athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti bahutarā…pe… samasamā…pe… thokatarā. Uddiṭṭhaṃ suuddiṭṭhaṃ, tesaṃ santike pārisuddhi ārocetabbā. Uddesakānaṃ āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble—four or more. They know that other resident bhikkhus have not come. Perceiving the act as being of the Dhamma, perceiving it as being of the Vinaya, and, being an incomplete group, perceiving themselves as an incomplete group, they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. As soon as the Pātimokkha has been recited by them… and so on… while the assembly has not yet risen… and so on… after a portion of the assembly has risen… and so on… after the entire assembly has risen, other resident bhikkhus arrive, more numerous… and so on… equal in number… and so on… fewer in number. What has been recited is well-recited; purity should be declared in their presence. There is an offense of wrong-doing for the reciters.

Vaggāvaggasaññipannarasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section of fifteen cases on being a divided group and perceiving it as a divided group is concluded.

97. Vematikapannarasakaṃ

97. The Section of Fifteen on Doubt.

174. Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te, kappati nu kho amhākaṃ uposatho kātuṃ na nu kho kappatīti, vematikā [V 0.0166] uposathaṃ karonti, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddissamāne pātimokkhe, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti bahutarā. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi puna pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ āpatti dukkaṭassa.

174. Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble, four or more. They know: 'There are other resident bhikkhus who have not arrived.' Being uncertain, 'Is it permissible for us to perform the Uposatha, or is it not permissible?', they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. While the Pātimokkha is being recited by them, other resident bhikkhus arrive, who are more numerous. Bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha should be recited again by those bhikkhus. There is an offense of wrong-doing for the reciters.

Idha [M 0.0178] pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti, te “kappati nu kho amhākaṃ uposatho kātuṃ, na nu kho kappatī”ti, vematikā uposathaṃ karonti, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddissamāne pātimokkhe, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti samasamā. Uddiṭṭhaṃ suuddiṭṭhaṃ, avasesaṃ sotabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble, four or more. They know: 'There are other resident bhikkhus who have not arrived.' Being uncertain, 'Is it permissible for us to perform the Uposatha, or is it not permissible?', they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. While the Pātimokkha is being recited by them, other resident bhikkhus arrive, equal in number. What has been recited is well-recited; the remainder should be heard. There is an offense of wrong-doing for the reciters.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū [T 1.0258] anāgatāti, te kappati nu kho amhākaṃ uposatho kātuṃ, na nu kho kappatīti, vematikā uposathaṃ karonti, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddissamāne pātimokkhe athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti thokatarā. Uddiṭṭhaṃ suuddiṭṭhaṃ, avasesaṃ sotabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble, four or more. They know: 'There are other resident bhikkhus who have not arrived.' Being uncertain, 'Is it permissible for us to perform the Uposatha, or is it not permissible?', they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. While the Pātimokkha is being recited by them, other resident bhikkhus arrive, fewer in number. What has been recited is well-recited; the remainder should be heard. There is an offense of wrong-doing for the reciters.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te, “kappati nu kho amhākaṃ uposatho kātuṃ na nu kho kappatī”ti, vematikā uposathaṃ karonti, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddiṭṭhamatte pātimokkhe,…pe… avuṭṭhitāya parisāya…pe… ekaccāya vuṭṭhitāya parisāya…pe… sabbāya vuṭṭhitāya parisāya, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti bahutarā…pe… samasamā…pe… thokatarā. Uddiṭṭhaṃ suuddiṭṭhaṃ, tesaṃ santike pārisuddhi ārocetabbā. Uddesakānaṃ āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble, four or more. They know: 'There are other resident bhikkhus who have not arrived.' Being doubtful, 'Is it permissible for us to perform the Uposatha, or is it not permissible?', they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. Just as the Pātimokkha has been recited by them… and so on… while the assembly has not yet risen… and so on… after a portion of the assembly has risen… and so on… after the entire assembly has risen, other resident bhikkhus arrive, more numerous… and so on… equal in number… and so on… fewer in number. What has been recited is well-recited; purity should be declared in their presence. There is an offense of wrong-doing for the reciters.

Vematikapannarasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section of Fifteen on Doubt is concluded.

98. Kukkuccapakatapannarasakaṃ

98. The Section of Fifteen on Being Afflicted by Scruples.

175. Idha [V 0.0167] pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te “kappateva amhākaṃ [M 0.0179] uposatho kātuṃ nāmhākaṃ na kappatī”ti, kukkuccapakatā uposathaṃ karonti, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddissamāne pātimokkhe, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti bahutarā. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi puna pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ āpatti dukkaṭassa.

175. Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble, four or more. They know: 'There are other resident bhikkhus who have not arrived.' Being afflicted by scruples, thinking, 'It is indeed permissible for us to perform the Uposatha; it is not that it is not permissible for us,' they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. While the Pātimokkha is being recited by them, other resident bhikkhus arrive, who are more numerous. Bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha should be recited again by those bhikkhus. There is an offense of wrong-doing for the reciters.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te “kappateva amhākaṃ uposatho kātuṃ nāmhākaṃ na kappatī”ti, kukkuccapakatā uposathaṃ karonti, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddissamāne pātimokkhe, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti samasamā. Uddiṭṭhaṃ suuddiṭṭhaṃ, avasesaṃ sotabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble, four or more. They know: 'There are other resident bhikkhus who have not arrived.' Being afflicted by scruples, thinking, 'It is indeed permissible for us to perform the Uposatha; it is not that it is not permissible for us,' they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. While the Pātimokkha is being recited by them, other resident bhikkhus arrive, who are equal in number. What has been recited is well-recited; the remainder should be heard. There is an offense of wrong-doing for the reciters.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te “kappateva amhākaṃ uposatho kātuṃ, nāmhākaṃ na kappatī”ti, kukkuccapakatā uposathaṃ karonti, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddissamāne pātimokkhe, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti thokatarā. Uddiṭṭhaṃ suuddiṭṭhaṃ, avasesaṃ sotabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble, four or more. They know: 'There are other resident bhikkhus who have not arrived.' Being afflicted by scruples, thinking, 'It is indeed permissible for us to perform the Uposatha; it is not that it is not permissible for us,' they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. While the Pātimokkha is being recited by them, other resident bhikkhus arrive, who are fewer in number. What has been recited is well-recited; the remainder should be heard. There is an offense of wrong-doing for the reciters.

Idha pana, bhikkhave[T 1.0259], aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te “kappateva amhākaṃ uposatho kātuṃ nāmhākaṃ na kappatī”ti, kukkuccapakatā uposathaṃ karonti, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddiṭṭhamatte pātimokkhe,…pe… avuṭṭhitāya parisāya…pe… ekaccāya vuṭṭhitāya parisāya…pe… sabbāya vuṭṭhitāya parisāya, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti bahutarā…pe… samasamā [V 0.0168] …pe… thokatarā. Uddiṭṭhaṃ suuddiṭṭhaṃ, tesaṃ santike pārisuddhi ārocetabbā. Uddesakānaṃ āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Moreover, in this Dispensation, O bhikkhus, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble, being four or more than four. They know thus: 'There are other resident bhikkhus who have not come.' Being afflicted by scruple, they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha, thinking: 'It is indeed allowable for us to perform the Uposatha; it is not that it is not allowable for us.' As soon as the Pātimokkha has been recited by them... before the assembly has risen... when a certain part of the assembly has risen... when the entire assembly has risen, then other resident bhikkhus arrive, who are more numerous... equal in number... or fewer in number. What has been recited is well-recited. Purity should be declared in their presence. For the reciters, there is an offense of wrong conduct.

Kukkuccapakatapannarasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section of Fifteen on Being Afflicted by Scruple is concluded.

99. Bhedapurekkhārapannarasakaṃ

99. The Fifteen Cases with Schism as the Foremost Aim

176. Idha [M 0.0180] pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te “nassantete, vinassantete, ko tehi attho”ti – bhedapurekkhārā uposathaṃ karonti, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddissamāne pātimokkhe, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti bahutarā. Tehi[T 1.0260], bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi puna pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ āpatti thullaccayassa[P 1.0132].

176. Moreover, in this Dispensation, O bhikkhus, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble, being four or more than four. They know thus: 'There are other resident bhikkhus who have not come.' Having schism as their foremost aim, they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha, thinking: 'Let these bhikkhus perish, let them be destroyed, what use are they?' While the Pātimokkha is being recited by them, other resident bhikkhus arrive, who are more numerous. O bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha should be recited again by those bhikkhus. For the reciters, there is a grave offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te “nassantete, vinassantete, ko tehi attho”ti – bhedapurekkhārā uposathaṃ karonti, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddissamāne pātimokkhe, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti samasamā. Uddiṭṭhaṃ suuddiṭṭhaṃ, avasesaṃ sotabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ āpatti thullaccayassa.

Moreover, in this Dispensation, O bhikkhus, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble, being four or more. They know: 'There are other resident bhikkhus who have not come.' With schism as their foremost aim, thinking, 'Let them perish, let them be destroyed, what is the use of them?', they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. While the Pātimokkha is being recited by them, other resident bhikkhus, equal in number, arrive. What has been recited is well-recited; the remainder should be heard. For the reciters, there is a grave offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te “nassantete, vinassantete, ko tehi attho”ti – bhedapurekkhārā uposathaṃ karonti, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddissamāne pātimokkhe, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti thokatarā. Uddiṭṭhaṃ suuddiṭṭhaṃ, avasesaṃ sotabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ āpatti thullaccayassa.

Moreover, in this Dispensation, O bhikkhus, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident bhikkhus assemble, being four or more. They know: 'There are other resident bhikkhus who have not come.' With schism as their foremost aim, thinking, 'Let them perish, let them be destroyed, what is the use of them?', they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. While the Pātimokkha is being recited by them, other resident bhikkhus, fewer in number, arrive. What has been recited is well-recited; the remainder should be heard. For the reciters, there is a grave offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti[V 0.0169]. Te “nassantete, vinassantete, ko tehi attho”ti – bhedapurekkhārā uposathaṃ karonti, pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Tehi uddiṭṭhamatte pātimokkhe athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti bahutarā. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi puna pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Uddesakānaṃ āpatti thullaccayassa.

With schism as their foremost aim, thinking, 'Let them perish, let them be destroyed, what is the use of them?', they perform the Uposatha and recite the Pātimokkha. As soon as the Pātimokkha has been recited by them, other resident bhikkhus, who are more numerous, arrive. O bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha should be recited again by those bhikkhus. For the reciters, there is a grave offense.

Idha [M 0.0181] pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Bhedapurekkhārapannarasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section of fifteen cases on being intent on schism is concluded.

Pañcavīsatikā niṭṭhitā.

The section of twenty-five is concluded.

100. Sīmokkantikapeyyālaṃ

100. The Elaboration on Entering the Boundary

177. Idha [M 0.0184] pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahuposathe sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti cattāro vā atirekā vā. Te na jānanti “aññe āvāsikā bhikkhū antosīmaṃ okkamantī”ti [T 1.0261] …pe… te na jānanti “aññe āvāsikā bhikkhū antosīmaṃ okkantā”ti…pe… te na passanti aññe āvāsike bhikkhū antosīmaṃ okkamante [V 0.0172] …pe… te na passanti aññe āvāsike bhikkhū antosīmaṃ okkante…pe… te na suṇanti “aññe āvāsikā bhikkhū antosīmaṃ okkamantī”ti…pe… te na suṇanti “aññe āvāsikā bhikkhū antosīmaṃ okkantā”ti…pe….

177. Here, monks, in a certain monastery on that Uposatha day, many resident monks assemble, four or more. They do not know, 'Other resident monks are entering the boundary'… they do not know, 'Other resident monks have entered the boundary'… they do not see other resident monks entering the boundary… they do not see other resident monks who have entered the boundary… they do not hear, 'Other resident monks are entering the boundary'… they do not hear, 'Other resident monks have entered the boundary'…

Āvāsikena āvāsikā ekasatapañcasattati tikanayato, āvāsikena āgantukā, āgantukena āvāsikā, āgantukena āgantukā peyyālamukhena satta tikasatāni honti.

Between resident monks and resident monks, there are one hundred and seventy-five triads according to the triad method. It is likewise for resident monks with visiting monks, for visiting monks with resident monks, and for visiting monks with visiting monks. By way of elaboration, there are seven hundred triads.

178. Idha pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cātuddaso hoti, āgantukānaṃ pannaraso. Sace āvāsikā bahutarā honti, āgantukehi āvāsikānaṃ anuvattitabbaṃ. Sace samasamā honti, āgantukehi āvāsikānaṃ anuvattitabbaṃ. Sace āgantukā bahutarā honti, āvāsikehi āgantukānaṃ anuvattitabbaṃ.

178. Here, monks, for the resident monks it is the fourteenth-day Uposatha, and for the visiting monks it is the fifteenth-day Uposatha. If the resident monks are more numerous, the visiting monks should conform to the resident monks. If they are equal in number, the visiting monks should conform to the resident monks. If the visiting monks are more numerous, the resident monks should conform to the visiting monks.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pannaraso hoti, āgantukānaṃ cātuddaso. Sace āvāsikā bahutarā honti, āgantukehi āvāsikānaṃ anuvattitabbaṃ. Sace samasamā honti, āgantukehi āvāsikānaṃ anuvattitabbaṃ. Sace āgantukā bahutarā honti, āvāsikehi āgantukānaṃ anuvattitabbaṃ.

Here, monks, for the resident monks it is the fifteenth-day Uposatha, and for the visiting monks it is the fourteenth-day Uposatha. If the resident monks are more numerous, the visiting monks should conform to the resident monks. If they are equal in number, the visiting monks should conform to the resident monks. If the visiting monks are more numerous, the resident monks should conform to the visiting monks.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭipado hoti, āgantukānaṃ pannaraso. Sace āvāsikā bahutarā honti, āvāsikehi [T 1.0262] āgantukānaṃ nākāmā dātabbā sāmaggī. Āgantukehi nissīmaṃ gantvā uposatho kātabbo. Sace samasamā honti, āvāsikehi āgantukānaṃ nākāmā dātabbā sāmaggī. Āgantukehi nissīmaṃ [M 0.0185] gantvā uposatho kātabbo. Sace āgantukā bahutarā honti, āvāsikehi āgantukānaṃ sāmaggī vā dātabbā nissīmaṃ vā gantabbaṃ.

Here, monks, for the resident monks it is the first day of the fortnight, and for the visiting monks it is the fifteenth-day Uposatha. If the resident monks are more numerous, they should not grant harmony to the visiting monks against their will; the visiting monks should go outside the boundary and perform the Uposatha. If they are equal in number, the resident monks should not grant harmony to the visiting monks against their will; the visiting monks should go outside the boundary and perform the Uposatha. If the visiting monks are more numerous, the resident monks should either grant harmony to the visiting monks or go outside the boundary.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pannaraso hoti, āgantukānaṃ [P 1.0133]

Here, monks, for the resident monks it is the fifteenth-day Uposatha, and for the visiting monks...

Pāṭipado. Sace āvāsikā bahutarā honti, āgantukehi āvāsikānaṃ sāmaggī vā dātabbā nissīmaṃ [V 0.0173] vā gantabbaṃ. Sace samasamā honti, āgantukehi āvāsikānaṃ sāmaggī vā dātabbā nissīmaṃ vā gantabbaṃ. Sace āgantukā bahutarā honti, āgantukehi āvāsikānaṃ nākāmā dātabbā sāmaggī. Āvāsikehi nissīmaṃ gantvā uposatho kātabbo.

...it is the first day of the fortnight. If the resident monks are more numerous, the visiting monks should either grant harmony to the resident monks or go outside the boundary. If they are equal in number, the visiting monks should either grant harmony to the resident monks or go outside the boundary. If the visiting monks are more numerous, they should not grant harmony to the resident monks against their will; the resident monks should go outside the boundary and perform the Uposatha.

Sīmokkantikapeyyālaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Elaboration on Entering the Boundary is concluded.

101. Liṅgādidassanaṃ

101. The Observation of Signs and so forth

179. Idha pana, bhikkhave, āgantukā bhikkhū passanti āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āvāsikākāraṃ, āvāsikaliṅgaṃ, āvāsikanimittaṃ, āvāsikuddesaṃ, supaññattaṃ mañcapīṭhaṃ, bhisibibbohanaṃ, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ sūpaṭṭhitaṃ, pariveṇaṃ susammaṭṭhaṃ; passitvā vematikā honti – “atthi nu kho āvāsikā bhikkhū natthi nu kho”ti. Te vematikā na vicinanti; avicinitvā uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te vematikā vicinanti; vicinitvā na passanti; apassitvā uposathaṃ karonti. Anāpatti. Te vematikā vicinanti; vicinitvā passanti; passitvā ekato [T 1.0263] uposathaṃ karonti. Anāpatti. Te vematikā vicinanti; vicinitvā passanti; passitvā pāṭekkaṃ uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te vematikā vicinanti; vicinitvā passanti; passitvā – “nassantete, vinassantete, ko tehi attho”ti – bhedapurekkhārā uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti thullaccayassa.

179. Here, monks, visiting monks see the manner of resident monks, their marks, their signs, and indications of their presence: a well-arranged couch and chair, a mattress and cushion, drinking water and water for use properly set out, and the precincts well-swept. Seeing this, they become doubtful: “Are there resident monks, or are there not?” Being doubtful, they do not investigate. Without investigating, they perform the Uposatha. There is an offense of wrong-doing. Being doubtful, they investigate. Having investigated, they do not see them. Not seeing them, they perform the Uposatha. There is no offense. Being doubtful, they investigate. Having investigated, they see them. Seeing them, they perform the Uposatha together. There is no offense. Being doubtful, they investigate. Having investigated, they see them. Seeing them, they perform the Uposatha separately. There is an offense of wrong-doing. Being doubtful, they investigate. Having investigated, they see them. Seeing them, thinking, “Let them perish, let them be destroyed, what use are they?” they perform the Uposatha with the intention of causing a schism. There is a grave offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, āgantukā bhikkhū suṇanti āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āvāsikākāraṃ, āvāsikaliṅgaṃ, āvāsikanimittaṃ, āvāsikuddesaṃ, caṅkamantānaṃ padasaddaṃ, sajjhāyasaddaṃ, ukkāsitasaddaṃ, khipitasaddaṃ; sutvā vematikā honti – “atthi nu kho āvāsikā bhikkhū natthi nu kho”ti. Te vematikā na vicinanti; avicinitvā uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te vematikā vicinanti; vicinitvā na passanti; apassitvā uposathaṃ [M 0.0186] karonti. Anāpatti. Te vematikā vicinanti; vicinitvā passanti; passitvā ekato uposathaṃ karonti. Anāpatti. Te vematikā vicinanti; vicinitvā passanti; passitvā pāṭekkaṃ uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te vematikā vicinanti; vicinitvā passanti; passitvā – “nassantete, vinassantete, ko tehi attho”ti – bhedapurekkhārā uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti thullaccayassa.

Here, monks, visiting monks hear the manner of resident monks, their marks, their signs, and indications of their presence: the sound of footsteps of those walking in meditation, the sound of recitation, the sound of coughing, and the sound of sneezing. Hearing this, they become doubtful: “Are there resident monks or are there not?” Being doubtful, they do not investigate. Without investigating, they perform the Uposatha. There is an offense of wrong-doing. Being doubtful, they investigate. Having investigated, they do not see them. Not seeing them, they perform the Uposatha. There is no offense. Being doubtful, they investigate. Having investigated, they see them. Seeing them, they perform the Uposatha together. There is no offense. Being doubtful, they investigate. Having investigated, they see them. Seeing them, they perform the Uposatha separately. There is an offense of wrong-doing. Being doubtful, they investigate. Having investigated, they see them. Seeing them, thinking, “Let them perish, let them be destroyed, what use are they?” they perform the Uposatha with the intention of causing a schism. There is a grave offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikā bhikkhū passanti āgantukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āgantukākāraṃ, āgantukaliṅgaṃ, āgantukanimittaṃ, āgantukuddesaṃ, aññātakaṃ pattaṃ, aññātakaṃ [V 0.0174] cīvaraṃ, aññātakaṃ nisīdanaṃ, pādānaṃ dhotaṃ, udakanissekaṃ; passitvā [T 1.0264] vematikā honti – “atthi nu kho āgantukā bhikkhū natthi nu kho”ti. Te vematikā na vicinanti; avicinitvā uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te vematikā vicinanti; vicinitvā na passanti; apassitvā uposathaṃ karonti. Anāpatti. Te vematikā vicinanti; vicinitvā passanti; passitvā ekato uposathaṃ karonti. Anāpatti. Te vematikā vicinanti; vicinitvā passanti; passitvā pāṭekkaṃ uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te vematikā vicinanti; vicinitvā passanti; passitvā – “nassantete, vinassantete, ko tehi attho”ti – bhedapurekkhārā uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti thullaccayassa.

Here, monks, resident monks see the manner of visiting monks, their characteristic marks, signs of them, indications of them, an unfamiliar bowl, an unfamiliar robe, an unfamiliar sitting cloth, and the dripping of water from washed feet. Seeing this, they become doubtful: “Are there visiting monks or not?” Being doubtful, they do not investigate. Without investigating, they perform the Uposatha. There is an offense of wrong-doing. Being doubtful, they investigate. Having investigated, they do not see them. Not seeing them, they perform the Uposatha. There is no offense. Being doubtful, they investigate. Having investigated, they see them. Seeing them, they perform the Uposatha together. There is no offense. Being doubtful, they investigate. Having investigated, they see them. Seeing them, they perform the Uposatha separately. There is an offense of wrong-doing. Being doubtful, they investigate. Having investigated, they see them. Seeing them, they think, “May these monks perish, may they be destroyed, what use are they?” and perform the Uposatha with the intention of causing dissension. There is a grave offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikā bhikkhū suṇanti āgantukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āgantukākāraṃ, āgantukaliṅgaṃ, āgantukanimittaṃ, āgantukuddesaṃ, āgacchantānaṃ padasaddaṃ, upāhanapapphoṭanasaddaṃ, ukkāsitasaddaṃ, khipitasaddaṃ; sutvā vematikā honti – “atthi nu kho āgantukā bhikkhū natthi nu kho”ti. Te vematikā na vicinanti; avicinitvā uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te vematikā vicinanti; vicinitvā na passanti; apassitvā uposathaṃ karonti. Anāpatti. Te vematikā vicinanti; vicinitvā passanti; passitvā ekato uposathaṃ karonti. Anāpatti. Te vematikā vicinanti; vicinitvā passanti; passitvā pāṭekkaṃ uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te vematikā vicinanti; vicinitvā passanti; passitvā – “nassantete, vinassantete[T 1.0265], ko tehi attho”ti – bhedapurekkhārā uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti thullaccayassa[P 1.0134].

Furthermore, monks, resident monks hear the manner of visiting monks, their characteristic marks, signs of them, indications of them, the sound of footsteps of those arriving, the sound of shaking sandals, the sound of coughing, and the sound of sneezing. Having heard this, they become doubtful: “Are there visiting monks or not?” Being doubtful, they do not investigate. Without investigating, they perform the Uposatha. There is an offense of wrong-doing. Being doubtful, they investigate. Having investigated, they do not see them. Not seeing them, they perform the Uposatha. There is no offense. Being doubtful, they investigate. Having investigated, they see them. Seeing them, they perform the Uposatha together. There is no offense. Being doubtful, they investigate. Having investigated, they see them. Seeing them, they perform the Uposatha separately. There is an offense of wrong-doing. Being doubtful, they investigate. Having investigated, they see them. Seeing them, they think, “May these monks perish, may they be destroyed, what use are they?” and perform the Uposatha with the intention of causing dissension. There is a grave offense.

Liṅgādidassanaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Exposition on Signs, etc., is concluded.

102. Nānāsaṃvāsakādīhi uposathakaraṇaṃ

102. Performing the Uposatha with those of different communions, etc.

180. Idha [M 0.0187] pana, bhikkhave, āgantukā bhikkhū passanti āvāsike bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsake. Te samānasaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhanti; samānasaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhitvā na pucchanti; apucchitvā ekato uposathaṃ karonti. Anāpatti. Te pucchanti; pucchitvā nābhivitaranti; anabhivitaritvā ekato uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te pucchanti; pucchitvā nābhivitaranti; anabhivitaritvā pāṭekkaṃ uposathaṃ karonti. Anāpatti.

180. Furthermore, monks, visiting monks see resident monks who are of different communions. They acquire the view that they are of the same communion; having acquired the view that they are of the same communion, they do not ask. Without asking, they perform the Uposatha together. There is no offense. They ask; having asked, they cannot convince them; not having convinced them, they perform the Uposatha together. There is an offense of wrong-doing. They ask; having asked, they cannot convince them; not having convinced them, they perform the Uposatha separately. There is no offense.

Idha [V 0.0175] pana, bhikkhave, āgantukā bhikkhū passanti āvāsike bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsake. Te nānāsaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhanti; nānāsaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhitvā na pucchanti; apucchitvā ekato uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te pucchanti; pucchitvā abhivitaranti; abhivitaritvā pāṭekkaṃ uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te pucchanti; pucchitvā abhivitaranti; abhivitaritvā ekato uposathaṃ karonti. Anāpatti.

Furthermore, monks, visiting monks see resident monks who are of the same communion. They acquire the view that they are of different communions; having acquired that view, they do not ask. Without asking, they perform the Uposatha together. There is an offense of wrong-doing. They ask; having asked, they convince them; having convinced them, they perform the Uposatha separately. There is an offense of wrong-doing. They ask; having asked, they convince them; having convinced them, they perform the Uposatha together. There is no offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikā bhikkhū passanti āgantuke bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsake. Te samānasaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhanti; samānasaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhitvā na pucchanti; apucchitvā ekato uposathaṃ karonti. Anāpatti. Te pucchanti; pucchitvā nābhivitaranti; anabhivitaritvā ekato uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te pucchanti; pucchitvā nābhivitaranti[T 1.0266]; anabhivitaritvā pāṭekkaṃ uposathaṃ karonti. Anāpatti.

Furthermore, monks, resident monks see visiting monks who are of different communions. They acquire the view that they are of the same communion; having acquired that view, they do not ask. Without asking, they perform the Uposatha together. There is no offense. They ask; having asked, they cannot convince them; not having convinced them, they perform the Uposatha together. There is an offense of wrong-doing. They ask; having asked, they cannot convince them; not having convinced them, they perform the Uposatha separately. There is no offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikā bhikkhū passanti āgantuke bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsake. Te nānāsaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhanti; nānāsaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhitvā na pucchanti; apucchitvā ekato uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te pucchanti; pucchitvā abhivitaranti; abhivitaritvā pāṭekkaṃ uposathaṃ karonti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te pucchanti; pucchitvā abhivitaranti; abhivitaritvā ekato uposathaṃ karonti. Anāpatti.

Furthermore, monks, resident monks see visiting monks who are of the same communion. They acquire the view that they are of different communions; having acquired that view, they do not ask. Without asking, they perform the Uposatha together. There is an offense of wrong-doing. They ask; having asked, they convince them; having convinced them, they perform the Uposatha separately. There is an offense of wrong-doing. They ask; having asked, they convince them; having convinced them, they perform the Uposatha together. There is no offense.

Nānāsaṃvāsakādīhi uposathakaraṇaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section on performing the Uposatha with those of different communions and so forth is concluded.

103. Nagantabbavāro

103. The Section on What Should Not Be Gone To

181. Na, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave[M 0.0188], tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā.

181. Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from a residence with monks to a residence without monks, except by the Saṅgha, except in case of danger. Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from a residence with monks to a non-residence without monks, except by the Saṅgha, except in case of danger. Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from a residence with monks to either a residence or a non-residence without monks, except by the Saṅgha, except in case of danger.

Na[V 0.0176], bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā anāvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā anāvāsā abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā anāvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from a non-residence with monks to a residence without monks, except with the Saṅgha, except in case of danger. Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from a non-residence with monks to a non-residence without monks, except with the Saṅgha, except in case of danger. Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from a non-residence with monks to either a residence or a non-residence without monks, except with the Saṅgha, except in case of danger.

Na, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave[P 1.0135], tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā abhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from either a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks to a residence without monks, except with the Saṅgha, except in case of danger. Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from either a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks to a non-residence without monks, except with the Saṅgha, except in case of danger. Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from either a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks to either a residence or a non-residence without monks, except with the Saṅgha, except in case of danger.

Na, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe [T 1.0267] sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from a residence with monks to a residence with monks where there are monks of different communions, except with the Saṅgha, except in case of danger. Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from a residence with monks to a non-residence with monks where there are monks of different communions, except with the Saṅgha, except in case of danger. Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from a residence with monks to a residence or a non-residence with monks where there are monks of different communions, except with the Saṅgha, except in case of danger.

Na, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe [M 0.0189] sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from a non-residence with monks to a residence with monks where there are monks of different communions, except with the Saṅgha, except in case of danger. Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from a non-residence with monks to a non-residence with monks where there are monks of different communions, except with the Saṅgha, except in case of danger. Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from a non-residence with monks to a residence or a non-residence with monks where there are monks of different communions, except with the Saṅgha, except in case of danger.

Na, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe [V 0.0177] sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from a residence with monks or from a non-residence with monks to a residence with monks where there are monks of different communions, except with the Saṅgha, except in case of danger. Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should not go from a residence with monks or from a non-residence with monks to a non-residence with monks where there are monks of different communions, except with the Saṅgha, except in case of danger. Nagantabbavāro niṭṭhito.

The Section on What Should Not Be Gone To is concluded.

104. Gantabbavāro

104. The Section on What Should Be Gone To

182. Gantabbo, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā – “sakkomi ajjeva gantu”nti. Gantabbo, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko anāvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā – “sakkomi ajjeva gantu”nti.

182. Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should go from a residence with monks to a residence with monks, where there are monks of the same communion, if one should know, 'I am able to go there today.' Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should go from a residence with monks to a non-residence with monks... or to a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks, where there are monks of the same communion, if one should know, 'I am able to go there today.'

Gantabbo, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko [T 1.0268] āvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā – “sakkomi ajjeva gantu”nti.

Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should go from a non-residence with monks to a residence with monks... or to a non-residence with monks... or to a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks, where there are monks of the same communion, if one should know, 'I am able to go there today.'

Gantabbo, bhikkhave, tadahuposathe sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko āvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā – “sakkomi ajjeva gantu”nti.

Monks, on that Uposatha day, one should go from a residence with monks or from a non-residence with monks to a residence with monks... or to a non-residence with monks... or to a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks, where there are monks of the same communion, if one should know, 'I am able to go there today.'

Gantabbavāro niṭṭhito.

The Section on What Should Be Gone To is concluded.

105. Vajjanīyapuggalasandassanā

105. The Exposition of Individuals to be Avoided

183. Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā nisinnaparisāya pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Yo uddiseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na sikkhamānāya…pe… na sāmaṇerassa [M 0.0190] …pe… na sāmaṇeriyā…pe… na sikkhāpaccakkhātakassa…pe… na antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannakassa nisinnaparisāya pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Yo uddiseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

183. Monks, the Pātimokkha should not be recited in an assembly where a bhikkhunī is seated. Whichever monk should recite it, commits an offense of wrong conduct. It should not be recited in an assembly where a female probationer is seated... a male novice... a female novice... one who has renounced the training... or one who has committed an ultimate offense. Whichever monk should recite it, commits an offense of wrong conduct.

Na [V 0.0178] āpattiyā adassane ukkhittakassa nisinnaparisāya pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Yo uddiseyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo. Na āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittakassa nisinnaparisāya…pe… na pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittakassa nisinnaparisāya pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Yo uddiseyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo.

The Pātimokkha should not be recited in an assembly where a monk suspended for not seeing an offense is seated. Whichever monk should recite it is to be dealt with according to the Dhamma. The Pātimokkha should not be recited in an assembly where a monk suspended for not making amends for an offense is seated... nor where a monk suspended for not relinquishing a bad view is seated. Whichever monk should recite it is to be dealt with according to the Dhamma.

Na paṇḍakassa nisinnaparisāya pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Yo uddiseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na theyyasaṃvāsakassa…pe… [P 1.0136] na titthiyapakkantakassa…pe… na tiracchānagatassa…pe… [T 1.0269] na mātughātakassa…pe… na pitughātakassa…pe… na arahantaghātakassa…pe… na bhikkhunidūsakassa…pe… na saṅghabhedakassa…pe… na lohituppādakassa…pe… na ubhatobyañjanakassa nisinnaparisāya pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbaṃ. Yo uddiseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

The Pātimokkha should not be recited in an assembly in which a paṇḍaka is seated. A bhikkhu who recites it commits a dukkaṭa offense. The Pātimokkha should not be recited in an assembly in which one who lives in communion by theft is seated... nor one who has gone over to another sect... nor an animal... nor a matricide... nor a patricide... nor a murderer of an arahant... nor a defiler of a bhikkhunī... nor a schismatic... nor one who has maliciously shed the Buddha's blood... nor a person with both male and female characteristics is seated. A bhikkhu who recites it commits a dukkaṭa offense.

Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikapārisuddhidānena uposatho kātabbo, aññatra avuṭṭhitāya parisāya. Na ca, bhikkhave, anuposathe uposatho kātabbo, aññatra saṅghasāmaggiyāti.

Bhikkhus, the Uposatha should not be performed by conveying the purity of one on probation, except when the assembly has not yet dispersed. And, bhikkhus, the Uposatha should not be performed on a non-Uposatha day, except for the purpose of Saṅgha reunification.

Vajjanīyapuggalasandassanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of Individuals to be Avoided is concluded.

Tatiyabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The Third Recitation Section is concluded.

Uposathakkhandhako dutiyo.

The Uposatha Chapter, the Second.

106. Tassuddānaṃ

106. The summary thereof:

Titthiyā bimbisāro ca, sannipatituṃ tuṇhikā;

Dhammaṃ raho pātimokkhaṃ, devasikaṃ tadā sakiṃ.

Heretics and Bimbisāra, permission to assemble, silence; The Dhamma, solitude, the Pātimokkha; then daily, and once.

Yathāparisā samaggaṃ, sāmaggī maddakucchi ca;

Sīmā mahatī nadiyā, anu dve khuddakāni ca.

According to the assembly, the united, harmony, and Maddakucchi; A boundary, a great one, one on a river; in every parish, two, and small ones.

Navā [V 0.0179] rājagahe ceva, sīmā avippavāsanā;

Sammanne sammane (ka.) paṭhamaṃ sīmaṃ, pacchā sīmaṃ samūhane.

Junior bhikkhus, and in Rājagaha, the boundary of not living apart; First establishing a boundary, afterwards removing a boundary.

Asammatā [M 0.0191] gāmasīmā, nadiyā samudde sare;

Udakukkhepo bhindanti, tathevajjhottharanti ca.

Unestablished are: the village boundary, river, sea, natural lake, and water-splash boundaries; Intersecting boundaries, and likewise overlapping them.

Kati [T 1.0270] kammāni uddeso, savarā asatīpi ca;

Dhammaṃ vinayaṃ tajjenti, puna vinayatajjanā.

How many acts, how many recitations; danger, and reciting in brief even without it; Teaching Dhamma and asking Vinaya uninvited; threatening, and again, threatening with the Vinaya.

Codanā kate okāse, adhammappaṭikkosanā;

Catupañcaparā āvi, sañcicca cepi vāyame.

Accusation without leave, and with leave having been granted; protesting an act against the Dhamma; four or five protesting; speaking aloud, resolving in the heart; intentionally not being heard, and striving to be heard.

Sagahaṭṭhā anajjhiṭṭhā, codanamhi na jānati;

Sambahulā na jānanti, sajjukaṃ na ca gacchare.

With laypeople, unrequested; at Codana; one does not know; many dwelling who do not know; a same-day messenger, and not wishing to go.

Katimī kīvatikā dūre, ārocetuñca nassari;

Uklāpaṃ āsanaṃ dīpo, disā añño bahussuto.

How many days, how many bhikkhus, a distant place; announcing, and forgetting the date; Rubbish, a seat, a lamp; a journey, another learned one.

Sajjukaṃ sajjuvassaruposatho (ka.) vassuposatho, suddhikammañca ñātakā;

Gaggo catutayo dveko, āpattisabhāgā sari.

A same-day messenger, the rains-residence, Uposatha, purity, and a formal act; Relatives, Gagga; for four, three, two, and one; An offense, a similar one, and remembering.

Sabbo saṅgho vematiko, na jānanti bahussuto;

Bahū samasamā thokā, parisā avuṭṭhitāya ca.

The entire Saṅgha; doubtful; they do not know; a learned one; many; an equal number; few; and before the assembly has risen.

Ekaccā vuṭṭhitā sabbā, jānanti ca vematikā;

Kappatevāti kukkuccā, jānaṃ passaṃ suṇanti ca.

Some having risen; all; and they know; the doubtful; worrying, 'Is it allowable?'; knowing; seeing; and hearing.

Āvāsikena āgantu, cātupannaraso puna;

Pāṭipado pannaraso, liṅgasaṃvāsakā ubho.

With the resident; the visitor; the fourteenth; the fifteenth; again, the first day; the fifteenth; the sign of co-residents; both communions.

Pārivāsānuposatho[V 0.0180], aññatra saṅghasāmaggiyā;

Ete vibhattā uddānā, vatthuvibhūtakāraṇāti.

Probationers; on a non-Uposatha day; except for the Saṅgha's harmony. These summaries have been set out for the purpose of clarifying the subject matters.

Imasmiṃ khandhake vatthūni chaasīti.

In this chapter, there are eighty-six subject matters.

Uposathakkhandhako niṭṭhito.

The Chapter on the Uposatha is concluded.

3. Vassūpanāyikakkhandhako

3. The Chapter on Undertaking the Rains Residence

107. Vassūpanāyikānujānanā

107. Authorization for Undertaking the Rains Residence

184. Tena [T 1.0271][P 1.0137][M 0.0192][V 0.0181] samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ vassāvāso apaññatto hoti. Teidha bhikkhū hemantampi gimhampi vassampi cārikaṃ caranti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā hemantampi gimhampi vassampi cārikaṃ carissanti, haritāni tiṇāni sammaddantā, ekindriyaṃ jīvaṃ viheṭhentā, bahū khuddake pāṇe saṅghātaṃ āpādentā. Ime hi nāma aññatitthiyā durakkhātadhammā vassāvāsaṃ allīyissanti saṅkasāyissanti. Ime hi nāma sakuntakā rukkhaggesu kulāvakāni karitvā vassāvāsaṃ allīyissanti saṅkasāyissanti saṅkāsayissanti (sī. syā.). Ime pana samaṇā sakyaputtiyā hemantampi gimhampi vassampi cārikaṃ caranti, haritāni tiṇāni sammaddantā, ekindriyaṃ jīvaṃ viheṭhentā, bahū khuddake pāṇe saṅghātaṃ āpādentā”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vassaṃ upagantu”nti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kadā nu kho vassaṃ upagantabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vassāne vassaṃ upagantunti.

184. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary. Now at that time, the rains-residence had not been prescribed for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One. Those bhikkhus wandered on tour during the winter, the summer, and the rains. People complained, criticized, and grumbled: “How can the Sakyan ascetics wander on tour during the winter, the summer, and the rains, trampling green grass, harming one-facultied life, and causing the destruction of many small creatures? Indeed, these followers of other sects, whose teachings are poorly proclaimed, will settle down and remain for the rains-residence. Indeed, these birds, having made nests in the treetops, will settle down and remain for the rains-residence. But these Sakyan ascetics wander on tour during the winter, the summer, and the rains, trampling green grass, harming one-facultied life, and causing the destruction of many small creatures!” The bhikkhus heard those people complaining, criticizing, and grumbling. Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the bhikkhus: “I allow, bhikkhus, to enter upon the rains.” Then this thought occurred to the bhikkhus: “When, indeed, should the rains be entered upon?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, bhikkhus, to enter upon the rains during the rainy season.”

Atha [T 1.0272] kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kati nu kho vassūpanāyikā”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ

Then this thought occurred to the bhikkhus: “How many commencements of the rains-residence are there?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Ārocesuṃ. Dvemā, bhikkhave, vassūpanāyikā – purimikā, pacchimikā. Aparajjugatāya āsāḷhiyā purimikā upagantabbā, māsagatāya āsāḷhiyā pacchimikā upagantabbā – imā kho, bhikkhave, dve vassūpanāyikāti.

“There are, bhikkhus, these two commencements of the rains-residence: the earlier and the later. The earlier is to be entered upon on the day after the full moon of Āsāḷha; the later is to be entered upon on the day after a month has passed since the full moon of Āsāḷha. These, bhikkhus, are the two commencements of the rains-residence.”

Vassūpanāyikānujānanā niṭṭhitā.

The Authorization for Undertaking the Rains Residence is concluded.

108. Vassāne cārikāpaṭikkhepādi

108. The Prohibition of Wandering During the Rains, and So On

185. Tena [P 1.0138][V 0.0182] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū vassaṃ upagantvā antarāvassaṃ cārikaṃ caranti. Manussā tatheva ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi [M 0.0193] nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā hemantampi gimhampi vassampi cārikaṃ carissanti, haritāni tiṇāni sammaddantā, ekindriyaṃ jīvaṃ viheṭhentā, bahū khuddake pāṇe saṅghātaṃ āpādentā. Ime hi nāma aññatitthiyā durakkhātadhammā vassāvāsaṃ allīyissanti saṅkasāyissanti. Ime hi nāma sakuntakā rukkhaggesu kulāvakāni karitvā vassāvāsaṃ allīyissanti saṅkasāyissanti. Ime pana samaṇā sakyaputtiyā hemantampi gimhampi vassampi cārikaṃ caranti, haritāni tiṇāni sammaddantā, ekindriyaṃ jīvaṃ viheṭhentā, bahū khuddake pāṇe saṅghātaṃ āpādentā”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū [T 1.0273] vassaṃ upagantvā antarāvassaṃ cārikaṃ carissantī”ti? Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, vassaṃ upagantvā purimaṃ vā temāsaṃ pacchimaṃ vā temāsaṃ avasitvā cārikā pakkamitabbā. Yo pakkameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

185. Now at that time the group-of-six bhikkhus, having entered the rains residence, went wandering during the rains. People complained, grumbled, and criticized: “How can these Sakyan ascetics wander during the winter, the summer, and the rains, trampling green grass, harming one-facultied living beings, and destroying many small creatures? Ascetics of other sects, even with their poorly proclaimed Dhamma, settle down and abide during the rains residence. Even birds, having made nests in the treetops, settle down and abide during the rains residence. But these Sakyan ascetics wander during the winter, the summer, and the rains, trampling green grass, harming one-facultied living beings, and destroying many small creatures.” The bhikkhus heard those people complaining, grumbling, and criticizing. Those bhikkhus who were modest… complained, grumbled, and criticized: “How can the group-of-six bhikkhus, having entered the rains residence, go wandering during the rains?” Then those bhikkhus reported the matter to the Blessed One. Then, on that occasion, in that connection, the Blessed One gave a Dhamma talk and addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, having entered the rains residence, one should not depart on a tour without having remained for either the first three months or the last three months. Whoever departs commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

186. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū na icchanti vassaṃ upagantuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, vassaṃ na upagantabbaṃ. Yo na upagaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

186. At that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus did not wish to enter the rains residence. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, the rains residence must be entered. Whoever does not enter commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū tadahu vassūpanāyikāya vassaṃ anupagantukāmā sañcicca āvāsaṃ atikkamanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, tadahu vassūpanāyikāya vassaṃ anupagantukāmena sañcicca āvāso atikkamitabbo. Yo atikkameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, the bhikkhus of the group of six, not wishing to enter the rains-residence on that day of entering the rains, intentionally passed beyond the dwelling. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, on the day for entering the rains-residence, a dwelling is not to be intentionally passed beyond by one who does not wish to enter the rains-residence. Whoever passes beyond it commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro vassaṃ ukkaḍḍhitukāmo

At that time, King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha wished to postpone the rains-residence.

Bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – yadi panāyyā āgame juṇhe vassaṃ upagaccheyyunti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, rājūnaṃ anuvattitunti.

He sent a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: “It would be well if the venerable sirs would enter the rains-residence in the coming bright fortnight.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow compliance with kings.”

Vassāne cārikāpaṭikkhepādi niṭṭhitā.

The Prohibition of Wandering During the Rains, and So On, is Concluded.

109. Sattāhakaraṇīyānujānanā

109. Permission for Seven-Day Business

187. Atha [P 1.0139][V 0.0183] kho bhagavā rājagahe yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena sāvatthi tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena sāvatthi [M 0.0194][T 1.0274] tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena kosalesu janapade udenena upāsakena saṅghaṃ uddissa vihāro kārāpito hoti. So bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – “āgacchantu bhadantā, icchāmi dānañca dātuṃ, dhammañca sotuṃ, bhikkhū ca passitu”nti. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “bhagavatā, āvuso, paññattaṃ ‘na vassaṃ upagantvā purimaṃ vā temāsaṃ pacchimaṃ vā temāsaṃ avasitvā cārikā pakkamitabbā’ti. Āgametu udeno upāsako, yāva bhikkhū vassaṃ vasanti. Vassaṃvuṭṭhā āgamissanti. Sace panassa accāyikaṃ karaṇīyaṃ, tattheva āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ santike vihāraṃ patiṭṭhāpetū”ti. Udeno upāsako ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma bhadantā mayā pahite na āgacchissanti. Ahañhi dāyako kārako saṅghupaṭṭhāko”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū udenassa upāsakassa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sattannaṃ sattāhakaraṇīyena pahite gantuṃ, na tveva appahite. Bhikkhussa, bhikkhuniyā, sikkhamānāya, sāmaṇerassa, sāmaṇeriyā, upāsakassa, upāsikāya – anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imesaṃ sattannaṃ sattāhakaraṇīyena pahite gantuṃ, na tveva appahite. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo”.

187. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Rājagaha as long as he pleased, set out on a journey to Sāvatthī. Traveling stage by stage, he arrived at Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One stayed in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, in the Kosalan country, the lay follower Udena had a monastery built for the Sangha. He sent a messenger to the bhikkhus: “Come, venerable sirs, I wish to give a gift, to hear the Dhamma, and to see the bhikkhus.” The bhikkhus replied: “Friend, the Blessed One has laid down the rule: ‘Having entered the rains-residence, one should not set out on a journey without having stayed for either the first three months or the last three months.’ Let the lay follower Udena wait for as long as the bhikkhus are observing the rains-residence. Having completed the rains-residence, they will come. But if he has urgent business, let him establish the monastery there in the presence of the resident bhikkhus.” The lay follower Udena complained, grumbled, and criticized: “How is it that the venerable sirs will not come when sent for by me? For I am a donor, a worker, and a supporter of the Sangha.” The bhikkhus heard the lay follower Udena complaining, grumbling, and criticizing. Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then, on that occasion, in that connection, the Blessed One gave a talk on the Dhamma and addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow you to go when sent for by one of seven people for a matter to be attended to within seven days, but not when you are not sent for. A bhikkhu, a bhikkhunī, a female probationer, a male novice, a female novice, a male lay follower, or a female lay follower—Bhikkhus, I allow you to go when sent for by these seven for a matter to be attended to within seven days, but not when you are not sent for. A return must be made within seven days.”

188. Idha pana, bhikkhave, upāsakena [T 1.0275] saṅghaṃ uddissa vihāro kārāpito hoti. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “āgacchantu bhadantā, icchāmi dānañca dātuṃ, dhammañca sotuṃ, bhikkhū ca passitu”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, pahite, na tveva appahite. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

188. Moreover, bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, a lay follower has had a monastery built for the Sangha. If he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: ‘May the venerable sirs come. I wish to make a donation, to hear the Dhamma, and to see the bhikkhus,’ then, bhikkhus, when sent, you are to go for a matter to be attended to within seven days, but not when you are not sent. A return must be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, upāsakena saṅghaṃ uddissa aḍḍhayogo kārāpito hoti…pe… pāsādo kārāpito hoti… hammiyaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti… guhā kārāpitā hoti… pariveṇaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti… koṭṭhako kārāpito hoti… upaṭṭhānasālā kārāpitā hoti… aggisālā kārāpitā hoti… kappiyakuṭi kārāpitā hoti… vaccakuṭi kārāpitā hoti… caṅkamo kārāpito hoti [M 0.0195]… caṅkamanasālā kārāpitā hoti… udapāno kārāpito hoti [V 0.0184] … udapānasālā kārāpitā hoti… jantāgharaṃ kārāpitaṃ [P 1.0140] hoti… jantāgharasālā kārāpitā hoti… pokkharaṇī kārāpitā hoti… maṇḍapo kārāpito hoti… ārāmo kārāpito hoti… ārāmavatthu kārāpitaṃ hoti. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “āgacchantu bhadantā, icchāmi dānañca dātuṃ, dhammañca sotuṃ, bhikkhū ca passitu”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, pahite, na tveva appahite. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, herein a lay follower has had a lean-to dwelling built, dedicated to the Saṅgha... a storied building built... a terraced building built... a cave dug... an enclosure made... a gateway made... a service hall built... a fire hall built... a hut for allowable things built... a toilet built... a walking path made... a hall for walking built... a well dug... a hall by a well built... a steam-bath house built... a hall for a steam-bath house built... a pond made... a pavilion built... a park made... a site for a park made. If he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: ‘May the venerable sirs come. I wish to give alms, to hear the Dhamma, and to see the bhikkhus,’ then, bhikkhus, when invited, you should go on a seven-day business; but not, indeed, when uninvited. A return must be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, upāsakena sambahule bhikkhū uddissa…pe… ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ uddissa vihāro kārāpito hoti… aḍḍhayogo kārāpito hoti… pāsādo kārāpito hoti [T 1.0276]… hammiyaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti… guhā kārāpitā hoti… pariveṇaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti… koṭṭhako kārāpito hoti… upaṭṭhānasālā kārāpitā hoti… aggisālā kārāpitā hoti… kappiyakuṭi kārāpitā hoti… vaccakuṭi kārāpitā hoti… caṅkamo kārāpito hoti… caṅkamanasālā kārāpitā hoti… udapāno kārāpito hoti… udapānasālā kārāpitā hoti… jantāgharaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti… jantāgharasālā kārāpitā hoti… pokkharaṇī kārāpitā hoti… maṇḍapo kārāpito hoti… ārāmo kārāpito hoti… ārāmavatthu kārāpitaṃ hoti. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “āgacchantu bhadantā, icchāmi dānañca dātuṃ, dhammañca sotuṃ, bhikkhū ca passitu”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, pahite, na tveva appahite. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, herein a lay follower has had a monastery built, dedicated to many bhikkhus... or dedicated to a single bhikkhu... a lean-to dwelling built... a storied building built... a terraced building built... a cave dug... an enclosure made... a gateway made... a service hall built... a fire hall built... a hut for allowable things built... a toilet built... a walking path made... a hall for walking built... a well dug... a hall by a well built... a steam-bath house built... a hall for a steam-bath house built... a pond made... a pavilion built... a park made... a site for a park made. If he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: ‘May the venerable sirs come. I wish to give alms, to hear the Dhamma, and to see the bhikkhus,’ then, bhikkhus, when invited, you should go on a seven-day business; but not, indeed, when uninvited. A return must be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, upāsakena bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ uddissa…pe… sambahulā bhikkhuniyo uddissa…pe… ekaṃ bhikkhuniṃ uddissa…pe… sambahulā sikkhamānāyo uddissa…pe… ekaṃ sikkhamānaṃ uddissa…pe… sambahule sāmaṇere uddissa…pe… ekaṃ sāmaṇeraṃ uddissa…pe… sambahulā sāmaṇeriyo uddissa…pe… ekaṃ sāmaṇeriṃ uddissa vihāro kārāpito hoti…pe… aḍḍhayogo kārāpito hoti… pāsādo kārāpito hoti… hammiyaṃ [M 0.0196] kārāpitaṃ hoti… guhā kārāpitā hoti… pariveṇaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti… koṭṭhako kārāpito hoti… upaṭṭhānasālā kārāpitā hoti… aggisālā kārāpitā hoti [T 1.0277]… kappiyakuṭi kārāpitā hoti… caṅkamo kārāpito hoti… caṅkamanasālā kārāpitā hoti… udapāno kārāpito hoti… udapānasālā kārāpitā hoti… pokkharaṇī kārāpitā hoti… maṇḍapo kārāpito hoti… ārāmo kārāpito hoti… ārāmavatthu kārāpitaṃ hoti. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “āgacchantu bhadantā, icchāmi dānañca dātuṃ[V 0.0185], dhammañca sotuṃ, bhikkhū ca passitu”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, pahite, na tveva appahite. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, herein a lay follower has had a monastery built, dedicated to the community of bhikkhunīs... dedicated to many bhikkhunīs... dedicated to one bhikkhunī... dedicated to many female probationers... dedicated to one female probationer... dedicated to many male novices... dedicated to one male novice... dedicated to many female novices... dedicated to one female novice... a lean-to dwelling built... a storied building built... a terraced building built... a cave dug... an enclosure made... a gateway made... a service hall built... a fire hall built... a hut for allowable things built... a toilet built... a walking path made... a hall for walking built... a well dug... a hall by a well built... a steam-bath house built... a hall for a steam-bath house built... a pond made... a pavilion built... a park made... a site for a park made. If he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: ‘May the venerable sirs come. I wish to give alms, to hear the Dhamma, and to see the bhikkhus,’ then, bhikkhus, when invited, you should go on a seven-day business; but not, indeed, when uninvited. A return must be made within seven days.

189. Idha pana, bhikkhave, upāsakena attano atthāya nivesanaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti…pe… sayanigharaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti… udosito kārāpito hoti… aṭṭo kārāpito hoti… māḷo kārāpito hoti… āpaṇo kārāpito hoti… āpaṇasālā kārāpitā hoti… pāsādo kārāpito hoti… hammiyaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti… guhā kārāpitā hoti… pariveṇaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti… koṭṭhako kārāpito hoti… upaṭṭhānasālā kārāpitā hoti… aggisālā kārāpitā hoti… rasavatī kārāpitā hoti… caṅkamo kārāpito hoti… caṅkamanasālā kārāpitā hoti… udapāno kārāpito hoti… udapānasālā kārāpitā hoti… pokkharaṇī kārāpitā hoti… maṇḍapo kārāpito hoti… ārāmo kārāpito hoti [T 1.0278]… ārāmavatthu kārāpitaṃ hoti… puttassa vā vāreyyaṃ hoti… dhītuyā vā vāreyyaṃ hoti… gilāno vā hoti… abhiññātaṃ vā suttantaṃ bhaṇati. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – ‘āgacchantu bhadantā, imaṃ suttantaṃ pariyāpuṇissanti, purāyaṃ suttanto [P 1.0141] na palujjatī’ti. Aññataraṃ vā panassa kiccaṃ hoti – karaṇīyaṃ vā, so ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “āgacchantu bhadantā, icchāmi dānañca dātuṃ, dhammañca sotuṃ, bhikkhū ca passitu”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, pahite, na tveva appahite. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

189. Furthermore, bhikkhus, herein a lay follower has had a residence built for his own use... a sleeping chamber built... a storehouse built... a watchtower built... a pavilion built... a shop built... a hall for a shop built... a storied building built... a terraced building built... a cave dug... an enclosure made... a gateway made... a service hall built... a fire hall built... a kitchen built... a walking path made... a hall for walking built... a well dug... a hall by a well built... a pond made... a pavilion built... a park made... a site for a park made... or he wishes to arrange a marriage for his son... or he wishes to arrange a marriage for his daughter... or he is ill... or he recites a well-known discourse. If he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: ‘May the venerable sirs come and learn this discourse before it is lost.’ Or if that lay follower has some other business or task, and if he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: ‘May the venerable sirs come; I wish to give alms, to hear the Dhamma, and to see the bhikkhus,’ then, bhikkhus, when invited, you should go on a seven-day business; but not, indeed, when uninvited. A return must be made within seven days.

190. Idha [M 0.0197] pana, bhikkhave, upāsikāya saṅghaṃ uddissa vihāro kārāpito hoti. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi dānañca dātuṃ, dhammañca sotuṃ, bhikkhū ca passitu”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, pahite, na tveva appahite. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

190. Furthermore, O monks, a female lay follower has had a monastery built, dedicated to the Sangha. If she should send a messenger to the monks, saying: ‘May the venerable sirs come; I wish to give alms, to hear the Dhamma, and to see the monks,’ then, O monks, when sent, one should go on an affair of up to seven days, but not indeed when unsent. A return should be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, upāsikāya saṅghaṃ uddissa aḍḍhayogo kārāpito hoti…pe… pāsādo kārāpito hoti… hammiyaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti… guhā kārāpitā hoti… pariveṇaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti… koṭṭhako kārāpito hoti… upaṭṭhānasālā kārāpitā hoti… aggisālā kārāpitā hoti… kappiyakuṭi kārāpitā hoti… vaccakuṭi kārāpitā hoti… caṅkamo kārāpito hoti… caṅkamanasālā kārāpitā hoti… udapāno kārāpito hoti… udapānasālā [T 1.0279] kārāpitā hoti… jantāgharaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti… jantāgharasālā kārāpitā [V 0.0186] hoti… pokkharaṇī kārāpitā hoti… maṇḍapo kārāpito hoti… ārāmo kārāpito hoti… ārāmavatthu kārāpitaṃ hoti. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi dānañca dātuṃ, dhammañca sotuṃ, bhikkhū ca passitu”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, pahite, na tveva appahite. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, O monks, a female lay follower has had a building with a lean-to roof built, dedicated to the Sangha... or a storied building... a gabled mansion... a cave... an enclosure... a gatehouse... an assembly hall... a fire-hall... a steward's quarters... a toilet... a walkway... a hall for walking... a well... a well-house... a steam-bath house... a hall for the steam-bath house... a pond... a pavilion... a park... a site for a park. If she should send a messenger to the monks, saying: ‘May the venerable sirs come; I wish to give alms, to hear the Dhamma, and to see the monks,’ then, O monks, when sent, one should go on an affair of up to seven days, but not indeed when unsent. A return should be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, upāsikāya sambahule bhikkhū uddissa…pe… ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ uddissa…pe… bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ uddissa…pe… sambahulā bhikkhuniyo uddissa…pe… ekaṃ bhikkhuniṃ uddissa…pe… sambahulā sikkhamānāyo uddissa…pe… ekaṃ sikkhamānaṃ uddissa…pe… sambahule sāmaṇere uddissa…pe… ekaṃ sāmaṇeraṃ uddissa…pe… sambahulā sāmaṇeriyo uddissa…pe… ekaṃ sāmaṇeriṃ uddissa…pe….

Furthermore, O monks, a female lay follower has had a building constructed, dedicated to many monks... or to one monk... to the Sangha of nuns... to many nuns... to one nun... to many female probationers... to one female probationer... to many male novices... to one male novice... to many female novices... or to one female novice...

191. Idha pana, bhikkhave, upāsikāya attano atthāya nivesanaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti…pe… sayanigharaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti… udosito kārāpito hoti… aṭṭo kārāpito hoti… māḷo kārāpito hoti… āpaṇo kārāpito hoti… āpaṇasālā kārāpitā hoti… pāsādo kārāpito hoti… hammiyaṃ [M 0.0198] kārāpitaṃ hoti… guhā kārāpitā hoti… pariveṇaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti… koṭṭhako kārāpito hoti… upaṭṭhānasālā kārāpitā hoti… aggisālā kārāpitā hoti… rasavatī kārāpitā hoti… caṅkamo kārāpito hoti… caṅkamanasālā kārāpitā hoti… udapāno kārāpito hoti [T 1.0280]… udapānasālā kārāpitā hoti… pokkharaṇī kārāpitā hoti… maṇḍapo kārāpito hoti… ārāmo kārāpito hoti… ārāmavatthu kārāpitaṃ hoti… puttassa vā vāreyyaṃ hoti… dhītuyā vā vāreyyaṃ hoti… gilānā vā hoti… abhiññātaṃ vā suttantaṃ bhaṇati. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “āgacchantu ayyā, imaṃ suttantaṃ pariyāpuṇissanti, purāyaṃ suttanto palujjatī”ti. Aññataraṃ vā panassā kiccaṃ hoti karaṇīyaṃ vā, sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi dānañca dātuṃ, dhammañca sotuṃ, bhikkhū ca passitu”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, pahite, na tveva appahite. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

191. Furthermore, O monks, a female lay follower has had a house built for her own benefit… or a sleeping chamber… a storehouse… a watchtower… a hall… a shop… a shop-hall… a storied building… a gabled mansion… a cave… an enclosure… a gatehouse… an assembly hall… a fire-hall… a kitchen… a walkway… a hall for walking… a well… a well-house… a pond… a pavilion… a park… a site for a park… or she wishes to arrange a marriage for her son… or for her daughter… or she is ill… or she recites a renowned discourse. If she should send a messenger to the monks, saying, ‘May the venerable sirs come and learn this discourse before it perishes,’ or if she has some other business or duty to be done, and she should send a messenger to the monks, saying, ‘May the venerable sirs come; I wish to give alms, to hear the Dhamma, and to see the monks,’ then, O monks, when sent, one should go on an affair of up to seven days, but not indeed when unsent. A return should be made within seven days.

192.
