Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ uddissa…pe… bhikkhuniyā saṅghaṃ uddissa… sikkhamānāya saṅghaṃ uddissa… sāmaṇerena saṅghaṃ uddissa… sāmaṇeriyā saṅghaṃ uddissa [V 0.0187] … sambahule bhikkhū uddissa… ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ uddissa… bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ uddissa… sambahulā bhikkhuniyo uddissa… ekaṃ bhikkhuniṃ uddissa… sambahulā sikkhamānāyo uddissa… ekaṃ sikkhamānaṃ uddissa… sambahule sāmaṇere uddissa… ekaṃ sāmaṇeraṃ uddissa… sambahulā [P 1.0142] sāmaṇeriyo uddissa… ekaṃ sāmaṇeriṃ uddissa… attano atthāya vihāro kārāpito hoti…pe… aḍḍhayogo kārāpito hoti… pāsādo kārāpito hoti… hammiyaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti… guhā kārāpitā hoti… pariveṇaṃ kārāpitaṃ hoti [T 1.0281]… koṭṭhako kārāpito hoti… upaṭṭhānasālā kārāpitā hoti… aggisālā kārāpitā hoti… kappiyakuṭi kārāpitā hoti… caṅkamo kārāpito hoti… caṅkamanasālā kārāpitā hoti… udapāno kārāpito hoti… udapānasālā kārāpitā hoti… pokkharaṇī kārāpitā hoti… maṇḍapo kārāpito hoti… ārāmo kārāpito hoti… ārāmavatthu kārāpitaṃ hoti. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ [M 0.0199] santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya… “āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi dānañca dātuṃ, dhammañca sotuṃ, bhikkhū ca passitu”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, pahite, na tveva appahite. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabboti.

192. Furthermore, O monks, a monk has had a monastery built, dedicated to the Sangha... or a nun... a female probationer... a male novice... a female novice... or dedicated to many monks... to one monk... to the Sangha of nuns... to many nuns... to one nun... to many female probationers... to one female probationer... to many male novices... to one male novice... to many female novices... to one female novice... or for one's own benefit, a monastery has been built... or a building with a lean-to roof... a storied building... a gabled mansion... a cave... an enclosure... a gatehouse... an assembly hall... a fire-hall... a steward's quarters... a walkway... a hall for walking... a well... a well-house... a pond... a pavilion... a park... a site for a park. If that female novice should send a messenger to the monks, saying, ‘May the venerable sirs come; I wish to give alms, to hear the Dhamma, and to see the monks,’ then, O monks, when sent, one should go on an affair of up to seven days, but not indeed when unsent. A return should be made within seven days.

Sattāhakaraṇīyānujānatā niṭṭhitā.

The allowance for a seven-day affair is concluded.

110. Pañcannaṃ appahitepi anujānanā

110. Permission for five even when uninvited.

193. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu gilāno hoti. So bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – “ahañhi gilāno, āgacchantu bhikkhū, icchāmi bhikkhūnaṃ āgata”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ sattāhakaraṇīyena appahitepi gantuṃ, pageva pahite. Bhikkhussa, bhikkhuniyā, sikkhamānāya, sāmaṇerassa, sāmaṇeriyā – anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imesaṃ pañcannaṃ sattāhakaraṇīyena appahitepi gantuṃ, pageva pahite. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

193. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu was ill. He sent a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'I am indeed ill; let the bhikkhus come, I desire the coming of the bhikkhus.' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, I allow five persons to go on account of a seven-day matter even when not sent for, how much more so when sent for. A bhikkhu, a bhikkhunī, a sikkhamānā, a sāmaṇera, and a sāmaṇerī—Bhikkhus, I allow these five to go on account of a seven-day matter even when not sent for, how much more so when sent for. A return must be made within seven days.'

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu gilāno hoti. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi gilāno, āgacchantu bhikkhū, icchāmi bhikkhūnaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva [T 1.0282] pahite – “gilānabhattaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, gilānupaṭṭhākabhattaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, gilānabhesajjaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, pucchissāmi vā, upaṭṭhahissāmi vā”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Teaching, a bhikkhu is ill. If he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'I am indeed ill; let the bhikkhus come, I desire the coming of the bhikkhus,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on account of a seven-day matter, even if not sent for, how much more so when sent for, with the thought: 'I will seek food for the ill person, or food for the one attending the ill person, or medicine for the ill person; or I will inquire, or I will attend to him.' A return must be made within seven days.

Idha [V 0.0188] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa anabhirati uppannā hoti. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “anabhirati me uppannā, āgacchantu bhikkhū, icchāmi bhikkhūnaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “anabhirataṃ vūpakāsessāmi vā, vūpakāsāpessāmi vā, dhammakathaṃ vāssa karissāmī”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Teaching, discontent has arisen in a bhikkhu. If he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'Discontent has arisen in me; let the bhikkhus come, I desire the coming of the bhikkhus,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on account of a seven-day matter, even if not sent for, how much more so when sent for, with the thought: 'I will either lead the discontented one into seclusion, or have him led into seclusion, or I will give him a Dhamma talk.' A return must be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa kukkuccaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “kukkuccaṃ me uppannaṃ, āgacchantu bhikkhū, icchāmi bhikkhūnaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “kukkuccaṃ vinodessāmi vā, vinodāpessāmi vā, dhammakathaṃ vāssa karissāmī”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Teaching, remorse has arisen in a bhikkhu. If he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'Remorse has arisen in me; let the bhikkhus come, I desire the coming of the bhikkhus,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on account of a seven-day matter, even if not sent for, how much more so when sent for, with the thought: 'I will either dispel his remorse, or have it dispelled, or I will give him a Dhamma talk.' A return must be made within seven days.

Idha [M 0.0200] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ [P 1.0143] santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “diṭṭhigataṃ me uppannaṃ, āgacchantu bhikkhū, icchāmi bhikkhūnaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “diṭṭhigataṃ vivecessāmi vā, vivecāpessāmi vā, dhammakathaṃ vāssa karissāmī”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Teaching, a wrong view has arisen in a bhikkhu. If he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'A wrong view has arisen in me; let the bhikkhus come, I desire the coming of the bhikkhus,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on account of a seven-day matter, even if not sent for, how much more so when sent for, with the thought: 'I will either resolve his wrong view, or have it resolved, or I will give him a Dhamma talk.' A return must be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu garudhammaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti parivāsāraho. So [T 1.0283] ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi garudhammaṃ ajjhāpanno parivāsāraho, āgacchantu bhikkhū, icchāmi bhikkhūnaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “parivāsadānaṃ ussukkaṃ karissāmi vā, anussāvessāmi vā, gaṇapūrako vā bhavissāmī”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Teaching, a bhikkhu has committed a grave offense and is deserving of probation. If he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'I have indeed committed a grave offense and am deserving of probation; let the bhikkhus come, I desire the coming of the bhikkhus,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on account of a seven-day matter, even if not sent for, how much more so when sent for, with the thought: 'I will either make an effort for the granting of probation, or make the formal announcement, or be one who completes the quorum.' A return must be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mūlāya paṭikassanāraho hoti. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi mūlāya paṭikassanāraho, āgacchantu bhikkhū, icchāmi bhikkhūnaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “mūlāya paṭikassanaṃ ussukkaṃ karissāmi vā, anussāvessāmi vā, gaṇapūrako vā bhavissāmī”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Teaching, a bhikkhu is deserving of being sent back to the beginning. If he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'I am indeed deserving of being sent back to the beginning; let the bhikkhus come, I desire the coming of the bhikkhus,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on account of a seven-day matter, even if not sent for, how much more so when sent for, with the thought: 'I will either make an effort for the sending back to the beginning, or make the formal announcement, or be one who completes the quorum.' A return must be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mānattāraho hoti. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi mānattāraho, āgacchantu bhikkhū, icchāmi bhikkhūnaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “mānattadānaṃ ussukkaṃ karissāmi vā, anussāvessāmi vā, gaṇapūrako vā bhavissāmī”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Teaching, a bhikkhu is deserving of penance. If he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'I am indeed deserving of penance; let the bhikkhus come, I desire the coming of the bhikkhus,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on account of a seven-day matter, even if not sent for, how much more so when sent for, with the thought: 'I will either make an effort for the granting of penance, or make the formal announcement, or be one who completes the quorum.' A return must be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu abbhānāraho hoti. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya [V 0.0189] – “ahañhi abbhānāraho, āgacchantu bhikkhū, icchāmi bhikkhūnaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “abbhānaṃ ussukkaṃ karissāmi vā, anussāvessāmi [T 1.0284] vā, gaṇapūrako vā bhavissāmī”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Teaching, a bhikkhu is deserving of rehabilitation. If he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'I am indeed deserving of rehabilitation; let the bhikkhus come, I desire the coming of the bhikkhus,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on account of a seven-day matter, even if not sent for, how much more so when sent for, with the thought: 'I will either make an effort for the rehabilitation, or make the formal announcement, or be one who completes the quorum.' A return must be made within seven days.

Idha [M 0.0201] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa saṅgho kammaṃ kattukāmo hoti tajjanīyaṃ vā, niyassaṃ vā, pabbājanīyaṃ vā, paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā, ukkhepanīyaṃ vā. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “saṅgho me kammaṃ kattukāmo, āgacchantu bhikkhū, icchāmi bhikkhūnaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “kinti nu [P 1.0144] kho saṅgho kammaṃ na kareyya, lahukāya vā pariṇāmeyyā”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Teaching, the Saṅgha wishes to carry out a formal act against a bhikkhu—whether an act of censure, an act of subordination, an act of banishment, an act of reconciliation, or an act of suspension. If that bhikkhu should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'The Saṅgha wishes to carry out a formal act against me; let the bhikkhus come, I desire the coming of the bhikkhus,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on account of a seven-day matter, even if not sent for, how much more so when sent for, with the thought: 'How might the Saṅgha not carry out the formal act, or how might it be changed to a lighter one?' A return must be made within seven days.

Kataṃ vā panassa hoti saṅghena kammaṃ tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā pabbājanīyaṃ vā paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā ukkhepanīyaṃ vā. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya “saṅgho me kammaṃ akāsi, āgacchantu bhikkhū, icchāmi bhikkhūnaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “kinti nu kho sammā vatteyya, lomaṃ pāteyya, netthāraṃ vatteyya, saṅgho taṃ kammaṃ paṭippassambheyyā”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Or, if the Saṅgha has performed an act against a bhikkhu—whether of censure, subordination, banishment, reconciliation, or suspension—and he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'The Saṅgha has performed an act against me; let the bhikkhus come, I desire the coming of the bhikkhus,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on a matter that can be settled within seven days, even if not sent for—how much more so when sent for—thinking, 'How might he conduct himself properly, humble himself, and conduct himself for rehabilitation, so that the Saṅgha might revoke that act?' A return should be made within seven days.

194. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī gilānā hoti. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi gilānā, āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi ayyānaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “gilānabhattaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, gilānupaṭṭhākabhattaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, gilānabhesajjaṃ vā [T 1.0285] pariyesissāmi, pucchissāmi vā, upaṭṭhahissāmi vā”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

194. Furthermore, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī is sick. If she should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'I am sick; let the venerable sirs come, I desire the coming of the venerable sirs,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on a matter that can be settled within seven days, even if not sent for—how much more so when sent for—thinking, 'I will seek food for the sick, or food for the one attending the sick, or medicine for the sick; or I will inquire after her, or I will attend to her.' A return should be made within seven days.

Idha [V 0.0190] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā anabhirati uppannā hoti. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “anabhirati me uppannā, āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi ayyānaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “anabhirataṃ vūpakāsessāmi vā, vūpakāsāpessāmi vā, dhammakathaṃ vāssā karissāmī”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, discontent has arisen in a bhikkhunī. If she should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'Discontent has arisen in me; let the venerable sirs come, I desire the coming of the venerable sirs,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on a matter that can be settled within seven days, even if not sent for—how much more so when sent for—thinking, 'I will lead the discontented one away, or have her led away, or I will give her a Dhamma talk.' A return should be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā kukkuccaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “kukkuccaṃ me uppannaṃ, āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi ayyānaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva [M 0.0202] pahite – “kukkuccaṃ vinodessāmi vā, vinodāpessāmi vā, dhammakathaṃ vāssā karissāmī”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, remorse has arisen in a bhikkhunī. If she should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'Remorse has arisen in me; let the venerable sirs come, I desire the coming of the venerable sirs,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on a matter that can be settled within seven days, even if not sent for—how much more so when sent for—thinking, 'I will dispel the remorse, or cause it to be dispelled, or I will give her a Dhamma talk.' A return should be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “diṭṭhigataṃ me uppannaṃ, āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi ayyānaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “diṭṭhigataṃ vivecessāmi vā, vivecāpessāmi vā, dhammakathaṃ vāssā karissāmī”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, a wrong view has arisen in a bhikkhunī. If she should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'A wrong view has arisen in me; let the venerable sirs come, I desire the coming of the venerable sirs,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on a matter that can be settled within seven days, even if not sent for—how much more so when sent for—thinking, 'I will resolve the wrong view, or cause it to be resolved, or I will give her a Dhamma talk.' A return should be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī garudhammaṃ ajjhāpannā hoti mānattārahā. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi garudhammaṃ [P 1.0145] ajjhāpannā mānattārahā[T 1.0286], āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi ayyānaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “mānattadānaṃ ussukkaṃ karissāmī”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī has committed a grave offense and is worthy of mānatta. If she should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'I have committed a grave offense and am worthy of mānatta; let the venerable sirs come, I desire the coming of the venerable sirs,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on a matter that can be settled within seven days, even if not sent for—how much more so when sent for—thinking, 'I will make an effort for the giving of mānatta.' A return should be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī mūlāya paṭikassanārahā hoti. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi mūlāya paṭikassanārahā, āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi ayyānaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “mūlāya paṭikassanaṃ ussukkaṃ karissāmī”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī is worthy of being sent back to the beginning. If she should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'I am worthy of being sent back to the beginning; let the venerable sirs come, I desire the coming of the venerable sirs,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on a matter that can be settled within seven days, even if not sent for—how much more so when sent for—thinking, 'I will make an effort for the sending back to the beginning.' A return should be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī abbhānārahā hoti. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi abbhānārahā, āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi ayyānaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ[V 0.0191], bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “abbhānaṃ ussukkaṃ karissāmī”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhunī is worthy of reinstatement. If she should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'I am worthy of reinstatement; let the venerable sirs come, I desire the coming of the venerable sirs,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on a matter that can be settled within seven days, even if not sent for—how much more so when sent for—thinking, 'I will make an effort for her reinstatement.' A return should be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā saṅgho kammaṃ kattukāmo hoti – tajjanīyaṃ vā, niyassaṃ vā, pabbājanīyaṃ vā, paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā, ukkhepanīyaṃ vā. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “saṅgho me kammaṃ kattukāmo, āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi ayyānaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “kinti nu kho saṅgho kammaṃ na kareyya, lahukāya vā pariṇāmeyyā”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, the Saṅgha intends to carry out an act against a bhikkhunī—whether of censure, subordination, banishment, reconciliation, or suspension. If she should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'The Saṅgha intends to carry out an act against me; let the venerable sirs come, I desire the coming of the venerable sirs,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on a matter that can be settled within seven days, even if not sent for—how much more so when sent for—thinking, 'How might the Saṅgha not carry out the act, or change it to a lighter one?' A return should be made within seven days.

Kataṃ [M 0.0203] vā panassā hoti saṅghena kammaṃ – tajjanīyaṃ vā[T 1.0287], niyassaṃ vā, pabbājanīyaṃ vā, paṭisāraṇīyaṃ vā, ukkhepanīyaṃ vā. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “saṅgho me kammaṃ akāsi, āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi ayyānaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “kinti nu kho sammā vatteyya, lomaṃ pāteyya, netthāraṃ vatteyya, saṅgho taṃ kammaṃ paṭippassambheyyā”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Or, if the Saṅgha has performed an act against a bhikkhunī—whether of censure, subordination, banishment, reconciliation, or suspension—and she should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying, 'The Saṅgha has performed an act against me; let the venerable sirs come, I desire the coming of the venerable sirs,' then, Bhikkhus, one should go on a matter that can be settled within seven days, even if not sent for—how much more so when sent for—thinking, 'How might she conduct herself properly, humble herself, and conduct herself for rehabilitation, so that the Saṅgha might revoke that act?' A return should be made within seven days.

195. Idha pana, bhikkhave, sikkhamānā gilānā hoti. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi gilānā, āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi ayyānaṃ āgata”nti – gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “gilānabhattaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, gilānupaṭṭhākabhattaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, gilānabhesajjaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, pucchissāmi vā, upaṭṭhahissāmi vā”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

195. Here, bhikkhus, a probationer is sick. If she should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: “I am indeed sick. May the Venerable Sirs come; I desire the coming of the Venerable Sirs,” then, bhikkhus, one should go on a seven-day errand, even if not sent, and how much more so if sent, thinking, “I will seek food for the sick, or I will seek food for the sick-attendant, or I will seek medicine for the sick, or I will ask, or I will attend to her.” A return should be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, sikkhamānāya [P 1.0146] anabhirati uppannā hoti…pe… sikkhamānāya kukkuccaṃ uppannaṃ hoti… sikkhamānāya diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti… sikkhamānāya sikkhā kupitā hoti. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “sikkhā me kupitā, āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi ayyānaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “sikkhāsamādānaṃ ussukkaṃ karissāmī”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, discontent has arisen for a probationer… remorse has arisen for a probationer… a wrong view has arisen for a probationer… a probationer’s training has been broken. If she should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: “My training has been broken; may the Venerable Sirs come; I desire the coming of the Venerable Sirs,” then, bhikkhus, one should go on a seven-day errand, even if not sent, and how much more so if sent, thinking, “I will make an effort for the undertaking of the training.” A return should be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, sikkhamānā upasampajjitukāmā hoti. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi upasampajjitukāmā, āgacchantu ayyā[T 1.0288], icchāmi ayyānaṃ [V 0.0192] āgata”nti gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – upasampadaṃ ussukkaṃ karissāmi vā, anussāvessāmi vā, gaṇapūrako vā bhavissāmīti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, a probationer desires to receive full ordination. If she should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: “I indeed desire to receive full ordination; may the Venerable Sirs come; I desire the coming of the Venerable Sirs,” then, bhikkhus, one should go on a seven-day errand, even if not sent, and how much more so if sent, thinking, “I will make an effort for the full ordination, or I will recite the motion and proclamation, or I will be one to complete the quorum.” A return should be made within seven days.

196. Idha pana, bhikkhave, sāmaṇero gilāno hoti. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi gilāno, āgacchantu bhikkhū[M 0.0204], icchāmi bhikkhūnaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “gilānabhattaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, gilānupaṭṭhākabhattaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, gilānabhesajjaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, pucchissāmi vā, upaṭṭhahissāmi vā”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

196. Here, bhikkhus, a novice is sick. If he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: “I am indeed sick. May the bhikkhus come; I desire the coming of the bhikkhus,” then, bhikkhus, one should go on a seven-day errand, even if not sent, and how much more so if sent, thinking, “I will seek food for the sick, or I will seek food for the sick-attendant, or I will seek medicine for the sick, or I will ask, or I will attend to him.” A return should be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, sāmaṇerassa anabhirati uppannā hoti…pe… sāmaṇerassa kukkuccaṃ uppannaṃ hoti… sāmaṇerassa diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti… sāmaṇero vassaṃ pucchitukāmo hoti. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi vassaṃ pucchitukāmo, āgacchantu bhikkhū, icchāmi bhikkhūnaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “pucchissāmi vā, ācikkhissāmi vā”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, discontent has arisen for a novice… remorse has arisen for a novice… a wrong view has arisen for a novice… a novice wishes to ask about the Rains-residence. If he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: “I indeed wish to ask about the Rains-residence; may the bhikkhus come; I desire the coming of the bhikkhus,” then, bhikkhus, one should go on a seven-day errand, even if not sent, and how much more so if sent, thinking, “I will ask, or I will inform.” A return should be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, sāmaṇero upasampajjitukāmo hoti. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi upasampajjitukāmo, āgacchantu bhikkhū, icchāmi bhikkhūnaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “upasampadaṃ ussukkaṃ karissāmi vā, anussāvessāmi [T 1.0289] vā, gaṇapūrako vā bhavissāmī”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, a novice wishes to receive full ordination. If he should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: “I indeed wish to receive full ordination; may the bhikkhus come; I desire the coming of the bhikkhus,” then, bhikkhus, one should go on a seven-day errand, even if not sent, and how much more so if sent, thinking, “I will make an effort for the full ordination, or I will recite the motion and proclamation, or I will be one who completes the quorum.” A return should be made within seven days.

197. Idha pana, bhikkhave, sāmaṇerī gilānā hoti. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi gilānā, āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi ayyānaṃ āgata”nti[P 1.0147], gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “gilānabhattaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, gilānupaṭṭhākabhattaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, gilānabhesajjaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, pucchissāmi vā, upaṭṭhahissāmi vā”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

197. Here, bhikkhus, a female novice is sick. If she should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: “I am indeed sick. May the Venerable Sirs come; I desire the coming of the Venerable Sirs,” then, bhikkhus, one should go on a seven-day errand, even if not sent, and how much more so if sent, thinking, “I will seek food for the sick, or I will seek food for the sick-attendant, or I will seek medicine for the sick, or I will ask, or I will attend to her.” A return should be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, sāmaṇeriyā anabhirati uppannā hoti…pe… sāmaṇeriyā kukkuccaṃ [V 0.0193] uppannaṃ hoti… sāmaṇeriyā diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti… sāmaṇerī vassaṃ pucchitukāmā hoti. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi vassaṃ pucchitukāmā, āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi ayyānaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “pucchissāmi vā, ācikkhissāmi vā”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, discontent has arisen for a female novice… remorse has arisen for a female novice… a wrong view has arisen for a female novice… a female novice wishes to ask about the Rains-residence. If she should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: “I indeed wish to ask about the Rains-residence; may the Venerable Sirs come; I desire the coming of the Venerable Sirs,” then, bhikkhus, one should go on a seven-day errand, even if not sent, and how much more so if sent, thinking, “I will ask, or I will inform.” A return should be made within seven days.

Idha [M 0.0205] pana, bhikkhave, sāmaṇerī sikkhaṃ samādiyitukāmā hoti. Sā ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi sikkhaṃ samādiyitukāmā, āgacchantu ayyā, icchāmi ayyānaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “sikkhāsamādānaṃ ussukkaṃ karissāmī”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabboti.

Here, bhikkhus, a female novice desires to undertake the training. If she should send a messenger to the bhikkhus, saying: “I indeed desire to undertake the training; may the Venerable Sirs come; I desire the coming of the Venerable Sirs,” then, bhikkhus, one should go on a seven-day errand, even if not sent, and how much more so if sent, thinking, “I will make an effort for the undertaking of the training.” A return should be made within seven days.

Pañcannaṃ appahitepi anujānanā niṭṭhitā.

The allowance concerning the five, even when not sent for, is concluded.

111. Sattannaṃ appahitepi anujānanā

111. Allowance for the Seven Even When Unsent

198. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno mātā gilānā hoti. Sā puttassa santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – “ahañhi gilānā, āgacchatu me putto, icchāmi puttassa āgata”nti. Atha kho tassa bhikkhuno etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ sattannaṃ sattāhakaraṇīyena pahite gantuṃ, na tveva appahite; pañcannaṃ sattāhakaraṇīyena appahitepi gantuṃ, pageva pahiteti. Ayañca me mātā gilānā, sā ca anupāsikā, kathaṃ [T 1.0290] nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sattannaṃ sattāhakaraṇīyena appahitepi gantuṃ, pageva pahite. Bhikkhussa, bhikkhuniyā, sikkhamānāya, sāmaṇerassa, sāmaṇeriyā, mātuyā ca pitussa ca – anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imesaṃ sattannaṃ sattāhakaraṇīyena appahitepi gantuṃ, pageva pahite. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

198. At that time, a certain monk’s mother was ill. She sent a messenger to her son, saying, “I am ill; let my son come, I desire my son's arrival.” Then this thought occurred to that monk: “The Blessed One has laid it down that for seven persons, one may go for a duty to be completed within seven days when sent for, but not when unsent for; for five persons, one may go for a duty to be completed within seven days even when unsent for, how much more so when sent for. And this mother of mine is ill, and she is not a lay disciple. How indeed should I act?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow seven persons to go for a duty to be completed within seven days even when unsent for; how much more so when sent for. For a monk, a nun, a female probationer, a male novice, a female novice, and for a mother and a father—Monks, I allow these seven persons to go for a duty to be completed within seven days even when unsent for; how much more so when sent for. A return must be made within seven days.”

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa mātā gilānā hoti. Sā ce puttassa santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi gilānā, āgacchatu me putto, icchāmi puttassa āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “gilānabhattaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, gilānupaṭṭhākabhattaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, gilānabhesajjaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, pucchissāmi vā, upaṭṭhahissāmi vā”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Here, monks, a monk’s mother is ill. If she should send a messenger to her son, saying, “I am ill; let my son come, I desire my son's arrival,” one should go, monks, for a duty to be completed within seven days, even when unsent for, how much more so when sent for, thinking: “I will seek food for the sick, or seek food for the attendant of the sick, or seek medicine for the sick, or I will inquire, or I will attend to her.” A return must be made within seven days.

Idha [V 0.0194] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa [P 1.0148] pitā gilāno hoti. So ce puttassa santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi gilāno, āgacchatu me putto, icchāmi puttassa āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, appahitepi, pageva pahite – “gilānabhattaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, gilānupaṭṭhākabhattaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, gilānabhesajjaṃ vā pariyesissāmi, pucchissāmi vā, upaṭṭhahissāmi vā”ti. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Here, monks, a monk's father is ill. If he should send a messenger to his son, saying: 'I am ill, let my son come, I desire my son's arrival,' then, monks, he should go for a duty to be completed within seven days, even if not sent for—how much more so when sent for—thinking: 'I will seek food for the sick, or I will seek food for the attendant of the sick, or I will seek medicine for the sick, or I will inquire, or I will attend to him.' A return must be made within seven days.

Sattannaṃ appahitepi anujānanā niṭṭhitā.

The allowance for the seven, even when not sent for, is concluded.

112. Pahiteyeva anujānanā

112. The Allowance Only When Sent For

199 . Idha [M 0.0206] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa bhātā gilāno hoti. So ce bhātuno santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi gilāno, āgacchatu me bhātā, icchāmi bhātuno āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave[T 1.0291], sattāhakaraṇīyena, pahite, na tveva appahite. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

199. Here, monks, a monk's brother is ill. If he should send a messenger to his brother, saying: 'I am ill, let my brother come, I desire my brother's arrival,' then, monks, he should go for a duty to be completed within seven days when sent for, but certainly not when not sent for. A return must be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa bhaginī gilānā hoti. Sā ce bhātuno santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi gilānā, āgacchatu me bhātā, icchāmi bhātuno āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, pahite, na tveva appahite. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Here, monks, a monk's sister is ill. If she should send a messenger to her brother, saying: 'I am ill, let my brother come, I desire my brother's arrival,' then, monks, he should go for a duty to be completed within seven days when sent for, but certainly not when not sent for. A return must be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa ñātako gilāno hoti. So ce bhikkhussa santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi gilāno, āgacchatu bhadanto, icchāmi bhadantassa āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, pahite, na tveva appahite. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Here, monks, a monk's relative is ill. If that relative should send a messenger to the monk, saying: 'I am ill, let the venerable one come, I desire the venerable one's arrival,' then, monks, he should go for a duty to be completed within seven days when sent for, but certainly not when not sent for. A return must be made within seven days.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhugatiko gilāno hoti. So ce bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pahiṇeyya – “ahañhi gilāno, āgacchantu bhadantā, icchāmi bhadantānaṃ āgata”nti, gantabbaṃ, bhikkhave, sattāhakaraṇīyena, pahite, na tveva appahite. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabbo.

Here, monks, a man who lives in the same monastery is ill. If that man should send a messenger to the monks, saying: 'I am ill, let the venerable ones come, I desire the venerable ones' arrival,' then, monks, they should go for a duty to be completed within seven days when sent for, but certainly not when not sent for. A return must be made within seven days.

Tena [V 0.0195] kho pana samayena saṅghassa vihāro undriyati. Aññatarena upāsakena araññe bhaṇḍaṃ chedāpitaṃ hoti. So bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – “sace bhadantā taṃ bhaṇḍaṃ āvahāpeyyuṃ, dajjāhaṃ taṃ bhaṇḍa”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghakaraṇīyena gantuṃ. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabboti.

Now at that time, the Sangha's monastery was collapsing. A certain lay follower had timber for the monastery cut in the forest. He sent a messenger to the monks, saying: 'If the venerable ones would have that timber brought, I would give that timber.' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: 'Monks, I allow you to go for a Sangha matter. The return must be made within seven days.'

Pahiteyeva anujānanā niṭṭhitā.

The allowance only when sent for is concluded.

Vassāvāsabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The recitation section on the Rains-residence is concluded.

113. Antarāye anāpattivassacchedavāro

113. The Chapter on No Offense in Breaking the Rains-Residence Due to an Obstacle

200. Tena [T 1.0292] kho pana samayena kosalesu janapade aññatarasmiṃ āvāse vassūpagatā bhikkhū vāḷehi ubbāḷhā honti. Gaṇhiṃsupi paripātiṃsupi. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

200. Now at that time, in a certain residence in the country of the Kosalans, monks who had entered the rains-residence were harassed by wild animals. They seized them and pursued them. They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha [M 0.0207] pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagatā bhikkhū vāḷehi ubbāḷhā honti. Gaṇhantipi paripātentipi. Eseva antarāyoti pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Here, monks, monks who have entered the rains-residence are harassed by wild animals. They seize them and pursue them. This itself is an obstacle; one should depart. There is no offense for breaking the rains-residence.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagatā bhikkhū sarīsapehi ubbāḷhā honti. Ḍaṃsantipi paripātentipi. Eseva antarāyoti pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa[P 1.0149].

Here, monks, monks who have entered the rains-residence are harassed by snakes. They bite them and pursue them. This itself is an obstacle; one should depart. There is no offense for breaking the rains-residence.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagatā bhikkhū corehi ubbāḷhā honti. Vilumpantipi ākoṭentipi. Eseva antarāyoti pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Here, monks, monks who have entered the rains-residence are harassed by thieves. They rob them and beat them. This itself is an obstacle; one should depart. There is no offense for breaking the rains-residence.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagatā bhikkhū pisācehi ubbāḷhā honti. Āvisantipi hanantipi ojampi haranti (sī.), harantipi (syā.). Eseva antarāyoti pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Here, monks, monks who have entered the rains-residence are harassed by demons. They possess them and kill them. This itself is an obstacle; one should depart. There is no offense for breaking the rains-residence.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ gāmo agginā daḍḍho hoti. Bhikkhū piṇḍakena kilamanti. Eseva antarāyoti pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Here, monks, the alms-round village of monks who have entered the rains-residence is burned by fire, and the monks are troubled for alms-food. This itself is an obstacle; one should depart. There is no offense for breaking the rains-residence.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ senāsanaṃ agginā daḍḍhaṃ hoti. Bhikkhū senāsanena kilamanti. Eseva antarāyoti pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Here, monks, the lodging of monks who have entered the rains is burned by fire, and the monks are troubled on account of the lodging. Thinking, 'This itself is an obstacle,' one should depart. There is no offense for one who breaks the rains.

Idha [V 0.0196] pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ gāmo udakena [T 1.0293] vūḷho hoti. Bhikkhū piṇḍakena kilamanti. Eseva antarāyoti pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Here, monks, the alms-village of monks who have entered the rains is carried away by water. The monks are troubled on account of alms-food. Thinking, 'This itself is an obstacle,' one should depart. There is no offense for one who breaks the rains.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ senāsanaṃ udakena vūḷhaṃ hoti. Bhikkhū senāsanena kilamanti. Eseva antarāyoti pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassāti.

Here, monks, the lodging of monks who have entered the rains is carried away by water. The monks are troubled on account of the lodging. Thinking, 'This itself is an obstacle,' one should depart. There is no offense for one who breaks the rains.

201. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse vassūpagatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ gāmo corehi vuṭṭhāsi. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yena gāmo tena gantunti.

201. Now at that time, in a certain monastery, the alms-village of monks who had entered the rains was depopulated on account of thieves. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, 'Monks, I allow you to go where the village is.'

Gāmo [M 0.0208] dvedhā bhijjittha. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yena bahutarā tena gantunti.

The village split in two. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, 'Monks, I allow you to go where there are more people.'

Bahutarā assaddhā honti appasannā. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yena saddhā pasannā tena gantunti.

The more numerous people were faithless and not devoted. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, 'Monks, I allow you to go where the people are faithful and devoted.'

Tena kho pana samayena kosalesu janapade aññatarasmiṃ āvāse vassūpagatā bhikkhū na labhiṃsu lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṃ pāripūriṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

Now at that time, in a certain monastery in the country of the Kosalans, monks who had entered the rains did not obtain a sufficiency of either coarse or fine food according to their needs. They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagatā bhikkhū na labhanti lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṃ pāripūriṃ. Eseva antarāyoti pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Here, monks, monks who have entered the rains do not obtain a sufficiency of either coarse or fine food according to their needs. Thinking, 'This itself is an obstacle,' one should depart. There is no offense for one who breaks the rains.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagatā bhikkhū labhanti lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṃ pāripūriṃ, na labhanti sappāyāni bhojanāni. Eseva antarāyoti pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti [T 1.0294] vassacchedassa.

Here, monks, monks who have entered the rains obtain a sufficiency of either coarse or fine food according to their needs, but they do not obtain suitable foods. Thinking, 'This itself is an obstacle,' one should depart. There is no offense for one who breaks the rains.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagatā bhikkhū labhanti lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṃ pāripūriṃ, labhanti sappāyāni bhojanāni[P 1.0150], na labhanti sappāyāni bhesajjāni. Eseva antarāyoti pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Here, monks, monks who have entered the rains obtain a sufficiency of either coarse or fine food according to their needs, and they obtain suitable foods, but they do not obtain suitable medicines. Thinking, 'This itself is an obstacle,' one should depart. There is no offense for one who breaks the rains.

Idha [V 0.0197] pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagatā bhikkhū labhanti lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṃ pāripūriṃ, labhanti sappāyāni bhojanāni, labhanti sappāyāni bhesajjāni, na labhanti patirūpaṃ upaṭṭhākaṃ. Eseva antarāyoti pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Here, monks, monks who have entered the rains obtain a sufficiency of either coarse or fine food according to their needs, they obtain suitable foods, and they obtain suitable medicines, but they do not obtain a suitable attendant. Thinking, 'This itself is an obstacle,' one should depart. There is no offense for one who breaks the rains.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagataṃ bhikkhuṃ itthī nimanteti – “ehi, bhante, hiraññaṃ vā te demi, suvaṇṇaṃ vā te demi, khettaṃ vā te demi, vatthuṃ vā te demi, gāvuṃ vā te demi, gāviṃ vā te demi, dāsaṃ vā te demi, dāsiṃ vā te demi, dhītaraṃ vā te demi bhariyatthāya, ahaṃ vā te bhariyā homi, aññaṃ vā te bhariyaṃ ānemī”ti. Tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti, ‘lahuparivattaṃ kho cittaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, siyāpi me brahmacariyassa antarāyo’ti, pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Here, monks, a woman invites a monk who has entered the rains, saying: ‘Come, venerable sir, I will give you silver, or I will give you gold, or I will give you a field, or I will give you a plot of land, or I will give you an ox, or I will give you a cow, or I will give you a male slave, or I will give you a female slave, or I will give you my daughter to be your wife, or I myself will be your wife, or I will bring another wife for you.’ If, on that occasion, it occurs to the monk thus: ‘Indeed, the mind has been declared by the Blessed One to be fickle; there might be an obstacle to my holy life,’ he should depart. There is no offense for one who breaks the rains.

Idha [M 0.0209] pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagataṃ bhikkhuṃ vesī nimanteti…pe… thullakumārī nimanteti… paṇḍako nimanteti… ñātakā nimantenti… rājāno nimantenti… corā nimantenti… dhuttā nimantenti – “ehi, bhante, hiraññaṃ vā te dema, suvaṇṇaṃ vā te dema, khettaṃ vā te dema, vatthuṃ vā te dema[T 1.0295], gāvuṃ vā te dema, gāviṃ vā te dema, dāsaṃ vā te dema, dāsiṃ vā te dema, dhītaraṃ vā te dema bhariyatthāya, aññaṃ vā te bhariyaṃ ānemā”ti. Tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti, ‘lahuparivattaṃ kho cittaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, siyāpi me brahmacariyassa antarāyo’ti, pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Here, monks, a monk who has entered the rains is invited by a prostitute… by a mature maiden… by a eunuch… by relatives… by kings… by thieves… or by rogues, saying: ‘Come, venerable sir, we will give you silver, or we will give you gold, or we will give you a field, or we will give you a plot of land, or we will give you an ox, or we will give you a cow, or we will give you a male slave, or we will give you a female slave, or we will give you our daughter to be your wife, or we will bring another wife for you.’ If, on that occasion, it occurs to the monk thus: ‘Indeed, the mind has been declared by the Blessed One to be fickle; there might be an obstacle to my holy life,’ he should depart. There is no offense for one who breaks the rains.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagato bhikkhu assāmikaṃ nidhiṃ passati. Tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti, ‘lahuparivattaṃ kho cittaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, siyāpi me brahmacariyassa antarāyo’ti, pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Here, monks, a monk who has entered the rains sees an ownerless treasure. If, on that occasion, it occurs to the monk thus: ‘Indeed, the mind has been declared by the Blessed One to be fickle; there might be an obstacle to my holy life,’ he should depart. There is no offense for one who breaks the rains.

Antarāye anāpattivassacchedavāro niṭṭhito.

The section on no offense for breaking the rains due to an obstacle is concluded.

114. Saṅghabhede anāpattivassacchedavāro

114. The Section on No Offense for Breaking the Rains in Case of a Schism in the Saṅgha

202. Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagato bhikkhu passati sambahule bhikkhū saṅghabhedāya parakkamante. Tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti, ‘garuko kho saṅghabhedo vutto bhagavatā; mā mayi sammukhībhūte saṅgho bhijjī’ti, pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

202. Here, monks, a monk who has entered the rains sees many monks striving for a schism in the Saṅgha. If, on that occasion, it occurs to the monk thus: ‘Indeed, a schism in the Saṅgha has been declared by the Blessed One to be a grave matter; may the Saṅgha not split while I am present,’ he should depart. There is no offense for one who breaks the rains.

Idha [V 0.0198] pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagato bhikkhu suṇāti – “asukasmiṃ kira āvāse sambahulā bhikkhū saṅghabhedāya parakkamantī”ti. Tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti, ‘garuko kho saṅghabhedo vutto bhagavatā; mā mayi sammukhībhūte saṅgho bhijjī’ti, pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Here, monks, a monk who has entered the rains hears: ‘It is said that in a certain monastery, many monks are striving for a schism in the Saṅgha.’ If, on that occasion, it occurs to the monk thus: ‘Indeed, a schism in the Saṅgha has been declared by the Blessed One to be a grave matter; may the Saṅgha not split while I am present,’ he should depart. There is no offense for one who breaks the rains.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagato bhikkhu suṇāti – “asukasmiṃ kira āvāse sambahulā bhikkhū saṅghabhedāya parakkamantī”ti. Tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti – “te kho me bhikkhū mittā. Tyāhaṃ vakkhāmi ‘garuko kho, āvuso, saṅghabhedo vutto bhagavatā; māyasmantānaṃ saṅghabhedo ruccitthā’ti. Karissanti [T 1.0296] me vacanaṃ, sussūsissanti, sotaṃ odahissantī”ti, pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Furthermore, monks, a monk who has entered the rains-residence hears: ‘It is said that in a certain monastery, many monks are striving for a schism in the Saṅgha.’ If it occurs to that monk: ‘Indeed, those monks are my friends. I will say to them: “Venerable sirs, a schism in the Saṅgha has been declared by the Blessed One to be a grave matter; may a schism in the Saṅgha not be agreeable to the venerable ones.” They will heed my word, listen attentively, and pay attention,’ he should depart. There is no offense for breaking the rains-residence.

Idha [M 0.0210] pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagato bhikkhu suṇāti – “asukasmiṃ kira āvāse sambahulā bhikkhū saṅghabhedāya [P 1.0151] parakkamantī”ti. Tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti – “te kho me bhikkhū na mittā; api ca ye tesaṃ mittā, te me mittā. Tyāhaṃ vakkhāmi. Te vuttā te vakkhanti ‘garuko kho, āvuso, saṅghabhedo vutto bhagavatā; māyasmantānaṃ saṅghabhedo ruccitthā’ti. Karissanti tesaṃ vacanaṃ, sussūsissanti, sotaṃ odahissantī”ti, pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Furthermore, monks, a monk who has entered the rains-residence hears: ‘It is said that in a certain monastery, many monks are striving for a schism in the Saṅgha.’ If it occurs to that monk: ‘Indeed, those monks are not my friends; however, their friends are my friends. I will speak to them. When spoken to, they will say to those monks: “Venerable sirs, a schism in the Saṅgha has been declared by the Blessed One to be a grave matter; may a schism in the Saṅgha not be agreeable to the venerable ones.” They will heed their words, listen attentively, and pay attention,’ he should depart. There is no offense for breaking the rains-residence.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagato bhikkhu suṇāti – “asukasmiṃ kira āvāse sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saṅgho bhinno”ti. Tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti – “te kho me bhikkhū mittā. Tyāhaṃ vakkhāmi ‘garuko kho, āvuso, saṅghabhedo vutto bhagavatā; māyasmantānaṃ saṅghabhedo ruccitthā’ti. Karissanti me vacanaṃ, sussūsissanti, sotaṃ odahissantī”ti, pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Furthermore, monks, a monk who has entered the rains-residence hears: ‘It is said that in a certain monastery, the Saṅgha has been split by many monks.’ If it occurs to that monk: ‘Indeed, those monks are my friends. I will say to them: “Venerable sirs, a schism in the Saṅgha has been declared by the Blessed One to be a grave matter; may a schism in the Saṅgha not be agreeable to the venerable ones.” They will heed my word, listen attentively, and pay attention,’ he should depart. There is no offense for breaking the rains-residence.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagato bhikkhu suṇāti – “asukasmiṃ kira āvāse sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saṅgho bhinno”ti. Tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti – “te kho me bhikkhū na mittā; api ca, ye tesaṃ mittā te me mittā. Tyāhaṃ vakkhāmi. Te vuttā te vakkhanti ‘garuko kho, āvuso, saṅghabhedo vutto bhagavatā; māyasmantānaṃ saṅghabhedo ruccitthā’ti. Karissanti tesaṃ vacanaṃ, sussūsissanti[T 1.0297], sotaṃ odahissantī”ti, pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Furthermore, monks, a monk who has entered the rains-residence hears: ‘It is said that in a certain monastery, the Saṅgha has been split by many monks.’ If it occurs to that monk: ‘Indeed, those monks are not my friends; however, their friends are my friends. I will speak to them. When spoken to, they will say to those monks: “Venerable sirs, a schism in the Saṅgha has been declared by the Blessed One to be a grave matter; may a schism in the Saṅgha not be agreeable to the venerable ones.” They will heed their words, listen attentively, and pay attention,’ he should depart. There is no offense for breaking the rains-residence.

Idha [V 0.0199] pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagato bhikkhu [T 1.0298] suṇāti – “amukasmiṃ kira āvāse sambahulā bhikkhuniyo saṅghabhedāya parakkamantī”ti. Tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti – “tā kho me bhikkhuniyo mittā. Tāhaṃ vakkhāmi ‘garuko kho, bhaginiyo, saṅghabhedo vutto bhagavatā; mā bhaginīnaṃ saṅghabhedo ruccitthā’ti. Karissanti me vacanaṃ, sussūsissanti, sotaṃ odahissantī”ti, pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassa.

Furthermore, monks, a monk who has entered the rains-residence hears: ‘It is said that in a certain monastery, many nuns are striving for a schism in the Saṅgha.’ If it occurs to that monk: ‘Indeed, those nuns are my friends. I will say to them: “Sisters, a schism in the Saṅgha has been declared by the Blessed One to be a grave matter; may a schism in the Saṅgha not be agreeable to the sisters.” They will heed my word, listen attentively, and pay attention,’ he should depart. There is no offense for breaking the rains-residence.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagato bhikkhu suṇāti – “amukasmiṃ kira āvāse sambahulā bhikkhuniyo saṅghabhedāya parakkamantī”ti. Tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti – “tā kho me bhikkhuniyo na mittā. Api ca, yā tāsaṃ mittā, tā me mittā. Tāhaṃ vakkhāmi. Tā vuttā tā vakkhanti ‘garuko [M 0.0211] kho, bhaginiyo, saṅghabhedo vutto bhagavatā. Mā bhaginīnaṃ saṅghabhedo ruccitthā’ti. Karissanti tāsaṃ vacanaṃ, sussūsissanti, sotaṃ odahissantī”ti, pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassati.

Furthermore, monks, a monk who has entered the rains-residence hears: ‘It is said that in a certain monastery, many nuns are striving for a schism in the Saṅgha.’ If it occurs to that monk: ‘Indeed, those nuns are not my friends; however, their friends are my friends. I will speak to them. When spoken to, they will say to those other nuns: “Sisters, a schism in the Saṅgha has been declared by the Blessed One to be a grave matter; may a schism in the Saṅgha not be agreeable to the sisters.” They will heed their words, listen attentively, and pay attention,’ he should depart. There is no offense for breaking the rains-residence.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagato bhikkhu suṇāti – “amukasmiṃ kira āvāse sambahulāhi bhikkhunīhi saṅgho bhinno”ti. Tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti – “tā kho me bhikkhuniyo mittā. Tāhaṃ vakkhāmi ‘garuko kho, bhaginiyo, saṅghabhedo vutto bhagavatā. Mā bhaginīnaṃ saṅghabhedo ruccitthā’ti. Karissanti me vacanaṃ, sussūsissanti, sotaṃ odahissantī”ti, pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassati.

Furthermore, monks, a monk who has entered the rains-residence hears: ‘It is said that in a certain monastery, the Saṅgha has been split by many nuns.’ If it occurs to that monk: ‘Indeed, those nuns are my friends. I will say to them: “Sisters, a schism in the Saṅgha has been declared by the Blessed One to be a grave matter; may a schism in the Saṅgha not be agreeable to the sisters.” They will heed my word, listen attentively, and pay attention,’ he should depart. There is no offense for breaking the rains-residence.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassūpagato bhikkhu suṇāti – “amukasmiṃ kira āvāse sambahulāhi bhikkhunīhi saṅgho bhinno”ti. Tatra ce bhikkhuno evaṃ hoti – “tā kho me bhikkhuniyo na mittā. Api ca, yā tāsaṃ mittā tā me mittā. Tāhaṃ vakkhāmi. Tā vuttā tā vakkhanti ‘garuko kho, bhaginiyo ayyāyo (sī.), saṅghabhedo vutto bhagavatā; mā bhaginīnaṃ ayyānaṃ (sī.) saṅghabhedo ruccitthā’ti. Karissanti tāsaṃ vacanaṃ, sussūsissanti, sotaṃ odahissantī”ti, pakkamitabbaṃ. Anāpatti vassacchedassāti.

Furthermore, monks, a monk who has entered the rains-residence hears: ‘It is said that in a certain monastery, the Saṅgha has been split by many nuns.’ If it occurs to that monk: ‘Indeed, those nuns are not my friends; however, their friends are my friends. I will speak to them. When spoken to, they will say to those other nuns: “Sisters, a schism in the Saṅgha has been declared by the Blessed One to be a grave matter; may a schism in the Saṅgha not be agreeable to the sisters.” They will heed their words, listen attentively, and pay attention,’ he should depart. There is no offense for breaking the rains-residence.

Saṅghabhede anāpattivassacchedavāro niṭṭhito.

The section on no offense for breaking the rains-residence in a case of schism in the Saṅgha is finished.

115. Vajādīsu vassūpagamanaṃ

115. Entering the Rains-Residence in Cattle-Pens and Other Such Places

203. Tena [V 0.0200] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu vaje vassaṃ upagantukāmo [P 1.0152] hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vaje vassaṃ upagantunti. Vajo vuṭṭhāsi. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yena vajo tena gantunti.

203. Now at that time, a certain monk wished to enter the rains-residence in a cattle-pen. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. The Buddha said: 'Monks, I allow entering the rains-residence in a cattle-pen.' The cattle-pen was relocated. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. The Buddha said: 'Monks, I allow you to go to wherever the cattle-pen is.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu upakaṭṭhāya vassūpanāyikāya satthena gantukāmo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, satthe vassaṃ upagantunti.

Now at that time, as the time for the rains-residence was approaching, a certain monk wished to travel with a caravan. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. The Buddha said: 'Monks, I allow entering the rains-residence in a caravan.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu upakaṭṭhāya vassūpanāyikāya nāvāya gantukāmo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, nāvāya vassaṃ upagantunti.

Now at that time, when the time for entering the Rains was near, a certain monk was desirous of going by boat. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. 'Monks, I allow entering the Rains on a boat.'

Vajādīsu vassūpagamanaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section on entering the Rains in pastures, etc., is finished.

116. Vassaṃ anupagantabbaṭṭhānāni

116. Places Where the Rains Should Not Be Entered

204. Tena [M 0.0212] kho pana samayena bhikkhū rukkhasusire vassaṃ upagacchanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “seyyathāpi pisācillikā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, rukkhasusire [T 1.0299] vassaṃ upagantabbaṃ. Yo upagaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

204. Now at that time, monks were entering the Rains in a tree hollow. People complained, criticized, and disparaged them, saying: 'They are just like goblins!' They informed the Blessed One of this matter. 'Monks, the Rains should not be entered in a tree hollow. Whoever should enter commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū rukkhaviṭabhiyā vassaṃ upagacchanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “seyyathāpi migaluddakā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, rukkhaviṭabhiyā vassaṃ upagantabbaṃ. Yo upagaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, monks were entering the Rains in a tree fork. People complained, criticized, and disparaged them, saying: “Just like hunters!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, the Rains should not be entered in a tree fork. Whoever should enter commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū ajjhokāse vassaṃ upagacchanti. Deve vassante rukkhamūlampi [V 0.0201] nibbakosampi upadhāvanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, ajjhokāse vassaṃ upagantabbaṃ. Yo upagaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, monks were entering the Rains in the open. When it rained, they ran to the foot of a tree or to a sheltered place. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, the Rains should not be entered in the open. Whoever should enter commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū asenāsanikā vassaṃ upagacchanti. Sītenapi kilamanti, uṇhenapi kilamanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, asenāsanikena vassaṃ upagantabbaṃ. Yo upagaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, monks without lodgings were entering the Rains. They were exhausted by the cold and also by the heat. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, the Rains should not be entered without lodgings. Whoever should enter commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū chavakuṭikāya vassaṃ upagacchanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “seyyathāpi chavaḍāhakā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, chavakuṭikāya vassaṃ upagantabbaṃ. Yo upagaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, monks were entering the Rains in a charnel hut. People complained, criticized, and disparaged them, saying: “Just like corpse burners!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, the Rains should not be entered in a charnel hut. Whoever should enter commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū chatte vassaṃ upagacchanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “seyyathāpi gopālakā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, chatte vassaṃ upagantabbaṃ. Yo upagaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, monks were entering the Rains under a parasol. People complained, criticized, and disparaged them, saying: “Just like cowherds!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, the Rains should not be entered under a parasol. Whoever should enter commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena [P 1.0153] kho pana samayena bhikkhū [T 1.0300] cāṭiyā vassaṃ upagacchanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “seyyathāpi titthiyā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, cāṭiyā vassaṃ upagantabbaṃ. Yo upagaccheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, monks were entering the Rains in a large pot. People complained, criticized, and disparaged them, saying: “Just like sectarians!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, the Rains should not be entered in a large pot. Whoever should enter commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Vassaṃ anupagantabbaṭṭhānāni niṭṭhitā.

The places where the Rains should not be entered are concluded.

117. Adhammikakatikā

117. Unlawful Agreement

205. Tena [M 0.0213] kho pana samayena sāvatthiyā saṅghena evarūpā katikā katā hoti – antarāvassaṃ na pabbājetabbanti. Visākhāya migāramātuyā nattā bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā pabbajjaṃ yāci. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “saṅghena kho, āvuso, evarūpā katikā katā ‘antarāvassaṃ na pabbājetabba’nti. Āgamehi, āvuso, yāva bhikkhū vassaṃ vasanti. Vassaṃvuṭṭhā pabbājessantī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū vassaṃvuṭṭhā visākhāya migāramātuyā nattāraṃ etadavocuṃ – “ehi, dāni, āvuso, pabbajāhī”ti. So evamāha – “sacāhaṃ, bhante, pabbajito assaṃ, abhirameyyāmahaṃ abhirameyyaṃ cāhaṃ (sī.). Na dānāhaṃ, bhante, pabbajissāmī”ti. Visākhā migāramātā [V 0.0202] ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma ayyā evarūpaṃ katikaṃ karissanti ‘na antarāvassaṃ pabbājetabba’nti. Kaṃ kālaṃ dhammo na caritabbo”ti? Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū visākhāya migāramātuyā ujjhāyantiyā khiyyantiyā vipācentiyā. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, evarūpā katikā kātabbā – ‘na antarāvassaṃ pabbājetabba’nti. Yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

205. Now at that time, the Saṅgha in Sāvatthī had made an agreement of this kind: 'One should not be ordained during the Rains.' The grandson of Visākhā, Migāra's mother, approached the monks and requested ordination. The monks said to him: 'Friend, the Saṅgha has indeed made an agreement of this kind: "One should not be ordained during the Rains." Wait, friend, for as long as the monks are observing the Rains. Having completed the Rains, they will ordain you.' Then, having completed the Rains, those monks said to the grandson of Visākhā, Migāra's mother: 'Come now, friend, be ordained.' He replied: 'Venerable sirs, if I had been ordained, I would have been delighted. But now, venerable sirs, I will not be ordained.' Visākhā, Migāra's mother, complained, criticized, and disparaged: 'How indeed could the venerable ones make such an agreement: "One should not be ordained during the Rains"? At what time should the Dhamma not be practiced?' The monks heard Visākhā, Migāra's mother, complaining, criticizing, and disparaging. Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, an agreement of this kind should not be made: "One should not be ordained during the Rains." Whoever does so, commits an offense of wrong conduct.'

Adhammikakatikā niṭṭhitā.

The Unlawful Agreement is concluded.

118. Paṭissavadukkaṭāpatti

118. The Offense of Wrong Conduct Regarding a Promise

206. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmatā upanandena sakyaputtena [T 1.0301] rañño pasenadissa kosalassa vassāvāso paṭissuto hoti purimikāya. So taṃ āvāsaṃ gacchanto addasa antarāmagge dve āvāse bahucīvarake. Tassa etadahosi – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ imesu dvīsu āvāsesu vassaṃ vaseyyaṃ. Evaṃ me bahuṃ cīvaraṃ bahucīvaraṃ (ka.) uppajjissatī”ti. So tesu dvīsu āvāsesu vassaṃ vasi. Rājā pasenadi kosalo ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma ayyo upanando sakyaputto amhākaṃ vassāvāsaṃ paṭissuṇitvā visaṃvādessati. Nanu bhagavatā anekapariyāyena musāvādo garahito, musāvādā veramaṇī pasatthā”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū rañño pasenadissa kosalassa ujjhāyantassa khiyyantassa vipācentassa. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā [P 1.0154] upanando sakyaputto [M 0.0214] rañño pasenadissa kosalassa vassāvāsaṃ paṭissuṇitvā visaṃvādessati. Nanu bhagavatā anekapariyāyena musāvādo garahito, musāvādā veramaṇī pasatthā”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā āyasmantaṃ upanandaṃ sakyaputtaṃ paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, upananda, rañño pasenadissa kosalassa vassāvāsaṃ paṭissuṇitvā visaṃvādesī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, rañño pasenadissa kosalassa vassāvāsaṃ paṭissuṇitvā visaṃvādessasi. Nanu mayā, moghapurisa, anekapariyāyena [T 1.0302] musāvādo garahito, musāvādā veramaṇī pasatthā. Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

206. Now at that time, the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan had accepted a rains-residence from King Pasenadi of Kosala for the earlier period. While on his way to that residence, he saw two residences along the way that had plenty of robes. This thought occurred to him: “It would be good if I were to spend the rains-retreat in these two residences. In this way, many robes will arise for me.” So he spent the rains-retreat in those two residences. King Pasenadi of Kosala complained, grumbled, and criticized him, saying, “How indeed could the noble Upananda the Sakyan, having accepted our rains-residence, break his word? Has not the Blessed One in many ways criticized false speech and praised abstaining from false speech?” The monks heard King Pasenadi of Kosala complaining, grumbling, and criticizing. Those monks who were of few wishes… complained, grumbled, and criticized him, saying, “How indeed could the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan, having accepted the rains-residence of King Pasenadi of Kosala, break his word? Has not the Blessed One in many ways criticized false speech and praised abstaining from false speech?” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having convened the Sangha of monks, questioned the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan: “Is it true, Upananda, that you accepted the rains-residence of King Pasenadi of Kosala and then broke your word?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “How indeed, foolish man, could you, having accepted the rains-residence of King Pasenadi of Kosala, break your word? Have not I, foolish man, in many ways criticized false speech and praised abstaining from false speech? This, foolish man, does not lead to confidence for the unconfident…” Having rebuked him… having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks:

207. Idha [V 0.0203] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā vassāvāso paṭissuto hoti purimikāya. So taṃ āvāsaṃ gacchanto passati antarāmagge dve āvāse bahucīvarake. Tassa evaṃ hoti – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ imesu dvīsu āvāsesu vassaṃ vaseyyaṃ. Evaṃ me bahuṃ cīvaraṃ uppajjissatī”ti. So tesu dvīsu āvāsesu vassaṃ vasati. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimikā ca na paññāyati, paṭissave ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

207. Here, O monks, a monk has accepted a rains-residence for the earlier period. While on his way to that residence, he sees along the way two residences with many robes. To him, this thought occurs: ‘It would be good if I were to spend the rains-residence in these two residences. In this way, many robes will arise for me.’ So he spends the rains-residence in those two residences. For that monk, O monks, the earlier rains-residence is not established, and for his promise, he commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā vassāvāso paṭissuto hoti purimikāya. So taṃ āvāsaṃ gacchanto bahiddhā uposathaṃ karoti, pāṭipade pāṭipadena (ka.) vihāraṃ upeti, senāsanaṃ paññapeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjati. So tadaheva akaraṇīyo pakkamati. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimikā ca na paññāyati, paṭissave ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Here, O monks, a monk has accepted a rains-residence for the earlier period. While on his way to that residence, he performs the Uposatha outside. On the first day of the new fortnight, he goes to the monastery, prepares a lodging, sets out drinking water and water for use, and sweeps the compound. Then, on that very day, he departs without having any business to attend to. For that monk, O monks, the earlier rains-residence is not established, and for his promise, he commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā vassāvāso paṭissuto hoti purimikāya. So taṃ āvāsaṃ gacchanto bahiddhā uposathaṃ karoti, pāṭipade vihāraṃ upeti, senāsanaṃ paññapeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjati. So tadaheva sakaraṇīyo pakkamati. Tassa[M 0.0215], bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimikā ca na paññāyati, paṭissave ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Here, O monks, a monk has accepted a rains-residence for the earlier period. While on his way to that residence, he performs the Uposatha outside. On the first day of the new fortnight, he goes to the monastery, prepares a lodging, sets out drinking water and water for use, and sweeps the compound. Then, on that very day, he departs, having business to attend to. For that monk, O monks, the earlier rains-residence is not established, and for his promise, he commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā vassāvāso paṭissuto hoti purimikāya. So taṃ āvāsaṃ gacchanto [T 1.0303] bahiddhā uposathaṃ karoti, pāṭipade vihāraṃ upeti, senāsanaṃ paññapeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjati. So dvīhatīhaṃ vasitvā akaraṇīyo pakkamati. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimikā ca na paññāyati, paṭissave ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Here, O monks, a monk has accepted a rains-residence for the earlier period. While on his way to that residence, he performs the Uposatha outside. On the first day of the new fortnight, he goes to the monastery, prepares a lodging, sets out drinking water and water for use, and sweeps the compound. Having stayed for two or three days, he departs without having any business to attend to. For that monk, O monks, the earlier rains-residence is not established, and for his promise, he commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā vassāvāso paṭissuto hoti purimikāya. So taṃ āvāsaṃ gacchanto bahiddhā uposathaṃ karoti, pāṭipade vihāraṃ upeti, senāsanaṃ paññapeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjati. So dvīhatīhaṃ vasitvā sakaraṇīyo pakkamati. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimikā ca na paññāyati, paṭissave ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Here, O monks, a monk has accepted a rains-residence for the earlier period. While on his way to that residence, he performs the Uposatha outside. On the first day of the new fortnight, he goes to the monastery, prepares a lodging, sets out drinking water and water for use, and sweeps the compound. Having stayed for two or three days, he departs, having business to attend to. For that monk, O monks, the earlier rains-residence is not established, and for his promise, he commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā vassāvāso paṭissuto hoti purimikāya. So taṃ āvāsaṃ [V 0.0204] gacchanto bahiddhā uposathaṃ karoti, pāṭipade vihāraṃ upeti, senāsanaṃ paññapeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjati. So dvīhatīhaṃ vasitvā sattāhakaraṇīyena pakkamati. So taṃ sattāhaṃ bahiddhā vītināmeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno purimikā ca na paññāyati, paṭissave ca āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Here, O monks, a monk has accepted a rains-residence for the earlier period. While on his way to that residence, he performs the Uposatha outside. On the first day of the new fortnight, he goes to the monastery, prepares a lodging, sets out drinking water and water for use, and sweeps the compound. Having stayed for two or three days, he departs on business that allows for a seven-day leave. He spends those seven days outside. For that monk, O monks, the earlier rains-residence is not established, and for his promise, he commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā vassāvāso paṭissuto hoti purimikāya. So taṃ āvāsaṃ gacchanto bahiddhā uposathaṃ karoti, pāṭipade vihāraṃ upeti, senāsanaṃ paññapeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjati. Moreover, monks, a monk has promised a rains-residence for the earlier period. While on his way to that dwelling, he performs the Uposatha outside. On the first day of the fortnight, he approaches the monastery, prepares a lodging, sets out drinking water and water for use, and sweeps the compound. Having stayed for two or three days, he departs on business that allows for a seven-day leave. He returns within that seven-day period. For that monk, monks, the earlier period is reckoned, and for the promise, there is no offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave[T 1.0304], bhikkhunā vassāvāso paṭissuto hoti purimikāya. Moreover, in this Dispensation, O monks, a monk has undertaken the rains-residence for the later period. While going to that residence, he performs the Uposatha outside, approaches the monastery on the first day, prepares the lodging, sets out drinking water and water for use, and sweeps the compound. Having stayed for two or three days, he departs on a seven-day business. He makes a return within that seven-day period. For that monk, O monks, the later period is reckoned, and there is no offense for the undertaking.

So taṃ āvāsaṃ gacchanto bahiddhā uposathaṃ karoti, pāṭipade vihāraṃ upeti, senāsanaṃ paññapeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjati. While going to that residence, he performs the Uposatha outside, approaches the monastery on the first day, prepares the lodging, sets out drinking water and water for use, and sweeps the compound. He departs on some business when less than seven days remain until the Komudī four-monthly full moon. Whether that monk, O monks, should come to that residence or should not come, for that monk, O monks, the later period is reckoned, and there is no offense for the undertaking.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā vassāvāso paṭissuto hoti pacchimikāya. So taṃ āvāsaṃ gantvā uposathaṃ karoti, pāṭipade vihāraṃ upeti, senāsanaṃ paññapeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjati. So tadaheva akaraṇīyo pakkamati.
