On that very day, he departs, having no business to do. For that monk, O monks, the later period is not reckoned, and for the undertaking, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā vassāvāso paṭissuto hoti pacchimikāya. So taṃ āvāsaṃ gantvā uposathaṃ karoti, pāṭipade vihāraṃ upeti, senāsanaṃ paññapeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjati. So tadaheva sakaraṇīyo pakkamati…pe… so dvīhatīhaṃ vasitvā akaraṇīyo pakkamati [T 1.0307] …pe… so dvīhatīhaṃ vasitvā sakaraṇīyo pakkamati…pe… so dvīhatīhaṃ vasitvā sattāhakaraṇīyena pakkamati. So taṃ sattāhaṃ bahiddhā vītināmeti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pacchimikā ca na paññāyati, paṭissave ca āpatti dukkaṭassa…pe… so dvīhatīhaṃ vasitvā sattāhakaraṇīyena pakkamati. So taṃ sattāhaṃ [V 0.0207] anto sannivattaṃ karoti. Tassa bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pacchimikā ca paññāyati, paṭissave ca anāpatti.

Moreover, in this Dispensation, O monks, a monk has undertaken the rains-residence for the later period. Having gone to that residence, he performs the Uposatha; on the first day, he approaches the monastery, prepares the lodging, sets out drinking water and water for use, and sweeps the compound. On that very day, having a duty to perform, he departs… or, having stayed for two or three days, he departs without a duty to perform… or, having stayed for two or three days, he departs with a duty to perform… or, having stayed for two or three days, he departs on a seven-day business. He spends those seven days outside. For that monk, O monks, the later rains-residence is not established, and because of the undertaking, there is an offense of wrong-doing… or, having stayed for two or three days, he departs on a seven-day business. He makes a return within those seven days. For that monk, O monks, the later rains-residence is established, and because of the undertaking, there is no offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā vassāvāso paṭissuto hoti pacchimikāya. So taṃ āvāsaṃ gantvā uposathaṃ karoti, pāṭipade vihāraṃ upeti, senāsanaṃ paññapeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, pariveṇaṃ sammajjati. So sattāhaṃ anāgatāya komudiyā cātumāsiniyā sakaraṇīyo pakkamati. Āgaccheyya vā so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu taṃ āvāsaṃ na vā āgaccheyya, tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pacchimikā ca paññāyati, paṭissave ca anāpattīti.

Moreover, in this Dispensation, O monks, a monk has undertaken the rains-residence for the later period. Having gone to that residence, he observes the Uposatha; on the first day, he approaches the monastery, prepares the lodging, sets out drinking water and water for use, and sweeps the compound. He departs with a duty to perform when less than seven days remain until the Komudī four-monthly full moon. Whether that monk, O monks, returns to that residence or does not return, for that monk, O monks, the later rains-residence is established, and because of the undertaking, there is no offense.

Paṭissavadukkaṭāpatti niṭṭhitā.

The Offense of Wrong-doing by Promising is concluded.

Vassūpanāyikakkhandhako tatiyo.

The third chapter, on Entering the Rains-Residence, is concluded.

119. Tassuddānaṃ

The summary:

Upagantuṃ [M 0.0219] kadā ceva, kati antarāvassa ca;

Na icchanti ca sañcicca, ukkaḍḍhituṃ upāsako.

119. Entering, and when; how many, and interruption of the rains; not wishing, and intentionally; postponing, the lay follower.

Gilāno [P 1.0156] mātā ca pitā, bhātā ca atha ñātako;

Bhikkhugatiko vihāro, vāḷā cāpi sarīsapā.

A sick person, mother, and father; brother, and then a relative; a monk's co-resident, a monastery; and also beasts of prey and reptiles.

Coro ceva pisācā ca, daḍḍhā tadubhayena ca;

Vūḷhodakena vuṭṭhāsi, bahutarā ca dāyakā.

A thief, and also pisācas; and both being burned; swept away by water, an abandoned village; more populous places, and supporters.

Lūkhappaṇītasappāya, bhesajjupaṭṭhakena [T 1.0308] ca;

Itthī vesī kumārī ca, paṇḍako ñātakena ca.

Coarse, refined, and suitable food; medicine and an attendant; a woman, a prostitute, a maiden, a eunuch, and a relative.

Rājā corā dhuttā nidhi, bhedaaṭṭhavidhena bhedā aṭṭhavidhena (sī. syā.) ca;

Vajasatthā ca nāvā ca, susire viṭabhiyā ca.

A king, thieves, rogues, a treasure, schism, and the eight kinds; a cattle-pen, a caravan, a boat, a hollow tree, and the fork of a tree.

Ajjhokāse [V 0.0208] vassāvāso, asenāsanikena ca;

Chavakuṭikā chatte ca, cāṭiyā ca upenti te.

They enter the rains-residence in the open air, without a lodging, in a charnel-house hut, under a parasol, and in a jar.

Katikā paṭissuṇitvā, bahiddhā ca uposathā;

Purimikā pacchimikā, yathāñāyena yojaye.

An unlawful agreement, defaulting after having agreed, and the Uposatha outside; the earlier and the later rains-residences, one should connect according to the proper method.

Akaraṇī pakkamati, sakaraṇī tatheva ca;

Dvīhatīhā ca puna ca dvīhatīhaṃ vasitvāna (sī.), sattāhakaraṇīyena ca.

Departing without business, and likewise with business; for two or three days, and again on seven-day business.

Sattāhanāgatā ceva, āgaccheyya na eyya vā;

Vatthuddāne antarikā, tantimaggaṃ nisāmayeti.

When less than seven days remain, and whether one comes or does not come; in the summary of topics, this intervening verse, one should attend to the thread of the text.

Imamhi khandhake vatthūni dvepaṇṇāsa.

In this chapter, there are fifty-two topics.

Vassūpanāyikakkhandhako niṭṭhito.

The Chapter on Entering the Rains-Residence is finished.

4. Pavāraṇākkhandhako

The Chapter on the Invitation Ceremony

120. Aphāsukavihāro

4. Uncomfortable Living

209. Tena [P 1.0157][M 0.0220][V 0.0209][T 1.0309] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā sandiṭṭhā sambhattā bhikkhū kosalesu janapade aññatarasmiṃ āvāse vassaṃ upagacchiṃsu. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho mayaṃ upāyena samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vaseyyāma, na ca piṇḍakena kilameyyāmā”ti. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “sace kho mayaṃ aññamaññaṃ neva ālapeyyāma na sallapeyyāma – yo paṭhamaṃ gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkameyya so āsanaṃ paññapeyya, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipeyya, avakkārapātiṃ dhovitvā upaṭṭhāpeyya, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeyya; yo pacchā gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkameyya, sacassa bhuttāvaseso, sace ākaṅkheyya bhuñjeyya, no ce ākaṅkheyya appaharite vā chaḍḍeyya, appāṇake vā udake opilāpeyya; so āsanaṃ uddhareyya, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ paṭisāmeyya, avakkārapātiṃ dhovitvā paṭisāmeyya, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ paṭisāmeyya, bhattaggaṃ sammajjeyya; yo passeyya pānīyaghaṭaṃ vā paribhojanīyaghaṭaṃ vā vaccaghaṭaṃ vā rittaṃ tucchaṃ so upaṭṭhāpeyya; sacassa hoti avisayhaṃ, hatthavikārena dutiyaṃ āmantetvā hatthavilaṅghakena upaṭṭhāpeyya; na tveva tappaccayā vācaṃ bhindeyya – evaṃ kho mayaṃ samaggā [T 1.0310] sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vaseyyāma, na ca piṇḍakena kilameyyāmā”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū aññamaññaṃ neva ālapiṃsu, na sallapiṃsu. Yo paṭhamaṃ gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamati, so āsanaṃ paññapeti, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipati, avakkārapātiṃ dhovitvā upaṭṭhāpeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti[P 1.0158]. Yo pacchā gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamati, sace hoti bhuttāvaseso, sace ākaṅkhati bhuñjati, no ce ākaṅkhati appaharite vā chaḍḍeti, appāṇake vā udake opilāpeti; so āsanaṃ uddharati, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ [V 0.0210] pādakathalikaṃ paṭisāmeti, avakkārapātiṃ dhovitvā paṭisāmeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ paṭisāmeti, bhattaggaṃ [M 0.0221] sammajjati. Yo passati pānīyaghaṭaṃ vā paribhojanīyaghaṭaṃ vā vaccaghaṭaṃ vā rittaṃ tucchaṃ so upaṭṭhāpeti. Sacassa hoti avisayhaṃ, hatthavikārena dutiyaṃ āmantetvā hatthavilaṅghakena upaṭṭhāpeti, na tveva tappaccayā vācaṃ bhindati.

209. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, many monks who were acquainted and had partaken of meals together entered upon the rains-residence in a certain monastery in the Kosalan country. Then this thought occurred to those monks: “By what means indeed could we dwell in unity, rejoicing together, without disputing, spend the rains-residence comfortably, and not be weary on account of alms-food?” Then this thought occurred to those monks: “If indeed we were neither to speak first nor converse with one another—whoever should return first from the village from the alms-round, he should prepare the seat, place nearby the foot-washing water, the footstool, and the potsherd for rubbing the feet, wash the refuse bowl and set it out, and set out drinking water and water for use. Whoever should return later from the village from the alms-round, if there are leftovers from his meal and if he should wish, he should eat; if he should not wish, he should discard them on ground free of greenery or pour them into water without living beings. He should clear away the seat, store away the foot-washing water, the footstool, and the potsherd for rubbing the feet, wash and store away the refuse bowl, store away the drinking water and water for use, and sweep the dining hall. Whoever should see that the drinking water pot, the pot for water for use, or the toilet water pot is empty and void, he should set it up. If it should be too heavy for him to lift, he should call a second person by a hand gesture and, by linking hands, set it up; but on account of that, he should not break his silence. In this way, indeed, we could dwell in unity, rejoicing together, without disputing, spend the rains-residence comfortably, and not be weary on account of alms-food.” Then those monks neither spoke first nor conversed with one another. Whoever returns first from the village from the alms-round prepares the seat, places nearby the foot-washing water, the footstool, and the potsherd for rubbing the feet, washes the refuse bowl and sets it out, and sets out drinking water and water for use. Whoever returns later from the village from the alms-round, if there are leftovers from his meal and if he wishes, he eats; if he does not wish, he discards them on ground free of greenery or pours them into water without living beings. He clears away the seat, stores away the foot-washing water, the footstool, and the potsherd for rubbing the feet, washes and stores away the refuse bowl, stores away the drinking water and water for use, and sweeps the dining hall. Whoever sees that the drinking water pot, the pot for water for use, or the toilet water pot is empty and void, he sets it up. If it is too heavy for him to lift, he calls a second person by a hand gesture and, by linking hands, sets it up; but on account of that, he does not break his silence.

Āciṇṇaṃ kho panetaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū vassaṃvuṭṭhā temāsaccayena senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena sāvatthi tena pakkamiṃsu. Anupubbena yena sāvatthi jetavanaṃ anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāmo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Āciṇṇaṃ kho panetaṃ buddhānaṃ [T 1.0311] bhagavantānaṃ āgantukehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ paṭisammodituṃ. Atha kho bhagavā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “kacci, bhikkhave, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kacci samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vasittha, na ca piṇḍakena kilamitthā”ti? “Khamanīyaṃ bhagavā, yāpanīyaṃ bhagavā. Samaggā ca mayaṃ, bhante, sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vasimhā, na ca piṇḍakena kilamimhā”ti. Jānantāpi tathāgatā pucchanti, jānantāpi na pucchanti. Kālaṃ viditvā pucchanti, kālaṃ viditvā na pucchanti. Atthasaṃhitaṃ tathāgatā pucchanti, no anatthasaṃhitaṃ. Anatthasaṃhite setughāto tathāgatānaṃ. Dvīhākārehi buddhā bhagavanto bhikkhū paṭipucchanti – dhammaṃ vā desessāma, sāvakānaṃ vā sikkhāpadaṃ paññapessāmāti. Atha kho bhagavā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “yathākathaṃ pana tumhe, bhikkhave, samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vasittha, na ca piṇḍakena kilamitthā”ti.

Now it is customary for monks who have completed the rains residence to visit the Blessed One. Then those monks, having completed the rains residence after three months, put their lodgings in order, took their bowls and robes, and set out for Sāvatthī. Gradually, they arrived at Sāvatthī, at Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery, and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Now it is customary for the Blessed Buddhas to exchange greetings with visiting monks. Then the Blessed One said to those monks: “I hope, monks, it has been tolerable; I hope it has been bearable? I hope you have spent the rains in harmony, rejoicing together, without dispute, comfortably, and without trouble obtaining alms-food?” “It has been tolerable, Blessed One; it has been bearable, Blessed One. We have spent the rains, venerable sir, in harmony, rejoicing together, without dispute, comfortably, and without trouble obtaining alms-food.” Even though the Tathāgatas know, they ask; even though they know, they do not ask. They ask knowing the right time, and they do not ask knowing the right time. The Tathāgatas ask what is connected with benefit, not what is not connected with benefit. The Tathāgatas have a barrier against what is not connected with benefit. The Blessed Buddhas question the monks for two reasons: either to teach the Dhamma or to lay down a training rule for the disciples. Then the Blessed One said to those monks: “But how, monks, did you spend the rains in harmony, rejoicing together, without dispute, comfortably, and without trouble obtaining alms-food?”

Idha mayaṃ, bhante, sambahulā sandiṭṭhā sambhattā bhikkhū kosalesu janapade aññatarasmiṃ āvāse vassaṃ upagacchimhā. Tesaṃ no, bhante, amhākaṃ etadahosi – “kena nu kho mayaṃ upāyena samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vaseyyāma, na ca [P 1.0159] piṇḍakena kilameyyāmā”ti. Tesaṃ no, bhante, amhākaṃ etadahosi – “sace kho mayaṃ aññamaññaṃ neva ālapeyyāma na sallapeyyāma – yo paṭhamaṃ gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkameyya so āsanaṃ paññapeyya, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ [T 1.0312] pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipeyya, avakkārapātiṃ dhovitvā upaṭṭhāpeyya, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeyya; yo pacchā gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkameyya, sacassa bhuttāvaseso[M 0.0222], sace ākaṅkheyya bhuñjeyya, no ce ākaṅkheyya appaharite vā chaḍḍeyya, appāṇake vā udake opilāpeyya; so āsanaṃ uddhareyya, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ paṭisāmeyya[V 0.0211], avakkārapātiṃ dhovitvā paṭisāmeyya, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ paṭisāmeyya, bhattaggaṃ sammajjeyya; yo passeyya pānīyaghaṭaṃ vā paribhojanīyaghaṭaṃ vā vaccaghaṭaṃ vā rittaṃ tucchaṃ so upaṭṭhāpeyya; sacassa hoti avisayhaṃ, hatthavikārena dutiyaṃ āmantetvā hatthavilaṅghakena upaṭṭhāpeyya; na tveva tappaccayā vācaṃ bhindeyya – evaṃ kho mayaṃ samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vaseyyāma, na ca piṇḍakena kilameyyāmā”ti. Atha kho mayaṃ, bhante, aññamaññaṃ neva ālapimhā na sallavimhā. Yo paṭhamaṃ gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamati so āsanaṃ paññapeti, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipati, avakkārapātiṃ dhovitvā upaṭṭhāpeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti. Yo pacchā gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamati, sace hoti bhuttāvaseso, sace ākaṅkhati bhuñjati, no ce ākaṅkhati appaharite vā chaḍḍeti, appāṇake vā udake opilāpeti, so āsanaṃ uddharati, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ paṭisāmeti, avakkārapātiṃ dhovitvā paṭisāmeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ [T 1.0313] paṭisāmeti, bhattaggaṃ sammajjati. Yo passati pānīyaghaṭaṃ vā paribhojanīyaghaṭaṃ vā vaccaghaṭaṃ vā rittaṃ tucchaṃ so upaṭṭhāpeti. Sacassa hoti avisayhaṃ, hatthavikārena dutiyaṃ āmantetvā hatthavilaṅghakena upaṭṭhāpeti, na tveva tappaccayā vācaṃ bhindati. Evaṃ kho mayaṃ, bhante, samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vasimhā, na ca piṇḍakena kilamimhāti.

Here, venerable sir, several bhikkhus, acquainted and associated with each other, entered the rains residence in a certain dwelling in the Kosala country. Then, venerable sir, this occurred to us: “By what means could we dwell in concord, in harmony, without dispute, spending the rains comfortably, without being troubled by almsfood?” Then, venerable sir, this occurred to us: “Suppose we neither address nor converse with one another. Whoever returns first from the village after the alms-round should prepare the seats, set out the foot-washing water, the footstool, and the foot-wiping shard, wash the refuse bowl and set it out, and set out drinking water and water for use. Whoever returns later from the village after the alms-round, if there are leftovers, if he wishes, he may eat; if he does not wish to eat, he should discard them where there is no green grass or pour them into water where there are no living beings. He should put away the seats, store the foot-washing water, the footstool, and the foot-wiping shard, wash the refuse bowl and store it, and store the drinking water and water for use. He should sweep the refectory. Whoever sees that the drinking water pot, the water for use pot, or the toilet pot is empty and void, he should set it up. If it is too heavy for him to lift, he should call a second person with a hand gesture and, by passing it from hand to hand, set it in place; but he should not break into speech on that account. In this way, we could dwell in concord, in harmony, without dispute, spending the rains comfortably, without being troubled by almsfood.” Then, venerable sir, we neither addressed nor conversed with one another. Whoever returned first from the village after the alms-round prepared the seats, set out the foot-washing water, the footstool, and the foot-wiping shard, washed the refuse bowl and set it out, and set out drinking water and water for use. Whoever returned later from the village after the alms-round, if there were leftovers, if he wished, he ate; if he did not wish to eat, he discarded them where there was no green grass or poured them into water where there are no living beings. He put away the seats, stored the foot-washing water, the footstool, and the foot-wiping shard, washed the refuse bowl and stored it, and stored the drinking water and water for use. He swept the refectory. Whoever saw that the drinking water pot, the water for use pot, or the toilet pot was empty and void, he set it up. If it was too heavy for him to lift, he called a second person with a hand gesture and, by passing it from hand to hand, they set it in place; but he did not break into speech on that account. In this way, venerable sir, we dwelled in concord, in harmony, without dispute, spending the rains comfortably, and were not troubled by almsfood.

Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “aphāsuññeva aphāsukaññeva (sī.) kirame kirime (ka.), bhikkhave, moghapurisā vuṭṭhā vutthā (ka.) samānā phāsumhā phāsukamhā (sī.) vuṭṭhāti paṭijānanti. Pasusaṃvāsaññeva kirame, bhikkhave, moghapurisā vuṭṭhā samānā phāsumhā vuṭṭhāti paṭijānanti. Eḷakasaṃvāsaññeva kirame, bhikkhave, moghapurisā vuṭṭhā samānā phāsumhā vuṭṭhāti paṭijānanti. Sapattasaṃvāsaññeva kirame, bhikkhave, moghapurisā vuṭṭhā samānā phāsumhā vuṭṭhāti paṭijānanti. Kathañhi nāmime, bhikkhave, moghapurisā mūgabbataṃ titthiyasamādānaṃ samādiyissa”nti. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā dhammiṃ [M 0.0223] kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – na, bhikkhave, mūgabbataṃ titthiyasamādānaṃ samādiyitabbaṃ. Yo samādiyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ tīhi ṭhānehi pavāretuṃ – diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Sā vo bhavissati aññamaññānulomatā āpattivuṭṭhānatā vinayapurekkhāratā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, pavāretabbaṃ. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo [T 1.0314] –

Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, it is said that these foolish men, having lived only in discomfort, declare, ‘We have lived in comfort.’ It is said that these foolish men, bhikkhus, having lived only a dwelling like that of cattle, declare, ‘We have lived in comfort.’ It is said that these foolish men, bhikkhus, having lived only a dwelling like that of goats, declare, ‘We have lived in comfort.’ It is said that these foolish men, bhikkhus, having lived only a dwelling like that of enemies, declare, ‘We have lived in comfort.’ How indeed, bhikkhus, can these foolish men undertake the vow of silence, a practice adopted by sectarians?” This is not, bhikkhus, for inspiring confidence in those who are not yet confident… Having rebuked them and given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, the vow of silence, a practice adopted by sectarians, should not be undertaken. Whoever should undertake it, commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, bhikkhus, for bhikkhus who have completed the rains-residence to invite correction on three grounds: by what has been seen, by what has been heard, or by what is suspected. That invitation of yours will be for mutual agreeableness, for rising from offenses, and for holding the discipline as foremost. And thus, bhikkhus, the invitation should be made. The Sangha should be informed by a competent and able bhikkhu:

210. “Suṇātu [V 0.0212] me, bhante, saṅgho. Ajja pavāraṇā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho pavāreyyā”ti.

210. “Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. Today is the Pavāraṇā. If it is timely for the Sangha, the Sangha should perform the Pavāraṇā.”

Therena bhikkhunā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “saṅghaṃ, āvuso, pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadantu maṃ āyasmanto anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmi. Dutiyampi, āvuso, saṅghaṃ pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadantu maṃ āyasmanto anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmi. Tatiyampi, āvuso, saṅghaṃ pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadantu maṃ āyasmanto anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmī”ti.

By an elder bhikkhu, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having sat down squatting, and having raised his joined palms, it should be said thus: 'Friends, I invite the Saṅgha by what is seen, or by what is heard, or by what is suspected. Let the venerable ones speak to me out of compassion. Seeing it, I will make amends. For a second time, friends, I invite the Saṅgha by what is seen, or by what is heard, or by what is suspected. Let the venerable ones speak to me out of compassion. Seeing it, I will make amends. For a third time, friends, I invite the Saṅgha by what is seen, or by what is heard, or by what is suspected. Let the venerable ones speak to me out of compassion. Seeing it, I will make amends.'

Navakena bhikkhunā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “saṅghaṃ, bhante, pavāremi diṭṭhena [P 1.0160] vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadantu maṃ āyasmanto anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmi. Dutiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ…pe… tatiyampi, bhante, saṅghaṃ pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadantu maṃ āyasmanto anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmī”ti.

A junior bhikkhu, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having sat down squatting, and having raised his joined palms, should speak thus: 'Venerable sirs, I invite the Saṅgha regarding what has been seen, what has been heard, or what is suspected. Let the venerable ones speak to me out of compassion. Seeing an offense, I will make amends. For a second time, venerable sirs, I invite the Saṅgha… For a third time, venerable sirs, I invite the Saṅgha regarding what has been seen, what has been heard, or what is suspected. Let the venerable ones speak to me out of compassion. Seeing an offense, I will make amends.'

211. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū theresu bhikkhūsu ukkuṭikaṃ nisinnesu pavārayamānesu āsanesu acchanti. Ye te bhikkhū [T 1.0315] appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū theresu bhikkhūsu ukkuṭikaṃ nisinnesu pavārayamānesu āsanesu acchissantī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū theresu bhikkhūsu ukkuṭikaṃ nisinnesu pavārayamānesu āsanesu acchantī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi [M 0.0224] buddho bhagavā…pe… “kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā theresu bhikkhūsu ukkuṭikaṃ nisinnesu pavārayamānesu āsanesu acchissa”nti. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya, pasannānaṃ vā bhiyyobhāvāya…pe… vigarahitvā dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, theresu bhikkhūsu ukkuṭikaṃ nisinnesu pavārayamānesu āsanesu acchitabbaṃ. Yo accheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sabbeheva ukkuṭikaṃ nisinnehi pavāretu”nti.

211. Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus remained on their seats while the elder bhikkhus, sitting squatting, were performing the Pavāraṇā. Those bhikkhus who were of few wishes… criticized, scorned, and disparaged them, saying: “How can the group-of-six bhikkhus remain on their seats while the elder bhikkhus, sitting squatting, are performing the Pavāraṇā?” Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that the group-of-six bhikkhus remain on their seats while the elder bhikkhus, sitting squatting, are performing the Pavāraṇā?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Blessed One, the Buddha, rebuked them… “How indeed, bhikkhus, can those foolish men remain on their seats while the elder bhikkhus, sitting squatting, are performing the Pavāraṇā? Bhikkhus, this does not lead to the confidence of the unconfident, nor to the increase of confidence in the confident…” Having rebuked them and given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, one should not remain on a seat while elder bhikkhus, sitting squatting, are performing the Pavāraṇā. Whoever should remain, commits an offense of wrong conduct. Bhikkhus, I allow that all may perform the Pavāraṇā while sitting squatting.”

Tena [V 0.0213] kho pana samayena aññataro thero jarādubbalo yāva sabbe pavārentīti yāva sabbe pavārenti (syā.) ukkuṭikaṃ nisinno āgamayamāno mucchito papati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tadamantarā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīdituṃ yāva pavāreti, pavāretvā āsane nisīditunti.

At that time, a certain elder bhikkhu, weak with age, while waiting for all to perform the Pavāraṇā, sat squatting, fainted, and fell. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow one to sit squatting during the interval of performing the Pavāraṇā, and having performed the Pavāraṇā, to sit on a seat.”

Aphāsukavihāro niṭṭhito.

The Chapter on Dwelling in Discomfort is concluded.

121. Pavāraṇābhedā

The Divisions of Pavāraṇā

212. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kati nu kho pavāraṇā”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Dvemā, bhikkhave, pavāraṇā – cātuddasikā ca pannarasikā ca. Imā kho, bhikkhave, dve pavāraṇāti.

121. Then this thought arose in the bhikkhus: “How many Pavāraṇās are there?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, there are these two Pavāraṇās: the fourteenth-day and the fifteenth-day. These, bhikkhus, are the two Pavāraṇās.”

Atha [T 1.0316] kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kati nu kho pavāraṇakammānī”ti? pavāraṇākammānīti (syā.) Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, pavāraṇakammāni – adhammena vaggaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ, adhammena samaggaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ, dhammena vaggaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ, dhammena samaggaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ. Tatra, bhikkhave, yadidaṃ adhammena vaggaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ, na, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ kātabbaṃ; na ca mayā evarūpaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ anuññātaṃ. Tatra, bhikkhave, yadidaṃ adhammena samaggaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ, na, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ kātabbaṃ; na ca mayā evarūpaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ anuññātaṃ. Tatra, bhikkhave, yadidaṃ dhammena vaggaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ, na, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ kātabbaṃ; na ca mayā evarūpaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ anuññātaṃ. Tatra, bhikkhave, yadidaṃ dhammena samaggaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ, evarūpaṃ, bhikkhave, pavāraṇakammaṃ kātabbaṃ; evarūpañca mayā pavāraṇakammaṃ anuññātaṃ. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ karissāma yadidaṃ dhammena samagganti, evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbanti.

212. Then this thought arose in the bhikkhus: “How many acts of Pavāraṇā are there?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, there are these four acts of Pavāraṇā: an unlawful act of Pavāraṇā by a divided community, an unlawful act of Pavāraṇā by a united community, a lawful act of Pavāraṇā by a divided community, and a lawful act of Pavāraṇā by a united community. Among these, bhikkhus, that which is an unlawful act of Pavāraṇā by a divided community should not be performed; nor has such an act of Pavāraṇā been permitted by me. Among these, bhikkhus, that which is an unlawful act of Pavāraṇā by a united community should not be performed; nor has such an act of Pavāraṇā been permitted by me. Among these, bhikkhus, that which is a lawful act of Pavāraṇā by a divided community should not be performed; nor has such an act of Pavāraṇā been permitted by me. Among these, bhikkhus, that which is a lawful act of Pavāraṇā by a united community should be performed; and such an act of Pavāraṇā has been permitted by me. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We shall perform such an act of Pavāraṇā that is lawful and by a united community.’”

Pavāraṇābhedā niṭṭhitā.

The Divisions of Pavāraṇā are concluded.

122. Pavāraṇādānānujānanā

Permission for the Giving of Pavāraṇā

213. Atha [M 0.0225] kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “sannipatatha, bhikkhave. Saṅgho pavāressatī”ti. Evaṃ vutte aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “atthi, bhante, bhikkhu gilāno[V 0.0214], so anāgato”ti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānena bhikkhunā pavāraṇaṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbā – tena gilānena bhikkhunā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ [P 1.0161] upasaṅkamitvā [T 1.0317] ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “pavāraṇaṃ dammi, pavāraṇaṃ me hara, pavāraṇaṃ me ārocehi, mamatthāya pavārehī”ti kāyena viññāpeti, vācāya viññāpeti, kāyena vācāya viññāpeti, dinnā hoti pavāraṇā; na kāyena viññāpeti, na vācāya viññāpeti, na kāyena vācāya viññāpeti, na dinnā hoti pavāraṇā. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, so, bhikkhave, gilāno bhikkhu mañcena vā pīṭhena vā saṅghamajjhe ānetvā pavāretabbaṃ. Sace, bhikkhave, gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “sace kho mayaṃ gilānaṃ ṭhānā cāvessāma, ābādho vā abhivaḍḍhissati, kālaṃkiriyā vā bhavissatī”ti na, bhikkhave, gilāno bhikkhu ṭhānā cāvetabbo. Saṅghena tattha gantvā pavāretabbaṃ; na tveva vaggena saṅghena pavāretabbaṃ. Pavāreyya ce, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

213. Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Gather, bhikkhus. The Saṅgha will perform the Pavāraṇā.” When this was said, a certain bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, there is a sick bhikkhu who has not come.” “Bhikkhus, I permit a sick bhikkhu to give the Pavāraṇā. And thus, bhikkhus, it should be given: that sick bhikkhu should approach one bhikkhu, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, squat down, raise his joined palms, and say thus: ‘I give the Pavāraṇā; convey my Pavāraṇā; announce my Pavāraṇā; perform the Pavāraṇā on my behalf.’ If he makes it known by body, by speech, or by both body and speech, the Pavāraṇā is given. If he does not make it known by body, by speech, or by both body and speech, the Pavāraṇā is not given. If he obtains it thus, that is good. If he does not obtain it, then, bhikkhus, that sick bhikkhu should be brought into the midst of the Saṅgha on a bed or a chair, and the Pavāraṇā should be performed. If, bhikkhus, the bhikkhus attending the sick bhikkhu think: ‘If we move the sick one from his place, the illness might increase, or he might die,’ then, bhikkhus, the sick bhikkhu should not be moved from his place. The Saṅgha should go there and perform the Pavāraṇā. But the Pavāraṇā should not be performed by a factional Saṅgha. If one performs it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

Pavāraṇahārako pavāraṇāhārako (syā.) ce, bhikkhave, dinnāya pavāraṇāya tattheva pakkamati, aññassa dātabbā pavāraṇā. Pavāraṇahārako ce, bhikkhave, dinnāya pavāraṇāya tattheva vibbhamati…pe… kālaṃkaroti… sāmaṇero paṭijānāti… sikkhaṃ paccakkhātako paṭijānāti… antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannako paṭijānāti… ummattako paṭijānāti… khittacitto paṭijānāti… vedanāṭṭo paṭijānāti… āpattiyā adassane ukkhittako paṭijānāti… āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittako paṭijānāti… pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittako paṭijānāti… paṇḍako [T 1.0318] paṭijānāti… theyyasaṃvāsako paṭijānāti… titthiyapakkantako paṭijānāti… tiracchānagato paṭijānāti… mātughātako paṭijānāti… pitughātako paṭijānāti… arahantaghātako paṭijānāti… bhikkhunidūsako paṭijānāti… saṅghabhedako paṭijānāti [M 0.0226]… lohituppādako paṭijānāti… ubhatobyañjanako paṭijānāti, aññassa dātabbā pavāraṇā.

If, bhikkhus, the Pavāraṇā-bearer departs right there after the Pavāraṇā has been given, the Pavāraṇā should be given to another. If, bhikkhus, the Pavāraṇā-bearer disrobes right there after the Pavāraṇā has been given… dies… declares himself a novice… declares himself one who has renounced the training… declares himself one who has incurred an ultimate offense… declares himself insane… declares himself deranged… declares himself afflicted by pain… declares himself suspended for not seeing an offense… declares himself suspended for not making amends for an offense… declares himself suspended for not relinquishing a wrong view… declares himself a paṇḍaka… declares himself one who lives in communion by theft… declares himself one who has gone over to another sect… declares himself an animal… declares himself a matricide… declares himself a patricide… declares himself a murderer of an arahant… declares himself a defiler of a bhikkhunī… declares himself a schismatic of the Saṅgha… declares himself one who has maliciously drawn the Tathāgata’s blood… declares himself one with the characteristics of both sexes, the Pavāraṇā should be given to another.

Pavāraṇahārako ce, bhikkhave, dinnāya pavāraṇāya antarāmagge pakkamati, anāhaṭā hoti pavāraṇā. Pavāraṇahārako ce, bhikkhave, dinnāya pavāraṇāya antarāmagge vibbhamati…pe… kālaṃkaroti… sāmaṇero paṭijānāti… sikkhaṃ paccakkhātako paṭijānāti… antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannako paṭijānāti… ummattako paṭijānāti… khittacitto paṭijānāti… vedanāṭṭo paṭijānāti… āpattiyā adassane ukkhittako paṭijānāti… āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittako paṭijānāti… pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge [V 0.0215] ukkhittako paṭijānāti… paṇḍako paṭijānāti… theyyasaṃvāsako paṭijānāti… titthiyapakkantako paṭijānāti… tiracchānagato paṭijānāti… mātughātako paṭijānāti… pitughātako paṭijānāti… arahantaghātako paṭijānāti… bhikkhunidūsako paṭijānāti… saṅghabhedako paṭijānāti… lohituppādako paṭijānāti… ubhatobyañjanako paṭijānāti, anāhaṭā hoti pavāraṇā.

If, bhikkhus, the Pavāraṇā-bearer departs on the way after the Pavāraṇā has been given, the Pavāraṇā is not brought. If, bhikkhus, the Pavāraṇā-bearer disrobes on the way after the Pavāraṇā has been given… dies… declares himself a novice… declares himself one who has renounced the training… declares himself one who has incurred an ultimate offense… declares himself insane… declares himself deranged… declares himself afflicted by pain… declares himself suspended for not seeing an offense… declares himself suspended for not making amends for an offense… declares himself suspended for not relinquishing a wrong view… declares himself a paṇḍaka… declares himself one who lives in communion by theft… declares himself one who has gone over to another sect… declares himself an animal… declares himself a matricide… declares himself a patricide… declares himself a murderer of an arahant… declares himself a defiler of a bhikkhunī… declares himself a schismatic of the Saṅgha… declares himself one who has maliciously drawn the Tathāgata’s blood… declares himself one with the characteristics of both sexes, the Pavāraṇā is not brought.

Pavāraṇahārako ce, bhikkhave, dinnāya pavāraṇāya saṅghappatto pakkamati, āhaṭā hoti pavāraṇā. Pavāraṇahārako ce, bhikkhave, dinnāya pavāraṇāya saṅghappatto vibbhamati…pe… kālaṃkaroti… sāmaṇero paṭijānāti… sikkhaṃ paccakkhātako paṭijānāti… antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannako paṭijānāti… ummattako paṭijānāti… khittacitto paṭijānāti… vedanāṭṭo paṭijānāti… āpattiyā adassane ukkhittako paṭijānāti… āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittako paṭijānāti… pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittako paṭijānāti… paṇḍako paṭijānāti… theyyasaṃvāsako paṭijānāti… titthiyapakkantako paṭijānāti… tiracchānagato paṭijānāti… mātughātako paṭijānāti… pitughātako paṭijānāti… arahantaghātako paṭijānāti… bhikkhunidūsako paṭijānāti… saṅghabhedako paṭijānāti… lohituppādako paṭijānāti… ubhatobyañjanako paṭijānāti, āhaṭā hoti pavāraṇā.

If, bhikkhus, the Pavāraṇā-bearer departs, having reached the Saṅgha after the Pavāraṇā has been given, the Pavāraṇā is brought. If, bhikkhus, the Pavāraṇā-bearer disrobes, having reached the Saṅgha after the Pavāraṇā has been given… dies… declares himself a novice… declares himself one who has renounced the training… declares himself one who has incurred an ultimate offense… declares himself insane… declares himself deranged… declares himself afflicted by pain… declares himself suspended for not seeing an offense… declares himself suspended for not making amends for an offense… declares himself suspended for not relinquishing a wrong view… declares himself a paṇḍaka… declares himself one who lives in communion by theft… declares himself one who has gone over to another sect… declares himself an animal… declares himself a matricide… declares himself a patricide… declares himself a murderer of an arahant… declares himself a defiler of a bhikkhunī… declares himself a schismatic of the Saṅgha… declares himself one who has maliciously drawn the Tathāgata’s blood… declares himself one with the characteristics of both sexes, the Pavāraṇā is brought.

Pavāraṇahārako ce, bhikkhave, dinnāya pavāraṇāya saṅghappatto sutto nāroceti, āhaṭā hoti pavāraṇā. Pavāraṇahārakassa anāpatti[M 0.0227]. Pavāraṇahārako ce, bhikkhave, dinnāya pavāraṇāya saṅghappatto pamatto nāroceti…pe… samāpanno nāroceti, āhaṭā hoti pavāraṇā. Pavāraṇahārakassa anāpatti.

If, bhikkhus, the Pavāraṇā-bearer, having reached the Saṅgha after the Pavāraṇā has been given, falls asleep and does not announce it, the Pavāraṇā is brought. There is no offense for the Pavāraṇā-bearer. If, bhikkhus, the Pavāraṇā-bearer, having reached the Saṅgha after the Pavāraṇā has been given, is negligent and does not announce it… is in an attainment and does not announce it, the Pavāraṇā is brought. There is no offense for the Pavāraṇā-bearer.

Pavāraṇahārako ce, bhikkhave[T 1.0319], dinnāya pavāraṇāya saṅghappatto sañcicca nāroceti, āhaṭā hoti pavāraṇā. Pavāraṇahārakassa āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya pavāraṇaṃ dentena chandampi dātuṃ, santi saṅghassa karaṇīyanti.

Bhikkhus, if the Pavāraṇā-bearer, having reached the Saṅgha after the Pavāraṇā has been given, intentionally does not announce it, the Pavāraṇā is considered brought. The Pavāraṇā-bearer commits an offense of wrong-doing. Bhikkhus, I allow a bhikkhu giving his Pavāraṇā on that Pavāraṇā day to also give his consent, should there be business for the Saṅgha.

Pavāraṇādānānujānanā niṭṭhitā.

The Permission to Give Pavāraṇā is concluded.

123. Ñātakādiggahaṇakathā

123. The Discussion on Seizing by Relatives, etc.

214. Tena [V 0.0216] kho pana samayena aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ tadahu pavāraṇāya ñātakā gaṇhiṃsu. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ tadahu pavāraṇāya ñātakā gaṇhanti. Te ñātakā bhikkhūhi evamassu vacanīyā – “iṅgha, tumhe āyasmanto imaṃ bhikkhuṃ muhuttaṃ muñcatha, yāvāyaṃ bhikkhu pavāretī”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, te ñātakā bhikkhūhi evamassu vacanīyā – “iṅgha, tumhe āyasmanto muhuttaṃ ekamantaṃ hotha, yāvāyaṃ bhikkhu pavāraṇaṃ detī”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, te ñātakā bhikkhūhi evamassu vacanīyā – “iṅgha, tumhe āyasmanto imaṃ bhikkhuṃ muhuttaṃ nissīmaṃ netha, yāva saṅgho pavāretī”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, na tveva vaggena saṅghena pavāretabbaṃ. Pavāreyya ce, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

214. Now on that occasion, relatives seized a certain bhikkhu on the day of the Pavāraṇā. They informed the Blessed One about this matter. 'Bhikkhus, in this teaching, should relatives seize a bhikkhu on the day of the Pavāraṇā, those relatives should be addressed by the bhikkhus thus: “Please, venerable sirs, release this bhikkhu for a moment, until this bhikkhu has performed the Pavāraṇā.” If this is achieved, it is good. If not, those relatives should be addressed by the bhikkhus thus: “Please, venerable sirs, stand aside for a moment, until this bhikkhu has given the Pavāraṇā.” If this is achieved, it is good. If not, those relatives should be addressed by the bhikkhus thus: “Please, venerable sirs, take this bhikkhu outside the boundary for a moment, until the Saṅgha has performed the Pavāraṇā.” If this is achieved, it is good. If not, the Pavāraṇā should not be performed by an incomplete Saṅgha. If they perform it, they commit an offense of wrong-doing.'

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ tadahu pavāraṇāya rājāno gaṇhanti…pe… corā gaṇhanti [P 1.0162]… dhuttā gaṇhanti… bhikkhupaccatthikā gaṇhanti. Te bhikkhupaccatthikā bhikkhūhi evamassu vacanīyā – “iṅgha, tumhe āyasmanto imaṃ bhikkhuṃ muhuttaṃ muñcatha, yāvāyaṃ bhikkhu pavāretī”ti[T 1.0320]. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, te bhikkhupaccatthikā bhikkhūhi evamassu vacanīyā – “iṅgha, tumhe āyasmanto muhuttaṃ ekamantaṃ hotha, yāvāyaṃ bhikkhu pavāraṇaṃ detī”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, te bhikkhupaccatthikā bhikkhūhi evamassu vacanīyā – “iṅgha, tumhe āyasmanto imaṃ bhikkhuṃ muhuttaṃ nissīmaṃ netha, yāva saṅgho pavāretī”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, na [M 0.0228] tveva vaggena saṅghena pavāretabbaṃ. Pavāreyya ce, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Bhikkhus, in this teaching, on the day of Pavāraṇā, kings may seize a bhikkhu... or thieves may seize him... or profligates may seize him... or hostile bhikkhus may seize him. Those hostile bhikkhus should be addressed by the other bhikkhus thus: ‘Please, Venerables, release this bhikkhu for a moment, until this bhikkhu has performed the Pavāraṇā.’ If this is achieved, it is good. If it is not achieved, those hostile bhikkhus should be addressed by the other bhikkhus thus: ‘Please, Venerables, stand aside for a moment, until this bhikkhu has given the Pavāraṇā.’ If this is achieved, it is good. If it is not achieved, those hostile bhikkhus should be addressed by the other bhikkhus thus: ‘Please, Venerables, take this bhikkhu outside the boundary for a moment, until the Saṅgha has performed the Pavāraṇā.’ If this is achieved, it is good. If it is not achieved, the Pavāraṇā should certainly not be performed by a factional Saṅgha. Should they perform it, they commit an offense of wrong-doing.

Ñātakādiggahaṇakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Seizing by Relatives, etc., is finished.

124. Saṅghapavāraṇādippabhedā

124. The Various Kinds of Saṅgha Pavāraṇā, etc.

215. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya pañca bhikkhū viharanti. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘saṅghena pavāretabba’nti. Mayañcamhā pañca janā. Kathaṃ nu kho amhehi pavāretabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ saṅghe pavāretunti.

215. Now at that time, in a certain monastery, five bhikkhus were dwelling on the day of the Pavāraṇā. Then this thought occurred to those bhikkhus: 'It has been laid down by the Blessed One that "the Pavāraṇā should be performed by the Saṅgha." And we are five persons. How then should the Pavāraṇā be performed by us?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Bhikkhus, I allow five to perform the Pavāraṇā as a Saṅgha.'

216. Tena [V 0.0217] kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya cattāro bhikkhū viharanti. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “bhagavatā anuññātaṃ pañcannaṃ saṅghe pavāretunti. Mayañcamhā cattāro janā. Kathaṃ nu kho amhehi pavāretabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ aññamaññaṃ pavāretuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, pavāretabbaṃ. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena te bhikkhū ñāpetabbā –

216. Now at that time, in a certain monastery, four bhikkhus were dwelling on that Pavāraṇā day. Then this thought occurred to those bhikkhus: ‘The Blessed One has allowed five to perform Pavāraṇā in the Saṅgha. And we are four persons. How should the Pavāraṇā be performed by us?’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Bhikkhus, I allow four to perform Pavāraṇā with one another. And thus, bhikkhus, should the Pavāraṇā be performed. A competent and capable bhikkhu should inform those bhikkhus:

“Suṇantu me āyasmanto. Ajja pavāraṇā. Yadāyasmantānaṃ [T 1.0321] pattakallaṃ, mayaṃ aññamaññaṃ pavāreyyāmā”ti.

‘Venerable sirs, listen to me. Today is the Pavāraṇā day. If it is the proper time for the venerable sirs, let us perform Pavāraṇā with one another.’

Therena bhikkhunā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā te bhikkhū evamassu vacanīyā – “ahaṃ, āvuso, āyasmante pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadantu maṃ āyasmanto anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmi. Dutiyampi…pe… tatiyampi ahaṃ, āvuso, āyasmante pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadantu maṃ āyasmanto anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmī”ti.

The elder bhikkhu, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having sat down in a squatting position, and having raised his hands in añjali, should address those bhikkhus thus: ‘Friends, I invite the venerable ones regarding what has been seen, heard, or suspected. May the venerable ones speak to me out of compassion. Seeing it, I will make amends. For the second time… and for the third time, friends, I invite the venerable ones regarding what has been seen, heard, or suspected. May the venerable ones speak to me out of compassion. Seeing it, I will make amends.’

Navakena bhikkhunā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā te bhikkhū evamassu vacanīyā – “ahaṃ, bhante, āyasmante pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadantu maṃ āyasmanto anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmi. Dutiyampi…pe… tatiyampi ahaṃ, bhante, āyasmante pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya [M 0.0229] vā. Vadantu maṃ āyasmanto anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmī”ti.

The junior bhikkhu, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having sat down in a squatting position, and having raised his hands in añjali, should address those bhikkhus thus: ‘Venerable sirs, I invite the venerable ones regarding what has been seen, heard, or suspected. May the venerable ones speak to me out of compassion. Seeing it, I will make amends. For the second time… and for the third time, venerable sirs, I invite the venerable ones regarding what has been seen, heard, or suspected. May the venerable ones speak to me out of compassion. Seeing it, I will make amends.’

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya tayo bhikkhū viharanti. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ [T 1.0322] etadahosi – “bhagavatā anuññātaṃ pañcannaṃ saṅghe pavāretuṃ, catunnaṃ aññamaññaṃ pavāretuṃ. Mayañcamhā tayo janā. Kathaṃ nu kho amhehi pavāretabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṃ aññamaññaṃ pavāretuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, pavāretabbaṃ. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena te bhikkhū ñāpetabbā –

Now on that occasion, in a certain monastery, on the day of the Pavāraṇā, three monks were dwelling. Then it occurred to those monks: "The Blessed One has allowed five to perform Pavāraṇā in the Saṅgha, and four to perform Pavāraṇā with one another. But we are three. How should we perform Pavāraṇā?" They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "I allow, monks, three to perform Pavāraṇā with one another. And thus, monks, should Pavāraṇā be performed. A competent and capable monk should inform those monks:"

“Suṇantu [V 0.0218] me āyasmantā. Ajja pavāraṇā. Yadāyasmantānaṃ pattakallaṃ, mayaṃ aññamaññaṃ pavāreyyāmā”ti.

"Let the venerable ones hear me. Today is the Pavāraṇā. If it is suitable for the venerable ones, let us perform Pavāraṇā with one another."

Therena bhikkhunā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā te bhikkhū evamassu vacanīyā – “ahaṃ, āvuso, āyasmante pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadantu maṃ āyasmantā anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmi. Dutiyampi…pe… tatiyampi ahaṃ, āvuso, āyasmante pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadantu maṃ āyasmantā anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmī”ti.

The senior monk, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having sat down in a squatting position, and having raised his joined palms, should address those monks thus: "I, friends, invite the venerable ones by what has been seen, by what has been heard, or by what is suspected. May the venerable ones speak to me out of compassion. Seeing it, I will make amends. For the second time... For the third time, I, friends, invite the venerable ones by what has been seen, by what has been heard, or by what is suspected. May the venerable ones speak to me out of compassion. Seeing it, I will make amends."

Navakena bhikkhunā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā te bhikkhū evamassu vacanīyā – “ahaṃ, bhante, āyasmante pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadantu maṃ āyasmantā anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmi. Dutiyampi…pe… [T 1.0323] tatiyampi ahaṃ, bhante, āyasmante pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadantu maṃ āyasmantā anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmī”ti[P 1.0163].

The junior monk, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having sat down in a squatting position, and having raised his joined palms, should address those monks thus: "I, venerable sirs, invite the venerable ones by what has been seen, by what has been heard, or by what is suspected. May the venerable ones speak to me out of compassion. Seeing it, I will make amends. For the second time... For the third time, I, venerable sirs, invite the venerable ones by what has been seen, by what has been heard, or by what is suspected. May the venerable ones speak to me out of compassion. Seeing it, I will make amends."

217. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya dve bhikkhū viharanti. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “bhagavatā anuññātaṃ pañcannaṃ saṅghe pavāretuṃ, catunnaṃ aññamaññaṃ pavāretuṃ, tiṇṇaṃ [M 0.0230] aññamaññaṃ pavāretuṃ. Mayañcamhā dve janā. Kathaṃ nu kho amhehi pavāretabba”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dvinnaṃ aññamaññaṃ pavāretuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, pavāretabbaṃ. Therena bhikkhunā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā navo bhikkhu evamassa vacanīyo – “ahaṃ, āvuso, āyasmantaṃ pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadatu maṃ āyasmā anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmi. Dutiyampi…pe… tatiyampi ahaṃ, āvuso, āyasmantaṃ pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadatu maṃ āyasmā anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmī”ti.

217. Now at that time, in a certain monastery, two monks were dwelling on the day of the Pavāraṇā. Then this thought occurred to those monks: "The Blessed One has allowed five monks to perform Pavāraṇā in the Saṅgha, four to perform Pavāraṇā with one another, and three to perform Pavāraṇā with one another. We are two. How then should we perform Pavāraṇā?" They reported this matter to the Blessed One. "Monks, I allow two to perform Pavāraṇā with one another. And, monks, it should be performed in this way. The senior monk, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having sat down squatting, and having raised his joined palms, should address the junior monk thus: ‘Friend, I invite the venerable one by what has been seen, by what has been heard, or by what is suspected. May the venerable one speak to me out of compassion. Seeing it, I will make amends. For a second time... For a third time, friend, I invite the venerable one by what has been seen, by what has been heard, or by what is suspected. May the venerable one speak to me out of compassion. Seeing it, I will make amends.’"

Navakena bhikkhunā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā [T 1.0324] añjaliṃ paggahetvā thero bhikkhu evamassa vacanīyo – “ahaṃ, bhante, āyasmantaṃ pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadatu maṃ āyasmā anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmi. Dutiyampi…pe… tatiyampi ahaṃ, bhante, āyasmantaṃ pavāremi diṭṭhena vā sutena [V 0.0219] vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadatu maṃ āyasmā anukampaṃ upādāya. Passanto paṭikarissāmī”ti.

The junior monk, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having sat down squatting, and having raised his joined palms, should address the senior monk thus: 'Venerable sir, I invite the venerable one by what has been seen, by what has been heard, or by what is suspected. May the venerable one speak to me out of compassion. Seeing it, I will make amends. For a second time... For a third time, venerable sir, I invite the venerable one by what has been seen, by what has been heard, or by what is suspected. May the venerable one speak to me out of compassion. Seeing it, I will make amends.'

218. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya eko bhikkhu viharati. Atha kho tassa bhikkhuno etadahosi – “bhagavatā anuññātaṃ pañcannaṃ saṅghe pavāretuṃ, catunnaṃ aññamaññaṃ pavāretuṃ, tiṇṇaṃ aññamaññaṃ pavāretuṃ, dvinnaṃ aññamaññaṃ pavāretuṃ. Ahañcamhi ekako. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā pavāretabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

218. Now at that time, in a certain monastery, a single monk was dwelling on the day of the Pavāraṇā. Then this thought occurred to that monk: "The Blessed One has allowed five to perform Pavāraṇā in the Saṅgha, four to perform Pavāraṇā with one another, three to perform Pavāraṇā with one another, and two to perform Pavāraṇā with one another. But I am alone. How then should I perform Pavāraṇā?" They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya eko bhikkhu viharati. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā yattha bhikkhū paṭikkamanti upaṭṭhānasālāya vā maṇḍape vā rukkhamūle vā, so deso sammajjitvā pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā āsanaṃ paññapetvā padīpaṃ katvā nisīditabbaṃ. Sace aññe bhikkhū āgacchanti, tehi saddhiṃ pavāretabbaṃ; no ce āgacchanti, ‘ajja me pavāraṇā’ti adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ. No ce adhiṭṭheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

In this teaching, monks, a single monk might be dwelling in a certain monastery on the day of the Pavāraṇā. That monk, monks, should sweep the place where monks assemble—whether an assembly hall, a pavilion, or the foot of a tree—set out drinking water and water for use, prepare a seat, light a lamp, and sit down. If other monks arrive, he should perform Pavāraṇā with them; if they do not arrive, he should make the determination: ‘Today is my Pavāraṇā.’ Should he not make the determination, he commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Tatra[M 0.0231], bhikkhave, yattha [T 1.0325] pañca bhikkhū viharanti, na ekassa pavāraṇaṃ āharitvā

There, monks, where five monks dwell, having brought the Pavāraṇā of one,

Catūhi saṅghe pavāretabbaṃ. Pavāreyyuṃ ce, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tatra, bhikkhave, yattha cattāro bhikkhū viharanti, na ekassa pavāraṇaṃ āharitvā tīhi aññamaññaṃ pavāretabbaṃ. Pavāreyyuṃ ce, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tatra, bhikkhave, yattha tayo bhikkhū viharanti, na [P 1.0164] ekassa pavāraṇaṃ āharitvā dvīhi aññamaññaṃ pavāretabbaṃ. Pavāreyyuṃ ce, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Tatra, bhikkhave, yattha dve bhikkhū viharanti, na ekassa pavāraṇaṃ āharitvā ekena adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ. Adhiṭṭheyya ce, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

the four should not perform Pavāraṇā in the Saṅgha. Should they do so, they commit an offense of wrong-doing. There, monks, where four monks dwell, having brought the Pavāraṇā of one, the three should not perform Pavāraṇā with one another. Should they do so, they commit an offense of wrong-doing. There, monks, where three monks dwell, having brought the Pavāraṇā of one, the two should not perform Pavāraṇā with one another. Should they do so, they commit an offense of wrong-doing. There, monks, where two monks dwell, having brought the Pavāraṇā of one, the one should not make a determination. Should he make a determination, he commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Saṅghapavāraṇādippabhedā niṭṭhitā.

The Sections on the Saṅgha's Pavāraṇā and so forth are concluded.

125. Āpattipaṭikammavidhi

125. The Procedure for Remedying an Offense

219. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu tadahu pavāraṇāya āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. Atha kho tassa bhikkhuno etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘na sāpattikena pavāretabba’nti. Ahañcamhi āpattiṃ āpanno. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ ārocesi (ka.).

219. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu had incurred an offense on the day of the Pavāraṇā. Then it occurred to that bhikkhu: “The Blessed One has laid down that ‘one who has an offense should not perform the Pavāraṇā.’ I have incurred an offense. How should I proceed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha [V 0.0220] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tadahu pavāraṇāya āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “ahaṃ, āvuso, itthannāmaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno, taṃ paṭidesemī”ti. Tena vattabbo – “passasī”ti. Āma passāmīti. Āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsīti.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has incurred an offense on the day of the Pavāraṇā. That bhikkhu, bhikkhus, should approach another bhikkhu, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, squat down, raise his joined palms, and say this: “Friend, I have incurred an offense of such-and-such a name; I declare it.” He should be asked: “Do you see it?” “Yes, I see it.” “You should restrain yourself in the future.”

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tadahu pavāraṇāya āpattiyā vematiko hoti. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā [T 1.0326] ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo – “ahaṃ, āvuso, itthannāmāya āpattiyā vematiko; yadā nibbematiko bhavissāmi tadā taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmī”ti vatvā pavāretabbaṃ; na tveva tappaccayā pavāraṇāya antarāyo kātabboti.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is uncertain about an offense on the day of the Pavāraṇā. That bhikkhu, bhikkhus, should approach another bhikkhu, arrange his upper robe over one shoulder, squat down, raise his joined palms, and say this: “Friend, I am uncertain about an offense of such-and-such a name; when I am free from uncertainty, I will remedy that offense.” Having said this, the Pavāraṇā should be performed; and on that account, an obstacle to the Pavāraṇā should certainly not be made.

Āpattipaṭikammavidhi niṭṭhitā.

The Procedure for Remedying an Offense is concluded.

126. Āpattiāvikaraṇavidhi

126. The Procedure for Disclosing an Offense

220. Tena [M 0.0232] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu pavārayamāno āpattiṃ sarati. Atha kho tassa bhikkhuno etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘na sāpattikena pavāretabba’nti. Ahañcamhi āpattiṃ āpanno. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

220. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu, while performing the Pavāraṇā, recalled an offense. Then it occurred to that bhikkhu: “The Blessed One has laid down that ‘one who has an offense should not perform the Pavāraṇā.’ I have incurred an offense. How should I proceed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pavārayamāno āpattiṃ sarati. Tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā sāmanto bhikkhu evamassa vacanīyo – “ahaṃ, āvuso, itthannāmaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno. Ito vuṭṭhahitvā taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmī”ti vatvā pavāretabbaṃ; na tveva tappaccayā pavāraṇāya antarāyo kātabbo.

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, while performing the Pavāraṇā, recalls an offense. That bhikkhu, bhikkhus, should say this to a nearby bhikkhu: ‘Friend, I have incurred an offense of such-and-such a name. After rising from this place, I will remedy that offense.’ Having said this, the Pavāraṇā should be performed; and on that account, an obstacle to the Pavāraṇā should certainly not be made.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pavārayamāno āpattiyā vematiko hoti. Tena, bhikkhave,

Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, while performing the Pavāraṇā, is uncertain about an offense. That bhikkhu, bhikkhus,

Bhikkhunā sāmanto bhikkhu evamassa vacanīyo – “ahaṃ, āvuso, itthannāmāya āpattiyā vematiko; yadā nibbematiko bhavissāmi tadā taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmī”ti vatvā pavāretabbaṃ; na tveva tappaccayā pavāraṇāya antarāyo kātabboti.

should say this to a nearby bhikkhu: ‘Friend, I am uncertain about an offense of such-and-such a name; when I am free from uncertainty, I will remedy that offense.’ Having said this, the Pavāraṇā should be performed; and on that account, an obstacle to the Pavāraṇā should certainly not be made.

Āpatti āvikaraṇavidhi niṭṭhitā.

The Procedure for Disclosing an Offense is concluded.

127. Sabhāgāpattipaṭikammavidhi

127. The Procedure for Remedying a Shared Offense

221. Tena [V 0.0221] kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya sabbo saṅgho sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ [T 1.0327] etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘na sabhāgā āpatti desetabbā, na sabhāgā āpatti paṭiggahetabbā’ti. Ayañca sabbo saṅgho sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno. Kathaṃ nu kho amhehi paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

221. At that time, in a certain dwelling, on the day of the Pavāraṇā, the entire Saṅgha had incurred a shared offense. Then those bhikkhus thought: ‘The Blessed One has laid down that “a shared offense should not be confessed, nor should a shared offense be accepted.” And this entire Saṅgha has incurred a shared offense. How should we proceed?’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya sabbo saṅgho sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi eko bhikkhu sāmantā āvāsā sajjukaṃ pāhetabbo – gacchāvuso, taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikaritvā āgaccha, mayaṃ te santike taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmāti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Here, bhikkhus, in a certain dwelling, on the day of the Pavāraṇā, the entire Saṅgha has incurred a shared offense. Those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, should send one bhikkhu to a nearby dwelling to return on the same day, saying: ‘Go, friend, remedy that offense and return; we will then remedy that offense in your presence.’ If this is achieved, it is good. If it is not achieved, a competent and capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu [M 0.0233] me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ sabbo saṅgho sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ āpanno. Yadā aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ suddhaṃ anāpattikaṃ passissati tadā tassa santike taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissatī”ti vatvā pavāretabbaṃ; na tveva tappaccayā pavāraṇāya antarāyo kātabbo.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This entire Saṅgha has incurred a shared offense. When it sees another bhikkhu who is pure and without offense, it will then remedy that offense in his presence.’ Having said this, the Pavāraṇā should be performed; and on that account, an obstacle to the Pavāraṇā should certainly not be made.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya sabbo saṅgho sabhāgāya āpattiyā vematiko hoti. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Here, bhikkhus, in a certain dwelling, on the day of the Pavāraṇā, the entire Saṅgha is uncertain about a shared offense. A competent and capable bhikkhu should inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ sabbo saṅgho sabhāgāya āpattiyā vematiko. Yadā nibbematiko bhavissati tadā taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissatī”ti vatvā, pavāretabbaṃ, na tveva tappaccayā pavāraṇāya antarāyo kātabboti.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This entire Saṅgha is uncertain about a shared offense. When it is free from uncertainty, it will then remedy that offense.’ Having said this, the Pavāraṇā should be performed; and on that account, an obstacle to the Pavāraṇā should certainly not be made.

Sabhāgāpattipaṭikammavidhi niṭṭhitā.

The Procedure for Remedying a Shared Offense is concluded.

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The first recitation section is concluded.

128. Anāpattipannarasakaṃ

128. The Fifteen Cases of No Offense

222. Tena [T 1.0328][V 0.0222] kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatiṃsu, pañca vā atirekā vā. Te na jāniṃsu “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te dhammasaññino vinayasaññino vaggā samaggasaññino pavāresuṃ. Tehi pavāriyamāne athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchiṃsu bahutarā. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

222. At that time, in a certain dwelling, on the day of the Pavāraṇā, many resident bhikkhus had assembled, five or more. They did not know: ‘There are other resident bhikkhus who have not yet arrived.’ Perceiving it as a lawful act, perceiving it as a Vinaya act, though being an incomplete group they perceived it as a complete one, and they performed the Pavāraṇā. While they were performing the Pavāraṇā, other resident bhikkhus arrived, who were more numerous. They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti, pañca [P 1.0165] vā atirekā vā. Te na jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te dhammasaññino vinayasaññino vaggā samaggasaññino pavārenti. Tehi pavāriyamāne athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti bahutarā. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi puna pavāretabbaṃ. Pavāritānaṃ anāpatti.

Furthermore, O monks, in a certain monastery on that Pavāraṇā day, many resident bhikkhus assemble, five or more. Pavāritānaṃ āpatti dukkaṭassa.

130. Vematikapannarasakaṃ

130. The Section of Fifteen Cases on Uncertainty

224. Idha [M 0.0238] pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya sambahulā [T 1.0332] āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti, pañca vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te “kappati nu kho amhākaṃ pavāretuṃ, na nu kho kappatī”ti vematikā pavārenti. Tehi pavāriyamāne athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti bahutarā. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi puna pavāretabbaṃ. Pavāritānaṃ āpatti dukkaṭassa.

224. Here, bhikkhus, in a certain monastery on that Pavāraṇā day, many resident bhikkhus assemble—five or more. They know: 'There are other resident bhikkhus who have not arrived.' Being uncertain, thinking, 'Is it allowable for us to perform Pavāraṇā, or is it not allowable?' they perform Pavāraṇā. While they are performing Pavāraṇā, other resident bhikkhus, who are more numerous, arrive. Bhikkhus, those bhikkhus should perform Pavāraṇā again. For those who have performed Pavāraṇā, an offense of wrong-doing is incurred.

Pavāritānaṃ āpatti dukkaṭassa.

Vematikapannarasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section of Fifteen on Doubt is finished.

131. The Section of Fifteen on Being Afflicted by Scruple

225. Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti, pañca vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te “kappateva [T 1.0333] amhākaṃ pavāretuṃ, nāmhākaṃ na kappatī”ti kukkuccapakatā pavārenti. Tehi pavāriyamāne athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti bahutarā. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi puna pavāretabbaṃ. Pavāritānaṃ āpatti dukkaṭassa.

132. Bhedapurekkhārapannarasakaṃ

132. The Section of Fifteen on Intending Division

226. Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya [P 1.0167] sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti, pañca vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te “nassantete, vinassantete, ko tehi attho”ti bhedapurekkhārā pavārenti. Tehi pavāriyamāne athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti bahutarā[T 1.0334]. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi puna pavāretabbaṃ. Pavāritānaṃ āpatti thullaccayassa.

Intending division, they perform Pavāraṇā, thinking: 'May those bhikkhus be destroyed, may they perish! What use are they?' While they are performing Pavāraṇā, other resident bhikkhus, who are more numerous, arrive. Bhikkhus, those bhikkhus should perform Pavāraṇā again. For those who have performed Pavāraṇā, a grave offense is incurred.

Pavāritānaṃ āpatti thullaccayassa.

While they are performing the Pavāraṇā, other resident bhikkhus, equal in number, arrive. The Pavāraṇā is well-performed; the Pavāraṇā should be performed by the remaining bhikkhus. Those who have performed the Pavāraṇā incur a thullaccaya offense.
