The Pavāraṇā should be performed in their presence. For those who have performed the Pavāraṇā, there is the incurring of a thullaccaya offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti, pañca vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te “nassantete, vinassantete, ko tehi attho”ti bhedapurekkhārā pavārenti. Tehi [V 0.0231] pavāritamatte, sabbāya vuṭṭhitāya parisāya, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti bahutarā. Tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi puna pavāretabbaṃ. Pavāritānaṃ āpatti thullaccayassa.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, in this teaching, in a certain monastery on that Pavāraṇā day, many resident bhikkhus, five or more, assemble. They know, ‘There are other resident bhikkhus who have not arrived.’ With schism as their foremost aim, they perform the Pavāraṇā, thinking, ‘Let these bhikkhus perish, let them be destroyed! What is the use of them?’ Just as they have finished the Pavāraṇā, after the entire assembly has risen, other resident bhikkhus, who are more numerous, arrive. Bhikkhus, those bhikkhus should perform the Pavāraṇā again. For those who have performed the Pavāraṇā, there is the incurring of a thullaccaya offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti, pañca vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te “nassantete, vinassantete, ko tehi attho”ti bhedapurekkhārā pavārenti. Tehi pavāritamatte, sabbāya vuṭṭhitāya parisāya, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti samasamā. Pavāritā suppavāritā, tesaṃ santike pavāretabbaṃ. Pavāritānaṃ āpatti thullaccayassa.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, in this teaching, in a certain monastery on that Pavāraṇā day, many resident bhikkhus, five or more, assemble. They know, ‘There are other resident bhikkhus who have not arrived.’ With schism as their foremost aim, they perform the Pavāraṇā, thinking, ‘Let these bhikkhus perish, let them be destroyed! What is the use of them?’ Just as they have finished the Pavāraṇā, after the entire assembly has risen, other resident bhikkhus, equal in number, arrive. The Pavāraṇā is well-performed. The Pavāraṇā should be performed in their presence. For those who have performed the Pavāraṇā, there is the incurring of a thullaccaya offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya sambahulā āvāsikā

Furthermore, bhikkhus, in this teaching, in a certain monastery on that Pavāraṇā day, many resident...

Bhikkhū sannipatanti, pañca vā atirekā vā. Te jānanti “atthaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū anāgatā”ti. Te “nassantete, vinassantete, ko tehi attho”ti bhedapurekkhārā pavārenti. Tehi pavāritamatte, sabbāya vuṭṭhitāya parisāya, athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchanti thokatarā. Pavāritā suppavāritā, tesaṃ santike pavāretabbaṃ. Pavāritānaṃ āpatti thullaccayassa.

Bhikkhus assemble, five or more. They know, ‘There are other resident bhikkhus who have not arrived.’ With schism as their foremost aim, they perform the Pavāraṇā, thinking, ‘Let them perish, let them be destroyed! What is the use of them?’ Just as they have finished the Pavāraṇā, after the entire assembly has risen, other resident bhikkhus, fewer in number, arrive. The Pavāraṇā is well-performed. The Pavāraṇā should be performed in their presence. For those who have performed the Pavāraṇā, there is the incurring of a thullaccaya offense.

Bhedapurekkhārapannarasakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The fifteenfold section on schism as the foremost aim is concluded.

Pañcavīsattikā niṭṭhitā.

The section of twenty-five is concluded.

133. Sīmottantikapeyyālaṃ

133. The Abbreviation Section on Entering the Boundary

227. Idha [M 0.0244] pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya sambahulā āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatanti, pañca vā atirekā vā. Te na jānanti “aññe āvāsikā bhikkhū antosīmaṃ okkamantī”ti…pe… te na jānanti “aññe āvāsikā bhikkhū antosīmaṃ okkantā”ti…pe… te na passanti aññe āvāsike bhikkhū antosīmaṃ [T 1.0335] okkamante…pe… te na passanti aññe āvāsike bhikkhū antosīmaṃ okkante…pe… te na suṇanti “aññe āvāsikā bhikkhū antosīmaṃ okkamantī”ti…pe… te na suṇanti “aññe āvāsikā bhikkhū antosīmaṃ okkantā”ti…pe….

227. Furthermore, bhikkhus, in this teaching, in a certain monastery on that Pavāraṇā day, many resident bhikkhus, five or more, assemble. They do not know, ‘Other resident bhikkhus are entering the boundary’… (and so on) … they do not know, ‘Other resident bhikkhus have entered the boundary’… (and so on) … they do not see other resident bhikkhus entering the boundary… (and so on) … they do not see other resident bhikkhus who have entered the boundary… (and so on) … they do not hear, ‘Other resident bhikkhus are entering the boundary’… (and so on) … they do not hear, ‘Other resident bhikkhus have entered the boundary’… (and so on).

Āvāsikena [V 0.0232] āvāsikā ekasatapañcasattati tikanayato, āvāsikena āgantukā, āgantukena āvāsikā, āgantukena āgantukā, peyyālamukhena satta tikasatāni honti.

For resident with residents, by the method of triads, there are one hundred and seventy-five triads. For resident with visitors, visitor with residents, and visitor with visitors, by way of the abbreviation section, there are seven hundred triads.

Sīmokkantikapeyyālaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Abbreviation Section on Entering the Boundary is concluded.

134. Divasanānattaṃ

134. Difference of Days

228. Idha pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cātuddaso hoti, āgantukānaṃ pannaraso. Sace āvāsikā bahutarā honti, āgantukehi āvāsikānaṃ anuvattitabbaṃ. Sace samasamā honti, āgantukehi āvāsikānaṃ anuvattitabbaṃ. Sace āgantukā bahutarā honti, āvāsikehi āgantukānaṃ anuvattitabbaṃ.

228. Furthermore, bhikkhus, in this teaching, for the resident bhikkhus it is the fourteenth day, while for the visiting bhikkhus it is the fifteenth. If the resident bhikkhus are more numerous, the visiting bhikkhus should conform to the resident bhikkhus. If they are equal in number, the visiting bhikkhus should conform to the resident bhikkhus. If the visiting bhikkhus are more numerous, the resident bhikkhus should conform to the visiting bhikkhus.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pannaraso hoti, āgantukānaṃ cātuddaso. Sace āvāsikā bahutarā honti, āgantukehi āvāsikānaṃ anuvattitabbaṃ. Sace samasamā honti, āgantukehi āvāsikānaṃ anuvattitabbaṃ. Sace āgantukā bahutarā honti, āvāsikehi āgantukānaṃ anuvattitabbaṃ.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, in this teaching, for the resident bhikkhus it is the fifteenth day, while for the visiting bhikkhus it is the fourteenth. If the resident bhikkhus are more numerous, the visiting bhikkhus should conform to the resident bhikkhus. If they are equal in number, the visiting bhikkhus should conform to the resident bhikkhus. If the visiting bhikkhus are more numerous, the resident bhikkhus should conform to the visiting bhikkhus.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭipado hoti, āgantukānaṃ pannaraso. Sace āvāsikā bahutarā honti, āvāsikehi āgantukānaṃ nākāmā dātabbā sāmaggī; āgantukehi nissīmaṃ gantvā pavāretabbaṃ. Sace samasamā honti, āvāsikehi āgantukānaṃ [T 1.0336] nākāmā dātabbā sāmaggī; āgantukehi nissīmaṃ gantvā pavāretabbaṃ[M 0.0245]. Sace āgantukā bahutarā honti, āvāsikehi āgantukānaṃ sāmaggī vā dātabbā, nissīmaṃ vā gantabbaṃ.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, in this teaching, for the resident bhikkhus it is the first day of the fortnight, while for the visiting bhikkhus it is the fifteenth. If the resident bhikkhus are more numerous, concord should not be given to the visiting bhikkhus by the resident bhikkhus against their will; the visiting bhikkhus should go outside the boundary and perform the Pavāraṇā. If they are equal in number, concord should not be given to the visiting bhikkhus by the resident bhikkhus against their will; the visiting bhikkhus should go outside the boundary and perform the Pavāraṇā. If the visiting bhikkhus are more numerous, the resident bhikkhus should either give concord to the visiting bhikkhus or go outside the boundary.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ pannaraso hoti, āgantukānaṃ pāṭipado. Sace āvāsikā bahutarā honti, āgantukehi āvāsikānaṃ sāmaggī vā dātabbā, nissīmaṃ vā gantabbaṃ. Sace samasamā honti, āgantukehi āvāsikānaṃ sāmaggī vā dātabbā, nissīmaṃ vā gantabbaṃ. Sace āgantukā bahutarā honti, āgantukehi āvāsikānaṃ nākāmā dātabbā sāmaggī; āvāsikehi nissīmaṃ gantvā pavāretabbaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, for the resident monks it is the fifteenth-day Pavāraṇā, and for the visiting monks it is the first day. If the resident monks are more numerous, the visiting monks should either give concord to the resident monks or go outside the boundary. If they are equal in number, the visiting monks should either give concord to the resident monks or go outside the boundary. If the visiting monks are more numerous, concord should not be given by the visiting monks to the resident monks against their will; the resident monks should go outside the boundary and perform the Pavāraṇā.

Divasanānattaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section on different days is concluded.

135. Liṅgādidassanaṃ

135. Seeing Signs, etc.

229. Idha [V 0.0233] pana, bhikkhave, āgantukā bhikkhū passanti āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āvāsikākāraṃ, āvāsikaliṅgaṃ, āvāsikanimittaṃ, āvāsikuddesaṃ, suppaññattaṃ mañcapīṭhaṃ bhisibibbohanaṃ, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ sapaṭṭhitaṃ, pariveṇaṃ susammaṭṭhaṃ; passitvā vematikā honti – “atthi nu kho āvāsikā bhikkhū, natthi nu kho”ti. Te vematikā na vicinanti, avicinitvā pavārenti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa…pe… te vematikā vicinanti, vicinitvā na passanti, apassitvā pavārenti. Anāpatti. Te vematikā vicinanti, vicinitvā passanti, passitvā ekato pavārenti. Anāpatti. Te vematikā vicinanti, vicinitvā passanti, passitvā pāṭekkaṃ pavārenti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te vematikā vicinanti, vicinitvā passanti, passitvā – “nassantete, vinassantete, ko tehi attho”ti – bhedapurekkhārā pavārenti. Āpatti thullaccayassa.

229. Furthermore, monks, visiting monks see the behavior of resident monks, their characteristics, their signs, the requisites they indicate, a well-arranged bed and chair, a mattress and bolster, prepared drinking water and water for use, and a well-swept enclosure. Seeing this, they become doubtful: “Are there resident monks, or are there not?” Being doubtful, they do not investigate. Without investigating, they perform the Pavāraṇā. There is an offense of wrong-doing. Being doubtful, they investigate; having investigated, they do not see them; not seeing them, they perform the Pavāraṇā. There is no offense. Being doubtful, they investigate; having investigated, they see them; seeing them, they perform the Pavāraṇā together. There is no offense. Being doubtful, they investigate; having investigated, they see them; seeing them, they perform the Pavāraṇā separately. There is an offense of wrong-doing. Being doubtful, they investigate; having investigated, they see them; seeing them and thinking, “Let them be ruined, let them be destroyed, what is the use of them?” they perform the Pavāraṇā with the intention of causing dissension. There is a grave offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, āgantukā bhikkhū suṇanti āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āvāsikākāraṃ, āvāsikaliṅgaṃ, āvāsikanimittaṃ, āvāsikuddesaṃ, caṅkamantānaṃ padasaddaṃ, sajjhāyasaddaṃ, ukkāsitasaddaṃ, khipitasaddaṃ; sutvā vematikā honti – “atthi nu kho āvāsikā bhikkhū, natthi nu kho”ti. Te vematikā na vicinanti, avicinitvā pavārenti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te vematikā vicinanti, vicinitvā na passanti, apassitvā pavārenti. Anāpatti. Te vematikā vicinanti, vicinitvā passanti, passitvā ekato pavārenti. Anāpatti. Te vematikā vicinanti, vicinitvā passanti, passitvā [M 0.0246] pāṭekkaṃ pavārenti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te [T 1.0337] vematikā vicinanti, vicinitvā passanti, passitvā “nassantete, vinassantete, ko tehi attho”ti bhedapurekkhārā pavārenti. Āpatti thullaccayassa.

Furthermore, monks, visiting monks hear the behavior of resident monks, their characteristics, their signs, the requisites they indicate, the sound of footsteps of those walking back and forth, the sound of recitation, the sound of coughing, and the sound of sneezing. Having heard this, they become doubtful: ‘Are there resident monks, or are there not?’ Being doubtful, they do not investigate. Without investigating, they perform the Pavāraṇā. There is an offense of wrong-doing. Being doubtful, they investigate; having investigated, they do not see them; not seeing them, they perform the Pavāraṇā. There is no offense. Being doubtful, they investigate; having investigated, they see them; seeing them, they perform the Pavāraṇā together. There is no offense. Being doubtful, they investigate; having investigated, they see them; seeing them, they perform the Pavāraṇā separately. There is an offense of wrong-doing. Being doubtful, they investigate; having investigated, they see them; seeing them, with the intention of causing dissension, they perform the Pavāraṇā, thinking: ‘May these monks perish! May these monks be destroyed! What is the use of them?’ There is a grave offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikā bhikkhū passanti āgantukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āgantukākāraṃ, āgantukaliṅgaṃ, āgantukanimittaṃ, āgantukuddesaṃ, aññātakaṃ pattaṃ, aññātakaṃ cīvaraṃ, aññātakaṃ nisīdanaṃ, pādānaṃ dhotaṃ, udakanissekaṃ; passitvā vematikā honti – “atthi nu kho āgantukā bhikkhū, natthi nu kho”ti. Te vematikā na vicinanti, avicinitvā pavārenti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te vematikā [T 1.0338] vicinanti, vicinitvā na passanti, apassitvā pavārenti. Anāpatti. Te vematikā vicinanti, vicinitvā [V 0.0234] passanti, passitvā ekato pavārenti. Anāpatti. Te vematikā vicinanti, vicinitvā passanti, passitvā pāṭekkaṃ pavārenti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te vematikā vicinanti, vicinitvā passanti, passitvā – nassantete, vinassantete, ko tehi atthoti – bhedapurekkhārā pavārenti. Āpatti thullaccayassa.

Furthermore, monks, resident monks see the behavior of visiting monks, their characteristics, their signs, the requisites they indicate, an unfamiliar bowl, an unfamiliar robe, an unfamiliar sitting-cloth, and the dripping of water from washed feet. Having seen this, they become doubtful: ‘Are there visiting monks, or are there not?’ Being doubtful, they do not investigate; without investigating, they perform the Pavāraṇā. There is an offense of wrong-doing. Being doubtful, they investigate; having investigated, they do not see them; not seeing them, they perform the Pavāraṇā. There is no offense. Being doubtful, they investigate; having investigated, they see them; having seen them, they perform the Pavāraṇā together. There is no offense. Being doubtful, they investigate; having investigated, they see them; having seen them, they perform the Pavāraṇā separately. There is an offense of wrong-doing. Being doubtful, they investigate; having investigated, they see them; having seen them, thinking, ‘May these monks perish, may these monks be destroyed, what use are they?’ they perform the Pavāraṇā with the intention of causing dissension. There is a grave offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikā bhikkhū suṇanti āgantukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āgantukākāraṃ,

Furthermore, monks, resident monks hear the behavior of visiting monks,

Āgantukaliṅgaṃ, āgantukanimittaṃ, āgantukuddesaṃ, āgacchantānaṃ padasaddaṃ, upāhanapapphoṭanasaddaṃ, ukkāsitasaddaṃ, khipitasaddaṃ; sutvā vematikā honti – “atthi nu kho āgantukā bhikkhū, natthi nu kho”ti. Te vematikā na vicinanti, avicinitvā pavārenti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te vematikā vicinanti, vicinitvā na passanti, apassitvā pavārenti. Anāpatti. Te vematikā vicinanti, vicinitvā passanti, passitvā ekato pavārenti. Anāpatti. Te vematikā vicinanti, vicinitvā passanti, passitvā pāṭekkaṃ pavārenti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te vematikā vicinanti, vicinitvā passanti, passitvā – nassantete, vinassantete, ko tehi atthoti – bhedapurekkhārā pavārenti. Āpatti thullaccayassa.

their characteristics, their signs, the requisites they indicate, the sound of footsteps of those arriving, the sound of shaking sandals, the sound of coughing, and the sound of sneezing. Having heard these, they become doubtful: ‘Are there visiting monks, or are there not?’ Being doubtful, they do not investigate; without investigating, they perform the Pavāraṇā. There is an offense of wrong-doing. Being doubtful, they investigate; having investigated, they do not see them; not having seen them, they perform the Pavāraṇā. There is no offense. Being doubtful, they investigate; having investigated, they see them; having seen them, they perform the Pavāraṇā together. There is no offense. Being doubtful, they investigate; having investigated, they see them; having seen them, they perform the Pavāraṇā separately. There is an offense of wrong-doing. Being doubtful, they investigate; having investigated, they see them; having seen them, with the intention of causing dissension, they perform the Pavāraṇā, thinking: ‘Let these monks be destroyed, let them perish, what is the use of them?’ There is a grave offense.

Liṅgādidassanaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section on seeing signs and so forth is concluded.

136. Nānāsaṃvāsakādīhi pavāraṇā

136. The Pavāraṇā with those of different communion and so forth.

230. Idha pana, bhikkhave, āgantukā bhikkhū passanti āvāsike bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsake. Te samānasaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhanti, samānasaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ [T 1.0339][M 0.0247] paṭilabhitvā na pucchanti, apucchitvā ekato pavārenti. Anāpatti. Te pucchanti, pucchitvā nābhivitaranti, anabhivitaritvā ekato pavārenti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te pucchanti, pucchitvā nābhivitaranti, anabhivitaritvā pāṭekkaṃ pavārenti. Anāpatti.

230. Furthermore, monks, visiting monks see resident monks who are of different communion. They acquire the view of being of the same communion; having acquired the view of being of the same communion, they do not ask; without asking, they perform the Pavāraṇā together. There is no offense. They ask; having asked, they are not able to convince them; not having been able to convince them, they perform the Pavāraṇā together. There is an offense of wrong-doing. They ask; having asked, they are not able to convince them; not having been able to convince them, they perform the Pavāraṇā separately. There is no offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, āgantukā bhikkhū passanti āvāsike bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsake. Te nānāsaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhanti, nānāsaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhitvā na pucchanti, apucchitvā ekato pavārenti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te pucchanti, pucchitvā abhivitaranti, abhivitaritvā pāṭekkaṃ pavārenti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te pucchanti, pucchitvā abhivitaranti, abhivitaritvā ekato pavārenti. Anāpatti.

Again, monks, in this case, visiting monks see resident monks who are of the same communion. They acquire the view of being of different communion; having acquired the view of being of different communion, they do not ask; not having asked, they perform Pavāraṇā together. There is an offense of wrong-doing. They ask; having asked, they are able to convince them; having been able to convince them, they perform Pavāraṇā separately. There is an offense of wrong-doing. They ask; having asked, they are able to convince them; having been able to convince them, they perform Pavāraṇā together. There is no offense.

Idha [V 0.0235] pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikā bhikkhū passanti āgantuke bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsake. Te samānasaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhanti, samānasaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhitvā na pucchanti, apucchitvā ekato pavārenti. Anāpatti. Te pucchanti, pucchitvā nābhivitaranti, anabhivitaritvā ekato pavārenti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te pucchanti, pucchitvā nābhivitaranti, anabhivitaritvā pāṭekkaṃ pavārenti. Anāpatti.

Again, monks, in this case, resident monks see visiting monks of different communion. They acquire the view of being of the same communion; having acquired the view of being of the same communion, they do not ask; not having asked, they perform Pavāraṇā together. There is no offense. They ask; having asked, they are not able to convince them; not having been able to convince them, they perform Pavāraṇā together. There is an offense of wrong-doing. They ask; having asked, they are not able to convince them; not having been able to convince them, they perform Pavāraṇā separately. There is no offense.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, āvāsikā bhikkhū passanti āgantuke bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsake. Te nānāsaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhanti, nānāsaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ paṭilabhitvā na pucchanti, apucchitvā [T 1.0340] ekato pavārenti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te pucchanti, pucchitvā abhivitaranti, abhivitaritvā pāṭekkaṃ pavārenti. Āpatti dukkaṭassa. Te pucchanti, pucchitvā abhivitaranti, abhivitaritvā ekato pavārenti. Anāpatti.

Again, monks, in this case, resident monks see visiting monks of the same communion. They acquire the view of being of different communion; having acquired the view of being of different communion, they do not ask; not having asked, they perform Pavāraṇā together. There is an offense of wrong-doing. They ask; having asked, they are able to convince them; having been able to convince them, they perform Pavāraṇā separately. There is an offense of wrong-doing. They ask; having asked, they are able to convince them; having been able to convince them, they perform Pavāraṇā together. There is no offense.

Nānāsaṃvāsakādīhi pavāraṇā niṭṭhitā.

The section on the Pavāraṇā with those of different communion and so forth is concluded.

137. Na gantabbavāro

137. The Section on Not Going

231. Na, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā āvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā.

231. Monks, on that day of Pavāraṇā, one should not go from a residence with monks to a residence without monks, except for the Saṅgha, or except in case of an obstacle. Monks, on that day of Pavāraṇā, one should not go from a residence with monks to a non-residence without monks, except for the Saṅgha, or except in case of an obstacle. Monks, on that day of Pavāraṇā, one should not go from a residence with monks to a residence or a non-residence without monks, except for the Saṅgha, or except in case of an obstacle.

Na[M 0.0248], bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā anāvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā anāvāsā abhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā anāvāsā abhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, on that day of Pavāraṇā, one should not go from a non-residence with monks to a non-residence without monks, except for the Saṅgha, or except in case of an obstacle. Monks, on that day of Pavāraṇā, one should not go from a non-residence with monks to either a residence or a non-residence without monks, except for the Saṅgha, or except in case of an obstacle.

Na, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, on that day of Pavāraṇā, one should not go from a residence with monks to a residence with monks where there are monks of different communion, except for the Saṅgha, or except in case of an obstacle. Monks, on that day of Pavāraṇā, one should not go from a residence with monks to a non-residence with monks where there are monks of different communion, except for the Saṅgha, or except in case of an obstacle. Monks, on that day of Pavāraṇā, one should not go from a residence with monks to either a residence or a non-residence with monks where there are monks of different communion, except for the Saṅgha, or except in case of an obstacle.

Na, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā.

Monks, on that day of Pavāraṇā, from a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks...

Vā sabhikkhuko āvāso gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko anāvāso gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā. Na, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā gantabbo, yatthassu bhikkhū nānāsaṃvāsakā, aññatra saṅghena, aññatra antarāyā.

...one should not go to a residence with monks where there are monks of different communion, except for the Saṅgha, or except in case of an obstacle. Monks, on that day of Pavāraṇā, one should not go from a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks to a non-residence with monks where there are monks of different communion, except for the Saṅgha, or except in case of an obstacle. Monks, on that day of Pavāraṇā, one should not go from a residence with monks or a non-residence with monks to a residence or a non-residence with monks where there are monks of different communion, except for the Saṅgha, or except in case of an obstacle.

Na gantabbavāro niṭṭhito.

The Section on Not Going is concluded.

138. Gantabbavāro

138. The Section on Going

232. Gantabbo, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso[V 0.0237], yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā “sakkomi ajjeva gantu”nti. Gantabbo, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā āvāsā sabhikkhuko anāvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā “sakkomi ajjeva gantu”nti.

232. Monks, on that Pavāraṇā day, one should go from a residence with monks to a residence with monks, where the monks are of the same communion, if one knows, 'I am able to arrive this very day.' Monks, on that Pavāraṇā day, one should go from a residence with monks to a non-residence with monks... and so on... to a residence or a non-residence with monks, where the monks are of the same communion, if one knows, 'I am able to arrive this very day.'

Gantabbo[T 1.0342], bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā anāvāsā sabhikkhuko āvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā “sakkomi ajjeva gantu”nti.

Monks, on that Pavāraṇā day, one should go from a non-residence with monks to a residence with monks... to a non-residence with monks... to that residence with monks or that non-residence with monks, where there are monks of the same communion, if one knows, 'I am able to arrive this very day.'

Gantabbo, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya sabhikkhukā āvāsā vā anāvāsā vā sabhikkhuko

Monks, on that Pavāraṇā day, one should go from a residence with monks or from a non-residence with monks to a place with monks...

Āvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko anāvāso…pe… sabhikkhuko āvāso vā anāvāso vā, yatthassu bhikkhū samānasaṃvāsakā, yaṃ jaññā “sakkomi ajjeva gantu”nti.

...to a residence... to a non-residence with monks... to that residence with monks or that non-residence with monks, where there are monks of the same communion, if one knows, 'I am able to arrive this very day.'

Gantabbavāro niṭṭhito.

The Section on Going is concluded.

139. Vajjanīyapuggalasandassanā

The Exposition of Individuals to be Avoided

233. Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā nisinnaparisāya pavāretabbaṃ. Yo pavāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na, bhikkhave, sikkhamānāya…pe… na sāmaṇerassa…pe… na sāmaṇeriyā…pe… na sikkhaṃ paccakkhātakassa…pe… na antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannakassa nisinnaparisāya pavāretabbaṃ. Yo pavāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa[P 1.0168].

139. Monks, one should not perform the Pavāraṇā in an assembly where a bhikkhunī is seated. Whoever should perform it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. Monks, one should not perform the Pavāraṇā in an assembly where a female probationer... a male novice... a female novice... one who has given up the training... or one who has committed a terminal offense is seated. Whoever should perform it, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Na [M 0.0250] āpattiyā adassane ukkhittakassa nisinnaparisāya pavāretabbaṃ. Yo pavāreyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo. Na āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittakassa…pe… na pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittakassa nisinnaparisāya pavāretabbaṃ. Yo pavāreyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo.

233. One should not perform the Pavāraṇā in an assembly where one who has been suspended for not seeing an offense is seated. Whoever should perform it, should be dealt with according to the Dhamma. One should not perform the Pavāraṇā in an assembly where one who has been suspended for not making amends for an offense is seated... or where one who has been suspended for not relinquishing a bad view is seated. Whoever should perform it, should be dealt with according to the Dhamma.

Na paṇḍakassa nisinnaparisāya pavāretabbaṃ. Yo pavāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na theyyasaṃvāsakassa…pe… na titthiyapakkantakassa…pe… na tiracchānagatassa…pe… na mātughātakassa…pe… na pitughātakassa…pe… na arahantaghātakassa…pe… na bhikkhunidūsakassa [V 0.0238] …pe… na saṅghabhedakassa…pe… na lohituppādakassa [T 1.0343] …pe… na ubhatobyañjanakassa nisinnaparisāya pavāretabbaṃ. Yo pavāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

One should not perform the Pavāraṇā in an assembly where a paṇḍaka is seated. Whoever should perform it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. One should not perform the Pavāraṇā in an assembly where one who lives in communion by theft is seated... or where one who has gone over to the sectarians is seated... or where an animal is seated... or where a matricide is seated... or where a patricide is seated... or where a murderer of an arahant is seated... or where a violator of a bhikkhunī is seated... or where a creator of schism in the Saṅgha is seated... or where one who has caused the Buddha's blood to flow is seated... or where one with both male and female characteristics is seated. Whoever should perform it, commits an offense of wrong-doing.

Na, bhikkhave, pārivāsikapavāraṇādānena pavāretabbaṃ, aññatra avuṭṭhitāya parisāya. Na ca, bhikkhave, appavāraṇāya pavāretabbaṃ, aññatra saṅghasāmaggiyāti.

Monks, the Pavāraṇā should not be performed by conveying the Pavāraṇā of a probationer, except when the assembly has not arisen. And, monks, the Pavāraṇā should not be performed on a non-Pavāraṇā day, except for the sake of the Saṅgha's unity.

Vajjanīyapuggalasandassanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition of Individuals to be Avoided is concluded.

Dutiyabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The Second Recitation Section is concluded.

140. Dvevācikādipavāraṇā

The Pavāraṇā with Two Declarations, etc.

234. Tena kho pana samayena kosalesu janapade aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya savarabhayaṃ ahosi. Bhikkhū nāsakkhiṃsu tevācikaṃ pavāretuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dvevācikaṃ pavāretunti.

At that time, in a certain residence in the country of Kosala, on the day of the Pavāraṇā, there arose a danger from tribesmen. The monks were unable to perform the Pavāraṇā with three declarations. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, 'Monks, I allow you to perform the Pavāraṇā with two declarations.'

Bāḷhataraṃ savarabhayaṃ ahosi. Bhikkhū nāsakkhiṃsu dvevācikaṃ pavāretuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekavācikaṃ pavāretunti.

140. The danger from tribesmen became more severe. The monks were unable to perform the Pavāraṇā with two declarations. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, 'Monks, I allow you to perform the Pavāraṇā with one declaration.'

Bāḷhataraṃ savarabhayaṃ ahosi. Bhikkhū nāsakkhiṃsu ekavācikaṃ pavāretuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, samānavassikaṃ pavāretunti.

234. The danger from tribesmen became even more severe. The monks were unable to perform the Pavāraṇā with one declaration. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, 'Monks, I allow you to perform the Pavāraṇā by those of the same seniority.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya manussehi dānaṃ dentehi yebhuyyena ratti khepitā hoti. Atha kho tesaṃ [M 0.0251] bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “manussehi dānaṃ dentehi yebhuyyena ratti khepitā. Sace saṅgho tevācikaṃ pavāressati, appavāritova saṅgho bhavissati, athāyaṃ ratti vibhāyissati. Kathaṃ nu kho amhehi paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya manussehi dānaṃ dentehi yebhuyyena ratti khepitā hoti. Tatra ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “manussehi dānaṃ [T 1.0344] dentehi yebhuyyena ratti khepitā. Sace saṅgho tevācikaṃ pavāressati, appavāritova saṅgho bhavissati, athāyaṃ ratti vibhāyissatī”ti, byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

At that time, in a certain residence, on the day of the Pavāraṇā, people had spent most of the night giving alms. Then it occurred to those monks: 'People have spent most of the night giving alms. If the Saṅgha performs the Pavāraṇā with three declarations, the Saṅgha will remain without having performed the Pavāraṇā, and this night will dawn. What should we do?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'In this case, monks, in a certain residence, on the day of the Pavāraṇā, people have spent most of the night giving alms. If, monks, it occurs to the monks thus: “People have spent most of the night giving alms. If the Saṅgha performs the Pavāraṇā with three declarations, the Saṅgha will remain without having performed the Pavāraṇā, and this night will dawn,” then a competent and capable monk should inform the Saṅgha:'

“Suṇātu [V 0.0239] me, bhante, saṅgho. Manussehi dānaṃ [P 1.0169] dentehi yebhuyyena ratti khepitā. Sace saṅgho tevācikaṃ pavāressati, appavāritova saṅgho bhavissati, athāyaṃ ratti vibhāyissati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho dvevācikaṃ, ekavācikaṃ, samānavassikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. While people were giving alms, most of the night has been spent. If the Saṅgha were to perform the Pavāraṇā with three declarations, the Saṅgha would remain without having performed the Pavāraṇā, and this night would dawn. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Pavāraṇā with two declarations, with one declaration, or by those of the same seniority.”

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya bhikkhūhi dhammaṃ bhaṇantehi…pe… suttantikehi suttantaṃ saṅgāyantehi… vinayadharehi vinayaṃ vinicchinantehi… dhammakathikehi dhammaṃ sākacchantehi… bhikkhūhi kalahaṃ karontehi yebhuyyena ratti khepitā hoti. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “bhikkhūhi kalahaṃ karontehi yebhuyyena ratti khepitā. Sace saṅgho tevācikaṃ pavāressati, appavāritova saṅgho bhavissati, athāyaṃ ratti vibhāyissatī”ti, byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Furthermore, monks, in a certain residence, on the day of the Pavāraṇā, while monks were reciting Dhamma… while reciters of Suttas were chanting Suttas… while Vinaya-holders were deciding Vinaya… while Dhamma-speakers were discussing Dhamma… or while monks were quarreling, most of the night had been spent. If it occurs to the monks thus: ‘While monks were quarreling, most of the night has been spent. If the Saṅgha were to perform the Pavāraṇā with three declarations, the Saṅgha would remain without having performed the Pavāraṇā, and this night would dawn,’ then a competent and capable monk should inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Bhikkhūhi kalahaṃ karontehi yebhuyyena ratti khepitā. Sace saṅgho tevācikaṃ pavāressati, appavāritova saṅgho bhavissati, athāyaṃ ratti vibhāyissati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho dvevācikaṃ, ekavācikaṃ, samānavassikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. While monks were quarreling, most of the night has been spent. If the Saṅgha were to perform the Pavāraṇā with three recitations, the Saṅgha would remain without having performed the Pavāraṇā, and this night would dawn. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Pavāraṇā with two recitations, with one recitation, or for those of the same rains-residence.”

Tena kho pana samayena kosalesu [T 1.0345] janapade aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya mahābhikkhusaṅgho sannipatito hoti[M 0.0252], parittañca anovassikaṃ anovassakaṃ (ka.) hoti, mahā ca megho uggato hoti. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho mahābhikkhusaṅgho sannipatito, parittañca anovassikaṃ, mahā ca megho uggato. Sace saṅgho tevācikaṃ pavāressati, appavāritova saṅgho bhavissati, athāyaṃ megho pavassissati. Kathaṃ nu kho amhehi paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya mahābhikkhusaṅgho sannipatito hoti, parittañca anovassikaṃ hoti, mahā ca megho uggato hoti. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho mahābhikkhusaṅgho sannipatito, parittañca anovassikaṃ, mahā ca megho uggato. Sace saṅgho tevācikaṃ pavāressati, appavāritova saṅgho bhavissati, athāyaṃ megho pavassissatī”ti. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

At that time, in a certain monastery in the country of Kosala, on that Pavāraṇā day, a great community of monks was assembled. The place sheltered from rain was small, and a great cloud had arisen. Then this thought occurred to those monks: ‘This great community of monks is assembled, the place sheltered from rain is small, and a great cloud has arisen. If the Saṅgha were to perform the Pavāraṇā with three recitations, the Saṅgha would be left with the Pavāraṇā unperformed, and then this cloud would rain. How indeed should we proceed?’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Here, O monks, in a certain monastery, on that Pavāraṇā day, a great community of monks is assembled, the place sheltered from rain is small, and a great cloud has arisen. If, in that situation, it occurs to the monks thus: “This great community of monks is assembled, the place sheltered from rain is small, and a great cloud has arisen. If the Saṅgha were to perform the Pavāraṇā with three recitations, the Saṅgha would be left with the Pavāraṇā unperformed, and then this cloud would rain,” then the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ mahābhikkhusaṅgho sannipatito, parittañca anovassikaṃ, mahā ca megho uggato. Sace saṅgho tevācikaṃ pavāressati, appavāritova saṅgho [V 0.0240] bhavissati, athāyaṃ megho pavassissati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho dvevācikaṃ, ekavācikaṃ, samānavassikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This great community of monks is assembled, the place sheltered from rain is small, and a great cloud has arisen. If the Saṅgha were to perform the Pavāraṇā with three recitations, the Saṅgha would be left with the Pavāraṇā unperformed, and then this cloud would rain. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Pavāraṇā with two recitations, with one recitation, or for those of the same rains-residence.’

Idha pana, bhikkhave, aññatarasmiṃ āvāse tadahu pavāraṇāya rājantarāyo hoti…pe… corantarāyo hoti… agyantarāyo hoti… udakantarāyo [T 1.0346] hoti… manussantarāyo hoti… amanussantarāyo hoti… vāḷantarāyo hoti… sarīsapantarāyo hoti… jīvitantarāyo hoti… brahmacariyantarāyo hoti. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, brahmacariyantarāyo[P 1.0170]. Sace saṅgho tevācikaṃ pavāressati, appavāritova saṅgho bhavissati, athāyaṃ brahmacariyantarāyo bhavissatī”ti, byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Furthermore, O monks, in a certain monastery, on that Pavāraṇā day, a danger from a king may arise... a danger from thieves may arise... a danger from fire may arise... a danger from water may arise... a danger from humans may arise... a danger from non-humans may arise... a danger from wild beasts may arise... a danger from creeping creatures may arise... a danger to life may arise... a danger to the holy life may arise. If it occurs to the monks there thus: ‘Indeed, this is a danger to the holy life. If the Saṅgha were to perform the Pavāraṇā with three recitations, the Saṅgha would remain without having performed the Pavāraṇā, and then this danger to the holy life would occur,’ then a competent and capable monk should inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ brahmacariyantarāyo. Sace saṅgho tevācikaṃ pavāressati, appavāritova saṅgho bhavissati, athāyaṃ [M 0.0253] brahmacariyantarāyo bhavissati. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho dvevācikaṃ, ekavācikaṃ, samānavassikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This is a danger to the holy life. If the Saṅgha were to perform the Pavāraṇā with three recitations, the Saṅgha would remain without having performed the Pavāraṇā, and then this danger to the holy life would occur. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Pavāraṇā with two recitations, with one recitation, or for those of the same rains-residence.”

Dvevācikādipavāraṇā niṭṭhitā.

The Pavāraṇā with Two Recitations, etc., is concluded.

141. Pavāraṇāṭhapanaṃ

141. The Suspension of the Pavāraṇā

235. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sāpattikā pavārenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, sāpattikena pavāretabbaṃ. Yo pavāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yo sāpattiko pavāreti, tassa okāsaṃ kārāpetvā āpattiyā codetunti.

235. Now at that time, the group-of-six monks performed the Pavāraṇā while having an offense. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘O monks, the Pavāraṇā should not be performed by one who has an offense. Whoever should perform it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, O monks, that a monk who performs the Pavāraṇā while having an offense may, after leave has been granted, be charged with the offense.’

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū okāsaṃ kārāpiyamānā na icchanti okāsaṃ kātuṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, okāsaṃ akarontassa pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapetuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, ṭhapetabbā. Tadahu pavāraṇāya cātuddase vā pannarase vā tasmiṃ puggale sammukhībhūte saṅghamajjhe udāharitabbaṃ – “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmo puggalo sāpattiko[T 1.0347]. Tassa pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapemi. Na tasmiṃ sammukhībhūte pavāretabba”nti. Ṭhapitā hoti pavāraṇāti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six, when requested to grant leave, did not wish to grant leave. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘I allow, monks, the suspension of the Pavāraṇā for one who does not grant leave. And this, monks, is how it should be suspended. On the Pavāraṇā day, whether the fourteenth or the fifteenth, with that person present, it should be announced in the midst of the Saṅgha: “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The person named so-and-so has an offense. I suspend his Pavāraṇā. The Pavāraṇā should not be performed while he is present.”’ In this way, the Pavāraṇā is suspended.

Tena [V 0.0241] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū – puramhākaṃ pesalā bhikkhū pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapentīti – paṭikacceva suddhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anāpattikānaṃ avatthusmiṃ akāraṇe pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapenti, pavāritānampi pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, suddhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anāpattikānaṃ avatthusmiṃ akāraṇe pavāraṇā ṭhapetabbā. Yo ṭhapeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na, bhikkhave, pavāritānampi pavāraṇā ṭhapetabbā. Yo ṭhapeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa.

At that time, the monks of the group of six, thinking, ‘The amiable monks will suspend our Pavāraṇā first,’ would preemptively suspend the Pavāraṇā for pure monks who were without offense, without grounds and without reason; and they would also suspend the Pavāraṇā for those who had already performed it. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Monks, the Pavāraṇā should not be suspended for pure monks who are without offense, without grounds and without reason. Whoever should suspend it, commits an offense of wrong-doing. Monks, the Pavāraṇā should not be suspended for those who have already performed it. Whoever should suspend it, commits an offense of wrong-doing.’

236. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, ṭhapitā hoti pavāraṇā, evaṃ aṭṭhapitā. Kathañca, bhikkhave, aṭṭhapitā hoti pavāraṇā? Tevācikāya ce, bhikkhave, pavāraṇāya bhāsitāya lapitāya pariyositāya pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, aṭṭhapitā hoti pavāraṇā. Dvevācikāya ce, bhikkhave,… ekavācikāya ce, bhikkhave,… samānavassikāya ce, bhikkhave, pavāraṇāya bhāsitāya lapitāya pariyositāya pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti[M 0.0254], aṭṭhapitā [P 1.0171] hoti pavāraṇā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭhapitā hoti pavāraṇā.

236. Thus, monks, the Pavāraṇā is suspended, and thus it is not suspended. And how, monks, is the Pavāraṇā not suspended? If, monks, one suspends the Pavāraṇā after the Pavāraṇā with three recitations has been spoken, uttered, and completed, the Pavāraṇā is not suspended. If, monks, after the Pavāraṇā with two recitations… after the Pavāraṇā with one recitation… after the Pavāraṇā for those of the same rains-residence has been spoken, uttered, and completed, one suspends the Pavāraṇā, the Pavāraṇā is not suspended. Thus, monks, the Pavāraṇā is not suspended.

Kathañca, bhikkhave, ṭhapitā hoti pavāraṇā? Tevācikāya, ce, bhikkhave, pavāraṇāya bhāsitāya lapitāya apariyositāya pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, ṭhapitā hoti pavāraṇā. Dvevācikāya ce, bhikkhave,… ekavācikāya ce, bhikkhave,… samānavassikāya ce, bhikkhave, pavāraṇāya bhāsitāya lapitāya apariyositāya [T 1.0348] pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, ṭhapitā hoti pavāraṇā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, ṭhapitā hoti pavāraṇā.

And how, monks, is the Pavāraṇā suspended? If, monks, one suspends the Pavāraṇā while the three-time Pavāraṇā has been spoken and recited, but is not yet finished, the Pavāraṇā is suspended. If, monks, while the two-time Pavāraṇā… the one-time Pavāraṇā… or the Pavāraṇā for those of equal seniority has been spoken and recited, but is not yet finished, one suspends the Pavāraṇā, the Pavāraṇā is suspended. Thus, monks, is the Pavāraṇā suspended.

237. Idha pana, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya bhikkhu bhikkhussa pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti. Taṃ ce bhikkhuṃ aññe bhikkhū jānanti, “ayaṃ kho āyasmā aparisuddhakāyasamācāro, aparisuddhavacīsamācāro, aparisuddhājīvo, bālo, abyatto, na paṭibalo anuyuñjīyamāno anuyogaṃ dātu”nti, ‘alaṃ, bhikkhu, mā bhaṇḍanaṃ, mā kalahaṃ, mā viggahaṃ, mā vivāda’nti omadditvā saṅghena pavāretabbaṃ.

237. Here in this Teaching, monks, on the day of the Pavāraṇā, a monk suspends the Pavāraṇā of another monk. If other monks know of that monk thus: ‘This venerable one has impure bodily conduct, impure verbal conduct, and an impure livelihood; he is foolish, unskilled, and when questioned, is unable to give an answer,’ then, having subdued him with the words, ‘Enough, monk! Do not make a dispute, do not make a quarrel, do not make a contention, do not make an argument,’ the Pavāraṇā should be performed by the Saṅgha.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya bhikkhu bhikkhussa pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti. Taṃ ce bhikkhuṃ aññe bhikkhū jānanti, “ayaṃ kho āyasmā parisuddhakāyasamācāro, aparisuddhavacīsamācāro, aparisuddhājīvo, bālo, abyatto, na paṭibalo anuyuñjīyamāno anuyogaṃ [V 0.0242] dātu”nti, ‘alaṃ, bhikkhu, mā bhaṇḍanaṃ, mā kalahaṃ, mā viggahaṃ, mā vivāda’nti omadditvā saṅghena pavāretabbaṃ.

Here in this Teaching, monks, on the day of the Pavāraṇā, a monk suspends the Pavāraṇā of another monk. If other monks know of that monk thus: ‘This venerable one has pure bodily conduct, impure verbal conduct, and an impure livelihood; he is foolish, unskilled, and when questioned, is unable to give an answer,’ then, having subdued him with the words, ‘Enough, monk! Do not make a dispute, do not make a quarrel, do not make a contention, do not make an argument,’ the Pavāraṇā should be performed by the Saṅgha.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya bhikkhu bhikkhussa pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti. Taṃ ce bhikkhuṃ aññe bhikkhū jānanti, “ayaṃ kho āyasmā parisuddhakāyasamācāro, parisuddhavacīsamācāro, aparisuddhājīvo, bālo, abyatto, na paṭibalo anuyuñjīyamāno anuyogaṃ dātu”nti, ‘alaṃ, bhikkhu, mā bhaṇḍanaṃ, mā kalahaṃ, mā viggahaṃ, mā vivāda’nti omadditvā saṅghena pavāretabbaṃ.

Here in this Teaching, monks, on the day of the Pavāraṇā, a monk suspends the Pavāraṇā of another monk. If other monks know of that monk thus: ‘This venerable one has pure bodily conduct, pure verbal conduct, and an impure livelihood; he is foolish, unskilled, and when questioned, is unable to give an answer,’ then, having subdued him with the words, ‘Enough, monk! Do not make a dispute, do not make a quarrel, do not make a contention, do not make an argument,’ the Pavāraṇā should be performed by the Saṅgha.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya bhikkhu bhikkhussa pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti. Taṃ ce bhikkhuṃ aññe bhikkhū jānanti, “ayaṃ kho āyasmā parisuddhakāyasamācāro[T 1.0349], parisuddhavacīsamācāro, parisuddhājīvo, bālo, abyatto[M 0.0255], na paṭibalo anuyuñjīyamāno anuyogaṃ dātu”nti, ‘alaṃ, bhikkhu, mā bhaṇḍanaṃ, mā kalahaṃ, mā viggahaṃ, mā vivāda’nti omadditvā saṅghena pavāretabbaṃ.

Here in this Teaching, monks, on the day of the Pavāraṇā, a monk suspends the Pavāraṇā of another monk. If other monks know of that monk thus: ‘This venerable one has pure bodily conduct, pure verbal conduct, and a pure livelihood; he is foolish, unskilled, and when questioned, is unable to give an answer,’ then, having subdued him with the words, ‘Enough, monk! Do not make a dispute, do not make a quarrel, do not make a contention, do not make an argument,’ the Pavāraṇā should be performed by the Saṅgha.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, tadahu pavāraṇāya bhikkhu bhikkhussa pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti. Taṃ ce bhikkhuṃ aññe bhikkhū jānanti, “ayaṃ kho āyasmā parisuddhakāyasamācāro, parisuddhavacīsamācāro, parisuddhājīvo, paṇḍito, byatto, paṭibalo anuyuñjīyamāno anuyogaṃ dātu”nti, so evamassa vacanīyo, “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imassa bhikkhuno pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapesi, kimhi naṃ ṭhapesi, sīlavipattiyā vā ṭhapesi, ācāravipattiyā vā ṭhapesi, diṭṭhivipattiyā [P 1.0172] vā ṭhapesī”ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “sīlavipattiyā vā ṭhapemi, ācāravipattiyā vā ṭhapemi, diṭṭhivipattiyā vā ṭhapemī”ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “jānāsi panāyasmā sīlavipattiṃ, jānāsi ācāravipattiṃ, jānāsi diṭṭhivipatti”nti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “jānāmi kho ahaṃ, āvuso, sīlavipattiṃ, jānāmi ācāravipattiṃ, jānāmi diṭṭhivipatti”nti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “katamā panāvuso, sīlavipatti, katamā ācāravipatti, katamā diṭṭhivipattī”ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “cattāri pārājikāni, terasa saṅghādisesā, ayaṃ sīlavipatti; thullaccayaṃ, pācittiyaṃ, pāṭidesanīyaṃ, dukkaṭaṃ, dubbhāsitaṃ, ayaṃ ācāravipatti; micchādiṭṭhi, antaggāhikādiṭṭhi, ayaṃ diṭṭhivipattī”ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “yaṃ kho tvaṃ[T 1.0350], āvuso, imassa bhikkhuno pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapesi, diṭṭhena vā ṭhapesi, sutena vā ṭhapesi, parisaṅkāya vā ṭhapesī”ti? So ce [V 0.0243] evaṃ vadeyya – “diṭṭhena vā ṭhapemi, sutena vā ṭhapemi, parisaṅkāya vā ṭhapemī”ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imassa bhikkhuno diṭṭhena pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapesi, kiṃ te diṭṭhaṃ, kinti te diṭṭhaṃ, kadā te diṭṭhaṃ, kattha te diṭṭhaṃ, pārājikaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho, saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho, thullaccayaṃ… pācittiyaṃ… pāṭidesanīyaṃ… dukkaṭaṃ… dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpajjanto diṭṭho, kattha ca tvaṃ ahosi, kattha cāyaṃ bhikkhu ahosi, kiñca tvaṃ karosi, kiñcāyaṃ bhikkhu karotī”ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, imassa bhikkhuno diṭṭhena pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapemi, apica sutena pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapemī”ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imassa bhikkhuno [M 0.0256] sutena pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapesi, kiṃ te sutaṃ, kinti te sutaṃ, kadā te sutaṃ, kattha te sutaṃ, pārājikaṃ ajjhāpannoti sutaṃ, saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpannoti sutaṃ, thullaccayaṃ… pācittiyaṃ… pāṭidesanīyaṃ… dukkaṭaṃ… dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpannoti sutaṃ, bhikkhussa sutaṃ, bhikkhuniyā sutaṃ, sikkhamānāya sutaṃ, sāmaṇerassa sutaṃ, sāmaṇeriyā sutaṃ, upāsakassa sutaṃ, upāsikāya sutaṃ, rājūnaṃ sutaṃ, rājamahāmattānaṃ sutaṃ, titthiyānaṃ sutaṃ, titthiyasāvakānaṃ suta”nti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, imassa bhikkhuno sutena pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapemi[T 1.0351], apica parisaṅkāya pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapemī”ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “yaṃ kho tvaṃ, āvuso, imassa bhikkhuno parisaṅkāya pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapesi, kiṃ parisaṅkasi, kinti parisaṅkasi, kadā parisaṅkasi, kattha parisaṅkasi, pārājikaṃ [P 1.0173] ajjhāpannoti parisaṅkasi, saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpannoti parisaṅkasi, thullaccayaṃ… pācittiyaṃ… pāṭidesanīyaṃ… dukkaṭaṃ… dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpannoti parisaṅkasi, bhikkhussa sutvā parisaṅkasi, bhikkhuniyā sutvā parisaṅkasi, sikkhamānāya sutvā parisaṅkasi, sāmaṇerassa sutvā parisaṅkasi, sāmaṇeriyā sutvā parisaṅkasi, upāsakassa sutvā parisaṅkasi, upāsikāya sutvā parisaṅkasi, rājūnaṃ sutvā parisaṅkasi, rājamahāmattānaṃ sutvā parisaṅkasi, titthiyānaṃ sutvā parisaṅkasi, titthiyasāvakānaṃ sutvā parisaṅkasī”ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – “na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, imassa bhikkhuno parisaṅkāya pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapemi, api ca ahampi na jānāmi kena panāhaṃ imassa bhikkhuno pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapemī”ti. So ce, bhikkhave, codako bhikkhu anuyogena viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ cittaṃ na ārādheti, ananuvādo cudito bhikkhūti alaṃ vacanāya. So ce, bhikkhave, codako bhikkhu anuyogena viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ cittaṃ ārādheti, sānuvādo cudito bhikkhūti alaṃ vacanāya. So ce, bhikkhave, codako bhikkhu amūlakena pārājikena anuddhaṃsitaṃ paṭijānāti, saṅghādisesaṃ āropetvā saṅghena pavāretabbaṃ. So [T 1.0352] ce, bhikkhave, codako bhikkhu amūlakena saṅghādisesena anuddhaṃsitaṃ paṭijānāti, yathādhammaṃ kārāpetvā saṅghena pavāretabbaṃ. So ce, bhikkhave, codako, bhikkhu amūlakena thullaccayena… pācittiyena… pāṭidesanīyena… dukkaṭena… dubbhāsitena anuddhaṃsitaṃ paṭijānāti, yathādhammaṃ kārāpetvā [V 0.0244] saṅghena pavāretabbaṃ. So [M 0.0257] ce, bhikkhave, cudito bhikkhu pārājikaṃ ajjhāpannoti paṭijānāti, nāsetvā saṅghena pavāretabbaṃ. So ce, bhikkhave, cudito bhikkhu saṅghādisesaṃ ajjhāpannoti paṭijānāti, saṅghādisesaṃ āropetvā saṅghena pavāretabbaṃ. So ce, bhikkhave, cudito bhikkhu thullaccayaṃ… pācittiyaṃ… pāṭidesanīyaṃ… dukkaṭaṃ… dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpannoti paṭijānāti, yathādhammaṃ kārāpetvā saṅghena pavāretabbaṃ.

Here, monks, on the day of the Pavāraṇā, a monk stops another monk's Pavāraṇā. If other monks know of this monk, 'This venerable one is pure in bodily conduct, pure in verbal conduct, pure in livelihood, discerning, capable, and able to give a reply when questioned,' he should be addressed thus: 'Friend, when you stopped this monk's Pavāraṇā, on what grounds did you stop it? Did you stop it on grounds of corruption of virtue, corruption of conduct, or corruption of view?' If he replies, 'I stopped it on grounds of corruption of virtue, corruption of conduct, or corruption of view,' he should be asked further: 'But do you, venerable one, know what a corruption of virtue is, what a corruption of conduct is, what a corruption of view is?' If he says, 'I know, friend, what a corruption of virtue is, what a corruption of conduct is, what a corruption of view is,' he should be asked: 'What, friend, is a corruption of virtue, what is a corruption of conduct, what is a corruption of view?' If he replies, 'The four pārājikas and the thirteen saṅghādisesas—this is corruption of virtue; the thullaccaya, pācittiya, pāṭidesanīya, dukkaṭa, and dubbhāsita—this is corruption of conduct; wrong view and extremist view—this is corruption of view,' he should then be asked: 'Friend, when you stopped this monk's Pavāraṇā, did you stop it based on what you saw, what you heard, or on suspicion?' If he says, 'I stopped it based on what I saw, what I heard, or on suspicion,' he should be asked: 'Friend, when you stopped this monk's Pavāraṇā based on what you saw, what did you see? In what way did you see it? When did you see it? Where did you see it? Did you see him committing a pārājika? Did you see him committing a saṅghādisesa? Did you see him committing a thullaccaya, a pācittiya, a pāṭidesanīya, a dukkaṭa, or a dubbhāsita? Where were you, and where was this monk? What were you doing, and what was this monk doing?' If he then says, 'No, friend, I did not stop this monk's Pavāraṇā based on what I saw, but rather based on what I heard,' he should be asked: 'Friend, when you stopped this monk's Pavāraṇā based on what you heard, what did you hear? In what way did you hear it? When did you hear it? Where did you hear it? Did you hear that he had committed a pārājika? Did you hear that he had committed a saṅghādisesa? Did you hear that he had committed a thullaccaya, a pācittiya, a pāṭidesanīya, a dukkaṭa, or a dubbhāsita? Did you hear it from a monk, a nun, a female trainee, a novice monk, a novice nun, a male lay follower, a female lay follower, kings, royal ministers, sectarians, or disciples of sectarians?' If he then says, 'No, friend, I did not stop this monk's Pavāraṇā based on what I heard, but rather on suspicion,' he should be asked: 'Friend, when you stopped this monk's Pavāraṇā based on suspicion, what do you suspect? In what way do you suspect it? When did you suspect it? Where did you suspect it? Do you suspect that he committed a pārājika? Do you suspect that he committed a saṅghādisesa? Do you suspect that he committed a thullaccaya, a pācittiya, a pāṭidesanīya, a dukkaṭa, or a dubbhāsita? Do you suspect after hearing from a monk, a nun, a female trainee, a novice monk, a novice nun, a male lay follower, a female lay follower, kings, royal ministers, sectarians, or disciples of sectarians?' If he then says, 'No, friend, I did not stop this monk's Pavāraṇā based on suspicion, but I myself do not know for what reason I stopped this monk's Pavāraṇā.' Then, monks, if the accusing monk does not satisfy the wise fellow practitioners with his questioning, it is sufficient to say that the accused monk is not to be reproached. But if the accusing monk satisfies the wise fellow practitioners with his questioning, it is sufficient to say that the accused monk is to be reproached. If, monks, the accusing monk admits to having groundlessly accused another of a pārājika, the Saṅgha should perform Pavāraṇā after imposing a saṅghādisesa on him. If, monks, the accusing monk admits to having groundlessly accused another of a saṅghādisesa, the Saṅgha should perform Pavāraṇā after dealing with him according to the rule. If, monks, the accusing monk admits to having groundlessly accused another of a thullaccaya, a pācittiya, a pāṭidesanīya, a dukkaṭa, or a dubbhāsita, the Saṅgha should perform Pavāraṇā after dealing with him according to the rule. If, monks, the accused monk admits to having committed a pārājika, the Saṅgha should perform Pavāraṇā after expelling him. If, monks, the accused monk admits to having committed a saṅghādisesa, the Saṅgha should perform Pavāraṇā after imposing the saṅghādisesa penalty. If, monks, the accused monk admits to having committed a thullaccaya, a pācittiya, a pāṭidesanīya, a dukkaṭa, or a dubbhāsita, the Saṅgha should perform Pavāraṇā after dealing with him according to the rule.

Pavāraṇāṭhapanaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section on the postponement of the Pavāraṇā is concluded.

142. Thullaccayavatthukādi

142. Cases involving grave offenses, and so forth.

238. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tadahu pavāraṇāya thullaccayaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti. Ekacce bhikkhū thullaccayadiṭṭhino honti, ekacce bhikkhū saṅghādisesadiṭṭhino honti. Ye te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū thullaccayadiṭṭhino, tehi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ekamantaṃ apanetvā yathādhammaṃ kārāpetvā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – “yaṃ kho so, āvuso, bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpanno, sāssa yathādhammaṃ paṭikatā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho pavāreyyā”ti.

238. Here, monks, a monk on that Pavāraṇā day has committed a grave offense. Some monks are of the view that it is a grave offense, while some monks are of the view that it is a saṅghādisesa offense. Monks, those monks who are of the view that it is a grave offense should take that monk aside, have him make amends according to the Dhamma, and then approach the Saṅgha and say thus: ‘Friends, whatever offense that monk has committed, that offense of his has been remedied according to the Dhamma. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Pavāraṇā.’

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tadahu pavāraṇāya thullaccayaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti. Ekacce bhikkhū thullaccayadiṭṭhino honti, ekacce bhikkhū pācittiyadiṭṭhino [T 1.0353] honti…pe… ekacce bhikkhū [P 1.0174] thullaccayadiṭṭhino honti, ekacce bhikkhū pāṭidesanīyadiṭṭhino honti… ekacce bhikkhū thullaccayadiṭṭhino honti, ekacce bhikkhū dukkaṭadiṭṭhino honti… ekacce bhikkhū thullaccayadiṭṭhino honti, ekacce bhikkhū dubbhāsitadiṭṭhino honti. Ye te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū thullaccayadiṭṭhino, tehi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ekamantaṃ apanetvā yathādhammaṃ kārāpetvā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – “yaṃ kho so, āvuso, bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpanno, sāssa yathādhammaṃ paṭikatā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho pavāreyyā”ti.

Here, monks, a monk on that Pavāraṇā day has committed a grave offense. Some monks are of the view that it is a grave offense, while others are of the view that it is a pācittiya offense; … some monks are of the view that it is a grave offense, while others are of the view that it is a pāṭidesanīya offense; … some monks are of the view that it is a grave offense, while others are of the view that it is a dukkaṭa offense; … some monks are of the view that it is a grave offense, while others are of the view that it is a dubbhāsita offense. Monks, those monks who are of the view that it is a grave offense should take that monk aside, have him make amends according to the Dhamma, and then approach the Saṅgha and say thus: ‘Friends, whatever offense that monk has committed, that offense of his has been remedied according to the Dhamma. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Pavāraṇā.’

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tadahu pavāraṇāya pācittiyaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti…pe… pāṭidesanīyaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti… dukkaṭaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti… dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti. Ekacce bhikkhū dubbhāsitadiṭṭhino honti, ekacce bhikkhū saṅghādisesadiṭṭhino honti. Ye [V 0.0245] te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū dubbhāsitadiṭṭhino, tehi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ekamantaṃ [M 0.0258] apanetvā yathādhammaṃ kārāpetvā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – “yaṃ kho so, āvuso, bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpanno, sāssa yathādhammaṃ paṭikatā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho pavāreyyā”ti.

Here, monks, a monk on that Pavāraṇā day has committed a pācittiya offense; … has committed a pāṭidesanīya offense; … has committed a dukkaṭa offense; … has committed a dubbhāsita offense. Some monks are of the view that it is a dubbhāsita offense, while some monks are of the view that it is a saṅghādisesa offense. Monks, those monks who are of the view that it is a dubbhāsita offense should take that monk aside, have him make amends according to the Dhamma, and then approach the Saṅgha and say thus: ‘Friends, whatever offense that monk has committed, that offense of his has been remedied according to the Dhamma. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Pavāraṇā.’

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tadahu pavāraṇāya dubbhāsitaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti. Ekacce bhikkhū dubbhāsitadiṭṭhino honti, ekacce bhikkhū thullaccayadiṭṭhino honti…pe… ekacce bhikkhū dubbhāsitadiṭṭhino honti, ekacce bhikkhū pācittiyadiṭṭhino [T 1.0354] honti… ekacce bhikkhū dubbhāsitadiṭṭhino honti, ekacce bhikkhū pāṭidesanīyadiṭṭhino honti… ekacce bhikkhū dubbhāsitadiṭṭhino honti, ekacce bhikkhū dukkaṭadiṭṭhino honti. Ye te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū dubbhāsitadiṭṭhino, tehi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ekamantaṃ apanetvā yathādhammaṃ kārāpetvā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – “yaṃ kho so, āvuso, bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpanno, sāssa yathādhammaṃ paṭikatā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho pavāreyyā”ti.

Here, monks, a monk on that Pavāraṇā day has committed a dubbhāsita offense. Some monks are of the view that it is a dubbhāsita offense, while some monks are of the view that it is a grave offense; … some monks are of the view that it is a dubbhāsita offense, while some monks are of the view that it is a pācittiya offense; … some monks are of the view that it is a dubbhāsita offense, while some monks are of the view that it is a pāṭidesanīya offense; … some monks are of the view that it is a dubbhāsita offense, while some monks are of the view that it is a dukkaṭa offense. Monks, those monks who are of the view that it is a dubbhāsita offense should take that monk aside, have him make amends according to the Dhamma, and then approach the Saṅgha and say thus: ‘Friends, whatever offense that monk has committed, that offense of his has been remedied according to the Dhamma. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the Pavāraṇā.’

Thullaccayavatthukādi niṭṭhitā.

The section on cases involving grave offenses, and so forth, is concluded.

143. Vatthuṭhapanādi

143. Setting Aside the Matter, and So Forth

239. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tadahu pavāraṇāya saṅghamajjhe udāhareyya – “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Idaṃ vatthu paññāyati, na puggalo. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, vatthuṃ ṭhapetvā saṅgho pavāreyyā”ti. So evamassa vacanīyo – “bhagavatā kho, āvuso, visuddhānaṃ pavāraṇā paññattā. Sace vatthu paññāyati, na puggalo, idāneva naṃ vadehī”ti.

239. Here, monks, a monk on that Pavāraṇā day might declare in the midst of the Saṅgha: ‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This matter is apparent, but the person is not. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, having set aside the matter, the Saṅgha should perform the Pavāraṇā.’ That monk should be spoken to thus: ‘Friend, the Blessed One has prescribed the Pavāraṇā for the purified. If the matter is apparent, but the person is not, name him now.’

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tadahu pavāraṇāya saṅghamajjhe udāhareyya – “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṃ puggalo paññāyati, na vatthu. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, puggalaṃ ṭhapetvā saṅgho pavāreyyā”ti. So evamassa vacanīyo – “bhagavatā kho, āvuso, samaggānaṃ pavāraṇā paññattā. Sace puggalo paññāyati, na vatthu, idāneva naṃ vadehī”ti.

Here, monks, a monk on that Pavāraṇā day might declare in the midst of the Saṅgha: ‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This person is apparent, but the matter is not. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, having set aside the person, the Saṅgha should perform the Pavāraṇā.’ That monk should be spoken to thus: ‘Friend, the Blessed One has prescribed the Pavāraṇā for those who are in concord. If the person is apparent, but the matter is not, state the matter now.’

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tadahu pavāraṇāya saṅghamajjhe udāhareyya – “suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Idaṃ vatthu ca puggalo ca paññāyati. Yadi [M 0.0259] saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, vatthuñca [T 1.0355] puggalañca [V 0.0246] ṭhapetvā saṅgho pavāreyyā”ti. So evamassa vacanīyo – “bhagavatā kho, āvuso, visuddhānañca samaggānañca pavāraṇā paññattā. Sace vatthu ca puggalo ca paññāyati, idāneva naṃ vadehī”ti.

Here, monks, a monk on that Pavāraṇā day might declare in the midst of the Saṅgha: ‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This matter and this person are apparent. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, having set aside both the matter and the person, the Saṅgha should perform the Pavāraṇā.’ That monk should be spoken to thus: ‘Friend, the Blessed One has prescribed the Pavāraṇā for the purified and for those in concord. If the matter and the person are apparent, state them now.’

Pubbe ce, bhikkhave, pavāraṇāya vatthu paññāyati, pacchā puggalo, kallaṃ vacanāya. Pubbe ce, bhikkhave, pavāraṇāya [P 1.0175] puggalo paññāyati, pacchā vatthu, kallaṃ vacanāya. Pubbe ce, bhikkhave, pavāraṇāya vatthu ca puggalo ca paññāyati, taṃ ce katāya pavāraṇāya ukkoṭeti, ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyanti.

Monks, if, before the Pavāraṇā, the matter is apparent and afterwards the person, it is suitable to make an accusation. Monks, if, before the Pavāraṇā, the person is apparent and afterwards the matter, it is suitable to make an accusation. Monks, if, before the Pavāraṇā, both the matter and the person are apparent, and one brings it up again after the Pavāraṇā has been performed, it is a pācittiya offense for bringing it up again.

Vatthuṭhapanādi niṭṭhitā.

The section on setting aside the matter, and so forth, is concluded.

144. Bhaṇḍanakārakavatthu

144. The Case of the Quarrelsome Monk

240. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā sandiṭṭhā sambhattā bhikkhū kosalesu janapade aññatarasmiṃ āvāse vassaṃ upagacchiṃsu. Tesaṃ sāmantā aññe bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā vassaṃ upagacchiṃsu – mayaṃ tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ pavāraṇāya pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapessāmāti. Assosuṃ kho te bhikkhū – “amhākaṃ kira sāmantā aññe bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā vassaṃ upagatā – mayaṃ tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ pavāraṇāya pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapessāmā”ti. Kathaṃ nu kho amhehi paṭipajjitabbanti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

240. Now at that time, many bhikkhus who were acquainted and companions entered the rains-residence in a certain monastery in the country of Kosala. Near them, other bhikkhus—makers of quarrels, makers of strife, makers of disputes, brawlers, and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha—entered the rains-residence, thinking: ‘When those bhikkhus have completed the rains-residence, we will obstruct their Pavāraṇā on the day of Pavāraṇā.’ Those bhikkhus heard: ‘It is said that near us, other bhikkhus—makers of quarrels, makers of strife, makers of disputes, brawlers, and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha—have entered the rains-residence, thinking: “When those bhikkhus have completed the rains-residence, we will obstruct their Pavāraṇā on the day of Pavāraṇā.”’ The thought occurred to them: ‘How indeed should we act?’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, sambahulā sandiṭṭhā sambhattā bhikkhū aññatarasmiṃ āvāse vassaṃ upagacchanti. Tesaṃ sāmantā aññe bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā [T 1.0356] saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā vassaṃ upagacchanti – mayaṃ tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ pavāraṇāya pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapessāmāti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tehi bhikkhūhi dve tayo uposathe cātuddasike kātuṃ – kathaṃ mayaṃ tehi bhikkhūhi paṭhamataraṃ pavāreyyāmāti. Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā taṃ āvāsaṃ āgacchanti, tehi, bhikkhave, āvāsikehi bhikkhūhi lahuṃ lahuṃ sannipatitvā pavāretabbaṃ, pavāretvā vattabbā – “pavāritā [M 0.0260] kho mayaṃ, āvuso; yathāyasmantā maññanti tathā [V 0.0247] karontū”ti. Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā asaṃvihitā taṃ āvāsaṃ āgacchanti, tehi, bhikkhave, āvāsikehi bhikkhūhi āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipitabbaṃ, paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetabbaṃ, pānīyena paripucchitabbā; tesaṃ vikkhitvā vikkhipāpetvā (paṭivisodhakānaṃ mati), ācikkhitvā (ka.) nissīmaṃ gantvā pavāretabbaṃ, pavāretvā vattabbā – “pavāritā kho mayaṃ, āvuso; yathāyasmantā maññanti tathā karontū”ti. Evañcetaṃ labhetha, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. No ce labhetha, āvāsikena bhikkhunā byattena paṭibalena āvāsikā bhikkhū ñāpetabbā –

Here, O bhikkhus, many acquainted and companion bhikkhus enter the Rains-residence in a certain monastery. Nearby, other bhikkhus—makers of quarrels, makers of strife, makers of disputes, brawlers, and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha—also enter the Rains-residence, thinking: ‘We will obstruct the Pavāraṇā of those bhikkhus after they have completed the Rains.’ I allow, O bhikkhus, those bhikkhus to perform two or three Uposathas on the fourteenth day, thinking: ‘How might we perform the Pavāraṇā before those bhikkhus?’ If, O bhikkhus, those bhikkhus—makers of quarrels, makers of strife, makers of disputes, brawlers, and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha—arrive at that monastery, the resident bhikkhus should assemble very quickly and perform the Pavāraṇā. After performing it, they should say: ‘Friends, we have indeed performed the Pavāraṇā; let the venerable ones act as they see fit.’ If, O bhikkhus, those bhikkhus—makers of quarrels, makers of strife, makers of disputes, brawlers, and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha—arrive at that monastery unannounced, the resident bhikkhus should prepare seats; water for the feet, a footstool, and a pot-sherd for rubbing the feet should be set out; they should go out to meet them and receive their bowls and robes; they should be asked about drinking water. Then, having distracted them, they should go outside the boundary and perform the Pavāraṇā. After performing it, they should say: ‘Friends, we have indeed performed the Pavāraṇā; let the venerable ones act as they see fit.’ If you can accomplish this, it is good. If you cannot, a resident bhikkhu who is expert and competent should inform the resident bhikkhus:

“Suṇantu me, āyasmanto āyasmantā (ka.), āvāsikā. Yadāyasmantānaṃ pattakallaṃ, idāni uposathaṃ kareyyāma, pātimokkhaṃ uddiseyyāma[P 1.0176], āgame kāḷe pavāreyyāmā”ti. Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā [T 1.0357] vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā te bhikkhū evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – “sādhāvuso, idāneva no pavārethā”ti, te evamassu vacanīyā – “anissarā kho tumhe, āvuso, amhākaṃ pavāraṇāya; na tāva mayaṃ pavāreyyāmā”ti. Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā taṃ kāḷaṃ anuvaseyyuṃ, āvāsikena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā byattena paṭibalena āvāsikā bhikkhū ñāpetabbā –

‘Venerable residents, listen to my words. If it is the proper time for the venerable ones, let us now perform the Uposatha, recite the Pātimokkha, and perform the Pavāraṇā on the approaching dark-moon day.’ If, O bhikkhus, those bhikkhus—makers of quarrels, makers of strife, makers of disputes, brawlers, and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha—should say thus: ‘Friends, we ask you, please perform the Pavāraṇā right now,’ they should be told thus: ‘Indeed, friends, you are not in authority over our Pavāraṇā; we shall not yet perform the Pavāraṇā.’ If, O bhikkhus, those bhikkhus—makers of quarrels, makers of strife, makers of disputes, brawlers, and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha—should remain until that dark-moon day, a competent, capable resident bhikkhu should inform the resident bhikkhus:

“Suṇantu me, āyasmanto, āvāsikā. Yadāyasmantānaṃ pattakallaṃ, idāni uposathaṃ kareyyāma, pātimokkhaṃ uddiseyyāma, āgame juṇhe pavāreyyāmā”ti. Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā te bhikkhū evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – “sādhāvuso, idāneva no pavāreyyāthā”ti, te evamassu vacanīyā – “anissarā kho tumhe, āvuso, amhākaṃ pavāraṇāya, na tāva mayaṃ pavāreyyāmā”ti. Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā [M 0.0261] tampi juṇhaṃ anuvaseyyuṃ, tehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi sabbeheva āgame juṇhe komudiyā cātumāsiniyā akāmā pavāretabbaṃ.

‘Venerable residents, listen to my words. If it is the proper time for the venerable ones, let us now perform the Uposatha, recite the Pātimokkha, and perform the Pavāraṇā on the approaching bright fortnight.’ If, O bhikkhus, those bhikkhus—makers of quarrels, makers of strife, makers of disputes, brawlers, and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha—should say thus: ‘Friends, we ask you, please perform the Pavāraṇā right now,’ they should be told thus: ‘Indeed, friends, you are not in authority over our Pavāraṇā; we shall not yet perform the Pavāraṇā.’ If, O bhikkhus, those bhikkhus—makers of quarrels, makers of strife, makers of disputes, brawlers, and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha—should remain until that bright fortnight as well, the Pavāraṇā must be performed by all those bhikkhus, even unwillingly, on the approaching Komudī, the fourth-month full-moon day.

Tehi ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi pavāriyamāne gilāno agilānassa pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “āyasmā kho gilāno. Gilāno ca ananuyogakkhamo vutto bhagavatā. Āgamehi, āvuso, yāva arogo hosi. Arogo ākaṅkhamāno [T 1.0358] codessasī”ti. Evañce vuccamāno codeti, anādariye pācittiyaṃ. Tehi ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi pavāriyamāne [V 0.0248] agilāno gilānassa pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu gilāno. Gilāno ca ananuyogakkhamo vutto bhagavatā. Āgamehi, āvuso, yāvāyaṃ bhikkhu arogo hoti. Arogaṃ ākaṅkhamāno codessasī”ti. Evañce vuccamāno codeti, anādariye pācittiyaṃ. Tehi ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi pavāriyamāne gilāno gilānassa pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “āyasmantā kho gilānā. Gilāno ca ananuyogakkhamo vutto bhagavatā. Āgamehi, āvuso, yāva arogā hotha. Arogo arogaṃ ākaṅkhamāno codessasī”ti yāva arogo hoti, arogaṃ ākaṅkhamāno codessasīti (ka.). Evañce vuccamāno codeti, anādariye pācittiyaṃ. Tehi ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi pavāriyamāne agilāno agilānassa pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, ubho saṅghena samanuyuñjitvā samanugāhitvā samanubhāsitvā (sī.) yathādhammaṃ kārāpetvā saṅghena pavāretabbanti.

Monks, if while those monks are performing the Pavāraṇā, a sick monk stops the Pavāraṇā of a healthy one, he should be told thus: ‘Venerable sir, you are indeed sick. And a sick person has been declared by the Blessed One as unfit for questioning. Wait, friend, until you are well. When you are well, if you wish, you may make an accusation.’ If, having been spoken to thus, he still makes an accusation, there is a pācittiya offense for disrespect. Monks, if while those monks are performing the Pavāraṇā, a healthy monk stops the Pavāraṇā of a sick one, he should be told thus: ‘Friend, this monk is indeed sick. And a sick person has been declared by the Blessed One as unfit for questioning. Wait, friend, until this monk is well. When he is well, if you wish, you may make an accusation.’ If, having been spoken to thus, he still makes an accusation, there is a pācittiya offense for disrespect. Monks, if while those monks are performing the Pavāraṇā, a sick monk stops the Pavāraṇā of another sick one, he should be told thus: ‘Venerable sirs, you are sick. And a sick person has been declared by the Blessed One as unfit for questioning. Wait, friends, until you are well. When you are well, you may, if you wish, accuse one who is well.’ If, having been spoken to thus, he still makes an accusation, there is a pācittiya offense for disrespect. Monks, if while those monks are performing the Pavāraṇā, a healthy monk stops the Pavāraṇā of another healthy one, the Saṅgha, having questioned and investigated both of them and having had the matter settled according to the Dhamma, should then perform the Pavāraṇā.

Bhaṇḍanakārakavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section on the quarrel-maker is concluded.

145. Pavāraṇāsaṅgaho

145. Deferral of the Pavāraṇā

241. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā sandiṭṭhā sambhattā bhikkhū [P 1.0177] kosalesu janapade aññatarasmiṃ āvāse vassaṃ upagacchiṃsu. Tesaṃ samaggānaṃ sammodamānānaṃ avivadamānānaṃ viharataṃ aññataro phāsuvihāro adhigato hoti. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “amhākaṃ kho samaggānaṃ sammodamānānaṃ avivadamānānaṃ viharataṃ aññataro phāsuvihāro adhigato. Sace mayaṃ idāni pavāressāma[M 0.0262], siyāpi [T 1.0359] bhikkhū pavāretvā cārikaṃ pakkameyyuṃ. Evaṃ mayaṃ imamhā phāsuvihārā paribāhirā bhavissāma. Kathaṃ nu kho amhehi paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

241. Now at that time, many monks who were acquainted and companions entered upon the rains-residence in a certain monastery in the country of Kosala. For them, while living in concord, rejoicing, and without dispute, a certain comfortable living was attained. Then this thought occurred to those monks: ‘For us, while living in concord, rejoicing, and without dispute, a certain comfortable living has been attained.
