If we were to perform the Pavāraṇā now, it might be that the monks, having performed the Pavāraṇā, would depart on a journey. In that case, we would be deprived of this comfortable living. How indeed should we act?’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, sambahulā sandiṭṭhā sambhattā bhikkhū aññatarasmiṃ āvāse vassaṃ upagacchanti. Tesaṃ samaggānaṃ sammodamānānaṃ avivadamānānaṃ viharataṃ aññataro phāsuvihāro adhigato hoti. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “amhākaṃ kho samaggānaṃ sammodamānānaṃ avivadamānānaṃ viharataṃ aññataro phāsuvihāro adhigato. Sace mayaṃ idāni pavāressāma, siyāpi bhikkhū pavāretvā cārikaṃ pakkameyyuṃ. Evaṃ mayaṃ imamhā phāsuvihārā paribāhirā bhavissāmā”ti, anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tehi bhikkhūhi pavāraṇāsaṅgahaṃ kātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbo. Sabbeheva ekajjhaṃ sannipatitabbaṃ – sannipatitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Moreover, monks, in this Teaching, many monks who are acquainted and companions enter upon the rains-residence in a certain monastery. For them, while living in concord, rejoicing, and without dispute, a certain comfortable living is attained. If in that case it occurs to those monks: ‘For us, while living in concord, rejoicing, and without dispute, a certain comfortable living has been attained. If we were to perform the Pavāraṇā now, it might be that the monks, having performed the Pavāraṇā, would depart on a journey. In that case, we would be deprived of this comfortable living,’ then, monks, I allow those monks to perform a deferral of the Pavāraṇā. And, monks, it should be done in this way. All should assemble together. Having assembled, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and able monk:

“Suṇātu [V 0.0249] me, bhante, saṅgho. Amhākaṃ samaggānaṃ sammodamānānaṃ avivadamānānaṃ viharataṃ aññataro phāsuvihāro adhigato. Sace mayaṃ idāni pavāressāma, siyāpi bhikkhū pavāretvā cārikaṃ pakkameyyuṃ. Evaṃ mayaṃ imamhā phāsuvihārā paribāhirā bhavissāma. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho pavāraṇāsaṅgahaṃ kareyya, idāni uposathaṃ kareyya, pātimokkhaṃ uddiseyya, āgame juṇhe komudiyā cātumāsiniyā pavāreyya. Esā ñatti.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. While we have been living in concord, rejoicing together, and without dispute, a certain comfortable living has been attained. If we were now to perform the Pavāraṇā, it is possible that monks, having performed the Pavāraṇā, might set out on a journey. Thus, we would be deprived of this comfortable living. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform a deferral of the Pavāraṇā, should perform the Uposatha now, should recite the Pātimokkha, and should perform the Pavāraṇā in the coming bright fortnight, on the four-monthly day of Komudī. This is the motion.’

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Amhākaṃ samaggānaṃ sammodamānānaṃ avivadamānānaṃ viharataṃ [T 1.0360] aññataro phāsuvihāro adhigato. Sace mayaṃ idāni pavāressāma, siyāpi bhikkhū pavāretvā cārikaṃ pakkameyyuṃ. Evaṃ mayaṃ imamhā phāsuvihārā paribāhirā bhavissāma. Saṅgho pavāraṇāsaṅgahaṃ karoti, idāni uposathaṃ karissati, pātimokkhaṃ uddisissati, āgame juṇhe komudiyā cātumāsiniyā pavāressati. Yassāyasmato khamati pavāraṇāsaṅgahassa karaṇaṃ, idāni uposathaṃ karissati, pātimokkhaṃ uddisissati, āgame juṇhe komudiyā cātumāsiniyā pavāressati, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

‘Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha listen to me. While we have been living in concord, rejoicing together, and without dispute, a certain comfortable living has been attained. If we were now to perform the Pavāraṇā, it is possible that monks, having performed the Pavāraṇā, might set out on a journey. Thus, we would be deprived of this comfortable living. The Saṅgha performs a deferral of the Pavāraṇā; it will perform the Uposatha now, will recite the Pātimokkha, and will perform the Pavāraṇā in the coming bright fortnight, on the four-monthly day of Komudī. To the venerable one to whom the performance of the deferral of the Pavāraṇā is agreeable—that the Uposatha will be performed now, the Pātimokkha will be recited, and the Pavāraṇā will be performed in the coming bright fortnight, on the four-monthly day of Komudī—he should remain silent. To whom it is not agreeable, he should speak.’

“Kato [M 0.0263] saṅghena pavāraṇāsaṅgaho, idāni uposathaṃ karissati, pātimokkhaṃ uddisissati, āgame juṇhe komudiyā cātumāsiniyā pavāressati. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

‘The deferral of the Pavāraṇā has been performed by the Saṅgha; it will perform the Uposatha now, will recite the Pātimokkha, and will perform the Pavāraṇā in the coming bright fortnight, on the four-monthly day of Komudī. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold this.’

Tehi ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi kate pavāraṇāsaṅgahe aññataro bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya – “icchāmahaṃ, āvuso, janapadacārikaṃ pakkamituṃ; atthi me janapade karaṇīya”nti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “sādhāvuso, pavāretvā gacchāhī”ti. So ce[P 1.0178], bhikkhave, bhikkhu pavārayamāno aññatarassa bhikkhuno pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “anissaro kho me tvaṃ, āvuso, pavāraṇāya, na tāvāhaṃ pavāressāmī”ti. Tassa ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pavārayamānassa aññataro bhikkhu tassa bhikkhuno pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, ubho saṅghena samanuyuñjitvā samanugāhitvā yathādhammaṃ kārāpetabbā. So ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu janapade taṃ karaṇīyaṃ tīretvā [T 1.0361] punadeva anto komudiyā cātumāsiniyā taṃ āvāsaṃ āgacchati, tehi ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi pavāriyamāne aññataro bhikkhu tassa bhikkhuno pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapeti, so evamassa vacanīyo – “anissaro kho me tvaṃ, āvuso, pavāraṇāya; pavārito aha”nti. Tehi ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi pavāriyamāne so bhikkhu aññatarassa bhikkhuno pavāraṇaṃ [V 0.0250] ṭhapeti, ubho saṅghena samanuyuñjitvā samanugāhitvā yathādhammaṃ kārāpetvā saṅghena pavāretabbanti.

Bhikkhus, if after the support for the Pavāraṇā has been made by those bhikkhus, a certain bhikkhu should say thus: ‘Friends, I wish to depart on a tour of the country; I have business in the country,’ he should be told thus: ‘Very well, friend, go after having performed the Pavāraṇā.’ If, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu, while performing the Pavāraṇā, stops the Pavāraṇā of a certain bhikkhu, he should be told thus: ‘Friend, you have no authority over my Pavāraṇā; I will not yet perform the Pavāraṇā.’ If, bhikkhus, while that bhikkhu is performing the Pavāraṇā, another bhikkhu stops the Pavāraṇā of that bhikkhu, both should be interrogated and questioned by the Saṅgha and be dealt with according to the Dhamma. If, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu, having completed that business in the country, returns once again to that residence within the Komudī of the fourth month, and if, bhikkhus, while those bhikkhus are performing the Pavāraṇā, a certain bhikkhu stops the Pavāraṇā of that bhikkhu, he should be told thus: ‘Friend, you have no authority over my Pavāraṇā; I have already performed the Pavāraṇā.’ If, bhikkhus, while those bhikkhus are performing the Pavāraṇā, that bhikkhu stops the Pavāraṇā of a certain bhikkhu, both should be interrogated and questioned by the Saṅgha, dealt with according to the Dhamma, and then the Saṅgha should perform the Pavāraṇā.

Pavāraṇāsaṅgaho niṭṭhito.

The Section on the Support for the Pavāraṇā is concluded.

Pavāraṇākkhandhako catuttho.

The Fourth Pavāraṇā Chapter is concluded.

146. Tassuddānaṃ

146. The Summary:

Vassaṃvuṭṭhā kosalesu, agamuṃ satthu dassanaṃ;

Aphāsuṃ pasusaṃvāsaṃ, aññamaññānulomatā.

Those who had completed the rains-residence in Kosala went to see the Teacher; the uncomfortable living like cattle; the mutual agreeableness.

Pavārentā paṇāmañca pavārentāsane dve ca (sī. syā.), kammaṃ gilānañātakā;

Rājā corā ca dhuttā ca, bhikkhupaccatthikā tathā.

Performing Pavāraṇā and not bowing down; the formal act; the sick bhikkhu and relatives; kings, thieves, and drunkards; likewise hostile bhikkhus.

Pañca catutayo dveko, āpanno vematī sari;

Sabbo saṅgho vematiko, bahū samā ca thokikā.

Five, four, three, two, one; the offender, the one in doubt, the one who remembers; the entire Saṅgha being in doubt; many, an equal number, and a few.

Āvāsikā [M 0.0264] cātuddasa, liṅgasaṃvāsakā ubho;

Gantabbaṃ [T 1.0362] na nisinnāya, chandadāne pavāraṇā chandadānapavāraṇā (ka.).

Residents on the fourteenth; the characteristic and the two kinds of communion; what is to be gone to; not in a seated assembly; Pavāraṇā in the giving of consent.

Savarehi khepitā megho, antarā ca pavāraṇā;

Na icchanti puramhākaṃ, aṭṭhapitā ca bhikkhuno.

Due to tribals, by passing the night, by rain, and by dangers; they do not permit the Pavāraṇā; 'ours first;' and what is not to be postponed for a bhikkhu.

Kimhi vāti katamañca, diṭṭhena sutasaṅkāya;

Codako cuditako ca, thullaccayaṃ vatthu bhaṇḍanaṃ;

Pavāraṇāsaṅgaho ca, anissaro pavārayeti.

'In what case is it postponed?' and 'What is it?'; by what is seen, by what is heard, by suspicion; the accuser and the accused, a grave offense, a clear case, a quarrel; and the support for Pavāraṇā, not having authority, one should perform Pavāraṇā.

Imamhi khandhake vatthūni chacattārīsāti.

In this chapter, there are forty-six topics.

Pavāraṇākkhandhako niṭṭhito.

The Pavāraṇā Chapter is concluded.

5. Cammakkhandhako

5. The Chapter on Leather

147. Soṇakoḷivisavatthu

147. The Story of Soṇa Koḷivisa

242. Tena [T 2.0001][P 1.0179][M 0.0265][V 0.0251] samayena buddho bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Tena kho pana samayena rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro asītiyā gāmasahassesu issariyādhipaccaṃ rajjaṃ kāreti. Tena kho pana samayena campāyaṃ soṇo nāma koḷiviso koḷivīso (sī.) seṭṭhiputto sukhumālo hoti. Tassa pādatalesu lomāni jātāni honti. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro tāni asīti gāmikasahassāni sannipātāpetvā kenacideva karaṇīyena soṇassa koḷivisassa santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – āgacchatu soṇo, icchāmi soṇassa āgatanti. Atha kho soṇassa koḷivisassa mātāpitaro soṇaṃ koḷivisaṃ etadavocuṃ – “rājā te, tāta soṇa, pāde dakkhitukāmo. Mā kho tvaṃ, tāta soṇa, yena rājā tena pāde abhippasāreyyāsi. Rañño purato pallaṅkena nisīda. Nisinnassa te rājā pāde dakkhissatī”ti. Atha kho soṇaṃ koḷivisaṃ sivikāya ānesuṃ. Atha kho soṇo koḷiviso yena rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ seniyaṃ bimbisāraṃ abhivādetvā rañño purato pallaṅkena nisīdi. Addasā [T 2.0002] kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro soṇassa koḷivisassa pādatalesu lomāni jātāni. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro tāni asīti gāmikasahassāni diṭṭhadhammike atthe anusāsitvā uyyojesi – “tumhe khvattha, bhaṇe, mayā diṭṭhadhammike atthe anusāsitā; gacchatha, taṃ bhagavantaṃ payirupāsatha; so no bhagavā samparāyike atthe anusāsissatī”ti.

242. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha on the Vulture Peak mountain. Now at that time King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha was ruling with sovereign power over eighty thousand villages. At that time, in Campā, there was a young man named Soṇa Koḷivisa, the son of a wealthy merchant, who was very delicate. Hairs had grown on the soles of his feet. Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, having assembled those eighty thousand village headmen for some business, sent a messenger to Soṇa Koḷivisa with the words: "Let Soṇa come; I desire Soṇa's arrival." Then Soṇa Koḷivisa’s parents said this to Soṇa Koḷivisa: "Dear Soṇa, the king wishes to see your feet. Do not, dear Soṇa, stretch out your feet toward the king. Sit cross-legged before the king. When you are seated, the king will see your feet." Then Soṇa Koḷivisa approached King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, and having approached, he paid homage to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha and sat cross-legged before the king. King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha saw the hairs that had grown on the soles of Soṇa Koḷivisa’s feet. Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, having instructed those eighty thousand village headmen in matters pertaining to this life, dismissed them, saying: "Sirs, you have been instructed by me in matters pertaining to this life; go, attend upon that Blessed One; that Blessed One will instruct us in matters pertaining to the future life."

Atha kho tāni asīti gāmikasahassāni yena gijjhakūṭo pabbato tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā sāgato bhagavato upaṭṭhāko hoti. Atha kho tāni asīti gāmikasahassāni yenāyasmā sāgato tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ [M 0.0266] sāgataṃ etadavocuṃ [P 1.0180][V 0.0252] – “imāni, bhante, asīti gāmikasahassāni idhūpasaṅkantāni bhagavantaṃ dassanāya; sādhu mayaṃ, bhante, labheyyāma bhagavantaṃ dassanāyā”ti. “Tena hi tumhe āyasmanto muhuttaṃ idheva tāva hotha, yāvāhaṃ bhagavantaṃ paṭivedemī”ti. Atha kho āyasmā sāgato tesaṃ asītiyā gāmikasahassānaṃ purato pekkhamānānaṃ pāṭikāya nimujjitvā bhagavato purato ummujjitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “imāni, bhante, asīti gāmikasahassāni idhūpasaṅkantāni bhagavantaṃ dassanāya; yassa dāni, bhante, bhagavā kālaṃ maññatī”ti. “Tena hi tvaṃ, sāgata, vihārapacchāyāyaṃ āsanaṃ paññapehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā sāgato [T 2.0003] bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā pīṭhaṃ gahetvā bhagavato purato nimujjitvā tesaṃ asītiyā gāmikasahassānaṃ purato pekkhamānānaṃ pāṭikāya ummujjitvā vihārapacchāyāyaṃ āsanaṃ paññapeti. Atha kho bhagavā vihārā nikkhamitvā vihārapacchāyāyaṃ paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho tāni asīti gāmikasahassāni yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Atha kho tāni asīti gāmikasahassāni āyasmantaṃyeva sāgataṃ samannāharanti, no tathā bhagavantaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā tesaṃ asītiyā gāmikasahassānaṃ cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya āyasmantaṃ sāgataṃ āmantesi – “tena hi tvaṃ, sāgata, bhiyyosomattāya uttarimanussadhammaṃ iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ dassehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā sāgato bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā ākāse antalikkhe caṅkamatipi, tiṭṭhatipi, nisīdatipi, seyyampi kappeti, dhūmāyatipi dhūpāyatipi (sī.), padhūpāyatipi (syā.) pajjalatipi, antaradhāyatipi. Atha kho āyasmā sāgato ākāse antalikkhe anekavihitaṃ uttarimanussadhammaṃ iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ dassetvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “satthā me, bhante, bhagavā; sāvakohamasmi. Satthā me, bhante, bhagavā; sāvakohamasmī”ti. Atha kho tāni asīti gāmikasahassāni “acchariyaṃ vata bho! Abbhutaṃ vata bho! Sāvakopi nāma evaṃ mahiddhiko bhavissati, evaṃ mahānubhāvo, aho nūna satthā”ti bhagavantaṃyeva samannāharanti, no [T 2.0004] tathā āyasmantaṃ sāgataṃ.

Then those eighty thousand village headmen approached Vulture Peak Mountain. Now at that time, the Venerable Sāgata was the Blessed One’s attendant. Then those eighty thousand village headmen approached the Venerable Sāgata and said: “Venerable sir, these eighty thousand village headmen have come here to see the Blessed One. It would be good, venerable sir, if we could obtain a sight of the Blessed One.” “Well then, sirs, wait here for a moment while I inform the Blessed One.” Then the Venerable Sāgata, while those eighty thousand village headmen were watching, dived down at the stone slab at the foot of the stairs and emerged before the Blessed One, saying: “Venerable sir, these eighty thousand village headmen have come here to see the Blessed One. Now is the time, venerable sir, as the Blessed One deems fit.” “Well then, Sāgata, prepare a seat in the shade of the monastery.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied the Venerable Sāgata to the Blessed One. Taking a stool, he dived down before the Blessed One and, while those eighty thousand village headmen were watching, emerged at the stone slab at the foot of the stairs and prepared a seat in the shade of the monastery. Then the Blessed One came out of the monastery and sat down on the prepared seat in the shade of the monastery. Then those eighty thousand village headmen approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. But those eighty thousand village headmen paid attention only to the Venerable Sāgata, and not so to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, knowing the thoughts of their minds with his own mind, addressed the Venerable Sāgata: “Well then, Sāgata, display an even greater superhuman miracle of psychic power.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied the Venerable Sāgata to the Blessed One. Rising into the air, he walked, stood, sat, and lay down in the open air, in the sky. He emitted smoke and flames, then vanished. Having displayed various superhuman miracles of psychic power in the open air, in the sky, the Venerable Sāgata bowed his head at the Blessed One’s feet and said: “Venerable sir, the Blessed One is my Teacher; I am a disciple. Venerable sir, the Blessed One is my Teacher; I am a disciple.” Then those eighty thousand village headmen thought: “It is wonderful, sirs! It is amazing, sirs! If a disciple can be of such great psychic power, of such great might, what then of the Teacher!” And they paid attention only to the Blessed One, and not so to the Venerable Sāgata.

Atha [M 0.0267] kho bhagavā tesaṃ asītiyā gāmikasahassānaṃ cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ[P 1.0181], kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ, nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā te bhagavā aññāsi kallacitte, muducitte, vinīvaraṇacitte, udaggacitte, pasannacitte, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā, taṃ pakāsesi – dukkhaṃ, samudayaṃ, nirodhaṃ, maggaṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evamevaṃ tesaṃ asītiyā gāmikasahassānaṃ tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ [V 0.0253] vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – “yaṃkiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma”nti. Te diṭṭhadhammā pattadhammā viditadhammā pariyogāḷhadhammā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante. Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – “cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī”ti, evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Ete mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma. Dhammañca, bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsake no bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupete saraṇaṃ gate”ti.

Then the Blessed One, knowing with his mind the thoughts in the minds of those eighty thousand village headmen, delivered a gradual discourse, that is: talk on generosity, talk on virtue, talk on heaven; he revealed the danger, futility, and defilement of sensual pleasures, and the benefit of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that their minds were receptive, pliant, free from hindrances, uplifted, and serene, then he revealed the teaching exalted by the Buddhas themselves: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth, free from stains, would perfectly absorb dye, even so, in those eighty thousand village headmen, as they sat there, arose the dust-free, stainless vision of the Dhamma: “Whatever is subject to origination is all subject to cessation.” Having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, known the Dhamma, plunged into the Dhamma, having crossed over doubt, dispelled uncertainty, attained to confidence, and being independent of others in the Teacher's Dispensation, they said this to the Blessed One: "Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as if one were to set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or hold up a lamp in the dark, so that those with eyes might see forms, even so has the Dhamma been made clear by the Blessed One in many ways. We go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. May the Blessed One accept us as lay followers who have gone for refuge, from this day forth, for as long as life lasts.”

Soṇassa pabbajjā

The Going Forth of Soṇa

243. Atha kho soṇassa koḷivisassa etadahosi “yathā yathā kho ahaṃ [T 2.0005] bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ; yaṃnūnāhaṃ kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya”nti. Atha kho tāni asīti gāmikasahassāni bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkamisuṃ. Atha kho soṇo koḷiviso acirapakkantesu tesu asītiyā gāmikasahassesu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho soṇo koḷiviso bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yathā yathāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Icchāmahaṃ, bhante, kesamassuṃ ohāretvā [M 0.0268] kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Pabbājetu maṃ, bhante, bhagavā”ti. Alattha kho soṇo koḷiviso bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ. Acirupasampanno ca [P 1.0182] panāyasmā soṇo sītavane viharati. Tassa accāraddhavīriyassa caṅkamato pādā bhijjiṃsu. Caṅkamo lohitena phuṭo hoti, seyyathāpi gavāghātanaṃ. ito paraṃ yāva imassa vatthussa avasānaṃ tāva pāṭho a. ni. 6.55 ādayo Atha kho āyasmato soṇassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “ye [T 2.0006] kho keci bhagavato sāvakā āraddhavīriyā viharanti, ahaṃ tesaṃ aññataro. Atha ca pana me nānupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuccati. Saṃvijjanti kho pana me kule bhogā; sakkā bhoge ca bhuñjituṃ, puññāni ca kātuṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ hīnāyāvattitvā bhoge ca bhuñjeyyaṃ, puññāni ca kareyya”nti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmato soṇassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya – seyyathāpi [V 0.0254] nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya evameva – gijjhakūṭe pabbate antarahito sītavane pāturahosi. Atha kho bhagavā sambahulehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ senāsanacārikaṃ āhiṇḍanto yenāyasmato soṇassa caṅkamo tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho bhagavā āyasmato soṇassa caṅkamaṃ lohitena phuṭaṃ, disvāna bhikkhū āmantesi – “kassa nvāyaṃ, bhikkhave, caṅkamo lohitena phuṭo, seyyathāpi gavāghātana”nti? “Āyasmato, bhante, soṇassa accāraddhavīriyassa caṅkamato pādā bhijjiṃsu. Tassāyaṃ caṅkamo lohitena phuṭo, seyyathāpi gavāghātana”nti.

243. Then this thought occurred to Soṇa of the Koḷivisa clan: “In whatever way I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, it is not easy for one living in a household to practice this holy life that is utterly complete, utterly pure, like a polished conch shell. What if I were to shave off my hair and beard, put on the ochre robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness?” Then, those eighty thousand village headmen, having delighted in and rejoiced at the Blessed One’s words, rose from their seats, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping him to their right, and departed. Then, not long after those eighty thousand village headmen had departed, Soṇa of the Koḷivisa clan approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Soṇa of the Koḷivisa clan said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, in whatever way I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, it is not easy for one living in a household to practice this holy life that is utterly complete, utterly pure, like a polished conch shell. I wish, venerable sir, to shave off my hair and beard, put on the ochre robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness. May the Blessed One, venerable sir, give me the going forth.” Soṇa of the Koḷivisa clan received the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One; he received the higher ordination. Not long after his higher ordination, the Venerable Soṇa was dwelling in the Sītavana. As he was practicing walking meditation with excessively aroused energy, his feet split open. The walking path was covered with blood, just like a cattle slaughter-ground. Then, to the Venerable Soṇa, who had gone to a secluded place and was in solitude, this thought arose in his mind: “Among the Blessed One’s disciples who dwell with aroused energy, I am one of them. And yet, my mind is not liberated from the taints without clinging. There is wealth in my family; it is possible both to enjoy that wealth and to make merit. What if I were to revert to the lower life, enjoy wealth, and make merit?” Then the Blessed One, having known with his own mind the thought in the Venerable Soṇa’s mind—just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm—disappeared from the Gijjhakūṭa mountain and reappeared in the Sītavana. Then the Blessed One, while wandering on a tour of the lodgings with a number of bhikkhus, approached the Venerable Soṇa’s walking path. The Blessed One saw the Venerable Soṇa’s walking path covered with blood, and having seen it, he addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, whose walking path is this, covered with blood, just like a cattle slaughter-ground?” “Venerable sir, as the Venerable Soṇa was practicing walking meditation with excessively aroused energy, his feet split open. This is his walking path, covered with blood, just like a cattle slaughter-ground.”

Atha kho bhagavā yenāyasmato soṇassa vihāro tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Āyasmāpi kho soṇo bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ soṇaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “nanu te, soṇa, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘ye kho keci bhagavato sāvakā āraddhavīriyā viharanti, ahaṃ [T 2.0007] tesaṃ aññataro. Atha ca pana me nānupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuccati. Saṃvijjanti kho pana me kule bhogā; sakkā bhoge ca bhuñjituṃ, puññāni ca kātuṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ hīnāyāvattitvā bhoge ca bhuñjeyyaṃ, puññāni ca kareyya’”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”ti[M 0.0269]. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, soṇa, kusalo tvaṃ pubbe agārikabhūto vīṇāya tantissare”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, soṇa, yadā te vīṇāya tantiyo accāyatā honti, api nu te vīṇā tasmiṃ samaye saravatī vā hoti, kammaññā vā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, soṇa, yadā te vīṇāya tantiyo atisithilā honti, api nu te vīṇā tasmiṃ samaye saravatī vā hoti, kammaññā vā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”ti. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, soṇa, yadā te vīṇāya tantiyo neva accāyatā honti nātisithilā, same guṇe patiṭṭhitā, api nu te vīṇā tasmiṃ samaye saravatī vā hoti, kammaññā vā”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”ti. “Evameva kho, soṇa, accāraddhavīriyaṃ uddhaccāya saṃvattati[P 1.0183], atilīnavīriyaṃ kosajjāya saṃvattati. Tasmātiha tvaṃ, soṇa, vīriyasamataṃ adhiṭṭhaha, indriyānañca samataṃ paṭivijjha, tattha ca nimittaṃ gaṇhāhī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā soṇo bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ soṇaṃ iminā ovādena ovaditvā – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso [T 2.0008] sammiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya evameva – sītavane āyasmato soṇassa sammukhe antarahito gijjhakūṭe pabbate pāturahosi. Atha kho āyasmā soṇo aparena samayena vīriyasamataṃ adhiṭṭhāsi, indriyānañca samataṃ paṭivijjhi, tattha ca nimittaṃ [V 0.0255] aggahesi. Atha kho āyasmā soṇo, eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto, na cirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti – tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti abhiññāsi. Aññataro ca panāyasmā soṇo arahataṃ ahosi.

Then the Blessed One went to Venerable Soṇa’s dwelling. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Venerable Soṇa also paid homage to the Blessed One and sat to one side. The Blessed One said this to Venerable Soṇa, who was sitting to one side: “Soṇa, while you were alone in seclusion, did this thought not occur to you: ‘Among the Blessed One’s disciples who dwell with aroused energy, I am one. Yet my mind is not freed from the taints through non-clinging. There is wealth in my family; it is possible to enjoy wealth and do meritorious deeds. What if I were to revert to the lower life, enjoy wealth, and do meritorious deeds’?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “What do you think, Soṇa? Were you not skilled in playing the lute when you were a householder?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “What do you think, Soṇa? When the strings of your lute were too taut, was your lute in tune and playable at that time?” “No, venerable sir.” “What do you think, Soṇa? When the strings of your lute were too slack, was your lute in tune and playable at that time?” “No, venerable sir.” “What do you think, Soṇa? When the strings of your lute were neither too taut nor too slack but established in even tension, was your lute in tune and playable at that time?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “In the same way, Soṇa, over-aroused energy leads to agitation, and overly slack energy leads to laziness. Therefore, Soṇa, resolve upon a balance of energy, penetrate the evenness of the faculties, and grasp the sign therein.” “Yes, venerable sir,” Venerable Soṇa replied to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, having given this advice to Venerable Soṇa, vanished from Venerable Soṇa’s presence in Sītavana—just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm—and reappeared on Vulture Peak. Then, after some time, Venerable Soṇa resolved upon a balance of energy, penetrated the evenness of the faculties, and grasped the sign therein. Then, dwelling alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute, before long, in this very life, he realized for himself with direct knowledge that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and he dwelt having attained it. He directly knew: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’ And Venerable Soṇa became one of the Arahants.

244. Atha kho āyasmato soṇassa arahattappattassa etadahosi – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhagavato santike aññaṃ byākareyya”nti. Atha kho āyasmā soṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā soṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – yo so, bhante, bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaññojano [M 0.0270] sammadaññā vimutto, so chaṭṭhānāni adhimutto hoti – nekkhammādhimutto hoti, pavivekādhimutto hoti, abyāpajjādhimutto hoti, upādānakkhayādhimutto hoti, taṇhakkhayādhimutto hoti[T 2.0009], asammohādhimutto hoti.

244. Then this thought occurred to Venerable Soṇa, who had attained Arahantship: “What if I were to declare final knowledge in the presence of the Blessed One?” Then Venerable Soṇa went to the Blessed One, and after approaching, paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Venerable Soṇa said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, whichever bhikkhu is an Arahant—one whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own goal, whose fetter of existence is utterly destroyed, and who is liberated by right knowledge—he is intent on six things: he is intent on renunciation, he is intent on seclusion, he is intent on non-affliction, he is intent on the destruction of clinging, he is intent on the destruction of craving, he is intent on non-delusion.

“Siyā kho pana, bhante, idhekaccassa āyasmato evamassa – ‘kevalaṃ saddhāmattakaṃ nūna ayamāyasmā nissāya nekkhammādhimutto’ti, na kho panetaṃ, bhante, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Khīṇāsavo, bhante, bhikkhu, vusitavā, katakaraṇīyo, karaṇīyamattānaṃ asamanupassanto katassa vā paṭicayaṃ khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā nekkhammādhimutto hoti, khayā dosassa vītadosattā nekkhammādhimutto hoti, khayā mohassa vītamohattā nekkhammādhimutto hoti.

“Venerable sir, it might be that some venerable one here might think: ‘Surely this venerable one is intent on renunciation by relying merely on faith.’ But, venerable sir, it should not be regarded thus. Venerable sir, a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, who has done what had to be done, not seeing anything further to be done for himself or any accumulation for what has been done—because of the destruction of lust, being free from lust, he is intent on renunciation; because of the destruction of hatred, being free from hatred, he is intent on renunciation; because of the destruction of delusion, being free from delusion, he is intent on renunciation.”

“Siyā kho pana, bhante, idhekaccassa āyasmato evamassa – ‘lābhasakkārasilokaṃ nūna ayamāyasmā nikāmayamāno [P 1.0184] pavivekādhimutto’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, bhante, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Khīṇāsavo, bhante, bhikkhu, vusitavā, katakaraṇīyo, karaṇīyamattānaṃ karaṇīyaṃ attano (aṅguttarapāḷiyaṃ) asamanupassanto katassa vā paṭicayaṃ, khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā pavivekādhimutto hoti, khayā dosassa vītadosattā pavivekādhimutto hoti, khayā mohassa vītamohattā pavivekādhimutto hoti.

“Venerable sir, it might be that some venerable one here might think: ‘Surely this venerable one, desiring gain, honor, and praise, is intent on seclusion.’ But, venerable sir, it should not be regarded thus. Venerable sir, a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, who has done what had to be done, not seeing anything further to be done for himself or any accumulation for what has been done—because of the destruction of lust, being free from lust, he is intent on seclusion; because of the destruction of hatred, being free from hatred, he is intent on seclusion; because of the destruction of delusion, being free from delusion, he is intent on seclusion.”

“Siyā kho pana, bhante, idhekaccassa āyasmato evamassa – ‘sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ nūna ayamāyasmā sārato paccāgacchanto abyāpajjādhimutto’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, bhante, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Khīṇāsavo, bhante, bhikkhu, vusitavā, katakaraṇīyo, karaṇīyamattānaṃ asamanupassanto [V 0.0256] katassa vā paṭicayaṃ, khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā abyāpajjādhimutto hoti, khayā dosassa vītadosattā abyāpajjādhimutto hoti, khayā mohassa vītamohattā abyāpajjādhimutto [T 2.0010] hoti.

Venerable sir, it may be that here some venerable one might think thus: ‘Surely this venerable one, by regarding adherence to the ascetic practice of an ox as the essence, is resolved on the state of non-affliction.’ But, venerable sir, this should not be regarded thus. Venerable sir, a monk whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, done what was to be done, seeing no further task for himself, nor any accumulation of what has been done, is resolved on the state of non-affliction because of the destruction of lust, due to being without lust; he is resolved on the state of non-affliction because of the destruction of hatred, due to being without hatred; he is resolved on the state of non-affliction because of the destruction of delusion, due to being without delusion.

“Khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā upādānakkhayādhimutto hoti, khayā dosassa vītadosattā upādānakkhayādhimutto hoti, khayā mohassa vītamohattā upādānakkhayādhimutto hoti.

Because of the destruction of lust, due to being without lust, he is resolved on the destruction of clinging; because of the destruction of hatred, due to being without hatred, he is resolved on the destruction of clinging; because of the destruction of delusion, due to being without delusion, he is resolved on the destruction of clinging.

“Khayā [M 0.0271] rāgassa vītarāgattā taṇhakkhayādhimutto hoti, khayā dosassa vītadosattā taṇhakkhayādhimutto hoti, khayā mohassa vītamohattā taṇhakkhayādhimutto hoti.

Because of the destruction of lust, due to being without lust, he is resolved on the destruction of craving; because of the destruction of hatred, due to being without hatred, he is resolved on the destruction of craving; because of the destruction of delusion, due to being without delusion, he is resolved on the destruction of craving.

“Khayā rāgassa vītarāgattā asammohādhimutto hoti, khayā dosassa vītadosattā asammohādhimutto hoti, khayā mohassa vītamohattā asammohādhimutto hoti.

Because of the destruction of lust, due to being without lust, he is resolved on non-delusion; because of the destruction of hatred, due to being without hatred, he is resolved on non-delusion; because of the destruction of delusion, due to being without delusion, he is resolved on non-delusion.

“Evaṃ sammā vimuttacittassa, bhante, bhikkhuno bhusā cepi cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā cakkhussa āpāthaṃ āgacchanti, nevassa cittaṃ pariyādiyanti. Amissīkatamevassa cittaṃ hoti, ṭhitaṃ, āneñjappattaṃ, vayañcassānupassati. Bhusā cepi sotaviññeyyā saddā…pe… ghānaviññeyyā gandhā… jivhāviññeyyā rasā… kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā… manoviññeyyā dhammā manassa āpāthaṃ āgacchanti, nevassa cittaṃ pariyādiyanti; amissīkatamevassa cittaṃ hoti, ṭhitaṃ, āneñjappattaṃ, vayañcassānupassati. Seyyathāpi, bhante, selo pabbato acchiddo asusiro ekagghano, puratthimāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya bhusā vātavuṭṭhi, neva naṃ saṅkampeyya na sampakampeyya na sampavedheyya; pacchimāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya bhusā [T 2.0011] vātavuṭṭhi…pe… uttarāya cepi disāya…pe… dakkhiṇāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya bhusā vātavuṭṭhi, neva naṃ saṅkampeyya na sampakampeyya na sampavedheyya, evameva kho, bhante, evaṃ sammā vimuttacittassa bhikkhuno bhusā cepi cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā cakkhussa āpāthaṃ āgacchanti, nevassa cittaṃ pariyādiyanti; amissīkatamevassa cittaṃ hoti, ṭhitaṃ, āneñjappattaṃ, vayañcassānupassati. Bhusā cepi sotaviññeyyā saddā…pe… ghānaviññeyyā gandhā… jivhāviññeyyā rasā… kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā… manoviññeyyā dhammā manassa āpāthaṃ āgacchanti, nevassa cittaṃ pariyādiyanti; amissīkatamevassa cittaṃ hoti, ṭhitaṃ, āneñjappattaṃ, vayañcassānupassatī”ti.

Venerable sir, for a monk whose mind is thus well-liberated, even if powerful forms cognizable by the eye come into the range of the eye, they do not overwhelm his mind. His mind is indeed unmixed, established, having reached the imperturbable, and he observes its passing away. Even if powerful sounds cognizable by the ear… odors cognizable by the nose… tastes cognizable by the tongue… tangible objects cognizable by the body… or mental phenomena cognizable by the mind come into the range of the mind, they do not overwhelm his mind; his mind is indeed unmixed, established, having reached the imperturbable, and he observes its passing away. Just as, venerable sir, a rocky mountain—without fissures, without hollows, a single solid mass—even if a powerful wind and rain were to come from the eastern direction, it would not be made to shake, tremble, or be agitated; even if from the western direction… from the northern direction… or if a powerful wind and rain were to come from the southern direction, it would not be made to shake, tremble, or be agitated; in the very same way, venerable sir, for a monk whose mind is thus well-liberated, even if powerful forms cognizable by the eye come into the range of the eye, they do not overwhelm his mind; his mind is indeed unmixed, established, having reached the imperturbable, and he observes its passing away. Even if powerful sounds cognizable by the ear… odors cognizable by the nose… tastes cognizable by the tongue… tangible objects cognizable by the body… or mental phenomena cognizable by the mind come into the range of the mind, they do not overwhelm his mind; his mind is indeed unmixed, established, having reached the imperturbable, and he observes its passing away.

Nekkhammaṃ [V 0.0257] adhimuttassa, pavivekañca cetaso;

Abyāpajjādhimuttassa, upādānakkhayassa ca.

For one who is intent on renunciation and on solitude of mind, for one who is intent on non-affliction and on the destruction of clinging.

Taṇhakkhayādhimuttassa[P 1.0185], asammohañca cetaso;

Disvā āyatanuppādaṃ, sammā cittaṃ vimuccati.

For one who is intent on the destruction of craving and on non-delusion of mind, having seen the arising of the sense bases, the mind is rightly liberated.

Tassa [M 0.0272] sammāvimuttassa, santacittassa bhikkhuno;

Katassa paṭicayo natthi, karaṇīyaṃ na vijjati.

For that monk, rightly liberated, with a peaceful mind, there is no accumulation for what has been done; no further duty is to be found.

Selo yathā ekagghano, vātena na samīrati;

Evaṃ rūpā rasā saddā, gandhā phassā ca kevalā.

Just as a solid, single-mass rock is not stirred by the wind, so too forms, tastes, sounds, smells, and touches, all of them.

Iṭṭhā dhammā aniṭṭhā ca, na pavedhenti tādino;

Ṭhitaṃ [T 2.0012] cittaṃ vippamuttaṃ, vayañcassānupassatīti.

Desirable and undesirable objects do not agitate one who is steadfast; his mind is firm and liberated, and he observes its passing away.

Soṇakoḷivisavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story of Soṇa Koḷivisa is concluded.

148. Diguṇādiupāhanapaṭikkhepo

148. The Prohibition of Double-Layered Sandals and So On

245. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, kulaputtā aññaṃ byākaronti, attho ca vutto, attā ca anupanīto. Atha ca, panidhekacce moghapurisā hasamānakaṃ, maññe, aññaṃ byākaronti, te pacchā vighātaṃ āpajjantī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ soṇaṃ āmantesi – “tvaṃ khosi, soṇa, sukhumālo. Anujānāmi te, soṇa, ekapalāsikaṃ upāhana”nti. “Ahaṃ kho, bhante, asītisakaṭavāhe hiraññaṃ ohāya agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito, sattahatthikañca anīkaṃ. Athāhaṃ bhante ekapalāsikaṃ ce upāhanaṃ pariharissāmi, tassa me bhavissanti vattāro ‘soṇo koḷiviso asītisakaṭavāhe hiraññaṃ ohāya agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito, sattahatthikañca anīkaṃ. So dānāyaṃ ekapalāsikāsu upāhanāsu satto’ti. Sace bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghassa anujānissati ahampi paribhuñjissāmi; no ce bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghassa anujānissati, ahampi na paribhuñjissāmī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū [V 0.0258] āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekapalāsikaṃ upāhanaṃ. Na, bhikkhave, diguṇā upāhanā dhāretabbā. Na tiguṇā upāhanā dhāretabbā. Na guṇaṅguṇūpāhanā gaṇaṅgaṇūpāhanā (bahūsu) dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

245. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'Thus, monks, do sons of good family declare final knowledge: the reason is stated, and the self is not brought forward. And yet, some worthless men here, I suppose, declare final knowledge as if it were a laughing matter; they later fall into distress.' Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Soṇa: 'You, Soṇa, are indeed delicate. I allow you, Soṇa, a single-layered sandal.' 'Venerable sir, I went forth from the household life into homelessness having abandoned eighty cart-loads of gold and an army of seven elephants. If I, venerable sir, were to wear a single-layered sandal, there will be those who say of me: “Soṇa Koḷivisa went forth from the household life into homelessness having abandoned eighty cart-loads of gold and an army of seven elephants. Now this man is attached to single-layered sandals.” If the Blessed One allows it for the Saṅgha of monks, I too will use it; if the Blessed One does not allow it for the Saṅgha of monks, I too will not use it.' Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a discourse on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: 'I allow, monks, a single-layered sandal. Monks, a double-layered sandal is not to be worn. A triple-layered sandal is not to be worn. A multi-layered sandal is not to be worn. Whoever should wear one, commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

Diguṇādiupāhanapaṭikkhepo niṭṭhito.

The Prohibition of Double-Layered Sandals and So On is Concluded.

149. Sabbanīlikādipaṭikkhepo

149. The Prohibition of Entirely Blue Sandals and So On

246. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sabbanīlikā upāhanāyo dhārenti…pe… sabbapītikā upāhanāyo dhārenti… sabbalohitikā upāhanāyo dhārenti… sabbamañjiṭṭhikā [T 2.0013] sabbamañjeṭṭhikā (ka.) upāhanāyo dhārenti [M 0.0273]… sabbakaṇhā upāhanāyo dhārenti… sabbamahāraṅgarattā upāhanāyo dhārenti… sabbamahānāmarattā upāhanāyo dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti, “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, sabbanīlikā upāhanā dhāretabbā…pe… na sabbapītikā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na sabbalohitikā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na sabbamañjiṭṭhikā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na sabbakaṇhā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na sabbamahāraṅgarattā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na sabbamahānāmarattā upāhanā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

246. At that time, the monks of the group of six wore sandals that were entirely blue... entirely yellow... entirely red... entirely madder-colored... entirely black... entirely the color of the mahāraṅga insect's back... entirely the color of a withered leaf. People criticized, condemned, and spread disparaging remarks, saying: “They are just like laypeople who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, sandals that are entirely blue are not to be worn... entirely yellow are not to be worn, entirely red are not to be worn, entirely madder-colored are not to be worn, entirely black are not to be worn, entirely the color of the mahāraṅga insect's back are not to be worn, entirely the color of a withered leaf are not to be worn. Whoever should wear them, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā [P 1.0186] bhikkhū nīlakavaddhikā vaṭṭikā (sī.) upāhanāyo dhārenti, pītakavaddhikā upāhanāyo dhārenti, lohitakavaddhikā upāhanāyo dhārenti, mañjiṭṭhikavaddhikā upāhanāyo dhārenti, kaṇhavaddhikā upāhanāyo dhārenti, mahāraṅgarattavaddhikā upāhanāyo dhārenti, mahānāmarattavaddhikā upāhanāyo dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti, “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, nīlakavaddhikā upāhanā dhāretabbā…pe… na pītakavaddhikā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na lohitakavaddhikā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na mañjiṭṭhikavaddhikā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na [T 2.0014] kaṇhavaddhikā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na mahāraṅgarattavaddhikā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na mahānāmarattavaddhikā upāhanā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six wore sandals with blue straps, sandals with yellow straps, sandals with red straps, sandals with madder-colored straps, sandals with black straps, sandals with straps the color of the mahāraṅga insect's back, and sandals with straps the color of a withered leaf. People criticized, condemned, and spread disparaging remarks, saying: “They are just like laypeople who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, sandals with blue straps are not to be worn... sandals with yellow straps are not to be worn, sandals with red straps are not to be worn, sandals with madder-colored straps are not to be worn, sandals with black straps are not to be worn, sandals with straps the color of the mahāraṅga insect's back are not to be worn, and sandals with straps the color of a withered leaf are not to be worn. Whoever should wear them, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū khallakabaddhā …bandhā (ka.) upāhanāyo dhārenti…pe… puṭabaddhā upāhanāyo dhārenti, pāliguṇṭhimā upāhanāyo dhārenti, tūlapuṇṇikā upāhanāyo dhārenti[V 0.0259], tittirapattikā upāhanāyo dhārenti, meṇḍavisāṇavaddhikā upāhanāyo dhārenti, ajavisāṇavaddhikā upāhanāyo dhārenti, vicchikāḷikā upāhanāyo dhārenti, morapiñcha morapiñja (sī. syā.) parisibbitā upāhanāyo dhārenti, citrā upāhanāyo dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti, “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave[M 0.0274], khallakabaddhā upāhanā dhāretabbā…pe… na puṭabaddhā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na pāliguṇṭhimā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na tūlapuṇṇikā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na tittirapattikā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na meṇḍavisāṇavaddhikā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na ajavisāṇavaddhikā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na vicchikāḷikā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na morapiñchaparisibbitā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na citrā upāhanā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks wore footwear with heel-coverings... footwear with instep-coverings, footwear with heel- and instep-coverings, footwear stuffed with cotton, footwear with straps mottled like a partridge's wing, footwear with ram's horn attachments, footwear with goat's horn attachments, footwear with scorpion's tail attachments, footwear sewn with peacock feathers, and decorated footwear. People complained, criticized, and spoke disparagingly, saying, “Just like laypeople who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, footwear with heel-coverings are not to be worn... footwear with instep-coverings are not to be worn, footwear with heel- and instep-coverings are not to be worn, footwear stuffed with cotton are not to be worn, footwear with straps mottled like a partridge's wing are not to be worn, footwear with ram's horn attachments are not to be worn, footwear with goat's horn attachments are not to be worn, footwear with scorpion's tail attachments are not to be worn, footwear sewn with peacock feathers are not to be worn, decorated footwear are not to be worn. Whoever wears them commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sīhacammaparikkhaṭā upāhanāyo dhārenti…pe… byagghacammaparikkhaṭā upāhanāyo [T 2.0015] dhārenti, dīpicammaparikkhaṭā upāhanāyo dhārenti, ajinacammaparikkhaṭā upāhanāyo dhārenti, uddacammaparikkhaṭā upāhanāyo dhārenti, majjāracammaparikkhaṭā upāhanāyo dhārenti, kāḷakacammaparikkhaṭā upāhanāyo dhārenti, luvakacammaparikkhaṭā ulūkacammaparikkhaṭā (yojanā) upāhanāyo dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti, “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, sīhacammaparikkhaṭā upāhanā dhāretabbā…pe… na byagghacammaparikkhaṭā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na dīpicammaparikkhaṭā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na ajinacammaparikkhaṭā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na uddacammaparikkhaṭā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na majjāracammaparikkhaṭā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na kāḷakacammaparikkhaṭā upāhanā dhāretabbā, na luvakacammaparikkhaṭā upāhanā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six wore sandals edged with lion skin... sandals edged with tiger skin, sandals edged with leopard skin, sandals edged with black antelope skin, sandals edged with otter skin, sandals edged with cat skin, sandals edged with black squirrel skin, and sandals edged with flying squirrel skin. People criticized, condemned, and spread disparaging remarks, saying: “They are just like laypeople who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, sandals edged with lion skin are not to be worn... sandals edged with tiger skin are not to be worn, sandals edged with leopard skin are not to be worn, sandals edged with black antelope skin are not to be worn, sandals edged with otter skin are not to be worn, sandals edged with cat skin are not to be worn, sandals edged with black squirrel skin are not to be worn, and sandals edged with flying squirrel skin are not to be worn. Whoever wears them commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Sabbanīlikādipaṭikkhepo niṭṭhito.

The Prohibition of Entirely Blue Sandals and So On is Concluded.

150. Omukkaguṇaṅguṇūpāhanānujānanā

150. The Allowance of Multi-layered Used Footwear

247. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi, aññatarena bhikkhunā pacchāsamaṇena. Atha kho so bhikkhu khañjamāno bhagavantaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhi. Addasā kho aññataro upāsako guṇaṅguṇūpāhanā ārohitvā bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ; disvā upāhanā ārohitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ [V 0.0260] abhivādetvā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ abhivādetvā [T 2.0016] etadavoca – “kissa, bhante, ayyo khañjatī”ti[M 0.0275]? “Pādā me, āvuso, phalitā”ti phālitāti (ka.). “Handa, bhante, upāhanāyo”ti. “Alaṃ[P 1.0187], āvuso, paṭikkhittā bhagavatā guṇaṅguṇūpāhanā”ti. “Gaṇhāhetā, bhikkhu, upāhanāyo”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, omukkaṃ guṇaṅguṇūpāhanaṃ. Na, bhikkhave, navā guṇaṅguṇūpāhanā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

247. Then, in the morning, the Blessed One, having dressed, taking his bowl and robe, entered Rājagaha for alms with a certain bhikkhu as his attendant. Then that bhikkhu, limping, followed closely behind the Blessed One. A certain lay follower, wearing sandals with multiple layers, saw the Blessed One coming from afar. Having seen him, he took off his sandals and approached the Blessed One. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he then approached that bhikkhu. Having approached and paid homage to that bhikkhu, he said this: “Why, venerable sir, is the noble one limping?” “My feet, friend, are cracked.” “Venerable sir, please take these sandals.” “Enough, friend; sandals with multiple layers have been prohibited by the Blessed One.” The Blessed One said: “Bhikkhu, take these sandals.” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the bhikkhus: “I allow, bhikkhus, used sandals with multiple layers. Bhikkhus, new sandals with multiple layers are not to be worn. Whoever should wear them, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Omukkaguṇaṅguṇūpāhanānujānanā niṭṭhitā.

The allowance of used sandals with multiple layers is concluded.

151. Ajjhārāme upāhanapaṭikkhepo

151. The Prohibition of Footwear Within the Monastery

248. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā ajjhokāse anupāhano caṅkamati. Satthā anupāhano caṅkamatīti, therāpi bhikkhū anupāhanā caṅkamanti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhū, satthari anupāhane caṅkamamāne, theresupi bhikkhūsu anupāhanesu caṅkamamānesu, saupāhanā caṅkamanti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū, satthari anupāhane caṅkamamāne, theresupi bhikkhūsu anupāhanesu caṅkamamānesu, saupāhanā caṅkamissantī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū, satthari anupāhane caṅkamamāne, theresupi bhikkhūsu anupāhanesu caṅkamamānesu, saupāhanā caṅkamantī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… “kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā, satthari anupāhane caṅkamamāne, theresupi bhikkhūsu anupāhanesu caṅkamamānesu, saupāhanā caṅkamissanti. Ime hi nāma, bhikkhave[T 2.0017], gihī odātavatthavasanakā abhijīvanikassa sippassa kāraṇā ācariyesu sagāravā sappatissā sabhāgavuttikā viharissanti. Idha kho taṃ, bhikkhave, sobhetha, yaṃ tumhe evaṃ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā ācariyesu ācariyamattesu upajjhāyesu upajjhāyamattesu agāravā appatissā asabhāgavuttikā sagāravā saggatissā sabhāgavuttikā (ka.) vihareyyātha. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, ācariyesu ācariyamattesu upajjhāyesu upajjhāyamattesu anupāhanesu caṅkamamānesu saupāhanena caṅkamitabbaṃ. Yo caṅkameyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa[V 0.0261]. Na ca, bhikkhave, ajjhārāme upāhanā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

248. At that time the Blessed One was walking up and down in the open air without footwear. Thinking, “The Teacher is walking without footwear,” the elder bhikkhus also walked without footwear. The bhikkhus of the Group of Six, while the Teacher was walking without footwear and the elder bhikkhus were walking without footwear, walked up and down wearing footwear. Those bhikkhus who were modest… grumbled, criticized, and spread it about, “How can the bhikkhus of the Group of Six walk up and down wearing footwear while the Teacher is walking without footwear and the elder bhikkhus are walking without footwear?” Then those bhikkhus reported the matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, bhikkhus, that the bhikkhus of the Group of Six walk up and down wearing footwear while the Teacher is walking without footwear and the elder bhikkhus are walking without footwear?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How, bhikkhus, can these foolish men walk up and down wearing footwear while the Teacher is walking without footwear and the elder bhikkhus are walking without footwear? For, bhikkhus, even these householders dressed in white, for the sake of a craft that is their livelihood, live showing respect, deference, and appropriate conduct towards their teachers. How would it be fitting, bhikkhus, that you, having gone forth in this well-expounded Dhamma and Discipline, should live without respect, without deference, and without appropriate conduct towards teachers, those like teachers, preceptors, and those like preceptors? This, bhikkhus, is not for the confidence of the uninspired… Having rebuked them… having given a Dhamma talk, he addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, one should not walk up and down wearing footwear when one’s teachers, those like teachers, preceptors, or those like preceptors, are walking without footwear. Whoever does so, commits an offense of wrong conduct. And, bhikkhus, footwear should not be worn within the monastery. Whoever wears it, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

249. Tena [M 0.0276] kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno pādakhilābādho hoti. Taṃ bhikkhū pariggahetvā uccārampi passāvampi nikkhāmenti. Addasā kho bhagavā senāsanacārikaṃ āhiṇḍanto te bhikkhū taṃ bhikkhuṃ pariggahetvā uccārampi [P 1.0188] passāvampi nikkhāmente, disvāna yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “kiṃ imassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ābādho”ti? “Imassa, bhante, āyasmato pādakhilābādho; imaṃ mayaṃ pariggahetvā uccārampi passāvampi nikkhāmemā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ [T 2.0018] katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yassa pādā vā dukkhā, pādā vā phalitā, pādakhilo vā ābādho pādakhilābādho vā (syā.) upāhanaṃ dhāretu”nti.

249. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu had an ailment of a fleshy growth like a stake on the sole of his foot. The bhikkhus carried him out to defecate and urinate. The Blessed One, while wandering on a tour of the lodgings, saw those bhikkhus carrying that bhikkhu out to defecate and urinate. Having seen them, he approached those bhikkhus. Having approached, he said this to those bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, what is this bhikkhu’s ailment?” “Venerable sir, this venerable one has an ailment of a fleshy growth like a stake on the sole of his foot. We carry him out to defecate and urinate.” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: “I allow, bhikkhus, one whose feet are painful, or whose feet are cracked, or who has an ailment of a fleshy growth like a stake on the sole of his foot, to wear footwear.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū adhotehi pādehi mañcampi pīṭhampi abhiruhanti; cīvarampi senāsanampi dussati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ‘idāni mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā abhiruhissāmī”ti upāhanaṃ dhāretunti.

Now at that time, bhikkhus were climbing onto beds and chairs with unwashed feet, and the robes and bedding were being soiled. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, bhikkhus, the wearing of footwear with the thought, ‘Now I will climb onto a bed or a chair.’”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū rattiyā uposathaggampi sannisajjampi gacchantā andhakāre khāṇumpi kaṇṭakampi akkamanti; pādā dukkhā honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ajjhārāme upāhanaṃ dhāretuṃ, ukkaṃ, padīpaṃ, kattaradaṇḍanti.

Now at that time, bhikkhus, while going in the darkness of the night to the Uposatha hall or to an assembly, stepped on stumps and thorns, and their feet became painful. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, bhikkhus, the wearing of footwear within the monastery, and the carrying of a torch, a lamp, and a walking stick.”

Ajjhārāme upāhanapaṭikkhepo niṭṭhito.

The Prohibition of Footwear Within the Monastery is concluded.

152. Kaṭṭhapādukādipaṭikkhepo

152. The Prohibition of Wooden Sandals and So On

250. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya kaṭṭhapādukāyo abhiruhitvā ajjhokāse caṅkamanti, uccāsaddā mahāsaddā khaṭakhaṭasaddā, anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ kathentā, seyyathidaṃ imā tiracchānakathāyo pāci. 508; dī. ni. 1.7; ma. ni. 2.223; saṃ. ni. 5.1080; a. ni. 10.69 ādayo – rājakathaṃ, corakathaṃ, mahāmattakathaṃ, senākathaṃ, bhayakathaṃ, yuddhakathaṃ, annakathaṃ, pānakathaṃ, vatthakathaṃ, sayanakathaṃ, mālākathaṃ, gandhakathaṃ, ñātikathaṃ, yānakathaṃ, gāmakathaṃ, nigamakathaṃ, nagarakathaṃ, janapadakathaṃ, itthikathaṃ itthikathaṃ purisakathaṃ (ka.), sūrakathaṃ, visikhākathaṃ, kumbhaṭṭhānakathaṃ[V 0.0262], pubbapetakathaṃ, nānattakathaṃ, lokakkhāyikaṃ, samuddakkhāyikaṃ, itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā; kīṭakampi akkamitvā mārenti, bhikkhūpi samādhimhā cāventi. Ye [M 0.0277] te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū rattiyā [T 2.0019] paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya kaṭṭhapādukāyo abhiruhitvā ajjhokāse caṅkamissanti, uccāsaddā mahāsaddā khaṭakhaṭasaddā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ kathentā, seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ, corakathaṃ…pe… itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā, kīṭakampi akkamitvā māressanti, bhikkhūpi samādhimhā cāvessantī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya kaṭṭhapādukāyo abhiruhitvā ajjhokāse caṅkamanti, uccāsaddā mahāsaddā khaṭakhaṭasaddā, anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ kathentā, seyyathidaṃ, – rājakathaṃ, corakathaṃ…pe… itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā, kīṭakampi akkamitvā mārenti, bhikkhūpi samādhimhā [P 1.0189] cāventī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, kaṭṭhapādukā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

250. Now at that time the monks of the group of six, having risen at dawn, put on wooden sandals and walked up and down in the open, making loud noises, great noises, clattering noises, and engaging in various kinds of worldly talk, such as: talk about kings, talk about thieves, talk about chief ministers, talk about armies, talk about fears, talk about battles, talk about food, talk about drink, talk about clothing, talk about bedding, talk about garlands, talk about perfumes, talk about relatives, talk about vehicles, talk about villages, talk about market towns, talk about cities, talk about countries, talk about women, talk about heroes, talk about streets, talk about watering places, talk about those long dead, miscellaneous talk, speculation about the world, speculation about the ocean, and talk about becoming and non-becoming. They also stepped on and killed insects, and they caused monks to fall away from their concentration. Those monks who were of few wishes… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can the monks of the group of six rise at dawn, put on wooden sandals, and walk up and down in the open, making loud noises, great noises, clattering noises, and engaging in various kinds of worldly talk, such as: talk about kings, talk about thieves… talk about becoming and non-becoming? How can they step on and kill insects, and cause monks to fall away from their concentration?” Then those monks told this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, monks, that the monks of the group of six rise at dawn, put on wooden sandals, and walk up and down in the open, making loud noises, great noises, clattering noises, and engaging in various kinds of worldly talk, such as: talk about kings, talk about thieves… talk about becoming and non-becoming; and that they also step on and kill insects, and cause monks to fall away from their concentration?” “It is true, Blessed One.” … Having rebuked them and given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, wooden sandals are not to be worn. Whoever should wear them commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Atha kho bhagavā rājagahe yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena bārāṇasī tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena bārāṇasī tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ viharati isipatane migadāye. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū – bhagavatā kaṭṭhapādukā paṭikkhittāti – tālataruṇe chedāpetvā tālapattapādukāyo dhārenti; tāni tālataruṇāni chinnāni milāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā [T 2.0020] tālataruṇe chedāpetvā tālapattapādukāyo dhāressanti; tāni tālataruṇāni chinnāni milāyanti; ekindriyaṃ samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jīvaṃ viheṭhentī”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū tālataruṇe chedāpetvā tālapattapādukāyo dhārenti; tāni tālataruṇāni chinnāni milāyantī”ti? Saccaṃ bhagavāti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā tālataruṇe chedāpetvā tālapattapādukāyo dhāressanti; tāni tālataruṇāni chinnāni milāyanti. Jīvasaññino hi, bhikkhave, manussā rukkhasmiṃ. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ [M 0.0278] vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, tālapattapādukā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

Then the Blessed One, having stayed in Rājagaha for as long as he wished, set out on a journey toward Bārāṇasī. Traveling in stages, he eventually arrived at Bārāṇasī. There the Blessed One stayed in the Deer Park at Isipatana near Bārāṇasī. Now at that time, the monks of the group of six, thinking, “Wooden sandals have been prohibited by the Blessed One,” had young palm trees cut down and wore sandals made of palm leaves. Those young palm trees, having been cut, withered. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can these Sakyan ascetics have young palm trees cut down and wear sandals made of palm leaves? Those young palm trees, once cut, wither. These Sakyan ascetics are harming life with a single faculty!” The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Then those monks told this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, monks, that the monks of the group of six had young palm trees cut down and wear sandals made of palm leaves, and that those young palm trees, once cut, wither?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How, monks, can those foolish men have young palm trees cut down and wear sandals made of palm leaves? Those young palm trees, once cut, wither. Monks, people perceive trees as having life. This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident…” Having rebuked them and given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, sandals made of palm leaves are not to be worn. Whoever should wear them commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena [V 0.0263] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ‘bhagavatā tālapattapādukā paṭikkhittā’ti veḷutaruṇe chedāpetvā veḷupattapādukāyo dhārenti. Tāni veḷutaruṇāni chinnāni milāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā veḷutaruṇe chedāpetvā veḷupattapādukāyo dhāressanti. Tāni veḷutaruṇāni chinnāni milāyanti. Ekindriyaṃ samaṇā sakyaputtiyā jīvaṃ viheṭhentī”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ [T 2.0021] vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… jīvasaññino hi, bhikkhave, manussā rukkhasmiṃ…pe… na, bhikkhave, veḷupattapādukā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Now at that time the monks of the group of six, thinking, “Sandals made of palm leaves have been prohibited by the Blessed One,” had young bamboo cut down and wore sandals made of bamboo strips. Those young bamboo, having been cut, withered. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can these Sakyan ascetics have young bamboo cut down and wear sandals made of bamboo strips? Those young bamboo, once cut, wither. These Sakyan ascetics are harming life with a single faculty!” The monks heard those people complaining, criticizing, and spreading it about. Then those monks told this matter to the Blessed One… “Monks, people perceive trees as having life… Monks, sandals made of bamboo strips are not to be worn. Whoever should wear them commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

251. Atha kho bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena bhaddiyaṃ tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena bhaddiyaṃ tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā bhaddiye viharati jātiyā vane. Tena kho [P 1.0190] pana samayena bhaddiyā bhikkhū anekavihitaṃ pādukamaṇḍanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti, tiṇapādukaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, muñjapādukaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, pabbajapādukaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, hintālapādukaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, kamalapādukaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, kambalapādukaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi, riñcanti uddesaṃ paripucchaṃ adhisīlaṃ adhicittaṃ adhipaññaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhaddiyā bhikkhū anekavihitaṃ pādukamaṇḍanānuyogamanuyuttā viharissanti, tiṇapādukaṃ karissantipi kārāpessantipi, muñjapādukaṃ karissantipi kārāpessantipi, pabbajapādukaṃ karissantipi kārāpessantipi, hintālapādukaṃ karissantipi kārāpessantipi, kamalapādukaṃ karissantipi kārāpessantipi, kambalapādukaṃ karissantipi kārāpessantipi, riñcissanti uddesaṃ paripucchaṃ adhisīlaṃ adhicittaṃ adhipañña”nti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato [T 2.0022] etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhaddiyā bhikkhū anekavihitaṃ pādukamaṇḍanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti, tiṇapādukaṃ karontipi kārāpentipi…pe… riñcanti uddesaṃ paripucchaṃ adhisīlaṃ adhicittaṃ [M 0.0279] adhipañña”nti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… “kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā anekavihitaṃ pādukamaṇḍanānuyogamanuyuttā viharissanti, tiṇapādukaṃ karissantipi kārāpessantipi…pe… riñcissanti uddesaṃ paripucchaṃ adhisīlaṃ adhicittaṃ adhipaññaṃ. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, tiṇapādukā dhāretabbā, na muñjapādukā dhāretabbā, na pabbajapādukā dhāretabbā, na hintālapādukā dhāretabbā, na kamalapādukā dhāretabbā[V 0.0264], na kambalapādukā dhāretabbā, na sovaṇṇamayā pādukā dhāretabbā, na rūpiyamayā pādukā dhāretabbā, na maṇimayā pādukā dhāretabbā, na veḷuriyamayā pādukā dhāretabbā, na [T 2.0023] phalikamayā pādukā dhāretabbā, na kaṃsamayā pādukā dhāretabbā, na kācamayā pādukā dhāretabbā, na tipumayā pādukā dhāretabbā, na sīsamayā pādukā dhāretabbā, na tambalohamayā pādukā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na ca, bhikkhave, kāci saṅkamaniyā pādukā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tisso pādukā dhuvaṭṭhāniyā asaṅkamaniyāyo – vaccapādukaṃ, passāvapādukaṃ, ācamanapāduka”nti.

251. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Bārāṇasī for as long as he wished, set out on a journey to Bhaddiya. Wandering in due course, he arrived at Bhaddiya. There, the Blessed One stayed in Bhaddiya at the Jātiyā Grove. Now at that time, the monks of Bhaddiya were living devoted to the practice of decorating footwear in many various ways. They would make for themselves and have others make sandals of grass, sandals of muñja grass, sandals of pabbaja grass, sandals of hintāla palm leaves, sandals of kamala grass, and woolen sandals. They neglected recitation, questioning, the higher virtue, the higher mind, and the higher wisdom. Those monks who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How can the monks of Bhaddiya live devoted to the practice of decorating footwear in many various ways? How can they make for themselves and have others make sandals of grass, sandals of muñja grass, sandals of pabbaja grass, sandals of hintāla palm leaves, sandals of kamala grass, and woolen sandals, while neglecting recitation, questioning, the higher virtue, the higher mind, and the higher wisdom?” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, it is said, monks, that the monks of Bhaddiya are living devoted to the practice of decorating footwear in many various ways, making for themselves and having others make sandals of grass… and that they neglect recitation, questioning, the higher virtue, the higher mind, and the higher wisdom?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… “How, monks, can these foolish men live devoted to the practice of decorating footwear in many various ways? How can they make for themselves and have others make sandals of grass… while neglecting recitation, questioning, the higher virtue, the higher mind, and the higher wisdom? This, monks, does not lead to the inspiring of confidence in the uninspired….” Having rebuked them… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks, saying: “Monks, sandals of grass should not be worn. Sandals of muñja grass should not be worn. Sandals of pabbaja grass should not be worn. Sandals of hintāla palm leaves should not be worn. Sandals of kamala grass should not be worn. Woolen sandals should not be worn. Sandals made of gold should not be worn. Sandals made of silver should not be worn. Sandals made of jewels should not be worn. Sandals made of beryl should not be worn. Sandals made of crystal should not be worn. Sandals made of bronze should not be worn. Sandals made of glass should not be worn. Sandals made of tin should not be worn. Sandals made of lead should not be worn. Sandals made of copper should not be worn. Whoever should wear them commits an offense of wrong-doing. And, monks, no moveable sandals of any kind should be worn. Whoever should wear them commits an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, three kinds of fixed, immoveable sandals: sandals for the latrine, sandals for the urinal, and sandals for the place of rinsing.”

252. Atha kho bhagavā bhaddiye yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena sāvatthi tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena sāvatthi tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū [P 1.0191] aciravatiyā nadiyā gāvīnaṃ tarantīnaṃ visāṇesupi gaṇhanti, kaṇṇesupi gaṇhanti, gīvāyapi gaṇhanti, cheppāpi gaṇhanti, piṭṭhimpi abhiruhanti, rattacittāpi aṅgajātaṃ chupanti, vacchatarimpi ogāhetvā mārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā gāvīnaṃ tarantīnaṃ visāṇesupi gahessanti…pe… seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ [T 2.0024] vipācentānaṃ. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave,…pe… saccaṃ bhagavāti…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, gāvīnaṃ visāṇesu gahetabbaṃ, na kaṇṇesu gahetabbaṃ, na gīvāya gahetabbaṃ, na cheppāya gahetabbaṃ, na piṭṭhi abhiruhitabbā[M 0.0280]. Yo abhiruheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na ca, bhikkhave, rattacittena aṅgajātaṃ chupitabbaṃ. Yo chupeyya, āpatti thullaccayassa. Na vacchatarī māretabbā. Yo māreyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.

252. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Bhaddiya as long as he pleased, set out on a journey to Sāvatthī. Traveling in stages, he arrived at Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One stayed in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. At that time the group-of-six monks, while cows were crossing the Aciravatī River, would grab them by their horns, ears, necks, or tails, or climb onto their backs, and with lustful minds touch their genitals. They even submerged and killed a young bovine. People complained, criticized, and spread disparaging remarks, saying, “How can these Sakyan ascetics grab cows by their horns... just like householders indulging in sensual pleasures?” The monks heard these people complaining, criticizing, and spreading disparaging remarks. Then those monks reported the matter to the Blessed One... “Is it true, monks...?” “It is true, Blessed One.”... After rebuking them... and having given a Dhamma talk, he addressed the monks: “Monks, one should not grab cows by their horns, nor by their ears, nor by their necks, nor by their tails. One should not climb onto their backs. Whoever should climb on commits an offense of wrong-doing. And, monks, one should not touch the genitals with a lustful mind. Whoever should touch them commits a serious offense. A young bovine should not be killed. Whoever should kill one is to be dealt with according to the Dhamma.”

Kaṭṭhapādukādipaṭikkhepo niṭṭhito.

The Prohibition Concerning Wooden Sandals, etc., is concluded.

153. Yānādipaṭikkhepo

153. Prohibition Concerning Vehicles, etc.

253. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū yānena yāyanti, itthiyuttenapi purisantarena, purisayuttenapi itthantarena. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “seyyathāpi gaṅgāmahiyāyā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, yānena yāyitabbaṃ[V 0.0265]. Yo yāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu kosalesu janapade sāvatthiṃ gacchanto bhagavantaṃ dassanāya antarāmagge gilāno hoti. Atha kho so bhikkhu maggā okkamma aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisīdi. Manussā taṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā etadavocuṃ – “kahaṃ, bhante, ayyo gamissatī”ti? “Sāvatthiṃ kho ahaṃ, āvuso, gamissāmi bhagavantaṃ dassanāyā”ti. “Ehi, bhante, gamissāmā”ti. “Nāhaṃ, āvuso, sakkomi, gilānomhī”ti. “Ehi, bhante, yānaṃ abhiruhā”ti. “Alaṃ, āvuso, paṭikkhittaṃ bhagavatā yāna”nti kukkuccāyanto yānaṃ nābhiruhi. Atha kho so bhikkhu sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ [T 2.0025] etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānassa yānanti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “itthiyuttaṃ nu kho purisayuttaṃ nu kho”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi[P 1.0192], bhikkhave, purisayuttaṃ hatthavaṭṭakanti.

253. At that time, the group-of-six monks were traveling by vehicle: sometimes one yoked with female animals and driven by a man, and sometimes one yoked with male animals and driven by a woman. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “Just like those who sport on the Ganges and Mahi rivers!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, one should not travel by vehicle. Whoever should travel commits an offense of wrong conduct.” At that time, a certain monk in the Kosala country, while going to Sāvatthī to see the Blessed One, became ill on the way. Then that monk, having left the road, sat down at the foot of a certain tree. People, seeing that monk, said this: “Venerable sir, where will the noble one go?” “Friends, I am going to Sāvatthī to see the Blessed One.” “Come, venerable sir, let us go.” “Friends, I am not able, I am ill.” “Come, venerable sir, get into the vehicle.” “Enough, friends, a vehicle has been rejected by the Blessed One.” Being scrupulous, he did not get into the vehicle. Then that monk, having gone to Sāvatthī, told this matter to the monks. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a vehicle for one who is ill.” Then this occurred to the monks: “Is it one yoked with a female animal or one yoked with a male animal?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a vehicle yoked with a male animal and a hand-pushed cart.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno yānugghātena bāḷhataraṃ aphāsu ahosi. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sivikaṃ pāṭaṅkinti.

At that time, a certain monk experienced a very severe discomfort due to the jolting of the vehicle. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a palanquin and a litter.”

Yānādipaṭikkhepo niṭṭhito.

The section on the prohibition of vehicles and so forth is concluded.

154. Uccāsayanamahāsayanapaṭikkhepo

154. The Prohibition of High and Grand Beds

254. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāsayanamahāsayanāni dhārenti, seyyathidaṃ – āsandiṃ, pallaṅkaṃ, gonakaṃ, cittakaṃ, paṭikaṃ, paṭalikaṃ, tūlikaṃ, vikatikaṃ, uddhalomiṃ undalomiṃ (ka.), uddalomiṃ (ka.), ekantalomiṃ, kaṭṭissaṃ, koseyyaṃ[M 0.0281], kuttakaṃ, hatthattharaṃ, assattharaṃ, rathattharaṃ, ajinapaveṇiṃ, kadalimigapavarapaccattharaṇaṃ, sauttaracchadaṃ, ubhatolohitakūpadhānanti. Manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.
