Na, bhikkhave, uccāsayanamahāsayanāni dhāretabbāni, seyyathidaṃ – āsandi, pallaṅko, gonako, cittako, paṭikā, paṭalikā, tūlikā, vikatikā, uddhalomi, ekantalomi, kaṭṭissaṃ, koseyyaṃ, kuttakaṃ, hatthattharaṃ, assattharaṃ, rathattharaṃ, ajinapaveṇi, kadalimigapavarapaccattharaṇaṃ, sauttaracchadaṃ, ubhatolohitakūpadhānaṃ. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

254. Now at that time, the monks of the group of six used high and grand beds. What are these? A couch with legs exceeding the standard measure, a couch with animal figures on the legs, a large rug with long fleece, a woolen coverlet variegated with stitching, a white woolen coverlet, a woolen coverlet with a solid floral design, a coverlet filled with cotton, a woolen coverlet variegated with figures of lions and tigers, a woolen coverlet with fleece on one side, a woolen coverlet with fleece on both sides, a bedspread made of kaṭṭissa silk sewn with jewels and gold thread, a bedspread woven with silk and sewn with jewels and gold thread, a woolen coverlet on which sixteen dancers could dance, an elephant saddle-cloth, a horse saddle-cloth, a chariot covering, a coverlet made by sewing together skins of black antelope to the size of a couch, a superior bedspread made from the skin of the kadali deer, a couch with a red canopy above, and a couch with red pillows at both ends. People, wandering on a tour of the monasteries, saw this and complained, scorned, and spread the word disparagingly, saying, “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, high and grand beds are not to be used. What are these? A couch with legs exceeding the standard measure, a couch with animal figures on the legs, a large rug with long fleece, a woolen coverlet variegated with stitching, a white woolen coverlet, a woolen coverlet with a solid floral design, a coverlet filled with cotton, a woolen coverlet variegated with figures of lions and tigers, a woolen coverlet with fleece on one side, a woolen coverlet with fleece on both sides, a bedspread made of kaṭṭissa silk sewn with jewels and gold thread, a bedspread woven with silk and sewn with jewels and gold thread, a woolen coverlet on which sixteen dancers could dance, an elephant saddle-cloth, a horse saddle-cloth, a chariot covering, a coverlet made by sewing together skins of black antelope to the size of a couch, a superior bedspread made from the skin of the kadali deer, a couch with a red canopy above, and a couch with red pillows at both ends. Whoever should use them commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Uccāsayanamahāsayanapaṭikkhepo niṭṭhito.

The Prohibition of High and Grand Beds is concluded.

155. Sabbacammapaṭikkhepo

155. The Prohibition of All Hides

255. Tena [T 2.0026][V 0.0266] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū – bhagavatā uccāsayanamahāsayanāni paṭikkhittānīti – mahācammāni dhārenti, sīhacammaṃ byagghacammaṃ dīpicammaṃ. Tāni mañcappamāṇenapi chinnāni honti, pīṭhappamāṇenapi chinnāni honti, antopi mañce paññattāni honti, bahipi mañce paññattāni honti, antopi pīṭhe paññattāni honti, bahipi pīṭhe paññattāni honti. Manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, mahācammāni dhāretabbāni, sīhacammaṃ byagghacammaṃ dīpicammaṃ. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

255. At that time the monks of the group of six—thinking, “High and luxurious beds have been rejected by the Blessed One”—used large hides: lion hide, tiger hide, and leopard hide. They were cut to the size of a bed, and cut to the size of a stool; they were spread inside the bed, and outside the bed; they were spread inside the stool, and outside the stool. People wandering on a tour of the monasteries saw this and complained, criticized, and spread the word disparagingly: “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, large hides—lion hide, tiger hide, and leopard hide—are not to be used. Whoever should use one commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū – bhagavatā mahācammāni paṭikkhittānīti – gocammāni dhārenti. Tāni mañcappamāṇenapi chinnāni honti, pīṭhappamāṇenapi chinnāni honti, antopi mañce paññattāni honti, bahipi mañce paññattāni honti, antopi pīṭhe paññattāni honti, bahipi pīṭhe paññattāni honti. Aññataropi pāpabhikkhu aññatarassa pāpupāsakassa kulūpako hoti. Atha kho so pāpabhikkhu pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena tassa pāpupāsakassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho so [P 1.0193] pāpupāsako yena so pāpabhikkhu tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā taṃ pāpabhikkhuṃ abhivādetvā [T 2.0027] ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Tena kho pana samayena tassa pāpupāsakassa vacchako hoti taruṇako abhirūpo dassanīyo [M 0.0282] pāsādiko citro, seyyathāpi dīpicchāpo. Atha kho so pāpabhikkhu taṃ vacchakaṃ sakkaccaṃ upanijjhāyati. Atha kho so pāpupāsako taṃ pāpabhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “kissa, bhante, ayyo imaṃ vacchakaṃ sakkaccaṃ upanijjhāyatī”ti? “Attho me, āvuso, imassa vacchakassa cammenā”ti. Atha kho so pāpupāsako taṃ vacchakaṃ vadhitvā cammaṃ vidhunitvā tassa pāpabhikkhuno pādāsi. Atha kho so pāpabhikkhu taṃ cammaṃ saṅghāṭiyā paṭicchādetvā agamāsi. Atha kho sā gāvī vacchagiddhinī taṃ pāpabhikkhuṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhi. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “kissa tyāyaṃ, āvuso, gāvī piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhī”ti? “Ahampi kho, āvuso, na jānāmi kena kenaci (ka.) myāyaṃ gāvī piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhī”ti. Tena kho pana samayena tassa pāpabhikkhuno saṅghāṭi lohitena makkhitā hoti. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “ayaṃ pana te, āvuso, saṅghāṭi kiṃ katā”ti? Atha kho so pāpabhikkhu bhikkhūnaṃ [V 0.0267] etamatthaṃ ārocesi. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, āvuso, pāṇātipāte samādapesī”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhu pāṇātipāte samādapessati, nanu bhagavatā anekapariyāyena pāṇātipāto garahito, pāṇātipātā veramaṇī pasatthā”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

At that time, the group-of-six monks—thinking, “The Blessed One has prohibited large hides”—used cowhides. These were cut to the size of beds and cut to the size of stools; they were spread inside beds and outside beds; they were spread inside stools and outside stools. Now, a certain wicked monk was a regular visitor at the house of a certain wicked lay follower. Then that wicked monk, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, went to the dwelling of that wicked lay follower. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then that wicked lay follower approached that wicked monk, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. At that time, that wicked lay follower had a young calf that was beautiful, lovely to see, pleasing, and spotted, just like a leopard cub. Then that wicked monk carefully observed that calf. Then that wicked lay follower said to that wicked monk, “Venerable sir, why is the noble one carefully observing this calf?” “Friend, I have need of this calf’s hide.” Then that wicked lay follower killed that calf, skinned it, and gave the hide to that wicked monk. Then that wicked monk, having concealed the hide with his outer robe, departed. Then that cow, longing for her calf, followed that wicked monk from behind. The monks said, “Friend, why is this cow following you from behind?” “Friends, I too do not know why this cow is following me from behind.” At that time, that wicked monk’s outer robe was stained with blood. The monks said, “But friend, what has been done to your outer robe?” Then that wicked monk informed the monks of this matter. “But friend, did you instigate the taking of life?” “Yes, friends.” Those monks who were of few wishes complained, condemned, and spread it about: “How indeed could a monk instigate the taking of life? Has not the taking of life been condemned by the Blessed One in many ways, and has not abstaining from taking life been praised?” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Atha [T 2.0028] kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā taṃ pāpabhikkhuṃ paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, bhikkhu, pāṇātipāte samādapesī”ti? Saccaṃ bhagavāti…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, pāṇātipāte samādapessasi, nanu mayā, moghapurisa, anekapariyāyena pāṇātipāto garahito, pāṇātipātā veramaṇī pasatthā. Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, pāṇātipāte samādapetabbaṃ. Yo samādapeyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo. Na, bhikkhave, gocammaṃ dhāretabbaṃ. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na ca, bhikkhave, kiñci cammaṃ dhāretabbaṃ. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

Then the Blessed One, on account of this incident, on this occasion, had the Sangha of bhikkhus convened and questioned that wicked bhikkhu: “Is it true, bhikkhu, that you incited the taking of life?” “It is true, Blessed One.” … “How could you, foolish man, incite the taking of life? Have I not, foolish man, in many ways criticized the taking of life and praised abstaining from the taking of life? This, foolish man, is not for the confidence of those who are not yet confident…” Having rebuked him and given a Dhamma talk, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, one should not incite the taking of life. Whoever does so should be dealt with according to the Dhamma. Bhikkhus, a cowhide should not be used. Whoever uses one commits an offense of wrong-doing. And, bhikkhus, no hide whatsoever should be used. Whoever uses one commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Sabbacammapaṭikkhepo niṭṭhito.

The section on the prohibition of all hides is concluded.

156. Gihivikatānuññātādi

156. Allowances for Items Prepared by Householders, etc.

256. Tena [P 1.0194][M 0.0283] kho pana samayena manussānaṃ mañcampi pīṭhampi cammonaddhāni honti, cammavinaddhāni. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nābhinisīdanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gihivikataṃ abhinisīdituṃ, na tveva abhinipajjitunti.

256. At that time, people had beds and stools that were upholstered with hide and bound with hide. The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, would not sit on them. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow you to sit on what is prepared by householders, but I do not allow you to lie down on it.”

Tena kho pana samayena vihārā cammavaddhehi ogumphiyanti ogumbhiyanti (ka.). Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā nābhinisīdanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bandhanamattaṃ abhinisīditunti.

At that time, monasteries were bound with leather straps. The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, would not lean against them. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow you to lean against what is merely a binding.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū saupāhanā gāmaṃ pavisanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[V 0.0268]. Na, bhikkhave, saupāhanena [T 2.0029] gāmo pavisitabbo. Yo paviseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, the group-of-six bhikkhus were entering the village wearing footwear. People complained, condemned, and spread it about, saying: “Just like householders enjoying sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, a village should not be entered while wearing footwear. Whoever enters commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu gilāno hoti, na sakkoti vinā upāhanena gāmaṃ pavisituṃ. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānena bhikkhunā saupāhanena gāmaṃ pavisitunti.

At that time, a certain bhikkhu was sick; he was not able to enter the village without footwear. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Bhikkhus, I allow a sick bhikkhu to enter the village with footwear.”

Gihivikatānuññātādi niṭṭhitā.

The section on Allowances for Items Prepared by Householders, etc., is concluded.

157. Soṇakuṭikaṇṇavatthu

157. The Story of Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa.

257. udā. 46 sokasuttena saṃsanditvā passitabbaṃ Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā mahākaccāno avantīsu viharati kuraraghare kururaghare (ka.) papatake papāte (sī. syā.) pavatthe (udā. 46) pabbate. Tena kho pana samayena soṇo upāsako kuṭikaṇṇo āyasmato mahākaccānassa upaṭṭhāko hoti. Atha kho soṇo upāsako kuṭikaṇṇo yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho soṇo upāsako kuṭikaṇṇo āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etadavoca – “yathā yathāhaṃ, bhante, ayyena mahākaccānena dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Icchāmahaṃ, bhante, kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ[M 0.0284]. Pabbājetu maṃ, bhante, ayyo mahākaccāno”ti. ( ) (evaṃ vutte āyasmā mahākaccāyano soṇaṃ upāsakaṃ kuṭikaṇṇaṃ etadavoca) (syā. udā. 46) “Dukkaraṃ kho, soṇa, yāvajīvaṃ ekaseyyaṃ ekabhattaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Iṅgha, tvaṃ, soṇa[T 2.0030], tattheva agārikabhūto buddhānaṃ sāsanaṃ anuyuñja, kālayuttaṃ ekaseyyaṃ ekabhattaṃ brahmacariya”nti. Atha kho soṇassa upāsakassa kuṭikaṇṇassa yo ahosi pabbajjābhisaṅkhāro so paṭippassambhi. Dutiyampi kho soṇo upāsako kuṭikaṇṇo [P 1.0195]…pe… tatiyampi kho soṇo upāsako kuṭikaṇṇo yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho soṇo upāsako kuṭikaṇṇo āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etadavoca – “yathā yathāhaṃ, bhante, ayyena mahākaccānena dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi, nayidaṃ sukaraṃ agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā ekantaparipuṇṇaṃ ekantaparisuddhaṃ saṅkhalikhitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ. Icchāmahaṃ, bhante, kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Pabbājetu maṃ, bhante, ayyo mahākaccāno”ti. Atha kho āyasmā [V 0.0269] mahākaccāno soṇaṃ upāsakaṃ kuṭikaṇṇaṃ pabbājesi. Tena kho pana samayena avantidakkhiṇāpatho appabhikkhuko hoti. Atha kho āyasmā mahākaccāno tiṇṇaṃ vassānaṃ accayena kicchena kasirena tato tato dasavaggaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā āyasmantaṃ soṇaṃ upasampādesi.

257. At that time, the Venerable Mahākaccāna was dwelling in Avanti, at Kuraraghara on Mount Papataka. At that time, the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa was the attendant of the Venerable Mahākaccāna. Then the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa approached the Venerable Mahākaccāna, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa said to the Venerable Mahākaccāna: “Venerable sir, as I understand the Dhamma taught by the Venerable Mahākaccāna, it is not easy for one living at home to lead this perfectly complete, perfectly pure holy life, polished like a conch shell. I wish, venerable sir, to shave off my hair and beard, put on the ochre robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness. May the Venerable Mahākaccāna give me the going forth.” “Soṇa, it is difficult to lead the holy life for one's whole life, sleeping alone and eating only one meal. Come now, Soṇa, you should, right there as a householder, apply yourself to the teaching of the Buddhas, and at suitable times, to the holy life of sleeping alone and eating only one meal.” Then the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa’s aspiration for going forth subsided. A second time, the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa … A third time, the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa approached the Venerable Mahākaccāna, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa said to the Venerable Mahākaccāna: “Venerable sir, as I understand the Dhamma taught by the Venerable Mahākaccāna, it is not easy for one living at home to lead this perfectly complete, perfectly pure holy life, polished like a conch shell. I wish, venerable sir, to shave off my hair and beard, put on the ochre robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness. May the Venerable Mahākaccāna give me the going forth.” Then the Venerable Mahākaccāna gave the going forth to the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa. At that time, the southern region of Avanti had few monks. Then, after the lapse of three years, the Venerable Mahākaccāna, with difficulty and trouble, assembled from various places a Saṅgha of ten monks and gave the higher ordination to the Venerable Soṇa.

Soṇakuṭikaṇṇavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Story of Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa is concluded.

158. Mahākaccānassa pañcavaraparidassanā

158. The Exposition of Mahākaccāna's Five Boons

Atha kho āyasmato soṇassa vassaṃvuṭṭhassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “sutoyeva kho me so bhagavā ediso ca ediso cāti, na ca mayā sammukhā [T 2.0031] diṭṭho, gaccheyyāhaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ, sace maṃ upajjhāyo anujāneyyā”ti. Atha kho āyasmā soṇo sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā soṇo āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etadavoca – “idha mayhaṃ, bhante, rahogatassa [M 0.0285] paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘suto yeva kho me so bhagavā ediso ca ediso cāti, na ca mayā sammukhā diṭṭho, gaccheyyāhaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ, sace maṃ upajjhāyo anujāneyyā’ti; gaccheyyāhaṃ, bhante, taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ, sace maṃ upajjhāyo anujānātī”ti. “Sādhu sādhu, soṇa. Gaccha tvaṃ, soṇa, taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ. Dakkhissasi tvaṃ, soṇa, taṃ bhagavantaṃ pāsādikaṃ pasādanīyaṃ santindriyaṃ santamānasaṃ uttamadamathasamathaṃ amanuppattaṃ dantaṃ guttaṃ yatindriyaṃ nāgaṃ. Tena hi tvaṃ, soṇa, mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vanda – ‘upajjhāyo me, bhante, āyasmā mahākaccāno bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’”ti. Evañca vadehi – “avantidakkhiṇāpatho, bhante, appabhikkhuko, tiṇṇaṃ me vassānaṃ accayena kicchena kasirena tato tato dasavaggaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā upasampadaṃ alatthaṃ; appeva nāma bhagavā avantidakkhiṇāpathe [T 2.0032] appatarena gaṇena upasampadaṃ anujāneyya. Avantidakkhiṇāpathe, bhante, kaṇhuttarā bhūmi kharā gokaṇṭakahatā; appeva nāma bhagavā avantidakkhiṇāpathe [P 1.0196] guṇaṅguṇūpāhanaṃ anujāneyya. Avantidakkhiṇāpathe, bhante, nahānagarukā manussā udakasuddhikā; appeva nāma bhagavā avantidakkhiṇāpathe dhuvanahānaṃ anujāneyya. Avantidakkhiṇāpathe, bhante, cammāni attharaṇāni, eḷakacammaṃ [V 0.0270] ajacammaṃ migacammaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhante, majjhimesu janapadesu eragū moragū majjārū majjhārū (ka.) jantū, evameva kho, bhante, avantidakkhiṇāpathe cammāni attharaṇāni, eḷakacammaṃ ajacammaṃ migacammaṃ; appeva nāma bhagavā avantidakkhiṇāpathe cammāni attharaṇāni anujāneyya, eḷakacammaṃ ajacammaṃ migacammaṃ. Etarahi, bhante, manussā nissīmagatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cīvaraṃ denti – ‘imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa demā’”ti. Te āgantvā ārocenti – ‘itthannāmehi te, āvuso, manussehi cīvaraṃ dinna’nti te kukkuccāyantā na sādiyanti – ‘mā no nissaggiyaṃ ahosī’ti; appeva nāma bhagavā cīvare pariyāyaṃ ācikkheyyā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā soṇo āyasmato mahākaccānassa paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya [M 0.0286] yena sāvatthi tena pakkāmi. Anupubbena yena sāvatthi jetavanaṃ anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāmo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā [T 2.0033] ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “imassa, ānanda, āgantukassa bhikkhuno senāsanaṃ paññāpehī”ti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando – “yassa kho maṃ bhagavā āṇāpeti, ‘imassa, ānanda, āgantukassa bhikkhuno senāsanaṃ paññāpehī’ti, icchati bhagavā tena bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekavihāre vatthuṃ, icchati bhagavā āyasmatā soṇena saddhiṃ ekavihāre vatthu”nti – yasmiṃ vihāre bhagavā viharati tasmiṃ vihāre āyasmato soṇassa senāsanaṃ paññāpesi.

Then, when the Venerable Soṇa had completed the rains-residence, while he was in seclusion and solitude, this thought arose in his mind: “I have only heard about the Blessed One—that he is of such and such a nature—but I have not seen him face to face. If my preceptor were to permit me, I would go to see that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.”

Then, in the evening, the Venerable Soṇa emerged from seclusion and approached the Venerable Mahākaccāna. Having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Mahākaccāna and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Soṇa said this to the Venerable Mahākaccāna: “Venerable sir, while I was here in seclusion and solitude, this thought arose in my mind: ‘I have only heard about the Blessed One—that he is of such and such a nature—but I have not seen him face to face. If my preceptor were to permit me, I would go to see that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.’ Venerable sir, if my preceptor permits me, I would go to see that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.”

“Good, good, Soṇa. Go, Soṇa, to see that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One. You will see, Soṇa, that Blessed One who is inspiring, confidence-inspiring, with peaceful faculties and a peaceful mind, who has attained the highest taming and calm, who is controlled, guarded, with restrained faculties, a faultless one. Therefore, Soṇa, with my words, bow with your head at the feet of the Blessed One and say: ‘Venerable sir, my preceptor, the Venerable Mahākaccāna, bows with his head at the feet of the Blessed One.’ And say this: ‘Venerable sir, the Avanti southern region has few monks. After three years had passed, with difficulty and hardship, having gathered a community of ten monks from here and there, I obtained the higher ordination. May the Blessed One please allow the higher ordination in the Avanti southern region with a smaller group. Venerable sir, in the Avanti southern region, the ground has black soil on its surface, is rough, and is damaged by cattle hooves. May the Blessed One please allow multi-layered footwear in the Avanti southern region. Venerable sir, in the Avanti southern region, the people place great importance on bathing and believe in purification by water. May the Blessed One please allow constant bathing in the Avanti southern region. Venerable sir, in the Avanti southern region, there are spreads of hide: sheepskin, goatskin, and deerskin. Just as in the middle countries, venerable sir, there are mats of eraka grass, moragu grass, majjāru grass, and jantu grass, even so, venerable sir, in the Avanti southern region, there are spreads of hide: sheepskin, goatskin, and deerskin. May the Blessed One please allow spreads of hide in the Avanti southern region: sheepskin, goatskin, and deerskin. Now, venerable sir, people give robes to monks who have gone outside the boundary, saying: “We give this robe to the one with such-and-such a name.” Those monks, upon returning, are informed: “Friend, a robe was given to you by people with such-and-such a name.” Being scrupulous, they do not accept it, thinking: “May this not become an item to be forfeited by us.” May the Blessed One please explain a permissible method regarding robes.’”

“Very well, venerable sir,” the Venerable Soṇa replied to the Venerable Mahākaccāna. Rising from his seat, he paid homage to the Venerable Mahākaccāna, circumambulated him to the right, put his lodging in order, took his bowl and robe, and departed for Sāvatthī. Traveling in due course, he went to Sāvatthī, to Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery, to where the Blessed One was. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side.

Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Ānanda, prepare a lodging for this visiting monk.”

Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Ānanda: “For whichever monk the Blessed One commands me, ‘Ānanda, prepare a lodging for this visiting monk,’ the Blessed One wishes to live together with that monk in the same dwelling. The Blessed One wishes to live together with the Venerable Soṇa in the same dwelling.” So, in the same dwelling where the Blessed One was residing, he prepared a lodging for the Venerable Soṇa.

258. Atha kho bhagavā bahudeva rattiṃ ajjhokāse vītināmetvā vihāraṃ pāvisi. Āyasmāpi kho soṇo bahudeva rattiṃ ajjhokāse vītināmetvā vihāraṃ pāvisi. Atha kho bhagavā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya āyasmantaṃ soṇaṃ ajjhesi – “paṭibhātu taṃ, bhikkhu, dhammo bhāsitu”nti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā soṇo bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā sabbāneva aṭṭhakavaggikāni sarena abhāsi. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmato soṇassa sarabhaññapariyosāne abbhānumodi – “sādhu, sādhu, bhikkhu. Suggahitāni kho te, bhikkhu, aṭṭhakavaggikāni[P 1.0197], sumanasikatāni sūpadhāritāni. Kalyāṇiyāpi vācāya samannāgato, vissaṭṭhāya, anelagalāya aneḷagalāya (ka.), atthassa viññāpaniyā. Kativassosi tvaṃ, bhikkhū”ti? “Ekavassohaṃ, bhagavā”ti. “Kissa pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, evaṃ ciraṃ akāsī”ti? “Ciraṃ diṭṭho me, bhante, kāmesu ādīnavo, api ca sambādhā [T 2.0034] gharāvāsā bahukiccā bahukaraṇīyā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

258. Then the Blessed One, having spent much of the night in the open, entered the dwelling. The Venerable Soṇa also, having spent much of the night in the open, entered the dwelling. Then the Blessed One, having risen at dawn, urged the Venerable Soṇa: “Let the Dhamma occur to you, monk, to recite.” “Even so, venerable sir,” replied the Venerable Soṇa to the Blessed One, and then he recited all the verses of the Aṭṭhakavagga by chanting. Then the Blessed One, at the conclusion of the Venerable Soṇa’s chanting, expressed his approval: “Good, good, monk. Well learned by you, monk, are the verses of the Aṭṭhakavagga, well attended to, well borne in mind. You are endowed with a beautiful voice, clear, faultless, and expressive of the meaning. How many years have you been ordained, monk?” “I have been ordained for one year, Blessed One.” “But why then, monk, did you take so long?” “For a long time, venerable sir, I have seen the danger in sensual pleasures; and yet, the household life is confining, with many duties and many things to be done.” Then the Blessed One, having understood the meaning of this, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

udā. 46 udānepi “Disvā [V 0.0271] ādīnavaṃ loke, ñatvā dhammaṃ nirūpadhiṃ;

Ariyo na ramatī pāpe, pāpe na ramatī sucī”ti.

“Having seen the danger in the world, and known the Dhamma free from substrates, the noble one does not delight in evil; the pure one does not delight in evil.”

Atha kho āyasmā soṇo – paṭisammodati kho maṃ bhagavā, ayaṃ khvassa kālo yaṃ me upajjhāyo paridassīti – uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ [M 0.0287] etadavoca – “upajjhāyo me, bhante, āyasmā mahākaccāno bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, evañca vadeti avantidakkhiṇāpatho, bhante, appabhikkhuko. Tiṇṇaṃ me vassānaṃ accayena kicchena kasirena tato tato dasavaggaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā upasampadaṃ alatthaṃ, appeva nāma bhagavā avantidakkhiṇāpathe appatarena gaṇena upasampadaṃ anujāneyya. Avantidakkhiṇāpathe, bhante, kaṇhuttarā bhūmi kharā gokaṇṭakahatā; appeva nāma bhagavā avantidakkhiṇāpathe guṇaṅguṇūpāhanaṃ anujāneyya. Avantidakkhiṇāpathe, bhante, nahānagarukā manussā udakasuddhikā, appeva nāma bhagavā avantidakkhiṇāpathe dhuvanahānaṃ anujāneyya. Avantidakkhiṇāpathe, bhante, cammāni attharaṇāni, eḷakacammaṃ ajacammaṃ migacammaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhante, majjhimesu janapadesu eragū moragū majjārū jantū[T 2.0035], evameva kho, bhante, avantidakkhiṇāpathe cammāni attharaṇāni, eḷakacammaṃ ajacammaṃ migacammaṃ; appeva nāma bhagavā avantidakkhiṇāpathe cammāni attharaṇāni anujāneyya, eḷakacammaṃ ajacammaṃ migacammaṃ. Etarahi, bhante, manussā nissīmagatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cīvaraṃ denti – ‘imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa demā’ti. Te āgantvā ārocenti – ‘itthannāmehi te, āvuso, manussehi cīvaraṃ dinna’nti. Te kukkuccāyantā na sādiyanti – ‘mā no nissaggiyaṃ ahosī’ti; appeva nāma bhagavā cīvare pariyāyaṃ ācikkheyyā”ti.

Then the Venerable Soṇa, thinking, “The Blessed One has indeed welcomed me. This would be the time to deliver the message with which my preceptor charged me,” rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, fell with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, and said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, my preceptor, the Venerable Mahākaccāna, venerates the Blessed One’s feet with his head and says this: ‘Venerable sir, the Avanti southern country has few monks. After three years had passed, with difficulty and with trouble, having gathered a Saṅgha of ten monks from here and there, I was able to arrange an ordination. It would be good if the Blessed One were to allow ordination in the Avanti southern country with a smaller group. Venerable sir, in the Avanti southern country the ground has black topsoil, is rough, and is damaged by cattle hooves. It would be good if the Blessed One were to allow multi-layered footwear in the Avanti southern country. Venerable sir, in the Avanti southern country, the people are devoted to bathing and believe in purification by water. It would be good if the Blessed One were to allow constant bathing in the Avanti southern country. Venerable sir, in the Avanti southern country, there are skin-spreads: ram skin, goat skin, and deer skin. Just as, venerable sir, in the middle countries there are mats of eraka-grass, moragū-grass, majjārū-grass, and jantu-grass, so too, venerable sir, in the Avanti southern country there are skin-spreads: ram skin, goat skin, and deer skin. It would be good if the Blessed One were to allow skin-spreads in the Avanti southern country: ram skin, goat skin, and deer skin. Furthermore, venerable sir, people now give a robe for a monk who has gone outside the boundary, saying, “We give this robe to the one with such-and-such a name.” When the other monks return, they inform him, saying: “Friend, a robe was given to you by people of such-and-such a name.” Being scrupulous, they do not accept, thinking, “May this not become an item for forfeiture for us.” It would be good if the Blessed One were to explain the proper procedure concerning robes.’”

259. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “avantidakkhiṇāpatho, bhikkhave, appabhikkhuko. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sabbapaccantimesu janapadesu vinayadharapañcamena gaṇena upasampadaṃ. Tatrime paccantimā janapadā – puratthimāya disāya gajaṅgalaṃ kajaṅgalaṃ (sī. syā.) nāma nigamo, tassa parena mahāsālā, tato parā paccantimā janapadā, orato majjhe; puratthimadakkhiṇāya disāya sallavatī salalavatī (sī.) nāma nadī, tato parā paccantimā janapadā, orato majjhe; dakkhiṇāya disāya setakaṇṇikaṃ nāma nigamo, tato parā paccantimā janapadā, orato majjhe; pacchimāya disāya thūṇaṃ nāma brāhmaṇagāmo, tato parā paccantimā janapadā, orato majjhe; uttarāya [M 0.0288] disāya usīraddhajo nāma pabbato, tato parā paccantimā janapadā, orato majjhe[T 2.0036]. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, evarūpesu paccantimesu [V 0.0272] janapadesu vinayadharapañcamena gaṇena upasampadaṃ. Avantidakkhiṇāpathe, bhikkhave, kaṇhuttarā bhūmi kharā gokaṇṭakahatā. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sabbapaccantimesu janapadesu guṇaṅguṇūpāhanaṃ. Avantidakkhiṇāpathe, bhikkhave, nahānagarukā manussā udakasuddhikā. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sabbapaccantimesu janapadesu dhuvanahānaṃ. Avantidakkhiṇāpathe, bhikkhave, cammāni attharaṇāni, eḷakacammaṃ ajacammaṃ [P 1.0198] migacammaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, majjhimesu janapadesu eragū moragū majjārū jantū, evameva kho, bhikkhave, avantidakkhiṇāpathe cammāni attharaṇāni, eḷakacammaṃ ajacammaṃ migacammaṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sabbapaccantimesu janapadesu cammāni attharaṇāni, eḷakacammaṃ ajacammaṃ migacammaṃ. Idha pana, bhikkhave, manussā nissīmagatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cīvaraṃ denti – ‘imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa demā’ti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sādituṃ, na tāva taṃ gaṇanūpagaṃ yāva na hatthaṃ gacchatī”ti.

259. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this matter, having given a discourse on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: 'Monks, the country of Avantidakkhiṇāpatha has few monks. I allow, monks, in all the border districts, ordination by a group with a Vinaya expert as the fifth. Herein, these are the border districts: in the eastern direction, there is a market town named Gajaṅgala, and beyond it, the great Sāla tree. Beyond that are the border districts; within is the middle country. In the southeastern direction, there is a river named Sallavatī. Beyond that are the border districts; within is the middle country. In the southern direction, there is a market town named Setakaṇṇika. Beyond that are the border districts; within is the middle country. In the western direction, there is a brahmin village named Thūṇa. Beyond that are the border districts; within is the middle country. In the northern direction, there is a mountain named Usīraddhaja. Beyond that are the border districts; within is the middle country. I allow, monks, in such border districts, ordination by a group with a Vinaya expert as the fifth. In Avantidakkhiṇāpatha, monks, the land has black topsoil, is rough, and is ruined by cattle-hoof thorns. I allow, monks, in all the border districts, multi-layered footwear. In Avantidakkhiṇāpatha, monks, the people place importance on bathing and hold that purification is by water. I allow, monks, in all the border districts, constant bathing. In Avantidakkhiṇāpatha, monks, there are spreads made of hide: sheepskin, goatskin, and deerskin. Just as, monks, in the middle districts there are mats woven from eraka grass, moragu grass, majjāru grass, and jantu grass, even so, monks, in Avantidakkhiṇāpatha there are spreads made of hide: sheepskin, goatskin, and deerskin. I allow, monks, in all the border districts, spreads made of hide: sheepskin, goatskin, and deerskin. Furthermore, monks, here people give a robe to monks who have gone outside the boundary, saying, “We give this robe to the one named so-and-so.” I allow, monks, to consent to it; it does not come into reckoning as long as it has not come to hand.'

Mahākaccānassa pañcavaraparidassanā niṭṭhitā.

The exposition of Mahākaccāna's five boons is concluded.

Cammakkhandhako pañcamo.

The fifth Chapter on Hides is concluded.

159. Tassuddānaṃ

159. The summary of that is:

Rājā ca māgadho soṇo, asītisahassissaro;

Sāgato gijjhakūṭasmiṃ, bahuṃ dasseti uttariṃ.

The Magadhan king and Soṇa, lord of eighty thousand; Sāgata at Vulture Peak, showing much that is superior.

Pabbajjāraddhabhijjiṃsu[T 2.0037], vīṇaṃ ekapalāsikaṃ;

Nīlā pītā lohitikā, mañjiṭṭhā kaṇhameva ca.

Going forth, strenuous effort and splitting, the lute, single-soled; blue, yellow, red, madder, and black.

Mahāraṅgamahānāmā, vaddhikā ca paṭikkhipi;

Khallakā puṭapāli ca, tūlatittirameṇḍajā.

Deeply colored, with great patterns, and straps were rejected; with heel-coverings and with instep-coverings, stuffed with cotton, speckled like a partridge, and made with ram's horns.

Vicchikā moracitrā ca, sīhabyagghā ca dīpikā;

Ajinuddā majjārī ca, kāḷaluvakaparikkhaṭā.

With scorpion-tail straps and decorated with peacock feathers; bordered with lion, tiger, and panther skin; with antelope, otter, and cat skin, and bordered with black squirrel or flying squirrel skin.

Phalitupāhanā [V 0.0273] khilā, dhotakhāṇukhaṭakhaṭā;

Tālaveḷutiṇaṃ ceva, muñjapabbajahintālā.

Sandals for cracked feet, a protruding sore, unwashed feet, stumps, clattering; palmyra, bamboo, and grass, muñja, pabbaja, and hintāla.

Kamalakambalasovaṇṇā[M 0.0289], rūpikā maṇiveḷuriyā;

Phalikā kaṃsakācā ca, tipusīsañca tambakā.

Kamala grass, wool, gold, silver, gems, beryl; crystal, bronze, and glass, tin, lead, and copper.

Gāvī yānaṃ gilāno ca, purisāyuttasivikā;

Sayanāni mahācammā, gocammehi ca pāpako.

Cows, vehicles, and a sick person, drawn by men, a palanquin; seats, large hides, and with cowhides, a wicked one.

Gihīnaṃ cammavaddhehi, pavisanti gilāyano;

Mahākaccāyano soṇo, sarena aṭṭhakavaggikaṃ.

Of laypeople, with leather thongs, entering, a sick person; Mahākaccāna, Soṇa, the Aṭṭhakavagga by voice.

Upasampadaṃ pañcahi, guṇaṅguṇā dhuvasinā;

Cammattharaṇānuññāsi, na tāva gaṇanūpagaṃ;

Adāsi me vare pañca, soṇattherassa nāyakoti.

Ordination by five, multi-layered sandals, constant bathing; he permitted hide spreads, not yet come into reckoning; the Leader gave five boons to the Elder Soṇa.

Imamhi khandhake vatthūni tesaṭṭhi.

In this chapter, there are sixty-three topics.

Cammakkhandhako niṭṭhito.

The Chapter on Hides is finished.

6. Bhesajjakkhandhako

6. The Chapter on Medicines

160. Pañcabhesajjakathā

160. The Discourse on the Five Medicines

260. Tena [P 1.0199][M 0.0290][V 0.0274][T 2.0038] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhūnaṃ sāradikena ābādhena phuṭṭhānaṃ yāgupi pītā uggacchati, bhattampi bhuttaṃ uggacchati. Te tena kisā honti, lūkhā, dubbaṇṇā, uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajātā, dhamanisanthatagattā. Addasā kho bhagavā te bhikkhū kise lūkhe dubbaṇṇe uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajāte dhamanisanthatagatte, disvāna āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “kiṃ nu kho, ānanda, etarahi bhikkhū kisā, lūkhā, dubbaṇṇā, uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajātā, dhamanisanthatagattā”ti? “Etarahi, bhante, bhikkhūnaṃ sāradikena ābādhena phuṭṭhānaṃ yāgupi pītā uggacchati, bhattampi bhuttaṃ uggacchati. Te tena kisā honti, lūkhā, dubbaṇṇā, uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajātā, dhamanisanthatagattā”ti. Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “etarahi kho bhikkhūnaṃ sāradikena ābādhena phuṭṭhānaṃ yāgupi pītā uggacchati, bhattampi bhuttaṃ uggacchati. Te tena kisā honti, lūkhā, dubbaṇṇā, uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajātā, dhamanisanthatagattā. Kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bhesajjaṃ anujāneyyaṃ, yaṃ bhesajjañceva assa bhesajjasammatañca lokassa, āhāratthañca phareyya, na ca oḷāriko āhāro paññāyeyyā”ti? Atha kho bhagavato [T 2.0039] etadahosi – “imāni kho pañca bhesajjāni, seyyathidaṃ – sappi, navanītaṃ, telaṃ, madhu, phāṇitaṃ; bhesajjāni ceva bhesajjasammatāni ca lokassa, āhāratthañca pharanti, na ca oḷāriko āhāro paññāyati. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ imāni pañca bhesajjāni anujāneyyaṃ, kāle paṭiggahetvā kāle paribhuñjitu”nti. Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “idha mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘etarahi kho bhikkhūnaṃ sāradikena ābādhena [V 0.0275] phuṭṭhānaṃ yāgupi pītā uggacchati, bhattampi bhuttaṃ uggacchati. Te tena kisā honti, lūkhā, dubbaṇṇā, uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajātā, dhamanisanthatagattā. Kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bhesajjaṃ anujāneyyaṃ, yaṃ bhesajjañceva assa bhesajjasammatañca lokassa, āhāratthañca [M 0.0291] phareyya, na ca oḷāriko āhāro paññāyeyyā’ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi ‘imāni kho pañca bhesajjāni[P 1.0200], seyyathidaṃ – sappi, navanītaṃ, telaṃ, madhu, phāṇitaṃ; bhesajjāni ceva bhesajjasammatāni ca lokassa, āhāratthañca pharanti, na ca oḷāriko āhāro paññāyati. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ imāni pañca bhesajjāni anujāneyyaṃ, kāle paṭiggahetvā kāle paribhuñjitu’nti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tāni pañca bhesajjāni kāle paṭiggahetvā kāle paribhuñjitu”nti.

260. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Now at that time, the monks, being afflicted with an autumnal illness, vomited the gruel they drank and the food they ate. For that reason, they became thin, haggard, of poor complexion, pale and yellowish, with prominent veins on their bodies. The Blessed One saw those monks who were thin, haggard, of poor complexion, pale and yellowish, with prominent veins on their bodies. Having seen them, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Ānanda, why are the monks now so thin, haggard, of poor complexion, pale and yellowish, with prominent veins on their bodies?” “Venerable sir, the monks are now afflicted with an autumnal illness; they vomit the gruel they drink and the food they eat. For that reason, they are thin, haggard, of poor complexion, pale and yellowish, with prominent veins on their bodies.” Then, as the Blessed One was alone in retreat, this thought arose in his mind: “The monks are now afflicted with an autumnal illness; they vomit the gruel they drink and the food they eat. For that reason, they have become thin, haggard, of poor complexion, pale and yellowish, with prominent veins on their bodies. What medicine should I allow for the monks that would be a medicine, be considered a medicine by the world, also serve as nourishment, and not appear as coarse food?” Then it occurred to the Blessed One: “There are these five medicines: ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, and molasses. They are medicines, are considered medicines by the world, also serve as nourishment, and do not appear as coarse food. What if I were to allow the monks these five medicines, to be received at the proper time and consumed at the proper time?” Then, in the evening, the Blessed One emerged from retreat and, on this occasion, in connection with this matter, delivered a Dhamma talk and addressed the monks: “Here, monks, as I was alone in retreat, this thought arose in my mind: ‘The monks are now afflicted with an autumnal illness; they vomit the gruel they drink and the food they eat. For that reason, they have become thin, haggard, of poor complexion, pale and yellowish, with prominent veins on their bodies. What medicine should I allow for the monks that would be a medicine, be considered a medicine by the world, also serve as nourishment, and not appear as coarse food?’ Then it occurred to me: ‘There are these five medicines: ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, and molasses. They are medicines, are considered medicines by the world, also serve as nourishment, and do not appear as coarse food. What if I were to allow the monks these five medicines, to be received at the proper time and consumed at the proper time?’ Monks, I allow these five medicines to be received at the proper time and consumed at the proper time.”

261. Tena [T 2.0040] kho pana samayena bhikkhū tāni pañca bhesajjāni kāle paṭiggahetvā kāle paribhuñjanti. Tesaṃ yānipi tāni pākatikāni lūkhāni bhojanāni tānipi nacchādenti, pageva senesitāni senesikāni (sī. syā.), senehikāni (yojanā). Te tena ceva sāradikena ābādhena phuṭṭhā, iminā ca bhattācchādakena bhattācchannakena (ka.), tadubhayena bhiyyosomattāya kisā honti, lūkhā, dubbaṇṇā, uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajātā, dhamanisanthatagattā. Addasā kho bhagavā te bhikkhū bhiyyosomattāya kise lūkhe dubbaṇṇe uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajāte dhamanisanthatagatte, disvāna āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “kiṃ nu kho, ānanda, etarahi bhikkhū bhiyyosomattāya kisā, lūkhā, dubbaṇṇā, uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajātā, dhamanisanthatagattā”ti? “Etarahi, bhante, bhikkhū tāni ca pañca bhesajjāni kāle paṭiggahetvā kāle paribhuñjanti. Tesaṃ yānipi tāni pākatikāni lūkhāni bhojanāni tānipi nacchādenti, pageva senesikāni. Te tena ceva sāradikena ābādhena phuṭṭhā, iminā ca bhattācchādakena, tadubhayena bhiyyosomattāya kisā, lūkhā, dubbaṇṇā, uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajātā, dhamanisanthatagattā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tāni pañca bhesajjāni paṭiggahetvā kālepi vikālepi paribhuñjitu”nti.

261. At that time, the monks, having received the five medicines at the proper time, consumed them at the proper time. They could not digest even the coarse, regular foods they consumed, let alone refined foods. Afflicted by both that autumnal illness and this indigestion, they became exceedingly thin, haggard, of poor complexion, pale and yellowish, with veins standing out on their bodies. The Blessed One saw those monks who were exceedingly thin, haggard, of poor complexion, pale and yellowish, with veins standing out on their bodies. Having seen them, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Ānanda, why are the monks at present so exceedingly thin, haggard, of poor complexion, pale and yellowish, with veins standing out on their bodies?” “Venerable Sir, at present the monks, having received those five medicines at the proper time, consume them at the proper time. They cannot digest even the coarse, regular foods they consume, let alone refined foods. Afflicted by both that autumnal illness and this indigestion, they have become exceedingly thin, haggard, of poor complexion, pale and yellowish, with veins standing out on their bodies.” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow those five medicines, having been received, to be consumed both at the proper time and at the improper time.”

262. Tena [T 2.0041] kho pana samayena gilānānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vasehi bhesajjehi attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vasāni bhesajjāni – acchavasaṃ, macchavasaṃ, susukāvasaṃ[M 0.0292], sūkaravasaṃ, gadrabhavasaṃ – kāle paṭiggahitaṃ kāle nippakkaṃ nipakkaṃ (ka.) kāle saṃsaṭṭhaṃ telaparibhogena paribhuñjituṃ. Vikāle ce, bhikkhave, paṭiggahitaṃ vikāle nippakkaṃ vikāle saṃsaṭṭhaṃ, taṃ ce paribhuñjeyya, āpatti tiṇṇaṃ dukkaṭānaṃ. Kāle ce, bhikkhave, paṭiggahitaṃ vikāle nippakkaṃ vikāle saṃsaṭṭhaṃ, taṃ ce paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dvinnaṃ dukkaṭānaṃ. Kāle ce, bhikkhave, paṭiggahitaṃ [V 0.0276] kāle nippakkaṃ vikāle saṃsaṭṭhaṃ, taṃ ce paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Kāle ce, bhikkhave, paṭiggahitaṃ kāle nippakkaṃ kāle saṃsaṭṭhaṃ, taṃ ce paribhuñjeyya, anāpattīti.

262. Now at that time, sick monks had need of medicines that are animal fats. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow medicines that are animal fats—the fat of a bear, the fat of a fish, the fat of a crocodile, the fat of a pig, the fat of a donkey—if received at the proper time, cooked at the proper time, and strained at the proper time, to be consumed in the manner of consuming oil. Monks, if it is received at the wrong time, cooked at the wrong time, and strained at the wrong time, and if one should consume it, one commits three offenses of wrong-doing. Monks, if it is received at the proper time, but cooked at the wrong time and strained at the wrong time, and if one should consume it, one commits two offenses of wrong-doing. Monks, if it is received at the proper time and cooked at the proper time, but strained at the wrong time, and if one should consume it, one commits an offense of wrong-doing. Monks, if it is received at the proper time, cooked at the proper time, and strained at the proper time, and if one should consume it, there is no offense.'

Pañcabhesajjakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Five Medicines is concluded.

161. Mūlādibhesajjakathā

161. The Discourse on Medicines such as Roots

263. Tena kho pana samayena gilānānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ mūlehi bhesajjehi attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi[P 1.0201], bhikkhave, mūlāni bhesajjāni – haliddiṃ, siṅgiveraṃ, vacaṃ, vacatthaṃ vacatthaṃ (sī. syā.), ativisaṃ, kaṭukarohiṇiṃ, usīraṃ, bhaddamuttakaṃ, yāni vā panaññānipi atthi mūlāni bhesajjāni, neva khādanīye khādanīyatthaṃ pharanti, na bhojanīye bhojanīyatthaṃ pharanti, tāni – paṭiggahetvā yāvajīvaṃ pariharituṃ; sati paccaye paribhuñjituṃ. Asati paccaye paribhuñjantassa āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

263. Now at that time, sick monks had need of medicines that are roots. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow medicines that are roots—turmeric, ginger, orris root, sweet flag, ativisa, kaṭukarohiṇī, vetiver, bhaddamuttaka, and whatever other root medicines there may be that do not fulfill the function of a hard food nor the function of a soft food—these I allow to be received and kept for life, and to be consumed when there is a reason. For one who consumes them when there is no reason, there is an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana [T 2.0042] samayena gilānānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ mūlehi bhesajjehi piṭṭhehi attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, nisadaṃ nisadapotakanti.

Now at that time, sick monks had need of powdered root medicines. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow a grinding slab and a hand-stone.'

Tena kho pana samayena gilānānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kasāvehi bhesajjehi attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kasāvāni kasāvabhesajjāni (ka.) bhesajjāni – nimbakasāvaṃ, kuṭajakasāvaṃ, paṭolakasāvaṃ, phaggavakasāvaṃ, nattamālakasāvaṃ, yāni vā panaññānipi atthi kasāvāni bhesajjāni neva khādanīye khādanīyatthaṃ pharanti, na bhojanīye bhojanīyatthaṃ pharanti, tāni – paṭiggahetvā yāvajīvaṃ pariharituṃ; sati paccaye paribhuñjituṃ. Asati paccaye paribhuñjantassa āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Now at that time, sick monks had need of astringent medicines. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow astringent medicines—neem astringent, kuṭaja astringent, paṭola astringent, phaggava astringent, nattamāla astringent, or whatever other astringent medicines there are that do not fulfill the function of a hard food, nor the function of a soft food—to be received and kept for a lifetime, and to be used when there is a reason. For one who uses them when there is no reason, there is an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena gilānānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ paṇṇehi bhesajjehi attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave[M 0.0293], paṇṇāni bhesajjāni – nimbapaṇṇaṃ, kuṭajapaṇṇaṃ, paṭolapaṇṇaṃ, sulasipaṇṇaṃ, kappāsapaṇṇaṃ, yāni vā panaññānipi atthi paṇṇāni bhesajjāni, neva khādanīye khādanīyatthaṃ pharanti, na bhojanīye bhojanīyatthaṃ pharanti…pe….

Now at that time, sick monks had need of medicines of leaves. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow medicines of leaves—neem leaf, kuṭaja leaf, paṭola leaf, tulasi leaf, cotton leaf, or whatever other medicinal leaves there may be that do not fulfill the function of a hard food, nor the function of a soft food... and so on...'

Tena [V 0.0277] kho pana samayena gilānānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ phalehi bhesajjehi attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, phalāni [T 2.0043] bhesajjāni – bilaṅgaṃ, pippaliṃ, maricaṃ, harītakaṃ, vibhītakaṃ, āmalakaṃ, goṭṭhaphalaṃ goṭhaphalaṃ (syā.), koṭṭhaphalaṃ (ka.), yāni vā panaññānipi atthi phalāni bhesajjāni, neva khādanīye khādanīyatthaṃ pharanti, na bhojanīye bhojanīyatthaṃ pharanti…pe….

Now at that time, sick monks had need of medicines of fruits. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow medicines of fruits—bilaṅga, long pepper, black pepper, harītaka, vibhītaka, āmalaka, goṭṭhaphala, or whatever other medicinal fruits there may be that do not fulfill the function of a hard food, nor the function of a soft food... and so on...'

Tena kho pana samayena gilānānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ jatūhi bhesajjehi attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, jatūni bhesajjāni – hiṅguṃ, hiṅgujatuṃ, hiṅgusipāṭikaṃ, takaṃ, takapattiṃ, takapaṇṇiṃ[P 1.0202], sajjulasaṃ, yāni vā panaññānipi atthi jatūni bhesajjāni, neva khādanīye khādanīyatthaṃ pharanti…pe….

Now at that time, sick monks had need of medicines of resins. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow medicines of resins—asafoetida, hiṅgujatu, hiṅgusipāṭikā, taka, takapatti, takapaṇṇī, sajjulasa, or whatever other medicinal resins there may be that do not fulfill the function of a hard food, nor the function of a soft food... and so on...'

Tena kho pana samayena gilānānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ loṇehi bhesajjehi attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, loṇāni bhesajjāni – sāmuddaṃ, kāḷaloṇaṃ, sindhavaṃ, ubbhidaṃ ubbhiraṃ (ka.), bilaṃ biḷālaṃ (sī.), yāni vā panaññānipi atthi loṇāni bhesajjāni, neva khādanīye khādanīyatthaṃ pharanti, na bhojanīye bhojanīyatthaṃ pharanti, tāni – paṭiggahetvā yāvajīvaṃ pariharituṃ; sati paccaye paribhuñjituṃ. Asati paccaye paribhuñjantassa āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Now at that time, sick monks had need of salt-medicines. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow salt-medicines—sea salt, black salt, rock salt, ubbhida salt, bila salt, or whatever other salt-medicines there may be that do not fulfill the function of a hard food, nor the function of a soft food—to be received and kept for life, and to be used when there is a reason. For one who uses them when there is no reason, there is an offense of wrong-doing.'

264. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato ānandassa upajjhāyassa [T 2.0044] āyasmato belaṭṭhasīsassa thullakacchābādho hoti. Tassa lasikāya cīvarāni kāye lagganti, tāni bhikkhū udakena temetvā temetvā apakaḍḍhanti. Addasā kho bhagavā senāsanacārikaṃ āhiṇḍanto te bhikkhū tāni cīvarāni udakena temetvā temetvā apakaḍḍhante, disvāna yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “kiṃ imassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ābādho”ti? “Imassa, bhante, āyasmato thullakacchābādho, lasikāya cīvarāni kāye lagganti, tāni mayaṃ udakena temetvā temetvā apakaḍḍhāmā”ti[M 0.0294]. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yassa kaṇḍu vā, piḷakā vā, assāvo vā, thullakacchu vā ābādho, kāyo vā duggandho, cuṇṇāni bhesajjāni; agilānassa chakaṇaṃ mattikaṃ rajananippakkaṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udukkhalaṃ musala”nti.

264. At that time, the Venerable Ānanda’s preceptor, the Venerable Belaṭṭhasīsa, had a severe skin disease. Due to the discharge, his robes were sticking to his body, and the monks were repeatedly moistening them with water and pulling them off. The Blessed One, while touring the lodgings, saw those monks repeatedly moistening the robes with water and pulling them off. Having seen them, he approached those monks and said this: 'Monks, what is this monk's illness?' 'Venerable sir, this venerable one has a severe skin disease. Due to the discharge, his robes are sticking to his body, so we are repeatedly moistening them with water and pulling them off.' Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: 'Monks, for one who has an itch, or a boil, or a discharging sore, or a severe skin disease, or whose body has a bad odor, I allow powdered medicines. For one who is not ill, I allow dried cow dung, fine clay, and the residue from boiling dye. Monks, I allow a mortar and a pestle.'

Tena kho pana samayena gilānānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cuṇṇehi bhesajjehi cālitehi attho hoti[V 0.0278]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cuṇṇacālininti. Saṇhehi attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dussacālininti.

At that time, sick monks had need of sifted powdered medicines. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. "Monks, I allow a powder-sifter." There was a need for fine powders. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. "Monks, I allow a cloth-sifter."

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno amanussikābādho hoti. Taṃ ācariyupajjhāyā upaṭṭhahantā nāsakkhiṃsu arogaṃ kātuṃ. So sūkarasūnaṃ gantvā āmakamaṃsaṃ khādi, āmakalohitaṃ pivi[T 2.0045]. Tassa so amanussikābādho paṭippassambhi. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[P 1.0203]. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, amanussikābādhe āmakamaṃsaṃ āmakalohitanti.

At that time, a certain monk had a disease caused by non-human beings. His teachers and preceptors, attending to him, were unable to make him well. He went to a pork butchery, ate raw meat, and drank raw blood. That disease caused by non-human beings subsided for him. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. "Monks, in the case of a disease caused by non-human beings, I allow raw meat and raw blood."

265. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno cakkhurogābādho hoti. Taṃ bhikkhū pariggahetvā uccārampi passāvampi nikkhāmenti. Addasā kho bhagavā senāsanacārikaṃ āhiṇḍanto te bhikkhū taṃ bhikkhuṃ pariggahetvā uccārampi passāvampi nikkhāmente, disvāna yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “kiṃ imassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ābādho”ti? “Imassa, bhante, āyasmato cakkhurogābādho. Imaṃ mayaṃ pariggahetvā uccārampi passāvampi nikkhāmemā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, añjanaṃ – kāḷañjanaṃ, rasañjanaṃ, sotañjanaṃ, gerukaṃ, kapalla”nti. Añjanūpapisanehi attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, candanaṃ, tagaraṃ, kāḷānusāriyaṃ, tālīsaṃ, bhaddamuttakanti. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū piṭṭhāni añjanāni carukesupi thālakesupi (sī. syā.) sarāvakesupi nikkhipanti; tiṇacuṇṇehipi paṃsukehipi okiriyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, añjaninti.

265. At that time, a certain monk was suffering from an eye disease. The monks attended to him and helped him relieve himself of both feces and urine. The Blessed One, while on a tour of the lodgings, saw those monks attending to that monk as he relieved himself of both feces and urine. Having seen them, he approached those monks and asked, “Monks, what is this monk’s ailment?” “Venerable sir, this venerable one has an eye disease. We are attending to him as he relieves himself of both feces and urine.” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow eye-ointment—black eye-ointment, compound eye-ointment, antimony eye-ointment, red ochre, and soot.” There was a need for ingredients for grinding with the eye-ointment. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Monks, I allow sandalwood, tagara, kāḷānusāriya, tālīsa, and bhaddamuttaka.” At that time, monks placed ground eye-ointments in small bowls and saucers; they became mixed with grass dust and dirt. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Monks, I allow an eye-ointment container.”

Tena [M 0.0295] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāvacā añjaniyo dhārenti – sovaṇṇamayaṃ, rūpiyamayaṃ. Manussā ujjhāyanti [T 2.0046] khiyyanti vipācenti – “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, uccāvacā añjanī dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhimayaṃ, dantamayaṃ, visāṇamayaṃ, naḷamayaṃ, veḷumayaṃ, kaṭṭhamayaṃ, jatumayaṃ, phalamayaṃ, lohamayaṃ, saṅkhanābhimayanti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six were carrying various kinds of ointment containers—made of gold, made of silver. People complained, criticized, and spread it about: “Just like householders indulging in sensual pleasures.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, various kinds of ointment containers should not be carried. Whoever carries one incurs an offense of wrong-doing. Monks, I allow those made of bone, ivory, horn, reed, bamboo, wood, lac, crystal, bronze, or conch-shell core.”

Tena kho pana samayena añjaniyo apārutā honti, tiṇacuṇṇehipi paṃsukehipi okiriyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, apidhānanti. Apidhānaṃ nipatati[V 0.0279]. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, suttakena bandhitvā añjaniyā bandhitunti. Añjanī phalati nipatati (ka.). Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, suttakena sibbetunti.

At that time, the ointment containers were open and were strewn with grass dust and dirt. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a cover.” The cover fell off. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow tying it with a thread to the ointment container.” The ointment container broke. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow sewing it with a thread.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū aṅguliyā añjanti, akkhīni dukkhāni honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, añjanisalākanti.

At that time, monks were applying ointment with their fingers, and their eyes became sore. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow an ointment applicator.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāvacā añjanisalākāyo dhārenti – sovaṇṇamayaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ. Manussā [P 1.0204] ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti, “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, uccāvacā añjanisalākā dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhimayaṃ…pe… saṅkhanābhimayanti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six were carrying various kinds of ointment applicators—made of gold, made of silver. People complained, criticized, and spread it about: “Just like householders enjoying sensual pleasures.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, various kinds of ointment applicators should not be carried. Whoever carries one, commits an offense of wrong-doing. Monks, I allow those made of bone…of conch-shell core.”

Tena kho pana samayena añjanisalākā bhūmiyaṃ patitā pharusā hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[T 2.0047]. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, salākaṭhāniyanti salākodhāniyanti (sī. syā.).

At that time, an ointment applicator, having fallen on the ground, became rough. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow an applicator holder.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū añjanimpi añjanisalākampi hatthena pariharanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, añjanitthavikanti. Aṃsabaddhako na hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṃsabaddhakaṃ bandhanasuttakanti.

At that time, monks carried both the ointment pot and the ointment applicator in their hands. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow an ointment bag.” There was no shoulder strap. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a shoulder strap and a tying string.”

266. Tena [M 0.0296] kho pana samayena āyasmato pilindavacchassa sīsābhitāpo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, muddhani telakanti. Nakkhamaniyo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, natthukammanti. Natthu galati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, natthukaraṇinti.

266. At that time, the Venerable Pilindavaccha was suffering from a head ailment. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow oil for the head.” It was not effective. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow nasal treatment.” The nasal medication dripped out. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a nasal inhaler.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāvacā natthukaraṇiyo dhārenti – sovaṇṇamayaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti, “seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, uccāvacā natthukaraṇī dhāretabbā. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhimayaṃ…pe… saṅkhanābhimayanti. Natthuṃ visamaṃ āsiñcanti natthu visamaṃ āsiñciyati (sī. syā.). Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave[V 0.0280], yamakanatthukaraṇinti. Nakkhamaniyo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dhūmaṃ pātunti. Taññeva vaṭṭiṃ ālimpetvā pivanti[T 2.0048], kaṇṭho dahati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dhūmanettanti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six used various kinds of nasal inhalers—some made of gold, some made of silver. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, various kinds of nasal inhalers are not to be used. Whoever should use one, commits an offense of wrong-doing. Monks, I allow those made of bone… or made of conch-shell.” They applied the nasal medicine unevenly. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a double-nasal inhaler.” It was not effective. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow the inhalation of smoke.” They lit that very wick and inhaled, burning their throats. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a smoke-inhalation pipe.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū uccāvacāni dhūmanettāni dhārenti – sovaṇṇamayaṃ rūpiyamayaṃ. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, uccāvacāni dhūmanettāni dhāretabbāni. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhimayaṃ…pe… saṅkhanābhimayanti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six used various kinds of smoke-inhalation pipes—some made of gold, some made of silver. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, various kinds of smoke-inhalation pipes are not to be used. Whoever should use one, commits an offense of wrong-doing. Monks, I allow those made of bone… or made of conch-shell.”

Tena kho pana samayena dhūmanettāni apārutāni honti, pāṇakā pavisanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, apidhānanti.

At that time, the smoke-inhalation pipes were uncovered, and insects entered them. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a lid.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū dhūmanettāni hatthena pariharanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dhūmanettathavikanti. Ekato ghaṃsiyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yamakathavikanti. Aṃsabaddhako na hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṃsabaddhakaṃ bandhanasuttakanti.

At that time, monks carried smoke-inhalation pipes by hand. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a bag for the smoke-inhalation pipe.” They were abraded on one side. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a double bag.” There was no shoulder strap. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a shoulder strap and a fastening cord.”

267. Tena [M 0.0297] kho pana samayena āyasmato pilindavacchassa vātābādho [P 1.0205] hoti. Vejjā evamāhaṃsu – “telaṃ pacitabba”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, telapākanti. Tasmiṃ kho pana telapāke majjaṃ pakkhipitabbaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, telapāke majjaṃ pakkhipitunti.

267. At that time, the Venerable Pilindavaccha was suffering from a wind-illness. The physicians said, “Oil should be cooked.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow cooked oil.” Now, in that cooked oil, an intoxicant had to be added. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow an intoxicant to be added to cooked oil.”

Tena [T 2.0049] kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū atipakkhittamajjāni atikhittamajjāni (ka.) telāni pacanti, tāni pivitvā majjanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, atipakkhittamajjaṃ telaṃ pātabbaṃ. Yo piveyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yasmiṃ telapāke majjassa na vaṇṇo na gandho na raso paññāyati, evarūpaṃ majjapakkhittaṃ telaṃ pātunti.

At that time, the monks of the group of six were cooking oils with an excessive amount of intoxicant, and having drunk them, they became intoxicated. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, oil with an excessive amount of intoxicant is not to be drunk. Whoever should drink it is to be dealt with according to the Dhamma. Monks, I allow the drinking of oil with intoxicant added in which the color, smell, and taste of the intoxicant are not apparent.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhūnaṃ bahuṃ atipakkhittamajjaṃ telaṃ pakkaṃ hoti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ [V 0.0281] etadahosi – “kathaṃ nu kho atipakkhittamajje tele paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, abbhañjanaṃ adhiṭṭhātunti.

At that time, the monks had a large quantity of cooked oil with an excessive amount of intoxicant. Then this thought occurred to the monks: “How indeed should we act regarding this oil with an excessive amount of intoxicant?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow it to be determined for use as an ointment.”

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato pilindavacchassa bahutaraṃ telaṃ pakkaṃ hoti, telabhājanaṃ na vijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tīṇi tumbāni – lohatumbaṃ, kaṭṭhatumbaṃ, phalatumbanti.

At that time, the Venerable Pilindavaccha had a very large quantity of cooked oil, but there was no oil container. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow three kinds of containers: a metal container, a wooden container, and a fruit-gourd container.”

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato pilindavacchassa aṅgavāto hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sedakammanti. Nakkhamaniyo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sambhārasedanti. Nakkhamaniyo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mahāsedanti. Nakkhamaniyo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhaṅgodakanti. Nakkhamaniyo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udakakoṭṭhakanti.

Now at that time, the Venerable Pilindavaccha had a wind disease in the limbs. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow the act of inducing sweat.” It was not sufficient. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow inducing sweat with various kinds of leaves.” It was not sufficient. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a great sweat-inducing treatment.” It was not sufficient. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow water boiled with various kinds of leaves.” It was not sufficient. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow inducing sweat in a large water vessel.”

Tena [T 2.0050] kho pana samayena āyasmato pilindavacchassa pabbavāto hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, lohitaṃ [M 0.0298] mocetunti. Nakkhamaniyo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, lohitaṃ mocetvā visāṇena gāhetunti gahetunti (sī. syā.).

Now at that time, the Venerable Pilindavaccha had a wind disease in the joints. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow the letting of blood.” It was not sufficient. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow, after letting the blood, to draw it with a horn.”

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato pilindavacchassa pādā phalitā phālitā (ka.) honti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pādabbhañjananti. Nakkhamaniyo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pajjaṃ abhisaṅkharitunti.

Now at that time, the feet of the Venerable Pilindavaccha were cracked. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow a foot-anointing oil.' It was not bearable. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow the preparation of a foot remedy.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno gaṇḍābādho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, satthakammanti. Kasāvodakena attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kasāvodakanti. Tilakakkena attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tilakakkanti. Kabaḷikāya attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kabaḷikanti. Vaṇabandhanacoḷena attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vaṇabandhanacoḷanti. Vaṇo kaṇḍuvati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sāsapakuṭṭena sāsapakuḍḍena (sī. syā.) phositunti. Vaṇo kilijjittha. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi[P 1.0206], bhikkhave, dhūmaṃ [V 0.0282] kātunti. Vaḍḍhamaṃsaṃ vuṭṭhāti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, loṇasakkharikāya chinditunti. Vaṇo na ruhati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vaṇatelanti. Telaṃ galati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi[T 2.0051], bhikkhave, vikāsikaṃ sabbaṃ vaṇapaṭikammanti.

At that time, a certain monk had a boil. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow lancing.' There was a need for astringent water. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow astringent water.' There was a need for sesame paste. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow sesame paste.' There was a need for a compress. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow a compress.' There was a need for a wound-binding cloth. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow a wound-binding cloth.' The wound itched. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow sprinkling with mustard powder.' The wound festered. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow fumigation.' Proud flesh grew on the wound. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow cutting it with a razor.' The wound did not heal. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow wound oil.' The oil dripped. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow a bandage and all kinds of wound treatment.'

268. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu ahinā daṭṭho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cattāri mahāvikaṭāni dātuṃ – gūthaṃ, muttaṃ, chārikaṃ, mattikanti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “appaṭiggahitāni nu kho udāhu paṭiggahetabbānī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sati kappiyakārake paṭiggahāpetuṃ, asati kappiyakārake sāmaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjitunti.

268. At that time, a certain monk was bitten by a snake. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow the giving of four great potent remedies—dung, urine, ashes, and clay.' Then this thought occurred to the monks: 'Are these things that need not be formally received, or must they be formally received?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow that if a designated lay attendant is present, you are to have it formally offered by them; if a designated lay attendant is not present, you may take it yourselves and use it.'

Tena [M 0.0299] kho pana samayena aññatarena bhikkhunā visaṃ pītaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi bhikkhave gūthaṃ pāyetunti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “appaṭiggahitaṃ nu kho udāhu paṭiggahetabbo”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yaṃ karonto paṭiggaṇhāti, sveva paṭiggaho kato, na puna kato pana (?) paṭiggahetabboti.

At that time, a certain monk had drunk poison. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow excrement to be drunk.' Then this thought occurred to the monks: 'Should it be formally received or not?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow that when the one producing it receives it, that itself is the formal receiving; it need not be formally received again.'

269. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno gharadinnakābādho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sītāloḷiṃ pāyetunti.

269. At that time, a certain monk had an illness caused by medicine given by a householder. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow earth from a ploughshare to be mixed with water and drunk.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu duṭṭhagahaṇiko hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āmisakhāraṃ pāyetunti.

At that time, a certain monk suffered from indigestion. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow lye made from burnt rice to be drunk.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno paṇḍurogābādho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[T 2.0052]. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, muttaharītakaṃ pāyetunti.

At that time, a certain monk was afflicted with jaundice. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow myrobalan soaked in cow urine to be drunk.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno chavidosābādho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gandhālepaṃ kātunti.

At that time, a certain monk had a skin disease. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow the application of scented ointment.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu abhisannakāyo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[V 0.0283]. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, virecanaṃ pātunti. Acchakañjiyā attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, acchakañjinti. Akaṭayūsena attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, akaṭayūsanti. Kaṭākaṭena attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kaṭākaṭanti. Paṭicchādanīyena attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paṭicchādanīyanti.

At that time, a certain monk had a body with corrupted humors. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow the taking of a purgative.' There was a need for clear rice gruel. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow clear rice gruel.' There was a need for unstrained bean soup. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow unstrained bean soup.' There was a need for partially strained bean soup. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow partially strained bean soup.' There was a need for meat broth. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow meat broth.'

Mūlādibhesajjakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on medicines, beginning with roots, is concluded.

162. Pilindavacchavatthu

162. The Story of Pilindavaccha

270. idaṃ vatthu pārā. 618 ādayo Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā pilindavaccho rājagahe pabbhāraṃ sodhāpeti leṇaṃ kattukāmo. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo [M 0.0300] bimbisāro yenāyasmā pilindavaccho tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ pilindavacchaṃ [P 1.0207] abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro āyasmantaṃ pilindavacchaṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ, bhante, thero kārāpetī”ti? “Pabbhāraṃ, mahārāja, sodhāpemi, leṇaṃ kattukāmo”ti. “Attho, bhante, ayyassa [T 2.0053] ārāmikenā”ti? “Na kho, mahārāja, bhagavatā ārāmiko anuññāto”ti. “Tena hi, bhante, bhagavantaṃ paṭipucchitvā mama āroceyyāthā”ti. ‘Evaṃ, mahārājā’ti kho āyasmā pilindavaccho rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa paccassosi. Atha kho āyasmā pilindavaccho rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ seniyaṃ bimbisāraṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi, samādapesi, samuttejesi, sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro āyasmatā pilindavacchena dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito uṭṭhāyāsanā āyasmantaṃ pilindavacchaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

270. Now at that time the Venerable Pilindavaccha was having a mountain slope cleared at Rājagaha, wishing to make a cave-dwelling. Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha approached the Venerable Pilindavaccha, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha said this to the Venerable Pilindavaccha: “Venerable sir, what is the elder having done?” “Great king, I am having a mountain slope cleared, wishing to make a cave-dwelling.” “Venerable sir, does the noble one have need of a monastery attendant?” “Great king, a monastery attendant has not been permitted by the Blessed One.” “In that case, venerable sir, please inquire of the Blessed One and inform me.” ‘Very well, great king,’ the Venerable Pilindavaccha consented to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha. Then the Venerable Pilindavaccha instructed, urged, inspired, and gladdened King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha with a Dhamma talk. Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, having been instructed, urged, inspired, and gladdened by the Venerable Pilindavaccha with a Dhamma talk, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Venerable Pilindavaccha, circumambulated him, and departed.

Atha kho āyasmā pilindavaccho bhagavato santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – “rājā, bhante, māgadho seniyo bimbisāro ārāmikaṃ dātukāmo. Kathaṃ nu kho, bhante, mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ārāmika”nti. Dutiyampi kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro yenāyasmā pilindavaccho tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ pilindavacchaṃ [V 0.0284] abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro āyasmantaṃ pilindavacchaṃ etadavoca – “anuññāto, bhante, bhagavatā ārāmiko”ti? “Evaṃ, mahārājā”ti. “Tena hi, bhante, ayyassa ārāmikaṃ dammī”ti.
