Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro [T 2.0054] āyasmato pilindavacchassa ārāmikaṃ paṭissutvā, vissaritvā, cirena satiṃ paṭilabhitvā, aññataraṃ sabbatthakaṃ mahāmattaṃ āmantesi – “yo mayā, bhaṇe, ayyassa ārāmiko paṭissuto, dinno so ārāmiko”ti? “Na kho, deva, ayyassa ārāmiko dinno”ti. “Kīva ciraṃ nu kho, bhaṇe, ito ito ratti (syā.) hi taṃ hotī”ti? Atha kho so [M 0.0301] mahāmatto rattiyo gaṇetvā vigaṇetvā (sī.) rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ seniyaṃ bimbisāraṃ etadavoca – “pañca, deva, rattisatānī”ti. Tena hi, bhaṇe, ayyassa pañca ārāmikasatāni dehīti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho so mahāmatto rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa paṭissutvā āyasmato pilindavacchassa pañca ārāmikasatāni pādāsi, pāṭiyekko gāmo nivisi. ‘Ārāmikagāmakoti’pi naṃ āhaṃsu[P 1.0208], ‘pilindagāmako’tipi naṃ āhaṃsu.

Then the Venerable Pilindavaccha sent a messenger to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha wishes to give a monastery attendant. How should I proceed, venerable sir?” Then the Blessed One, having given a Dhamma talk on this occasion and in connection with this matter, addressed the monks: “I allow, monks, a monastery attendant.” For a second time, King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha approached the Venerable Pilindavaccha; having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Pilindavaccha and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha said this to the Venerable Pilindavaccha: “Venerable sir, has a monastery attendant been permitted by the Blessed One?” “Yes, great king.” “In that case, venerable sir, I will give a monastery attendant to the venerable one.” Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, having promised a monastery attendant to the Venerable Pilindavaccha, forgot, and after a long time, he remembered. He addressed a certain chief minister in charge of all affairs: “Good sir, the monastery attendant I promised to the venerable one, has that monastery attendant been given?” “No, Your Majesty, the monastery attendant has not been given to the venerable one.” “How long has it been, good sir, since then?” Then that chief minister counted the nights and said to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha: “Five hundred nights, Your Majesty.” “In that case, good sir, give the venerable one five hundred monastery attendants.” “Yes, Your Majesty,” that chief minister replied to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha and gave five hundred monastery attendants to the Venerable Pilindavaccha. A separate village was established. They called it ‘Ārāmikagāmaka’ (Monastery Attendant Village), and they also called it ‘Pilindagāmaka’ (Pilinda’s small village).

271. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā pilindavaccho tasmiṃ gāmake kulūpako hoti. Atha kho āyasmā pilindavaccho pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya pilindagāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Tena kho pana samayena tasmiṃ gāmake ussavo hoti. Dārakā alaṅkatā mālākitā kīḷanti. Atha kho āyasmā pilindavaccho pilindagāmake [T 2.0055] sapadānaṃ piṇḍāya caramāno yena aññatarassa ārāmikassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Tena kho pana samayena tassā ārāmikiniyā dhītā aññe dārake alaṅkate mālākite passitvā rodati – ‘mālaṃ me detha, alaṅkāraṃ me dethā’ti. Atha kho āyasmā pilindavaccho taṃ ārāmikiniṃ etadavoca – “kissāyaṃ dārikā rodatī”ti? “Ayaṃ, bhante, dārikā aññe dārake alaṅkate mālākite passitvā rodati – ‘mālaṃ me detha, alaṅkāraṃ me dethā’ti. Kuto amhākaṃ duggatānaṃ mālā, kuto alaṅkāro”ti? Atha kho āyasmā pilindavaccho aññataraṃ tiṇaṇḍupakaṃ gahetvā taṃ ārāmikiniṃ etadavoca – “handimaṃ tiṇaṇḍupakaṃ tassā dārikāya sīse paṭimuñcā”ti. Atha kho sā ārāmikinī taṃ tiṇaṇḍupakaṃ gahetvā tassā dārikāya sīse paṭimuñci. Sā ahosi suvaṇṇamālā abhirūpā, dassanīyā, pāsādikā; natthi tādisā raññopi antepure suvaṇṇamālā. Manussā rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa ārocesuṃ – “amukassa, deva, ārāmikassa ghare suvaṇṇamālā abhirūpā, dassanīyā, pāsādikā; natthi tādisā devassapi [V 0.0285] antepure suvaṇṇamālā; kuto tassa duggatassa? Nissaṃsayaṃ corikāya ābhatā”ti.

271. Now at that time, the Venerable Pilindavaccha was a frequent guest in that village. Then, the Venerable Pilindavaccha, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and entered the village of Pilinda for alms. Now at that time, there was a festival in that village. Children, adorned and garlanded, were playing. Then, the Venerable Pilindavaccha, walking for alms from house to house in the village of Pilinda, approached the dwelling of a certain monastery attendant and sat down on the prepared seat. Now at that time, the daughter of that female monastery attendant, seeing other children adorned and garlanded, cried: “Give me a garland! Give me an ornament!” Then, the Venerable Pilindavaccha said to that female monastery attendant: “Why is this girl crying?” “Venerable sir, this girl sees other children adorned and garlanded and cries: ‘Give me a garland! Give me an ornament!’ But where would we poor people get a garland or an ornament?” Then, the Venerable Pilindavaccha took a coil of grass and said to that female monastery attendant: “Here, place this coil of grass on the girl’s head.” Then, that female monastery attendant took the coil of grass and placed it on the girl’s head. It became a golden garland—beautiful, lovely, and pleasing. There was no such golden garland even in the king’s inner palace. People informed King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha: “Sire, in the house of such-and-such a monastery attendant, there is a golden garland—beautiful, lovely, and pleasing. There is no such golden garland even in your inner palace. How could such a poor person have it? Surely, it must have been obtained by theft!”

Atha [M 0.0302] kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro taṃ ārāmikakulaṃ bandhāpesi. Dutiyampi [T 2.0056] kho āyasmā pilindavaccho pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya pilindagāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Pilindagāmake sapadānaṃ piṇḍāya caramāno yena tassa ārāmikassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paṭivissake pucchi – “kahaṃ imaṃ ārāmikakulaṃ gata”nti? “Etissā, bhante, suvaṇṇamālāya kāraṇā raññā bandhāpita”nti. Atha kho āyasmā pilindavaccho yena rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro yenāyasmā pilindavaccho tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ pilindavacchaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho [P 1.0209] rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ seniyaṃ bimbisāraṃ āyasmā pilindavaccho etadavoca – “kissa, mahārāja, ārāmikakulaṃ bandhāpita”nti? “Tassa, bhante, ārāmikassa ghare suvaṇṇamālā abhirūpā, dassanīyā, pāsādikā; natthi tādisā amhākampi antepure suvaṇṇamālā; kuto tassa duggatassa? Nissaṃsayaṃ corikāya ābhatā”ti. Atha kho āyasmā pilindavaccho rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa pāsādaṃ suvaṇṇanti adhimucci; so ahosi sabbasovaṇṇamayo. “Idaṃ pana te, mahārāja, tāva bahuṃ suvaṇṇaṃ kuto”ti? ‘Aññātaṃ, bhante, ayyasseveso [T 2.0057] iddhānubhāvo’ti taṃ ārāmikakulaṃ muñcāpesi.

Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha had that groundskeeper’s family arrested. On the second day, the Venerable Pilindavaccha, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, entered the village of Pilinda for alms. While wandering for alms from house to house in the village of Pilinda, he approached the dwelling of that groundskeeper. Having approached, he asked the neighbors, “Where has this groundskeeper’s family gone?” “Venerable sir, because of that golden garland, the king had them arrested.” Then the Venerable Pilindavaccha approached the palace of King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha approached the Venerable Pilindavaccha; having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Pilindavaccha and sat down to one side. The Venerable Pilindavaccha then said this to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, who was sitting to one side: “Great King, why was the groundskeeper’s family arrested?” “Venerable sir, in that groundskeeper’s house there was a golden garland—beautiful, lovely, and splendid. There is no such golden garland even in our inner palace. From where would that poor person get it? Without a doubt, it was brought by theft.” Then the Venerable Pilindavaccha willed the palace of King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha to be golden, and it became entirely made of gold. “Great King, from where, then, did you obtain this much gold?” “I understand, venerable sir. This is the venerable one’s psychic power.” And he had that groundskeeper’s family released.

Manussā “ayyena kira pilindavacchena sarājikāya parisāya uttarimanussadhammaṃ iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ dassita”nti attamanā abhippasannā āyasmato pilindavacchassa pañca bhesajjāni abhihariṃsu, seyyathidaṃ – sappiṃ, navanītaṃ, telaṃ, madhuṃ sappi navanītaṃ telaṃ madhu (ka.), phāṇitaṃ. Pakatiyāpi ca āyasmā pilindavaccho lābhī hoti pañcannaṃ bhesajjānaṃ; laddhaṃ laddhaṃ parisāya vissajjeti. Parisā cassa hoti bāhullikā; laddhaṃ laddhaṃ kolambepi koḷumbepi (ka.), ghaṭepi, pūretvā paṭisāmeti; parissāvanānipi, thavikāyopi, pūretvā vātapānesu laggeti. Tāni olīnavilīnāni tiṭṭhanti. Undūrehipi vihārā okiṇṇavikiṇṇā honti. Manussā vihāracārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā passitvā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “antokoṭṭhāgārikā ime samaṇā sakyaputtiyā[M 0.0303], seyyathāpi rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā, te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti [V 0.0286] vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhū evarūpāya bāhullāya cetessantī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū te anekapariyāyena vigarahitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū evarūpāya bāhullāya cetentī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavāti…pe… vigarahitvā dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “yāni kho pana tāni gilānānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ [T 2.0058] paṭisāyanīyāni bhesajjāni, seyyathidaṃ – sappi, navanītaṃ, telaṃ, madhu, phāṇitaṃ, tāni paṭiggahetvā sattāhaparamaṃ sannidhikārakaṃ paribhuñjitabbāni. Taṃ atikkāmayato yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.

The people, delighted and exceedingly faithful, thinking, 'It is said that the venerable Pilindavaccha has displayed a superhuman state, a miracle of psychic power, in the assembly with the king,' brought forward the five medicines to the venerable Pilindavaccha: that is, ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, and molasses. And by nature, the venerable Pilindavaccha was a receiver of the five medicines; whatever he received, he gave away to his retinue. His retinue, for its part, was given to accumulation; whatever they received, they stored in water pots and jars, filling them up and putting them aside. They also filled water strainers and bags and hung them in the windows. Those medicines remained smeared and stuck. The monasteries were also strewn about by rats. People wandering on a tour of the monasteries saw this and complained, grumbled, and criticized: 'These recluses, sons of the Sakyan, have an inner granary, just like King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha!' The monks heard those people complaining, grumbling, and criticizing. Those monks who were of few desires complained, grumbled, and criticized: 'How indeed can monks strive for such abundance?' Then those monks, after rebuking them in many ways, reported this matter to the Blessed One… 'Is it true, it is said, O monks, that monks strive for such abundance?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' … Having rebuked them and given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: 'There are those medicines that are to be consumed by sick monks—that is, ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, and molasses. Having accepted them, they are to be consumed having been stored for a maximum of seven days. One who exceeds that is to be dealt with according to the rule.'

Pilindavacchavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story of Pilindavaccha is concluded.

Bhesajjānuññātabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito paṭhamo.

The first recitation section on the allowance of medicines is concluded.

163. Guḷādianujānanā

163. The Allowance of Molasses, etc.

272. Atha kho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā [P 1.0210] yena rājagahaṃ tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Addasā kho āyasmā kaṅkhārevato antarāmagge guḷakaraṇaṃ, okkamitvā guḷe piṭṭhampi chārikampi pakkhipante, disvāna “akappiyo guḷo sāmiso, na kappati guḷo vikāle paribhuñjitu”nti kukkuccāyanto sapariso guḷaṃ na paribhuñjati. Yepissa sotabbaṃ maññanti, tepi guḷaṃ na paribhuñjanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Kimatthāya kimatthiyā (ka.), bhikkhave, guḷe piṭṭhampi chārikampi pakkhipantīti? Thaddhatthāya bandhanatthāya (sī. syā.) bhagavāti. Sace, bhikkhave, thaddhatthāya guḷe piṭṭhampi chārikampi pakkhipanti, so ca guḷotveva saṅkhaṃ gacchati. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yathāsukhaṃ guḷaṃ paribhuñjitunti.

272. Then the Blessed One, having stayed in Sāvatthī for as long as he wished, set out on a journey towards Rājagaha. On the way, the Venerable Kaṅkhārevata entered a shed where jaggery was being made and saw them adding flour and ash to the jaggery. Having seen this, being scrupulous, he thought, 'This jaggery with admixture is not allowable; it is not allowable to consume jaggery at the wrong time.' He and his retinue did not consume the jaggery. Those bhikkhus who thought he should be listened to also did not consume the jaggery. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. The Blessed One asked, 'For what purpose, Bhikkhus, do they add flour and ash to the jaggery?' 'For the purpose of firmness, Blessed One.' 'If, Bhikkhus, they add flour and ash to the jaggery for the purpose of firmness, it is reckoned only as jaggery. I allow you, Bhikkhus, to consume jaggery as you please.'

Addasā kho āyasmā kaṅkhārevato antarāmagge vacce muggaṃ jātaṃ, passitvā “akappiyā muggā; pakkāpi muggā jāyantīti” kukkuccāyanto sapariso muggaṃ na paribhuñjati. Yepissa sotabbaṃ maññanti, tepi muggaṃ na paribhuñjanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Sace sacepi (?), bhikkhave, pakkāpi muggā jāyanti[T 2.0059], anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yathāsukhaṃ muggaṃ paribhuñjitunti.

The Venerable Kaṅkhārevata saw mung beans that had sprouted in excrement on the way. Having seen this, being scrupulous, he thought, 'Mung beans are not allowable; even when cooked, mung beans sprout.' He and his retinue did not consume the mung beans. Those bhikkhus who thought he should be listened to also did not consume the mung beans. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'If, Bhikkhus, mung beans sprout even when cooked, I allow you, Bhikkhus, to consume mung beans as you please.'

273. Tena [M 0.0304] kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno udaravātābādho hoti. So loṇasovīrakaṃ apāyi. Tassa so udaravātābādho paṭippassambhi. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[V 0.0287]. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānassa loṇasovīrakaṃ; agilānassa udakasambhinnaṃ pānaparibhogena paribhuñjitunti.

273. Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu had an illness of wind in the stomach. He drank loṇasovīraka. That illness of wind in the stomach subsided for him. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'I allow, Bhikkhus, loṇasovīraka for one who is sick; for one who is not sick, I allow it to be consumed as a drink mixed with water.'

Guḷādianujānanā niṭṭhitā.

The allowance concerning jaggery and so forth is concluded.

164. Antovuṭṭhādipaṭikkhepakathā

164. The Discourse on the Prohibition of What is Stored Inside, and So Forth

274. Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena rājagahaṃ tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavato udaravātābādho hoti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando – ‘pubbepi bhagavato udaravātābādho tekaṭulayāguyā phāsu hotī’ti – sāmaṃ tilampi, taṇḍulampi, muggampi viññāpetvā, anto vāsetvā, anto sāmaṃ pacitvā bhagavato upanāmesi – “pivatu bhagavā tekaṭulayāgu”nti. Jānantāpi tathāgatā pucchanti, jānantāpi na pucchanti; kālaṃ viditvā pucchanti, kālaṃ viditvā na pucchanti; atthasaṃhitaṃ tathāgatā pucchanti, no anatthasaṃhitaṃ. Anatthasaṃhite setughāto tathāgatānaṃ. Dvīhi ākārehi buddhā bhagavanto bhikkhū paṭipucchanti – dhammaṃ vā desessāma, sāvakānaṃ vā sikkhāpadaṃ paññapessāmāti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ [P 1.0211] ānandaṃ āmantesi – “kutāyaṃ, ānanda[T 2.0060], yāgū”ti? Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – ‘ananucchavikaṃ, ānanda, ananulomikaṃ, appatirūpaṃ, assāmaṇakaṃ, akappiyaṃ, akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, ānanda, evarūpāya bāhullāya cetessasi. Yadapi, ānanda, anto vuṭṭhaṃ vutthaṃ (sī. syā. ka.) tadapi akappiyaṃ; yadapi anto pakkaṃ tadapi akappiyaṃ; yadapi sāmaṃ pakkaṃ, tadapi akappiyaṃ. Netaṃ, ānanda, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, anto vuṭṭhaṃ, anto pakkaṃ, sāmaṃ pakkaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo paribhuñjeya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anto ce, bhikkhave, vuṭṭhaṃ, anto pakkaṃ, sāmaṃ pakkaṃ tañce paribhuñjeyya, āpatti tiṇṇaṃ dukkaṭānaṃ. Anto ce, bhikkhave, vuṭṭhaṃ, anto pakkaṃ, aññehi pakkaṃ, tañce paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dvinnaṃ dukkaṭānaṃ. Anto [M 0.0305] ce, bhikkhave, vuṭṭhaṃ, bahi pakkaṃ, sāmaṃ pakkaṃ, tañce paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dvinnaṃ dukkaṭānaṃ. Bahi ce, bhikkhave, vuṭṭhaṃ, anto pakkaṃ, sāmaṃ pakkaṃ, tañce paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dvinnaṃ dukkaṭānaṃ. Anto ce, bhikkhave, vuṭṭhaṃ, bahi pakkaṃ, aññehi pakkaṃ, tañce paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Bahi ce, bhikkhave, vuṭṭhaṃ, anto pakkaṃ, aññehi pakkaṃ, tañce paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Bahi ce, bhikkhave, vuṭṭhaṃ, bahi pakkaṃ, sāmaṃ pakkaṃ, tañce paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Bahi ce, bhikkhave, vuṭṭhaṃ, bahi pakkaṃ[V 0.0288][T 2.0061], aññehi pakkaṃ, tañce paribhuñjeyya, anāpattī’”ti.

274. Then the Blessed One, wandering by degrees, arrived at Rājagaha. There the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Ground. At that time, the Blessed One was suffering from a wind ailment in his stomach. Then the Venerable Ānanda—thinking, 'Previously, the Blessed One’s wind ailment in his stomach was relieved by a three-ingredient gruel'—personally requested sesame, rice, and mung beans, stored them inside, and cooked them himself inside, and offered them to the Blessed One, saying, 'May the Blessed One drink this three-ingredient gruel.' The Tathāgatas ask questions knowing, and they do not ask questions knowing; knowing the time, they ask, and knowing the time, they do not ask. The Tathāgatas ask questions that are meaningful, not meaningless. For the Tathāgatas, meaningless talk is cut off. The Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, question the bhikkhus for two reasons: either to teach the Dhamma or to lay down a training rule for the disciples. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: 'Ānanda, where did this gruel come from?' Then the Venerable Ānanda informed the Blessed One of this matter. The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him: 'Ānanda, this is unbefitting, unsuitable, improper, not the conduct of a recluse, unallowable, and not to be done. How could you, Ānanda, strive for such abundance? Whatever is stored inside is unallowable; whatever is cooked inside is unallowable; whatever is cooked by oneself is unallowable. This, Ānanda, does not lead to the faith of the faithless…' Having rebuked him and given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus: 'Bhikkhus, one should not consume what is stored inside, cooked inside, or cooked by oneself. Whoever does so commits an offense of wrong-doing. If, Bhikkhus, something is stored inside, cooked inside, and cooked by oneself, and one consumes it, one commits three offenses of wrong-doing. If, Bhikkhus, something is stored inside, cooked inside, and cooked by others, and one consumes it, one commits two offenses of wrong-doing. If, Bhikkhus, something is stored inside, cooked outside, and cooked by oneself, and one consumes it, one commits two offenses of wrong-doing. If, Bhikkhus, something is stored outside, cooked inside, and cooked by oneself, and one consumes it, one commits two offenses of wrong-doing. If, Bhikkhus, something is stored inside, cooked outside, and cooked by others, and one consumes it, one commits an offense of wrong-doing. If, Bhikkhus, something is stored outside, cooked inside, and cooked by others, and one consumes it, one commits an offense of wrong-doing. If, Bhikkhus, something is stored outside, cooked outside, and cooked by oneself, and one consumes it, one commits an offense of wrong-doing. If, Bhikkhus, something is stored outside, cooked outside, and cooked by others, and one consumes it, there is no offense.'

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū “bhagavatā sāmaṃpāko paṭikkhitto”ti puna pāke kukkuccāyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, puna pākaṃ pacitunti.

At that time, the bhikkhus, thinking, 'The Blessed One has prohibited cooking by oneself,' felt scrupulous about re-heating food. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, 'Bhikkhus, I allow re-heating.'

Tena kho pana samayena rājagahaṃ dubbhikkhaṃ hoti. Manussā loṇampi, telampi, taṇḍulampi, khādanīyampi ārāmaṃ āharanti. Tāni bhikkhū bahi vāsenti; ukkapiṇḍakāpi khādanti, corāpi haranti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, anto vāsetunti. Anto vāsetvā bahi pācenti. Damakā parivārenti. Bhikkhū avissaṭṭhā paribhuñjanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, anto pacitunti. Dubbhikkhe kappiyakārakā bahutaraṃ haranti, appataraṃ bhikkhūnaṃ denti. Bhagavato [P 1.0212] etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sāmaṃ pacituṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, anto vuṭṭhaṃ, anto pakkaṃ, sāmaṃ pakkanti.

At that time, there was a famine in Rājagaha. People brought salt, oil, rice, and edible food to the monastery. The bhikkhus stored these things outside; vermin also ate them, and thieves also stole them. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, 'Bhikkhus, I allow storing them inside.' Having stored them inside, they cooked outside. Scavengers surrounded them. The bhikkhus ate with discomfort. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, 'Bhikkhus, I allow cooking inside.' During the famine, the attendants took more and gave less to the bhikkhus. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said, 'Bhikkhus, I allow cooking by oneself. Bhikkhus, I allow what is stored inside, what is cooked inside, and what is cooked by oneself.'

Antovuṭṭhādipaṭikkhepakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on the prohibition of what is stored inside, and so forth, is concluded.

165. Uggahitapaṭiggahaṇā

165. The Re-acceptance of Offerings

275. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū kāsīsu vassaṃvuṭṭhā rājagahaṃ gacchantā bhagavantaṃ dassanāya antarāmagge na labhiṃsu lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṃ pāripūriṃ; bahuñca phalakhādanīyaṃ [T 2.0062] ahosi; kappiyakārako ca na ahosi. Atha kho te bhikkhū kilantarūpā yena rājagahaṃ veḷuvanaṃ kalandakanivāpo, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Āciṇṇaṃ kho panetaṃ buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ āgantukehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ paṭisammodituṃ. Atha kho bhagavā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “kacci[M 0.0306], bhikkhave, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kaccittha appakilamathena addhānaṃ āgatā; kuto ca tumhe, bhikkhave, āgacchathā”ti? “Khamanīyaṃ bhagavā, yāpanīyaṃ bhagavā. Idha mayaṃ, bhante, kāsīsu vassaṃvuṭṭhā rājagahaṃ āgacchantā bhagavantaṃ dassanāya antarāmagge na labhimhā lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṃ pāripūriṃ; bahuñca phalakhādanīyaṃ [V 0.0289] ahosi; kappiyakārako ca na ahosi; tena mayaṃ kilantarūpā addhānaṃ āgatā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yattha phalakhādanīyaṃ passati, kappiyakārako ca na hoti, sāmaṃ gahetvā, haritvā, kappiyakārake passitvā, bhūmiyaṃ nikkhipitvā, paṭiggahāpetvā paribhuñjituṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uggahitaṃ paṭiggahitu”nti.

275. At that time, a number of monks who had spent the rains-residence in Kāsī were traveling to Rājagaha to see the Blessed One. Along the way, they could not obtain a sufficient supply of either coarse or fine food; and there was much fruit to eat, but there was no one to make it allowable. Then those monks, weary, approached the Blessed One at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Now it is the custom for the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, to exchange greetings with newly arrived monks. Then the Blessed One said this to those monks: “Monks, is it tolerable, is it bearable? Have you come on the long journey without fatigue? And from where, monks, have you come?” “It is tolerable, Blessed One; it is bearable, Blessed One. Venerable sir, we, having spent the rains-residence in Kāsī, while coming to Rājagaha to see the Blessed One, did not obtain a sufficient supply of either coarse or fine food along the way. And there was much fruit to eat, but there was no one to make it allowable. Therefore, we have come on the long journey, weary.” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow that where one sees fruit to eat and there is no one to make it allowable, one may take it oneself, carry it away, and after seeing a person who can make it allowable, place it on the ground, have it made allowable, and then consume it. Monks, I allow what has been taken up to be formally received.”

276. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa brāhmaṇassa navā ca tilā navañca madhu uppannā honti. Atha kho tassa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi [T 2.0063] – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ nave ca tile navañca madhuṃ buddhappamukhassa bhikkhusaṅghassa dadeyya”nti. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ paṭisammodi, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me bhavaṃ gotamo svātanāya bhattaṃ, saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena[P 1.0213]. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā pakkāmi. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo tassā rattiyā accayena paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – “kālo, bho gotama, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena tassa brāhmaṇassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi, saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā, samādapetvā, samuttejetvā, sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

276. Now at that time, for a certain brahmin, new sesame seeds and new honey had been produced. Then this thought occurred to that brahmin: 'It would be good if I were to give the new sesame seeds and new honey to the community of monks with the Buddha at its head.' Then that brahmin approached the Blessed One, and having approached, exchanged joyful greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded a pleasant and memorable conversation, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, that brahmin said this to the Blessed One: 'May the venerable Gotama accept my meal for tomorrow, together with the community of monks.' The Blessed One consented by means of silence. Then that brahmin, having understood the Blessed One's consent, departed. Then that brahmin, at the passing of that night, had excellent hard and soft food prepared and had the time announced to the Blessed One: 'It is time, venerable Gotama, the meal is ready.' Then the Blessed One, in the morning time, having put on his lower robe and taking his bowl and outer robe, went to that brahmin's residence. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the community of monks. Then that brahmin, with his own hands, served and satisfied the community of monks headed by the Buddha with excellent hard and soft food until they indicated they were satisfied. When the Blessed One had finished his meal and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, the brahmin sat down to one side. The Blessed One instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened that brahmin, who was sitting to one side, with a talk on the Dhamma. Then, rising from his seat, he departed.

Atha [M 0.0307] kho tassa brāhmaṇassa acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi – “yesaṃ kho mayā atthāya buddhappamukho bhikkhusaṅgho nimantito, ‘nave ca tile navañca madhuṃ dassāmī’ti[T 2.0064], te mayā pamuṭṭhā dātuṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ nave ca tile navañca madhuṃ kolambehi ca ghaṭehi ca ārāmaṃ harāpeyya”nti. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo nave ca tile navañca madhuṃ kolambehi ca ghaṭehi ca ārāmaṃ harāpetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yesaṃ kho mayā, bho gotama, atthāya buddhappamukho bhikkhusaṅgho nimantito, ‘nave ca tile navañca madhuṃ dassāmī’ti, te mayā pamuṭṭhā dātuṃ. Paṭiggaṇhātu me bhavaṃ gotamo nave ca tile navañca madhu”nti. Tena hi, brāhmaṇa, bhikkhūnaṃ dehīti[V 0.0290]. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū dubbhikkhe appamattakepi pavārenti, paṭisaṅkhāpi paṭikkhipanti, sabbo ca saṅgho pavārito hoti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā na paṭiggaṇhanti. Paṭiggaṇhatha, bhikkhave, paribhuñjatha. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tato nīhaṭaṃ bhuttāvinā pavāritena anatirittaṃ paribhuñjitunti.

Then, soon after the Blessed One had departed, this thought occurred to that brahmin: 'I invited the community of monks with the Buddha at its head for the purpose of giving new sesame and new honey, but I have forgotten to give them. Suppose I were to have the new sesame and new honey brought to the monastery in pails and jars.' Then that brahmin had new sesame and new honey brought to the monastery in pails and jars. He approached the Blessed One, and having approached, stood to one side. Standing to one side, that brahmin said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Gotama, I invited the community of monks with the Buddha at its head for the purpose of giving new sesame and new honey, but I have forgotten to give them. May the Venerable Gotama accept from me the new sesame and new honey.' 'In that case, brahmin, give it to the monks.' Now at that time, during a famine, the monks would indicate they had had enough even with a small amount; reflecting, they would decline, and the entire Saṅgha had already indicated their satisfaction. The monks, being scrupulous, did not accept it. 'Accept it, monks, and consume it. I allow, monks, that food brought from that occasion may be consumed by one who has eaten and indicated satisfaction, without it having been made a leftover.'

Uggahitapaṭiggahaṇā niṭṭhitā.

The section on Taking Up and Receiving is concluded.

166. Paṭiggahitādianujānanā

166. Allowance Concerning What Has Been Received, and so forth

277. pāci. 295 Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato upanandassa sakyaputtassa upaṭṭhākakulaṃ saṅghassatthāya khādanīyaṃ pāhesi – ayyassa upanandassa dassetvā saṅghassa dātabbanti. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā upanando sakyaputto [P 1.0214] gāmaṃ piṇḍāya paviṭṭho hoti[T 2.0065]. Atha kho te manussā ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhū pucchiṃsu – “kahaṃ, bhante, ayyo upanando”ti? “Esāvuso, āyasmā upanando sakyaputto gāmaṃ piṇḍāya paviṭṭho”ti. “Idaṃ, bhante, khādanīyaṃ ayyassa upanandassa dassetvā saṅghassa dātabba”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Tena hi, bhikkhave, paṭiggahetvā nikkhipatha yāva upanando āgacchatīti. Atha kho āyasmā upanando sakyaputto purebhattaṃ kulāni payirupāsitvā divā āgacchati. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū dubbhikkhe appamattakepi pavārenti, paṭisaṅkhāpi paṭikkhipanti, sabbo ca saṅgho pavārito hoti, bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā na paṭiggaṇhanti. Paṭiggaṇhatha, bhikkhave, paribhuñjatha. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, purebhattaṃ paṭiggahitaṃ bhuttāvinā pavāritena anatirittaṃ paribhuñjitunti.

277. At that time, a supporter family of the Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan prince, sent some edibles for the Saṅgha, saying, “After showing them to the Venerable Upananda, they are to be given to the Saṅgha.” At that time, the Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan prince, had entered a village for alms. Then those people went to the monastery and asked the bhikkhus, “Where, venerable sirs, is the Venerable Upananda?” “Friends, this Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan prince, has entered a village for alms.” “Venerable sirs, these edibles are to be given to the Saṅgha after showing them to the Venerable Upananda.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Then, Bhikkhus, receive it and put it aside until Upananda returns.” Then the Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan prince, having visited families before the meal, returned during the day. At that time, during a famine, the bhikkhus would declare satisfaction even for small amounts and decline after reflection, and the entire Saṅgha had made the declaration of satisfaction. The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not accept it. “Receive it, Bhikkhus, and consume it. I allow, Bhikkhus, for one who has eaten and declared satisfaction to consume what was received before the meal, without it having been made a leftover.”

278. Atha [M 0.0308] kho bhagavā rājagahe yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena sāvatthi tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena sāvatthi tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato sāriputtassa kāyaḍāhābādho hoti. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “pubbe te, āvuso sāriputta, kāyaḍāhābādho kena phāsu hotī”ti? “Bhisehi ca me, āvuso[T 2.0066], muḷālikāhi cā”ti. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso sammiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva jetavane antarahito mandākiniyā pokkharaṇiyā tīre pāturahosi. Addasā kho aññataro nāgo āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ dūratova [V 0.0291] āgacchantaṃ, disvāna āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ etadavoca – “etu kho, bhante, ayyo mahāmoggallāno. Svāgataṃ, bhante, ayyassa mahāmoggallānassa. Kena, bhante, ayyassa attho; kiṃ dammī”ti? “Bhisehi ca me, āvuso, attho, muḷālikāhi cā”ti. Atha kho so nāgo aññataraṃ nāgaṃ āṇāpesi – “tena hi, bhaṇe, ayyassa bhise ca muḷālikāyo ca yāvadatthaṃ dehī”ti. Atha kho so nāgo mandākiniṃ pokkharaṇiṃ ogāhetvā, soṇḍāya bhisañca muḷālikañca abbāhitvā, suvikkhālitaṃ [P 1.0215] vikkhāletvā, bhaṇḍikaṃ bandhitvā yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva – mandākiniyā pokkharaṇiyā tīre antarahito jetavane pāturahosi. Sopi kho nāgo mandākiniyā pokkharaṇiyā tīre antarahito jetavane pāturahosi. Atha kho so nāgo āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa bhise ca muḷālikāyo [T 2.0067] ca paṭiggahāpetvā jetavane antarahito mandākiniyā pokkharaṇiyā tīre pāturahosi. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno āyasmato sāriputtassa bhise ca muḷālikāyo ca upanāmesi. Atha kho āyasmato sāriputtassa bhise ca muḷālikāyo ca bhuttassa kāyaḍāhābādho paṭippassambhi. Bahū bhisā ca [M 0.0309] muḷālikāyo ca avasiṭṭhā honti. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū dubbhikkhe appamattakepi pavārenti, paṭisaṅkhāpi paṭikkhipanti, sabbo ca saṅgho pavārito hoti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā na paṭiggaṇhanti. Paṭiggaṇhatha, bhikkhave, paribhuñjatha. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vanaṭṭhaṃ pokkharaṭṭhaṃ bhuttāvinā pavāritena anatirittaṃ paribhuñjitunti.

278. Then the Blessed One, having stayed in Rājagaha as long as he pleased, set out on a journey to Sāvatthī. Traveling in stages, he eventually arrived at Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One stayed in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. At that time, the Venerable Sāriputta was suffering from a bodily burning ailment. Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna approached the Venerable Sāriputta and said, “Friend Sāriputta, in the past, by what were you relieved of this bodily burning ailment?” “Friend, I am relieved by lotus stalks and lotus roots.” Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna—just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm—vanished from the Jeta Grove and reappeared on the shore of the Mandākinī Pond. A certain elephant saw the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna approaching from afar and, having seen him, said to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, “Let the noble Mahāmoggallāna come, venerable sir. Welcome to the noble Mahāmoggallāna, venerable sir. What does the noble one need, venerable sir? What shall I give?” “Friend, I need lotus stalks and lotus roots.” Then that elephant instructed another elephant, “Well then, friend, give the noble one as many lotus stalks and lotus roots as he needs.” Then that elephant entered the Mandākinī Pond, pulled up lotus stalks and lotus roots with its trunk, washed them thoroughly, tied them into a bundle, and approached the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna—just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm—vanished from the shore of the Mandākinī Pond and reappeared in the Jeta Grove. That elephant also vanished from the shore of the Mandākinī Pond and reappeared in the Jeta Grove. Then that elephant, having had the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna accept the lotus stalks and lotus roots, vanished from the Jeta Grove and reappeared on the shore of the Mandākinī Pond. Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna offered the lotus stalks and lotus roots to the Venerable Sāriputta. After the Venerable Sāriputta had consumed the lotus stalks and lotus roots, his bodily burning ailment subsided. Many lotus stalks and lotus roots remained. At that time, during a famine, the bhikkhus would declare satisfaction even for small amounts, or decline after reflection, and the entire Saṅgha had made the declaration of satisfaction. The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not accept them. “Accept them, Bhikkhus, and consume them. I allow, Bhikkhus, for one who has eaten and declared satisfaction to consume what grows in the forest and what grows in a lotus pond, without it having been made a leftover.”

Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyaṃ bahuṃ phalakhādanīyaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, kappiyakārako ca na hoti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā phalaṃ na paribhuñjanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, abījaṃ nibbattabījaṃ nibbaṭṭabījaṃ (sī.), nibbaṭabījaṃ (syā.), nippaṭṭabījaṃ (ka.) akatakappaṃ phalaṃ paribhuñjitunti.

At that time in Sāvatthī, a great quantity of fruit edibles had become available, but there was no one to make it allowable. The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not consume the fruit. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, Bhikkhus, to consume fruit that is without viable seeds or has had its seeds removed, without it having been made allowable.”

Paṭiggahitādi anujānanā niṭṭhitā.

The allowance concerning what has been received, and so forth, is concluded.

167. Satthakammapaṭikkhepakathā

167. The Discourse on the Prohibition of Surgical Operations

279. Atha kho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena rājagahaṃ tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena rājagahaṃ tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno bhagandalābādho [V 0.0292] hoti. Ākāsagotto vejjo satthakammaṃ [T 2.0068] karoti. Atha kho bhagavā senāsanacārikaṃ āhiṇḍanto yena tassa bhikkhuno vihāro tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho ākāsagotto vejjo bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ, disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “āgacchatu bhavaṃ gotamo, imassa bhikkhuno vaccamaggaṃ passatu, seyyathāpi godhāmukha”nti[P 1.0216]. Atha kho bhagavā – “so maṃ khvāyaṃ moghapuriso uppaṇḍetī”ti – tatova paṭinivattitvā, etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā, bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “atthi kira, bhikkhave, amukasmiṃ vihāre bhikkhu gilāno”ti? “Atthi bhagavā”ti. “Kiṃ tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ābādho”ti? “Tassa, bhante, āyasmato bhagandalābādho, ākāsagotto vejjo satthakammaṃ karotī”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ, bhikkhave, tassa moghapurisassa, ananulomikaṃ, appatirūpaṃ, assāmaṇakaṃ, akappiyaṃ, akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma so, bhikkhave, moghapuriso sambādhe satthakammaṃ kārāpessati. Sambādhe, bhikkhave, sukhumā chavi, duropayo vaṇo[M 0.0310], dupparihāraṃ satthaṃ. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, sambādhe satthakammaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ. Yo kārāpeyya, āpatti thullaccayassā”ti.

279. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Sāvatthī as long as he pleased, set out on a journey toward Rājagaha. Traveling in stages, he eventually arrived at Rājagaha. There the Blessed One stayed in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place. Now at that time, a certain monk had a fistula. The physician Ākāsagotta was performing surgery. Then the Blessed One, while on a tour of the lodgings, approached that monk’s dwelling. The physician Ākāsagotta saw the Blessed One coming from afar and, upon seeing him, said to the Blessed One: “May the venerable Gotama come and see this monk’s passage for excrement; it is like the mouth of a monitor lizard.” Then the Blessed One, thinking, “This foolish man is mocking me,” turned back from that very place. On this occasion, in this matter, he had the Saṅgha of monks assembled and questioned the monks: “Monks, is there a sick monk in such-and-such a dwelling?” “There is, Blessed One.” “Monks, what is that monk’s illness?” “Venerable sir, that venerable one has a fistula; the physician Ākāsagotta is performing surgery.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him: “Monks, for that foolish man, this is inappropriate, unsuitable, improper, unbecoming of a recluse, impermissible, not to be done. How indeed, monks, could that foolish man have surgery performed in a confined space? Monks, in a confined space, the skin is delicate, the wound is difficult to heal, and the surgical instrument is difficult to handle. This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… Having rebuked him… and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, one should not have surgery performed in a confined space. Whoever has it performed commits a grave offense.”

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū – bhagavatā satthakammaṃ paṭikkhittanti – vatthikammaṃ kārāpenti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā, te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma [T 2.0069] chabbaggiyā bhikkhū vatthikammaṃ kārāpessantī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū vatthikammaṃ kārāpentī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti…pe… vigarahitvā dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, sambādhassa sāmantā dvaṅgulā satthakammaṃ vā vatthikammaṃ vā kārāpetabbaṃ. Yo kārāpeyya, āpatti thullaccayassā”ti.

Now at that time, the monks of the group of six, thinking, 'Surgery has been prohibited by the Blessed One,' had binding performed. Those monks who were of few wishes criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying: 'How indeed can the monks of the group of six have binding performed?' Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, is it true, as is said, that the monks of the group of six are having binding performed?' 'It is true, Blessed One.' … Having rebuked them and having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: 'Monks, one should not have surgery or binding performed within two finger-breadths of a confined place. Whoever has it performed commits a grave offense.'

Satthakammapaṭikkhepakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Prohibition of Surgery is concluded.

168. Manussamaṃsapaṭikkhepakathā

168. The Account of the Prohibition of Human Flesh

280. Atha kho bhagavā rājagahe yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena bārāṇasī tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena bārāṇasī tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ viharati isipatane migadāye. Tena kho pana samayena bārāṇasiyaṃ suppiyo ca upāsako suppiyā [V 0.0293] ca upāsikā ubhatopasannā honti, dāyakā, kārakā, saṅghupaṭṭhākā. Atha kho suppiyā upāsikā ārāmaṃ gantvā vihārena vihāraṃ pariveṇena pariveṇaṃ upasaṅkamitvā bhikkhū pucchati – “ko, bhante, gilāno, kassa kiṃ āhariyatū”ti? Tena kho pana samayena aññatarena bhikkhunā virecanaṃ [P 1.0217] pītaṃ hoti. Atha kho so bhikkhu suppiyaṃ upāsikaṃ etadavoca – “mayā kho, bhagini, virecanaṃ pītaṃ. Attho me paṭicchādanīyenā”ti. “Suṭṭhu, ayya, āhariyissatī”ti gharaṃ gantvā antevāsiṃ āṇāpesi – “gaccha, bhaṇe, pavattamaṃsaṃ jānāhī”ti. Evaṃ, ayyeti kho so puriso suppiyāya [T 2.0070] upāsikāya paṭissuṇitvā kevalakappaṃ bārāṇasiṃ āhiṇḍanto na addasa pavattamaṃsaṃ. Atha kho so puriso yena suppiyā upāsikā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā suppiyaṃ upāsikaṃ etadavoca – “natthayye pavattamaṃsaṃ. Māghāto ajjā”ti. Atha kho suppiyāya upāsikāya etadahosi – “tassa kho gilānassa bhikkhuno paṭicchādanīyaṃ alabhantassa ābādho vā abhivaḍḍhissati, kālaṅkiriyā [M 0.0311] vā bhavissati. Na kho metaṃ patirūpaṃ yāhaṃ paṭissuṇitvā na harāpeyya”nti. Potthanikaṃ gahetvā ūrumaṃsaṃ ukkantitvā dāsiyā adāsi – “handa, je, imaṃ maṃsaṃ sampādetvā amukasmiṃ vihāre bhikkhu gilāno, tassa dajjāhi. Yo ca maṃ pucchati, ‘gilānā’ti paṭivedehī”ti. Uttarāsaṅgena ūruṃ veṭhetvā ovarakaṃ pavisitvā mañcake nipajji. Atha kho suppiyo upāsako gharaṃ gantvā dāsiṃ pucchi – “kahaṃ suppiyā”ti? “Esāyya ovarake nipannā”ti. Atha kho suppiyo upāsako yena suppiyā upāsikā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā suppiyaṃ upāsikaṃ etadavoca – “kissa nipannāsī”ti? “Gilānāmhī”ti. “Kiṃ te ābādho”ti? Atha kho suppiyā upāsikā suppiyassa upāsakassa etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Atha kho suppiyo upāsako – acchariyaṃ vata bho! Abbhutaṃ vata bho! Yāva saddhāyaṃ suppiyā pasannā, yatra hi nāma attanopi maṃsāni pariccattāni! Kimpimāya kiṃ panimāya (sī. syā.) aññaṃ kiñci [T 2.0071] adeyyaṃ bhavissatīti – haṭṭho udaggo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho suppiyo upāsako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ, saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho suppiyo upāsako bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho suppiyo upāsako tassā rattiyā accayena paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – “kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena suppiyassa [P 1.0218] upāsakassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi, saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena[V 0.0294]. Atha kho suppiyo upāsako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho suppiyaṃ upāsakaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “kahaṃ suppiyā”ti? “Gilānā bhagavā”ti. “Tena hi āgacchatū”ti. “Na bhagavā ussahatī”ti. “Tena hi pariggahetvāpi ānethā”ti. Atha kho suppiyo upāsako suppiyaṃ upāsikaṃ pariggahetvā [M 0.0312] ānesi. Tassā, saha dassanena bhagavato, tāva mahāvaṇo ruḷaho ahosi, succhavilomajāto. Atha kho suppiyo ca upāsako suppiyā ca upāsikā – “acchariyaṃ vata bho! Abbhutaṃ vata bho! Tathāgatassa mahiddhikatā [T 2.0072] mahānubhāvatā, yatra hi nāma saha dassanena bhagavato tāva mahāvaṇo ruḷaho bhavissati, succhavilomajāto”ti – haṭṭhā udaggā buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Atha kho bhagavā suppiyañca upāsakaṃ suppiyañca upāsikaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

280. Then the Blessed One, having stayed in Rājagaha as long as he pleased, set out on a journey towards Bārāṇasī. Traveling in stages, he arrived at Bārāṇasī. There the Blessed One stayed in the Deer Park at Isipatana near Bārāṇasī. At that time in Bārāṇasī, there were a lay follower named Suppiya and a laywoman named Suppiyā, who were both devout, generous, helpful, and supporters of the Saṅgha. Then Suppiyā the laywoman went to the monastery and, approaching from dwelling to dwelling, from compound to compound, asked the monks: “Venerable sirs, who is sick? What should be brought for whom?” At that time, a certain monk had taken a purgative. Then that monk said to Suppiyā the laywoman: “Sister, I have taken a purgative. I have need of a meat soup.” “Very well, venerable sir, it will be brought.” Having said this, she went home and instructed her attendant: “Go, my good man, and find some readily available meat.” “Yes, madam,” that man replied to Suppiyā the laywoman and, wandering all over Bārāṇasī, he did not see any readily available meat. Then that man approached Suppiyā the laywoman and, having approached, said this to her: “Madam, there is no readily available meat. Today is a day of non-slaughter.” Then this thought occurred to Suppiyā the laywoman: “For that sick monk, if he does not get the meat soup, his illness will either worsen, or he will pass away. It is not proper for me that, having promised, I should not have it brought.” Taking a small knife, she cut the flesh from her thigh and gave it to her maidservant, saying: “Here, my girl, prepare this meat and give it to the sick monk in such-and-such a monastery. And whoever asks about me, inform them, ‘She is sick.’” Having wrapped her thigh with her upper garment, she entered an inner chamber and lay down on a couch. Then Suppiya the lay follower, having gone home, asked the maidservant: “Where is Suppiyā?” “Sir, she is lying down in the inner chamber.” Then Suppiya the lay follower approached Suppiyā the laywoman and, having approached, said this to her: “Why are you lying down?” “I am sick.” “What is your ailment?” Then Suppiyā the laywoman related this matter to Suppiya the lay follower. Then Suppiya the lay follower thought: “It is wonderful, sirs! It is marvelous, sirs! How faithful and devout is Suppiyā, in that she has even given up her own flesh! What other thing could there be that would not be given by her?” Joyful and elated, he approached the Blessed One, and having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Suppiya the lay follower said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One consent to a meal from me tomorrow, together with the Saṅgha of monks.” The Blessed One consented by his silence. Then Suppiya the lay follower, having understood the Blessed One’s consent, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping his right side towards him, and departed. Then Suppiya the lay follower, at the passing of that night, had excellent hard and soft food prepared and had the time announced to the Blessed One: “It is time, venerable sir, the meal is ready.” Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and approached the residence of Suppiya the lay follower. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat, together with the Saṅgha of monks. Then Suppiya the lay follower approached the Blessed One, and having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he stood to one side. To Suppiya the lay follower standing to one side, the Blessed One said this: “Where is Suppiyā?” “She is sick, Blessed One.” “In that case, let her come.” “She is not able, Blessed One.” “In that case, carrying her, bring her.” Then Suppiya the lay follower, carrying Suppiyā the laywoman, brought her. At the very sight of the Blessed One, her great wound healed; her skin became smooth and hair grew upon it. Then Suppiya the lay follower and Suppiyā the laywoman exclaimed: “It is wonderful, sirs! It is marvelous, sirs! Such is the great psychic power and great majesty of the Tathāgata, in that at the very sight of the Blessed One, the great wound has healed, and her skin has become smooth with hair grown upon it!” Joyful and elated, with their own hands they satisfied and served the Saṅgha of monks with the Buddha at its head with excellent hard and soft food. When the Blessed One had finished his meal and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, they sat down to one side. Then the Blessed One, having instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened Suppiya the lay follower and Suppiyā the laywoman with a talk on the Dhamma, rose from his seat and departed.

Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū

Then, on that occasion, in that matter, the Blessed One had the Saṅgha of monks assembled and addressed the monks:

Paṭipucchi – “ko, bhikkhave, suppiyaṃ upāsikaṃ maṃsaṃ viññāpesī”ti? Evaṃ vutte so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ahaṃ kho, bhante, suppiyaṃ upāsikaṃ maṃsaṃ viññāpesi”nti. “Āhariyittha bhikkhū”ti? “Āhariyittha bhagavā”ti. “Paribhuñji tvaṃ bhikkhū”ti? “Paribhuñjāmahaṃ bhagavā”ti. “Paṭivekkhi tvaṃ bhikkhū”ti? “Nāhaṃ bhagavā paṭivekkhi”nti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, appaṭivekkhitvā maṃsaṃ paribhuñjissasi. Manussamaṃsaṃ kho tayā, moghapurisa, paribhuttaṃ. Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “santi, bhikkhave, manussā saddhā pasannā, tehi attanopi maṃsāni pariccattāni. Na, bhikkhave, manussamaṃsaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo paribhuñjeyya, āpatti thullaccayassa. Na ca, bhikkhave, appaṭivekkhitvā maṃsaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo [T 2.0073] paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

He questioned, “Who, monks, requested meat from Suppiyā the lay follower?” When this was said, that monk replied to the Blessed One, “I, venerable sir, requested meat from Suppiyā the lay follower.” “Was it brought, monk?” “It was brought, Blessed One.” “Did you consume it, monk?” “I consumed it, Blessed One.” “Did you investigate it, monk?” “I did not investigate it, Blessed One.” The Blessed One, the Buddha, rebuked him... “How could you, worthless man, consume meat without investigating it? You have consumed human flesh, worthless man! This, worthless man, is not for inspiring faith in the faithless...!” Having rebuked him and given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, there are faithful and devoted people who even give up their own flesh. Monks, human flesh should not be consumed. Whoever consumes it commits a grave offense. And, monks, meat should not be consumed without investigating it. Whoever consumes it commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Manussamaṃsapaṭikkhepakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Prohibition of Human Flesh is concluded.

169. Hatthimaṃsādipaṭikkhepakathā

169. The Account of the Prohibition of Elephant Meat and So Forth

281. Tena kho pana samayena rañño hatthī maranti[P 1.0219]. Manussā dubbhikkhe hatthimaṃsaṃ paribhuñjanti[V 0.0295], bhikkhūnaṃ piṇḍāya carantānaṃ hatthimaṃsaṃ denti. Bhikkhū hatthimaṃsaṃ paribhuñjanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā hatthimaṃsaṃ paribhuñjissanti. Rājaṅgaṃ hatthī, sace rājā jāneyya, na nesaṃ attamano assā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ [M 0.0313] ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, hatthimaṃsaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

281. Now at that time, the king’s elephants were dying. People, in the famine, were eating elephant meat, and they gave elephant meat to the monks going for alms. The monks ate the elephant meat. People complained, grumbled, and spread it about: “How can these Sakyan recluses eat elephant meat? An elephant is a royal emblem. If the king were to find out, he would not be pleased with them.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, elephant meat should not be eaten. Whoever eats it commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena rañño assā maranti. Manussā dubbhikkhe assamaṃsaṃ paribhuñjanti, bhikkhūnaṃ piṇḍāya carantānaṃ assamaṃsaṃ denti. Bhikkhū assamaṃsaṃ paribhuñjanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā assamaṃsaṃ paribhuñjissanti. Rājaṅgaṃ assā, sace rājā jāneyya, na nesaṃ attamano assā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, assamaṃsaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Now at that time, the king’s horses died. People, in a time of famine, were eating horse meat, and they gave horse meat to the monks who were going for alms. The monks ate the horse meat. People criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the recluses, the sons of the Sakyan, eat horse meat? A horse is an attribute of royalty. If the king were to know, he would not be pleased with them.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, horse meat is not to be eaten. Whoever should eat it, incurs an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena manussā dubbhikkhe sunakhamaṃsaṃ paribhuñjanti, bhikkhūnaṃ piṇḍāya carantānaṃ sunakhamaṃsaṃ denti. Bhikkhū sunakhamaṃsaṃ paribhuñjanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā sunakhamaṃsaṃ paribhuñjissanti, jeguccho [T 2.0074] sunakho paṭikūlo”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, sunakhamaṃsaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Now at that time, people, in a time of famine, were eating dog meat, and they gave dog meat to the monks who were going for alms. The monks ate the dog meat. People criticized, condemned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the recluses, the sons of the Sakyan, eat dog meat? A dog is disgusting and repulsive.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, dog meat is not to be eaten. Whoever should eat it, incurs an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena manussā dubbhikkhe ahimaṃsaṃ paribhuñjanti, bhikkhūnaṃ piṇḍāya carantānaṃ ahimaṃsaṃ denti. Bhikkhū ahimaṃsaṃ paribhuñjanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā ahimaṃsaṃ paribhuñjissanti, jeguccho ahi paṭikūlo”ti. Supassopi suphasso (sī.) nāgarājā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho supasso nāgarājā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “santi, bhante, nāgā assaddhā appasannā. Te appamattakehipi bhikkhū viheṭheyyuṃ. Sādhu, bhante, ayyā ahimaṃsaṃ na paribhuñjeyyu”nti. Atha kho bhagavā supassaṃ nāgarājānaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi…pe… padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ [P 1.0220] katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, ahimaṃsaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

Now at that time, people, during a famine, were consuming snake meat. When monks were wandering for alms, they gave them snake meat. The monks consumed the snake meat. People criticized, condemned, and spoke disparagingly: 'How indeed could the recluses, sons of the Sakyan, consume snake meat? A snake is disgusting and repulsive!' Then the Nāga king Supassa approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Nāga king Supassa said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, there are Nāgas who are faithless and displeased. They might harass the monks even for a trifle. It would be good, venerable sir, if the noble ones would not consume snake meat.' Then the Blessed One instructed the Nāga king Supassa with a talk on the Dhamma... and so on... After circumambulating him, he departed. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: 'Monks, snake meat is not to be consumed. Whoever should consume it, commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena [M 0.0314][V 0.0296] kho pana samayena luddakā sīhaṃ hantvā sīhamaṃsaṃ maṃsaṃ (ka.) paribhuñjanti, bhikkhūnaṃ piṇḍāya [T 2.0075] carantānaṃ sīhamaṃsaṃ denti. Bhikkhū sīhamaṃsaṃ paribhuñjitvā araññe viharanti. Sīhā sīhamaṃsagandhena bhikkhū paripātenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, sīhamaṃsaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Now at that time, hunters, having killed a lion, were consuming lion meat. When monks were wandering for alms, they gave them lion meat. The monks, having consumed the lion meat, were dwelling in the forest. Lions pursued the monks because of the smell of lion meat. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, lion meat is not to be consumed. Whoever should consume it, commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena kho pana samayena luddakā byagghaṃ hantvā…pe… dīpiṃ hantvā…pe… acchaṃ hantvā…pe… taracchaṃ hantvā taracchamaṃsaṃ paribhuñjanti, bhikkhūnaṃ piṇḍāya carantānaṃ [T 2.0076] taracchamaṃsaṃ denti. Bhikkhū taracchamaṃsaṃ paribhuñjitvā araññe viharanti. Taracchā taracchamaṃsagandhena bhikkhū paripātenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, taracchamaṃsaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

Now at that time, hunters killed a tiger… killed a leopard… killed a bear… killed a hyena and were eating the hyena meat. While on their almsround, they gave hyena meat to the monks. The monks, having eaten the hyena meat, lived in the wilderness. Hyenas, because of the smell of hyena meat, pursued the monks. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, hyena meat should not be eaten. Whoever eats it commits a dukkata offense.”

Hatthimaṃsādipaṭikkhepakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Prohibition of Elephant Meat and So Forth is concluded.

Suppiyabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito dutiyo.

The second recitation section on Suppiyā is concluded.

170. Yāgumadhugoḷakānujānanā

170. The Permission for Rice Gruel and Honey-Balls

282. Atha kho bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena andhakavindaṃ tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi, mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ, aḍḍhatelasehi bhikkhusatehi. Tena kho pana samayena jānapadā manussā bahuṃ loṇampi, telampi, taṇḍulampi, khādanīyampi sakaṭesu āropetvā buddhappamukhassa bhikkhusaṅghassa piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhā honti – yadā paṭipāṭiṃ labhissāma tadā bhattaṃ karissāmāti, pañcamattāni ca vighāsādasatāni. Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena andhakavindaṃ tadavasari. Atha kho aññatarassa brāhmaṇassa paṭipāṭiṃ alabhantassa etadahosi – “atītāni adhikāni (sī. syā.) kho me dve māsāni buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ anubandhantassa ‘yadā paṭipāṭiṃ labhissāmi tadā bhattaṃ karissāmī’ti, na ca me paṭipāṭi labbhati, ahañcamhi ekattako ekato (sī. syā.), bahu ca me gharāvāsattho hāyati. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhattaggaṃ olokeyyaṃ; yaṃ bhattagge nāssa, taṃ paṭiyādeyya”nti. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo bhattaggaṃ olokento dve nāddasa – yāguñca [M 0.0315] madhugoḷakañca[T 2.0077]. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “idha me, bho ānanda, paṭipāṭiṃ alabhantassa etadahosi ‘atītāni kho me [P 1.0221] dve māsāni buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ anubandhantassa, yadā paṭipāṭiṃ labhissāmi tadā bhattaṃ karissāmīti. Na ca me paṭipāṭi labbhati[V 0.0297], ahañcamhi ekattako, bahu ca me gharāvāsattho hāyati. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhattaggaṃ olokeyyaṃ; yaṃ bhattagge nāssa, taṃ paṭiyādeyya’nti. So kho ahaṃ, bho ānanda, bhattaggaṃ olokento dve nāddasaṃ – yāguñca madhugoḷakañca. Sacāhaṃ, bho ānanda, paṭiyādeyyaṃ yāguñca madhugoḷakañca, paṭiggaṇheyya me bhavaṃ gotamo”ti? “Tena hi, brāhmaṇa, bhagavantaṃ paṭipucchissāmī”ti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Tena hānanda, paṭiyādetūti. Tena hi, brāhmaṇa, paṭiyādehīti. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo tassā rattiyā accayena pahūtaṃ yāguñca madhugoḷakañca paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato upanāmesi – paṭiggaṇhātu me bhavaṃ gotamo yāguñca madhugoḷakañcāti. Tena hi, brāhmaṇa, bhikkhūnaṃ dehīti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā na paṭiggaṇhanti. Paṭiggaṇhatha, bhikkhave, paribhuñjathāti. Atha kho so brāhmaṇo buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pahūtāya yāguyā ca madhugoḷakena ca sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā bhagavantaṃ dhotahatthaṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ [T 2.0078] bhagavā etadavoca –

282. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Bārāṇasī as long as he pleased, set out on a journey to Andhakavinda with a large company of bhikkhus—twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus. At that time, many country folk loaded carts with salt, oil, rice, and hard food and followed behind the Sangha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha, thinking, “When we get our turn, we will prepare a meal.” And five hundred scrap-eaters also followed. Then the Blessed One, traveling by stages, arrived at Andhakavinda. Then a certain brahmin, not getting his turn, thought: “For the past two months I have been following the Sangha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha, thinking, ‘When I get my turn, I will prepare a meal.’ But I have not gotten my turn. I am alone, and much of my household business is being neglected. Why don’t I inspect the meal hall? Whatever is not in the meal hall, I will provide.” Then that brahmin, inspecting the meal hall, did not see two things: rice gruel and honey-balls. Then that brahmin approached the Venerable Ānanda and said: “Venerable Ānanda, not getting my turn, this thought occurred to me: ‘For the past two months I have been following the Sangha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha, thinking, “When I get my turn, I will prepare a meal.” But I have not gotten my turn. I am alone, and much of my household business is being neglected. Why don’t I inspect the meal hall? Whatever is not in the meal hall, I will provide.’ Venerable Ānanda, inspecting the meal hall, I did not see two things: rice gruel and honey-balls. If I were to provide rice gruel and honey-balls, would Master Gotama accept them from me?” “Then, brahmin, I will ask the Blessed One.” Then the Venerable Ānanda informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Then, Ānanda, let him provide them.” “Then, brahmin, provide them.” Then that brahmin, when the night had passed, had abundant rice gruel and honey-balls prepared and offered them to the Blessed One, saying: “May Master Gotama accept the rice gruel and honey-balls from me.” “Then, brahmin, give them to the bhikkhus.” The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not accept them. “Accept them, bhikkhus, and partake of them.” Then that brahmin, with his own hands, served and satisfied the Sangha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha with abundant rice gruel and honey-balls until they declined any more. When the Blessed One had washed his hands and removed his hand from the bowl, the brahmin sat down to one side. The Blessed One said this to that brahmin who was sitting to one side:

“Dasayime, brāhmaṇa, ānisaṃsā yāguyā. Katame dasa? Yāguṃ dento āyuṃ deti, vaṇṇaṃ deti, sukhaṃ deti, balaṃ deti, paṭibhānaṃ deti, yāgu pītā khuddaṃ khudaṃ (sī. syā.) paṭihanati, pipāsaṃ vineti, vātaṃ anulometi, vatthiṃ sodheti, āmāvasesaṃ pāceti – ime kho, brāhmaṇa, dasānisaṃsā yāguyā”ti pacchimā pañca ānisaṃsā a. ni. 5.207.

“Brahmin, these are the ten benefits of rice gruel. What ten? One who gives rice gruel gives life, gives beauty, gives happiness, gives strength, and gives intelligence. Rice gruel, when drunk, wards off hunger, dispels thirst, regulates the wind, cleanses the bladder, and digests the remnant of undigested food. Brahmin, these are the ten benefits of rice gruel.”

a. ni. 4.58-59 thokaṃ visadisaṃ Yo saññatānaṃ paradattabhojinaṃ;

Kālena sakkacca dadāti yāguṃ;

Dasassa ṭhānāni anuppavecchati;

Āyuñca vaṇṇañca sukhaṃ balañca.

The person who, at a suitable time, respectfully gives rice gruel to those who are restrained and live on what is given by others, bestows ten things upon that recipient: life, beauty, happiness, and strength.

Paṭibhānamassa [M 0.0316] upajāyate tato;

Khuddaṃ pipāsañca byapaneti vātaṃ;

Sodheti vatthiṃ pariṇāmeti bhuttaṃ;

Bhesajjametaṃ sugatena vaṇṇitaṃ.

Intelligence arises in him from that; it dispels hunger, thirst, and wind; it cleanses the bladder and digests what has been eaten. This medicine was praised by the Sugata.

Tasmā hi yāguṃ alameva dātuṃ;

Niccaṃ manussena sukhatthikena;

Dibbāni [V 0.0298] vā patthayatā sukhāni;

Manussasobhagyatamicchatā vāti.

Therefore indeed, it is always proper for a person desiring happiness, or one aspiring for divine pleasures, or one wishing for human good fortune, to give rice gruel.

Atha [P 1.0222] kho bhagavā taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ imāhi gāthāhi anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe [T 2.0079] dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yāguñca madhugoḷakañcā”ti.

Then the Blessed One, having expressed his appreciation to the brahmin with these verses, rose from his seat and departed. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow rice gruel and honey-balls.”

Yāgumadhugoḷakānujānanā niṭṭhitā.

The allowance for rice gruel and honey-balls is concluded.

171. Taruṇapasannamahāmattavatthu

171. The Story of the Newly Devoted High Official

283. Assosuṃ kho manussā bhagavatā kira yāgu anuññātā madhugoḷakañcāti. Te kālasseva, bhojjayāguṃ paṭiyādenti madhugoḷakañca. Bhikkhū kālasseva bhojjayāguyā dhātā madhugoḷakena ca bhattagge na cittarūpaṃ paribhuñjanti. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarena taruṇapasannena mahāmattena svātanāya buddhappamukho bhikkhusaṅgho nimantito hoti. Atha kho tassa taruṇapasannassa mahāmattassa etadahosi – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ aḍḍhatelasannaṃ bhikkhusatānaṃ aḍḍhatelasāni maṃsapātisatāni paṭiyādeyyaṃ, ekamekassa bhikkhuno ekamekaṃ maṃsapātiṃ upanāmeyya”nti. Atha kho so taruṇapasanno mahāmatto tassā rattiyā accayena paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā aḍḍhatelasāni ca maṃsapātisatāni, bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – “kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena tassa taruṇapasannassa mahāmattassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi, saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho so taruṇapasanno mahāmatto bhattagge bhikkhū parivisati. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “thokaṃ, āvuso, dehi; thokaṃ, āvuso, dehī”ti. “Mā kho tumhe, bhante, – ‘ayaṃ taruṇapasanno mahāmatto’ti [M 0.0317][T 2.0080] – thokaṃ thokaṃ paṭiggaṇhatha. Bahuṃ me khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyattaṃ, aḍḍhatelasāni ca maṃsapātisatāni. Ekamekassa bhikkhuno ekamekaṃ maṃsapātiṃ upanāmessāmīti. Paṭiggaṇhatha, bhante, yāvadattha”nti. “Na kho mayaṃ, āvuso, etaṃkāraṇā thokaṃ thokaṃ paṭiggaṇhāma, api ca mayaṃ kālasseva bhojjayāguyā dhātā madhugoḷakena ca. Tena mayaṃ thokaṃ thokaṃ paṭiggaṇhāmā”ti. Atha kho so taruṇapasanno mahāmatto ujjhāyati khiyyati vipāceti – “kathañhi nāma bhadantā mayā nimantitā aññassa bhojjayāguṃ paribhuñjissanti, na cāhaṃ paṭibalo yāvadatthaṃ dātu”nti [V 0.0299] kupito anattamano āsādanāpekkho bhikkhūnaṃ patte pūrento agamāsi – bhuñjatha vā haratha vāti. Atha kho so taruṇapasanno mahāmatto buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena [P 1.0223] khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho taṃ taruṇapasannaṃ mahāmattaṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

283. The people heard, it is said, 'Gruel and sweet cakes made with molasses have been allowed by the Blessed One.' Those people prepared thick gruel and sweet cakes made with molasses very early in the morning. The monks, being satiated with thick gruel and sweet cakes made with molasses very early in the morning, did not eat according to their liking in the dining hall. Now at that time, a certain newly devout great minister had invited the community of monks headed by the Buddha for the next day. Then this thought occurred to that newly devout great minister: 'It would be good if I were to prepare twelve hundred and fifty bowls of curry for twelve hundred and fifty monks, and it would be good if I were to offer one bowl of curry to each and every monk.' Then that newly devout great minister, after that night had passed, had excellent hard and soft food and twelve hundred and fifty bowls of curry prepared, and had the time announced to the Blessed One, saying: 'Venerable sir, it is time; the meal is ready.' Then the Blessed One, in the morning time, having adjusted his lower robe and taking his bowl and outer robe, approached the residence of that newly devout great minister. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the community of monks. Then that newly devout great minister served the monks in the dining hall. The monks said: 'Give a little, friend; give a little, friend.' He replied: 'Venerable sirs, please do not accept just a little thinking, "This great minister is newly devout." Much hard and soft food and twelve hundred and fifty bowls of curry have been prepared by me. I intend to offer one bowl of curry to each and every monk. Venerable sirs, please accept as much as you wish.' The monks said: 'Indeed, friend, we do not accept just a little for that reason. But rather, we are already satiated from very early in the morning with thick gruel and sweet cakes made with molasses. Therefore, we accept just a little.' Then that newly devout great minister complained, disparaged, and criticized, saying: 'How indeed could the venerable ones, having been invited by me, partake of another's thick gruel? Am I not able to give as much as is wished?' Being angry, displeased, and desiring to cause disrespect, he went away after filling the monks' bowls, saying, 'Either eat or take it away!' Then that newly devout great minister, having satisfied and served until they refused more the community of monks headed by the Buddha with excellent hard and soft food with his own hands, and having observed that the Blessed One had finished eating and had removed his hand from the bowl, sat down to one side. The Blessed One, with a talk on the Dhamma, instructed, encouraged, incited, and gladdened that newly devout great minister who was sitting to one side. Then, rising from his seat, he departed.

Atha kho tassa taruṇapasannassa mahāmattassa acirapakkantassa bhagavato ahudeva kukkuccaṃ, ahu vippaṭisāro – “alābhā vata me, na vata me lābhā; dulladdhaṃ vata me, na vata me suladdhaṃ; yohaṃ kupito anattamano āsādanāpekkho bhikkhūnaṃ [T 2.0081] patte pūrento agamāsiṃ – ‘bhuñjatha vā haratha vā’ti. Kiṃ nu kho mayā bahuṃ pasutaṃ puññaṃ vā apuññaṃ vā”ti? Atha kho so taruṇapasanno mahāmatto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so taruṇapasanno mahāmatto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idha mayhaṃ, bhante, acirapakkantassa bhagavato ahudeva kukkuccaṃ, ahu vippaṭisāro ‘alābhā vata me, na vata me lābhā; dulladdhaṃ vata me, na vata me suladdhaṃ; yohaṃ kupito anattamano āsādanāpekkho bhikkhūnaṃ patte pūrento agamāsiṃ – bhuñjatha vā haratha vāti. Kiṃ nu kho mayā bahuṃ pasutaṃ, puññaṃ vā apuññaṃ vā’ti. Kiṃ nu kho mayā, bhante, bahuṃ pasutaṃ, puññaṃ vā apuññaṃ vā”ti? “Yadaggena tayā, āvuso, svātanāya buddhappamukho bhikkhusaṅgho nimantito tadaggena te bahuṃ puññaṃ pasutaṃ. Yadaggena te [M 0.0318] ekamekena bhikkhunā ekamekaṃ sitthaṃ paṭiggahitaṃ tadaggena te bahuṃ puññaṃ pasutaṃ, saggā te āraddhā”ti. Atha kho so taruṇapasanno mahāmatto – “lābhā kira me, suladdhaṃ kira me, bahuṃ kira mayā puññaṃ pasutaṃ, saggā kira me āraddhā”ti – haṭṭho udaggo uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū [T 2.0082] paṭipucchi – “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū aññatra nimantitā aññassa bhojjayāguṃ paribhuñjantī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā aññatra nimantitā aññassa bhojjayāguṃ paribhuñjissanti. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi [P 1.0224] – “na, bhikkhave, aññatra nimantitena aññassa bhojjayāgu paribhuñjitabbā. Yo paribhuñjeyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.

Then, not long after the Blessed One had departed, remorse and regret arose in that newly devoted high official: ‘Alas, it is my loss, not my gain; it is ill-gotten by me, not well-gotten, that I, being angry and displeased, seeking an occasion for offense, went and filled the monks’ bowls, saying, “Eat it or take it away.” I wonder what I have produced in abundance—merit or demerit?’ Then that newly devoted high official approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, he said to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, not long after the Blessed One departed, remorse and regret arose in me: “Alas, it is my loss, not my gain; it is ill-gotten by me, not well-gotten, that I, being angry and displeased, seeking an occasion for offense, went and filled the monks’ bowls, saying, ‘Eat it or take it away.’ I wonder what I have produced in abundance—merit or demerit?” Venerable sir, what have I produced in abundance—merit or demerit?’ ‘Friend, from the moment you invited the community of monks with the Buddha at its head for tomorrow, you have produced abundant merit. From the moment each monk accepted a single morsel from you, you have produced abundant merit; you have undertaken what leads to heaven.’ Then that newly devoted high official, joyful and elated, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and departed, thinking: ‘Truly, it is my gain! Truly, it is well-gotten by me! Truly, I have produced abundant merit! Truly, I have undertaken what leads to heaven!’ Then, on this occasion, the Blessed One convened the community of monks and asked the monks: ‘Is it true, monks, that monks, when invited elsewhere, partake of another’s congee?’ ‘It is true, Blessed One.’ The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... and so on... ‘How indeed, monks, can those foolish men, when invited elsewhere, partake of another’s congee? This, monks, does not lead to inspiring faith in the faithless... and so on...’ Having rebuked them and given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: ‘Monks, one who is invited elsewhere should not partake of another’s congee. Whoever should partake of it should be dealt with according to the rule.’

Taruṇapasannamahāmattavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Story of the Newly Devoted High Official is concluded.

172. Belaṭṭhakaccānavatthu

172. The Story of Belaṭṭha Kaccāna

284. Atha [V 0.0300] kho bhagavā andhakavinde yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena rājagahaṃ tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi, mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ, aḍḍhatelasehi bhikkhusatehi. Tena kho pana samayena belaṭṭho kaccāno rājagahā andhakavindaṃ addhānamaggappaṭipanno hoti, pañcamattehi sakaṭasatehi, sabbeheva guḷakumbhapūrehi. Addasā kho bhagavā belaṭṭhaṃ kaccānaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ, disvāna maggā okkamma aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisīdi. Atha kho belaṭṭho kaccāno yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho belaṭṭho kaccāno bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “icchāmahaṃ, bhante, ekamekassa bhikkhuno ekamekaṃ guḷakumbhaṃ dātu”nti. “Tena hi tvaṃ, kaccāna, ekaṃyeva guḷakumbhaṃ [T 2.0083] āharā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho belaṭṭho kaccāno bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā ekaṃyeva guḷakumbhaṃ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ābhato āhaṭo (sī. syā. ka.), bhante, guḷakumbho; kathāhaṃ, bhante, paṭipajjāmī”ti? “Tena hi tvaṃ, kaccāna, bhikkhūnaṃ guḷaṃ dehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho belaṭṭho kaccāno bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā [M 0.0319] bhikkhūnaṃ guḷaṃ datvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “dinno, bhante, bhikkhūnaṃ guḷo, bahu cāyaṃ guḷo avasiṭṭho. Kathāhaṃ, bhante, paṭipajjāmī”ti? “Tena hi tvaṃ, kaccāna, bhikkhūnaṃ guḷaṃ yāvadatthaṃ dehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho belaṭṭho kaccāno bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā bhikkhūnaṃ guḷaṃ yāvadatthaṃ datvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “dinno, bhante, bhikkhūnaṃ guḷo yāvadattho, bahu cāyaṃ guḷo avasiṭṭho. Kathāhaṃ, bhante, paṭipajjāmī”ti? “Tena hi tvaṃ, kaccāna, bhikkhū guḷehi santappehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho belaṭṭho kaccāno bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā bhikkhū guḷehi santappesi. Ekacce bhikkhū pattepi pūresuṃ parissāvanānipi thavikāyopi pūresuṃ. Atha kho belaṭṭho kaccāno bhikkhū guḷehi santappetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “santappitā, bhante, bhikkhū guḷehi, bahu cāyaṃ guḷo avasiṭṭho. Kathāhaṃ, bhante, paṭipajjāmī”ti? “Tena hi [P 1.0225] tvaṃ, kaccāna, vighāsādānaṃ guḷaṃ dehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho belaṭṭho kaccāno bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā vighāsādānaṃ guḷaṃ datvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “dinno, bhante[T 2.0084], vighāsādānaṃ guḷo, bahu cāyaṃ guḷo avasiṭṭho.
