Kathāhaṃ, bhante, paṭipajjāmī”ti? “Tena hi tvaṃ, kaccāna, vighāsādānaṃ guḷaṃ yāvadatthaṃ dehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho belaṭṭho kaccāno bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā vighāsādānaṃ guḷaṃ yāvadatthaṃ datvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “dinno, bhante, vighāsādānaṃ guḷo yāvadattho, bahu cāyaṃ guḷo avasiṭṭho. Kathāhaṃ, bhante, paṭipajjāmī”ti? “Tena hi tvaṃ, kaccāna, vighāsāde guḷehi santappehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti [V 0.0301] kho belaṭṭho kaccāno bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā vighāsāde guḷehi santappesi. Ekacce vighāsādā kolambepi ghaṭepi pūresuṃ, piṭakānipi ucchaṅgepi pūresuṃ. Atha kho belaṭṭho kaccāno vighāsāde guḷehi santappetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “santappitā, bhante, vighāsādā guḷehi, bahu cāyaṃ guḷo avasiṭṭho. Kathāhaṃ, bhante, paṭipajjāmī”ti? “Nāhaṃ taṃ, kaccāna, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya yassa so guḷo paribhutto sammā pariṇāmaṃ gaccheyya, aññatra tathāgatassa vā tathāgatasāvakassa vā. Tena hi tvaṃ, kaccāna, taṃ guḷaṃ appaharite vā chaḍḍehi, appāṇake vā udake opilāpehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho belaṭṭho kaccāno bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā taṃ guḷaṃ appāṇake udake [M 0.0320] opilāpeti. Atha kho so guḷo udake pakkhitto cicciṭāyati ciṭiciṭāyati padhūpāyati [T 2.0085] sandhūpāyati (sī. syā.) sampadhūpāyati. Seyyathāpi nāma phālo divasaṃsantatto udake pakkhitto cicciṭāyati ciṭiciṭāyati padhūpāyati sampadhūpāyati, evameva so guḷo udake pakkhitto cicciṭāyati ciṭiciṭāyati padhūpāyati sampadhūpāyati.

284. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Andhakavinda as long as he pleased, set out on a journey to Rājagaha with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus—one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikkhus. Now at that time, Belaṭṭha Kaccāna was traveling on the long road from Rājagaha to Andhakavinda with five hundred carts, all filled with pots of molasses. From a distance, the Blessed One saw Belaṭṭha Kaccāna approaching. Seeing him, he stepped off the road and sat down at the foot of a certain tree. Then Belaṭṭha Kaccāna approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, Belaṭṭha Kaccāna said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I wish to give each bhikkhu one pot of molasses.” “Then, Kaccāna, bring just one pot of molasses.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied Belaṭṭha Kaccāna to the Blessed One. He took just one pot of molasses, approached the Blessed One, and said: “Venerable sir, the pot of molasses has been brought. How, venerable sir, should I proceed?” “Then, Kaccāna, give the molasses to the bhikkhus.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied Belaṭṭha Kaccāna to the Blessed One. After giving the molasses to the bhikkhus, he said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the molasses has been given to the bhikkhus, and much of this molasses is left over. How, venerable sir, should I proceed?” “Then, Kaccāna, give the bhikkhus molasses as much as they desire.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied Belaṭṭha Kaccāna to the Blessed One. After giving the bhikkhus molasses as much as they desired, he said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the molasses has been given to the bhikkhus as much as they desired, and much of this molasses is left over. How, venerable sir, should I proceed?” “Then, Kaccāna, satisfy the bhikkhus with molasses.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied Belaṭṭha Kaccāna to the Blessed One, and he satisfied the bhikkhus with molasses. Some bhikkhus filled their bowls, and they also filled their water strainers and bags. Then Belaṭṭha Kaccāna, having satisfied the bhikkhus with molasses, said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the bhikkhus have been satisfied with molasses, and much of this molasses is left over. How, venerable sir, should I proceed?” “Then, Kaccāna, give the molasses to those who eat leftovers.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied Belaṭṭha Kaccāna to the Blessed One. After giving the molasses to those who eat leftovers, he said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the molasses has been given to those who eat leftovers, and much of this molasses is left over. How, venerable sir, should I proceed?” “Then, Kaccāna, give those who eat leftovers molasses as much as they desire.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied Belaṭṭha Kaccāna to the Blessed One. After giving those who eat leftovers molasses as much as they desired, he said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the molasses has been given to those who eat leftovers as much as they desired, and much of this molasses is left over. How, venerable sir, should I proceed?” “Then, Kaccāna, satisfy those who eat leftovers with molasses.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied Belaṭṭha Kaccāna to the Blessed One, and he satisfied those who eat leftovers with molasses. Some of those who eat leftovers filled their jars and pots, and they also filled their baskets and laps. Then Belaṭṭha Kaccāna, having satisfied those who eat leftovers with molasses, said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, those who eat leftovers have been satisfied with molasses, and much of this molasses is left over. How, venerable sir, should I proceed?” “Kaccāna, I do not see anyone in this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans, by whom that molasses, having been consumed, could be properly digested, except for the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata. Therefore, Kaccāna, either discard that molasses in a place without green grass or immerse it in water where there are no living beings.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied Belaṭṭha Kaccāna to the Blessed One, and he immersed that molasses in water where there were no living beings. Then that molasses, having been thrown into the water, sizzled and sputtered, smoked and steamed. Just as a plowshare heated all day, when thrown into water, sizzles and sputters, smokes and steams, in the same way, that molasses, when thrown into the water, sizzled and sputtered, smoked and steamed.

Atha kho belaṭṭho kaccāno saṃviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnassa kho belaṭṭhassa kaccānassa bhagavā anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – “dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ, kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ, nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā bhagavā aññāsi belaṭṭhaṃ kaccānaṃ kallacittaṃ, muducittaṃ, vinīvaraṇacittaṃ, udaggacittaṃ, pasannacittaṃ, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā, taṃ pakāsesi…pe… evameva belaṭṭhassa [P 1.0226] kaccānassa tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhammanti. Atha kho belaṭṭho kaccāno diṭṭhadhammo pattadhammo viditadhammo pariyogāḷhadhammo tiṇṇavicikiccho vigatakathaṃkatho vesārajjappatto aparappaccayo satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante. Abhikkantaṃ, bhante. Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya…pe… [T 2.0086] evamevaṃ kho bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi, dhammañca, bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇagata”nti.

Then Belaṭṭha Kaccāna, agitated and with his hair standing on end, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. To Belaṭṭha Kaccāna, who was sitting to one side, the Blessed One gave a progressive talk, that is to say: a talk on generosity, a talk on virtue, a talk on heaven; he explained the danger, degradation, and defilement of sensual pleasures, and the benefits of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that Belaṭṭha Kaccāna's mind was ready, pliable, free from hindrances, uplifted, and confident, he revealed the teaching exalted by the Buddhas. … Just so, for Belaṭṭha Kaccāna, as he sat right there, the dust-free, stainless vision of the Dhamma arose: “Whatever is subject to origination is all subject to cessation.” Then Belaṭṭha Kaccāna, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, penetrated the Dhamma, having crossed beyond doubt, gotten rid of perplexity, attained assurance, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s Dispensation, said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as, venerable sir, one might set upright what had been overturned … in the same way, the Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by the Blessed One. I go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward, for as long as life lasts.”

Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena rājagahaṃ tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena rājagahe guḷo ussanno hoti. Bhikkhū – gilānasseva bhagavatā guḷo anuññāto, no agilānassāti – kukkuccāyantā [V 0.0302] guḷaṃ na bhuñjanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānassa guḷaṃ, agilānassa guḷodakanti.

Then the Blessed One, journeying by stages, arrived at Rājagaha. There the Blessed One stayed in Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Feeding Ground. Now at that time, molasses was plentiful in Rājagaha. The bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not consume molasses, thinking: “The Blessed One has allowed molasses only for the sick, not for the healthy.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “I allow, bhikkhus, molasses for the sick and molasses-water for the healthy.”

Belaṭṭhakaccānavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story of Belaṭṭha Kaccāna is concluded.

173. Pāṭaligāmavatthu

173. The Story of Pāṭaligāma

285. ito paraṃ mahāva. 286-287 ‘tiṇṇā medhāvino janā’ti pāṭho dī. ni. 2.148; udā. 76 ādayo Atha [M 0.0321] kho bhagavā rājagahe yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena pāṭaligāmo tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi, mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ, aḍḍhatelasehi bhikkhusatehi. Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena pāṭaligāmo tadavasari. Assosuṃ kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā – “bhagavā kira pāṭaligāmaṃ anuppatto”ti. Atha kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho pāṭaligāmike upāsake bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi, samādapesi, samuttejesi, sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā bhagavatā dhammiyā [T 2.0087] kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “adhivāsetu no, bhante, bhagavā āvasathāgāraṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ [P 1.0227] katvā yena āvasathāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā sabbasanthariṃ āvasathāgāraṃ santharitvā, āsanāni paññapetvā, udakamaṇikaṃ patiṭṭhāpetvā, telapadīpaṃ āropetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “sabbasantharisanthataṃ, bhante, āvasathāgāraṃ. Āsanāni paññattāni. Udakamaṇiko patiṭṭhāpito. Telapadīpo āropito. Yassadāni, bhante, bhagavā kālaṃ maññatī”ti.

285. Then the Blessed One, having stayed in Rājagaha for as long as he wished, set out on a journey toward Pāṭaligāma with a great Bhikkhu Saṅgha, with twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus. Journeying by stages, the Blessed One arrived at Pāṭaligāma. The lay followers of Pāṭaligāma heard: “The Blessed One, it is said, has arrived at Pāṭaligāma.” Then the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. The Blessed One instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma, who were seated to one side, with a Dhamma talk. Then the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma, having been instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One consent to our rest house, together with the Bhikkhu Saṅgha.” The Blessed One consented by his silence. Then the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma, understanding the Blessed One's consent, rose from their seats, paid homage to him, circumambulated him, and approached the rest house. Having approached, they spread the rest house all over with coverings, prepared seats, set up a water pot, and lit an oil lamp. Then they approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the rest house is spread all over with coverings, seats are prepared, a water pot is set up, and an oil lamp is lit. Now, venerable sir, it is for the Blessed One to know the time.”

Atha kho bhagavā nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena yena āvasathāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā pāde pakkhāletvā āvasathāgāraṃ pavisitvā majjhimaṃ thambhaṃ nissāya puratthābhimukho nisīdi. Bhikkhusaṅghopi kho pāde pakkhāletvā āvasathāgāraṃ pavisitvā pacchimaṃ bhittiṃ nissāya puratthābhimukho nisīdi, bhagavantaṃyeva purakkhatvā. Pāṭaligāmikāpi kho upāsakā pāde pakkhāletvā āvasathāgāraṃ pavisitvā puratthimaṃ bhittiṃ nissāya pacchimābhimukhā [T 2.0088][V 0.0303] nisīdiṃsu, bhagavantaṃyeva purakkhatvā. Atha kho bhagavā pāṭaligāmike upāsake āmantesi –

Then the Blessed One, having dressed, taking his bowl and outer robe, approached the rest house together with the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. Having approached, he washed his feet, entered the rest house, and sat down facing east, leaning against the central pillar. The Bhikkhu Saṅgha also washed their feet, entered the rest house, and sat down facing east, leaning against the western wall, with the Blessed One before them. The lay followers of Pāṭaligāma also washed their feet, entered the rest house, and sat down facing west, leaning against the eastern wall, with the Blessed One before them. Then the Blessed One addressed the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma:

[M 0.0322] dī. ni. 3.316; a. ni. 5.213 ādayo, Gahapatayo, ādīnavā dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā. Katame pañca? Idha, gahapatayo, dussīlo sīlavipanno pamādādhikaraṇaṃ mahatiṃ bhogajāniṃ nigacchati. Ayaṃ paṭhamo ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā. Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, dussīlassa sīlavipannassa pāpako kittisaddo abbhuggacchati. Ayaṃ dutiyo ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā. Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, dussīlo sīlavipanno yaññadeva parisaṃ upasaṅkamati, yadi khattiyaparisaṃ, yadi brāhmaṇaparisaṃ, yadi gahapatiparisaṃ, yadi samaṇaparisaṃ, avisārado upasaṅkamati maṅkubhūto. Ayaṃ tatiyo ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā. Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, dussīlo sīlavipanno sammūḷho kālaṃkaroti. Ayaṃ catuttho ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā. Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, dussīlo sīlavipanno kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ pañcamo ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā. Ime kho, gahapatayo, pañca ādīnavā dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.

Householders, these are the five drawbacks of failure in virtue for an immoral person. What five? Here, householders, an immoral person who has failed in virtue, on account of negligence, incurs a great loss of wealth. This is the first drawback of failure in virtue for an immoral person. Furthermore, householders, an evil report spreads about an immoral person who has failed in virtue. This is the second drawback of failure in virtue for an immoral person. Furthermore, householders, an immoral person who has failed in virtue, whatever assembly he approaches—whether an assembly of nobles, an assembly of brahmins, an assembly of householders, or an assembly of ascetics—he approaches unassured and dispirited. This is the third drawback of failure in virtue for an immoral person. Furthermore, householders, an immoral person who has failed in virtue dies confused. This is the fourth drawback of failure in virtue for an immoral person. Furthermore, householders, an immoral person who has failed in virtue, on the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the plane of misery, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell. This is the fifth drawback of failure in virtue for an immoral person. These, householders, are the five drawbacks of failure in virtue for an immoral person.

dī. ni. 3.316; a. ni. 5.213 ādayo “Pañcime, gahapatayo, ānisaṃsā sīlavato sīlasampadāya. Katame [P 1.0228] pañca? Idha, gahapatayo, sīlavā sīlasampanno appamādādhikaraṇaṃ mahantaṃ bhogakkhandhaṃ adhigacchati. Ayaṃ paṭhamo ānisaṃso sīlavato sīlasampadāya[T 2.0089]. Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, sīlavato sīlasampannassa kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchati. Ayaṃ dutiyo ānisaṃso sīlavato sīlasampadāya. Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, sīlavā sīlasampanno yaññadeva parisaṃ upasaṅkamati, yadi khattiyaparisaṃ, yadi brāhmaṇaparisaṃ, yadi gahapatiparisaṃ, yadi samaṇaparisaṃ, visārado upasaṅkamati amaṅkubhūto. Ayaṃ tatiyo ānisaṃso sīlavato sīlasampadāya. Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, sīlavā sīlasampanno asammūḷho kālaṃkaroti. Ayaṃ catuttho ānisaṃso sīlavato sīlasampadāya. Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, sīlavā sīlasampanno kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ pañcamo ānisaṃso sīlavato sīlasampadāya. Ime kho, gahapatayo, pañca ānisaṃsā sīlavato sīlasampadāyāti.

Householders, there are these five benefits for a virtuous person who is accomplished in virtue. What are the five? Here, householders, a virtuous person who is accomplished in virtue, on account of diligence, acquires a great mass of wealth. This is the first benefit for a virtuous person who is accomplished in virtue. Furthermore, householders, for a virtuous person who is accomplished in virtue, a good reputation spreads. This is the second benefit for a virtuous person who is accomplished in virtue. Furthermore, householders, a virtuous person who is accomplished in virtue, approaches whatever assembly—be it an assembly of nobles, an assembly of brahmins, an assembly of householders, or an assembly of ascetics—confidently and unabashed. This is the third benefit for a virtuous person who is accomplished in virtue. Furthermore, householders, a virtuous person who is accomplished in virtue dies unconfused. This is the fourth benefit for a virtuous person who is accomplished in virtue. Furthermore, householders, a virtuous person who is accomplished in virtue, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. This is the fifth benefit for a virtuous person who is accomplished in virtue. These, indeed, householders, are the five benefits for a virtuous person who is accomplished in virtue.

Atha kho bhagavā pāṭaligāmike upāsake bahudeva rattiṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uyyojesi [M 0.0323] – “abhikkantā kho, gahapatayo, ratti. Yassadāni tumhe kālaṃ maññathā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti, kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā bhagavato [V 0.0304] paṭissuṇitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkantesu pāṭaligāmikesu upāsakesu suññāgāraṃ pāvisi.

Then the Blessed One, having instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma with a Dhamma talk far into the night, dismissed them, saying: ‘The night has passed, householders. Now is the time for you to do as you see fit.’ ‘So be it, venerable sir,’ the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma replied to the Blessed One. Then, rising from their seats, they paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping him to their right, and departed. Then, not long after the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma had departed, the Blessed One entered a secluded dwelling.

Pāṭaligāmavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The account of Pāṭaligāma is concluded.

174. Sunidhavassakāravatthu

174. The Story of Sunidha and Vassakāra

286. Tena [T 2.0090] kho pana samayena sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā pāṭaligāme nagaraṃ māpenti vajjīnaṃ paṭibāhāya. Addasā kho bhagavā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena sambahulā devatāyo pāṭaligāme vatthūni pariggaṇhantiyo. Yasmiṃ padese mahesakkhā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, mahesakkhānaṃ tattha rājūnaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Yasmiṃ padese majjhimā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, majjhimānaṃ tattha rājūnaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Yasmiṃ padese nīcā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, nīcānaṃ tattha rājūnaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “ke nu kho te, ānanda, pāṭaligāme nagaraṃ māpentī”ti? “Sunidhavassakārā[P 1.0229], bhante, magadhamahāmattā pāṭaligāme nagaraṃ māpenti vajjīnaṃ paṭibāhāyā”ti. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, devehi tāvatiṃsehi saddhiṃ mantetvā, evameva kho, ānanda, sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā pāṭaligāme nagaraṃ māpenti vajjīnaṃ paṭibāhāya. Idhāhaṃ, ānanda, rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya addasaṃ dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena sambahulā devatāyo pāṭaligāme vatthūni pariggaṇhantiyo. Yasmiṃ padese mahesakkhā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, mahesakkhānaṃ tattha rājūnaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Yasmiṃ [T 2.0091] padese majjhimā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, majjhimānaṃ tattha rājūnaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Yasmiṃ padese nīcā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, nīcānaṃ tattha rājūnaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Yāvatā, ānanda, ariyaṃ āyatanaṃ, yāvatā vaṇippatho, idaṃ agganagaraṃ bhavissati pāṭaliputtaṃ puṭabhedanaṃ. Pāṭaliputtassa kho, ānanda, tayo antarāyā [M 0.0324] bhavissanti – aggito vā udakato vā abbhantarato vā mithubhedāti.

286. Now at that time, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, were building a city at Pāṭaligāma to repel the Vajjis. The Blessed One, having risen in the early morning at the time of dawn, saw with his divine eye—which is pure and surpasses that of humans—numerous deities in Pāṭaligāma taking possession of sites. In whatever region deities of great power take possession of sites, the minds of kings and royal chief ministers of great power incline to build dwellings there. In whatever region middling deities take possession of sites, the minds of middling kings and royal chief ministers incline to build dwellings there. In whatever region lowly deities take possession of sites, the minds of lowly kings and royal chief ministers incline to build dwellings there. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: 'Ānanda, who are they that are building a city at Pāṭaligāma?' 'Venerable Sir, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, are building a city at Pāṭaligāma to repel the Vajjis.' 'Ānanda, it is as if they had consulted with the Tāvatiṃsa devas; even so, Ānanda, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, are building a city at Pāṭaligāma to repel the Vajjis. Here, Ānanda, having risen in the early morning at the time of dawn, I saw with my divine eye—which is pure and surpasses that of humans—numerous deities in Pāṭaligāma taking possession of sites. In whatever region deities of great power take possession of sites, the minds of kings and royal chief ministers of great power incline to build dwellings there. In whatever region middling deities take possession of sites, the minds of middling kings and royal chief ministers incline to build dwellings there. In whatever region lowly deities take possession of sites, the minds of lowly kings and royal chief ministers incline to build dwellings there. Ānanda, as far as the sphere of the noble ones extends, as far as there is a trade route, this will be the chief city, Pāṭaliputta, a place for the unbinding of goods. Indeed, Ānanda, there will be three dangers for Pāṭaliputta: from fire, from water, or from internal dissension.'

Atha kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā [V 0.0305] saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “adhivāsetu no bhavaṃ gotamo ajjatanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesuṃ – “kālo, bho gotama, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena sunidhavassakārānaṃ magadhamahāmattānaṃ parivesanā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena[T 2.0092]. Atha kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho sunidhavassakāre magadhamahāmatte bhagavā imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –

Then the chief ministers of Magadha, Sunidha and Vassakāra, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they exchanged joyful greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded a courteous and memorable conversation, they stood to one side. Standing to one side, the chief ministers of Magadha, Sunidha and Vassakāra, said this to the Blessed One: “May the venerable Gotama accept our meal for today, together with the community of monks.” The Blessed One consented by his silence. Then the chief ministers of Magadha, Sunidha and Vassakāra, having understood the Blessed One’s consent, departed. Then the chief ministers of Magadha, Sunidha and Vassakāra, having had excellent hard and soft food prepared, had the time announced to the Blessed One: “It is time, venerable Gotama, the meal is ready.” Then, in the morning, the Blessed One, having put on his lower robe and taking his bowl and outer robe, approached the serving hall of the chief ministers of Magadha, Sunidha and Vassakāra. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the community of monks. Then the chief ministers of Magadha, Sunidha and Vassakāra, with their own hands, served and satisfied the community of monks with the Buddha at its head with excellent hard and soft food until they indicated they had had enough. When they perceived that the Blessed One had finished his meal and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, they sat down to one side. When the chief ministers of Magadha, Sunidha and Vassakāra, were seated to one side, the Blessed One expressed his appreciation with these verses:

“Yasmiṃ padese kappeti, vāsaṃ paṇḍitajātiyo;

Sīlavantettha bhojetvā, saññate brahmacārayo brahmacārino (syā.).

“In whatever region a person of a wise nature makes a dwelling, there, having fed the virtuous, the restrained, those who lead the holy life...

“Yā tattha devatā āsuṃ, tāsaṃ dakkhiṇamādise;

Tā pūjitā pūjayanti, mānitā mānayanti naṃ.

“To whatever deities were there, one should dedicate the offering. Being worshipped, they worship in return; being revered, they revere that person in return.

“Tato [P 1.0230] naṃ anukampanti, mātā puttaṃva orasaṃ;

Devatānukampito poso, sadā bhadrāni passatī”ti.

“Therefore, they have compassion for that person, as a mother for her own son. A person shown compassion by the deities always sees good fortune.”

Atha kho bhagavā sunidhavassakāre magadhamahāmatte imāhi gāthāhi anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Tena kho pana samayena sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā bhagavantaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhā honti, “yenajja samaṇo gotamo dvārena nikkhamissati, taṃ gotamadvāraṃ nāma bhavissati[M 0.0325]; yena titthena gaṅgaṃ nadiṃ uttarissati, taṃ gotamatitthaṃ nāma bhavissatī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā yena dvārena nikkhami, taṃ gotamadvāraṃ nāma ahosi. Atha kho bhagavā yena gaṅgā nadī tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho pana samayena gaṅgā nadī pūrā hoti samatittikā kākapeyyā. Manussā aññe nāvaṃ pariyesanti[T 2.0093], aññe uḷumpaṃ pariyesanti, aññe kullaṃ bandhanti orā pāraṃ gantukāmā. Addasā kho bhagavā te manusse aññe nāvaṃ pariyesante, aññe uḷumpaṃ pariyesante, aññe kullaṃ bandhante orā pāraṃ gantukāme, disvāna seyyathāpi [V 0.0306] nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva kho gaṅgāya nadiyā orimatīre antarahito pārimatīre paccuṭṭhāsi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

Then the Blessed One, having expressed his appreciation to Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, with these verses, rose from his seat and departed. Now at that time, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, followed closely behind the Blessed One, thinking, “The gate by which the ascetic Gotama departs today shall be named the Gotama Gate, and the ford by which he crosses the Ganges River shall be named the Gotama Ford.” Then, the gate by which the Blessed One departed came to be known as the Gotama Gate. Then the Blessed One approached the Ganges River. Now at that time, the Ganges River was full, level with the banks, so that a crow could drink from it. Some people, desiring to go from this shore to the far shore, were searching for a boat; some were searching for a log-raft; and some were binding together a raft. The Blessed One saw those people desiring to go from this shore to the far shore: some searching for a boat, some searching for a log-raft, and some binding together a raft. Having seen this, just as a strong man might stretch out his bent arm or bend his outstretched arm, even so did the Blessed One vanish from this near bank of the Ganges River and reappear on the far bank together with the Saṅgha of monks. Then the Blessed One, understanding the significance of this, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

“Ye taranti aṇṇavaṃ saraṃ;

Setuṃ katvāna visajja pallalāni;

Kullañhi jano bandhati;

Tiṇṇā medhāvino janā”ti.

“They cross the great flood, having built a causeway and forsaken the mires. While the common folk bind a raft, the wise have crossed over.”

Sunidhavassakāravatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story of Sunidha and Vassakāra is concluded.

175. Koṭigāme saccakathā

175. Discourse on the Truths at Koṭigāma

287. Atha kho bhagavā yena koṭigāmo tenupasaṅkami. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā koṭigāme viharati. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – dī. ni. 2.155 “catunnaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasaccānaṃ ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Dukkhassa, bhikkhave, ariyasaccassa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Dukkhasamudayassa ariyasaccassa…pe… dukkhanirodhassa ariyasaccassa…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ariyasaccassa [T 2.0094] ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Tayidaṃ, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ [P 1.0231] anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, dukkhasamudayaṃ dukkhasamudayo (syā.) ariyasaccaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, dukkhanirodhaṃ dukkhanirodho (syā.) ariyasaccaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, ucchinnā bhavataṇhā, khīṇā bhavanetti, natthidāni punabbhavo”ti.

287. Then the Blessed One approached Koṭigāma. There, indeed, the Blessed One dwelt in Koṭigāma. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'Monks, it is through not awakening to, through not penetrating the four Noble Truths that both I and you have thus run on and transmigrated for this long course of time. Which four? Monks, it is through not awakening to, through not penetrating the Noble Truth of suffering that both I and you have thus run on and transmigrated for this long course of time. The Noble Truth of the origin of suffering... The Noble Truth of the cessation of suffering... It is through not awakening to, through not penetrating the Noble Truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering that both I and you have thus run on and transmigrated for this long course of time. Monks, this Noble Truth of suffering has been awakened to and penetrated; the Noble Truth of the origin of suffering has been awakened to and penetrated; the Noble Truth of the cessation of suffering has been awakened to and penetrated; the Noble Truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering has been awakened to and penetrated. Craving for existence has been cut off, the guide to existence is exhausted, and now there is no more renewed existence.'

Catunnaṃ [M 0.0326] ariyasaccānaṃ, yathābhūtaṃ adassanā;

Saṃsitaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ, tāsu tāsveva jātisu.

Through not seeing the Four Noble Truths as they really are, long have we transmigrated through just these various births.

Tāni [V 0.0307] etāni diṭṭhāni, bhavanetti samūhatā;

Ucchinnaṃ mūlaṃ dukkhassa, natthidāni punabbhavoti.

These have been seen; the guide to existence has been uprooted; the root of suffering has been cut off; now there is no more renewed existence.

Koṭigāme saccakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Truths at Koṭigāma is concluded.

176. Ambapālīvatthu

176. The Narrative of Ambapālī

288. dī. ni. 2.161 ādayo Assosi kho ambapālī gaṇikā – bhagavā kira koṭigāmaṃ anuppattoti. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni yojāpetvā bhadraṃ bhadraṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā bhadrehi bhadrehi yānehi vesāliyā niyyāsi bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi, yānena gantvā, yānā paccorohitvā, pattikāva yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho ambapāliṃ gaṇikaṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya [T 2.0095] sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

288. The courtesan Ambapālī heard: “The Blessed One, it is said, has arrived at Koṭigāma.” Then the courtesan Ambapālī had very fine carriages harnessed, mounted a very fine carriage, and set out from Vesālī with very fine carriages to see the Blessed One. Having gone by carriage as far as the ground was passable for a carriage, she dismounted from the carriage and approached the Blessed One on foot. Having approached, she paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. The Blessed One instructed, inspired, roused, and gladdened the courtesan Ambapālī, who was sitting to one side, with a Dhamma talk. Then the courtesan Ambapālī, having been instructed, inspired, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One consent to my meal for tomorrow, together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.” The Blessed One consented by means of silence. Then the courtesan Ambapālī, having understood the Blessed One’s consent, rose from her seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping her right side towards him, and departed.

Ambapālīvatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Narrative of Ambapālī is concluded.

177. Licchavīvatthu

177. The Narrative of the Licchavis

289. dī. ni. 2.161 ādayo Assosuṃ kho vesālikā licchavī – bhagavā kira koṭigāmaṃ anuppattoti. Atha kho vesālikā licchavī bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni yojāpetvā bhadraṃ bhadraṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā bhadrehi bhadrehi yānehi vesāliyā niyyāsuṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Appekacce licchavī nīlā honti nīlavaṇṇā nīlavatthā nīlālaṅkārā, appekacce licchavī pītā honti pītavaṇṇā pītavatthā pītālaṅkārā, appekacce licchavī lohitā honti lohitavaṇṇā lohitavatthā lohitālaṅkārā, appekacce licchavī odātā honti odātavaṇṇā odātavatthā odātālaṅkārā. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā daharānaṃ daharānaṃ licchavīnaṃ īsāya īsaṃ yugena yugaṃ cakkena cakkaṃ akkhena akkhaṃ paṭivaṭṭesi paṭivattesi (ka.). Atha [P 1.0232][M 0.0327] kho te licchavī ambapāliṃ gaṇikaṃ [V 0.0308] etadavocuṃ – “kissa, je ambapāli, daharānaṃ daharānaṃ amhākaṃ daharānaṃ daharānaṃ (sī. syā.) licchavīnaṃ īsāya īsaṃ yugena yugaṃ cakkena cakkaṃ akkhena akkhaṃ paṭivaṭṭesī”ti? “Tathā hi pana [T 2.0096] mayā, ayyaputtā, svātanāya buddhappamukho bhikkhusaṅgho nimantito”ti. “Dehi, je ambapāli, amhākaṃ etaṃ bhattaṃ satasahassenā”ti. “Sacepi me, ayyaputtā, vesāliṃ sāhāraṃ dajjeyyātha, neva dajjāhaṃ taṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho te licchavī aṅguliṃ phoṭesuṃ – “jitamhā vata, bho, ambakāya, parājitamha vata, bho, ambakāyā”ti. Atha kho te licchavī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Addasā kho bhagavā te licchavī dūratova āgacchante, disvāna bhikkhū āmantesi – “yehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi devā tāvatiṃsā adiṭṭhapubbā, oloketha, bhikkhave, licchavīparisaṃ; apaloketha, bhikkhave, licchavīparisaṃ; upasaṃharatha, bhikkhave, licchavīparisaṃ tāvatiṃsaparisa”nti. Atha kho te licchavī yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi, yānena gantvā yānā paccorohitvā pattikāva yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho te licchavī bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho te licchavī, bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “adhivāsetu no, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. “Adhivuṭṭhomhi, licchavī, svātanāya ambapāliyā gaṇikāya bhatta”nti. Atha kho te licchavī aṅguliṃ phoṭesuṃ – “jitamha vata, bho, ambakāya, parājitamha vata[T 2.0097], bho, ambakāyā”ti. Atha kho te licchavī bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkamiṃsu.

289. The Licchavis of Vesālī heard: “The Blessed One, it is said, has arrived at Koṭigāma.” Then the Licchavis of Vesālī had excellent carriages harnessed, mounted excellent carriages, and set out from Vesālī in their excellent carriages to see the Blessed One. Some Licchavis were blue, of blue complexion, with blue garments and blue adornments. Some Licchavis were yellow, of yellow complexion, with yellow garments and yellow adornments. Some Licchavis were red, of red complexion, with red garments and red adornments. Some Licchavis were white, of white complexion, with white garments and white adornments. Then the courtesan Ambapālī jostled against the very young Licchavis, pole against pole, yoke against yoke, wheel against wheel, and axle against axle. Then those Licchavis said to the courtesan Ambapālī: “Why, Ambapālī, do you jostle against the very young Licchavis, pole against pole, yoke against yoke, wheel against wheel, and axle against axle?” “It is because, my lords, I have invited the community of monks with the Buddha at its head for tomorrow.” “Give us this meal for a hundred thousand, Ambapālī.” “My lords, even if you were to give me Vesālī with its territories, I would not give up that meal.” Then those Licchavis snapped their fingers, saying: “Sirs, we have been conquered by the woman! Sirs, we have been defeated by the woman!” Then those Licchavis approached the place where the Blessed One was. The Blessed One saw those Licchavis coming from afar, and having seen them, he addressed the monks: “Monks, those of you who have not seen the Tāvatiṃsa devas before, look at this assembly of the Licchavis; gaze upon this assembly of the Licchavis; compare this assembly of the Licchavis to the assembly of the Tāvatiṃsa.” Then those Licchavis went as far as the ground was passable by carriage, then dismounted from their carriages and approached the Blessed One on foot. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. While they were sitting to one side, the Blessed One instructed, inspired, aroused, and gladdened those Licchavis with a talk on the Dhamma. Then those Licchavis, having been instructed, inspired, aroused, and gladdened by the Blessed One’s talk on the Dhamma, said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One, together with the community of monks, accept our meal for tomorrow.” “Licchavis, I have accepted the meal for tomorrow from the courtesan Ambapālī.” Then those Licchavis snapped their fingers, saying: “Sirs, we have been conquered by the woman! Sirs, we have been defeated by the woman!” Then those Licchavis, having rejoiced and delighted in the Blessed One’s words, rose from their seats, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping him to their right, and departed.

Atha kho bhagavā koṭigāme yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā mahāparinibbānasutte anusandhi aññathā āgato yena nātikā nādikā (sī. syā.) tenupasaṅkami. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā nātike viharati giñjakāvasathe. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā tassā rattiyā accayena sake ārāme paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – “kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ [M 0.0328] nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena ambapāliyā gaṇikāya parivesanā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena[P 1.0233]. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho ambapālī gaṇikā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “imāhaṃ, bhante, ambavanaṃ buddhappamukhassa bhikkhusaṅghassa dammī”ti. Paṭiggahesi bhagavā ārāmaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā ambapāliṃ gaṇikaṃ dhammiyā kathāya [V 0.0309] sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena mahāvanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ.

Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Koṭigāma as long as he pleased, approached Nātikā. There the Blessed One stayed at Nātikā in the Brick House. Then the courtesan Ambapālī, when the night had passed, had excellent hard and soft food prepared in her own park and had the time announced to the Blessed One: “It is time, venerable sir, the meal is ready.” Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and outer robe and approached the place of serving of the courtesan Ambapālī. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the community of monks. Then the courtesan Ambapālī, with her own hand, served and satisfied the community of monks headed by the Buddha with excellent hard and soft food until they indicated they had had enough. When she observed that the Blessed One had finished his meal and had removed his hand from the bowl, she sat down at one side. Seated at one side, the courtesan Ambapālī said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I give this mango grove to the community of monks headed by the Buddha.” The Blessed One accepted the park. Then the Blessed One, having instructed, inspired, aroused, and gladdened the courtesan Ambapālī with a talk on the Dhamma, rose from his seat and approached the Great Wood. There the Blessed One stayed at Vesālī in the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof.

Licchavīvatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Narrative of the Licchavis is concluded.

Licchavibhāṇavāro niṭṭhito tatiyo.

The Third Recitation Section on the Licchavis is concluded.

178. Sīhasenāpativatthu

The Story of General Sīha

290. a. ni. 8.12 ādayo Tena [T 2.0098] kho pana samayena abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī sandhāgāre santhāgāre (sī. syā.) sannisinnā sannipatitā anekapariyāyena buddhassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti, dhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti, saṅghassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti. Tena kho pana samayena sīho senāpati nigaṇṭhasāvako tassaṃ parisāyaṃ nisinno hoti. Atha kho sīhassa senāpatissa etadahosi – “nissaṃsayaṃ kho so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bhavissati, tathā hime abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī santhāgāre sannisinnā sannipatitā anekapariyāyena buddhassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti, dhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti, saṅghassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkameyyaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha”nti. Atha kho sīho senāpati yena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ etadavoca – “icchāmahaṃ, bhante, samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamitu”nti. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, sīha, kiriyavādo samāno akiriyavādaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissasi? Samaṇo hi, sīha, gotamo akiriyavādo akiriyāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī”ti. Atha kho sīhassa senāpatissa yo ahosi gamikābhisaṅkhāro bhagavantaṃ dassanāya, so [M 0.0329] paṭippassambhi. Dutiyampi kho abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī sandhāgāre sannisinnā sannipatitā anekapariyānena buddhassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti, dhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti, saṅghassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti. Dutiyampi kho sīhassa senāpatissa etadahosi – “nissaṃsayaṃ kho so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bhavissati, tathā hime abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī sandhāgāre sannisinnā sannipatitā anekapariyāyena buddhassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti, dhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti, saṅghassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkameyyaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha”nti. Dutiyampi kho sīho senāpati yena [P 1.0234] nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā nigaṇṭhaṃ nāṭaputtaṃ etadavoca – “icchāmahaṃ, bhante, samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamitu”nti. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, sīha, kiriyavādo samāno akiriyavādaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissasi? Samaṇo hi, sīha, gotamo akiriyavādo akiriyāya dhammaṃ deseti[V 0.0310], tena ca sāvake vinetī”ti. Dutiyampi kho sīhassa senāpatissa yo ahosi gamikābhisaṅkhāro bhagavantaṃ dassanāya, so paṭippassambhi. Tatiyampi kho abhiññātā abhiññātā [T 2.0099] licchavī sandhāgāre sannisinnā sannipatitā anekapariyāyena buddhassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti, dhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti, saṅghassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti. Tatiyampi kho sīhassa senāpatissa etadahosi – “nissaṃsayaṃ kho so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bhavissati, tathā hime abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī sandhāgāre sannisinnā sannipatitā anekapariyāyena buddhassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti, dhammassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti, saṅghassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsanti. Kiñhi me karissanti nigaṇṭhā apalokitā vā anapalokitā vā? Yaṃnūnāhaṃ anapaloketvāva nigaṇṭhe taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkameyyaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha”nti.

290. Now at that time, the very renowned Licchavis were seated and assembled in the assembly hall, speaking in many ways of the virtues of the Buddha, the virtues of the Dhamma, and the virtues of the Saṅgha. At that time, General Sīha, a disciple of the Nigaṇṭhas, was sitting in that assembly. Then this thought occurred to General Sīha: ‘Without a doubt, that Blessed One must be an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, for these very renowned Licchavis are seated and assembled in the assembly hall, speaking in many ways of the virtues of the Buddha, the virtues of the Dhamma, and the virtues of the Saṅgha. What if I were to go to see that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One?’ Then General Sīha approached the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta and, having approached, said this to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta: ‘Venerable sir, I wish to go to see the ascetic Gotama.’ ‘Why, Sīha, would you, being a proponent of action, go to see the ascetic Gotama, a proponent of non-action? For the ascetic Gotama, Sīha, is a proponent of non-action; he teaches the Dhamma for non-action, and he trains his disciples in it.’ Then the intention that had arisen in General Sīha to go to see the Blessed One subsided. For a second time, the very renowned Licchavis were seated and assembled in the assembly hall, speaking in many ways of the virtues of the Buddha, the virtues of the Dhamma, and the virtues of the Saṅgha. For a second time, this thought occurred to General Sīha: ‘Without a doubt, that Blessed One must be an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, for these very renowned Licchavis are seated and assembled in the assembly hall, speaking in many ways of the virtues of the Buddha, the virtues of the Dhamma, and the virtues of the Saṅgha. What if I were to go to see that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One?’ For a second time, General Sīha approached the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta and, having approached, said this to the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta: ‘Venerable sir, I wish to go to see the ascetic Gotama.’ ‘Why, Sīha, would you, being a proponent of action, go to see the ascetic Gotama, a proponent of non-action? For the ascetic Gotama, Sīha, is a proponent of non-action; he teaches the Dhamma for non-action, and he trains his disciples in it.’ For a second time, the intention that had arisen in General Sīha to go to see the Blessed One subsided. For a third time, the very renowned Licchavis were seated and assembled in the assembly hall, speaking in many ways of the virtues of the Buddha, the virtues of the Dhamma, and the virtues of the Saṅgha. For a third time, this thought occurred to General Sīha: ‘Without a doubt, that Blessed One must be an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, for these very renowned Licchavis are seated and assembled in the assembly hall, speaking in many ways of the virtues of the Buddha, the virtues of the Dhamma, and the virtues of the Saṅgha. What can the Nigaṇṭhas do to me, whether I ask their leave or not? What if I were to go to see that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, without first asking leave of the Nigaṇṭhas?’

Atha kho sīho senāpati pañcahi rathasatehi divā divassa vesāliyā niyyāsi bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi, yānena gantvā yānā paccorohitvā pattikova yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho sīho senāpati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ me taṃ, bhante, ‘akiriyavādo samaṇo gotamo akiriyāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’ti. Ye te, bhante, evamāhaṃsu ‘akiriyavādo samaṇo [M 0.0330] gotamo, akiriyāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī’ti. Kacci te, bhante, bhagavato vuttavādino, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhanti, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākaronti, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo [T 2.0100] gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchati? Anabbhakkhātukāmā hi mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavanta”nti.

Then General Sīha set out from Vesālī at midday with five hundred chariots to see the Blessed One. As far as the ground was passable for a vehicle, he went by vehicle; then, having dismounted from the vehicle, he approached the Blessed One on foot. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, General Sīha said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, I have heard this: "The ascetic Gotama is a proponent of non-action; he teaches the Dhamma for non-action, and with it he trains his disciples." Those, venerable sir, who have said thus: "The ascetic Gotama is a proponent of non-action; he teaches the Dhamma for non-action, and with it he trains his disciples"—is it that they are speaking what was said by the Blessed One, and not misrepresenting the Blessed One with what is untrue? Do they explain the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and does no legitimate assertion or subsequent assertion give grounds for censure? For indeed, venerable sir, we do not wish to misrepresent the Blessed One.'

291. “Atthi, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – akiriyavādo samaṇo gotamo, akiriyāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti. Atthi, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – kiriyavādo samaṇo gotamo kiriyāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti. Atthi, sīha, pariyāyo yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ucchedavādo samaṇo gotamo ucchedāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti. Atthi, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – jegucchī samaṇo gotamo, jegucchitāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti. Atthi, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – venayiko samaṇo gotamo, vinayāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti. Atthi, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – tapassī samaṇo gotamo, tapassitāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena [V 0.0311] ca sāvake vinetīti. Atthi, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – apagabbho samaṇo gotamo, apagabbhatāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti. Atthi, sīha[T 2.0101], pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – assattho samaṇo gotamo, assāsāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti.

291. Sīha, there is a way in which one, speaking rightly, might say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is an advocate of non-action; he teaches a doctrine for non-action, and by that doctrine he trains his disciples.’ Sīha, there is a way in which one, speaking rightly, might say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is an advocate of action; he teaches a doctrine for action, and by that doctrine he trains his disciples.’ Sīha, there is a way in which one, speaking rightly, might say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is an advocate of annihilation; he teaches a doctrine for annihilation, and by that doctrine he trains his disciples.’ Sīha, there is a way in which one, speaking rightly, might say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is one who abhors; he teaches a doctrine for abhorrence, and by that doctrine he trains his disciples.’ Sīha, there is a way in which one, speaking rightly, might say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is one who dispels; he teaches a doctrine for dispelling, and by that doctrine he trains his disciples.’ Sīha, there is a way in which one, speaking rightly, might say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is one who torments; he teaches a doctrine for tormenting, and by that doctrine he trains his disciples.’ Sīha, there is a way in which one, speaking rightly, might say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is one who is not reborn in a womb; he teaches a doctrine for not being reborn in a womb, and by that doctrine he trains his disciples.’ Sīha, there is a way in which one, speaking rightly, might say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is one who is reassured; he teaches a doctrine for reassurance, and by that doctrine he trains his disciples.’

292. “Katamo ca, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – akiriyavādo samaṇo gotamo, akiriyāya dhammaṃ deseti[P 1.0235], tena ca sāvake vinetīti? Ahañhi, sīha, akiriyaṃ vadāmi kāyaduccaritassa vacīduccaritassa manoduccaritassa; anekavihitānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ akiriyaṃ vadāmi. Ayaṃ kho, sīha, pariyāyo[M 0.0331], yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – akiriyavādo samaṇo gotamo, akiriyāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti.

292. And what, Sīha, is the way by which one, speaking rightly, might say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is a proponent of non-action; he teaches the Dhamma for non-action, and by it he trains his disciples’? For I, Sīha, teach non-action in regard to bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, and mental misconduct; I teach non-action in regard to many kinds of evil, unwholesome states. This, Sīha, is indeed the way by which one, speaking rightly, might say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is a proponent of non-action; he teaches the Dhamma for non-action, and by it he trains his disciples.’

“Katamo ca, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – kiriyavādo samaṇo gotamo, kiriyāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti? Ahañhi, sīha, kiriyaṃ vadāmi kāyasucaritassa vacīsucaritassa manosucaritassa, anekavihitānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ kiriyaṃ vadāmi. Ayaṃ kho, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – kiriyavādo samaṇo gotamo, kiriyāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti.

And what, Sīha, is the way by which one, speaking rightly, might say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is a proponent of action; he teaches the Dhamma for action, and by it he trains his disciples’? For I, Sīha, teach action in regard to good bodily conduct, good verbal conduct, and good mental conduct; I teach action in regard to many kinds of wholesome states. This, Sīha, is indeed the way by which one, speaking rightly, might say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is a proponent of action; he teaches the Dhamma for action, and by it he trains his disciples.’

“Katamo ca, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ucchedavādo samaṇo gotamo, ucchedāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti? Ahañhi, sīha, ucchedaṃ vadāmi rāgassa dosassa mohassa; anekavihitānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ucchedaṃ vadāmi. Ayaṃ kho[T 2.0102], sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ucchedavādo samaṇo gotamo ucchedāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti.

And what, Sīha, is the way by which one, speaking rightly, might say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is a proponent of annihilation; he teaches the Dhamma for annihilation, and by it he trains his disciples’? For I, Sīha, teach the annihilation of greed, hatred, and delusion; I teach the annihilation of many kinds of evil, unwholesome states. This, Sīha, is indeed the way by which one, speaking rightly, might say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is a proponent of annihilation; he teaches the Dhamma for annihilation, and by it he trains his disciples.’

“Katamo ca, sīha, pariyāyo yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – jegucchī samaṇo gotamo, jegucchitāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti? Ahañhi, sīha, jigucchāmi kāyaduccaritena vacīduccaritena manoduccaritena; anekavihitānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā jigucchāmi. Ayaṃ kho, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena [V 0.0312] sammā vadamāno vadeyya – jegucchī samaṇo gotamo, jegucchitāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti.

And what, Sīha, is the way in which one speaking rightly could say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is one who abhors; he teaches the Dhamma for the purpose of abhorrence, and by it he trains his disciples’? For I, Sīha, abhor bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, and mental misconduct; I abhor the attainment of various kinds of evil, unwholesome states. This, Sīha, is indeed the way in which one speaking rightly could say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is one who abhors; he teaches the Dhamma for the purpose of abhorrence, and by it he trains his disciples.’

“Katamo ca, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – venayiko samaṇo gotamo, vinayāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti? Ahañhi, sīha, vinayāya dhammaṃ desemi rāgassa dosassa mohassa; anekavihitānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ [M 0.0332] dhammānaṃ vinayāya dhammaṃ desemi. Ayaṃ kho, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – venayiko samaṇo gotamo, vinayāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti.

And what, Sīha, is the way in which one speaking rightly could say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is a dispeller; he teaches the Dhamma for the purpose of dispelling, and by it he trains his disciples’? For I, Sīha, teach the Dhamma for the purpose of dispelling greed, hatred, and delusion; I teach the Dhamma for the purpose of dispelling various kinds of evil, unwholesome states. This, Sīha, is indeed the way in which one speaking rightly could say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is a dispeller; he teaches the Dhamma for the purpose of dispelling, and by it he trains his disciples.’

“Katamo ca, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – tapassī samaṇo gotamo, tapassitāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti? Tapanīyāhaṃ, sīha, pāpake akusale dhamme vadāmi – kāyaduccaritaṃ vacīduccaritaṃ manoduccaritaṃ. Yassa kho, sīha, tapanīyā pāpakā akusalā dhammā [T 2.0103] pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā, tamahaṃ tapassīti vadāmi. Tathāgatassa kho, sīha, tapanīyā pāpakā akusalā dhammā pahīnā ucchīnnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Ayaṃ kho, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya “tapassī samaṇo gotamo [P 1.0236] tapassitāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī”ti.

And what, Sīha, is the way by which one speaking rightly might say of me: 'The ascetic Gotama is one who torments; he teaches the Dhamma for the purpose of tormenting, and by it he trains his disciples'? Sīha, I say that evil, unwholesome states are tormenting—bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, and mental misconduct. For whomever, Sīha, these tormenting, evil, unwholesome states are abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm-tree stump, brought to non-existence, and are subject to non-arising in the future, him I call 'one who torments'. For the Tathāgata, Sīha, these tormenting, evil, unwholesome states have been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm-tree stump, brought to non-existence, and are subject to non-arising in the future. This, Sīha, is the way by which one speaking rightly might say of me: 'The ascetic Gotama is one who torments; he teaches the Dhamma for the purpose of tormenting, and by it he trains his disciples.'

“Katamo ca, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – apagabbho samaṇo gotamo apagabbhatāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti? Yassa kho, sīha, āyatiṃ gabbhaseyyā punabbhavābhinibbatti pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā, tamahaṃ apagabbhoti vadāmi. Tathāgatassa kho, sīha, āyatiṃ gabbhaseyyā punabbhavābhinibbatti pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Ayaṃ kho, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – apagabbho samaṇo gotamo, apagabbhatāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti.

And what, Sīha, is the principle by which one speaking rightly might say of me: 'The recluse Gotama is one who is free from the womb; he teaches the Dhamma for freedom from the womb, and by it he trains his disciples'? For whomever, Sīha, future lying in the womb and rebirth in a new existence are abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm-tree stump, brought to non-existence, and are subject to non-arising in the future, him I call 'one who is free from the womb'. For the Tathāgata, Sīha, future lying in the womb and rebirth in a new existence have been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm-tree stump, brought to non-existence, and are subject to non-arising in the future. This, Sīha, is the principle by which one speaking rightly might say of me: 'The recluse Gotama is one who is free from the womb; he teaches the Dhamma for freedom from the womb, and by it he trains his disciples.'

“Katamo ca, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā vadamāno vadeyya – assattho samaṇo gotamo assāsāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetīti? Ahañhi, sīha, assattho [V 0.0313] paramena assāsena, assāsāya dhammaṃ desemi, tena ca sāvake vinemi. Ayaṃ kho, sīha, pariyāyo, yena maṃ pariyāyena sammā [T 2.0104] vadamāno vadeyya – assattho samaṇo gotamo assāsāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī”ti.

“And what, Sīha, is the principle by which one speaking rightly might say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is consoled; he teaches the Dhamma for consolation, and by it he trains his disciples’? For I, Sīha, am consoled with the supreme consolation; I teach the Dhamma for consolation, and by it I train my disciples. This, Sīha, is the principle by which one speaking rightly might say of me: ‘The ascetic Gotama is consoled; he teaches the Dhamma for consolation, and by it he trains his disciples.’”

293. Evaṃ [M 0.0333] vutte sīho senāpati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. “Anuviccakāraṃ anuvijjakāraṃ (ka.) kho, sīha, karohi; anuviccakāro tumhādisānaṃ ñātamanussānaṃ sādhu hotī”ti. “Imināpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato bhiyyosomattāya attamano abhiraddho, yaṃ maṃ bhagavā evamāha – ‘anuviccakāraṃ kho, sīha, karohi; anuviccakāro tumhādisānaṃ ñātamanussānaṃ sādhu hotī’ti. Mamañhi, bhante, aññatitthiyā sāvakaṃ labhitvā kevalakappaṃ vesāliṃ paṭākaṃ parihareyyuṃ – ‘sīho kho amhākaṃ senāpati sāvakattaṃ upagato’ti. Atha ca pana maṃ bhagavā evamāha – ‘anuviccakāraṃ kho, sīha, karohi; anuviccakāro tumhādisānaṃ ñātamanussānaṃ sādhu hotī’ti. Esāhaṃ, bhante, dutiyampi bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā [T 2.0105] dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. “Dīgharattaṃ kho te, sīha, nigaṇṭhānaṃ opānabhūtaṃ kulaṃ, yena nesaṃ upagatānaṃ piṇḍakaṃ dātabbaṃ maññeyyāsī”ti. “Imināpāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato bhiyyosomattāya attamano abhiraddho, yaṃ maṃ bhagavā evamāha – ‘dīgharattaṃ kho te, sīha, nigaṇṭhānaṃ opānabhūtaṃ kulaṃ, yena nesaṃ upagatānaṃ piṇḍakaṃ dātabbaṃ maññeyyāsī’ti. Sutaṃ me taṃ, bhante, samaṇo gotamo evamāha – ‘mayhameva dānaṃ dātabbaṃ, na aññesaṃ dānaṃ dātabbaṃ; mayhameva sāvakānaṃ dānaṃ dātabbaṃ, na aññesaṃ sāvakānaṃ dānaṃ dātabbaṃ[P 1.0237]; mayhameva dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ, na aññesaṃ dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ; mayhameva sāvakānaṃ dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ, na aññesaṃ sāvakānaṃ dinnaṃ mahapphala’nti. Atha ca pana maṃ bhagavā nigaṇṭhesupi dāne samādapeti. Api ca, bhante, mayamettha kālaṃ jānissāma. Esāhaṃ, bhante, tatiyampi bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

293. When this was said, General Sīha said this to the Blessed One: “Magnificent, venerable sir! … May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts.” “Consider carefully, Sīha; careful consideration is good for people like you, who are well-known.” “Venerable sir, I am even more pleased and delighted with the Blessed One for saying this: ‘Consider carefully, Sīha; careful consideration is good for people like you, who are well-known.’ For if other sectarians were to obtain me as a disciple, they would carry a banner all around Vesālī, proclaiming: ‘General Sīha has become our disciple!’ Yet the Blessed One tells me: ‘Consider carefully, Sīha; careful consideration is good for people like you, who are well-known.’ So, venerable sir, for the second time I go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts.” “Your family, Sīha, has long been like a well of water for the Nigaṇṭhas, so you should think of giving alms to them when they come.” “Venerable sir, I am even more pleased and delighted with the Blessed One for saying this: ‘Your family, Sīha, has long been like a well of water for the Nigaṇṭhas, so you should think of giving alms to them when they come.’ For I have heard, venerable sir, that the ascetic Gotama says: ‘Gifts should be given only to me; gifts should not be given to others. Gifts should be given only to my disciples; gifts should not be given to the disciples of others. What is given to me is of great fruit; what is given to others is not of great fruit. What is given to my disciples is of great fruit; what is given to the disciples of others is not of great fruit.’ Yet the Blessed One encourages me to give to the Nigaṇṭhas as well. But, venerable sir, we will know the proper time for this. So, venerable sir, for the third time I go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts.”

Atha kho bhagavā sīhassa senāpatissa anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ…pe… [T 2.0106] aparappaccayo satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha [M 0.0334] kho sīho senāpati bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

Then the Blessed One gave General Sīha a progressive discourse, namely: a talk on generosity… and so on… Having become one not dependent on another in the Teacher's Dispensation, he said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One, together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, consent to a meal from me tomorrow.' The Blessed One consented by remaining silent. Then General Sīha, knowing the Blessed One's consent, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping him to the right, and departed.

294. Atha [V 0.0314] kho sīho senāpati aññataraṃ purisaṃ āṇāpesi – “gaccha, bhaṇe, pavattamaṃsaṃ jānāhī”ti. Atha kho sīho senāpati tassā rattiyā accayena paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – “kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena sīhassa senāpatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena.

294. Then General Sīha ordered a certain man, saying: 'Go, good man, and find out about readily available meat.' Then, when that night had passed, General Sīha had excellent hard and soft foods prepared and had the time announced to the Blessed One, saying: 'Venerable Sir, it is time; the meal is ready.' Then the Blessed One, in the morning, having put on his lower robe and taking his bowl and outer robe, went to the residence of General Sīha. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.

Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā nigaṇṭhā vesāliyaṃ rathikāya rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ bāhā paggayha kandanti – “ajja sīhena senāpatinā thūlaṃ pasuṃ vadhitvā samaṇassa gotamassa bhattaṃ kataṃ, taṃ samaṇo gotamo jānaṃ [T 2.0107] uddissakataṃ maṃsaṃ paribhuñjati paṭiccakamma”nti. Atha kho aññataro puriso yena sīho senāpati tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā sīhassa senāpatissa upakaṇṇake ārocesi “yagghe, bhante, jāneyyāsi, ete sambahulā nigaṇṭhā vesāliyaṃ rathikāya rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ bāhā paggayha kandanti – ‘ajja sīhena senāpatinā thūlaṃ pasuṃ vadhitvā samaṇassa gotamassa bhattaṃ kataṃ, taṃ samaṇo gotamo jānaṃ uddissakataṃ maṃsaṃ paribhuñjati paṭiccakamma’”nti. “Alaṃ ayyo, dīgharattampi te āyasmantā avaṇṇakāmā buddhassa, avaṇṇakāmā dhammassa, avaṇṇakāmā saṅghassa; na ca pana te āyasmantā jiridanti taṃ bhagavantaṃ asatā tucchā musā abhūtena abbhācikkhantā; na ca mayaṃ jīvitahetupi sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropeyyāmā”ti. Atha kho sīho senāpati buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā [P 1.0238] sampavāretvā bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho sīhaṃ senāpatiṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, jā naṃ uddissakataṃ [T 2.0108] maṃsaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo [M 0.0335] paribhuñjeyya āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tikoṭiparisuddhaṃ macchamaṃsaṃ – adiṭṭhaṃ assutaṃ aparisaṅkita”nti.

At that time, many Nigaṇṭhas, going from street to street and from crossroads to crossroads in Vesālī, were raising their arms and lamenting: 'Today, General Sīha, having killed a large animal, has prepared a meal for the ascetic Gotama. The ascetic Gotama knowingly partakes of meat prepared on purpose for him, an act done on his account.' Then a certain man approached General Sīha and, having approached, reported it near his ear: 'Venerable sir, may you please know, these many Nigaṇṭhas, going from street to street and from crossroads to crossroads in Vesālī, are raising their arms and lamenting: "Today, General Sīha, having killed a large animal, has prepared a meal for the ascetic Gotama. The ascetic Gotama knowingly partakes of meat prepared on purpose for him, an act done on his account."' 'Enough, good sir. For a long time, these venerable ones have been desirous of the Buddha's dispraise, desirous of the Dhamma's dispraise, desirous of the Saṅgha's dispraise. And these venerable ones do not cease from accusing the Blessed One with what is non-existent, empty, false, and untrue. As for us, we would not intentionally deprive a living being of life, even for the sake of our own life.' Then General Sīha, with his own hands, served and satisfied the Saṅgha of monks with the Buddha at its head with excellent hard and soft food. When the Blessed One had finished his meal and had removed his hand from the bowl, he sat down to one side. To General Sīha, who was sitting to one side, the Blessed One instructed, established, roused, and gladdened him with a Dhamma talk, then rose from his seat and departed. Then, on this occasion, in this connection, the Blessed One, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: 'Monks, meat known to have been prepared on purpose should not be partaken of. Whoever should partake of it, there is an offense of wrong-doing. I allow, monks, fish and meat that is pure in three respects: not seen, not heard, and not suspected.'

Sīhasenāpativatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story of General Sīha is concluded.

179. Kappiyabhūmianujānanā

179. The Allowance Concerning Suitable Grounds

295. Tena [V 0.0315] kho pana samayena vesālī subhikkhā hoti susassā sulabhapiṇḍā, sukarā uñchena paggahena yāpetuṃ. Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “yāni tāni mayā bhikkhūnaṃ anuññātāni dubbhikkhe dussasse dullabhapiṇḍe anto vuṭṭhaṃ anto pakkaṃ sāmaṃ pakkaṃ uggahitapaṭiggahitakaṃ tato nīhaṭaṃ purebhattaṃ paṭiggahitaṃ vanaṭṭhaṃ pokkharaṭṭhaṃ, ajjāpi nu kho tāni bhikkhū paribhuñjantī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “yāni tāni, ānanda, mayā bhikkhūnaṃ anuññātāni dubbhikkhe dussasse dullabhapiṇḍe anto vuṭṭhaṃ anto pakkaṃ sāmaṃ pakkaṃ uggahitapaṭiggahitakaṃ tato nīhaṭaṃ purebhattaṃ paṭiggahitaṃ vanaṭṭhaṃ pokkharaṭṭhaṃ, ajjāpi nu kho tāni bhikkhū paribhuñjantī”ti? “Paribhuñjanti bhagavā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “yāni tāni, bhikkhave, mayā bhikkhūnaṃ anuññātāni dubbhikkhe dussasse dullabhapiṇḍe anto vuṭṭhaṃ anto pakkaṃ sāmaṃ pakkaṃ uggahitapaṭiggahitakaṃ tato nīhaṭaṃ purebhattaṃ paṭiggahitaṃ vanaṭṭhaṃ pokkharaṭṭhaṃ, tānāhaṃ ajjatagge paṭikkhipāmi. Na, bhikkhave, anto vuṭṭhaṃ anto pakkaṃ sāmaṃ pakkaṃ [T 2.0109] uggahitapaṭiggahitakaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na ca, bhikkhave, tato nīhaṭaṃ purebhattaṃ paṭiggahitaṃ vanaṭṭhaṃ pokkharaṭṭhaṃ bhuttāvinā pavāritena anatirittaṃ paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Yo paribhuñjeyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.

295. At that time, Vesālī was prosperous, with good crops and readily available almsfood; it was easy to sustain oneself by going for alms with bowl in hand. Then, as the Blessed One had gone to a secluded place and was dwelling in solitude, this reflection arose in his mind: ‘Those things which were permitted by me for the monks during a famine, when there are bad crops, when almsfood is difficult to obtain—namely, what is stored indoors, what is cooked indoors, what is cooked by oneself, re-accepting what has become invalidly offered, what is brought from there, what is accepted before the mealtime, what is from the forest, and what is from a lotus pond—I wonder, do the monks still consume these things even today?’ Then, in the evening, the Blessed One, having arisen from his solitude, addressed the Venerable Ānanda: ‘Ānanda, those things which were permitted by me for the monks during a famine, when there are bad crops, when almsfood is difficult to obtain—namely, what is stored indoors, what is cooked indoors, what is cooked by oneself, re-accepting what has become invalidly offered, what is brought from there, what is accepted before the mealtime, what is from the forest, and what is from a lotus pond—I wonder, do the monks still consume these things even today?’ ‘They do consume them, Blessed One.’ Then, on this occasion and in this matter, the Blessed One, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: ‘Monks, those things which were permitted by me for the monks during a famine, when there are bad crops, when almsfood is difficult to obtain—namely, what is stored indoors, what is cooked indoors, what is cooked by oneself, re-accepting what has become invalidly offered, what is brought from there, what is accepted before the mealtime, what is from the forest, and what is from a lotus pond—those things I now, from this day forward, prohibit. Monks, what is stored indoors, what is cooked indoors, what is cooked by oneself, and re-accepting what has become invalidly offered should not be consumed. Whichever monk should consume them, he commits an offense of wrong-doing. And, monks, what is brought from there, what is accepted before the mealtime, what is from the forest, and what is from a lotus pond should not be consumed by a monk who has finished eating and has refused more food, unless it has been made a formal leftover. Whichever monk should consume them, he is to be dealt with according to the rule.’

Tena kho pana samayena jānapadā manussā bahuṃ loṇampi, telampi, taṇḍulampi, khādanīyampi sakaṭesu āropetvā bahārāmakoṭṭhake sakaṭaparivaṭṭaṃ karitvā acchanti – yadā paṭipāṭiṃ labhissāma, tadā bhattaṃ karissāmāti. Mahā ca megho [P 1.0239] uggato hoti. Atha kho te manussā yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavocuṃ – “idha, bhante ānanda, bahuṃ loṇampi, telampi, taṇḍulampi, khādanīyampi sakaṭesu āropitā tiṭṭhanti, mahā ca megho uggato[M 0.0336]; kathaṃ nu kho, bhante ānanda, paṭipajjitabba”nti? Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. “Tena hānanda, saṅgho paccantimaṃ vihāraṃ kappiyabhūmiṃ sammannitvā tattha vāsetu, yaṃ saṅgho ākaṅkhati vihāraṃ vā aḍḍhayogaṃ vā pāsādaṃ vā hammiyaṃ vā guhaṃ vā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbā. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

At that time, people from the countryside had loaded much salt, oil, rice, and edible food onto carts. Having arranged their carts in a circle outside the monastery gate-house, they were staying there, thinking, 'When we get our turn, we will make a meal offering.' And a great cloud had arisen. Then those people approached the Venerable Ānanda and, having approached, said this to the Venerable Ānanda: 'Venerable Ānanda, here much salt, oil, rice, and edible food have been loaded onto carts and are standing by, and a great cloud has arisen. How, Venerable Ānanda, should we proceed?' Then the Venerable Ānanda informed the Blessed One of this matter. 'In that case, Ānanda, let the Saṅgha designate a remote dwelling as permissible grounds and store the provisions there—whatever the Saṅgha desires: a dwelling, a gabled building, a mansion, a terraced building, or a cave. And, monks, it should be designated in this way. The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and able monk:

“Suṇātu [V 0.0316] me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ vihāraṃ kappiyabhūmiṃ sammanneyya, esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. If it is timely for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should designate the dwelling of such-and-such a name as permissible grounds. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ vihāraṃ kappiyabhūmiṃ sammannati[T 2.0110]. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa vihārassa kappiyabhūmiyā sammuti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me. The Saṅgha designates the dwelling of such-and-such a name as permissible grounds. To whichever venerable one the designation of the dwelling of such-and-such a name as permissible grounds is agreeable, he should be silent. To whom it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Sammato saṅghena itthannāmo vihāro kappiyabhūmi. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The dwelling of such-and-such a name has been designated by the Saṅgha as permissible grounds. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha; therefore, there is silence. Thus I take it.

Tena kho pana samayena manussā tattheva sammutiyā sammatikāya (syā.) kappiyabhūmiyā yāguyo pacanti, bhattāni pacanti, sūpāni sampādenti, maṃsāni koṭṭenti, kaṭṭhāni phālenti. Assosi kho bhagavā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya uccāsaddaṃ mahāsaddaṃ kākoravasaddaṃ, sutvāna āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “kiṃ nu kho so, ānanda, uccāsaddo mahāsaddo kākoravasaddo”ti? “Etarahi, bhante, manussā tattheva sammutiyā kappiyabhūmiyā yāguyo pacanti, bhattāni pacanti, sūpāni sampādenti, maṃsāni koṭṭenti, kaṭṭhāni phālenti. So eso, bhagavā, uccāsaddo mahāsaddo kākoravasaddo”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, sammuti sammatikā (syā.) kappiyabhūmi paribhuñjitabbā. Yo paribhuñjeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tisso kappiyabhūmiyo – ussāvanantikaṃ gonisādikaṃ gahapati”nti.

At that time, people were cooking gruel, cooking rice, preparing curries, chopping meat, and splitting firewood right there in the designated permissible ground. The Blessed One, having risen at dawn, heard a high sound, a great sound, the cawing sound of crows.
