Having heard this, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Ānanda, what is that high sound, that great sound, that cawing sound of crows?” “Venerable sir, people are now cooking gruel, cooking rice, preparing curries, chopping meat, and splitting firewood right there in the designated permissible ground. That, Blessed One, is this high sound, this great sound, this cawing sound of crows.” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: “Monks, a designated permissible ground should not be used. Whoever uses it, commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow, monks, three types of permissible grounds: an area designated by proclamation, a cattle-resting place, and a householder's residence.”

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā yasojo gilāno hoti. Tassatthāya bhesajjāni āhariyanti. Tāni bhikkhū bahi vāsenti. Ukkapiṇḍikāpi [T 2.0111] khādanti, corāpi haranti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi[M 0.0337], bhikkhave, sammutiṃ kappiyabhūmiṃ paribhuñjituṃ[P 1.0240]. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, catasso kappiyabhūmiyo – ussāvanantikaṃ gonisādikaṃ gahapatiṃ sammutinti.

At that time, the Venerable Yasojā was ill. Medicines were brought for his sake. The monks kept them outside. Vermin also ate them, and thieves also stole them. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow the use of a designated permissible ground. I allow, monks, four types of permissible grounds: an area designated by proclamation, a cattle-resting place, a householder's residence, and an area designated by formal resolution.”

Kappiyabhūmianujānanā niṭṭhitā.

The authorization of permissible grounds is concluded.

Sīhabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito catuttho.

The fourth recitation section, the Sīha section, is concluded.

180. Meṇḍakagahapativatthu

180. The Story of the Householder Meṇḍaka

296. Tena [V 0.0317] kho pana samayena bhaddiyanagare meṇḍako gahapati paṭivasati. Tassa evarūpo iddhānubhāvo hoti – sīsaṃ nahāyitvā dhaññāgāraṃ sammajjāpetvā bahidvāre nisīdati, antalikkhā dhaññassa dhārā opatitvā dhaññāgāraṃ pūreti. Bhariyāya evarūpo iddhānubhāvo hoti – ekaṃyeva āḷhakathālikaṃ upanisīditvā ekañca sūpabhiñjanakaṃ sūpabhiñjarakaṃ (sī.) dāsakammakaraporisaṃ bhattena parivisati, na tāva taṃ khiyyati khīyati (sī. syā.) yāva sā na vuṭṭhāti. Puttassa evarūpo iddhānubhāvo hoti – ekaṃyeva sahassathavikaṃ gahetvā dāsakammakaraporisassa chamāsikaṃ vetanaṃ deti, na tāva taṃ khiyyati yāvassa hatthagatā. Suṇisāya evarūpo iddhānubhāvo hoti – ekaṃyeva catudoṇikaṃ piṭakaṃ upanisīditvā dāsakammakaraporisassa chamāsikaṃ bhattaṃ deti, na tāva taṃ khiyyati yāva sā na vuṭṭhāti. Dāsassa evarūpo iddhānubhāvo hoti – ekena naṅgalena kasantassa satta sītāyo gacchanti.

296. Now at that time, the householder Meṇḍaka resided in the city of Bhaddiya. He possessed such supernormal power: after washing his head and having the granary swept, he would sit outside the door, and streams of grain would fall from the sky, filling the granary. His wife possessed such supernormal power: sitting down beside a single āḷhaka-measure rice pot and a single curry pot, she would serve food to the servants and workers, and it would not be exhausted until she rose. Their son possessed such supernormal power: taking a single purse containing a thousand, he would give six months’ wages to the servants and workers, and it would not be exhausted as long as it remained in his hand. Their daughter-in-law possessed such supernormal power: sitting down beside a single four-doṇa basket, she would give six months’ rations to the servants and workers, and it would not be exhausted until she rose. Their slave possessed such supernormal power: when plowing with a single plowshare, seven furrows would be made.

Assosi kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro – “amhākaṃ [T 2.0112] kira vijite bhaddiyanagare meṇḍako gahapati paṭivasati. Tassa evarūpo iddhānubhāvo – sīsaṃ nahāyitvā dhaññāgāraṃ sammajjāpetvā bahidvāre nisīdati, antalikkhā dhaññassa dhārā opatitvā dhaññāgāraṃ pūreti. Bhariyāya evarūpo iddhānubhāvo – ekaṃyeva āḷhakathālikaṃ upanisīditvā ekañca sūpabhiñjanakaṃ dāsakammakaraporisaṃ bhattena parivisati, na tāva taṃ khiyyati yāva sā na vuṭṭhāti. Puttassa evarūpo iddhānubhāvo – ekaṃyeva sahassathavikaṃ gahetvā dāsakammakaraporisassa chamāsikaṃ vetanaṃ deti, na tāva taṃ khiyyati yāvassa hatthagatā. Suṇisāya evarūpo [M 0.0338] iddhānubhāvo – ekaṃyeva catudoṇikaṃ piṭakaṃ upanisīditvā dāsakammakaraporisassa chamāsikaṃ bhattaṃ deti, na tāva taṃ khiyyati yāva sā na vuṭṭhāti. Dāsassa evarūpo iddhānubhāvo – ekena naṅgalena kasantassa satta sītāyo gacchantī”ti. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro aññataraṃ sabbatthakaṃ mahāmattaṃ āmantesi – “amhākaṃ kira, bhaṇe, vijite bhaddiyanagare meṇḍako gahapati paṭivasati. Tassa evarūpo iddhānubhāvo [P 1.0241] – sīsaṃ nahāyitvā dhaññāgāraṃ sammajjāpetvā bahidvāre nisīdati, antalikkhā dhaññassa dhārā opatitvā dhaññāgāraṃ pūreti. Bhariyāya…pe… puttassa… suṇisāya… dāsassa evarūpo iddhānubhāvo, ekena naṅgalena kasantassa satta sītāyo gacchantīti. Gaccha, bhaṇe, jānāhi. Yathā mayā sāmaṃ diṭṭho, evaṃ tava diṭṭho bhavissatī”ti.

King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha heard: “It is said that in our territory, in the city of Bhaddiya, lives the householder Meṇḍaka. He possesses such supernormal power—after washing his head and having the granary swept, he sits outside the door, and streams of grain fall from the sky, filling the granary. His wife has such supernormal power—sitting down with just one āḷhaka-measure pot and one pot of curry and relish, she serves the servants and workers with food, and it does not run out until she gets up. His son has such supernormal power—taking just one purse containing a thousand, he gives six months’ wages to the servants and workers, and it does not run out as long as it remains in his hand. His daughter-in-law has such supernormal power—sitting down with just one four-doṇa basket, she gives six months’ rations to the servants and workers, and it does not run out until she gets up. His slave has such supernormal power—when plowing with one plow, seven furrows are made at once.” Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha addressed a certain general minister: “Sir, it is said that in our territory, in the city of Bhaddiya, lives the householder Meṇḍaka. He possesses such supernormal power—after washing his head… his wife… his son… his daughter-in-law… his slave has such supernormal power, and when plowing with one plow, seven furrows are made at once. Go, sir, and find out. Your seeing it will be as if I had seen it myself.”

297. Evaṃ[V 0.0318], devāti [T 2.0113] kho so mahāmatto rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa paṭissuṇitvā caturaṅginiyā senāya yena bhaddiyaṃ tena pāyāsi. Anupubbena yena bhaddiyaṃ yena meṇḍako gahapati tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā meṇḍakaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “ahañhi, gahapati, raññā āṇatto ‘amhākaṃ kira, bhaṇe, vijite bhaddiyanagare meṇḍako gahapati paṭivasati, tassa evarūpo iddhānubhāvo, sīsaṃ nahāyitvā…pe… bhariyāya… puttassa… suṇisāya… dāsassa evarūpo iddhānubhāvo, ekena naṅgalena kasantassa satta sītāyo gacchantī’ti, gaccha, bhaṇe, jānāhi. Yathā mayā sāmaṃ diṭṭho, evaṃ tava diṭṭho bhavissatī’ti. Passāma te, gahapati, iddhānubhāva”nti. Atha kho meṇḍako gahapati sīsaṃ nahāyitvā dhaññāgāraṃ sammajjāpetvā bahidvāre nisīdi, antalikkhā dhaññassa dhārā opatitvā dhaññāgāraṃ pūresi. “Diṭṭho te, gahapati, iddhānubhāvo. Bhariyāya te iddhānubhāvaṃ [T 2.0114] passissāmā”ti. Atha kho meṇḍako gahapati bhariyaṃ āṇāpesi – “tena hi caturaṅginiṃ senaṃ bhattena parivisā”ti. Atha kho meṇḍakassa gahapatissa bhariyā ekaṃyeva āḷhakathālikaṃ upanisīditvā ekañca sūpabhiñjanakaṃ caturaṅginiṃ senaṃ bhattena parivisi, na tāva taṃ khiyyati, yāva sā na vuṭṭhāti. “Diṭṭho te, gahapati, bhariyāyapi iddhānubhāvo. Puttassa te iddhānubhāvaṃ passissāmā”ti. Atha kho meṇḍako gahapati puttaṃ āṇāpesi – “tena hi caturaṅginiyā senāya chamāsikaṃ vetanaṃ dehī”ti[M 0.0339]. Atha kho meṇḍakassa gahapatissa putto ekaṃyeva sahassathavikaṃ gahetvā caturaṅginiyā senāya chamāsikaṃ vetanaṃ adāsi, na tāva taṃ khiyyati, yāvassa hatthagatā. “Diṭṭho te, gahapati, puttassapi iddhānubhāvo. Suṇisāya te iddhānubhāvaṃ passissāmā”ti. Atha kho meṇḍako gahapati suṇisaṃ āṇāpesi – “tena hi caturaṅginiyā senāya chamāsikaṃ bhattaṃ dehī”ti. Atha kho meṇḍakassa gahapatissa suṇisā ekaṃyeva catudoṇikaṃ piṭakaṃ upanisīditvā caturaṅginiyā senāya chamāsikaṃ bhattaṃ adāsi, na tāva taṃ khiyyati yāva sā na vuṭṭhāti. “Diṭṭho te, gahapati, suṇisāyapi iddhānubhāvo. Dāsassa te iddhānubhāvaṃ passissāmā”ti. “Mayhaṃ kho, sāmi, dāsassa iddhānubhāvo khette passitabbo”ti. “Alaṃ, gahapati, diṭṭho te dāsassapi iddhānubhāvo”ti. Atha kho so mahāmatto caturaṅginiyā senāya punadeva rājagahaṃ paccāgañchi. Yena rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa etamatthaṃ ārocesi.

297. “Very well, lord,” replied the great minister to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha. Then, with the fourfold army, he set out for Bhaddiya. In due course, he reached Bhaddiya and approached the householder Meṇḍaka. Upon arrival, he said to Meṇḍaka the householder: “Householder, I have been commanded by the king: ‘It is said, great minister, that in our realm, in the city of Bhaddiya, dwells the householder Meṇḍaka, who possesses such supernormal power—after he washes his head… his wife… his son… his daughter-in-law… his slave possesses such supernormal power, and when he plows with a single plow, seven furrows are made.’ Go, great minister, and find out. Just as it has been seen by me myself, so it will be seen by you. Let us witness your supernormal power, householder.” Then Meṇḍaka the householder washed his head, had the granary swept clean, and sat outside the door. A shower of grain fell from the sky and filled the granary. “Your supernormal power has been seen, householder. We shall see your wife’s supernormal power.” Meṇḍaka then instructed his wife: “Well then, serve the fourfold army with food.” His wife sat down with a single āḷhaka-measure pot and a single pot of curry and relish, and served the fourfold army with food. It was not exhausted until she rose from her seat. “Your wife’s supernormal power has also been seen, householder. We shall see your son’s supernormal power.” Meṇḍaka instructed his son: “Well then, give the fourfold army six months’ wages.” His son took a single purse containing a thousand and gave the fourfold army six months’ wages. It was not exhausted as long as it remained in his hand. “Your son’s supernormal power has also been seen, householder. We shall see your daughter-in-law’s supernormal power.” Meṇḍaka instructed his daughter-in-law: “Well then, give the fourfold army six months’ rations.” His daughter-in-law sat down with a single four-doṇa basket and gave the fourfold army six months’ rations. It was not exhausted until she rose from her seat. “Your daughter-in-law’s supernormal power has also been seen, householder. We shall see your slave’s supernormal power.” “My lord, my slave’s supernormal power is to be seen in the field.” “Enough, householder, your slave’s supernormal power has been seen too.” Then the great minister returned once more to Rājagaha with the fourfold army. He approached King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha and reported this matter to him.

298. Atha [P 1.0242] kho bhagavā vesāliyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena bhaddiyaṃ tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhatelasehi bhikkhusatehi. Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ [V 0.0319] caramāno yena [T 2.0115] bhaddiyaṃ tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā bhaddiye viharati jātiyā vane. Assosi kho meṇḍako gahapati – “samaṇo khalu bho gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito bhaddiyaṃ anuppatto bhaddiye viharati jātiyā vane. Taṃ kho pana bhagavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ bhagavāti (ka.). So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti. So dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti. Sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ hotī”ti. Atha kho meṇḍako gahapati bhadrāni bhadrāni yānāni yojāpetvā bhadraṃ bhadraṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā bhadrehi bhadrehi yānehi [M 0.0340] bhaddiyā niyyāsi bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Addasaṃsu kho sambahulā titthiyā meṇḍakaṃ gahapatiṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ, disvāna meṇḍakaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavocuṃ – “kahaṃ tvaṃ, gahapati, gacchasī”ti? “Gacchāmahaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ idaṃ padaṃ sī. syā. potthakesu natthi samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāyā”ti. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, gahapati, kiriyavādo samāno akiriyavādaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamissasi? Samaṇo hi, gahapati, gotamo akiriyavādo akiriyāya dhammaṃ deseti, tena ca sāvake vinetī”ti. Atha kho meṇḍakassa gahapatissa [T 2.0116] etadahosi – “nissaṃsayaṃ, kho so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bhavissati, yathayime titthiyā usūyantī”ti. Yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi, yānena gantvā yānā paccorohitvā pattikova yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnassa kho meṇḍakassa gahapatissa bhagavā anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ…pe… aparappaccayo satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante…pe… [T 2.0117] upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gataṃ[P 1.0243]. Adhivāsetu ca me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho meṇḍako gahapati bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

298. Then the Blessed One, having dwelt in Vesālī as long as he pleased, set out on a journey to Bhaddiya with a great Saṅgha of bhikkhus, with twelve hundred and fifty bhikkhus. Traveling in stages, the Blessed One arrived at Bhaddiya. There the Blessed One dwelt in the Jātiyā Grove. The householder Meṇḍaka heard: “The ascetic Gotama, a son of the Sakyans who has gone forth from the Sakyan clan, has arrived at Bhaddiya and is dwelling in the Jātiyā Grove. Of that Blessed One Gotama, such a good report of his fame has spread: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, accomplished in true knowledge and conduct, the Fortunate One, knower of the world, the unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Enlightened One, the Blessed One.’ He, having realized this world with its devas, its Māras, and its Brahmās, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans, for himself with special knowledge, makes it known. He teaches the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and phrasing; he reveals the holy life that is entirely complete and perfectly pure. It is indeed good to see such Arahants.” Then the householder Meṇḍaka had excellent vehicles harnessed, mounted an excellent vehicle, and with excellent vehicles, set out from Bhaddiya to see the Blessed One. Many sectarians saw the householder Meṇḍaka coming from a distance and, having seen him, said: “Where are you going, householder?” “I am going, venerable sirs, to see the Blessed One, the ascetic Gotama.” “But why, householder, would you, a proponent of action, go to see the ascetic Gotama, a proponent of non-action? For the ascetic Gotama is a proponent of non-action; he teaches a doctrine for non-action, and with it he trains his disciples.” Then it occurred to the householder Meṇḍaka: “Surely, that Blessed One must be an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, judging by the way these sectarians are envious.” He went as far as the vehicle could go, then dismounted from the vehicle and approached the Blessed One on foot. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. To the householder Meṇḍaka who was sitting to one side, the Blessed One gave a gradual discourse, that is to say: a talk on giving… and so on, until he was independent of others in the Teacher's Dispensation. He then said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! … From this day forth, may the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life. And, venerable sir, may the Blessed One accept my meal for tomorrow, together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.” The Blessed One consented by silence. Then the householder Meṇḍaka, understanding the Blessed One's consent, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, and departed.

Atha kho meṇḍako gahapati tassā rattiyā accayena paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – “kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena meṇḍakassa gahapatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho meṇḍakassa gahapatissa bhariyā ca putto ca suṇisā ca dāso ca yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu[V 0.0320], upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Tesaṃ bhagavā anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ…pe… [T 2.0118] aparappaccayā satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante…pe… ete mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsake no bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupete saraṇaṃ [M 0.0341] gate”ti. Atha kho meṇḍako gahapati buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho meṇḍako gahapati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yāva, bhante, bhagavā bhaddiye viharati tāva ahaṃ buddhappamukhassa bhikkhusaṅghassa dhuvabhattenā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā meṇḍakaṃ gahapatiṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

Then, when that night had passed, the householder Meṇḍaka, having had excellent hard and soft food prepared, had the time announced to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is time; the meal is ready.” Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and approached the residence of the householder Meṇḍaka. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. Then the wife, son, daughter-in-law, and male servant of the householder Meṇḍaka approached the Blessed One. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side. The Blessed One gave them a gradual discourse, that is to say: a talk on giving… and so on, until they were independent of others in the Teacher's Dispensation. They then said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! … Venerable sir, we go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May the Blessed One remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge from this day forth for as long as life lasts.” Then the householder Meṇḍaka, with his own hands, served and satisfied the Saṅgha of bhikkhus with the Buddha at its head with excellent hard and soft food until they indicated they had had enough. When he observed that the Blessed One had finished eating and had removed his hand from the bowl, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the householder Meṇḍaka said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, for as long as the Blessed One dwells in Bhaddiya, I will attend upon the Saṅgha of bhikkhus with the Buddha at its head with a constant supply of food.” Then the Blessed One, having instructed, roused, inspired, and gladdened the householder Meṇḍaka with a Dhamma talk, rose from his seat and departed.

Meṇḍakagahapativattha niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story of the householder Meṇḍaka is concluded.

181. Pañcagorasādianujānanā

181. The Allowance of the Five Kinds of Milk Products

299. Atha kho bhagavā bhaddiye yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā meṇḍakaṃ gahapatiṃ anāpucchā yena aṅguttarāpo tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhatelasehi bhikkhusatehi. Assosi kho [T 2.0119] meṇḍako gahapati – “bhagavā kira yena aṅguttarāpo tena cārikaṃ pakkanto mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhatelasehi bhikkhusatehī”ti. Atha kho meṇḍako gahapati dāse ca kammakare ca āṇāpesi – “tena hi, bhaṇe, bahuṃ loṇampi, telampi, taṇḍulampi, khādanīyampi sakaṭesu āropetvā āgacchatha, aḍḍhatelasāni ca gopālakasatāni aḍḍhatelasāni ca dhenusatāni ādāya āgacchantu, yattha bhagavantaṃ passissāma tattha taruṇena dhāruṇhena (sī. syā.) khīrena bhojessāmā”ti. Atha kho meṇḍako gahapati [P 1.0244] bhagavantaṃ antarāmagge kantāre sambhāvesi. Atha kho meṇḍako gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho meṇḍako gahapati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho meṇḍako gahapati bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

299. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Bhaddiya as long as he pleased, set out for Aṅguttarāpa without taking leave of the householder Meṇḍaka, accompanied by a great community of monks, one thousand two hundred and fifty in number. The householder Meṇḍaka heard: “The Blessed One, it is said, has set out for Aṅguttarāpa accompanied by a great community of monks, one thousand two hundred and fifty in number.” Then the householder Meṇḍaka ordered his servants and workers: “Well then, my good men, load much salt, oil, rice, and foodstuffs onto carts and come. And let one thousand two hundred and fifty cowherds and one thousand two hundred and fifty milch cows come, taking them with you. Wherever we shall see the Blessed One, there we will offer a meal with fresh milk.” Then the householder Meṇḍaka caught up with the Blessed One along the road in a desolate area. Then the householder Meṇḍaka approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the householder Meṇḍaka said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One, together with the community of monks, accept my meal for tomorrow.” The Blessed One consented by remaining silent. Then the householder Meṇḍaka, knowing of the Blessed One’s consent, paid homage to him, circumambulated him keeping him to the right, and departed.

Atha kho meṇḍako gahapati tassā rattiyā accayena paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – “kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho bhagavā [V 0.0321] pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena meṇḍakassa gahapatissa parivesanā tenupasaṅkami[M 0.0342]; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho meṇḍako gahapati aḍḍhatelasāni gopālakasatāni āṇāpesi [T 2.0120] – “tenahi, bhaṇe, ekamekaṃ dhenuṃ gahetvā ekamekassa bhikkhuno upatiṭṭhatha taruṇena khīrena bhojessāmā”ti. Atha kho meṇḍako gahapati buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi, taruṇena ca khīrena. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā khīraṃ na paṭiggaṇhanti. Paṭiggaṇhatha, bhikkhave, paribhuñjathāti. Atha kho meṇḍako gahapati buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā taruṇena ca khīrena bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho meṇḍako gahapati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “santi, bhante, maggā kantārā, appodakā appabhakkhā, na sukarā apātheyyena gantuṃ. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhūnaṃ pātheyyaṃ anujānātū”ti. Atha kho bhagavā meṇḍakaṃ gahapatiṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañca gorase – khīraṃ, dadhiṃ, takkaṃ, navanītaṃ, sappiṃ. Santi, bhikkhave, maggā kantārā appodakā appabhakkhā, na sukarā apātheyyena gantuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pātheyyaṃ pariyesituṃ taṇḍulo taṇḍulatthikena, muggo muggatthikena, māso māsatthikena, loṇaṃ loṇatthikena[T 2.0121][P 1.0245], guḷo guḷatthikena, telaṃ telatthikena, sappi sappitthikena. Santi, bhikkhave, manussā, saddhā pasannā, te kappiyakārakānaṃ hatthe hiraññaṃ upanikkhipanti – ‘iminā ayyassa yaṃ kappiyaṃ taṃ dethā’ti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yaṃ tato kappiyaṃ taṃ sādituṃ; na tvevāhaṃ, bhikkhave, kenaci pariyāyena jātarūparajataṃ sāditabbaṃ pariyesitabbanti vadāmī”ti.

Then, when the night had passed, the householder Meṇḍaka had fine food, both hard and soft, prepared and announced the time to the Blessed One: “It is time, Venerable Sir, the meal is ready.” Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and went to the place where the meal was being served at the householder Meṇḍaka’s residence. Having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the community of monks. Then the householder Meṇḍaka instructed twelve hundred and fifty cowherds: “Come now, sirs, take one cow each and attend to each monk; we shall serve them with fresh milk.” Then the householder Meṇḍaka personally served and satisfied the community of monks headed by the Buddha with fine food, both hard and soft, and with fresh milk. The monks, being scrupulous, did not accept the milk. The Blessed One said: “Accept it, monks, and consume it.” Then, after the householder Meṇḍaka had personally served and satisfied the community of monks headed by the Buddha with fine food, both hard and soft, and with fresh milk, and when the Blessed One had finished his meal and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the householder Meṇḍaka said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, there are roads through wildernesses, with little water and little food, where it is not easy to travel without provisions. It would be good, Venerable Sir, if the Blessed One would allow provisions for the monks.” Then the Blessed One instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened the householder Meṇḍaka with a Dhamma talk, after which he rose from his seat and departed. Then, on this occasion, the Blessed One gave a Dhamma talk and addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow the five products of the cow: milk, curd, buttermilk, butter, and ghee. There are, monks, roads through wildernesses with little water and little food, where it is not easy to travel without provisions. I allow, monks, that provisions be sought: rice by one who needs rice, mung beans by one who needs mung beans, beans by one who needs beans, salt by one who needs salt, jaggery by one who needs jaggery, oil by one who needs oil, and ghee by one who needs ghee. There are, monks, faithful and devoted people who place gold and silver in the hands of stewards, saying, ‘With this, give the venerable one what is allowable.’ I allow, monks, that you make use of what is allowable from that. However, I do not say in any way that gold and silver should be sought or accepted.”

Pañcagorasādianujānanā niṭṭhitā.

The allowance regarding the five products of the cow and so forth is concluded.

182. Keṇiyajaṭilavatthu

182. The Story of the Matted-Hair Ascetic Keṇiya

300. ma. ni. 2.396 ādayo; su. ni. selasuttampi passitabbaṃ Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena āpaṇaṃ tadavasari. Assosi kho keṇiyo jaṭilo – “samaṇo khalu bho gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito āpaṇaṃ anuppatto, taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato…pe… sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ hotī”ti. Atha kho keṇiyassa [M 0.0343][V 0.0322] jaṭilassa etadahosi – “kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ samaṇassa gotamassa harāpeyya”nti. Atha kho keṇiyassa jaṭilassa etadahosi – “yepi kho te [T 2.0122] brāhmaṇānaṃ ayaṃ pāṭho dī. ni. 1.285, 526, 536; ma. ni. 2.427; a. ni. 5.191-192 ādayo pubbakā isayo mantānaṃ kattāro mantānaṃ pavattāro, yesamidaṃ etarahi brāhmaṇā porāṇaṃ mantapadaṃ gītaṃ pavuttaṃ samihitaṃ, tadanugāyanti tadanubhāsanti, bhāsitamanubhāsanti, vācitamanuvācenti, seyyathidaṃ – aṭṭhako vāmako vāmadevo vessāmitto yamataggi yamadaggi (ka.) aṅgīraso bhāradvājo vāseṭṭho kassapo bhagu ayaṃ pāṭho dī. ni. 1.285, 526, 536; ma. ni. 2.427; a. ni. 5.191-192 ādayo, rattūparatā viratā vikālabhojanā, te evarūpāni pānāni sādiyiṃsu. Samaṇopi gotamo rattūparato virato vikālabhojanā, arahati samaṇopi gotamo evarūpāni pānāni sādiyitu”nti pahūtaṃ pānaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā kājehi gāhāpetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi; sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho keṇiyo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “paṭiggaṇhātu me bhavaṃ gotamo pāna”nti. Tena hi, keṇiya, bhikkhūnaṃ dehīti. Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo bhikkhūnaṃ deti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā na paṭiggaṇhanti. Paṭiggaṇhatha, bhikkhave, paribhuñjathāti. Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pahūtehi pānehi sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā bhagavantaṃ dhotahatthaṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho keṇiyaṃ jaṭilaṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho [P 1.0246] keṇiyo jaṭilo bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me [T 2.0123] bhavaṃ gotamo svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Mahā kho, keṇiya, bhikkhusaṅgho aḍḍhatelasāni bhikkhusatāni, tvañca brāhmaṇesu abhippasannoti. Dutiyampi kho keṇiyo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kiñcāpi kho, bho gotama, mahā bhikkhusaṅgho aḍḍhatelasāni bhikkhusatāni, ahañca brāhmaṇesu abhippasanno, adhivāsetu me bhavaṃ gotamo svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Mahā kho, keṇiya, bhikkhusaṅgho aḍḍhatelasāni bhikkhusatāni, tvañca brāhmaṇesu abhippasannoti[M 0.0344]. Tatiyampi kho keṇiyo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kiñcāpi kho, bho gotama, mahā bhikkhusaṅgho aḍḍhatelasāni bhikkhusatāni, ahañca brāhmaṇesu abhippasanno, adhivāsetu bhavaṃ gotamo svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭha pānāni – ambapānaṃ jambupānaṃ cocapānaṃ mocapānaṃ madhūkapānaṃ madhupānaṃ (sī. syā.) muddikapānaṃ sālūkapānaṃ phārusakapānaṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ phalarasaṃ ṭhapetvā dhaññaphalarasaṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ pattarasaṃ ṭhapetvā [V 0.0323] ḍākarasaṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ puppharasaṃ ṭhapetvā madhūkapuppharasaṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ucchurasa”nti.

300. Then the Blessed One, traveling by stages, arrived at Āpaṇa. The matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya heard: “Indeed, the ascetic Gotama, the son of the Sakyans, who has gone forth from the Sakyan clan, has arrived at Āpaṇa. A good report about Master Gotama has spread thus... It is good to see such Arahants.” Then the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya thought: “What should I have brought to the ascetic Gotama?” Then the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya thought: “Those ancient seers among the brahmins, the makers of mantras, the expounders of mantras, whose ancient mantras—chanted, pronounced, and compiled—the brahmins of today now chant after them, recite after them, speak what was spoken, and teach what was taught—namely, Aṭṭhaka, Vāmaka, Vāmadeva, Vessāmitta, Yamataggi, Aṅgīrasa, Bhāradvāja, Vāseṭṭha, Kassapa, and Bhagu—they abstained from food at night, refrained from eating at improper times, and they enjoyed such drinks. The ascetic Gotama also abstains from food at night and refrains from eating at improper times. The ascetic Gotama is worthy to enjoy such drinks.” Having had abundant drinks prepared and carried on carrying poles, he approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One, and when the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya said to the Blessed One: “May Master Gotama accept my drink.” “Then, Keṇiya, give it to the monks.” So the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya gave it to the monks. The monks, being scrupulous, did not accept it. “Accept it, monks, and consume it.” Then the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya, with his own hand, served and satisfied the community of monks headed by the Buddha with abundant drinks. When he saw that the Blessed One had washed his hands and removed them from the bowl, he sat down to one side. The Blessed One instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya, who was sitting to one side, with a Dhamma talk. Then the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya, having been instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One’s Dhamma talk, said to him: “May Master Gotama, together with the community of monks, consent to my meal for tomorrow.” “The community of monks is large, Keṇiya, consisting of twelve hundred and fifty monks, and you are especially devoted to the brahmins.” A second time, the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya said to the Blessed One: “Even though, Master Gotama, the community of monks is large, consisting of twelve hundred and fifty monks, and I am especially devoted to the brahmins, may Master Gotama, together with the community of monks, consent to my meal for tomorrow.” “The community of monks is large, Keṇiya, consisting of twelve hundred and fifty monks, and you are especially devoted to the brahmins.” A third time, the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya said to the Blessed One: “Even though, Master Gotama, the community of monks is large, consisting of twelve hundred and fifty monks, and I am especially devoted to the brahmins, may Master Gotama, together with the community of monks, consent to my meal for tomorrow.” The Blessed One consented by silence. Then the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya, understanding the Blessed One’s consent, rose from his seat and left. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow eight kinds of drinks: mango drink, rose-apple drink, wild banana drink, cultivated banana drink, Madhuka drink, grape drink, lotus root drink, and phārusaka drink. I allow all fruit juices, excepting the juice of grains. I allow all leaf juices, excepting the juice from cooked vegetables. I allow all flower juices, excepting Madhuka flower juice. I allow sugarcane juice.”

Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo tassā rattiyā [T 2.0124] accayena sake assame paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – “kālo, bho gotama, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena keṇiyassa jaṭilassa assamo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho keṇiyo jaṭilo buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho keṇiyaṃ jaṭilaṃ bhagavā imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –

Then, when the night had passed, the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya had fine hard and soft food prepared in his own hermitage and had the time announced to the Blessed One: “It is time, Master Gotama, the meal is ready.” Then the Blessed One, having put on his lower robe in the morning, took his bowl and robes and went to the hermitage of the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya. Having gone there, he sat down on the prepared seat together with the community of monks. Then the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya, with his own hands, served and satisfied the community of monks headed by the Buddha with fine hard and soft food. When he perceived that the Blessed One had finished eating and had withdrawn his hand from the bowl, he sat down to one side. The Blessed One then expressed his appreciation to the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya, who was sitting to one side, with these verses:

“Aggihuttamukhā yaññā, sāvittī chandaso mukhaṃ;

Rājā mukhaṃ manussānaṃ, nadīnaṃ sāgaro mukhaṃ.

“Of sacrifices, the fire offering is foremost; of meters, the Sāvitrī is foremost. The king is the foremost of men; the ocean is the foremost of rivers.

“Nakkhattānaṃ mukhaṃ cando, ādicco tapataṃ mukhaṃ;

Puññaṃ ākaṅkhamānānaṃ saṅgho, ve yajataṃ mukha”nti.

“The moon is the foremost of the constellations, the sun is the foremost of those that shine; and for those who, desiring merit, make offerings, the Saṅgha is indeed the foremost.”

Atha kho bhagavā keṇiyaṃ jaṭilaṃ imāhi gāthāhi anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

Then the Blessed One, having expressed his appreciation to the matted-hair ascetic Keṇiya with these verses, rose from his seat and departed.

Keṇiyajaṭilavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Account of Keṇiya the Matted-Hair Ascetic is concluded.

183. Rojamallavatthu

The Account of Roja the Malla

301. Atha [P 1.0247][M 0.0345] kho bhagavā āpaṇe yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena kusinārā tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhatelasehi bhikkhusatehi. Assosuṃ kho kosinārakā mallā – “bhagavā kira kusināraṃ āgacchati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhatelasehi bhikkhusatehī”ti. Te saṅgaraṃ saṅkaraṃ (ka.) akaṃsu – “yo bhagavato paccuggamanaṃ na [T 2.0125] karissati, pañcasatānissa daṇḍo”ti. Tena kho pana samayena rojo mallo āyasmato ānandassa sahāyo hoti. Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena kusinārā tadavasari. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā bhagavato paccuggamanaṃ akaṃsu. Atha kho rojo mallo [V 0.0324] bhagavato paccuggamanaṃ karitvā yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ kho rojaṃ mallaṃ āyasmā ānando etadavoca – “uḷāraṃ kho te idaṃ, āvuso roja, yaṃ tvaṃ bhagavato paccuggamanaṃ akāsī”ti. “Nāhaṃ, bhante ānanda, bahukato buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā; api ca ñātīhi saṅgaro kato – ‘yo bhagavato paccuggamanaṃ na karissati, pañcasatānissa daṇḍo’”ti; so kho ahaṃ, bhante ānanda, ñātīnaṃ daṇḍabhayā evāhaṃ bhagavato paccuggamanaṃ akāsinti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando anattamano ahosi’ kathañhi nāma rojo mallo evaṃ vakkhatī’ti? Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ayaṃ, bhante, rojo mallo abhiññāto ñātamanusso. Mahatthiko kho pana evarūpānaṃ ñātamanussānaṃ imasmiṃ dhammavinaye pasādo. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā tathā [T 2.0126] karotu, yathā rojo mallo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye pasīdeyyā”ti. “Na kho taṃ, ānanda, dukkaraṃ tathāgatena, yathā rojo mallo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye pasīdeyyā”ti.

301. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Āpaṇa as long as he pleased, set out on a journey to Kusinārā with a large company of bhikkhus, with one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikkhus. The Mallas of Kusinārā heard: “The Blessed One, it is said, is coming to Kusinārā with a large company of bhikkhus, with one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikkhus.” They made an agreement: “Whoever does not go out to meet the Blessed One will be fined five hundred.” Now at that time, Roja the Malla was a friend of the Venerable Ānanda. Then the Blessed One, traveling by stages, arrived at Kusinārā. Then the Mallas of Kusinārā went out to meet the Blessed One. Then Roja the Malla, having gone out to meet the Blessed One, approached the Venerable Ānanda, paid homage to him, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to Roja the Malla: “It is excellent, friend Roja, that you went out to meet the Blessed One.” “I, Venerable Ānanda, am not greatly devoted to the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Saṅgha. However, an agreement was made by my kinsmen: ‘Whoever does not go out to meet the Blessed One will be fined five hundred.’ So, Venerable Ānanda, it was only out of fear of the fine from my kinsmen that I went out to meet the Blessed One.” Then the Venerable Ānanda was displeased, thinking: “How could Roja the Malla say such a thing?” Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “This Roja the Malla, Bhante, is a prominent and well-known person. The confidence of such prominent and well-known people in this Dhamma and Discipline is of great consequence. It would be good, Bhante, if the Blessed One would act in such a way that Roja the Malla might gain confidence in this Dhamma and Discipline.” “It is not difficult, Ānanda, for the Tathāgata to act in such a way that Roja the Malla might gain confidence in this Dhamma and Discipline.”

Atha kho bhagavā rojaṃ mallaṃ mettena cittena pharitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisi. Atha kho rojo mallo bhagavato mettena cittena phuṭṭho, seyyathāpi nāma gāviṃ taruṇavaccho, evameva, vihārena [M 0.0346] vihāraṃ pariveṇena pariveṇaṃ upasaṅkamitvā bhikkhū pucchati – “kahaṃ nu kho, bhante, etarahi so bhagavā viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, dassanakāmā hi mayaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha”nti. “Esāvuso roja, vihāro [P 1.0248] saṃvutadvāro, tena appasaddo upasaṅkamitvā ataramāno āḷindaṃ pavisitvā ukkāsitvā aggaḷaṃ ākoṭehi, vivarissati te bhagavā dvāra”nti. Atha kho rojo mallo yena so vihāro saṃvutadvāro, tena appasaddo upasaṅkamitvā ataramāno āḷindaṃ pavisitvā ukkāsitvā aggaḷaṃ ākoṭesi. Vivari bhagavā dvāraṃ. Atha kho rojo mallo vihāraṃ pavisitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnassa kho rojassa mallassa bhagavā anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ…pe… [T 2.0127] aparappaccayo satthusāsane bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu, bhante, ayyā mamaññeva paṭiggaṇheyyuṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ, no aññesa”nti. “Yesaṃ kho, roja, sekkhena ñāṇena sekkhena dassanena dhammo diṭṭho seyyathāpi tayā, tesampi evaṃ hoti – ‘aho nūna ayyā amhākaññeva paṭiggaṇheyyuṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ, no aññesa’nti. Tena hi, roja, tava ceva paṭiggahissanti aññesañcā”ti.

Then the Blessed One, having suffused Roja the Malla with a mind of loving-kindness, rose from his seat and entered the dwelling. Then Roja the Malla, touched by the Blessed One’s mind of loving-kindness, just as a young calf seeks its mother cow, so too, he went from dwelling to dwelling, from enclosure to enclosure, and asked the bhikkhus: “Venerable sirs, where is that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, dwelling now? For we wish to see that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.” “Friend Roja, that is the dwelling with the door closed. Approach it quietly, without haste, enter the verandah, clear your throat, and knock on the door-bolt. The Blessed One will open the door for you.” Then Roja the Malla approached that dwelling with the closed door quietly, without haste, entered the verandah, cleared his throat, and knocked on the door-bolt. The Blessed One opened the door. Then Roja the Malla entered the dwelling, paid homage to the Blessed One, and sat down to one side. To Roja the Malla who was sitting to one side, the Blessed One gave a progressive discourse, that is to say, a discourse on generosity... and so on... until he became one who did not rely on others in the Teacher's Dispensation. He then said to the Blessed One: “It would be good, venerable sir, if the venerable ones would accept robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick from me only, and not from others.” “Roja, for those who have seen the Dhamma with the trainee's knowledge and the trainee's vision—just as you have—for them, too, this thought occurs: ‘Ah, if only the venerable ones would accept robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick from us only, and not from others.’ Therefore, Roja, they will accept from you as well as from others.”

302. Tena [V 0.0325] kho pana samayena kusinārāyaṃ paṇītānaṃ bhattānaṃ bhattapaṭipāṭi aṭṭhitā hoti. Atha kho rojassa mallassa paṭipāṭiṃ alabhantassa etadahosi – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhattaggaṃ olokeyyaṃ, yaṃ bhattagge nāssa, taṃ paṭiyādeyya”nti. Atha kho rojo mallo bhattaggaṃ olokento dve nāddasa – ḍākañca piṭṭhakhādanīyañca. Atha kho rojo mallo yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ [T 2.0128] etadavoca – “idha me, bhante ānanda, paṭipāṭiṃ alabhantassa etadahosi – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhattaggaṃ olokeyyaṃ, yaṃ bhattagge nāssa, taṃ paṭiyādeyya’nti. So kho ahaṃ, bhante ānanda, bhattaggaṃ olokento dve nāddasaṃ – ḍākañca piṭṭhakhādanīyañca. Sacāhaṃ, bhante ānanda, paṭiyādeyyaṃ ḍākañca piṭṭhakhādanīyañca, paṭiggaṇheyya me bhagavā”ti? “Tena hi, roja, bhagavantaṃ paṭipucchissāmī”ti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. “Tena hānanda, paṭiyādetū”ti. “Tena hi, roja, paṭiyādehī”ti. Atha kho rojo mallo tassā rattiyā accayena [M 0.0347] pahūtaṃ ḍākañca piṭṭhakhādanīyañca paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato upanāmesi “paṭiggaṇhātu me, bhante, bhagavā ḍākañca piṭṭhakhādanīyañcā”ti. “Tena hi, roja, bhikkhūnaṃ dehī”ti. Atha kho rojo mallo bhikkhūnaṃ deti. Bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā na paṭiggaṇhanti[P 1.0249]. “Paṭiggaṇhatha, bhikkhave, paribhuñjathā”ti. Atha kho rojo mallo buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pahūtehi ḍākehi ca piṭṭhakhādanīyehi ca sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā bhagavantaṃ dhotahatthaṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho rojaṃ mallaṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sabbañca ḍākaṃ sabbañca piṭṭhakhādanīya”nti.

302. Now at that time in Kusinārā, a regular turn for offering excellent meals was established. Then it occurred to Roja the Malla, who had not received his turn: “What if I were to inspect the refectory? Whatever is not in the refectory, that I would prepare.” Then Roja the Malla, while inspecting the refectory, did not see two things: boiled greens and foods made from flour. Then Roja the Malla approached the Venerable Ānanda; having approached, he said this to the Venerable Ānanda: “Here, Venerable Ānanda, not having received my turn, it occurred to me: ‘What if I were to inspect the refectory? Whatever is not in the refectory, that I would prepare.’ I, Venerable Ānanda, while inspecting the refectory, did not see two things: boiled greens and foods made from flour. If I, Venerable Ānanda, were to prepare boiled greens and foods made from flour, would the Blessed One accept them from me?” “In that case, Roja, I will ask the Blessed One.” Then the Venerable Ānanda informed the Blessed One of this matter. “In that case, Ānanda, let him prepare it.” “In that case, Roja, prepare it.” Then Roja the Malla, when that night had passed, had abundant boiled greens and foods made from flour prepared and offered them to the Blessed One, saying: “Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One accept the boiled greens and foods made from flour from me.” “In that case, Roja, give them to the monks.” Then Roja the Malla gave them to the monks. The monks, being scrupulous, did not accept them. “Accept, monks, and consume them.” Then Roja the Malla, with his own hands, having served and satisfied the community of monks with the Buddha at its head with abundant boiled greens and foods made from flour, sat down to one side when the Blessed One had washed his hands and removed his hand from the bowl. The Blessed One instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened Roja the Malla, who was sitting to one side, with a Dhamma talk, then rose from his seat and departed. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this context, having given a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow all boiled greens and all foods made from flour.”

Rojamallavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story of Roja the Malla is concluded.

184. Vuḍḍhapabbajitavatthu

184. The Story of the Monk Who Ordained in Old Age

303. Atha [T 2.0129] kho bhagavā kusinārāyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena ātumā tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhatelasehi bhikkhusatehi. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro vuḍḍhapabbajito ātumāyaṃ paṭivasati nahāpitapubbo. Tassa dve dārakā honti, mañjukā paṭibhāneyyakā, dakkhā pariyodātasippā sake ācariyake nahāpitakamme. Assosi kho so vuḍḍhapabbajito – “bhagavā kira ātumaṃ āgacchati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhatelasehi [V 0.0326] bhikkhusatehī”ti. Atha kho so vuḍḍhapabbajito te dārake etadavoca – “bhagavā kira, tātā, ātumaṃ āgacchati mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aḍḍhatelasehi bhikkhusatehi. Gacchatha tumhe, tātā, khurabhaṇḍaṃ ādāya nāḷiyāvāpakena anugharakaṃ anugharakaṃ āhiṇḍatha, loṇampi, telampi, taṇḍulampi, khādanīyampi saṃharatha, bhagavato āgatassa yāgupānaṃ karissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, tātā”ti kho te dārakā tassa vuḍḍhapabbajitassa paṭissuṇitvā khurabhaṇḍaṃ ādāya nāḷiyāvāpakena anugharakaṃ anugharakaṃ āhiṇḍanti, loṇampi, telampi, taṇḍulampi, khādanīyampi saṃharantā. Manussā te dārake mañjuke paṭibhāneyyake passitvā yepi na kārāpetukāmā tepi kārāpenti, kārāpetvāpi bahuṃ denti. Atha kho te dārakā bahuṃ loṇampi, telampi, taṇḍulampi, khādanīyampi saṃhariṃsu.

303. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Kusinārā as long as he pleased, set out on a tour towards Ātumā with a great community of monks, numbering twelve hundred and fifty. Now at that time, a certain monk who ordained in old age, formerly a barber, was residing in Ātumā. He had two sons, who were sweet-voiced and ingenious, skillful and with perfected craft in their hereditary craft of barbering. That monk who ordained in old age heard: “The Blessed One, it is said, is coming to Ātumā with a great community of monks, numbering twelve hundred and fifty.” Then that monk who ordained in old age said to those boys: “Dear sons, the Blessed One, it is said, is coming to Ātumā with a great community of monks, numbering twelve hundred and fifty. Go, dear sons, take your barber’s tools and a collection container, and wander from house to house, collecting salt, oil, rice, and edibles. We will prepare gruel and drink for the Blessed One when he arrives.” “Yes, father,” replied the boys to that monk who ordained in old age. Taking their barber’s tools and a collection container, they wandered from house to house, collecting salt, oil, rice, and edibles. People, seeing those sweet-voiced and ingenious boys, even those who did not wish to have their services done, had them done, and after having them done, gave them much. Thus, the boys gathered a great deal of salt, oil, rice, and edibles.

Atha [M 0.0348] kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena [T 2.0130] ātumā tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā ātumāyaṃ viharati bhusāgāre. Atha kho so vuḍḍhapabbajito tassā rattiyā accayena pahūtaṃ yāguṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato upanāmesi – “paṭiggaṇhātu me, bhante, bhagavā yāgu”nti. Jānantāpi [P 1.0250] tathāgatā pucchanti…pe… sāvakānaṃ vā sikkhāpadaṃ paññapessāmāti. Atha kho bhagavā taṃ vuḍḍhapabbajitaṃ etadavoca – “kutāyaṃ, bhikkhu yāgū”ti? Atha kho so vuḍḍhapabbajito bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā, “ananucchavikaṃ, moghapurisa, ananulomikaṃ appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, pabbajito akappiye samādapessasi samādapesi (ka.). Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi ‘na, bhikkhave, pabbajitena akappiye samādapetabbaṃ, yo samādapeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Na ca, bhikkhave, nahāpitapubbena khurabhaṇḍaṃ pariharitabbaṃ. Yo parihareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā’”ti.

Then the Blessed One, traveling by stages, arrived at Ātumā. There the Blessed One stayed in a chaff-house in Ātumā. Then that monk who had ordained in old age, when the night had passed, had a large quantity of rice-gruel prepared and offered it to the Blessed One, saying, “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One accept my rice-gruel.” Even though the Tathāgatas know, they ask… so that they might lay down a training rule for the disciples. Then the Blessed One said to that monk who had ordained in old age, “Monk, where did this rice-gruel come from?” Then that monk who had ordained in old age told the Blessed One of this matter. The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him: “It is unseemly, foolish man, unsuitable, inappropriate, unbecoming for a recluse, improper, not to be done. How could you, foolish man, having gone forth, instruct in what is improper? This is not, foolish man, for inspiring confidence in those without it…” Having rebuked him and given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, one who has gone forth should not instruct in what is improper. Whoever does so, commits an offense of wrong-doing. And, monks, one who was formerly a barber should not carry barber’s tools. Whoever carries them, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Atha kho bhagavā ātumāyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena sāvatthi [T 2.0131] tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena sāvatthi tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyaṃ bahuṃ phalakhādanīyaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kiṃ nu kho bhagavatā phalakhādanīyaṃ anuññātaṃ, kiṃ ananuññāta”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ phalakhādanīya”nti.

Then the Blessed One, having stayed in Ātumā for as long as he wished, set out on tour towards Sāvatthī. Traveling by stages, he arrived at Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One stayed in Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time in Sāvatthī, much edible fruit had become available. Then this thought occurred to the monks: “What edible fruit has the Blessed One allowed, and what has he not allowed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow all edible fruit.”

304. Tena [V 0.0327] kho pana samayena saṅghikāni bījāni puggalikāya bhūmiyā ropiyanti, puggalikāni bījāni saṅghikāya bhūmiyā ropiyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Saṅghikāni, bhikkhave, bījāni puggalikāya bhūmiyā ropitāni bhāgaṃ datvā paribhuñjitabbāni. Puggalikāni bījāni saṅghikāya bhūmiyā ropitāni bhāgaṃ datvā paribhuñjitabbānīti.

304. Now at that time, seeds belonging to the Sangha were being planted in land belonging to an individual, and seeds belonging to an individual were being planted in land belonging to the Sangha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, seeds belonging to the Sangha planted in land belonging to an individual are to be used after giving a share to the landowners. Seeds belonging to an individual planted in land belonging to the Sangha are to be used after giving a share to the landowners.”

Vuḍḍhapabbajitavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story of the one who went forth in old age is concluded.

185. Catumahāpadesakathā

185. The Discourse on the Four Great References

305. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhūnaṃ kismiñci kismiñci ṭhāne kukkuccaṃ uppajjati – “kiṃ nu kho bhagavatā anuññātaṃ, kiṃ ananuññāta”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Yaṃ, bhikkhave, mayā ‘idaṃ na kappatī’ti appaṭikkhittaṃ tañce [M 0.0349] akappiyaṃ anulometi, kappiyaṃ paṭibāhati, taṃ vo na kappati. Yaṃ, bhikkhave, mayā ‘idaṃ na kappatī’ti appaṭikkhittaṃ [P 1.0251] tañce kappiyaṃ anulometi, akappiyaṃ paṭibāhati, taṃ vo kappati. Yaṃ, bhikkhave, mayā ‘idaṃ kappatī’ti ananuññātaṃ tañce akappiyaṃ anulometi, kappiyaṃ paṭibāhati, taṃ vo [T 2.0132] na kappati. Yaṃ, bhikkhave, mayā ‘idaṃ kappatī’ti ananuññātaṃ, tañce kappiyaṃ anulometi, akappiyaṃ paṭibāhati, taṃ vo kappatī”ti.

305. Now at that time, in various matters, a scruple arose for the monks: “What, I wonder, has been allowed by the Blessed One, and what has not been allowed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, whatever I have not forbidden by saying, ‘This is not allowable,’ if that thing conforms with the unallowable and obstructs the allowable, that is not allowable for you. Monks, whatever I have not forbidden by saying, ‘This is not allowable,’ if that thing conforms with the allowable and obstructs the unallowable, that is allowable for you. Monks, whatever I have not allowed by saying, ‘This is allowable,’ if that thing conforms with the unallowable and obstructs the allowable, that is not allowable for you. Monks, whatever I have not allowed by saying, ‘This is allowable,’ if that thing conforms with the allowable and obstructs the unallowable, that is allowable for you.”

Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kappati nu kho yāvakālikena yāmakālikaṃ, na nu kho kappati? Kappati nu kho yāvakālikena sattāhakālikaṃ, na nu kho kappati? Kappati nu kho yāvakālikena yāvajīvikaṃ, na nu kho kappati? Kappati nu kho yāmakālikena sattāhakālikaṃ, na nu kho kappati? Kappati nu kho yāmakālikena yāvajīvikaṃ, na nu kho kappati? Kappati nu kho sattāhakālikena yāvajīvikaṃ, na nu kho kappatī”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Yāvakālikena, bhikkhave, yāmakālikaṃ, tadahu paṭiggahitaṃ kāle kappati, vikāle na kappati. Yāvakālikena, bhikkhave, sattāhakālikaṃ, tadahu paṭiggahitaṃ kāle kappati, vikāle na kappati. Yāvakālikena, bhikkhave, yāvajīvikaṃ, tadahu paṭiggahitaṃ kāle kappati, vikāle na kappati. Yāmakālikena, bhikkhave, sattāhakālikaṃ, tadahu paṭiggahitaṃ yāme kappati, yāmātikkante na kappati. Yāmakālikena, bhikkhave, yāvajīvikaṃ, tadahu paṭiggahitaṃ yāme kappati, yāmātikkante [V 0.0328] na kappati. Sattāhakālikena, bhikkhave, yāvajīvikaṃ paṭiggahitaṃ, sattāhaṃ kappati, sattāhātikkante na kappatī”ti.

Then this reflection arose in the minds of the monks: ‘Is a yāmakālika allowable with a yāvakālika, or is it not allowable? Is a sattāhakālika allowable with a yāvakālika, or is it not allowable? Is a yāvajīvika allowable with a yāvakālika, or is it not allowable? Is a sattāhakālika allowable with a yāmakālika, or is it not allowable? Is a yāvajīvika allowable with a yāmakālika, or is it not allowable? Is a yāvajīvika allowable with a sattāhakālika, or is it not allowable?’ They reported this matter to the Blessed One. ‘Monks, a yāmakālika with a yāvakālika, if received on that day, is allowable at the proper time, but not allowable at the wrong time. Monks, a sattāhakālika with a yāvakālika, if received on that day, is allowable at the proper time, but not allowable at the wrong time. Monks, a yāvajīvika with a yāvakālika, if received on that day, is allowable at the proper time, but not allowable at the wrong time. Monks, a sattāhakālika with a yāmakālika, if received on that day, is allowable within the watch, but not allowable after the watch has passed. Monks, a yāvajīvika with a yāmakālika, if received on that day, is allowable within the watch, but not allowable after the watch has passed. Monks, a yāvajīvika with a sattāhakālika, if received, is allowable for seven days, but not allowable after seven days have passed.’

Catumahāpadesakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on the four great references is concluded.

Bhesajjakkhandhako chaṭṭho.

The Chapter on Medicines is the sixth.

186. Tassuddānaṃ

186. Its summary:

Sāradike [T 2.0133] vikālepi, vasaṃ mūle piṭṭhehi ca;

Kasāvehi paṇṇaṃ phalaṃ, jatu loṇaṃ chakaṇañca.

Autumnal sickness, even at the wrong time; fat, roots, and with powders; with astringents, leaves, fruit, resin, salt, and cow dung.

Cuṇṇaṃ cālini maṃsañca, añjanaṃ upapisanī upapiṃ sanī (sī.), upapiṃ sanaṃ (syā.);

Añjanī uccāpārutā, salākā salākaṭhāniṃ salākodhanī (sī. syā.).

Powder, a sieve, and flesh; collyrium, a grinding slab; a collyrium pot, high ones, a lid; an applicator, a case for the applicator.

Thavikaṃsabaddhakaṃ [M 0.0350] suttaṃ, muddhanitelanatthu ca;

Natthukaraṇī dhūmañca, nettañcāpidhanatthavi.

A bag, a shoulder strap, thread; oil for the head, and snuff; a snuff-tube, smoke, and a pipe; a lid, a bag.

Telapākesu majjañca, atikkhittaṃ abbhañjanaṃ;

Tumbaṃ sedaṃ sambhārañca, mahā bhaṅgodakaṃ tathā.

In oil decoctions and intoxicants; what is excessive, anointing; a gourd, a sweat-bath, and with ingredients; a great sweat-bath, likewise water with leaves.

Dakakoṭṭhaṃ lohitañca, visāṇaṃ pādabbhañjanaṃ;

Pajjaṃ satthaṃ kasāvañca, tilakakkaṃ kabaḷikaṃ.

A large water pot, and bloodletting; a horn, anointing the feet with oil; a foot poultice, a lancet, and an astringent decoction; sesame paste, a poultice.

Coḷaṃ [P 1.0252] sāsapakuṭṭañca, dhūma sakkharikāya ca;

Vaṇatelaṃ vikāsikaṃ, vikaṭañca paṭiggahaṃ.

A coarse cloth, and mustard powder; fumigation, and a razor; oil for a wound, applying powder to a cloth; and the four great medicines, receiving with the hand.

Gūthaṃ karonto loḷiñca, khāraṃ muttaharītakaṃ;

Gandhā virecanañceva, acchākaṭaṃ kaṭākaṭaṃ.

Drinking feces, receiving while on the move, and earth from a ploughshare; alkaline water, urine, and myrobalan; perfumes, and purgatives; rice-water, unstrained bean juice, lightly strained bean juice.

Paṭicchādani [T 2.0134][V 0.0329] pabbhārā, ārāma sattāhena ca;

Guḷaṃ muggaṃ sovīrañca, sāmaṃpākā punāpace.

Meat broth, clearing a mountain slope; a monastery attendant, and storing medicines for seven days; molasses, beans, and loṇasovīraka; disallowing self-cooking, reheating.

Punānuññāsi dubbhikkhe, phalañca tilakhādanī;

Purebhattaṃ kāyaḍāho, nibbattañca bhagandalaṃ.

Again allowing during a famine, and fruit; sesame, hard foods; before the meal, a feverish illness; and fruit with removable seeds, a fistula.

Vatthikammañca suppiñca, manussamaṃsameva ca;

Hatthiassā sunakho ca, ahi sīhañca dīpikaṃ hatthiassasunakhāhi, sīhabyagghañca dīpikaṃ (sī.).

And bandaging, and Suppiya; and human flesh; elephant, horse, and dog; snake, lion, and leopard.

Acchataracchamaṃsañca, paṭipāṭi ca yāgu ca;

Taruṇaṃ aññatra guḷaṃ, sunidhāvasathāgāraṃ.

Bear and hyena flesh; and order of serving, and rice gruel; a young minister, elsewhere than the invitation, molasses; Sunidha, a rest house.

Gaṅgā koṭisaccakathā, ambapālī ca licchavī;

Uddissa kataṃ subhikkhaṃ, punadeva paṭikkhipi.

The Ganges, Koṭigāma, discourse on the truths; Ambapālī, and the Licchavis; meat from an animal killed specifically, a time of abundance; again rejecting.

Megho yaso meṇḍako, ca gorasaṃ pātheyyakena ca;

Keṇi ambo jambu coca, mocamadhumuddikasālukaṃ.

Megha, Yasoja, and Meṇḍaka; the five products of the cow, and provisions for a journey; Keṇiya, mango juice, rose-apple juice, wild banana juice; cultivated banana juice, honey-liquorice juice, grape juice, lotus root juice.

Phārusakā ḍākapiṭṭhaṃ, ātumāyaṃ nahāpito;

Sāvatthiyaṃ phalaṃ bījaṃ, kismiṃ ṭhāne ca kāliketi.

Phārusaka fruit juice, boiled vegetables, food made from flour; the barber in Ātumā; fruit in Sāvatthī, seeds; and in what circumstance, the time-limited items. Thus.

Imamhi khandhake vatthū ekasataṃ chavatthu.

In this chapter, there are one hundred and six stories.

Bhesajjakkhandhako niṭṭhito.

The Chapter on Medicines is concluded.

7. Kathinakkhandhako

7. The Chapter on the Kaṭhina

187. Kathinānujānanā

187. The Allowance of the Kaṭhina

306. Tena [P 1.0253][M 0.0351][V 0.0330][T 2.0135] samayena buddho bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena tiṃsamattā pāveyyakā pāṭheyyakā (sī. syā.) bhikkhū, sabbe āraññikā sabbe piṇḍapātikā sabbe paṃsukūlikā sabbe tecīvarikā sāvatthiṃ āgacchantā bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upakaṭṭhāya vassūpanāyikāya nāsakkhiṃsu sāvatthiyaṃ vassūpanāyikaṃ sambhāvetuṃ; antarāmagge sākete vassaṃ upagacchiṃsu. Te ukkaṇṭhitarūpā vassaṃ vasiṃsu – āsanneva no bhagavā viharati ito chasu yojanesu, na ca mayaṃ labhāma bhagavantaṃ dassanāyāti. Atha kho te bhikkhū vassaṃvuṭṭhā, temāsaccayena katāya pavāraṇāya, deve vassante, udakasaṅgahe udakacikkhalle okapuṇṇehi cīvarehi kilantarūpā yena sāvatthi jetavanaṃ anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāmo, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Āciṇṇaṃ kho panetaṃ buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ āgantukehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ paṭisammodituṃ. Atha kho bhagavā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “kacci, bhikkhave, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kacci samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vasittha, na ca piṇḍakena kilamitthā”ti? “Khamanīyaṃ, bhagavā; yāpanīyaṃ, bhagavā; samaggā ca mayaṃ, bhante, sammodamānā avivadamānā vassaṃ vasimhā, na ca piṇḍakena kilamimhā[T 2.0136]. Idha mayaṃ, bhante, tiṃsamattā pāveyyakā bhikkhū sāvatthiṃ āgacchantā bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upakaṭṭhāya vassūpanāyikāya nāsakkhimhā sāvatthiyaṃ vassūpanāyikaṃ sambhāvetuṃ, antarāmagge sākete vassaṃ upagacchimhā. Te mayaṃ, bhante, ukkaṇṭhitarūpā vassaṃ vasimhā [P 1.0254] – ‘āsanneva no bhagavā viharati ito chasu yojanesu, na ca mayaṃ labhāma bhagavantaṃ dassanāyā’ti. Atha kho mayaṃ, bhante, vassaṃvuṭṭhā, temāsaccayena katāya pavāraṇāya, deve vassante, udakasaṅgahe udakacikkhalle okapuṇṇehi cīvarehi kilantarūpā addhānaṃ āgatāti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ [V 0.0331] nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ [M 0.0352] kathinaṃ kaṭhinaṃ (sī. syā.) attharituṃ. Atthatakathinānaṃ vo, bhikkhave, pañca kappissanti – anāmantacāro, asamādānacāro, gaṇabhojanaṃ, yāvadatthacīvaraṃ, yo ca tattha cīvaruppādo so nesaṃ bhavissatīti. Atthatakathinānaṃ vo, bhikkhave, imāni pañca kappissanti. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, kathinaṃ attharitabbaṃ. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

306. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. Now at that time, about thirty monks from Pāvā—all of them forest-dwellers, all of them alms-food-eaters, all of them refuse-rag-robe-wearers, and all of them triple-robe-wearers—were traveling to Sāvatthī to see the Blessed One. But as the day for entering the Rains was near, they were unable to reach Sāvatthī in time for the Rains-residence, so they entered the Rains-residence on the way at Sāketa. They spent the Rains-residence discontented, thinking, “The Blessed One is staying nearby, just six yojanas away, yet we do not get to see him.” Then, when those monks had completed the Rains-residence and had performed the Pavāraṇā ceremony at the end of the three months, with rain falling, amidst floods and mud, and with their robes full of water, being weary, they went to Sāvatthī, to the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery, where the Blessed One was. Having approached the Blessed One, they paid homage to him and sat down to one side. Now it is the custom for the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, to exchange friendly greetings with newly arrived monks. So the Blessed One said to them, “Monks, are you keeping well? Are you getting by? Did you spend the Rains united, rejoicing together, without dispute, and in comfort? And were you not weary with the alms-round?” “We are keeping well, Blessed One; we are getting by, Blessed One. We spent the Rains, Venerable Sir, united, rejoicing together, without dispute, and in comfort, and we were not weary with the alms-round. But, Venerable Sir, we, about thirty monks from Pāvā, were traveling to Sāvatthī to see the Blessed One. As the day for entering the Rains was near, we were unable to reach Sāvatthī in time for the Rains-residence, so we entered the Rains-residence on the way at Sāketa. We spent the Rains-residence discontented, thinking, ‘The Blessed One is staying nearby, just six yojanas away, yet we do not get to see him.’ Then, Venerable Sir, after completing the Rains-residence and performing the Pavāraṇā ceremony at the end of the three months, with rain falling, amidst floods and mud, and with our robes full of water, being weary, we have come this long way." Then the Blessed One, having given a Dhamma talk on this occasion, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow monks who have completed the Rains-residence to spread the kaṭhina. For those who have spread the kaṭhina, monks, five things will be allowable: going about without asking leave, going about without the set of three robes, a group meal, as many robes as are desired, and whatever robe-material arises there will be for them. For those who have spread the kaṭhina, monks, these five things will be allowable. And this, monks, is how the kaṭhina should be spread: A competent and capable monk should inform the Saṅgha:

307. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Idaṃ saṅghassa kathinadussaṃ uppannaṃ. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho imaṃ kathinadussaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dadeyya kathinaṃ attharituṃ. Esā ñatti.

307. “Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This kaṭhina cloth has arisen for the Saṅgha. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give this kaṭhina cloth to the monk named so-and-so to spread the kaṭhina. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Idaṃ saṅghassa kathinadussaṃ uppannaṃ. Saṅgho imaṃ kathinadussaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno deti kathinaṃ [T 2.0137] attharituṃ. Yassāyasmato khamati imassa kathinadussassa itthannāmassa bhikkhuno dānaṃ kathinaṃ attharituṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. This kaṭhina cloth has arisen for the Saṅgha. The Saṅgha gives this kaṭhina cloth to the monk named so-and-so to spread the kaṭhina. Whichever venerable one approves of the giving of this kaṭhina cloth to the monk named so-and-so to spread the kaṭhina, let him be silent. Whoever does not approve, let him speak.”

“Dinnaṃ idaṃ saṅghena kathinadussaṃ itthannāmassa bhikkhuno kathinaṃ attharituṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“This kaṭhina cloth has been given by the Saṅgha to the monk named so-and-so to spread the kaṭhina. The Saṅgha approves, therefore it is silent. Thus do I understand it.”

308. “Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, evaṃ anatthataṃ. Kathañca pana, bhikkhave, anatthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ? Na ullikhitamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na dhovanamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na cīvaravicāraṇamattena na gaṇṭusakaraṇamattena (ka.) atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na chedanamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na bandhanamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na ovaṭṭiyakaraṇamattena na ovaṭṭeyyakaraṇamattena (sī. syā.), na ovadeyyakaraṇamattena (ka.) atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na kaṇḍusakaraṇamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na daḷhīkammakaraṇamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na anuvātakaraṇamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na paribhaṇḍakaraṇamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na ovaddheyyakaraṇamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na kambalamaddanamattena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na nimittakatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na parikathākatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na kukkukatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na sannidhikatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na nissaggiyena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na akappakatena atthataṃ [M 0.0353] hoti kathinaṃ[T 2.0138], na aññatra saṅghāṭiyā atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na [P 1.0255] aññatra uttarāsaṅgena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na aññatra antaravāsakena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na aññatra pañcakena vā atirekapañcakena vā tadaheva sañchinnena samaṇḍalīkatena [V 0.0332] atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, na aññatra puggalassa atthārā atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ; sammā ceva atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, tañce nissīmaṭṭho anumodati, evampi anatthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, anatthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ.

308. Monks, in this way the Kathina is spread, and in this way it is not spread. And how, monks, is the Kathina not spread? The Kathina is not spread merely by taking the measurements. The Kathina is not spread merely by washing. The Kathina is not spread merely by arranging the robe into sections. The Kathina is not spread merely by cutting. The Kathina is not spread merely by tacking. The Kathina is not spread merely by sewing the length along the tacking line. The Kathina is not spread merely by covering with a patch. The Kathina is not spread merely by joining the first two main panels. The Kathina is not spread merely by adding the lengthwise border. The Kathina is not spread merely by adding the widthwise border. The Kathina is not spread merely by attaching the shoulder-strap. The Kathina is not spread merely by dyeing it once to the color of ivory. The Kathina is not spread with a cloth obtained by making a sign. The Kathina is not spread with a cloth obtained through hinting. The Kathina is not spread with a borrowed cloth. The Kathina is not spread with a cloth that has been stored. The Kathina is not spread with a cloth that is to be forfeited. The Kathina is not spread with a robe that has not had the kappabindu mark applied. The Kathina is not spread with anything other than the double-layered outer robe. The Kathina is not spread with anything other than the upper robe. The Kathina is not spread with anything other than the lower robe. The Kathina is not spread with anything other than a robe of five or more sections, cut and made with its major and minor panels on that very day. The Kathina is not spread except by the spreading of an individual. And if the Kathina is properly spread, but a monk residing outside the boundary gives his approval, in that case also the Kathina is not spread. In this way, monks, the Kathina is not spread.

309. “Kathañca, bhikkhave, atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ? Ahatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, ahatakappena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, pilotikāya atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, paṃsukūlena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, pāpaṇikena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, animittakatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, aparikathākatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, akukkukatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, asannidhikatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, anissaggiyena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, kappakatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, saṅghāṭiyā atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, uttarāsaṅgena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, antaravāsakena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, pañcakena vā atirekapañcakena vā tadaheva sañchinnena samaṇḍalīkatena atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, puggalassa atthārā atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ; sammā ce atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ, tañce sīmaṭṭho anumodati, evampi atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ[T 2.0139]. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, atthataṃ hoti kathinaṃ.

309. And how, monks, is the Kathina spread? The Kathina is spread with new cloth, with cloth like new, with a piece of cloth, with rag-robe cloth, with cloth from a shop-front, with cloth obtained without making a sign, with cloth obtained without indirect speech, with unborrowed cloth, with cloth that has not been stored, with cloth that is not to be forfeited, with a robe that has been made allowable, with the double-layered robe, with the upper robe, with the lower robe, with a robe of five or more than five panels, cut and made with panels on that very day, by the spreading of an individual; and if the Kathina is well spread, and if a monk within the boundary rejoices in it, in this way too the Kathina is spread. Thus, monks, is the Kathina spread.

310. “Kathañca, bhikkhave, ubbhataṃ hoti kathinaṃ? Aṭṭhimā, bhikkhave, mātikā kathinassa ubbhārāya – pakkamanantikā, niṭṭhānantikā, sanniṭṭhānantikā, nāsanantikā, savanantikā, āsāvacchedikā, sīmātikkantikā, sahubbhārā”ti saubbhārāti (ka.).

310. And how, monks, is the Kathina withdrawn? There are these eight grounds, monks, for the withdrawal of the Kathina: withdrawal ending with departure, withdrawal ending with completion, withdrawal ending with a firm decision, withdrawal ending with loss, withdrawal ending with hearing, withdrawal ending with the cutting off of hope, withdrawal ending with the transgression of the boundary, and withdrawal together with the Sangha.

Kathinānujānanā niṭṭhitā.

The Allowance for the Kathina is concluded.

188. Ādāyasattakaṃ

The Heptad on Taking

311. Bhikkhu atthatakathino katacīvaraṃ ādāya pakkamati – “na paccessa”nti. Tassa bhikkhuno pakkamanantiko kathinuddhāro.

188. A monk for whom the Kathina has been spread, having taken a completed robe, departs with the thought, 'I will not return.' For that monk, the withdrawal of the Kathina is one that ends with departure.

Bhikkhu [M 0.0354] atthatakathino cīvaraṃ ādāya pakkamati. Tassa bahisīmagatassa evaṃ hoti – “idhevimaṃ cīvaraṃ kāressaṃ, na paccessa”nti. So taṃ cīvaraṃ kāreti. Tassa bhikkhuno niṭṭhānantiko kathinuddhāro.

311. A monk for whom the Kathina has been spread, having taken robe-cloth, departs. Having gone outside the boundary, it occurs to him thus: 'I will make this robe right here; I will not return.' He makes that robe. For that monk, the withdrawal of the Kathina is one that ends with completion.

Bhikkhu [V 0.0333] atthatakathino cīvaraṃ ādāya pakkamati. Tassa bahisīmagatassa evaṃ hoti – “nevimaṃ cīvaraṃ kāressaṃ, na paccessa”nti. Tassa bhikkhuno sanniṭṭhānantiko kathinuddhāro.

A monk for whom the Kathina has been spread takes a robe-cloth and departs. Having gone outside the boundary, it occurs to him thus: 'I will not make this robe-cloth, nor will I return.' For that monk, the withdrawal of the Kathina is one that ends with a firm decision.

Bhikkhu atthatakathino cīvaraṃ ādāya pakkamati. Tassa bahisīmagatassa evaṃ hoti – “idhevimaṃ cīvaraṃ kāressaṃ, na paccessa”nti. So taṃ cīvaraṃ kāreti. Tassa taṃ cīvaraṃ kayiramānaṃ nassati. Tassa bhikkhuno nāsanantiko kathinuddhāro.

A monk for whom the Kathina has been spread takes a robe-cloth and departs. Having gone outside the boundary, it occurs to him thus: 'I will make this robe-cloth right here, and I will not return.' He makes that robe-cloth. While that robe-cloth is being made, it is lost. For that monk, the withdrawal of the Kathina is one that ends with loss.

Bhikkhu atthatakathino cīvaraṃ ādāya pakkamati – “paccessa”nti. So bahisīmagato taṃ cīvaraṃ kāreti. So katacīvaro suṇāti “ubbhataṃ [P 1.0256] kira tasmiṃ āvāse kathina”nti. Tassa bhikkhuno savanantiko kathinuddhāro.

A monk for whom the Kathina has been spread takes a robe-cloth and departs, intending, 'I will return.' Having gone outside the boundary, he makes that robe-cloth. Having completed the robe, he hears, 'It is said the Kathina has been withdrawn in that monastery.' For that monk, the withdrawal of the Kathina is one that ends with hearing.

Bhikkhu atthatakathino cīvaraṃ ādāya pakkamati – “paccessa”nti[T 2.0140]. So bahisīmagato taṃ cīvaraṃ kāreti. So katacīvaro – “paccessaṃ paccessa”nti – bahiddhā kathinuddhāraṃ vītināmeti. Tassa bhikkhuno sīmātikkantiko kathinuddhāro.

A monk for whom the Kathina has been spread takes a robe-cloth and departs, intending, 'I will return.' Having gone outside the boundary, he makes that robe-cloth. Having completed the robe, while intending, 'I will return, I will return,' he lets the time for the withdrawal of the Kathina pass by while outside the boundary. For that monk, the withdrawal of the Kathina is one that ends with the transgression of the boundary.

Bhikkhu atthatakathino cīvaraṃ ādāya pakkamati – “paccessa”nti. So bahisīmagato taṃ cīvaraṃ kāreti. So katacīvaro – “paccessaṃ paccessa”nti – sambhuṇāti kathinuddhāraṃ. Tassa bhikkhuno saha bhikkhūhi kathinuddhāro.

A monk for whom the Kathina has been spread takes a robe-cloth and departs, intending, 'I will return.' Having gone outside the boundary, he makes that robe-cloth. Having completed the robe, while intending, 'I will return, I will return,' he arrives in time for the withdrawal of the Kathina. For that monk, the withdrawal of the Kathina occurs together with the other monks.

Ādāyasattakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ …dutiyaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ (ka.).

The Heptad on Taking is concluded.

189. Samādāyasattakaṃ

The Heptad on Undertaking

312. Bhikkhu atthatakathino katacīvaraṃ samādāya pakkamati “na paccessa”nti. Tassa bhikkhuno pakkamanantiko kathinuddhāro.

312. A monk for whom the Kathina has been spread, having taken up a completed robe, departs with the intention, 'I will not return.' For that monk, the withdrawal of the Kathina is one that is terminated by departure.

Bhikkhu [M 0.0355] atthatakathino cīvaraṃ samādāya pakkamati. Tassa bahisīmagatassa evaṃ hoti – “idhevimaṃ cīvaraṃ kāressaṃ, na paccessa”nti. So taṃ cīvaraṃ kāreti. Tassa bhikkhuno niṭṭhānantiko kathinuddhāro.

A monk for whom the Kathina has been spread, having taken up a robe, departs. Having gone outside the boundary, it occurs to him thus: 'I will make this robe right here; I will not return.' He makes that robe. For that monk, the withdrawal of the Kathina is one that is terminated by completion.

A bhikkhu, the kathina having been spread, having properly taken an unfinished robe, departs thinking, 'I will return.' Having gone outside the boundary, he has that robe made. He, with the robe completed, hears, 'Indeed, in that monastery the kathina has been withdrawn.' For that bhikkhu, the withdrawal of the kathina is one that is terminated by hearing.
