So tena kiso lūkho [T 2.0183] dubbaṇṇo uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajāto dhamanisanthatagatto. Sādhu devo jīvakaṃ vejjaṃ [P 1.0276] āṇāpetu puttaṃ me tikicchitu”nti.

333. Now at that time, the son of a merchant of Bārāṇasī, while playing by performing acrobatics, developed an intestinal obstruction. Because of this illness, the gruel he drank was not properly digested, the rice he ate was not properly digested, and his feces and urine were not regular. Due to that illness, he became thin, emaciated, of poor complexion, pale like a withered leaf, and his body was covered with protruding veins. Then this thought occurred to the merchant of Bārāṇasī: “My son has such an illness that the gruel he drinks is not properly digested, the rice he eats is not properly digested, and his feces and urine are not regular. Because of that illness, he has become thin, emaciated, of poor complexion, pale like a withered leaf, and his body is covered with protruding veins. What if I were to go to Rājagaha and ask the king for the physician Jīvaka to treat my son?” Then the merchant of Bārāṇasī went to Rājagaha and approached King Bimbisāra of Magadha, who had a great army. Having approached, he said this to King Bimbisāra of Magadha, who had a great army: “Your Majesty, my son has such an illness that the gruel he drinks is not properly digested, the rice he eats is not properly digested, and his feces and urine are not regular. Because of that illness, he has become thin, emaciated, of poor complexion, pale like a withered leaf, and his body is covered with protruding veins. May Your Majesty be pleased to command the physician Jīvaka to treat my son.”

Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro jīvakaṃ komārabhaccaṃ āṇāpesi – “gaccha, bhaṇe jīvaka, bārāṇasiṃ gantvā bārāṇaseyyakaṃ seṭṭhiputtaṃ tikicchāhī”ti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho jīvako komārabhacco rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa paṭissutvā bārāṇasiṃ gantvā yena bārāṇaseyyako seṭṭhiputto tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bārāṇaseyyakassa seṭṭhiputtassa vikāraṃ sallakkhetvā janaṃ ussāretvā [M 0.0387] tirokaraṇiyaṃ parikkhipitvā thambhe ubbandhitvā upanibandhitvā (sī. syā.) bhariyaṃ purato ṭhapetvā udaracchaviṃ uppāṭetvā antagaṇṭhiṃ nīharitvā bhariyāya dassesi – “passa te sāmikassa ābādhaṃ, iminā yāgupi pītā na sammā pariṇāmaṃ gacchati, bhattampi bhuttaṃ na sammā pariṇāmaṃ gacchati, uccāropi passāvopi na paguṇo; imināyaṃ kiso lūkho dubbaṇṇo uppaṇḍuppaṇḍukajāto dhamanisanthatagatto”ti. Antagaṇṭhiṃ viniveṭhetvā antāni paṭipavesetvā udaracchaviṃ sibbitvā ālepaṃ adāsi. Atha kho bārāṇaseyyako seṭṭhiputto nacirasseva arogo ahosi. Atha kho bārāṇaseyyako seṭṭhi ‘putto me arogo ṭhito’ti arogāpitoti (sī.) jīvakassa komārabhaccassa soḷasasahassāni pādāsi. Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco tāni soḷasasahassāni ādāya punadeva rājagahaṃ paccāgañchi[T 2.0184].

Then King Bimbisāra of Magadha, who had a great army, commanded Jīvaka Komārabhacca: “Go, Jīvaka, go to Bārāṇasī and treat the son of the merchant of Bārāṇasī.” “Yes, Your Majesty,” replied Jīvaka Komārabhacca. Having consented to King Bimbisāra of Magadha, who had a great army, he went to Bārāṇasī and approached the son of the merchant of Bārāṇasī. Having approached, he observed the disorder of the son of the merchant of Bārāṇasī, cleared the people away, had a screen put up, tied him to a post, placed his wife in front, cut open the skin of the abdomen, took out the intestinal knot, and showed it to his wife, saying: “Look at your husband’s illness. Because of this, the gruel he drinks is not properly digested, the rice he eats is not properly digested, and his feces and urine are not regular. Because of this illness, he is thin, emaciated, of poor complexion, pale like a withered leaf, and his body is covered with protruding veins.” Having untangled the intestinal knot, put the intestines back in, and stitched up the skin of the abdomen, he applied an ointment. Then, not long after, the son of the merchant of Bārāṇasī became free from illness. Then the merchant of Bārāṇasī, thinking, “My son is now well,” gave Jīvaka Komārabhacca sixteen thousand. Then Jīvaka Komārabhacca, having taken those sixteen thousand, returned again to Rājagaha.

Seṭṭhiputtavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story of the merchant's son is concluded.

207. Pajjotarājavatthu

207. The Story of King Pajjota

334. Tena [V 0.0365] kho pana samayena rañño ujjeniyaṃ rañño (syā.) pajjotassa paṇḍurogābādho hoti. Bahū mahantā mahantā disāpāmokkhā vejjā āgantvā nāsakkhiṃsu arogaṃ kātuṃ. Bahuṃ hiraññaṃ ādāya agamaṃsu. Atha kho rājā pajjoto rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – “mayhaṃ kho tādiso ābādho, sādhu devo jīvakaṃ vejjaṃ āṇāpetu, so maṃ tikicchissatī”ti. Atha kho rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro jīvakaṃ komārabhaccaṃ āṇāpesi – “gaccha, bhaṇe jīvaka; ujjeniṃ gantvā rājānaṃ pajjotaṃ tikicchāhī”ti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho jīvako komārabhacco rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa paṭissutvā ujjeniṃ gantvā yena rājā pajjoto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rañño pajjotassa vikāraṃ sallakkhetvā rājānaṃ pajjotaṃ etadavoca – “sappiṃ dehi idaṃ padadvayaṃ sī. syā. potthakesu natthi, sappiṃ deva, nippacissāmi. Taṃ devo pivissatī”ti. “Alaṃ, bhaṇe jīvaka, yaṃ te sakkā vinā sappinā arogaṃ kātuṃ taṃ karohi. Jegucchaṃ me sappi, paṭikūla”nti. Atha kho jīvakassa komārabhaccassa etadahosi [P 1.0277] – “imassa kho rañño tādiso ābādho[M 0.0388], na sakkā vinā sappinā arogaṃ kātuṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ sappiṃ nippaceyyaṃ [T 2.0185] kasāvavaṇṇaṃ kasāvagandhaṃ kasāvarasa”nti. Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco nānābhesajjehi sappiṃ nippaci kasāvavaṇṇaṃ kasāvagandhaṃ kasāvarasaṃ. Atha kho jīvakassa komārabhaccassa etadahosi – “imassa kho rañño sappi pītaṃ pariṇāmentaṃ uddekaṃ dassati. Caṇḍoyaṃ rājā ghātāpeyyāpi maṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ paṭikacceva āpuccheyya”nti. Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco yena rājā pajjoto tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṃ pajjotaṃ etadavoca – “mayaṃ kho, deva, vejjā nāma tādisena muhuttena mūlāni uddharāma bhesajjāni saṃharāma. Sādhu devo vāhanāgāresu ca dvāresu ca āṇāpetu – yena vāhanena jīvako icchati tena vāhanena gacchatu, yena dvārena icchati tena dvārena gacchatu, yaṃ kālaṃ icchati taṃ kālaṃ gacchatu, yaṃ kālaṃ icchati taṃ kālaṃ pavisatū”ti. Atha kho rājā pajjoto vāhanāgāresu ca dvāresu ca āṇāpesi – “yena vāhanena jīvako icchati tena vāhanena gacchatu, yena dvārena icchati tena dvārena gacchatu, yaṃ kālaṃ icchati taṃ kālaṃ gacchatu, yaṃ kālaṃ icchati taṃ kālaṃ pavisatū”ti.

334. Now at that time, King Pajjota was afflicted with jaundice. Many great and renowned physicians came, but were unable to cure him. They took much gold and silver and departed. Then King Pajjota sent a messenger to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, saying, “I have such an illness. It would be good if Your Majesty were to send Jīvaka, the physician; he will treat me.” Then King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha commanded Jīvaka Komārabhacca, saying, “Go, friend Jīvaka; travel to Ujjenī and treat King Pajjota.” “Yes, Your Majesty,” replied Jīvaka Komārabhacca, and having consented to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha, he went to Ujjenī and approached King Pajjota. After observing the king’s condition, he said to him, “Give ghee, Your Majesty. I will prepare the ghee, and Your Majesty shall drink it.” “Enough, friend Jīvaka, do what you can to cure me without ghee. Ghee is loathsome to me; it is repulsive.” Then Jīvaka Komārabhacca thought, “This king has such an illness that it cannot be cured without ghee. What if I were to prepare ghee with an astringent color, an astringent smell, and an astringent taste?” So Jīvaka Komārabhacca prepared ghee with various medicines, giving it an astringent color, an astringent smell, and an astringent taste. Then Jīvaka Komārabhacca thought, “After this king drinks the ghee, as it is being digested, it will cause him to belch. This king is fierce—he might even have me killed. What if I were to take my leave beforehand?” So Jīvaka Komārabhacca approached King Pajjota and said, “We physicians, Your Majesty, extract roots and collect medicines at a particular moment. It would be good if Your Majesty were to issue orders at the vehicle houses and gates: ‘Let Jīvaka go by whatever vehicle he wishes, go out by whatever gate he wishes, depart at whatever time he wishes, and enter at whatever time he wishes.’” Then King Pajjota issued orders at the vehicle houses and gates: “Let Jīvaka go by whatever vehicle he wishes, go out by whatever gate he wishes, depart at whatever time he wishes, and enter at whatever time he wishes.”

Tena kho pana samayena rañño pajjotassa bhaddavatikā nāma hatthinikā paññāsayojanikā hoti. Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco rañño pajjotassa sappiṃ taṃ sappiṃ (syā.) upanāmesi [V 0.0366] – “kasāvaṃ devo pivatū”ti. Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco rājānaṃ pajjotaṃ sappiṃ pāyetvā hatthisālaṃ gantvā bhaddavatikāya hatthinikāya nagaramhā nippati[T 2.0186].

Now at that time, King Pajjota had a female riding elephant named Bhaddavatikā, which was able to travel fifty yojanas in a day. Then Jīvaka Komārabhacca offered the ghee to King Pajjota, saying, “May Your Majesty drink the astringent medicine.” Then, after having King Pajjota drink the ghee, Jīvaka Komārabhacca went to the elephant stable and departed from the city by means of the female riding elephant Bhaddavatikā.

Atha kho rañño pajjotassa taṃ sappi pītaṃ pariṇāmentaṃ uddekaṃ adāsi. Atha kho rājā pajjoto manusse etadavoca – “duṭṭhena, bhaṇe, jīvakena sappiṃ pāyitomhi. Tena hi, bhaṇe, jīvakaṃ vejjaṃ vicinathā”ti. “Bhaddavatikāya, deva, hatthinikāya nagaramhā nippatito”ti. Tena kho pana samayena rañño pajjotassa kāko nāma dāso saṭṭhiyojaniko hoti, amanussena paṭicca jāto. Atha kho rājā pajjoto kākaṃ dāsaṃ āṇāpesi – “gaccha, bhaṇe kāka, jīvakaṃ vejjaṃ [M 0.0389] nivattehi – rājā taṃ, ācariya, nivattāpetīti. Ete kho, bhaṇe kāka, vejjā nāma bahumāyā. Mā cassa kiñci paṭiggahesī”ti.

Then, as the ghee King Pajjota had drunk was being digested, it caused him to belch. Then King Pajjota said to his men, “Sirs, I have been made to drink ghee by the wicked Jīvaka. Therefore, sirs, seek out the physician Jīvaka.” They informed him, “Your Majesty, he has departed from the city by means of the female riding elephant Bhaddavatikā.” Now at that time, King Pajjota had a slave named Kāka, who was able to travel sixty yojanas in a day, born in dependence on a non-human being. Then King Pajjota commanded the slave Kāka, “Go, sir Kāka, and make the physician Jīvaka return, saying, ‘Teacher, the king is having you return.’ These physicians, sir Kāka, are very deceitful. Do not accept anything from him.”

Atha kho kāko dāso jīvakaṃ komārabhaccaṃ antarāmagge kosambiyaṃ sambhāvesi

Then the slave Kāka caught up with Jīvaka Komārabhacca on the way, at Kosambī.

Pātarāsaṃ karontaṃ. Atha kho kāko dāso jīvakaṃ komārabhaccaṃ etadavoca [P 1.0278] – “rājā taṃ, ācariya, nivattāpetī”ti. “Āgamehi, bhaṇe kāka, yāva bhuñjāma bhuñjāmi (sī. syā.). Handa, bhaṇe kāka, bhuñjassū”ti. “Alaṃ, ācariya, raññāmhi āṇatto – ete kho, bhaṇe kāka, vejjā nāma bahumāyā, mā cassa kiñci paṭiggahesī”ti. Tena kho pana samayena jīvako komārabhacco nakhena bhesajjaṃ olumpetvā āmalakañca khādati pānīyañca pivati. Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco kākaṃ dāsaṃ etadavoca – “handa, bhaṇe kāka, āmalakañca khāda pānīyañca pivassū”ti. Atha kho kāko dāso – ayaṃ kho vejjo āmalakañca [T 2.0187] khādati pānīyañca pivati, na arahati kiñci pāpakaṃ hotunti – upaḍḍhāmalakañca khādi pānīyañca apāyi. Tassa taṃ upaḍḍhāmalakaṃ khāditaṃ tattheva nicchāresi. Atha kho kāko dāso jīvakaṃ komārabhaccaṃ etadavoca – “atthi me, ācariya, jīvita”nti? “Mā, bhaṇe kāka, bhāyi, tvaṃ ceva arogo bhavissasi rājā ca. Caṇḍo so rājā ghātāpeyyāpi maṃ, tenāhaṃ na nivattāmī”ti bhaddavatikaṃ hatthinikaṃ kākassa niyyādetvā yena rājagahaṃ tena pakkāmi. Anupubbena yena rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa etamatthaṃ ārocesi. “Suṭṭhu, bhaṇe jīvaka, akāsi yampi na nivatto, caṇḍo so rājā ghātāpeyyāpi ta”nti. Atha kho rājā pajjoto arogo samāno jīvakassa komārabhaccassa santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – “āgacchatu jīvako, varaṃ dassāmī”ti. “Alaṃ, ayyo deva (syā.), adhikāraṃ me devo saratū”ti.

Then the slave Kāka said this to Jīvaka Komārabhacca: “Master, the king is recalling you.” “Wait, friend Kāka, until we have eaten. Come now, friend Kāka, eat.” “Enough, master. I have been commanded by the king: ‘Friend Kāka, these physicians are very deceitful; do not accept anything from him.’” At that time, Jīvaka Komārabhacca, having scooped up medicine with his fingernail, was eating an āmalaka fruit and drinking water. Then Jīvaka Komārabhacca said this to the slave Kāka: “Come now, friend Kāka, eat an āmalaka and drink water.” Then the slave Kāka, thinking, “This physician is eating an āmalaka and drinking water; it is not possible for anything bad to happen,” ate half an āmalaka and drank water. Having been eaten, that half āmalaka caused him to purge right there. Then the slave Kāka said this to Jīvaka Komārabhacca: “Master, will I live?” “Do not be afraid, friend Kāka. You will be free from illness, and so will the king. That king is fierce; he might have me killed. Therefore, I am not returning.” Having entrusted the she-elephant Bhaddavatika to Kāka, he departed for Rājagaha. In due course, he approached King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha. Having approached, he related this matter to King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha. “You did well, friend Jīvaka, in not returning. That king is fierce; he might have had you killed.” Then King Pajjota, having become free from illness, sent a messenger to Jīvaka Komārabhacca, saying: “Let Jīvaka come; I will grant him a boon.” “Enough, my lord. May Your Majesty remember my service.”

Pajjotarājavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Story of King Pajjota is concluded.

208. Siveyyakadussayugakathā

The Story of the Siveyyaka Pair of Cloths

335. Tena [V 0.0367] kho pana samayena rañño pajjotassa siveyyakaṃ dussayugaṃ uppannaṃ hoti – bahūnaṃ bahunnaṃ (sī. syā.) dussānaṃ bahūnaṃ dussayugānaṃ bahūnaṃ dussayugasatānaṃ bahūnaṃ dussayugasahassānaṃ bahūnaṃ dussayugasatasahassānaṃ [M 0.0390] aggañca seṭṭhañca mokkhañca uttamañca pavarañca. Atha kho rājā pajjoto taṃ siveyyakaṃ dussayugaṃ jīvakassa komārabhaccassa pāhesi. Atha kho jīvakassa [T 2.0188] komārabhaccassa etadahosi – “idaṃ kho me siveyyakaṃ dussayugaṃ raññā pajjotena pahitaṃ – bahūnaṃ dussānaṃ bahūnaṃ dussayugānaṃ bahūnaṃ dussayugasatānaṃ bahūnaṃ dussayugasahassānaṃ bahūnaṃ dussayugasatasahassānaṃ aggañca seṭṭhañca mokkhañca uttamañca pavarañca. Nayidaṃ añño koci paccārahati aññatra tena bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena, raññā vā māgadhena seniyena bimbisārenā”ti.

208. Now at that time, a pair of Siveyyaka cloths had arisen for King Pajjota—the foremost, finest, most prominent, supreme, and most excellent of many cloths, many pairs of cloths, hundreds of pairs of cloths, thousands of pairs of cloths, and hundreds of thousands of pairs of cloths. Then King Pajjota sent that pair of Siveyyaka cloths to Jīvaka Komārabhacca. Then this thought occurred to Jīvaka Komārabhacca: 'This pair of Siveyyaka cloths has been sent to me by King Pajjota—the foremost, finest, most prominent, supreme, and most excellent of many cloths, many pairs of cloths, hundreds of pairs of cloths, thousands of pairs of cloths, and hundreds of thousands of pairs of cloths. No one else is worthy to wear this except for the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, or King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha.'

Siveyyakadussayugakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Story of the Siveyyaka Cloth Pair is concluded.

209. Samattiṃsavirecanakathā

335. The Account of the Thirty Purgings

336. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavato kāyo dosābhisanno hoti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “dosābhisanno [P 1.0279] kho, ānanda, tathāgatassa kāyo. Icchati tathāgato virecanaṃ pātu”nti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena jīvako komārabhacco tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā jīvakaṃ komārabhaccaṃ etadavoca – “dosābhisanno kho, āvuso jīvaka, tathāgatassa kāyo. Icchati tathāgato virecanaṃ pātu”nti. “Tena hi, bhante ānanda, bhagavato kāyaṃ katipāhaṃ sinehethā”ti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato kāyaṃ katipāhaṃ sinehetvā yena jīvako komārabhacco tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā jīvakaṃ komārabhaccaṃ etadavoca – “siniddho kho, āvuso jīvaka, tathāgatassa kāyo. Yassa dāni kālaṃ maññasī”ti. Atha kho jīvakassa komārabhaccassa etadahosi – “na kho metaṃ patirūpaṃ yohaṃ bhagavato oḷārikaṃ virecanaṃ dadeyya”nti. Tīṇi uppalahatthāni nānābhesajjehi paribhāvetvā yena [T 2.0189] bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃ uppalahatthaṃ bhagavato upanāmesi – “imaṃ, bhante, bhagavā paṭhamaṃ uppalahatthaṃ upasiṅghatu. Idaṃ bhagavantaṃ dasakkhattuṃ virecessatī”ti. Dutiyaṃ uppalahatthaṃ bhagavato upanāmesi – “imaṃ, bhante, bhagavā dutiyaṃ uppalahatthaṃ upasiṅghatu. Idaṃ bhagavantaṃ dasakkhattuṃ virecessatī”ti. Tatiyaṃ uppalahatthaṃ bhagavato upanāmesi – “imaṃ, bhante[V 0.0368], bhagavā tatiyaṃ uppalahatthaṃ upasiṅghatu. Idaṃ bhagavantaṃ dasakkhattuṃ virecessatī”ti[M 0.0391]. Evaṃ bhagavato samattiṃsāya virecanaṃ bhavissatīti. Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco bhagavato samattiṃsāya virecanaṃ datvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho jīvakassa komārabhaccassa bahi dvārakoṭṭhakā nikkhantassa etadahosi – “mayā kho bhagavato samattiṃsāya virecanaṃ dinnaṃ. Dosābhisanno tathāgatassa kāyo[T 2.0190]. Na bhagavantaṃ samattiṃsakkhattuṃ virecessati, ekūnattiṃsakkhattuṃ bhagavantaṃ virecessati. Api ca, bhagavā viritto nahāyissati. Nahātaṃ bhagavantaṃ sakiṃ virecessati. Evaṃ bhagavato samattiṃsāya virecanaṃ bhavissatī”ti.

336. Now on that occasion, the Blessed One’s body was afflicted by a disturbance of the humors. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Ānanda, the Tathāgata’s body is afflicted by a disturbance of the humors. The Tathāgata wishes to drink a purgative.” Then the Venerable Ānanda approached Jīvaka Komārabhacca; having approached, he said to Jīvaka Komārabhacca: “Friend Jīvaka, the Tathāgata’s body is afflicted by a disturbance of the humors. The Tathāgata wishes to drink a purgative.” “If that is so, Venerable Ānanda, please anoint the Blessed One’s body with oil for a few days.” Then the Venerable Ānanda, having anointed the Blessed One’s body with oil for a few days, approached Jīvaka Komārabhacca; having approached, he said to Jīvaka Komārabhacca: “Friend Jīvaka, the Tathāgata’s body has been anointed with oil. Now you may know the proper time.” Then this thought occurred to Jīvaka Komārabhacca: “It is not proper for me to give the Blessed One a coarse purgative.” Having imbued three lotuses with various medicines, he approached the Blessed One and offered the first lotus to the Blessed One, saying: “Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One first smell this lotus. This will purge the Blessed One ten times.” He offered the second lotus to the Blessed One, saying: “Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One smell this second lotus. This will purge the Blessed One ten times.” He offered the third lotus to the Blessed One, saying: “Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One smell this third lotus. This will purge the Blessed One ten times.” Thus, there would be thirty purges for the Blessed One. Then Jīvaka Komārabhacca, having given the Blessed One the purgative for thirty purges, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and departed. As Jīvaka Komārabhacca was leaving the outer gatehouse, this thought occurred to him: “I have given the Blessed One a purgative for thirty purges. The Tathāgata’s body is afflicted by a disturbance of the humors. It will not purge the Blessed One thirty times; it will purge the Blessed One twenty-nine times. Moreover, the Blessed One will bathe after being purged. After bathing, he will be purged once more. Thus, there will be thirty purges for the Blessed One.”

Atha kho bhagavā jīvakassa komārabhaccassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “idhānanda, jīvakassa komārabhaccassa bahi dvārakoṭṭhakā nikkhantassa etadahosi – ‘mayā kho bhagavato samattiṃsāya virecanaṃ dinnaṃ. Dosābhisanno tathāgatassa kāyo. Na bhagavantaṃ samatiṃsakkhattuṃ virecessati, ekūnatiṃsakkhattuṃ bhagavantaṃ virecessati. Api ca, bhagavā viritto nahāyissati. Nahātaṃ bhagavantaṃ sakiṃ virecessati. Evaṃ bhagavato samattiṃsāya virecanaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Tena hānanda, uṇhodakaṃ paṭiyādehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā uṇhodakaṃ [P 1.0280] paṭiyādesi.

Then the Blessed One, knowing with his mind the thought in Jīvaka Komārabhacca’s mind, addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Ānanda, just now as Jīvaka Komārabhacca was leaving the outer gatehouse, this thought occurred to him: ‘I have given the Blessed One a purgative for thirty purges. The Tathāgata’s body is afflicted by a disturbance of the humors. It will not purge the Blessed One thirty times; it will purge the Blessed One twenty-nine times. Moreover, the Blessed One will bathe after being purged. After bathing, he will be purged once more. Thus, there will be thirty purges for the Blessed One.’ Therefore, Ānanda, prepare hot water.” “Yes, Venerable Sir,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One and prepared hot water.

Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho jīvako komārabhacco bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “viritto, bhante, bhagavā”ti? “Virittomhi, jīvakā”ti. Idha mayhaṃ, bhante, bahi dvārakoṭṭhakā nikkhantassa etadahosi – “mayā kho bhagavato samattiṃsāya virecanaṃ dinnaṃ. Dosābhisanno tathāgatassa kāyo. Na bhagavantaṃ samattiṃsakkhattuṃ virecessati, ekūnattiṃsakkhattuṃ bhagavantaṃ virecessati. Api ca, bhagavā viritto nahāyissati. Nahātaṃ bhagavantaṃ sakiṃ virecessati. Evaṃ bhagavato samattiṃsāya virecanaṃ bhavissatī”ti. Nahāyatu, bhante, bhagavā, nahāyatu sugatoti. Atha kho bhagavā uṇhodakaṃ nahāyi. Nahātaṃ bhagavantaṃ sakiṃ virecesi. Evaṃ bhagavato samattiṃsāya virecanaṃ ahosi. Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco bhagavantaṃ [M 0.0392] etadavoca – “yāva, bhante, bhagavato kāyo pakatatto hoti, alaṃ ahaṃ tāva yūsapiṇṭapātenāti (sī.), alaṃ yūsapiṇṭakenāti (syā.) yūsapiṇḍapātenā”ti.

Then Jīvaka Komārabhacca approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Jīvaka Komārabhacca said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, has the Blessed One been purged?” “I have been purged, Jīvaka.” “Venerable Sir, just now as I was leaving the outer gatehouse, this thought occurred to me: ‘I have given the Blessed One a purgative for thirty purges. The Tathāgata’s body is afflicted by a disturbance of the humors. It will not purge the Blessed One thirty times; it will purge the Blessed One twenty-nine times. Moreover, the Blessed One will bathe after being purged. After bathing, he will be purged once more. Thus, there will be thirty purges for the Blessed One.’ Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One bathe, let the Sugata bathe.” Then the Blessed One bathed in hot water. After he had bathed, he was purged once. Thus, for the Blessed One, there were thirty purges. Then Jīvaka Komārabhacca said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, until the Blessed One’s body returns to its normal state, almsfood with broth is sufficient.”

Samattiṃsavirecanakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Thirty Purges is concluded.

210. Varayācanākathā

210. The Account of the Request for a Boon

337. Atha [V 0.0369] kho bhagavato kāyo nacirasseva pakatatto ahosi. Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco taṃ siveyyakaṃ dussayugaṃ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami[T 2.0191], upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho jīvako komārabhacco bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ekāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ varaṃ yācāmī”ti. “Atikkantavarā kho, jīvaka, tathāgatā”ti. “Yañca, bhante, kappati yañca anavajja”nti. “Vadehi, jīvakā”ti. “Bhagavā, bhante, paṃsukūliko, bhikkhusaṅgho ca. Idaṃ me, bhante, siveyyakaṃ dussayugaṃ raññā pajjotena pahitaṃ – bahūnaṃ dussānaṃ bahūnaṃ dussayugānaṃ bahūnaṃ dussayugasatānaṃ bahūnaṃ dussayugasahassānaṃ bahūnaṃ dussayugasatasahassānaṃ aggañca seṭṭhañca mokkhañca uttamañca pavarañca. Paṭiggaṇhātu me, bhante, bhagavā siveyyakaṃ dussayugaṃ; bhikkhusaṅghassa ca gahapaticīvaraṃ anujānātū”ti. Paṭiggahesi bhagavā siveyyakaṃ dussayugaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā jīvakaṃ komārabhaccaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gahapaticīvaraṃ. Yo icchati, paṃsukūliko hotu. Yo icchati, gahapaticīvaraṃ sādiyatu. Itarītarenapāhaṃ pahaṃ (sī.), cāhaṃ (syā.), bhikkhave, santuṭṭhiṃ vaṇṇemī”ti.

337. Then, not long after, the Blessed One’s body returned to its natural state. Then Jīvaka Komārabhacca took that pair of Sivi cloth and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, Jīvaka Komārabhacca said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I ask one boon of the Blessed One.” “Jīvaka, the Tathāgatas are past granting boons.” “But, venerable sir, I ask for that which is allowable and blameless.” “Speak, Jīvaka.” “Venerable sir, the Blessed One is a wearer of rag-robes, and so is the community of monks. Venerable sir, this pair of Sivi cloth was sent to me by King Pajjota—it is the foremost, the best, the chief, the supreme, and the most excellent of many cloths, many pairs of cloth, many hundreds of pairs of cloth, many thousands of pairs of cloth, and many hundreds of thousands of pairs of cloth. Venerable sir, may the Blessed One accept this pair of Sivi cloth from me, and may he allow robes from householders for the community of monks.” The Blessed One accepted the pair of Sivi cloth. Then the Blessed One instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened Jīvaka Komārabhacca with a Dhamma talk. Then Jīvaka Komārabhacca, having been instructed, encouraged, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping his right side toward him, and departed. Then, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a Dhamma talk, the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow robes from householders. Whoever wishes may be a wearer of rag-robes; whoever wishes may accept robes from householders. Monks, I praise contentment with either one or the other.”

Assosuṃ kho rājagahe manussā – “bhagavatā kira [P 1.0281] bhikkhūnaṃ gahapaticīvaraṃ [T 2.0192] anuññāta”nti. Te ca manussā haṭṭhā ahesuṃ udaggā “idāni kho mayaṃ dānāni dassāma puññāni karissāma, yato bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ gahapaticīvaraṃ anuññāta”nti. Ekāheneva rājagahe bahūni cīvarasahassāni uppajjiṃsu.

The people in Rājagaha heard: “The Blessed One, it seems, has allowed monks to accept robes provided by householders.” Those people were delighted and joyful, thinking: “Now we can give gifts and perform meritorious deeds, since the Blessed One has allowed monks to accept robes provided by householders.” In just one day, many thousands of robes arose in Rājagaha.

Assosuṃ [M 0.0393] kho jānapadā manussā – “bhagavatā kira bhikkhūnaṃ gahapaticīvaraṃ anuññāta”nti. Te ca manussā haṭṭhā ahesuṃ udaggā – “idāni kho mayaṃ dānāni dassāma puññāni karissāma, yato bhagavatā bhikkhūnaṃ gahapaticīvaraṃ anuññāta”nti. Janapadepi ekāheneva bahūni cīvarasahassāni uppajjiṃsu.

The people in the countryside heard, “The Blessed One, it seems, has allowed monks to accept robes from householders.” And those people were joyful and elated, thinking, “Now we can give gifts and do meritorious deeds, since the Blessed One has allowed monks to accept robes from householders.” In the countryside, too, many thousands of robes arose in just one day.

Tena [V 0.0370] kho pana samayena saṅghassa pāvāro uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pāvāranti.

At that time, a mantle had arisen for the Saṅgha. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a mantle.”

Koseyyapāvāro uppanno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, koseyyapāvāranti.

A silk mantle had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a silk mantle.”

Kojavaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kojavanti.

A woolen rug had arisen. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a woolen rug.”

Varayācanākathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Request for a Boon is concluded.

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The First Recitation Section is concluded.

211. Kambalānujānanādikathā

211. The Account Beginning with the Allowance of a Woolen Blanket

338. Tena kho pana samayena kāsirājā jīvakassa komārabhaccassa aḍḍhakāsikaṃ kambalaṃ pāhesi upaḍḍhakāsinaṃ khamamānaṃ. Atha kho jīvako komārabhacco taṃ aḍḍhakāsikaṃ kambalaṃ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho jīvako komārabhacco bhagavantaṃ [T 2.0193] etadavoca – “ayaṃ me, bhante, aḍḍhakāsiko kambalo kāsiraññā pahito upaḍḍhakāsinaṃ khamamāno. Paṭiggaṇhātu me, bhante, bhagavā kambalaṃ, yaṃ mamassa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā”ti. Paṭiggahesi bhagavā kambalaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā jīvakaṃ komārabhaccaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi…pe… padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kambala”nti.

338. Now at that time, the king of Kāsī sent Jīvaka Komārabhacca a woolen blanket worth five hundred. Then Jīvaka Komārabhacca took that woolen blanket worth five hundred and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Jīvaka Komārabhacca said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, this woolen blanket worth five hundred was sent to me by the king of Kāsī. May the Blessed One accept the woolen blanket from me, for what would be for my long-term welfare and happiness.” The Blessed One accepted the woolen blanket. Then the Blessed One instructed Jīvaka Komārabhacca with a talk on the Dhamma... and then, having circumambulated him respectfully, he departed. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow a woolen blanket.”

339. Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa uccāvacāni cīvarāni uppannāni honti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kiṃ nu kho bhagavatā cīvaraṃ anuññātaṃ[M 0.0394], kiṃ ananuññāta”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cha cīvarāni – khomaṃ kappāsikaṃ koseyyaṃ kambalaṃ sāṇaṃ bhaṅganti.

339. At that time, various kinds of robes had arisen for the Saṅgha. Then the monks thought: “What kind of robe has the Blessed One allowed, and what has he not allowed?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow six kinds of robes: linen, cotton, silk, woolen, hemp, and mixed-fabric.”

340. Tena kho pana samayena ye te bhikkhū gahapaticīvaraṃ [P 1.0282] sādiyanti te kukkuccāyantā [V 0.0371] paṃsukūlaṃ na sādiyanti – ekaṃyeva bhagavatā cīvaraṃ anuññātaṃ, na dveti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gahapaticīvaraṃ sādiyantena paṃsukūlampi sādiyituṃ; tadubhayenapāhaṃ, bhikkhave, santuṭṭhiṃ vaṇṇemīti.

340. At that time, those monks who accepted robes offered by householders, being scrupulous, did not accept rag-robes, thinking: “Only one kind of robe has been allowed by the Blessed One, not two.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow one who accepts a robe offered by a householder to also accept a rag-robe. Monks, I praise contentment with both of these.”

Kambalānujānanādikathā niṭṭhitā.

The account concerning the allowance of a woolen blanket and so on is concluded.

212. Paṃsukūlapariyesanakathā

212. The Account of Seeking Rag-Robes

341. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū kosalesu janapade [T 2.0194] addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Ekacce bhikkhū susānaṃ okkamiṃsu paṃsukūlāya, ekacce bhikkhū nāgamesuṃ. Ye te bhikkhū susānaṃ okkamiṃsu paṃsukūlāya te paṃsukūlāni labhiṃsu. Ye te bhikkhū nāgamesuṃ te evamāhaṃsu – “amhākampi, āvuso, bhāgaṃ dethā”ti. Te evamāhaṃsu – “na mayaṃ, āvuso, tumhākaṃ bhāgaṃ dassāma. Kissa tumhe nāgamitthā”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, nāgamentānaṃ nākāmā bhāgaṃ dātunti.

341. Now at that time, many monks were traveling on a long road in the country of Kosala. Some monks entered a charnel ground for the sake of rag-robes, while some monks did not wait. Those monks who entered the charnel ground for the sake of rag-robes obtained rag-robes. Those monks who did not wait said thus: “Venerable sirs, give us a share too.” Those monks said thus: “Venerable sirs, we will not give you a share. Why did you not wait?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: “Monks, if they are unwilling, I allow that a share not be given to those who did not wait.”

Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū kosalesu janapade addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Ekacce bhikkhū susānaṃ okkamiṃsu paṃsukūlāya, ekacce bhikkhū āgamesuṃ. Ye te bhikkhū susānaṃ okkamiṃsu paṃsukūlāya te paṃsukūlāni labhiṃsu. Ye te bhikkhū āgamesuṃ te evamāhaṃsu – “amhākampi, āvuso, bhāgaṃ dethā”ti. Te evamāhaṃsu – “na mayaṃ, āvuso, tumhākaṃ bhāgaṃ dassāma. Kissa tumhe na okkamitthā”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āgamentānaṃ akāmā bhāgaṃ dātunti.

Now at that time, many monks were traveling on a long road in the country of Kosala. Some monks entered a charnel ground for the sake of rag-robes, while some monks waited. Those monks who entered the charnel ground for the sake of rag-robes obtained rag-robes. Those monks who waited said thus: “Venerable sirs, give us a share too.” Those monks said thus: “Venerable sirs, we will not give you a share. Why did you not enter?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: “Monks, I allow that a share be given to those who waited, even if the givers are unwilling.”

Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū kosalesu janapade addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Ekacce bhikkhū paṭhamaṃ susānaṃ okkamiṃsu paṃsukūlāya, ekacce bhikkhū pacchā okkamiṃsu. Ye te bhikkhū paṭhamaṃ susānaṃ okkamiṃsu paṃsukūlāya te paṃsukūlāni labhiṃsu. Ye te bhikkhū [M 0.0395] pacchā okkamiṃsu te na labhiṃsu. Te evamāhaṃsu – “amhākampi, āvuso[T 2.0195], bhāgaṃ dethā”ti. Te evamāhaṃsu – “na mayaṃ, āvuso, tumhākaṃ bhāgaṃ dassāma. Kissa tumhe pacchā okkamitthā”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pacchā okkantānaṃ nākāmā bhāgaṃ dātunti.

At that time, many monks were traveling on a long journey in the country of Kosala. Some monks entered a charnel ground first for the sake of rag-robes; some monks entered later. Those monks who entered the charnel ground first for the sake of rag-robes obtained rag-robes. Those monks who entered later did not obtain any. They said thus: “Venerable sirs, give us a share too.” The others said thus: “Venerable sirs, we will not give you a share. Why did you enter later?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: “Monks, I allow that a share not be given to those who entered later, if the givers are unwilling.”

Tena [V 0.0372] kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū kosalesu janapade addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Te sadisā susānaṃ okkamiṃsu paṃsukūlāya. Ekacce bhikkhū paṃsukūlāni labhiṃsu, ekacce bhikkhū na labhiṃsu[P 1.0283]. Ye te bhikkhū na labhiṃsu, te evamāhaṃsu – “amhākampi, āvuso, bhāgaṃ dethā”ti. Te evamāhaṃsu – “na mayaṃ, āvuso, tumhākaṃ bhāgaṃ dassāma. Kissa tumhe na labhitthā”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sadisānaṃ okkantānaṃ akāmā bhāgaṃ dātunti.

At that time, many monks were traveling on a long journey in the country of Kosala. They entered a charnel ground together for the sake of rag-robes. Some monks obtained rag-robes; some monks did not obtain any. Those monks who did not obtain any said thus: “Venerable sirs, give us a share too.” The others said thus: “Venerable sirs, we will not give you a share. Why did you not obtain any?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: “Monks, I allow that a share be given to those who entered together, even if the givers are unwilling.”

Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū kosalesu janapade addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Te katikaṃ katvā susānaṃ okkamiṃsu paṃsukūlāya. Ekacce bhikkhū paṃsukūlāni labhiṃsu, ekacce bhikkhū na labhiṃsu. Ye te bhikkhū na labhiṃsu te evamāhaṃsu – “amhākampi, āvuso, bhāgaṃ dethā”ti. Te evamāhaṃsu – “na mayaṃ, āvuso, tumhākaṃ bhāgaṃ dassāma. Kissa tumhe na labhitthā”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, katikaṃ katvā okkantānaṃ akāmā bhāgaṃ dātunti.

At that time, many monks were traveling on a long journey in the country of Kosala. Having made an agreement, they entered a charnel ground for the sake of rag-robes. Some monks obtained rag-robes; some monks did not obtain any. Those monks who did not obtain any said thus: “Venerable sirs, give us a share too.” The others said thus: “Venerable sirs, we will not give you a share. Why did you not obtain any?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. He said: “Monks, I allow that a share be given to those who entered after making an agreement, even if the givers are unwilling.”

Paṃsukūlapariyesanakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of Seeking Rag-robes is concluded.

213. Cīvarapaṭiggāhakasammutikathā

213. The Account of the Appointment of a Robe-Receiver

342. Tena kho pana samayena manussā cīvaraṃ ādāya ārāmaṃ āgacchanti. Te paṭiggāhakaṃ alabhamānā paṭiharanti. Cīvaraṃ parittaṃ [T 2.0196] uppajjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvarapaṭiggāhakaṃ sammannituṃ – yo na chandāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na dosāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na mohāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na bhayāgatiṃ gaccheyya, gahitāgahitañca jāneyya. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbo. Paṭhamaṃ bhikkhu yācitabbo; yācitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

342. Now at that time, people came to the monastery bringing robes. Not finding a receiver, they took them back. Robes arose only in small quantity. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow you to appoint a monk endowed with five qualities as a robe-receiver: one who would not follow a wrong course through desire, would not follow a wrong course through hatred, would not follow a wrong course through delusion, would not follow a wrong course through fear, and who would know what has been received and what has not been received. And, monks, he is to be appointed thus. First, a monk should be requested; having requested, the Sangha should be informed by a competent and able monk:'

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvarapaṭiggāhakaṃ sammanneyya. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it is ready for the Sangha, let the Sangha appoint the monk named so-and-so as the robe-receiver. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu [M 0.0396] me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvarapaṭiggāhakaṃ sammannati. Yassāyasmato [V 0.0373] khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno cīvarapaṭiggāhakassa sammuti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. The Sangha appoints the monk named so-and-so as the robe-receiver. If the appointment of the monk named so-and-so as the robe-receiver is agreeable to the venerable ones, let them remain silent; if it is not agreeable, let them speak.”

“Sammato saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu cīvarapaṭiggāhako. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“The monk named so-and-so has been appointed as the robe-receiver by the Sangha. It is approved by the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold it.”

Tena kho pana samayena cīvarapaṭiggāhakā bhikkhū cīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā tattheva ujjhitvā pakkamanti. Cīvaraṃ nassati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave[P 1.0284], pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvaranidahakaṃ sammannituṃ – yo na chandāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na dosāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na mohāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na bhayāgatiṃ gaccheyya, nihitānihitañca jāneyya. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbo. Paṭhamaṃ bhikkhu yācitabbo; yācitvā byattena [T 2.0197] bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

Now at that time, the monks who were robe-receivers, having received robes, would abandon them right there and depart. The robes were lost. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow you to appoint a monk endowed with five qualities as a robe-depositor: one who would not follow a wrong course through desire, would not follow a wrong course through hatred, would not follow a wrong course through delusion, would not follow a wrong course through fear, and who would know what has been deposited and what has not been deposited. And, monks, he is to be appointed thus. First, a monk should be requested; having requested, the Sangha should be informed by a competent and able monk:'

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvaranidahakaṃ sammanneyya. Esā ñatti. “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvaranidahakaṃ sammannati. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno cīvaranidahakassa sammuti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should appoint the monk named so-and-so as a robe-storer. This is the motion. Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. The Sangha appoints the monk named so-and-so as a robe-storer. To whichever venerable one the appointment of the monk named so-and-so as a robe-storer is agreeable, he should remain silent; to whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Sammato saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu cīvaranidahako. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The monk named so-and-so has been appointed as a robe-storer by the Sangha. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I record it.

Cīvarapaṭiggāhakasammutikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Appointment of a Robe Receiver is concluded.

214. Bhaṇḍāgārasammutiādikathā

The Account of the Designation of a Storehouse and So Forth.

343. Tena kho pana samayena cīvaranidahako bhikkhu maṇḍapepi rukkhamūlepi nibbakosepi cīvaraṃ nidahati, undūrehipi upacikāhipi khajjanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhaṇḍāgāraṃ sammannituṃ, yaṃ saṅgho ākaṅkhati vihāraṃ vā aḍḍhayogaṃ vā pāsādaṃ vā hammiyaṃ vā guhaṃ vā. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbo. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

214. Now at that time, the robe-storing monk would store robes in a pavilion, at the foot of a tree, or under the eaves, and they were eaten by rats and termites. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. 'Monks, I allow you to designate as a storehouse whatever the Sangha desires: a dwelling, a lean-to, a long building, a gabled mansion, or a cave. And, monks, it should be designated thus. The Sangha is to be informed by a competent and capable monk:'

“Suṇātu [V 0.0374] me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ vihāraṃ bhaṇḍāgāraṃ sammanneyya. Esā ñatti.

343. Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should designate the dwelling named so-and-so as a storehouse. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ vihāraṃ bhaṇḍāgāraṃ sammannati. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa vihārassa bhaṇḍāgārassa sammuti, so tuṇhassa; yassa [M 0.0397] nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. The Sangha designates the dwelling named so-and-so as a storehouse. To whichever venerable one the designation of the dwelling named so-and-so as a storehouse is agreeable, he should remain silent; to whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Sammato saṅghena itthannāmo vihāro bhaṇḍāgāraṃ. Khamati saṅghassa[T 2.0198], tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The dwelling named so-and-so has been designated as a storehouse by the Sangha. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I record it.

Tena kho pana samayena saṅghassa bhaṇḍāgāre cīvaraṃ aguttaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ bhaṇḍāgārikaṃ sammannituṃ – yo na chandāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na dosāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na mohāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na bhayāgatiṃ gaccheyya, guttāguttañca jāneyya. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbo. Paṭhamaṃ bhikkhu yācitabbo; yācitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

At that time, a robe in the Sangha’s storehouse was unguarded. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow you to appoint as storekeeper a monk endowed with five factors: one who would not be led astray by desire, would not be led astray by hatred, would not be led astray by delusion, would not be led astray by fear, and who would know what is guarded and unguarded. And, monks, he should be appointed in this way. First, a monk should be requested. Having made the request, the Sangha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:'

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ bhaṇḍāgārikaṃ sammanneyya. Esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should appoint the monk named so-and-so as storekeeper. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ bhaṇḍāgārikaṃ sammannati. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno bhaṇḍāgārikassa sammuti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. The Sangha appoints the monk named so-and-so as storekeeper. To whichever venerable one the appointment of the monk named so-and-so as storekeeper is agreeable, he should remain silent; to whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Sammato saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu bhaṇḍāgāriko. Khamati [P 1.0285] saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The monk named so-and-so has been appointed by the Sangha as storekeeper. It is agreeable to the Sangha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I record it.

Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhaṇḍāgārikaṃ vuṭṭhāpenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, bhaṇḍāgāriko vuṭṭhāpetabbo. Yo vuṭṭhāpeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, the group-of-six monks were removing the storekeeper. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, a storekeeper should not be removed. Whoever should remove one, commits an offense of wrong-doing.'

Tena [V 0.0375] kho pana samayena saṅghassa bhaṇḍāgāre cīvaraṃ ussannaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave[T 2.0199], sammukhībhūtena saṅghena bhājetunti.

At that time, robes were abundant in the Sangha’s storehouse. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow for them to be distributed by the Sangha when it is assembled.'

Tena kho pana samayena saṅgho cīvaraṃ bhājento kolāhalaṃ akāsi. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvarabhājakaṃ sammannituṃ – yo na chandāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na dosāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na mohāgatiṃ gaccheyya, na bhayāgatiṃ gaccheyya, bhājitābhājitañca jāneyya. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbo. Paṭhamaṃ bhikkhu yācitabbo; yācitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

At that time, the Sangha made a commotion while distributing robes. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow you to appoint as a distributor of robes a monk endowed with five qualities: one who would not be led astray by desire, would not be led astray by hatred, would not be led astray by delusion, would not be led astray by fear, and who knows what has been distributed and what has not. And, monks, he should be appointed thus. First, the monk should be requested; having made the request, the Sangha should be informed by a competent and capable monk:'

“Suṇātu [M 0.0398] me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvarabhājakaṃ sammanneyya. Esā ñatti.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. If it is the proper time for the Sangha, the Sangha should appoint the monk named so-and-so as a distributor of robes. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvarabhājakaṃ sammannati. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmassa bhikkhuno cīvarabhājakassa sammuti, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

Venerable sirs, may the Sangha hear me. The Sangha appoints the monk named so-and-so as a distributor of robes. To whichever venerable one the appointment of the monk named so-and-so as a distributor of robes is agreeable, he should remain silent; to whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.

“Sammato saṅghena itthannāmo bhikkhu cīvarabhājako. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

The monk named so-and-so has been appointed by the Sangha as a distributor of robes. It is agreeable to the Sangha; therefore, it is silent. Thus do I record it.

Atha kho cīvarabhājakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kathaṃ nu kho cīvaraṃ bhājetabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṃ uccinitvā tulayitvā vaṇṇāvaṇṇaṃ katvā bhikkhū gaṇetvā vaggaṃ bandhitvā cīvarapaṭivīsaṃ ṭhapetunti.

Then this thought occurred to the robe-distributing monks: 'How, indeed, should robes be distributed?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow you first to sort the robes, appraise their value, and make them of equal worth. Then, having counted the monks and formed them into groups, you may set aside the robe-shares.'

Atha kho cīvarabhājakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kathaṃ nu kho sāmaṇerānaṃ cīvarapaṭivīso dātabbo”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sāmaṇerānaṃ upaḍḍhapaṭivīsaṃ [T 2.0200] dātunti.

Then this thought occurred to the robe-distributing monks: 'How, indeed, should a robe-share be given to the novices?' They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow you to give the novices a half-share.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu sakena bhāgena uttaritukāmo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uttarantassa sakaṃ bhāgaṃ dātunti.

At that time, a certain monk wished to go on a journey with his own share. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow you to give his own share to one who is going on a journey.'

Tena [V 0.0376] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu atirekabhāgena uttaritukāmo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, anukkhepe dinne atirekabhāgaṃ dātunti.

At that time, a certain monk wished to travel with an extra share. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow an extra share to be given when an extra meal has been given.”

Atha kho cīvarabhājakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kathaṃ nu kho cīvarapaṭivīso dātabbo, āgatapaṭipāṭiyā āgatāgatapaṭipāṭiyā (ka.) nu kho udāhu yathāvuḍḍha”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vikalake tosetvā kusapātaṃ kātunti.

Then this thought occurred to the monks who were robe-distributors: “How, indeed, should the share of robes be given? Should it be according to the order of arrival, or according to seniority?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow you, having satisfied the monks who are deficient in robes, to cast lots.”

Bhaṇḍāgārasammutiādikathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on the designation of a storehouse and so forth is concluded.

215. Cīvararajanakathā

215. The Discourse on Dyeing Robes

344. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū chakaṇenapi paṇḍumattikāyapi [P 1.0286] cīvaraṃ rajanti. Cīvaraṃ dubbaṇṇaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi[M 0.0399], bhikkhave, cha rajanāni – mūlarajanaṃ, khandharajanaṃ, tacarajanaṃ, pattarajanaṃ, puppharajanaṃ, phalarajananti.

344. At that time, monks were dyeing robes with cow dung and with reddish clay. The robes were of poor color. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow six kinds of dye: root dye, stem dye, bark dye, leaf dye, flower dye, and fruit dye.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū sītudakāya sītundikāya (sī.), sītūdakāya (syā.) cīvaraṃ rajanti. Cīvaraṃ duggandhaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, rajanaṃ pacituṃ cullaṃ rajanakumbhinti. Rajanaṃ uttariyati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uttarāḷumpaṃ uttarāḷupaṃ (yojanā), uttarāḷupaṃ (syā.) bandhitunti.

At that time, monks were dyeing robes with cold water. The robes had a bad smell. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a small dye-pot to cook the dye.” The dye boiled over. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a rim to be attached.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū na jānanti rajanaṃ pakkaṃ vā apakkaṃ vā. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udake vā nakhapiṭṭhikāya vā thevakaṃ [T 2.0201] dātunti.

At that time, monks did not know whether the dye was cooked or uncooked. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a drop of dye to be placed in water or on the back of a fingernail.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū rajanaṃ oropentā kumbhiṃ āviñchanti āviñjanti (sī.), āvaṭṭanti (syā.). Kumbhī bhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, rajanuḷuṅkaṃ rajanāḷuṅkaṃ (yojanā) daṇḍakathālakanti.

At that time, while taking out the dye, monks tilted the pot. The pot broke. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a dye ladle and a small bowl with a handle.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhūnaṃ rajanabhājanaṃ na saṃvijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, rajanakolambaṃ rajanaghaṭanti.

At that time, the monks did not have a dye container. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a dye-trough and a dye-jar.”

Tena [V 0.0377] kho pana samayena bhikkhū pātiyāpi pattepi cīvaraṃ omaddanti. Cīvaraṃ paribhijjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, rajanadoṇikanti.

At that time, monks were kneading a robe in a bowl and also in an alms-bowl. The robe tore. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a dyeing trough.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū chamāya cīvaraṃ pattharanti. Cīvaraṃ paṃsukitaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tiṇasanthārakanti.

At that time, monks were spreading a robe on the ground. The robe became soiled with dust. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a grass mat.”

Tiṇasanthārako upacikāhi khajjati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cīvaravaṃsaṃ cīvararajjunti.

The grass mat was eaten by termites. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a robe-bamboo and a robe-rope.”

Majjhena laggenti. Rajanaṃ ubhato galati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kaṇṇe bandhitunti.

They hung it by the middle. The dye dripped from both sides. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow it to be tied at the corners.”

Kaṇṇo [M 0.0400] jīrati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kaṇṇasuttakanti.

The corner wore out. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow a corner-loop.”

Rajanaṃ ekato galati. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, samparivattakaṃ samparivattakaṃ rajetuṃ, na ca acchinne theve pakkamitunti.

The dye dripped down from one side. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow you to dye by turning it around repeatedly, and not to go away before the dripping has ceased.”

Tena kho pana samayena cīvaraṃ patthinnaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, udake osāretunti.

At that time, a robe had become stiff. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow it to be immersed in water.”

Tena kho pana samayena cīvaraṃ pharusaṃ hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi[T 2.0202], bhikkhave, pāṇinā ākoṭetunti[P 1.0287].

At that time, a robe was rough. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow it to be beaten with the hand.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū acchinnakāni cīvarāni dhārenti dantakāsāvāni. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – seyyathāpi nāma seyyathāpi (?) gihī kāmabhoginoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, acchinnakāni cīvarāni dhāretabbāni. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

At that time, monks were wearing uncut, ivory-colored robes. People complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying, “Just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, uncut robes are not to be worn. Whoever should wear one commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Cīvararajanakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on dyeing robes is concluded.

216. Chinnakacīvarānujānanā

216. The Allowance for Cut Robes

345. Atha [V 0.0378] kho bhagavā rājagahe yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena dakkhiṇāgiri tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Addasā kho bhagavā magadhakhettaṃ acchibaddhaṃ accibaddhaṃ (sī. syā.), acchibandhaṃ (ka.) pāḷibaddhaṃ mariyādabaddhaṃ siṅghāṭakabaddhaṃ, disvāna āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “passasi no tvaṃ, ānanda, magadhakhettaṃ acchibaddhaṃ pāḷibaddhaṃ mariyādabaddhaṃ siṅghāṭakabaddha”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”ti. “Ussahasi tvaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhūnaṃ evarūpāni cīvarāni saṃvidahitu”nti? “Ussahāmi, bhagavā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā dakkhiṇāgirismiṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā punadeva rājagahaṃ paccāgañchi. Atha kho āyasmā ānando sambahulānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cīvarāni saṃvidahitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “passatu me passatha tumhe (ka.), bhante, bhagavā cīvarāni saṃvidahitānī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe [T 2.0203] dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “paṇḍito, bhikkhave, ānando; mahāpañño, bhikkhave, ānando; yatra hi nāma mayā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānissati, kusimpi nāma karissati, aḍḍhakusimpi nāma karissati, maṇḍalampi nāma karissati[M 0.0401], aḍḍhamaṇḍalampi nāma karissati, vivaṭṭampi nāma karissati, anuvivaṭṭampi nāma karissati, gīveyyakampi nāma karissati, jaṅgheyyakampi nāma karissati, bāhantampi nāma karissati, chinnakaṃ bhavissati, satthalūkhaṃ samaṇasāruppaṃ paccatthikānañca anabhicchitaṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, chinnakaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ chinnakaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ chinnakaṃ antaravāsaka”nti.

345. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Rājagaha as long as he pleased, set out on a journey toward Dakkhiṇāgiri. The Blessed One saw the Magadhan fields, laid out in squares, laid out in rows, divided by partitions, and laid out like a crossroads. Seeing this, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda: 'Do you see, Ānanda, the Magadhan fields, laid out in squares, laid out in rows, divided by partitions, and laid out like a crossroads?' 'Yes, venerable sir.' 'Are you able, Ānanda, to prepare robes of such a pattern for the monks?' 'I am able, Blessed One.' Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Dakkhiṇāgiri as long as he pleased, returned again to Rājagaha. Then the Venerable Ānanda, having prepared robes for many monks, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he said this to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One, venerable sir, look at the robes I have prepared.' Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: 'Monks, Ānanda is wise; monks, Ānanda has great wisdom. For Ānanda is one who understands in detail the meaning of what was spoken in brief by me. He will make the long strips, the short strips, the large panels, the half-panels, the central dividing strip, the flanking strips, the neck-piece, the shin-piece, and the arm-piece. It will be cut, made coarse by the knife, suitable for recluses, and undesirable to enemies. I allow, monks, a cut saṅghāṭi, a cut uttarāsaṅga, and a cut antaravāsaka.'

Chinnakacīvarānujānanā niṭṭhitā.

The Allowance Regarding Cut Robes is concluded.

217. Ticīvarānujānanā

The Allowance of the Three Robes

346. Atha kho bhagavā rājagahe yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena vesālī tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Addasa kho bhagavā antarā ca rājagahaṃ antarā ca vesāliṃ addhānamaggappaṭipanno sambahule bhikkhū cīvarehi ubbhaṇḍite ubbhaṇḍīkate (syā.) sīsepi cīvarabhisiṃ karitvā khandhepi cīvarabhisiṃ karitvā kaṭiyāpi cīvarabhisiṃ karitvā āgacchante, disvāna bhagavato etadahosi – “atilahuṃ kho ime moghapurisā cīvare bāhullāya āvattā[P 1.0288]. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cīvare sīmaṃ bandheyyaṃ, mariyādaṃ ṭhapeyya”nti. Atha kho bhagavā anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena vesālī tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati gotamake cetiye. Tena kho pana samayena [V 0.0379] bhagavā sītāsu hemantikāsu rattīsu antaraṭṭhakāsu himapātasamaye rattiṃ ajjhokāse ekacīvaro nisīdi. Na bhagavantaṃ [T 2.0204] sītaṃ ahosi. Nikkhante paṭhame yāme sītaṃ bhagavantaṃ ahosi. Dutiyaṃ bhagavā cīvaraṃ pārupi. Na bhagavantaṃ sītaṃ ahosi. Nikkhante majjhime yāme sītaṃ bhagavantaṃ ahosi. Tatiyaṃ bhagavā cīvaraṃ pārupi. Na bhagavantaṃ sītaṃ ahosi. Nikkhante pacchime yāme uddhaste aruṇe nandimukhiyā rattiyā sītaṃ bhagavantaṃ ahosi. Catutthaṃ bhagavā cīvaraṃ pārupi. Na bhagavantaṃ sītaṃ ahosi. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “yepi kho te kulaputtā imasmiṃ dhammavinaye sītālukā sītabhīrukā tepi sakkonti ticīvarena yāpetuṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cīvare sīmaṃ bandheyyaṃ, mariyādaṃ ṭhapeyyaṃ, ticīvaraṃ anujāneyya”nti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “idhāhaṃ, bhikkhave, antarā ca rājagahaṃ antarā ca vesāliṃ addhānamaggappaṭipanno addasaṃ sambahule bhikkhū [M 0.0402] cīvarehi ubbhaṇḍite sīsepi cīvarabhisiṃ karitvā khandhepi cīvarabhisiṃ karitvā kaṭiyāpi cīvarabhisiṃ karitvā āgacchante, disvāna me etadahosi – ‘atilahuṃ kho ime moghapurisā cīvare bāhullāya āvattā. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cīvare sīmaṃ bandheyyaṃ, mariyādaṃ ṭhapeyya’nti. Idhāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sītāsu hemantikāsu rattīsu antaraṭṭhakāsu himapātasamaye rattiṃ ajjhokāse ekacīvaro nisīdiṃ. Na maṃ sītaṃ ahosi. Nikkhante paṭhame yāme sītaṃ maṃ ahosi. Dutiyāhaṃ cīvaraṃ pārupiṃ. Na maṃ sītaṃ [T 2.0205] ahosi. Nikkhante majjhime yāme sītaṃ maṃ ahosi. Tatiyāhaṃ cīvaraṃ pārupiṃ. Na maṃ sītaṃ ahosi. Nikkhante pacchime yāme uddhaste aruṇe nandimukhiyā rattiyā sītaṃ maṃ ahosi. Catutthāhaṃ cīvaraṃ pārupiṃ. Na maṃ sītaṃ ahosi. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi – “yepi kho te kulaputtā imasmiṃ dhammavinaye sītālukā sītabhīrukā tepi sakkonti ticīvarena yāpetuṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cīvare sīmaṃ bandheyyaṃ, mariyādaṃ ṭhapeyyaṃ[P 1.0289], ticīvaraṃ anujāneyya’nti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ticīvaraṃ – diguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ, ekacciyaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ, ekacciyaṃ antaravāsaka”nti.

217. Then the Blessed One, having dwelt at Rājagaha as he pleased, set out on a journey toward Vesālī. While journeying on the long road between Rājagaha and Vesālī, the Blessed One saw many monks coming, laden with robes, having made cushion-like piles of robes on their heads, on their backs, and on their waists. Having seen this, this thought occurred to the Blessed One: “How very quickly these worthless men have reverted to an abundance of robes. What if I were to set a limit for the monks regarding robes, and establish a boundary?” Then the Blessed One, journeying in due course, arrived at Vesālī. There, the Blessed One dwelt at the Gotamaka shrine in Vesālī. Now at that time, during the cold winter nights, in the eight-day intervals of the cold season, at a time of snowfall, the Blessed One sat at night in the open with a single robe. The Blessed One did not feel cold. When the first watch had passed, the Blessed One felt cold. The Blessed One put on a second robe. The Blessed One did not feel cold. When the middle watch had passed, the Blessed One felt cold. The Blessed One put on a third robe. The Blessed One did not feel cold. When the last watch had passed and the pleasing-faced dawn arose, the Blessed One felt cold. The Blessed One put on a fourth robe. The Blessed One did not feel cold. Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: “Even those sons of good family in this Dhamma and Vinaya who are susceptible to cold and fearful of cold are able to maintain themselves with three robes. What if I were to set a limit for the monks regarding robes, establish a boundary, and permit the three robes?” Then the Blessed One, on this cause, on this matter, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “Here, monks, while journeying on the long road between Rājagaha and Vesālī, I saw many monks coming, laden with robes, having made cushion-like piles of robes on their heads, on their backs, and on their waists. Having seen this, this thought occurred to me: ‘How very quickly these worthless men have reverted to an abundance of robes. What if I were to set a limit for the monks regarding robes, and establish a boundary?’ Here, monks, during the cold winter nights, in the eight-day intervals of the cold season, at a time of snowfall, I sat at night in the open with a single robe. I did not feel cold. When the first watch had passed, I felt cold. I put on a second robe. I did not feel cold. When the middle watch had passed, I felt cold. I put on a third robe. I did not feel cold. When the last watch had passed and the pleasing-faced dawn arose, I felt cold. I put on a fourth robe. I did not feel cold. To me then, monks, this thought occurred: ‘Even those sons of good family in this Dhamma and Vinaya who are susceptible to cold and fearful of cold are able to maintain themselves with three robes. What if I were to set a limit for the monks regarding robes, establish a boundary, and permit the three robes?’ I permit, monks, the three robes: a double-layered outer cloak, a single-layered upper robe, and a single-layered lower garment.”

Ticīvarānujānanā niṭṭhitā.

The allowance concerning the three robes is concluded.

218. Atirekacīvarakathā

218. The Discourse on Extra Robes

347. pārā. 461 Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhagavatā ticīvaraṃ anuññātanti aññeneva ticīvarena gāmaṃ pavisanti, aññena ticīvarena ārāme acchanti, aññena ticīvarena [V 0.0380] nahānaṃ otaranti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū atirekacīvaraṃ dhāressantī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, atirekacīvaraṃ dhāretabbaṃ. Yo dhāreyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.

347. At that time, the group-of-six monks, thinking, “The Blessed One has allowed the three robes,” entered the village with one set of three robes, stayed in the monastery with another, and went down to the bathing place with another. Those monks who were of few wishes criticized, scorned, and found fault, saying: “How indeed can the group-of-six monks wear an extra robe?” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a discourse on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “Monks, an extra robe is not to be worn. Whoever should wear one is to be dealt with according to the Dhamma.”

pārā. 461 Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato ānandassa atirekacīvaraṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Āyasmā ca ānando taṃ cīvaraṃ āyasmato sāriputtassa dātukāmo hoti. Āyasmā ca [T 2.0206] sāriputto sākete viharati. Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – “bhagavatā sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ ‘na atirekacīvaraṃ dhāretabba’nti. Idañca me atirekacīvaraṃ uppannaṃ[M 0.0403]. Ahañcimaṃ cīvaraṃ āyasmato sāriputtassa dātukāmo. Āyasmā ca sāriputto sākete viharati. Kathaṃ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. “Kīvaciraṃ panānanda, sāriputto āgacchissatī”ti? “Navamaṃ vā, bhagavā, divasaṃ, dasamaṃ vā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dasāhaparamaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ dhāretu”nti.

At that time, an extra robe had arisen for the Venerable Ānanda. And the Venerable Ānanda wished to give that robe to the Venerable Sāriputta. And the Venerable Sāriputta was dwelling in Sāketa. Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Ānanda: “A training rule has been laid down by the Blessed One: ‘An extra robe is not to be worn.’ And this extra robe has arisen for me. I wish to give this robe to the Venerable Sāriputta, and the Venerable Sāriputta is dwelling in Sāketa. How now should I act?” He reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Ānanda, in how long will Sāriputta come?” “Blessed One, on the ninth day or on the tenth day.” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a discourse on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow an extra robe to be worn for at most ten days.”

Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhūnaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kathaṃ nu kho amhehi atirekacīvare paṭipajjitabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, atirekacīvaraṃ vikappetunti.

At that time, an extra robe had arisen for the monks. Then this thought occurred to the monks: “How indeed should we act in regard to the extra robe?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow an extra robe to be placed under shared ownership.”

348. Atha kho bhagavā vesāliyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena bārāṇasī tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena bārāṇasī tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ viharati isipatane migadāye. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno antaravāsako chiddo hoti. Atha kho tassa bhikkhuno etadahosi – “bhagavatā ticīvaraṃ anuññātaṃ – diguṇā saṅghāṭi, ekacciyo uttarāsaṅgo[P 1.0290][T 2.0207], ekacciyo antaravāsako. Ayañca me antaravāsako chiddo. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ aggaḷaṃ acchupeyyaṃ, samantato dupaṭṭaṃ bhavissati, majjhe ekacciya”nti. Atha kho so bhikkhu aggaḷaṃ acchupesi. Addasā kho bhagavā senāsanacārikaṃ āhiṇḍanto taṃ bhikkhuṃ aggaḷaṃ acchupentaṃ acchupantaṃ (ka.), disvāna yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ tvaṃ, bhikkhu, karosī”ti? “Aggaḷaṃ, bhagavā, acchupemī”ti. “Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhu; sādhu kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, aggaḷaṃ acchupesī”ti[V 0.0381]. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ahatānaṃ dussānaṃ ahatakappānaṃ diguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ, ekacciyaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ, ekacciyaṃ antaravāsakaṃ; utuddhaṭānaṃ dussānaṃ catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ, diguṇaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ, diguṇaṃ [M 0.0404] antaravāsakaṃ; paṃsukūle yāvadatthaṃ; pāpaṇike ussāho karaṇīyo. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aggaḷaṃ tunnaṃ ovaṭṭikaṃ kaṇḍusakaṃ daḷhīkamma”nti.

348. Then the Blessed One, having stayed in Vesālī for as long as he wished, set out on a journey toward Bārāṇasī. Traveling in stages, he arrived at Bārāṇasī. There the Blessed One stayed in the deer park at Isipatana. Now at that time, a certain monk’s lower robe had a hole in it. Then this thought occurred to that monk: 'The Blessed One has allowed three robes: a double outer robe, a single upper robe, and a single lower robe. And this lower robe of mine has a hole in it. What if I were to apply a patch? It would be double-layered all around and single-layered in the middle.' So that monk applied a patch. The Blessed One, while touring the lodgings, saw that monk applying a patch. Having seen him, he went to that monk and, on arrival, said to him: 'What are you doing, monk?' 'I am applying a patch, Blessed One.' 'Good, good, monk. It is good, monk, that you are applying a patch.' Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this connection, gave a discourse on the Dhamma and addressed the monks: 'Monks, for new cloth and for cloth that is like new, I allow a double outer robe, a single upper robe, and a single lower robe. For worn-out cloth, I allow a quadruple outer robe, a double upper robe, and a double lower robe. For a rag-robe, I allow as many layers as desired. Effort should be made to find cloth at a shop. Monks, I allow patching, darning, hemming, a kaṇḍusaka patch, and strengthening by patching over.'

Atirekacīvarakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on extra robes is concluded.

219. Visākhāvatthu

219. The Story of Visākhā

349. Atha kho bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena sāvatthi tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena sāvatthi tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho visākhā migāramātā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho visākhaṃ migāramātaraṃ bhagavā [T 2.0208] dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho visākhā migāramātā, bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā, bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho visākhā migāramātā bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

349. Then the Blessed One, having stayed in Bārāṇasī as long as he pleased, set out on a journey toward Sāvatthī. Traveling stage by stage, he arrived at Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Monastery. Then Visākhā Migāramātā approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. The Blessed One instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened Visākhā Migāramātā with a Dhamma talk. Then Visākhā Migāramātā, having been instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One’s Dhamma talk, said to him: "May the Blessed One, together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, accept my meal tomorrow." The Blessed One consented by silence. Then Visākhā Migāramātā, knowing the Blessed One’s consent, rose from her seat, paid homage to him, circumambulated him, and departed.

Tena kho pana samayena tassā rattiyā accayena cātuddīpiko mahāmegho pāvassi. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “yathā, bhikkhave, jetavane vassati evaṃ catūsu dīpesu vassati. Ovassāpetha, bhikkhave, kāyaṃ. Ayaṃ pacchimako cātuddīpiko mahāmegho”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā [P 1.0291] nikkhittacīvarā kāyaṃ ovassāpenti. Atha kho visākhā migāramātā paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā dāsiṃ āṇāpesi – “gaccha, je. Ārāmaṃ gantvā kālaṃ ārocehi – kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. “Evaṃ, ayye”ti kho sā dāsī visākhāya migāramātuyā paṭissuṇitvā ārāmaṃ gantvā addasa bhikkhū nikkhittacīvare kāyaṃ ovassāpente, disvāna ‘natthi ārāme bhikkhū, ājīvakā kāyaṃ ovassāpentī’ti yena visākhā migāramātā tenupasaṅkami[V 0.0382]; upasaṅkamitvā visākhaṃ migāramātaraṃ etadavoca – “natthayye, ārāme bhikkhū, ājīvakā kāyaṃ ovassāpentī”ti. Atha kho visākhāya migāramātuyā [T 2.0209] paṇḍitāya viyattāya medhāviniyā etadahosi – “nissaṃsayaṃ kho ayyā nikkhittacīvarā kāyaṃ ovassāpenti. Sāyaṃ [M 0.0405] bālā maññittha – natthi ārāme bhikkhū, ājīvakā kāyaṃ ovassāpentī”ti, puna dāsiṃ āṇāpesi – “gaccha, je. Ārāmaṃ gantvā kālaṃ ārocehi – kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho te bhikkhū gattāni sītiṃ karitvā sītīkaritvā (syā.) kallakāyā cīvarāni gahetvā yathāvihāraṃ pavisiṃsu. Atha kho sā dāsī ārāmaṃ gantvā bhikkhū apassantī ‘natthi ārāme bhikkhū, suñño ārāmo’ti yena visākhā migāramātā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā visākhaṃ migāramātaraṃ etadavoca – “natthayye, ārāme bhikkhū, suñño ārāmo”ti. Atha kho visākhāya migāramātuyā paṇḍitāya viyattāya medhāviniyā etadahosi – “nissaṃsayaṃ kho ayyā gattāni sītiṃ karitvā kallakāyā cīvarāni gahetvā yathāvihāraṃ paviṭṭhā. Sāyaṃ bālā maññittha – natthi ārāme bhikkhū, suñño ārāmo”ti, puna dāsiṃ āṇāpesi – “gaccha, je. Ārāmaṃ gantvā kālaṃ ārocehi – kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti.

At that time, with the passing of the night, a great cloud raining over the four continents poured down. Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, just as it is raining in Jetavana, so it is raining over the four continents. Drench your bodies, bhikkhus. This is the last great cloud raining over the four continents.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One, and laying aside their robes, they drenched their bodies. Then Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, having prepared choice hard and soft food, instructed a servant girl: “Go, dear. Go to the monastery and announce the time: ‘Venerable sir, it is time, the meal is ready.’” “Yes, madam,” that servant girl replied to Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, and went to the monastery. There she saw the bhikkhus drenching their bodies with their robes laid aside. Seeing this, she thought, “There are no bhikkhus in the monastery; the Ājīvakas are drenching their bodies,” and she went to where Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, was. Having approached, she said to Visākhā, Migāra’s mother: “Madam, there are no bhikkhus in the monastery; the Ājīvakas are drenching their bodies.” Then this thought occurred to Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, who was wise, discerning, and intelligent: “Without a doubt, the venerable ones have laid aside their robes and are drenching their bodies. This foolish girl thought, ‘There are no bhikkhus in the monastery; the Ājīvakas are drenching their bodies.’” She instructed the servant girl again: “Go, dear. Go to the monastery and announce the time: ‘Venerable sir, it is time, the meal is ready.’” Then those bhikkhus, having cooled their limbs and with refreshed bodies, took up their robes and entered their respective dwellings. Then that servant girl went to the monastery and, not seeing the bhikkhus, thought, “There are no bhikkhus in the monastery; the monastery is empty,” and she went to where Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, was. Having approached, she said to Visākhā, Migāra’s mother: “Madam, there are no bhikkhus in the monastery; the monastery is empty.” Then this thought occurred to Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, who was wise, discerning, and intelligent: “Without a doubt, the venerable ones have cooled their limbs, have refreshed bodies, have taken up their robes, and have entered their respective dwellings. This foolish girl thought, ‘There are no bhikkhus in the monastery; the monastery is empty.’” She instructed the servant girl again: “Go, dear. Go to the monastery and announce the time: ‘Venerable sir, it is time, the meal is ready.’”

350. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “sandahatha sannahatha (sī. syā.), bhikkhave, pattacīvaraṃ; kālo bhattassā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso sammiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva – jetavane antarahito visākhāya migāramātuyā koṭṭhake [T 2.0210] pāturahosi. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Atha kho visākhā migāramātā – “acchariyaṃ vata bho! Abbhutaṃ vata bho! Tathāgatassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā, yatra hi nāma jaṇṇukamattesupi oghesu pavattamānesu, kaṭimattesupi oghesu pavattamānesu, na hi nāma [P 1.0292] ekabhikkhussapi pavattamānesu na ekabhikkhussapi (?) pādā vā cīvarāni vā allāni bhavissantī”ti – haṭṭhā udaggā buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappetvā sampavāretvā bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho visākhā migāramātā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “aṭṭhāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ varāni yācāmī”ti. “Atikkantavarā kho, visākhe, tathāgatā”ti. “Yāni ca, bhante, kappiyāni [M 0.0406] yāni ca anavajjānī”ti. “Vadehi, visākhe”ti. “Icchāmahaṃ, bhante, saṅghassa yāvajīvaṃ vassikasāṭikaṃ dātuṃ, āgantukabhattaṃ dātuṃ, gamikabhattaṃ dātuṃ, gilānabhattaṃ dātuṃ, gilānupaṭṭhākabhattaṃ dātuṃ, gilānabhesajjaṃ dātuṃ, dhuvayāguṃ dātuṃ, bhikkhunisaṅghassa [V 0.0383] udakasāṭikaṃ dātu”nti. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, visākhe, atthavasaṃ sampassamānā tathāgataṃ aṭṭha varāni yācasī”ti?

350. Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Prepare your bowls and robes, bhikkhus; it is time for the meal.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.
