Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe—just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm—so did he vanish from the Jeta Grove and reappear in the gateway of Visākhā Migāramātā. The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. Then Visākhā Migāramātā exclaimed: “How wonderful, sirs! How astonishing, sirs! Such is the great psychic power and great majesty of the Tathāgata, that even while floods were flowing knee-deep and waist-deep, not even a single bhikkhu’s feet or robes became wet!”—joyful and elated, with her own hands she served and satisfied the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha with excellent hard and soft food. When the Blessed One had finished his meal and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, she sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, Visākhā Migāramātā said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I ask the Blessed One for eight boons.” “Tathāgatas, Visākhā, are beyond granting boons.” “Venerable sir, they are allowable and blameless.” “Speak, Visākhā.” “I wish, venerable sir, for as long as I live to give the Saṅgha rains-cloths, to give food for incoming bhikkhus, to give food for travelling bhikkhus, to give food for the sick, to give food for those who attend the sick, to give medicine for the sick, to give constant gruel, and to give bathing cloths for the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs.” “But what benefit, Visākhā, do you foresee that you ask the Tathāgata for these eight boons?”

“Idhāhaṃ, bhante, dāsiṃ āṇāpesiṃ – ‘gaccha, je. Ārāmaṃ gantvā kālaṃ ārocehi – kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta’”nti. Atha kho sā, bhante, dāsī ārāmaṃ gantvā addasa bhikkhū nikkhittacīvare kāyaṃ ovassāpente, disvāna [T 2.0211] “natthi ārāme bhikkhū, ājīvakā kāyaṃ ovassāpentī”ti yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ etadavoca – “natthayye, ārāme bhikkhū, ājīvakā kāyaṃ ovassāpentī”ti. Asuci, bhante, naggiyaṃ jegucchaṃ paṭikūlaṃ. Imāhaṃ, bhante, atthavasaṃ sampassamānā icchāmi saṅghassa yāvajīvaṃ vassikasāṭikaṃ dātuṃ.

“Venerable Sir, just now I commanded a servant girl: ‘Go, girl. Go to the monastery and announce the time: “Venerable Sir, it is time; the meal is ready.”’ Then, Venerable Sir, that servant girl went to the monastery and saw bhikkhus with their robes put aside, letting the rain drench their bodies. Seeing this, she supposed, ‘There are no bhikkhus in the monastery; Ājīvakas are letting the rain drench their bodies,’ and she came to where I was. Having approached, she told me this: ‘Madam, there are no bhikkhus in the monastery; Ājīvakas are letting the rain drench their bodies.’ Venerable Sir, nakedness is unseemly, disgusting, and repulsive. Venerable Sir, seeing this benefit, I wish to give the Saṅgha rain-bathing cloths for as long as I live.”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhante, āgantuko bhikkhu na vīthikusalo na gocarakusalo kilanto piṇḍāya carati. So me āgantukabhattaṃ bhuñjitvā vīthikusalo gocarakusalo akilanto piṇḍāya carissati. Imāhaṃ, bhante, atthavasaṃ sampassamānā icchāmi saṅghassa yāvajīvaṃ āgantukabhattaṃ dātuṃ.

Furthermore, Venerable Sir, a visiting bhikkhu, not being skilled in the streets and not skilled in the alms-round, wanders for alms weary. Having eaten my food for visiting bhikkhus, he will become skilled in the streets and skilled in the alms-round, and will wander for alms without weariness. Venerable Sir, seeing this special benefit, I wish to offer food for visiting bhikkhus to the Saṅgha for as long as I live.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhante, gamiko bhikkhu attano bhattaṃ pariyesamāno satthā vā vihāyissati, yattha vā vāsaṃ gantukāmo bhavissati tattha vikāle upagacchissati, kilanto addhānaṃ gamissati. So me gamikabhattaṃ bhuñjitvā satthā na vihāyissati, yattha vāsaṃ gantukāmo bhavissati tattha kāle upagacchissati, akilanto addhānaṃ gamissati. Imāhaṃ, bhante, atthavasaṃ sampassamānā icchāmi saṅghassa yāvajīvaṃ gamikabhattaṃ dātuṃ.

Furthermore, Venerable Sir, a traveling bhikkhu, while searching for his own meal, might be left behind by his traveling companions, or he might arrive at the residence he wishes to go to at the wrong time; he will travel the long road weary. Having eaten my food for traveling bhikkhus, he will not be left behind by his traveling companions, he will arrive at the residence he wishes to go to at the proper time, and he will travel the long road without weariness. Venerable Sir, seeing this special benefit, I wish to offer food for traveling bhikkhus to the Saṅgha for as long as I live.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhante, gilānassa bhikkhuno sappāyāni bhojanāni alabhantassa ābādho vā abhivaḍḍhissati, kālaṃkiriyā vā bhavissati. Tassa me gilānabhattaṃ bhuttassa ābādho [P 1.0293] na abhivaḍḍhissati, kālaṃkiriyā na bhavissati. Imāhaṃ, bhante, atthavasaṃ sampassamānā icchāmi saṅghassa yāvajīvaṃ gilānabhattaṃ dātuṃ[T 2.0212]. “Puna [M 0.0407] caparaṃ, bhante, gilānupaṭṭhāko bhikkhu attano bhattaṃ pariyesamāno gilānassa ussūre bhattaṃ nīharissati, bhattacchedaṃ karissati. So me gilānupaṭṭhākabhattaṃ bhuñjitvā gilānassa [V 0.0384] kālena bhattaṃ nīharissati, bhattacchedaṃ na karissati. Imāhaṃ, bhante, atthavasaṃ sampassamānā icchāmi saṅghassa yāvajīvaṃ gilānupaṭṭhākabhattaṃ dātuṃ.

Furthermore, Venerable Sir, if a sick bhikkhu does not obtain suitable food, his illness will worsen, or he will die. If he eats my food for the sick, his illness will not worsen, and he will not die. Seeing this special benefit, Venerable Sir, I wish to give food for the sick to the Saṅgha for as long as I live. Furthermore, Venerable Sir, a bhikkhu attending the sick, while seeking his own meal, will bring food to the sick person late; he will cause an interruption of the meal. If he eats my food for those attending the sick, he will bring food to the sick person at the proper time; he will not cause an interruption of the meal. Seeing this special benefit, Venerable Sir, I wish to give food for those attending the sick to the Saṅgha for as long as I live.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhante, gilānassa bhikkhuno sappāyāni bhesajjāni alabhantassa ābādho vā abhivaḍḍhissati, kālaṃkiriyā vā bhavissati. Tassa me gilānabhesajjaṃ paribhuttassa ābādho na abhivaḍḍhissati, kālaṃkiriyā na bhavissati. Imāhaṃ, bhante, atthavasaṃ sampassamānā icchāmi saṅghassa yāvajīvaṃ gilānabhesajjaṃ dātuṃ.

Furthermore, Venerable Sir, if a sick bhikkhu does not obtain suitable medicines, his illness will worsen, or he will die. If he consumes my medicine for the sick, his illness will not worsen, and he will not die. Seeing this special benefit, Venerable Sir, I wish to give medicine for the sick to the Saṅgha for as long as I live.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā andhakavinde dasānisaṃse sampassamānena yāgu anuññātā. Tyāhaṃ, bhante, ānisaṃse sampassamānā icchāmi saṅghassa yāvajīvaṃ dhuvayāguṃ dātuṃ.

Furthermore, Venerable Sir, gruel was allowed in Andhakavinda by the Blessed One, who saw ten benefits. Seeing those benefits, Venerable Sir, I wish to give a constant supply of gruel to the Saṅgha for as long as I live.

“Idha, bhante, bhikkhuniyo aciravatiyā nadiyā vesiyāhi saddhiṃ naggā ekatitthe nahāyanti. Tā, bhante, vesiyā bhikkhuniyo uppaṇḍesuṃ – ‘kiṃ nu kho nāma tumhākaṃ, ayye, daharānaṃ daharānaṃ daharānaṃ (sī.) brahmacariyaṃ ciṇṇena, nanu nāma kāmā paribhuñjitabbā; yadā jiṇṇā bhavissatha tadā brahmacariyaṃ carissatha. Evaṃ tumhākaṃ ubho atthā pariggahitā bhavissantī’ti. Tā, bhante, bhikkhuniyo vesiyāhi uppaṇḍiyamānā maṅkū ahesuṃ. Asuci, bhante, mātugāmassa naggiyaṃ jegucchaṃ paṭikūlaṃ. Imāhaṃ, bhante, atthavasaṃ sampassamānā icchāmi bhikkhunisaṅghassa [T 2.0213] yāvajīvaṃ udakasāṭikaṃ dātu”nti.

Venerable Sir, here the bhikkhunīs bathe naked at a single ford in the river Aciravatī together with prostitutes. Venerable Sir, those prostitutes taunted the bhikkhunīs, saying: ‘Ladies, what benefit is there for you in practicing the holy life while you are still young? Surely, sensual pleasures are to be enjoyed. When you become old, then you will practice the holy life. In this way, both benefits will be secured by you.’ Venerable Sir, being taunted by the prostitutes, those bhikkhunīs became ashamed. Venerable Sir, the nakedness of a woman is impure, disgusting, and repulsive. Seeing this special benefit, Venerable Sir, I wish to give bathing cloths to the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs for as long as I live.

351. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, visākhe, ānisaṃsaṃ sampassamānā tathāgataṃ aṭṭha varāni yācasī”ti? “Idha, bhante, disāsu vassaṃvuṭṭhā bhikkhū sāvatthiṃ āgacchissanti bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Te bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pucchissanti – ‘itthannāmo, bhante, bhikkhu kālaṅkato, tassa kā gati ko abhisamparāyo’ti? Taṃ bhagavā byākarissati sotāpattiphale vā sakadāgāmiphale vā anāgāmiphale vā arahatte vā. Tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pucchissāmi – ‘āgatapubbā nu kho, bhante, tena ayyena sāvatthī’ti? Sace me [M 0.0408] vakkhanti – ‘āgatapubbā tena bhikkhunā sāvatthī’ti niṭṭhamettha [P 1.0294] gacchissāmi – nissaṃsayaṃ me paribhuttaṃ tena ayyena vassikasāṭikā vā āgantukabhattaṃ vā gamikabhattaṃ vā gilānabhattaṃ vā gilānupaṭṭhākabhattaṃ vā gilānabhesajjaṃ vā dhuvayāgu vāti. Tassā me tadanussarantiyā pāmujjaṃ jāyissati, pamuditāya pīti jāyissati, pītimanāya kāyo passambhissati, passaddhakāyā sukhaṃ [V 0.0385] vediyissāmi, sukhiniyā cittaṃ samādhiyissati. Sā me bhavissati indriyabhāvanā balabhāvanā bojjhaṅgabhāvanā. Imāhaṃ, bhante, ānisaṃsaṃ sampassamānā tathāgataṃ aṭṭha varāni yācāmī”ti. “Sādhu sādhu, visākhe; sādhu kho tvaṃ, visākhe, imaṃ ānisaṃsaṃ sampassamānā tathāgataṃ aṭṭha varāni yācasi. Anujānāmi te, visākhe, aṭṭha varānī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā visākhaṃ migāramātaraṃ imāhi [T 2.0214] gāthāhi anumodi –

351. “But, Visākhā, seeing what benefit do you ask the Tathāgata for these eight boons?” “Here, Venerable Sir, bhikkhus who have spent the rains in various regions will come to Sāvatthī to see the Blessed One. They will approach the Blessed One and ask: ‘Venerable Sir, the bhikkhu named so-and-so has passed away. What is his destination, what is his future state?’ The Blessed One will declare that he has attained the fruit of stream-entry, or of once-returning, or of non-returning, or of Arahantship. Then I will approach them and ask: ‘Venerable Sirs, had that venerable one ever come to Sāvatthī?’ If they tell me: ‘That bhikkhu had indeed come to Sāvatthī,’ I will reach this conclusion: ‘Surely, that venerable one must have used my rains-cloth, or the meal for incoming bhikkhus, or the meal for traveling bhikkhus, or the meal for the sick, or the meal for those who nurse the sick, or the medicine for the sick, or the regular gruel.’ Remembering this, joy will arise in me. Being joyful, rapture will arise. With a rapturous mind, my body will be tranquil. With a tranquil body, I will feel happiness. Being happy, my mind will become concentrated. This will be for me the development of the faculties, the development of the powers, and the development of the enlightenment factors. Seeing this benefit, Venerable Sir, I ask the Tathāgata for these eight boons.” “Good, good, Visākhā! It is good that you see this benefit and ask the Tathāgata for these eight boons. I grant you, Visākhā, these eight boons.” Then the Blessed One expressed his appreciation to Visākhā, Migāra's mother, with these verses:

“Yā annapānaṃ dadatippamoditā;

Sīlūpapannā sugatassa sāvikā;

Dadāti dānaṃ abhibhuyya maccharaṃ;

Sovaggikaṃ sokanudaṃ sukhāvahaṃ.

That virtuous female disciple of the Well-Gone One, who gives food and drink with great joy, gives a gift—having overcome stinginess—that is heavenly, sorrow-dispelling, and happiness-bringing.

“Dibbaṃ sā labhate āyuṃ dibbaṃ balaṃ sā labhate ca āyuṃ (sī. syā.);

Āgamma maggaṃ virajaṃ anaṅgaṇaṃ;

Sā puññakāmā sukhinī anāmayā;

Saggamhi kāyamhi ciraṃ pamodatī”ti.

Having reached the path that is free from dust and without defilement, she obtains a divine lifespan. Desiring merit, endowed with happiness, and free from illness, she rejoices for a long time in the heavenly realm.

352. Atha kho bhagavā visākhaṃ migāramātaraṃ imāhi gāthāhi anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vassikasāṭikaṃ, āgantukabhattaṃ, gamikabhattaṃ, gilānabhattaṃ, gilānupaṭṭhākabhattaṃ, gilānabhesajjaṃ, dhuvayāguṃ, bhikkhunisaṅghassa udakasāṭika”nti.

352. Then the Blessed One, having expressed his appreciation to Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, with these verses, rose from his seat and departed. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this matter, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: 'I allow, monks, a rains-bathing cloth, a meal for visiting monks, a meal for traveling monks, a meal for sick monks, a meal for those attending the sick, medicine for the sick, constant gruel, and a water-bathing cloth for the community of nuns.'

Visākhāvatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story of Visākhā is concluded.

Visākhābhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The recitation section concerning Visākhā is concluded.

220. Nisīdanādianujānanā

220. The Allowance of Sitting Cloths and So Forth

353. Tena [M 0.0409] kho pana samayena bhikkhū paṇītāni bhojanāni bhuñjitvā muṭṭhassatī asampajānā niddaṃ okkamanti. Tesaṃ muṭṭhassatīnaṃ asampajānānaṃ niddaṃ okkamantānaṃ supinantena asuci muccati, senāsanaṃ asucinā makkhiyati. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmatā ānandena pacchāsamaṇena senāsanacārikaṃ āhiṇḍanto addasa senāsanaṃ [T 2.0215] asucinā makkhitaṃ, disvāna [V 0.0386] āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “kiṃ etaṃ, ānanda, senāsanaṃ makkhita”nti? “Etarahi, bhante, bhikkhū paṇītāni bhojanāni [P 1.0295] bhuñjitvā muṭṭhassatī asampajānā niddaṃ okkamanti. Tesaṃ muṭṭhassatīnaṃ asampajānānaṃ niddaṃ okkamantānaṃ supinantena asuci muccati; tayidaṃ, bhagavā, senāsanaṃ asucinā makkhita”nti. “Evametaṃ, ānanda, evametaṃ, ānanda. Muccati hi, ānanda, muṭṭhassatīnaṃ asampajānānaṃ niddaṃ okkamantānaṃ supinantena asuci. Ye te, ānanda, bhikkhū upaṭṭhitassatī sampajānā niddaṃ okkamanti, tesaṃ asuci na muccati. Yepi te, ānanda, puthujjanā kāmesu vītarāgā, tesampi asuci na muccati. Aṭṭhānametaṃ, ānanda, anavakāso yaṃ arahato asuci mucceyyā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “idhāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ānandena pacchāsamaṇena senāsanacārikaṃ āhiṇḍanto addasaṃ senāsanaṃ asucinā makkhitaṃ, disvāna ānandaṃ āmantesiṃ ‘kiṃ etaṃ, ānanda, senāsanaṃ makkhita’nti? ‘Etarahi, bhante, bhikkhū paṇītāni bhojanāni bhuñjitvā muṭṭhassatī asampajānā niddaṃ okkamanti. Tesaṃ muṭṭhassatīnaṃ asampajānānaṃ niddaṃ okkamantānaṃ supinantena asuci muccati; tayidaṃ, bhagavā, senāsanaṃ asucinā makkhita’nti. ‘Evametaṃ, ānanda, evametaṃ, ānanda, muccati hi, ānanda, muṭṭhassatīnaṃ asampajānānaṃ niddaṃ okkamantānaṃ supinantena [T 2.0216] asuci. Ye te, ānanda, bhikkhū upaṭṭhitassatī sampajānā niddaṃ okkamanti, tesaṃ asuci na muccati. Yepi te, ānanda, puthujjanā kāmesu vītarāgā tesampi asuci na muccati. Aṭṭhānametaṃ, ānanda, anavakāso yaṃ arahato asuci mucceyyā’”ti.

353. At that time, monks, having eaten choice foods, fell asleep with lapsed mindfulness and without clear comprehension. For those who fell asleep with lapsed mindfulness and without clear comprehension, impurity was released through a dream, and the lodging was soiled with impurity. Then the Blessed One, while touring the lodgings with Venerable Ānanda as his attendant monk, saw a lodging soiled with impurity. Having seen it, he addressed Venerable Ānanda: “Ānanda, what is this that has soiled the lodging?” “Venerable sir, at present, monks, having eaten choice foods, fall asleep with lapsed mindfulness and without clear comprehension. For those who fall asleep with lapsed mindfulness and without clear comprehension, impurity is released through a dream; thus, Blessed One, the lodging is soiled with impurity.” “So it is, Ānanda, so it is. Indeed, Ānanda, impurity is released through a dream for those who fall asleep with lapsed mindfulness and without clear comprehension. Those monks, Ānanda, who fall asleep with mindfulness established and with clear comprehension, for them impurity is not released. And those ordinary people, Ānanda, who are free from lust for sensual pleasures, for them also impurity is not released. It is impossible, Ānanda, it is not the occasion that an Arahant should release impurity.” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion, in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “Here, monks, while touring the lodgings with Ānanda as my attendant monk, I saw a lodging soiled with impurity. Having seen it, I addressed Ānanda, ‘Ānanda, what is this that has soiled the lodging?’ ‘Venerable sir, at present, monks, having eaten choice foods, fall asleep with lapsed mindfulness and without clear comprehension. For those who fall asleep with lapsed mindfulness and without clear comprehension, impurity is released through a dream; thus, Blessed One, the lodging is soiled with impurity.’ ‘So it is, Ānanda, so it is. Indeed, Ānanda, impurity is released through a dream for those who fall asleep with lapsed mindfulness and without clear comprehension. Those monks, Ānanda, who fall asleep with mindfulness established and with clear comprehension, for them impurity is not released. And those ordinary people, Ānanda, who are free from lust for sensual pleasures, for them also impurity is not released. It is impossible, Ānanda, it is not the occasion that an Arahant should release impurity.’”

“Pañcime, bhikkhave, ādīnavā muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa niddaṃ okkamato – dukkhaṃ supati, dukkhaṃ paṭibujjhati, pāpakaṃ supinaṃ passati, devatā na rakkhanti, asuci muccati. Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa niddaṃ okkamato.

Monks, there are these five dangers for one with lapsed mindfulness, who lacks clear comprehension when falling asleep: one sleeps in discomfort, one wakes in discomfort, one sees a bad dream, deities do not protect one, and semen is emitted. These, monks, are the five dangers for one with lapsed mindfulness, who lacks clear comprehension when falling asleep.

“Pañcime[M 0.0410], bhikkhave, ānisaṃsā upaṭṭhitassatissa sampajānassa niddaṃ okkamato – sukhaṃ supati, sukhaṃ paṭibujjhati, na pāpakaṃ supinaṃ passati, devatā rakkhanti, asuci na muccati. Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṃsā upaṭṭhitassatissa sampajānassa niddaṃ okkamato.

Monks, there are these five benefits for one with established mindfulness, who possesses clear comprehension when falling asleep: one sleeps in comfort, one wakes in comfort, one does not see a bad dream, deities protect one, and semen is not emitted. These, monks, are the five benefits for one with established mindfulness, who possesses clear comprehension when falling asleep.

“Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kāyaguttiyā cīvaraguttiyā senāsanaguttiyā nisīdana”nti.

Monks, I allow a sitting cloth for the protection of the body, for the protection of the robes, and for the protection of the lodging.

Tena [V 0.0387] kho pana samayena atikhuddakaṃ nisīdanaṃ na sabbaṃ senāsanaṃ saṃgopeti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yāvamahantaṃ paccattharaṇaṃ ākaṅkhati tāvamahantaṃ paccattharaṇaṃ kātunti.

Now at that time, a very small sitting cloth did not cover the entire lodging. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. 'Monks, I allow one to make a covering as large as one wishes.'

354. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato ānandassa upajjhāyassa āyasmato belaṭṭhasīsassa thullakacchābādho hoti. Tassa lasikāya cīvarāni kāye lagganti. Tāni bhikkhū udakena temetvā temetvā apakaḍḍhanti. Addasā kho bhagavā senāsanacārikaṃ āhiṇḍanto te [T 2.0217] bhikkhū tāni cīvarāni udakena temetvā temetvā apakaḍḍhante, disvāna yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami, upaṅkamitvā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “kiṃ imassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ābādho”ti? “Imassa, bhante, āyasmato [P 1.0296] thullakacchābādho. Lasikāya cīvarāni kāye lagganti. Tāni mayaṃ udakena temetvā temetvā apakaḍḍhāmā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, yassa kaṇḍu vā piḷakā vā assāvo vā thullakacchu vā ābādho kaṇḍuppaṭicchādi”nti.

354. At that time, the preceptor of the Venerable Ānanda, the Venerable Belaṭṭhasīsa, had a severe skin disease. His robes would stick to his body with exudate. The monks would repeatedly soak them with water and pull them off. The Blessed One, while touring the monastic lodgings, saw those monks repeatedly soaking those robes with water and pulling them off. Having seen them, he approached those monks and said, “Monks, what is this monk’s affliction?” “Venerable Sir, this venerable one has a severe skin disease. The robes stick to his body with exudate. We are repeatedly soaking them with water and pulling them off.” Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the monks: “Monks, I allow a sore-covering cloth for any monk who has an affliction of itching, or boils, or a discharging sore, or a severe skin disease.”

355. Atha kho visākhā migāramātā mukhapuñchanacoḷaṃ mukhapuñjanacoḷaṃ (ka.) ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho visākhā migāramātā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “paṭiggaṇhātu me, bhante, bhagavā mukhapuñchanacoḷaṃ, yaṃ mamassa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā”ti. Paṭiggahesi bhagavā mukhapuñchanacoḷaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā visākhaṃ migāramātaraṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho visākhā migāramātā bhagavatā dhammiyā [M 0.0411] kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mukhapuñchanacoḷaka”nti mukhapuñchanacolanti (syā.).

355. Then Visākhā Migāramātā, taking a face-wiping cloth, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, she paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, Visākhā Migāramātā said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One accept this face-wiping cloth from me, which will be for my long-term welfare and happiness.” The Blessed One accepted the face-wiping cloth. Then the Blessed One instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened Visākhā Migāramātā with a talk on the Dhamma. Then Visākhā Migāramātā, having been instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a talk on the Dhamma, rose from her seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him to the right, and departed. Then the Blessed One, on this occasion and in this connection, having given a talk on the Dhamma, addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I allow a face-wiping cloth.”

356. Tena [T 2.0218] kho pana samayena rojo mallo āyasmato ānandassa sahāyo hoti. Rojassa mallassa khomapilotikā āyasmato ānandassa hatthe nikkhittā hoti. Āyasmato ca ānandassa khomapilotikāya attho hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa vissāsaṃ gahetuṃ – sandiṭṭho ca hoti, sambhatto ca, ālapito [V 0.0388] ca, jīvati ca, jānāti ca, gahite me attamano bhavissatīti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi pañcahaṅgehi samannāgatassa vissāsaṃ gahetunti.

356. At that time, Roja the Mallan was a friend of the Venerable Ānanda. A worn linen cloth of Roja the Mallan had been placed in the Venerable Ānanda’s hand. And the Venerable Ānanda had need for the worn linen cloth. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, I allow the taking on trust from one who is endowed with five factors: he is an acquaintance, he is an intimate, he has been told one may take it, he is alive, and one knows, ‘When it is taken by me, he will be pleased.’ Bhikkhus, I allow the taking on trust from one who is endowed with these five factors.”

357. Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhūnaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ hoti ticīvaraṃ. Attho ca hoti parissāvanehipi thavikāhipi. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, parikkhāracoḷakanti.

357. At that time, the bhikkhus had a full set of three robes. And there was a need for water strainers and bags. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, I allow a requisites-cloth.”

Nisīdanādianujānanā niṭṭhitā.

The Allowance of Sitting Cloths and so forth is Concluded.

221. Pacchimavikappanupagacīvarādikathā

221. Discourse on Robes and so forth, and the Minimum for Making Over

358. Atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “yāni tāni bhagavatā anuññātāni ticīvaranti vā vassikasāṭikāti vā nisīdananti vā paccattharaṇanti vā kaṇḍuppaṭicchādīti [P 1.0297] vā mukhapuñchanacoḷanti vā parikkhāracoḷanti vā, sabbāni tāni adhiṭṭhātabbāni nu kho, udāhu, vikappetabbānī”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ticīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ na vikappetuṃ; vassikasāṭikaṃ vassānaṃ cātumāsaṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ, tato paraṃ vikappetuṃ; nisīdanaṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ na vikappetuṃ; paccattharaṇaṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ [T 2.0219] na vikappetuṃ; kaṇḍuppaṭicchādiṃ yāvaābādhā adhiṭṭhātuṃ tato paraṃ vikappetuṃ; mukhapuñchanacoḷaṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ na vikappetuṃ; parikkhāracoḷaṃ adhiṭṭhātuṃ na vikappetunti.

358. Then this reflection arose in the bhikkhus: “Those robes that the Blessed One has allowed—the three robes, the rains-bathing cloth, the sitting cloth, the bed-sheet, the sore-covering cloth, the face-wiping cloth, or the requisites-cloth—should all of these be determined, or should they be made over?” They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, I allow the three robes to be determined, not to be made over; the rains-bathing cloth to be determined for the four months of the rains, and after that to be made over; the sitting cloth to be determined, not to be made over; the bed-sheet to be determined, not to be made over; the sore-covering cloth to be determined for as long as the illness lasts, and after that to be made over; the face-wiping cloth to be determined, not to be made over; and the requisites-cloth to be determined, not to be made over.”

Atha [M 0.0412] kho bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kittakaṃ pacchimaṃ nu kho cīvaraṃ vikappetabba”nti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, āyāmena aṭṭhaṅgulaṃ sugataṅgulena caturaṅgulavitthataṃ pacchimaṃ cīvaraṃ vikappetunti.

Then this thought arose in the bhikkhus: “What is the minimum size of a robe that should be made over?” They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, I allow a robe of the minimum size of eight fingerbreadths in length and four fingerbreadths in width, by the Sugata's fingerbreadth, to be made over.”

359. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato mahākassapassa paṃsukūlakato garuko hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, suttalūkhaṃ kātunti. Vikaṇṇo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, vikaṇṇaṃ uddharitunti. Suttā okiriyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, anuvātaṃ paribhaṇḍaṃ āropetunti.

359. At that time, the Venerable Mahākassapa's robe made of rags was heavy. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, I allow mending with thread.” It was crooked. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, I allow cutting off the crooked part.” The threads came out. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, I allow attaching a border along the length and a border along the width.”

Tena [V 0.0389] kho pana samayena saṅghāṭiyā pattā lujjanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhapadakaṃ kātunti.

At that time, the borders of the outer robe were getting ruined. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, I allow making a checkerboard pattern stitch.”

360. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno ticīvare kayiramāne sabbaṃ chinnakaṃ nappahoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dve chinnakāni ekaṃ acchinnakanti.

360. At that time, for a certain bhikkhu who was having his three robes made, there was not enough material if all were cut. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, I allow two to be cut and one to be uncut.”

Dve chinnakāni ekaṃ acchinnakaṃ nappahoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dve acchinnakāni ekaṃ chinnakanti.

When two were cut and one was uncut, there was not enough. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, I allow two to be uncut and one to be cut.”

Dve acchinnakāni [T 2.0220] ekaṃ chinnakaṃ nappahoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, anvādhikampi āropetuṃ, na ca, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ acchinnakaṃ dhāretabbaṃ. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

When two were uncut and one was cut, there was not enough. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, I allow attaching a supporting strip as well. And, bhikkhus, an entirely uncut robe should not be worn. Whoever should wear one incurs an offense of wrong conduct.”

361. Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno bahuṃ cīvaraṃ uppannaṃ hoti. So ca taṃ cīvaraṃ mātāpitūnaṃ dātukāmo hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Mātāpitaroti mātāpitūnaṃ kho (sī.) kho, bhikkhave, dadamāne vadamāno (ka.), vadamāne (?) kiṃ vadeyyāma? Anujānāmi[P 1.0298], bhikkhave, mātāpitūnaṃ dātuṃ. Na ca, bhikkhave, saddhādeyyaṃ vinipātetabbaṃ. Yo vinipāteyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

361. At that time, much robe-cloth had arisen for a certain bhikkhu. And that bhikkhu wished to give that robe-cloth to his mother and father. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Bhikkhus, what should we say to one who is giving to his mother and father? I allow, bhikkhus, giving to mother and father. And, bhikkhus, an offering of faith should not be destroyed. Whoever should destroy it, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

362. Tena [M 0.0413] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu andhavane cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā santaruttarena gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Corā taṃ cīvaraṃ avahariṃsu. So bhikkhu duccoḷo hoti lūkhacīvaro. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “kissa tvaṃ, āvuso, duccoḷo lūkhacīvarosī”ti? “Idhāhaṃ so ahaṃ (katthaci), āvuso, andhavane cīvaraṃ nikkhipitvā santaruttarena gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ. Corā taṃ cīvaraṃ avahariṃsu. Tenāhaṃ duccoḷo lūkhacīvaro”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Na, bhikkhave, santaruttarena gāmo pavisitabbo. Yo paviseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

362. At that time, a certain monk, having left his double-layered robe in the Blind Forest, entered a village for alms with only his lower and upper robes. Thieves stole that robe. That monk was poorly clothed and had a shabby robe. The monks asked him, “Friend, why are you poorly clothed and have a shabby robe?” “Friends, I left my double-layered robe in the Blind Forest and entered a village for alms with only my lower and upper robes. Thieves stole that robe. That is why I am poorly clothed and have a shabby robe.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, a village is not to be entered with only the lower and upper robes. Whoever should enter commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ānando assatiyā santaruttarena gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavocuṃ – “nanu[T 2.0221], āvuso ānanda, bhagavatā paññattaṃ – ‘na santaruttarena gāmo pavisitabbo’ti? Kissa tvaṃ, āvuso ānanda, santaruttarena [V 0.0390] gāmaṃ paviṭṭho”ti? “Saccaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā paññattaṃ – ‘na santaruttarena gāmo pavisitabbo’ti. Api cāhaṃ assatiyā paviṭṭho”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, through forgetfulness, entered a village for alms with only his lower and upper robes. The monks said this to the Venerable Ānanda: “Friend Ānanda, was it not laid down by the Blessed One, ‘A village is not to be entered with only the lower and upper robes’? Why then, friend Ānanda, have you entered the village with only your lower and upper robes?” “It is true, friends, that the Blessed One laid down, ‘A village is not to be entered with only the lower and upper robes.’ However, I entered through forgetfulness.” They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

Pañcime, bhikkhave, paccayā saṅghāṭiyā nikkhepāya – gilāno vā hoti, vassikasaṅketaṃ vā hoti, nadīpāraṃ gantuṃ vā hoti, aggaḷaguttivihāro vā hoti, atthatakathinaṃ vā hoti. Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca paccayā saṅghāṭiyā nikkhepāya.

Monks, there are these five reasons for setting aside the double-layered robe: one is sick; or it is the designated rainy season; or one is going to the other side of a river; or there is a monastery secured by a bolt; or the Kathina has been spread. These, monks, are the five reasons for setting aside the double-layered robe.

Pañcime, bhikkhave, paccayā uttarāsaṅgassa nikkhepāya…pe… antaravāsakassa nikkhepāya – gilāno vā hoti, vassikasaṅketaṃ vā hoti, nadīpāraṃ gantuṃ vā hoti, aggaḷaguttivihāro vā hoti, atthatakathinaṃ vā hoti. Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca paccayā uttarāsaṅgassa antaravāsakassa nikkhepāya.

Monks, there are these five reasons for setting aside the upper robe… or the lower robe: one is sick; or it is the designated rainy season; or one is going to the other side of a river; or there is a monastery secured by a bolt; or the Kathina has been spread. These, monks, are the five reasons for setting aside the upper robe and the lower robe.

Pañcime, bhikkhave, paccayā vassikasāṭikāya nikkhepāya – gilāno vā hoti, nissīmaṃ gantuṃ vā hoti, nadīpāraṃ gantuṃ vā hoti, aggaḷaguttivihāro vā hoti, vassikasāṭikā akatā vā hoti vippakatā [T 2.0222] vā. Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca paccayā vassikasāṭikāya nikkhepāyāti.

Monks, there are these five reasons for setting aside the rain-bathing cloth: one is sick; or one is going beyond the boundary; or one is going to the other side of a river; or there is a monastery secured by a bolt; or the rain-bathing cloth is unmade or unfinished. These, monks, are the five reasons for setting aside the rain-bathing cloth.

Pacchimavikappanupagacīvarādikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Robes and So Forth Subject to Subsequent Designation is concluded.

222. Saṅghikacīvaruppādakathā

The Discourse on the Arising of Robes Belonging to the Saṅgha

363. Tena [M 0.0414] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu eko vassaṃ vasi. Tattha manussā saṅghassa demāti cīvarāni adaṃsu. Atha kho tassa bhikkhuno etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘catuvaggo pacchimo saṅgho’ti. Ahañcamhi ekako. Ime ca manussā [P 1.0299] saṅghassa demāti cīvarāni adaṃsu. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ imāni saṅghikāni cīvarāni sāvatthiṃ hareyya”nti. Atha kho so bhikkhu tāni cīvarāni ādāya sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesi. “Tuyheva, bhikkhu, tāni cīvarāni yāva kathinassa ubbhārāyā”ti. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu eko vassaṃ vasati. Tattha manussā saṅghassa demāti cīvarāni denti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tasseva tāni cīvarāni yāva kathinassa ubbhārāyāti.

222. At that time, a certain monk spent the rains residence alone. There, people gave robes, saying, “We give to the Saṅgha.” Then this thought occurred to that monk: “The Blessed One has laid down that ‘the minimum Saṅgha is a group of four.’ But I am alone. And these people have given robes, saying, ‘We give to the Saṅgha.’ What if I were to take these robes belonging to the Saṅgha to Sāvatthī?” Then that monk took those robes, went to Sāvatthī, and reported the matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, those robes are yours until the removal of the Kathina.” “In this teaching, monks, a monk spends the rains residence alone. There, people give robes, saying, ‘We give to the Saṅgha.’ I allow, monks, that those robes belong to him alone until the removal of the Kathina.”

Tena [V 0.0391] kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu utukālaṃ eko vasi. Tattha manussā saṅghassa demāti cīvarāni adaṃsu. Atha kho tassa bhikkhuno etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ ‘catuvaggo pacchimo saṅgho’ti. Ahañcamhi ekako. Ime ca manussā saṅghassa demāti cīvarāni adaṃsu. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ imāni saṅghikāni cīvarāni sāvatthiṃ hareyya”nti. Atha kho so bhikkhu tāni cīvarāni ādāya sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ ārocesi. Bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave[T 2.0223], sammukhībhūtena saṅghena bhājetuṃ. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu utukālaṃ eko vasati. Tattha manussā saṅghassa demāti cīvarāni denti. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, tena bhikkhunā tāni cīvarāni adhiṭṭhātuṃ – “mayhimāni cīvarānī”ti. Tassa ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno taṃ cīvaraṃ anadhiṭṭhite añño bhikkhu āgacchati, samako dātabbo bhāgo. Tehi ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi taṃ cīvaraṃ bhājiyamāne, apātite kuse, añño bhikkhu āgacchati, samako dātabbo bhāgo. Tehi ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi taṃ cīvaraṃ bhājiyamāne, pātite kuse, añño bhikkhu āgacchati, nākāmā dātabbo bhāgoti.

363. At that time, a certain monk was staying alone during the season outside the rains. There, people gave robes, saying, “We give to the Saṅgha.” Then this thought occurred to that monk: “The Blessed One has laid down that ‘the minimum Saṅgha is a group of four.’ But I am alone. And these people have given robes, saying, ‘We give to the Saṅgha.’ What if I were to take these robes belonging to the Saṅgha to Sāvatthī?” Then that monk took those robes, went to Sāvatthī, and reported this matter to the monks. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow them to be divided by the Saṅgha that is present. In this teaching, monks, a monk stays alone during the season outside the rains. There, people give robes, saying, ‘We give to the Saṅgha.’ I allow, monks, that monk to determine those robes, thinking, ‘These robes are mine.’ If, monks, another monk arrives before that monk has determined that robe, an equal share should be given. If, monks, while those monks are dividing that robe, another monk arrives before the lots are cast, an equal share should be given. If, monks, while those monks are dividing that robe, another monk arrives after the lots have been cast, a share need not be given if they are unwilling.”

Tena kho pana samayena dve bhātikā therā, āyasmā ca isidāso āyasmā ca isibhaṭo, sāvatthiyaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭhā aññataraṃ gāmakāvāsaṃ agamaṃsu. Manussā cirassāpi therā āgatāti sacīvarāni bhattāni [M 0.0415] adaṃsu. Āvāsikā bhikkhū there pucchiṃsu – “imāni, bhante, saṅghikāni cīvarāni there āgamma uppannāni, sādiyissanti therā bhāga”nti. Therā evamāhaṃsu – “yathā kho mayaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāma, tumhākaṃyeva tāni cīvarāni yāva kathinassa ubbhārāyā”ti.

At that time, two elder monks who were brothers, the Venerable Isidāsa and the Venerable Isibhaṭa, having spent the rains residence in Sāvatthī, went to a certain village monastery. The people, thinking, “The elders have come after a long time,” gave meals together with robes. The resident monks asked the elders, “Venerable sirs, these robes belonging to the Saṅgha have arisen on account of the elders. Will the elders accept a share?” The elders replied, “Friends, as we understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those robes are yours alone until the removal of the Kathina.”

Tena kho pana samayena tayo bhikkhū rājagahe vassaṃ vasanti. Tattha manussā saṅghassa

At that time, three monks were spending the rains residence in Rājagaha. There, people gave robes to the Saṅgha.

Demāti cīvarāni denti. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “bhagavatā paññattaṃ [P 1.0300] ‘catuvaggo pacchimo saṅgho’ti. Mayañcamhā tayo janā. Ime ca manussā saṅghassa demāti cīvarāni [T 2.0224] denti. Kathaṃ nu kho amhehi paṭipajjitabba”nti? Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā therā, āyasmā ca nilavāsī āyasmā ca sāṇavāsī āyasmā ca gotako āyasmā ca bhagu āyasmā ca phaḷikasantāno, pāṭaliputte viharanti kukkuṭārāme. Atha kho te bhikkhū pāṭaliputtaṃ gantvā there pucchiṃsu. Therā evamāhaṃsu – “yathā kho mayaṃ āvuso bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāma, tumhākaṃyeva tāni cīvarāni yāva kathinassa ubbhārāyā”ti.

They give robes, thinking, 'We will give.' Then this thought occurred to those monks: 'The Blessed One has laid down, “The minimum Saṅgha is a group of four.” And we are three persons. And these people are giving robes, thinking, “We give to the Saṅgha.” How indeed should we act?' Now at that time, many elders—the Venerable Nilavāsī, the Venerable Sāṇavāsī, the Venerable Gotako, the Venerable Bhagu, and the Venerable Phaḷikasantāno—were dwelling at the Kukkuṭārāma in Pāṭaliputta. Then those monks, having gone to Pāṭaliputta, asked the elders. The elders said thus: 'Friends, as we understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those robes are yours alone until the removal of the Kathina.'

Saṅghikacīvaruppādakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Arising of Robes Belonging to the Saṅgha is concluded.

223. Upanandasakyaputtavatthu

223. The Story of Upananda the Sakyan Prince

364. Tena [V 0.0392] kho pana samayena āyasmā upanando sakyaputto sāvatthiyaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭho aññataraṃ gāmakāvāsaṃ agamāsi. Tattha ca bhikkhū cīvaraṃ bhājetukāmā sannipatiṃsu. Te evamāhaṃsu – “imāni kho, āvuso, saṅghikāni cīvarāni bhājiyissanti, sādiyissasi bhāga”nti? “Āmāvuso, sādiyissāmī”ti. Tato cīvarabhāgaṃ gahetvā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ agamāsi. Tatthapi bhikkhū cīvaraṃ bhājetukāmā sannipatiṃsu. Tepi evamāhaṃsu – “imāni kho, āvuso, saṅghikāni cīvarāni bhājiyissanti, sādiyissasi bhāga”nti? “Āmāvuso, sādiyissāmī”ti. Tatopi cīvarabhāgaṃ gahetvā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ agamāsi. Tatthapi bhikkhū cīvaraṃ bhājetukāmā sannipatiṃsu. Tepi evamāhaṃsu – “imāni kho, āvuso, saṅghikāni cīvarāni bhājiyissanti, sādiyissasi bhāga”nti? “Āmāvuso, sādiyissāmī”ti. Tatopi cīvarabhāgaṃ gahetvā mahantaṃ cīvarabhaṇḍikaṃ ādāya punadeva sāvatthiṃ paccāgañchi. Bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “mahāpuññosi tvaṃ[T 2.0225], āvuso upananda, bahuṃ te cīvaraṃ uppanna”nti. “Kuto me[M 0.0416], āvuso, puññaṃ? Idhāhaṃ, āvuso, sāvatthiyaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭho aññataraṃ gāmakāvāsaṃ agamāsiṃ. Tattha bhikkhū cīvaraṃ bhājetukāmā sannipatiṃsu. Te maṃ evamāhaṃsu – ‘imāni kho, āvuso, saṅghikāni cīvarāni bhājiyissanti, sādiyissasi bhāga’nti? ‘Āmāvuso, sādiyissāmī’ti. Tato cīvarabhāgaṃ gahetvā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ agamāsiṃ. Tatthapi bhikkhū cīvaraṃ bhājetukāmā sannipatiṃsu. Tepi maṃ evamāhaṃsu – ‘imāni kho, āvuso, saṅghikāni cīvarāni bhājiyissanti, sādiyissasi bhāga’”nti? ‘Āmāvuso, sādiyissāmī’ti. Tatopi cīvarabhāgaṃ gahetvā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ [P 1.0301] agamāsiṃ. Tatthapi bhikkhū cīvaraṃ bhājetukāmā sannipatiṃsu. Tepi maṃ evamāhaṃsu – ‘imāni kho, āvuso, saṅghikāni cīvarāni bhājiyissanti, sādiyissasi bhāga’nti? ‘Āmāvuso, sādiyissāmī’ti. Tatopi cīvarabhāgaṃ aggahesiṃ. Evaṃ me bahuṃ cīvaraṃ uppannanti. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, āvuso upananda, aññatra vassaṃvuṭṭho aññatra cīvarabhāgaṃ sādiyī”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma āyasmā upanando sakyaputto aññatra vassaṃvuṭṭho aññatra cīvarabhāgaṃ sādiyissatī”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, upananda, aññatra vassaṃvuṭṭho aññatra cīvarabhāgaṃ sādiyī”ti? “Saccaṃ bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, aññatra vassaṃvuṭṭho aññatra [T 2.0226] cīvarabhāgaṃ sādiyissasi. Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ [V 0.0393] kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, aññatra vassaṃvuṭṭhena aññatra cīvarabhāgo sāditabbo. Yo sādiyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

364. At that time the Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan prince, having completed the rains retreat in Sāvatthī, went to a certain village monastery. There, monks assembled, desiring to distribute robes. They said, “Friend, indeed, these robes belonging to the Saṅgha will be distributed. Will you accept a share?” “Yes, friends, I will accept,” he replied. Then, having taken a share of the robes, he went to another monastery. There too, monks assembled, desiring to distribute robes. They also said, “Friend, indeed, these robes belonging to the Saṅgha will be distributed. Will you accept a share?” “Yes, friends, I will accept,” he replied. From there also, having taken a share of the robes, he went to another monastery. There too, monks assembled, desiring to distribute robes. They also said, “Friend, indeed, these robes belonging to the Saṅgha will be distributed. Will you accept a share?” “Yes, friends, I will accept,” he replied. From there also, having taken a share of the robes and taking up a large bundle of robes, he returned again to Sāvatthī. The monks said, “You are of great merit, friend Upananda; many robes have arisen for you.” “From where is there merit for me, friends? Here, friends, having completed the rains retreat in Sāvatthī, I went to a certain village monastery. There, monks assembled, desiring to distribute robes. They said to me, ‘Friend, indeed, these robes belonging to the Saṅgha will be distributed. Will you accept a share?’ ‘Yes, friends, I will accept,’ I replied. Then, having taken a share of the robes, I went to another monastery. There too, monks assembled, desiring to distribute robes. They also said to me, ‘Friend, indeed, these robes belonging to the Saṅgha will be distributed. Will you accept a share?’ ‘Yes, friends, I will accept,’ I replied. From there also, having taken a share of the robes, I went to another monastery. There too, monks assembled, desiring to distribute robes. They also said to me, ‘Friend, indeed, these robes belonging to the Saṅgha will be distributed. Will you accept a share?’ ‘Yes, friends, I will accept,’ I replied. From there also, I took a share of the robes. In this way, many robes have arisen for me.” “But, friend Upananda, having completed the rains retreat in one place, did you accept a share of robes in another place?” “Yes, friends,” he replied. Those monks who were of few wishes… they criticized, scorned, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed could the Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan prince, having completed the rains retreat in one place, accept a share of robes in another place?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, as is said, Upananda, that having completed the rains retreat in one place, you accepted a share of robes in another place?” “It is true, Blessed One,” he replied. The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him… “How indeed, worthless man, could you, having completed the rains retreat in one place, accept a share of robes in another place? This, worthless man, is not for the faith of the unfaithful… Having rebuked him… and given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, a share of robes in another place is not to be accepted by one who has completed the rains retreat in one place. Whoever should accept one, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā upanando sakyaputto eko dvīsu āvāsesu vassaṃ vasi – “evaṃ me bahuṃ cīvaraṃ uppajjissatī”ti. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “kathaṃ nu kho āyasmato upanandassa sakyaputtassa cīvarapaṭivīso dātabbo”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Detha, bhikkhave, moghapurisassa ekādhippāyaṃ. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu eko dvīsu āvāsesu vassaṃ vasati – “evaṃ me bahuṃ cīvaraṃ uppajjissatī”ti. Sace amutra upaḍḍhaṃ amutra upaḍḍhaṃ vasati, amutra upaḍḍho amutra upaḍḍho cīvarapaṭivīso dātabbo. Yattha vā pana bahutaraṃ vasati, tato cīvarapaṭivīso dātabboti.

At that time the Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan prince, being alone, observed the rains retreat in two monasteries, thinking: “Thus many robes will arise for me.” Then this thought occurred to those monks: “How should the share of robes be given to the Venerable Upananda, the Sakyan prince?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, give a single share to that worthless man. Here, monks, a monk, being alone, observes the rains retreat in two monasteries, thinking: ‘Thus many robes will arise for me.’ If he resides half the time in one and half in the other, half a share of robes should be given from the one and half a share of robes from the other. Or wherever he resides longer, from there the share of robes should be given.”

Upanandasakyaputtavatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Story of Upananda the Sakyan Prince is concluded.

224. Gilānavatthukathā

224. The Story of the Sick Monk

365. Tena [M 0.0417] kho pana samayena aññatarassa bhikkhuno kucchivikārābādho hoti. So sake muttakarīse palipanno seti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmatā ānandena pacchāsamaṇena senāsanacārikaṃ āhiṇḍanto yena tassa bhikkhuno vihāro tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho bhagavā taṃ bhikkhuṃ sake muttakarīse palipannaṃ sayamānaṃ, disvāna yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ te, bhikkhu, ābādho”ti? “Kucchivikāro me, bhagavā”ti. “Atthi [T 2.0227] pana te, bhikkhu, upaṭṭhāko”ti? “Natthi, bhagavā”ti[P 1.0302]. “Kissa taṃ bhikkhū na upaṭṭhentī”ti? “Ahaṃ kho, bhante, bhikkhūnaṃ akārako; tena maṃ bhikkhū na upaṭṭhentī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “gacchānanda, udakaṃ āhara, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ nahāpessāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā udakaṃ āhari. Bhagavā udakaṃ āsiñci. Āyasmā ānando paridhovi. Bhagavā sīsato aggahesi. Āyasmā ānando pādato uccāretvā mañcake nipātesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṃ nidāne etasmiṃ pakaraṇe bhikkhusaṅghaṃ sannipātāpetvā bhikkhū paṭipucchi – “atthi, bhikkhave, amukasmiṃ vihāre bhikkhu gilāno”ti? “Atthi, bhagavā”ti. “Kiṃ tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ābādho”ti? “Tassa, bhante, āyasmato kucchivikārābādho”ti. “Atthi pana, bhikkhave, tassa bhikkhuno upaṭṭhāko”ti? “Natthi, bhagavā”ti[V 0.0394]. “Kissa taṃ bhikkhū na upaṭṭhentī”ti? “Eso, bhante, bhikkhu bhikkhūnaṃ akārako; tena taṃ bhikkhū na upaṭṭhentī”ti. “Natthi vo, bhikkhave, mātā, natthi pitā, ye vo upaṭṭhaheyyuṃ. Tumhe ce, bhikkhave, aññamaññaṃ na upaṭṭhahissatha, atha ko carahi upaṭṭhahissati? Yo, bhikkhave, maṃ upaṭṭhaheyya so gilānaṃ upaṭṭhaheyya. Sace upajjhāyo hoti, upajjhāyena yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhātabbo; vuṭṭhānamassa āgametabbaṃ. Sace ācariyo hoti, ācariyena yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhātabbo; vuṭṭhānamassa āgametabbaṃ. Sace saddhivihāriko hoti[T 2.0228], saddhivihārikena yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhātabbo; vuṭṭhānamassa āgametabbaṃ. Sace antevāsiko hoti, antevāsikena yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhātabbo; vuṭṭhānamassa āgametabbaṃ. Sace samānupajjhāyako hoti, samānupajjhāyakena yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhātabbo[M 0.0418]; vuṭṭhānamassa āgametabbaṃ. Sace samānācariyako hoti, samānācariyakena yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhātabbo; vuṭṭhānamassa āgametabbaṃ. Sace na hoti upajjhāyo vā ācariyo vā saddhivihāriko vā antevāsiko vā samānupajjhāyako vā samānācariyako vā saṅghena upaṭṭhātabbo. No ce upaṭṭhaheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa”.

365. Now at that time a certain bhikkhu was suffering from a stomach ailment. He lay wallowing in his own urine and feces. Then the Blessed One, wandering on a tour of the lodgings with the Venerable Ānanda as his attendant, approached that bhikkhu’s dwelling. The Blessed One saw that bhikkhu lying wallowing in his own urine and feces. Seeing him, he went up to him and said, “What is your ailment, bhikkhu?” “I have a stomach ailment, Blessed One.” “But do you have an attendant, bhikkhu?” “No, Blessed One.” “Why do the bhikkhus not attend to you?” “Venerable sir, I am of no service to the bhikkhus; that is why they do not attend to me.” Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, “Go, Ānanda, fetch water. We shall bathe this bhikkhu.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied Ānanda, and he fetched water. The Blessed One poured the water, and the Venerable Ānanda washed the bhikkhu. The Blessed One took hold of him by the head, and the Venerable Ānanda lifted him by the feet. They laid him on a bed. Then, on that occasion, the Blessed One had the Saṅgha of bhikkhus assembled and questioned the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, is there a sick bhikkhu in a certain dwelling?” “There is, Blessed One.” “What is that bhikkhu's ailment?” “Venerable sir, that venerable one has a stomach ailment.” “Does that bhikkhu have an attendant?” “No, Blessed One.” “Why do the bhikkhus not attend to him?” “Venerable sir, that bhikkhu is of no service to the bhikkhus; that is why they do not attend to him.” “Bhikkhus, you have no mother or father to attend to you. If you do not attend to one another, who then will attend to you? Whoever would attend to me should attend to the sick. If he has a preceptor, the preceptor should attend to him for life, awaiting his recovery. If he has a teacher, the teacher should attend to him for life, awaiting his recovery. If he has a co-resident pupil, the co-resident pupil should attend to him for life, awaiting his recovery. If he has a pupil, the pupil should attend to him for life, awaiting his recovery. If he has a co-resident under the same preceptor, the co-resident should attend to him for life, awaiting his recovery. If he has a co-resident under the same teacher, the co-resident should attend to him for life, awaiting his recovery. If he has neither a preceptor, teacher, co-resident pupil, pupil, co-resident under the same preceptor, nor co-resident under the same teacher, the Saṅgha should attend to him. If they do not, they commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

366. Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato gilāno dūpaṭṭho hoti – asappāyakārī hoti, sappāye mattaṃ na jānāti, bhesajjaṃ na paṭisevitā hoti, atthakāmassa gilānupaṭṭhākassa yathābhūtaṃ ābādhaṃ nāvikattā hoti ‘abhikkamantaṃ vā abhikkamatīti, paṭikkamantaṃ vā paṭikkamatīti, ṭhitaṃ vā ṭhito’ti, uppannānaṃ sārīrikānaṃ vedanānaṃ dukkhānaṃ tibbānaṃ kharānaṃ kaṭukānaṃ asātānaṃ amanāpānaṃ pāṇaharānaṃ anadhivāsakajātiko hoti. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato gilāno dūpaṭṭho hoti.

366. Bhikkhus, a sick person endowed with five qualities is difficult to attend to: he does what is unsuitable; he does not know the measure in what is suitable; he does not take medicine; he does not truthfully reveal his illness to a caregiver who wishes for his welfare, stating whether it is increasing, decreasing, or stable; and he is of a nature that cannot endure arisen bodily feelings that are painful, sharp, racking, bitter, uncongenial, disagreeable, and life-taking. Bhikkhus, a sick person endowed with these five qualities is difficult to attend to.

Pañcahi, bhikkhave[P 1.0303], aṅgehi samannāgato gilāno sūpaṭṭho hoti – sappāyakārī hoti, sappāye mattaṃ jānāti, bhesajjaṃ paṭisevitā hoti, atthakāmassa gilānupaṭṭhākassa yathābhūtaṃ ābādhaṃ āvikattā hoti ‘abhikkamantaṃ vā abhikkamatīti, paṭikkamantaṃ vā paṭikkamatīti, ṭhitaṃ [T 2.0229] vā ṭhito’ti, uppannānaṃ sārīrikānaṃ vedanānaṃ dukkhānaṃ tibbānaṃ kharānaṃ kaṭukānaṃ asātānaṃ amanāpānaṃ pāṇaharānaṃ adhivāsakajātiko hoti. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato gilāno sūpaṭṭho hoti.

Bhikkhus, a sick person endowed with five qualities is easy to attend to: he does what is suitable; he knows the measure in what is suitable; he takes medicine; he truthfully reveals his illness to a caregiver who wishes for his welfare, stating whether it is increasing, decreasing, or stable; and he is of a nature that endures arisen bodily feelings that are painful, sharp, racking, bitter, uncongenial, disagreeable, and life-taking. Bhikkhus, a sick person endowed with these five qualities is easy to attend to.

Pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato gilānupaṭṭhāko nālaṃ gilānaṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ – na paṭibalo hoti bhesajjaṃ saṃvidhātuṃ, sappāyāsappāyaṃ na jānāti, asappāyaṃ upanāmeti sappāyaṃ apanāmeti, āmisantaro gilānaṃ upaṭṭhāti no mettacitto, jegucchī hoti uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ [V 0.0395] vā kheḷaṃ vā vantaṃ vā nīhātuṃ, na paṭibalo hoti gilānaṃ kālena kālaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetuṃ samādapetuṃ samuttejetuṃ sampahaṃsetuṃ. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato gilānupaṭṭhāko nālaṃ gilānaṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ.

Bhikkhus, a caregiver endowed with five qualities is unfit to attend to a sick person: he is not able to prepare medicine; he does not know what is suitable and unsuitable, offering what is unsuitable and removing what is suitable; he attends to the sick person with material motives, not with a mind of loving-kindness; he is disgusted at removing feces, urine, spittle, or vomit; and he is not able to instruct, urge, arouse, and gladden the sick person from time to time with a Dhamma talk. Bhikkhus, a caregiver endowed with these five qualities is unfit to attend to a sick person.

Pañcahi[M 0.0419], bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato gilānupaṭṭhāko alaṃ gilānaṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ – paṭibalo hoti bhesajjaṃ saṃvidhātuṃ, sappāyāsappāyaṃ jānāti, asappāyaṃ apanāmeti sappāyaṃ upanāmeti, mettacitto gilānaṃ upaṭṭhāti no āmisantaro, ajegucchī hoti uccāraṃ vā passāvaṃ vā kheḷaṃ vā vantaṃ vā nīhātuṃ, paṭibalo hoti gilānaṃ kālena kālaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetuṃ samādapetuṃ samuttejetuṃ sampahaṃsetuṃ. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, pañcahaṅgehi samannāgato gilānupaṭṭhāko alaṃ gilānaṃ upaṭṭhātunti.

“Monks, a caregiver endowed with five qualities is fit to care for a patient: they are able to prepare medicine; they know what is suitable and unsuitable, removing what is unsuitable and offering what is suitable; they attend to the patient with a mind of loving-kindness, not for the sake of material gain; they are not disgusted to remove feces, urine, saliva, or vomit; and they are able, from time to time, to instruct, urge, rouse, and gladden the patient with a Dhamma talk. Monks, a caregiver endowed with these five qualities is fit to care for a patient.”

Gilānavatthukathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Sick is concluded.

225. Matasantakakathā

225. The Account of the Belongings of the Deceased

367. Tena kho pana samayena dve bhikkhū kosalesu janapade addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti. Te aññataraṃ āvāsaṃ upagacchiṃsu. Tattha [T 2.0230] aññataro bhikkhu gilāno hoti. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “bhagavatā kho, āvuso, gilānupaṭṭhānaṃ vaṇṇitaṃ. Handa, mayaṃ, āvuso, imaṃ bhikkhuṃ upaṭṭhahemā”ti. Te taṃ upaṭṭhahiṃsu. So tehi upaṭṭhahiyamāno kālamakāsi. Atha kho te bhikkhū tassa bhikkhuno pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. “Bhikkhussa, bhikkhave, kālaṅkate saṅgho sāmī pattacīvare, apica gilānupaṭṭhākā bahūpakārā. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghena ticīvarañca [P 1.0304] pattañca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbaṃ. Tena gilānupaṭṭhākena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘itthannāmo, bhante, bhikkhu kālaṅkato. Idaṃ tassa ticīvarañca patto cā’”ti. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

367. At that time, two monks were traveling on a long road in the Kosala country. They arrived at a certain monastery. There, a certain monk was sick. Then those monks thought: “Friends, the Blessed One has praised the nursing of the sick. Come, friends, let us nurse this monk.” They nursed him. While being nursed by them, he passed away. Then those monks, taking that monk’s bowl and robes, went to Sāvatthī and reported the matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, when a monk has passed away, the Saṅgha is the owner of his bowl and robes; moreover, those who nurse the sick are very helpful. I allow, monks, the Saṅgha to give the set of three robes and the bowl to those who nurse the sick. And, monks, it should be given in this way: The monk who nursed the sick should approach the Saṅgha and say: ‘Venerable sirs, the monk named so-and-so has passed away. This is his set of three robes and bowl.’ A competent and able monk should then inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmo bhikkhu kālaṅkato. Idaṃ tassa ticīvarañca patto ca. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho imaṃ ticīvarañca pattañca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The monk named so-and-so has passed away. This is his set of three robes and bowl. If it seems fit to the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give this set of three robes and this bowl to those who nursed the sick. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu [V 0.0396] me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmo bhikkhu kālaṅkato. Idaṃ tassa ticīvarañca patto ca. Saṅgho imaṃ ticīvarañca pattañca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati imassa ticīvarassa ca pattassa ca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The monk named so-and-so has passed away. This is his set of three robes and bowl. The Saṅgha gives this set of three robes and this bowl to those who nursed the sick. To whichever venerable one the giving of this set of three robes and this bowl to those who nursed the sick is agreeable, he should remain silent; to whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.”

“Dinnaṃ [M 0.0420] idaṃ saṅghena ticīvarañca patto ca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti[T 2.0231].

“This set of three robes and this bowl have been given by the Saṅgha to those who nursed the sick. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.”

368. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro sāmaṇero kālaṅkato hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Sāmaṇerassa, bhikkhave, kālaṅkate saṅgho sāmī pattacīvare, api ca gilānupaṭṭhākā bahūpakārā. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghena cīvarañca pattañca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dātuṃ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, dātabbaṃ. Tena gilānupaṭṭhākena bhikkhunā saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo – “itthannāmo, bhante, sāmaṇero kālaṅkato, idaṃ tassa cīvarañca patto cā”ti. Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

368. At that time, a certain novice had passed away. They informed the Blessed One of this matter. “Monks, when a novice has passed away, the Saṅgha is the owner of his bowl and robes; but those who nursed the sick are of great help. I allow, monks, the Saṅgha to give the robe and the bowl to those who nursed the sick. And monks, it should be given in this way. The monk who nursed the sick should approach the Saṅgha and say: ‘Venerable sirs, the novice named so-and-so has passed away. This is his robe and bowl.’ A competent and able monk should inform the Saṅgha:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmo sāmaṇero kālaṅkato. Idaṃ tassa cīvarañca patto ca. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho imaṃ cīvarañca pattañca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dadeyya. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The novice named so-and-so has passed away. This is his robe and bowl. If it seems fit to the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should give this robe and this bowl to those who nursed the sick. This is the motion.”

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmo sāmaṇero kālaṅkato. Idaṃ tassa cīvarañca patto ca. Saṅgho imaṃ cīvarañca pattañca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ deti. Yassāyasmato khamati imassa cīvarassa ca pattassa ca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dānaṃ, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. The novice named so-and-so has passed away. This is his robe and bowl. The Saṅgha gives this robe and this bowl to those who nurse the sick. To whichever venerable one the giving of this robe and this bowl to those who nurse the sick is agreeable, he should remain silent; to whomever it is not agreeable, he should speak.”

“Dinnaṃ idaṃ saṅghena cīvarañca patto ca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“This robe and this bowl have been given by the Saṅgha to those who nurse the sick. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus I hold it.”

369. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu ca sāmaṇero ca gilānaṃ upaṭṭhahiṃsu. So tehi upaṭṭhahiyamāno kālamakāsi. Atha kho tassa gilānupaṭṭhākassa bhikkhuno etadahosi [P 1.0305] – “kathaṃ nu kho gilānupaṭṭhākassa [T 2.0232] sāmaṇerassa cīvarapaṭivīso dātabbo”ti[V 0.0397]? Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānupaṭṭhākassa sāmaṇerassa samakaṃ paṭivīsaṃ dātunti.

369. At that time, a certain monk and a novice were nursing a sick monk. While being nursed by them, that monk passed away. Then this thought occurred to the monk who had nursed the sick: “How should a share of the robes be given to the novice who nursed the sick?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, I allow an equal share to be given to the novice who nursed the sick.”

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu bahubhaṇḍo bahuparikkhāro kālaṅkato hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ. Bhikkhussa, bhikkhave, kālaṅkate saṅgho sāmī pattacīvare, api ca gilānupaṭṭhākā bahūpakārā. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, saṅghena ticīvarañca pattañca [M 0.0421] gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dātuṃ. Yaṃ tattha lahubhaṇḍaṃ lahuparikkhāraṃ taṃ sammukhībhūtena saṅghena bhājetuṃ. Yaṃ tattha garubhaṇḍaṃ garuparikkhāraṃ taṃ āgatānāgatassa cātuddisassa saṅghassa avissajjikaṃ avebhaṅgikanti.

At that time, a certain monk with many possessions and many requisites had passed away. They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, when a monk has passed away, the Saṅgha is the owner of his bowl and robes; but those who nurse the sick are very helpful. Monks, I allow the Saṅgha to give the set of three robes and the bowl to those who nurse the sick. Whatever light goods and light requisites there are, I allow that to be distributed by the Saṅgha that is present. Whatever heavy goods and heavy requisites there are, that belongs to the Saṅgha of the four directions, of those who have come and those who have not yet come; it is not to be relinquished and not to be divided.”

Matasantakakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Belongings of the Deceased is concluded.

226. Naggiyapaṭikkhepakathā

226. The Account of the Rejection of Nudity

370. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu naggo hutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “bhagavā, bhante, anekapariyāyena appicchassa santuṭṭhassa sallekhassa dhutassa pāsādikassa apacayassa vīriyārambhassa vaṇṇavādī. Idaṃ, bhante, naggiyaṃ anekapariyāyena appicchatāya santuṭṭhitāya sallekhāya dhutatāya dhutattāya (ka.) pāsādikatāya apacayāya vīriyārambhāya saṃvattati. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhūnaṃ naggiyaṃ anujānātū”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ, moghapurisa, ananulomikaṃ appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, naggiyaṃ titthiyasamādānaṃ samādiyissasi. Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe…” vigarahitvā dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, naggiyaṃ [T 2.0233] titthiyasamādānaṃ samādiyitabbaṃ. Yo samādiyeyya, āpatti thullaccayassā”ti.

370. At that time, a certain monk, being naked, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, the Blessed One in many ways speaks in praise of one who has few desires, is content, effaces defilements, shakes off defilements, is inspiring of confidence, diminishes defilements, and is of energetic striving. Venerable sir, this practice of nudity in many ways conduces to fewness of desires, to contentment, to the effacement of defilements, to the shaking off of defilements, to inspiring confidence, to the diminishing of defilements, and to energetic striving. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would permit the practice of nudity for the monks.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him: 'Worthless man, this is unsuitable, improper, unbecoming, not the conduct of a recluse, not allowable, and not to be done. How indeed, worthless man, can you undertake the practice of nudity, an observance of the sectarians? This, worthless man, is not for the inspiring of confidence in the uninspired... and so on...' Having rebuked him and given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: 'Monks, the practice of nudity, an observance of the sectarians, is not to be undertaken. Whoever should undertake it, commits an offense of grave transgression.'

Naggiyapaṭikkhepakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Rejection of Nudity is concluded.

227. Kusacīrādipaṭikkhepakathā

227. Account of the Rejection of Grass Robes and So Forth

371. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu kusacīraṃ nivāsetvā…pe… vākacīraṃ [V 0.0398] nivāsetvā…pe… phalakacīraṃ nivāsetvā…pe… kesakambalaṃ nivāsetvā…pe… vāḷakambalaṃ nivāsetvā…pe… ulūkapakkhaṃ nivāsetvā…pe… ajinakkhipaṃ nivāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “bhagavā, bhante, anekapariyāyena appicchassa santuṭṭhassa sallekhassa dhutassa pāsādikassa apacayassa vīriyārambhassa vaṇṇavādī. Idaṃ, bhante, ajinakkhipaṃ anekapariyāyena appicchatāya santuṭṭhitāya sallekhāya dhutatāya pāsādikatāya apacayāya vīriyārambhāya saṃvattati. Sādhu, bhante[P 1.0306], bhagavā bhikkhūnaṃ ajinakkhipaṃ anujānātū”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ, moghapurisa, ananulomikaṃ appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ [M 0.0422] akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, ajinakkhipaṃ titthiyadhajaṃ dhāressasi. Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, ajinakkhipaṃ titthiyadhajaṃ dhāretabbaṃ. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti thullaccayassā”ti.

371. At that time, a certain monk, having dressed in a grass robe… having dressed in a bark robe… having dressed in a robe of wood-strips… having dressed in a blanket of human hair… having dressed in a blanket of animal-tail hair… having dressed in an owl’s-wing robe… having dressed in a black antelope hide, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, the Blessed One in many ways speaks in praise of one who has few desires, is content, effaces defilements, shakes off defilements, is inspiring of confidence, diminishes defilements, and is of energetic striving. Venerable sir, this black antelope hide in many ways conduces to fewness of desires, to contentment, to the effacement of defilements, to the shaking off of defilements, to inspiring confidence, to the diminishing of defilements, and to energetic striving. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would permit the black antelope hide for the monks.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him: 'Worthless man, this is unsuitable, improper, unbecoming, not the conduct of a recluse, not allowable, and not to be done. How indeed, worthless man, can you wear the black antelope hide, the banner of sectarians? This, worthless man, is not for the inspiring of confidence in the uninspired…' Having rebuked him… having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: 'Monks, the black antelope hide, the banner of sectarians, is not to be worn. Whoever should wear it, commits an offense of grave transgression.'

Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu akkanāḷaṃ nivāsetvā…pe… potthakaṃ nivāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “bhagavā, bhante, anekapariyāyena appicchassa santuṭṭhassa sallekhassa dhutassa pāsādikassa apacayassa vīriyārambhassa, vaṇṇavādī. Ayaṃ, bhante, potthako anekapariyāyena appicchatāya [T 2.0234] santuṭṭhitāya sallekhāya dhutatāya pāsādikatāya apacayāya vīriyārambhāya saṃvattati. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhūnaṃ potthakaṃ anujānātū”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ, moghapurisa, ananulomikaṃ appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma tvaṃ, moghapurisa, potthakaṃ nivāsessasi. Netaṃ, moghapurisa, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, potthako nivāsetabbo. Yo nivāseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

At that time, a certain monk, having dressed in a garment of akka-stalk fiber…pe… having dressed in a bark-cloth, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, the Blessed One in many ways speaks in praise of one who has few desires, is content, effaces defilements, shakes off defilements, is inspiring of confidence, diminishes defilements, and is of energetic striving. Venerable sir, this bark-cloth in many ways conduces to fewness of desires, to contentment, to the effacement of defilements, to the shaking off of defilements, to inspiring confidence, to the diminishing of defilements, and to energetic striving. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would permit bark-cloth for the monks.' The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him: 'Worthless man, this is unsuitable, improper, unbecoming, not the conduct of a recluse, not allowable, and not to be done. How indeed, worthless man, could you wear a bark-cloth? This, worthless man, is not for the inspiring of confidence in the uninspired…pe…' Having rebuked him…pe… having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: 'Monks, a bark-cloth is not to be worn. Whoever should wear one, commits an offense of dukkaṭa.'

Kusacīrādipaṭikkhepakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Rejection of Grass Robes and So Forth is concluded.

228. Sabbanīlakādipaṭikkhepakathā

228. The Account of the Rejection of All-Blue Robes and the Like

372. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū sabbanīlakāni cīvarāni dhārenti…pe… sabbapītakāni cīvarāni dhārenti…pe… sabbalohitakāni cīvarāni dhārenti…pe… sabbamañjiṭṭhakāni sabbamañjeṭṭhakāni (sī. syā.) cīvarāni dhārenti…pe… sabbakaṇhāni cīvarāni dhārenti [V 0.0399] …pe… sabbamahāraṅgarattāni cīvarāni dhārenti…pe… sabbamahānāmarattāni cīvarāni dhārenti…pe… acchinnadasāni cīvarāni dhārenti…pe… dīghadasāni cīvarāni dhārenti…pe… pupphadasāni cīvarāni dhārenti…pe… phaṇadasāni phaladasāni (ka.) cīvarāni dhārenti…pe… kañcukaṃ dhārenti…pe… tirīṭakaṃ dhārenti…pe… veṭhanaṃ dhārenti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā veṭhanaṃ dhāressanti, seyyathāpi gihī kāmabhogino”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ[M 0.0423]. Na, bhikkhave, sabbanīlakāni cīvarāni dhāretabbāni, na sabbapītakāni cīvarāni dhāretabbāni, na sabbalohitakāni cīvarāni dhāretabbāni, na sabbamañjiṭṭhakāni cīvarāni dhāretabbāni, na sabbakaṇhāni cīvarāni dhāretabbāni, na sabbamahāraṅgarattāni cīvarāni dhāretabbāni, na [T 2.0235] sabbamahānāmarattāni cīvarāni dhāretabbāni, na acchinnadasāni cīvarāni dhāretabbāni, na dīghadasāni cīvarāni dhāretabbāni, na pupphadasāni cīvarāni dhāretabbāni, na phaṇadasāni cīvarāni dhāretabbāni, na kañcukaṃ dhāretabbaṃ, na tirīṭakaṃ dhāretabbaṃ, na veṭhanaṃ dhāretabbaṃ. Yo dhāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassāti.

372. At that time, the monks of the group of six wore robes that were entirely blue... entirely yellow... entirely red... entirely madder-colored... entirely black... dyed entirely with mahāraṅga dye... dyed entirely with mahānāmaratta dye... robes with uncut borders... with long borders... with flower-like borders... with cobra-hood-like borders... they wore jackets... robes of tirīṭa bark... and head-wraps. People complained, criticized, and spread disparaging remarks: “How can the Sakyan ascetics wear a head-wrap, just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures?” They reported this matter to the Blessed One. “Monks, robes that are entirely blue, entirely yellow, entirely red, entirely madder-colored, entirely black, dyed entirely with mahāraṅga dye, or dyed entirely with mahānāmaratta dye should not be worn; nor should robes with uncut borders, with long borders, with flower-like borders, or with cobra-hood-like borders be worn; nor should a jacket, a robe of tirīṭa bark, or a head-wrap be worn. Whoever should wear one, commits an offense of wrong-doing.”

Sabbanīlakādipaṭikkhepakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Rejection of All-Blue Robes and the Like is concluded.

229. Vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ anuppannacīvarakathā

229. The Account Concerning Robes Not Yet Arisen for Those Who Have Completed the Rains Residence

373. Tena kho pana samayena vassaṃvuṭṭhā bhikkhū anuppanne cīvare [P 1.0307] pakkamantipi, vibbhamantipi, kālampi karonti, sāmaṇerāpi paṭijānanti, sikkhaṃ paccakkhātakāpi paṭijānanti, antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannakāpi paṭijānanti, ummattakāpi paṭijānanti, khittacittāpi paṭijānanti, vedanāṭṭāpi paṭijānanti, āpattiyā adassane ukkhittakāpi paṭijānanti, āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittakāpi paṭijānanti, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittakāpi paṭijānanti, paṇḍakāpi paṭijānanti, theyyasaṃvāsakāpi paṭijānanti, titthiyapakkantakāpi paṭijānanti, tiracchānagatāpi paṭijānanti, mātughātakāpi paṭijānanti, pitughātakāpi paṭijānanti, arahantaghātakāpi paṭijānanti, bhikkhunidūsakāpi paṭijānanti, saṅghabhedakāpi paṭijānanti, lohituppādakāpi paṭijānanti, ubhatobyañjanakāpi paṭijānanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

373. At that time, monks who had completed the rains-residence, before a robe had arisen, departed, disrobed, or died. They also acknowledged being novices, those who have given up the training, those who have committed a final offense, the insane, those of deranged mind, those afflicted by pain, those suspended for not seeing an offense, those suspended for not making amends for an offense, those suspended for not relinquishing a wrong view, eunuchs, those in communion by theft, those who have gone over to another sect, animals, matricides, patricides, murderers of arahants, defilers of nuns, schismatics of the Saṅgha, those who have caused the Buddha's blood to flow, or hermaphrodites. They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

374. Idha [V 0.0400] pana, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭho bhikkhu anuppanne cīvare pakkamati, sante patirūpe gāhake dātabbaṃ.

374. Here, O monks, in this Teaching, if a monk who has completed the rains-residence departs before a robe has arisen, it should be given if there is a suitable recipient.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭho bhikkhu anuppanne cīvare vibbhamati, kālaṃ karoti, sāmaṇero paṭijānāti, sikkhaṃ paccakkhātako paṭijānāti[T 2.0236], antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannako paṭijānāti, saṅgho sāmī.

Here, O monks, in this Teaching, if a monk who has completed the rains-residence, before a robe has arisen, disrobes or dies, or acknowledges being a novice, one who has given up the training, or one who has committed a final offense, the Saṅgha is the owner.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭho bhikkhu anuppanne cīvare ummattako paṭijānāti, khittacitto paṭijānāti, vedanāṭṭo paṭijānāti, āpattiyā [M 0.0424] adassane ukkhittako paṭijānāti, āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittako paṭijānāti, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittako paṭijānāti, sante patirūpe gāhake dātabbaṃ.

Here, O monks, in this Teaching, if a monk who has completed the rains-residence, before a robe has arisen, acknowledges being insane, of deranged mind, afflicted by pain, suspended for not seeing an offense, suspended for not making amends for an offense, or suspended for not relinquishing a wrong view, it should be given if there is a suitable recipient.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭho bhikkhu anuppanne cīvare paṇḍako paṭijānāti, theyyasaṃvāsako paṭijānāti, titthiyapakkantako paṭijānāti, tiracchānagato paṭijānāti, mātughātako paṭijānāti, pitughātako paṭijānāti, arahantaghātako paṭijānāti, bhikkhunidūsako paṭijānāti, saṅghabhedako paṭijānāti, lohituppādako paṭijānāti, ubhatobyañjanako paṭijānāti, saṅgho sāmī.

Here, O monks, in this Teaching, if a monk who has completed the rains-residence, before a robe has arisen, confesses to being a paṇḍaka, or one who co-resides by theft, or one who has gone over to the ascetics of other views, or an animal, or a matricide, or a patricide, or a killer of an Arahant, or a defiler of a bhikkhunī, or a creator of schism in the Saṅgha, or one who has caused the Buddha's blood to flow, or an ubhatobyañjanaka, the Saṅgha is the owner.

375. Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭho bhikkhu uppanne cīvare abhājite pakkamati, sante patirūpe gāhake dātabbaṃ.

375. Here, O monks, in this Teaching, if a monk who has completed the rains-residence departs when a robe has arisen but has not yet been distributed, it should be given if there is a suitable recipient.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭho bhikkhu uppanne cīvare abhājite vibbhamati, kālaṃ karoti, sāmaṇero paṭijānāti, sikkhaṃ paccakkhātako paṭijānāti, antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannako paṭijānāti, saṅgho sāmī.

Here, O monks, in this Teaching, if a monk who has completed the rains-residence, when a robe has arisen but has not yet been distributed, disrobes, dies, confesses to being a novice, confesses to being one who has given up the training, or confesses to being one who has committed a final offense, the Saṅgha is the owner.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭho bhikkhu uppanne cīvare abhājite ummattako paṭijānāti. Khittacitto paṭijānāti, vedanāṭṭo paṭijānāti, āpattiyā adassane ukkhittako paṭijānāti, āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittako paṭijānāti, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittako paṭijānāti, sante patirūpe gāhake dātabbaṃ.
