Here, O monks, in this Teaching, if a monk who has completed the rains-residence, when a robe has arisen but has not yet been distributed, confesses to being insane, of deranged mind, afflicted by pain, one suspended for not seeing an offense, one suspended for not making amends for an offense, or one suspended for not relinquishing a wrong view, it should be given if there is a suitable recipient.

Idha [V 0.0401] pana, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭho bhikkhu uppanne cīvare abhājite paṇḍako paṭijānāti, theyyasaṃvāsako paṭijānāti, titthiyapakkantako paṭijānāti, tiracchānagato paṭijānāti, mātughātako paṭijānāti, pitughātako paṭijānāti, arahantaghātako paṭijānāti, bhikkhunidūsako paṭijānāti, saṅghabhedako paṭijānāti, lohituppādako paṭijānāti, ubhatobyañjanako paṭijānāti, saṅgho sāmī.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, if a bhikkhu who has completed the rains-residence, when a robe has arisen but has not yet been distributed, confesses to being a paṇḍaka, or one who co-resides by theft, or one who has gone over to the heretics, or an animal, or a matricide, or a patricide, or a killer of an Arahant, or a defiler of a bhikkhunī, or a creator of schism in the Saṅgha, or one who has caused the Buddha's blood to flow, or an ubhatobyañjanaka, the Saṅgha is the owner.

Vassaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ anuppannacīvarakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account Concerning Robes Not Yet Arisen for Those Who Have Completed the Rains-Residence is concluded.

230. Saṅghe bhinne cīvaruppādakathā

230. The Discourse on the Arising of Robes When the Saṅgha is Split

376. Idha [M 0.0425] pana, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ [T 2.0237] bhikkhūnaṃ anuppanne cīvare saṅgho bhijjati. Tattha manussā ekasmiṃ pakkhe udakaṃ denti, ekasmiṃ pakkhe cīvaraṃ denti – saṅghassa demāti. Saṅghassevetaṃ.

376. Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, before a robe has arisen for the bhikkhus who have completed the rains-residence, the Saṅgha splits. In that situation, people give water to one faction and a robe to another faction, thinking, 'We give to the Saṅgha.' This belongs to the Saṅgha.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anuppanne cīvare saṅgho bhijjati. Tattha manussā ekasmiṃ pakkhe udakaṃ denti, tasmiṃyeva pakkhe cīvaraṃ denti – saṅghassa [P 1.0308] demāti. Saṅghassevetaṃ.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, before a robe has arisen for the bhikkhus who have completed the rains-residence, the Saṅgha splits. In that situation, people give water to one faction and a robe to that same faction, thinking, 'We give to the Saṅgha.' This belongs to the Saṅgha.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anuppanne cīvare saṅgho bhijjati. Tattha manussā ekasmiṃ pakkhe udakaṃ denti, ekasmiṃ pakkhe cīvaraṃ denti – pakkhassa demāti. Pakkhassevetaṃ.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, before a robe has arisen for the bhikkhus who have completed the rains-residence, the Saṅgha splits. In that situation, people give water to one faction and a robe to another faction, thinking, 'We give to the faction.' This belongs to that faction alone.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anuppanne cīvare saṅgho bhijjati. Tattha manussā ekasmiṃ pakkhe udakaṃ denti, tasmiṃyeva pakkhe cīvaraṃ denti – pakkhassa demāti. Pakkhassevetaṃ.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, before a robe has arisen for the bhikkhus who have completed the rains-residence, the Saṅgha splits. In that situation, people give water to one faction and a robe to that same faction, thinking, 'We give to the faction.' This belongs to that faction alone.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ uppanne cīvare abhājite saṅgho bhijjati. Sabbesaṃ samakaṃ bhājetabbanti.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, when a robe has arisen for the bhikkhus who have completed the rains-residence but has not been distributed, the Saṅgha splits. It should be distributed equally among all.

Saṅghe bhinne cīvaruppādakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Arising of Robes When the Saṅgha is Split is Concluded.

231. Duggahitasuggahitādikathā

231. The Discourse on Improper and Proper Taking, and so forth

377. Tena [V 0.0402] kho pana samayena āyasmā revato aññatarassa bhikkhuno hatthe āyasmato sāriputtassa cīvaraṃ pāhesi – “imaṃ cīvaraṃ therassa dehī”ti. Atha kho so bhikkhu antarāmagge āyasmato revatassa vissāsā taṃ cīvaraṃ aggahesi. Atha kho āyasmā revato āyasmatā sāriputtena samāgantvā pucchi – “ahaṃ, bhante, therassa cīvaraṃ pāhesiṃ. Sampattaṃ taṃ cīvara”nti? “Nāhaṃ taṃ, āvuso, cīvaraṃ passāmī”ti. Atha kho āyasmā revato taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “ahaṃ, āvuso[T 2.0238], āyasmato hatthe therassa cīvaraṃ pāhesiṃ. Kahaṃ taṃ cīvara”nti? “Ahaṃ, bhante, āyasmato vissāsā taṃ cīvaraṃ aggahesi”nti. Bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ.

377. Now at that time, the Venerable Revata sent a robe for the Venerable Sāriputta in the care of a certain bhikkhu, saying, 'Give this robe to the Elder.' Then that bhikkhu, on the way, took that robe out of familiarity with the Venerable Revata. Then the Venerable Revata, having met with the Venerable Sāriputta, asked, 'Venerable sir, I sent a robe for the Elder. Has that robe arrived?' 'Friend, I have not seen that robe.' Then the Venerable Revata said this to that bhikkhu, 'Friend, I sent a robe for the Elder in your care. Where is that robe?' 'Venerable sir, out of familiarity with the Venerable one, I took that robe.' They reported this matter to the Blessed One.

378. Idha [M 0.0426] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhikkhussa hatthe cīvaraṃ pahiṇati – “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dehī”ti. So antarāmagge yo pahiṇati tassa vissāsā gaṇhāti. Suggahitaṃ. Yassa pahiyyati tassa vissāsā gaṇhāti. Duggahitaṃ.

378. Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, a bhikkhu sends a robe in the care of another bhikkhu, saying, 'Give this robe to the one with such-and-such a name.' If, on the way, the messenger takes it out of familiarity with the one who sends it, it is properly taken. If he takes it out of familiarity with the one to whom it is sent, it is improperly taken.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhikkhussa hatthe cīvaraṃ pahiṇati – “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dehī”ti. So antarāmagge yassa pahiyyati tassa vissāsā gaṇhāti. Duggahitaṃ. Yo pahiṇati tassa vissāsā gaṇhāti. Suggahitaṃ.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, a bhikkhu sends a robe in the care of another bhikkhu, saying, 'Give this robe to the one with such-and-such a name.' If, on the way, the messenger takes it out of familiarity with the one to whom it is sent, it is improperly taken. If he takes it out of familiarity with the one who sends it, it is properly taken.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhikkhussa hatthe cīvaraṃ pahiṇati – “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dehī”ti. So antarāmagge suṇāti – yo pahiṇati so kālaṅkatoti. Tassa matakacīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhāti. Svādhiṭṭhitaṃ. Yassa pahiyyati tassa vissāsā gaṇhāti. Duggahitaṃ.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, a bhikkhu sends a robe in the care of another bhikkhu, saying, 'Give this robe to the one with such-and-such a name.' If, on the way, the messenger hears, 'The one who sent it has passed away,' he should determine it as a robe of the deceased. This is a proper determination. If he takes it out of familiarity with the one to whom it is sent, it is improperly taken.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhikkhussa hatthe cīvaraṃ pahiṇati – “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dehī”ti. So antarāmagge suṇāti – yassa pahiyyati so kālaṅkatoti. Tassa matakacīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhāti. Dvādhiṭṭhitaṃ. Yo pahiṇati tassa vissāsā gaṇhāti. Suggahitaṃ.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, a bhikkhu sends a robe in the care of another bhikkhu, saying, 'Give this robe to the one with such-and-such a name.' If, on the way, the messenger hears, 'The one to whom it was sent has passed away,' and he determines it as the robe of that deceased one, this is an improper determination. If he takes it out of familiarity with the one who sends it, it is properly taken.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhikkhussa hatthe cīvaraṃ pahiṇati – “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dehī”ti. So [P 1.0309] antarāmagge suṇāti – ubho kālaṅkatāti. Yo pahiṇati tassa matakacīvaraṃ [V 0.0403] adhiṭṭhāti. Svādhiṭṭhitaṃ. Yassa pahiyyati [T 2.0239] tassa matakacīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhāti. Dvādhiṭṭhitaṃ.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, a bhikkhu sends a robe in the care of another bhikkhu, saying, 'Give this robe to the one with such-and-such a name.' If, on the way, the messenger hears, 'Both have passed away,' and he determines it as the robe of the deceased who sent it, this is a proper determination. If he determines it as the robe of the deceased to whom it was sent, this is an improper determination.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhikkhussa hatthe cīvaraṃ pahiṇati – “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dammī”ti. So antarāmagge yo pahiṇati tassa vissāsā gaṇhāti. Duggahitaṃ. Yassa pahiyyati tassa vissāsā gaṇhāti. Suggahitaṃ.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, a bhikkhu sends a robe in the care of another bhikkhu, saying, 'I give this robe to the one with such-and-such a name.' If, on the way, the messenger takes it out of familiarity with the one who sent it, it is improperly taken. If he takes it out of familiarity with the one to whom it was sent, it is properly taken.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhikkhussa hatthe cīvaraṃ pahiṇati – “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dammī”ti. So antarāmagge yassa pahiyyati tassa vissāsā gaṇhāti. Suggahitaṃ. Yo pahiṇati tassa vissāsā gaṇhāti. Duggahitaṃ.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, a bhikkhu sends a robe in the care of another bhikkhu, saying, 'I give this robe to the one with such-and-such a name.' If, on the way, the messenger takes it out of familiarity with the one to whom it was sent, it is properly taken. If he takes it out of familiarity with the one who sent it, it is improperly taken.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhikkhussa hatthe cīvaraṃ pahiṇati – “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dammī”ti. So antarāmagge suṇāti – “yo pahiṇati so [M 0.0427] kālaṅkato”ti. Tassa matakacīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhāti. Dvādhiṭṭhitaṃ. Yassa pahiyyati tassa vissāsā gaṇhāti. Suggahitaṃ.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, a bhikkhu sends a robe in the care of another bhikkhu, saying, 'I give this robe to the one with such-and-such a name.' If, on the way, the messenger hears, 'The one who sent it has passed away,' and he determines it as the robe of that deceased one, this is an improper determination. If he takes it out of familiarity with the one to whom it was sent, it is properly taken.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhikkhussa hatthe cīvaraṃ pahiṇati – “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dammī”ti. So antarāmagge suṇāti – “yassa pahiyyati so kālaṅkato”ti. Tassa matakacīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhāti. Svādhiṭṭhitaṃ. Yo pahiṇati tassa vissāsā gaṇhāti. Duggahitaṃ.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, in this Teaching, a bhikkhu sends a robe by the hand of another bhikkhu, saying, 'I give this robe to the venerable one of such-and-such a name.' While on the way, that bhikkhu hears, 'The one to whom it was being sent has passed away.' If he determines it as a robe of the deceased, it is well-determined. If he takes it through familiarity with the one who sent it, it is wrongly taken.

Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhikkhussa hatthe cīvaraṃ pahiṇati – “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dammī”ti. So antarāmagge suṇāti “ubho kālaṅkatā”ti. Yo pahiṇati tassa matakacīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhāti. Dvādhiṭṭhitaṃ. Yassa pahiyyati tassa matakacīvaraṃ adhiṭṭhāti. Svādhiṭṭhitaṃ.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, in this Teaching, a bhikkhu sends a robe by the hand of another bhikkhu, saying, 'I give this robe to the venerable one of such-and-such a name.' While on the way, that bhikkhu hears, 'Both have passed away.' If he determines it as the robe of the deceased who sent it, it is wrongly determined. If he determines it as the robe of the deceased to whom it was being sent, it is well-determined.

Duggahitasuggahitādikathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on what is wrongly taken and well-taken is concluded.

232. Aṭṭhacīvaramātikā

232. The Eight Headings on Robes

379. Aṭṭhimā[V 0.0404], bhikkhave, mātikā cīvarassa uppādāya – sīmāya deti[T 2.0240], katikāya deti, bhikkhāpaññattiyā deti, saṅghassa deti, ubhatosaṅghassa deti, vassaṃvuṭṭhasaṅghassa deti, ādissa deti, puggalassa deti.

379. Bhikkhus, these are the eight headings for the arising of robes: one gives for a boundary, one gives for an agreement, one gives for an established meal offering, one gives to the Saṅgha, one gives to the double Saṅgha, one gives to the Saṅgha that has completed the rains-residence, one gives by dedicating, one gives to an individual.

Sīmāya deti – yāvatikā bhikkhū antosīmagatā tehi bhājetabbaṃ. Katikāya deti – sambahulā āvāsā samānalābhā honti ekasmiṃ āvāse dinne sabbattha dinnaṃ hoti. Bhikkhāpaññattiyā deti, yattha saṅghassa dhuvakārā kariyyanti, tattha deti. Saṅghassa deti, sammukhībhūtena saṅghena bhājetabbaṃ. Ubhatosaṅghassa deti, bahukāpi bhikkhū honti, ekā bhikkhunī hoti, upaḍḍhaṃ dātabbaṃ, bahukāpi bhikkhuniyo honti, eko bhikkhu hoti, upaḍḍhaṃ dātabbaṃ. Vassaṃvuṭṭhasaṅghassa deti, yāvatikā bhikkhū tasmiṃ āvāse vassaṃvuṭṭhā, tehi bhājetabbaṃ. Ādissa deti, yāguyā vā bhatte vā khādanīye vā cīvare vā senāsane vā bhesajje vā[P 1.0310]. Puggalassa deti, “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dammī”ti.

One gives for a boundary: it should be divided among whichever bhikkhus are within that boundary. One gives for an agreement: where many monasteries have an equal share of gains, when a gift is given in one monastery, it is considered given everywhere. One gives for an established meal offering: one gives where permanent offerings are made to the Saṅgha. One gives to the Saṅgha: it should be divided by the Saṅgha that is present. One gives to the double Saṅgha: if there are many bhikkhus and one bhikkhunī, half should be given; if there are many bhikkhunīs and one bhikkhu, half should be given. One gives to the Saṅgha that has completed the rains-residence: it should be divided among whichever bhikkhus have completed the rains-residence in that monastery. One gives by dedicating: for gruel, or for a meal, or for edibles, or for a robe, or for lodging, or for medicine. One gives to an individual, saying: 'I give this robe to the venerable one of such-and-such a name.'

Aṭṭhacīvaramātikā niṭṭhitā.

The Eight Headings on Robes are concluded.

Cīvarakkhandhako aṭṭhamo.

The Eighth Chapter on Robes.

233. Tassuddānaṃ

233. The Summary Thereof

Rājagahako [M 0.0428] negamo, disvā vesāliyaṃ gaṇiṃ;

Puna rājagahaṃ gantvā, rañño taṃ paṭivedayi.

A merchant from Rājagaha, having seen a courtesan in Vesālī, went again to Rājagaha and informed the king about her.

Putto [T 2.0241] sālavatikāya, abhayassa hi atrajo;

Jīvatīti kumārena, saṅkhāto jīvako iti.

The son of Sālavatī, who was indeed the natural son of Abhaya, was named Jīvaka because the prince asked, 'Does he live?'

So hi takkasīlaṃ gantvā, uggahetvā mahābhiso;

Sattavassikaābādhaṃ, natthukammena nāsayi.

Indeed, having gone to Takkasilā and studied, he became a great physician; he cured a seven-year illness with a nasal treatment.

Rañño [V 0.0405] bhagandalābādhaṃ, ālepena apākaḍḍhi;

Mamañca itthāgārañca, buddhasaṅghaṃ cupaṭṭhahi.

He cured the king's fistula with an ointment and attended to me, the women's quarters, and the Saṅgha headed by the Buddha.

Rājagahako ca seṭṭhi, antagaṇṭhi tikicchitaṃ;

Pajjotassa mahārogaṃ, ghatapānena nāsayi.

He treated the merchant of Rājagaha and one with an intestinal knot; he cured the great disease of Pajjota by administering ghee.

Adhikārañca siveyyaṃ, abhisannaṃ sinehati;

Tīhi uppalahatthehi, samattiṃsavirecanaṃ.

A service and a Siveyya cloth; anointing an afflicted one; with three handfuls of lotuses, a thirty-fold purgative.

Pakatattaṃ varaṃ yāci, siveyyañca paṭiggahi;

Cīvarañca gihidānaṃ, anuññāsi tathāgato.

He requested a boon from the one restored to health; the Tathāgata accepted the Siveyya cloth and permitted robes given by householders.

Rājagahe janapade bahuṃ, uppajji cīvaraṃ;

Pāvāro kosiyañceva, kojavo aḍḍhakāsikaṃ.

In Rājagaha and the countryside, many robes arose; cloaks, silk cloth, woolen blankets, and a blanket worth five hundred.

Uccāvacā ca santuṭṭhi, nāgamesāgamesuṃ ca;

Paṭhamaṃ pacchā sadisā, katikā ca paṭiharuṃ.

Robes of high and low quality, and contentment; not waiting and waiting; first, later, together; an agreement; and taking robes back.

Bhaṇḍāgāraṃ aguttañca, vuṭṭhāpenti tatheva ca;

Ussannaṃ kolāhalañca, kathaṃ bhāje kathaṃ dade.

A storeroom, and it being unguarded; they appoint a storekeeper; likewise, abundant robes and an uproar: 'How to divide? How to give?'

Sakātirekabhāgena, paṭivīso kathaṃ dade;

Chakaṇena [T 2.0242] sītudakā sītundī ca (sī.), sītuṇhi ca (katthaci), uttaritu na jānare.

With one's own extra share; how to give a portion; with cow-dung and cold water, they did not know how to complete the dyeing.

Āropentā bhājanañca, pātiyā ca chamāya ca;

Upacikāmajjhe jīranti, ekato patthinnena ca.

Placing dye in a vessel, a bowl, and on the ground; termites; wearing out in the middle; and being stiff on one side.

Pharusācchinnacchibandhā[M 0.0429], addasāsi ubbhaṇḍite;

Vīmaṃsitvā sakyamuni, anuññāsi ticīvaraṃ.

Rough and uncut robes, and the pattern of rice paddies; he saw bundled-up robes; having investigated, the Sakyan Sage permitted the three robes.

Aññena [V 0.0406] atirekena, uppajji chiddameva ca;

Cātuddīpo varaṃ yāci, dātuṃ vassikasāṭikaṃ.

Another robe, an extra one, and a torn one arose; the 'Four-Continents' one requested the boon to give the rains-cloth.

Āgantugamigilānaṃ, upaṭṭhākañca bhesajjaṃ;

Dhuvaṃ udakasāṭiñca, paṇītaṃ atikhuddakaṃ.

For the incoming, outgoing, and sick; for an attendant, and medicine; constant food, and a bathing cloth; fine food, and a very small sitting-cloth.

Thullakacchumukhaṃ khomaṃ, paripuṇṇaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ;

Pacchimaṃ kato garuko, vikaṇṇo suttamokiri.

A severe skin disease, a face-cloth, linen; being complete, determination; the smallest robe, a heavy made-robe; uneven corners, and a loose thread.

Lujjanti [P 1.0311] nappahonti, ca anvādhikaṃ bahūni ca;

Andhavane assatiyā, eko vassaṃ utumhi ca.

They are destroyed and are not sufficient; a coverlet and many robes; in the Andhavana forest, due to forgetfulness; spending the rains-residence alone, and in season.

Dve bhātukā rājagahe, upanando puna dvisu;

Kucchivikāro gilāno, ubho ceva gilānakā gilāyanā (ka.).

Two brothers in Rājagaha; Upananda again with two; a sick one with a stomach ailment; and both attending to the sick.

Naggā kusā vākacīraṃ, phalako kesakambalaṃ;

Vāḷaulūkapakkhañca, ajinaṃ akkanāḷakaṃ.

Nakedness; garments of kusa grass, bark, wood shavings, human hair, horse-tail hair, owl's wings, animal hide, and `akka` plant fibers.

Potthakaṃ nīlapītañca, lohitaṃ mañjiṭṭhena ca;

Kaṇhā mahāraṅganāma, acchinnadasikā tathā.

A garment of woven bark; robes all blue, yellow, red, and crimson; black, and one named Mahāraṅga; likewise, a robe with an uncut border.

Dīghapupphaphaṇadasā[T 2.0243], kañcutirīṭaveṭhanaṃ;

Anuppanne pakkamati, saṅgho bhijjati tāvade.

Long fringes, flower fringes, and snake-hood fringes; a tunic, a bark-cloth garment, and a turban; departing before a robe arises; the Saṅgha splits before that.

Pakkhe dadanti saṅghassa, āyasmā revato pahi;

Vissāsagāhādhiṭṭhāti, aṭṭha cīvaramātikāti.

Giving to the Saṅgha in one faction; the venerable Revata sent a robe; taking through familiarity, and determination; the eight headings on robes.

Imamhi khandhake vatthū channavuti.

In this chapter, there are ninety-six stories.

Cīvarakkhandhako niṭṭhito.

The Chapter on Robes is concluded.

9. Campeyyakkhandhako

9. The Chapter on Campeyya

234. Kassapagottabhikkhuvatthu

234. The Story of the Bhikkhu Kassapagotta

380. Tena [P 1.0312][M 0.0430][V 0.0407][T 2.0244] samayena buddho bhagavā campāyaṃ viharati gaggarāya pokkharaṇiyā tīre. Tena kho pana samayena kāsīsu janapade vāsabhagāmo nāma hoti. Tattha kassapagotto nāma bhikkhu āvāsiko hoti tantibaddho ussukkaṃ āpanno – kinti anāgatā ca pesalā bhikkhū āgaccheyyuṃ, āgatā ca pesalā bhikkhū phāsu vihareyyuṃ, ayañca āvāso vuddhiṃ viruḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjeyyāti. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū kāsīsu cārikaṃ caramānā yena vāsabhagāmo tadavasaruṃ. Addasā kho kassapagotto bhikkhu te bhikkhū dūratova āgacchante, disvāna āsanaṃ paññapesi, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipi, paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahesi, pānīyena āpucchi, nahāne ussukkaṃ akāsi, ussukkampi akāsi yāguyā khādanīye bhattasmiṃ. Atha kho tesaṃ āgantukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “bhaddako kho ayaṃ, āvuso, āvāsiko bhikkhu nahāne ussukkaṃ karoti, ussukkampi karoti yāguyā khādanīye bhattasmiṃ. Handa, mayaṃ, āvuso, idheva vāsabhagāme nivāsaṃ kappemā”ti. Atha kho te āgantukā bhikkhū tattheva vāsabhagāme nivāsaṃ kappesuṃ.

380. At that time the Blessed One, the Buddha, was dwelling at Campā on the bank of the Gaggarā Pond. Now at that time, in the country of Kāsī, there was a village named Vāsabhagāma. There, a monk named Kassapagotta was the resident incumbent. He was occupied with his duties and zealous, thinking: “How might virtuous monks who have not yet come, arrive? And how might the virtuous monks who have come, dwell comfortably? And how might this residence attain growth, increase, and expansion?” Now at that time, many monks, while wandering on tour in the Kāsī country, arrived at Vāsabhagāma. The monk Kassapagotta saw those monks coming from afar. Having seen them, he prepared seats, and placed nearby water for washing the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet. Having gone out to meet them, he received their bowl and robe, and inquired about drinking water. He made an effort concerning their bathing, and he also made an effort concerning gruel, solid food, and the meal. Then this thought occurred to those visiting monks: “Friends, this resident monk is a good man. He makes an effort concerning our bathing, and he also makes an effort concerning gruel, solid food, and the meal. Come now, friends, let us take up residence right here in Vāsabhagāma.” Then those visiting monks took up residence right there in Vāsabhagāma.

Atha kho kassapagottassa bhikkhuno etadahosi – “yo kho imesaṃ [T 2.0245] āgantukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āgantukakilamatho so paṭippassaddho. Yepime gocare appakataññuno tedānime gocare pakataññuno. Dukkaraṃ kho pana parakulesu yāvajīvaṃ ussukkaṃ kātuṃ, viññatti ca manussānaṃ amanāpā. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ na ussukkaṃ kareyyaṃ yāguyā khādanīye bhattasmi”nti. So na ussukkaṃ akāsi yāguyā khādanīye bhattasmiṃ. Atha kho tesaṃ āgantukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ [P 1.0313] etadahosi – “pubbe khvāyaṃ, āvuso, āvāsiko bhikkhu nahāne ussukkaṃ akāsi, ussukkampi akāsi yāguyā khādanīye bhattasmiṃ. Sodānāyaṃ na ussukkaṃ karoti yāguyā khādanīye bhattasmiṃ. Duṭṭhodānāyaṃ, āvuso, āvāsiko bhikkhu. Handa, mayaṃ, āvuso, āvāsikaṃ [V 0.0408] imaṃ āvāsikaṃ (syā.) bhikkhuṃ ukkhipāmā”ti. Atha kho te [M 0.0431] āgantukā bhikkhū sannipatitvā kassapagottaṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavocuṃ – “pubbe kho tvaṃ, āvuso, nahāne ussukkaṃ karosi, ussukkampi karosi yāguyā khādanīye bhattasmiṃ. Sodāni tvaṃ na ussukkaṃ karosi yāguyā khādanīye bhattasmiṃ. Āpattiṃ tvaṃ, āvuso, āpanno. Passasetaṃ āpatti”nti? “Natthi me, āvuso, āpatti, yamahaṃ passeyya”nti. Atha kho te āgantukā bhikkhū kassapagottaṃ bhikkhuṃ āpattiyā adassane ukkhipiṃsu.

Then the monk Kassapagotta thought: 'The fatigue of these visiting monks is now calmed. Those who were previously unacquainted with my alms-resort are now acquainted with it. Indeed, it is difficult to make an effort in others' families for one's whole life, and requesting is displeasing to people. What if I were not to make an effort regarding gruel, solid food, and the meal?' So he did not make an effort regarding gruel, solid food, and the meal. Then those visiting monks thought: 'Friends, previously this resident monk made an effort regarding bathing, and he also made an effort regarding gruel, solid food, and the meal. But now he does not make an effort regarding gruel, solid food, and the meal. Friends, this resident monk is now corrupt. Come, friends, let us suspend the resident monk.' Then those visiting monks, having assembled, said this to the monk Kassapagotta: 'Friend, previously you made an effort regarding bathing, and you also made an effort regarding gruel, solid food, and the meal. But now you do not make an effort regarding gruel, solid food, and the meal. You have fallen into an offense, friend. See that offense.' 'Friends, there is no offense for me that I should see.' Then those visiting monks suspended the monk Kassapagotta for not seeing the offense.

Atha kho kassapagottassa bhikkhuno etadahosi – “ahaṃ kho etaṃ na jānāmi ‘āpatti vā esā anāpatti vā, āpanno camhi vamhi (?) anāpanno vā, ukkhitto camhi [T 2.0246] anukkhitto vā, dhammikena vā adhammikena vā, kuppena vā akuppena vā, ṭhānārahena vā aṭṭhānārahena vā’. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ campaṃ gantvā bhagavantaṃ etamatthaṃ puccheyya”nti. Atha kho kassapagotto bhikkhu senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena campā tena pakkāmi. Anupubbena yena campā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Āciṇṇaṃ kho panetaṃ buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ āgantukehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ paṭisammodituṃ. Atha kho bhagavā kassapagottaṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “kacci, bhikkhu, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kacci appakilamathena addhānaṃ āgato, kuto ca tvaṃ, bhikkhu, āgacchasī”ti? “Khamanīyaṃ, bhagavā; yāpanīyaṃ, bhagavā; appakilamathena cāhaṃ, bhante, addhānaṃ āgato. Atthi, bhante, kāsīsu janapade vāsabhagāmo nāma. Tatthāhaṃ, bhagavā, āvāsiko tantibaddho ussukkaṃ āpanno – ‘kinti anāgatā ca pesalā bhikkhū āgaccheyyuṃ, āgatā ca pesalā bhikkhū phāsu vihareyyuṃ, ayañca āvāso vuddhiṃ viruḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjeyyā’ti. Atha kho, bhante, sambahulā bhikkhū kāsīsu cārikaṃ caramānā yena vāsabhagāmo tadavasaruṃ. Addasaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, te bhikkhū dūratova āgacchante, disvāna āsanaṃ paññapesiṃ, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipiṃ, paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahesiṃ, pānīyena apucchiṃ, nahāne ussukkaṃ akāsiṃ, ussukkampi akāsiṃ yāguyā khādanīye bhattasmiṃ[T 2.0247]. Atha kho tesaṃ, bhante, āgantukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – ‘bhaddako kho [M 0.0432] ayaṃ āvuso āvāsiko bhikkhu nahāne ussukkaṃ karoti, ussukkampi karoti yāguyā khādanīye bhattasmiṃ. Handa, mayaṃ, āvuso, idheva vāsabhagāme nivāsaṃ kappemā’ti. Atha kho [P 1.0314] te, bhante, āgantukā bhikkhū tattheva vāsabhagāme nivāsaṃ kappesuṃ. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘yo kho imesaṃ āgantukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āgantukakilamatho so paṭippassaddho. Yepime gocare appakataññuno tedānime gocare pakataññuno. Dukkaraṃ kho pana parakulesu [V 0.0409] yāvajīvaṃ ussukkaṃ kātuṃ, viññatti ca manussānaṃ amanāpā. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ na ussukkaṃ kareyyaṃ yāguyā khādanīye bhattasmi’nti. So kho ahaṃ, bhante, na ussukkaṃ akāsiṃ yāguyā khādanīye bhattasmiṃ. Atha kho tesaṃ, bhante, āgantukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – ‘pubbe khvāyaṃ, āvuso, āvāsiko bhikkhu nahāne ussukkaṃ karoti, ussukkampi karoti yāguyā khādanīye bhattasmiṃ. Sodānāyaṃ na ussukkaṃ karoti yāguyā khādanīye bhattasmiṃ. Duṭṭhodānāyaṃ, āvuso, āvāsiko bhikkhu. Handa, mayaṃ, āvuso, āvāsikaṃ bhikkhuṃ ukkhipāmā’ti. Atha kho te, bhante, āgantukā bhikkhū sannipatitvā maṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘pubbe kho tvaṃ, āvuso, nahāne ussukkaṃ karosi, ussukkampi karosi yāguyā khādanīye bhattasmiṃ. Sodāni tvaṃ na ussukkaṃ karosi yāguyā khādanīye bhattasmiṃ. Āpattiṃ tvaṃ, āvuso, āpanno. Passasetaṃ āpatti’nti[T 2.0248]? ‘Natthi me, āvuso, āpatti yamahaṃ passeyya’nti. Atha kho te, bhante, āgantukā bhikkhū maṃ āpattiyā adassane ukkhipiṃsu. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘ahaṃ kho etaṃ na jānāmi ‘āpatti vā esā anāpatti vā, āpanno camhi anāpanno vā, ukkhitto camhi anukkhitto vā, dhammikena vā adhammikena vā, kuppena vā akuppena vā, ṭhānārahena vā aṭṭhānārahena vā’. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ campaṃ gantvā bhagavantaṃ etamatthaṃ puccheyya’nti. Tato ahaṃ, bhagavā, āgacchāmī”ti. “Anāpatti esā, bhikkhu, nesā āpatti. Anāpannosi, nasi āpanno. Anukkhittosi, nasi ukkhitto. Adhammikenāsi kammena ukkhitto kuppena aṭṭhānārahena. Gaccha tvaṃ, bhikkhu, tattheva vāsabhagāme nivāsaṃ kappehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho kassapagotto bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissuṇitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā yena vāsabhagāmo tena pakkāmi.

Then the monk Kassapagotta thought: 'I do not know whether this is an offense or not, whether I have committed an offense or not, whether I have been suspended or not, whether by a lawful or an unlawful act, by a revocable or an irrevocable act, or by a justifiable or an unjustifiable act. What if I were to go to Campā and ask the Blessed One about this matter?' Then the monk Kassapagotta, having set his lodging in order and taken his bowl and robe, set out for Campā. Traveling in stages, he went to where Campā and the Blessed One were. Having approached the Blessed One and paid homage, he sat down to one side. Now, it is the custom for the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, to exchange friendly greetings with visiting monks. Then the Blessed One said this to the monk Kassapagotta: 'Monk, are you keeping well? Are you managing? Did you travel the long road with little fatigue? And from where, monk, do you come?' 'I am keeping well, Blessed One; I am managing, Blessed One. And I have traveled the long road with little fatigue, venerable sir. Venerable sir, in the country of the Kāsīs there is a village named Vāsabhagāma. There, Blessed One, I was the resident monk, bound by my duties and making an effort, thinking: "How might virtuous monks who have not yet come, arrive? And how might the virtuous monks who have come dwell in comfort? And how might this residence attain growth, increase, and expansion?" Then, venerable sir, many monks, while wandering on tour in the Kāsī country, arrived at Vāsabhagāma. I saw those monks coming from afar, venerable sir, and having seen them, I prepared a seat; I set out water for the feet, a footstool, and a foot-scraper; I went to meet them and took their bowls and robes; I inquired about water for drinking; I made an effort regarding their bathing; and I also made an effort regarding gruel, solid food, and the meal. Then, venerable sir, this thought occurred to those visiting monks: "Friends, this resident monk is a good man. He makes an effort regarding our bathing, and he also makes an effort regarding gruel, solid food, and the meal. Come, friends, let us take up residence right here in Vāsabhagāma." Then, venerable sir, those visiting monks took up residence right there in Vāsabhagāma. Then, venerable sir, this thought occurred to me: "The travel-fatigue of these visiting monks has now subsided. Those who were unacquainted with my alms-resort are now acquainted with it. But it is difficult to make an effort for other families for one's whole life, and requests are disagreeable to people. What if I were not to make an effort regarding gruel, solid food, and the meal?" So, venerable sir, I did not make an effort regarding gruel, solid food, and the meal. Then, venerable sir, this thought occurred to those visiting monks: "Friends, previously this resident monk made an effort regarding our bathing, and he also made an effort regarding gruel, solid food, and the meal. But now he does not make an effort regarding gruel, solid food, and the meal. This resident monk has now become corrupt. Come, friends, let us suspend the resident monk." Then, venerable sir, those visiting monks assembled and said this to me: "Friend, previously you made an effort regarding our bathing, and you also made an effort regarding gruel, solid food, and the meal. But now you do not make an effort regarding gruel, solid food, and the meal. Friend, you have committed an offense. Do you see that offense?" "Friends, I have no offense that I should see." Then, venerable sir, those visiting monks suspended me for not seeing an offense. Then, venerable sir, this thought occurred to me: 'I do not know whether this is an offense or not, whether I have committed an offense or not, whether I have been suspended or not, whether by a lawful or an unlawful act, by a revocable or an irrevocable act, or by a justifiable or an unjustifiable act. What if I were to go to Campā and ask the Blessed One about this matter?' It is from there, Blessed One, that I come.' 'This is a non-offense, monk; it is not an offense. You have not committed an offense; you are not one who has committed an offense. You have not been suspended; you are not one who has been suspended. You have been suspended by an unlawful, revocable, and unjustifiable act. Go, monk, and take up residence right there in Vāsabhagāma.' 'Yes, venerable sir.' The monk Kassapagotta, having assented to the Blessed One, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping his right side toward him, and set out for Vāsabhagāma.

381. Atha [M 0.0433] kho tesaṃ āgantukānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ahudeva kukkuccaṃ, ahu vippaṭisāro – “alābhā vata no, na vata no lābhā, dulladdhaṃ vata no, na vata no suladdhaṃ, ye mayaṃ suddhaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpattikaṃ avatthusmiṃ akāraṇe ukkhipimhā. Handa, mayaṃ, āvuso, campaṃ gantvā bhagavato santike accayaṃ accayato desemā”ti. Atha kho te āgantukā bhikkhū senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena campā tena pakkamiṃsu. Anupubbena [T 2.0249] yena campā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Āciṇṇaṃ kho panetaṃ buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ āgantukehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ paṭisammodituṃ. Atha kho bhagavā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “kacci, bhikkhave, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kaccittha appakilamathena addhānaṃ āgatā, kuto ca tumhe, bhikkhave, āgacchathā”ti[V 0.0410]? “Khamanīyaṃ, bhagavā; yāpanīyaṃ, bhagavā; appakilamathena ca mayaṃ, bhante, addhānaṃ āgatā. Atthi, bhante, kāsīsu janapade vāsabhagāmo nāma. Tato mayaṃ, bhagavā, āgacchāmā”ti. “Tumhe, bhikkhave, āvāsikaṃ bhikkhuṃ ukkhipitthā”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”ti. “Kismiṃ, bhikkhave, vatthusmiṃ kāraṇe”ti? “Avatthusmiṃ, bhagavā, akāraṇe”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ, moghapurisā, ananulomikaṃ [P 1.0315] appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma tumhe, moghapurisā, suddhaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpattikaṃ avatthusmiṃ akāraṇe ukkhipissatha. Netaṃ, moghapurisā, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe…” vigarahitvā dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “na, bhikkhave, suddho bhikkhu anāpattiko avatthusmiṃ akāraṇe ukkhipitabbo. Yo ukkhipeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

381. Then those visiting monks experienced remorse and regret: “Indeed, it is a loss for us, not a gain for us; indeed, it is ill-gotten for us, not well-gotten for us, that we suspended a pure monk without offense, without grounds, without reason. Come, friends, let us go to Campā and confess our transgression as a transgression in the presence of the Blessed One.” Then those visiting monks put their lodging in order, took their bowls and robes, and set out for Campā. Gradually, they arrived at Campā and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. It is customary for the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, to exchange greetings with visiting monks. Then the Blessed One addressed those monks: “Monks, are you well? Are you managing? Have you come this long journey without much fatigue? And from where have you come, monks?” “We are well, Blessed One; we are managing, Blessed One; and we have come this long journey without much fatigue, venerable sir. There is, venerable sir, a village called Vāsabhagāma in the Kāsī country. From there, Blessed One, we have come.” “Monks, did you suspend a resident monk?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “On what grounds, monks, for what reason?” “Without grounds, Blessed One, without reason.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them: “It is unseemly, foolish men, inappropriate, unbecoming, unworthy of ascetics, improper, not to be done. How could you, foolish men, suspend a pure monk without offense, without grounds, without reason? This, foolish men, will not cause confidence to arise in those who lack it…” Having rebuked them, he gave a Dhamma talk and addressed the monks: “Monks, a pure monk without offense should not be suspended without grounds, without reason. Whoever suspends one incurs an offense of wrong-doing.”

Atha kho te bhikkhū uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “accayo no, bhante, accagamā yathābāle yathāmūḷhe [T 2.0250] yathāakusale, ye mayaṃ suddhaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpattikaṃ avatthusmiṃ akāraṇe ukkhipimhā. Tesaṃ no, bhante, bhagavā accayaṃ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu āyatiṃ saṃvarāyā”ti. “Taggha, tumhe, bhikkhave, accayo accagamā yathābāle yathāmūḷhe yathāakusale, ye tumhe suddhaṃ bhikkhuṃ anāpattikaṃ avatthusmiṃ akāraṇe ukkhipittha. Yato ca kho tumhe, bhikkhave, accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikarotha, taṃ vo mayaṃ paṭiggaṇhāma. Vuddhihesā[M 0.0434], bhikkhave, ariyassa vinaye yo accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikaroti, āyatiṃ āyatiṃ ca (sī.) saṃvaraṃ āpajjatī”ti.

Then those monks rose from their seats, arranged their upper robes over one shoulder, bowed down with their heads at the Blessed One's feet, and said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, a transgression has overcome us, who were foolish, deluded, and unskillful, in that we suspended a pure monk without offense, without grounds, and without reason. Venerable sir, may the Blessed One accept our transgression as a transgression, for the sake of future restraint.' 'Indeed, monks, a transgression has overcome you, who were foolish, deluded, and unskillful, in that you suspended a pure monk without offense, without grounds, and without reason. And since you, monks, having seen the transgression as a transgression, make amends according to the Dhamma, we accept that of you. For this, monks, is growth in the Noble One's discipline: that one who, having seen a transgression as a transgression, makes amends according to the Dhamma, undertakes future restraint.'

Kassapagottabhikkhuvatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story of the monk Kassapagotta is concluded.

235. Adhammena vaggādikammakathā

235. Discourse on Factional and Other Acts Performed Unlawfully

382. Tena kho pana samayena campāyaṃ bhikkhū evarūpāni kammāni karonti – adhammena vaggakammaṃ karonti, adhammena samaggakammaṃ karonti; dhammena vaggakammaṃ karonti, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ karonti; dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ karonti; ekopi ekaṃ ukkhipati, ekopi dve ukkhipati, ekopi sambahule ukkhipati, ekopi saṅghaṃ ukkhipati; dvepi ekaṃ ukkhipanti, dvepi dve ukkhipanti, dvepi sambahule ukkhipanti, dvepi saṅghaṃ ukkhipanti[V 0.0411]; sambahulāpi [T 2.0251] ekaṃ ukkhipanti; sambahulāpi dve ukkhipanti, sambahulāpi sambahule ukkhipanti, sambahulāpi saṅghaṃ ukkhipanti; saṅghopi saṅghaṃ ukkhipati. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma campāyaṃ bhikkhū evarūpāni kammāni karissanti – adhammena vaggakammaṃ karissanti, adhammena samaggakammaṃ karissanti, dhammena vaggakammaṃ karissanti, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ karissanti, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ karissanti, ekopi ekaṃ ukkhipissati, ekopi dve ukkhipissati, ekopi sambahule ukkhipissati, ekopi saṅghaṃ ukkhipissati, dvepi ekaṃ ukkhipissanti, dvepi dve ukkhipissanti, dvepi sambahule ukkhipissanti, dvepi saṅghaṃ ukkhipissanti, sambahulāpi ekaṃ ukkhipissanti, sambahulāpi dve ukkhipissanti, sambahulāpi sambahule ukkhipissanti, sambahulāpi saṅghaṃ ukkhipissanti, saṅghopi saṅghaṃ ukkhipissatī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, campāyaṃ bhikkhū evarūpāni kammāni karonti – adhammena [P 1.0316] vaggakammaṃ karonti…pe… saṅghopi saṅghaṃ ukkhipatī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā – “ananucchavikaṃ, bhikkhave, tesaṃ moghapurisānaṃ ananulomikaṃ appatirūpaṃ assāmaṇakaṃ akappiyaṃ akaraṇīyaṃ. Kathañhi nāma te, bhikkhave, moghapurisā evarūpāni kammāni karissanti – adhammena vaggakammaṃ karissanti…pe… saṅghopi saṅghaṃ ukkhipissati. Netaṃ, bhikkhave, appasannānaṃ vā pasādāya…pe… vigarahitvā…pe… dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

382. At that time, in Campā, the monks were performing acts of such a nature: they were performing factional acts unlawfully, they were performing concordant acts unlawfully; they were performing factional acts lawfully, they were performing factional acts with a counterfeit of the Dhamma; they were performing concordant acts with a counterfeit of the Dhamma; one monk suspended one monk, one monk suspended two monks, one monk suspended many monks, one monk suspended the Saṅgha; two monks suspended one monk, two monks suspended two monks, two monks suspended many monks, two monks suspended the Saṅgha; many monks suspended one monk; many monks suspended two monks, many monks suspended many monks, many monks suspended the Saṅgha; the Saṅgha also suspended the Saṅgha. Those monks who were of few desires… complained, criticized, and spread it about, saying: “How indeed can the monks in Campā perform acts of such a nature: perform factional acts unlawfully, perform concordant acts unlawfully, perform factional acts lawfully, perform factional acts with a counterfeit of the Dhamma, perform concordant acts with a counterfeit of the Dhamma, one monk suspending one monk, one monk suspending two monks, one monk suspending many monks, one monk suspending the Saṅgha, two monks suspending one monk, two monks suspending two monks, two monks suspending many monks, two monks suspending the Saṅgha, many monks suspending one monk, many monks suspending two monks, many monks suspending many monks, many monks suspending the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha also suspending the Saṅgha?” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Is it true, it is said, monks, that in Campā the monks are performing acts of such a nature: performing factional acts unlawfully… the Saṅgha also suspending the Saṅgha?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them: “It is unfitting, monks, for those foolish men, unsuitable, unbecoming, unworthy of ascetics, improper, and not to be done. How indeed, monks, can those foolish men perform acts of such a nature: perform factional acts unlawfully… the Saṅgha also suspending the Saṅgha? This, monks, is not for the confidence of the unconfident… Having rebuked them… having given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks:

383. “Adhammena [M 0.0435] ce, bhikkhave, vaggakammaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ, adhammena adhammena ce bhikkhave (syā.) samaggakammaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ; dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ; ekopi ekaṃ ukkhipati akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ, ekopi dve ukkhipati akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ, ekopi sambahule ukkhipati akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ, ekopi saṅghaṃ ukkhipati akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ; dvepi ekaṃ ukkhipanti akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ, dvepi dve ukkhipanti akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ, dvepi sambahule ukkhipanti akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ, dvepi [T 2.0252] saṅghaṃ ukkhipanti akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ; sambahulāpi ekaṃ ukkhipanti akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ, sambahulāpi dve ukkhipanti akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ, sambahulāpi sambahule ukkhipanti akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ, sambahulāpi saṅghaṃ ukkhipanti akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ; saṅghopi saṅghaṃ ukkhipati akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ.

383. “Monks, if a factional act is performed unlawfully, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If a concordant act is performed unlawfully, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If a factional act is performed lawfully, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If a factional act is performed with a counterfeit of the Dhamma, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If a concordant act is performed with a counterfeit of the Dhamma, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If even one monk suspends one monk, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If even one monk suspends two monks, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If even one monk suspends many monks, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If even one monk suspends the Saṅgha, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If even two monks suspend one monk, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If even two monks suspend two monks, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If even two monks suspend many monks, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If even two monks suspend the Saṅgha, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If even many monks suspend one monk, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If even many monks suspend two monks, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If even many monks suspend many monks, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If even many monks suspend the Saṅgha, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If even the Saṅgha suspends the Saṅgha, it is not a valid act and should not be done.”

384. “Cattārimāni[V 0.0412], bhikkhave, kammāni – adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammena samaggakammaṃ. Tatra, bhikkhave, yadidaṃ adhammena vaggakammaṃ, idaṃ, bhikkhave, kammaṃ adhammattā vaggattā kuppaṃ aṭṭhānārahaṃ; na, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ kammaṃ kātabbaṃ, na ca mayā evarūpaṃ kammaṃ anuññātaṃ. Tatra, bhikkhave, yadidaṃ adhammena samaggakammaṃ, idaṃ, bhikkhave, kammaṃ adhammattā kuppaṃ aṭṭhānārahaṃ; na, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ kammaṃ kātabbaṃ, na ca mayā evarūpaṃ kammaṃ anuññātaṃ. Tatra, bhikkhave, yadidaṃ dhammena vaggakammaṃ, idaṃ, bhikkhave, kammaṃ vaggattā kuppaṃ aṭṭhānārahaṃ; na, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ kammaṃ kātabbaṃ, na ca mayā evarūpaṃ kammaṃ anuññātaṃ. Tatra, bhikkhave, yadidaṃ dhammena samaggakammaṃ, idaṃ, bhikkhave, kammaṃ dhammattā samaggattā akuppaṃ ṭhānārahaṃ; evarūpaṃ, bhikkhave, kammaṃ kātabbaṃ, evarūpañca mayā kammaṃ anuññātaṃ. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evarūpaṃ kammaṃ karissāma yadidaṃ dhammena samagganti – evañhi [T 2.0253] vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti.

384. “Monks, there are these four acts: a factional act performed unlawfully, a concordant act performed unlawfully, a factional act performed lawfully, and a concordant act performed lawfully. Among these, monks, that which is a factional act performed unlawfully—this act, monks, is invalid and unfit to stand because it is unlawful and factional. Monks, such an act should not be performed, nor has such an act been permitted by me. Among these, monks, that which is a concordant act performed unlawfully—this act, monks, is invalid and unfit to stand because it is unlawful. Monks, such an act should not be performed, nor has such an act been permitted by me. Among these, monks, that which is a factional act performed lawfully—this act, monks, is invalid and unfit to stand because it is factional. Monks, such an act should not be performed, nor has such an act been permitted by me. Among these, monks, that which is a concordant act performed lawfully—this act, monks, is not invalid and is fit to stand because it is lawful and concordant. Monks, such an act should be performed, and such an act has been permitted by me. Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We shall perform such an act as is lawful and concordant.’”

Adhammena vaggādikammakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on factional and other acts performed unlawfully is concluded.

236. Ñattivipannakammādikathā

236. The Discourse on Acts with Defective Motions and so forth

385. Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhū evarūpāni kammāni karonti – adhammena vaggakammaṃ karonti, adhammena samaggakammaṃ karonti; dhammena vaggakammaṃ [M 0.0436] karonti, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ karonti, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ karonti; ñattivipannampi kammaṃ karonti anussāvanasampannaṃ, anussāvanavipannampi kammaṃ karonti ñattisampannaṃ, ñattivipannampi [P 1.0317] anussāvanavipannampi kammaṃ karonti; aññatrāpi dhammā kammaṃ karonti, aññatrāpi vinayā kammaṃ karonti, aññatrāpi satthusāsanā kammaṃ karonti; paṭikuṭṭhakatampi kammaṃ karonti adhammikaṃ kuppaṃ aṭṭhānārahaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā…pe… te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma chabbaggiyā bhikkhū evarūpāni kammāni karissanti – adhammena vaggakammaṃ karissanti, adhammena samaggakammaṃ karissanti; dhammena vaggakammaṃ karissanti, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ karissanti, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ karissanti; ñattivipannampi kammaṃ karissanti anussāvanasampannaṃ, anussāvanavipannampi kammaṃ karissanti ñattisampannaṃ, ñattivipannampi anussāvanavipannampi kammaṃ karissanti; aññatrāpi dhammā kammaṃ karissanti, aññatrāpi vinayā kammaṃ karissanti, aññatrāpi satthusāsanā kammaṃ karissanti; paṭikuṭṭhakatampi kammaṃ karissanti adhammikaṃ kuppaṃ aṭṭhānāraha”nti. Atha kho te bhikkhū [V 0.0413] bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, chabbaggiyā bhikkhū evarūpāni kammāni karonti – adhammena vaggakammaṃ karonti…pe… paṭikuṭṭhakatampi kammaṃ karonti adhammikaṃ kuppaṃ aṭṭhānāraha”nti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… vigarahitvā dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi –

385. Now at that time the monks of the group of six were performing such acts: they performed a factional act unrighteously, they performed a unanimous act unrighteously; they performed a factional act righteously, they performed a factional act in semblance of the Dhamma, they performed a unanimous act in semblance of the Dhamma; they performed an act with a defective motion but a complete proclamation, they performed an act with a defective proclamation but a complete motion, they performed an act with both a defective motion and a defective proclamation; they performed an act apart from the Dhamma, they performed an act apart from the Discipline, they performed an act apart from the Teacher’s instruction; they even performed an act that was protested against, unrighteous, liable to be overturned, and unfit to stand. The monks who were of few wishes … complained, grumbled, and criticized them: “How can the monks of the group of six perform such acts: performing a factional act unrighteously, performing a unanimous act unrighteously; performing a factional act righteously, performing a factional act in semblance of the Dhamma, performing a unanimous act in semblance of the Dhamma; performing an act with a defective motion but a complete proclamation, performing an act with a defective proclamation but a complete motion, performing an act with both a defective motion and a defective proclamation; performing an act apart from the Dhamma, performing an act apart from the Discipline, performing an act apart from the Teacher’s instruction; even performing an act that was protested against, unrighteous, liable to be overturned, and unfit to stand?” Then those monks reported the matter to the Blessed One. … “Is it true, monks, that the monks of the group of six perform such acts: performing a factional act unrighteously … even performing an act that was protested against, unrighteous, liable to be overturned, and unfit to stand?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Blessed One, the Buddha, rebuked them … Having rebuked them, he gave a Dhamma talk and addressed the monks:

386. “Adhammena ce, bhikkhave, vaggakammaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ[T 2.0254]; adhammena samaggakammaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ; dhammena vaggakammaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ; dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ; dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Ñattivipannañce, bhikkhave, kammaṃ anussāvanasampannaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ; anussāvanavipannañce, bhikkhave, kammaṃ ñattisampannaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ; ñattivipannañce, bhikkhave, kammaṃ anussāvanavipannaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ; aññatrāpi dhammā kammaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ; aññatrāpi vinayā kammaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ; aññatrāpi satthusāsanā kammaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ; paṭikuṭṭhakatañce, bhikkhave, kammaṃ adhammikaṃ kuppaṃ aṭṭhānārahaṃ akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ.

386. “Monks, if a factional act is performed unrighteously, it is not a valid act and should not be performed. If a unanimous act is performed unrighteously, it is not a valid act and should not be performed. If a factional act is performed righteously, it is not a valid act and should not be performed. If a factional act is performed with a semblance of the Dhamma, it is not a valid act and should not be performed. If a unanimous act is performed with a semblance of the Dhamma, it is not a valid act and should not be performed. Monks, if an act is performed that is deficient in the motion but complete in the proclamation, it is not a valid act and should not be performed. If an act is performed that is deficient in the proclamation but complete in the motion, it is not a valid act and should not be performed. If an act is performed that is deficient in both the motion and the proclamation, it is not a valid act and should not be performed. If an act is performed apart from the Dhamma, it is not a valid act and should not be performed. If an act is performed apart from the Discipline, it is not a valid act and should not be performed. If an act is performed apart from the Teacher's instruction, it is not a valid act and should not be performed. Monks, if an act that is protested against, unrighteous, liable to be overturned, and unfit to stand is performed, it is not a valid act and should not be performed.”

387. Chayimāni, bhikkhave, kammāni – adhammakammaṃ, vaggakammaṃ, samaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena samaggakammaṃ.

387. “Monks, there are these six acts: an unrighteous act, a factional act, a unanimous act, a factional act with a semblance of the Dhamma, a unanimous act with a semblance of the Dhamma, and a unanimous act in accordance with the Dhamma.”

Katamañca[M 0.0437], bhikkhave, adhammakammaṃ? Ñattidutiye ce, bhikkhave, kamme ekāya ñattiyā kammaṃ karoti, na ca kammavācaṃ anussāveti – adhammakammaṃ. Ñattidutiye ce, bhikkhave, kamme dvīhi ñattīhi kammaṃ karoti, na ca kammavācaṃ anussāveti – adhammakammaṃ. Ñattidutiye ce, bhikkhave, kamme ekāya kammavācāya kammaṃ karoti, na ca ñattiṃ ṭhapeti [T 2.0255] – adhammakammaṃ. Ñattidutiye ce, bhikkhave, kamme dvīhi kammavācāhi kammaṃ karoti, na ca ñattiṃ ṭhapeti – adhammakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme ekāya ñattiyā kammaṃ karoti, na ca kammavācaṃ anussāveti – adhammakammaṃ[P 1.0318]. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme dvīhi ñattīhi kammaṃ karoti, na ca kammavācaṃ anussāveti – adhammakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme tīhi ñattīhi kammaṃ karoti, na ca kammavācaṃ anussāveti – adhammakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme catūhi ñattīhi kammaṃ karoti, na ca kammavācaṃ anussāveti – adhammakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme ekāya kammavācāya kammaṃ karoti, na ca ñattiṃ ṭhapeti – adhammakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme dvīhi kammavācāhi [V 0.0414] kammaṃ karoti, na ca ñattiṃ ṭhapeti – adhammakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme tīhi kammavācāhi kammaṃ karoti, na ca ñattiṃ ṭhapeti – adhammakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme catūhi kammavācāhi kammaṃ karoti, na ca ñattiṃ ṭhapeti – adhammakammaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhammakammaṃ.

“And what, monks, is an unrighteous act? Monks, in a motion-second act, if one performs the act with one motion but does not announce the proclamation—it is an unrighteous act. Monks, in a motion-second act, if one performs the act with two motions but does not announce the proclamation—it is an unrighteous act. Monks, in a motion-second act, if one performs the act with one proclamation but does not propose the motion—it is an unrighteous act. Monks, in a motion-second act, if one performs the act with two proclamations but does not propose the motion—it is an unrighteous act. Monks, in a motion-fourth act, if one performs the act with one motion but does not announce the proclamation—it is an unrighteous act. Monks, in a motion-fourth act, if one performs the act with two motions but does not announce the proclamation—it is an unrighteous act. Monks, in a motion-fourth act, if one performs the act with three motions but does not announce the proclamation—it is an unrighteous act. Monks, in a motion-fourth act, if one performs the act with four motions but does not announce the proclamation—it is an unrighteous act. Monks, in a motion-fourth act, if one performs the act with one proclamation but does not propose the motion—it is an unrighteous act. Monks, in a motion-fourth act, if one performs the act with two proclamations but does not propose the motion—it is an unrighteous act. Monks, in a motion-fourth act, if one performs the act with three proclamations but does not propose the motion—it is an unrighteous act. Monks, in a motion-fourth act, if one performs the act with four proclamations but does not propose the motion—it is an unrighteous act. This, monks, is called an unrighteous act.”

Katamañca, bhikkhave, vaggakammaṃ? Ñattidutiye ce, bhikkhave, kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te anāgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti – vaggakammaṃ. Ñattidutiye ce, bhikkhave, kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti – vaggakammaṃ. Ñattidutiye ce, bhikkhave, kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti – vaggakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā [T 2.0256] te anāgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti – vaggakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā [M 0.0438] paṭikkosanti – vaggakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti – vaggakammaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, vaggakammaṃ.

And what, bhikkhus, is a factional act? If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion as the second part, as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act have not arrived, the consent of those entitled to give consent has not been brought, and those present protest—this is a factional act. If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion as the second part, as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act have arrived, the consent of those entitled to give consent has not been brought, and those present protest—this is a factional act. If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion as the second part, as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act have arrived, the consent of those entitled to give consent has been brought, and those present protest—this is a factional act. If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion as the fourth part, as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act have not arrived, the consent of those entitled to give consent has not been brought, and those present protest—this is a factional act. If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion as the fourth part, as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act have arrived, the consent of those entitled to give consent has not been brought, and those present protest—this is a factional act. If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion as the fourth part, as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act have arrived, the consent of those entitled to give consent has been brought, and those present protest—this is a factional act. This, bhikkhus, is called a factional act.

Katamañca, bhikkhave, samaggakammaṃ? Ñattidutiye ce, bhikkhave, kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā, te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā na paṭikkosanti – samaggakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā, te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā na paṭikkosanti – samaggakammaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, samaggakammaṃ.

And what, bhikkhus, is an act of concord? If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion as the second part, as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act have arrived, the consent of those entitled to give consent has been brought, and those present do not protest—this is an act of concord. If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion as the fourth part, as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act have arrived, the consent of those entitled to give consent has been brought, and those present do not protest—this is an act of concord. This, bhikkhus, is called an act of concord.

Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ? Ñattidutiye ce, bhikkhave, kamme paṭhamaṃ kammavācaṃ anussāveti, pacchā ñattiṃ ṭhapeti, yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te anāgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti – dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ. Ñattidutiye ce, bhikkhave, kamme paṭhamaṃ kammavācaṃ anussāveti, pacchā ñattiṃ ṭhapeti, yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti – dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ. Ñattidutiye ce, bhikkhave[V 0.0415], kamme paṭhamaṃ kammavācaṃ [T 2.0257] anussāveti, pacchā ñattiṃ ṭhapeti, yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā [P 1.0319] paṭikkosanti – dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme paṭhamaṃ kammavācaṃ anussāveti, pacchā ñattiṃ ṭhapeti, yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te anāgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti – dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme paṭhamaṃ kammavācaṃ anussāveti, pacchā ñattiṃ ṭhapeti, yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando anāhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti – dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme paṭhamaṃ kammavācaṃ anussāveti, pacchā ñattiṃ ṭhapeti, yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti[M 0.0439], sammukhībhūtā paṭikkosanti – dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ.

And what, bhikkhus, is a factional act by means of a counterfeit of the Dhamma? If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion as the second part, one first announces the proclamation and afterwards states the motion, and as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act have not arrived, the consent of those entitled to give consent has not been brought, and those who are present protest—this is a factional act by means of a counterfeit of the Dhamma. If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion as the second part, one first announces the proclamation and afterwards states the motion, and as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act have arrived, but the consent of those entitled to give consent has not been brought, and those who are present protest—this is a factional act by means of a counterfeit of the Dhamma. If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion as the second part, one first announces the proclamation and afterwards states the motion, and as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act have arrived, the consent of those entitled to give consent has been brought, but those who are present protest—this is a factional act by means of a counterfeit of the Dhamma. If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion as the fourth part, one first announces the proclamation and afterwards states the motion, and as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act have not arrived, the consent of those entitled to give consent has not been brought, and those who are present protest—this is a factional act by means of a counterfeit of the Dhamma. If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion as the fourth part, one first announces the proclamation and afterwards states the motion, and as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act have arrived, but the consent of those entitled to give consent has not been brought, and those who are present protest—this is a factional act by means of a counterfeit of the Dhamma. If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion as the fourth part, one first announces the proclamation and afterwards states the motion, and as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act have arrived, the consent of those entitled to give consent has been brought, but those who are present protest—this is a factional act by means of a counterfeit of the Dhamma. This, bhikkhus, is called a factional act by means of a counterfeit of the Dhamma.

Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ? Ñattidutiye ce, bhikkhave, kamme paṭhamaṃ kammavācaṃ anussāveti, pacchā ñattiṃ [T 2.0258] ṭhapeti, yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā, te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā na paṭikkosanti – dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme paṭhamaṃ kammavācaṃ anussāveti, pacchā ñattiṃ ṭhapeti, yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā na paṭikkosanti – dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ.

And what, bhikkhus, is an act of concord by means of a counterfeit of the Dhamma? If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion as the second part, one first announces the proclamation and afterwards states the motion, and as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act have arrived, the consent of those entitled to give consent has been brought, and those present do not protest—this is an act of concord by means of a counterfeit of the Dhamma. If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion as the fourth part, one first announces the proclamation and afterwards states the motion, and as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act have arrived, the consent of those entitled to give consent has been brought, and those present do not protest—this is an act of concord by means of a counterfeit of the Dhamma. This, bhikkhus, is called an act of concord by means of a counterfeit of the Dhamma.

Katamañca, bhikkhave, dhammena samaggakammaṃ? Ñattidutiye ce, bhikkhave, kamme paṭhamaṃ ñattiṃ ṭhapeti, pacchā ekāya kammavācāya kammaṃ karoti, yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā na paṭikkosanti – dhammena samaggakammaṃ. Ñatticatutthe ce, bhikkhave, kamme paṭhamaṃ ñattiṃ ṭhapeti, pacchā tīhi kammavācāhi kammaṃ karoti, yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā, te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā na paṭikkosanti, dhammena samaggakammaṃ. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammena samaggakammaṃ.

And what, bhikkhus, is a united act in accordance with the Dhamma? If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion and one proclamation, one first states the motion and afterwards performs the act with one proclamation, and as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act are present, the consent of those entitled to give consent has been obtained, and those present do not protest—this is a united act in accordance with the Dhamma. If, bhikkhus, in an act with a motion and three proclamations, one first states the motion and afterwards performs the act with three proclamations, and as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act are present, the consent of those entitled to give consent has been obtained, and those present do not protest—this is a united act in accordance with the Dhamma. This, bhikkhus, is called a united act in accordance with the Dhamma.

Ñattivipannakammādikathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on acts defective in their motion and so forth is concluded.

237. Catuvaggakaraṇādikathā

237. The Discourse on Performance by a Quorum of Four and so forth

388. Pañca [V 0.0416] saṅghā – catuvaggo bhikkhusaṅgho pañcavaggo bhikkhusaṅgho, dasavaggo bhikkhusaṅgho, vīsativaggo bhikkhusaṅgho, atirekavīsativaggo bhikkhusaṅgho. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ catuvaggo bhikkhusaṅgho, ṭhapetvā tīṇi kammāni – upasampadaṃ pavāraṇaṃ abbhānaṃ, dhammena samaggo [T 2.0259] sabbakammesu kammappatto. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ pañcavaggo bhikkhusaṅgho, ṭhapetvā dve kammāni – majjhimesu janapadesu upasampadaṃ abbhānaṃ, dhammena samaggo sabbakammesu kammappatto. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ dasavaggo bhikkhusaṅgho, ṭhapetvā ekaṃ kammaṃ – abbhānaṃ, dhammena samaggo sabbakammesu kammappatto. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ vīsativaggo bhikkhusaṅgho dhammena samaggo sabbakammesu [M 0.0440] kammappatto. Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṃ atirekavīsativaggo bhikkhusaṅgho [P 1.0320] dhammena samaggo sabbakammesu kammappatto.

388. There are five Saṅghas: a Saṅgha of four bhikkhus, a Saṅgha of five bhikkhus, a Saṅgha of ten bhikkhus, a Saṅgha of twenty bhikkhus, and a Saṅgha of more than twenty bhikkhus. Therein, bhikkhus, the Saṅgha of four bhikkhus, setting aside three acts—higher ordination, Pavāraṇā, and rehabilitation—if in concord according to the Dhamma, is competent for all acts. Therein, bhikkhus, the Saṅgha of five bhikkhus, setting aside two acts—higher ordination in the middle countries and rehabilitation—if in concord according to the Dhamma, is competent for all acts. Therein, bhikkhus, the Saṅgha of ten bhikkhus, setting aside one act—rehabilitation—if in concord according to the Dhamma, is competent for all acts. Therein, bhikkhus, the Saṅgha of twenty bhikkhus, if in concord according to the Dhamma, is competent for all acts. Therein, bhikkhus, the Saṅgha of more than twenty bhikkhus, if in concord according to the Dhamma, is competent for all acts.

389. Catuvaggakaraṇañce, bhikkhave, kammaṃ bhikkhunicatuttho kammaṃ kareyya – akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Catuvaggakaraṇañce, bhikkhave, kammaṃ sikkhamānacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ…pe…. Sāmaṇeracatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Sāmaṇericatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Sikkhaṃ paccakkhātakacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannakacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Āpattiyā adassane ukkhittakacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittakacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittakacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Paṇḍakacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Theyyasaṃvāsakacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Titthiyapakkantakacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Tiracchānagatacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Mātughātakacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Pitughātakacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Arahantaghātakacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Bhikkhunidūsakacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Saṅghabhedakacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Lohituppādakacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Ubhatobyañjanakacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Nānāsaṃvāsakacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Nānāsīmāya ṭhitacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Iddhiyā vehāse ṭhitacatuttho kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ [V 0.0417] na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti, taṃcatuttho kammaṃ kareyya [T 2.0260]… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ.

389. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with a bhikkhunī as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with a sikkhamānā as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. … If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with a novice as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with a female novice as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with one who has renounced the training as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with one who has committed an ultimate offense as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with one suspended for not seeing an offense as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with one suspended for not making amends for an offense as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with one suspended for not relinquishing a wrong view as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with a eunuch as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with one who is in communion by theft as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with one who has defected to another sect as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with an animal as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with a matricide as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with a patricide as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with a murderer of an arahant as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with a violator of a bhikkhunī as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with a schismatic as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with one who sheds a Buddha’s blood as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with a hermaphrodite as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with one who lives in separate association as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with one who stands in a separate boundary as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with one who stands in the air by psychic power as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done. If, bhikkhus, a legal act requiring a four-member quorum is performed with the person against whom the Saṅgha is performing an act as the fourth member, that act is invalid and should not be done.

Catuvaraṇaṃ.

The performance of acts by a quorum of four is finished.

390. Pañcavaggakaraṇañce, bhikkhave, kammaṃ bhikkhunipañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Pañcavaggakaraṇañce, bhikkhave, kammaṃ sikkhamānapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya…pe…. Sāmaṇerapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… sāmaṇeripañcamo kammaṃ kareyya [M 0.0441]… sikkhaṃ paccakkhātakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… āpattiyā adassane ukkhittakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… paṇḍakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… theyyasaṃvāsakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… titthiyapakkantakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… tiracchānagatapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… mātughātakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… pitughātakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… arahantaghātakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… bhikkhunidūsakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… saṅghabhedakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… lohituppādakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… ubhatobyañjanakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… nānāsaṃvāsakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… nānāsīmāya ṭhitapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… iddhiyā vehāse ṭhitapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya… yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti, taṃpañcamo kammaṃ kareyya – akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ.

390. Monks, if an act requiring a group of five is performed with a bhikkhunī as the fifth member, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If it is performed with a probationer as the fifth member, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If it is performed with a male novice as the fifth member... with a female novice... with one who has renounced the training... with one who has committed an ultimate offense... with one suspended for not seeing an offense... with one suspended for not making amends for an offense... with one suspended for not relinquishing a wrong view... with a eunuch... with one who co-resides by theft... with one who has gone over to another sect... with an animal... with a matricide... with a patricide... with a murderer of an Arahant... with a defiler of a bhikkhunī... with a creator of schism in the Saṅgha... with one who has maliciously drawn the blood of a Buddha... with one of both sexes... with one of a different communion... with one standing in a different boundary... with one standing in the air by psychic power... or if an act is performed by a Saṅgha with the person on whom the act is being performed as the fifth member—it is not a valid act and should not be done.

Pañcavaggakaraṇaṃ.

The chapter on acts requiring a group of five is concluded.

391. Dasavaggakaraṇañce, bhikkhave, kammaṃ bhikkhunidasamo kammaṃ kareyya, akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Dasavaggakaraṇañce, bhikkhave, kammaṃ sikkhamānadasamo kammaṃ kareyya, akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ…pe…[T 2.0261]. Dasavaggakaraṇañce, bhikkhave, kammaṃ yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti, taṃdasamo kammaṃ kareyya – akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ.

391. Monks, if an act requiring a group of ten is performed with a bhikkhunī as the tenth member, it is not a valid act and should not be done. If it is performed with a probationer as the tenth member, it is not a valid act and should not be done... and so on... If an act is performed by a Saṅgha with the person on whom the act is being performed as the tenth member—it is not a valid act and should not be done.

Dasavaggakaraṇaṃ.

The chapter on acts requiring a group of ten is concluded.

392. Vīsativaggakaraṇañce, bhikkhave, kammaṃ bhikkhunivīso kammaṃ kareyya – akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ. Vīsativaggakaraṇañce, bhikkhave, kammaṃ sikkhamānavīso kammaṃ kareyya [V 0.0418] …pe… sāmaṇeravīso kammaṃ kareyya… sāmaṇerivīso kammaṃ kareyya… sikkhaṃ paccakkhātakavīso kammaṃ kareyya… antimavatthuṃ ajjhāpannakavīso kammaṃ kareyya… āpattiyā adassane ukkhittakavīso kammaṃ kareyya… āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittakavīso kammaṃ kareyya… pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittakavīso kammaṃ kareyya… paṇḍakavīso kammaṃ kareyya… theyyasaṃvāsakavīso kammaṃ kareyya… titthiyapakkantakavīso kammaṃ kareyya… tiracchānagatavīso kammaṃ kareyya… mātughātakavīso kammaṃ kareyya… pitughātakavīso kammaṃ kareyya… arahantaghātakavīso [M 0.0442] kammaṃ kareyya… bhikkhunidūsakavīso kammaṃ kareyya… saṅghabhedakavīso kammaṃ kareyya… lohituppādakavīso kammaṃ kareyya… ubhatobyañjanakavīso kammaṃ kareyya… nānāsaṃvāsakavīso kammaṃ kareyya… nānāsīmāya ṭhitavīso kammaṃ kareyya… iddhiyā vehāse ṭhitavīso kammaṃ kareyya… yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti, taṃvīso kammaṃ kareyya – akammaṃ na ca karaṇīyaṃ.

392. Monks, if an act requiring a group of twenty is performed with a bhikkhunī as the twentieth member, it is not a valid act and should not be done.
