The Discourse on the Act of Suspension for Non-rectification is concluded.

248. Appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammakathā

Discussion on the Act of Suspension for Not Relinquishing

417. Idha [M 0.0459] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na icchati pāpikaṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭinissajjituṃ. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu na icchati pāpikaṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭinissajjituṃ. Handassa mayaṃ pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karomā”ti. Te tassa pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karonti – adhammena vaggā. So tamhā āvāsā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ gacchati. Tatthapi bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammakato adhammena vaggehi. Handassa mayaṃ pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karomā”ti. Te tassa pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karonti – adhammena samaggā…pe… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā…pe….

In this Dispensation, monks, a monk does not wish to relinquish a wrong view. If the monks there think: ‘Friends, this monk does not wish to relinquish a wrong view. Come now, let us perform the act of suspension against this monk for not relinquishing a wrong view.’ They perform the act of suspension against that monk for not relinquishing a wrong view—unlawfully, by a divided group. That monk goes from that monastery to another monastery. There too, the monks think: ‘Friends, this monk has had the act of suspension performed against him by the Saṅgha for not relinquishing a wrong view, unlawfully, by a divided group. Come now, let us perform the act of suspension against this monk for not relinquishing a wrong view.’ They perform the act of suspension against that monk for not relinquishing a wrong view—unlawfully, by a united group… lawfully, by a divided group… by a semblance of the Dhamma, by a divided group… by a semblance of the Dhamma, by a united group….

Cakkaṃ kātabbaṃ.

248. The wheel is to be turned.

Appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Act of Suspension for Non-relinquishment is concluded.

249. Tajjanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā

417. Discussion on the Revocation of the Act of Censure

418. Idha [V 0.0435] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena tajjanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena tajjanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Handassa mayaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena vaggā. So tamhā āvāsā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ gacchati. Tatthapi bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “imassa kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno saṅghena tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassaddhaṃ adhammena samaggehi. Handassa mayaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena samaggā. So tamhāpi āvāsā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ gacchati. Tatthapi bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti [V 0.0436] – “imassa kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno saṅghena tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassaddhaṃ adhammena vaggehi. Handassa mayaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – dhammena vaggā. So tamhāpi āvāsā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ gacchati. Tatthapi bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “imassa kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno saṅghena tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassaddhaṃ dhammena vaggehi. Handassa [M 0.0460] mayaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – dhammapatirūpakena vaggā. So tamhāpi āvāsā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ gacchati. Tatthapi bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “imassa kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno saṅghena tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassaddhaṃ dhammapatirūpakena vaggehi. Handassa mayaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – dhammapatirūpakena samaggā.

418. Furthermore, O bhikkhus, here a bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of censure by the Saṅgha conducts himself properly, humbles himself, practices conduct for his rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of censure. If the bhikkhus in that monastery should think thus: ‘Venerable sirs, this bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of censure by the Saṅgha conducts himself properly, humbles himself, practices conduct for his rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of censure. Come now, let us revoke the act of censure for this bhikkhu.’ They revoke the act of censure for him—unrighteously, as a faction. He goes from that monastery to another monastery. In that monastery also, the bhikkhus think thus: ‘Venerable sirs, for this bhikkhu the act of censure has been revoked by the Saṅgha unrighteously, by a complete assembly. 250. Niyassakammapaṭippassaddhikathā

The Discussion on the Revocation of the Act of Dependence

423. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena niyassakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, niyassassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena niyassakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, niyassassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatthapi bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “imassa kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno saṅghena niyassakammaṃ paṭippassaddhaṃ adhammena vaggehi. Handassa mayaṃ niyassakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa niyassakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena samaggā…pe… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā…pe….

250. Furthermore, bhikkhus, in this case, a bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of dependence by the Saṅgha conducts himself properly, humbles himself, strives for his rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of dependence. If the bhikkhus in that residence think: ‘Venerable sirs, this bhikkhu, having been subjected to an act of dependence by the Saṅgha, conducts himself properly, humbles himself, strives for his rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of dependence. There too the bhikkhus think: ‘Venerable sirs, the Saṅgha has revoked the act of dependence for this bhikkhu unrighteously, as a faction. Come now, let us revoke the act of dependence for him.’ They revoke the act of dependence for him—unrighteously, in concord… righteously, as a faction… by a semblance of the Dhamma, as a faction… by a semblance of the Dhamma, in concord…

Cakkaṃ kātabbaṃ.

423. The wheel should be made.

Niyassakammapaṭippassaddhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Revocation of the Act of Dependence is concluded.

252. Paṭisāraṇīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā

424. The Discussion on the Revocation of the Act of Reconciliation

425. Idha [M 0.0464] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena paṭisāraṇīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, paṭisāraṇīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena paṭisāraṇīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, paṭisāraṇīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Handassa mayaṃ paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena vaggā. So tamhā āvāsā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ gacchati. Tatthapi bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “imassa kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno saṅghena paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassaddhaṃ adhammena vaggehi. Handassa mayaṃ paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena samaggā…pe… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā…pe….

425. Furthermore, monks, a monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to an act of reconciliation conducts himself properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of reconciliation. If it occurs to the monks there thus: ‘Friends, this monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to an act of reconciliation conducts himself properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of reconciliation. Come now, let us revoke the act of reconciliation for this monk.’ They revoke the act of reconciliation for him—unlawfully, by an incomplete quorum. He goes from that residence to another residence. There too, it occurs to the monks thus: ‘Friends, for this monk, the act of reconciliation has been revoked by the Saṅgha unlawfully, by an incomplete quorum. Come now, let us revoke the act of reconciliation for this monk.’ They revoke the act of reconciliation for him—unlawfully, by a complete quorum… lawfully, by an incomplete quorum… by what resembles the Dhamma, by an incomplete quorum… by what resembles the Dhamma, by a complete quorum…

Cakkaṃ kātabbaṃ.

The 'wheel' is to be enacted.

Paṭisāraṇīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Revocation of the Act of Reconciliation is concluded.

253. Adassane ukkhepanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā

253. The Discourse on the Revocation of the Act of Suspension for Not Seeing an Offense

426. Idha [V 0.0440] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, āpattiyā [T 2.0290] adassane ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Handassa mayaṃ āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena vaggā. So tamhā āvāsā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ gacchati. Tatthapi bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “imassa kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno saṅghena āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassaddhaṃ adhammena vaggehi. Handassa mayaṃ āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammaṃ [M 0.0465] paṭippassambhenti – adhammena samaggā…pe… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā…pe….

426. Furthermore, monks, a monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to an act of suspension for not seeing an offense conducts himself properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of suspension for not seeing an offense. If it occurs to the monks there thus: ‘Friends, this monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to an act of suspension for not seeing an offense conducts himself properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of suspension for not seeing an offense. Come now, let us revoke the act of suspension for not seeing an offense for this monk.’ They revoke the act of suspension for not seeing an offense for him—unlawfully, by an incomplete quorum. He goes from that residence to another residence. There too, it occurs to the monks thus: ‘Friends, for this monk, the act of suspension for not seeing an offense has been revoked by the Saṅgha unlawfully, by an incomplete quorum. Come now, let us revoke the act of suspension for not seeing an offense for this monk.’ They revoke the act of suspension for not seeing an offense for him—unlawfully, by a complete quorum… lawfully, by an incomplete quorum… by what resembles the Dhamma, by an incomplete quorum… by what resembles the Dhamma, by a complete quorum…

Cakkaṃ kātabbaṃ.

The 'wheel' is to be enacted.

Adassane ukkhepanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Revocation of the Act of Suspension for Not Seeing an Offense is concluded.

254. Appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā

254. The Discourse on the Revocation of the Act of Suspension for Non-Expiation

427. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Handassa mayaṃ āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena vaggā. So tamhā āvāsā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ gacchati. Tatthapi bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “imassa kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno saṅghena āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassaddhaṃ – adhammena vaggehi. Handassa mayaṃ āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa [V 0.0441] āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena samaggā…pe… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā…pe….

427. Furthermore, monks, a monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to an act of suspension for not making amends for an offense conducts himself properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense. If it occurs to the monks there thus: ‘Friends, this monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to an act of suspension for not making amends for an offense conducts himself properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense. Come now, let us revoke the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense for this monk.’ They revoke the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense for him—unlawfully, by an incomplete quorum. He goes from that residence to another residence. There too, it occurs to the monks thus: ‘Friends, for this monk, the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense has been revoked by the Saṅgha unlawfully, by an incomplete quorum. Come now, let us revoke the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense for this monk.’ They revoke the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense for him—unlawfully, by a complete quorum… lawfully, by an incomplete quorum… by what resembles the Dhamma, by an incomplete quorum… by what resembles the Dhamma, by a complete quorum…

Cakkaṃ kātabbaṃ.

The 'wheel' is to be enacted.

Appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Revocation of the Act of Suspension for Not Making Amends for an Offense is concluded.

255. Appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā

255. The Discourse on the Revocation of the Act of Suspension for Non-Relinquishment

428. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge [T 2.0291][P 1.0332] ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Handassa mayaṃ pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa [M 0.0466] pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena vaggā. So tamhā āvāsā aññaṃ āvāsaṃ gacchati. Tatthapi bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “imassa kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno saṅghena pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassaddhaṃ – adhammena vaggehi. Handassa mayaṃ pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti… adhammena samaggā…pe… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā…pe….

428. Here, monks, a monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view conducts himself properly, shows humility, acts in a way that leads to his rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view. If it occurs to the monks there: ‘Venerable sirs, this monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view conducts himself properly, shows humility, acts in a way that leads to his rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view. Come now, let us revoke the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view for this monk.’ They revoke the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view for him—unrighteously, as a faction. He goes from that residence to another residence. There too, it occurs to the monks: ‘Venerable sirs, for this monk, the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view has been revoked by the Saṅgha—unrighteously, by a faction. Come now, let us revoke the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view for this monk.’ They revoke the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wicked view for him… unrighteously, in concord… righteously, as a faction… by what resembles the Dhamma, as a faction… by what resembles the Dhamma, in concord…

Cakkaṃ kātabbaṃ.

The cycle is to be applied.

Appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Revocation of the Act of Suspension for Non-Relinquishment is concluded.

256. Tajjanīyakammavivādakathā

256. Discussion on the Dispute Concerning the Act of Censure

429. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu bhaṇḍanakārako…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako. Handassa mayaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ karomā”ti[V 0.0442]. Te tassa tajjanīyakammaṃ karonti – adhammena vaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “adhammena [T 2.0292] vaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino.

429. Here, monks, a monk is a maker of quarrels, a maker of strife, a maker of disputes, one who is verbose, and one who creates legal issues in the Saṅgha. If it occurs to the monks there: ‘Friends, this monk is a maker of quarrels… and one who creates legal issues in the Saṅgha. Come now, let us perform the act of censure against him.’ They perform the act of censure against him—unrighteously, as a faction. The Saṅgha residing there disputes: ‘An act performed unrighteously, as a faction; an act performed unrighteously, in concord; an act performed righteously, as a faction; an act performed with a semblance of the Dhamma, as a faction; an act performed with a semblance of the Dhamma, in concord; the act is not done, the act is badly done, the act should be done again.’ In this case, monks, those monks who said, ‘An act performed unrighteously, as a faction,’ and those who said, ‘The act is not done, the act is badly done, the act should be done again’—these monks are speakers of the Dhamma in this matter.

430. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhaṇḍanakārako hoti…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu bhaṇḍanakārako…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako. Handassa mayaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ karomā”ti. Te tassa tajjanīyakammaṃ karonti – adhammena samaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “adhammena samaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino.

430. Here, monks, a monk is a maker of quarrels… and one who creates legal issues in the Saṅgha. If it occurs to the monks there: ‘Friends, this monk is a maker of quarrels… and one who creates legal issues in the Saṅgha. Come now, let us perform the act of censure against him.’ They perform the act of censure against him—unrighteously, in concord. The Saṅgha residing there disputes: ‘An act performed unrighteously, as a faction; an act performed unrighteously, in concord; an act performed righteously, as a faction; an act performed with a semblance of the Dhamma, as a faction; an act performed with a semblance of the Dhamma, in concord; the act is not done, the act is badly done, the act should be done again.’ In this case, monks, those monks who said, ‘An act performed unrighteously, in concord,’ and those who said, ‘The act is not done, the act is badly done, the act should be done again’—these monks are speakers of the Dhamma in this matter.

431. Idha [M 0.0467] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhaṇḍanakārako hoti…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu bhaṇḍanakārako…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako handassa mayaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ karomā”ti. Te tassa tajjanīyakammaṃ karonti [T 2.0293] – dhammena vaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammena vaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino.

431. Here, monks, a monk is a maker of quarrels… and one who creates legal issues in the Saṅgha. If it occurs to the monks there: ‘Friends, this monk is a maker of quarrels… and one who creates legal issues in the Saṅgha. Come now, let us perform the act of censure against him.’ They perform the act of censure against him—righteously, as a faction. The Saṅgha residing there disputes: ‘An act performed unrighteously, as a faction; an act performed unrighteously, in concord; an act performed righteously, as a faction; an act performed with a semblance of the Dhamma, as a faction; an act performed with a semblance of the Dhamma, in concord; the act is not done, the act is badly done, the act should be done again.’ In this case, monks, those monks who said, ‘An act performed righteously, as a faction,’ and those monks who said, ‘The act is not done, the act is badly done, the act should be done again’—these monks are speakers of the Dhamma in this matter.

432. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhaṇḍanakārako hoti…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu bhaṇḍanakārako…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako. Handassa mayaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ karomā”ti. Te tassa [V 0.0443] tajjanīyakammaṃ karonti – dhammapatirūpakena vaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammapatirūpakena samaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino.

432. Here, monks, a monk is quarrelsome... a creator of legal issues in the Sangha. If it occurs to the monks there: ‘Friends, this monk is quarrelsome... a creator of legal issues in the Sangha. Come now, let us perform the act of censure against him.’ They perform the act of censure against him—with a semblance of the Dhamma, as a faction. The Sangha residing there disputes: ‘An unlawful act by a faction; an unlawful act in concord; a lawful act by a faction; an act by a faction with a semblance of the Dhamma; an act in concord with a semblance of the Dhamma; the act is not done, the act is badly done, the act should be done again.’ In this case, monks, those monks who said, ‘An act in concord with a semblance of the Dhamma,’ and those monks who said, ‘The act is not done, the act is badly done, the act should be done again’—these monks there are speakers of the Dhamma.

433. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhaṇḍanakārako hoti…pe… [T 2.0294] saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu bhaṇḍanakārako hoti…pe… saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako. Handassa mayaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ karomā”ti. Te tassa tajjanīyakammaṃ karonti – dhammapatirūpakena samaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammapatirūpakena samaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino.

433. Here, monks, a monk is quarrelsome... a creator of legal issues in the Sangha. If it occurs to the monks there: ‘Friends, this monk is quarrelsome... a creator of legal issues in the Sangha. Come now, let us perform the act of censure against him.’ They perform the act of censure against him—with a semblance of the Dhamma, in concord. The Sangha residing there disputes: ‘An unlawful act by a faction; an unlawful act in concord; a lawful act by a faction; an act by a faction with a semblance of the Dhamma; an act in concord with a semblance of the Dhamma; the act is not done, the act is badly done, the act should be done again.’ In this case, monks, those monks who said, ‘An act in concord with a semblance of the Dhamma,’ and those monks who said, ‘The act is not done, the act is badly done, the act should be done again’—these monks there are speakers of the Dhamma.

Tajjanīyakammavivādakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Dispute Concerning the Act of Censure is concluded.

257. Niyassakammavivādakathā

257. The Discussion on the Dispute Concerning the Act of Subordination

434. Idha [M 0.0468] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bālo hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno, gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu bālo abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno, gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi gihisaṃsaggehi. Handassa mayaṃ niyassakammaṃ karomā”ti. Te tassa niyassakammaṃ karonti – adhammena vaggā…pe… adhammena samaggā… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ[T 2.0295], dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammapatirūpakena samaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu [V 0.0444] – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino. Ime pañca vārā saṃkhittā.

434. Here, monks, a monk is foolish, incompetent, has many offenses, is of boundless wrongdoing, and dwells associated with householders through associations improper for monks. If it occurs to the monks there: ‘Friends, this monk is foolish, incompetent, has many offenses, is of boundless wrongdoing, and dwells associated with householders through associations improper for monks. Come now, let us perform the act of subordination against him.’ They perform the act of subordination against him unlawfully as a faction... unlawfully in concord... lawfully as a faction... with a semblance of the Dhamma as a faction... with a semblance of the Dhamma in concord. The Sangha residing there disputes: ‘An unlawful act by a faction; an unlawful act in concord; a lawful act by a faction; an act by a faction with a semblance of the Dhamma; an act in concord with a semblance of the Dhamma; the act is not done, the act is badly done, the act should be done again.’ In this case, monks, those monks who said, ‘An act in concord with a semblance of the Dhamma,’ and those monks who said, ‘The act is not done, the act is badly done, the act should be done again’—these monks there are speakers of the Dhamma. These five cases are summarized.

Niyassakammavivādakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Dispute Concerning the Act of Subordination is concluded.

258. Pabbājanīyakammavivādakathā

258. The Discussion on the Dispute Concerning the Act of Banishment

435. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kuladūsako hoti pāpasamācāro. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu kuladūsako pāpasamācāro. Handassa mayaṃ pabbājanīyakammaṃ karomā”ti. Te tassa pabbājanīyakammaṃ karonti – adhammena vaggā…pe… adhammena samaggā… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammapatirūpakena samaggakamma”nti ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino. Ime pañca vārā saṃkhittā.

435. Here, monks, a monk is a corrupter of families and of evil conduct. If it occurs to the monks there: ‘Friends, this monk is a corrupter of families and of evil conduct. Come now, let us perform the act of banishment against him.’ They perform the act of banishment against him unlawfully as a faction... unlawfully in concord... lawfully as a faction... with a semblance of the Dhamma as a faction... with a semblance of the Dhamma in concord. The Sangha residing there disputes: ‘An unlawful act by a faction; an unlawful act in concord; a lawful act by a faction; an act by a faction with a semblance of the Dhamma; an act in concord with a semblance of the Dhamma; the act is not done, the act is badly done, the act should be done again.’ In this case, monks, those monks who said, ‘An act in concord with a semblance of the Dhamma,’ and those monks who said, ‘The act is not done, the act is badly done, the act should be done again’—these monks there are speakers of the Dhamma. These five cases are summarized.

Pabbājanīyakammavivādakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Dispute Concerning the Act of Banishment is concluded.

259. Paṭisāraṇīyakammavivādakathā

259. The Discussion on the Dispute Concerning the Act of Requiring Amends

436. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu gihī akkosati paribhāsati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu gihī akkosati [M 0.0469] paribhāsati. Handassa mayaṃ paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ [P 1.0333] karomā”ti. Te [T 2.0296] tassa paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ karonti – adhammena vaggā…pe… adhammena samaggā… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammapatirūpakena samaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ [V 0.0445] dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino. Ime pañca vārā saṃkhittā.

436. Furthermore, monks, here a monk insults and reviles a householder. If it occurs to the monks there: 'Friends, this monk insults and reviles a householder. Come now, let us perform the act of requiring amends against him.' They perform the act of requiring amends against him—unrighteously as a faction… unrighteously as a united body… righteously as a faction… with a semblance of the Dhamma as a faction… with a semblance of the Dhamma as a united body. The Sangha present there disputes, saying: 'It is an act by a faction contrary to the Dhamma, an act by a united body contrary to the Dhamma, an act by a faction in accordance with the Dhamma, an act by a faction with a semblance of the Dhamma, an act by a united body with a semblance of the Dhamma; the act is not done, the act is ill-done, the act should be done again.' Therein, monks, those monks who said, 'It is an act by a united body with a semblance of the Dhamma,' and those monks who said, 'The act is not done, the act is ill-done, the act should be done again,' these monks therein are speakers of the Dhamma. These five sections are summarized.

Paṭisāraṇīyakammavivādakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion of disputes concerning the act of requiring amends is concluded.

260. Adassane ukkhepanīyakammavivādakathā

260. Discussion of Disputes Concerning the Act of Suspension for Not Seeing an Offense

437. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchati āpattiṃ passituṃ. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchati āpattiṃ passituṃ. Handassa mayaṃ āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karomā”ti. Te tassa āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karonti – adhammena vaggā…pe… adhammena samaggā… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye [T 2.0297] te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammapatirūpakena samaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino. Ime pañca vārā saṃkhittā.

437. Furthermore, monks, here a monk, having committed an offense, does not wish to see the offense. If it occurs to the monks there: 'Friends, this monk, having committed an offense, does not wish to see the offense. Come now, let us perform the act of suspension against him for not seeing the offense.' They perform the act of suspension against him for not seeing the offense—unrighteously as a faction… unrighteously as a united body… righteously as a faction… with a semblance of the Dhamma as a faction… with a semblance of the Dhamma as a united body. The Sangha present there disputes, saying: 'It is an act by a faction contrary to the Dhamma, an act by a united body contrary to the Dhamma, an act by a faction in accordance with the Dhamma, an act by a faction with a semblance of the Dhamma, an act by a united body with a semblance of the Dhamma; the act is not done, the act is ill-done, the act should be done again.' Therein, monks, those monks who said, 'It is an act by a united body with a semblance of the Dhamma,' and those monks who said, 'The act is not done, the act is ill-done, the act should be done again,' these monks therein are speakers of the Dhamma. These five sections are summarized.

Adassane ukkhepanīyakammavivādakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion of disputes concerning the act of suspension for not seeing an offense is concluded.

261. Appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammavivādakathā

261. Discussion of Disputes Concerning the Act of Suspension for Not Making Amends

438. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchati āpattiṃ paṭikātuṃ. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpajjitvā na icchati āpattiṃ paṭikātuṃ. Handassa mayaṃ āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karomā”ti. Te tassa āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karonti – adhammena vaggā…pe… adhammena samaggā… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena [M 0.0470] vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ [V 0.0446] kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammapatirūpakena samaggakamma”nti; ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino. Ime pañca vārā saṃkhittā.

438. Furthermore, monks, here a monk, having committed an offense, does not wish to make amends for the offense. If it occurs to the monks there: 'Friends, this monk, having committed an offense, does not wish to make amends for the offense. Come now, let us perform the act of suspension against him for not making amends for the offense.' They perform the act of suspension against him for not making amends for the offense—unrighteously as a faction… unrighteously as a united body… righteously as a faction… with a semblance of the Dhamma as a faction… with a semblance of the Dhamma as a united body. The Sangha present there disputes, saying: 'It is an act by a faction contrary to the Dhamma, an act by a united body contrary to the Dhamma, an act by a faction in accordance with the Dhamma, an act by a faction with a semblance of the Dhamma, an act by a united body with a semblance of the Dhamma; the act is not done, the act is ill-done, the act should be done again.' Therein, monks, those monks who said, 'It is an act by a united body with a semblance of the Dhamma,' and those monks who said, 'The act is not done, the act is ill-done, the act should be done again,' these monks therein are speakers of the Dhamma. These five sections are summarized.

Appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammavivādakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion of disputes concerning the act of suspension for not making amends is concluded.

262. Appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammavivādakathā

262. Discussion of Disputes Concerning the Act of Suspension for Not Relinquishing a Wrong View

439. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na icchati pāpikaṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭinissajjituṃ. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu na icchati pāpikaṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭinissajjituṃ. Handassa mayaṃ pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge [T 2.0298] ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karomā”ti. Te tassa pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karonti – adhammena vaggā…pe… adhammena samaggā… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammapatirūpakena samaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino. Ime pañca vārā saṃkhittā.

439. Furthermore, monks, here a monk does not wish to relinquish an evil view. If it occurs to the monks there: 'Friends, this monk does not wish to relinquish an evil view. Come now, let us perform the act of suspension against him for not relinquishing an evil view.' They perform the act of suspension against him for not relinquishing an evil view—unrighteously as a faction… unrighteously as a united body… righteously as a faction… with a semblance of the Dhamma as a faction… with a semblance of the Dhamma as a united body. The Sangha present there disputes, saying: 'It is an act by a faction contrary to the Dhamma, an act by a united body contrary to the Dhamma, an act by a faction in accordance with the Dhamma, an act by a faction with a semblance of the Dhamma, an act by a united body with a semblance of the Dhamma; the act is not done, the act is ill-done, the act should be done again.' Therein, monks, those monks who said, 'It is an act by a united body with a semblance of the Dhamma,' and those monks who said, 'The act is not done, the act is ill-done, the act should be done again,' these monks therein are speakers of the Dhamma. These five sections are summarized.

Appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammavivādakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion of disputes concerning the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wrong view is concluded.

263. Tajjanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā

263. Discourse on the Revocation of the Act of Censure

440. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena tajjanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena tajjanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Handassa mayaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena vaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ [T 2.0299] kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ [V 0.0447] puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “adhammena vaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu [M 0.0471] – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino.

440. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of censure by the Saṅgha behaves properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for his rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of censure. If it occurs to the bhikkhus there thus: “Friends, this bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of censure by the Saṅgha behaves properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for his rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of censure. Come now, let us revoke the act of censure for him.” They revoke the act of censure for him—unlawfully, by a faction. The Saṅgha present there disputes: “An unlawful act by a faction, an unlawful act in concord, a lawful act by a faction, an act by a faction in semblance of the Dhamma, an act in concord in semblance of the Dhamma, an act not done, an act wrongly done, an act to be done again.” In this case, bhikkhus, those bhikkhus who say, “An unlawful act by a faction,” and those who say, “An act not done, an act wrongly done, an act to be done again”—these bhikkhus there are speakers of the Dhamma.

441. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena tajjanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena tajjanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Handassa mayaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena samaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “adhammena samaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino.

441. Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of censure by the Saṅgha behaves properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for his rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of censure. If it occurs to the bhikkhus there thus: “Friends, this bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of censure by the Saṅgha behaves properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for his rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of censure. Come now, let us revoke the act of censure for him.” They revoke the act of censure for him—unlawfully, in concord. The Saṅgha present there disputes: “An unlawful act by a faction, an unlawful act in concord, a lawful act by a faction, an act by a faction in semblance of the Dhamma, an act in concord in semblance of the Dhamma, an act not done, an act wrongly done, an act to be done again.” In this case, bhikkhus, those bhikkhus who say, “An unlawful act in concord,” and those who say, “An act not done, an act wrongly done, an act to be done again”—these bhikkhus there are speakers of the Dhamma.

442. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena tajjanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso[T 2.0300], bhikkhu saṅghena tajjanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Handassa mayaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – dhammena vaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammena vaggakamma”nti ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino.

442. Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of censure by the Saṅgha behaves properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for his rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of censure. If it occurs to the bhikkhus there thus: “Friends, this bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of censure by the Saṅgha behaves properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for his rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of censure. Come now, let us revoke the act of censure for him.” They revoke the act of censure for him—lawfully, by a faction. The Saṅgha present there disputes: “An unlawful act by a faction, an unlawful act in concord, a lawful act by a faction, an act by a faction in semblance of the Dhamma, an act in concord in semblance of the Dhamma, an act not done, an act wrongly done, an act to be done again.” In this case, bhikkhus, those bhikkhus who say, “A lawful act by a faction,” and those who say, “An act not done, an act wrongly done, an act to be done again”—these bhikkhus there are speakers of the Dhamma.

443. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena tajjanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena tajjanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Handassa mayaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ [M 0.0472][V 0.0448] paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – dhammapatirūpakena vaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra[T 2.0301], bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammapatirūpakena vaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino.

443. Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of censure by the Saṅgha behaves properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for his rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of censure. If it occurs to the bhikkhus there thus: “Friends, this bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of censure by the Saṅgha behaves properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for his rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of censure. Come now, let us revoke the act of censure for him.” They revoke the act of censure for him—by a faction, in semblance of the Dhamma. The Saṅgha present there disputes: “An unlawful act by a faction, an unlawful act in concord, a lawful act by a faction, an act by a faction in semblance of the Dhamma, an act in concord in semblance of the Dhamma, an act not done, an act wrongly done, an act to be done again.” In this case, bhikkhus, those bhikkhus who say, “An act by a faction in semblance of the Dhamma,” and those who say, “An act not done, an act wrongly done, an act to be done again”—these bhikkhus there are speakers of the Dhamma.

444. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena tajjanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena tajjanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, tajjanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Handassa mayaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa tajjanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – dhammapatirūpakena samaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammapatirūpakena samaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino.

444. Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of censure by the Saṅgha behaves properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of censure. If it occurs to the bhikkhus there thus: ‘Friends, this bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of censure by the Saṅgha behaves properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of censure. Come now, let us revoke the act of censure for this bhikkhu.’ They revoke the act of censure for that bhikkhu—in concord, by what is a semblance of the Dhamma. The Saṅgha present there disputes: ‘An act by a faction contrary to the Dhamma, an act in concord contrary to the Dhamma, an act by a faction in accordance with the Dhamma, an act by a faction by what is a semblance of the Dhamma, an act in concord by what is a semblance of the Dhamma, an act not done, an act wrongly done, an act to be done again.’ In this case, bhikkhus, those bhikkhus who said thus, ‘An act in concord by what is a semblance of the Dhamma,’ and those bhikkhus who said thus, ‘An act not done, an act wrongly done, an act to be done again’—these bhikkhus there are speakers of the Dhamma.

Tajjanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Revocation of the Act of Censure is concluded.

264. Niyassakammapaṭippassaddhikathā

264. The Discourse on the Revocation of the Act of Subordination

445. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena niyassakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, niyassassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena niyassakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati[T 2.0302], niyassassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Handassa mayaṃ niyassakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa niyassakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena vaggā…pe… adhammena samaggā… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ [V 0.0449] puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave[M 0.0473], ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammapatirūpakena samaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino. Imepi ime (sī. syā. evamuparipi) pañca vārā saṃkhittā.

445. Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of subordination by the Saṅgha behaves properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of subordination. If it occurs to the bhikkhus there thus: ‘Friends, this bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of subordination by the Saṅgha behaves properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of subordination. Come now, let us revoke the act of subordination for this bhikkhu.’ They revoke the act of subordination for that bhikkhu—contrary to the Dhamma, by a faction... contrary to the Dhamma, in concord... in accordance with the Dhamma, by a faction... by what is a semblance of the Dhamma, by a faction... by what is a semblance of the Dhamma, in concord. The Saṅgha present there disputes: ‘An act by a faction contrary to the Dhamma, an act in concord contrary to the Dhamma, an act by a faction in accordance with the Dhamma, an act by a faction by what is a semblance of the Dhamma, an act in concord by what is a semblance of the Dhamma, an act not done, an act wrongly done, an act to be done again.’ In this case, bhikkhus, those bhikkhus who said thus, ‘An act in concord by what is a semblance of the Dhamma,’ and those bhikkhus who said thus, ‘An act not done, an act wrongly done, an act to be done again’—these bhikkhus there are speakers of the Dhamma. These five instances are also summarized.

Niyassakammapaṭippassaddhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Revocation of the Act of Subordination is concluded.

265. Pabbājanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā

265. The Discourse on the Revocation of the Act of Banishment

446. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena pabbājanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, pabbājanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena pabbājanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, pabbājanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Handassa mayaṃ pabbājanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa pabbājanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena vaggā…pe… adhammena samaggā… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena [T 2.0303] samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammapatirūpakena samaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino. Imepi pañca vārā saṃkhittā.

446. Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of banishment by the Saṅgha behaves properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of banishment. If it occurs to the bhikkhus there thus: ‘Friends, this bhikkhu who has been subjected to an act of banishment by the Saṅgha behaves properly, humbles himself, conducts himself for rehabilitation, and requests the revocation of the act of banishment. Come now, let us revoke the act of banishment for this bhikkhu.’ They revoke the act of banishment for that bhikkhu—contrary to the Dhamma, by a faction... contrary to the Dhamma, in concord... in accordance with the Dhamma, by a faction... by what is a semblance of the Dhamma, by a faction... by what is a semblance of the Dhamma, in concord. The Saṅgha present there disputes: ‘An act by a faction contrary to the Dhamma, an act in concord contrary to the Dhamma, an act by a faction in accordance with the Dhamma, an act by a faction by what is a semblance of the Dhamma, an act in concord by what is a semblance of the Dhamma, an act not done, an act wrongly done, an act to be done again.’ In this case, bhikkhus, those bhikkhus who said thus, ‘An act in concord by what is a semblance of the Dhamma,’ and those bhikkhus who said thus, ‘An act not done, an act wrongly done, an act to be done again’—these bhikkhus there are speakers of the Dhamma. These five instances are also summarized.

Pabbājanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Revocation of the Act of Banishment is concluded.

266. Paṭisāraṇīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā

266. The Discourse on the Revocation of the Act of Reconciliation

447. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena paṭisāraṇīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, paṭisāraṇīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena paṭisāraṇīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, paṭisāraṇīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Handassa mayaṃ paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena vaggā…pe… adhammena samaggā… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena [V 0.0450] vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ[M 0.0474], dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammapatirūpakena samaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Ime [T 2.0304] tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino. Imepi pañca vārā saṃkhittā.

447. Here, monks, a monk who has been subjected to the act of reconciliation by the Saṅgha behaves properly, humbles himself, undertakes his rehabilitation, and requests the rescinding of the act of reconciliation. If the monks think: 'Friends, this monk who has been subjected to the act of reconciliation by the Saṅgha behaves properly, humbles himself, undertakes his rehabilitation, and requests the rescinding of the act of reconciliation. Come, let us rescind the act of reconciliation for him.' They rescind the act of reconciliation for him—unlawfully by a faction… unlawfully by a united Saṅgha… lawfully by a faction… by a faction under a semblance of the Dhamma… by a united Saṅgha under a semblance of the Dhamma. The Saṅgha present there disputes: 'This is an unlawful act by a faction, an unlawful act by a united Saṅgha, a lawful act by a faction, an act by a faction under a semblance of the Dhamma, a united act under a semblance of the Dhamma; the act was not done, the act was wrongly done, the act should be done again.' Therein, monks, those monks who said, 'It is a united act under a semblance of the Dhamma,' and those who said, 'The act was not done, the act was wrongly done, the act should be done again,' these monks among them are speakers of the Dhamma. These five instances are also stated in brief.

Paṭisāraṇīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Rescinding of the Act of Reconciliation is concluded.

267. Adassane ukkhepanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā

267. The Discourse on the Rescinding of the Act of Suspension for Not Seeing an Offense.

448. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Handassa mayaṃ āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena vaggā…pe… adhammena samaggā… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammapatirūpakena samaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino. Imepi pañca vārā saṃkhittā.

448. Here, monks, a monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to an act of suspension for not seeing an offense conducts himself properly, humbles himself, undertakes his rehabilitation, and requests the rescinding of the act of suspension for not seeing an offense. If the monks think: 'Friends, this monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to an act of suspension for not seeing an offense conducts himself properly, humbles himself, undertakes his rehabilitation, and requests the rescinding of the act of suspension for not seeing an offense. Come, let us now rescind for him the act of suspension for not seeing an offense.' They rescind for him the act of suspension for not seeing an offense—unlawfully by a faction… unlawfully by a united Saṅgha… lawfully by a faction… by a faction under a semblance of the Dhamma… by a united Saṅgha under a semblance of the Dhamma. The Saṅgha present there disputes, saying: 'This is an unlawful act by a faction, an unlawful act by a united Saṅgha, a lawful act by a faction, an act by a faction under a semblance of the Dhamma, a united act under a semblance of the Dhamma; the act was not done, the act was wrongly done, the act should be done again.' Here, monks, those monks who say, 'It is a united act under a semblance of the Dhamma,' and those who say, 'The act was not done, the act was wrongly done, the act should be done again,' these monks among them are speakers of the Dhamma. These five instances are also stated in brief.

Adassane ukkhepanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Rescinding of the Act of Suspension for Not Seeing an Offense is concluded.

268. Appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā

268. The Discourse on the Rescinding of the Act of Suspension for Not Making Amends for an Offense.

449. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammakato [V 0.0451] sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, āpattiyā appaṭikamme [T 2.0305] ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Handassa mayaṃ āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammaṃ [M 0.0475] paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena vaggā…pe… adhammena samaggā… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammapatirūpakena samaggakamma”nti, ye ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino. Imepi pañca vārā saṃkhittā.

449. Here, monks, a monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to an act of suspension for not making amends for an offense behaves properly, humbles himself, undertakes his rehabilitation, and requests the rescinding of the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense. If the monks think: 'Friends, this monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to an act of suspension for not making amends for an offense behaves properly, humbles himself, undertakes his rehabilitation, and requests the rescinding of the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense. Come, let us rescind for him the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense.' They rescind for him the act of suspension for not making amends for an offense—unlawfully by a faction… unlawfully by a united Saṅgha… lawfully by a faction… by a faction under a semblance of the Dhamma… by a united Saṅgha under a semblance of the Dhamma. The Saṅgha present there disputes, saying: 'This is an unlawful act by a faction, an unlawful act by a united Saṅgha, a lawful act by a faction, an act by a faction under a semblance of the Dhamma, a united act under a semblance of the Dhamma; the act was not done, the act was wrongly done, the act should be done again.' Here, monks, those monks who say, 'It is a united act under a semblance of the Dhamma,' and those who say, 'The act was not done, the act was wrongly done, the act should be done again,' these monks among them are speakers of the Dhamma. These five instances are also stated in brief.

Appaṭikamme ukkhepanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Rescinding of the Act of Suspension for Not Making Amends for an Offense is concluded.

269. Appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā

269. The Discourse on the Rescinding of the Act of Suspension for Non-Relinquishment.

450. Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅghena pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammakato sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Tatra ce bhikkhūnaṃ evaṃ hoti – “ayaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu saṅghena pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammakato [T 2.0306] sammā vattati, lomaṃ pāteti, netthāraṃ vattati, pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyassa kammassa paṭippassaddhiṃ yācati. Handassa mayaṃ pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhemā”ti. Te tassa pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammaṃ paṭippassambhenti – adhammena vaggā…pe… adhammena samaggā… dhammena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena vaggā… dhammapatirūpakena samaggā. Tatraṭṭho saṅgho vivadati – “adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammaṃ, dhammena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena vaggakammaṃ, dhammapatirūpakena samaggakammaṃ, akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti. Tatra, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “dhammapatirūpakena samaggakamma”nti, ye [V 0.0452] ca te bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – “akataṃ kammaṃ dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti, ime tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino. Imepi pañca vārā saṃkhittā.

450. Here, monks, a monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to an act of suspension for not relinquishing a wrong view conducts himself properly, humbles himself, and behaves in a way that leads to restoration, and he requests the revocation of the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wrong view. If it occurs to the monks: “Friends, this monk who has been subjected by the Saṅgha to an act of suspension for not relinquishing a wrong view conducts himself properly, humbles himself, and behaves in a way that leads to restoration, and he requests the revocation of the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wrong view. Come now, let us revoke for him the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wrong view.” They revoke for him the act of suspension for not relinquishing a wrong view—unlawfully as a faction… unlawfully in unity… lawfully as a faction… seemingly lawfully as a faction… seemingly lawfully in unity. The Saṅgha residing there disputes: “The act was done unlawfully as a faction, the act was done unlawfully in unity, the act was done lawfully as a faction, the act was done seemingly lawfully as a faction, the act was done seemingly lawfully in unity. The act was not done, the act was wrongly done, the act must be done again.” There, monks, those monks who say, “The act was done seemingly lawfully in unity,” and those monks who say, “The act was not done, the act was wrongly done, the act must be done again”—these monks are speakers of the Dhamma in that matter. These five cases are also stated in brief.

Appaṭinissagge ukkhepanīyakammapaṭippassaddhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Revocation of the Act of Suspension for Non-Relinquishment is concluded.

Campeyyakkhandhako navamo.

The Campeyyaka Chapter, the Ninth.

270. Tassuddānaṃ

270. The Summary of It:

Campāyaṃ [M 0.0476] bhagavā āsi, vatthu vāsabhagāmake;

Āgantukānamussukkaṃ, akāsi icchitabbake icchitabbako (ka.).

The Blessed One was in Campā, the story in Vāsabhagāmaka; he made an effort for the incoming monks, as was a desirable thing.

Pakataññunoti ñatvā, ussukkaṃ na karī tadā;

Ukkhitto [T 2.0307] na karotīti, sāgamā jinasantike.

Knowing they knew what to do, he then made no effort; he was suspended for 'not acting,' and went to the presence of the Conqueror.

Adhammena [P 1.0334] vaggakammaṃ, samaggaṃ adhammena ca;

Dhammena vaggakammañca, patirūpakena vaggikaṃ.

An act by a faction unlawfully; a unified act unlawfully; an act by a faction lawfully; and a factional act by what is a counterfeit of the law.

Patirūpakena samaggaṃ, eko ukkhipatekakaṃ;

Eko ca dve sambahule, saṅghaṃ ukkhipatekako.

A unified act by what is a counterfeit of the law; one monk suspends one monk; and one monk suspends two, many, or the Saṅgha.

Duvepi sambahulāpi, saṅgho saṅghañca ukkhipi;

Sabbaññupavaro sutvā, adhammanti paṭikkhipi.

Even two monks, and even many, and the Saṅgha suspended the Saṅgha; the supreme All-Knowing One, having heard, rejected it as 'unlawful'.

Ñattivipannaṃ yaṃ kammaṃ, sampannaṃ anusāvanaṃ;

Anussāvanavipannaṃ, sampannaṃ ñattiyā ca yaṃ.

Whatever act is defective in the motion but complete in the announcement; and whatever act is defective in the announcement but complete in the motion.

Ubhayena vipannañca, aññatra dhammameva ca;

Vinayā satthu paṭikuṭṭhaṃ, kuppaṃ aṭṭhānārahikaṃ.

Whatever act is defective in both, and is done setting aside the true nature, and is censured in the Teacher's Vinaya—that act is invalid and groundless.

Adhammavaggaṃ [V 0.0453] samaggaṃ, dhamma patirūpāni ye duve;

Dhammeneva ca sāmaggiṃ, anuññāsi tathāgato.

The unlawful factional act, the unlawful unified act, and those two which are counterfeits of the law, He rejected. The Tathāgata permitted only a unified act that is in accordance with the law.

Catuvaggo pañcavaggo, dasavaggo ca vīsati;

Parovīsativaggo ca atirekavīsativaggo (syā.), saṅgho pañcavidho tathā.

A group of four, a group of five, a group of ten, and a group of twenty; and a group of more than twenty—thus the Saṅgha is of five kinds.

Ṭhapetvā upasampadaṃ, yañca kammaṃ pavāraṇaṃ;

Abbhānakammena saha, catuvaggehi kammiko.

Setting aside the act of higher ordination, the act of Pavāraṇā, together with the act of rehabilitation, a group of four is competent for all other acts.

Duve kamme ṭhapetvāna, majjhadesūpasampadaṃ;

Abbhānaṃ pañcavaggiko, sabbakammesu kammiko.

Setting aside two acts—higher ordination in the middle country and rehabilitation—a group of five is competent for all other acts.

Abbhānekaṃ ṭhapetvāna, ye bhikkhū dasavaggikā;

Sabbakammakaro [T 2.0308] saṅgho, vīso sabbattha kammiko.

Setting aside the one act of rehabilitation, those monks who are a group of ten can perform all other acts. A Saṅgha of twenty is competent in all matters.

Bhikkhunī [M 0.0477] sikkhamānā, ca sāmaṇero sāmaṇerī;

Paccakkhātantimavatthū, ukkhittāpattidassane.

A bhikkhunī, a sikkhamānā, a sāmaṇera, a sāmaṇerī, one who has given up the training, one who has committed a terminal offense, and one suspended for not seeing an offense.

Appaṭikamme diṭṭhiyā, paṇḍako theyyasaṃvāsakaṃ;

Titthiyā tiracchānagataṃ, mātu pitu ca ghātakaṃ.

One suspended for not making amends for an offense, one suspended for not abandoning a wrong view, a paṇḍaka, one who has stolen communion, one who has gone over to the sectarians, an animal, a matricide, and a patricide.

Arahaṃ bhikkhunīdūsi, bhedakaṃ lohituppādaṃ;

Byañjanaṃ nānāsaṃvāsaṃ, nānāsīmāya iddhiyā.

A killer of an Arahant, a defiler of a bhikkhunī, a schismatic, one who has caused the Buddha's blood to flow, an ubhatobyañjanaka, one of a different communion, one in a different boundary, and one in the sky by psychic power.

Yassa saṅgho kare kammaṃ, hontete catuvīsati;

Sambuddhena paṭikkhittā, na hete gaṇapūrakā.

These twenty-four individuals, as well as the one for whom the Saṅgha is performing an act, are rejected by the Fully Awakened One; they are not quorum-fillers.

Pārivāsikacatuttho, parivāsaṃ dadeyya vā;

Mūlā mānattamabbheyya, akammaṃ na ca karaṇaṃ.

If a Saṅgha with a monk on probation as the fourth member were to grant probation, or send him back to the beginning, or grant mānatta, or rehabilitate him, it is not a valid act and it should not be done.

Mūlā [V 0.0454] arahamānattā, abbhānārahameva ca;

Na kammakārakā pañca, sambuddhena pakāsitā.

One who deserves to be sent back to the beginning, one who is on probation, one who deserves mānatta, one who is undergoing mānatta, and one who deserves rehabilitation—these five have been declared by the Fully Awakened One not to be performers of a formal act.

Bhikkhunī sikkhamānā ca, sāmaṇero sāmaṇerikā;

Paccakkhantimaummattā, khittāvedanadassane.

A bhikkhunī, a female probationer, a male novice, a female novice; one who has given up the training, one who has committed a pārājika offense, one who is insane, one who is mentally deranged, one who is afflicted by pain, and one suspended for not seeing an offense.

Appaṭikamme diṭṭhiyā, paṇḍakāpi ca byañjanā ito paraṃ syāmamūle diyaḍḍhagāthāhi abhabbapuggalā samattaṃ dassitā;

Nānāsaṃvāsakā sīmā, vehāsaṃ yassa kamma ca.

One suspended for not making amends for an offense, one suspended for not abandoning a wrong view, and also a paṇḍaka and an ubhatobyañjanaka; one of a different communion, one who is outside the boundary, one who is in the sky by psychic power, and the one against whom the formal act is performed.

Aṭṭhārasannametesaṃ, [T 2.0309][P 1.0335] paṭikkosaṃ na ruhati;

Bhikkhussa pakatattassa, ruhati paṭikkosanā.

The protest of these eighteen persons is not valid; the protest of a monk who is in a normal state is valid.

Suddhassa dunnisārito, bālo hi sunissārito;

Paṇḍako theyyasaṃvāso, pakkanto tiracchānagato.

To expel a pure one is an improper expulsion; indeed, to expel a foolish one is a proper expulsion. A paṇḍaka, one who has stolen communion, one who has gone over to another sect, and one who is an animal.

Mātu pitu arahanta, dūsako saṅghabhedako;

Lohituppādako ceva, ubhatobyañjano ca yo.

A matricide, a patricide, an arahant-killer, a corrupter of a bhikkhunī, a creator of schism in the Saṅgha; and one who has caused the Buddha's blood to flow, and one who is an ubhatobyañjanaka.

Ekādasannaṃ etesaṃ, osāraṇaṃ na yujjati;

Hatthapādaṃ tadubhayaṃ, kaṇṇanāsaṃ tadūbhayaṃ.

For these eleven persons, reinstatement is not proper. One with a severed hand, one with a severed foot, one with both severed; one with a severed ear, one with a severed nose, one with both severed.

Aṅguli aḷakaṇḍaraṃ, phaṇaṃ khujjo ca vāmano;

Gaṇḍī lakkhaṇakasā, ca likhitako ca sīpadī.

One with a severed finger or toe, one with a severed thumb or big toe, one with a severed tendon, one with webbed fingers, and a hunchback, a dwarf; one with a goiter, one who has been branded, one who has been flogged, one registered as a criminal, and one with elephantiasis.

Pāpā [M 0.0478] parisakāṇo ca, kuṇī khañjo hatopi ca;

Iriyāpathadubbalo, andho mūgo ca badhiro.

One with a wasting disease, a corrupter of the assembly, and one who is blind in one eye, one with a crippled hand, one who is lame, and one who is paralyzed; one who is crippled, one who is feeble from old age, one who is blind in both eyes, and one who is mute, and one who is deaf.

Andhamūgandhabadhiro mūgabadhirameva ca;

Andhamūgabadhiro ca, dvattiṃsete anūnakā.

One who is blind and mute, one who is blind and deaf, and one who is mute and deaf; and one who is blind, mute, and deaf. These are exactly thirty-two persons, no more and no less.

Tesaṃ [V 0.0455] osāraṇaṃ hoti, sambuddhena pakāsitaṃ;

Daṭṭhabbā paṭikātabbā, nissajjetā na vijjati.

For those persons, reinstatement is possible; this was declared by the Fully Enlightened One. For a monk for whom there is no offense to be seen, no offense to be amended, and no wrong view to be abandoned...

Tassa ukkhepanā kammā, satta honti adhammikā;

Āpannaṃ anuvattantaṃ, satta tepi adhammikā.

For such a monk, the seven acts of suspension are unlawful. For one who has committed an offense but is compliant, those seven acts are also unlawful.

Āpannaṃ nānuvattantaṃ, satta kammā sudhammikā;

Sammukhā paṭipucchā ca, paṭiññāya ca kāraṇā.

For one who has committed an offense and is not compliant, the seven acts are lawful. These acts are lawful when done in the monk's presence, after questioning, and performed upon his confession.

Sati [T 2.0310] amūḷhapāpikā, tajjanīniyassena ca;

Pabbājanīya paṭisāro, ukkhepaparivāsa ca.

The Sativinaya, the Amūḷhavinaya, the Tassapāpiyasikākamma; and the Tajjanīyakamma and Niyassakamma; the Pabbājanīyakamma, the Paṭisāraṇīyakamma, the Ukkhepanīyakamma, and Parivāsa.

Mūlā mānattaabbhānā, tatheva upasampadā;

Aññaṃ kareyya aññassa, soḷasete adhammikā.

Mūlāyapaṭikassanā, Mānatta, Abbhāna, and likewise Upasampadā. If one were to perform a different act for one deserving of another, these sixteen acts are unlawful.

Taṃ taṃ kareyya taṃ tassa, soḷasete sudhammikā;

Paccāropeyya aññaññaṃ, soḷasete adhammikā.

If one were to perform the appropriate act for the one who deserves it, these sixteen acts are lawful. If one were to impose a different act upon one deserving of another, these sixteen acts are unlawful.

Dve dve tammūlakaṃ tassa dve dve mūlā katā kassa (syā.), dodotamūlakantassa (ka.), tepi soḷasa dhammikā;

Ekekamūlakaṃ cakkaṃ, “adhamma”nti jinobravi.

For that one, when it is rooted in two factors, those sixteen acts are also lawful. A cycle rooted in a single factor, the Jina declared as 'unlawful'.

Akāsi tajjanīyaṃ kammaṃ, saṅgho bhaṇḍanakārako;

Adhammena vaggakammaṃ, aññaṃ āvāsaṃ gacchi so.

The Saṅgha performed an unlawful, factional act of censure against a quarrelsome monk. That monk went to another residence.

Tatthādhammena samaggā, tassa tajjanīyaṃ karuṃ;

Aññattha vaggādhammena, tassa tajjanīyaṃ karuṃ.

There, a united Saṅgha unlawfully performed an act of censure against him; elsewhere, a faction lawfully performed an act of censure against him.

Patirūpena vaggāpi, samaggāpi tathā karuṃ;

Adhammena samaggā ca, dhammena vaggameva ca.

Even a faction performed it by what is seemingly lawful, and likewise, even a united Saṅgha performed it. And a united Saṅgha unlawfully, and indeed a faction lawfully.

Patirūpakena vaggā ca, samaggā ca ime padā;

Ekekamūlakaṃ katvā, cakkaṃ bandhe vicakkhaṇo.

And a faction by what is seemingly lawful, and a united Saṅgha by what is seemingly lawful—these are the terms. Having made each one a basis, the wise person should construct the wheel.

Bālā [M 0.0479][V 0.0456] byattassa niyassaṃ, pabbāje kuladūsakaṃ;

Paṭisāraṇīyaṃ kammaṃ, kare akkosakassa ca.

For the foolish but competent bhikkhu, one should perform the act of subordination; one should banish a corrupter of families; and for one who abuses, one should perform the act of reconciliation.

Adassanāppaṭikamme[P 1.0336], yo ca diṭṭhiṃ na nissajje;

Tesaṃ ukkhepanīyakammaṃ, satthavāhena bhāsitaṃ.

For not seeing an offense, for not making amends, and for one who does not relinquish a wrong view; for them, the act of suspension was spoken by the Teacher.

Upari [T 2.0311] nayakammānaṃ upavinayakammānaṃ (syā.), ukkhepanīyakammānaṃ (ka.) pañño tajjanīyaṃ naye;

Tesaṃyeva anulomaṃ, sammā vattati yācite yācati (syā.), yācito (sī.).

A wise person should understand the procedure for the acts above by the procedure for the act of censure; for those very acts, one should conduct oneself properly in conformity when requested.

Passaddhi tesaṃ kammānaṃ, heṭṭhā kammanayena ca;

Tasmiṃ tasmiṃ tu kammesu, tatraṭṭho ca vivadati.

The revocation of those acts is by the method of the formal act described below; but regarding each and every one of those acts, the Saṅgha residing there disputes.

Akataṃ dukkaṭañceva, punakātabbakanti ca;

Kamme passaddhiyā cāpi, te bhikkhū dhammavādino.

Regarding a formal act or its revocation, those bhikkhus who say, 'It was not done,' 'It was badly done,' and 'It should be done again,' are speakers of the Dhamma.

Vipattibyādhite disvā, kammappatte mahāmuni;

Paṭippassaddhimakkhāsi, sallakattova osadhanti.

Having seen the bhikkhus subject to a formal act, afflicted by the disease of transgression, the Great Sage declared the revocation, just like a surgeon prescribing a remedy.

Imamhi khandhake vatthūni chattiṃsāti.

In this Khandhaka, there are thirty-six topics.

Campeyyakkhandhako niṭṭhito.

The Campeyya Khandhaka is concluded.

10. Kosambakakkhandhako

10. The Kosambaka Khandhaka

271. Kosambakavivādakathā

271. The Account of the Dispute at Kosambī

451. Tena [T 2.0312][P 1.0337][M 0.0480][V 0.0457] samayena buddho bhagavā kosambiyaṃ viharati ghositārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. So tassā āpattiyā āpattidiṭṭhi āpattidiṭṭhī (sī.) hoti; aññe bhikkhū tassā āpattiyā anāpattidiṭṭhino honti.
