So aparena samayena tassā āpattiyā anā pattidiṭṭhi hoti; aññe bhikkhū tassā āpattiyā āpattidiṭṭhino honti. Atha kho te bhikkhū taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavocuṃ – “āpattiṃ tvaṃ, āvuso, āpanno, passasetaṃ āpatti”nti? “Natthi me, āvuso, āpatti yamahaṃ passeyya”nti. Atha kho te bhikkhū sāmaggiṃ labhitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ āpattiyā adassane ukkhipiṃsu. So ca bhikkhu bahussuto hoti āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito byatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. Atha kho so bhikkhu sandiṭṭhe sambhatte bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – “anāpatti esā, āvuso, nesā āpatti. Anāpannomhi, namhi āpanno. Anukkhittomhi, namhi ukkhitto. Adhammikenamhi kammena ukkhitto kuppena aṭṭhānārahena. Hotha me āyasmanto dhammato vinayato pakkhā”ti. Alabhi kho so bhikkhu sandiṭṭhe sambhatte bhikkhū pakkhe. Jānapadānampi sandiṭṭhānaṃ sambhattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – anāpatti esā, āvuso, nesā [T 2.0313] āpatti. Anāpannomhi, namhi āpanno. Anukkhittomhi, namhi ukkhitto. Adhammikenamhi kammena ukkhitto kuppena aṭṭhānārahena. Hontu me āyasmanto dhammato vinayato pakkhā”ti. Alabhi kho so bhikkhu jānapadepi sandiṭṭhe sambhatte bhikkhū pakkhe. Atha kho te ukkhittānuvattakā bhikkhū yena ukkhepakā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā ukkhepake bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “anāpatti esā, āvuso, nesā āpatti. Anāpanno eso bhikkhu, neso bhikkhu āpanno. Anukkhitto eso bhikkhu, neso bhikkhu ukkhitto[P 1.0338]. Adhammikena kammena ukkhitto kuppena [M 0.0481] aṭṭhānārahenā”ti. Evaṃ vutte [V 0.0458] ukkhepakā bhikkhū ukkhittānuvattake bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “āpatti esā āvuso, nesā anāpatti. Āpanno eso bhikkhu, neso bhikkhu anāpanno. Ukkhitto eso bhikkhu, neso bhikkhu anukkhitto. Dhammikena kammena ukkhitto akuppena ṭhānārahena. Mā kho tumhe āyasmanto etaṃ ukkhittakaṃ bhikkhuṃ anuvattittha anuparivārethā”ti. Evampi kho te ukkhittānuvattakā bhikkhū ukkhepakehi bhikkhūhi vuccamānā tatheva taṃ ukkhittakaṃ bhikkhuṃ anuvattiṃsu anuparivāresuṃ.

451. At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery. Now at that time, a certain monk had committed an offense. He held the view that it was an offense, while other monks held the view that it was not an offense. At a later time, he came to hold the view that it was not an offense, while other monks held the view that it was an offense. Then those monks said to that monk: “Friend, you have committed an offense. See this offense.” He replied, “Friends, there is no offense for me that I should see.” Then those monks, having reached unanimity, suspended that monk for not seeing the offense. And that monk was learned, had mastered the traditions, was a bearer of the Dhamma, a bearer of the Vinaya, a bearer of the Mātikā; he was wise, competent, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of the training. Then that monk approached monks who were his acquaintances and companions and said: “Friends, this is a non-offense; it is not an offense. I have not committed an offense. I have not been suspended. I have been suspended by an unrighteous act, one that is invalid and without a valid basis. Venerables, please take my side in accordance with the Dhamma and the Vinaya.” That monk gained a faction of monks who were his acquaintances and companions. He also sent a messenger to monks in the countryside who were his acquaintances and companions, saying: “Friends, this is a non-offense; it is not an offense. I have not committed an offense. I have not been suspended. I have been suspended by an unrighteous act, one that is invalid and without a valid basis. Venerables, please take my side in accordance with the Dhamma and the Vinaya.” That monk also gained a faction of monks in the countryside who were his acquaintances and companions. Then those monks who were followers of the suspended one approached the suspending monks and said to them: “Friends, this is a non-offense; it is not an offense. This monk has not committed an offense. This monk has not been suspended. He has been suspended by an unrighteous act, one that is invalid and without a valid basis.” When this was said, the suspending monks said to the followers of the suspended one: “Friends, this is an offense; it is not a non-offense. This monk has committed an offense. This monk has been suspended. He has been suspended by a righteous act, one that is valid and has a valid basis. Venerables, do not follow that suspended monk or attend upon him.” But even though they were spoken to thus by the suspending monks, those followers of the suspended one continued to follow that suspended monk and attend upon him.

452. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idha, bhante, aññataro bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpanno ahosi. So tassā āpattiyā āpattidiṭṭhi [T 2.0314] ahosi, aññe bhikkhū tassā āpattiyā anāpattidiṭṭhino ahesuṃ. So aparena samayena tassā āpattiyā anāpattidiṭṭhi ahosi, aññe bhikkhū tassā āpattiyā āpattidiṭṭhino ahesuṃ. Atha kho te, bhante, bhikkhū taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘āpattiṃ tvaṃ, āvuso, āpanno, passasetaṃ āpatti’nti? “Natthi me, āvuso, āpatti yamahaṃ passeyya”nti. Atha kho te, bhante, bhikkhū sāmaggiṃ labhitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ āpattiyā adassane ukkhipiṃsu. So ca, bhante, bhikkhu bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito byatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. Atha kho so, bhante, bhikkhu sandiṭṭhe sambhatte bhikkhū upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca – ‘anāpatti esā, āvuso; nesā āpatti. Anāpannomhi, namhi āpanno. Anukkhittomhi, namhi ukkhitto. Adhammikenamhi kammena ukkhitto kuppena aṭṭhānārahena. Hotha me āyasmanto dhammato vinayato pakkhā’ti. Alabhi kho so, bhante, bhikkhu sandiṭṭhe sambhatte bhikkhū pakkhe. Jānapadānampi sandiṭṭhānaṃ sambhattānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pāhesi – ‘anāpatti esā, āvuso; nesā āpatti. Anāpannomhi, namhi āpanno. Anukkhittomhi, namhi ukkhitto. Adhammikenamhi kammena ukkhitto kuppena aṭṭhānārahena. Hontu me āyasmanto dhammato vinayato pakkhā’ti. Alabhi kho so, bhante, bhikkhu jānapadepi sandiṭṭhe sambhatte [T 2.0315][M 0.0482] bhikkhū pakkhe. Atha kho te, bhante, ukkhittānuvattakā bhikkhū yena ukkhepakā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā ukkhepake bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – ‘anāpatti esā, āvuso; nesā āpatti. Anāpanno eso bhikkhu, neso bhikkhu āpanno. Anukkhitto eso bhikkhu, neso bhikkhu ukkhitto. Adhammikena kammena ukkhitto kuppena aṭṭhānārahenā’ti. Evaṃ vutte te, bhante, ukkhepakā bhikkhū ukkhittānuvattake bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – ‘āpatti esā, āvuso; nesā anāpatti. Āpanno [V 0.0459] eso bhikkhu, neso bhikkhu anāpanno. Ukkhitto eso bhikkhu, neso bhikkhu anukkhitto. Dhammikena kammena ukkhitto akuppena ṭhānārahena. Mā kho tumhe āyasmanto etaṃ ukkhittakaṃ bhikkhuṃ anuvattittha anuparivārethā’ti. Evampi kho te, bhante, ukkhittānuvattakā bhikkhū ukkhepakehi bhikkhūhi vuccamānā tatheva taṃ ukkhittakaṃ bhikkhuṃ anuvattanti anuparivārentī”ti.

452. Then a certain monk approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, that monk said to the Blessed One: “Here, Venerable Sir, a certain monk had committed an offense. He had the view that it was an offense, while other monks had the view that it was not an offense. Later, he came to have the view that it was not an offense, while other monks had the view that it was an offense. Then, Venerable Sir, those monks said to that monk: ‘Friend, you have committed an offense; see this offense.’ He replied: ‘Friends, there is no offense for me that I should see.’ Then, Venerable Sir, those monks, having achieved unanimity, suspended that monk for not seeing the offense. And that monk, Venerable Sir, was learned, a master of the traditions, a Dhamma-bearer, a Vinaya-bearer, a Mātikā-bearer; he was wise, competent, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training. Then, Venerable Sir, that monk approached the monks who were his friends and companions and said: ‘Friends, this is a non-offense; this is not an offense. I have not committed an offense; I am not one who has committed an offense. I am not suspended; I am not one who has been suspended. I have been suspended by an unlawful, invalid, and groundless act. May the venerable ones be my supporters according to the Dhamma and the Vinaya.’ That monk, Venerable Sir, indeed obtained supporters among the monks who were his friends and companions. He also sent a messenger to the monks in the countryside who were his friends and companions, saying: ‘Friends, this is a non-offense; this is not an offense. I have not committed an offense; I am not one who has committed an offense. I am not suspended; I am not one who has been suspended. I have been suspended by an unlawful, invalid, and groundless act. May the venerable ones be my supporters according to the Dhamma and the Vinaya.’ That monk, Venerable Sir, indeed obtained supporters also among the monks in the countryside who were his friends and companions. Then, Venerable Sir, the followers of the suspended monk approached the suspending monks and said: ‘Friends, this is a non-offense; this is not an offense. This monk has not committed an offense; this monk is not one who has committed an offense. This monk is not suspended; this monk is not one who has been suspended. He has been suspended by an unlawful, invalid, and groundless act.’ When this was said, Venerable Sir, the suspending monks said to the followers of the suspended monk: ‘Friends, this is an offense; it is not a non-offense. This monk has committed an offense; this monk is not one who has not committed an offense. This monk is suspended; this monk is not one who has not been suspended. He has been suspended by a lawful, valid, and well-grounded act. Venerable sirs, do not follow or associate with this suspended monk.’ Even so, Venerable Sir, the followers of the suspended monk, although being spoken to by the suspending monks, continued to follow and associate with that suspended monk just as before.”

453. Atha kho bhagavā ‘bhinno bhikkhusaṅgho, bhinno bhikkhusaṅgho’ti – uṭṭhāyāsanā yena ukkhepakā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi, nisajja kho bhagavā ukkhepake bhikkhū etadavoca – “mā kho tumhe, bhikkhave, ‘paṭibhāti no, paṭibhāti no’ti yasmiṃ vā tasmiṃ vā bhikkhuṃ ukkhipitabbaṃ maññittha”.

453. Then the Blessed One, thinking, ‘The community of monks is divided, the community of monks is divided,’ rose from his seat and went to where the suspending monks were. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the suspending monks: ‘Monks, do not, thinking, “It is clear to us, it is clear to us,” consider that a monk should be suspended on just any grounds whatsoever.’”

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. So tassā āpattiyā anāpattidiṭṭhi hoti, aññe bhikkhū tassā āpattiyā āpattidiṭṭhino honti[T 2.0316]. Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū taṃ bhikkhuṃ evaṃ jānanti – ‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito byatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. Sace mayaṃ imaṃ bhikkhuṃ āpattiyā adassane ukkhipissāma, na mayaṃ iminā bhikkhunā saddhiṃ [P 1.0339] uposathaṃ karissāma, vinā iminā bhikkhunā uposathaṃ karissāma, bhavissati saṅghassa tatonidānaṃ bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇa’nti, bhedagarukehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi na so bhikkhu āpattiyā adassane ukkhipitabbo.

“Here, monks, a monk has fallen into an offense. He has the view that it is not an offense, while other monks have the view that it is an offense. If those monks know this monk to be learned, a master of the traditions, a Dhamma-bearer, a Vinaya-bearer, a Mātikā-bearer; wise, competent, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training, and think: ‘If we suspend this monk for not seeing the offense, we will not perform the Uposatha with this monk; we will perform the Uposatha without this monk, and because of that there will be disputes, quarrels, contentions, disagreements, schism in the Sangha, a split in the Sangha, a separation of the Sangha, and a division of the Sangha’—then, monks, by monks who take schism seriously, that monk should not be suspended for not seeing the offense.”

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. So tassā āpattiyā anāpattidiṭṭhi hoti, aññe bhikkhū tassā āpattiyā āpattidiṭṭhino [M 0.0483] honti. Te ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhū taṃ bhikkhuṃ evaṃ jānanti – ‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo paṇḍito byatto medhāvī lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo. Sace mayaṃ imaṃ bhikkhuṃ āpattiyā adassane ukkhipissāma, na mayaṃ iminā bhikkhunā saddhiṃ pavāressāma, vinā iminā bhikkhunā pavāressāma. Na mayaṃ iminā bhikkhunā saddhiṃ saṅghakammaṃ karissāma, vinā iminā bhikkhunā saṅghakammaṃ karissāma. Na mayaṃ iminā bhikkhunā saddhiṃ āsane nisīdissāma, vinā iminā bhikkhunā āsane nisīdissāma. Na mayaṃ iminā bhikkhunā saddhiṃ yāgupāne nisīdissāma, vinā iminā bhikkhunā yāgupāne nisīdissāma[V 0.0460]. Na mayaṃ iminā bhikkhunā saddhiṃ bhattagge nisīdissāma, vinā iminā bhikkhunā bhattagge nisīdissāma. Na mayaṃ iminā bhikkhunā saddhiṃ ekacchanne vasissāma, vinā iminā bhikkhunā [T 2.0317] ekacchanne vasissāma. Na mayaṃ iminā bhikkhunā saddhiṃ yathāvuḍḍhaṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ karissāma, vinā iminā bhikkhunā yathāvuḍḍhaṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ karissāma. Bhavissati saṅghassa tatonidānaṃ bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇa’nti, bhedagarukehi, bhikkhave, bhikkhūhi na so bhikkhu āpattiyā adassane ukkhipitabbo”ti.

Here, monks, a monk has committed an offense. He holds the view that it is not an offense, while other monks hold the view that it is an offense. If, monks, those monks know that monk thus: ‘This venerable one is learned, has mastered the traditions, is an upholder of the Dhamma, an upholder of the Vinaya, and an upholder of the Mātikā; he is wise, skilled, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training. If we suspend this monk for not seeing the offense, we will not perform the Pavāraṇā with him; we will perform it without him. We will not perform a Saṅgha act with him; we will perform it without him. We will not sit with him on a seat; we will sit there without him. We will not sit with him at the drinking of rice-gruel; we will sit there without him. We will not sit with him in the refectory; we will sit there without him. We will not dwell with him under one roof; we will dwell there without him. We will not perform towards him, according to seniority, paying homage, rising up, making the añjali gesture, and proper duties; we will perform them without him. From this cause, there will arise for the Saṅgha quarreling, strife, conflict, arguments, schism, a rift in the Saṅgha, a splitting of the Saṅgha, and disunity in the Saṅgha’—monks, by monks who hold schism as a grave matter, that monk should not be suspended for not seeing the offense.

454. Atha kho bhagavā ukkhepakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ bhāsitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena ukkhittānuvattakā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi, nisajja kho bhagavā ukkhittānuvattake bhikkhū etadavoca – “mā kho tumhe, bhikkhave, āpattiṃ āpajjitvā ‘nāmha āpannā, nāmha āpannā’ti āpattiṃ na paṭikātabbaṃ maññittha”.

454. Then the Blessed One, having spoken on this matter to the suspending monks, rose from his seat and approached the monks who were followers of the suspended one. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One said this to the monks who were followers of the suspended one: “Monks, having committed an offense, do not think, ‘We have not committed an offense, we have not committed an offense,’ and thus that the offense should not be remedied.”

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. So tassā āpattiyā anāpattidiṭṭhi hoti, aññe bhikkhū tassā āpattiyā āpattidiṭṭhino honti. So ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu te bhikkhū evaṃ jānāti – ‘ime kho āyasmanto āyasmantā (ka.) bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā paṇḍitā byattā medhāvino lajjino kukkuccakā sikkhākāmā, nālaṃ mamaṃ vā kāraṇā aññesaṃ vā kāraṇā chandā dosā [M 0.0484] mohā bhayā agatiṃ gantuṃ. Sace maṃ ime bhikkhū āpattiyā adassane ukkhipissanti[P 1.0340], na mayā saddhiṃ uposathaṃ karissanti, vinā mayā uposathaṃ karissanti, bhavissati [T 2.0318] saṅghassa tatonidānaṃ bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇa’nti, bhedagarukena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā paresampi saddhāya sā āpatti desetabbā.

“Here, monks, a monk has committed an offense. He holds the view that it is not an offense, while other monks hold the view that it is an offense. If, monks, that monk knows those monks thus: ‘These venerable ones are of great learning, have mastered the traditions, are upholders of the Dhamma, upholders of the Vinaya, upholders of the Mātikā, wise, skilled, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of training. They are not capable of going the wrong way for my sake or for the sake of others, due to desire, hatred, delusion, or fear. If these monks suspend me for not seeing the offense, they will not perform the Uposatha with me; they will perform the Uposatha without me. From this cause, there will arise for the Saṅgha quarreling, strife, conflict, arguments, schism in the Saṅgha, a rift in the Saṅgha, a splitting of the Saṅgha, and disunity in the Saṅgha.’ Monks, by a monk who holds schism as a grave matter, that offense should be confessed, even out of faith in others.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āpattiṃ āpanno hoti. So tassā āpattiyā anāpattidiṭṭhi hoti, aññe bhikkhū tassā āpattiyā āpattidiṭṭhino honti. So ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu te bhikkhū evaṃ jānāti – ‘ime kho āyasmanto bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā paṇḍitā byattā medhāvino lajjino kukkuccakā sikkhākāmā, nālaṃ mamaṃ vā kāraṇā aññesaṃ vā kāraṇā chandā dosā mohā bhayā agatiṃ gantuṃ. Sace maṃ ime bhikkhū āpattiyā adassane ukkhipissanti, na mayā saddhiṃ pavāressanti[V 0.0461], vinā mayā pavāressanti. Na mayā saddhiṃ saṅghakammaṃ karissanti, vinā mayā saṅghakammaṃ karissanti. Na mayā saddhiṃ āsane nisīdissanti, vinā mayā āsane nisīdissanti. Na mayā saddhiṃ yāgupāne nisīdissanti, vinā mayā yāgupāne nisīdissanti. Na mayā saddhiṃ bhattagge nisīdissanti vinā mayā bhattagge nisīdissanti. Na mayā saddhiṃ ekacchanne vasissanti, vinā mayā ekacchanne vasissanti. Na mayā saddhiṃ yathāvuḍḍhaṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ karissanti, vinā mayā yathāvuḍḍhaṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ karissanti, bhavissati saṅghassa tatonidānaṃ bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇa’nti[T 2.0319], bhedagarukena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā paresampi saddhāya sā āpatti desetabbā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā ukkhittānuvattakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etamatthaṃ bhāsitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

“Moreover, in this Dispensation, monks, a monk has committed an offense. He holds the view that it is not an offense, while other monks hold the view that it is an offense. If, monks, that monk knows of those monks thus: ‘These venerable ones are learned, have mastered the traditions, are upholders of the Dhamma, upholders of the Vinaya, upholders of the Mātikā, wise, discerning, intelligent, conscientious, scrupulous, and desirous of the training. They are not capable of going the wrong way for my sake or for the sake of others through favoritism, hostility, delusion, or fear. If these monks suspend me for not seeing the offense, they will not perform the Pavāraṇā with me; they will perform it without me. They will not perform a Saṅgha act with me; they will perform it without me. They will not sit on a seat with me; they will sit on a seat without me. They will not sit with me at the drinking of rice-gruel; they will sit there without me. They will not sit with me in the refectory; they will sit there without me. They will not dwell with me under one roof; they will dwell there without me. They will not perform towards me, according to seniority, paying homage, rising up, making the añjali gesture, and proper duties; they will perform them without me. From this cause, there will arise for the Saṅgha quarreling, strife, conflict, arguments, schism in the Saṅgha, a rift in the Saṅgha, a splitting of the Saṅgha, and disunity in the Saṅgha.’ Monks, by a monk who holds schism as a grave matter, that offense should be confessed, even out of faith in others.” Then the Blessed One, having spoken on this matter to the monks who were followers of the suspended one, rose from his seat and departed.

455. Tena kho pana samayena ukkhittānuvattakā bhikkhū tattheva antosīmāya uposathaṃ karonti, saṅghakammaṃ karonti. Ukkhepakā pana bhikkhū nissīmaṃ gantvā uposathaṃ karonti, saṅghakammaṃ karonti. Atha kho aññataro ukkhepako bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho [M 0.0485] so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “te, bhante, ukkhittānuvattakā bhikkhū tattheva antosīmāya uposathaṃ karonti, saṅghakammaṃ karonti. Mayaṃ pana ukkhepakā bhikkhū nissīmaṃ gantvā uposathaṃ karoma, saṅghakammaṃ karomā”ti. “Te ce, bhikkhu, ukkhittānuvattakā bhikkhū tattheva antosīmāya uposathaṃ karissanti, saṅghakammaṃ karissanti, yathā mayā ñatti ca anussāvanā ca paññattā, tesaṃ tāni kammāni dhammikāni kammāni bhavissa”nti akuppāni ṭhānārahāni. Tumhe ce, bhikkhu, ukkhepakā bhikkhū tattheva antosīmāya uposathaṃ karissatha, saṅghakammaṃ karissatha, yathā mayā ñatti ca anussāvanā ca paññattā, tumhākampi tāni kammāni dhammikāni kammāni bhavissanti akuppāni ṭhānārahāni. Taṃ kissa hetu? Nānāsaṃvāsakā ete te (syā.) bhikkhū bhikkhu (sī. syā.) tumhehi, tumhe ca tehi nānāsaṃvāsakā.

455. Now at that time, the monks who follow the suspended one performed the Uposatha and performed a formal act of the Saṅgha right there within the boundary. The suspending monks, however, having gone outside the boundary, performed the Uposatha and performed a formal act of the Saṅgha. Then a certain suspending monk approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, that monk said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, those monks who follow the suspended one perform the Uposatha and perform a formal act of the Saṅgha right there within the boundary. We, the suspending monks, however, having gone outside the boundary, perform the Uposatha and perform a formal act of the Saṅgha.” “Monk, if those monks who follow the suspended one perform the Uposatha and perform a formal act of the Saṅgha right there within the boundary, according to the motion and the proclamation as laid down by me, those acts of theirs will be lawful acts, unshakeable, and fit to stand. Monk, if you, the suspending monks, perform the Uposatha and perform a formal act of the Saṅgha right there within the boundary, according to the motion and the proclamation as laid down by me, your acts too will be lawful acts, unshakeable, and fit to stand. For what reason? These monks are of a different communion from you, and you too are of a different communion from them.”

“Dvemā, bhikkhu, nānāsaṃvāsakabhūmiyo – attanā [T 2.0320] vā attānaṃ nānāsaṃvāsakaṃ karoti, samaggo vā naṃ saṅgho ukkhipati adassane vā appaṭikamme vā appaṭinissagge vā. Imā kho, bhikkhu, dve nānāsaṃvāsakabhūmiyo. Dvemā, bhikkhu, samānasaṃvāsakabhūmiyo – attanā vā attānaṃ samānasaṃvāsaṃ karoti, samaggo vā naṃ saṅgho ukkhittaṃ osāreti adassane vā appaṭikamme vā appaṭinissagge vā. Imā kho, bhikkhu, dve samānasaṃvāsakabhūmiyo”ti.

“Monk, there are these two grounds for different communion: either one makes oneself of different communion, or the unified Saṅgha expels one for not seeing an offense, for not making amends for an offense, or for not relinquishing a wrong view. These, monk, are the two grounds for different communion. Monk, there are these two grounds for same communion: either one makes oneself of same communion, or the unified Saṅgha reinstates one who was expelled for not seeing an offense, for not making amends for an offense, or for not relinquishing a wrong view. These, monk, are the two grounds for same communion.”

456. Tena [P 1.0341][V 0.0462] kho pana samayena bhikkhū bhattagge antaraghare bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ ananulomikaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ upadaṃsenti, hatthaparāmāsaṃ karonti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma samaṇā sakyaputtiyā bhattagge antaraghare bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ ananulomikaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ upadaṃsessanti, hatthaparāmāsaṃ karissantī”ti. Assosuṃ kho bhikkhū tesaṃ manussānaṃ ujjhāyantānaṃ khiyyantānaṃ vipācentānaṃ. Ye te bhikkhū appicchā te ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti – “kathañhi nāma bhikkhū bhattagge antaraghare bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ ananulomikaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ upadaṃsessanti[M 0.0486], hatthaparāmāsaṃ karissantī”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ…pe… “saccaṃ kira, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhattagge antaraghare bhaṇḍanajātā…pe… hatthaparāmāsaṃ karontī”ti? “Saccaṃ, bhagavā”ti. Vigarahi buddho bhagavā…pe… vigarahitvā [T 2.0321] dhammiṃ kathaṃ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhinne, bhikkhave, saṅghe adhammiyāyamāne adhammiyamāne (sī. syā. katthaci) adhammīyamāne (ka.) asammodikāya vattamānāya -“asammodikāvattamānāya” iti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ saṃvaṇṇetabbapāṭho ‘ettāvatā na aññamaññaṃ ananulomikaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ upadaṃsessāma, hatthaparāmāsaṃ karissāmā’ti āsane nisīditabbaṃ. Bhinne, bhikkhave, saṅghe dhammiyāyamāne sammodikāya vattamānāya āsanantarikāya nisīditabba”nti.

456. Now at that time, monks in a dining hall or within the village, having become quarrelsome, contentious, and having fallen into dispute, were showing unsuitable bodily and verbal actions to one another; they were touching with the hand. People criticized, condemned, and spread it about: “How indeed can these ascetics, sons of the Sakyan, in a dining hall or within the village, having become quarrelsome, contentious, and having fallen into dispute, show unsuitable bodily and verbal actions to one another; how can they touch with the hand?” The monks heard those people criticizing, condemning, and spreading it about. Those monks who were of few wishes criticized, condemned, and spread it about: “How indeed can monks in a dining hall or within the village, having become quarrelsome, contentious, and having fallen into dispute, show unsuitable bodily and verbal actions to one another; how can they touch with the hand?” Then those monks reported this matter to the Blessed One… “Monks, is it true, as has been heard, that monks in a dining hall or within the village, having become quarrelsome… are touching with the hand?” “It is true, Blessed One.” The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them… Having rebuked them and given a talk on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks, when the Saṅgha is divided, is acting unrighteously, and there is disharmony, one should sit on a seat close by, thinking: ‘With this much, we will not show unsuitable bodily or verbal actions to one another, nor will we touch with the hand.’ Monks, when the Saṅgha is divided, is acting righteously, and there is harmony, one should sit leaving a seat's space in between.”

457. ma. ni. 3.236 thokaṃ visadisaṃ Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū saṅghamajjhe bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharanti. Te na sakkonti taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idha, bhante, bhikkhū saṅghamajjhe bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharanti. Te na sakkonti taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasametuṃ. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho bhagavā yena te bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi, nisajja kho bhagavā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “alaṃ, bhikkhave, mā bhaṇḍanaṃ mā kalahaṃ mā viggahaṃ mā vivāda”nti. Evaṃ vutte aññataro adhammavādī bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “āgametu, bhante, bhagavā dhammassāmī; appossukko, bhante, bhagavā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāramanuyutto viharatu. Mayametena bhaṇḍanena [T 2.0322] kalahena viggahena vivādena paññāyissāmā”ti. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “alaṃ, bhikkhave, mā bhaṇḍanaṃ mā kalahaṃ mā viggahaṃ mā vivāda”nti. Dutiyampi kho so adhammavādī bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “āgametu[P 1.0342], bhante, bhagavā dhammassāmī; appossukko, bhante[V 0.0463], bhagavā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāramanuyutto [M 0.0487] viharatu. Mayametena bhaṇḍanena kalahena viggahena vivādena paññāyissāmā”ti.

457. Now at that time, monks in the midst of the Saṅgha were quarrelsome, contentious, and had fallen into dispute, piercing one another with verbal spears. They were not able to settle that dispute. Then a certain monk approached the Blessed One, and having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, that monk said this to the Blessed One: “Here, venerable sir, monks in the midst of the Saṅgha are quarrelsome, contentious, and have fallen into dispute, piercing one another with verbal spears. They are not able to settle that dispute. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would approach those monks out of compassion.” The Blessed One consented by his silence. Then the Blessed One approached those monks, and having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One said this to those monks: “Enough, monks! Do not quarrel, do not be contentious, do not engage in physical conflict, do not dispute.” When this was said, a certain monk who was a speaker of non-Dhamma said this to the Blessed One: “Let the Blessed One, the Lord of the Dhamma, wait. Venerable sir, let the Blessed One, being free from care, dwell devoted to the pleasant abiding in this very life. We will become known by this quarreling, by this contention, by this physical conflict, and by this dispute.” A second time, the Blessed One said this to those monks: “Enough, monks! Do not quarrel, do not be contentious, do not engage in physical conflict, do not dispute.” A second time, that monk who was a speaker of non-Dhamma said this to the Blessed One: “Let the Blessed One, the Lord of the Dhamma, wait. Venerable sir, let the Blessed One, being free from care, dwell devoted to the pleasant abiding in this very life. We will become known by this quarreling, by this contention, by this physical conflict, and by this dispute.”

Kosambakavivādakathā niṭṭhitā.

The story of the dispute at Kosambī is concluded.

272. Dīghāvuvatthu

272. The Story of Dīghāvu

458. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, bārāṇasiyaṃ vajirabuddhiṭīkā oloketabbā brahmadatto nāma kāsirājā ahosi aḍḍho mahaddhano mahābhogo mahabbalo mahāvāhano mahāvijito paripuṇṇakosakoṭṭhāgāro. Dīghīti nāma kosalarājā ahosi daliddo appadhano appabhogo appabalo appavāhano appavijito aparipuṇṇakosakoṭṭhāgāro. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā caturaṅginiṃ senaṃ sannayhitvā dīghītiṃ kosalarājānaṃ abbhuyyāsi. Assosi kho, bhikkhave, dīghīti kosalarājā – “brahmadatto kira kāsirājā caturaṅginiṃ senaṃ sannayhitvā mamaṃ abbhuyyāto”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghītissa kosalarañño etadahosi – “brahmadatto kho kāsirājā aḍḍho mahaddhano mahābhogo mahabbalo mahāvāhano mahāvijito paripuṇṇakosakoṭṭhāgāro, ahaṃ panamhi daliddo appadhano appabhogo appabalo appavāhano appavijito aparipuṇṇakosakoṭṭhāgāro, nāhaṃ [T 2.0323] paṭibalo brahmadattena kāsiraññā ekasaṅghātampi sahituṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ paṭikacceva nagaramhā nippateyya”nti.

458. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Once upon a time, monks, in Bārāṇasī there was a king of Kāsī named Brahmadatta, who was rich, with great wealth, with vast possessions, with great strength, with great forces, with a vast kingdom, and with full storehouses and treasuries. There was a king of Kosala named Dīghīti, who was poor, with little wealth, with few possessions, with little strength, with small forces, with a small kingdom, and with unfilled storehouses and treasuries. Then, monks, Brahmadatta, the king of Kāsī, having assembled a fourfold army, marched against Dīghīti, the king of Kosala. Dīghīti, the king of Kosala, heard, monks: ‘Brahmadatta, the king of Kāsī, it is said, having assembled a fourfold army, is marching against me.’ Then, monks, this thought occurred to Dīghīti, the king of Kosala: ‘Brahmadatta, the king of Kāsī, is rich, with great wealth, with vast possessions, with great strength, with great forces, with a vast kingdom, and with full storehouses and treasuries; whereas I am poor, with little wealth, with few possessions, with little strength, with small forces, with a small kingdom, and with unfilled storehouses and treasuries. I am not able to withstand even a single assault by Brahmadatta, the king of Kāsī. It would be best if I were to flee from the city beforehand.’”

Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghīti kosalarājā mahesiṃ ādāya paṭikacceva nagaramhā nippati. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā dīghītissa kosalarañño balañca vāhanañca janapadañca kosañca koṭṭhāgārañca abhivijiya ajjhāvasati. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghīti kosalarājā sapajāpatiko yena vārāṇasī tena pakkāmi. Anupubbena yena bārāṇasī tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ, bhikkhave, dīghīti kosalarājā sapajāpatiko bārāṇasiyaṃ aññatarasmiṃ paccantime okāse kumbhakāranivesane aññātakavesena paribbājakacchannena paṭivasati. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghītissa kosalarañño mahesī nacirasseva gabbhinī ahosi. Tassā evarūpo dohaḷo uppanno hoti – “icchati sūriyassa uggamanakāle caturaṅginiṃ senaṃ sannaddhaṃ vammikaṃ subhūme ṭhitaṃ passituṃ[M 0.0488], khaggānañca dhovanaṃ pātuṃ”. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghītissa kosalarañño mahesī dīghītiṃ kosalarājānaṃ etadavoca – “gabbhinīmhi, deva. Tassā me evarūpo dohaḷo uppanno – icchāmi sūriyassa uggamanakāle [V 0.0464] caturaṅginiṃ senaṃ sannaddhaṃ vammikaṃ vammitaṃ (sī.) subhūme ṭhitaṃ passituṃ, khaggānañca dhovanaṃ pātu”nti. “Kuto, devi, amhākaṃ duggatānaṃ caturaṅginī senā sannaddhā vammikā subhūme ṭhitā, khaggānañca dhovanaṃ pātu”nti khaggānañca dhovananti (sī. syā.) “sacāhaṃ, deva, na labhissāmi, marissāmī”ti.

Then, monks, King Dīghīti of Kosala, taking his chief queen, promptly fled from the city. Then, monks, King Brahmadatta of Kāsī, having conquered the army, vehicles, country, treasury, and storehouses of King Dīghīti of Kosala, took up residence there. Then, monks, King Dīghīti of Kosala, together with his queen, departed for Bārāṇasī. In due course, he arrived at Bārāṇasī. There, monks, King Dīghīti of Kosala, together with his queen, lived in a potter’s dwelling in a certain outlying area of Bārāṇasī, in the guise of an unknown person and disguised as a wanderer. Then, monks, not long after, the chief queen of King Dīghīti of Kosala became pregnant. A pregnancy craving of this kind arose in her: she desired to see, at sunrise, a fourfold army, fully equipped and wearing armor, standing on level ground, and to drink the water from the washing of swords. Then, monks, the chief queen of King Dīghīti of Kosala said this to King Dīghīti of Kosala: 'I am pregnant, Your Majesty. A pregnancy craving of this kind has arisen in me: I desire to see, at sunrise, a fourfold army, fully equipped and wearing armor, standing on level ground, and to drink the water from the washing of swords.' 'O queen, for us who are destitute, from where could we obtain a fourfold army, fully equipped and wearing armor, standing on level ground, and the water from the washing of swords to drink?' 'If I do not obtain it, Your Majesty, I shall die.'

459. Tena kho pana samayena, brahmadattassa [T 2.0324] kāsirañño purohito brāhmaṇo dīghītissa kosalarañño sahāyo hoti[P 1.0343]. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghīti kosalarājā yena brahmadattassa kāsirañño purohito brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā brahmadattassa kāsirañño purohitaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – “sakhī te, samma, gabbhinī. Tassā evarūpo dohaḷo uppanno – icchati sūriyassa uggamanakāle caturaṅginiṃ senaṃ sannaddhaṃ vammikaṃ subhūme ṭhitaṃ passituṃ, khaggānañca dhovanaṃ pātu”nti. “Tena hi, deva, mayampi deviṃ passāmā”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghītissa kosalarañño mahesī yena brahmadattassa kāsirañño purohito brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho, bhikkhave, brahmadattassa kāsirañño purohito brāhmaṇo dīghītissa kosalarañño mahesiṃ dūratova āgacchantiṃ, disvāna uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena dīghītissa kosalarañño mahesī tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā tikkhattuṃ udānaṃ udānesi – “kosalarājā vata bho kucchigato, kosalarājā vata bho kucchigato”ti. Attamanā avimanā (sī. syā. katthaci, devi, hohi. Lacchasi sūriyassa uggamanakāle caturaṅginiṃ senaṃ sannaddhaṃ vammikaṃ subhūme ṭhitaṃ passituṃ, khaggānañca dhovanaṃ pātunti.

459. Now at that time, the brahmin chaplain of King Brahmadatta of Kāsī was a friend of King Dīghīti of Kosala. Then, monks, King Dīghīti of Kosala approached the brahmin chaplain of King Brahmadatta of Kāsī and said to him: “Friend, your friend the queen is pregnant. A craving of this kind has arisen in her: she wishes to see at sunrise a fourfold army, arrayed and armored, standing on level ground, and to drink the water from washing swords.” “Well then, sire, let us also see the queen.” Then, monks, the chief queen of King Dīghīti of Kosala approached the brahmin chaplain of King Brahmadatta of Kāsī. The brahmin chaplain of King Brahmadatta of Kāsī saw the chief queen of King Dīghīti of Kosala coming from afar, and rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, he extended his joined hands in reverential salutation towards the chief queen of King Dīghīti of Kosala and uttered an inspired utterance three times: “The king of Kosala is indeed in the womb! The king of Kosala is indeed in the womb!” “Be pleased, O Queen. You shall get to see at sunrise a fourfold army, arrayed and armored, standing on level ground, and to drink the water from washing swords.”

Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadattassa kāsirañño purohito brāhmaṇo yena brahmadatto kāsirājā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā brahmadattaṃ kāsirājānaṃ etadavoca – “tathā, deva, nimittāni dissanti, sve sūriyuggamanakāle [T 2.0325] caturaṅginī senā sannaddhā vammikā subhūme tiṭṭhatu, khaggā ca dhoviyantū”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā manusse āṇāpesi [M 0.0489] – “yathā, bhaṇe, purohito brāhmaṇo āha tathā karothā”ti. Alabhi kho, bhikkhave, dīghītissa kosalarañño mahesī sūriyassa uggamanakāle caturaṅginiṃ senaṃ sannaddhaṃ vammikaṃ subhūme ṭhitaṃ passituṃ, khaggānañca dhovanaṃ pātuṃ. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghītissa kosalarañño mahesī tassa gabbhassa paripākamanvāya puttaṃ vijāyi. Tassa dīghāvūti nāmaṃ akaṃsu. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvu kumāro nacirasseva viññutaṃ pāpuṇi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghītissa kosalarañño etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho brahmadatto kāsirājā bahuno amhākaṃ anatthassa kārako, iminā amhākaṃ balañca vāhanañca janapado ca koso ca koṭṭhāgārañca acchinnaṃ, sacāyaṃ amhe jānissati, sabbeva tayo ghātāpessati, yaṃnūnāhaṃ dīghāvuṃ [V 0.0465] kumāraṃ bahinagare vāseyya”nti. Atha kho bhikkhave dīghīti kosalarājā dīghāvuṃ kumāraṃ bahinagare vāsesi. Atha kho bhikkhave dīghāvu kumāro [P 1.0344] bahinagare paṭivasanto nacirasseva sabbasippāni sikkhi.

Then, monks, the brahmin chaplain of King Brahmadatta of Kāsī approached King Brahmadatta of Kāsī and said this: “Thus, sire, the signs are seen. At sunrise tomorrow, let the fourfold army stand on level ground, equipped and armored, and let the swords be washed.” Then, monks, King Brahmadatta of Kāsī commanded his men: “Do as the brahmin chaplain says.” Indeed, monks, the chief queen of King Dīghīti of Kosala got to see at sunrise the fourfold army standing on level ground, equipped and armored, and also got to drink the water from the washing of the swords. Then, monks, when her pregnancy came to term, the chief queen of King Dīghīti of Kosala gave birth to a son. They named him Dīghāvu. Then, monks, Prince Dīghāvu soon attained discernment. Then, this thought occurred to King Dīghīti of Kosala: “This King Brahmadatta of Kāsī has caused us much harm. He has seized our forces, our vehicles, our territory, our treasury, and our storehouses. If he finds out about us, he will have all three of us killed. It would be best if I had Prince Dīghāvu live outside the city.” Then, monks, King Dīghīti of Kosala had Prince Dīghāvu live outside the city. Then, monks, Prince Dīghāvu, while residing outside the city, soon mastered all the arts.

460. Tena kho pana samayena dīghītissa kosalarañño kappako brahmadatte kāsiraññe paṭivasati. Addasā kho, bhikkhave, dīghītissa kosalarañño kappako dīghītiṃ kosalarājānaṃ sapajāpatikaṃ bārāṇasiyaṃ aññatarasmiṃ paccantime okāse kumbhakāranivesane aññātakavesena [T 2.0326] paribbājakacchannena paṭivasantaṃ, disvāna yena brahmadatto kāsirājā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā brahmadattaṃ kāsirājānaṃ etadavoca – “dīghīti, deva, kosalarājā sapajāpatiko bārāṇasiyaṃ aññatarasmiṃ paccantime okāse kumbhakāranivesane aññātakavesena paribbājakacchannena paṭivasatī”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā manusse āṇāpesi – “tena hi, bhaṇe, dīghītiṃ kosalarājānaṃ sapajāpatikaṃ ānethā”ti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho, bhikkhave, te manussā brahmadattassa kāsirañño paṭissutvā dīghītiṃ kosalarājānaṃ sapajāpatikaṃ ānesuṃ. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā manusse āṇāpesi – “tena hi, bhaṇe, dīghītiṃ kosalarājānaṃ sapajāpatikaṃ daḷhāya rajjuyā pacchābāhaṃ gāḷhabandhanaṃ bandhitvā khuramuṇḍaṃ karitvā kharassarena paṇavena rathikāya rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ parinetvā dakkhiṇena dvārena nikkhāmetvā dakkhiṇato [M 0.0490] nagarassa catudhā chinditvā catuddisā bilāni nikkhipathā”ti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho, bhikkhave, te manussā brahmadattassa kāsirañño paṭissutvā dīghītiṃ kosalarājānaṃ sapajāpatikaṃ daḷhāya rajjuyā pacchābāhaṃ gāḷhabandhanaṃ bandhitvā khuramuṇḍaṃ karitvā kharassarena paṇavena rathikāya rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ parinenti.

460. Now at that time, the barber of King Dīghīti of Kosala was dwelling with King Brahmadatta of Kāsi. The barber, monks, saw King Dīghīti of Kosala together with his queen consort dwelling incognito in a potter’s dwelling in a certain remote place in Bārāṇasī, disguised as wandering ascetics. Having seen them, he approached King Brahmadatta of Kāsi and said: “Your Majesty, King Dīghīti of Kosala, together with his queen consort, is dwelling incognito in a potter’s dwelling in a certain remote place in Bārāṇasī, disguised as wandering ascetics.” Then, monks, King Brahmadatta of Kāsi ordered his men: “Well then, sirs, bring King Dīghīti of Kosala together with his queen consort.” “Yes, Your Majesty,” replied those men to King Brahmadatta of Kāsi, and they brought King Dīghīti of Kosala together with his queen consort. Then, monks, King Brahmadatta of Kāsi ordered his men: “Well then, sirs, bind King Dīghīti of Kosala together with his queen consort firmly with a strong rope, their hands behind their backs, shave their heads, and lead them around from street to street, from crossroads to crossroads, with a harsh drumbeat. Then take them out through the southern gate and, to the south of the city, cut them into four pieces and cast the pieces in the four directions.” “Yes, Your Majesty,” replied those men to King Brahmadatta of Kāsi, and they bound King Dīghīti of Kosala together with his queen consort firmly with a strong rope, their hands behind their backs, shaved their heads, and led them around from street to street, from crossroads to crossroads, with a harsh drumbeat.

Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvussa kumārassa etadahosi – “ciraṃdiṭṭhā kho me mātāpitaro. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ [T 2.0327] mātāpitaro passeyya”nti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvu kumāro bārāṇasiṃ pavisitvā addasa mātāpitaro daḷhāya rajjuyā pacchābāhaṃ gāḷhabandhanaṃ bandhitvā khuramuṇḍaṃ karitvā kharassarena paṇavena rathikāya rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ parinente, disvāna yena mātāpitaro tenupasaṅkami. Addasā kho, bhikkhave, dīghīti kosalarājā dīghāvuṃ kumāraṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ; disvāna dīghāvuṃ kumāraṃ etadavoca – “mā kho tvaṃ, tāta dīghāvu, dīghaṃ passa, mā rassaṃ. Na hi, tāta dīghāvu, verena [P 1.0345] verā sammanti; averena hi, tāta dīghāvu, verā sammantī”ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, te manussā dīghītiṃ kosalarājānaṃ etadavocuṃ [V 0.0466] – “ummattako ayaṃ dīghīti kosalarājā vippalapati. Ko imassa dīghāvu? Kaṃ ayaṃ evamāha – ‘mā kho tvaṃ, tāta dīghāvu, dīghaṃ passa, mā rassaṃ. Na hi, tāta dīghāvu, verena verā sammanti; averena hi, tāta dīghāvu, verā sammantī”ti. “Nāhaṃ, bhaṇe, ummattako vippalapāmi, api ca yo viññū so vibhāvessatī”ti. Dutiyampi kho, bhikkhave…pe… tatiyampi kho, bhikkhave, dīghīti kosalarājā dīghāvuṃ kumāraṃ etadavoca – “mā kho tvaṃ, tāta dīghāvu, dīghaṃ passa, mā rassaṃ. Na hi, tāta dīghāvu, verena verā sammanti; averena hi, tāta dīghāvu, verā sammantī”ti. Tatiyampi kho, bhikkhave, te manussā dīghītiṃ kosalarājānaṃ etadavocuṃ – “ummattako ayaṃ dīghīti kosalarājā vippalapati. Ko imassa dīghāvu[T 2.0328]? Kaṃ ayaṃ evamāha – mā kho tvaṃ, tāta dīghāvu, dīghaṃ passa, mā rassaṃ. Na hi, tāta dīghāvu, verena verā sammanti; averena hi, tāta dīghāvu, verā sammantī”ti. “Nāhaṃ, bhaṇe, ummattako vippalapāmi, api ca yo viññū so vibhāvessatī”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, te manussā dīghītiṃ kosalarājānaṃ sapajāpatikaṃ rathikāya rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ parinetvā [M 0.0491] dakkhiṇena dvārena nikkhāmetvā dakkhiṇato nagarassa catudhā chinditvā catuddisā bilāni nikkhipitvā gumbaṃ ṭhapetvā pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvu kumāro bārāṇasiṃ pavisitvā suraṃ nīharitvā gumbiye pāyesi. Yadā te mattā ahesuṃ patitā, atha kaṭṭhāni saṃkaḍḍhitvā citakaṃ karitvā mātāpitūnaṃ sarīraṃ citakaṃ āropetvā aggiṃ datvā pañjaliko tikkhattuṃ citakaṃ padakkhiṇaṃ akāsi.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to Prince Dīghāvu: 'It has been a long time since I have seen my parents. It would be well if I were to see my parents.' Then, monks, Prince Dīghāvu entered Bārāṇasī and saw his parents bound tightly with a strong rope, their hands behind their backs, their heads shaven, being led from street to street and from crossroads to crossroads to the sound of a harsh drum. Having seen them, he approached his parents. Monks, King Dīghīti of Kosala saw Prince Dīghāvu coming from afar. Having seen him, he said this to Prince Dīghāvu: 'Do not, dear Dīghāvu, look to the long, nor to the short. For, dear Dīghāvu, enmities are never appeased by enmity; by non-enmity, dear Dīghāvu, are enmities appeased.' When this was said, monks, those people said to King Dīghīti of Kosala: 'This King Dīghīti of Kosala is mad and babbling. Who is this Dīghāvu of his? To whom does he say this: “Do not, dear Dīghāvu, look to the long, nor to the short. For, dear Dīghāvu, enmities are never appeased by enmity; by non-enmity, dear Dīghāvu, are enmities appeased”?' 'Sirs, I am not mad and babbling. But one who is discerning will understand.' For a second time, monks… For a third time, monks, King Dīghīti of Kosala said this to Prince Dīghāvu: 'Do not, dear Dīghāvu, look to the long, nor to the short. For, dear Dīghāvu, enmities are never appeased by enmity; by non-enmity, dear Dīghāvu, are enmities appeased.' For a third time, monks, those people said to King Dīghīti of Kosala: 'This King Dīghīti of Kosala is mad and babbling. Who is this Dīghāvu of his? To whom does he say this: “Do not, dear Dīghāvu, look to the long, nor to the short. For, dear Dīghāvu, enmities are never appeased by enmity; by non-enmity, dear Dīghāvu, are enmities appeased”?' 'Sirs, I am not mad and babbling. But one who is discerning will understand.' Then, monks, those people led King Dīghīti of Kosala together with his consort from street to street and from crossroads to crossroads, led them out by the southern gate, and to the south of the city, cut them into four pieces, placed the portions in the four directions, set a guard, and departed. Then, monks, Prince Dīghāvu entered Bārāṇasī, brought out liquor, and gave it to the guards to drink. When they were intoxicated and had fallen down, he gathered wood, made a pyre, placed his parents’ bodies upon the pyre, lit the fire, and with hands reverently joined, he circumambulated the pyre three times.

461. Tena kho pana samayena brahmadatto kāsirājā uparipāsādavaragato hoti. Addasā kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā dīghāvuṃ kumāraṃ pañjalikaṃ tikkhattuṃ citakaṃ padakkhiṇaṃ karontaṃ, disvānassa etadahosi – “nissaṃsayaṃ kho so manusso dīghītissa kosalarañño ñāti vā sālohito vā, aho me anatthato, na hi nāma me koci ārocessatī”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvu kumāro araññaṃ gantvā yāvadatthaṃ kanditvā roditvā khappaṃ bappaṃ (sī. syā.) puñchitvā bārāṇasiṃ pavisitvā antepurassa sāmantā hatthisālaṃ gantvā hatthācariyaṃ etadavoca – “icchāmahaṃ, ācariya, sippaṃ [T 2.0329] sikkhitu”nti. “Tena hi, bhaṇe māṇavaka, sikkhassū”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvu kumāro rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya hatthisālāyaṃ mañjunā sarena gāyi, vīṇañca vādesi. Assosi kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya hatthisālāyaṃ mañjunā sarena gītaṃ vīṇañca vāditaṃ, sutvāna manusse pucchi – “ko, bhaṇe, rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ [P 1.0346] paccuṭṭhāya hatthisālāyaṃ [V 0.0467] mañjunā sarena gāyi, vīṇañca vādesī”ti? “Amukassa, deva, hatthācariyassa antevāsī māṇavako rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya hatthisālāyaṃ mañjunā sarena gāyi, vīṇañca vādesī”ti. “Tena hi, bhaṇe, taṃ māṇavakaṃ ānethā”ti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho, bhikkhave, te manussā brahmadattassa kāsirañño paṭissutvā dīghāvuṃ kumāraṃ ānesuṃ. “Tvaṃ bhaṇe māṇavaka, rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya hatthisālāyaṃ mañjunā sarena gāyi, vīṇañca vādesī”ti? “Evaṃ, devā”ti. “Tena hi tvaṃ, bhaṇe māṇavaka, gāyassu, vīṇañca vādehī”ti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvu kumāro brahmadattassa kāsirañño paṭissutvā ārādhāpekkho mañjunā sarena gāyi[M 0.0492], vīṇañca vādesi. “Tvaṃ, bhaṇe māṇavaka, maṃ upaṭṭhahā”ti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvu kumāro brahmadattassa kāsirañño paccassosi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvu [T 2.0330] kumāro brahmadattassa kāsirañño pubbuṭṭhāyī ahosi pacchānipātī kiṅkārapaṭissāvī manāpacārī piyavādī. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā dīghāvuṃ kumāraṃ nacirasseva abbhantarime vissāsikaṭṭhāne ṭhapesi.

461. At that time, King Brahmadatta of Kāsi was on the upper terrace of his excellent palace. O monks, King Brahmadatta of Kāsi saw Prince Dīghāvu with hands clasped in reverence, circumambulating the pyre three times. Having seen him, this thought occurred to him: 'Without a doubt, that person must be a maternal or paternal relative of King Dīghīti of Kosala. Alas, what a detriment to me! Surely no one will inform me.' Then, O monks, Prince Dīghāvu went into the forest and, having lamented and wept to his heart's content, wiped his tears, entered Bārāṇasī, went to the elephant stable near the inner palace, and said this to the elephant master: 'Teacher, I wish to learn the art.' 'Well then, young man, learn.' Then, O monks, Prince Dīghāvu, having arisen early in the pre-dawn hours of the night, sang in the elephant stable with a sweet voice and played the lute. O monks, King Brahmadatta of Kāsi, having also arisen early in the pre-dawn hours of the night, heard the song sung with a sweet voice and the lute being played in the elephant stable. Having heard it, he asked his men: 'Sirs, who is it that, having arisen early in the pre-dawn hours of the night, sang in the elephant stable with a sweet voice and played the lute?' They replied: 'Your Majesty, a young man, a resident pupil of a certain elephant master, having arisen early in the pre-dawn hours of the night, sang in the elephant stable with a sweet voice and played the lute.' 'Well then, sirs, bring that young man.' 'Yes, Your Majesty,' O monks, those men replied in assent to King Brahmadatta of Kāsi and brought Prince Dīghāvu. The king asked: 'Young man, was it you who, having arisen early in the pre-dawn hours of the night, sang in the elephant stable with a sweet voice and played the lute?' 'Yes, Your Majesty.' 'Well then, young man, you are to sing and play the lute.' 'Yes, Your Majesty,' O monks, Prince Dīghāvu replied in assent to King Brahmadatta of Kāsi, and wishing to please him, he sang with a sweet voice and played the lute. The king said: 'Young man, you are to attend upon me.' 'Yes, Your Majesty,' O monks, Prince Dīghāvu consented to serve King Brahmadatta of Kāsi. Then, O monks, Prince Dīghāvu became one who rose before King Brahmadatta of Kāsi and went to bed after him, who was responsive to his commands, acted agreeably, and spoke pleasantly. Then, O monks, before long, King Brahmadatta of Kāsi appointed Prince Dīghāvu to a position of innermost trust.

462. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā dīghāvuṃ kumāraṃ etadavoca – “tena hi, bhaṇe māṇavaka, rathaṃ yojehi, migavaṃ gamissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvu kumāro brahmadattassa kāsirañño paṭissutvā rathaṃ yojetvā brahmadattaṃ kāsirājānaṃ etadavoca – “yutto kho te, deva, ratho, yassa dāni kālaṃ maññasī”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā rathaṃ abhiruhi. Dīghāvu kumāro rathaṃ pesesi. Tathā tathā rathaṃ pesesi yathā yathā aññeneva senā agamāsi aññeneva ratho. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā dūraṃ gantvā dīghāvuṃ kumāraṃ etadavoca – “tena hi, bhaṇe māṇavaka, rathaṃ muñcassu, kilantomhi, nipajjissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvu kumāro brahmadattassa kāsirañño paṭissutvā rathaṃ muñcitvā pathaviyaṃ pallaṅkena nisīdi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā dīghāvussa kumārassa ucchaṅge sīsaṃ katvā seyyaṃ kappesi. Tassa kilantassa muhuttakeneva niddā okkami. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvussa kumārassa etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho brahmadatto kāsirājā bahuno amhākaṃ anatthassa [P 1.0347] kārako. Iminā amhākaṃ balañca vāhanañca janapado ca koso ca koṭṭhāgārañca [T 2.0331] acchinnaṃ. Iminā ca me mātāpitaro hatā. Ayaṃ khvassa kālo yohaṃ veraṃ appeyya”nti kosiyā khaggaṃ nibbāhi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvussa kumārassa etadahosi – “pitā kho maṃ maraṇakāle avaca ‘mā kho tvaṃ, tāta dīghāvu, dīghaṃ passa, mā rassaṃ. Na hi, tāta dīghāvu, verena verā sammanti; averena hi, tāta dīghāvu, verā sammantī’ti. Na kho metaṃ patirūpaṃ[V 0.0468], yvāhaṃ pituvacanaṃ atikkameyya”nti kosiyā khaggaṃ pavesesi. Dutiyampi kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvussa kumārassa etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho brahmadatto kāsirājā bahuno amhākaṃ anatthassa kārako, imino amhākaṃ balañca [M 0.0493] vāhanañca janapado ca koso ca koṭṭhāgārañca acchinnaṃ, iminā ca me mātāpitaro hatā, ayaṃ khvassa kālo yohaṃ veraṃ appeyya”nti kosiyā khaggaṃ nibbāhi. Dutiyampi kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvussa kumārassa etadahosi – “pitā kho maṃ maraṇakāle avaca ‘mā kho tvaṃ tāta dīghāvu, dīghaṃ passa, mā rassaṃ, na hi tāta dīghāvu verena verā sammanti; averena hi, tāta dīghāvu, verā sammantī’ti. Na kho metaṃ patirūpaṃ, yvāhaṃ pituvacanaṃ atikkameyya”nti. Punadeva kosiyā khaggaṃ pavesesi. Tatiyampi kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvussa kumārassa etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho brahmadatto kāsirājā bahuno amhākaṃ anatthassa kārako. Iminā amhākaṃ balañca vāhanañca janapado ca koso ca koṭṭhāgārañca acchinnaṃ. Iminā ca me mātāpitaro hatā. Ayaṃ khvassa kālo yohaṃ veraṃ appeyya”nti kosiyā khaggaṃ nibbāhi. Tatiyampi kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvussa kumārassa etadahosi – “pitā kho maṃ maraṇakāle avaca ‘mā kho tvaṃ, tāta dīghāvu, dīghaṃ passa, mā rassaṃ. Na hi, tāta dīghāvu, verena verā sammanti; averena hi, tāta dīghāvu, verā sammantī’ti. Na kho metaṃ patirūpaṃ, yvāhaṃ pituvacanaṃ atikkameyya’”nti punadeva kosiyā khaggaṃ pavesesi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā bhīto ubbiggo ussaṅkī utrasto sahasā vuṭṭhāsi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvu kumāro brahmadattaṃ kāsirājānaṃ etadavoca – “kissa tvaṃ[T 2.0332], deva, bhīto ubbiggo ussaṅkī utrasto sahasā vuṭṭhāsī”ti? Idha maṃ, bhaṇe māṇavaka, dīghītissa kosalarañño putto dīghāvu kumāro supinantena khaggena paripātesi. Tenāhaṃ bhīto ubbiggo ussaṅkī utrasto sahasā vuṭṭhāsinti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvu kumāro vāmena hatthena brahmadattassa kāsirañño sīsaṃ parāmasitvā dakkhiṇena hatthena khaggaṃ nibbāhetvā brahmadattaṃ kāsirājānaṃ etadavoca – “ahaṃ kho so, deva, dīghītissa kosalarañño putto dīghāvu kumāro. Bahuno tvaṃ amhākaṃ anatthassa kārako. Tayā amhākaṃ balañca vāhanañca janapado ca koso ca koṭṭhāgārañca acchinnaṃ. Tayā ca me mātāpitaro hatā. Ayaṃ khvassa kālo yvāhaṃ veraṃ appeyya”nti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā dīghāvussa kumārassa pādesu sirasā nipatitvā dīghāvuṃ kumāraṃ etadavoca – “jīvitaṃ me, tāta dīghāvu, dehi. Jīvitaṃ me, tāta dīghāvu, dehī”ti. “Kyāhaṃ ussahāmi devassa jīvitaṃ dātuṃ[M 0.0494]? Devo kho me jīvitaṃ dadeyyā”ti. “Tena hi, tāta dīghāvu, tvañceva me jīvitaṃ dehi, ahañca te jīvitaṃ [V 0.0469] dammī”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto ca kāsirājā dīghāvu ca kumāro aññamaññassa jīvitaṃ adaṃsu, pāṇiñca aggahesuṃ, sapathañca akaṃsu addūbhāya adrūbhāya, adubbhāya (ka.).

462. Then, bhikkhus, Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi, said to Prince Dīghāvu: “Well then, young man, harness the chariot; we will go to the deer forest.” “Yes, Your Majesty,” Prince Dīghāvu replied to Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi. Having harnessed the chariot, he said to Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi: “Your chariot is harnessed, Your Majesty; now is the time for whatever you deem fit.” Then, bhikkhus, Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi, mounted the chariot. Prince Dīghāvu drove the chariot. He drove it in such a way that the army went one way and the chariot another. Then, bhikkhus, Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi, after traveling a distance, said to Prince Dīghāvu: “Well then, young man, unharness the chariot; I am tired; I will lie down.” “Yes, Your Majesty,” Prince Dīghāvu replied to Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi. Having unharnessed the chariot, he sat cross-legged on the ground. Then, bhikkhus, Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi, laid his head on Prince Dīghāvu’s lap and lay down. Being tired, sleep overcame him in a moment. Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to Prince Dīghāvu: “This Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi, has caused us much misfortune. By him, our army and vehicles, our country, our treasury, and our storehouses have been seized. By him, my parents were killed. Now is the time for me to settle the enmity.” He drew his sword from its scabbard. Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to Prince Dīghāvu: “My father, at the time of his death, said to me: ‘Do not, dear Dīghāvu, consider the long enmity; do not consider the short friendship. For, dear Dīghāvu, enmities are never settled by enmity; enmities are settled by non-enmity.’ It would not be proper for me to transgress my father’s words.” He sheathed his sword. A second time, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to Prince Dīghāvu: “This Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi, has caused us much misfortune. By him, our army and vehicles, our country, our treasury, and our storehouses have been seized. By him, my parents were killed. Now is the time for me to settle the enmity.” He drew his sword from its scabbard. A second time, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to Prince Dīghāvu: “My father, at the time of his death, said to me: ‘Do not, dear Dīghāvu, consider the long enmity; do not consider the short friendship. For, dear Dīghāvu, enmities are never settled by enmity; enmities are settled by non-enmity.’ It would not be proper for me to transgress my father’s words.” He sheathed his sword again. A third time, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to Prince Dīghāvu: “This Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi, has caused us much misfortune. By him, our army and vehicles, our country, our treasury, and our storehouses have been seized. By him, my parents were killed. Now is the time for me to settle the enmity.” He drew his sword from its scabbard. A third time, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to Prince Dīghāvu: “My father, at the time of his death, said to me: ‘Do not, dear Dīghāvu, consider the long enmity; do not consider the short friendship. For, dear Dīghāvu, enmities are never settled by enmity; enmities are settled by non-enmity.’ It would not be proper for me to transgress my father’s words.” He sheathed his sword again. Then, bhikkhus, Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi, suddenly arose, frightened, agitated, apprehensive, and terrified. Then, bhikkhus, Prince Dīghāvu said to Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi: “Why, Your Majesty, have you suddenly arisen, frightened, agitated, apprehensive, and terrified?” “Just now, young man, Prince Dīghāvu, the son of King Dīghīti of Kosala, was attacking me with a sword in a dream. That is why I have suddenly arisen, frightened, agitated, apprehensive, and terrified.” Then, bhikkhus, Prince Dīghāvu, holding Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi’s head with his left hand and drawing his sword with his right hand, said to Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi: “I, Your Majesty, am that Prince Dīghāvu, the son of King Dīghīti of Kosala. You have caused us much misfortune. By you, our army and vehicles, our country, our treasury, and our storehouses have been seized. By you, my parents were killed. Now is the time for me to settle the enmity.” Then, bhikkhus, Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi, fell with his head at Prince Dīghāvu’s feet and said to Prince Dīghāvu: “Grant me my life, dear Dīghāvu! Grant me my life, dear Dīghāvu!” “How can I presume to grant Your Majesty life? It is Your Majesty who should grant me life.” “Well then, dear Dīghāvu, you grant me life, and I will grant you life.” Then, bhikkhus, Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi, and Prince Dīghāvu granted each other their lives, took each other by the hand, and swore an oath of non-betrayal.

Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā dīghāvuṃ kumāraṃ etadavoca – “tena [P 1.0348] hi, tāta dīghāvu, rathaṃ yojehi[T 2.0333], gamissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho, bhikkhave, dīghāvu kumāro brahmadattassa kāsirañño paṭissutvā rathaṃ yojetvā brahmadattaṃ kāsirājānaṃ etadavoca – “yutto kho te, deva, ratho, yassa dāni kālaṃ maññasī”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā rathaṃ abhiruhi. Dīghāvu kumāro rathaṃ pesesi. Tathā tathā rathaṃ pesesi yathā yathā nacirasseva senāya samāgañchi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā bārāṇasiṃ pavisitvā amacce pārisajje sannipātāpetvā etadavoca – “sace, bhaṇe, dīghītissa kosalarañño puttaṃ dīghāvuṃ kumāraṃ passeyyātha, kinti naṃ kareyyāthā”ti? Ekacce evamāhaṃsu – “mayaṃ, deva, hatthe chindeyyāma. Mayaṃ, deva, pāde chindeyyāma. Mayaṃ, deva, hatthapāde chindeyyāma. Mayaṃ, deva, kaṇṇe chindeyyāma. Mayaṃ, deva, nāsaṃ chindeyyāma. Mayaṃ, deva, kaṇṇanāsaṃ chindeyyāma. Mayaṃ, deva, sīsaṃ chindeyyāmā”ti. “Ayaṃ kho, bhaṇe, dīghītissa kosalarañño putto dīghāvu kumāro. Nāyaṃ labbhā kiñci kātuṃ. Iminā ca me jīvitaṃ dinnaṃ, mayā ca imassa jīvitaṃ dinna”nti.

Then, Bhikkhus, Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi, said this to Prince Dīghāvu: “If that is so, dear Dīghāvu, harness the chariot; we shall go.” “Yes, Your Majesty,” Bhikkhus, Prince Dīghāvu replied to Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi. Having harnessed the chariot, he said this to Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi: “The chariot is harnessed for you, Your Majesty; it is now time for whatever you deem fit.” Then, Bhikkhus, Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi, mounted the chariot. Prince Dīghāvu drove the chariot. He drove the chariot in such a way that before long they rejoined the army. Then, Bhikkhus, Brahmadatta, the King of Kāsi, entered Bārāṇasī, had his ministers and assembly gathered, and said this: “If, sirs, you were to see Prince Dīghāvu, the son of King Dīghīti of Kosala, what would you do to him?” Some said thus: “We would cut off his hands, Your Majesty. We would cut off his feet, Your Majesty. We would cut off his hands and feet, Your Majesty. We would cut off his ears, Your Majesty. We would cut off his nose, Your Majesty. We would cut off his ears and nose, Your Majesty. We would cut off his head, Your Majesty.” “This, sirs, is Prince Dīghāvu, the son of King Dīghīti of Kosala. It is not possible to do anything to him. For by him my life was given, and by me his life was given.”

463. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā dīghāvuṃ kumāraṃ etadavoca – “yaṃ kho te, tāta dīghāvu, pitā maraṇakāle avaca ‘mā kho tvaṃ, tāta dīghāvu, dīghaṃ passa, mā rassaṃ. Na hi, tāta dīghāvu, verena verā sammanti; averena hi, tāta dīghāvu, verā sammantī’ti, kiṃ te pitā sandhāya avacā”ti? “Yaṃ kho me[T 2.0334], deva, pitā maraṇakāle avaca ‘mā dīgha’nti mā ciraṃ veraṃ akāsīti. Imaṃ kho me, deva, pitā maraṇakāle avaca mā dīghanti. Yaṃ kho me, deva, pitā maraṇakāle avaca ‘mā rassa’nti mā khippaṃ mittehi bhijjitthā”ti. Imaṃ kho me, deva, pitā maraṇakāle avaca [M 0.0495] mā rassanti. Yaṃ kho me, deva, pitā maraṇakāle avaca “na hi, tāta dīghāvu, verena verā sammanti, averena hi, tāta dīghāvu, verā sammantī”ti devena me mātāpitaro hatāti. Sacāhaṃ devaṃ jīvitā voropeyyaṃ, ye devassa atthakāmā te maṃ jīvitā voropeyyuṃ, ye me atthakāmā te te jīvitā voropeyyuṃ – evaṃ taṃ veraṃ verena na vūpasameyya. Idāni ca pana me devena jīvitaṃ dinnaṃ, mayā ca devassa jīvitaṃ dinnaṃ. Evaṃ taṃ veraṃ averena vūpasantaṃ. Imaṃ kho me, deva, pitā maraṇakāle avaca – na hi, tāta dīghāvu, verena verā sammanti; averena hi[V 0.0470], tāta dīghāvu, verā sammantī”ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, brahmadatto kāsirājā – “acchariyaṃ [P 1.0349] vata bho! Abbhutaṃ vata bho! Yāva paṇḍito ayaṃ dīghāvu kumāro, yatra hi nāma pituno saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānissatī”ti pettikaṃ balañca vāhanañca janapadañca kosañca koṭṭhāgārañca paṭipādesi, dhītarañca adāsi. Tesañhi nāma, bhikkhave, rājūnaṃ ādinnadaṇḍānaṃ ādinnasatthānaṃ evarūpaṃ khantisoraccaṃ bhavissati. Idha kho pana taṃ, bhikkhave[T 2.0335], sobhetha yaṃ tumhe evaṃ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā khamā ca bhaveyyātha soratā cāti? Tatiyampi kho bhagavā te bhikkhū etadavoca – “alaṃ, bhikkhave, mā bhaṇḍanaṃ mā kalahaṃ mā viggahaṃ mā vivāda”nti. Tatiyampi kho so adhammavādī bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “āgametu, bhante, bhagavā dhammassāmī; appossukko, bhante, bhagavā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāramanuyutto viharatu. Mayametena bhaṇḍanena kalahena viggahena vivādena paññāyissāmā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā – pariyādinnarūpā kho ime moghapurisā, nayime sukarā saññāpetunti – uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

463. Then, Bhikkhus, King Brahmadatta of Kāsī said this to Prince Dīghāvu: ‘Dear Dīghāvu, that which your father said at the time of his death—“Dear Dīghāvu, do not look at the long, nor at the short. For, dear Dīghāvu, enmities are not appeased by enmity; indeed, dear Dīghāvu, enmities are appeased by non-enmity”—with what intention did your father say this?’ ‘Your Majesty, that which my father said at the time of his death, “Not long,” meant: “Do not maintain enmity for long.” This, Your Majesty, is what my father said at the time of his death: “Not long.” That which my father said at the time of his death, “Not short,” meant: “Do not quickly break with friends.” This, Your Majesty, is what my father said at the time of his death: “Not short.” That which my father said at the time of his death—“For, dear Dīghāvu, enmities are not appeased by enmity; indeed, dear Dīghāvu, enmities are appeased by non-enmity”—meant this: “Your Majesty has killed my mother and father. If I were to deprive Your Majesty of life, those who wish Your Majesty well would deprive me of life, and those who wish me well would deprive them of life. Thus that enmity would not be appeased by enmity. But now, Your Majesty has given me my life, and I have given Your Majesty his life. Thus that enmity is appeased by non-enmity.” This, Your Majesty, is what my father said at the time of his death: “For, dear Dīghāvu, enmities are not appeased by enmity; indeed, dear Dīghāvu, enmities are appeased by non-enmity.”’ Then, Bhikkhus, King Brahmadatta of Kāsī said: ‘Wonderful, sirs! Astonishing, sirs! How very wise is this Prince Dīghāvu, in that he understands in detail the meaning of what was spoken in brief by his father!’ And he restored his paternal army, vehicles, country, treasury, and granary, and he gave him his daughter. ‘For those kings, Bhikkhus, who have taken up the rod and taken up the sword, such patience and gentleness can arise. How much more, then, should it befit you, Bhikkhus, who have gone forth in such a well-expounded Dhamma and Vinaya, that you be patient and gentle?’ For a third time, the Blessed One said this to those bhikkhus: ‘Enough, Bhikkhus! No quarreling, no contention, no dispute, no strife.’ For a third time, that bhikkhu who was a speaker of non-Dhamma said this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, let the Blessed One, the Lord of the Dhamma, wait. Venerable sir, let the Blessed One dwell unconcerned, devoted to a pleasant abiding in this very life. We will become known by this quarreling, this contention, this dispute, and this strife.’ Then the Blessed One thought: ‘These worthless men are incorrigible; it is not easy to make them understand.’ And rising from his seat, he departed.

Dīghāvubhāṇavāro niṭṭhito paṭhamo.

The first Dīghāvu recitation section is completed.

464. ma. ni. 3.236 Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya kosambiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Kosambiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya saṅghamajjhe ṭhitakova imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

464. Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Kosambī for alms. Having wandered for alms in Kosambī, after the meal, on returning from the alms round, having put his lodging in order, he took his bowl and robe, and standing right in the midst of the Sangha, spoke these verses:

ma. ni. 3.237 “Puthusaddo [M 0.0496] samajano, na bālo koci maññatha;

Saṅghasmiṃ bhijjamānasmiṃ, nāññaṃ bhiyyo amaññaruṃ.

This like-minded group is loud-voiced; not a single one thinks, ‘I am a fool.’ When the Sangha was being broken, they considered nothing further.

ma. ni. 3.237 “Parimuṭṭhā paṇḍitābhāsā, vācāgocarabhāṇino;

Yāvicchanti mukhāyāmaṃ, yena nītā na taṃ vidū.

They are unmindful, wise in their own estimation, speakers whose domain is mere words. They speak as much as they wish, with mouths wide open, yet they do not know that by which they are led.

ma. ni. 3.237 “Akkocchi maṃ avadhi maṃ, ajini maṃ ahāsi me;

Ye [T 2.0336] ca taṃ upanayhanti, veraṃ tesaṃ na sammati.

“He abused me, he struck me, he defeated me, he robbed me.” For those who bear such a grudge, hatred never ceases.

ma. ni. 3.237 “Akkocchi maṃ avadhi maṃ, ajini maṃ ahāsi me;

Ye ca taṃ nupanayhanti, veraṃ tesūpasammati.

“He abused me, he struck me, he defeated me, he robbed me.” For those who do not bear such a grudge, hatred is appeased.

ma. ni. 3.237 “Na [V 0.0471] hi verena verāni, sammantīdha kudācanaṃ;

Averena ca sammanti, esadhammo sanantano.

For hatreds are never appeased by hatred here; they are appeased by non-hatred. This is an eternal law.

ma. ni. 3.237 “Pare ca na vijānanti, mayamettha yamāmase;

Ye ca tattha vijānanti, tato sammanti medhagā.

Others do not realize, “We are perishing here.” But those who do realize it, their quarrels are thereby appeased.

ma. ni. 3.237 “Aṭṭhicchinnā [P 1.0350] pāṇaharā, gavāssadhanahārino;

Raṭṭhaṃ vilumpamānānaṃ, tesampi hoti saṅgati.

Those who break bones, take life, steal cattle, horses, and wealth, and those who plunder a kingdom—even for them there is reconciliation.

“Kasmā tumhāka no siyā;

ma. ni. 3.237 “Sace labhetha nipakaṃ sahāyaṃ;

Saddhiṃcaraṃ sādhuvihāri dhīraṃ;

Abhibhuyya sabbāni parissayāni;

Careyya tenattamano satīmā.

Why should it not be so for you? If one should find a prudent companion, one who lives well and is steadfast, who fares together with one, having overcome all dangers, one should fare with him, glad at heart and mindful.

ma. ni. 3.237 “No ce labhetha nipakaṃ sahāyaṃ;

Saddhiṃ caraṃ sādhuvihāri dhīraṃ;

Rājāva raṭṭhaṃ vijitaṃ pahāya;

Eko care mātaṅgaraññeva nāgo.

If one should not find a prudent companion, one who lives well and is steadfast, who fares together with one, then like a king who has abandoned his conquered kingdom, one should fare alone, like a Mātaṅga elephant in the forest.

ma. ni. 3.237 “Ekassa caritaṃ seyyo;

Natthi bāle sahāyatā;

Eko [T 2.0337] care na ca pāpāni kayirā;

Appossukko mātaṅgaraññeva nāgo”ti.

It is better to fare alone; there is no companionship with a fool. One should fare alone and do no evil, with few wishes, like a Mātaṅga elephant in the forest.

Dīghāvuvatthu niṭṭhitaṃ.

The story of Dīghāvu is concluded.

273. Bālakaloṇakagamanakathā

273. The Account of the Journey to Bālakaloṇaka

465. Atha [M 0.0497] kho bhagavā saṅghamajjhe ṭhitakova imā gāthāyo bhāsitvā yena bālakaloṇakagāmo [V 0.0472] bālakaloṇakāragāmo (sī. syā.) tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā bhagu bālakaloṇakagāme viharati. Addasā kho āyasmā bhagu bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ, disvāna āsanaṃ paññapesi, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipi, paccuggantvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahesi. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane, nisajja kho bhagavā pāde pakkhālesi. Āyasmāpi kho bhagu bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ bhaguṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “kacci, bhikkhu, khamanīyaṃ; kacci yāpanīyaṃ, kacci piṇḍakena na kilamasī”ti? “Khamanīyaṃ, bhagavā, yāpanīyaṃ, bhagavā; na cāhaṃ, bhante, piṇḍakena kilamāmī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ bhaguṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena pācīnavaṃsadāyo tenupasaṅkami.

465. Then the Blessed One, standing in the midst of the Saṅgha, having spoken these verses, approached the village of Bālakaloṇaka. Now at that time the Venerable Bhagu was dwelling in the village of Bālakaloṇaka. The Venerable Bhagu saw the Blessed One coming from afar. When he saw him, he prepared a seat, set out water for the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet, and went forth to receive his bowl and robe. The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat, and having sat down, he washed his feet. Then the Venerable Bhagu, having paid homage to the Blessed One, sat down to one side. As the Venerable Bhagu was sitting to one side, the Blessed One said to him: “I hope, Bhikkhu, you are keeping well; I hope you are managing; I hope you are not weary from the alms-round?” “I am keeping well, Blessed One; I am managing, Blessed One; and I am not weary from the alms-round, Venerable Sir.” Then the Blessed One, having instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened the Venerable Bhagu with a Dhamma talk, rose from his seat and approached Pācīnavaṃsadāya.

Bālakaloṇakagamanakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Journey to Bālakaloṇaka is concluded.

274. Pācīnavaṃsadāyagamanakathā

274. The Account of the Journey to Pācīnavaṃsadāya

466. ma. ni. 1.325 ādayo passitabbaṃ Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ca anuruddho āyasmā ca nandiyo āyasmā ca kimilo kimbilo (sī. syā.) pācīnavaṃsadāye viharanti. Addasā kho dāyapālo bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ, disvāna bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “mā, samaṇa, etaṃ dāyaṃ pāvisi. Santettha tayo kulaputtā attakāmarūpā [T 2.0338] viharanti. Mā tesaṃ aphāsumakāsī”ti. Assosi kho āyasmā anuruddho dāyapālassa bhagavatā saddhiṃ mantayamānassa, sutvāna dāyapālaṃ etadavoca – “māvuso, dāyapāla, bhagavantaṃ vāresi[P 1.0351]. Satthā no bhagavā anuppatto”ti. Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho yenāyasmā ca nandiyo āyasmā ca kimilo tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantañca nandiyaṃ āyasmantañca kimilaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkamathāyasmanto abhikkamathāyasmanto, satthā no bhagavā anuppatto”ti. Atha kho āyasmā ca anuruddho āyasmā ca nandiyo āyasmā ca kimilo bhagavantaṃ paccuggantvā eko bhagavato pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahesi, eko āsanaṃ paññapesi, eko pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipi. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane[M 0.0498], nisajja kho bhagavā pāde pakkhālesi. Tepi kho āyasmanto bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “kacci vo, anuruddhā, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ; kacci piṇḍakena na kilamathā”ti? “Khamanīyaṃ bhagavā, yāpanīyaṃ bhagavā; na ca mayaṃ, bhante, piṇḍakena kilamāmā”ti.

466. Now at that time, the Venerable Anuruddha, the Venerable Nandiya, and the Venerable Kimbila were dwelling in the Eastern Bamboo Grove. The grove-keeper saw the Blessed One coming from afar. When he saw him, he said to the Blessed One: “Do not enter this grove, ascetic. There are three sons of good family dwelling here who desire their own welfare. Do not cause them discomfort.” The Venerable Anuruddha heard the grove-keeper conversing with the Blessed One. When he heard him, he said to the grove-keeper: “Friend grove-keeper, do not prevent the Blessed One. Our Teacher, the Blessed One, has arrived.” Then the Venerable Anuruddha approached the Venerable Nandiya and the Venerable Kimbila. Having approached them, he said to them: “Come forth, venerable sirs, come forth! Our Teacher, the Blessed One, has arrived.” Then the Venerable Anuruddha, the Venerable Nandiya, and the Venerable Kimbila went forth to meet the Blessed One. One received the Blessed One’s bowl and robe, one prepared a seat, and one set out water for the feet, a footstool, and a potsherd for rubbing the feet. The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat, and having sat down, he washed his feet. Those venerable ones, having paid homage to the Blessed One, sat down to one side. As the Venerable Anuruddha was sitting to one side, the Blessed One said to him: “I hope, Anuruddhas, you are keeping well, I hope you are getting by; I hope you are not wearied by alms-gathering?” “We are keeping well, Blessed One, we are getting by, Blessed One, and, venerable sir, we are not wearied by alms-gathering.”

“Kacci [V 0.0473] pana vo anuruddhā samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṃ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharathā”ti? “Taggha mayaṃ, bhante, samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṃ [T 2.0339] piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharāmā”ti. “Yathā kathaṃ pana tumhe, anuruddhā, samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṃ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharathā”ti? “Idha mayhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ hoti – ‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yohaṃ evarūpehi sabrahmacārīhi saddhiṃ viharāmī’”ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, imesu āyasmantesu mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi ceva raho ca; mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ… mettaṃ manokammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi ceva raho ca. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ hoti – “‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ sakaṃ cittaṃ nikkhipitvā imesaṃyeva āyasmantānaṃ cittassa vasena vatteyya’nti. So kho ahaṃ, bhante, sakaṃ cittaṃ nikkhipitvā imesaṃyeva āyasmantānaṃ cittassa vasena vattāmi. Nānā hi kho no, bhante, kāyā, ekañca pana maññe citta”nti.

“I hope, Anuruddhas, you are dwelling in concord, with mutual appreciation, without dispute, blending like milk and water, regarding each other with kindly eyes?” “Indeed, venerable sir, we are dwelling in concord, with mutual appreciation, without dispute, blending like milk and water, regarding each other with kindly eyes.” “But how, Anuruddhas, do you dwell in such concord?” “Here, venerable sir, it occurs to me: ‘It is a gain for me, it is a great gain for me, that I am dwelling with such companions in the holy life.’ Towards these venerable ones, loving-kindness in bodily action is present to me, both openly and in private; loving-kindness in verbal action… loving-kindness in mental action is present to me, both openly and in private. It occurs to me: ‘Suppose I were to set aside my own mind and act according to the minds of these venerable ones?’ So, venerable sir, I set aside my own mind and act according to the minds of these venerable ones. Though our bodies are different, venerable sir, I believe our mind is one.”

Āyasmāpi kho nandiyo…pe… āyasmāpi kho kimilo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “mayhampi kho, bhante, evaṃ hoti – ‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yohaṃ evarūpehi sabrahmacārīhi saddhiṃ viharāmī’ti.
