Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, imesu āyasmantesu mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi ceva raho ca; mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ mettaṃ manokammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi ceva raho ca. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ hoti ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ sakaṃ cittaṃ nikkhipitvā imesaṃyeva āyasmantānaṃ cittassa vasena vatteyya’nti. So kho ahaṃ, bhante, sakaṃ cittaṃ nikkhipitvā imesaṃyeva āyasmantānaṃ cittassa vasena vattāmi. Nānā [T 2.0340] hi kho no, bhante, kāyā, ekañca pana maññe cittanti. Evaṃ kho mayaṃ, bhante, samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṃ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharāmā”ti.

The Venerable Nandiya… and the Venerable Kimila also spoke to the Blessed One thus: “For me too, venerable sir, this thought occurs: ‘It is a gain for me, indeed! It is well-gained for me, indeed, that I dwell with such companions in the holy life.’ For me, venerable sir, towards these venerable ones, loving bodily action is established, both openly and in private; loving verbal action and loving mental action are established, both openly and in private. To me, venerable sir, this thought occurs: ‘What if I were to set aside my own mind and act according to the will of these venerable ones?’ So, venerable sir, I set aside my own mind and act according to the will of these venerable ones. Our bodies are indeed different, venerable sir, but I think our minds are as one. Thus, venerable sir, we dwell in concord, with mutual appreciation, without dispute, blending like milk and water, regarding each other with loving eyes.”

“Kacci [M 0.0499] pana vo, anuruddhā, appamattā [P 1.0352] ātāpino pahitattā viharathā”ti? “Taggha mayaṃ, bhante, appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharāmā”ti. “Yathā kathaṃ pana tumhe, anuruddhā, appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharathā”ti? “Idha, bhante, amhākaṃ yo paṭhamaṃ gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamati so āsanaṃ paññapeti, pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ upanikkhipati, avakkārapātiṃ dhovitvā upaṭṭhāpeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti. Yo pacchā gāmato piṇḍāya paṭikkamati, sace hoti bhuttāvaseso, sace ākaṅkhati bhuñjati, no ce ākaṅkhati appaharite vā chaḍḍeti. Appāṇake vā udake opilāpeti. So āsanaṃ uddharati[V 0.0474], pādodakaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ pādakathalikaṃ paṭisāmeti, avakkārapātiṃ dhovitvā paṭisāmeti, pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ paṭisāmeti, bhattaggaṃ sammajjati. Yo passati pānīyaghaṭaṃ vā paribhojanīyaghaṭaṃ vā vaccaghaṭaṃ vā rittaṃ tucchaṃ so upaṭṭhāpeti. Sacassa hoti avisayhaṃ, hatthavikārena dutiyaṃ āmantetvā hatthavilaṅghakena upaṭṭhāpema, na tveva mayaṃ, bhante, tappaccayā vācaṃ bhindāma. Pañcāhikaṃ kho pana mayaṃ, bhante, sabbarattiṃ dhammiyā kathāya sannisīdāma. Evaṃ kho mayaṃ, bhante, appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharāmā”ti.

“I hope, Anuruddhas, you are dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute?” “Indeed, venerable sir, we are dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute.” “But how, Anuruddhas, do you dwell diligent, ardent, and resolute?” “Here, venerable sir, whoever among us returns first from the village from the alms round prepares the seats, sets out water for the feet, a footstool, and a foot-rubbing potsherd, washes and sets out the slop basin, and prepares drinking water and water for use. Whoever returns later from the village from the alms round, if there is any leftover food, he eats it if he wishes; if he does not wish, he discards it where there is no green vegetation or pours it into water where there are no living beings. He puts away the seats, clears away the water for the feet, the footstool, and the foot-rubbing potsherd, washes and puts away the slop basin, clears away the drinking water and water for use, and sweeps the refectory. Whoever sees that the drinking water pot, the water for use pot, or the toilet pot is empty or void, he sets it up. If it is too much for him, having beckoned a second person with a hand gesture, we set it up with our hands joined; but, venerable sir, we do not break into speech on account of that. Indeed, venerable sir, every five days we sit together for the whole night for a Dhamma talk. Thus, venerable sir, we are dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute.”

Pācinavaṃsadāyagamanakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Journey to Pācinavaṃsadāya is concluded.

275. Pālileyyakagamanakathā

The Account of the Journey to Pālileyyaka

467. udā. 35 ādayo thokaṃ visadisaṃ Atha [T 2.0341] kho bhagavā āyasmantañca anuruddhaṃ āyasmantañca nandiyaṃ āyasmantañca kimilaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena pālileyyakaṃ pārileyyakaṃ (sī. syā.) tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena pālileyyakaṃ tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā pālileyyake viharati rakkhitavanasaṇḍe bhaddasālamūle. Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “ahaṃ kho pubbe ākiṇṇo na phāsu vihāsiṃ tehi kosambakehi kosabbhikehi (syā.) bhikkhūhi bhaṇḍanakārakehi kalahakārakehi vivādakārakehi bhassakārakehi saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakehi. Somhi etarahi eko adutiyo sukhaṃ phāsu viharāmi aññatreva tehi kosambakehi bhikkhūhi bhaṇḍanakārakehi kalahakārakehi vivādakārakehi bhassakārakehi saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakehī”ti.

275. Then the Blessed One, having instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened Venerable Anuruddha, Venerable Nandiya, and Venerable Kimila with a Dhamma talk, rose from his seat and set out for Pālileyyaka. Journeying by stages, he arrived at Pālileyyaka. There the Blessed One dwelt in Pālileyyaka, in the Rakkhita Grove, at the foot of a splendid sal tree. Then, while the Blessed One was alone and in seclusion, this reflection arose in his mind: “Formerly, I lived crowded and not at ease with those monks of Kosambī who were makers of quarrels, makers of strife, makers of disputes, makers of much talk, and makers of issues in the Saṅgha. But now, I live alone, without a companion, happily and at ease, quite apart from those monks of Kosambī who are makers of quarrels, makers of strife, makers of disputes, makers of much talk, and makers of issues in the Saṅgha.”

Aññataropi [M 0.0500] kho hatthināgo ākiṇṇo viharati hatthīhi hatthinīhi hatthikaḷabhehi hatthicchāpehi, chinnaggāni ceva tiṇāni khādati, obhaggobhaggañcassa sākhābhaṅgaṃ khādanti, āvilāni ca pānīyāni pivati, ogāhā cassa otiṇṇassa hatthiniyo kāyaṃ upanighaṃsantiyo gacchanti. Atha kho tassa [P 1.0353] hatthināgassa etadahosi – “ahaṃ kho ākiṇṇo viharāmi hatthīhi hatthinīhi hatthikaḷabhehi hatthicchāpehi, chinnaggāni ceva tiṇāni khādāmi, obhaggobhaggañca me sākhābhaṅgaṃ [T 2.0342] khādanti, āvilāni ca pānīyāni pivāmi, ogāhā ca me otiṇṇassa hatthiniyo kāyaṃ upanighaṃsantiyo gacchanti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ ekova gaṇasmā vūpakaṭṭho vihareyya”nti. Atha kho so hatthināgo yūthā apakkamma yena pālileyyakaṃ rakkhitavanasaṇḍo bhaddasālamūlaṃ yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā soṇḍāya bhagavato pānīyaṃ [V 0.0475] paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhāpeti, appaharitañca karoti. Atha kho tassa hatthināgassa etadahosi – “ahaṃ kho pubbe ākiṇṇo na phāsu vihāsiṃ hatthīhi hatthinīhi hatthikaḷabhehi hatthicchāpehi, chinnaggāni ceva tiṇāni khādiṃ, obhaggobhaggañca me sākhābhaṅgaṃ khādiṃsu, āvilāni ca pānīyāni apāyiṃ ogāhā ca me otiṇṇassa ogāhañcassa otiṇṇassa (syā.), ogāhā cassa uttiṇṇassa (sī.) hatthiniyo kāyaṃ upanighaṃsantiyo agamaṃsu. Somhi etarahi eko adutiyo sukhaṃ phāsu viharāmi aññatreva hatthīhi hatthinīhi hatthikaḷabhehi hatthicchāpehī”ti.

467. A certain bull elephant, too, lived crowded by elephants, she-elephants, elephant calves, and young elephants. He ate grass with the tips cut off, and they ate the branches he had repeatedly broken off. He drank turbid water, and when he came up from the watering place, the she-elephants went along, rubbing against his body. Then this thought occurred to that bull elephant: “I live crowded by elephants, she-elephants, elephant calves, and young elephants. I eat grass with the tips cut off, and they eat the branches I have repeatedly broken off. I drink turbid water, and when I come up from the watering place, the she-elephants go along, rubbing against my body. Suppose I were to live alone, secluded from the herd.” Then that bull elephant, having left the herd, approached the Blessed One where he was at the protected forest grove at Pālileyyaka, at the foot of a splendid sal tree. Having approached, he provided the Blessed One with water for drinking and for use with his trunk, and made the place free of greenery. Then this thought occurred to that bull elephant: “Formerly, I lived crowded and uncomfortably, surrounded by elephants, she-elephants, elephant calves, and young elephants. I ate grass with the tips cut off, they ate the branches I had repeatedly broken off, I drank turbid water, and when I came up from the watering place, the she-elephants went along, rubbing against my body. But now I live alone, without a companion, happily and at ease, quite apart from elephants, she-elephants, elephant calves, and young elephants.”

Atha kho bhagavā attano ca pavivekaṃ viditvā tassa ca hatthināgassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

Then the Blessed One, knowing his own solitude and comprehending with his mind the thought in the mind of that bull elephant, at that time uttered this inspired utterance:

udā. 35 “Etaṃ evaṃ (ka.) nāgassa nāgena, īsādantassa hatthino;

Sameti cittaṃ cittena, yadeko ramatī vane”ti.

The mind of the bull elephant with tusks like plough-poles accords with that of the Great One (Nāga), mind with mind, since he delights alone in the forest.

Atha kho bhagavā pālileyyake yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā yena sāvatthi tena cārikaṃ pakkāmi. Anupubbena cārikaṃ caramāno yena [T 2.0343] sāvatthi tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho kosambakā upāsakā – “ime kho ayyā kosambakā bhikkhū bahuno amhākaṃ anatthassa kārakā[M 0.0501]. Imehi ubbāḷho bhagavā pakkanto. Handa mayaṃ ayye kosambake bhikkhū neva abhivādeyyāma, na paccuṭṭheyyāma, na añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ kareyyāma, na sakkareyyāma, na garuṃ kareyyāma, na māneyyāma, na bhajeyyāma, na pūjeyyāma, upagatānampi piṇḍakaṃ na dajjeyyāma – evaṃ ime amhehi asakkariyamānā agarukariyamānā amāniyamānā abhajiyamānā apūjiyamānā asakkārapakatā pakkamissanti vā vibbhamissanti vā bhagavantaṃ vā pasādessantī”ti. Atha kho kosambakā upāsakā kosambake bhikkhū neva abhivādesuṃ, na paccuṭṭhesuṃ, na añjalikammaṃ [P 1.0354] sāmīcikammaṃ akaṃsu, na sakkariṃsu, na garuṃ kariṃsu, na mānesuṃ, na bhajesuṃ na pūjesuṃ, upagatānampi piṇḍakaṃ na adaṃsu. Atha kho kosambakā bhikkhū kosambakehi upāsakehi asakkariyamānā agarukariyamānā amāniyamānā abhajiyamānā apūjiyamānā asakkārapakatā evamāhaṃsu – “handa mayaṃ, āvuso, sāvatthiṃ gantvā bhagavato santike imaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasameyyāmā”ti.

Then the Blessed One, having dwelt at Pālileyyaka for as long as he wished, set out on a journey for Sāvatthī. Journeying by stages, he arrived at Sāvatthī. There the Blessed One dwelt in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Monastery. Then the lay followers of Kosambī deliberated: “These venerable monks of Kosambī are the cause of much harm to us. Harassed by them, the Blessed One departed. Come, let us neither pay homage to the venerable monks of Kosambī, nor rise up for them, nor perform the gesture of reverence and the act of respect, nor honor them, nor revere them, nor esteem them, nor associate with them, nor venerate them. Even if they approach, we will not give them almsfood. Thus, not being honored, not being revered, not being esteemed, not being associated with, not being venerated, and being afflicted by this lack of hospitality from us, they will either depart, or they will disrobe, or they will appease the Blessed One.” Then the lay followers of Kosambī neither paid homage to the monks of Kosambī, nor rose up for them, nor performed the gesture of reverence and the act of respect, nor honored them, nor revered them, nor esteemed them, nor associated with them, nor venerated them. Even when they approached, they did not give them almsfood. Then the monks of Kosambī, not being honored, not being revered, not being esteemed, not being associated with, not being venerated, and being afflicted by this lack of hospitality from the lay followers of Kosambī, said this: “Come, friends, let us go to Sāvatthī and settle this dispute in the presence of the Blessed One.”

Pālileyyakagamanakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Journey to Pālileyyaka is concluded.

276. Aṭṭhārasavatthukathā

The Account of the Eighteen Matters

468. Atha [V 0.0476] kho kosambakā bhikkhū senāsanaṃ saṃsāmetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena sāvatthi tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Assosi kho āyasmā sāriputto – “te kira kosambakā bhikkhū [T 2.0344] bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā sāvatthiṃ āgacchantī”ti. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “te kira, bhante, kosambakā bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā sāvatthiṃ āgacchanti. Kathāhaṃ, bhante, tesu bhikkhūsu paṭipajjāmī”ti? “Tena hi tvaṃ, sāriputta, yathā dhammo tathā tiṭṭhāhī”ti. “Kathāhaṃ, bhante, jāneyyaṃ dhammaṃ vā adhammaṃ vā”ti?

276. Then the monks from Kosambī, having put away their lodging and taken their bowl and robes, approached Sāvatthī. The Venerable Sāriputta heard: “It is said that those monks from Kosambī—makers of quarrels, makers of strife, makers of disputes, makers of chatter, and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha—are coming to Sāvatthī.” Then the Venerable Sāriputta approached the Blessed One, and having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, it is said that those monks from Kosambī—makers of quarrels, makers of strife, makers of disputes, makers of chatter, and makers of legal issues in the Saṅgha—are coming to Sāvatthī. How, Venerable Sir, should I conduct myself toward those monks?” “In that case, Sāriputta, you should stand as the Dhamma stands.” “But how, Venerable Sir, am I to know the Dhamma or the non-Dhamma?”

Aṭṭhārasahi kho, sāriputta, vatthūhi adhammavādī jānitabbo. Idha, sāriputta, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti; avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti; abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena [M 0.0502] bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti; anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti; apaññattaṃ tathāgatena paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, paññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti; anāpattiṃ āpattīti dīpeti, āpattiṃ anāpattīti dīpeti; lahukaṃ āpattiṃ garukā āpattīti dīpeti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ lahukā āpattīti dīpeti; sāvasesaṃ āpattiṃ anavasesā [T 2.0345] āpattīti dīpeti, anavasesaṃ āpattiṃ sāvasesā āpattīti dīpeti; duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti – imehi kho, sāriputta, aṭṭhārasahi vatthūhi adhammavādī jānitabbo.

468. Sāriputta, a speaker of what is not the Dhamma should be known by eighteen matters. In this Dispensation, Sāriputta, a monk declares what is not the Dhamma as the Dhamma, and the Dhamma as what is not the Dhamma; what is not the Discipline as the Discipline, and the Discipline as what is not the Discipline; what was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata, and what was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata; what was not practiced by the Tathāgata as practiced by the Tathāgata, and what was practiced by the Tathāgata as not practiced by the Tathāgata; what was not prescribed by the Tathāgata as prescribed by the Tathāgata, and what was prescribed by the Tathāgata as not prescribed by the Tathāgata; a non-offense as an offense, and an offense as a non-offense; a light offense as a grave offense, and a grave offense as a light offense; an offense with a remainder as an offense without a remainder, and an offense without a remainder as an offense with a remainder; a gross offense as a non-gross offense, and a non-gross offense as a gross offense—by these eighteen matters, Sāriputta, a speaker of what is not the Dhamma should be known.

Aṭṭhārasahi ca kho, sāriputta, vatthūhi dhammavādī jānitabbo. Idha, sāriputta, bhikkhu adhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti; avinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti; abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena [P 1.0355] abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti; anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti; apaññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, paññattaṃ tathāgatena paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti[V 0.0477]; anāpattiṃ anāpattīti dīpeti, āpattiṃ āpattīti dīpeti; lahukaṃ āpattiṃ lahukā āpattīti dīpeti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ garukā āpattīti dīpeti; sāvasesaṃ āpattiṃ sāvasesā āpattīti dīpeti, anavasesaṃ āpattiṃ anavasesā āpattīti dīpeti; duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti – imehi kho, sāriputta, aṭṭhārasahi vatthūhi dhammavādī jānitabboti.

Furthermore, Sāriputta, a speaker of the Dhamma is to be known by eighteen points. Here, Sāriputta, a monk declares what is not the Dhamma as 'not the Dhamma', and the Dhamma as 'the Dhamma'; what is not the Discipline as 'not the Discipline', and the Discipline as 'the Discipline'; what was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as 'not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata', and what was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as 'spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata'; what was not practiced by the Tathāgata as 'not practiced by the Tathāgata', and what was practiced by the Tathāgata as 'practiced by the Tathāgata'; what was not prescribed by the Tathāgata as 'not prescribed by the Tathāgata', and what was prescribed by the Tathāgata as 'prescribed by the Tathāgata'; a non-offense as 'a non-offense', and an offense as 'an offense'; a light offense as 'a light offense', and a grave offense as 'a grave offense'; an offense with a remainder as 'an offense with a remainder', and an offense without a remainder as 'an offense without a remainder'; a gross offense as 'a gross offense', and a non-gross offense as 'a non-gross offense'—by these eighteen points, Sāriputta, a speaker of the Dhamma is to be known.

469. Assosi kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno…pe… assosi kho āyasmā mahākassapo… assosi kho āyasmā mahākaccāno… assosi kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko [T 2.0346]… assosi kho āyasmā mahākappino… assosi kho āyasmā mahācundo… assosi kho āyasmā anuruddho… assosi kho āyasmā revato [M 0.0503] … assosi kho āyasmā upāli… assosi kho āyasmā ānando… assosi kho āyasmā rāhulo – “te kira kosambakā bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā sāvatthiṃ āgacchantī”ti. Atha kho āyasmā rāhulo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā rāhulo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “te kira, bhante, kosambakā bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā sāvatthiṃ āgacchanti. Kathāhaṃ, bhante, tesu bhikkhūsu paṭipajjāmī”ti? “Tena hi tvaṃ, rāhula, yathā dhammo tathā tiṭṭhāhī”ti. “Kathāhaṃ, bhante, jāneyyaṃ dhammaṃ vā adhammaṃ vā”ti?

469. Venerable Mahāmoggallāna heard … Venerable Mahākassapa heard … Venerable Mahākaccāna heard … Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika heard … Venerable Mahākappina heard … Venerable Mahācunda heard … Venerable Anuruddha heard … Venerable Revata heard … Venerable Upāli heard … Venerable Ānanda heard … Venerable Rāhula heard: “It is said that those monks from Kosambī who are quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, verbose, and who create disputes in the Saṅgha are coming to Sāvatthī.” Then Venerable Rāhula approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Venerable Rāhula said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is said that those monks from Kosambī who are quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, verbose, and who create disputes in the Saṅgha are coming to Sāvatthī. How, venerable sir, should I conduct myself toward those monks?” “In that case, Rāhula, you should stand in accordance with the Dhamma.” “But how, venerable sir, am I to know what is the Dhamma and what is not the Dhamma?”

Aṭṭhārasahi kho, rāhula, vatthūhi adhammavādī jānitabbo. Idha, rāhula, bhikkhu adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti; avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti; abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti; anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti; apaññattaṃ tathāgatena paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, paññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti; anāpattiṃ āpattīti dīpeti, āpattiṃ anāpattīti dīpeti; lahukaṃ āpattiṃ garukā āpattīti dīpeti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ lahukā āpattīti dīpeti; sāvasesaṃ āpattiṃ anavasesā āpattīti dīpeti, anavasesaṃ āpattiṃ sāvasesā āpattīti dīpeti; duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti – imehi kho, rāhula, aṭṭhārasahi vatthūhi adhammavādī jānitabbo.

Rāhula, a speaker of what is not the Dhamma is to be known by eighteen points. Here, Rāhula, a monk declares what is not the Dhamma as 'the Dhamma', and the Dhamma as 'what is not the Dhamma'; he declares what is not the Discipline as 'the Discipline', and the Discipline as 'what is not the Discipline'; he declares what was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as 'spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata', and what was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as 'not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata'; he declares what was not practiced by the Tathāgata as 'practiced by the Tathāgata', and what was practiced by the Tathāgata as 'not practiced by the Tathāgata'; he declares what was not prescribed by the Tathāgata as 'prescribed by the Tathāgata', and what was prescribed by the Tathāgata as 'not prescribed by the Tathāgata'; he declares a non-offense as 'an offense', and an offense as 'a non-offense'; he declares a light offense as 'a grave offense', and a grave offense as 'a light offense'; he declares an offense with a remainder as 'an offense without a remainder', and an offense without a remainder as 'an offense with a remainder'; he declares a gross offense as 'a non-gross offense', and a non-gross offense as 'a gross offense'. By these eighteen points, Rāhula, a speaker of what is not the Dhamma is to be known.

Aṭṭhārasahi [V 0.0478] ca kho, rāhula, vatthūhi dhammavādī jānitabbo. Idha, rāhula, bhikkhu adhammaṃ adhammoti dīpeti, dhammaṃ dhammoti dīpeti; avinayaṃ avinayoti dīpeti, vinayaṃ vinayoti dīpeti; abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti; anāciṇṇaṃ [M 0.0504] tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti; apaññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti, paññattaṃ tathāgatena paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpeti; anāpattiṃ anāpattīti dīpeti, āpattiṃ āpattīti dīpeti; lahukaṃ āpattiṃ lahukā āpattīti dīpeti, garukaṃ āpattiṃ garukā āpattīti dīpeti; sāvasesaṃ āpattiṃ sāvasesā āpattīti dīpeti, anavasesaṃ āpattiṃ anavasesā āpattīti dīpeti; duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullā āpattīti dīpeti – imehi kho, rāhula, aṭṭhārasahi vatthūhi dhammavādī jānitabboti.

Furthermore, Rāhula, a speaker of the Dhamma is to be known by eighteen points. Here, Rāhula, a monk declares what is not the Dhamma as 'not the Dhamma', and the Dhamma as 'the Dhamma'; he declares what is not the Discipline as 'not the Discipline', and the Discipline as 'the Discipline'; he declares what was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as 'not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata', and what was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as 'spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata'; he declares what was not practiced by the Tathāgata as 'not practiced by the Tathāgata', and what was practiced by the Tathāgata as 'practiced by the Tathāgata'; he declares what was not prescribed by the Tathāgata as 'not prescribed by the Tathāgata', and what was prescribed by the Tathāgata as 'prescribed by the Tathāgata'; he declares a non-offense as 'a non-offense', and an offense as 'an offense'; he declares a light offense as 'a light offense', and a grave offense as 'a grave offense'; he declares an offense with a remainder as 'an offense with a remainder', and an offense without a remainder as 'an offense without a remainder'; he declares a gross offense as 'a gross offense', and a non-gross offense as 'a non-gross offense'. By these eighteen points, Rāhula, a speaker of the Dhamma is to be known.

470. Assosi kho mahāpajāpati mahāpajāpatī (sī. syā.) gotamī – “te kira kosambakā bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā [T 2.0347] sāvatthiṃ āgacchantī”ti. Atha kho mahāpajāpati gotamī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho mahāpajāpati gotamī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “te kira, bhante, kosambakā bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā sāvatthiṃ āgacchanti. Kathāhaṃ, bhante, tesu bhikkhūsu paṭipajjāmī”ti? “Tena hi tvaṃ, gotami, ubhayattha dhammaṃ suṇa. Ubhayattha dhammaṃ sutvā ye tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino tesaṃ diṭṭhiñca khantiñca ruciñca ādāyañca rocehi. Yañca kiñci bhikkhunisaṅghena bhikkhusaṅghato paccāsīsitabbaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ dhammavāditova paccāsīsitabba”nti.

470. Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī heard: 'It is said that those monks from Kosambī—who are quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, wrangling, and who cause formal disputes in the Saṅgha—are coming to Sāvatthī.' Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Blessed One, and having approached, paid homage to him and stood to one side. Standing to one side, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, it is said that those monks from Kosambī—who are quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, wrangling, and who cause formal disputes in the Saṅgha—are coming to Sāvatthī. How, venerable sir, should I conduct myself towards those monks?' 'In that case, Gotamī, you should listen to the Dhamma from both factions. Having listened to the Dhamma from both factions, you should accept and approve of the view, the preference, and the inclination of those monks who are speakers of the Dhamma. And whatever the community of nuns is to expect from the community of monks, all of that should be expected only from those who are speakers of the Dhamma.'

471. Assosi kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati – “te kira kosambakā bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā sāvatthiṃ āgacchantī”ti. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “te kira, bhante, kosambakā bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā [M 0.0505] saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā sāvatthiṃ āgacchanti. Kathāhaṃ, bhante, tesu bhikkhūsu paṭipajjāmī”ti? “Tena hi tvaṃ, gahapati, ubhayattha dānaṃ dehi. Ubhayattha dānaṃ [V 0.0479] datvā ubhayattha dhammaṃ suṇa. Ubhayattha dhammaṃ sutvā ye tattha [T 2.0348] bhikkhū dhammavādino tesaṃ diṭṭhiñca khantiñca ruciñca ādāyañca rocehī”ti.

471. The householder Anāthapiṇḍika heard: 'It is said that those monks from Kosambī—who are quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, wrangling, and who cause formal disputes in the Saṅgha—are coming to Sāvatthī.' Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika approached the Blessed One, and having approached, paid homage to him and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, it is said that those monks from Kosambī—who are quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, wrangling, and who cause formal disputes in the Saṅgha—are coming to Sāvatthī. How, venerable sir, should I conduct myself towards those monks?' 'In that case, householder, you should give alms to both factions. Having given alms to both factions, listen to the Dhamma from both factions. Having listened to the Dhamma from both factions, you should accept and approve of the view, the preference, and the inclination of those monks among them who are speakers of the Dhamma.'

472. Assosi kho visākhā migāramātā – “te kira kosambakā bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā sāvatthiṃ āgacchantī”ti[P 1.0356]. Atha kho visākhā migāramātā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho visākhā migāramātā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “te kira, bhante, kosambakā bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā sāvatthiṃ āgacchanti. Kathāhaṃ, bhante, tesu bhikkhūsu paṭipajjāmī”ti? “Tena hi tvaṃ, visākhe, ubhayattha dānaṃ dehi. Ubhayattha dānaṃ datvā ubhayattha dhammaṃ suṇa. Ubhayattha dhammaṃ sutvā ye tattha bhikkhū dhammavādino tesaṃ diṭṭhiñca khantiñca ruciñca ādāyañca rocehī”ti.

472. Visākhā Migāramātā heard: 'It is said that those monks from Kosambī—who are quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, wrangling, and who cause formal disputes in the Saṅgha—are coming to Sāvatthī.' Then Visākhā Migāramātā approached the Blessed One, and having approached, paid homage to him and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Visākhā Migāramātā said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, it is said that those monks from Kosambī—who are quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, wrangling, and who cause formal disputes in the Saṅgha—are coming to Sāvatthī. How, venerable sir, should I conduct myself towards those monks?' 'In that case, Visākhā, you should give alms to both factions. Having given alms to both factions, listen to the Dhamma from both factions. Having listened to the Dhamma from both factions, you should accept and approve of the view, the preference, and the inclination of those monks among them who are speakers of the Dhamma.'

473. Atha kho kosambakā bhikkhū anupubbena yena sāvatthi tadavasaruṃ. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “te kira, bhante, kosambakā bhikkhū bhaṇḍanakārakā kalahakārakā vivādakārakā bhassakārakā saṅghe adhikaraṇakārakā sāvatthiṃ anuppattā. Kathaṃ [T 2.0349] nu kho, bhante, tesu bhikkhūsu senāsane senāsanesu (ka.), senāsanaṃ (syā.) paṭipajjitabba”nti? “Tena hi, sāriputta, vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ dātabba”nti. “Sace pana, bhante, vivittaṃ na hoti, kathaṃ paṭipajjitabba”nti? “Tena hi, sāriputta, vivittaṃ katvāpi dātabbaṃ, na tvevāhaṃ, sāriputta, kenaci pariyāyena vuḍḍhatarassa bhikkhuno senāsanaṃ paṭibāhitabbanti vadāmi. Yo paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.

473. Then the monks from Kosambī, traveling in stages, arrived at Sāvatthī. Then the venerable Sāriputta approached the Blessed One, and having approached, paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the venerable Sāriputta said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, it is said that those monks from Kosambī—who are quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, wrangling, and who cause formal disputes in the Saṅgha—have arrived at Sāvatthī. How, venerable sir, should one act towards those monks with regard to lodging?' 'In that case, Sāriputta, a secluded lodging should be given.' 'But if, venerable sir, a secluded lodging is not available, how should one act?' 'In that case, Sāriputta, having made one secluded, it should be given. However, Sāriputta, I do not say that by any means the lodging of a more senior monk should be denied. Whoever should deny it, incurs an offense of wrong-doing.'

“Āmise pana, bhante, kathaṃ paṭipajjitabba”nti? “Āmisaṃ kho, sāriputta, sabbesaṃ samakaṃ bhājetabba”nti.

“And with regard to material requisites, venerable sir, how should one act?” “Material requisites, Sāriputta, should be distributed equally to all.”

Aṭṭhārasavatthukathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on the eighteen topics is concluded.

277. Osāraṇānujānanā

Permission for Reinstatement

474. Atha [M 0.0506][V 0.0480] kho tassa ukkhittakassa bhikkhuno dhammañca vinayañca paccavekkhantassa etadahosi – “āpatti esā, nesā anāpatti. Āpannomhi, namhi anāpanno. Ukkhittomhi, namhi anukkhitto. Dhammikenamhi kammena ukkhitto akuppena ṭhānārahenā”ti. Atha kho so ukkhittako bhikkhu yena ukkhittānuvattakā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā ukkhittānuvattake bhikkhū etadavoca – “āpatti esā, āvuso; nesā anāpatti. Āpannomhi, namhi anāpanno. Ukkhittomhi, namhi anukkhitto. Dhammikenamhi kammena ukkhitto akuppena ṭhānārahena. Etha maṃ āyasmanto osārethā”ti. Atha kho te ukkhittānuvattakā bhikkhū taṃ ukkhittakaṃ bhikkhuṃ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “ayaṃ, bhante, ukkhittako bhikkhu evamāha – ‘āpatti esā[T 2.0350], āvuso; nesā anāpatti. Āpannomhi, namhi anāpanno. Ukkhittomhi, namhi anukkhitto. Dhammikenamhi kammena ukkhitto akuppena ṭhānārahena. Etha maṃ āyasmanto osārethā’ti. Kathaṃ nu kho, bhante, paṭipajjitabba”nti? “Āpatti esā, bhikkhave; nesā anāpatti. Āpanno eso bhikkhu, neso bhikkhu anāpanno. Ukkhitto eso bhikkhu, neso bhikkhu anukkhitto[P 1.0357]. Dhammikena kammena ukkhitto akuppena ṭhānārahena. Yato ca kho so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āpanno ca ukkhitto ca passati ca, tena hi, bhikkhave, taṃ bhikkhuṃ osārethā”ti.

474. Then that monk who had been expelled, reflecting on the Dhamma and the Vinaya, thought: “This is an offense, not a non-offense. I have committed an offense; I am not one who has not committed an offense. I have been expelled; I am not one who has not been expelled. I have been expelled by a lawful act, irreversible, worthy to stand.” Then that monk who had been expelled approached the monks who supported the expelled monk, and upon arrival said to them: “This is an offense, friends; it is not a non-offense. I have committed an offense; I am not one who has not committed an offense. I have been expelled; I am not one who has not been expelled. I have been expelled by a lawful act, irreversible, worthy to stand. Come, Venerables, reinstate me.” Then those monks who supported the expelled monk took that monk who had been expelled and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, those monks said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, this monk who had been expelled says: ‘This is an offense, friends; it is not a non-offense. I have committed an offense; I am not one who has not committed an offense. I have been expelled; I am not one who has not been expelled. I have been expelled by a lawful act, irreversible, worthy to stand. Come, Venerables, reinstate me.’ How then, Venerable Sir, should we proceed?” “This is an offense, bhikkhus; it is not a non-offense. This monk has committed an offense; he is not one who has not committed an offense. This monk has been expelled; he is not one who has not been expelled. He has been expelled by a lawful act, irreversible, worthy to stand. Since, bhikkhus, that monk has committed an offense and has been expelled, and he sees it, therefore, bhikkhus, you should reinstate that monk.”

Osāraṇānujānanā niṭṭhitā.

The Permission for Reinstatement is concluded.

278. Saṅghasāmaggīkathā

Discourse on Harmony in the Saṅgha

475. Atha kho te ukkhittānuvattakā bhikkhū taṃ ukkhittakaṃ bhikkhuṃ osāretvā yena ukkhepakā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā ukkhepake bhikkhū etadavocuṃ – “yasmiṃ, āvuso, vatthusmiṃ ahosi saṅghassa bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇaṃ[T 2.0351], so eso bhikkhu āpanno ca ukkhitto ca passi passī (itipi) ca osārito ca. Handa mayaṃ, āvuso, tassa vatthussa vūpasamāya saṅghasāmaggiṃ karomā”ti.

278. Then those monks who were followers of the expelled one, having reinstated that expelled monk, approached the monks who had expelled him. Having approached, they said to the monks who had expelled him: “Friends, regarding the matter in which there was dispute, quarrel, contention, and argument in the Saṅgha, a schism in the Saṅgha, a rift in the Saṅgha, a separation in the Saṅgha, and dissension in the Saṅgha—that monk has committed an offense, has been expelled, has seen it, and has been reinstated. Come now, friends, let us perform Saṅgha harmony for the settlement of that matter.”

Atha [M 0.0507][V 0.0481] kho te ukkhepakā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “te, bhante, ukkhittānuvattakā bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu – ‘yasmiṃ, āvuso, vatthusmiṃ ahosi saṅghassa bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇaṃ, so eso bhikkhu āpanno ca ukkhitto ca passi ca osārito ca. Handa mayaṃ, āvuso, tassa vatthussa vūpasamāya saṅghasāmaggiṃ karomā’ti. Kathaṃ nu kho, bhante, paṭipajjitabba”nti? Yato ca kho so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āpanno ca ukkhitto ca passi ca osārito ca, tena hi, bhikkhave, saṅgho tassa vatthussa vūpasamāya saṅghasāmaggiṃ karotu. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, kātabbā. Sabbeheva ekajjhaṃ sannipatitabbaṃ gilānehi ca agilānehi ca. Na kehici chando dātabbo. Sannipatitvā byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo –

475. Then those monks who had expelled him approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those monks said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, those monks who are followers of the expelled one said thus: ‘Friends, regarding the matter in which there was dispute, quarrel, contention, and argument in the Saṅgha, a schism in the Saṅgha, a rift in the Saṅgha, a separation in the Saṅgha, and dissension in the Saṅgha—that monk has committed an offense, has been expelled, has seen it, and has been reinstated. Come now, friends, let us perform Saṅgha harmony for the settlement of that matter.’ How then, Venerable Sir, should we proceed?” “Bhikkhus, since that monk has committed an offense, has been expelled, has seen it, and has been reinstated, then, bhikkhus, the Saṅgha should perform Saṅgha harmony for the settlement of that matter. And this, bhikkhus, is how it should be done. All should gather together, both the sick and the healthy. Consent should not be given by anyone. Having gathered, the Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and capable bhikkhu:

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ ahosi saṅghassa bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇaṃ, so eso bhikkhu āpanno ca ukkhitto ca passi ca osārito ca. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho tassa vatthussa vūpasamāya saṅghasāmaggiṃ kareyya. Esā ñatti.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my words. In whatever matter there arose for the Saṅgha dispute, quarrel, contention, argument, schism in the Saṅgha, a rift in the Saṅgha, a separation in the Saṅgha, and dissension in the Saṅgha—that monk has both committed an offense and been expelled, has seen it and been reinstated. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should bring about harmony in the Saṅgha for the pacification of that matter. This is the motion.

“Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ ahosi saṅghassa bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇaṃ, so eso bhikkhu āpanno ca ukkhitto ca passi ca osārito ca. Saṅgho tassa vatthussa vūpasamāya saṅghasāmaggiṃ karoti. Yassāyasmato khamati tassa vatthussa vūpasamāya saṅghasāmaggiyā karaṇaṃ, so tuṇhassa, yassa nakkhamati so bhāseyya.

“Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear my words. In whatever matter there arose for the Saṅgha dispute, quarrel, contention, argument, schism in the Saṅgha, a rift in the Saṅgha, a separation in the Saṅgha, and dissension in the Saṅgha—that monk has both committed an offense and been expelled, has seen it and been reinstated. The Saṅgha is bringing about harmony in the Saṅgha for the pacification of that matter. To whichever venerable one the bringing about of harmony in the Saṅgha for the pacification of that matter is agreeable, he should be silent; he to whom it is not agreeable should speak.

“Katā saṅghena tassa vatthussa vūpasamāya saṅghasāmaggī. Nihato [T 2.0352] saṅghabhedo, nihatā saṅgharāji, nihataṃ saṅghavavatthānaṃ, nihataṃ saṅghanānākaraṇaṃ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti.

“Harmony in the Saṅgha has been brought about by the Saṅgha for the pacification of that matter. Schism in the Saṅgha has been struck down, the rift in the Saṅgha has been struck down, the separation in the Saṅgha has been struck down, and the dissension in the Saṅgha has been struck down. It is agreeable to the Saṅgha, therefore it is silent. Thus do I bear this in mind.”

Tāvadeva uposatho kātabbo, pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabbanti.

The Uposatha should be performed right then, and the Pātimokkha should be recited.

Saṅghasāmaggīkathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Harmony in the Saṅgha is concluded.

279. Upālisaṅghasāmaggīpucchā

Upāli’s Question on Saṅgha Harmony

476. Atha [P 1.0358][M 0.0508][V 0.0482] kho āyasmā upāli yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā upāli bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yasmiṃ, bhante, vatthusmiṃ hoti saṅghassa bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇaṃ, saṅgho taṃ vatthuṃ avinicchinitvā amūlā mūlaṃ gantvā saṅghasāmaggiṃ karoti, dhammikā nu kho sā, bhante, saṅghasāmaggī”ti? “Yasmiṃ[T 2.0353], upāli, vatthusmiṃ hoti saṅghassa bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇaṃ, saṅgho taṃ vatthuṃ avinicchinitvā amūlā mūlaṃ gantvā saṅghasāmaggiṃ karoti, adhammikā sā, upāli, saṅghasāmaggī”ti.

476. Then the Venerable Upāli approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Upāli said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, in a matter wherein arises for the Saṅgha quarreling, disputing, contention, disagreement, schism in the Saṅgha, a crack in the Saṅgha, separation in the Saṅgha, and causing dissension in the Saṅgha, if the Saṅgha, without having resolved that matter, having gone from what is not the root to the root, establishes unity for the Saṅgha, is that unity of the Saṅgha, Venerable Sir, in accordance with the Dhamma?' 'Upāli, in a matter wherein arises for the Saṅgha quarreling, disputing, contention, disagreement, schism in the Saṅgha, a crack in the Saṅgha, separation in the Saṅgha, and causing dissension in the Saṅgha, if the Saṅgha, without having resolved that matter, having gone from what is not the root to the root, establishes unity for the Saṅgha, that unity of the Saṅgha, Upāli, is not in accordance with the Dhamma.'

“Yasmiṃ pana, bhante, vatthusmiṃ hoti saṅghassa bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇaṃ, saṅgho taṃ vatthuṃ vinicchinitvā mūlā mūlaṃ gantvā saṅghasāmaggiṃ karoti, dhammikā nu kho sā, bhante, saṅghasāmaggī”ti? “Yasmiṃ, upāli, vatthusmiṃ hoti saṅghassa bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇaṃ, saṅgho taṃ vatthuṃ vinicchinitvā mūlā mūlaṃ gantvā saṅghasāmaggiṃ karoti, dhammikā sā, upāli, saṅghasāmaggī”ti.

'But, Venerable Sir, in a matter wherein arises for the Saṅgha quarreling, disputing, contention, disagreement, schism in the Saṅgha, a crack in the Saṅgha, separation in the Saṅgha, and causing dissension in the Saṅgha, if the Saṅgha, having resolved that matter, having gone from the root to the root, establishes unity for the Saṅgha, is that unity of the Saṅgha, Venerable Sir, in accordance with the Dhamma?' 'Upāli, in a matter wherein arises for the Saṅgha quarreling, disputing, contention, disagreement, schism in the Saṅgha, a crack in the Saṅgha, separation in the Saṅgha, and causing dissension in the Saṅgha, if the Saṅgha, having resolved that matter, having gone from the root to the root, establishes unity for the Saṅgha, that unity of the Saṅgha, Upāli, is in accordance with the Dhamma.'

“Kati nu kho, bhante, saṅghasāmaggiyo”ti? “Dvemā, upāli, saṅghasāmaggiyo – atthupāli, saṅghasāmaggī atthāpetā byañjanupetā; atthupāli, saṅghasāmaggī atthupetā ca byañjanupetā ca. Katamā ca, upāli, saṅghasāmaggī atthāpetā byañjanupetā? Yasmiṃ, upāli, vatthusmiṃ hoti saṅghassa bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇaṃ, saṅgho taṃ vatthuṃ avinicchinitvā amūlā mūlaṃ gantvā saṅghasāmaggiṃ karoti, ayaṃ vuccati, upāli, saṅghasāmaggī atthāpetā byañjanupetā. Katamā ca, upāli, saṅghasāmaggī atthupetā ca byañjanupetā ca? Yasmiṃ, upāli, vatthusmiṃ hoti saṅghassa bhaṇḍanaṃ kalaho viggaho vivādo saṅghabhedo saṅgharāji saṅghavavatthānaṃ saṅghanānākaraṇaṃ, saṅgho taṃ vatthuṃ vinicchinitvā mūlā mūlaṃ gantvā saṅghasāmaggiṃ karoti, ayaṃ vuccati, upāli, saṅghasāmaggī atthupetā ca byañjanupetā ca. Imā kho, upāli, dve saṅghasāmaggiyo”ti.

“Venerable Sir, how many unities of the Saṅgha are there?” “Upāli, there are these two unities of the Saṅgha: there is, Upāli, a unity of the Saṅgha that is devoid of meaning but endowed with expression; and there is, Upāli, a unity of the Saṅgha that is endowed with both meaning and expression. And what, Upāli, is the unity of the Saṅgha that is devoid of meaning but endowed with expression? Herein, Upāli, regarding a matter wherein there arises for the Saṅgha dispute in absence, quarrel in presence, physical contention, contradictory speech, schism in the Saṅgha, a crack in the Saṅgha, separation in the Saṅgha, and making the Saṅgha diverse, the Saṅgha, without having decided that matter, having proceeded from what is not the root to a root, establishes unity of the Saṅgha. This, Upāli, is called the unity of the Saṅgha that is devoid of meaning but endowed with expression. And what, Upāli, is the unity of the Saṅgha that is endowed with both meaning and expression? Herein, Upāli, regarding a matter wherein there arises for the Saṅgha dispute in absence, quarrel in presence, physical contention, contradictory speech, schism in the Saṅgha, a crack in the Saṅgha, separation in the Saṅgha, and making the Saṅgha diverse, the Saṅgha, having decided that matter, having proceeded from the root to the root, establishes unity of the Saṅgha. This, Upāli, is called the unity of the Saṅgha that is endowed with both meaning and expression. These, indeed, Upāli, are the two unities of the Saṅgha.”

477. Atha [M 0.0509][V 0.0483] kho āyasmā upāli uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

477. Then the Venerable Upāli rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, extended his joined palms in reverential salutation toward the Blessed One, and addressed the Blessed One in verse:

“Saṅghassa [T 2.0354] kiccesu ca mantanāsu ca;

Atthesu jātesu vinicchayesu ca;

Kathaṃpakārodha naro mahatthiko;

Bhikkhu kathaṃ hotidha paggahārahoti.

“In the Saṅgha’s affairs and in consultations,

When matters have arisen and in their determinations,

What kind of person here is of great benefit?

What kind of monk here is worthy of being extolled?”

“Anānuvajjo [P 1.0359] paṭhamena sīlato;

Avekkhitācāro susaṃvutindriyo;

Paccatthikā nūpavadanti dhammato;

Na hissa taṃ hoti vadeyyu yena naṃ.

“Primarily, he is irreproachable in terms of virtue;

His conduct is well-considered, his faculties well-restrained.

Adversaries cannot rightfully reproach him,

For that fault by which they might blame him does not exist in him.”

“So tādiso sīlavisuddhiyā ṭhito;

Visārado hoti visayha bhāsati;

Nacchambhati parisagato na vedhati;

Atthaṃ na hāpeti anuyyutaṃ bhaṇaṃ.

“Such a monk, established in purity of virtue,

Is confident when he enters an assembly; he speaks having overcome.

He is not intimidated, nor does he tremble.

Speaking on what is relevant, he does not forsake the meaning.”

“Tatheva pañhaṃ parisāsu pucchito;

Na ceva pajjhāyati na maṅku hoti;

So kālāgataṃ byākaraṇārahaṃ vaco;

Rañjeti viññūparisaṃ vicakkhaṇo.

“Likewise, when asked a question in assemblies,

He is not bewildered, nor does he become downcast;

That wise one, speaking a word that is timely and worthy of explanation,

Delights the assembly of the wise.”

“Sagāravo vuḍḍhataresu bhikkhusu;

Ācerakamhi ca sake visārado;

Alaṃ pametuṃ paguṇo kathetave;

Paccatthikānañca viraddhikovido.

“Respectful toward elder monks,

And confident in his own teacher's tradition;

Capable of investigating, practiced in speaking,

And skilled in refuting the errors of opponents.”

“Paccatthikā [T 2.0355] yena vajanti niggahaṃ;

Mahājano saññapanañca gacchati;

Sakañca [V 0.0484] ādāyamayaṃ na riñcati;

Viyākaraṃ so byākaraṃ (sī.), veyyākaraṃ (syā.) pañhamanūpaghātikaṃ.

“By which speech opponents are led to defeat

And the great populace attains understanding;

This monk, explaining a non-injurious question,

Does not abandon his own tradition.”

“Dūteyyakammesu [M 0.0510] alaṃ samuggaho;

Saṅghassa kiccesu ca āhu naṃ yathā;

Karaṃ vaco bhikkhugaṇena pesito;

Ahaṃ karomīti na tena maññati.

“Competent in the duties of a messenger, he undertakes the affairs of the Saṅgha well, just as one would accept a worthy offering.

Sent by the community of monks, he is obedient to their word;

On that account, he does not think conceitedly, 'It is I who am doing this.'”

“Āpajjati yāvatakesu vatthusu;

Āpattiyā hoti yathā ca vuṭṭhiti;

Ete vibhaṅgā ubhayassa svāgatā;

Āpatti vuṭṭhānapadassa kovido.

“In however many cases one incurs an offense,

And how there is rehabilitation from an offense—

Both these analyses are well-mastered by him;

He is skilled in the procedure for rehabilitation from an offense.”

“Nissāraṇaṃ gacchati yāni cācaraṃ;

Nissārito hoti yathā ca vattanā vatthunā (sī. syā.);

Osāraṇaṃ taṃvusitassa jantuno;

Etampi jānāti vibhaṅgakovido.

“He knows by what conduct one is liable for expulsion,

And how one who has been expelled should behave;

He knows the reinstatement for the person who has completed that practice—

The one skilled in the analyses knows this too.”

“Sagāravo vuḍḍhataresu bhikkhusu;

Navesu theresu ca majjhimesu ca;

Mahājanassatthacarodha paṇḍito;

So tādiso bhikkhu idha paggahāraho”ti.

“Respectful toward senior monks,

And toward new, elder, and middle-ranking monks;

Wise, he acts for the welfare of the great populace here.

Such a monk is worthy of esteem in this Dispensation.”

Upālisaṅghasāmaggīpucchā niṭṭhitā.

The Questions of Upāli on Saṅgha Unity are concluded.

Kosambakakkhandhako dasamo.

The Kosambaka Chapter, the tenth, is concluded.

280. Tassuddānaṃ [P 1.0360]

The Summary:

Kosambiyaṃ [T 2.0356] jinavaro, vivādāpattidassane;

Nukkhipeyya yasmiṃ tasmiṃ, saddhāyāpatti desaye.

280. The Best of Victors at Kosambī; dispute over not seeing an offense; one should not suspend for any reason whatsoever; confessing an offense through faith.

Antosīmāyaṃ [V 0.0485] tattheva, bālakañceva vaṃsadā;

Pālileyyā ca sāvatthi, sāriputto ca kolito.

Within the boundary, in that very place; the wise understand; departing all alone; Pārileyyaka and Sāvatthī; Sāriputta and Kolita.

Mahākassapakaccānā, koṭṭhiko kappinena ca;

Mahācundo ca anuruddho, revato upāli cubho.

Mahākassapa and Kaccāna; Koṭṭhika and Kappina; Mahācunda and Anuruddha; Revata and Upāli, both.

Ānando [M 0.0511] rāhulo ceva, gotamīnāthapiṇḍiko;

Senāsanaṃ vivittañca, āmisaṃ samakampi ca.

Ānanda and Rāhula; Gotamī and Anāthapiṇḍika; a secluded lodging; and material requisites equally.

Na kehi chando dātabbo, upāliparipucchito;

Anānuvajjo sīlena, sāmaggī jinasāsaneti.

By whom consent should not be given; questioned by Upāli; blameless in virtue; unity in the Victor's Dispensation.

Kosambakakkhandhako niṭṭhito.

The Kosambaka Chapter is concluded.

Mahāvaggapāḷi niṭṭhitā.

The Pāḷi of the Great Division is concluded.
